name: Morris Chang
current_role: Founder and retired chairman (since 2018), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC)
profile: Chinese-born, US-educated engineer who spent ~25 years at Texas Instruments, then led Taiwan's ITRI and in 1987 founded TSMC, the world's first dedicated chip foundry, whose customers include Apple, Nvidia and Qualcomm. Retired as chairman in 2018; now in his mid-90s, he keeps a low profile (a rare public dinner with Jensen Huang in Jan 2026).
interesting_fact: He pioneered pricing chips 'ahead of the cost curve' at TI - sacrificing early profit for market share and yield - and later invented the pure-play foundry model; TSMC was the first Taiwanese firm to list on the NYSE (1997).
deep_cut_fact: His 1964 Stanford PhD (sponsored by Texas Instruments, finished in about two years under John L. Moll) was on 'Optical absorption and photoluminescence of doped GaAs and (InxGa1-x)As'; earlier he had turned down a Ford Motor job offer in 1955 to join Sylvania's small semiconductor unit.
notes: Retired; age ~95, rarely appears publicly (reportedly using a wheelchair in Jan 2026). TSMC press office is the only realistic route; no personal social accounts. His two-volume autobiography (2024) is a good outreach hook.

name: Kelcy Warren
current_role: Executive Chairman, Energy Transfer LP (Dallas)
profile: Texas pipeline billionaire who cofounded Energy Transfer with Ray Davis in 1996 and built it into one of the largest US midstream companies (~130,000 miles of oil and gas pipeline, incl. Dakota Access). He stepped down as CEO in 2020 and remains executive chairman; SEC Form 4 filings show him still buying ET units in 2026.
interesting_fact: He started out sweeping warehouses for Sun Oil, where his father was a supply clerk, and spent teenage summers as a welder's assistant on Sun Pipeline; Energy Transfer later came to own Sun's pipeline business. He gave $10M+ to build Klyde Warren Park, the 5-acre deck park over a Dallas freeway, named for his son.
deep_cut_fact: A serious music fan, Warren co-founded the independent Texas roots/Americana label Music Road Records in 2007 with singer-songwriter Jimmy LaFave and Fred Remmert, and collects music memorabilia (e.g. Eagles-signed drumsticks). He holds a 1978 civil-engineering degree from UT Arlington.
notes: Politically outspoken (major Trump donor) and Dakota Access is a sensitive topic; energy/infrastructure angle is the natural hook. No personal social accounts found; route via Energy Transfer media relations.

name: Liu Chunlan
current_role: Executive director, Victory Giant Technology (Huizhou) Co. (SZSE: 300476; HKEX: 2476)
profile: Liu Chunlan is a director of Victory Giant Technology, the Huizhou-based PCB maker founded by her husband Chen Tao that has become a core Nvidia supplier of boards for AI servers and accelerator cards. The couple's fortune comes from their ~27% stake; shares rose 530%+ in 2025 and the company added a Hong Kong listing in April 2026.
interesting_fact: Victory Giant was 2025's top performer on the MSCI Asia Pacific Index (+530%), giving Liu and Chen Tao a combined ~US$9.1bn fortune per Bloomberg; the bet that paid off was a 2019 decision to build an HDI division for high-end graphics boards.
notes: Low public profile; Chen Tao is the public face and Bloomberg reported the company did not respond to comment requests. Best route is the securities/board office (zqb@shpcb.com, board secretary Zhu Xiyao per 2025 interim report).

name: Juan Esteller Roig
current_role: Executive Chairman and majority shareholder, Mercadona (Spain's largest supermarket chain)
profile: The Wikidata item (Q5952391) is Juan Roig Alfonso (Valencia, b. 1949). In 1981 he bought Mercadona from his parents, who had started it in 1977 out of the family's Cárnicas Roig butcher shops, and built it into Spain's dominant grocery chain. He and his wife Hortensia Herrero (vice-chair) own about 80%. He also owns Valencia Basket, the Roig Arena and the Aspar Circuit.
interesting_fact: Roig funds entrepreneurship in Valencia through Marina de Empresas: the EDEM business school, the Lanzadera startup accelerator and Angels Capital. Lanzadera alone has put more than €20M into 190+ startups.
deep_cut_fact: One of his best-known aphorisms: 'You don't have to do a job you like; you have to make your job something you like doing.' In 2022 he and a group of businessmen bought the Circuit de la Ribera in Guadassuar and turned it into the Aspar Circuit, now the base of the Aspar MotoGP-family team.
notes: The name in the input looks garbled: Wikidata Q5952391 is labelled 'Juan Esteller Roig' but links to Juan Roig Alfonso's Wikipedia pages. Check for a duplicate 'Juan Roig' record in other lanes. For an entrepreneurship podcast, the Lanzadera/EDEM route is the most natural approach; he speaks publicly mainly at Mercadona's annual results press conference.

name: Leo KoGuan
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, SHI International Corp. (Somerset, NJ IT solutions provider; ~$16B sales)
profile: Indonesian-born (1955) Chinese-American lawyer-turned-entrepreneur, educated at Columbia SIPA and New York Law School. In 1989 he bought a small software reseller that became SHI International, now run by co-founder and ex-wife Thai Lee as CEO. He became famous as a huge retail Tesla investor, later trimming his stake and moving into Treasuries.
interesting_fact: At one point he claimed to be Tesla's third-largest individual shareholder after selling Baidu and Nvidia shares at the start of the pandemic to buy long-dated Tesla call options.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond the KoGuan School of Law at Shanghai Jiao Tong ($30M, 2008), he gave $28M to Peking University, which named a law-school building after him (the Leo KoGuan Building); his Chinese name is Liao Kaiyuan (廖凯原).
notes: Active and outspoken on X (posts about Tesla/Musk/markets), but handle not verified from an official page here. SHI recently acted as lead integrator for a New Jersey AI supercomputer initiative (data-center angle). SHI press has used agency Gregory FCA; no current verified press email found.

name: James Clark
current_role: Private technology investor; co-founder of Silicon Graphics, Netscape and Healtheon/WebMD; 10%+ shareholder of Ibotta (NYSE: IBTA)
profile: Jim Clark, a former Stanford professor, co-founded Silicon Graphics (1982) and then Netscape (1994), whose 1995 IPO helped ignite the dot-com boom, followed by Healtheon/WebMD and myCFO. He has since multiplied his wealth through early stakes in Apple, Facebook, Twitter and Palantir and remains a large holder in Ibotta; he is also a keen sailor and backer of ocean causes.
interesting_fact: Clark was the key financial backer of 'The Cove', the Oscar-winning documentary about dolphin hunting in Japan, and keeps a ~30,000-bottle Burgundy collection he calls his 'liquid asset'.
deep_cut_fact: A high-school dropout who learned electronics in the Navy and earned credits at Tulane night school, he did his 1974 Utah PhD under computer-graphics pioneer Ivan Sutherland on '3-D design of free-form B-spline surfaces', then built the 'Geometry Engine' graphics accelerator with Stanford students in 1979, the basis of SGI.
notes: No published personal, office or press contact found; he has no active public social accounts. Possible routes: via Ibotta IR (as a major holder) or Stanford/computer-graphics community, but none is an official channel for him. Born 1944 (age 82).

name: Justin Sun
current_role: Founder, TRON blockchain (TRX); controls/advises exchanges HTX and Poloniex; owner of BitTorrent
profile: Justin Sun (b. 1990; Peking University BA, Penn MA) adopted Bitcoin early in 2012, worked for Ripple, then founded TRON in 2017; it is now a major stablecoin network. He also owns HTX, Poloniex and BitTorrent. He was Grenada's WTO ambassador (2021-23). The SEC's 2023 case over TRX/BTT settled in March 2026 for $10M, paid by an affiliate.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he won Blue Origin's $28M auction for the first paid seat on New Shepard but missed the flight due to a scheduling conflict; he finally flew to space in August 2025 aboard Blue Origin NS-34.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 he joined the inaugural class of Jack Ma's Hupan University entrepreneurship school as its only member born in the 1990s, finishing the three-year programme in 2018 with a thesis on blockchain. Before TRON he launched Peiwo (2014), a social app that matched users via 10-second voice clips.
notes: Highly public and media-friendly; very active on X (@justinsuntron), which is the most direct route. Reputationally sensitive: ongoing regulatory and litigation coverage (SEC settlement, WLFI dispute, UK FCA action vs HTX) — journalist should do own diligence.

name: Alexei Kuzmichev
current_role: Co-founder/shareholder, Alfa Group Consortium (listed as supervisory board member); stepped down from LetterOne board in 2022
profile: Russian businessman (b. 1962, Kirov) who co-founded Alfa Group with Mikhail Fridman and German Khan, later LetterOne. Wealth from oil (TNK-BP stake sold to Rosneft in 2013), Alfa-Bank, VimpelCom and X5 Retail. Sanctioned by the EU/UK (2022) and US (2023); sold his Alfa-Bank stake in 2023 and has been under French investigation since Oct 2023.
interesting_fact: He is friends with photographer Trevor Paglen and owns one of Paglen's most famous works, the night photograph of the NSA headquarters.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alfa, he served 1980-82 as an army radio operator on the Soviet-Chinese border; in 1988 he, Fridman and Khan started Alfa Photo, a business importing photo chemicals, the seed of Alfa Group.
notes: Sanctioned by UK, EU, US (OFAC SDN, Aug 2023), Canada and Australia; French money-laundering/sanctions-evasion charges pending. Any engagement may raise legal/compliance issues. No published personal or office contact found; former Alfa Group/LetterOne bio pages are offline.

name: Guan Yamei
current_role: Chairman (president) of Tongwei Group, Chengdu; long-time executive alongside board chairman Liu Hanyuan
profile: Guan Yamei (管亚梅) is a senior leader of Tongwei Group, the Chengdu conglomerate that grew from aquafeed into one of the world's largest polysilicon and solar cell makers (Tongwei Co., 600438.SH). Hurun lists her wealth jointly with Tongwei founder Liu Hanyuan; she has served as Tongwei Co. president and later as Tongwei Group chairman.
interesting_fact: Tongwei, which she helps lead, started in fish feed and is now one of the world's largest producers of high-purity polysilicon and solar cells, while still running a major aquaculture/feed business.

name: Ye Senran
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jiangxi Redboard Technology (红板科技, SSE: 603459), Ji'an, Jiangxi
profile: Ye Senran (叶森然), a PCB-industry veteran of 40+ years, founded Redboard in 2005. He skipped the crowded low-end board market to build HDI (high-density interconnect) lines, and Redboard now holds ~13% of the global phone-HDI market, supplying Honor, OPPO and vivo. It listed on the Shanghai main board on 8 April 2026, raising 1.77bn yuan, and is moving into AI optical-module PCBs (MSAP), IC substrates and servers, with a plant in Vietnam.
interesting_fact: Redboard is riding the AI data-centre build-out: its MSAP process is one of the few able to mass-produce PCBs for 1.6T/3.2T high-speed optical modules. Ye says mid-2025 was the 'watershed' when optical modules abandoned the old subtractive process.
deep_cut_fact: Redboard has developed a 26-layer any-layer interconnect board, at the limit of civilian PCB processes. Ye plays it down as a small-batch job for a Korean customer, arguing that real core technology means holding >90% yield at scale, not making record samples.
notes: Very low public profile and no personal channels found. Redboard's IR contact (board secretary) should be in its SSE filings and annual report at sse.com.cn (code 603459); I could not confirm a published email. Strong fit for the AI-hardware supply-chain angle.

name: Pavel Tykac
current_role: Owner, Sev.en Global Investments / Sev.en Group (coal, power, steel, oil & gas; Prague)

The site shows emails through JS anti-spam markup (decoded with the site's own script).

name: Piero Ferrari
current_role: Vice Chairman, Ferrari N.V. (since 1988); Chairman, HPE COXA; non-executive director, Ferretti Group
profile: Piero Ferrari, Enzo Ferrari's only surviving son, owns about 10% of Ferrari and has been vice chairman since 1988. He became a billionaire at Ferrari's 2015 NYSE listing. He worked in Ferrari's motorsport division from 1970 to 1988, founded Modena engineering firm HPE (now HPE COXA) in 1998 and chaired Piaggio Aerospace from 1999 to 2014.
interesting_fact: He supports Centro Dino Ferrari, a research center for muscular and neurodegenerative diseases that his father co-founded in memory of Piero's half-brother Dino.

notes: Age 80. Cavaliere del Lavoro (2004). Engineering angle: HPE COXA does advanced design/simulation and high-precision prototype manufacturing. Ferrari media/IR emails come from Ferrari N.V. press releases (seen via search). Possible route: HPE COXA in Modena.

name: Hasmukh Chudgar
current_role: Founder and patriarch, Intas Pharmaceuticals (Ahmedabad); trustee, Intas Welfare Trust. Operations run by his sons
profile: Hasmukh Chudgar, a pharmacist, founded Intas Pharmaceuticals in Ahmedabad in 1977; it was incorporated in 1985. Bootstrapped for decades without diluting equity, it became India's largest unlisted drugmaker, with about $3.5B revenue and Europe and India as its biggest markets. His sons Nimish, Binish and Urmish now run it. Recent moves include buying biosimilar Udenyca from Coherus for $558M in 2025.
interesting_fact: Intas makes Eleftha, an affordable biosimilar of Roche's breast-cancer drug Herceptin. Abu Dhabi Investment Authority bought a 3% stake in the still-private company from Temasek in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before he became an industrialist, Chudgar was a pharmacy professor. He started Intas by making medicines in a small facility in Gujarat and deliberately refused outside equity in the early years.
notes: Very low profile and elderly; no interviews found. Binish Chudgar (dealmaker, Accord/Actavis UK deal) and Urmish (biopharma) are the active public faces. The only published corporate inbox is Intas's general queries email.

name: Pauline MacMillan Keinath
current_role: Cargill heiress and believed largest individual shareholder; no executive role
profile: Pauline MacMillan Keinath (b. 1934) is a great-granddaughter of W.W. Cargill and believed to be Cargill's largest individual shareholder, with a roughly 9-13% stake inherited after her father's death in 1968. Her late brother Whitney MacMillan was the last family CEO (to 1995). She lives in St. Louis and keeps an extremely low profile.

public_contacts.value: media@cargill.com (Cargill corporate media; not her personal office)

notes: Age 92 and extremely private; no public foundation, interviews or personal channels found. Cargill media office will not speak for individual family shareholders. Probably not a realistic podcast guest.

name: Guo Jinshu
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Inner Mongolia Huineng Coal & Electricity Group (Ordos)
profile: Guo Jinshu (郭金树), a former head of the Ordos municipal coal bureau, founded Huineng in the early 1990s from restructured small coal mines. It grew into a private coal, coal-to-gas/LNG, coal chemicals and power group with >RMB100bn in assets; he is now pushing into solar, new materials and acquisitions (e.g. Asia-Potash stake, ST Xinchao bid).
interesting_fact: Huineng began as a company of 600+ laid-off coal workers who pooled their own money; Guo says those who didn't take buyouts all became shareholders. Its Ordos coal-to-natural-gas plant became a national demonstration project.
deep_cut_fact: Guo explains the name: 汇 'gather' + 能 meaning energy, power, talent and ability, and preaches four qualities for running a business: 定力, 控制力, 穿透力, 平衡力 (composure, control, penetration, balance). In his 70s (2023) he still targeted RMB250bn in assets by 2030.
notes: Input's SEC link (Luckin Coffee CEO) is a mismatch: Luckin's CEO is Guo Jinyi, a different person. Very low-profile private Chinese coal tycoon; no published personal contacts found. Company site reportedly huinenggroup.com (unreachable, unverified). 2025 Asia-Potash filings name him as Huineng's sole actual controller.

name: Ray Lee Hunt
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Hunt Consolidated, Inc. (Dallas; oil & gas, LNG, real estate, investments)
profile: Son of wildcatter H.L. Hunt, Ray Hunt (b. 1943, SMU grad) took over Hunt Oil after his father's 1974 death and built Hunt Consolidated into a conglomerate spanning oil and gas, Peru LNG, power/infrastructure and real estate (Hunt Realty, Reunion in Dallas). Now chairman emeritus; son Hunter Hunt runs the energy and infrastructure businesses.
interesting_fact: Hunt Oil was one of the first companies to land an exploration deal in Iraq's Kurdistan region after the fall of Saddam Hussein (2007), and it holds stakes in Peru's natural gas fields and its gas liquefaction plant.
deep_cut_fact: Hunt and John Scovell were 20-somethings who 'didn't know rebar from structural steel' when they started the Reunion project in 1972; Hunt made Scovell president of Woodbine Development as its only employee, and at 32 refused even to read the $35M construction contract, trusting him. Reunion Tower opened April 15, 1978.
notes: Very private family company. Best route is Hunt Consolidated public affairs (media line (214) 978-8534 published on same page). Also trustee/director emeritus at SMU and George W. Bush Presidential Center; son Hunter Hunt is the operational lead for energy/infrastructure.

name: Sri Prakash Lohia
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Indorama Corporation
profile: Kolkata-born (1952) Indonesian billionaire who moved to Indonesia in 1973 with his father to start Indorama Synthetics (spun yarns, 1976). He built Indorama Corporation into a diversified petrochemicals, fertilizer, polyester and gloves group; his 2006 purchase of a Nigerian olefins plant became West Africa's largest petrochemical complex. Son Amit is vice chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he acquired a struggling integrated olefin plant in Nigeria and turned it into the largest petrochemical company in West Africa; Indorama marked its 50th anniversary (Golden Jubilee) in Dubai in late 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started buying a few old hand-coloured 'colour plate' books around 2008 as a hobby; it grew into one of the world's premier private collections of the genre (21,500+ images), which he had digitised and made freely viewable online so anyone, regardless of language, can enjoy the plates.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Brother-in-law of Lakshmi Mittal. Son Amit Lohia (vice chairman) is the more public face. Not to be confused with brother Aloke Lohia of Indorama Ventures (Thailand).

name: Li Yanhong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Baidu Inc.
profile: Li Yanhong (Robin Li) co-founded Baidu in 2000 with Eric Xu after search-engine stints at IDD/Dow Jones and Infoseek in the US. Baidu became China's dominant search engine; Li has since steered it into AI (ERNIE large models, AI cloud) and Apollo/Apollo Go autonomous driving.
interesting_fact: Before Baidu, Li built RankDex (1996), an early search engine that ranked pages by the links pointing to them, a link-analysis idea that predated Google's PageRank.
deep_cut_fact: Li is the named inventor on US patent 5,920,859, 'Hypertext Document Retrieval System and Method' (filed Feb 1997, issued July 1999), written while he was at IDD Information Services, a Dow Jones unit where he also worked on software for the online Wall Street Journal.
notes: Known in English as Robin Li. The listed SEC insider roles (Datadog CPO, Equinix director) belong to a different person, Yanbing Li; this is a name-match error, not Robin Li. Best route is via Baidu corporate/IR.

name: Cao Renxian
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. (300274.SZ)
profile: Cao Renxian (曹仁贤) grew up in a poor rural family, studied industrial automation at Hefei University of Technology and taught there before founding Sungrow in 1997. Sungrow became one of the world's largest makers of solar PV inverters and energy storage systems, selling into the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Europe and the U.S. He remains chairman of the Shenzhen-listed company.
interesting_fact: Sungrow, founded by a university lecturer in renewable-energy power electronics, grew into what it calls the world's leading inverter and energy storage system supplier, with over 269 GW of inverters installed worldwide by mid-2022.
deep_cut_fact: Cao launched Sungrow on 28 November 1997 in a humble rented house in Anhui at age 30, quitting his secure university teaching job while newly married, and funded it with about 80,000 yuan of his own savings plus money from friends and relatives.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Best route is Sungrow corporate communications or IR (the IR email is the company's published investor contact). Deep-cut source for the rented-house date is Sungrow's 25th-anniversary release (aap.com.au link); the savings figure comes from Wikipedia.

name: Sudhir Mehta
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Torrent Group (Torrent Pharmaceuticals, Torrent Power), Ahmedabad
profile: Elder son of Torrent founder U.N. Mehta, Sudhir Mehta became group chairman in 1998 and built Torrent from a pharma firm (Trinity Laboratories) into a pharma-power-gas conglomerate. He handed the chair to brother Samir in the 2010s and stepped off the Torrent Pharma board in March 2024, remaining Chairman Emeritus.
interesting_fact: He pushed Torrent Pharma into exports, entering Russia during its 1990s political turmoil; Torrent later built a strong presence in Europe, Russia and Brazil. Business Standard describes him as extremely media-shy, avoiding interviews and press briefings.
deep_cut_fact: When India opened power to private players in 1991, he began quietly buying shares of Ahmedabad Electricity Co. and Surat Electricity Co., taking majority stakes by the late 1990s - the origin of Torrent Power, which went on to build the 1,147.5 MW Sugen gas-fired plant.
notes: Very media-shy; largely retired from active business. Brother Samir Mehta is group chairman; approach via Torrent corporate/company secretary channels. Group energy arm (Torrent Power, Torrent Gas) is the podcast-relevant angle.

name: Samir Mehta
current_role: Chairman, Torrent Group; Executive Chairman, Torrent Pharmaceuticals (reappointed for 5 years from Apr 2025)
profile: Ahmedabad-based chairman of the Torrent Group (pharmaceuticals, power, and more), founded by his father U.N. Mehta. He succeeded his elder brother Sudhir as group chairman in 2014 and has grown Torrent Pharma into a global generics player in ~40 countries, while Torrent Power is a major Indian power utility/generator.
interesting_fact: In March 2025 the Torrent Group completed the purchase of a 67% majority stake in IPL cricket franchise Gujarat Titans from CVC-controlled Irelia, reportedly for about Rs 5,035 crore.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Torrent, he serves as President of the Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance (IPA), the lobby group of India's largest research-based drugmakers, where his bio highlights his push for an employee-centric workplace promoting equality and fairness.
notes: Energy angle is Torrent Power (Ahmedabad/Surat utility, renewables, pumped storage). Low public profile; route via Torrent corporate communications/IR.

name: Michael Kadoorie
current_role: Non-executive Chairman, CLP Holdings; Non-executive Chairman, The Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels (Peninsula Hotels)
profile: Sir Michael Kadoorie (b. 1941) heads the Kadoorie family interests in Hong Kong: CLP Holdings, the power utility the family co-founded that serves ~80% of Hong Kong, and Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels, owner of The Peninsula hotels. Still chairing CLP in 2026, he opened its May 2026 AGM and is overseeing power investment for the Northern Metropolis.
interesting_fact: He is the scion of a Baghdadi-Jewish family whose grandfather Elly Kadoorie settled in Shanghai in 1880; he is also a keen photographer and classic-car collector (Bugatti Type 57, Hispano-Suiza J12, Lamborghini Miura).
deep_cut_fact: He is a helicopter pilot: Heliservices (HK) was founded in 1978 after he bought Hong Kong's first private helicopter. He still chairs it, and it flies from the Peninsula's rooftop helipad and washes power-line insulators for HK utilities.
notes: Very private, aged 85; no personal social media. CLP press office (named contact changes per release) or the HSH/Peninsula corporate office are the realistic routes. Aviation (Heliservices, Metrojet) is a good conversational hook.

name: Rinat Akhmetov
current_role: Founder and owner, System Capital Management (SCM) group (Metinvest, DTEK); president of FC Shakhtar Donetsk
profile: Ukraine's richest person and the son of a Donetsk coal miner. He built SCM by buying mining and steel assets during 1990s privatisation; it now holds steelmaker Metinvest and energy company DTEK, Ukraine's largest private power producer. His plants and substations have been heavily damaged in the war, but he has stayed in Ukraine and funds reconstruction and aid.
interesting_fact: Through SCM's 'Steel Front' initiative, his companies make fortifications and other defensive equipment for Ukraine's military, including protection for US-supplied Abrams tanks.
deep_cut_fact: His 'Heart of Azovstal' project began with a call to Azovstal commander Denys Prokopenko 15 minutes before the defenders left the plant. Prokopenko asked him to 'take care of my men', and Akhmetov launched the project in January 2023 with $25M for Mariupol defenders and families of fallen soldiers.
notes: Very private; speaks mainly through SCM press statements. SCM's communications director is Natalia Yemchenko (Kyiv Post). DTEK (energy arm) is the most relevant angle for an energy podcast. scm.com.ua and dtek.com sit behind bot protection, so their contact pages could not be verified. Avoid oligarch/politics framing.

name: Li Ping
current_role: Vice Chairman, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. (CATL)
profile: Li Ping (b. 1968) is vice chairman and co-controlling shareholder (with chairman Robin Zeng) of CATL, the world's largest EV battery maker, founded in 2011 and dual-listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong; he holds ~4.3% of the company. He previously worked at electrical engineering firms and holds a Fudan degree and a CEIBS MBA. CATL licenses tech to Ford's Michigan battery plant, completed June 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2025 Li and his wife Liao Mei donated 4.05 million CATL shares (about 1 billion yuan) to their alma mater Fudan University; the transfer was registered on July 10, 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Li studied polymers at Fudan (class of 1985), while his wife Liao Mei was a Fudan history major (class of 1986); their 1-billion-yuan gift funds Fudan's new Xue Min Institute of Advanced Studies.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews (some speeches at CATL events). The only route is CATL corporate (IR/media). Sources disagree on when he became vice chairman (2015 or 2017).

name: Oleg Deripaska
current_role: Founder, Basic Element; major shareholder of En+ Group (which controls Rusal)
profile: Russian industrialist who built Siberian Aluminium in the 1990s and merged it with Abramovich's assets in 2000 to form Rusal. Founder of Basic Element (metals, energy, construction, agriculture). Sanctioned by the US (2018), UK and EU; his En+/Rusal stake was cut to resolve US sanctions on the companies in 2019. In 2026 he is a vocal commentator on Russia's economy.
interesting_fact: Through his Volnoe Delo foundation he has funded the Phanagoria excavation since 2004, which made him Russia's single biggest donor to archaeology and Phanagoria the country's best-financed dig.
deep_cut_fact: He enrolled in physics at Moscow State University in 1985 and graduated with honours in 1993. Before that he served in the Soviet Strategic Missile Forces in Trans-Baikal from 1986 to 1989. Shrinking academic funding ended his plan to become a theoretical physicist, and he moved into metals trading.
notes: Sanctioned by the US, UK, EU, Canada and Australia, so check compliance and legal issues before any outreach. He posts on an official Telegram channel that the press quotes often, but I could not verify the exact handle. His official site deripaska.com and the Basic Element site basel.ru were unreachable from this environment.

name: Mikhail Gutseriev
current_role: Founder and main shareholder / chairman, Safmar Group (oil, coal, real estate, retail; Russia)
profile: Russian-Ingush billionaire (b. 1958, Akmolinsk) who ran Slavneft, then founded oil producer RussNeft in 2002; fled to London in 2007 amid tax charges and returned in 2010. Built Safmar Group (RussNeft, Russian Coal, Neftisa, A101 developer). Sanctioned by UK and EU in 2021 over ties to Lukashenko; in 2022 transferred assets to a relative.
interesting_fact: He owns Moscow's Hotel National, where Donald Trump stayed on his first Russia trip in 1987, owns radio stations incl. Radio Shanson, and writes song lyrics performed by well-known Russian singers.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil, he trained in 'Leather and Fur Technology' (Dzhambul Technological Institute, 1981) and worked as a process engineer in Grozny; in 2005 he funded the rebuilding of his old Grozny high school No. 23, destroyed in the First Chechen War.
notes: Contact is the SAFMAR Charitable Foundation (his foundation) site, which looks dated (c.2014). Subject to UK sanctions (EU sanctions litigated; EU General Court annulled some listings 2025-26). Reputational/legal sensitivity for any engagement.

name: Mike Brown
current_role: Owner and President, Cincinnati Bengals (NFL)
profile: Mike Brown (b. 1935) is the son of coaching legend Paul Brown. He helped his father found the Cincinnati Bengals in 1967–68, served as assistant GM, and took over as owner after Paul's death in 1991. The Brown family still runs the team, with daughter Katie Blackburn as executive VP. Forbes valued the Bengals at more than $5B in 2025.
interesting_fact: The Bengals reached Super Bowl LVI under Brown's ownership in the 2021 season. That run brought the franchise's first playoff win since 1990 and its first-ever road playoff win.
deep_cut_fact: Brown played quarterback at Dartmouth (class of 1957) and graduated from Harvard Law School in 1960. As a young man he had a summer job as a deck hand at Kinsman Marine Transit, hired by George Steinbrenner long before either of them owned a pro sports team.
notes: He is 91 and rarely gives interviews beyond team press events. Bengals media relations (bengals.com/news/media) is the professional route. He is a poor fit for an energy/data-center angle.

name: Daniel Nadler
current_role: Cofounder & CEO, OpenEvidence
profile: Canadian-born AI entrepreneur with a Harvard Ph.D. in economics. Cofounded Kensho (AI for financial analytics), sold to S&P Global for $550M in 2018. In 2022 cofounded OpenEvidence, an AI medical-search tool free for verified doctors and ad-supported; valued at ~$12B in early 2026, with Nadler owning nearly 60%.
interesting_fact: OpenEvidence has signed up more than 758,000 doctors and was adding ~55,000 per month; it is free for verified clinicians and earns money from advertising.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published poet: his debut collection 'Lacunae: 100 Imagined Ancient Love Poems' (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2016) presents short poems as imagined translations of lost ancient texts. He studied poetry at Harvard under Pulitzer winner Jorie Graham.
notes: contact@openevidence.com is the general company contact in the site footer, not a dedicated press line. Poetry is a good angle for outreach; Forbes notes his Ph.D. thesis was on credit-derivative pricing.

name: Bruce Cheng
current_role: Founder and Honorary Chairman, Delta Electronics (Taiwan); Chairman, Delta Electronics Foundation
profile: Electrical engineer (BSEE, National Cheng Kung University) who founded Delta Electronics in 1971 as a TV-parts maker and built it into the world's leading switching power-supply maker, now a major supplier of power and thermal management for AI data centres, EVs and automation. He stepped down as chairman in 2012; son Ping Cheng is chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Taiwanese media dubbed him Taiwan's first 'CEO — Chief Environmental Officer'; since 2006 Delta has built all its new offices and factories worldwide as green buildings, and in March 2026 he joined Amory Lovins on a Delta 55th-anniversary panel on energy and AI.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 the International Astronomical Union named asteroid 168126 'Chengbruce' in his honour for his environmental work. Before founding Delta he worked at TRW and at Air Asia Co.
notes: Born 1936; still active in Delta events in 2026. Excellent fit for energy/data-center podcast (Delta is a key AI-server power supplier). Chinese name 鄭崇華. Delta Electronics Foundation is the most natural route for an energy/sustainability conversation.

name: Jacques Servier
profile: Jacques Servier (1922-2014), French physician and founder of pharmaceutical group Laboratoires Servier, died on 16 April 2014 in Neuilly-sur-Seine, aged 92. Servier is now controlled by a foundation structure.
notes: Deceased (16 April 2014) per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Servier ; skipped remaining research. Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Khalaf Al Habtoor
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Al Habtoor Group (Dubai)
profile: Khalaf Ahmad Al Habtoor (b. 1949, Dubai) went to work at 14 and founded Al Habtoor Engineering in 1970. It became Al Habtoor Group: hotels (with Hilton and Marriott), car distribution (Mitsubishi, Bugatti), real estate, education and publishing. A prolific political columnist, in 2025 he agreed to invest in Syria, including a bus network.
interesting_fact: His 572-page autobiography (Motivate Publishing, 2012) won 'Best International Book on Business and Economics' at the 2013 Sharjah International Book Fair; in 2017 he opened an interactive 'Life Journey' exhibition about his own life.
deep_cut_fact: From 1994 to 1997 he was the only non-American member of the USO (United Services Organization) World Board of Governors; he has also served on the UAE Federal National Council and chaired the Commercial Bank of Dubai.
notes: Highly media-friendly; writes columns and gives interviews. His personal website contact form and X account are the best direct routes. Outspoken on Middle East politics — keep outreach to business/entrepreneurship.

name: JK Irving
profile: James K. (J.K.) Irving, longtime chairman of J.D. Irving Ltd. and eldest son of K.C. Irving, died June 21, 2024 in Saint John, New Brunswick, aged 96.
interesting_fact: He was the last surviving son of Irving Group founder K.C. Irving; his brother Arthur (Irving Oil) died about a month before him.
notes: Deceased (June 21, 2024). Source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-06-21/james-k-irving-canadian-forestry-billionaire-dies-at-96 . His son Robert K. Irving, co-CEO of JDI, reportedly died May 2026; Jim (J.D.) Irving remains co-CEO.

name: Stephen M. Ross
current_role: Founder & non-executive chairman, Related Companies; owner, Miami Dolphins and Hard Rock Stadium; chairman, Related Ross
profile: Detroit-raised Stephen Ross founded Related Companies in 1972 and built it into a $60B+ real-estate empire whose signature project is Manhattan's Hudson Yards. Now non-executive chairman, he focuses on Related Ross, the Miami Dolphins and the Miami F1 Grand Prix. Related's data-center arm Related Digital (launched 2025) is building a $16B, 1GW+ Oracle/OpenAI AI campus in Saline Township, Michigan.
interesting_fact: He is among the University of Michigan's largest donors — its business school and athletic campus bear his name — and founded RISE (Ross Initiative in Sports for Equality) to use sports to fight racism.
deep_cut_fact: A former Coopers & Lybrand tax attorney, he started Related in 1972 living off a $10,000 loan from his mother, using his tax-law know-how to syndicate deals for subsidized affordable housing — and earned $150,000 in his first year. His law degrees were financed by a loan from his uncle Max Fisher.
notes: Age ~86. Related's published press inbox is the best route. Strong data-center angle via Related Digital (see https://www.related.com/press-releases/2026-04-24/related-digital-announces-financing-16-billion-oracle-data-center-project). Avoid: 2020 fundraiser backlash and 2022 NFL tampering suspension.

name: Mao Wenchao
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Xiaohongshu (RedNote), Shanghai
profile: Wuhan-born (1985) Mao Wenchao (Charlwin Mao) studied mechatronics at Shanghai Jiao Tong, worked at Bain & Company and in private equity, then took a Stanford GSB MBA (2013). He returned that June to co-found Xiaohongshu with Miranda Qu. RedNote has ~300M+ users and drew 'TikTok refugees' in Jan 2025, and Reuters reported in June 2026 that it hired Goldman and CICC for a Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: The 'Little Red Book' name has no Mao Zedong reference, he says: it came from the red colours of Bain and Stanford. The product began in 2013 as downloadable PDF shopping guides for Chinese tourists, and the first app was called 'Hong Kong Shopping Guide'.
deep_cut_fact: Xiaohongshu uses in-house nicknames: Mao goes by 'Seiya' and co-founder Miranda Qu by 'Mulan'. Staff can bring dogs and cats to the office on Fridays. Before founding it he had travelled to 20+ countries, which inspired the overseas-shopping idea.
notes: Keeps a low public profile; co-founder Miranda Qu is more often the public face. No published press or IR email found. If the Hong Kong IPO proceeds, the prospectus will list IR contacts. Approach via Xiaohongshu's official account or corporate PR.

name: Joseph Liemandt
current_role: Principal of Alpha School / founder of 2 Hour Learning; founder of ESW Capital and Trilogy Software
profile: Joe Liemandt dropped out of Stanford to found Trilogy Software and was the youngest self-made member of the 1996 Forbes 400. His ESW Capital has bought 100+ software companies. He now leads Alpha School and its AI-driven '2 Hour Learning' model, reportedly funding its AI software with about $1B of his own money.
interesting_fact: After his Forbes-cover fame, he 'vanished from public life for 25 years' before re-emerging as Alpha School's principal. He aims to bring AI tutoring to a billion learners.
deep_cut_fact: On The Knowledge Project (2026) he discussed sleeping on the floor in Trilogy's early days and being mentored by GE's Jack Welch.

public_contacts.value: Alpha School media contact: Daphne Ortiz, 312.488.3472 (listed on Alpha School press releases)

notes: Long reclusive but since 2025 a regular podcast guest (Knowledge Project, Joe Lonsdale, Peter Attia, Masters of Scale), so podcast outreach about AI/education is plausible. MacKenzie Price is Alpha's main public face. Avoid the critical coverage of Alpha's results and ESW's labor model.

name: Ali Ghodsi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Databricks (San Francisco); adjunct professor, UC Berkeley
profile: Iranian-born Swedish-American computer scientist (b. 1978) whose family fled to Sweden after the 1979 revolution. A KTH PhD, he joined UC Berkeley's AMPLab in 2009 and helped start Apache Mesos and Apache Spark. In 2013 he co-founded Databricks with six Berkeley colleagues, became CEO in 2016, and led its turnaround into the 'data lakehouse'/AI platform, valued at $134B in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: Ghodsi joined Databricks in 2013 as a part-time engineer and was a first-time CEO when tapped in 2016 amid revenue struggles. He then rebuilt the leadership and products, taking the company to a $134B private valuation.
deep_cut_fact: He co-invented 'Dominant Resource Fairness' (NSDI 2011, with Zaharia, Shenker, Stoica and others), a scheme for fairly sharing CPU and memory across cluster users that shaped scheduling in Hadoop YARN and Mesos. Earlier he co-founded Stockholm P2P startup Peerialism.
notes: Very accessible and a frequent podcast guest; a strong fit for the data-center/AI angle. Best route is Databricks press (press@databricks.com). He is active on X and LinkedIn, but no handle was verified from an official page in this pass. He learned to program on a broken Commodore 64 as a child (btw.media, secondary source).

name: Marian Ilitch
current_role: Chairman, Ilitch Holdings; owner of Little Caesars, Detroit Red Wings and MotorCity Casino Hotel
profile: Marian Ilitch (b. 1933, Dearborn) co-founded Little Caesars Pizza with her husband Mike in 1959 in Garden City, Michigan; after his 2017 death she became sole owner of the chain (5bn+ in systemwide sales), the Detroit Red Wings and MotorCity Casino, while son Chris runs Ilitch Holdings as CEO. In 2026 the family formed Ilitch Gaming to expand into casinos beyond Detroit.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding Little Caesars she worked as a Delta Air Lines ticket agent; she met Mike Ilitch on a blind date, and in the early days had to stop him from giving away free pizzas.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Dearborn to Macedonian immigrants, she was honored when Michigan's governor proclaimed 'Marian Ilitch Day' on May 8, the anniversary of the 1959 opening of the first 'Little Caesars Pizza Treat', and the NHL called her 'the most impactful woman owner in the league'.
notes: In her 90s and rarely gives interviews; Chris Ilitch is the family's public face. No published media email found; route via Ilitch Companies communications (Ilitch News Hub). Ilitch family charities have given $250m+, incl. $40m to Wayne State (Mike Ilitch School of Business).

name: Maximilian Viessmann
current_role: CEO & President, Viessmann Generations Group GmbH & Co. KG; board member, Carrier Global
profile: Fourth-generation heir (b. 1989) of the Viessmann heating dynasty. Ex-BCG consultant who joined in 2015 and became CEO; sold Viessmann Climate Solutions to Carrier for ~EUR 12bn (agreed 2023, closed Jan 2024) and joined Carrier's board. Now runs family investor Viessmann Generations Group (2026: AI push, FC Bayern stake).
interesting_fact: The Viessmann brand stayed with the family: Viessmann Generations Group owns it and licenses it to Carrier after the EUR 12bn sale of Viessmann Climate Solutions.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the Advisory Council of the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), and before joining the family firm he was an angel investor in Europe and Asia as well as a BCG consultant.
notes: Press contact named on 2026 VGG releases is Nicola Boya (byan@viessmann.com). Group communications inbox listed in imprint. Very relevant for energy/heat-pump angle.

name: Luo Jinhong
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder of EVE Energy (Huizhou); holds 50% of controlling shareholder Tibet EVE Holding (not a director/officer)
profile: Luo Jinhong (骆锦红) co-founded EVE Energy in 2001 with her husband, chairman Liu Jincheng, after both worked at Desay Energy in Huizhou. EVE grew from lithium primary cells into a top Chinese EV and energy-storage battery maker. The couple are joint actual controllers; Hurun 2025 put their joint wealth at RMB 52.5B.
interesting_fact: In EVE's 2022 private placement the couple personally subscribed RMB 6B (Luo 4B, Liu 2B) alongside RMB 3B from their holding company, a large founder bet on capacity expansion.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding EVE she worked at three battery makers in Huizhou: Huizhou Bohui Battery, Times Battery and Desay Energy Technology; EVE's first entity (2001) was set up via relatives' nominee shareholding while Liu was still Desay's deputy GM.
notes: Very low public profile; she is not an executive and gives no interviews found. Husband Liu Jincheng is the public face (gives English-language interviews, e.g. electrive 2025). Route via EVE securities department (IR email).

name: Jayshree Ullal
current_role: Chairperson and CEO, Arista Networks; director, Snowflake
profile: London-born, Delhi-raised engineer (SFSU, Santa Clara) who ran Cisco's switching business before becoming CEO of Arista Networks in 2008, when it had no revenue and under 50 employees. Arista now sells $9B+ a year of high-speed Ethernet switches, a core supplier to cloud and AI data-center buildouts; she owns roughly 2% of the stock.
interesting_fact: She joined Arista as CEO when the startup had no revenue and fewer than 50 employees; it now generates more than $9 billion in annual revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Early in her career at AMD she designed high-speed memory chips for IBM and Hitachi; she joined Cisco in 1993 when it bought Crescendo Communications, Cisco's very first acquisition, and built the Catalyst switching business.
notes: Press email is Arista corporate communications (Amanda Jaramillo) as listed on 2026 releases. No verified personal social accounts found. Frequently speaks about AI networking/back-end AI clusters; strong data-center fit.

name: Maria Fernanda Amorim
current_role: Matriarch/co-owner (with daughters Paula, Marta, Luisa) of the Americo Amorim Group; no executive role
profile: Widow of cork magnate Americo Amorim (d. 2017); she and her three daughters inherited his fortune and top Forbes Portugal's rich list (~EUR 5.8B, Jan 2026). The core asset is the family's control of Amorim Energia, which owns ~37.5% of oil & gas group Galp (chaired by eldest daughter Paula), plus Corticeira Amorim stakes, Amorim Luxury and real estate.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes she has founded two museums: one dedicated to Port wine and another, in Grijo, focused on arts and crafts.
notes: Very private, elderly, no public profile or interviews found. The family's public face is daughter Paula Amorim (chair of Galp and Amorim Energia) - for an energy podcast she is the realistic guest; route via the Americo Amorim Group general email or Galp media relations. Couldn't verify the museum names independently.

name: Albert Avdolyan
current_role: Owner, A-Property (holding behind ELSI / Elga coal complex, Pacific Railway, Yakut Fuel & Energy Co.)
profile: Krasnodar-born (1970) investor who co-founded Russian telecom Scartel/Yota with Sergey Adoniev, then sold out of the MegaFon-linked holding in 2013. Through A-Property he bought the giant Elga coking-coal deposit in Yakutia (2020), merged coal assets into ELSI (2022), owns gas producer YATEC and is building the ~530 km private Pacific Railway to a Sea of Okhotsk port.
interesting_fact: The Pacific Railway he is building from Elga to Port Elga on the Sea of Okhotsk is ~531 km long (626 km of track with junctions), a record for a private railway in Russia.
deep_cut_fact: In 2013 he founded the 'New Home' charitable foundation, which builds 'Point of the Future' (Tochka Budushchego) in Irkutsk: a free school for 1,000 pupils plus a village of cottages for foster families with orphaned and disabled children; a second complex began in Yakutia in 2022.
notes: Sanctions sensitivity: US Treasury sanctioned Elga coal entities (June 2024) and Sibanthracite; a news report says he was personally added to the EU sanctions list (unverified here). Russian company sites (elsi-group.ru) were unreachable from this environment so no press email was confirmed. Very low public profile.

name: Robert Bass
current_role: President, Keystone Group LP (Fort Worth family investment holding company); founder of the Oak Hill investment funds
profile: Fort Worth-born Yale (1971) and Stanford MBA (1974) investor, one of the four Bass brothers whose fortune traces to great-uncle Sid Richardson's oil. Built his own wealth through Keystone and the Oak Hill family of funds (Oak Hill Capital, Oak Hill Advisors), plus 1980s deals such as Taft Broadcasting and American Savings. Major donor to Stanford, Duke, Yale and Brookings.
interesting_fact: Bass sold New York's Plaza Hotel to Donald Trump in 1988 for $390 million.
deep_cut_fact: He began his business career at Wells Fargo after Yale, and is a past chairman of both Stanford's board of trustees and the National Trust for Historic Preservation.
notes: Very private; no published personal/office contact found. Keystone Group LP (Fort Worth) is his office; Oak Hill Advisors/Oak Hill Capital press offices are an indirect route. Founder of the defunct supersonic-jet firm Aerion (avoid as an opener).

name: Walther Moreira Salles
current_role: Filmmaker and co-founder of production company VideoFilmes; Itaú Unibanco heir (Moreira Salles family holding)
profile: This is most likely Walter (Walther) Moreira Salles Júnior (b. 1956), son of banker-diplomat Walther Moreira Salles. With his brothers he shares the family's controlling stake in Itaú Unibanco, Brazil's largest private bank, via the family holding. He is best known as an acclaimed director: Central Station, The Motorcycle Diaries, and I'm Still Here, which won Brazil's Oscar for Best International Feature in 2025.
interesting_fact: Thanks to his Itaú stake he is often described as the world's third-richest filmmaker, behind Steven Spielberg and George Lucas. His film I'm Still Here brought Brazil its first Academy Award for Best International Feature.
deep_cut_fact: Salles spent about ten years making non-fiction documentaries before switching to fiction. He was drawn to his 2001 film Behind the Sun after his younger brother handed him Ismail Kadare's novel Broken April, saying 'If I know you well, this will touch you.'
notes: Hurun's 'Walther Moreira Salles' (Itaú, 2014–2026) must be a living heir; the father of that name died in 2001. It is almost certainly the filmmaker son, whose legal name is Walther/Walter Moreira Salles Júnior. Brothers Fernando, Pedro (Itaú chairman) and João are listed separately. He is a filmmaker rather than a business operator, so his fit for an energy/data-center podcast is limited.

name: Hans Michel Piech
current_role: Deputy Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Porsche Automobil Holding SE; supervisory board member of Volkswagen AG, Porsche AG and Audi AG
profile: Vienna-born (1942) lawyer and grandson of Ferdinand Porsche, and one of the leaders of the Piëch branch of the Porsche-Piëch family that controls Volkswagen via Porsche SE. He practised law in Vienna from 1977 to 2021 and has sat on the Porsche SE supervisory board since 1989 and on VW's since 2009.
interesting_fact: In March 2026 he spoke for Porsche SE's board on the extension of CEO Hans Dieter Pötsch's term, saying continuity matters as 'the transformation of the automotive industry presents major challenges.'
deep_cut_fact: After his 1970 law doctorate from the University of Vienna he started his career at Gulf Oil in Pittsburgh, then was a managing director at Porsche KG in Stuttgart in 1971–72. He also sits on the board of Schmittenhöhebahn AG, the cable-car company in Zell am See.
notes: Very private; virtually no interviews. Only routes are Porsche SE communications/IR. Brother of the late Ferdinand Piëch; avoid family-dispute topics.

name: Andre Hoffmann
current_role: Vice-Chairman of Roche Holding (board since 1996, vice-chair since 2006); Chairman of Massellaz SA (family office) and President of Fondation Tour du Valat
profile: A descendant of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche, he represents the founding families' voting pool on Roche's board. After St. Gallen, M&A at James Capel, Nestlé and an INSEAD MBA, he joined the board in 1996; today he is a leading voice for nature-positive capitalism via WEF, the Capitals Coalition, Systemiq and INSEAD's Hoffmann Institute.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he published the book 'The New Nature of Business' (with Peter Vanham), arguing companies must account for natural and social capital, not just short-term profit; he launched it at a literary festival in his hometown of Morges.
deep_cut_fact: His first job (1983-85) was acting administrator of the Tour du Valat biological research station in France's Camargue wetlands, founded by his conservationist father Luc Hoffmann; he also sits on the board of the Restaurant de l'Hôtel de Ville de Crissier, one of Switzerland's most celebrated restaurants.
notes: Unusually accessible for a billionaire: personal site lists office@massellaz.ch as the contact and he does book talks/podcasts. Strong sustainability/energy-transition angle (Systemiq board, Capitals Coalition). Wealth is shared across the Hoffmann/Oeri Roche heirs.

name: Lilian Wernighaus
current_role: Presumed shareholder in WEG S.A. via the Werninghaus founding family (unconfirmed)
profile: Listed by Hurun (2015-2026) with ~US$7B from WEG, the Jaraguá do Sul, Brazil electric-motor and power-equipment maker founded in 1961 by Werner Voigt, Eggon João da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus (WEG = their initials). The three families control WEG through holding company WPA Participações. No public source found that mentions a 'Lilian Werninghaus' (or 'Wernighaus').
interesting_fact: WEG's name is an acronym of its three founders' first names — Werner, Eggon and Geraldo — and the company has produced more Forbes-listed heirs than almost any other Brazilian firm.
notes: Identity unverified: name appears only in Hurun data (possibly misspelt or a family-representative label). Forbes Brasil coverage instead names Geraldo Werninghaus's granddaughters (e.g., Anne Werninghaus) as the family's main heirs. Do not contact without first confirming who this is.

name: Andreas Oeri
current_role: Orthopedic surgeon in private practice, Basel; Roche founding-family shareholder (Roche board member 1996–2020)
profile: Dr. Andreas Oeri (b. 1949) is a member of the Hoffmann/Oeri founding family that, through a shareholder pool, controls the majority of Roche's voting shares — the source of his fortune. He sat on Roche's board for about 25 years as a representative of that pool, chairing its corporate governance and sustainability committee, and stepped down at the 2020 AGM.
interesting_fact: Unusually for a pharma billionaire, he kept a full medical career: a board-certified orthopedic surgeon (1988), he has run his own orthopedic practice in Basel since 1988, even while serving on Roche's board.
deep_cut_fact: Before private practice he trained at the surgical clinic of Kantonsspital Liestal, Basel's institute for physical medicine and the University of Basel surgical department, and was deputy senior physician at Basel University Orthopedic Hospital (1986–88).
notes: Very private; no public contacts beyond his medical practice listing (not included — it is a clinical practice, not a press channel). Roche media relations would be the only institutional route. Little connection to energy/data centers.

name: Catherine Oeri
current_role: Roche founding-family shareholder (member of the Hoffmann/Oeri voting pool); Basel philanthropist
profile: Catherine Oeri is a Basel-based descendant of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche, the Oeri branch of the family. She is a member of the family shareholder pool that controls ~45% of Roche's voting bearer shares, alongside André Hoffmann, Andreas Oeri, Sabine Duschmalé-Oeri and the family's charitable Stiftung Wolf. She lives a private life focused on Basel cultural philanthropy.
interesting_fact: The Hoffmann-Oeri family pool still controls ~45% of Roche's voting shares, more than 125 years after the company's founding in Basel in 1896, one of Europe's longest-lasting family controls of a pharma giant.
deep_cut_fact: In 1998 she personally bought the 759-object Gerd-Wolfgang Essen Tibet collection for Basel's Museum der Kulturen, giving it a comprehensive overview of Tibetan Buddhist art; the museum previously owned only a few Tibetan objects. It was later shown as 'Tibet: Buddhas, Gods, Saints'.
notes: Very private, with no personal public channels. Alive status is unconfirmed: she is still listed by Hurun (2026) and I found no death report, but the Museum der Kulturen's 2021 annual report says she left its commission for reasons of age. Stiftung Wolf (Basel, a grant-giving umbrella foundation of the Oeri family) is the closest institutional route; its website loads only via JavaScript and shows no published email. Little energy/AI link.

name: Sabine Duschmale Oeri
current_role: Roche founding-family shareholder; member of the foundation board (Stiftungsrat) of the Paul Sacher Stiftung, Basel
profile: Sabine Duschmalé-Oeri is a member of the Hoffmann-Oeri family, whose shareholder pool controls the voting majority of Basel pharma group Roche. Hurun lists her wealth (about $7B) as coming from Roche. She keeps a very low profile; her known public role is on the board of Basel's Paul Sacher Stiftung, a music research foundation tied to the family.
interesting_fact: The Paul Sacher Stiftung, on whose board she sits alongside André Hoffmann, was founded in 1973 to preserve conductor-patron Paul Sacher's music library. It now holds around a hundred estates and collections of major composers and performers.
deep_cut_fact: She is listed as 'Sabine Duschmalé' on the Paul Sacher Stiftung's foundation board in Basel, one of the world's leading archives for 20th-century music manuscripts.

public_contacts.value: Paul Sacher Stiftung contact form (Kontaktformular, linked in site footer)

notes: Extremely private, with almost no public footprint. I found no source explicitly tying 'Sabine Duschmalé' (Sacher board) to the Oeri branch, though the name and Roche-family foundation context match strongly. Treat the identity as probable, not confirmed. No direct contact; a Roche-family route would go via Roche corporate communications. No energy/data-center link.

name: Vera Michalski Hoffmann
current_role: Publisher and head of Groupe Libella (Éditions Noir sur Blanc, etc.); founder and president of the Jan Michalski Foundation, Montricher, Switzerland
profile: Vera Michalski-Hoffmann (b. 1954, Basel) is an heir to the Hoffmann branch of the Roche pharmaceutical fortune. In 1986 she and her late husband Jan Michalski founded the Swiss publishing house Éditions Noir sur Blanc to bridge Eastern and Western European literature; it grew into the Libella publishing group. In 2004 she created the Jan Michalski Foundation for writing and literature in his memory.
interesting_fact: Her Jan Michalski Foundation at the foot of the Jura in Montricher runs a writers' residency, a large multilingual public library and the annual Jan Michalski Prize for world literature. Its campus was conceived as a small community under one big canopy.
deep_cut_fact: She graduated from Geneva's Graduate Institute of International Studies. With Jan Michalski, a Polish-born sociologist, she launched Éditions Noir sur Blanc in 1986 with the explicit aim of building 'literary bridges' between Eastern and Western Europe.
notes: Private, culture-focused Roche heir with no energy or tech involvement; best reached via the foundation's journalist contact (Aurélie Baudrier). Wealth figure comes from Hurun only.

name: Maja Hoffmann
current_role: Founder and President, LUMA Foundation (Zurich) and LUMA Arles
profile: Maja Hoffmann (b. 1956), a descendant of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche and heir to the family's Roche stake, is a former film student and documentary producer. She founded the LUMA Foundation in Zurich in 2004 and LUMA Arles in 2013, a creative campus with a Frank Gehry tower opened in 2021, and is a major contemporary-art patron.
interesting_fact: She arrived in Arles at 15 days old and grew up in the Camargue, where her father, ornithologist Luc Hoffmann (a WWF co-founder), had founded the Tour du Valat wetlands research station in 1954.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1990s she worked at her father's Tour du Valat on breeding Przewalski's horses and helped reintroduce them to their native Mongolia in 2004; she was also executive producer of the documentary 'Jean-Michel Basquiat: The Radiant Child'.

public_contacts.value: Finn Partners - thomas.lozinski@finnpartners.com, julie.camdessus@finnpartners.com (national & international press for LUMA Arles)

notes: Strong environmental/sustainability angle via LUMA's materials-research lab (Atelier LUMA) and Camargue roots, though not an energy investor. Best route: LUMA press office or Finn Partners.

name: Yang Zhiling
current_role: Founder and CEO, Moonshot AI (Beijing; maker of the Kimi chatbot and open-weight Kimi models)
profile: Yang Zhilin (b. 1992, Shantou) studied CS at Tsinghua and did a CMU PhD under Ruslan Salakhutdinov and William Cohen, co-authoring Transformer-XL and XLNet. After founding Recurrent AI, he co-founded Moonshot AI in 2023 with Tsinghua classmates; it raised ~$2B at a $20B+ valuation in May 2026 and has reportedly raised more since, ahead of a planned Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: A prog-rock devotee, he named Moonshot AI in honour of Pink Floyd's album The Dark Side of the Moon; a white piano reportedly stands prominently in the Beijing office.
deep_cut_fact: At Tsinghua he was the drummer in a campus band called Splay and organised music competitions; he won admission there after taking first prize in China's National Olympiad in Informatics.
notes: Name usually romanised Yang Zhilin (杨植麟). Keeps a low profile: rarely gives interviews and has no public personal social-media account (Caixin). Best route is Moonshot's global PR address; X handle is the company's, not his.

name: Zhu Hongmei
current_role: Co-actual controller of Shenghong Group / Eastern Shenghong (000301.SZ); director of controlling shareholder Jiangsu Shenghong Technology
profile: Zhu Hongmei (朱红梅) is the wife and business partner of Miao Hangen, founder of Suzhou-based Shenghong Group; the couple are joint actual controllers of Eastern Shenghong. Shenghong grew over ~30 years from printing and dyeing in Shengze, Wujiang into polyester fibre, refining and petrochemicals (Shenghong Petrochemical in Lianyungang) and new-energy materials. She holds no executive post at the listed company.
interesting_fact: The couple took Shenghong public via a 2018 backdoor listing into Wujiang state-owned 'Oriental Market' (renamed Eastern Shenghong), reported as the largest A-share asset restructuring of 2018 and a mixed-ownership reform test case.
notes: Very private; virtually no personal public profile or interviews. Husband Miao Hangen (chairman of Shenghong/Eastern Shenghong) is the public face; best route is Eastern Shenghong's securities/IR office in Shengze, Suzhou (board secretary Wang Jun). Hurun lists wealth jointly with Miao Hangen.

name: Tench Coxe
current_role: Director, NVIDIA (since 1993; audit and compensation committees); former Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures
profile: Venture capitalist who joined Sutter Hill Ventures in 1987 and was managing director 1989-2020, focused on IT investments. Sutter Hill backed Nvidia at its founding and Coxe has sat on Nvidia's board since 1993; his stake made him a billionaire as Nvidia became the AI-datacenter giant. Now Austin-based, he is a philanthropist and was an Artisan Partners director until 2025.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he and his wife Simone gave $100M, unrestricted, to launch UT Austin's new academic medical center (with an MD Anderson expansion) - one of the largest gifts in the university's history.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he was Director of Marketing and MIS at Digital Communication Associates; he holds an economics BA from Dartmouth and a Harvard MBA. In 2025 he also became a minority owner of MLS club Austin FC.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Austin FC ownership: https://austinfc.com/news/austin-fc-announces-additions-to-clubs-ownership-group. Best formal route is Nvidia corporate PR; Austin philanthropy (UT/Dell Med) is a friendly hook.

name: Mike Adenuga
current_role: Chairman, Globacom (Glo) and Conoil; founder of Conoil Producing
profile: Nigerian tycoon (b. 1953) who made his first million at 26 trading lace and distributing soft drinks, then built Conoil Producing (oil blocks in the Niger Delta) and Globacom, a top-three Nigerian mobile operator that also built the Glo-1 submarine cable to the UK. Also owns 74% of listed fuel marketer Conoil and a stake in Sterling Financial Holdings.
interesting_fact: He paid his way through an MBA at Pace University in New York by working as a taxi driver; his Glo-1 cable runs about 6,100 miles from Nigeria to the UK via Ghana and Portugal.
deep_cut_fact: He personally funded the new Alliance Française de Lagos 'Mike Adenuga Centre' at 9 Osborne Road, Ikoyi: Emmanuel Macron inaugurated its first phase in July 2018 and it fully opened in May 2019, with an auditorium, library, art gallery and outdoor amphitheatre.
notes: Famously media-shy; rarely gives interviews and speaks via Globacom statements. No personal social accounts found. Turned 73 in April 2026. NCC has required Globacom to appoint a separate CEO (2025), so leadership structure may change; route via Globacom corporate communications.

name: Wang Qingtao
current_role: Founder/Chairman, Zhongrong Xinda Group (中融新大集团, formerly Shandong Coking Group), Qingdao — group in court-ordered bankruptcy restructuring since 2023
profile: Shandong-born (1962, Zouping) coal and coking entrepreneur known as the 'coking king'. Built Shandong Tiexiong Energy Coal Chemical from 2003, co-founded Shandong's largest coal-chemical park with Shagang in 2007, then renamed his group Zhongrong Xinda in 2016 and pivoted into bank stakes and mining (incl. a Peru iron mine). The group entered bankruptcy restructuring in 2023.
interesting_fact: Ranked Shandong's richest person on the 2021 New Fortune 500 list (RMB 59.65B), and was vice-chairman of the China Coking Industry Association.
deep_cut_fact: To win steel magnate Shen Wenrong's (Shagang) backing, he visited him in Jiangsu more than a dozen times in three months, telling him: 'You build the biggest steel mill, I'll build the biggest coking plant.' Earlier he served in the army and worked at the Zouping materials bureau before quitting to trade coal.
notes: Group in bankruptcy restructuring (Zibo Intermediate Court, 2023) and he reportedly faces numerous consumption-restriction orders; sensitive subject, not a likely podcast guest. No published personal/office contacts found. Also credited with a patented coke-oven smoke/dust removal device (cnpp.cn/focus/30788.html).

name: Eric Lefkofsky
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Tempus AI, Inc. (Nasdaq: TEM); cofounder of Lightbank
profile: Serial Chicago entrepreneur who made his fortune cofounding Groupon (2008) with Andrew Mason and longtime partner Brad Keywell, after earlier ventures including Starbelly, InnerWorkings, Echo Global Logistics and MediaOcean. Since 2015 he has run Tempus, which applies AI and molecular data to cancer care; it IPO'd in 2024 at about $6B, his fourth IPO. He also cofounded VC firm Lightbank.
interesting_fact: After a girlfriend dumped him in college at Michigan, he started his first business selling carpets, which he estimates generated hundreds of thousands of dollars in sales.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published author and longtime teacher: his 2007 book 'Accelerated Disruption' (Easton Studio Press) is about how technology reshapes business, and he has taught entrepreneurship/disruptive business models at Kellogg, DePaul and Chicago Booth.
notes: Personal site lefkofsky.com links his X and LinkedIn. Tempus media route is media@tempus.com. Strong AI/data angle (multimodal foundation models, large genomic datasets). Avoid personal/family health topics.

name: Xu Xin
current_role: Non-independent director (since July 2024) and co-actual controller, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology (300604.SZ)
profile: Xu Xin (徐昕, b. 1976) is co-actual controller, with chairman Zhao Yi (reported as her husband), of Hangzhou Changchuan Technology, a ChiNext-listed maker of chip test equipment (testers, handlers, AOI) founded 2008, listed 2017. She joined at founding as finance manager, later CFO and assistant GM; director since 2024.
interesting_fact: Changchuan has grown by buying foreign tool makers: Singapore AOI maker STI, the semiconductor division of Japan's SATO and Malaysia's test-equipment maker EXIS; it now employs about 4,500 people.
deep_cut_fact: Before Changchuan, she spent 1999-2005 as a sales clerk at Hangzhou Weili Trading; a Zhejiang Shuren University graduate, she joined Changchuan at its April 2008 founding as finance manager and ran its finances as CFO in 2015.
notes: Low public profile; husband Zhao Yi (ex-Silan Microelectronics production director, founder/chairman) is the public face. Best route is the company IR/board secretary office (secretary Shao Jingyang). Contacts are company-level, not personal.

name: Zhao Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology (CCTech, SZSE: 300604)
profile: Zhao Yi (b. 1976, Weiyuan, Neijiang, Sichuan) spent 1997-2007 at Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics, rising to production director, then founded Changchuan Technology in 2008 to make chip test and handling equipment (testers, handlers, probers, AOI). CCTech listed in Shenzhen in 2017; AI-driven demand for memory/advanced-packaging test pushed its market cap to ~CNY180B, and it is now pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: CCTech was billed as China's first listed semiconductor test-equipment company (Shenzhen ChiNext IPO, April 2017, at CNY9.94/share); its value rose from ~CNY27.7B to ~CNY180B in about 18 months to 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He started CCTech in April 2008 with just CNY500,000 in seed capital, launched its first gravity-type test handler that same year, and its in-house analog tester CTA8200 in 2009. The name 'Changchuan' combines the hometowns of the two co-founders: Changxing (Zhejiang) and Sichuan.
notes: Described in Chinese press as low-profile; co-founder and wife Xu Xin is a director (Hurun lists the fortune jointly). Board secretary Shao Jingyang handles investor contact. Hometown-name detail is from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Changchuan_Technology).

name: Rakesh Gangwal
current_role: Director, Southwest Airlines (chairman Nov 2024–Aug 2025); co-founder of InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo)
profile: Kolkata-born, IIT Kanpur- and Wharton-educated airline veteran. Gangwal rose through United Airlines and Air France, ran US Airways as CEO and chairman (1998–2001) and then Worldspan. In 2006 he co-founded IndiGo with Rahul Bhatia, starting with one aircraft; it is now India's largest airline. He left IndiGo's board in 2022 and is selling down his stake. He joined Southwest's board in 2024 and still serves as a director after a stint as chairman.
interesting_fact: IndiGo started in 2006 with a single aircraft and grew into India's largest airline by market share. Gangwal's stake in it is the source of his multibillion-dollar fortune.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2022 Gangwal gave ₹100 crore to his alma mater IIT Kanpur to set up the Gangwal School of Medical Sciences and Technology, a planned medical school with a super-speciality hospital on campus. He also joined the school's advisory board. Earlier in his career he was a production and planning engineer at Philips India and a financial analyst at Ford.
notes: Low public profile; he is Miami-based. Avoid the IndiGo governance dispute with Bhatia. No personal social accounts were found. The IIT Kanpur medical school philanthropy is the warmest angle.

name: Ma Jianrong
current_role: Executive Chairman, Shenzhou International Group Holdings (HKEX: 2313), Ningbo
profile: Former mill worker who joined Ningbo's Shenzhou knitting venture in 1989, rose to general manager, gained family control of the company in 1997–2004 and has been executive chairman since its 2005 Hong Kong listing. Shenzhou is China's largest vertically integrated knitwear maker, supplying Nike, Adidas, Uniqlo and Puma from plants in China, Vietnam and Cambodia.
interesting_fact: Shenzhou has been dubbed the 'Foxconn of apparel': a contract manufacturer that, despite thin-margin OEM work, became the most valuable listed apparel company in China by market value.
deep_cut_fact: Before Shenzhou he worked in a cotton spinning mill and a knitwear factory; at Shenzhou his first role was manager of the weaving department. The company itself was set up by the Beilun district government with Shanghai No. 20 Knitting Factory, where his father was technical deputy director.

public_contacts.value: iPR Limited (investor and press relations adviser)

notes: Aged 61 per 2025 annual report (Apr 2026). Very low media profile; rarely interviewed. Chinese name 马建荣. Best route via company secretary email or iPR.

name: Pierre Landolt
current_role: Owner/operator of Fazenda Tamanduá (biodynamic farm, Patos, Paraíba, Brazil) and sole investor in AxialPar sustainable-agribusiness company; Sandoz family heir and former Sandoz/Novartis board member
profile: Pierre Landolt is a French-Swiss member of the Sandoz family whose great-grandfather founded the group that became Novartis and Syngenta. He served on the Sandoz and Novartis boards until about 70 and helped create Syngenta in the 2000 agribusiness merger; since 1977 he has run a ~3,000-hectare biodynamic farm in Brazil's semi-arid sertão, producing mangoes, honey, dairy, rice and melons.
interesting_fact: Although his family fortune helped found agrochemical giant Syngenta, his Fazenda Tamanduá uses no chemicals: it follows Rudolf Steiner's biodynamic method, and over half the land is set aside as reserves and wildlife corridors, including ~350 ha of private natural heritage reserve.
deep_cut_fact: He came to Brazil at 29 after a law degree and a year as a paratrooper in the French army, and first went to the Paraíba backlands with a Dutch agronomist looking for land to grow senna, because war between Pakistan and India had disrupted world supply of the plant.
notes: Age ~78 (77 in April 2025 AgFeed interview). Very private; no published personal/office contact found (farm and AxialPar sites returned errors). Agri-sustainability angle rather than energy. IMD has 2006 case studies on AxialPar.

name: Paul-Louis Halley
profile: French retail entrepreneur who co-founded Promodès in 1961 with his father and brother; it merged with Carrefour in 1999, leaving him its principal shareholder (~11%). He died on 6 December 2003 in a TBM 700 plane crash on approach to Oxford Airport.
notes: Deceased 6 Dec 2003 (plane crash near Oxford, UK). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul-Louis_Halley. Skip for outreach.

name: Landolt family
current_role: Swiss family; descendants of the Sandoz founders and long-standing major shareholders of Novartis (via the Sandoz Family Foundation / Sandoz Family Office)
profile: The Landolts are the heirs of the Sandoz chemical/pharma dynasty through Elisabeth Sandoz and Jacques Landolt; their fortune comes from Sandoz shares that became Novartis in the 1996 Sandoz–Ciba merger (historically ~3.6% of Novartis). Pierre Landolt (b. 1947) chaired the Sandoz Family Foundation for decades and sat on Novartis's board 2010–2018; the family also has hotel and watchmaking interests.
interesting_fact: In 1998 Pierre Landolt said the family had stayed loyal to a single stock for 110 years — Sandoz, later Novartis — and had no intention of selling it.
deep_cut_fact: Pierre Landolt splits his life between Switzerland and Brazil, where, shocked by poverty in the Nordeste, he built a model farm and founded a bank to finance agricultural projects (Le Temps interview, 1998).
notes: Family entry, not one individual; Pierre Landolt is the most public member. Very discreet; no published contacts found for the Sandoz Family Office/Foundation. Reports of governance turmoil at the foundation exist (finews) — avoid in outreach.

name: Frederik Paulson
current_role: Chairman emeritus / principal shareholder, Ferring Pharmaceuticals (Saint-Prex, Switzerland); explorer and philanthropist
profile: Frederik Paulsen (correct spelling; born Stockholm 1950) is the son of Ferring founder Frederik Paulsen Sr. He has worked at Ferring since 1976 and led the reproductive-health and peptide drugmaker for decades; it passed €2.5B revenue in 2025. He moved to Switzerland in 2003, where Ferring is now headquartered, and has interests in real estate and viticulture. Since Feb 2026 Ferring's chair and CEO is Jean-Frédéric Paulsen.
interesting_fact: A serious polar explorer, he is described as the first person to visit all eight of Earth's poles (completed winter 2013). In 2007 he dived 14,000+ ft in a MIR submersible to the seabed at the North Pole.
deep_cut_fact: In 2010 he and companion François Bernard made the first crossing of the Bering Strait from America to Russia in an ultralight aircraft. Academically, he holds a doctorate in demography from EHESS in Paris and studied chemistry in Kiel.

public_contacts.value: carine.julen@ferring.com (Senior Manager, Corporate Communications & Public Affairs)

notes: Hurun spells the name 'Paulson'; the correct spelling is Paulsen. He was Russia's honorary consul in Lausanne (2009-2022) and received Russian state honours, so check reputational fit. Philanthropy includes ~$40M to the Museum Kunst der Westküste (Föhr) and support for the South Georgia Heritage Trust and Bhutan's Royal Textile Academy. Exploration is the best conversational hook.

name: James Cox Chambers
current_role: Board member, Communities In Schools; Cox Enterprises heir; self-described renewable-energy entrepreneur, biodynamic farmer and filmmaker
profile: Jim Cox Chambers is the son of Anne Cox Chambers (d. 2020) and grandson of Cox Enterprises founder James M. Cox. He inherited a large stake (~17% per LittleSis) in the family-owned media, cable and auto conglomerate but has no operating role. He has chaired Bard College's board (he is a 1981 alumnus) and been an Atlanta Hawks partner.
interesting_fact: His official bio calls him a 'renewable energy entrepreneur' and 'biodynamically trained farmer' whose life mission is 'an equitable, just, bounteously clean Mother Earth', an energy angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He describes himself as 'essentially a hippy since adolescence', 'born and bred in the cradle of the Civil Rights Movement, Atlanta.' His mother Anne Cox Chambers, Carter's ambassador to Belgium, was a formative early supporter of Communities In Schools, whose board he now sits on.
notes: Very private, with no personal website or verified social accounts found. He is no longer listed on Bard's current trustee leadership page, so the Bard chair role is past. I could not confirm his current Hawks ownership status or the name of his renewable-energy venture. Possible route: Communities In Schools national office.

name: Marcos Galperin
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, MercadoLibre (stepped down as CEO in 2026 after 26 years)
profile: Argentine entrepreneur Marcos Galperin founded MercadoLibre in 1999 while finishing his Stanford MBA, after stints at oil company YPF and a JPMorgan internship. He built it into Latin America's dominant e-commerce and fintech (Mercado Pago) platform, operating in 18 countries and Nasdaq-listed since 2007. In 2026 he handed the CEO role to a successor and became executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Galperin comes from Argentine business royalty: his grandfather founded tannery Sadesa, now one of the country's largest leather makers. He also helped organise Argentina's first-ever presidential debate before the 2015 election.
