deep_cut_fact: At Stanford GSB, finance professor Jack McDonald had him drive private-equity investor John Muse (Hicks Muse) to the airport. Galperin pitched MercadoLibre during the ride and won his first investor. In 2012 he gave $1.5M to name two spaces in the GSB's Knight Management Center.
notes: Lives in Uruguay. Very active on X, but the handle was not verified from an official page in this pass. MercadoLibre's media contact (Valeria Bazzi) is the published press route. Galperin is a vocal political commentator in Argentina.

name: Gao Dekang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Bosideng International Holdings (HKEX: 3998)
profile: Gao Dekang (b. 1952), from a family of tailors in Changshu, Jiangsu, started a village tailoring workshop with eight sewing machines in 1976, moved into OEM down jackets for Shanghai brands and launched his own Bosideng brand in the early 1990s. Bosideng is now China's leading down-apparel brand with thousands of stores, sold internationally, and Gao still chairs and runs it.
interesting_fact: In the early years he personally rode a Yongjiu bicycle some 100km each way between Changshu and Shanghai, before dawn, to pick up materials and deliver finished garments.
deep_cut_fact: The name Bosideng is a phonetic play on 'Boston': the jackets he first made under licence were branded 'Xiushideng' (echoing Houston), so when he registered his own brand in 1992 he picked a famously cold US city instead.
notes: Input lists him on 'Hurun Self-Made Women' - likely a data merge error (Gao Dekang is male; his wife Mei Dong is a director). He reportedly got the down-jacket idea after reading about a Chinese Everest expedition. Best route: Bosideng IR.

name: John Catsimatidis
current_role: Owner, Chairman and CEO, Red Apple Group (Gristedes/D'Agostino, United Refining, WABC radio); director, Turning Point Brands
profile: Greek-born (Nisyros, 1948), Harlem-raised grocer who dropped out of NYU to buy into the store he clerked at, opened the first Red Apple in 1971 and later bought Gristedes. In 1986 he acquired Pennsylvania refiner United Refining (Warren, PA), now the core of his energy holdings, alongside NYC real estate. Since 2020 he has owned WABC radio, where he hosts 'The Cats Roundtable'.
interesting_fact: He hosts a weekly political talk-radio show, The Cats Roundtable, and bought the station that airs it (WABC 770 AM) in 2020; he ran for NYC mayor as a Republican in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil he dabbled in aviation: he invested in charter carrier Capitol Air in 1984 and in 1992 launched his own charter airline, Capitol Air Express, which flew from 1993 to 1996 in the old Capitol Air livery. He studied electrical engineering at NYU (Brooklyn Tech '66) before quitting 8 credits short.

public_contacts.value: The Cats Roundtable (WABC 770 AM) - linked from his official site

notes: Very media-friendly; hosts his own radio show and does many interviews, so a guest-swap/radio angle may work. Red Apple Group HQ is 800 Third Ave, NYC (no published press email found). Wrote a memoir, 'How Far Do You Want to Go?' (listed on his site).

name: Trevor Rees-Jones
current_role: Founder, Chief Oil & Gas (Dallas); co-founder of The Rees-Jones Foundation
profile: Dallas oil-and-gas bankruptcy lawyer (Thompson & Knight) who switched to investing in wells in 1984 and founded Chief Oil & Gas in 1994. Chief was an early Barnett Shale and Marcellus driller; he sold Barnett assets to Devon in 2006 and Chief's Marcellus business to Chesapeake in 2022, and remains active in oil, gas and mining ventures plus large North Texas philanthropy.
interesting_fact: By 2005 Chief Oil & Gas was the second-largest producer in the Barnett Shale, having drilled more than 250 wells, and its 2006 Barnett sale to Devon and Crosstex brought roughly $2.6 billion in cash.
deep_cut_fact: He earned Eagle Scout with Troop 70 in 1966, and the Circle Ten Council's Trevor Rees-Jones Scout Camp is named after him; his foundation also funded the Rees-Jones Foundation Leadership Veranda at the Boy Scouts' Summit Bechtel Reserve.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews but did several with Hart Energy and D CEO. Foundation emails were taken from search snippets of the official contact page (site blocked direct fetch) - re-verify before use. Also a Dartmouth trustee (2010-14) and TCU trustee.

name: Lin Shu-hong
current_role: Co-founder and President (總裁) of Chang Chun Group, Taiwan petrochemicals (stepped down as chairman end-2013)
profile: Lin Shu-hong (林書鴻, also Suhon Lin, b. 1928) co-founded Chang Chun Group in 1949 with classmates Tseng Shin-yi and M.K. Liao on about $100. It grew into one of Asia's largest private petrochemical groups (resins, chemicals, electronic materials) with plants in Taiwan, China and SE Asia. Though he left the chairmanship in 2013, in his mid-90s he still toured plants weekly.
interesting_fact: Called 'the Edison of petrochemicals': in the early days he ran 5-6 experiments a day to perfect a plywood adhesive that won over 60+ Taiwanese plywood makers and was even sold to the US military. He was elected to ITRI's first class of Fellows (2012) and won a National S&T contribution award (2016).
deep_cut_fact: At 94 he still visited the Hsinchu, Miaoli, Mailiao, Changhua and Kaohsiung plants every week, read nightly before bed, and recommended Kazuo Inamori's book on work, which he had covered in sticky tabs and notes.
notes: Born 1 Aug 1928 (age ~98); Forbes 2026 still lists him and no death report found, but confirm before outreach. Famously low-profile; group is private with no press/IR desk found (website behind Cloudflare). Any approach would go via Chang Chun Group corporate office in Taipei.

name: Carlos Bulgheroni
current_role: Deceased (died 3 September 2016, aged 71, in the United States)
profile: Argentine oil and gas magnate who, with brother Alejandro, built Bridas (founded by their father) into Argentina's leading private energy group, later partnering with BP and CNOOC in Pan American Energy. He died of cancer in September 2016; Alejandro now leads the family business.
notes: Deceased: died 3 Sep 2016 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni ; https://www.pagina12.com.ar/diario/economia/2-308544-2016-09-04.html). Wealth was shared with brother Alejandro Bulgheroni (alive, chairman of Pan American Energy Group) - he would be the relevant outreach target instead.

name: Vladimir Kim
current_role: Major shareholder, KAZ Minerals (private copper miner, Kazakhstan/Kyrgyzstan); former chairman of Kazakhmys/KAZ Minerals
profile: Vladimir Kim joined Zhezkazgantsvetmet, later Kazakhmys, in 1995 and chaired Kazakhmys from 2005. It became the first Kazakh company listed in London. After the 2014 split he kept a big stake in copper producer KAZ Minerals, which he and Oleg Novachuk took private in 2021; it runs the Aktogay and Bozshakol mines. In 2025 he sold his majority stake in Kazakhmys Corp. to Nurlan Artykbaev.
interesting_fact: He is descended from Koreans whom Stalin deported to Kazakhstan, and for years he was ranked Kazakhstan's richest person.
deep_cut_fact: Kim was born on 29 October 1960 in the village of Slavyanka (now Myrzakent) in South Kazakhstan. He trained as an architect, graduating from the Almaty Architecture and Construction Institute in 1982, and holds a Candidate of Technical Sciences degree. After independence he did business internships in Germany, Switzerland and South Korea.
notes: Very private; he gives no interviews and has no social presence. Copper for electrification and data centers is a relevant angle. Approach only via KAZ Minerals corporate communications (head office now in Dubai). Politically connected, so avoid political topics.

name: Jeff Skoll
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Skoll Foundation; Chairman, Capricorn Investment Group (impact investing)
profile: Montreal-born, Toronto-raised electrical engineer and Stanford MBA who became eBay's first full-time hire and first president in 1996, leaving in 2001. He turned his eBay wealth into the Skoll Foundation (social entrepreneurship, Skoll World Forum) and Participant Media (An Inconvenient Truth, Spotlight), which he wound down in 2024, and invests via Capricorn.
interesting_fact: One of impact investing's earliest proponents: Capricorn Investment Group's early bets included Tesla, battery developer QuantumScape and air-taxi maker Joby Aviation; his Skoll Foundation and Fund have distributed some $1.3B since 1999.
deep_cut_fact: At the University of Toronto he co-edited the engineering students' satirical newspaper The Toike Oike. After graduating he backpacked around the world, then started two Toronto businesses: IT consultancy Skoll Engineering and computer-rental firm Micros on the Move.
notes: Best route is Skoll Foundation press (press@skoll.org). Strong climate/energy angle via Capricorn clean-tech investments. $1.3B giving figure per Forbes profile.

name: Franz Viegener
current_role: Co-Chair of the Viega Shareholders' Committee, Viega Group (Attendorn, Germany); board member, Viega Foundation
profile: Fifth-generation member of the family that owns Viega, the Attendorn-based maker of press-fitting piping, plumbing and HVAC installation systems (~5,500 staff; sites in Germany, the US and India). He co-chairs the shareholders' committee with cousin Anna Viegener while non-family executives run operations, and is involved in the Viega Foundation's clean-water work.
interesting_fact: Viega began in winter 1899 when founder Franz Anselm Viegener started making beer taps in his own farm shed for neighbouring breweries and pubs in the Sauerland town of Attendorn, before switching to water-pipe installation materials.
deep_cut_fact: At the June 2026 opening of Viega's sixth German plant, in former Michelin tyre-works warehouses in Kirkel, Saarland, he said: 'We operate globally... That said, Germany is and will continue to be a key production base for us,' citing the region's concentration of skilled metalworkers.
notes: Very private family-business owner; minimal personal press. Route via Viega Corporate Communication. Building-tech/water angle rather than energy, though HVAC/heat-pump installation is adjacent.

name: Thomas Kaeser
current_role: Owner and CEO (managing partner), Kaeser Kompressoren SE, Coburg, Germany
profile: Thomas Kaeser (b. 1953, Coburg) joined the family firm founded by his grandfather in 1919, became managing partner in 1985 and has led it since 2009 with his wife Tina-Maria Vlantoussi-Kaeser. As sole owner he built Kaeser into a global compressed-air and vacuum systems maker with ~8,800 staff in 140 countries and 2024 sales above €1.7B.
interesting_fact: He pioneered 'compressed air as a service' in an industry that sold machines: under the Sigma Air Utility model Kaeser runs the customer's whole air supply and bills for air used, on the motto 'customers need compressed air, not necessarily a compressor.'
deep_cut_fact: After his Abitur at Coburg's Ernestinum Gymnasium he studied industrial engineering (Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen) at TU Karlsruhe before joining the family firm in 1979; he later received the Preis Deutscher Maschinenbau, with the laudator calling him 'an entrepreneur in the classic sense. Not a manager. An entrepreneur!'
notes: Private, family-owned; rare interviews (mostly trade press). Company press releases list press contact Daniela Koehler (Kaeser press office, corporate line +49 9561 640452) — https://www.pressebox.de/newsroom/kaeser-kompressoren-gmbh. Compressed air is a large industrial energy user, a natural energy-efficiency angle.

name: Palmer Luckey
current_role: Founder, Anduril Industries (defense tech); founder, ModRetro
profile: Palmer Luckey built the Oculus Rift prototype as a teenager in his parents' Long Beach garage, founded Oculus VR in 2012 and sold it to Facebook in 2014 for ~$2B. After leaving Facebook in 2016 he founded Anduril in 2017, making autonomous drones, sensor towers and the Lattice AI software for the military (valued at $30.5B in June 2025). He also runs retro-gaming hardware maker ModRetro.
interesting_fact: He built more than 50 head-mounted display prototypes before the Rift, funding the work partly by repairing and reselling damaged iPhones (earning at least $36,000), and amassed a large collection of historic VR headsets.
deep_cut_fact: He majored in journalism at Cal State Long Beach and was Online Editor of the student newspaper, the Daily Forty-Niner; he also worked part-time at USC's ICT Mixed Reality Lab building low-cost VR for BRAVEMIND, an Army effort to treat veterans' PTSD.
notes: Very active and accessible on X; does many podcasts. Anduril media@ is the official press route. The journalism-major detail is a natural hook for a journalist. Energy/data-center angle is weak, but Anduril's Arsenal manufacturing campus (Ohio) is a big industrial build.

name: Penny Pritzker
current_role: Founder and Chairman, PSP Partners (Chicago); Senior Fellow of the Harvard Corporation; Microsoft board member
profile: An heir to the Hyatt/Pritzker fortune, Pritzker built and led businesses across real estate, senior living and finance, and was a key Obama fundraiser. She was U.S. Commerce Secretary (2013-17) and later U.S. Special Representative for Ukraine's Economic Recovery (2023-24). She now chairs PSP Partners (buyouts, VC, real estate), sits on Microsoft's board, and since 2022 has been the first woman Senior Fellow (chair) of the Harvard Corporation.
interesting_fact: She was the first U.S. commerce secretary to visit Myanmar. Before government she started five companies, including The Parking Spot airport-parking chain (co-founded 1998, sold for $360M in 2011).
deep_cut_fact: In the 1980s, after six months of training, she finished her first Ironman Triathlon in Hawaii in about 12 hours. She still calls herself a triathlete, and her family foundation started ChicagoRun, which prepares Chicago kids to run their first 5K.
notes: PSP's site publishes a dedicated media-requests email, the best route. Her X bio links to PSP. PSP's site also has a 'A Penny for Your Thoughts' content section. Microsoft board seat plus the Ukraine reconstruction role give AI and energy-infrastructure angles.

name: Anna Viegener
current_role: Co-chair (with Walter Viegener) of the Shareholders' Committee, Viega Group (Attendorn, Germany)
profile: Anna Viegener co-chairs the family shareholders' committee of Viega, the Attendorn maker of piping, plumbing and HVAC systems founded in 1899 and now in its fifth generation. Viega had about €1.8B in 2022 revenue and plants in Germany, the US, India, China and Switzerland. She helped pick CEO Markus Brettschneider in 2024.
interesting_fact: In 2024 she and co-chair Walter Viegener appointed an internal successor as CEO, Markus Brettschneider, previously head of Viega North America. They said they did so to preserve 'the cultural identity of our 125-year-old family business.'
deep_cut_fact: She sits on the board of the Viega Foundation, whose WASH (water, sanitation, hygiene) program funds projects in India such as a school-sanitation renovation in Gujarat and a sanitation project in Vedasandur. Viega has had its own Indian subsidiary since 2015.

public_contacts.value: Katharina.Schulte@viega.de (Senior Manager Corporate Communication, listed as press contact on Viega releases)

notes: Very private; quoted only in company releases, with no interviews found. Best route is Viega corporate communications. Building-technology/HVAC is a modest link to data-center cooling and plumbing.

name: Von Siemens family
current_role: Founding family of Siemens AG; holds roughly 6% via a family partnership, represented on Siemens' Supervisory Board by Nathalie von Siemens (until the 2027 AGM, to be succeeded by family member Christoph von Seidel)
profile: This is a family entry, not one person: descendants of Werner von Siemens, who co-founded Siemens & Halske in Berlin in 1847. Forbes listed the family in 1996-2000. The family still pools a stake of about 6% in Siemens AG, Germany's industrial, electrification and automation group, and keeps a seat on its Supervisory Board.
interesting_fact: In May 2026 Siemens said family representative Nathalie von Siemens will leave the Supervisory Board after the 2027 AGM, after more than 12 years, and that family member Christoph von Seidel will be proposed so the family stays represented.
notes: A family, not an individual, so there is no single person to profile. The natural podcast contact would be Nathalie von Siemens (Supervisory Board member, family spokesperson) via Siemens press, since the energy/electrification angle fits. The ~6% stake figure is from secondary reporting.

name: Rocco Comisso
current_role: Deceased (died January 2026, aged 76); was founder, chairman and CEO of Mediacom Communications and owner of ACF Fiorentina
profile: Rocco Commisso (correct spelling), the Italian-born founder of US cable operator Mediacom and owner of Serie A club Fiorentina since 2019, died in January 2026 at age 76, as announced by Fiorentina and Mediacom.
notes: Deceased - death announced Jan 17, 2026 (sources: https://wtop.com/world/2026/01/fiorentina-owner-and-mediacom-chairman-rocco-commisso-dies-at-76 , https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/rocco-commisso-dead-acf-fiorentina-owner-mediacom-ceo-1236477063/). Name misspelled 'Comisso' in input. Mediacom remains family-owned; rest skipped per instructions.

name: Liu Hanyuan
current_role: Chairman, Tongwei Group; NPC deputy and vice chairman of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Liu left a job at the Meishan county hydropower bureau in Sichuan to build a fish-feed business (founded 1986) that became Tongwei Group, a global leader in aquafeed. Tongwei later moved into polysilicon and solar cells, becoming one of the world's largest PV manufacturers. He is a prominent lawmaker-advocate for solar and renewable-energy policy.
interesting_fact: Tongwei ranks among the world's largest players in two unrelated industries at once: aquaculture feed and solar (polysilicon/cells). Liu regularly files NPC/CPPCC proposals pushing PV, e.g. solar to cut smog and tax cuts for the PV industry.
deep_cut_fact: In spring 1983, aged ~18, he pooled 200 yuan savings plus money from his parents selling two pigs (500 yuan total) to build a 64 m2 submerged fish cage in a Meishan canal; stocking 185 kg of carp yielded 1,390 kg by autumn, reportedly a Sichuan record for fish yield per unit area.
notes: ir_email is the published board-secretary (Yan Ke) contact of listed Tongwei Co. (600438) per its 2024 annual report summary; Tongwei's English site publishes many news items about Liu's policy proposals, a good angle for an energy podcast.

name: Gordon Getty
current_role: Composer and philanthropist (Gordon P. Getty Family Foundation); Getty Oil heir
profile: Son of oil tycoon J. Paul Getty, he led the 1984 sale of Getty Oil to Texaco for $10.1B and in 1985 split the family trust into separate trusts. Now in his 90s, he is a working classical composer (operas Plump Jack, Usher House, The Canterville Ghost, Goodbye, Mr. Chips) and a major San Francisco arts donor; he co-founded PlumpJack Winery with Gavin Newsom in 1995.
interesting_fact: He has given more than $450 million to his philanthropic foundation since 2008, and New Century Chamber Orchestra dedicated its entire 2025-26 season in his honor; he was one of ten inaugural inductees into Opera America's Opera Hall of Fame (2020).
deep_cut_fact: An English-literature graduate of the University of San Francisco and longtime poet, he writes his own librettos; his most-performed vocal work is The White Election (1981), a cycle setting 31 Emily Dickinson poems for soprano and piano, performed at Lincoln Center and the Hermitage Theatre.

public_contacts.value: Nancy Shear Arts Services - sheararts@gmail.com (PR/press for his music only)
mail@rorkmusic.com (Rork Music, his publisher; music inquiries only)

notes: Born 1933; very old and private on business matters. Only published routes are music-related (publisher Rork Music, PR via Nancy Shear Arts Services); his site says funding requests are discarded. An energy-angle pitch is a stretch; an arts/legacy framing fits better. Wikipedia notes 2026-released documents showing past Epstein correspondence - sensitive topic.

name: Li Min
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Rockchip Electronics Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603893), Fuzhou
profile: Li Min cofounded Rockchip in Fuzhou in 2001 with Huang Xu and remains chairman (reappointed general manager in Jan 2025). Rockchip designs SoCs for AIoT devices, tablets and edge-AI products and listed in Shanghai in 2020; Li holds roughly 37% of the company, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: Rockchip, a Fuzhou chip designer, counts Intel, Samsung and Google among its customers and focuses on intelligent IoT and edge-AI processors.
deep_cut_fact: In December 2025 he donated 175,000 Rockchip shares (worth roughly RMB 31M at the time) to the education foundation of his alma mater, Fuzhou No. 1 Middle School (福州一中), 'to give back to his alma mater'.
notes: Low media profile; English name in Chinese is 励民. Best route is via Rockchip's securities/IR department. Some unofficial sites say he was born 1965 and graduated Zhejiang University 1991 - not verified.

name: Steven Hao
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cognition (maker of the Devin AI software-engineering agent)
profile: MIT-trained competitive programmer and former early engineer at Scale AI who co-founded Cognition in late 2023 with Scott Wu and Walden Yan. Cognition's Devin autonomous coding agent (and its 2025 acquisition of Windsurf) drove rapid valuation jumps, making Hao a billionaire per Forbes.
interesting_fact: All three Cognition co-founders were International Olympiad in Informatics competitors; Forbes reported that the company's rapid growth made CTO Hao a billionaire within about two years of founding.
deep_cut_fact: At IOI 2014 in Taipei he placed 6th in the world for the United States, scoring perfect 100s on five of six problems (525/600) to win a gold medal.
notes: No published press email found; only company social accounts. CEO Scott Wu is the usual public face; Hao is the technical lead and appears at engineering conferences (e.g. GitNation speaker profile), a possible route.

name: Fan Hongwei
current_role: Chairman, Hengli Petrochemical Co. (SSE: 600346); Vice Chairman, Hengli Group
profile: Born 1967 in Wujiang, Suzhou, Fan co-founded what became Hengli Group with her husband Chen Jianhua, starting in textiles in 1994 and integrating upstream into polyester, PTA and a giant refinery-petrochemical complex on Changxing Island, Dalian. She chairs listed Hengli Petrochemical; Hengli Group posted 2024 revenue of RMB 871.5bn (Fortune Global 500 #81).
interesting_fact: Hengli's integrated 'from a drop of oil to a bolt of cloth' chain helped break foreign dominance of PX and PTA feedstocks in China; in July 2025 Fan was one of 100 private entrepreneurs given a national 'outstanding builder' award in Beijing.
deep_cut_fact: Hengli began in 1994 as the Wujiang Chemical Fiber Weaving Factory in Shengze, Suzhou, with just 27 employees; when Hengli Group was formally set up in 2003, Fan became its general manager running production and operations.
notes: hlzq@hengli.com is Hengli Petrochemical's board-office/investor mailbox (listed in 2025 and 2026 earnings-call notices); Chinese-language approach advisable. Very low international media profile.

name: Carlos
profile: Carlos Alberto Bulgheroni (1945-2016), Argentine co-owner (with brother Alejandro) of the family energy group Bridas, died on 3 September 2016. Record matched via source of wealth Bridas and shared_with Alejandro Bulgheroni.
notes: DECEASED 3 Sep 2016 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni). Name field is truncated ('Carlos'); country listed as Spain is wrong - he was Argentine. For Bridas/Pan American Energy, the living family principal is his brother Alejandro Bulgheroni.

name: Romesh Wadhwani
current_role: Founder & Chairman, SAIGroup (SymphonyAI, ConcertAI); Founder & Chairman, Wadhwani Foundation
profile: Born in Karachi in 1947 and educated at IIT Bombay and Carnegie Mellon (PhD), Wadhwani made his fortune founding Aspect Development and later ran software PE firm Symphony Technology Group. He now heads SAIGroup, which includes SymphonyAI (backed by his $1B commitment) and ConcertAI. His Wadhwani Foundation funds entrepreneurship and AI-for-good work in India.
interesting_fact: Aspect Development, which he founded in 1991, was acquired by i2 Technologies in 1999 for $9.3 billion in stock. In 2020 India awarded him the Padma Shri.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aspect, he spent a decade running two startups. One was American Robot Corporation, which made computer-integrated manufacturing software. The other was Compu-Guard Corporation, an early technology-enabled energy-management company.

public_contacts.value: Chris Gale (Gale Strategies), SymphonyAI media contact: Chris@GaleStrategies.com

notes: The Compu-Guard energy-management startup is a natural hook for an energy-focused podcast. He also sits on the boards of trustees of CSIS and the Kennedy Center. The best route is SymphonyAI's PR contact.

name: Zhenhua Yao
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Baoneng Group (Shenzhen)
profile: Yao Zhenhua (姚振华, b. 1970, Shantou, Guangdong) founded Shenzhen-based Baoneng Group in 1992. He grew it from agricultural trading and retail into a conglomerate spanning shopping malls, property, insurance (Foresea Life), healthcare and autos (Qoros). He became famous in 2015–16 for the hostile stake-building in China Vanke. He is no longer on Forbes' billionaire list; Baoneng has been working through heavy debts since 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2016 the Vanke share-buying campaign made Yao one of China's richest men; Hurun ranked him No. 4 with about RMB 115B. Chinese media nicknamed him one of the market's 'barbarians at the gate'.
deep_cut_fact: Yao graduated from South China University of Technology in 1992 with a double major in industrial management engineering and food engineering. He started out in the agricultural produce trade before founding Baoneng in Shenzhen that same year.
notes: Not a good outreach target: Baoneng faces extensive debt-enforcement cases, and he is barred from the insurance industry until 2027. Forbes lists him as 'former' billionaire, so his net worth is likely far below the listed figure. No published contact found.

name: Yao Zhenhua
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Baoneng Group (Shenzhen conglomerate: property, retail malls, insurance, autos)
profile: Shenzhen entrepreneur (b. ~1970) who grew Baoneng from a 1990s vegetable-supply business into a conglomerate spanning shopping malls, property, healthcare, Foresea Life insurance and Baoneng Motor. He became nationally known in 2015–16 when his insurer built a ~25% stake in China Vanke; Baoneng has been in financial distress since 2020.
interesting_fact: Baoneng began in 1992 under Shenzhen's 'Shopping Basket' food-supply programme as a vegetable wholesaling operation, which grew into one of the city's largest vegetable suppliers before becoming a mall and finance empire.
deep_cut_fact: In 2020 Baoneng bought the Shenzhen car plant of Changan PSA (the Changan–Peugeot Citroën joint venture), renaming it Baoneng Motor as his entry into carmaking.
notes: Caution: Baoneng is a distressed group facing creditor lawsuits (e.g. Bank of Shanghai won a 2.58B-yuan appeal in July 2026 naming Yao personally); he was barred from China's insurance industry for 10 years in 2017. Not a good outreach target; no published press contact found.

name: Xu Dongbo
current_role: Controlling shareholder (with his father, founder-chairman Xu Gaoming) of Laopu Gold Co. (HKEX: 6181); no listed executive or board title
profile: Son of Xu Gaoming, who founded Beijing-based Laopu Gold in 2009 as a 'heritage gold' brand of handcrafted jewellery using traditional Chinese goldsmithing. He holds shares directly and 30% of family vehicle Hongqiao Jinji; the family controlled ~58-61% after the 2024 Hong Kong IPO, whose shares soared with record gold prices.
interesting_fact: Laopu Gold positions itself as China's top 'heritage gold' brand: its pieces replicate textures of ancient royal jewellery and use at least two traditional handmade gold-crafting techniques, earning it comparisons with Western luxury houses.

public_contacts.value: ir@lphj.com (Laopu Gold, for the attention of the Board)

notes: Almost no public profile; father Xu Gaoming is the public face and the likelier interviewee. May 2026: Xu Dongbo personally bought ~HK$166M of Laopu H shares after a steep share-price decline. Consumer/luxury, not an energy or data-center fit.

name: Paul Foster
current_role: Founder & CEO, Franklin Mountain Investments (El Paso, TX); former founder/chairman of Western Refining
profile: A Baylor-trained CPA who kept the books for small Southwest refineries, Foster took over bankrupt El Paso Refining with partners in 1992, built Western Refining and sold it to Tesoro in 2017 ($6.4B deal). Via Franklin Mountain Investments he holds 30+ businesses (real estate, restaurants, sports); in 2025 he sold Franklin Mountain Energy for about $2.5B.
interesting_fact: He is part owner of the El Paso Chihuahuas Triple-A baseball team (via MountainStar Sports Group) and in 2007 gave $50M to help create the Paul L. Foster School of Medicine at Texas Tech in El Paso.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Lovington, New Mexico (class of 1975), he earned an accounting degree from Baylor in 1979 and then started out working at the local refinery back in Lovington before moving to El Paso.
notes: Very relevant to energy angle: serves on the Dallas Fed Energy Advisory Council and was appointed by Gov. Abbott to the ERCOT board selection committee (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-appoints-foster-to-ercot-board-selection-committee). Best route is Franklin Mountain Investments' general inbox.

name: Sofia Högberg Schörling
current_role: Vice Chairman, Melker Schörling AB (Schörling AB); board member of Hexagon, Securitas and ASSA ABLOY
profile: Sofia Schörling Högberg (b. 1978, BSc Business Administration) is co-majority owner with her sister of Melker Schörling AB, the Stockholm holding company built by her late father, investor Melker Schörling. It holds large stakes in listed Hexagon, AAK, ASSA ABLOY, Hexpol and Securitas. She has sat on its board since 2006 and been vice chairman since 2016.
interesting_fact: Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden attended her 2005 wedding, accompanied by Daniel Westling, now Prince Daniel.
deep_cut_fact: She joined the board of security giant Securitas in 2005, aged about 27, a year before joining the family holding company's board. She also sits on the board of the Stockholm Chamber of Commerce.

public_contacts.value: info@schorlingab.se (Melker Schörling AB / Schörling AB general inbox)

notes: Low public profile; acts as board-level owner rather than operator. Holding company's general inbox is the only published route. Securitas has a data-center security business, a possible hook.

name: Russ Savage
current_role: Founder of Rockstar Energy (sold to PepsiCo 2020); private investor, largely in luxury real estate; based in Miami Beach
profile: Russ Savage (born Russell Weiner, 1970; renamed in 2025 to honor his father, radio host Michael Savage) launched Rockstar energy drink in 2001 with a $50,000 mortgage on his Sausalito condo after Skyy Vodka founder Maurice Kanbar passed on the idea. He sold Rockstar to PepsiCo in 2020 in a deal worth $4B+ and has since focused on investing, notably luxury Florida real estate.
interesting_fact: When the first Rockstar cans hit stores and bars, he promoted the brand by driving around San Francisco in an old limo painted with the Rockstar logo.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Rockstar he ran a yard-service business in his Northern California neighborhood at age 8 and worked the Wendy's drive-thru at 15; later, after a political-science degree at San Diego State, he worked as a travel consultant.
notes: No published personal, office or press contacts found; Rockstar is now owned by PepsiCo (Celsius holds US/Canada rights since 2025), so company press channels don't reach him. Travel-consultant detail is from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Weiner). Avoid politics; he ran for CA Assembly in 1998.

name: Russ Weiner
current_role: Founder of Rockstar Energy (sold to PepsiCo in 2020); private investor
profile: Russell Weiner founded Rockstar energy drink in 2001 after his then-boss, Skyy Vodka founder Maurice Kanbar, passed on the idea. He funded the launch with a $50,000 mortgage on his Sausalito condo. He built Rockstar into a top-3 US energy-drink brand and sold it to PepsiCo in 2020 for more than $4 billion. He now keeps a low profile as a private investor and political donor.
interesting_fact: When the first Rockstar cans hit stores, Weiner promoted them by driving around San Francisco in an old limo painted with the Rockstar logo. As a boy he ran a yard-service business at age 8.
deep_cut_fact: Before beverages he ran for the California State Assembly in 1998 as a Republican. He won the primary by just five votes and was endorsed by the president of the Oakland NAACP branch, then lost the general election to incumbent Kerry Mazzoni.
notes: No published personal, office or press contact found. Rockstar is now part of PepsiCo, so PepsiCo media relations would only cover the brand, not him. Low energy/AI link (energy drinks, not energy). He is also a political fundraiser, so check fit.

name: Thomas Straumann
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Medartis Holding AG; major shareholder (~17%) of Straumann Holding; owner, Grand Hotel Les Trois Rois, Basel
profile: Thomas Straumann is the grandson of Reinhard Straumann, who founded Straumann in 1954 as an alloy research firm. His father Fritz built its titanium dental-implant business. Thomas joined the board in 1990 and refocused the company purely on dental, making it the world's largest dental-implant maker. In 1997 he founded bone-fixation implant company Medartis, which he chairs.
interesting_fact: He owns a stable of show-jumping horses and Basel's landmark Grand Hotel Les Trois Rois.
deep_cut_fact: When his family bought the 'Drei Könige' hotel and the adjacent Blumenrain 2 building in 2004, he had it restored under heritage-preservation rules with Basel architect Christian Lang, reconstructing parts from the original plans. Herzog & de Meuron later led a 2023-25 renovation.

public_contacts.value: Grand Hotel Les Trois Rois corporate media page

notes: Low public profile; Basel-based. Best route is Medartis investor relations, since he chairs Medartis. Little link to energy/data-center themes; more of a medtech and hospitality story.

name: Cai Haoyu
current_role: Co-founder, Anuttacon (AI-native games studio); co-founder and major shareholder of miHoYo/HoYoverse (stepped down as chairman 2023)
profile: Cai Haoyu (蔡浩宇) co-founded Shanghai game developer miHoYo in 2012 with Shanghai Jiao Tong University classmates Liu Wei and Luo Yuhao. miHoYo made global hits Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero. He handed the chairmanship to Liu in 2023 but kept a large stake, and co-founded Anuttacon, whose 2025 game Whispers from the Star centres on an AI companion called Stella.
interesting_fact: After visiting miHoYo's Shanghai headquarters in 2023, Apple CEO Tim Cook called the team 'phenomenal'.
deep_cut_fact: miHoYo began in January 2011 in dorm D32 at SJTU's Minhang campus. Its first release, FlyMe2theMoon (iOS, Sept 2011), was named after Evangelion's ending song. The 'H' in miHoYo comes from Cai Haoyu's name, and 'mi' was inspired by Hatsune Miku.
notes: Very private and rarely gives interviews. Anuttacon is the best entry point for an AI-and-games angle, but it publishes no press email (site only).

name: Charles Cadogan
current_role: Deceased (died 11 June 2023, aged 86); was 8th Earl Cadogan and head of Cadogan Estates (Chelsea, London)
profile: Charles Cadogan, 8th Earl Cadogan, whose family owns the Cadogan Estate of roughly 90+ acres in Chelsea and Knightsbridge, died at his Chelsea home on 11 June 2023. His son Edward Cadogan succeeded him as 9th Earl and head of the family's property interests.
notes: Deceased - died 11 June 2023 (sources: https://www.cadogan.co.uk/remembering-the-life-of-the-earl-cadogan , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Cadogan,_8th_Earl_Cadogan). Hurun still listed him through 2025. Successor is Edward Cadogan, 9th Earl; Cadogan Estates is run by CEO Hugh Seaborn.

name: Torbjorn Tornqvist
current_role: Former co-founder and CEO of Gunvor Group (oil trader, since renamed Centalion); stepped down Dec 2025 in a management buyout; head of Artemis Racing sailing team
profile: Stockholm-born (1953), Geneva-based oil trader who co-founded Gunvor in 1997 and grew it into one of the world's largest independent energy traders. He bought out co-founder Gennady Timchenko's stake in 2014. In Dec 2025 he resigned as CEO and agreed to sell his ~86% stake to ~60 senior employees, partly vendor-financed; the firm has since rebranded as Centalion.
interesting_fact: He founded the Artemis Racing sailing team in 2006, which reached the Louis Vuitton Cup final in the 2013 America's Cup challenger series and helped bring Sweden back into the America's Cup.
deep_cut_fact: He came to competitive sailing late: he started crewing with Russell Coutts at the Swan Worlds, Coutts 'talked me into a TP52', and they won the MedCup and the championship in the same season, after only about three years of sailing. He still helms his own RC44 on the 44Cup circuit.
notes: No personal or office contacts published. He has left Gunvor/Centalion, so company press office is no longer a route to him. Artemis Racing (sailing) is the only active public affiliation. Avoid Russia/Timchenko/US Treasury topics; they are the context of his exit.

name: Pyotr Aven
current_role: Co-founder/shareholder of LetterOne (L1) and Alfa Group; former chairman of Alfa-Bank (2011-2022); art collector based in Surrey, UK
profile: Moscow-born economist Pyotr (Petr) Aven was Russia's minister of foreign economic relations in 1992 before joining Alfa-Bank, which he ran as president (1994-2011) and chairman until 2022. With Mikhail Fridman and partners he co-owns Alfa Group and LetterOne. Sanctioned by the EU/UK in 2022, he stepped off LetterOne's board and now focuses on his art collection and writing.
interesting_fact: He owns what is described as the largest/best private collection of Russian art (Goncharova, Petrov-Vodkin, Chagall, Kandinsky), lent to Tate, the Royal Academy, MoMA and Fondation Louis Vuitton; in 2022 he bought a building in Riga for a planned private museum.
deep_cut_fact: His collecting began in childhood with stamps and toy cars; the first painting he bought was a 1920s still life by Pavel Kuznetsov. As a young economist he was seconded to IIASA in Laxenburg, Austria, and he has lectured at Moscow's Higher School of Economics since 2007.
notes: Under EU/UK/US sanctions since 2022 - check legal/editorial implications before any engagement. petraven.info describes itself as his website (email appears in its schema.org metadata); appears to be a reputation-style site, so treat accounts linked there with some caution. Books: 'The Age of Berezovsky', 'Gaidar's Revolution' (free at petr-aven-books.com).

name: Liu Debing
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director & Chairman, Knowledge Atlas Technology / Zhipu AI (Z.ai), HKEX: 2513
profile: Co-founder and chairman of Zhipu AI, the Beijing developer of the GLM large language models, spun out of Tsinghua University's knowledge-engineering lab (AMiner) in 2019. He handles fundraising and business decisions. Zhipu listed in Hong Kong in January 2026, billed as the world's first listed LLM company, raising about $560M, and in 2026 changed its English short name to Z.AI.
interesting_fact: Speaking to Bloomberg TV on the day Zhipu listed, Liu said the AI price war would go global: if Zhipu can keep its prices at about one-seventh of its rivals', international customers will have to accept it.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zhipu, Liu earned a computer science PhD at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Computing Technology, then worked at Technicolor's China research institute before joining Tsinghua as a senior engineer. He was one of Zhipu's six founders.
notes: Zhipu is on the U.S. Entity List (added 2025). No dedicated IR or press email found in its HKEX filings; best route is the company website or its HK IR channel. Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

name: Cai Huabo
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Shenzhen Longsys Electronics (江波龙, SZSE: 301308)
profile: Cai Huabo (蔡华波, b. 1976, Jiujiang, Jiangxi) went to Shenzhen after high school. In 1999 he and his twin sister Cai Lijiang turned a tiny Huaqiangbei electronics-market stall into Longsys, now a major memory/storage maker (FORESEE, Lexar, Zilia). It bought the Lexar brand from Micron in 2017 and listed in Shenzhen in 2022. Riding the AI-driven memory boom, its 2025 revenue reached RMB 22.8B, including SSDs for AI servers and data centers. It is pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: Longsys's growth was a 'snake swallows elephant' story: a company that began as a Huaqiangbei trading counter acquired the global premium flash brand Lexar from Micron in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Cai never went to university. His first job was selling resistors and capacitors at Huaqiangbei counters. The name 江波龙 combines 江 for their home province Jiangxi, 波 from Cai Huabo, and 龙 for the Year of the Dragon that he and his twin sister share.
notes: Forbes' bio text mistakenly names his twin sister Cai Lijiang (a minority co-shareholder) as chairman; the chairman is Cai Huabo. The AI-memory/data-center SSD angle is highly relevant. Route via the IR mailbox / board secretary; Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

name: Shen Bin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Shagang Group (Sha Steel), Zhangjiagang; actual controller of Jiangsu Shagang Co. (SZSE: 002075)
profile: Born 1979, the son of Shagang founder Shen Wenrong, he rose through Shagang Group as first deputy general manager and finance roles before becoming chairman; after his father died in June 2024 he inherited ~29% of the group and became controller of China's largest private steelmaker.
interesting_fact: Shagang is an unexpected data-centre player: it bought control of London-based Global Switch (carrier-neutral data centres in Europe and Asia-Pacific) from the Reuben Brothers in 2016–2019 and has repeatedly explored selling it.
notes: Chinese name 沈彬. Role/inheritance per July 2024 SZSE equity-change filing (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk03/finalpage/2024-07-19/ef74daed-5563-4d34-b4d7-413d6b58825d.PDF). Very low profile, no English interviews. Global Switch is the natural data-center hook. Avoid 2022 CSRC penalty.

name: Qu Fang
current_role: Co-founder and President, Xiaohongshu (RedNote), Shanghai
profile: Qu Fang (Miranda Qu), a Beijing Foreign Studies University graduate, left a Fortune 500 multinational in 2013 to co-found Xiaohongshu with Mao Wenchao in Shanghai. It grew from an overseas-shopping guide into one of China's biggest lifestyle and search platforms, briefly drawing millions of US 'TikTok refugees' in January 2025.
interesting_fact: Xiaohongshu launched in October 2013 as a professionally written shopping guide telling Chinese travellers what to buy and where abroad, before morphing into a user-generated 'what to buy' community nicknamed a 'Zhihu for overseas shopping'.
deep_cut_fact: She and co-founder Mao Wenchao are both from Wuhan; in a 2015 Yicai interview she summed up the mission as 'we want to be the user's shopping bestie (gouwu guimi)', explaining the community's ad-free reviews as the source of trust.
notes: No published press email found; company comms are China-based and not easily reached from outside. Wuhan origin detail from https://tech.ifeng.com/c/8PNSEfGRusO. Social/consumer internet, weak fit for an energy/data-center show unless discussing AI/search.

name: Cho Jyh-jer
current_role: Retired; former Vice Chairman of MediaTek (retired June 2015)
profile: MediaTek co-founding veteran who joined as president in 1997 when the chip designer was spun off from United Microelectronics (UMC), and was promoted to vice chairman in 2005 to focus on new products and strategy. He retired in June 2015; his wealth comes mainly from his MediaTek stake. No public role since retirement was found.
interesting_fact: One of the founding veterans who fought alongside MediaTek chairman Tsai Ming-kai from the company's optical-disc-drive chip days, before MediaTek became one of the world's top smartphone chip designers.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer from National Chiao Tung University (communication engineering), he came out of NCTU's famed 'Lab 307' under Prof. Wu Chung-yu, one of the first master's cohorts in a lab that produced many of Taiwan's IC-design leaders.
notes: Very private, retired since 2015; no published personal/office contact found. Deep-cut fact taken from search-indexed text of GVM/NYCU pages (gvm.com.tw not fetchable here) - double-check before use. Alive status not confirmed but no death report found; still on 2026 Forbes real-time list.

name: Lutz Mario Helmig
current_role: Founder and majority owner, ATON GmbH (family investment holding: engineering incl. EDAG, mining, medical, aviation)
profile: Lutz Helmig (b. 1946) is a vascular surgeon turned entrepreneur. He co-founded the Asklepios hospital group in 1987, then built Helios Kliniken, which his family sold to Fresenius in 2005 for €1.5B. Through ATON (founded 2001) and Horus Finanzholding he invests in engineering (EDAG), mining, medical and aviation businesses.
interesting_fact: In 2013 he paid off the entire €2.1M debt of Grebenhain, the Hessian village he has lived in since 1977, on condition it balance its budget for the following three years.
deep_cut_fact: After the 2006 sale of airline dba (he had bought 25.1%) to Air Berlin, he gave every dba employee 195 Air Berlin shares worth over €3,000 as a farewell gift. He also co-founded Asklepios with lawyer Bernard große Broermann in 1987 before splitting off to build Helios.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed; wrote a 2013 book on health economics, 'Gesundheit und Freiheit'. ATON's general inbox is the published route. Aged ~80.

name: Li Hua
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Futu Holdings (Futubull / moomoo), Hong Kong/Shenzhen
profile: Leaf Hua Li (b. 1977, Hunan University CS 2000) was Tencent's 18th employee, an early QQ developer and a founder of Tencent Video. He founded Futu in 2012, funding it partly by selling Tencent shares; its Futubull and moomoo trading apps are Nasdaq-listed (FUTU). Barred from signing new mainland users since 2022, Futu is expanding in the US, Singapore, Malaysia, Japan and beyond.
interesting_fact: He is named on 20+ Chinese and international patent applications from his Tencent years, where he also headed the multimedia business and innovation center.
deep_cut_fact: Futu's origin story is a mooncake: his broker once brought him one as thanks for roughly HK$5M in commissions he had paid that year — the first gift since he became a client in 2004 — and the lopsided deal convinced him to build a low-cost broker.
notes: Goes by 'Leaf'. Company PR/IR inboxes are published. Avoid the 2022 mainland regulatory crackdown as a topic. Moderate data-center relevance (heavy trading-infrastructure user).

name: David MacNeil
current_role: Founder, owner and CEO, WeatherTech (MacNeil Automotive Products), Bolingbrook, Illinois
profile: David MacNeil founded WeatherTech in 1989 and still owns 100% of it. The US-made auto-accessories and home-goods brand had about $800M in 2025 revenue. Trump nominated him to the FTC in Jan 2026; he was never confirmed, and a Nov 2026 MLex report says he withdrew. His vintage car collection is worth over $400M.
interesting_fact: His car collection includes a 1963 Ferrari 250 GTO, bought in 2018 for an estimated $75M and among the most expensive cars in the world. He is also a certified airline transport pilot who has flown to 39 countries.
deep_cut_fact: He started WeatherTech in 1989 by taking a second mortgage on his home and working out of his house, frustrated that 1980s floor mats were 'just these thin cheap rubber floor mats' that 'didn't do what a floor mat is supposed to do.'
notes: Known for Made-in-USA advocacy and Super Bowl ads; a GOP donor. FTC status: nominated Jan 2026; MLex (4 Nov 2026) reports the nomination withdrawn in favor of Chris Mufarrige (single source; avoid as a topic). No published press email found, and WeatherTech's site blocks automated fetches.

name: N. Murray Edwards
current_role: Executive Chairman, Canadian Natural Resources Ltd.; owner, Edco Financial Holdings; chairman/co-owner, Calgary Sports & Entertainment Corp. (Calgary Flames)
profile: Regina-born lawyer-turned-financier who built his fortune backing and running Canadian energy companies, above all oil-sands giant Canadian Natural Resources (executive chairman), plus Ensign Energy, Magellan Aerospace and Imperial Metals. He also leads the Calgary Flames ownership group and owns Resorts of the Canadian Rockies. He moved his residency from Calgary to London in 2016.
interesting_fact: In high school Edwards worked four nights a week as a hockey referee; he also worked on a garbage crew and had a summer job at a beer factory with unlimited beer on breaks.
deep_cut_fact: A keen investor as a student, Edwards rang the bell on Oct 3, 2002 to launch the 'N. Murray Edwards MarketWatch' stock-ticker board he donated to his alma mater's business school in Saskatoon, years before it was renamed the Edwards School of Business (2007).

public_contacts.value: https://www.cnrl.com/contact (Canadian Natural contact page incl. Investor Relations link)

notes: Very low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is likely via Canadian Natural's investor relations or the Edwards School of Business (USask), where he sits on the Dean's Advisory Council. Lives primarily in London (UK) since 2016.

name: Jiang Rensheng
current_role: Chairman and largest shareholder, Chongqing Zhifei Biological Products (Shenzhen-listed); controls Chongqing Genrix Biopharmaceutical (Shanghai-listed)
profile: Jiang Rensheng (蒋仁生, b. 1953, Guangxi), China's 'vaccine king', spent ~20 years in public epidemic prevention. He quit at about 46 to sell vaccines, and in 2002 bought a struggling Chongqing maker and renamed it Zhifei. Zhifei distributes Merck's HPV vaccine in China and partners with GSK; Jiang took Genrix public in 2023.
interesting_fact: Jiang is a classic late-blooming founder: he left a secure government job at about 46 to become a vaccine salesman in Chengdu, then started Zhifei in Chongqing at 49.
deep_cut_fact: At 17, with university exams suspended, he taught at his village school in Guangxi. He got into Guilin Medical College when the gaokao resumed in 1977. In Zhifei's cash-strapped early days he sold his own home and moved into the staff dormitory.
notes: Low international media profile; Chinese-language outreach recommended. His son Jiang Lingfeng is a Zhifei director and heir apparent. Zhifei's general office email is the only published channel; BD@zifibio.com is for business partnerships.

name: Todd Christopher
current_role: Founder of Vogue International (OGX, Maui Moisture); now a private investor based in Clearwater, Florida
profile: Todd Christopher, a high-school dropout and fourth-generation hairdresser, founded hair care company Vogue International in 1987, eventually building brands such as OGX and Maui Moisture. He sold a stake to Carlyle in 2014, and Johnson & Johnson bought the company for $3.3bn in 2016. He lives in Clearwater, Florida, and keeps a low public profile.
interesting_fact: Short on cash when he opened his first salon in his twenties, he slept in the salon to save money; he is one of very few high-school dropouts to make the Forbes 400.
deep_cut_fact: He got his start in hair care products in 1987 selling Pro-Vitamin hair-treatment capsules out of the trunk of his car, and has trademarked phrases such as 'Vitamin & Herbal Indulgence', 'Beach Bum Gear', 'Ego Trip' and 'Shampurity'.
notes: No current company role, official website or published contact channel found; Vogue International is now part of J&J's consumer spin-off Kenvue, which does not represent him. Common name - beware other Todd Christophers (e.g. a USC MBA/brewery co-founder is a different person). Very private.

name: James
profile: Most likely James K. 'J.K.' Irving, chairman of J.D. Irving Ltd. and brother of Arthur Irving (Irving Oil), with whom the Hurun 2014 entry is shared. He died on 21 June 2024, aged 96, in Saint John, New Brunswick. Record skipped per instructions.
notes: Entry gives only the first name 'James' (Irving Group, shared with Arthur Irving), so identity is inferred. J.K. Irving died 21 June 2024 (https://www.cbc.ca/1.7243426); Arthur Irving died in May 2024. If the entry meant J.K.'s son James D. 'Jim' Irving (co-CEO of J.D. Irving Ltd.), he is alive and would need separate research.

name: Alejandro Bulgheroni
current_role: Chairman, Pan American Energy Group (Argentina); owner of Bulgheroni family wine estates incl. Bodega Garzón (Uruguay)
profile: Argentine industrial engineer (b. 1943, Rufino) who joined his father's Bridas Corp. in 1965 and ran it with brother Carlos from 1985; sold 50% to CNOOC and in 2017 merged with BP's Argentine assets to form Pan American Energy Group, Argentina's largest private integrated energy firm. Lives in Uruguay; owns 10+ wineries worldwide and a large dairy complex.
interesting_fact: In 1992 he secured some of the first gas exploration concessions Turkmenistan granted to a foreign energy company. His Garzón wine club membership reportedly costs $200,000.
deep_cut_fact: His wine empire began as an energy idea: in 2006 he stood on a windy Uruguayan hilltop scouting a wind-farm site, advisers suggested vines instead, and when told quality would take 6-8 years he quipped, 'How old do you think I am?' (Wine Spectator, 2018).
notes: The PAE email is the company's general 'otras consultas' inbox, not a press desk. Son Marcos Bulgheroni is PAE Group CEO. The wine/energy angle (wind farm turned vineyard) is a natural hook.

name: Li Chunan
current_role: Chairman of Dalian Linton NC Machine Co. (Linton Technologies, BSE: 835368); cofounder and major shareholder of Longi Green Energy.
profile: Li Chunan (b. 1968, Nanyang, Henan) cofounded Longi Green Energy, one of the world's largest solar wafer and module makers, with Lanzhou University classmates Li Zhenguo and Zhong Baoshen. He also chairs Dalian-based Linton, which makes crystal-growing, wafer-slicing and other equipment for the solar and semiconductor industries.
interesting_fact: Longi's three cofounders were college friends from undergraduate days at Lanzhou University; Li studied in its physics department (entered 1986) and serves as a trustee of the Lanzhou University Education Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he was an inventor of magnetic separation gear: he holds a 1997 Chinese utility-model patent for a 'suspended permanent-magnet iron remover' (ZL97233990.6) and a 2010 invention patent for a circulating-oil-cooled electromagnetic iron remover, from his Fushun magnet-electric company days (cofounded 1993).
notes: IR email is the Linton board office contact (named staffer Jin Yao, tel 0411-62638881) published in an Aug 2025 shareholder-meeting notice. Deep-cut source is a user-contributed Chinese bio page (patent numbers are checkable on CNIPA). Avoid: 2024 CSRC Liaoning fine for insider-info leak.

name: April Goh
current_role: Fellow, Columbia University China Center for Social Policy (New York); Nippon Paint heir
profile: April Goh is a granddaughter of the late Singapore paints tycoon Goh Cheng Liang (d. August 2025), who partnered with Japan's Nippon Paint in 1962. In a 2025 transfer, six grandchildren received a combined 55% stake in Nippon Paint Holdings; she got the largest share, about US$3.4B, reportedly partly held for siblings. Voting control stays with her uncle Goh Hup Jin. She works in social policy, not the family business.
interesting_fact: Her grandfather broke with Asian convention by skipping a generation: he passed the bulk of his Nippon Paint fortune straight to his six grandchildren, making all of them billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: She formerly worked in finance and is now a fellow at Columbia University's China Center for Social Policy, focusing on gender-based violence. She was among the Goh family members who visited the patriarch's ancestral village in the Teochew region of Guangdong for a Chinese TV programme.
notes: A private, non-operating heir who declined to comment to Bloomberg; there are no business role or public channels. She is a poor fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast; recommend skipping or approaching only via academic channels if relevant.

name: Andrei Bokarev
current_role: Co-owner/partner in Iskander Makhmudov's holdings (UMMC, Transmashholding, Kuzbassrazrezugol, Ust-Luga Oil); stepped down from Transmashholding posts in April 2022
profile: Russian businessman and long-time partner of Iskander Makhmudov who ran Krutrade (coal exports for Kuzbassrazrezugol) and then chaired/led Transmashholding, Russia's largest rolling-stock and metro-car maker, until 2022. He co-owns stakes in Ural Mining Metallurgical Company and half of the Ust-Luga oil terminal.
interesting_fact: Transmashholding builds most of Russia's locomotives and Moscow metro trains; UMMC, in which he is a partner, spent $100M building the Shayba ice arena for the Sochi 2014 Olympics and handed it to the state afterwards.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK (Apr 2022), Australia, EU and US Treasury (Sept 2023); left Transmashholding roles due to sanctions. Not suitable for outreach; any contact could raise sanctions-compliance issues. No published contacts. Alive per 2025 sanctions-list updates.

name: Timur Kulibaev
current_role: Private investor; owner of Joint Resources holding and (with wife Dinara) majority shareholder of Halyk Bank; former chairman of KazEnergy (2005-2023) and Samruk-Kazyna
profile: Son-in-law of Kazakhstan's first president Nursultan Nazarbayev, he built a fortune in banking, telecoms, gold and oil and gas: sold Kar-Tel (2004) and Altynalmas Gold (2014) and, with his wife, controls Halyk Bank. Dubbed the 'oil prince', he sat on Gazprom's board 2011-22 and led KazEnergy until 2023; he has kept a low profile since 2022.
interesting_fact: He headed the Kazakhstan Boxing Federation from 2009 to 2024; in that period Kazakh boxers won gold, silver and bronze medals at both the 2012 London and 2016 Rio Olympics.
deep_cut_fact: After studying national economic planning at Moscow State University (1988), his first job was junior research assistant at the economics research institute of the Kazakh SSR's State Planning Committee; his 1999 PhD thesis was on enterprise management mechanisms in market conditions, using the oil industry as the example.
notes: Politically exposed person; extensive critical press (FT pipeline-contract reporting, offshore structures). Very private since 2022, no published personal or office contact found; Halyk Bank IR is the only corporate channel and does not represent him personally. Energy angle (Kazakh oil & gas) is strong but access is unlikely.

name: Igor Kesaev
current_role: Owner and President, Mercury Group (Megapolis tobacco distribution; retail)
profile: Igor Kesaev (b. 1966, Vladikavkaz; MGIMO graduate) founded Mercury in 1991 as a food and alcohol importer. Its Megapolis arm, co-founded with Sergei Katsiev, distributes ~70% of Russia's cigarettes; Philip Morris and JTI bought 40% of it in 2013 for $1.5B. In 2019 he merged his Dixy supermarkets with the Krasnoe & Beloe alcohol chain.
interesting_fact: He enjoys heli-skiing and mountain climbing.
notes: Sanctioned by the EU, UK (2022), Canada and the US (May 2023); Cyprus revoked his passport in 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Kesaev). Contacting or featuring him carries legal/reputational risk; recommend excluding from outreach. No published contacts collected.

name: Miguel Fluxa Rossello
current_role: Chairman and owner, Grupo Iberostar (Palma de Mallorca)
profile: Miquel/Miguel Fluxà Rosselló (b. 1938, Inca, Mallorca) is the third-generation heir of a Mallorcan shoemaking family who in 1986 opened the first Iberostar hotels and built the group into a global resort chain (~100 hotels). In 2006 he sold its tour-operator and travel-agency arms to Carlyle for $950M to focus on hotels. Daughters Sabina (vice chair & CEO) and Gloria (vice chair & CSO) now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: The family business dates to 1877, when his grandfather Antonio Fluxà set up a shoe workshop in Inca that within a decade had 11 workshops and five leather factories; his brother Lorenzo later founded the Camper shoe brand.
deep_cut_fact: After his father died in 1993, he led Iberostar's first international opening, in the Dominican Republic. He received the Gold Medal of the Balearic Islands in 2014 and in 2026 was named Mallorcadiario's 'Personaje del año' and awarded the Balearic College of Economists' Gold Medal.
notes: Age 88; low media profile. Iberostar's 'Wave of Change' ocean/coral program (led by daughter Gloria) is the group's signature sustainability story. 2026 awards: https://www.mallorcadiario.com/miguel-fluxa-personaje-mallorcadiario-2026 and https://www.mallorcadiario.com/miguel-fluxa-recibira-medalla-oro-colegio-economistas-baleares.

name: Pierre Chen Tai-Ming
current_role: Founder and Chairman, YAGEO Group (Taiwan, TWSE: 2327)
profile: Pierre Chen (Chen Tai-Ming) founded passive-component maker Yageo in Taipei in 1977. Through acquisitions such as KEMET and Pulse, it became one of the world's largest makers of resistors, capacitors and magnetics, components found in servers, EVs and data-center hardware. He also runs the YAGEO Foundation, which holds one of Asia's top contemporary-art collections.
interesting_fact: A mega-collector, he told Artnet in 2019 he owned seven Picassos, two Francis Bacons and ten Gerhard Richters. His YAGEO Foundation, set up in 1999, lent works to Tate's 'Capturing the Moment' and opened an art center in Taipei.
deep_cut_fact: He bought his first artworks in 1976, a year before founding Yageo. He has long planned a private museum in the Yangmingshan mountains outside Taipei.

public_contacts.value: IR@yageo.com (spokesperson Thomas Chang, Global Finance Senior Director)

notes: Hurun lists his country as China, but he is Taiwanese (Taipei). Also a renowned wine collector (Sotheby's 'Pierre Chen: An Epicurean Odyssey' sale). Data-center angle: Yageo/KEMET components are core to AI server power delivery. Best route: Yageo IR/spokesperson, or the YAGEO Foundation for art-related outreach.

name: Nikolai Buinov
current_role: Co-founder, chairman of the board and majority shareholder, Irkutsk Oil Company (INK)
profile: Krasnoyarsk-born (1967) founder of Irkutsk Oil Company, Russia's largest independent private oil producer. He started in timber, co-founded fuel supplier Bodaibo Energy with his father in 1995, bought his first oil licence in 1997, and in 2022 bought back Goldman Sachs' stake in INK. INK is now moving into petrochemicals with its Irkutsk Polymer Plant near Ust-Kut.
interesting_fact: In 2025 INK began launching the Irkutsk Polymer Plant near Ust-Kut, the first polymer plant in Eastern Siberia and the company's largest investment project.
deep_cut_fact: A transport-university graduate (St Petersburg, 1990), he financed the restoration of the historic Wawelberg Bank building on Nevsky Prospekt, a long-stalled St Petersburg project completed in 2021 and now operating as a hotel.
notes: Low public profile, based in Irkutsk. Best route is likely INK's press service via irkutskoil.ru (site unreachable from here, so no contact verified). Russian energy company; check sanctions exposure before outreach.

name: Rodger Riney
current_role: Founder of Scottrade (sold to TD Ameritrade 2017); philanthropist via the Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation (St. Louis); MMRF board member
profile: Rodger O. Riney (b. 1945) co-founded discount broker Scottrade in Scottsdale in 1980, after 1975 brokerage deregulation. He grew it in St. Louis to 3 million accounts and $170B in assets and sold it to TD Ameritrade for $4B in 2017. Since then he has given hundreds of millions to medical research, especially on blood cancers and neurodegenerative disease.
interesting_fact: After Scottrade launched online trading in 1996, its trade volume grew 15% a month, compounded, for 39 straight months. Fortune repeatedly named Scottrade one of its '100 Best Companies to Work For'.
deep_cut_fact: His grandparents got him into investing by giving him 10 shares of stock as a boy. He studied civil engineering (BS) and earned an MBA at the University of Missouri, and interned at Edward Jones before turning down an engineering job for a lower-paid role at a Missouri investment firm.
notes: Retired and private; no published personal, office or foundation contact found (rineyfoundation.org belongs to a different Riney family foundation). Possible routes are his Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation board role (themmrf.org) or Washington University in St. Louis, a major gift recipient.

name: Hu Baifan
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang NHU Co. (新和成, SZSE: 002001)
profile: Hu Baifan taught chemistry at a rural school before founding a school-run factory in Xinchang, Zhejiang in 1988 with money borrowed from fellow teachers. It grew into Zhejiang NHU, one of the world's largest makers of vitamins A and E, plus methionine, flavors and fragrances and new materials. He is chairman; his younger brother Hu Baishan is vice chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: NHU started as a school-run venture recycling waste alcohol in a rented workshop with borrowed money, no plant, workers or technology; it made a RMB 100k profit in its first year.
deep_cut_fact: While buying waste alcohol from a drug plant, a workshop director told him some pharma products sold for RMB 100k-2m a ton; that pushed him into high-value chemistry, and in 1991 his team developed ethoxymethylene, a norfloxacin intermediate, replacing imports - NHU's first national key new product.
notes: Low international media profile. Best route: NHU board office / IR (+86 575 86017157 is the company line in its sustainability report).

name: Otto Toto Sugiri
current_role: Cofounder and President Director (CEO), PT DCI Indonesia Tbk
profile: Indonesian tech pioneer (b. 1953, Bandung; RWTH Aachen grad) dubbed Indonesia's 'Bill Gates'. After running IT at Bank Bali from 1983 he founded Sigma Cipta Caraka (1989, now Telkomsigma) and cofounded Indonet (1994), Indonesia's first ISP. He has led DCI Indonesia, the country's largest data-center operator, which listed in 2021.
interesting_fact: DCI was the first data center in Southeast Asia to earn Uptime Institute's Tier IV Certification of Constructed Facility (2020); he was EY World Entrepreneur of the Year Indonesia 2023.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999 he founded Balicamp (PT Sigma Karya Sempurna), an export-oriented software development campus in Pacung village, Bali, meant to let young Indonesian programmers compete internationally.
notes: Received Bintang Jasa Utama from President Jokowi (Aug 2024). Several Bank Bali colleagues (e.g. Marina Budiman) are his long-time cofounders. Low-profile; route via DCI corporate secretary.

name: Sid Bass
current_role: Private investor, Fort Worth, Texas (Bass family oil and investment fortune)
profile: Sid Richardson Bass (b. 1942; Yale, Stanford GSB) took charge of the Fort Worth family oil fortune of great-uncle Sid W. Richardson and father Perry Bass in the late 1960s, growing a ~$50m company into a multibillion-dollar investment group. Now a low-profile private investor and arts philanthropist.
interesting_fact: He and the Bass family were the largest shareholders in The Walt Disney Company from 1984, backing the arrival of Michael Eisner's management team; his 2006 $25m gift to the Metropolitan Opera was then the largest individual gift in its history.
deep_cut_fact: In 1970, at about 27, he recruited his Stanford business-school classmate Richard Rainwater (then 26, at Goldman Sachs) to manage the Bass family investments - a partnership that ran until 1986 and made Rainwater one of the era's legendary dealmakers.
notes: Extremely private; no published office/press contact found. Only realistic route is via Fort Worth institutions he supports or a warm intro. Net worth ~$3.9-4.6bn.

name: Thomas Siebel
current_role: Chairman and CEO, C3 AI (NYSE: AI); resumed the CEO role in May 2026
profile: Chicago-born Tom Siebel was an Oracle executive, then founded CRM pioneer Siebel Systems, which Oracle bought for $5.8bn in 2006. In 2009 he founded C3 AI (originally C3 Energy), an enterprise-AI software company that started out serving utilities. He stepped back to executive chairman in 2025 and returned as CEO in May 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he set up a C3 AI programme that pays for employees to earn the University of Illinois online Master of Computer Science. Graduates get a 15% raise, a $25,000 bonus and extra stock options.
deep_cut_fact: Before he had a computer-science degree he earned a BA in history at Illinois, and he later endowed a Thomas M. Siebel Chair in the History of Science there. In 2015 his foundation launched the Siebel Energy Institute to fund research on managing power-grid data.
notes: A natural fit for an energy/AI podcast: C3 started as C3 Energy, serving utilities, and he wrote the book 'Digital Transformation' (2019). He stepped back from the CEO role in 2025 for health reasons and returned in May 2026; don't raise health in outreach. He also founded the Montana Meth Project and the Siebel Scholars programme.

name: Yang Yazhen

name: Laurence Graff
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Graff Diamonds (son François Graff is CEO)
profile: Laurence Graff OBE (b. 1938, Stepney, London) left school at 14 for a jewellery apprenticeship in Hatton Garden. He founded Graff Diamonds in 1960 and built it into a vertically integrated top-end diamond jeweller with 60+ stores, serving clients from the Sultan of Brunei to Hollywood. He also owns the Delaire Graff wine estate in Stellenbosch, has a major modern-art collection, and lives in Gstaad.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he paid £16.4M for the historic Wittelsbach Diamond and had it recut from 35.52 to about 31 carats to improve its clarity. The stone is now known as the Wittelsbach-Graff.
deep_cut_fact: His first big break came in 1966, when he commissioned designer Robert Thomas to create a diamond ribbon bracelet for De Beers' Diamond International Awards, and it won. By 1962 he already had two shops, including his first in Hatton Garden, where he had started out scrubbing toilets as an apprentice.
notes: No published press email was found on graff.com (only client-services and data-protection addresses). Use the Press Room / client contact on graff.com, or approach via the Delaire Graff Estate. He is 88, gives rare interviews, and is a weak fit for energy/data-center topics.

name: Theodore Leonsis
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Monumental Sports & Entertainment (Capitals, Wizards, Mystics, Capital One Arena); partner, Revolution Growth
profile: Brooklyn-born (1957) grandson of Greek immigrant mill workers and first in his family at university (Georgetown '77). He sold Redgate Communications to AOL in 1994, spent ~14 years as an AOL senior executive, then bought the Capitals (1999) and Wizards (2010) and built Monumental, now rebuilding Capital One Arena in downtown DC.
interesting_fact: Under his ownership the Capitals won the 2018 Stanley Cup; he also founded documentary platform SnagFilms and is a partner at Steve Case's Revolution Growth VC fund.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Harris Corp. in March 1981 he started LIST ('Leonsis Index to Software Technology'), one of the early magazines covering personal-computer software; earlier he did corporate communications at Wang Laboratories in his hometown of Lowell, Mass.

public_contacts.value: cbrowne@monumentalsports.com (Christopher Browne, MSE media contact as of Jan 2025)

notes: Very accessible, writes a long-running blog and is active on social media; author of 'The Business of Happiness'. Good entrepreneurship guest. Media contact email dates from Jan 2025 — check a recent MSE release before using.

name: George Bishop
current_role: Founder & Chairman/CEO, GeoSouthern Energy (The Woodlands, Texas)
profile: Mississippi-born petroleum geologist (MSU 1958) who founded GeoSouthern Energy in 1981 and became a billionaire when it sold its early Eagle Ford acreage to Devon for $6B in 2013. He redeployed into Haynesville gas via JVs with Blackstone Credit (sold 2021, $1.85B) and Williams (GEP Haynesville II, which sold a majority interest in its South Mansfield assets to Japan's JERA in Oct 2025).
interesting_fact: He and wife Kathy gave Mississippi State University $100 million in 2023 for scholarships, the largest gift to a higher-education institution in Mississippi's history.
deep_cut_fact: Received an honorary Doctor of Public Service from MSU in May 2019. On his giving he said: 'Mississippi State opened many doors for me... I especially want to help students that have the desire to work but don't have the funds.' He also owns the Eagleford Restaurant in Cuero, Texas, near his ranch.
notes: Born 1937 (about 89). Extremely private; GeoSouthern's website (geosouthern.com) is a placeholder with no contact info. Possible warm route via Mississippi State University Foundation, where he is a major donor and former board member. Kirkland & Ellis advised GEP Haynesville II on the 2025 JERA deal.

name: Carl Thoma
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Thoma Bravo (software-focused private equity, Chicago/San Francisco); co-founder, Carl & Marilynn Thoma Foundation
profile: Carl Thoma is one of the deans of private equity: he started at First Chicago Equity Group, co-founded Golder Thoma (later GTCR) in 1980, formed Thoma Cressey in 1998 where he hired Orlando Bravo, and split off Thoma Bravo in 2008. Pioneering the 'buy-and-build' strategy, Thoma Bravo has become one of the largest software investors, managing well over $180 billion.
interesting_fact: The Thoma Foundation's art collection spans Art of the Spanish Americas, digital and media art, Japanese bamboo baskets and post-war painting, shown at its own spaces in Santa Fe and Dallas and loaned to museums; the couple also run a vineyard in Oregon's Willamette Valley.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up on a cattle ranch in Cimarron County in the Oklahoma Panhandle and earned an agricultural economics degree from Oklahoma State in 1971 before a Stanford MBA; in 2024 the foundation created the Thoma Scholars Program at OSU for students from rural areas, and OSU's ag college named him a distinguished alumnus.
notes: Low-key; Orlando Bravo is the firm's public face. Rural-scholarship and art philanthropy are warm outreach hooks. Cimarron County detail from OSU scholarship story https://stories.okstate.edu/content/2024/carl_and_marilynn_thoma_foundation_create_life-changing_scholarship_program_at_osu (search-snippet confirmed; pages blocked direct fetch).

name: Yeow Chor
current_role: Group Managing Director and Chief Executive, IOI Corporation Berhad (Malaysia); Chairman, Malaysian Palm Oil Association
profile: Dato' Lee Yeow Chor (King's College London LLB, Gray's Inn barrister) leads IOI Corporation, the palm-oil plantation and oleochemicals group built by his late father Tan Sri Lee Shin Cheng. He joined IOI as a general manager in 1994 and has been group MD/CEO since 2019. Forbes lists him jointly with his brother Lee Yeow Seng, who runs sister company IOI Properties.
interesting_fact: He chaired the Malaysian Palm Oil Council from 2009 to 2020, has chaired the Malaysian Palm Oil Association since 2020, and sat on the board of Bank Negara Malaysia (the central bank) from 2015 to 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he spent four years (1990-94) in Malaysia's Attorney General's Chambers and the judiciary, and his last posting was as a magistrate.
notes: Dataset name 'Yeow Chor' = Lee Yeow Chor (shared Forbes entry with brother Lee Yeow Seng). Has given media interviews (e.g., CNBC Managing Asia, Apr 2024: https://www.ioigroup.com/news/cnbcs-managing-asia-interview-with-dato-lee-yeow-chor). IOI corporate communications is the best route.

name: Lynn Schusterman
current_role: Co-Founder and Chair Emerita, Charles and Lynn Schusterman Family Philanthropies (Tulsa)
profile: Tulsa philanthropist (b. 1939, Kansas City) whose fortune comes from Samson Resources, the oil & gas firm her late husband Charles founded in 1971; most assets were sold to a KKR-led group for $7.2B in 2011, with some oil & gas holdings kept in Samson Energy. She led the family foundation 2000-2018 and is now chair emerita; the family has given away $3.5B+.
interesting_fact: She and Stacy Schusterman (the foundation's current chair) received the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy in 2022 (alongside Dolly Parton), and in 2026 both were named to the TIME100 Philanthropy list.
deep_cut_fact: She began volunteering with the National Council of Jewish Women in the early 1960s; after Charles died in 2000 she became the first woman to lead a large Jewish philanthropic organization, and in 1994 she helped found Hillel in the former Soviet Union.
notes: Aged 87; energy link is legacy (Samson Resources/Samson Energy). Best route is the foundation's media inbox. Hillel-FSU detail is cited on her Wikipedia page (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn_Schusterman); NCJW/first-woman details from JWA. Spoke at ROI's final summit in Jerusalem, June 2026.

name: Albrecht Woeste
current_role: Honorary Chairman of the Henkel Group (since 2009); Henkel family shareholder
profile: Albrecht Woeste (b. Oct 30, 1935, Düsseldorf), a great-grandson of founder Fritz Henkel and a trained engineer (Dipl.-Ing.), ran his father's Düsseldorf firm R. Woeste & Co. before chairing both Henkel's Supervisory Board and Shareholders' Committee from 1990 to 2009, handing over to Simone Bagel-Trah. His wealth comes from the family's controlling stake in Henkel (Persil, Schwarzkopf, Loctite).
interesting_fact: He was president of the Düsseldorf Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) 1991–1999 and remains its honorary president; Düsseldorf made him an honorary citizen in 2015, and the IHK marked his 90th birthday in October 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A horse-racing devotee, he has been president of Germany's thoroughbred breeding and racing authority (Direktorium für Vollblutzucht und Rennen) since 2009 and vice-president of the Düsseldorf Riding and Racing Club; he also sits on Fortuna Düsseldorf's supervisory board (per his 2015 Henkel CV).
notes: Aged 91; alive as of the IHK's Oct-2025 90th-birthday release, and no death notice found by Nov 2026. The racing/Fortuna roles are from a 2015 CV and may have changed. Very low public profile; Henkel corporate comms is the only published route.
