name: Chey Tae-won
current_role: Chairman, SK Group (SK Inc.); Chairman, Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry
profile: Has chaired SK Group since 1998. SK is one of Korea's largest conglomerates, spanning energy and refining (SK Innovation), telecom (SK Telecom) and memory chips (SK Hynix, a key HBM supplier for AI data centers). name: Liu Jincheng
current_role: Founder and chairman, EVE Energy (亿纬锂能, Shenzhen-listed 300014), Huizhou

BMW Neue Klasse cylindrical cells) and storage batteries, ranked No. 2 in energy-storage cell shipments in 2025, and now pitches itself as an 'energy base for the AI world'.

name: Ray Davis

current_role: Chairman and CEO, MetaX Integrated Circuits (Shanghai) Co. (SSE STAR: 688802)

profile: London property billionaire who has run the family's privately held William Pears Group, founded in 1952 by his grandfather Bernard and father Clive, since his father's death in 1984 when he was 21. profile: Shanghai-born, UC Berkeley CS grad Weili Dai co-founded Marvell Technology with Sehat Sutardja in 1995 and served as its president until 2016. Based in Las Vegas, she now invests in tech and real estate and has co-founded several startups, including AI firm MeetKai (2018) and Silicon Box (2021), which runs a ~$2B chiplet-packaging fab in Singapore aimed at AI customers.

current_role: Group Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Shun Tak Holdings; co-chairperson, MGM China Holdings
profile: Daughter of the late Macau gaming magnate Stanley Ho, Pansy Ho runs Shun Tak Holdings (property, hotels and the Hong Kong-Macau TurboJET ferries) and holds stakes in MGM China and SJM Holdings. She made more than $1.5bn from MGM China's 2011 IPO and is now a prominent global tourism advocate, serving as a UN Tourism Ambassador.

name: Angela Bennett
current_role: Head of Wright Prospecting; principal of AMB Holdings (family investment company), Perth
profile: Australian iron-ore heiress whose wealth comes from Wright Prospecting's share of the Rio Tinto royalty negotiated by her father Peter Wright with Lang Hancock. Son Todd runs AMB Holdings.

name: Brendan Foody
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mercor (San Francisco)
profile: In 2023 Brendan Foody cofounded Mercor with two Bellarmine high school friends, Adarsh Hiremath and Surya Midha. The company supplies expert contractors who help the big AI labs train and evaluate their models. A $10B valuation in October 2025 made the three of them the world's youngest self-made billionaires at 22. Mercor reported $500M in annualized revenue in September 2025.

current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Mercor (stepped back from COO role Oct 2025)
profile: San Jose-raised son of immigrants from New Delhi; left Georgetown's School of Foreign Service in 2023 to co-found Mercor with high-school friends Brendan Foody and Adarsh Hiremath. Mercor pays domain experts to train frontier AI models; its 2025-26 rounds ($10B then ~$20B valuation) made the trio the youngest self-made billionaires. Thiel Fellow (2024).
interesting_fact: Forbes named Midha, Foody and Hiremath (all 22) the world's youngest self-made billionaires in late 2025, younger than Zuckerberg was on his list debut; Midha is the youngest of the three.
deep_cut_fact: With partner Adarsh Hiremath he was on the first team ever to win all three national policy-debate titles (TOC, NDCA, NSDA), and was top speaker at TOC and NDCA; he was Bellarmine salutatorian (2021) and later interned for Eswar Prasad at Brookings. Lists F1, tea and Halloween as loves.
notes: Unusually accessible: publishes his personal Gmail on his own site (obfuscated as 'suryamidha [at] gmail [dot] com'). Good AI/data-labor angle for the podcast. Company X: @mercor.

name: Reimann family
current_role: Family owners of JAB Holding Company (Luxembourg-based investment vehicle; stakes in Keurig Dr Pepper, Coty, Peet's, Krispy Kreme, Panera etc.)
profile: German family descended from chemist Ludwig Reimann, who joined Johann Adam Benckiser's chemicals firm in the 1820s and married into the founding family. Albert Reimann Jr. expanded into consumer goods; the business became Reckitt Benckiser, and four of his adopted children own most of JAB, run by professional partners.
interesting_fact: JAB takes its name from the initials of Johann Adam Benckiser, the founder of the 19th-century chemicals firm the family inherited.
notes: Family entry listed only on Forbes 1996-2000, so it's unclear which members are meant. Very private family; JAB says it is run by professional partners. Best route is JAB's corporate contact form. Avoid the Nazi-era history unless relevant.

name: Ronald Owen Perelman
current_role: Chairman & CEO, MacAndrews & Forbes Incorporated (New York); Chairman of Carnegie Hall since 2015
profile: Wharton-trained financier who built MacAndrews & Forbes, his wholly owned holding company, through leveraged buyouts from 1978 on, most famously Revlon; holdings have included Deluxe/Vericast, SIGA Technologies and Scientific Games. Since 2020 he has sold assets and the firm reportedly now operates more like a family office.
interesting_fact: He has been chairman of Carnegie Hall since May 2015 and gave $75 million toward the performing arts center at the World Trade Center site, which bears his name.
deep_cut_fact: His first big deal came in 1961 as a Wharton freshman: with his father he bought Philadelphia's Esslinger Brewery for $800,000 and sold it three years later for a $1 million profit. By age 11 he was regularly sitting in on his father's Belmont Iron Works board meetings.
notes: Net worth fell sharply since 2018 peak; avoid wealth/litigation topics. Best route is MacAndrews & Forbes contact form. Carnegie Hall connection is a warm, positive angle.

name: Clemmie Spangler, Jr.
notes: C.D. 'Dick' Spangler Jr., Charlotte businessman (Spangler Companies, investments) and former UNC System president (1986-1997), died July 22, 2018 at age 86. Source: https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2018/07/harvard-business-school-alum-benefactor-c-d-dick-spangler-dies-at-86 ; https://www.wfae.org/local-news/2018-07-23/charlotte-businessman-former-unc-president-c-d-spangler-jr-dies-at-86

name: Lin Rong San
profile: Taiwanese real estate developer, founder of Union Bank of Taiwan and of the Liberty Times newspaper group (incl. Taipei Times). Died 28 Nov 2015 in Taipei, aged 76.
notes: Deceased (2015) per Focus Taiwan obituary https://focustaiwan.tw/news/201511280016 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin_Rong-San. Any current Forbes listing likely reflects heirs/family; skipped rest per instructions.

name: Ernesto And Fabio Bertarelli
current_role: Ernesto Bertarelli: head of B-FLEXION (formerly Waypoint Capital), Geneva; co-chair, Bertarelli Foundation
profile: 1997 Forbes entry for father and son behind Swiss biotech Serono. Fabio Bertarelli died in 1998; son Ernesto (b. 1965) ran Serono from 1996, shifted it to biotech and sold it to Merck KGaA in 2007 for $13.3bn. He now invests the family fortune via B-FLEXION and co-chairs the Bertarelli Foundation with sister Dona.
interesting_fact: Ernesto founded sailing team Alinghi, which won the America's Cup in 2003 on its first attempt, bringing the Cup to Europe for the first time; he was the team's only Swiss national, serving as navigator.
deep_cut_fact: The name Alinghi comes from the Bertarelli family boats that raced around Porto Santo Stefano and Porto Ercole on Monte Argentario, where Ernesto spent his youth sailing.
notes: Fabio Bertarelli (the father) died in 1998, so alive=unknown covers the pair: Ernesto is alive, Fabio is not. Profile focuses on Ernesto. The family site lists no published email. Best route is probably B-FLEXION in Geneva or the Bertarelli Foundation, whose marine-conservation work has protected over 3m km2 of ocean since 2010.

name: Michael Schmidt-Ruthenbeck Bros.
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Rainer) of the family stake in retailer Metro AG, held via the Meridian Stiftung structure
profile: Michael Schmidt-Ruthenbeck (b. 1942) and his brother Rainer are sons of Wilhelm Schmidt-Ruthenbeck, who co-founded the German cash-and-carry wholesaler Metro in 1963/64. The family has held a large minority stake in Metro AG (about 16% around 2011), controlled through the Meridian Foundation vehicle, and is based in Duisburg. Listing is a combined entry for the brothers.
interesting_fact: The Schmidt-Ruthenbeck family holding was a key swing shareholder during Czech investor Daniel Kretinsky's 2019-2020 push for control of Metro AG.
deep_cut_fact: The Karl Schmidt family of Duisburg merchants founded Stiftung Mercator in 1996 and named it after the cartographer Gerhard Mercator, who lived in Duisburg for decades; it is now one of Germany's largest private foundations, with a climate-resilient-society programme.
notes: Very private family; no personal web/social presence found. No death reported, but no recent public appearance found either (born 1942). The only institutional route is the family's Stiftung Mercator (Essen), which is not a personal office. Forbes entry dates from 1997.

name: Rain
current_role: Likely Rainer (Reiner) Schmidt-Ruthenbeck, co-owner with brother Michael of the family's Metro AG stake
profile: Entry appears to be a truncated 'Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck' (Germany, listed jointly with brother Michael). Born 1941, son of Metro co-founder Wilhelm Schmidt-Ruthenbeck; the brothers' family holding owned roughly 13-16% of German retailer Metro AG. Lives in Duisburg; keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: Forbes ranked Michael and Reiner Schmidt-Ruthenbeck jointly at #722 on its 2016 billionaires list with US$2.4 billion.
deep_cut_fact: His family (the Karl Schmidt family of Duisburg merchants) set up Stiftung Mercator in 1996, one of Germany's largest private foundations, named after the cartographer Gerhard Mercator, who lived in Duisburg for decades.
notes: Identity inferred: input name 'Rain' with shared_with 'Schmidt-Ruthenbeck Bros., Michael' (Forbes 1997) most likely = Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck. Extremely private; no personal channels. The only route is via the family foundation (Stiftung Mercator), and it is indirect.

name: Thomas M Siebel
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, C3.ai (CEO until Sept 2025)
profile: Tom Siebel, an Oracle sales executive in the 1980s, founded CRM pioneer Siebel Systems in 1993 and sold it to Oracle for ~$5.8B in 2006. He founded enterprise-AI software firm C3.ai (originally C3 Energy, focused on smart-grid analytics), was CEO 2011-2025 and handed the CEO role to Stephen Ehikian in Sept 2025, remaining executive chairman.
interesting_fact: C3.ai began life in 2009 as C3 Energy, building analytics for utilities and the power grid -- a direct tie-in to an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 his Thomas and Stacey Siebel Foundation started the Montana Meth Project, a graphic teen-prevention ad campaign; he testified about it to the U.S. Senate Finance Committee in Sept 2007, and Montana teen meth use reportedly fell 63% over four years.
notes: Stepped back from CEO role in 2025; still executive chairman. Siebel Energy Institute and Siebel Scholars are relevant to energy/data themes. Best route is via C3.ai PR.

name: William R. Berkley Jr
current_role: President & CEO (and, since June 2026, Chairman) of W. R. Berkley Corporation
profile: W. Robert Berkley Jr. is the son of William R. Berkley, who founded commercial insurer W. R. Berkley Corp. in 1967 with $2,500 while studying for his Harvard MBA. The son joined the company in 1997, became President & CEO in 2015 (per Wikipedia), and was named chairman after his father died in June 2026.
interesting_fact: W. R. Berkley was founded in 1967 with $2,500 while the elder Berkley was an MBA student at Harvard; it grew into one of the largest US commercial lines insurers.
notes: IDENTITY: the Hurun $4.2B entry most likely reflects the founder William R. Berkley (not Jr.), who DIED in June 2026 aged 80 (source above). This record describes the living son W. Robert Berkley Jr. IR contact per company releases: Karen A. Horvath, VP External Financial Communications, (203) 629-3000 (corporate line); no published email found.

name: Johan H. Andresen
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Ferd AS (Oslo)
profile: Fifth-generation head of the Andresen family business (Tiedemanns tobacco, bought 1849), which he renamed Ferd in 2001 and turned into a Nordic investment group (Elopak, Aibel, Swix, real estate, funds). CEO 1998-2012, chairman since 2012; in 2007 he passed most shares to daughters Katharina and Alexandra, and in Dec 2023 said his A-shares will go to a Ferd Foundation.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he bid about NOK 11 billion for Swiss packaging maker SIG to merge it with Elopak, which would have made the world's No. 2 packaging group; he dropped the bid in 2007 after a bidding war.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he worked as a product manager at International Paper in the US (1989-91). In 2009 he founded Ferd Social Entrepreneurs, and he helped launch the Norwegian Microfinance Initiative (2008). He has also chaired the Council on Ethics for Norway's Government Pension Fund Global.
notes: Dropped the 'Jr.' from his name after his father died in 2011. Ferd's 2023 annual report lists Ferd JHA AS (100% his) as a shareholder alongside his daughters' holding companies. For an energy angle, Ferd co-owns the oil-services firm Aibel.

name: Rodger O. Riney
current_role: Founder of Scottrade (sold to TD Ameritrade 2017); trustee, Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation; family office Lightchain Capital (St. Louis)
profile: Riney founded Scottsdale Securities in Scottsdale, Arizona in 1980 after brokerage commissions were deregulated, moved it to St. Louis and built it into discount broker Scottrade, sold to TD Ameritrade in 2017. He now focuses on philanthropy via his foundation and investing via family office Lightchain.
interesting_fact: After Scottrade launched online trading in 1996, its trade volume grew about 15% per month, compounded, for 39 straight months.
deep_cut_fact: His grandparents got him into the stock market by giving him 10 shares of a stock; he went on to earn a civil engineering degree and an MBA at the University of Missouri and interned at Edward Jones.

public_contacts.note: published on foundation site for Managing Director Bobby W. Sandage Jr.

notes: Low public profile. Foundation is focused on medical research grants and funds by invitation only; best route is via the foundation's Managing Director. Wikipedia says born 1945 (category says 1946).

name: J.B. Pritzker
current_role: Governor of Illinois (re-elected to a third term on Nov 3, 2026)
profile: Hyatt hotel-fortune heir who co-founded Pritzker Group (private equity/venture) with brother Anthony and ran it until 2017. Elected Illinois governor in 2018, re-elected 2022 and won a rare third term in Nov 2026, beating Darren Bailey again; widely discussed as a possible 2028 presidential candidate.
interesting_fact: He is the first Democrat elected to three terms as Illinois governor and the first governor of either party to win a third term since Jim Thompson in the 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: Before politics he founded 1871 (2012), the Merchandise Mart startup incubator run by the Chicagoland Entrepreneurial Center and named for the rebuilding after the 1871 Chicago Fire; it was later ranked the world's top private business incubator (UBI Global, 2019).

public_contacts.value: alex.gough@illinois.gov (Press Secretary, Office of the Governor)

notes: Sitting governor; podcast requests best via the governor's scheduling-request form or press office. Strong fit for entrepreneurship angle (1871, Pritzker Group VC) and Illinois data-center/energy policy.

name: Julia Thiele-Schuerhoff
current_role: Member of the Supervisory Board, Knorr-Bremse AG; Chair of the Executive Board, Knorr-Bremse Global Care e.V.
profile: German lawyer and heiress of Heinz Hermann Thiele (d. 2021), who built rail/truck braking maker Knorr-Bremse and held stakes in Vossloh and Lufthansa. She has sat on Knorr-Bremse's supervisory board since 2016 and leads the company-affiliated charity Knorr-Bremse Global Care.
interesting_fact: She cofounded Knorr-Bremse Global Care in 2005 after the Indian Ocean tsunami; it funds partner projects worldwide in education, emergency relief and water/sanitation/hygiene.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the board she worked inside the company as a lawyer: an LMU Munich law graduate, she was a Knorr-Bremse in-house legal adviser from 2002 to 2008. Before the 2018 Frankfurt IPO, she and her father were Knorr-Bremse's sole owners.
notes: The Thiele family has long avoided publicity. The best route is Knorr-Bremse corporate communications (those contacts are for journalists only), or via Knorr-Bremse Global Care.

name: Phillip T. (Terry) Ragon
current_role: Founder, CEO and sole owner, InterSystems Corporation (Cambridge, MA)
profile: Terry Ragon, an MIT physics graduate, founded data-platform software company InterSystems in 1978; it still is wholly owned by him and has around $1B in annual sales, serving hospitals, banks and government health systems. With his wife Susan he funds the Ragon Institute of MGH, MIT and Harvard, endowed with a $200M gift in 2019, which works on HIV and other vaccines.
interesting_fact: After a 2009 trip to South Africa where they saw the toll of AIDS, Terry and Susan Ragon set up the Ragon Institute to pursue an HIV vaccine; they joined the Giving Pledge in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He got his first programming job at Meditech, an early electronic medical records company, after admitting in the interview, 'I really don't know much about computers... But I play guitar.' There he learned MUMPS, the hospital programming language InterSystems was later built on.
notes: Very low-profile; rarely gives interviews (the 2024 Forbes piece was described as a rare one). Best route is InterSystems PR. The Ragon Institute (ragoninstitute.org) is another angle.

name: Chao Chung-Hsin
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Jentech Precision Industrial Co., Ltd. (Taiwan, TPEx: 3653)
profile: Chao Chung-Hsin (also romanised Tsung-Hsin Chao) founded Jentech Precision with his younger brother Yung-Tsang in 1987 after learning mold-making on factory floors. Jentech grew from molds into heat spreaders, vapor-chamber lids and liquid-cooling modules for chips and AI servers, which drove its stock and his fortune; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: A high school dropout, he picked up industrial molding techniques by working in factories and started his own module business in 1978; Jentech's lids and liquid cooling now sit inside AI-server supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: His first company (1978) made molds for car audio systems, then a fast-growing Taiwanese sector; he studied at Hsin Chuang Senior High School and has been named one of Harvard Business Review's Top 100 Taiwan business leaders.
notes: Low-profile Taiwanese industrialist; little English-language press. Name appears as Chao Chung-Hsin (company site/Forbes) and Tsung-Hsin Chao (exchange filings). Best route is Jentech IR. Strong data-center angle (AI chip thermal management).

name: N.R. Narayana Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; principal of family office Catamaran Ventures
profile: Co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues and Rs 10,000 from his wife Sudha; CEO 1981-2002, chairman to 2011, briefly returned 2013-14. Still a minority Infosys shareholder; his family office Catamaran (est. ~2009) invests in startups and, increasingly, manufacturing, AI and data-centre-related opportunities.
interesting_fact: He says being arrested and expelled in 1974 at a border town near the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border while hitchhiking through Europe turned him from a 'confused leftist' into a 'compassionate capitalist'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and wrote a BASIC interpreter for ECIL; his first company, Softronics, folded after about 18 months before he joined Patni Computer Systems.
notes: Family office Catamaran (run by ex-Infosys CFO MD Ranganath and president Deepak Padaki) publishes an office address in Bengaluru but no email; Catamaran's 2025 thesis includes AI, data centres and precision manufacturing - relevant hook for an energy/data-center podcast. Frequently gives interviews/speeches in India.

name: Tu Huilong
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Haiya Group (Shenzhen) and Hong Kong Haiya Investment Ltd
profile: Tu Huilong (涂辉龙) heads Shenzhen-based Haiya Group, a private conglomerate in commercial real estate, shopping malls/department stores, urban complexes, cultural tourism, finance and hotels, with 42 subsidiaries and 38,000+ staff. A Hong Kong JP and long-serving CPPCC National Committee member (11th-14th).
interesting_fact: His flagship Haiya Mega Mall in Bao'an was western Shenzhen's first large commercial complex (~300,000 sqm, opened 2013) and hosted the world's first Burberry new-concept store.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2020 Two Sessions he proposed amending China's Property Law so residential, commercial and industrial land-use rights renew automatically, and pushed for Shenzhen-Zhongshan integration across the Pearl River Estuary.
notes: Low English-language profile; mostly covered in Chinese media. Also chairs the Hong Kong Federation of Guangdong Community Organisations-type bodies (香港广东社团首席会长) and sits on CUHK-Shenzhen board — HK civic channels may be a route. No published personal email found.

name: Yuan Jiangtao
current_role: Co-founder, Director and General Manager, Shenzhen JLC Technology Group (JLC/JLCPCB, SZSE: 001232)
profile: Jiangxi-born (Duchang, Jiujiang) electronics engineer who in 2006 founded the predecessor of JLC, pioneering cheap, fast PCB prototyping for small orders; he added the LCSC components marketplace in 2012 and merged with the Ding brothers' volume-PCB business in 2021. JLC listed on the Shenzhen main board in Aug 2026; he is its largest shareholder (~35%).
interesting_fact: JLC is nicknamed 'cyber bodhisattva' by Chinese engineers and students for its cheap PCB prototyping and its in-house EDA software (LCEDA/EasyEDA), whose core features are permanently free.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding JLC he spent five years as an electronics design engineer at an industrial drone company; in Nov 2006, aged 27 and with about RMB 100,000 in savings, he started out of a shared counter less than one metre wide in Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei electronics market.
notes: Chairman is Ding Hui; Yuan is GM. Nanchang University junior-college (dazhuan) graduate in mechatronics, 2000. JLC is known globally as JLCPCB/LCSC/EasyEDA, which is a good hook for data-center hardware. IR email is from the 2026 interim report summary.

name: Jeffrey Cheah
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sunway Group; Founder and Chancellor, Sunway University; Founder and Trustee, Jeffrey Cheah Foundation
profile: Malaysian tycoon who in 1974 left a job as an accountant at an auto assembly plant to buy a near-mined-out tin-mining company, then turned the land into Sunway City. Sunway now spans property, healthcare (Sunway Healthcare IPO'd in March 2026), construction, education and more; his children Sarena, Adrian and Evan work in the group.
interesting_fact: His Jeffrey Cheah Foundation, which owns Sunway University, is on track to award more than RM1 billion in scholarships and grants by 2026 - the largest such education foundation in Malaysia.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Pusing, a small tin-mining town in Perak about 200 km north of Kuala Lumpur; seeing the scarred mining land there shaped his idea to rehabilitate the ex-mine that became Sunway City. He also co-chairs Mission 4.7, a UN SDSN education-for-sustainability initiative.
notes: Go through Sunway Group Corporate Communications (media form). Sunway warns of impersonation scams - only use official sunway.com.my channels. Sunway hosts annual media nights and is press-friendly; energy/infrastructure angle via Sunway's autonomous transport and electric aviation plans (Oct 2026).

name: Ursula Bechtolsheimer-Kipp
current_role: Chairwoman (board president), Tschuggen Hotel Group / Tschuggen Collection (since 2016; current status not reconfirmed)
profile: German-born heiress (b. 1951), only daughter of Karl-Heinz Kipp, founder of the Massa department-store chain whose real estate was leased to Metro. She inherited much of his fortune in 2017 and chairs the family's Swiss luxury hotel group (Tschuggen Grand & Valsana Arosa, Carlton St. Moritz, Eden Roc Ascona). Lived for decades in Gloucestershire, running a horse breeding centre; now reported resident in Switzerland.
interesting_fact: The family fortune began with 500 bottles of rare wine her father sold on the post-war black market; her daughter is Olympic dressage gold medallist Laura Tomlinson.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016, alongside taking the Tschuggen chair from her 92-year-old father, she also became chair of Swiss property company Gassmann Immobilien- und Beteiligungs-AG and backed the Massa Nova project in Chur with her son Götz (per Bilanz).

public_contacts.value: c.maerzheuser@tschuggencollection.ch (Constanze Märzheuser, Director of PR, Tschuggen Collection)

notes: Very private; no personal social accounts found. Best route is the Tschuggen Collection PR director. Husband Wilfried died 2020 (avoid). Was dropped from Forbes real-time list after 2021.

name: Pat Stryker
current_role: Founder and president, Bohemian Foundation (Fort Collins, Colorado)
profile: Granddaughter of Stryker Corp. founder Homer Stryker; her fortune comes from inherited Stryker stock. Based in Fort Collins, she founded the Bohemian Foundation in 2001 (music, community, global and civic programs), has given ~$225M to charity, redevelops downtown Fort Collins real estate and is a major Democratic donor.
interesting_fact: In 2016 she and her brother Jon Stryker gave a combined $10M to fund the first US memorial to victims of racial-terror lynchings; she is also counted among Colorado's political 'Gang of Four' donors with Tim Gill, Jared Polis and Rutt Bridges.
deep_cut_fact: She once owned a California winery, Stryker Sonoma, which she sold to focus on the foundation; the foundation built The Music District, a creative hub and workspace for Fort Collins musicians, and was named after the Paris Bohemian movement of the early 1900s.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is the Bohemian Foundation (262 E. Mountain Ave, Fort Collins; main office line published on its contact page). Music/Fort Collins community angle is the natural hook.

name: Roger Samuelsson
current_role: Founder and majority owner (~68%), SHL Medical (Zug, Switzerland)
profile: Swedish entrepreneur who moved to Taiwan in 1988 and in 1989 co-founded SHL Group (now SHL Medical) with Martin Jelf; it grew into the world's largest maker of autoinjectors, supplying Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Pfizer and others. EQT holds roughly a third of the company. He also owns the 414-ft yacht Octopus, formerly Paul Allen's.
interesting_fact: He owns Octopus, the 414-foot explorer megayacht originally built for Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen.
deep_cut_fact: As a young amateur boxer, Samuelsson first visited Taiwan in 1983 out of curiosity to see where his boxing equipment was made; with a Swedish mechanical engineering degree he later returned to source merchandise for European importers before starting SHL.
notes: Press-shy; Forbes reports he declined multiple interview requests. Best route is SHL Medical communications (Carl Gillblad listed as media contact in releases).

name: John Caudwell
current_role: Investor and philanthropist; founder/chair of Caudwell Children and Caudwell LymeCo (ex-founder of Phones 4u)
profile: Stoke-raised entrepreneur who started wholesaling mobile phones with brother Brian in 1987, built Singlepoint (sold to Vodafone 2003) and Phones 4u, the UK's largest independent phone retailer, and sold out in 2006 and 2011. Now invests in property, fashion and other businesses and runs his charities; Giving Pledge signatory since 2013.
interesting_fact: He founded Caudwell Children in 2000 and in 2019 opened the Caudwell International Children's Centre in Staffordshire, providing services for autistic children.
deep_cut_fact: Before phones he was an engineering apprentice-turned-foreman at Michelin, earning an HNC in mechanical engineering while running a corner shop and a mail-order clothing business for motorcyclists on the side; he later owned the F1 powerboat team Caudwell Racing (2012-14).
notes: Media-friendly, frequent interviewee (podcasts, speaker agencies). Best route is via Caudwell Children PR or his Caudwell office (caudwell.com). Keen long-distance cyclist; avoid Lyme-disease controversy angle.

name: Anna Katharina Viessmann
current_role: Non-executive board member, Viessmann family holding (Viessmann Generations Group)
profile: Fourth-generation heir of Viessmann, the heating/cooling maker founded by great-grandfather Johann Viessmann in 1917. The family sold the Climate Solutions (heat pump) business to Carrier in 2023 for EUR 12B; proceeds now sit in Viessmann Generations Group, led by her brother Max. She sits on the family holding's board as a non-executive member.
interesting_fact: When the Viessmann Family Holding was created in 2019, she joined its board as a non-executive member alongside father Martin Viessmann (president) and outside directors from Flick Gocke Schaumburg and Dr. Oetker.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a bachelor's in International Cultural and Business Studies from the University of Passau and a master's in Corporate Management and Economics from Zeppelin University, Friedrichshafen.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Viessmann Generations Group communications. Energy angle: family sold its heat-pump business to Carrier. Deep-cut fact is only from Forbes facts (no more obscure sourced detail found).

name: Ronald McAulay
current_role: Private investor; Kadoorie-family shareholder in CLP Holdings (retired from CLP board 2016 and HKSH board 2017)
profile: Glasgow-educated Scottish chartered accountant who married into Hong Kong's Kadoorie family (wife Rita is Sir Michael Kadoorie's sister). He sat on the CLP Holdings board from 1968 and Hongkong & Shanghai Hotels (Peninsula) from 1972. His fortune derives mainly from a roughly 10% CLP stake held via family trusts.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of CLP, Hong Kong's largest power utility, in 1968 at age 32 and stayed nearly half a century until 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond power and hotels, McAulay was an Honorary Trustee of the Tate Foundation in London, the fundraising arm of the Tate galleries, per HKSH's 2015 annual report.
notes: About 90 years old and very private, with no public social media. No death reported; Forbes still listed him in 2026. Son Andrew McAulay chairs Kadoorie Farm and Botanic Garden. Any approach would go via Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons (Kadoorie family office), but I found no published contact.

name: Miao Hangen
current_role: Chairman & general manager, Jiangsu Eastern Shenghong (000301.SZ); chairman of parent Shenghong Group
profile: Born 1965 in Shenghong village, Wujiang (Suzhou), Miao rose from a village silk-mill job to run the Shenghong sand-washing/dyeing works founded in 1992, then built Shenghong Group into a textiles-to-petrochemicals giant. Eastern Shenghong now spans polyester fibres, a large Lianyungang refining/petrochemical complex and new materials; the group broke ground on a $4.2bn energy-storage battery plant in 2023.
interesting_fact: Eastern Shenghong has issued global depositary receipts listed in Switzerland (SIX Swiss Exchange), giving a Suzhou textile-born company a European capital-markets listing.
deep_cut_fact: After failing the gaokao in the early 1980s he joined the village silk factory for 30 yuan a month, working as accountant and storekeeper; at 27 he was made head of the new Shenghong sand-washing plant, whose early hit was a 'palm-print' (手掌花) fabric effect.
notes: Wife Zhu Hongmei is co-owner per Hurun. IR email is from the 2026 annual report summary (board secretary Wang Jun). Low international media profile; approach via IR/board secretary office, ideally in Chinese.

name: Kwak Dong-shin
current_role: Chairman & CEO and largest shareholder, Hanmi Semiconductor (promoted to chairman Dec 2024)
profile: Son of Hanmi founder Kwak Noh-kwon (an ex-Motorola Korea engineer), he joined the Incheon chip-packaging equipment maker in 1998 and has run it since 2007. He spearheaded its thermal-compression (TC) bonders, now the leading tool for stacking HBM memory for Nvidia AI GPUs, and supplies SK hynix, Micron and others. Also holds a stake in HPSP.
interesting_fact: He has argued publicly that Hanmi's TC bonders are sufficient for HBM4 and HBM5, pushing back on the industry shift to hybrid bonding (which he says costs over 2x as much per unit); Nvidia's Blackwell is built using Hanmi TC bonders.
deep_cut_fact: Hanmi's bet on HBM-style stacking long predates the AI boom: its 'TSV Dual Stacking TC Bonder' won Korea's IR52 Jang Young-sil Award back in 2017. On the day he was named chairman (Dec 16, 2024) he personally unveiled the new 'TC Bonder Griffin Super Bonding Head'.
notes: No published press/IR email found on Hanmi's English site (has an IR&PR section, mostly Korean). Gives media remarks at Computex and SEMICON; a trade-show booth or Korean press channel is the likeliest route. Name also romanized Gwak Dong-shin.

name: Ron Mannix
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Coril Holdings Ltd. (Calgary family asset manager); ownership passed to sons Stephen and Michael Mannix from 2016
profile: Third-generation heir of Calgary's Mannix construction/energy dynasty (founded 1898). With brother Fred he ran the Mancal/Loram group (Manalta Coal, Pembina Pipeline) and sold most energy assets for over C$2bn in 1997; Ron then founded Coril Holdings (rail equipment, real estate, health investments) and is a major Alberta arts and children's-development philanthropist.
interesting_fact: The Mannix family firms helped build the St. Lawrence Seaway, the Trans-Canada Highway, Toronto and Montreal subways and the Cold War DEW Line radar stations; Ron joined Manalta Coal in 1973 and was its president by 1974.
deep_cut_fact: A keen music patron, he founded the National Music Centre Foundation (Calgary's Studio Bell) and formerly chaired the Cantos Music Foundation and the Calgary International Organ Festival and Competition; he also founded the Norlien Foundation.
notes: Born 1948; very private. Hurun's 'Mancal' label belongs more to brother Fred Mannix (Mancal Group); Ron's vehicle is Coril. No longer listed on Coril's board (2026), sons run it. No death record found; most recent bio is JA Southern Alberta Hall of Fame (2021).

name: Victor Gradin
profile: Bahian economist and businessman who joined the Odebrecht group in 1974 at founder Norberto Odebrecht's invitation; his family became Odebrecht's second-largest shareholder (~20%). Died 26 May 2019 in Salvador, aged 86.
interesting_fact: Before joining Odebrecht he served as Bahia's state secretary of economic development (1963-1967) under governor Lomanto Junior.
notes: Deceased 26 May 2019 (sources: https://www.novacana.com/noticias/morre-86-anos-victor-gradin-empresario-grupo-odebrecht-270519 ; bnews.com.br obituary). Family's Odebrecht stake was later sold back to the Odebrechts after a long dispute. Not a podcast candidate.

name: Divyank Turakhia
current_role: Dubai-based tech entrepreneur and investor; founder and former CEO of Media.net, co-founder of Directi
profile: Mumbai-born programmer who co-founded web-hosting/domain group Directi with brother Bhavin in 1998 at age 16, then built contextual-ad network Media.net, sold in 2016 to a Chinese consortium for $900M, one of the largest ad-tech deals ever. Now based largely in Dubai, he invests and builds new ventures.
interesting_fact: He was named India's youngest billionaire three years running (2016-2018) and the youngest self-made Gulf billionaire in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He started coding at age eight; a 2021 interview with domain investor Mike Mann was titled 'From Wing Walking to Billion-Dollar Exits', and Entrepreneur India profiled his passion for flying planes and scuba diving.
notes: Low public profile; no verified personal social accounts or published office email found. Some web profiles about him are aggregator/AI-written; current title unverified. Don't confuse with brother Bhavin (Zeta, Flock).

name: Leopoldo Del Pino Y Calvo Sotelo
current_role: Private investor; major Ferrovial shareholder via his holding company Siemprelara (Ferrovial director 2010-2016)
profile: One of the children of Rafael del Pino y Moreno, who founded construction and infrastructure group Ferrovial in 1952; brother of Ferrovial chairman Rafael del Pino. He sat on Ferrovial's board from 2010 to early 2016 and has gradually sold down a stake that once exceeded 8%, investing through his vehicle Siemprelara and SICAVs.
interesting_fact: His Ferrovial shares came from the family holding Portman Baela, which distributed 40.82% of Ferrovial's capital directly to the siblings' individual vehicles, his being Siemprelara.
deep_cut_fact: Through Siemprelara he created and presides over the Fundación Estrella de los Mares, whose stated aims include promoting Spanish history, including its famous navigators.
notes: Very private; no personal site or social accounts found. MarketScreener lists him as a director of the Spanish parking association (Asociacion Espanola de Aparcamientos y Garajes). The foundation is the only possible route but no published contact was found.

name: Maria Del Pino Y Calvo Soleto
current_role: Non-Executive Director of Ferrovial N.V. and President of the Fundación Rafael del Pino
profile: María del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo is the eldest child of Ferrovial founder Rafael del Pino y Moreno (d. 2008) and holds about 8.7% of Ferrovial through her company Menosmares, S.L. She has sat on Ferrovial's board since 2006; her brother Rafael is executive chairman. Since 2000 she has also led the family's Fundación Rafael del Pino.
interesting_fact: Her father personally named her president of the Fundación Rafael del Pino when he created it in 2000. Its mission is to train future leaders, and it has since funded hundreds of 'Becas de Excelencia' scholarships for Spanish graduates.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business she interned at the European Commission in Brussels, worked in the International Relations Secretariat of Spain's UCD party from 1979, and later volunteered with the development NGO Codespa until 2000. She studied economics at Universidad Complutense and holds an IESE PDD.
notes: The input spells her name 'Calvo Soleto'; the correct spelling is Calvo-Sotelo. She is very private and has reportedly given only one interview. The best route is through the Fundación Rafael del Pino (general info email), which runs economics and energy-policy events. She also sits on the Princess of Asturias Foundation's board of trustees.

name: Prem Watsa
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Fairfax Financial Holdings (Toronto)
profile: Hyderabad-born, IIT Madras-trained engineer who emigrated to Canada in 1972, earned an MBA at Western's Ivey school, worked at Confederation Life, and in 1985 took control of what became Fairfax Financial, a value-investing insurance and investment holding company often compared to Berkshire Hathaway. He still runs Fairfax, which reported $1.39B Q2 2026 net earnings.
interesting_fact: Often called 'Canada's Warren Buffett', he has led Fairfax since 1985 with a value-investing approach and still delivers the opening remarks at its annual meeting (the 41st was held in April 2026).
deep_cut_fact: He arrived in London, Ontario with just 8 rupees and paid his way through his Ivey MBA by selling air conditioners and furnaces; in 2017 he became Huron University College's first-ever Chancellor.

public_contacts.value: John Varnell, VP Corporate Development, Fairfax Financial (published contact on press releases; phone +1 416-367-4941)

notes: No personal social accounts. Fairfax press releases list John Varnell as the contact (phone only, no email published). Watsa writes a widely read annual shareholder letter, a good hook for outreach.

name: Sergey Katsiev
current_role: Co-owner and board member (former president, until 2015), Megapolis tobacco/FMCG distribution group, Russia
profile: Russian businessman who founded tobacco distributor Megapolis in 1998 after running Igor Kesaev's Mercury Tobacco Corporation from 1993; the two firms merged in 2006 and Megapolis became Russia's largest tobacco distributor (Philip Morris and JTI each took 20% in 2013). He stepped down as president in 2015 but remains a shareholder; in 2022 he and partners bought Imperial Brands' Russian assets.
interesting_fact: In 2022 Katsiev and his partners bought the Russian business of British tobacco company Imperial Brands as Western firms exited Russia.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering business he studied at the Moscow Institute of International Relations (MGIMO) and, after the Soviet collapse, worked at a Russian government trade mission in the Netherlands.
notes: Extremely private; did not answer calls from Kommersant even when he stepped down (https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/2714727). No published personal or press contact found; Megapolis is part of Igor Kesaev's Mercury group. Russia-based tobacco business - consider sanctions/reputational context before outreach.

name: Mikheil Lomtadze
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman of the Management Board, Kaspi.kz
profile: Georgian-born Harvard MBA who joined Kaspi via private equity firm Baring Vostok, which invested in the Kazakh bank in 2006. As CEO he rebranded it Kaspi in 2011 and turned it into a super-app combining payments, marketplace and fintech; Kaspi listed in London (2020) and on Nasdaq (2024).
interesting_fact: Before Kaspi he was a partner at Baring Vostok, Russia's largest private equity fund; Kaspi's leadership team pointedly contained no career bankers when it pivoted to technology.
deep_cut_fact: While still a student in Tbilisi he founded his own audit and consulting firm, Georgia Consulting Group Audit (1995), which he later sold.

public_contacts.value: Fintech Leaders interview (Miguel Armaza) - prior podcast appearance

notes: Also spelled Mikhail Lomtadze. Does occasional long-form interviews (McKinsey, Fintech Leaders) - podcast-friendly. Best route: Kaspi IR.

name: Eric Duval
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Groupe Duval (Paris-area family real estate group; CEO is his daughter Pauline Boucon Duval)
profile: French entrepreneur who founded Groupe Duval in 1994 as a real estate developer. It grew into a family group of about 6,000 staff in 20 countries and roughly €1bn in revenue, spanning development, retail parks, Odalys tourist residences and golf. His children now run day-to-day operations, and the group is expanding in Africa and into energy-transition services.
interesting_fact: Groupe Duval bought Odalys in 2000, UGolf in 2009 and Bluegreen in 2022, which made it Europe's leading golf operator and the world's 5th largest.
deep_cut_fact: The group marked its 30th anniversary on 19 September 2024 at the Palais Brongniart (the old Paris stock exchange). Its plans include renewable energy and energy-transition services.
notes: Florian Silnicki is listed as Directeur de la Communication and Philippine Barneville as Responsable de la communication. The group's renewable-energy activities fit the podcast angle. Low personal media profile.

name: S Gopalakrishnan
current_role: Chairman, Axilor Ventures (Bengaluru seed fund/accelerator); co-founder of Infosys; Chair, IISc Council
profile: Senapathy 'Kris' Gopalakrishnan co-founded Infosys in 1981 and was its CEO/MD (2007-2011) and vice chairman (2011-2014). He now backs startups through Axilor Ventures and family investment arm Pratithi, and funds neuroscience and research through the Pratiksha Trust, while chairing IISc's Council and several Indian government innovation bodies.
interesting_fact: He gave Rs 2.25 billion to build the Centre for Brain Research at IISc, described as the largest individual gift the institute has received, and funds a cellular-level brain-mapping centre at IIT Madras.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a physicist, earning an M.Sc. in Physics (1977) before an M.Tech in Computer Science (1979) at IIT Madras, and his first job was as a software engineer at Patni Computer Systems in Mumbai in 1979, where he met the future Infosys founding team.
notes: Goes by 'Kris'. Very active public speaker on AI, deep tech and startups (CII, IISc); good podcast fit. Axilor's general inbox is the best published route; the Pratiksha Trust site lists no email.

name: NR Narayana Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; founder of family investment firm Catamaran Ventures
profile: N.R. Narayana Murthy (b. 1946) co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues, seeded by Rs 10,000 from his wife Sudha Murty, and built it into one of India's largest IT services companies, serving as CEO and chairman. Often called the father of the Indian IT sector, he is now Chairman Emeritus and invests via Catamaran Ventures.
interesting_fact: He has said being arrested and expelled near the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border in 1974, while hitchhiking back from Europe, turned him from a 'confused leftist' into a 'compassionate capitalist'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and designed a BASIC interpreter for ECIL; his first startup, Softronics, folded after about a year and a half.
notes: Infosys press email reaches the company, not him directly; Catamaran Ventures (his family office, catamaranventures.com) may be a more direct route but no published email was verified. Gives frequent public lectures and interviews, often on work ethic and entrepreneurship.

name: Peter P Gassner
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Veeva Systems
profile: Software engineer who worked at IBM's Silicon Valley Lab, led PeopleTools at PeopleSoft and ran technology at Salesforce before co-founding Veeva Systems in 2007. Veeva builds cloud software for the life-sciences industry and went public in 2013; Gassner remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Under Gassner, Veeva became a public benefit corporation in 2021, which made it the first public company to convert to a PBC.
deep_cut_fact: Gassner grew up in Portland, Oregon, the son of Swiss immigrants (his father had a machine shop). He earned a computer science degree from Oregon State University in 1989, and his first internship was at IBM.
notes: Low public profile but gives occasional founder interviews (Sramana Mitra, SaaStr) on vertical SaaS. The PBC claim is from Wikipedia; check it before using. Best route is Veeva PR.

name: Vince McMahon
current_role: Founder of 14TH & I, a private sports, media and entertainment investment firm (Connecticut)
profile: Former WWE chairman and CEO. He bought his father's wrestling company in 1982 and built WWE into a global media business, which merged with UFC to form TKO in 2023. He resigned from TKO in January 2024 and in 2025 launched 14TH & I, named for the D.C. intersection where his father's Capitol Wrestling Corp. was based.
interesting_fact: McMahon was behind the 1976 Muhammad Ali vs. Antonio Inoki match, years before he took over his father's promotion.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from East Carolina University in 1968 and working as a traveling salesman, he became a ring announcer in 1969. In 1971 he promoted his first card, in a small territory in Maine.
notes: Sensitive: he resigned from TKO in January 2024 amid a lawsuit alleging sexual misconduct, and in January 2025 he settled SEC charges over undisclosed payments (>$1.7m). Weigh reputational fit before any outreach. 14TH & I's site published no contact details; reported executives are Brad Blum (president) and David Spingarn (CIO), per https://wrestletalk.com/news/vince-mcmahon-new-company-wwe-exit-revealed/

name: Paul Georges Despature
current_role: Chairman of Edify (Despature family investment company); former chairman of Somfy's management board (1983-2014)
profile: Paul-Georges Despature is the patriarch of the French Despature family, which controls Somfy, the Cluses-based maker of motors and automation for blinds, shutters and gates. He ran Somfy as chairman of its management board from 1983 until the end of 2014, then moved to head the family investment arm Edify. His son Jean Guillaume Despature now chairs Somfy, which the family took private in 2022-23.
interesting_fact: The Despature family, which already owned the thermal-underwear brand Damart, bought Somfy in 1984 as a diversification into summer-season products; Somfy has since become a world leader in motorised blinds and the connected home.
deep_cut_fact: The name SOMFY is an acronym for 'Société d'Outillage et Mécanique du FaucignY', a 1969 spin-off of the Cluses precision-machining firm Carpano & Pons in the Arve valley, a region known for Swiss-watch part-making.

public_contacts.value: Agence Shan (Somfy press agency), 30 rue des Mathurins, 75008 Paris

notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Edify role per Somfy's December 2014 announcement (https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2014/12/FCECO035465_20141222.pdf); check whether he still holds it. Somfy press route is the corporate one, not a personal office.

name: Raja Bagmane
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Bagmane Group (Bagmane Developers Pvt Ltd), Bengaluru
profile: Bengaluru real-estate developer who founded Bagmane Group in 1996 and built it into one of the city's largest commercial/tech-park landlords (Bagmane Tech Park, Bagmane World Technology Center; ~30 mn sq ft operational). Blackstone took a minority stake in 2024, and the group sponsors Bagmane Prime Office REIT, which has listed in India. His sons Aditya and Shashank are directors.
interesting_fact: Bagmane Tech Park in C V Raman Nagar, launched in 2001, was one of Bengaluru's earliest IT parks; the group's portfolio is now hosted in a Blackstone-backed listed REIT.
notes: Low media profile; rarely gives interviews. The published email is a general company enquiries inbox. A data-center/tech-park angle is relevant: Bagmane hosts big tech occupiers in Bengaluru. His sons may be easier to reach for a conversation.

name: Naveen Jindal
current_role: Chairman, Jindal Steel Ltd (formerly Jindal Steel & Power); BJP Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) for Kurukshetra
profile: Naveen Jindal (b. 1970, Hisar), youngest son of O.P. Jindal, took over the group's Raigarh and Raipur steel operations in 1993 and built Jindal Steel & Power into a major steel, power and mining group. He is founding chancellor of O.P. Jindal Global University and, since 2024, a BJP MP; the group is now expanding Angul steel capacity and investing in nuclear and solar in Jharkhand.
interesting_fact: His 1990s court fight after hoisting the flag at his Raigarh factory led to the 2004 Supreme Court ruling that flying the Indian national flag on any day is part of citizens' freedom of expression.
deep_cut_fact: While earning his MBA at UT Dallas (1992) he served as Student Government VP then president and won Student Leader of the Year; the university's Naveen Jindal School of Management now bears his name. He is also a national-record skeet shooter in India.
notes: Highly public figure (industrialist + MP); active on X. Also captains the Jindal Panther polo team. Steer clear of the coal-block allocation case.

name: Nikolaus Knauf
current_role: Shareholder and longtime member/former chair of the shareholders' committee, Knauf Group (Iphofen, Germany)
profile: Born 1936, the eldest son of Knauf co-founder Alfons Knauf. From 1969 he co-ran the family plasterboard/building-materials group with cousin Baldwin Knauf, overseeing technology while it expanded across Europe, Russia and the CIS; he left management in 2008 for the shareholders' committee. Knauf remains fully family-owned (~EUR 15B sales).
interesting_fact: Knauf was founded in 1932 by brothers Alfons and Karl Knauf as a gypsum works in Perl on the Moselle before moving to Iphofen in Lower Franconia, where the family's Knauf-Museum (opened 1983) shows casts of great relief artworks.
deep_cut_fact: Within the cousin duo running Knauf, Nikolaus handled the technical side while Baldwin took administration; he has also served as a CSU councillor in the small municipality of Markt Einersheim near Iphofen and on the Kitzingen district council.

public_contacts.value: Gebr. Knauf KG, Corporate Communications, Iphofen (press-release contact)

notes: Aged ~90, very private, no personal channels. Was honorary consul of Russia in Nuremberg until March 2022 (Knauf's Russia business was a sensitive topic after 2022) -- avoid. Route via Knauf corporate communications.

name: GM Rao
current_role: Founder Chairman, GMR Group (infrastructure: airports, energy, highways, urban development)
profile: Grandhi Mallikarjuna Rao (b. 1950, Rajam, Andhra Pradesh) is a mechanical engineer who built GMR Group from a single jute mill bought in 1978 into one of India's largest infrastructure developers, running Delhi and Hyderabad airports plus energy and highway assets. He funded the move into power by selling his Vysya Bank stake; sons and family now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: He used the roughly Rs 3.4 billion from selling his entire ING Vysya Bank stake to fund GMR's entry into power and infrastructure; the group is also co-owner of IPL cricket team Delhi Capitals.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked as a shift engineer at a paper mill and then as a junior engineer in the Andhra Pradesh Public Works Department; he moved into commodities trading at his mother's insistence.
notes: Press email reported from GMR's media page (page returned 503 when re-checked; verify). Philanthropy via GMR Varalakshmi Foundation (est. 1991). Strong energy/infrastructure fit for the podcast.

name: Nirmal Kumar Minda
current_role: Chairman (Executive Chairman), UNO Minda Ltd; President of ASSOCHAM for 2025
profile: Second-generation head of UNO Minda (formerly Minda Industries), a Gurugram-based maker of auto switches, lighting, alloy wheels and EV components. He joined his father Shadilal's business in 1977 and ran it on his own after a 1996 split with his brother. He built it through Japanese and European joint ventures and moved from MD to Chairman in April 2025.
interesting_fact: The business goes back to 1958, when his father Shadilal Minda started importing ammeters from Japan. It moved to Delhi in 1962 to serve the tractor and motorcycle aftermarket.
deep_cut_fact: The group's first joint venture (1995) came from a quality push by Maruti. Minda asked the carmaker to help find a Japanese partner for switches, which led to Toyota-group supplier Tokai Rika. Separately, he and his wife Suman run Samarth-Jyoti, which operates two schools, a 100-bed hospital and 18 village centres.
notes: The Samarth-Jyoti detail comes from an India CSR profile (https://indiacsr.in/biography-nirmal-kumar-minda-president-assocham-2025/). EV components and ASSOCHAM policy work are possible podcast angles. Sources differ on his exact title (Chairman vs Chairman & MD).

name: Jonathan Burrell
current_role: CEO, Burrell Family Office; director of Garmin Ltd. (since 2018); president of the Burrell family charitable foundation
profile: Jonathan C. Burrell is the son of Garmin cofounder Gary Burrell (d. 2019), and his wealth comes from the family's Garmin stake. He formerly helped lead Garmin's engineering department, now runs the Burrell Family Office and sits on Garmin's board. He invests in financial, technology and clean-energy businesses.
interesting_fact: He is named as an inventor on 35 issued and pending U.S. patents, many of them owned by Garmin.
deep_cut_fact: He has a BS in mechanical engineering from Wichita State University and was a hands-on Garmin engineering leader before joining the board. Garmin's 2018 proxy says he invests in clean-energy businesses, which ties in with the podcast's energy theme.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Garmin contacts are company-level; he is an independent director, not an executive.

name: Jacob Brunsborg
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Lars Larsen Group (owner of JYSK)
profile: Son of JYSK founder Lars Larsen; became chairman of Lars Larsen Group (JYSK, ILVA, Actona, investments) in June 2019 shortly before his father's death. Rose through JYSK as head of purchasing and brand director, then did business development, entrepreneurship and board work; now steers the group's strategy, including investments in securities, property and green energy.
interesting_fact: He carries his mother's surname rather than Larsen, and his father reportedly warned him against aiming for the JYSK CEO job, insisting management be chosen on merit while ownership stays in the family.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1993 as a trainee ('elev') in the JYSK store on Grenåvej in Aarhus, and did his military service with the Royal Danish Life Guards (Dronningens Livregiment).

public_contacts.value: Press contact: Communications Director Lise Brøndum Wemmelund via Lars Larsen Group press room

notes: Rarely gives interviews and says he is less outgoing than his father (lex.dk). Group invests in green energy, a possible hook. Approach via the group's Communications Director.

name: Mette Brunsborg
current_role: Board member, Lars Larsen Group A/S (owner of JYSK) and Lars Larsens JYSK Fond
profile: Daughter of JYSK founder Lars Larsen (d. 2019). She and her brother Jacob Brunsborg (chairman) control Lars Larsen Group, the Silkeborg holding company that owns the JYSK home-furnishings chain plus BOLIA, ILVA, SOFACOMPANY and other investments. She joined the family foundation's board in 2019, taking her mother Kris Brunsborg's seat.
interesting_fact: When she joined the board of Lars Larsens JYSK Fond in 2019, she took the seat of her mother, Kris Brunsborg. The foundation's first gift under the new board was DKK 1m to Børns Vilkår to help children whose parents have mental illness.
deep_cut_fact: Away from the boardroom she runs her own farm (driver sit eget landbrug), according to the Danish encyclopedia Lex.
notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Brother Jacob Brunsborg is the family's public face. In July 2026 Lars Larsen Group announced a new renewable-energy agreement, which could be an angle for an energy podcast. Best route is Lars Larsen Group press.

name: Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua
current_role: King of Thailand (Rama X), since 2016
profile: Vajiralongkorn is the reigning King of Thailand, the only son of King Bhumibol Adulyadej; he took the throne in 2016 and was crowned in 2019. Hurun counts his wealth through his holdings in Siam Commercial Bank, assets once managed by the Crown Property Bureau that he took into direct ownership after his accession.
interesting_fact: He is a graduate of Australia's Royal Military College, Duntroon, and qualified as both a military fast-jet pilot and a commercial airline pilot.
deep_cut_fact: He was once known as the 'Football Prince': he played forward and later centre-back at Chitralada School, Millfield School in Somerset and Duntroon. Since 1978 he has personally handed out degrees at Rajabhat University commencements every year, estimated at over 2.1 million degrees.
notes: Reigning monarch, not a realistic podcast guest. Thailand's strict lese-majeste laws make any outreach or commentary sensitive. The only channel is formal, via the Bureau of the Royal Household. No personal contacts are published.

name: An Sumei
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Lin Lairong) of Zhongxing Group (众兴集团), controlling shareholder of Dazhong Mining (SZSE: 001203)
profile: An Sumei and her husband Lin Lairong are the actual controllers of Zhongxing Group, which holds ~41% of Inner Mongolia-based Dazhong Mining, listed in Shenzhen in May 2021. Dazhong mines and processes iron ore (iron concentrate, pellets, sulphuric acid) and has been adding spodumene/lithium resources. She keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Hurun's 'Zhongxing' is 众兴集团 (Zhongxing Group), not telecom maker ZTE; filings list Lin Lairong and An Sumei as joint actual controllers of Dazhong Mining, whose product line now includes spodumene (lithium) ore alongside iron concentrate.
notes: Very private; virtually no English-language coverage. Best route is via Dazhong Mining's board secretary office (IR email from annual report). Company chairman is Niu Guofeng; lithium pivot could be a hook for an energy podcast.

name: Madhusudhan Agarwal
current_role: Co-owner/director, Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd (Delhi branch of the Haldiram's family)
profile: Madhusudan Agarwal and his brother Manohar Lal Agarwal, grandsons of founder Ganga Bishan 'Haldiram' Agarwal (sons of Moolchand), built the Delhi-based Haldiram's snacks business. After the 2022-25 merger of the Delhi and Nagpur packaged-snacks units into Haldiram Snacks Food, the Delhi brothers hold ~56%; Temasek bought a ~9% stake in 2025 at a ~$10bn valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to a 1937 bhujia shop in Bikaner, Rajasthan; the merged company was valued at nearly US$10bn when Singapore's Temasek bought in in 2025.
notes: Family is famously interview-shy (Financial Express called the brothers 'elusive'). Most coverage focuses on Manohar Lal; very little on Madhusudan personally. Best route is via the company's corporate communications.

name: Brad Garlinghouse
current_role: CEO, Ripple (Ripple Labs)
profile: Kansas-born executive (b. 1971) who held senior roles at @Home, Dialpad, Yahoo (SVP running Homepage, Flickr, Mail, Messenger) and AOL, then ran Hightail (ex-YouSendIt). Joined Ripple as COO in 2015 and became CEO around end-2016; his wealth comes from Ripple equity and XRP. He continues to lead Ripple's global payments, custody and RLUSD stablecoin push.
interesting_fact: As a Yahoo SVP in 2006 he wrote the internal 'Peanut Butter Manifesto' memo, warning Yahoo was spreading itself too thin like peanut butter; it leaked to the Wall Street Journal and became a Silicon Valley strategy classic.
deep_cut_fact: He told Fortune his interest in technology began growing up in Kansas when his dad brought home a Tandy TRS-80 computer.
notes: Very media-accessible, active on X (@bgarlinghouse) and frequent podcast guest. Best route is Ripple's press team form. Avoid the long SEC-litigation saga as a hook.

name: Dmitry Pumpansky
current_role: Former owner and chairman of TMK (Russian steel-pipe maker); left TMK's board and beneficial ownership in March 2022
profile: Russian industrialist (b. 1964, usually spelled Dmitry Pumpyansky), graduate of the Ural Polytechnic Institute. Started as a metals trader, ran pipe plants including Sinarsky, joined TMK in 2002 and by 2006 owned 100% of it, building one of the world's largest makers of oil-and-gas tubulars. Said to have exited TMK in 2022; reported living in Geneva.
interesting_fact: After co-buying TMK with Sergei Popov and Andrey Melnichenko, he bought both partners out in 2006 to become its sole owner.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 he earned a Doctor of Technical Sciences degree with a dissertation on steels, alloys and production technologies for next-generation OCTG and specialty pipes, adding to his earlier engineering candidate degree and economics doctorate.
notes: Name in input is a variant spelling of Pumpyansky. Sanctioned by UK (2022) and named on the US CAATSA list; EU sanctions annulled by the EU General Court on appeal. Outreach carries compliance/reputational risk; no published personal or office contact found.

name: Rajendrakumar Shivkisan Agrawal
current_role: Director, Haldiram Foods International (Nagpur Haldiram's) and related family companies; shareholder in merged Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd
profile: Member of the Nagpur branch of the Haldiram's snack-food family; Indian company registries list him as a director of Haldiram Foods International and some 27 related companies. The family's fortune jumped after the Delhi and Nagpur businesses merged in 2025 into Haldiram Snacks Food (Nagpur ~44%) and Temasek, Alpha Wave and IHC bought stakes at a reported ~$10B valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal's bhujia shop in Bikaner; the Nagpur arm was built by Shivkisan Agrawal, who introduced kaju katli to Nagpur. Hurun named Rajendrakumar one of India's biggest wealth gainers in its 2026 Global Rich List.
notes: Almost no public profile, interviews or social accounts found. Sources call him part of the Nagpur Haldiram family but don't state the exact relation; the patronymic 'Shivkisan' suggests he is a son of Nagpur founder-chairman Shivkisan Agrawal, but that is unverified. The only email on the Haldiram's Nagpur site is customer support (support@haldirams.com), so it's a poor route. Corporate PR via Haldiram Snacks Food is likely better.

name: Hu Bopan
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Zhejiang NHU Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002001)
profile: Hu Baifan (胡柏藩; listed here as 'Hu Bopan') founded NHU in Xinchang, Zhejiang, growing it from a school-run workshop into one of the world's largest producers of vitamins (A, E), animal-nutrition ingredients, flavors and fragrances and specialty materials. He has chaired the Shenzhen-listed company since 2005 and indirectly controls roughly 31% of it.
interesting_fact: NHU began as a business started to fund a rural middle school; its first product was recycled waste alcohol, which earned about RMB 100,000 profit in year one before Hu pivoted to high-value pharma intermediates.
deep_cut_fact: Hu was a newly graduated chemistry teacher at a rural middle school in 1988 when the principal asked him to start a business; with borrowed tens of thousands of yuan, no plant, workers or product, he built it, and in 1991 his team developed ethoxymethylene malonate (a norfloxacin intermediate), NHU's first national key new product.
notes: Name in source list is a romanization variant; standard spelling is Hu Baifan (胡柏藩). Low international media profile; Chinese-language outreach via NHU Securities Department is the most direct route. His brother Hu Baishan is vice chairman.

name: lin Wenjing
profile: Lin Wenjing (Sutanto Djuhar, 1928-2018), Fuqing-born Indonesian-Chinese co-founder of the Salim Group, returned to Fuqing in 1987 and founded Rongqiao Group in 1989; died 2 July 2018.
notes: Deceased (2 July 2018) per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutanto_Djuhar. Rongqiao Group / Lin Wenjing Foundation now run by family; the Forbes listing may refer to heirs.

name: Arkady Volozh
current_role: Founder and CEO, Nebius Group N.V. (Nasdaq: NBIS), Amsterdam-based AI cloud/neocloud company
profile: Kazakhstan-born, Tel Aviv-based Volozh co-founded Yandex with Ilya Segalovich in 1997 and led it through its 2011 Nasdaq IPO. After Yandex sold its Russian assets in 2024 (~$5.4bn), he relaunched the remainder as Nebius, an AI-infrastructure cloud that has since signed deals with Microsoft (up to $19.4bn) and Meta (up to $27bn) and targets multi-gigawatt contracted power.
interesting_fact: Long before Yandex, he and Segalovich built search tools for patents, Russian classical literature and the Bible; in 1993 they built a search engine for 'non-structured information with Russian morphology'.
deep_cut_fact: He attended the Republican School of Physics and Mathematics in Almaty, studied applied maths at Moscow's Gubkin oil-and-gas university, worked at a state pipeline research institute, then started a small business importing PCs from Austria. In 2007 he set up the free Yandex School of Data Analysis.
notes: Highly relevant for data-center/AI-infra episode (Nebius is building multi-GW AI capacity, e.g. Finland, UK, US). He has appeared on Accel's podcast. Avoid leading with Russia/sanctions history; EU sanctions were lifted in 2024.

name: Chao Yung-Tsang
current_role: Co-founder & Vice Chairman, Jentech Precision Industrial Co. (TWSE: 3653), Taoyuan, Taiwan
profile: Co-founded Jentech Precision in 1987 with older brother and chairman Chung-Hsin Chao; early on he ran finance while Chung-Hsin ran R&D. Jentech grew from a tool-and-die shop into a key maker of heat spreaders, vapor-chamber and micro-channel lids and liquid-cooling parts for AI servers, EVs and chips. He oversees operations, finance and capacity planning.
interesting_fact: AI-chip cooling demand turned Jentech into one of Taiwan's highest-priced stocks: its shares broke through NT$5,000 in April 2026 as Nvidia-class processors adopted advanced lids such as micro-channel lids that build liquid coolant paths into the chip lid.
deep_cut_fact: Jentech's own board bio says he graduated from the Affiliated Senior High School of National Taiwan Normal University and showed 'a strong entrepreneurial spirit from an early age'; in the company's first years he ran finance while his brother handled R&D.
notes: Low public profile; brother Chung-Hsin Chao is chairman and the company's public face. Company form lets you pick a department. Jentech's ESG report also lists a sustainability-office email, but no press/IR email was found; the company's annual report names the general manager as spokesperson. Some hosts (jentech.com.tw, taipeitimes) blocked for WebFetch but reachable via curl.

name: Xia Zuoquan
current_role: Co-founder and non-executive director, BYD Co.; founder/chairman, Shenzhen Zhengxuan Investment
profile: One of BYD's three founders: an investor who put a few hundred thousand yuan into Wang Chuanfu's battery startup in 1995, served as executive director and VP running group operations 2001-2008, and remains a non-executive director holding ~2.8% of BYD. Since 2010 he has run his own VC firm, Zhengxuan Investment, backing robotics, aerospace, new energy and biotech companies.
interesting_fact: His 1995 investment of a few hundred thousand yuan in BYD returned more than 20,000x; he has sold BYD shares mainly to fund Zhengxuan's tech investments, including early, rescue-stage backing of robot maker UBTech.
deep_cut_fact: Xia, from Xiangyang in Hubei, first met Wang Chuanfu in November 1994; he didn't understand batteries, but the two talked for three days and two nights, going to bed at 4am each night, before he committed to invest in April 1995.
notes: Very low-profile; rarely gives interviews. db@byd.com is BYD's listed-company contact (board office) from its Shenzhen exchange profile. Zhengxuan Investment (正轩投资) would be the more personal route, but I found no published email for it.

name: Arthur James
notes: Likely a parsing artifact of the Forbes 2001-09 joint listing 'Arthur, James & John Irving' (Irving family, Canada). All are deceased: Arthur L. Irving d. 13 May 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Irving), James K. Irving d. 21 Jun 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Irving), John E. Irving d. 2010.

name: John Irving
current_role: Deceased (died July 21, 2010, Saint John, New Brunswick)
profile: John E. 'Jack' Irving (1932-2010), youngest son of K.C. Irving, co-owned the Irving Group with brothers J.K. and Arthur (listed jointly by Forbes 2001-2009). Died July 21, 2010 aged 78.
notes: Deceased - source: CBC News 'Industrialist Jack Irving dies at 78' (http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/new-brunswick/industrialist-jack-irving-dies-at-78-1.870034) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_E._Irving. Irving Oil (the energy arm) is run by Arthur Irving's family; consider them instead.

name: Joan Tisch
profile: Died November 2, 2017 in Manhattan at age 90; widow of Preston Robert Tisch (Loews Corp. co-founder, NY Giants co-owner). Death announced by the New York Giants.
notes: Deceased (source: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/joan-tisch-dead ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Tisch). Her stake passed to children Steve, Jonathan and Laurie Tisch. Remove from outreach list.

name: Robert McNair
current_role: Deceased (died 23 Nov 2018); was founder/owner of the NFL's Houston Texans
profile: Robert (Bob) McNair founded cogeneration firm Cogen Technologies in 1984, sold it to Enron in 1999, and used the proceeds to found the Houston Texans NFL franchise. He died on 23 November 2018; per instructions the rest of the profile is skipped.
notes: Died 23 Nov 2018 (Houston Chronicle obituary; Wikipedia 'Bob McNair'). Texans ownership passed to his widow and then to son Cal McNair (principal owner since 2024). Not a viable podcast guest.

name: Brijmohan Lall Munjal
profile: Founder of the Hero Group / Hero MotoCorp (motorcycles); died 1 November 2015 in New Delhi, aged 92.
notes: Deceased 1 Nov 2015 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brijmohan_Lall_Munjal ; https://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/hero-founder-brijmohan-lall-munjal-passes-away-9597). Son Pawan Munjal leads Hero MotoCorp.

name: Brenninkmeijer family
current_role: Family owners of COFRA Holding AG (Zug, Switzerland), parent of C&A, Bregal Investments and Sunrock; chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, with Florian Brenninkmeyer due to take over in April 2027
profile: This Dutch-German dynasty founded the C&A clothing chain in 1841 and owns it through the Swiss holding company COFRA, alongside private equity (Bregal), real estate and renewable energy investments. Around 2026 the group reported roughly €40bn under management and was handing control to the sixth generation, with Georg Wunderlin as its first non-family CEO.
interesting_fact: C&A takes its name from the initials of the founding brothers Clemens and August Brenninkmeyer, who opened their first textile shop in Sneek, Netherlands, in 1841. Six generations later the business is still entirely family-owned.
deep_cut_fact: Long before ESG became fashionable, Marcel Brenninkmeijer founded Good Energies in 2001 to run COFRA's renewables portfolio. It backed wind and solar developers and the Atlantic Wind Connection offshore transmission backbone, a strong energy hook.
notes: This is a family (hundreds of members), not an individual, and it is famously private. For an energy podcast, the best individual targets are probably COFRA chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, incoming chair Florian Brenninkmeyer, or the Sunrock solar business. Contact is through the COFRA newsroom; no email could be scraped. The family won the 2026 Kellogg Family Leadership Award.

name: Edward C. (Ned) Johnson
profile: Edward C. 'Ned' Johnson III, longtime chairman and CEO of Fidelity Investments, died on March 23, 2022 at age 91 at his home in Florida.
notes: Deceased March 23, 2022 (source: https://www.cnbc.com/2022/03/24/fidelity-investments-longtime-leader-edward-c-ned-johnson-iii-dies-at-91-.html). Fidelity is now led by his daughter Abigail Johnson; the family wealth is held by his heirs.

name: Abigail (Abigail P. Johnson)
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Fidelity Investments (Boston)
profile: Listed only as 'Abigail' sharing a 1997 Forbes entry with Edward C. (Ned) Johnson; this is almost certainly Abigail Johnson, Ned's daughter. She joined Fidelity full-time as an analyst in 1988 (after Hobart and William Smith and Harvard MBA), became CEO in 2014 and chairman in 2016, and runs the privately held, family-controlled asset manager today.
interesting_fact: An early Wall Street crypto champion: at Consensus 2017 she said she was 'still a believer' and revealed Fidelity had set up a small in-house bitcoin and ethereum mining operation; Fidelity Digital Assets followed in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Her first Fidelity job, straight out of high school in 1980, was answering phones in the customer-service department; she then majored in art history at Hobart and William Smith before Harvard Business School.
notes: Input record has only the first name 'Abigail' (Forbes 1997, shared with Ned Johnson); identification as Abigail Johnson is inferred, not confirmed by the source data. Publicity-shy; route via Fidelity corporate communications. Fidelity mining is a natural energy/data-center angle.

name: Alfred Lerner
profile: Deceased: Alfred Lerner (1933-2002), chairman of credit card giant MBNA and owner of the Cleveland Browns (1998-2002), died October 23, 2002 in Cleveland. Matches the 1996-2000 Forbes listing.
notes: Died 2002 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Lerner ; NYT obituary https://www.nytimes.com/2002/10/25/sports/alfred-lerner-69-banker-revived-cleveland-browns.html). Identity inferred from Forbes 1996-2000 US listing at ~$3.8B; no source_of_wealth given in input. Son Randy Lerner inherited the Browns.

name: Heinz-Georg Baus
profile: Founder of German DIY/home-improvement chain Bauhaus (founded 1960 in Mannheim). Died May 2016, aged 82.
interesting_fact: Died in May 2016 aged 82; Bauhaus was Germany's first DIY store chain, opened in Mannheim in 1960 on the American model.
notes: Deceased (May 2016) per DIY International and Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz-Georg_Baus). Not a candidate.

name: Sid Richardson Bass
current_role: Private investor and philanthropist, Fort Worth, Texas (head of the Bass family investment group since 1968)
profile: Fort Worth oil heir (grand-nephew of wildcatter Sid W. Richardson) who took control of the family business in 1968 and, per Vanity Fair, grew a ~$50M company into a ~$14B investment group. With his brothers he was Disney's largest shareholder from 1984 and is known for backing Michael Eisner's management. Yale 1965, Stanford MBA.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he and then-wife Mercedes Bass gave $25 million to the Metropolitan Opera, at the time the largest individual gift in the company's history.
deep_cut_fact: At just 28 he and his then-wife commissioned Paul Rudolph to design the Bass Residence in Fort Worth's Westover Hills, often called Rudolph's most ambitious residential project; it received the AIA Fort Worth chapter's 25 Year Honor Award in 2005.
notes: Very private; no published personal office email, website or social accounts found. Family office (Bass Enterprises, Fort Worth) does not publish contacts. Best route is likely a warm intro via Fort Worth civic/arts circles.

name: Mukesh Jagtiani
notes: Mukesh 'Micky' Jagtiani, founder and chairman of Dubai-based Landmark Group, died May 26, 2023 at age 70; his wife Renuka Jagtiani is chairwoman and CEO of the group. Source: https://www.arabianbusiness.com/culture-society/dubais-landmark-group-owner-micky-jagtiani-passes-away-at-age-70

name: Samwer Brothers
current_role: Oliver Samwer: CEO, Rocket Internet SE. Marc and Alexander Samwer: co-founders and investors (Rocket Internet / Global Founders Capital)
profile: Oliver, Marc and Alexander Samwer, from Cologne, sold their eBay-style auction site Alando to eBay in 1999 and later sold Jamba to VeriSign. They founded the Berlin incubator Rocket Internet in 2007, which built Zalando, Delivery Hero stakes, HelloFresh and others. Rocket went public in 2014 and was taken private in 2020. They now invest through Rocket and Global Founders Capital.
interesting_fact: Their first exit was Alando, a German auction site launched in 1999 and sold to eBay about 100 days later for roughly $43m. It became eBay Germany.
