notes: HIGH REPUTATIONAL RISK: multiple civil sexual-misconduct judgments since 2019 (incl. a reported $900M jury award in 2024) and other legal issues per Wikipedia; in 2021 he called earlier billionaire claims 'complete fiction'. Journalist should vet carefully before any outreach. No published contact route found.

name: the Leventis family
current_role: Family group: controlling shareholders (with the David family) of Coca-Cola HBC via Kar-Tess Holding; Leventis Group; A. G. Leventis Foundation (chaired by Anastasios Paul Leventis)
profile: Greek-Cypriot dynasty founded by Anastasios G. Leventis, whose West African trading house A. G. Leventis & Co. (1936) grew into a Nigerian/Ghanaian conglomerate. From the 1970s, Constantine Leventis expanded the family's soft-drinks business into Europe; the Hellenic Bottling Company merged with Coca-Cola Beverages to form Coca-Cola HBC, its main source of wealth today. Media assets come from relative Alki David.
interesting_fact: In the 1948 Accra riots, the most serious anti-colonial violence in post-war West Africa, the only large stores left unburned were those of A. G. Leventis & Co.
deep_cut_fact: Founder Anastasios G. Leventis was born in 1902 in the Cypriot mountain village of Lemythou, studied commerce in Bordeaux, and started out in 1920 as a manager for an Anglo-Hellenic firm in south-eastern Nigeria. In 2025 the family's foundation partnered with the Coca-Cola HBC Foundation on a EUR1m programme to restore fire-hit areas of Limassol.
notes: Multi-person family entry (Sunday Times 2020, shared with Alki David). For outreach, pick a specific member, e.g. Anastasios I. Leventis (Coca-Cola HBC non-exec director) or Anastasios P. Leventis (foundation chair). The CCHBC press office is the corporate route. Alive status is per-member, so it is left as 'unknown'.

name: Jason Murray
current_role: Co-Founder, CEO and Chairman, PACS Group, Inc. (NYSE: PACS)
profile: Jason Murray, a licensed nursing home administrator and former healthcare executive, co-founded PACS Group with Mark Hancock in 2013. Starting with two skilled nursing facilities, it has grown into a Utah-based post-acute care platform with about 387 facilities in 17 states. PACS listed on the NYSE in 2024; Murray owns roughly a third of the shares and still runs the company.
interesting_fact: PACS went from two skilled-nursing facilities in 2013 to a national post-acute care platform with nearly 400 facilities in about a decade, then listed on the NYSE in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He was named Ernst & Young's 2023 Mountain West Entrepreneur of the Year and was a finalist for EY's national award that year. He is a Fellow of the American College of Healthcare Executives (FACHE) and says he enjoys 'anything related to sports and athletics'.
notes: Route through Brooks Stevenson (corporate communications). PACS has faced short-seller and accounting scrutiny since 2024, so keep outreach focused on entrepreneurship and scaling. The web-search budget ran out at this point; facts come from the PACS IR site.

name: Richard Chandler
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Clermont Group (Singapore); founder, Chandler Foundation
profile: New Zealand-born investor who began investing in 1982, built Sovereign Global with his brother Christopher (a deep-value, emerging-markets investor), split assets in 2006 and founded Singapore-based Clermont Group. Clermont holds healthcare, financial services and aerospace assets, including India's SBFC, Vietnam's Hoan My hospitals and electric-aviation firm magniX; he also funds good-governance work.
interesting_fact: Clermont owns magniX, maker of electric powertrains and energy storage for aircraft, which won a $74M five-year NASA contract in 2021 for electrified aircraft propulsion research.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Matangi, New Zealand, the son of a beekeeper, he went on to found the Chandler Institute of Governance in Singapore (2019), which publishes the annual Chandler Good Government Index ranking 100+ countries.
notes: Private; no published email found. magniX (electric aviation) gives a natural energy-angle hook. Background sourced from Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Chandler_(businessman)

name: Alfred Gantner
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Partners Group (Baar-Zug, Switzerland); Chairman, Breitling SA (since Dec 2022)
profile: Swiss private-equity investor ('Fredy') who co-founded Partners Group in 1996 at age 28 with Goldman Sachs colleagues Marcel Erni and Urs Wietlisbach; he was CEO to 2005 and chairman 2005-2014. The firm listed in 2006 and manages $150bn+; he holds ~5%, chairs the founders' multi-family office PG3 and chairs Partners Group-owned watchmaker Breitling.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Partners Group banned staff from using the word 'deal', to push them to think like founders and long-term owners rather than short-term transaction investors.
deep_cut_fact: He started out with a banking apprenticeship at Cantrade Privatbank (a former UBS subsidiary) before his BYU MBA, and in 2002 helped with Swiss public relations for the Salt Lake City Winter Olympics.

public_contacts.value: Prosek Partners (Partners Group, Americas media): Pro-PartnersGroup@prosek.com

notes: Publicly outspoken on Swiss-EU relations (co-leads the Kompass/Europa business network), so open to media on policy topics. Partners Group invests heavily in infrastructure/energy platforms - possible podcast angle. Current PG board status per Wikipedia; verify against latest annual report.

name: Marcel Erni
current_role: Co-founder and large shareholder, Partners Group (Zug); long-time board member (verify current seat)
profile: Swiss financier who co-founded Partners Group in 1996 with Alfred Gantner and Urs Wietlisbach after stints at McKinsey and Goldman Sachs Zurich. The firm grew from a tiny Ikea-desk office into a global private-markets manager with $185bn+ AUM, listed since 2006; Erni holds ~5%. Chicago Booth MBA '91 and St. Gallen PhD.
interesting_fact: He has described Partners Group's start as 'no money, no clients, no clue'; the founders' original plan was just three partners, one or two deals a year, and time for skiing.
deep_cut_fact: At Chicago Booth he was in Merton Miller's finance class when Miller learned he had won the Nobel Prize, and he loves art: 'If you haven't seen the Seurat (A Sunday on La Grande Jatte) at the Art Institute, you haven't been to Chicago.'
notes: Lowest-profile of the three founders; Partners Group is a big infrastructure investor (incl. data centers/energy), good podcast angle. Could not confirm his 2025-26 board status (search budget exhausted).

name: Cristiano Crippa
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan: TPRO), since 2017
profile: Cristiano Crippa co-founded Technoprobe with his father Giuseppe Crippa (an ex-SGS/STMicroelectronics manager, d. 2025), which makes probe cards that test microchips; it is now the world's No. 2 probe-card maker with ~2,700 staff. Technoprobe listed in Milan in 2022 and later joined the FTSE MIB; Cristiano owns about 18% and has chaired the board since 2017.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Technoprobe became the first company in Italy to open a COVID vaccination hub for the general public inside its premises: a 4,300 m2 space where 160,000 doses were given to local residents over six months.
deep_cut_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco), while his father was still working at SGS/ST; in 1997 it bought its first building in nearby Cernusco Lombardone and moved in with about 10 employees.
notes: Founding year differs by source (Forbes: 1989 with his father; company history: garage start 1993, incorporated 1996). Family-run, low media profile; press@technoprobe.com is the published route. Father Giuseppe died July 2025 - avoid leading with that.

name: Roberto Crippa
current_role: Vice President (and Vice Chairman of the Board), Technoprobe S.p.A.
profile: Roberto Crippa is the son of the late Giuseppe Crippa (d. 2025), who founded probe-card maker Technoprobe in his garage in 1989. Roberto joined in 2002, ran Italian operations and has been Vice President since 2013; Technoprobe, whose probe cards test chips before packaging (including for AI processors), listed on Euronext Milan in 2022 and Roberto owns about 18%.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe began in 1989 in Giuseppe Crippa's garage and attic while he was still working at STMicroelectronics; it became a global top probe-card supplier and made the founder a billionaire in his late 80s.
deep_cut_fact: A chemical engineer from Politecnico di Milano, he started in a technical product-development role and is author or co-author of numerous international patents; in 2018 he and brother Cristiano led the 100% acquisition of hydraulics-components engineer DA-TOR, starting a diversification into an Italian industrial hub.
notes: Forbes named him among Italy's top 100 managers in 2019. Gave a 2023 interview to Corriere della Sera's L'Economia (https://technoprobe.com/news-and-press/news-events-publications/leconomia-interview-with-roberto-crippa). Company is in Cernusco Lombardone (Lecco). info@ is a general company address.

name: Augusto Perfetti
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Giorgio) of Perfetti Van Melle, the Italian-Dutch confectionery group headquartered in Lainate (Italy) and Breda (Netherlands)
profile: Son of Ambrogio Perfetti, who started a chewing-gum business near Milan with brother Egidio in 1946. Augusto and Giorgio grew it, notably through the 2001 Van Melle merger, into Perfetti Van Melle: Mentos, Chupa Chups, Airheads, Brooklyn and Mondelez's former gum brands (Trident, Dentyne). Revenue is over $4.8bn. Professional managers run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: He named his yacht and private jet after Mentos and Airheads, the company's best-selling brands. His father and uncle were inspired to start the business after seeing American WWII soldiers bring gum to Europe.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2026, for the company's 80th anniversary, Lainate named a square near the plant 'Largo Ambrogio ed Egidio Perfetti'. A giant replica of the first Brooklyn gum pack ('la gomma del ponte', launched 1956) was unveiled there.
notes: He keeps a very low public profile and I found no interviews. The company route goes through Perfetti Van Melle corporate communications (no press email is published; the contact page lists a data-protection address only). Corrado Bianchi is CEO of PVM Italia.

name: Kim Beom-su
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder of Kakao Corp. (Seoul); left the chairmanship and board in 2022 (any 2026 executive role not confirmed)
profile: Also known as Brian Kim. He grew up poor in Seoul, studied engineering at Seoul National University, founded online gaming portal Hangame (merged with Naver to form NHN) and launched KakaoTalk in 2010, now on about 90% of Korean smartphones. Kakao expanded into payments, mobility, games and banking, and he backs startups through K Cube Ventures.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he became one of the first Korean signers of the Giving Pledge, committing more than half his wealth to charity. He paid his way through college as a private tutor, sometimes skipping meals to save money.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a developer for an online communication service at Samsung's IT services unit. Hangame, founded in 1998 with $184,000 from friends and family, started as an internet café business before becoming Korea's first online gaming portal. In 2006 he set up IWILAB, a Mountain View incubator for Korean founders.
notes: Avoid the 2024 SM Entertainment stock case (acquitted Oct 2025) and gambling allegations. No published personal channel found. Kakao's press room is the corporate media route; its media contact details load dynamically and were not captured. Web search budget ran out before his 2026 role could be checked.

name: Remo Ruffini
current_role: Executive Chairman, Moncler S.p.A. (since 1 April 2026, when Bartolomeo Rongone became CEO); controls holding company Double R
profile: Como-born Remo Ruffini (b. 1961) took over near-bankrupt Moncler in 2003 and turned it into a global luxury brand, listing it in Milan in 2013 and buying Stone Island for about EUR 1.15B in 2020. He owns roughly 15% via Double R and in 2026 moved from chairman-CEO to executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Moncler's December 2013 IPO was one of Italy's largest in years; shares jumped 47% on the first afternoon, putting Ruffini on the Forbes billionaires list in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: At 23, after working in the U.S. for his father's company Gianfranco Ruffini Ltd, he went home to Como and founded his own label, New England, which he sold to the Stefanel Group 16 years later.
notes: Moncler Group site (press and IR contact pages) blocked automated access; press/IR contacts are listed there under Media / Investor Relations and on Moncler press releases. No verified personal social accounts found.

name: Mark Hancock
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Vice Chairman, PACS Group (NYSE: PACS); head of family office PV3 Investments
profile: Hancock co-founded Utah-based skilled-nursing operator PACS Group with Jason Murray in 2013. It grew from two facilities to more than 300 in 17 states and listed on the NYSE in 2024; he owns about 35%. He previously worked as an analyst at Ford, a director at a steel company and treasurer of a financial-services firm.
interesting_fact: In 2024 his family office PV3 Investments bought Utah carbon bike-component maker ENVE Composites from Amer Sports.
deep_cut_fact: Before buying ENVE, Hancock was a longtime customer and cycling enthusiast. ENVE's GM said he owns two custom ENVE road bikes and lives about 20 minutes from the Ogden factory, and called the deal 'an investment, not a private equity' play.
notes: Low media profile. Cycling and ENVE make a natural, friendly opening. Be aware that PACS has faced public accounting and short-seller scrutiny since late 2024.

name: Michael S. Smith
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Freeport LNG (Houston); director, Teledyne Technologies
profile: Made his first fortune with Basin Exploration, an E&P company he founded in Fort Collins in 1981 and sold to Stone Energy in 2001 for ~$428M. He founded Freeport LNG in 2002 as an import terminal, then flipped it to exports when shale arrived, raising $15B+ of debt to build three liquefaction trains in Freeport, Texas (~15 Mtpa). He still runs it and speaks publicly on U.S. LNG export economics.
interesting_fact: Freeport LNG was designed to import gas; when the shale boom hit he turned the strategy 180 degrees and built one of the largest U.S. LNG export terminals instead.
deep_cut_fact: Though he left CSU just shy of a chemistry degree, his 2016 $13M gift to Colorado State created 50 full-tuition business scholarships for the college's 50th anniversary and completed funding for the Michael Smith Natural Resources Building; he credited 'strong science and mathematics' at CSU for teaching him the oil business.
notes: Company is private. Freeport LNG press releases list media contact Heather Browne, Director Corporate Communications (phone 713-980-2888, office line), e.g. https://freeportlng.com/files/docs/FINAL-Restart-Press-Release-022123-2.pdf. Info@ email dates from a 2018 release. Speaks at CERAWeek/Milken - conference route possible.

name: Hubertus Benteler
current_role: Member of the supervisory board (former CEO), Benteler International AG, Salzburg
profile: Fourth-generation owner of Benteler International, which grew from Carl Benteler's 1876 ironware shop in Bielefeld into a roughly $9bn-revenue maker of automotive components, steel tubes and engineering equipment. He led the group from 1991, turning it into a global auto supplier, and moved to the supervisory board in 2017. Son Casper is expected to lead the family eventually.
interesting_fact: Benteler marks 150 years in 2026; the business began as a small ironware shop opened by Carl Benteler in Bielefeld, Germany, in 1876.
deep_cut_fact: Benteler's official timeline dates his era to 1991, when he took over management and remade the company into a global automotive partner. Its first Mexican plant opened in Puebla in 1992, and the Liberec (Czech) brownfield plant followed in 1995.
notes: Private family. Alive is inferred from Hurun Global 2026 and Forbes listings; no obituary was found. The press page loads its contacts dynamically, so no press email was captured. Corporate communications is the realistic route.

name: Eddie Zakay
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Topland Group (London); brother Sol Zakay is Founder & CEO
profile: Eddie Zakay and his brother Sol built Topland Group, a privately owned London property and investment group, starting in the UK in the 1980s/90s. Topland made its name with counter-cyclical bets and large sale-and-leaseback deals with Marks & Spencer, Tesco and Eroski, and sold its 26 Hallmark hotels in 2019. Today it runs a multi-billion-pound portfolio, a bridging-loan arm and a roughly GBP 0.8bn development pipeline.
interesting_fact: Between 2000 and 2010 Topland completed more than GBP 1.5 billion of sale-and-leasebacks with retailers including Marks & Spencer, Tesco, Sainsbury's, Aldi and Eroski.
deep_cut_fact: In the 2010s Topland moved beyond property into renewable-energy investing, and was an early aggregator of UK supported-living housing before selling the portfolio to long-term holders including Civitas.

public_contacts.value: 'Contact Eddie' form on Topland's People page

notes: Very private; no personal social accounts found. Topland's site has a dedicated per-person contact form for Eddie, which is the best published route. The renewable-energy angle could fit the podcast. Web search quota ran out here; facts come from the company site.

name: Sol Zakay
current_role: Founder and CEO, Topland Group (London)
profile: Israeli-born British property investor (b. 1952) who founded Topland Group with his brother Eddie in the early 1990s (incorporated 1991). Topland made its name on large sale-and-leaseback deals with M&S, Tesco, Sainsbury's, Aldi and Eroski (over £1.5bn in 2000-10). It then expanded into hotels (exited 2019), bridging finance and development, and now has a £0.8bn development pipeline.
interesting_fact: Topland describes itself as a pioneer of UK alternative real-estate lending. It was also an original aggregator of UK supported-living housing, building a portfolio before selling to long-term holders including Civitas.
deep_cut_fact: In the 2010s Topland moved beyond property into renewable-energy investment alongside its real-estate activities. That history fits the podcast's energy angle well.
notes: Very private, with no social accounts. The Topland website has a 'Contact Sol' form on the People page, which is the most direct published route. The company has a past legal dispute with the UK Ministry of Justice (2012); do not raise it.

name: Johan Johannson
current_role: Chairman (since 2022) and co-owner, NorgesGruppen ASA (Norway)
profile: Fifth-generation heir to a trading business founded in 1866 by an earlier Johan Johannson from Askim. With his father Knut Hartvig Johannson he controls about 75% of NorgesGruppen (Kiwi, Meny, Spar, Joker; ~40% of Norway's grocery market). A BI business graduate, he joined the family firm in 1995, ran retail, property and new ventures, and succeeded his father as chairman in 2022.
interesting_fact: The family business began in 1866 as a coffee importer/wholesaler (known for the Ali Kaffe brand) before evolving into Norway's largest grocery group.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent 1991-1995 as a consultant at Andersen Consulting (now Accenture); his uncle Torbjorn Johannson recruited him in 1995 to be the day-to-day driving force of holding company Joh. Johannson. He is also a certified retail worker (butikkfagarbeider).
notes: Forbes bio is outdated: he is now chairman (father stepped down 2022). Family keeps a low profile. Press emails are named NorgesGruppen communications staff listed in its NTB press room.

name: Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi
current_role: Shareholder/heir in Diagnósticos da América SA (Dasa); no public executive role found
profile: Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi is the daughter of Edson de Godoy Bueno (d. 2017), who co-founded Brazilian health insurer Amil and sold most of it to UnitedHealth for $4.9 billion in 2012. She and her brother Pedro Bueno (Dasa's president) inherited large stakes in lab-diagnostics group Dasa. She keeps a very low public profile; listed as UK-resident.
interesting_fact: Her father Edson Bueno, Brazil's richest healthcare billionaire, sold Amil to UnitedHealth for $4.9 billion in 2012, the source of the family's fortune.
notes: Very private; no personal public presence found. Only route is via Dasa IR (company contact, not hers). Low fit for the podcast.

name: Prasert Prasarttong-Osoth
profile: Died 21 April 2026, aged 93. He was a former surgeon who co-founded Bangkok Dusit Medical Services in 1972 and founded Bangkok Airways. Son Puttipong now leads the airline and daughter Poramaporn is president of BDMS.
notes: Deceased (21 Apr 2026), per Khaosod English and Nation Thailand (https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40065318). Profile skipped as per the instructions. For BDMS or Bangkok Airways, contact the next generation instead.

name: Vildan Gulcelik
current_role: Shareholder in ENKA İnşaat ve Sanayi A.Ş. (Gülçelik/Tara founding families); no executive role found
profile: Vildan Gülçelik is one of more than a dozen family members who hold shares in ENKA, one of Turkey's largest construction and energy companies. Sarık Tara and his brother-in-law Şadi Gülçelik cofounded ENKA in 1957. Today it is Turkey's leading private electricity producer and also has real estate (including large Moscow office and retail holdings), tourism and trade businesses.
interesting_fact: For roughly 20 years ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. embassy and consular buildings, with projects from Algeria and Nepal to Equatorial Guinea, the Dominican Republic and the Netherlands.
notes: Passive family shareholder with no public profile; her exact relationship to cofounder Şadi Gülçelik and her current status could not be confirmed (Forbes now lists her profile as former). ENKA's only published contact is the general corporate inbox. The energy angle (ENKA's gas-fired power plants) would go better through ENKA management (CEO Agah Mehmet Tara).

name: Jonathan Harmsworth (4th Viscount Rothermere)
current_role: Chairman, Daily Mail and General Trust (DMGT)
profile: Fourth-generation Harmsworth to run the Daily Mail empire; became chairman of DMGT in 1998 on his father's death. Built MailOnline into one of the world's most-read news sites, took DMGT private in 2021 (~£1.6bn), and in Nov 2025 agreed a £500m deal to buy The Telegraph, which faced a UK public-interest/competition review from Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: DMGT owned energy-market data firm Genscape (bought 2006 for ~$130m) and sold it to Verisk/Wood Mackenzie in 2019 for $364m, a useful energy-data angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Educated at Gordonstoun in Scotland, he went to university in the US, studying history at Duke University, before joining the family's Associated Newspapers.
notes: Very private, rarely interviewed. Telegraph deal status after the 2026 regulatory review not confirmed here; check before outreach. Route via DMGT PR.

name: Susan Williams
current_role: Independent Director, W.W. Grainger (since 2020); President, Donald Slavik Family Foundation; Director, Mark IV Capital
profile: Susan Slavik Williams owns about 5% of industrial distributor W.W. Grainger and has sat on its board since April 2020, serving on the nominating and compensation committees. She has been a director of Newport Beach real-estate firm Mark IV Capital since 1989, and she leads the Donald Slavik Family Foundation, which focuses on wildlife and environmental education.
interesting_fact: As president of the Donald Slavik Family Foundation since 1995, she funds wildlife conservation in North America and Africa. She also sits on the board of the St. Louis Zoo.
deep_cut_fact: Before her board career she was a manager at Capgemini US. With her husband Felix she ran a custom home-electronics firm, The Screening Room, for about 10 years. She also founded Four Palms Ventures LLC.
notes: Low public profile. Grainger corporate communications or the investor-relations page is the only published route. The deep-cut details come from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener) plus Forbes; confirm them in Grainger's proxy before using.

name: Ted Turner
notes: Died May 6, 2026, aged 87 (AP). Source: https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/may/6/ted-turner-cnn-founder-brash-outspoken-television-pioneer-died-age-87/. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Girdharilal Bawri
current_role: Chairman and co-founder, Macleods Pharmaceuticals (Mumbai)
profile: Girdharilal Bawri co-founded Macleods Pharmaceuticals in 1986 with brothers Rajendra Agarwal and Banwarilal Bawri; the family had owned a pharmacy in Jaipur. Privately held Macleods began with anti-TB drugs and is now a top-10 Indian pharma firm selling generics (HIV, malaria, diabetes, cardio, respiratory) in 170+ countries. Brother and MD Rajendra Agarwal died in November 2025.
interesting_fact: The company is named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks; the three brothers and their families lived together in the same Mumbai building.
deep_cut_fact: Macleods built its business on first- and second-line tuberculosis medicines and became a key exporter of affordable TB drugs; its first R&D centre opened in Mumbai in 2000.
notes: No interviews found; very low media profile. Family recently lost co-founder Rajendra Agarwal (Nov 2025) — be sensitive in timing/tone. Route via Macleods corporate office (contact page is JS-rendered; check https://www.macleodspharma.com/contact-us in a browser).

name: Xie Zhikun
profile: Founder of Beijing-based Zhongzhi Enterprise Group (est. 1995), who started in timber and real estate before building a large wealth-management/shadow-banking business. He died of a heart attack in Beijing on 18 December 2021, aged 61.
notes: DECEASED 18 Dec 2021 (heart attack, Beijing) - sources: https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3160259/chinese-rags-riches-tycoon-xie-zhikun-dies-aged-61 ; https://yicaiglobal.com/news/20211220-03---shares-of-firms-controlled-by-china-zhongzhi-dive-on-founder-sudden-death . Zhongzhi later collapsed and entered liquidation (2023-24). Not a podcast candidate.

name: Ravi Ruia
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Essar Group (senior family figure since brother Shashi's death in Nov 2024)
profile: Co-founded Essar with elder brother Shashi in 1969, growing it from a Chennai port construction contract into a conglomerate spanning steel, oil refining, power, ports and telecom. Essar bought the Stanlow refinery (Essar Oil UK, now EET Fuels) from Shell in 2011 and sold its Indian refiner to a Rosneft-led group for $12.9bn in 2017; it now pursues energy-transition projects at Stanlow.
interesting_fact: The name Essar comes from the brothers' initials, 'S' and 'R' (Shashi and Ravi); the group's first job was a 1969 contract worth about Rs 2.3 crore to build an outer breakwater for Chennai (Madras) Port.
deep_cut_fact: He is a mechanical engineer by training, a graduate of the College of Engineering, Guindy in Chennai - India's oldest engineering college (founded 1794) - and was singled out as one of its six most notable alumni when it turned 225 in 2018.
notes: Essar's corporate press contacts are on essar.com press releases (Essar Capital corporate affairs) and EET Fuels (Stanlow) releases, but those sites blocked automated fetching, so no email was verified. Forbes profile is joint with Shashi Ruia (died 2024). Best route: Essar corporate affairs office.

name: Walter Faria
current_role: Owner and controlling shareholder, Grupo Petrópolis (Itaipava, Crystal, Petra, Black Princess beers), Brazil
profile: Brazilian brewer (b. 1955, Pedranópolis, SP) who went from a cotton gin to Brazil's largest Schincariol distributor, then bought Cervejaria Petrópolis in 1998 at ~2% market share; by 2013 Itaipava made it Brazil's No. 2 brewer. The group also makes TNT energy drink - likely the source of the 'energy' tag, not the energy sector.
interesting_fact: Under Faria, Grupo Petrópolis grew from about 2% of Brazil's beer sales in 1998 to over 11% and the No. 2 national brand in 2013, largely through aggressive marketing and low prices.
deep_cut_fact: At 13, in the Macedônia district of Fernandópolis (SP), he sold eggs and piglets around town using a horse cart - a cart he kept as a keepsake. His savings then funded a coffee-processing business with a brother.

public_contacts.value: VCRP Brasil (press relations for Grupo Petrópolis, South/Southeast, appointed 2024)

notes: Very private, gives no interviews. Carries significant legal baggage (Lava Jato 2019 arrest; group filed for judicial recovery in 2023) - poor fit and sensitive; avoid these topics. Weak link to the energy theme (beverages only). Company site blocks automated access; press route is via the group's PR agencies.

name: Garibaldi Thohir
current_role: Vice President Commissioner, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (formerly Adaro Energy; stepped down as President Director at the June 2025 AGM)
profile: Garibaldi 'Boy' Thohir, son of Astra co-founder Teddy Thohir and brother of Erick Thohir, led the 2005 takeover of coal miner Adaro and ran it for ~2 decades, steering it toward aluminium smelting, minerals and renewables (now AlamTri; coal spun off as AADI in 2024). He is also a tech investor (ex-Gojek commissioner).
interesting_fact: He served as president commissioner of Gojek after founder Nadiem Makarim joined the cabinet in 2019, and has said he advised Nadiem informally for years before Gojek scaled.
deep_cut_fact: Back from his US MBA, he wanted a $2,000-a-month job at Citibank, but his father refused and told him to be an entrepreneur. His first venture (1991) was a plan to build a rental office on a 3,000 m2 plot along the new Saharjo-Kuningan road in Jakarta; it stalled because land clearances required at least 1 hectare.
notes: Widely known as 'Boy Thohir'. corsec@ is AlamTri's corporate secretary (company office, not personal). Some data sites still list him as President Director - outdated since June 2025. Energy-transition angle: AlamTri is building an aluminium smelter and hydro/renewables in North Kalimantan.

name: Semahat Arsel
current_role: Chair, Vehbi Koç Foundation board & executive committee; board member, Koç Holding; chair, Divan Group
profile: Semahat Sevim Arsel (b. 1928, Ankara) is the eldest child of Koç Group founder Vehbi Koç and holds a stake in Koç Holding, Turkey's largest conglomerate (energy via Tüpraş, Aygaz, autos, appliances, banking). On Koç's board since 1964, she built its tourism/hospitality arm and leads the family's main foundation.
interesting_fact: Turkey's only postgraduate nursing education center, SANERC (founded 1992 at the American Hospital, Istanbul), is named after her; she has chaired the Vehbi Koç Foundation's Nursing Committee since its nursing fund began in 1974.
deep_cut_fact: In 1972 she took charge of renovating Istanbul's Divan Hotel in Elmadağ and went on to turn 'Divan' into a luxury hospitality brand; she also co-founded TUGEV, a foundation for tourism training, and lived in Germany in 1959-60, studying at the Goethe Institute.
notes: Aged 98 and very private; no personal public channels. Best route is via the Vehbi Koç Foundation or Koç Holding corporate communications. Koç's energy link (Tüpraş refining, Aygaz, Entek power) is the podcast angle.

name: Lukas Henrik Lundin
profile: Swedish-Canadian resource financier who chaired the Lundin Group of mining and energy companies for 25+ years (Lundin Mining, Lucara Diamond, Filo Mining, NGEx etc.); family holdings were held via the Nemesia trust vehicle. He died on 26 July 2022 in Geneva, aged 64, after a two-year battle with brain cancer.
notes: Deceased 26 July 2022 (sources: https://www.mining.com/?p=1096241 ; https://filomining.mediaroom.com/2022-07-27-Filo-Minings-Founder-and-Former-Chairman-Lukas-H-Lundin-Passes-Away). Sons Adam and Jack Lundin now lead Lundin Group companies; the Lundin family remains long-term shareholders.

name: Henrik Mads Clausen
current_role: Shareholder of Danfoss A/S (no public executive or board role found)
profile: Born 1953, one of five children of Danfoss founder Mads Clausen and Bitten Clausen. He is listed as a direct owner of Danfoss alongside Clausen Controls A/S and the Bitten & Mads Clausen Foundation (largest shareholder). Danfoss, based in Nordborg, Denmark, makes drives, cooling, heating and power solutions, including for data centers.
interesting_fact: Danfoss was founded by his father Mads Clausen in 1933 in a farmhouse attic on the island of Als; the company now leads in energy-efficient cooling, drives and heat pumps.

public_contacts.value: lars.lohff@danfoss.com (Lars Grubak Lohff, Head of Media Relations, Danfoss)

notes: Very private; no public role. Family is represented on the Danfoss board by third-generation Mads Clausen and Mads-Peter Clausen - better interview targets for an energy/data-center podcast. Approach via Danfoss media relations.

name: Arvindkumar Poddar
current_role: CEO & Managing Director (chairman & MD in earlier filings), Balkrishna Industries Ltd (BKT Tires), Mumbai
profile: Arvind Poddar controls and runs Balkrishna Industries (BKT), the Mumbai-listed maker of off-highway tyres for agriculture, mining and earthmoving. BKT opened its first off-highway tyre plant in Aurangabad in 1987 and sells mainly into replacement markets in Europe and North America. It held about 8% of the global off-the-road tyre segment in 2014 and supplies OEMs such as JCB, John Deere and CNH.
interesting_fact: Under Poddar, BKT became a major sports sponsor: the official tyre of Monster Jam since 2014 and title sponsor of Italy's Serie BKT and France's Ligue 2 BKT (extended to 2028). In October 2026 it announced a 50:50 joint venture with Pirelli to make Pirelli-branded premium tyres in India.
notes: Web search budget ran out at this point, so research came from Wikipedia and BKT's site only and no sourced deep-cut fact was found. BKT runs a registration-only Press Hub for journalists, which is the logical route. The investor-relations email is in stock-exchange filings but was not verified here.

name: Sandeep Pravinbhai Engineer
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Astral Limited (Ahmedabad)
profile: Sandeep Engineer is a first-generation entrepreneur and chemical engineer. He spent eight years in pharmaceutical bulk drugs before founding Astral Poly Technik in 1996, now Astral Ltd, a leading Indian maker of plastic pipes and building materials. He has since expanded into adhesives (Resinova, 2014), water tanks (Sarita, 2020) and paints (Gem Paints).
interesting_fact: In 1998 Astral launched CPVC piping in India for the first time. Plastic pipes were then barely accepted against metal, so Engineer spent years educating plumbers and builders to create the category Astral now leads.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a project engineer at a pharmaceuticals company, then became a distributor and later manufactured pharmaceutical remedies. He said he had been fascinated by polymers since his graduation days, which led to the pivot into piping. He also completed Harvard Business School's OPM programme.
notes: Self-made founder story with a strong entrepreneurship angle. His wife Jagruti Engineer is a whole-time director. Contact is through Astral corporate (info@) or company secretary or IR via the investors page.

name: Rafique Abdul Malik
current_role: Chairman, Metro Brands Limited (Mumbai)
profile: Indian footwear retailer who turned the single Colaba, Mumbai shoe store his father Malik Tejani acquired in 1955 into Metro Brands, one of India's largest and most profitable footwear chains (~800 stores) with Metro Shoes, Mochi and Walkway plus franchises for Crocs, FitFlop, Fila and Foot Locker. Metro Brands is listed; daughter Farah Malik Bhanji is MD and Nissan Joseph CEO.
interesting_fact: Metro started as one standalone shoe shop in Colaba, Mumbai, and over three generations grew into a 'Made in India' footwear house of brands with roughly 800 stores.
deep_cut_fact: He has been chairman since 19 January 1977, the month Metro Shoes was incorporated, giving him nearly five decades at the helm; the company bio also notes he is a Harvard alumnus.
notes: Low public profile; daughter and MD Farah Malik Bhanji is the usual public face. The company site has a Media section that may list a PR contact.

name: Cecilia Morel
current_role: Former First Lady of Chile (2010-14, 2018-22); heir to the Piñera family fortune (family investment group Bancard)
profile: Cecilia Morel Montes is the widow of former Chilean president and billionaire investor Sebastián Piñera (d. 2024), whose fortune came from introducing credit cards to Chile and stakes including LATAM Airlines; Hurun lists her as holder of the family wealth. A trained family and youth counsellor, she chaired social foundations such as Integra and PRODEMU as First Lady.
interesting_fact: She was at the San José mine site with the president throughout the October 2010 rescue of the 33 trapped Copiapó miners, famously moved to tears when the first miner surfaced.
deep_cut_fact: In 1989, with professionals from the Instituto Carlos Casanueva, she founded 'La Casa de la Juventud', running personal-development workshops for young people in Santiago's Conchalí district; the project later spun off the Women Embark Foundation.
notes: Not an entrepreneur in her own right; wealth is inherited from Sebastián Piñera (family vehicle Grupo Bancard). No published personal/office contact verified (search budget exhausted). Recently widowed (2024) - handle sensitively. Weak fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast.

name: Jogi Hendra Atmadja
current_role: Founder and President Commissioner (chairman), PT Mayora Indah Tbk
profile: Jakarta-born (1946) University of Indonesia economics graduate who founded Mayora with his siblings in 1977, starting with a biscuit factory in Tangerang. Mayora now owns 50+ brands including Kopiko, Danisa, Beng-Beng, Torabika and Energen, runs 25 factories and exports to 100+ countries; son Andre Sukendra Atmadja is president director.
interesting_fact: Through its Kopiko brand, Mayora is often described as the world's largest coffee-candy maker; Kopiko is exported to more than 100 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Mayora, he started his career as a banker at Bank Central Asia.
notes: Very low public profile, in his late 70s. Deep-cut fact cited via Wikipedia to a Jakarta Post article that was paywalled/403 for me - verify before use. Mayora's published consumer email (consumer@mayora.co.id) is consumer-care only, not a press route.

name: Zhou Guodi
current_role: Listed by Hurun (with Cao Longxiang) as a principal owner of Jumpcan Pharmaceutical (济川药业, SSE: 600566), Taixing, Jiangsu
profile: Hurun lists Zhou Guodi together with Cao Longxiang as owners of Jumpcan Pharmaceutical. Jumpcan is a Jiangsu drugmaker with 4,000+ staff, focused on respiratory, paediatric, digestive and women's health, including the Pudilan brand. It went from state-owned to private in 1998 and listed in Shanghai via a 2013 reverse listing. I couldn't independently verify her personal role.
interesting_fact: Jumpcan went from state-owned to private shareholding in 1998 and first entered China's top-100 pharmaceutical manufacturers in 2001. It has since struck licensing deals for innovative drugs (e.g. with I-Mab in 2021 and Akeso in 2025).
notes: My web search quota ran out at this point, so verification is limited to the company site. Neither the company site nor any source I could reach names her. Cao Longxiang is the better-known figure (understood to be her husband/co-owner, not verified here). jc@jumpcan.com is the general/customer-service address.

name: Douglas Hsu Hsu-Tung
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Far Eastern Group (Taipei); re-elected chairman of Asia Cement in 2026
profile: Douglas Tong Hsu (徐旭東) is the son of founder Yu-Ziang Hsu and heads Far Eastern Group, a Taiwanese conglomerate of about 250 companies and nine listed firms. Its businesses span petrochemicals and energy (including Chiahui Power), polyester, cement, telecom (Far EasTone), banking, retail (SOGO, Far Eastern Department Stores) and hotels. Son Jeff Hsu debuted as group Chief Innovation Officer at 2026 AGMs.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Far Eastern New Century became the world's third-largest polyester textile maker (2018), and the group's family foundations established leading private universities and a medical-centre hospital in Taiwan.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his BA and MA at the University of Notre Dame, where he is an Emeritus Trustee, followed by postgraduate study at Columbia. His Committee of 100 profile calls him an 'architecture devotee' and collector of modern art and sculpture who enjoys diving and swimming.
notes: No personal or press email published on the FEG site (the only email listed is a mall customer-service address, so it is excluded). Energy and telecom holdings make him a podcast fit; best route is via group corporate communications or Far EasTone/FENC investor relations. Member of the Committee of 100 since 2005.

name: Maria Dolores Mantegazza
current_role: Heir and shareholder of the Globus family of travel brands (Globus, Cosmos, Avalon Waterways, Monograms; U.S. arm Group Voyagers); trustee, Sergio Mantegazza Charitable Foundation
profile: Maria Dolores Mantegazza (b. 1956) is the daughter of Sergio Mantegazza (1927-2024), longtime owner-chairman of Lugano-based Globus, the escorted-tour group behind Globus, Cosmos, Avalon Waterways and Monograms. She appeared on Hurun's 2024 global list after inheriting a share of the family fortune on her father's death in February 2024.
interesting_fact: The Globus travel empire traces back to 1928, when her grandfather Antonio Mantegazza started out with a single gondola carrying tourists and goods on Lake Lugano.
deep_cut_fact: She is a trustee, with Fabio and Geo Mantegazza, of the Sergio Mantegazza Charitable Foundation in Canton Ticino, which supports arts, youth sports, education and medical charities.
notes: Extremely private; no interviews or public channels found. Alive status inferred from Hurun 2024 listing, not independently confirmed (web-search budget exhausted). Globus press pages blocked automated access; best route is the Globus/Group Voyagers corporate press office.

name: TS Kalyanaraman
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd
profile: Born in Thrissur, Kerala in 1947, Kalyanaraman came from a family textile business founded by his grandfather in 1909. He opened the first Kalyan Jewellers store in Thrissur in 1993 and built it into one of India's largest jewellery chains, with stores in India and the Gulf. The company listed in 2021. He also runs Kalyan Developers.
interesting_fact: He opened the first Kalyan Jewellers showroom in Thrissur on 18 April 1993, after two decades in the family's textile retail business, Kalyan Silks.
deep_cut_fact: He was named after his grandfather T. S. Kalyanarama Iyer, who started the family business in 1909. He began learning trade at age 12 by helping in his father's shop, and in 2023 he published an autobiography, 'The Golden Touch'.
notes: The age-12 detail is from Wikipedia (citing Bloomberg 2013). His autobiography is a good conversation hook. The company's general inbox is the only published email; the IR page lists no separate address.

name: Basudeo Narain Singh
current_role: Executive Chairman, Alkem Laboratories Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Co-founder of Alkem Laboratories, one of India's largest pharma companies (incorporated 1973, listed on BSE/NSE), which he built with his elder brother Samprada Singh. Samprada, the Chairman Emeritus, has died; Basudeo is now Executive Chairman, and the next generation (e.g. MD Sandeep Singh) sits on the board.
interesting_fact: Alkem's own founders' story compares the two brothers' partnership to the Ramayana: 'a tale of two determined brothers' from Bihar who built a company now employing over 23,000 people.
deep_cut_fact: After the Jehanabad district school in Bihar and a degree from Patna University, he had started work as a professor when his brother called him into the business. In the early years he personally delivered stock to stockists and distributors.
notes: Listed as Executive Chairman on Alkem's board page (checked Nov 2026). Low media profile. Corporate head-office and IR channels are the published routes.

name: Guo Jianjun
current_role: Former general manager of Inner Mongolia Huineng Group (汇能集团); left Huineng's management and shareholding in July 2025
profile: Guo Jianjun (郭建军) is the son of Guo Jinshu, who quit as head of the Ordos coal bureau in 2004 to found Huineng Group (coal, coal-to-gas/power, roads, property). As Huineng's GM he led its capital-markets push, including a stake in Asia-Potash International and an offer for ST Xinchao (oil & gas). Hurun listed him 2019-2024; a July 2025 filing says he exited Huineng.
interesting_fact: Hurun ranked him alone under Huineng (coal, roads & bridges, property, Ordos), at No. 224 in 2024 with RMB 22bn, while his father Guo Jinshu remains Huineng's chairman.
deep_cut_fact: In his first media interview he said Huineng would enter capital markets 'in a long-term, good-faith, professional way' and would not take over companies 'like a barbarian' (不会选择'野蛮人'的方式入主).
notes: Identity confirmed (Hurun API: 郭建军/Huineng/Ordos; Sohu Aug 2026). Prior pass confused him with father Guo Jinshu. Per an Asia-Potash filing (July 2025) he left Huineng management/ownership after being penalised for disclosure violations in the ST Xinchao bid, so avoid that topic. No published personal contacts; Huineng is the only org route.

name: Pritviraj Jindal
current_role: Chairperson (Non-Executive), Jindal SAW Ltd. (O.P. Jindal Group)
profile: Prithavi Raj (P.R.) Jindal is the eldest son of O.P. Jindal, founder of the O.P. Jindal Group. When the group was split among the four brothers, he took Jindal SAW, a leading maker of submerged-arc-welded line pipe for oil, gas and water, and the family cross-holdings give him stakes in JSW Steel and other group companies. His daughters Sminu Jindal (MD) and Shraddha (Joint MD) now help run Jindal SAW.
interesting_fact: Jindal SAW credits him with introducing SAW (submerged-arc-welded) pipe manufacturing in India more than four decades ago, helping make India one of the world's leading line-pipe makers.
deep_cut_fact: Besides steel pipes, he is listed as a director of Sonabheel Tea Limited, a tea company, among his other board seats.
notes: Company spells his name 'Prithavi Raj Jindal' (also P.R. Jindal). Listed under UAE by Hurun. Low personal media profile; route through Jindal SAW corporate office (New Delhi). Pipe and energy-infrastructure angle (oil and gas, water) fits the podcast.

name: Patrice Pichet
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO (PDG), Groupe Pichet (Pessac, Gironde)
profile: Bordeaux-born (1959) property developer who started as a salesman for home-builder Maisons Phénix in 1983. He did his first property deal on a Bordeaux plot in 1988 and founded his own developer, Eurobat. Renamed Groupe Pichet in 2004, the family company now develops housing and commercial property across France, especially Île-de-France, and employs about 1,250-1,400 people.
interesting_fact: Groupe Pichet bought Château Les Carmes Haut-Brion (Pessac-Léognan) in 2010; it is the only Bordeaux château with an address inside the city of Bordeaux.
deep_cut_fact: He commissioned Philippe Starck (with architect Luc Arsène-Henry) to design a ship-shaped winery at Les Carmes Haut-Brion. Inaugurated in 2016 at a cost of about €10m, it was the first wine cellar of Starck's career.
notes: French-language outreach is advisable. The Groupe Pichet press office is the best route; the wine estate (les-carmes-haut-brion.com) is a softer conversational hook.

name: Bhushan Dua
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, T-Series (Super Cassettes Industries Pvt Ltd), Mumbai/Noida
profile: Bhushan Kumar Dua (b. 1977, Delhi), son of T-Series founder Gulshan Kumar, took charge of the music label as a teenager in 1997 with his uncle Krishan Kumar. He built T-Series into India's largest music label and a major Bollywood producer (Aashiqui 2, Hindi Medium, Animal, Bhool Bhulaiyaa franchise), and its YouTube channel became one of the world's most-subscribed.
interesting_fact: He is credited as producer on 100+ films since Tum Bin (2001); T-Series' Hindi Medium won him the Filmfare Award for Best Film.
notes: Listed as Bhushan Dua; publicly known as Bhushan Kumar. T-Series site says to contact exclusively via its contact page. Avoid father's 1997 murder and past allegations/tax probe. No sourced deep-cut fact found beyond widely known film credits.

name: Anand Suresh Deshpande
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Persistent Systems (Pune); stepped back from CEO role in 2019
profile: Anand Deshpande (IIT Kharagpur B.Tech; Indiana University PhD, 1989) founded Persistent Systems in Pune in 1990 with about Rs 2 lakh of own and borrowed money and built it into a listed global software/AI engineering firm (Q2 FY27 revenue $487.6M; 2026 takeover offer for Nagarro). Through the family's deAsra Foundation he supports small 'nano-entrepreneurs'.
interesting_fact: deAsra Foundation, named from his family's initials, has supported more than 750,000 nano-entrepreneurs with free help on registrations, finance and business setup.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Persistent he worked as a Member of Technical Staff at Hewlett-Packard Laboratories in Palo Alto (1989-1990), after a database-systems PhD at Indiana University, which later gave him its School of Informatics Career Achievement Award.
notes: Accessible, entrepreneurship-focused founder who speaks often at Indian tech/startup events; strong fit for an entrepreneurship podcast. deAsra (deasra.in) is another route.

name: Devi Prasad Shetty
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Narayana Health (Narayana Hrudayalaya Ltd), Bengaluru
profile: Cardiac surgeon from Karnataka, trained at Kasturba Medical College and Guy's Hospital, London. He founded Narayana Hrudayalaya in Bengaluru in 2001 and grew it into a listed hospital chain, including a facility in the Cayman Islands, built on assembly-line economies of scale. That model has pushed bypass surgery prices to a fraction of US costs, and his family holds a majority stake.
interesting_fact: The Wall Street Journal called him 'the Henry Ford of heart surgery'. His hospitals save money with tricks like cross-ventilation instead of air-conditioning, and their surgeons do 30-35 operations a day.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up the eighth of nine children in Kinnigoli village and chose heart surgery as a schoolboy after hearing of Christiaan Barnard's first heart transplant. In 1992 in Kolkata he performed India's first neonatal heart surgery, on a 21-day-old baby. He also co-designed Yeshasvini, Karnataka's low-cost farmers' health insurance scheme.
notes: Padma Shri (2004) and Padma Bhushan (2012). He speaks often about healthcare economics and frugal innovation, which suits an entrepreneurship podcast. No dedicated press email was found; investor relations is the best published route.

name: Hilmi Panigoro
current_role: President Director, PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MedcoEnergi), Jakarta
profile: Bandung-born geologist and younger brother of Medco founder Arifin Panigoro. Joined Medco as a director in 1998 and has run or overseen it since (President Director 2001-08 and again from 2015). MedcoEnergi spans oil & gas across Southeast Asia, power (incl. geothermal/solar) and a stake in copper-gold miner Amman Mineral.
interesting_fact: Holds an ITB geological engineering degree (1981), Thunderbird MBA core program (1984) and an MSc from the Colorado School of Mines (1988); he has over four decades in oil and gas and leads a company that has set net-zero targets.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1981 as a wellsite geologist at Huffco/Vico Indonesia, rising to VP & Director of Business Process Reengineering before his brother invited him to join Medco as a director in 1998.
notes: Regular speaker at energy conferences (SPE, Singapore International Energy Week) and has given interviews on energy transition, so reachable via MedcoEnergi corporate communications/IR.

name: Mary Vy Ty
current_role: Adviser to the Board, GT Capital Holdings and Metrobank; Honorary Chairman, GT Foundation; Trustee, Metrobank Foundation
profile: Mary Vy Ty is the widow of Metrobank founder George S.K. Ty (d. 2018) and the matriarch of the Ty family. The family controls GT Capital, the Philippine conglomerate behind Metrobank, Toyota Motor Philippines, Federal Land and stakes in Metro Pacific and AXA Philippines. She was GT Capital's Treasurer from its 2007 incorporation and became a Board Adviser in 2014.
interesting_fact: GT Capital, which takes its name from George Ty, combines Metrobank with the Philippine Toyota franchise. It is one of the country's largest listed conglomerates, with interests in banking, cars, property, infrastructure and insurance.
deep_cut_fact: She has more than 50 years of experience in banking and general business, is a University of Santo Tomas graduate, and served as GT Capital's first Treasurer from its incorporation in 2007.
notes: Elderly (her GT Capital bio gives her age as 85) and private, with an advisory rather than executive role. For a business conversation, GT Capital/Metrobank management are the active leaders. The corporate inbox is the realistic route.

name: Maximilian Rudolph von Finck
current_role: Heir/investor in the von Finck family fortune; board member of family holding Clair (per Bilanz)
profile: Middle son (b. c.1969) of the late Bavarian banker-investor August von Finck Jr. (d. Nov 2021), whose fortune included a large SGS (testing/inspection) stake, mostly sold in 2020 ahead of an equal four-way inheritance. Naturalised Swiss (canton Schwyz); Bilanz reports he is mainly active as an entrepreneur in the USA, e.g. in the seed business.
interesting_fact: The family sold SGS shares worth about CHF 2.3bn in 2020, reportedly to split a holding too big to divide equally among August von Finck Jr.'s four children.
notes: Extremely private; almost no public profile and no published contact. Identity matched to the von Finck SGS fortune via Bilanz, but his own business activities are not documented. Hurun listing likely reflects inherited share of the family fortune. Not a realistic podcast target.

name: Diane Goldman
current_role: Co-owner, Solil Management (Goldman family real estate, New York); philanthropist
profile: Diane Goldman Kemper (b. 1946) is a daughter of New York real-estate investor Sol Goldman (d. 1987) and one of four siblings who co-own Solil Management. Solil holds roughly 400 mostly Manhattan properties, including the land under Olympic Tower and the Cartier Building and part of the land under the World Trade Center. Her sister Jane runs day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: Solil's portfolio includes the land under Olympic Tower and the Cartier Building, The Peninsula New York hotel, and about 17% of the land under the World Trade Center complex.
deep_cut_fact: She studied at C.W. Post College and the New York School of Interior Design, and once worked in the family company's residential leasing department. Columbia University has a 'Diane Goldman Kemper Family Professor of Epidemiology in Psychiatry' chair.
notes: Known publicly as Diane Goldman Kemper. The family is famously private (Forbes: 'doesn't want you to know who they are'), and there is ongoing family litigation over Solil, so avoid that topic. She has no published personal or office contact. The only published family entity address is the Lillian Goldman Charitable Trust (postal). Low relevance to an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Jami Gertz
current_role: Co-owner, Atlanta Hawks (with husband Tony Ressler); actress; philanthropist (Ressler-Gertz Foundation)
profile: Jami Gertz is the actress known for The Lost Boys, Less than Zero, Twister and the CBS sitcom Still Standing. Her listed fortune is shared with her husband Tony Ressler, co-founder of Ares Management. Their group bought majority control of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks in 2015 for about $730M, and the couple give through the Ressler-Gertz Foundation to education, Los Angeles and Jewish causes.
interesting_fact: She was discovered by Norman Lear in a nationwide talent search and reportedly turned down the role of Rachel Green on Friends during pre-production.
deep_cut_fact: Between acting jobs she worked in Paris as a scent designer for the fashion house Lanvin. She grew up in Glenview, Illinois, and graduated from Maine East High School.
notes: Private; rarely appears in public. Wealth is through Tony Ressler (Ares Management), who is the better entrepreneurship or podcast angle. No personal or foundation contact was published; the Atlanta Hawks communications office is the institutional route. Gertz is also a Melanoma Research Alliance board member.

name: Sandra Irving
current_role: Philanthropist; co-owner of Irving Oil family interests; advisory board member, Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society (Dartmouth)
profile: Saint John, New Brunswick-born widow of Arthur L. Irving (d. May 2024), longtime chairman of Irving Oil, the private refiner/marketer that runs Canada's largest refinery in Saint John; their daughter Sarah Irving is now the family's leader at the company. Sandra is a major donor to education and medical research in Atlantic Canada and the US.
interesting_fact: With Arthur and Sarah, she co-funded the $80M lead gift that created Dartmouth's Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society, and she sits on its advisory board; she and Arthur were adopted as honorary members of Dartmouth's Class of 1972.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a BA with distinction from the University of New Brunswick and an MA in Political Science from the University of Toronto, and is an honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada; with Arthur she endowed chairs in cardiology and oncology at Massachusetts General Hospital.

public_contacts.value: https://irvingoil.com/en-CA/press-room (Irving Oil press room; media contact listed as Sam Robinson, Public Affairs)

notes: Very private; no personal public channels. Arthur Irving died May 13, 2024. Most plausible routes are Irving Oil Public Affairs or the Dartmouth Irving Institute (energy/society angle fits the podcast).

name: Ilya Sutskever
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI), Palo Alto / Tel Aviv
profile: Soviet-born Israeli-Canadian AI scientist (b. 1986) who co-created AlexNet with Hinton and Krizhevsky, co-founded OpenAI and served as chief scientist through GPT/ChatGPT and o1-style reasoning. He left in 2024 to co-found SSI, which raised $3B+ at a ~$32B valuation; CEO since July 2025. In July 2026 SSI announced an NVIDIA partnership to scale its compute 10x.
interesting_fact: He won the NeurIPS Test of Time Award three years in a row (2022-2024) and received the National Academy of Sciences Award for the Industrial Application of Science in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Jerusalem he began taking Open University of Israel classes in eighth grade; after moving to Canada at 16 he spent only about a month in high school before the University of Toronto admitted him straight into third year.
notes: Very media-shy; rare interviews (e.g. Dwarkesh Podcast, Nov 2025). SSI is compute-heavy (NVIDIA deal, earlier Google Cloud TPUs) - relevant data-center angle. comms@ssi.inc is the only published inquiry address.

name: Andre Desmarais
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Power Corporation of Canada and Power Financial Corporation
profile: André Desmarais (b. 1956, Ottawa) is the youngest son of Paul Desmarais Sr. He and his brother Paul Jr. were co-CEOs of Power Corporation, the Montreal financial holding company, for about 24 years until 2020. He remains deputy chairman and sits on group boards including Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial and Power Sustainable, the group's renewables arm.
interesting_fact: He is honorary chairman of the Canada China Business Council and served on the Hong Kong Chief Executive's Council of International Advisers from 1998 to 2007.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career at Campeau Corporation in 1979 and was a special assistant to Canada's Minister of Justice in 1980-81 before joining Power Corp in 1983. He also started and owned an experimental farm in Canada.

public_contacts.value: Media requests: Stéphane Lemay, VP, General Counsel & Secretary, Power Corporation of Canada (phone listed on contact page; no email published)

notes: No personal social accounts were found. The best route is Power Corporation's media-requests contact. For the energy angle, Power Sustainable (renewables and energy infrastructure) is the relevant group company. The first contact entry is a named media contact with a published phone number only; no email is published.

name: Paul Desmarais Jr.
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Power Corporation of Canada (and Power Financial); also long-time chairman of Groupe Bruxelles Lambert
profile: Eldest son of Power Corp builder Paul Desmarais Sr. (born Sudbury, 1954; McGill BComm, INSEAD MBA). He joined Power Corp in 1981, led the creation of Power Financial in 1984 and was co-CEO of Power Corp from 1996 until stepping back in 2020; he remains chairman. Power's holdings span Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial, GBL, Sagard and Power Sustainable.
interesting_fact: He sat on the boards of major European energy groups, serving as a director of GDF Suez (2008-2014) and of Total until 2017, via the family's stakes held through Pargesa/Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm in 1981 he cut his teeth at S.G. Warburg & Co. in London and at Standard Brands in New York; in 1984 he led the creation of Power Financial Corporation.
notes: Energy angle is Power Sustainable (renewables/infrastructure; media pr@powersustainable.com per its 2025 release, https://powersustainable.com/en/news/power-sustainable-announces-plan-to-invest-and-mobilize-more-than-10-billion-into-canadian-infrastructure-and-related-companies/). Power Corp releases name Stephane Lemay (VP, General Counsel) as contact. Not to be confused with son Paul Desmarais III.

name: Surender Pal Singh Saluja
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Premier Energies Ltd (Hyderabad solar cell & module maker; listed NSE/BSE 2024)
profile: Mechanical engineer who founded Premier Energies in Hyderabad in 1995, starting with solar lanterns and streetlights. The company grew into one of India's largest integrated solar cell and module manufacturers and listed in Sept 2024, making him a billionaire. His son Chiranjeev Singh Saluja is MD; the firm is expanding cell, module and storage capacity.
interesting_fact: Premier Energies began in 1995 selling small solar products such as lanterns and streetlights, decades before India's solar-manufacturing boom; it is now among the country's largest makers of solar cells and modules.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in mechanical engineering from Karnatak University, Dharwad, in 1969 and ran small ventures before solar; he has said his one slight regret is never having worked as an employee at a corporation early in his career.

public_contacts.value: mohit.chawla@premierenergies.com (Mohit Chawla, Marketing & Communications, Premier Energies)

notes: Name also spelled Surendar Singh Saluja. Day-to-day public face of the company is son and MD Chiranjeev Saluja; route through company communications. Strong energy/solar-manufacturing fit.

name: Lee Bass
current_role: Private investor (Lee M. Bass, Inc., Fort Worth); rancher and conservationist; Chairman Emeritus, The Peregrine Fund
profile: Lee M. Bass is one of the four Fort Worth Bass brothers who turned an inheritance from oilman uncle Sid Richardson into multibillion-dollar fortunes through oil and investing; in 2017 the brothers sold their oil company to ExxonMobil for $5.6B in stock. He runs his own investments, raises longhorns on South Texas ranches and is a leading Texas conservation philanthropist.
interesting_fact: He chaired the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission (named chair by Gov. George W. Bush; chairman emeritus since 2001) and with wife Ramona funded the reintroduction of the endangered Aplomado falcon in South Texas; they entered the Texas Conservation Hall of Fame in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He is a founding member of the International Rhino Foundation, and he and Ramona helped found 'South Texas Natives' (now the Texas Native Seeds Program) at the Caesar Kleberg Wildlife Research Institute; he has also chaired the TPWD White-Tailed Deer Advisory Committee.
notes: Very private; no personal website or social accounts found. Plausible indirect routes: The Peregrine Fund (peregrinefund.org) or Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, where he holds honorary/emeritus roles - neither publishes a contact for him personally.

name: Wang Hui (David H. Wang)
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, ACM Research Inc. (Nasdaq: ACMR); chairman of its Shanghai-listed subsidiary ACM Research (Shanghai) / Shengmei Semiconductor (盛美上海)
profile: Tsinghua- and Osaka-trained engineer who founded ACM Research in Silicon Valley in 1998, then built it out in Shanghai as a maker of wafer-cleaning, electroplating, furnace and PECVD equipment for chip fabs. His wealth comes mainly from the Shanghai STAR-listed unit. He still runs the company, which is expanding into advanced-packaging tools.
interesting_fact: EY's 2023 World Entrepreneur Of The Year program (Chinese mainland) credits Wang with inventing stress-free copper polishing and holding more than 100 patents. It says his cleaning technologies can cut use of hazardous chemicals such as sulfuric acid by 50-80%.
deep_cut_fact: Wang entered Tsinghua's precision instruments department in 1978. He first went to Japan to study industrial robotics at the University of Tokyo but was referred to Osaka University because his assigned professor was retiring. After a postdoc at the University of Cincinnati, he worked at Quester Technology (1993-98) before founding ACM.
notes: Known in English as David H. Wang. The IR contacts are at The Blueshirt Group (Steven Pelayo, US; Gary Dvorchak, China). Media contact is Alyssa Lundeen at Bodewell Group. Relevant to AI/data-center chip supply chains.

name: Carl Icahn
current_role: Chairman and controlling holder, Icahn Enterprises L.P. (Nasdaq: IEP); large holder in CVR Energy, CVR Partners, Southwest Gas, Centuri, Monro
profile: Veteran activist investor from Far Rockaway, Queens, who went from Dreyfus stockbroker to buying an NYSE seat in 1968 and became one of Wall Street's most famous corporate raiders. He invests mainly through Icahn Enterprises, whose energy arm CVR Energy (refining, fertilizer) is a core holding; Ted Papapostolou became IEP CEO in May 2026.
interesting_fact: His mother pushed him into medical school; he dropped out of NYU med school after two years because he hated it, joined the Army Reserve, and ended up on Wall Street. He has given about $200M to what is now the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai.
deep_cut_fact: His Princeton philosophy thesis, 'The Problem of Formulating an Adequate Explication of the Empiricist Criterion of Meaning,' won the McCosh Prize; he called writing it 'exhilarating,' said it was the most rewarding part of Princeton, and still keeps a copy. He also worked on the business side of The Daily Princetonian.
notes: Age ~90, now based in Florida (IEP moved HQ to Sunny Isles Beach). IR@ielp.com was the IEP investor contact in Feb 2026 releases; after May 2026 releases list only phone for CEO Ted Papapostolou. X account rarely used recently. Energy angle: CVR Energy/CVR Partners, Southwest Gas.

name: Marina Budiman
current_role: Co-founder & President Commissioner, PT DCI Indonesia Tbk (DCII)
profile: Indonesian tech entrepreneur who co-founded DCI Indonesia in 2011 with Otto Toto Sugiri and Han Arming Hanafia; DCI runs Southeast Asia's first Tier IV data center and leads Indonesia's colocation market. Earlier: Bank Bali banker, CFO of Sigma Cipta Caraka (2000-08), Indonet co-founder (1994). DCI president director 2012-16, president commissioner since.
interesting_fact: Named one of Forbes Asia's 20 'Asia's Power Businesswomen' in 2021; by 2025 she was ranked among Indonesia's 10 richest people and the country's richest woman.
deep_cut_fact: She has no tech degree (University of Toronto, finance/economics) and planned to be a banker; a 1985 software-installation project at Bank Bali convinced her tech could power business. Her line: 'You will never get bored with the tech sector.'
notes: Rarely interviewed; little personal media presence. DCI is central to Indonesia's AI/hyperscale data-center build-out, a strong podcast angle. Best route via DCI corporate secretary. Net worth figures vary widely with DCII's volatile share price.

name: Fernando Augusto Zobel de Ayala
current_role: Vice Chairman, Ayala Corporation; Chairman, AC Health; director of Ayala Land and BPI (as of 2025)
profile: Fernando Zobel de Ayala (b. 1960), seventh generation of the family behind Ayala Corporation, the Philippine conglomerate spanning property, banking, telecoms and energy (ACEN). He was Ayala's President/COO for 15 years and CEO 2021-2022, stepped back in 2022, and has since returned to board roles, chairing AC Health and Ayala Foundation.
interesting_fact: Long active in Habitat for Humanity: he was Vice Chairman of Habitat for Humanity International and chaired its Asia-Pacific capital campaign steering committee.
deep_cut_fact: A serious arts patron: he helped the founders develop Art Fair Philippines in its early days, sits on international advisory committees of Tate Modern, the Met and Art SG, and in 2025 funded CIMAM travel grants for Philippine curators and museum professionals.
notes: Input middle name 'Augusto' looks like a mix-up with his brother Jaime Augusto; he is Fernando Miranda Zobel de Ayala. Ayala's energy arm is ACEN. Route via Ayala Corporation corporate communications (ayala.com contact page); I could not verify a published press email. He took a medical leave in 2022, so avoid the topic.

name: Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala
current_role: Chairman, Ayala Corporation (Philippines); also chairs BPI and ACEN (formerly AC Energy)
profile: Eldest son of the Zobel de Ayala family (b. 1959; Harvard AB '81, MBA '87); succeeded his father as Ayala Corp. CEO in 1994 and led the conglomerate (property, banking, telecom, energy) as chairman & CEO 2006-2021. Now non-executive chairman; Ayala's ACEN is a major SE Asian renewables platform.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he became the first Filipino to receive Harvard Business School's Alumni Achievement Award, its highest honour; in 2017 the UN Global Compact named him the first Southeast Asian SDG Pioneer.
deep_cut_fact: A rugby devotee who played county-level rugby in Sussex as a teen at English boarding school, he flew to France for the 2007 World Cup to cheer the All Blacks; at Harvard he rowed lightweight crew briefly and calls quitting 'one of my big regrets.'
notes: Correct spelling is Jaime (not Jamie). Wikipedia links an official Facebook page for him. Best route is Ayala Corp. corporate communications; ACEN is the energy angle.

name: Vichai Bencharongkul
profile: Member of Thailand's Bencharongkul telecom family behind Total Access Communication (dtac), founded 1989 and led by Boonchai Bencharongkul in partnership with Telenor; the family sold most of its dtac shares in 2005 and dtac merged into True Corporation in 2023. Could not verify Vichai's individual role or current status.
notes: Research incomplete: the shared web-search budget ran out before this person, and Wikipedia has no page on him (family context from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boonchai_Bencharongkul and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DTAC). Benchachinda Holding is the likely family vehicle but its site blocked access. Verify identity and alive status before outreach.

name: Adani Vinodbhai Shantilal
current_role: Head of a Dubai-based family investment office (Excel Investment and Advisory Services; Adani Global Investment DMCC)
profile: Vinod Adani, born in Gujarat in 1949, is the elder brother of Gautam Adani. He has lived in Dubai since 1994 and holds Cypriot citizenship. He began in the family commodity trading business, founded VR Textile in Mumbai in 1976, traded commodities from Singapore from 1989, and helped finance the Adani group's early projects, including Mundra Port. He now runs a family investment office in Dubai.
interesting_fact: Forbes estimated his net worth at $16.4 billion in 2025, far above this list's older $2.9bn Hurun figure. He has also used the name Vinod Shantilal Shah since 1996.
deep_cut_fact: He founded his first business, VR Textile, in Mumbai in 1976, then moved to Singapore in 1989 to trade commodities before relocating to Dubai in 1994.
notes: Very private, with no public website, social accounts or published contact. He is the subject of regulatory and media controversy (Hindenburg 2023, SEBI 2024); the journalist should be aware before reaching out. Any approach would likely go via the Adani Group's corporate communications.

name: Peter Shu
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Transcend Information Inc. (TWSE: 2451), Taipei.
profile: Peter Shu (Shu Chung-won, b. 1954) is a National Cheng Kung University electrical-engineering graduate and ex-HP engineer who founded Transcend in 1988-89. He built it into a major global brand of memory modules, flash cards, SSDs and USB drives with thousands of niche SKUs. In 2026 he was again named among Harvard Business Review's Taiwan Top 100 CEOs as memory prices surged.
interesting_fact: Transcend has made more than 2,000 specialised memory and board products and served 5,000+ long-term customers; Shu said in 2026 the company had not borrowed from banks in 17 years.
deep_cut_fact: Transcend began with Chinese printing: as an HP engineer Shu had worked on Chinese support for HP's LaserJet; after leaving he wrote the Chinese printer software alone in 3-4 months working 13-14 hour days. It sold 12,000 sets in year one at NT$2,500 royalty each, funding the company.
notes: Taiwan-based (listed as China in input). IR email per Transcend's shareholder-services page and 2024 annual report (spokesperson listed as Chen Po-Shou); company sites were not reachable by curl from here, so verified via search snippets. Early product was the Key Pro software-protection dongle.

name: Martin
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Bouygues SA (CEO role passed to Olivier Roussat in 2021)
profile: Martin Bouygues, son of founder Francis Bouygues, ran the French construction, telecoms and media group Bouygues as chairman and CEO from 1989 to 2021 and remains chairman. With his brother Olivier he controls the family's stake through SCDM. The group spans Bouygues Construction, Colas, Equans (energy services), Bouygues Telecom and TF1.
interesting_fact: With his brother Olivier he owns Bordeaux's Château Montrose (a Saint-Estèphe second growth), Château Tronquoy-Lalande and the Loire's Clos Rougeard. Since 2018 he has also owned Burgundy's Domaine Henri Rebourseau.
deep_cut_fact: His only diploma is the baccalauréat. He joined Bouygues in 1974 as a site works supervisor (conducteur de travaux), worked on the Forum des Halles site in Paris, and founded catalogue home-builder Maison Bouygues in 1978. In 1989, at 37, he became the youngest CEO in the CAC 40.
notes: The input entry 'Martin' (Hurun, shared with Olivier Bouygues, source Bouygues) is Martin Bouygues, born 1952. Energy and data-centre angle: Equans and Bouygues Energies & Services do energy and data-centre infrastructure. Bouygues.com blocked automated access, so no press email was captured; use the group's press page. He is also Commander of the Ordre national du Mérite (2021).

name: Harindarpal Banga
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, The Caravel Group (Hong Kong); son Angad became Group CEO in January 2026
profile: Chandigarh-raised master mariner who moved to Hong Kong in 1979, became an early partner and later vice-chairman at commodity trader Noble Group over a 21-year career, then sold out by 2012 and founded The Caravel Group in 2013, which trades commodities and runs shipping. An early investor in Nykaa, he handed the CEO role to son Angad in 2026 and now focuses on strategy and governance.
interesting_fact: He was an early investor in Indian beauty e-retailer Nykaa and still holds a stake after its 2021 Mumbai IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Before trading commodities he was a seafarer: trained on the Training Ship Dufferin, India's oldest maritime academy, he earned his Master Mariner certificate in 1976 and was commanding merchant vessels at 27.
notes: Caravel issues releases via PR Newswire; no published email found on the site (JS-rendered). Philanthropy runs through The Caravel Foundation. Received India's Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2011.

name: Karthik Sarma
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, SRS Investment Management (New York); director, Avis Budget Group
profile: Indian-born hedge fund manager (IIT Madras, Princeton master's) who spent three years at McKinsey and five at Tiger Global before founding SRS Investment Management in 2006; it manages about $10bn. SRS is Avis Budget Group's largest shareholder (~43%), and Sarma has sat on Avis's board since May 2020.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he was one of eight hedge fund managers to personally earn over $1bn (about $2bn), mostly from Avis's roughly 5.5x share-price surge on talk of EV fleets.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wall Street he trained as an engineer at IIT Madras, then came to the US for a master's at Princeton, followed by three years as a McKinsey consultant.
notes: Very low public profile; SRS has no usable public website (srsinvest.com returned an error). Only published route found is via Avis Budget Group's media form, which reaches Avis rather than Sarma. Verify current Avis board status in latest proxy.

name: Wang Yun'an
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Guming Holdings (HKEX: 1364), operator of Good Me tea
profile: Born 1986, Wang co-founded Good Me (Guming) with college and high-school friends in 2010, opening a 30 sq m shop in Daxi, Wenling (Zhejiang). He franchised from 2011, focusing on lower-tier cities and building cold-chain supply before stores; Guming now has roughly 10,000 stores and listed in Hong Kong in Feb 2025.
interesting_fact: The first store opened on April 1, 2010 with about RMB 140,000; early daily sales were only RMB 300-500 and the partners debated quitting before it turned around.
deep_cut_fact: A materials-science graduate of Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, he made his first money in college selling quilts and radios, and he personally drew the site-selection and fit-out plans for Guming's first ~150 stores.
