notes: Young (b. 1986), first-generation founder - good entrepreneurship story. The press email is listed as Guming's media contact (媒体联系) on its homepage. Briefly worked at a car 4S dealership in Hangzhou before starting Guming.

name: Don Levin
current_role: Owner of D.R.L. Enterprises / Republic Brands (rolling papers: OCB, JOB, E-Z Wider) and owner of the AHL's Chicago Wolves
profile: Chicago entrepreneur, son of a used-car salesman. He bought a head shop called Adams Apple, saw demand for rolling papers, and started a distribution business that became Republic Brands. In 2000 he bought OCB and JOB from Vincent Bolloré. His group now owns a paper mill and a rolling-paper factory, with about $600m in estimated annual revenue.
interesting_fact: He co-founded the Chicago Wolves hockey club on 24 January 1994 with Buddy Meyers and Grant Mulvey. The team has won two IHL Turner Cups (1998, 2000) and three AHL Calder Cups (2002, 2008, 2022).
deep_cut_fact: He had planned to follow his father into selling cars, until a friend talked him into buying a Chicago head shop named Adams Apple. Most customers came in for rolling papers, which led to his distribution business.
notes: Very low media profile apart from the Chicago Wolves. The Wolves' front office is probably the most approachable route; I couldn't read their site, so check chicagowolves.com for media relations. Republic's only published email is salesinfo@ (sales), so I didn't include it.

name: Lottie Tham
current_role: Private investor; major H&M shareholder (no operating role at H&M)
profile: Helga Liselott 'Lottie' Tham (née Persson, b. 1949) is the daughter of H&M founder Erling Persson and the sister of former chairman Stefan Persson, and holds over 5% of H&M. With her husband, financier Pieter Tham, she invests in real estate including hotels, commercial buildings and land. She deliberately keeps out of the public eye.
interesting_fact: Her father got the idea for H&M (founded 1947 as Hennes in Västerås) on a road trip through the US after seeing New York's department stores.
notes: Very private, with no public role, website, social media or published office contact. Little energy/tech relevance. Low-priority outreach target; any approach would need a warm introduction.

name: Hal Jackman
current_role: Patriarch / largest family shareholder of E-L Financial Corporation (Toronto); former Lieutenant Governor of Ontario
profile: Henry N.R. 'Hal' Jackman (b. 1932) expanded the insurance and investment empire built by his father Harry Jackman, chairing National Trust and Empire Life; the family controls TSX-listed E-L Financial, now run by his son Duncan. He was Ontario's 25th Lieutenant Governor (1991-97) and U of T chancellor (1997-2003). In 2025 he gave $80M to U of T law, renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
interesting_fact: His September 2025 $80 million gift was the largest ever to a Canadian law school, bringing his giving to U of T's law faculty to $100 million; the school was renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
deep_cut_fact: While Lieutenant Governor in 1991, Jackman donated his historic collection of toy soldiers (over 650 figures) to the Royal Ontario Museum; he also served as honorary colonel of the Governor General's Horse Guards, a Toronto militia unit.
notes: Aged 94; no personal public channels. E-L Financial press releases name CFO Scott F. Ewert as the contact (published business line (416) 947-2578). Honorary-colonel detail from U of T/Victoria College sources: https://vic.utoronto.ca/henry-n-r-jackman-honoured-with-international-business-lnew-news-page

name: Glenn Dubin
current_role: Founder, Dubin & Co. (family office); co-founder, Engineers Gate; lead shareholder, Castleton Commodities International
profile: Dubin co-founded Highbridge Capital in 1992 and sold a majority stake to JPMorgan in 2004 for $1.3bn. He co-founded quant fund Engineers Gate and in 2012 led an investor group that bought energy trader Castleton Commodities. His family office, Dubin & Co., backs growth companies such as Brex and Scale AI.
interesting_fact: He is a founding board member of the Robin Hood Foundation. With his wife Eva, he funded the Dubin Breast Center at Mount Sinai, which opened in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Dubin and Highbridge co-founder Henry Swieca grew up a few blocks apart in Washington Heights. Highbridge, launched with $35m in 1992, is named after the 19th-century High Bridge aqueduct linking Washington Heights to the Bronx.
notes: His energy angle is Castleton Commodities (oil, gas and power trading and assets). Dubin & Co.'s site has no published email; it links his LinkedIn. He has appeared in Epstein-related press coverage, so expect him to be press-wary.

name: Rajiv Jain
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Chief Investment Officer, GQG Partners (Fort Lauderdale; ASX: GQG)
profile: India-born investor who came to the US in the early 1990s for an MBA at the University of Miami, joined Vontobel Asset Management in 1994 and became its co-CEO in 2014. In 2016 he co-founded GQG Partners with Tim Carver and listed it on the ASX in 2021; it now manages over US$150bn in long-only equities. He writes GQG's CIO Perspectives, which recently covered the AI investment cycle.
interesting_fact: In 2023, GQG invested about $1.9bn in four Adani Group companies, one of the most high-profile contrarian bets in emerging markets.
deep_cut_fact: Jain has backed Florida International University students since 2013, and GQG's community foundation funds FIU's First-Generation Scholarship for students pursuing STEM degrees as the first in their families to attend college.
notes: No published press email. GQG's published AI and semiconductor commentary (e.g. 'The Chips Are on the Table', Oct 2026; 'Always Evolving: Adapting as the AI cycle unfolds', Oct 2026) makes him a natural guest for the data-center and energy angle.

name: Jonathan Tisch
current_role: Executive Chairman, Loews Hotels; co-owner, board member and treasurer of the New York Giants; chairman of The Shed (NYC)
profile: Jonathan Tisch is the son of Bob Tisch, who co-founded Loews Corporation with his brother Laurence in 1946. Jonathan has led Loews Hotels since 1989 and was co-chairman of Loews Corp. until stepping back from its board at the end of 2024; he is now Executive Chairman of Loews Hotels. The family also owns 50% of the New York Giants, and he is a prominent civic philanthropist and chairman emeritus of the U.S. Travel Association.
interesting_fact: He hosts the interview programme 'Beyond the Boardroom with Jonathan Tisch' and has co-written three books, including 'Chocolates on the Pillow Aren't Enough: Reinventing the Customer Experience' (2007).
deep_cut_fact: In 1990, a year after becoming chairman of Loews Hotels, he launched the Loews Hotels 'Good Neighbor Policy' committing hotels to local community engagement. His $40M gift created the Tisch College of Civic Life at Tufts, his alma mater (class of 1976).
notes: Very media-friendly: a host and author himself, so a strong podcast candidate. Loews also owns natural-gas pipelines (Boardwalk), an energy angle. SEC data still lists him as a Loews director, but Wikipedia says he left the Loews Corp board on 31 Dec 2024; check before outreach.

name: Hayes Barnard
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, GoodLeap; Founder and Chairman, GivePower Foundation
profile: St. Louis-area native and former Oracle sales executive. He founded Paramount Equity Mortgage in 2003 and Paramount Solar in 2008, sold the solar unit to SolarCity, and was SolarCity's chief revenue officer. Back at his own firm, he turned it into Loanpal/GoodLeap, a point-of-sale platform that has financed over $26bn of solar and other green home upgrades and was valued at $12bn in 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2014 he founded the nonprofit GivePower, which builds solar-powered clean water and energy systems, including solar desalination, for underserved communities worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: He won a football scholarship to Central Missouri State but was injured as a freshman and transferred to Mizzou. On arriving in San Francisco in 1995 for the tech boom, his first jobs were staffing booths at trade shows.
notes: He is a strong fit for an energy podcast: residential solar finance, an ex-SolarCity executive, and GivePower solar water projects. He is publicly visible and does interviews; GoodLeap press is the best route.

name: Jian Yao
current_role: Shareholder, Shenzhen Mindray Bio-Medical Electronics (no known operating role)
profile: Per Forbes, Jian Yao is the ex-wife of Xu Hang, co-founder of Shenzhen medical-device maker Mindray (founded 1991), and obtained a minority stake in Mindray in 2020 after their divorce; that stake is the source of her fortune. No public role or activities found.
interesting_fact: Mindray, set up in Shenzhen in 1991, is one of China's largest medical-device makers; co-founder Xu Hang worked at Shenzhen Anke High-Tech (1987-1991), where he met fellow co-founders Li Xiting and Cheng Minghe.
notes: Wealth comes from a divorce settlement; she is a private individual with no public profile, so independent verification beyond Forbes was not possible. Not a good outreach target; avoid any reference to the divorce.

name: Safra Catz
current_role: Executive Vice Chair of the Board, Oracle Corporation (CEO 2014-Sept 2025); director, Paramount Skydance
profile: Israeli-born American executive who joined Oracle from investment bank DLJ in 1999 and rose to president, CFO and CEO (co-CEO with Mark Hurd from 2014, sole CEO from 2019). Her wealth is largely Oracle stock. In Sept 2025, amid Oracle's AI data-center build-out, she handed over to co-CEOs Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia and became executive vice chair.
interesting_fact: She is credited with driving Oracle's $10.3bn hostile takeover of PeopleSoft in 2005, and in 2011 was the highest-paid woman among Fortune 1000 companies.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Holon, Israel, she moved to Brookline, Massachusetts at age six and graduated from Brookline High School; alongside running Oracle she has been a lecturer in accounting at Stanford Graduate School of Business.
notes: SEC insider data still lists her as CEO; she became Executive Vice Chair on 22 Sept 2025. Very press-shy; best route is Oracle corporate communications.

name: Sathien Sathientham
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman/Vice Chairman, Carabao Group PCL (Thailand) (title varies by source)
profile: Sathien Sathientham (formerly Sathien Setthasit) co-founded Carabao in 2002 with folk-rock star Aed Carabao (Yuenyong Opakul); Carabao Dang outsells Red Bull in Thailand and the group listed in 2014. He has since pushed into large-scale beer brewing, packaging and cans; his sons run Carabao and CJ Express.
interesting_fact: Carabao is title sponsor of the English Football League Cup (the 'Carabao Cup'), and its energy drink outsells Red Bull in Red Bull's birthplace, Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: Before energy drinks he started out in real estate, and in 1999 he had early success pairing house-brewed beer with Thai food at Tawandang German Brewery in Bangkok, where he has been a director since 1999.
notes: One sponsored Khaosod piece credits Supote Teerawatanachai as Tawandang's founder, so say 'Tawandang' carefully (he is at least a long-time director). Searches may need both surnames (Setthasit/Sathientham).

name: Stephen Deckoff
current_role: Founder and Managing Principal, Black Diamond Capital Management (also director and 10%+ holder of KVH Industries)
profile: Distressed-credit and private-equity investor who worked at Drexel Burnham Lambert, Chemical Securities, Bear Stearns and Kidder, Peabody (SVP) before founding Black Diamond in 1995. The firm now manages more than $11B across CLOs, distressed funds and control private equity, with holdings including Werner ladders and Polynt. He has lived in the US Virgin Islands since 2011, where the firm has an office.
interesting_fact: He is an avid skier and named Black Diamond Capital after the ski-slope rating for the hardest runs.
deep_cut_fact: He studied operations research, earning a B.S. from Cornell's engineering school, and has sat on the boards of an unusually varied set of portfolio companies, including Werner Ladder, SmarteCarte, Sun World, Bayou Steel and ION Media.
notes: No published email or press contact; the firm site lists only office addresses (Stamford CT, St. Thomas USVI, Mumbai). In 2023 he bought Little and Great St. James islands (formerly Epstein's) for a resort, which is widely covered but sensitive, so avoid it as an opener. Reported >$1.2M in USVI nonprofit donations (St. John Source). Industrial portfolio (steel, paper, chemicals) may suit the energy angle.

name: Lucy Peng
current_role: Alibaba cofounder and former Ant Group chief executive/chair; no current public executive role confirmed (left Ant's board in Aug 2020)
profile: Peng Lei (彭蕾), one of Alibaba's 18 founders, joined Jack Ma in 1999 after five years as a university lecturer. She built Alibaba's HR function and was its chief people officer for over a decade. She ran Alipay (2010-13), led Ant Financial and sat on Paytm's board. She was an Ant director until August 2020 and has kept a low profile since Ant's IPO was halted.
interesting_fact: She led Alipay from January 2010 to February 2013, when it became China's dominant payment gateway. In 2016 Ant Financial raised $4.5B, then the largest private fundraising ever for an internet company.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alibaba she taught for five years at Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics. At Alibaba she created the 'mom and pop' management model, in which one manager ('mom') focused on teamwork and motivation and another ('pop') handled performance reviews.
notes: Very private since 2020; she has no personal website or social accounts. No published contact route was found, and Alibaba/Ant corporate channels are unlikely to forward requests. She spoke publicly at Stanford GSB's China 2.0 conference (2012). The web search budget ran out, so her current activities (e.g. any investing vehicle) were not verified.

name: The Lazari family
current_role: Owners of Lazari (Lazari Investments, Lazari Financial Holdings, Lazari Developments), Mayfair, London
profile: Family of the late Greek-Cypriot developer Chris (Christos) Lazari (d. 2015), who founded Lazari Investments in 1976. Widow Maritsa (co-founder) and children run a private group with 2.9m sq ft of prime London property and combined assets of over £4.1bn across eight London estates, including the West End and Euston Road.
interesting_fact: The group is now three businesses: the legacy property company, a property-finance lender and a development arm, with combined assets above £4.1bn.
deep_cut_fact: Founder Chris Lazari left Cyprus at 16 with just £20 aboard the MV Messapia, washed dishes and waited tables to study fashion design, and built the 'Drendie Girl' high-street clothing label before moving into property in 1978.
notes: Family entry: founder Chris Lazari died 2015; widow Maritsa (b. 1943) is alive per Wikipedia, and children are directors. Low-profile family; best route is FTI Consulting.

name: Katarina Martinson
current_role: Chair, Indutrade AB; board member, L E Lundbergföretagen AB and other Lundberg group companies
profile: Swedish businesswoman (b. 1981) who, with her sister Louise Lindh, owns about 15% stakes in the family investment company L E Lundbergföretagen. Founded by her grandfather in 1944 and led by her father Fredrik Lundberg, it holds stakes in Holmen, Handelsbanken, Sandvik, Skanska, Indutrade and others. She chairs industrial group Indutrade and invests privately in brands such as NN07 and Lyko.
interesting_fact: When she became chair of Indutrade, she was the youngest chair of any company listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Norrköping, she grew up in Norrköping, Switzerland and Djursholm and is a Stockholm School of Economics graduate. In 2021 she was elected a member of IVA, the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences.
notes: Fairly private. Lundbergs (whose holdings include Holmen, which owns forest and hydro/wind assets) and Indutrade are the routes. Her IVA membership suggests an interest in engineering and tech topics.

name: Qian Dongqi
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ecovacs Robotics (科沃斯, 603486.SH), Suzhou
profile: Qian Dongqi (b. 1958), a Nanjing University physics graduate with a master's in philosophy, worked in state-owned foreign trade before renting a village factory in Suzhou in 1998 to start Taiyikai Electric, an OEM vacuum maker. It became Ecovacs, one of China's largest robot-vacuum brands, and listed in Shanghai in 2018. The group also owns Tineco, the floor-cleaner brand run by his son David Qian.
interesting_fact: Before launching its own brands, the company made vacuums for other labels; by around 2006 this OEM business already brought in about RMB 1B a year.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for a robot vacuum reportedly came from a 1999/2000 news story about a robot soccer match, which made Qian wonder whether a robot could sweep floors. The company kept the name Taiyikai (泰怡凯) until 2011.
notes: The email is the general contact in the Ecovacs Group website's site config, not a named press office. For IR, use the SSE disclosures for 603486. The sources disagree on the year of the robot-soccer anecdote (1999 vs 2000). David Qian, chairman of Tineco, is the more media-facing family member.

name: Adebayo Ogunlesi
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Global Infrastructure Partners (a part of BlackRock); Senior Managing Director, BlackRock; OpenAI board member
profile: Nigerian-born lawyer turned banker and infrastructure investor. After Cravath and 23 years at Credit Suisse, he cofounded Global Infrastructure Partners in 2006, building it to $100B+ AUM across energy, transport, digital infrastructure and water before selling it to BlackRock for $12.5B in 2024. He joined OpenAI's board in January 2025.
interesting_fact: Early in his career he clerked for Justice Thurgood Marshall, the first Black U.S. Supreme Court justice; he holds degrees from Oxford (BA), Harvard Law (JD) and Harvard Business School (MBA).
deep_cut_fact: Alongside his dealmaking he has taught courses on transnational investment projects at Harvard Law School, Yale Law School and the Yale School of Management.
notes: Very strong energy + AI data-center angle (GIP owns energy/digital infra; OpenAI board; GIP part of the BlackRock/MGX/Microsoft AI Infrastructure Partnership). Also director of Kosmos Energy and Topgolf Callaway. Route via BlackRock Americas corporate communications.

name: Qian Peixin
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Wang Liping) of Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic Co. (SSE: 601100)
profile: Qian Peixin (钱佩新) is co-actual controller, with husband and chairman Wang Liping, of Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic, a Changzhou maker of hydraulic cylinders, pumps and valves for excavators and machinery. The family controls ~64% of the Shanghai-listed firm. She is not a public-facing executive.
interesting_fact: Hurun lists her among the world's self-made women billionaires (2020-2025) on the strength of the family's stake in Hengli Hydraulic, a key supplier of hydraulic components to excavator makers.
notes: Very low public profile; virtually no interviews. Only route is Hengli's board-secretary office (hlzqb@hengli.net, from 2025 annual report). Note: in March 2026 Hengli disclosed a provincial supervisory commission action concerning chairman Wang Liping; on 13 Apr 2026 it said he had resumed duties. Weak fit for an energy podcast.

name: Shen Xiqiang
current_role: Vice chairman and major shareholder, Jiangsu Yoke Technology Co. (雅克科技, 002409.SZ)
profile: Shen Xiqiang (沈锡强, about 78) co-founded Jiangsu Yoke in Yixing, Jiangsu in 1997 as a flame-retardant chemicals maker; it listed in Shenzhen in 2010. Yoke now makes semiconductor precursors, photoresists and specialty gases, plus LNG cryogenic insulation panels. His elder son Shen Qi is chairman and his younger son Shen Fu is deputy GM.
interesting_fact: Yoke is both a chip-materials and an LNG-shipping supplier. Its insulation panels went into the world's first large Mark III Flex LNG carrier, and its LNG panel business grew 57% in 2025, while its high-k precursors go into DRAM, 3D NAND and AI advanced-packaging chips.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews found. The family business is now run by his sons, so Yoke's IR office (board secretary Qin Hongjian, per the 2025 annual report) is the realistic route. Bridges both of the podcast's themes: LNG energy shipping and semiconductor materials for AI chips.

name: Richard Rainwater
current_role: Deceased (died 27 September 2015, Fort Worth, Texas, aged 71)
notes: Died 27 Sep 2015 at his Fort Worth home (announced by the Rainwater Charitable Foundation). Sources: https://www.keranews.org/news/2015-09-28/fort-worth-billionaire-richard-rainwater-dies ; https://fortune.com/2015/09/28/richard-rainwater-obituary/ . Legacy continues via the Rainwater Charitable Foundation.

name: Nitin Sandesara
current_role: Promoter, Sandesara Group; owner of Sterling Oil Exploration & Energy Production Co. (SEEPCO), Nigeria
profile: Gujarat-born promoter of the Sandesara Group (Sterling Biotech, gelatin/pharma, energy). Since the mid-2000s the group's main asset has been Nigerian upstream producer SEEPCO, which holds OML 143 (Okwuibome field). Lived abroad from 2017 amid an Indian bank-fraud case; India's Supreme Court let criminal proceedings be closed in 2025-26 after a settlement with lenders.
interesting_fact: SEEPCO says it is the only Indian-owned crude producer operating in an OPEC member country; between March and May 2026 it shipped about 6M barrels of Okwuibome crude to IOC, BPCL and HPCL, avoiding the Strait of Hormuz.
deep_cut_fact: In July 2015 Africa Oil & Gas Report called the Sandesara venture Sterling Energy 'the busiest company on rig sites in Nigeria', with five rigs active at once. SEEPCO won OML 143 (then OPL 280) in Nigeria's 2005 bid round.

public_contacts.value: SEEPCO media contact: Deepak Sodhi, sendvisesolution@gmail.com

notes: Reputationally sensitive. He was declared a fugitive economic offender in India over the Sterling Biotech loan-fraud case. India's Supreme Court conditionally agreed in Nov 2025 to quash proceedings on payment of Rs 5,100 crore, and reports say the matter was closed in April 2026. Based in Nigeria. Hurun figure (2015) is dated. Only route found is SEEPCO's press-release media contact.

name: Xu Yanming (徐延铭)
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Zhuhai CosMX Battery Co. (珠海冠宇, SSE STAR 688772); deputy to China's National People's Congress
profile: Harbin Institute of Technology graduate who has worked on batteries for nearly 30 years. He led a team from Harbin's Guangyu group to Zhuhai in 2007 to found what became CosMX, a maker of polymer lithium-ion batteries for laptops, tablets and phones, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. Per TSR data, CosMX ranked No.1 globally in laptop battery shipments in 2024.
interesting_fact: CosMX ranked first worldwide in notebook-PC lithium battery shipments and second in tablet batteries in 2024 (Techno Systems Research data), and held 2,400+ granted patents by mid-2025.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2026 Two Sessions he proposed that China's lithium-battery makers copy the solar industry's playbook: a cross-supply-chain patent pool led by top firms and a 'next-generation battery technology innovation alliance' to co-develop high-silicon anodes and solid-state batteries, replacing 'litigation instead of competition'.
notes: Chinese-language outreach advisable. Chaired CosMX board meeting March 30, 2026 per SSE filing. Founding story (Harbin Guangyu spin-out, HIT alumnus) from Chinese press profiles (cnstock); verify details before quoting. No personal social accounts found.

name: Li Xue
current_role: Shareholder and member of the controlling Lee family group of Yunnan Energy New Material (SEMCORP / 恩捷股份, 002812.SZ); no executive post
profile: Li Xue (李雪), registered as Sherry Lee, is one of six members of the Paul Xiaoming Lee family who jointly control Yunnan Energy New Material (Enjie/SEMCORP), the Yuxi-based world leader in wet-process lithium-battery separator film that grew out of a cigarette-packaging printer. Hurun's 2022 Self-Made Women list ranked her No. 33 with RMB 19.5bn. She holds no management role at the company.
interesting_fact: Enjie began as Yunnan Yuxi Chuangxin Color Printing, a packaging supplier to tobacco groups, before its 2018 merger with Shanghai Energy made it the global No. 1 in wet-process battery separators (about 37% share in H1 2018).
deep_cut_fact: She has been a direct shareholder since about 2010, when the Lee family moved stakes in the predecessor Chuangxin Color Printing from the offshore Newston vehicle to Heyi Investment, Li Xue and other family members.
notes: Identity confirmed: Hurun API (2022 women list: 李雪, Energy New Material/恩捷股份, Yuxi) plus Sina Finance naming 'Sherry Lee (李雪)' among Enjie's six actual controllers. She is Paul Xiaoming Lee's daughter (prior pass wrongly linked her to Li Xiaohua). Very private; no interviews or accounts found. Route only via Enjie's securities office.

name: Martin Viessmann
current_role: Non-executive member of the Board of Directors, Viessmann Generations Group (family investment holding, Battenberg/Allendorf, Germany)
profile: Grandson of founder Johann Viessmann (1917); led the heating-systems maker as managing partner/CEO from 1989 and pushed it into renewables and efficiency. After the 2024 sale of Viessmann Climate Solutions to Carrier, the family runs Viessmann Generations Group, an investment company 'co-creating living spaces for future generations', with son Max as co-CEO; Martin now sits on its board.
interesting_fact: A fitness buff and passionate skier, he holds a professional pilot's license and an honorary doctorate from the University of Wisconsin; Viessmann is a major winter-sports sponsor.
deep_cut_fact: In Dec 2012 he and wife Annette endowed UW Oshkosh's first-ever endowed chair, the Viessmann Endowed Chair in Sustainable Technology, capping a partnership that in 2011 opened the Western Hemisphere's first dry-fermentation anaerobic biodigester on that campus.

public_contacts.value: phiv@viessmann.com (Philine von Hardenberg, Director Corporate Communications, Viessmann Generations Group)

notes: Forbes bio calling him chairman of the executive board is outdated: group site lists him as non-executive board member; son Max Viessmann leads. Best route is Generations Group corporate communications. Strong US tie via UW Oshkosh partnership.

name: Sebastian Glaser
current_role: Managing director of Sick Holding GmbH; majority shareholder of sensor maker SICK AG (Waldkirch, Germany)
profile: Grandson of optical engineer Erwin Sick, who founded SICK in 1946 near Munich; Glaser is the majority shareholder and runs the family's Sick Holding GmbH. SICK, led by external CEO Mats Gokstorp, makes industrial sensors, LiDAR and safety light curtains for factory, logistics and process automation, with ~10,000+ employees and >$2B sales.
interesting_fact: SICK laser scanners helped Stanford's autonomous car 'Stanley' win the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge; the company's breakthrough was the first series-ready safety light curtain, shown at the Hannover fair in 1952.
notes: Low-profile family owner; operational spokespeople are SICK's executive board. Search budget ran out before a deep-cut fact or named press email could be sourced. Route via SICK corporate communications.

name: Susan Ocampo
current_role: Director, MACOM Technology Solutions (MTSI); co-founder, VP, Secretary & Treasurer of GaAs Labs LLC
profile: Filipino-American co-founder (with her late husband John Ocampo) of RF chipmaker Sirenza Microdevices in 1984 and of investment fund GaAs Labs in 2008, which bought MACOM in 2009. She is MACOM's largest individual shareholder (10%+ owner) and a board member; John died in November 2023. In 2026 she launched a $100M endowment fund in his memory for RF, microwave and photonics research.
interesting_fact: In May 2026 she announced the $100M John L. Ocampo Endowment Fund, one of the largest private funds ever for RF/microwave and photonics engineering research, with annual grants to universities (Tyndall National Institute in Cork was an early recipient).
deep_cut_fact: In 2021 she and John gave $25 million to Santa Clara University (John's alma mater, class of '79) to support STEM education and a new science and engineering facility.
notes: Extremely private; Gulf News noted almost no photos of her exist. Reportedly holds a BA from Maryknoll College, Manila (sources conflict). Best route likely MACOM IR or GaAs Labs (Los Altos, CA), which has no published contact found.

name: Gudrun Heine
current_role: Co-owner (about 44%) of Karl Storz SE & Co. KG, Tuttlingen; not in an executive role
profile: Daughter of Karl Storz, who founded the endoscopy company in Tuttlingen in 1945 to make ENT instruments and lamps. The company pioneered 'cold light' illumination (1960) and the rod-lens system (1965), which helped create modern endoscopy. It is privately held, with about EUR2.2bn revenue in 2023 and roughly 9,800 staff. She and her sister Sybill each own about 44%; Sybill's son Karl-Christian runs it.
interesting_fact: Karl Storz's 'cold light illumination', bringing bright light from an external source into the body via a flexible fibre-optic cable, laid the groundwork for modern endoscopy; the firm now has more than 15,000 products for human, veterinary and industrial use.
notes: Extremely low public profile. Almost no public information exists about her personally; her sister Sybill Storz was the public face. Only the corporate press inbox is available. Web search budget was exhausted, so research came from Wikipedia and the company site only.

name: Sybill Storz
profile: Dr. h.c. mult. Sybill Storz, longtime head and later chair of endoscopy maker KARL STORZ, died at 88, as announced by the company on 1 Dec 2025 (she died the preceding Friday).
notes: Deceased (late Nov 2025) per the KARL STORZ obituary press release. Her son Karl-Christian Storz has been sole managing director since 2019, and press@karlstorz.com is the company press contact if the family or company is of interest.

name: Christina Rohde
current_role: Largest shareholder, Rohde & Schwarz (Munich); no confirmed operating role
profile: Heir from the Rohde founding family and the largest shareholder of Rohde & Schwarz, the Munich test-and-measurement, broadcast, secure communications and defence-electronics group founded in 1933 by physicists Lothar Rohde and Hermann Schwarz. name: Richard Sands
current_role: Non-management Director, Constellation Brands (NYSE: STZ); former CEO (1993-2007) and chairman (1999-2018)
profile: Richard Sands joined his father Marvin's Canandaigua Wine Company in 1979 and, with his brother Rob, turned it through serial acquisitions into Constellation Brands. The ~$10bn-revenue group owns Robert Mondavi and holds the US rights to Corona and Modelo. He was CEO from 1993 to 2007 and chairman until 2018, and he still sits on the board. He lives in Canandaigua, New York.
interesting_fact: Under the Sands brothers, Constellation invested about $4bn in cannabis producer Canopy Growth in 2018, one of the largest bets by a mainstream drinks company on legal cannabis.
deep_cut_fact: He once worked as a delivery driver during a break from college (Forbes). He is also an RIT trustee: he and his wife Jennifer gave money for the Sands Family Studios in RIT's School for American Crafts, dedicated in 2011 as part of a $2m renovation.
notes: Confirmed on the board via the Constellation IR governance page (2026). The IR contact is corporate, not personal. In 2016 the Sands family gave $61m to the Rochester Area Community Foundation, its largest gift ever.

name: Jimmy John Liautaud
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Jimmy John's (now part of Inspire Brands); private investor
profile: Illinois entrepreneur who opened Jimmy John's in 1983 at 19 with a $25,000 loan from his father, an Army veteran, and grew it into a ~2,800-unit, almost entirely franchised sandwich chain. He sold a majority stake to Roark Capital in 2016 and merged his remaining stake into Roark's Inspire Brands in 2019.
interesting_fact: His father's $25,000 loan came with a condition: if the sandwich business failed, Jimmy John would enlist in the US Army; in exchange his father took a 48% stake.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he gave $1 million to his old high school, Elgin Academy, on condition the building also bear the name of James Lyons, the dean who disciplined him there; the upper school is now the Liautaud-Lyons Upper School.
notes: No published personal or office contact found; Jimmy John's media now handled by Inspire Brands. He also co-funded (with his father) the Liautaud Graduate School of Business at UIC with a $5M gift. Avoid big-game-hunting controversy in outreach.

name: Mathias Doepfner
current_role: CEO and co-owner, Axel Springer SE (Berlin)
profile: Bonn-born journalist (b. 1963) who rose from FAZ music critic to editor-in-chief of Die Welt, then Axel Springer CEO in 2002. He led its digital transformation (Business Insider, Politico) and in 2020 Friede Springer gave/sold him ~22% plus her voting rights; after a 2025 restructuring he and Springer hold ~95% of the media business.
interesting_fact: He started his career in 1982, aged 19, as a music critic for a Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung supplement and later earned a PhD in musicology; he is also a noted art collector.
deep_cut_fact: In autumn 2010 he was a visiting professor at the University of Cambridge (CRASSH), giving three lectures titled 'Freedom and the Digital Revolution' that framed digitization as the fourth great cultural revolution.
notes: High-profile, outspoken; owns Politico and Business Insider, so a US-media angle works. Politically polarizing recently (Politico staff letter 2026) - steer clear in outreach. Route via Axel Springer corporate communications.

name: Manuel Puig Rocha
current_role: Vice Chairman, Puig Brands (Barcelona; listed 2024), and its largest individual shareholder
profile: Grandson of Antonio Puig, who founded the Barcelona perfume and beauty house in 1914. He has been vice president of Puig since 2007, overseeing international subsidiaries. Puig owns Carolina Herrera, Paco Rabanne, Jean Paul Gaultier, Nina Ricci, Charlotte Tilbury and Byredo. It listed on the Spanish stock exchange in May 2024 at about €14bn; the family keeps the large majority of voting rights.
interesting_fact: The company's big break was the Milady lipstick in 1922, eight years after founding. Today at least 14 family members control Puig.
notes: Very low public profile. Marc Puig (his cousin) is chairman/CEO and the public face. Puig's website blocked automated access, so I couldn't capture the press/IR emails; check puig.com's press and investor pages manually. Search quota was exhausted while I was researching him.

name: Jack Cowin
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Competitive Foods Australia (Hungry Jack's); Chairman and largest shareholder, Domino's Pizza Enterprises
profile: Born in Windsor, Ontario, he moved to Perth in 1969 to open KFC franchises, then founded Hungry Jack's as Australia's Burger King franchisee. He also chairs and is the top shareholder of ASX-listed Domino's Pizza Enterprises, and owns plant-based meat maker v2food, meat processor Consolidated Foods and 40% of BridgeClimb Sydney.
interesting_fact: He is rolling out EV fast-charging units at his drive-through restaurants. He took the name Hungry Jack's only because someone else already held the Burger King trademark in Australia.
deep_cut_fact: He financed his first KFC outlets in Perth in December 1969 by raising C$10,000 each from thirty Canadians, after four years selling insurance for London Life in Toronto. As a student at Western Ontario he sold trees, shrubs and rocks, and later served as the university's chancellor (2015-2019).
notes: Good fit for an energy episode: EV charging at drive-throughs, plus v2food. Domino's IR email is the most direct published corporate address. Hungry Jack's lists only a customer-service email, so use its contact page for a media request.

name: Hu Kaijun
current_role: Chairman and CEO, China Grand Enterprises (Beijing); chairman/CEO of Beijing Yuanda Huachuang Investment
profile: Hu Kaijun heads China Grand Enterprises, a Beijing-based investment group with interests in healthcare, real estate, agriculture and financial services and parent of Hong Kong-listed Grand Pharmaceutical, Shenzhen-listed Huadong Medicine and Grand Industrial Holding. His wealth stems mainly from the stakes in Huadong Medicine and Grand Pharmaceutical.
interesting_fact: In 2023 Grand Pharmaceutical agreed to buy 87.5% of U.S.-based vascular drug maker BlackSwan Vascular for $37.5 million, part of its push into innovative cardiovascular and interventional products.
notes: Very low media profile; no interviews or personal channels found. Grand Pharma IR (Hong Kong) is the most reachable published channel. No sourced deep-cut fact found (web-search budget exhausted).

name: Devi Shetty
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Narayana Health
profile: UK-trained cardiac surgeon who founded Bangalore hospital chain Narayana Hrudayalaya (now Narayana Health) in 2000 and took it public in 2015. It has around 47 facilities, including a hospital in the Cayman Islands, and is known for high-volume, low-cost heart surgery. In 2025 it agreed to buy the UK's Practice Plus Group Hospitals.
interesting_fact: Shetty was Mother Teresa's personal physician. He also helped design Yeshasvini, a micro-insurance scheme for farmers in Karnataka.
deep_cut_fact: Born in the village of Kinnigoli, Karnataka, Shetty decided to become a heart surgeon as a schoolboy in 1967, when his teacher told the class about Christiaan Barnard's first heart transplant. In 1992 he performed India's first neonatal heart surgery, on a 21-day-old baby.
notes: Very media-accessible and speaks often on affordable healthcare. Sources differ on whether the Barnard moment was in 5th or 6th standard. No dedicated press email found; corporate communications via the IR inbox is the best published route.

name: Jay Hennick
current_role: Global Chairman & CEO and controlling shareholder, Colliers (Toronto; NASDAQ/TSX: CIGI); founder and chairman, FirstService; chairman, Hennick & Company
profile: Toronto entrepreneur who began in 1972 as a teenager running a commercial swimming pool business on a $1,000 loan from his father. He turned it into FirstService (CEO 1988-2015, listed 1993), merged it with Colliers in 2010 and spun Colliers off as a public company in 2015. Family firm Hennick & Co. holds stakes in Haventree Bank and BV Realty.
interesting_fact: His first job, aged 15, was as a summer lifeguard at an apartment complex, and it gave him the idea for his first company, which eventually became FirstService and Colliers.
deep_cut_fact: Through the Hennick Family Foundation he and his wife Barbara gave $36M that named Toronto's Hennick Bridgepoint Hospital, plus $50M to the Royal Ontario Museum and $10M to Yad Vashem. He also received the International Horatio Alger Award in 2019.
notes: Colliers' published IR email is the most direct institutional route. Colliers advises on data-center and infrastructure real estate, which suits the podcast's data-center theme.

name: Zhuo Jun
current_role: Director and major shareholder, Shenzhen Kinwong Electronic Co. (Shanghai-listed PCB maker)
profile: Zhuo Jun inherited a large stake in Shenzhen Kinwong Electronic after her husband and co-founder Shen Jitang died in 2013. Kinwong, founded in Shenzhen's Nanshan District in 1993, is one of China's largest printed-circuit-board makers. She sits on its board, and her younger brother Zhuo Yong is vice chairman. The company announced a Hong Kong dual listing in 2025.
interesting_fact: Kinwong is building its first overseas manufacturing base, a PCB plant in Thailand, due to start production in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: After high school she spent four years as a clerk at the Heung Yee Kuk, the statutory advisory body representing the interests of Hong Kong's New Territories.
notes: Very low public profile and not an executive spokesperson; the company route goes via the IR/securities office. PCBs for servers and data-centre hardware are relevant to the podcast. The deep-cut fact comes from Forbes, which already appeared in the input.

name: Chao Teng-hsiung
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder, Farglory Group (Farglory Land); son Frank Chao has chaired Farglory Land since 2014
profile: Born in 1944 in Houlong, Miaoli, Taiwan, into a poor family. He moved to Taipei and saved from odd jobs to supply cement to builders before developing his own factory-office buildings. He started in property in 1969, founded what became Farglory Land in 1978 and grew Farglory Group into a conglomerate spanning real estate, life insurance, hotels, air-cargo logistics and Hualien's Farglory Ocean Park.
interesting_fact: After junior high school, he started out as an apprentice in concrete formwork and masonry, the trade he later scaled into one of Taiwan's largest developers.
deep_cut_fact: Working with sculptor Ju Ming, he backed a 2011 arrangement letting primary-school children from Taipei and New Taipei visit the Juming Museum free all year round; then-Taipei mayor Hau Lung-bin praised him for it.
notes: Sensitive: he was convicted at first instance in 2022 in a bribery case (Taipei Dome/Farglory), with appeals ongoing per Forbes. Approach is likely unrealistic; any outreach should go via Farglory corporate IR. Mandarin is required.

name: Alan Trefler
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Pegasystems (Pega), Waltham, MA
profile: Son of a Holocaust survivor who ran a Boston antique-restoration shop, Trefler founded Pegasystems in 1983 at 27 and has led it since; Pega (IPO 1996) sells AI-powered workflow and customer-engagement software, with ~$1.5B in 2024 revenue and 5,000+ staff. He and wife Pamela run the Trefler Foundation, focused on Boston public education.
interesting_fact: As a Dartmouth sophomore in 1975, rated just 2075, he tied for first at the World Open chess tournament with grandmaster Pal Benko, finishing ahead of GMs Walter Browne and Nicolas Rossolimo.
deep_cut_fact: In the early 1980s he built computer chess-playing systems and then applied the same techniques to teaching computers to process business rules, the idea behind Pega. He also wrote 'Build for Change' (Wiley, 2014) and founded Union & Fifth (2015), a donated-clothing resale venture benefiting charities.
notes: Accessible, frequent keynote speaker (PegaWorld). Press email is Pega's Director of PR as listed on 2026 releases. Chess is a strong rapport topic.

name: Luana Lopes Lara
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Kalshi (CFTC-regulated prediction-market exchange, New York)
profile: Brazilian-born Luana Lopes Lara co-founded Kalshi in 2018 with MIT classmate Tarek Mansour after quant stints including Citadel Securities. Kalshi won CFTC approval in 2020 and in 2024 launched the first legal US election contracts in a century; valuation rose to about $11B (Dec 2025) and reportedly ~$22B (May 2026), making her the youngest self-made woman billionaire.
interesting_fact: Before MIT she danced professionally for a season of 'Swan Lake' at the Salzburger Landestheater in Austria, after training at the Bolshoi Theater School in Joinville, Brazil.
deep_cut_fact: At Escola Técnica Tupy in Joinville she competed in physics and astronomy olympiads; she was admitted to Harvard, Yale and Stanford as well as MIT, and attended MIT on a Fundação Estudar scholarship. Her father is an electrical engineer who worked at IBM and her mother a math teacher.
notes: Very podcast-friendly: has appeared on Barry Ritholtz's Masters in Business (2022) and Coin Stories. Best route: X DM or Kalshi comms. No published Kalshi press email found on-site.

name: Scott Wu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Cognition (maker of the Devin AI software engineer and owner of Windsurf)
profile: Louisiana-born competitive programmer who left Harvard after two years. He worked at Addepar, then co-founded and served as CTO of networking startup Lunchclub (2017-22). In 2023 he co-founded Cognition with fellow IOI gold medalists; its autonomous coding agent Devin made it one of the most highly valued AI-coding startups and him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: He won three IOI gold medals (2012-14), placing first overall in 2014. He also took third at the 2021 Google Code Jam and is a Codeforces Legendary Grandmaster with a peak rating of 3350.
deep_cut_fact: Before coding fame he was the 2011 national MATHCOUNTS individual champion, representing Louisiana from Baton Rouge Magnet High School. His older brother Neal, also a three-time IOI gold medalist, now works with him at Cognition.
notes: Appears often on podcasts (e.g. David Senra, June 2026; Latent Space), so he is receptive to long-form interviews. His personal X handle was not verified from an official source, so it is not listed. AI compute demand is a natural data-center angle.

name: Tarek Mansour
current_role: Cofounder and CEO, Kalshi
profile: Lebanese-American founder (b. 1996), raised in Lebanon. He studied math and computer science at MIT, where he met cofounder Luana Lopes Lara. Kalshi, founded in 2018, became the first CFTC-regulated U.S. prediction-market exchange. In 2024 it won approval for the first legal U.S. election contracts in over a century. It reached an $11B valuation in December 2025, and he owns an estimated 12%.
interesting_fact: Kalshi made history in 2024 when it won the right to list contracts on the U.S. presidential election, the first legal election betting market in the U.S. in more than 100 years.
deep_cut_fact: Before Kalshi he interned at Goldman Sachs in 2016 and then traded at Citadel. He has said that seeing clients want to hedge on real-world events inspired the 'democratize hedging' idea behind Kalshi. He went to high school at Collège Louise Wegmann in Beirut.
notes: Very active on X and in the media. No published press email was found on news.kalshi.com, so X DMs or Kalshi's newsroom are the realistic routes. Prediction markets on energy and data-center events could be a podcast hook.

name: Richard M. DeVos
profile: Richard Marvin 'Rich' DeVos, co-founder of Amway and owner of the Orlando Magic (the 1997 Forbes listing matches him). Died September 6, 2018, aged 92, in Ada, Michigan.
notes: Deceased (source: https://money.cnn.com/2018/09/06/news/amway-richard-devos/index.html ; NBA.com obituary). Not to be confused with his son Dick DeVos (Richard M. DeVos Jr.), former Amway president.

name: Samuel C. Johnson
profile: Samuel Curtis Johnson Jr. (1928-2004) was the fourth-generation leader of S.C. Johnson & Son in Racine, Wisconsin. He died on May 22, 2004 (listed on Forbes 1997 only).
notes: Deceased May 22, 2004 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Curtis_Johnson_Jr.). Identity inferred from the Forbes 1997 listing, which carries no source-of-wealth field. His daughter Winnie Johnson-Marquart (P03641) is in this lane, and his son Fisk Johnson now leads SC Johnson.

name: Marvin H. Davis
notes: Oil industrialist (Davis Petroleum; former owner of 20th Century Fox, Pebble Beach, Beverly Hills Hotel). Died September 25, 2004; he is on the Forbes 1997–98 lists. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Davis. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Huang Sheng
current_role: Chairman & GM, Wuhan Guide Sensmart Tech (高德智感); director/VP at Wuhan Guide Infrared (002414.SZ) through Dec 2025
profile: Huang Sheng (黄晟, b. 1989) is the son of Huang Li, founder and controlling shareholder of Wuhan Guide Infrared, a Shenzhen-listed maker of infrared detector chips, thermal imagers and defence systems. He joined the group in 2016, became a director and vice-GM, and runs its consumer/industrial thermal-imaging arm Guide Sensmart. Hurun lists the family wealth jointly with his father.
interesting_fact: Huang Li and Huang Sheng have been ranked by Hurun as Hubei's richest (by residence); Guide Infrared is credited with breaking Western restrictions to achieve home-grown infrared chips in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a 2013 master's in control engineering from Huazhong University of Science and Technology, and in 2022 was elected a part-time vice-chairman of the Wuhan Federation of Industry and Commerce.
notes: Source of wealth listed as 'Guide Electrics' corresponds to Wuhan Guide Infrared (高德红外); wealth shared with father Huang Li. His Guide Infrared director term ended 22 Dec 2025 per lixinger; confirm current title. Defence-related company; mostly Chinese-language press.

name: Dewi Kam
current_role: Minority shareholder (~10%), PT Bayan Resources; power-plant investor (reported President Commissioner, PT Sumber Segara Primadaya)
profile: Indonesian investor whose fortune comes mainly from a roughly 10% stake in Bayan Resources, Indonesia's third-largest coal producer, controlled by Low Tuck Kwong. She also has interests in building and operating coal-fired power plants. Bayan's soaring shares in 2022-23 made her one of Indonesia's richest people; she keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: In 2023 Forbes ranked her the richest woman in Southeast Asia, after Bayan's share price roughly tripled during 2022 on high coal prices.
deep_cut_fact: Her power business reportedly includes PT Sumber Segara Primadaya, operator of the Cilacap coal power plant in Central Java (a 51/49 JV with PLN's Pembangkitan Jawa Bali), where she is listed as President Commissioner, and the 2x125 MW Jeneponto plant in South Sulawesi with Bosowa.
notes: Very private: no interviews, website or social media found. Bayan's corporate secretary is only an indirect route because she is a shareholder, not an executive. In 2026, Bayan's controlling shareholder was reported to be in sale talks (Haji Isam). Avoid the Katadata article's ICW/offshore-leaks material.

name: Sun Shoukuan
current_role: Chairman, Liaoning Jiachen Group (Yingkou, Liaoning)
profile: Self-made founder-chairman of Jiachen Group, a private metallurgy and coal-mining conglomerate in Yingkou, Liaoning, with interests in steel, refractories, coal chemicals, power generation, real estate and construction. Forbes puts him among the wealthiest entrepreneurs in northeast China; Hurun ranked him Liaoning's richest person in 2021 (RMB 45B).
interesting_fact: Hurun's 2021 list ranked him No. 137 in China with RMB 45 billion, making him Liaoning province's richest person for a second straight year.
deep_cut_fact: Born in October 1949 in Dashiqiao, Liaoning (China's magnesite/refractories hub), he studied silicate engineering at what is now the University of Science and Technology Liaoning.
notes: Chinese name usually written 孙寿宽 (Forbes romanizes as Sun Shoukuan). Very private; no official company website or press contact found. Energy angle: Jiachen has coal-chemical and power-generation businesses. Sources for bio are a Chinese list aggregator citing Hurun; verify before use.

name: Zhang Jianzhong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager (CEO), Moore Threads Technology (Shanghai STAR Market)
profile: Zhang (James Zhang), born 1966 in Nanjing, was Nvidia's global VP and China GM for about 14 years before founding GPU designer Moore Threads in Beijing in October 2020. It makes full-function GPUs and AI training clusters. Its Dec 2025 STAR Market IPO rose about 425% on day one, making his roughly 36% stake worth billions.
interesting_fact: After Moore Threads was put on the US Entity List in October 2023, Zhang told staff China's GPU industry was not in its 'darkest hour' and vowed to build 'China's highest-quality full-function GPU'. Two years later the company listed at a valuation near US$40bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before Nvidia, Zhang studied computer science at Nanjing University of Science and Technology. He was then a senior researcher at the national computer lab of the Automation Research and Design Institute of Metallurgical Industry (1990-92), followed by stints at HP China (from 1992) and Dell China (2001-06).
notes: mkt@mthreads.com is Moore Threads' published marketing and promotion contact; no dedicated press address was found. The company is on the US Entity List, which may matter for a US-based podcast. He gives few English-language interviews.

name: Huang Xiaolei
current_role: Director & general manager (CEO), Eoptolink Technology (Chengdu, 300502.SZ); co-actual controller with chairman Gao Guangrong
profile: Electronics engineer (born 1969) who co-founded Chengdu-based optical-module maker Eoptolink in 2008 with Gao Guangrong and others, serving as technical director then general manager; it listed in Shenzhen in 2016. Eoptolink now supplies high-speed (800G/1.6T) optical transceivers for AI data centres, reportedly to Google and Nvidia, with a Thailand plant online since 2023 and a Hong Kong listing in preparation.
interesting_fact: Most of Eoptolink's revenue comes from overseas hyperscale/AI customers; its Thailand plant (first overseas base) started in 2023 and phase two came online in 2025. Huang was named to Forbes China's Best CEO list.
deep_cut_fact: A 1991 Southeast University radio-engineering grad, he spent 1991-98 as an engineer at Chengdu Qianfeng Electronic Instrument Factory and in 1999 founded his own small firm, Huida Electronics, before joining the optical-module world as a test engineer and technical director.
notes: Highly relevant for AI data-center optics angle. Runs operations while chairman Gao Guangrong handles strategy (per 2025 annual report). Board secretary Wang Cheng (Daniel.wang@eoptolink.com) is listed in filings as the formal contact. Low English-language media presence.

name: Fan Mingqiang
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'JML' (China). Could not confirm which company JML refers to or verify this person's role; note that Jinmailang (often abbreviated JML) instant-noodle maker was founded and is chaired by Fan Xianguo, not Fan Mingqiang, per Chinese Wikipedia.
notes: Research incomplete: shared web-search budget was exhausted before this person; no Forbes profile page or Wikipedia entry found. Possible link to Jinmailang (https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/今麦郎) is unconfirmed - verify identity before outreach.

name: Luo Tsai-Ren
current_role: Vice Chairman, Cheng Shin Rubber Industry Co. (Maxxis/CST tyres; TWSE: 2105), since May 2023
profile: Lo Tsai-jen (b. 1953, Changhua, Taiwan) is the second son of Luo Jye, who founded Cheng Shin Rubber in Yuanlin in 1967 as a bicycle-tyre maker; it grew into Maxxis, one of the world's largest tyre groups. He built and ran its mainland China operations, chaired the group from 2014 to 2020, and returned as vice chairman in 2023.
interesting_fact: He succeeded his father as chairman of Cheng Shin on 17 June 2014 and stepped down in June 2020, when former general manager Chen Rong-hua took over. He returned to the board as vice chairman in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He studied marketing and materials management at New Jersey Institute of Technology (entering 1972). In 1993 he was sent to Kunshan to build Cheng Shin's China plant. A 2014 Business Today profile was headlined that he 'doesn't like socialising' and 'made the factory his home for twenty years'.
notes: Taiwanese, though listed under China. Low-key and reportedly shuns socialising. No personal channels or published press contact found; CST/Maxxis corporate is the only route. Research was limited because the web search budget was exhausted.

name: Qi Zhenbo
current_role: Founder of Meione (美ONE / 美腕, Shanghai), per Hurun listings
profile: Hurun lists Qi Zhenbo (戚振波) as the founder of Meione, a Shanghai 'new retail' unicorn. Meione (美ONE) is the agency behind top livestream seller Li Jiaqi: it signed him in late 2016 after he won a L'Oréal-sponsored Taobao livestreaming contest, and it runs his livestream e-commerce business.
interesting_fact: 美ONE ran the late-2016 L'Oréal 'BA网红化' Taobao Live contest that discovered Li Jiaqi, who arrived in Shanghai with RMB 2,000 and became China's 'Lipstick King' of livestream selling.
notes: Low-profile founder. Identity rests on the Hurun listing (戚振波 / Meione); I could not independently confirm his biography because the web-search budget was exhausted and Baidu Baike blocked access. Treat this as a lead. The best route is probably through 美腕/美ONE corporate PR.

name: Zhou Zhiwen
current_role: Major shareholder of JOINN Laboratories (Beijing; SSE 603127 / HKEX 6127); current board title not verified
profile: Listed as a billionaire through his stake in JOINN Laboratories (昭衍新药), a Beijing contract research organization founded in 1995 that provides non-clinical safety/toxicology studies, clinical trial and pharmacovigilance services, and lab animal models, with facilities in Beijing, Suzhou, Guangzhou, San Francisco and Boston. It is dual-listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: JOINN, founded in Beijing in 1995, has passed China NMPA GLP certification ten times and runs research sites in San Francisco (since 2013) and Boston (since 2019), as well as across China.

public_contacts.value: jiafengsong@joinn-lab.com (JOINN investor relations contact Jia Fengsong; tel 010-67869582)

He is widely reported as co-founder alongside chair Feng Yuxia, but this was not verified here; check HKEX annual-report director bios before outreach. Media cooperation line on site: 010-67869966-1811.

name: Xia Yu
current_role: Founder, Chairwoman, President and CEO, Akeso Inc. (HKEX: 9926); director, Summit Therapeutics (Nasdaq: SMMT)
profile: Gansu-born scientist (Michelle Xia) with a Newcastle University PhD who did cancer research in the US and worked at Bayer, PDL BioPharma and Crown Bioscience before co-founding Akeso in Zhongshan in 2012 with under $3m. Akeso's bispecific antibody ivonescimab beat Merck's Keytruda in a 2024 China trial; partner Summit licensed it for the West.
interesting_fact: Named to TIME100 Health in 2025; Akeso's ivonescimab result versus Keytruda was hailed as a watershed moment for Chinese biotech.
deep_cut_fact: Akeso is named after Aceso, the Greek goddess of healing; at its founding the co-founders drew no salaries and hired researchers with only undergraduate degrees.
notes: Goes by Michelle Xia in English. Deep-cut fact sourced via Wikipedia citing WSJ (Apr 2025). Strong founder story; has done Western media (WSJ, Forbes, BioSpace).

profile: Hurun China lists Wang Chenghai and Luo Hongxia as the wealth holders behind Dingtong, an electronic-components company (Hurun China 2021-2026, Hurun Global 2026). I couldn't verify further details because my web search quota ran out.
notes: Not verified because the search quota was exhausted. name: Luo Hongxia
current_role: Listed by Hurun alongside Wang Chenghai as holder of Dongguan Dingtong Precision Technology (鼎通科技, SSE STAR 688668) wealth; personal role not confirmed
profile: Hurun attributes her wealth, shared with Wang Chenghai, to Dongguan Dingtong Precision Technology. Dingtong was founded in 2003 as a precision hardware maker and listed on the STAR Market, and makes precision components for high-speed communication connectors and automotive connectors. Chairman Wang Chenghai (b. 1970) has led the company since 2003.
