name: Wang Ping
current_role: Co-founder/major shareholder of Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical (SZSE: 002851), per Hurun; exact current title not verified
profile: Hurun lists Wang Ping, alongside chairman Tong Yongsheng, as a principal owner of Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical, a power-electronics maker founded in 2003 and listed in Shenzhen in 2017. Megmeet makes power supplies, EV drivetrain parts, industrial automation and appliance controls, and since 2023 has pushed into AI data-center (AIDC) power, with orders topping RMB 10B in 2025.
interesting_fact: Megmeet now pitches itself as a 'cornerstone of global computing-power infrastructure': its catalogue includes CRPS server power supplies, power shelves, BBU shelves and an 800V/570kW side rack for AI data centers.
notes: Highly relevant to a data-center/energy podcast via Megmeet's AI-server power business, but Wang Ping's personal role is unverified (common name; company management page did not list her/him). Web-search budget was exhausted; check Megmeet's annual report on cninfo before outreach. Tong Yongsheng is the company's public face.

name: Dmitry Mazepin
current_role: Former owner/CEO and remaining minority shareholder of Uralchem; President of the Aquatics Federation of Russia (since 2024)
profile: Minsk-born Mazepin worked in banking and insurance in the 1990s and ran oil and coal companies. He was First Deputy Chairman of the Russian Federal Property Fund in 2002. He then built Uralchem, one of the world's largest nitrogen and potash fertilizer producers, starting with a 2004 privatization purchase. After EU/UK sanctions in 2022 he stepped down as CEO and sold a 52% controlling stake.
interesting_fact: From 2022 to 2024 Uralchem made several humanitarian shipments of fertilizer to African countries.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from the Minsk Suvorov Military School in 1985, Mazepin served as a military interpreter in Afghanistan from 1986 to 1988. He later graduated in economics from MGIMO (1992) and earned a PhD in 2012 with a thesis on managing the stock-market potential of an oil producer.
notes: Under EU and UK sanctions since March 2022; check legal and compliance implications before any engagement. He sold control of Uralchem in 2022 (TASS: https://tass.ru/ekonomika/14033745), so the current stake should be verified. The Uralchem general inbox is the only published route.

name: Ni Zugen
current_role: Chairman, Kingclean Electric Co., Ltd. (莱克电气, Shanghai: 603355), Suzhou
profile: Ni Zugen worked at a Suzhou vacuum-cleaner factory before founding Kingclean in October 1994. The company makes cleaning appliances, water purifiers, coffee makers, kitchen appliances and garden tools, sold under its own Lexy brand and as an OEM. It listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2015.
interesting_fact: Kingclean describes its core technology as ultra-high-speed digital motors, and it also sells key motor components to other manufacturers alongside its consumer goods business.
notes: Alive is inferred from the Forbes real-time 2026 listing. Low international profile. The English corporate site loads its contact details dynamically, so no email was captured. IR contacts would be in the Shanghai exchange filings for 603355. Web search was unavailable for this entry (shared budget used up).

name: Prem Kumar Arora
current_role: Co-founder and Director - FHA (finance, HR and administration), Mankind Pharma Ltd.
profile: Prem Kumar (PK) Arora co-founded New Delhi-based Mankind Pharma with his brothers-in-law Ramesh and Rajeev Juneja. The company was incorporated in 1991 and began operations in 1995. It grew into India's fourth-largest drugmaker by domestic sales, selling affordable generics and consumer brands, and listed on NSE/BSE in May 2023. Arora oversees finance, HR and operations.
interesting_fact: Mankind entered consumer healthcare by launching the Manforce and Prega News brands, now household names in India, alongside its generics business.
notes: Mankind's own site calls him a co-founder; Forbes says the company was founded by his wife's brothers. Low personal media profile; the Juneja brothers are the public faces. No sourced personal deep-cut found; web search quota ran out before more digging.

name: F.C. Tseng
current_role: Director, TSMC (board member since 1997); Chairman, TSMC China and TSMC Education & Culture Foundation; Vice Chairman, Vanguard International Semiconductor
profile: Fan-Cheng Tseng is one of Morris Chang's longest-serving lieutenants: TSMC president 1998-2001, deputy CEO 2001-05 and vice chairman 2005-18. While Chang chased customers, Tseng consolidated TSMC internally. His TSMC shares made him a billionaire in 2024 amid the AI chip boom; he remains on the board and chairs TSMC China.
interesting_fact: Tseng has sat on TSMC's board since May 1997 and was its president from 1998 to 2001, before becoming vice chairman for 13 years (2005-2018).
deep_cut_fact: In 1976 ITRI sent him, with Shih Chin-tai and Robert Tsao, to RCA in the US for CMOS IC training: part of the first group of Taiwanese engineers to acquire integrated-circuit technology, seen as the spark of Taiwan's chip industry.
notes: Low public profile; appears at events in his role as chairman of the TSMC Education and Culture Foundation. TSMC corporate PR (press@tsmc.com) is the official route.

name: Tom Ford
current_role: Film director, writer and producer (Fade to Black); founder of Tom Ford International (sold to Estée Lauder, 2022)
profile: Texas-born designer who revived Gucci as creative director (1994-2004) and founded Tom Ford International in 2005. He sold the brand and its beauty business to Estée Lauder for $2.8bn in 2022 and stepped back fully at the end of 2023. He is now focused on film: after A Single Man and Nocturnal Animals, he is directing an adaptation of Anne Rice's Cry to Heaven, which began shooting in January 2026.
interesting_fact: He trained in interior architecture at Parsons rather than fashion. His Santa Fe ranch, Cerro Pelon, was designed by Japanese architect Tadao Ando.
deep_cut_fact: To land his first fashion job, he phoned designer Cathy Hardwick every day for a month. Asked his favourite European designers, he said 'Armani and Chanel', later admitting it was because she was wearing Armani. He worked as her design assistant for two years.
notes: No personal channels found; the Tom Ford brand accounts are now owned by Estée Lauder, not by him. The most realistic route is via his film company Fade to Black or his film publicists around the Cry to Heaven release. He is a weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Lirio Parisotto
current_role: Founder and chairman, Videolar-Innova (petrochemicals/plastics, Manaus); private equity investor
profile: Born in Nova Bassano, Rio Grande do Sul, and trained as a physician (Universidade de Caxias do Sul), Parisotto founded Videolar, a pioneer in Brazilian videocassette manufacturing, and reinvested its profits in dividend-paying Brazilian stocks (banks, power, mining, steel). Videolar later merged with Innova to make petrochemical products; he stepped back from day-to-day management in 2007.
interesting_fact: He has 11 siblings, holds a medical degree and also spent time in a monastery before turning to business.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Videolar reportedly came after he saw a videocassette in a New York store; and as a young man in 1971 he won a monograph contest run by Brazil's Army Ministry, putting the prize (worth about a VW Beetle) into his first stock-market investment.
notes: Sources differ on Videolar's founding year (1980 vs 1988). Sits on the board of Fundacao Amazonas Sustentavel (per MarketScreener). Low media profile; route via Videolar-Innova.

name: Thomas Kwok
current_role: Senior Director, Sun Hung Kai Real Estate Agency (subsidiary of Sun Hung Kai Properties), since 2020
profile: Thomas Kwok Ping-kwong is the second son of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng and, with brothers Raymond and Walter, inherited one of Hong Kong's largest developers in 1990. He was SHKP joint chairman until 2014; since 2020 he has been a senior director of the group's real estate agency arm, while his son Adam serves as an SHKP executive director.
interesting_fact: He and brother Raymond, both devout Christians, built the Noah's Ark theme park on Ma Wan island, Hong Kong, reflecting their evangelical faith.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a civil engineer (BSc, Imperial College London; MBA, London Business School), and in the 1990s set up a church in the 75th-floor pyramid atrium atop SHKP's Central Plaza tower.
notes: Sensitive history (2014 bribery conviction, released 2019); avoid in outreach. Approach via SHKP corporate communications. SHKP also runs data-centre business (SUNeVision/iAdvantage), a possible podcast angle.

name: Alexander Frolov
current_role: Investor; former CEO of Evraz (2007-2021) and still a major shareholder (~10%); no current executive role found
profile: A physicist (MIPT PhD) who left Moscow's Kurchatov Institute in 1994 to go into business. With partner Alexander Abramov he built the Evraz steel and coking-coal group, sold 40% of it to Roman Abramovich in 2006 for more than $3B, and was CEO from 2007 to 2021. He left the Evraz board in March 2022 and was sanctioned by the UK in November 2022. He also holds stakes in Norilsk Nickel, Yandex and Ivi.
interesting_fact: He started out as a research fellow at the I.V. Kurchatov Institute of Atomic Energy after earning a doctorate in physics and mathematics, an unusual path into steel and coal.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated with honours from the Department of Molecular and Chemical Physics at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology (1987). He was also one of the sponsors of the restoration of the Valaam Spaso-Preobrazhensky Monastery on Lake Ladoga.
notes: Under UK sanctions since November 2022 (Russia-related); check legal and reputational exposure before any outreach. Very private, with no published personal or office contacts found. The Valaam fact comes from Forbes facts (https://www.forbes.com/profile/alexander-frolov/).

name: Yusuf Hamied
current_role: Non-executive Chairman, Cipla Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Cambridge-trained chemist (b. 1936, Vilnius; raised in Bombay). He took over Cipla, the generic drugmaker his father founded in 1935, and became famous for taking on Big Pharma with low-cost generics. He is now Cipla's non-executive chairman and a major benefactor of Cambridge University.
interesting_fact: In 2001 he electrified global health by offering a triple-drug AIDS cocktail for about $1 a day, a fraction of branded prices. The price later fell to around 20 cents a day.
deep_cut_fact: He studied chemistry at Christ's College, Cambridge, under Nobel laureate Alexander (Lord) Todd. Cambridge's oldest chemistry professorship, the 1702 Chair, is now the Yusuf Hamied 1702 Chair, and there is a 'Todd-Hamied' laboratory and seminar room in tribute to both men. He was elected FRS in 2019.
notes: Aged 90 and now only a non-executive chairman, though he still gives occasional interviews on drug access. Cipla's pages blocked automated access, so its published IR/media email could not be captured; check cipla.com/investors manually. Childhood friend of conductor Zubin Mehta.

name: Zhao Weiguo
current_role: None. Former chairman of Tsinghua Unigroup; currently imprisoned in China
profile: A Tsinghua University alumnus who led chip conglomerate Tsinghua Unigroup and drove a major acquisition push in China's semiconductor industry in the 2010s. He lost control after Unigroup's 2021-22 restructuring, when his Jiankun group and Tsinghua Holdings exited. In May 2025 a Jilin court sentenced him to death with a two-year reprieve for embezzlement and related crimes.
notes: Not a viable outreach target: he is serving a suspended death sentence handed down at first instance on May 14, 2025 (https://www.caixinglobal.com/2025-05-15/former-tsinghua-unigroup-chairman-zhao-weiguo-receives-suspended-death-sentence-in-first-instance-for-embezzlement-of-particularly-huge-amounts-102319729.html). All his personal assets were ordered confiscated. Forbes lists him as 'former'.

name: Hans Georg Naeder
current_role: Chairman of the Board (Verwaltungsrat) / Chairman of the Management Board, Ottobock SE & Co. KGaA; majority owner via Näder Holding
profile: Hans Georg Näder (b. 1961, Duderstadt) is the third-generation head of Ottobock, the prosthetics and orthotics maker founded by his grandfather Otto Bock in 1919. He took over from his father in 1990 at age 28 and built it into a world leader with over 10,000 staff and 60 country branches. Ottobock listed in Frankfurt in October 2025; his family holding keeps roughly 80% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Ottobock has given on-site technical repair service at every Paralympic Games since Seoul 1988, became the IPC's first Worldwide Partner in 2005, and is signed on through Brisbane 2032.
deep_cut_fact: He has been an honorary professor at PFH Göttingen since 2005 and pushed for its new 'Orthobionik' (orthobionics) degree course. He has also been a guest professor at Capital Medical University in Beijing since 2009.
notes: Press contact is Merle Florstedt, Head of Corporate Communications, as named in Ottobock press releases. Avoid the pending VAT investigation over yacht purchases and the May 2026 short-seller report. He is a keen sailor (yacht Pink Gin won the 2007 Millennium Cup per Forbes), but no independent source was confirmed for that.

name: Bret Taylor
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Sierra (AI customer-service agents); Chairman of the board, OpenAI
profile: Stanford-trained engineer who led the team that co-created Google Maps, co-founded FriendFeed (sold to Facebook, where he became CTO), built Quip (sold to Salesforce, where he rose to co-CEO) and chaired Twitter's board through the Musk sale. Co-founded Sierra with Clay Bavor in 2023; a roughly 25% stake at a $10B valuation made him a billionaire, and he has chaired OpenAI since Nov 2023.
interesting_fact: Facebook's 'Like' button came from FriendFeed, the startup Taylor co-founded and sold to Facebook in 2009; in Dec 2025 he bought a ~1% minority stake in the San Francisco 49ers.
deep_cut_fact: Recounting Google's pre-Maps local search, Taylor noted that a search for 'coffee near Menlo Park' returned only Sun Microsystems pages, because Sun's Java-themed site was full of coffee puns. His follow-up, Google Local, was a formative near-miss that led to Google Maps.
notes: Very accessible publicly (frequent podcast guest). He lists his personal Gmail on his own homepage backchannel.org, which is the best direct route. Strong fit for AI/data-centre themes given his OpenAI chairmanship.

name: Clay Bavor
current_role: Cofounder, Sierra (AI customer-service agents), San Francisco
profile: Clay Bavor cofounded Sierra with Bret Taylor in 2023 after 18 years at Google, where he rose from associate product manager to VP running Google Labs and its AR/VR work (Cardboard, Daydream, ARCore, Lens, Project Starline). Sierra builds AI agents for customer service; a $350M round led by Greenoaks valued it at $10B.
interesting_fact: He and Bret Taylor were both hired into Google's associate product manager program by Marissa Mayer and stayed friends for ~20 years (incl. a 'monthly' poker game that met about twice a year) before founding Sierra.
deep_cut_fact: Sierra was hatched over a long lunch in December 2022, a week after ChatGPT launched. Though known as Google's 'AR/VR guy', Bavor says he had become obsessed with language models in Google Labs, the group that produced NotebookLM.
notes: No published press email for Sierra found; company X account and Bavor's own (lightly used) X account are the public routes. Frequent conference/podcast guest (Acquired, Slush 2025, AI Engineer), so podcast invitations are plausible.

name: Zadik Bino
current_role: Controlling shareholder (with family, via Bino Holdings) of FIBI Holdings / First International Bank of Israel
profile: Iraqi-born Israeli banker and investor (b. 1943/44). He was CEO of First International Bank of Israel (1978-86) and CEO of Bank Leumi (1987-89), then built a fortune controlling Paz Oil (from 1999, incl. the 2006 Ashdod refinery purchase and IPO) and later buying control of FIBI. He exited Paz in 2016-17; the Bino family still controls FIBI Holdings, chaired by his son Gil.
interesting_fact: Named Globes Man of the Year in 2006, a year in which he bought Bank Otsar Hahayal, acquired the Ashdod oil refinery and took Paz public.
deep_cut_fact: Arriving from Basra aged six in 1950, he grew up in Kiryat Ono helping in his parents' small grocery store, served as an Israeli Air Force flight technician, played midfield for Hapoel Kiryat Ono, and began his banking career as a junior teller at Bank Hapoalim.
notes: Low-profile, in his 80s; no personal channels found. Best route is via First International Bank of Israel (fibi.co.il) investor relations or Bino Holdings. Birth year given as 1943 (Wikipedia) or 13 Oct 1944 (Hebrew sources).

name: Drew Houston
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO of Dropbox (transitioning to executive chairman after co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi was named in May 2026); Meta board member
profile: Drew Houston co-founded Dropbox with MIT classmate Arash Ferdowsi in 2007 at age 24, took it public on Nasdaq in 2018 and remains its largest individual shareholder (20%+). In May 2026 Dropbox named Ashraf Alkarmi co-CEO; Houston is to move to executive chairman after a transition. He has sat on Meta's board since 2020.
interesting_fact: Houston conceived Dropbox after repeatedly forgetting his USB flash drive as an MIT student; Dropbox became touted as Y Combinator's most successful early investment. At 15 he worked at an industrial robotics startup (Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: His first company, an online SAT-prep startup called 'The Accolade Group, LLC', was founded with Andrew Crick in a Chili's over onion strings when he was 21; while burned out on it he wrote a poker bot. His 2013 MIT commencement 'cheat sheet': a tennis ball, a circle and the number 30,000.
notes: Leadership transition in progress (co-CEO Alkarmi named May 26, 2026). Houston is an active public speaker on AI and 'Dropbox Dash'; route via Dropbox press team.

name: Wu Kai
current_role: Chief Scientist, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. (CATL); Academician, Chinese Academy of Engineering (elected 2025)
profile: Wu Kai (b. 1968) is CATL's chief scientist and a long-time lieutenant of founder Robin Zeng: he met Zeng in 1999, served as VP of technology at ATL and joined CATL as chief scientist in 2011. His CATL shareholding made him a billionaire. He now fronts CATL's technology roadmap, announcing sodium-ion mass production in 2026 and talking up lithium-air as a future direction.
interesting_fact: He was elected an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering in November 2025; his credited inventions include a 'nano-rivet' reinforcement that stops high-nickel cathode materials cracking at high voltage, and a new wound full-tab power-battery process.
deep_cut_fact: Before batteries he trained as a naval engineer: his bachelor's and master's degrees from Shanghai Jiao Tong University are in ship engineering (doctorate in applied chemistry), and he began as a teacher at Wuhan University of Technology.
notes: No personal channels found; route via CATL corporate communications. He speaks often at CATL Super Tech Day and academic forums (e.g., SJTU GIFT lecture Dec 2025, where he is a distinguished professor) - a speaking-event angle may work better than cold outreach. Name is common; identity matched via CATL/batteries.

name: Michael Polsky
current_role: Founder and CEO, Invenergy (Chicago)
profile: Kyiv-born thermal engineer who fled the USSR as a refugee, co-founded Indeck Energy while a Chicago Booth evening MBA student, then sold gas-plant developer SkyGen to Calpine for ~$450M (2000-01). He founded Invenergy in 2001, now a top US private clean-energy developer (~33 GW), and is pushing the Grain Belt Express transmission line.
interesting_fact: He has given and pledged more than $150M to the University of Chicago, whose Polsky Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation bears his name; Invenergy also supplies power deals for data centers, e.g. ~800 MW for Meta.
deep_cut_fact: He arrived in the US with $500, four suitcases and no English, mailed his résumé to hundreds of companies he found in library directories, and won his first job, an engineering post at Bechtel, by communicating through math equations and sketches.
notes: Gives occasional long-form interviews (Brunswick Review, UChicago Big Brains podcast), so a strong podcast fit for energy and data-center power. Best route is Invenergy media relations. Avoid the divorce item in the Forbes bio.

name: Li Zhenguo
current_role: Founder, LONGi Green Energy Technology; President of its Central R&D Institute and CTO (stepped down as director/GM in May 2025)
profile: Li (b. 1968) studied semiconductor materials at Lanzhou University and worked at state semiconductor factories before cofounding LONGi with college classmates in 2000, initially reprocessing silicon. LONGi became the world's largest monocrystalline solar wafer/module maker. In May 2025, amid industry losses, he handed day-to-day management to chairman Zhong Baoshen to lead R&D (notably back-contact cells).
interesting_fact: He named LONGi after Jiang Longji, the former headmaster of his alma mater Lanzhou University.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after graduating in 1990 was at the Huashan Semiconductor Materials Factory; he later ran the crystal base of a Xi'an University of Technology factory before founding LONGi, which started out supplying reprocessed silicon rather than solar products.
notes: The SEC insider match (ADARx Pharmaceuticals CEO) is a DIFFERENT person with the same name; ignore it. Li regularly speaks at WEF/COP events and received a Lifetime Achievement Award at S&P Global Energy Awards; best route is LONGi's media office (PR@longi.com).

name: Sergei Gordeev
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~60%) of PIK Group, Russia's largest homebuilder; stepped down as CEO in 2022
profile: Moscow real-estate investor who made his fortune converting Soviet-era factories into offices (Rosbuilding, 1995; Horus Capital, sold 2010) and then took control of homebuilder PIK after buying a 20% stake from Suleiman Kerimov in 2013. He was PIK's CEO 2014-2022 and an early investor in Hyperloop One; he also served in Russia's Federation Council 2005-2010.
interesting_fact: He led the restoration of Moscow's constructivist Narkomfin building (Moisei Ginzburg, late 1920s), and his Stanislavsky Factory theatre-and-office conversion with John McAslan + Partners won a RIBA International Award (2011).
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he bought the Melnikov House in Moscow and donated it to the state as a public museum; that year he also founded the Russian Avant-garde foundation, which has published 80+ books, and he gave his architectural graphics collection to the Schusev Museum of Architecture.
notes: Russia-based; check current sanctions/compliance position before any engagement (not verified here - search budget exhausted). Architecture and avant-garde preservation are his evident passions. No published personal contact found; PIK corporate IR is the only obvious route.

name: Egon Durban
current_role: Managing Partner and CEO, Silver Lake; Chairman of Endeavor Group Holdings
profile: Durban was a founding principal of tech private-equity firm Silver Lake in 1999 after Morgan Stanley investment banking, and now leads it as Managing Partner and CEO. He orchestrated landmark deals in Skype and Dell; he chairs Endeavor and sits on boards incl. Dell, Electronic Arts, G42, Waymo, City Football Group, TKO and the TikTok USDS JV.
interesting_fact: His board seats span AI and data-center-adjacent bets (Dell, Abu Dhabi AI group G42, Waymo) as well as sport (TKO/UFC-WWE, City Football Group, Las Vegas Raiders board).
deep_cut_fact: A Texas native, he made his name at Silver Lake on Skype, where he was chairman of the operating committee through the buyout and the 2011 sale to Microsoft; he also serves on the Las Vegas Raiders' board of directors.

public_contacts.value: Edelman Smithfield (Silver Lake media contact on 2025 releases): Kelsey.nevius@edelmansmithfield.com

notes: Famously media-shy; best route is Silver Lake media inquiries. Silver Lake's site now lists him as 'Managing Partner and CEO' (Forbes bio calls him co-CEO; Greg Mondre was co-CEO).

name: Greg Mondre
current_role: Managing Partner and Co-Chairman, Silver Lake (previously Co-CEO), per the firm's current bio
profile: Technology private-equity investor who joined Silver Lake in 1999 after time as a principal at TPG (Texas Pacific Group) and as an investment banker in Goldman Sachs' Communications, Media & Entertainment group. He rose to co-lead the roughly $100bn firm, working on deals including Motorola Solutions, GoDaddy, GoodRx, Red Ventures and Expedia. His wealth comes from his Silver Lake partnership stake.
interesting_fact: Directly relevant to the data-center theme: he sits on the board of Vantage Data Centers North America, alongside Fanatics, Equinox, GoodRx, Red Ventures, Relativity, A Place for Mom and Imagine Learning.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.S. in Economics from Wharton. Before private equity he was an investment banker in Goldman Sachs' Communications, Media and Entertainment Group, and early boards he sat on included Network General and UGS Corporation.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center episode via Vantage Data Centers. No published personal contacts; the route is Silver Lake's media relations. Silver Lake's site blocks automated fetching, so the press contact could not be verified. His title appears to have changed from Co-CEO to Co-Chairman; confirm before outreach.

name: Kenneth Hao
current_role: Managing Partner and Co-Chairman, Silver Lake; director of Broadcom and Altera
profile: Ken Hao joined tech private-equity firm Silver Lake in 2000 after a decade as a managing director at Hambrecht & Quist, and rose to chairman (now co-chairman). He built Silver Lake's Asia business and sits on the boards of Broadcom and Altera, giving him a front-row seat on AI/data-center silicon.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he opened Silver Lake's offices in Asia and led the firm's investments in Alibaba Group and Ant Financial.
deep_cut_fact: He played on the tennis team at Harvard College (A.B. Economics) and today sits on the board of UTR Sports, the Universal Tennis Rating company, as well as the Metropolitan Museum of Art and UCSF.
notes: Silver Lake's own bio now says 'Managing Partner and Co-Chairman' (other sources still say Chairman). Ties to Broadcom/Altera make him relevant to the AI data-center angle. Best route: Silver Lake media inquiries.

name: Daniel Rocher
current_role: Major family shareholder of Groupe Rocher; founder of Daniel Jouvance (marine cosmetics)
profile: Daniel Rocher, son of Yves Rocher (founder of Groupe Rocher, 1959), founded the marine-ingredient skincare brand Daniel Jouvance in 1980; it later became part of the group. With his nephew Bris Rocher he is one of the largest shareholders of the family-controlled group (Yves Rocher, Arbonne, Dr Pierre Ricaud, Petit Bateau; about €2.4bn in sales). Forbes lists him as living in Rennes.
interesting_fact: He is a sculptor and art collector. In 2019 he bought a castle in Provence and turned it into an open-air sculpture gallery.
notes: Private; no personal channels found. The art and sculpture angle (the Provence castle gallery) is the best personal hook, but I could not find the castle's name or website because the web-search budget was exhausted. The Daniel Jouvance site blocked automated access.

name: Bris Rocher
current_role: Chairman, Groupe Rocher (La Gacilly / Issy-les-Moulineaux, France)
profile: Grandson of Yves Rocher, he joined the family company at 16 without finishing his baccalaureate, trained at Arthur Andersen in the US, and became CEO at 31 after his grandfather's death in 2009. He bought back Sanofi's 19.3% stake in 2012, acquired US-based Arbonne in 2018, and in 2023 handed the CEO role to Jean-David Schwartz while staying chairman of the family-controlled group (Yves Rocher, Arbonne, Sabon, Dr Pierre Ricaud, Petit Bateau).
interesting_fact: He joined Yves Rocher at 16 without a baccalaureate after his father Didier died; his grandfather groomed him as successor and he became CEO at 31.
deep_cut_fact: As a young man he wanted to become a jazz guitarist before joining the family business.
notes: Groupe Rocher markets itself as a 'mission-driven company' (entreprise a mission) focused on reconnecting people with nature, a good angle for sustainability-themed outreach. The site has a Press section but no press email found in static HTML.

name: Kamal Ghaffarian
current_role: Founder and executive chairman of X-energy (XE), Intuitive Machines (LUNR), Axiom Space and Quantum Space
profile: Iranian-born serial entrepreneur who came to the US at 17 and co-founded SGT (1994), NASA's No. 2 engineering-services contractor, sold to KBR for $355m in 2018. He founded SMR developer X-energy (2009, now public) and co-founded Intuitive Machines, Axiom Space and Quantum Space.
interesting_fact: His Intuitive Machines lander Odysseus made the first US moon landing since 1972 (Feb 2024); X-energy is building Xe-100 small modular reactors for Dow's Texas plant and evaluating gigawatt-scale deployment with Talen Energy.
deep_cut_fact: At Capitol Technology University's May 2026 commencement (his alma mater: BS 1983, PhD 2022) he handed every graduate a gold envelope with $1,500, saying it was inspired by the family support he got after immigrating. Watching Apollo 11 on TV as a boy in Iran sparked his space passion.
notes: Energy + space angle suits the podcast (SMRs for industrial/data-center power). X-energy comms lead in 2026 releases: Robert McEntyre. info@ is his nonprofit Limitless Space Institute. In 2026 he co-founded the Fermi Explorer Mission and won Armenia's State Award for high tech.

name: Mike Repole
current_role: Majority owner/chairman, NOBULL; founder, Repole Stable; investor in the United Football League
profile: Queens-born son of Italian immigrants (a waiter and a seamstress) who co-founded Glaceau (Vitaminwater, Smartwater; sold to Coca-Cola for $4.1bn in 2007) and BodyArmor (sold to Coca-Cola for $5.6bn in 2021). He now backs consumer brands, owning a majority of athletic brand NOBULL (merged with Tom Brady's TB12 brands in 2024), invested in the UFL in 2025 and runs a major thoroughbred stable.
interesting_fact: Kobe Bryant invested about $5m for 10% of BodyArmor in 2014 and became its creative director; Coca-Cola later bought the whole company for $5.6bn.
deep_cut_fact: Between his two beverage exits he chaired snack maker Pirate's Booty from 2009, growing it about 300% in under five years before its $195m sale to B&G Foods in 2013; his racehorse Uncle Mo was 2010 American Champion Two-Year-Old.
notes: Highly media-friendly (co-starred in Barstool's 'Big Brain', frequent podcast guest) - strong podcast fit. Verified personal social handles not confirmed here (search budget exhausted); check his X/Instagram before use.

name: Brian Venturo
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer, CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV)
profile: Brian Venturo co-founded CoreWeave in 2017 with Michael Intrator and Brannin McBee; it began as an Ethereum mining operation and pivoted into a GPU cloud for AI. CoreWeave went public in 2025 at about a $23B valuation (he owns roughly 6%) and supplies compute to Microsoft, OpenAI and Meta. Earlier he was a portfolio manager at natural-gas-focused hedge fund Hudson Ridge Asset Management.
interesting_fact: CoreWeave started as a crypto miner: at its peak it ran about 50,000 Nvidia consumer gaming GPUs and was, per Venturo, the largest Ethereum miner in the world for around two and a half years before pivoting to AI cloud.
deep_cut_fact: The first mining rigs sat on the pool table in the founders' Manhattan office, then moved to a closet, and then, as Venturo joked, to 'the most cliche place possible' - his grandfather's garage in New Jersey. He also recalls 'literally pounding on the dinner table' to win Magnetar's first $100M check.
notes: Strong fit for data-center/energy angle (energy-trading background, GPU/power infrastructure). Has done podcasts (Castle Island Ventures 'On the Brink' ep163 and EP.366), so is podcast-friendly. Best route: CoreWeave press team. No verified personal X handle found.

name: Riaz Valani
current_role: Investor; general partner at Global Asset Capital; longtime Juul Labs board member and major shareholder
profile: San Francisco-area investor who, through Global Asset Capital, was the first outside investor in Pax Labs/Juul, putting in a few million dollars for a stake of roughly 20%. Altria's 2018 $12.8bn deal for 35% of Juul reportedly brought him a ~$2.6bn pre-tax payout; he has remained a key Juul director and shareholder.
interesting_fact: He was the first person to invest in the e-cigarette maker that became Juul, years before it dominated the US vaping market.
notes: Very private, no personal site or social presence found. Juul is a litigation-heavy topic - keep outreach on investing/early-stage bets. Limited verification (web search budget exhausted); deep-cut left empty.

name: Haluk Bayraktar
current_role: CEO, Baykar (Turkish UAV maker); TÜBİTAK board member; founder of the Türkiye Technology Team (T3) Foundation
profile: Istanbul-born (1978) industrial engineer who joined his father Özdemir's company Baykar after graduate study in the US. He worked on Turkey's first national UAV systems. name: Alexander Skorobogatko
current_role: Co-owner (with Alexander Ponomarenko) of airport, port and real-estate holdings, including an interest in Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport
profile: Alexander Skorobogatko and long-time partner Alexander Ponomarenko began with a small perfume factory in Ukraine, then founded a bank in Moscow and moved into sea ports. In 2013 they and Arkady Rotenberg won the tender to develop the state-owned Sheremetyevo airport. Their TPS Real Estate held over half of Kyiv's Ocean Plaza mall, which Ukraine seized in 2023.

name: Thomas Steyer
current_role: Co-founder and co-executive chair, Galvanize Climate Solutions; 2026 California gubernatorial candidate (finished third in the June 2026 primary)
profile: Founded hedge fund Farallon Capital and ran it for 26 years before selling out in 2012 to focus on climate and politics. He founded NextGen Climate/America and ran for president in 2020. In 2021 he co-founded climate investor Galvanize with Katie Hall. He spent heavily on a 2026 run for California governor but placed third in the June primary and did not advance.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he and his wife Kat Taylor gave $41m to create the TomKat Center for Sustainable Energy at Stanford. In 2024 he published a climate book, 'Cheaper, Faster, Better: How We'll Win the Climate War'.
deep_cut_fact: He and Kat Taylor run TomKat Ranch in Pescadero, near Half Moon Bay, a working cattle ranch used to research and demonstrate regenerative, climate-friendly agriculture. The New York Times called it 'an accidental cattle ranch'.
notes: He is an excellent fit for an energy podcast (climate investing, energy research philanthropy, and a climate-economics book) and is very media-accessible. Galvanize media contact is the best route. Since he is fresh off a losing governor campaign, lead with energy and investing, not politics.

name: Keith Bentley
current_role: Co-founder and director, Bentley Systems (retired as CTO in 2023)
profile: Keith Bentley co-founded infrastructure-engineering software maker Bentley Systems with brother Barry in 1984, was CEO until 2000 and then CTO until retiring in 2023; he remains a board member. He wrote the program that became MicroStation, the company's flagship 3D CAD platform. Bentley (IPO 2020, ~$1.5B sales) is still majority family-owned.
interesting_fact: He worked more than 100 hours a week while developing the first version of MicroStation.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding the company he developed CAD software as a programmer at DuPont; Bentley's first commercial product, PseudoStation (1985), let engineers view and edit Intergraph design files on cheaper graphics terminals, the forerunner of MicroStation.
notes: Engineering-minded founder; strong fit for infrastructure/energy/data-center digital-twin topics (Bentley's iTwin platform). Route via Bentley media relations.

name: Andreas Pohl
current_role: Chairman of the Executive Board (Vorsitzender des Vorstandes), Deutsche Vermögensberatung AG (DVAG), Frankfurt
profile: Born in Marburg in 1964, son of DVAG founder Reinfried Pohl Sr. DVAG is Germany's largest independent financial-advisory sales organisation, selling funds, insurance and annuities. He joined in 1984, became general manager in 1991 and took over after his father died in 2014. He and his brother each own half of the family holding, which owns 60% of DVAG; Generali holds the other 40%.
interesting_fact: He is a vintage car aficionado who occasionally competes in vintage car races.
deep_cut_fact: He did not start at the top: after school in Marburg he trained as an insurance clerk (Versicherungskaufmann) and spent time in the USA before joining his father's company in 1984. As a teenager he went along to new branch openings with his father.
notes: DVAG's sales model has drawn public criticism in Germany (e.g. from Jan Böhmermann), so avoid it as an opener. Use the press office for requests. Not a natural energy or data-center fit; an entrepreneurship and family-succession angle works better.

name: Wesley Edens
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, New Fortress Energy (NASDAQ: NFE); cofounder of Fortress Investment Group; co-owner of the Milwaukee Bucks and Aston Villa
profile: Born in Helena, Montana (1961). He worked at Lehman and BlackRock before cofounding Fortress Investment Group in 1998 and became a billionaire when it went public in 2007. He founded LNG company New Fortress Energy in 2014. Through Fortress he built Brightline, the only private U.S. intercity passenger railroad (Miami-Orlando), and started Brightline West (Las Vegas-Southern California) in 2024.
interesting_fact: Brightline West is a roughly $12B, 260-mile line from Las Vegas to Rancho Cucamonga designed for speeds up to 200 mph. It is billed as the first true high-speed rail line in the U.S.
deep_cut_fact: Brightline was inspired by Les Standiford's book 'Last Train to Paradise', about Henry Flagler's Florida railroad. In 2007 Fortress bought Flagler's original Florida East Coast line. As a teenager in Montana, Edens was a competitive skier.
notes: Strong energy/infrastructure fit (LNG terminals in Jamaica, Brazil and Puerto Rico; high-speed rail). Steer clear of NFE's recent financial stress. The NFE IR page blocked automated access, so check it manually for a named IR/press email.

name: Alexey Repik
current_role: Chairman, All-Russian public organisation 'Delovaya Rossiya' (Business Russia); founder of R-Pharm
profile: Moscow-born (1979) Higher School of Economics graduate who founded R-Pharm in 2001 with $40,000, half of it from his mother. It grew into one of Russia's largest drugmakers and state suppliers, and Mitsui bought 10% in 2017. In 2022 he stepped down as R-Pharm chairman and reportedly sold his R-Pharm assets. He chairs the business lobby Delovaya Rossiya.
interesting_fact: He started R-Pharm in 2001 with $40,000 in startup capital, half of which came from his mother. He had taken his first healthcare job in 1995, aged about 16.
deep_cut_fact: He funded construction of a large dog shelter in Yaroslavl, about 250 km from Moscow, designed to handle about 1,500 dogs a year.
notes: CAUTION: under UK sanctions since Feb 2023 and Canadian sanctions since May 2023 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksey_Repik). In 2024 he was an authorised representative of Putin's presidential campaign. Check the legal and reputational implications before any outreach. The only published route is Delovaya Rossiya.

name: Aman Sanger
current_role: Co-founder, Cursor (Anysphere Inc.), now a wholly owned subsidiary of SpaceX after the August 2026 acquisition
profile: MIT-trained co-founder (with Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif and Arvid Lunnemark, 2022) of Cursor, the AI code editor used by millions of developers at firms like Nvidia, Adobe and Uber. Cursor passed $1B in annualized revenue and was acquired by SpaceX in an all-stock deal valued at $60B (closed Aug 2026), leaving each cofounder with SpaceX shares Forbes values at ~$2.4B.
interesting_fact: He started coding at 14, interned at Bridgewater Associates and Google, ran his own AI consultancy before Cursor, and was an avid squash player at MIT.
deep_cut_fact: Before the code editor, Sanger and Michael Truell worked on an earlier project also called Cursor for computer-aided design (CAD), training models from scratch to predict CAD operations, as he recounted on the Latent Space podcast in 2023.

public_contacts.value: hi@cursor.com (Cursor general contact, listed as customer service)

notes: Active on X (@amanrsanger) - most direct public channel. Net worth estimates vary widely ($2.4B Forbes vs $5.5B in Indian press). X handle attributed via his GitHub profile (Sanger2000) per search; profile page not directly viewable here. Good fit for AI/data-center compute angle (training models with SpaceX/xAI compute).

name: Arvid Lunnemark
current_role: Founder, Integrous Research (AI safety startup); co-founder of Cursor (Anysphere)
profile: Swedish-born MIT alum and former math olympiad champion who co-founded Anysphere, maker of the AI code editor Cursor, with three MIT friends in 2022. He left Cursor in October 2025 to start Integrous Research, focused on safer AI systems; Forbes says each co-founder got SpaceX shares worth ~$2.4B when SpaceX acquired Cursor for $60B in 2026.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding Cursor he interned in quantitative trading at Jane Street and in software engineering at Stripe; Cursor passed $1B in annualized revenue before its sale to SpaceX.
deep_cut_fact: His personal site keeps a public 'Questions' page of things he wants concrete answers to, such as 'Why is teleportation hard?' and 'Why is it so expensive to build tunnels?', and invites readers to email him answers. In 2021 he also wrote an essay arguing it is time to move beyond end-to-end encryption because it leaks metadata.
notes: Self-published Gmail on arvid.xyz (Cloudflare-obfuscated). GitHub: github.com/arvid220u (linked from his site). His 'Questions' page explicitly invites email, so a curiosity-led note may land well. Leaving post: arvid.xyz/posts/leaving/ (2025-10-17).

name: Michael Truell
current_role: Leads/works on AI Products at 'SpaceXSI' (SpaceX/xAI) per his own site and X bio; cofounder and CEO of Cursor (Anysphere), acquired by SpaceX in 2026
profile: New York-raised MIT CS/math dropout who cofounded Anysphere/Cursor in 2022 with MIT friends Aman Sanger, Sualeh Asif and Arvid Lunnemark. Cursor's AI code editor passed $1B in annualized revenue, and SpaceX agreed a ~$60B all-stock acquisition in 2026; Truell now works on AI products inside SpaceX.
interesting_fact: Cursor initially set out to build a 'copilot for mechanical engineers' (CAD) because it seemed a sleepy, uncompetitive niche, before pivoting to AI coding; he started coding at 11 to make his own mobile games.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenage Two Sigma summer intern in 2016, he co-created (with Ben Spector) Halite, the open-source AI bot-programming competition; he built the website and competition backend. Halite ran through Halite III and a Kaggle-hosted Halite IV.
notes: His personal site invites contact at 'mntruell at gmail dot com'. SpaceX deal closing date (reported Aug 2026) comes from Forbes input; Fortune (Jun 2026) confirms SpaceX exercised its option. Strong fit for AI/data-center compute angle.

name: Sualeh Asif
current_role: Co-founder (and reported Chief Product Officer), Anysphere / Cursor - acquired by SpaceX in 2026
profile: Karachi-raised MIT graduate who co-founded Anysphere, maker of the AI code editor Cursor, with MIT classmates Michael Truell, Aman Sanger and Arvid Lunnemark. SpaceX's ~$60bn all-stock purchase of Anysphere (reported closed Aug 2026, folded into SpaceXAI) made the co-founders billionaires; he continues building Cursor.

notes: Country listed as Panama in source data, but he is Pakistani (Karachi). hi@cursor.com is Cursor's general contact, not personal. Post-acquisition title not confirmed.

name: John Oyler
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, BeOne Medicines (formerly BeiGene; Nasdaq: ONC)
profile: Pittsburgh-raised MIT mechanical engineer and Stanford MBA who started at McKinsey, then founded Telephia (sold to Nielsen for $449M in 2007) and drug-discovery CRO BioDuro (sold to PPD). In 2010 he co-founded BeiGene with Chinese biochemist Xiaodong Wang; renamed BeOne, it is a global oncology company with ~11,000 staff, and he owns nearly 5%.
interesting_fact: BeOne's blood-cancer drug Brukinsa generated more than $2 billion in U.S. sales in 2024, and the company has 40+ drugs in its pipeline.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was a mechanical engineer by training (MIT) and a McKinsey consultant; his first startup, Telephia, measured consumer mobile-phone usage, a far cry from oncology.
notes: Entrepreneurial serial founder story (telecom data -> CRO -> oncology) fits an entrepreneurship podcast. Best route: BeOne media relations (media@beonemed.com).

name: Tomas Chrenek Sr
current_role: Controlling owner, AGEL healthcare group; major shareholder, Moravia Steel
profile: Slovak-born, self-made industrialist (age 63, based in Prague) who built his fortune in steel and healthcare. He is a major shareholder in Czech steel trader/producer Moravia Steel (linked to the Třinec steelworks) and controls AGEL, one of Central Europe's largest private hospital and healthcare groups, operating in the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

name: Michael Ying
current_role: Former chairman of Esprit Holdings; philanthropist (Yan Ai Foundation)
profile: Michael Ying Lee Yuen, born 1949 in Hong Kong, built the Asian sourcing and distribution arm of Esprit and helped turn it into a global brand, serving as chairman until 2006. He sold most of his stake over the following years; his remaining shares passed to his daughters, who sold them in 2021. He keeps a low profile and focuses on his Yan Ai Foundation, which funds education and healthcare for poor children in mainland China.
interesting_fact: During his 13-year tenure as chairman, Esprit's sales grew 30-fold, from HK$769.7m in 1993 to HK$23.3bn in fiscal 2006 (Bloomberg data).
deep_cut_fact: His Esprit story began in the early 1970s, when he started doing business with founders Susie and Doug Tompkins (Doug also co-founded The North Face). He became their Asian sourcing agent, which grew into Esprit Far East; his family roots are in Wenchang, Hainan.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. The Yan Ai Foundation (founded 2006) is the most plausible route, but I could not verify its website because the web-search budget was exhausted. Parts of his Wikipedia early-life section are unsourced, so confirm before quoting.

name: Igor Makarov
current_role: President, ARETI International Group (Limassol, Cyprus); Honorary President, Russian Cycling Federation
profile: Turkmenistan-born (1962) former Soviet national-team cyclist who founded Itera in 1992, which became Russia's first independent gas company and the main exporter of Turkmen gas; Rosneft bought it out for $2.9bn in 2013. He now runs ARETI, a Cyprus-based investment group, was appointed energy adviser to Turkmenistan's president in 2019, and renounced Russian citizenship in 2023.
interesting_fact: A former member of the USSR cycling team (1979-86, Master of Sports of International Class), he founded the UCI team Katusha in 2008, sat on the UCI Management Committee from 2011, and is honorary president of the Russian Cycling Federation.
deep_cut_fact: His current company's name, ARETI, is simply his first company ITERA spelled backwards (rebranded in 2015 after the Itera sale). In 2025 the Cyprus Cycling Federation gave him its Aristidis Konstantinidis Prize, and his Makarov Foundation funded the Mount Sinai Adult Autism Clinic.
notes: Sensitivity: UK sanctioned him in Sept 2022 but delisted him in March 2024 after a legal challenge; Australia and NZ also delisted (2025). Canada still lists him and he filed a $350m ICSID claim against Canada in Jan 2026. ARETI has a dedicated media contact. Don't confuse ARETI with areti.com (unrelated CPA firm).

name: Joe Lacob
current_role: Co-executive chairman and CEO, Golden State Warriors; principal owner, Golden State Valkyries (WNBA)
profile: New Bedford, Massachusetts native and former Kleiner Perkins partner (from 1987, 50+ startup investments) who led the group that bought the Golden State Warriors for $450M in 2010. The team has since won four NBA titles, opened the privately financed Chase Center, and launched the WNBA expansion Golden State Valkyries (record $50M fee), which have sold out home games and made the playoffs.
interesting_fact: The Warriors went 73-9 in 2015-16, the best regular-season record in NBA history, and have won four titles under his ownership; the team's value has risen roughly 15-fold since he bought it.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he trained in public health, earning a master's in epidemiology at UCLA; and in the 1990s he was a primary investor in the American Basketball League, an early women's pro league, decades before launching the Valkyries.

public_contacts.value: https://www.nba.com/warriors (Golden State Warriors; media relations via team)

notes: Best route is the Warriors' communications/media relations department. VC background (Kleiner Perkins, energy/cleantech-era investments) could be a natural podcast hook. Avoid mentioning his late wife.

name: Steve Case
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Revolution LLC (Washington, D.C.); chairman, Case Foundation
profile: Hawaii-born co-founder of AOL who joined predecessor Quantum Computer Services in 1985, became CEO in 1991 and led AOL's rise and its 2001 merger with Time Warner. Since 2005 he has run venture firm Revolution, whose Rise of the Rest seed fund and bus tours back startups outside the coastal hubs; author of 'The Third Wave' and 'The Rise of the Rest'.
interesting_fact: AOL began as Quantum Link (Q-Link), an online service for the Commodore 64 launched in 1985; Case believed the 'killer app' was community, which drove AOL's chat rooms and instant messaging.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech, he was an assistant brand manager at Procter & Gamble and in 1982 joined Pizza Hut in Wichita, Kansas, as manager of new pizza marketing; his entry into online services was consulting for GameLine, a dial-up game-download service for the Atari 2600.
notes: Very accessible and public-facing; frequent podcast/media guest on entrepreneurship outside Silicon Valley - excellent fit. Best route: media@revolution.com.

name: Zhang Jian
current_role: Founder and Chairman, AIMA Technology Group (Shanghai: 603529)
profile: Zhang Jian founded AIMA in Tianjin in 1999; the company entered electric bicycles in 2004 and grew into one of China's two biggest e-bike and e-scooter makers alongside rival Yadea. AIMA listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in June 2021 with annual revenue above RMB 10 billion.
interesting_fact: AIMA, founded in Tianjin in 1999, only moved into electric two-wheelers in 2004 and is now one of China's largest makers, competing head-to-head with Yadea.

Little English-language biography; Chinese sources (stcn.com) were unreachable from this session and web search budget was exhausted, so no deep-cut fact. AIMA (battery/EV two-wheelers) fits the energy theme. Corporate IR route via SSE filings recommended.

name: Pavan Jain
current_role: Chairman, INOX Group and INOX Air Products (Delhi)
profile: IIT Delhi chemical engineer with 50+ years in industry. He built INOX Air Products from a single plant into India's largest industrial and medical gas maker, and diversified the group into refrigerant gases, cryogenic equipment (INOXCVA / Inox India, listed in 2023) and cinemas (INOX Leisure, merged into PVR INOX). Son Siddharth runs the businesses day to day; his brother Vivek leads the separate Inox GFL group.
