deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chemical engineer at IIT Delhi. As chairman of INOX Air Products he grew it from a single plant into one of India's leading industrial gas companies.
notes: Industrial gases and cryogenics (LNG/hydrogen tanks) fit the energy angle. The media-centre email is shown as 'punnet.gupta' in the page text, but the mailto link is puneet.gupta@inoxap.com. Son Siddharth Jain is the more media-active family member.

name: Herbert Allen Jr
current_role: Former president (now senior figure and controlling family member) of Allen & Company, New York; son Herbert Allen III has run the firm since 2002
profile: Joined his uncle Charles's boutique investment bank Allen & Co. straight out of Williams College in 1962 and became president in 1966 at 26. The firm bought control of Columbia Pictures in 1973 and sold it to Coca-Cola in 1982, giving him a long-time Coke board seat. It advised on major tech deals and IPOs and hosts the invitation-only Sun Valley conference.
interesting_fact: He launched the Allen & Co. Sun Valley Conference in 1982, the 'summer camp for billionaires' where media and tech leaders such as Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg have gathered. He is also the largest individual holder of Coca-Cola stock.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Irvington, New York, joined Allen & Co. the year he left Williams College (1962), and became its president at 26. In 1998 he gave $20 million back to Williams.
notes: Allen & Co. is famously discreet: no public website, press office or published email. Now based in Cody, Wyoming (per Wikipedia), aged about 86. Realistic route is a warm introduction via the Sun Valley network or Herbert Allen III.

name: Ioannis Papalekas
current_role: Founder and ~66% shareholder of YODA PLC (Cyprus Stock Exchange-listed investment group); based in Nicosia
profile: Greek investor Ioannis Papalekas (about 50) made his name developing commercial real estate in Romania, then founded Globalworth, listing it in London in 2013 and selling his 13.5% stake for $315M in 2020. He founded YODA in 2019 and listed it in Cyprus in 2022; it invests in shipping and energy, hospitality, healthcare, technology and Greek/Cypriot real estate.
interesting_fact: Before founding Globalworth, his Romanian commercial real-estate developments reportedly earned a 175% rate of return for him and his investors.
deep_cut_fact: YODA listed on the Cyprus Stock Exchange's Emerging Companies Market in 2022 at EUR 0.50 a share, and in 2023 began buying Nasdaq-listed shipping/energy stock CCEC.
notes: Low media profile. YODA's general inbox is the only published channel found; IR announcements at yoda.com.cy/investor-relations/announcements/. Shipping/energy holdings give a possible energy angle.

name: Zygmunt Solorz
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Polsat Plus Group (Cyfrowy Polsat) and power producer ZE PAK
profile: Born in Radom in 1956, Solorz left communist Poland in 1977 for West Germany, where he ran a transport business and imported used cars. He launched Polsat by satellite in 1992 and built it into Cyfrowy Polsat / Polsat Plus Group, spanning pay-TV, mobile (Plus), Netia broadband, finance and energy. Energy assets include ZE PAK and green-hydrogen and renewables projects.
interesting_fact: A licensed pilot, Solorz flies as a hobby and controls Jet Story, a private-jet charter firm in Central Europe.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 his lignite power producer ZE PAK began working with Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power on possible small modular reactors at the Pątnów power station site, part of the group's move from coal to nuclear and renewables.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (ZE PAK's coal-to-nuclear/renewables shift, hydrogen). He rarely gives interviews. A widely reported family succession dispute has been running since 2024. Formerly known as Solorz-Żak. The forbes_facts entry 'Jest Story' is a typo for Jet Story.

name: Yvonne Bauer
current_role: Owner and Chair of the Board, Bauer Media Group (Hamburg)
profile: Fifth-generation owner of Bauer Media Group, which grew from an 1875 printing shop into a European publishing, audio and outdoor-media group with hundreds of magazine titles (InTouch, Grazia) and over 400 websites and apps. She took control in 2010 from her father Heinz Bauer, receiving 85% of the company. She has since expanded into newspapers, notably buying Mitteldeutsche Zeitung in 2020.
interesting_fact: Bauer Media has been family-owned for five generations since its founding as a small printing company in 1875; today it spans publishing, audio (radio) and outdoor advertising.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business in 2005, she served an apprenticeship at Hamburg publishing house Hoffmann und Campe. Inside Bauer she then worked in the German advertising and sales departments before taking over in 2010.
notes: Very private and rarely gives interviews. The corporate press-enquiry route on bauermedia.com is the published channel. The deep-cut fact combines Forbes (apprenticeship) with Bauer's management page (sales and advertising roles).

name: Natacha Nikolajevic
current_role: Heir and shareholder, via the estate of Olivier Dassault, in the Dassault family holding (Groupe Industriel Marcel Dassault)
profile: Natacha Nikolajevic married Olivier Dassault, a French National Assembly member and grandson of Dassault Aviation founder Marcel Dassault, in 2009. After his death in a helicopter crash in 2021 she inherited his share of the Dassault family fortune, which spans Dassault Aviation, Dassault Systèmes, Le Figaro and vineyards.
interesting_fact: She met her late husband Olivier Dassault at an auction where they were bidding against each other for the same item.
notes: Very private: no public role, website or social accounts found. Marriage date (5 Feb 2009) per French Wikipedia (https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier_Dassault). No direct outreach route found; any route would go through the Dassault family holding, which does not publish a personal contact. Web search quota ran out.

name: Serge Godin
current_role: Founder and co-chair of the board, CGI Inc. (daughter Julie Godin became executive chair in 2025)
profile: One of nine children from a Lac-Saint-Jean sawmill family. He studied computing and administration, then used $5,000 of savings to found CGI in Quebec City in 1976 at age 26. He was CEO until 2006 and grew CGI through 100+ acquisitions (including Bell Sygma in 1998) into a C$15bn-revenue global IT services and consulting firm. His family office, Distinction Capital, manages family capital and the Fondation Famille Godin.
interesting_fact: After his father's uninsured sawmill burned down, the young Godin worked at a convenience store after school and at a dry cleaner's on Saturdays to help pay the family's bills.
deep_cut_fact: He earned one of the first CEGEP diplomas in computer science ever awarded in Quebec, at the Collège de Jonquière. His family office, Distinction Capital, is based in Montreal's 1906 heritage William Alexander Molson house.
notes: French-language outreach is preferred. The family office email is the most direct published route; otherwise go through CGI media relations (cgi.com). CGI's IT services and data-center outsourcing fit the podcast's theme.

name: Leslie Alexander
current_role: Private investor; former owner of the NBA's Houston Rockets (1993-2017)
profile: Leslie Alexander (b. 1943) dropped out of Brooklyn Law School to trade bonds on Wall Street, founded The Alexander Group in 1980 and profited from a stake in student-loan securitizer First Marblehead. He bought the Houston Rockets for $85M in 1993, won titles in 1994 and 1995, and sold the team to Tilman Fertitta for $2.2B in 2017. He now invests privately and funds animal-welfare causes.
interesting_fact: He paid $85 million for the Rockets in 1993 and sold for $2.2 billion in 2017; Forbes named him the NBA's best owner in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He also owned the WNBA's Houston Comets (1997-2007), which won the league's first four championships (1997-2000); and he tried to buy the NHL's Edmonton Oilers in 1998.
notes: Very private since selling the Rockets; no published office/foundation contact found. Philanthropy via Clutch City Foundation (Rockets era) and a horse sanctuary in Middleburg, VA named after his mother Evelyn. Weak fit for energy/data-center themes.

name: Kevin Systrom
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Instagram; co-founder of Artifact (acquired by Yahoo, 2024); no new operating company announced as of 2026
profile: Stanford management science and engineering grad (2006) who co-founded Instagram with Mike Krieger in 2010. Facebook bought it for $1B in 2012, and he ran it until 2018, when it had about 1B monthly users. He later backed and joined the board of the Cazoo SPAC, and in 2023 co-launched the AI news app Artifact, which Yahoo acquired in 2024.
interesting_fact: Instagram began as Burbn, a cluttered HTML5 check-in app. Systrom and Krieger cut it down to its photo-sharing feature, and Systrom personally developed the X-Pro II filter that is still on Instagram.
deep_cut_fact: At Stanford he turned down a recruiting pitch from Mark Zuckerberg and spent a term in Florence studying photography. As one of 12 Mayfield Fellows he interned at Odeo, the podcasting startup that became Twitter.
notes: His public social accounts (@kevin on Instagram and X) are the most direct route. He has done many podcasts and talks about product, AI and the Artifact shutdown, so he is a good fit for an entrepreneurship show. His listed site systrom.com did not resolve.

name: David Fong
current_role: Managing Director and Co-chairman, Hip Shing Hong Group (Hong Kong)
profile: David Fong runs Hip Shing Hong, one of Hong Kong's largest private real-estate investment groups, with residential, commercial and hospitality holdings. The group was founded in 1948 and chaired by his late father Fong Yun Wah until 2022; it is now co-chaired by David and his uncle.
interesting_fact: The family's fortune started with a sesame-seed-processing business before it moved into property. Its roots go back to 1927, when Fong Yun Wah came to Hong Kong from Guangdong with his father.
notes: Private, low-profile family company with no verified official website or published contact found. The web search budget ran out before a group site or any family foundation (the Fong Yun Wah name appears on Chinese university buildings) could be checked; verify that before using it.

name: Leng Youbin
current_role: Chairman and CEO, China Feihe Ltd. (HKEX: 6186); deputy to the National People's Congress
profile: Heilongjiang dairy entrepreneur who herded cows as a child and worked at a state-owned dairy farm for about a decade. He then took stakes in the farm and a dairy plant and built Feihe into one of China's largest infant-formula makers, with its own farms in northeast China. Feihe listed in Hong Kong in 2019.
interesting_fact: He earned his degree from Northeast Agricultural University by correspondence course in 1995 and later an EMBA from Peking University. At the 2025 Harvard China Forum he lectured on scientific cattle-raising.
deep_cut_fact: He calls himself a 'second-generation builder of the Great Northern Wilderness (北大荒)'. When the property boom tempted Feihe to diversify into real estate, he refused: 'If we had done real estate then, there would be no Feihe deeply rooted in its core business.'
notes: Active NPC deputy who speaks publicly on black-soil protection and on making dairy ingredients domestically. Contact would go through Feihe's investor relations; no published email was retrievable. Weak fit for an energy podcast, except possibly agriculture and energy angles.

name: Liu Sheng
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director and President, Zhongji Innolight (Shenzhen 300308; Hong Kong listing 2026)
profile: Liu Sheng (刘圣), a Georgia Tech mechanical-engineering PhD, worked in Silicon Valley optical comms (Lucent, Pine Photonics, Opnext) before returning to found Suzhou InnoLight in 2008. Google-backed InnoLight was bought in 2016-17 by Shandong Zhongji, renamed Zhongji Innolight, now the world's largest optical-module supplier to AI data centers; he has chaired it since 2023.
interesting_fact: Per CIC figures in its Hong Kong listing, Zhongji Innolight has been the world's largest optical interconnect provider by revenue for five straight years since 2021, with 21.2% of the market in 2025; its 2026 HK IPO was billed as Hong Kong's biggest since Alibaba's in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: Born July 1971 in Daying County, Suining (Sichuan), he entered Tsinghua as the county's top science scorer; his first US job after the Georgia Tech PhD was R&D engineer at Lucent, and in 2008 he came back with four other US-trained PhDs to start InnoLight in Suzhou Industrial Park.
notes: Highly relevant to the AI data-center theme (800G/1.6T optical transceivers for Nvidia/Google/Amazon/Meta-type buyers). Route via board-secretary office email (listed in the 2025 interim report summary).

name: Ding Liguo
current_role: Chairman, Delong Holdings / Delong Steel Group; chairman of Tianjin Xin Tiangang Steel Group; actual controller of gas utility Delong Huineng (SZ: 000593)
profile: Tangshan-born (1970) steel entrepreneur who started a rolling mill in 1992, took over a struggling Xingtai steel plant in 1999 (renamed Delong Steel) and built Delong into a private steel group that absorbed Tianjin's state-owned Tiangang in 2019. He also controls listed natural-gas distributor Delong Huineng. A former deputy to the 11th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: Delong's working steel plant in Xingtai was rated a national 4A-level tourist attraction in 2020 - billed as Hebei's first operating steelworks to earn it - after the company retired old equipment and turned the space into parks and lawns, with RMB 3.55bn spent on environmental upgrades since 2014.
deep_cut_fact: Studied mechanical manufacturing at Hebei Institute of Technology (now North China University of Science and Technology) 1989-91, and founded his first company, Tangshan Changcheng Rolling Mill, in 1992 at about 22.
notes: IR email is the published board-secretary address of Delong Huineng (000593), his listed gas company - not Delong Steel directly. Deep-cut source (maigoo) is a Chinese bio aggregator, moderately reliable. Chinese-language outreach recommended; no personal social accounts found.

name: Liu Ling
current_role: Director and Administrative Affairs Director, Shenzhen Kstar Science & Technology (科士达, SZSE: 002518)
profile: Co-owner, alongside chairman/GM Liu Chengyu, of Kstar, a Shenzhen maker of UPS power systems, data-centre infrastructure (precision cooling, modular DC), PV inverters, energy storage and EV chargers, listed in Shenzhen since 2010. She joined the company in 1998 and has sat on its board since 2007; re-nominated in Nov 2025 for a term to 2028.
interesting_fact: Kstar grew out of a small company in Xiapu, Fujian (霞浦科士达) into a listed power-electronics group whose UPS and data-centre power products sit right at the energy/data-centre intersection, now expanding into energy storage.
deep_cut_fact: Before business she was a schoolteacher at Fujian's Xiapu No. 1 Middle School (福建霞浦一中); she later earned an EMBA from Peking University.
notes: Low public profile; Liu Chengyu (chairman) is the company's public face. Approach via the board secretary's office (stock@kstar.com.cn). Source for bio/email: Kstar 2025 annual report (Apr 2026).

name: Hu Haiyang
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Semight Instruments (Suzhou; Shanghai STAR Market: 688808)
profile: Hu Haiyang (b. 1973) cofounded Semight Instruments in 2017 after ~15 years at Agilent/Keysight in China, and chairs it. Semight makes optical-module and semiconductor test gear (BERTs, burn-in systems, source-measure units) riding AI data-center demand for 800G/1.6T optics; it listed on the STAR Market in April 2026.
interesting_fact: Semight is the world's second company to offer a full suite of core testing instruments for 1.6T optical modules, the high-speed links used inside AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Hu earned a PhD in optical engineering from the CAS Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics in 2001, then joined Agilent (later Keysight) as an application engineer, rising to lab director and senior technical consultant before founding Semight.
notes: Technical founder; highly relevant to the data-center/AI optics angle. IR is handled by the board secretary's office (ir@semight.com, as published in the April 2026 listing announcement).

name: Mikail Shishkhanov
current_role: No current major corporate role found; former main shareholder and board chairman of B&N Bank (Binbank)
profile: Russian financier (b. 1972, Grozny) who was majority owner (~59%) of B&N Bank (Binbank) and Rost Bank and co-owned real-estate developer INTECO, with interests linked to oil via the family Safmar group. Forbes put him at $2.3bn in 2016-17. The Bank of Russia took over Binbank in Sept 2017 and he has since left business rankings.
interesting_fact: Holds a doctorate in economics and a PhD in law and is an associate member of the Russian Academy of Natural Sciences; a graduate of Peoples' Friendship University (1995).
deep_cut_fact: Lists chess and boxing as his hobbies.
notes: No longer a billionaire: lost his banks in the 2017 state takeover and a Moscow Region court declared him bankrupt in July 2023. Avoid referencing wealth/losses. No published contact found. Likely not a fit for UHNW outreach.

name: Viktor Nusenkis
current_role: Co-owner and chairman, Energo concern (coal trading); founder of the Donetsksteel group
profile: Viktor Nusenkis, born 1954 in Donetsk, is a mining engineer who founded the Energo concern in 1992, which became the largest coal trader in Ukraine, Russia and Kazakhstan. In 2000 he formed Donetsksteel (Donetsk Metallurgical Plant, coke plants, mines) and later bought coal mines in Russia's Kemerovo region; he is now described as a Russian businessman.
interesting_fact: He built a coal-trading business, Energo, founded in 1992, into the largest coal trader across Ukraine, Russia and Kazakhstan, and later expanded into steel, coke and Kuzbass coal mines.
deep_cut_fact: A Donetsk Polytechnic graduate, he started underground: he worked at the Batova mine in Makiivka and went on to run the Zhdanivska mine before founding Energo. He also funded the Church of the Epiphany in Kozelsk, Russia.
notes: Extremely low profile; no official website or published contact found. Caution: in 2015 Ukraine's SBU opened a criminal case alleging his coke plants financed the so-called DNR (per LB.ua). No recent news found, so his current status is unverified. Probably not a suitable podcast target.

name: Vyacheslav Kantor
current_role: President, European Jewish Congress; major shareholder of Russian fertilizer producer Acron
profile: Russian-born investor and trained scientist (Viatcheslav Moshe Kantor) whose fortune comes from controlling fertilizer maker Acron. He has led the European Jewish Congress since 2007. He stepped back in 2022 after UK sanctions and was re-elected for a fifth term in 2025 after his EU delisting. He funds Holocaust-remembrance and community-security programmes.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he founded the World Holocaust Forum. Its 2020 edition at Yad Vashem, co-hosted by Kantor for the 75th anniversary of Auschwitz's liberation, drew nearly 50 heads of state: the largest diplomatic gathering ever held in Israel.
deep_cut_fact: He is the president of MAGMA, the Museum of Avant-Garde Mastery: a private Moscow museum founded in 2001 on his own collection of 20th-century art (Chagall, Soutine, El Lissitzky, Kabakov). Its first public showing was a 2009 exhibition in Geneva.
notes: Sanctions-sensitive: the UK has sanctioned him since 2022 over Acron. The EU and Switzerland delisted him in March 2025, and Poland then imposed national sanctions. Check compliance before engaging. Best route is the EJC office in Brussels; the EJC bio has the fullest account of his philanthropy.

name: Paul Desmarais Jr
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Power Corporation of Canada and Power Financial
profile: Paul Desmarais Jr. (b. 1954, Sudbury), eldest son of Power Corp builder Paul Desmarais Sr., joined Power in 1981, led the 1984 creation of Power Financial and was chairman and co-CEO of Power Corp 1996-2020. He remains chairman, overseeing a group spanning Great-West Lifeco, IGM, GBL and alternative-asset platforms Sagard and Power Sustainable. (Input name misspelled 'Demarais'.)
interesting_fact: Beyond finance he has sat on energy-industry boards: a director of GDF Suez (2008-2014) and of Total until 2017, and vice-chairman of Imerys (1998-2008).
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he started out at S.G. Warburg in London and Standard Brands in New York; and in 2014 he joined a True Patriot Love ski expedition to the North Magnetic Pole raising money for Canadian military families.

public_contacts.value: Stéphane Lemay, VP General Counsel & Secretary (Power Corp media contact), 514-286-7400

notes: Input spells name 'Demarais'; correct is Desmarais. Power Corp named James O'Sullivan CEO effective July 1, 2026 (Jeffrey Orr to vice-chair); Desmarais Jr. remains chairman. Data-center angle: May 2026 Power Corp release on a joint investment in a Sagard AI fund. Route via corporate media contact.

name: Jyoti Bansal
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Harness (AI software delivery platform); co-founder, Unusual Ventures and BIG Labs
profile: Grew up in a small Rajasthan town helping his father's farm-equipment business, studied computer science at IIT Delhi, and moved to Silicon Valley in 2000. Founded AppDynamics (2008), sold to Cisco for $3.7B in 2017 a day before its IPO; then founded Harness, which merged with his security startup Traceable in 2025 and was valued at $5.5B in a $240M Series E (Dec 2025).
interesting_fact: He says he fell in love with entrepreneurship after Bill Gates visited IIT Delhi while he was a student; he also waited about seven years on a work visa for a green card before he could start his own company.
deep_cut_fact: Before AppDynamics he led design and architecture for several products at Wily Technology, the Java performance-diagnostics pioneer later bought by Computer Associates for $375M, and earlier held senior engineering roles at Datasweep (bought by Rockwell Automation) and netLens.
notes: Very accessible founder-CEO; frequent podcast/conference speaker on DevOps, AI agents and immigration/green-card issues. Harness press team (press@harness.io) is the cleanest route.

name: B. Wayne Hughes Jr
current_role: Founder, American Commercial Equities (real estate); founder of Serving USA and the Hughes Charitable Foundation (Jackson, Wyoming)
profile: Son of Public Storage co-founder B. Wayne Hughes (d. 2021), he worked at Public Storage from 1983 for nearly two decades (VP acquisitions 1992-2002) and sat on its board until late 2020. In 2005 he launched American Commercial Equities, which owns property in Hawaii and California; he now focuses largely on philanthropy from Wyoming.
interesting_fact: His Hughes Charitable Foundation focuses on education, at-risk youth, and food and housing insecurity in his home state of Wyoming; he is a USC graduate.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Serving USA, which funds Christ-centered nonprofits serving prisoners, women in recovery and military veterans, including prison-ministry and urban ministry training partners such as TUMI.
notes: Private; philanthropy (prison re-entry, veterans, Wyoming) is the warmest hook. Not an obvious energy/data-center guest.

name: Manuel Villar
current_role: Chairman, Vista Land & Lifescapes and Villar Land Holdings; president of the Nacionalista Party
profile: Born in 1949 in Tondo, Manila, Manny Villar went from selling seafood with his mother to building the Philippines' largest homebuilder, Vista Land, now run by his son Paolo. He also controls mall operator Vistamalls, VistaREIT, AllHome, AllDay Marts and Premiere Island Power REIT, and is building the 3,500-hectare Villar City south of Manila. A former House speaker and Senate president.
interesting_fact: He started his business in 1975 delivering sand and gravel in Las Piñas with two reconditioned trucks. The firm later expanded into building and selling homes.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he was an accountant at SGV & Co. and then a financial analyst at the Private Development Corporation of the Philippines, where he sold World Bank loans. He holds a BBA (1970) and an MBA (1973) from UP Diliman.
notes: High public profile as a politician. Children Mark and Camille are senators; avoid. Premiere Island Power REIT (solar assets) is relevant to the energy theme. Vista Land and his own site blocked automated fetching, so no published press email was verified; Vista Land investor relations is the likely route. Named in Forbes Asia Heroes of Philanthropy 2024.

name: Bent Jensen
current_role: Owner and CEO, LINAK A/S (Nordborg, Denmark), per Forbes 2026
profile: Bent Jensen, a mechanical engineer, took over his grandfather's 1907 blacksmith business, Christian Jensen & Sons, in 1976. He reinvented it around the electric linear actuator, renaming it LINAK in 1984. The family-owned company now makes actuators for hospital beds, height-adjustable desks, furniture and industrial uses, with factories in Denmark, the US, China and Slovakia.
interesting_fact: LINAK is short for 'Lineær Aktuator'. The company kept a significant share of its production in Denmark by investing heavily in automation and robotics.
deep_cut_fact: In 1979, as a newly graduated engineer, he came up with the electric linear actuator while talking with a friend from his student days who had a disability and needed a way to adjust his wheelchair. That conversation is the origin of today's LINAK.

public_contacts.value: bsp@linak.com (Birgit Spek, PA to the CEO, press and media enquiries)

notes: Strong engineer-founder story with a manufacturing and automation angle. Conveniently, the published press contact is the CEO's PA.

name: Matthew Roszak
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Bloq (Chicago blockchain infrastructure company)
profile: Chicago-based venture capitalist (Lake Forest College, 1995) who worked in VC and as an entrepreneur in the 1990s-2000s, began building a crypto portfolio in 2012, and co-founded Bloq, which provides blockchain infrastructure, digital-asset custody consulting for banks and stablecoin transaction services.
interesting_fact: He co-led an initiative to give every member of the US Congress $50 worth of digital assets so lawmakers could experience crypto firsthand; some accepted.
notes: Bloq's website blocked automated access and web search budget ran out, so no verified contact or deep-cut fact. Bloq's own site or press page is the likely route. Avoid the 2006 SEC settlement (Blue Rhino) in outreach. Bloq's crypto/Bitcoin mining-adjacent infrastructure could tie into energy/data-center themes.

name: Chen Jinxia
current_role: Controlling shareholder/chair of Hunan Yongjin Group (investment holding)
profile: Shanghai University of Finance & Economics graduate who inherited control of Hunan Yongjin Group, the investment group founded by her late husband, entrepreneur Wei Dong, in 2008. Yongjin holds stakes in drug makers and financial businesses; Forbes and Hurun have listed her as a billionaire since 2008-2010.
interesting_fact: Graduate of Shanghai University of Finance & Economics; has appeared on Hurun's self-made women list since 2017 despite inheriting the core business.
notes: Identity marked uncertain only because the input's SEC field ('Sea Ltd - CPO, Shopee') almost certainly belongs to a different person with a similar romanized name - do not use it. The Forbes billionaire is the Yongjin heir. Extremely private; husband's death is a sensitive topic - avoid. No published contact found; web search budget exhausted.

name: Leonard Abess
current_role: Head of ThinkLab Ventures (Miami real-estate finance and investments); University of Miami trustee
profile: Miami banker (born 1948, Wharton graduate) who became majority owner and chairman of City National Bank of Florida in 1984. The bank his father co-founded in 1946 had about $400m in assets then; he grew it to about $2.75bn and sold his 83% stake to Caja Madrid in 2008 for $927m. He now invests via ThinkLab Ventures, owns about 4,000 acres in Miami and Vermont (some growing limes), and holds a stake in Jersey Jack Pinball.
interesting_fact: He shared $60m of the sale proceeds with 399 current and 72 former employees. President Obama praised him in his February 2009 address to Congress, and Time named him to the 2009 Time 100.
deep_cut_fact: He started at City National Bank in its print shop. With his wife he founded a floating research station in the Brazilian Amazon, and in 2006 he gave $5m to create the University of Miami's Abess Center for Ecosystem Science and Policy.
notes: I found no published contact; thinklabventures.com is a parked domain. Possible routes are the University of Miami Abess Center (he chaired UM's board 2011-2014) or Jersey Jack Pinball. Low media profile since 2009.

name: Inder Jaisinghani
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Polycab India Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Mumbai entrepreneur who, with his brothers, grew the family's small electrical-goods shop in Lohar Chawl into Polycab India, the country's largest wires-and-cables maker. Polycab added fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear from 2014, listed in 2019, and runs 28 plants exporting to 79 countries. The World Bank's IFC took a stake in 2008.
interesting_fact: Polycab grew from a trading firm started in 1986 into a listed manufacturer with 28 plants across India selling to 79 countries, supplying the cables behind India's power, infrastructure and data-centre build-out.
deep_cut_fact: Before Polycab became an industrial giant, the Jaisinghani brothers began their first wire-manufacturing experiments in a garage of about 100 square feet in Mumbai, while still running the family's electrical shop in Lohar Chawl.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit (power cables, grid and data-centre electrification). Low media profile. Polycab IR is the best published route. Deep-cut detail comes from YourStory (blocked to direct fetch) and was corroborated in search snippets from several Indian outlets, including DNA India.

name: Mika Anttonen
current_role: Founder, principal owner and Chairman of the Board, St1 (St1 Oy, formerly St1 Nordic Oy), Finland
profile: Finnish engineer who started as a crude-oil trader at Neste in the early 1990s, founded Greenergy Baltic in 1995 and renamed it St1 in 2005, building it into a Nordic fuel retailer and refiner (incl. Gothenburg refinery). He stepped back from operations to focus on strategy, using fossil-fuel profits to fund renewables: waste-based ethanol, wind, biogas, carbon sinks and deep geothermal.
interesting_fact: St1 drilled two wells roughly 6-7 km deep in Otaniemi, Espoo, to harvest geothermal heat for district heating, one of the deepest such projects in the world. He also plays hockey and is a New York Rangers fan.
deep_cut_fact: He has a Master's in engineering and likes to say 'I is a bad pronoun. We is much better.' He has argued that educating girls and women in developing nations would be the single most significant climate action (Aalto University interview, 2018).
notes: Press email is St1's published Communications Manager, Finland. Outspoken on climate policy (favours regulation, short-haul flight bans on rail routes); a natural podcast guest on energy transition from an oil-company owner's perspective. St1 Nordic renamed St1 Oy on 1 June 2026.

name: Wee Ee Lim
current_role: President & CEO, Haw Par Corporation (Tiger Balm); Chairman, UOL Group and Singapore Land Group; Director, United Overseas Bank
profile: Wee Ee Lim (64), son of late UOB patriarch Wee Cho Yaw, joined Tiger Balm maker Haw Par in 1986 and has been its president and CEO since 2003. After his father's death he became chairman of property developer UOL Group (2024) and Singapore Land Group, and sits on UOB's board; his wealth includes his share of the family stakes inherited in 2025.
interesting_fact: He has run Haw Par, owner of the century-old Tiger Balm ointment brand, for over two decades, while also chairing two listed property groups and serving on the board of UOB, one of Singapore's three big banks.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics in the U.S. at Clark University in Worcester, Massachusetts (BA Economics), and joined Haw Par's board in 1994, nine years before becoming CEO.
notes: Low-key; rarely interviewed. He is also a director of the family's Wee Foundation. UOL site blocked automated access; UOL's corporate communications contact is listed on uol.com.sg.

name: Roberto Sallouti
current_role: CEO, Banco BTG Pactual; partner of BTG Pactual Holding (São Paulo)
profile: Roberto Balls Sallouti has been at BTG Pactual since 1994 and is now CEO of the bank and a partner in BTG Pactual Holding, Latin America's largest investment bank, which runs as a meritocratic partnership. His partnership stake made him a Forbes billionaire in 2026. He also founded BTG Investments LP.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Inteli (Instituto de Tecnologia e Liderança), a nonprofit technology and leadership college in São Paulo, with fellow BTG billionaire André Esteves.
deep_cut_fact: He was part of the group that created an endowment fund and a new governance model that rescued the São Paulo Museum of Art (MASP) from bankruptcy.
notes: New to the Forbes list in 2026. BTG's IR email is the published institutional route; Inteli is a softer route on the tech and education angle. BTG is active in energy and infrastructure in Brazil.

name: Pan Weiming
current_role: Chairman, Fullsun Group (construction and property development, Guangdong), per Forbes; current status not verified
profile: Pan Weiming (潘伟明) quit his post as a magistrate in Conghua, Guangdong in 1993 and started his first property company with his brother. He went on to chair Fullsun Group, whose main businesses are construction and property development. He dropped off the Forbes and Hurun lists after 2019-2020.
interesting_fact: He was a local government magistrate in Conghua (Guangzhou) before leaving public service in 1993 to become a property developer.

notes: Low public profile; route via CATL IR/press. Board change: nominated non-independent director 6 Dec 2025 when the supervisory board was restructured (https://tech.ifeng.com/c/8orI8gQ7OKQ). Forbes profile still lists him as supervisory-board chairman.

name: Teo Swee Ann
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Espressif Systems (Shanghai STAR Market: 688018)
profile: Singaporean EE (NUS master's, 2000) who worked at Bluetooth startup Transilica, then Marvell and Montage Technology, before founding Espressif in Shanghai in 2008. Espressif's low-cost ESP8266/ESP32 Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chips power vast numbers of IoT devices; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019 and he still runs it.
interesting_fact: Espressif's ESP8266, a cheap Wi-Fi microcontroller, has been described as 'legendary' in the maker world; he started the company wanting to automate analogue chip design and at one point ran it as a design consultancy before making his own chips.
deep_cut_fact: His maths teacher at The Chinese High School, Mr Chew Kim Liong, entered him untrained into a national maths competition where he placed seventh, earning advanced number-theory classes; Teo says Chew 'changed the trajectory of my life'. He also chose to minor in law at NUS despite expecting to do poorly in it.
notes: Engineer-founder who answers press by email/chat (per Schoolbag). Publishes 'CEO Messages' on Espressif's site. No dedicated press email found; IR email is the only Espressif-published address. Forbes bio empty in input.

name: Ron Corio
current_role: Founder and former CEO of Array Technologies (Nasdaq: ARRY); private investor in Albuquerque, New Mexico
profile: Founded solar-tracker maker Array Technologies in Albuquerque in 1989, moving from home trackers to the horizontal single-axis trackers now standard on utility-scale solar farms after a first 250 kW BP Solar project in 2001. He stepped down as CEO in 2018, sold his ~38% stake for about $1.2bn within six months of the Oct 2020 IPO, and left the board in 2022.
interesting_fact: Forbes calls him the 'Godfather of Solar' and New Mexico's first (and only) billionaire; he now prefers to stay out of the spotlight.
deep_cut_fact: In Array's early days he built a solar tracker that hung from Steve Fossett's balloon on his first round-the-world attempt (keeping a flexible PV array pointed at the sun as the balloon rotated), supplied 'artistic trackers' for Robin Williams' Napa Valley home, and made fold-out tracking power trailers for anti-poaching patrols in Africa.
notes: Very private; no personal site, social accounts or office contact found. Array Technologies IR/press would not represent him since he left the board in 2022. Home Power magazine praised his first home tracker in a 1991 'Things That Work' review - good rapport hook for an energy podcast.

name: Alex Birkenstock
current_role: Private investor; former co-owner of Birkenstock (exited his remaining stake after the October 2023 IPO). Lives in Tegernsee, Germany.
profile: One of Karl Birkenstock's three sons, Alex took joint control of the family shoemaker in 2002, running his own brands under a multi-brand setup. He and brother Christian bought out brother Stephan in 2013 and sold a majority to L Catterton and Bernard Arnault's Financiere Agache in 2021 (>$4.5B), keeping minority stakes; Alex sold out after the 2023 NYSE IPO.
interesting_fact: The Birkenstock line traces to 1774 records of shoemaker Johannes Birkenstock in Hesse; his father Karl's 1963 'Original Birkenstock Footbed Sandal' (later the 'Madrid') was initially a commercial flop.
deep_cut_fact: His father Karl created, in 1962, the first standardized, permanently installed anatomical insole, which made healthy footwear mass-producible; earlier generations had made individually fitted insoles, and great-grandfather Konrad trademarked 'Fussbett' in 1925.
notes: Very private since exiting the company; no published personal contact or current venture found (search budget exhausted). Birkenstock corporate PR no longer represents him.

name: Li Jianquan
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Winner Medical Co. (Shenzhen-listed, Sept 2020)
profile: Founder-chairman of Winner Medical, which began making cotton-based medical dressings in 1991. It now supplies wound care, surgical and PPE products to around 150,000 Chinese pharmacies, 5,000+ hospitals and 110+ countries. He also built the consumer brand Purcotton (cotton daily-care products), and the group listed on the Shenzhen exchange in September 2020.
interesting_fact: Besides Winner, Li has chaired the Medical Dressing Branch of the China Medical Insurance Chamber of Commerce, and Winner was named a top-10 Chinese medical-dressing enterprise for 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Li (who signs as 'JQ Li') built Winner around a three-part tenet: 'Quality priority over profit; Brand priority over speed; Social value priority over enterprise value.'
notes: Goes by 'JQ Li' in English. The only published contact is the company's general info inbox; no personal channels were found. Not an obvious fit for an energy/data-center theme.

name: Avram Glazer
current_role: Executive Co-Chairman, Manchester United; co-owner, Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Chairman of the Board, INNOVATE Corp. (NYSE: VATE)
profile: Avram 'Avie' Glazer, son of the late shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer, has co-chaired Manchester United with his brother Joel since the family's 2005 takeover. The siblings sold a quarter of their stake to Jim Ratcliffe in 2023. The family has owned the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers since 1995, and he chairs holding company INNOVATE Corp. He also owns the Desert Vipers cricket club in Dubai.
interesting_fact: From 1995 to 2009 he was chairman and CEO of Zapata Corporation, the oil company founded by George H.W. Bush. He also previously ran Omega Protein and Safety Components International, giving him an energy-industry angle beyond sports.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Rochester, NY, he was named Junior Achievement's Outstanding Young Businessman of the Year in 1978. After law school he also studied at Peking University and Fudan University in Shanghai. With his wife Jill he founded Glazer Hall, a performing-arts centre in Palm Beach, in 2025.

public_contacts.value: ir@innovatecorp.com (INNOVATE Corp., where he is chairman)

notes: Glazer ownership is controversial among Man Utd fans, so avoid that in outreach; the energy (Zapata) or INNOVATE infrastructure angle is a better fit. INNOVATE sold DBM Global to IES Holdings in Oct 2026. The Manchester United IR site exposed no scrapeable email.

name: Bryan Glazer
current_role: Co-chairman, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (with brothers Joel and Edward); director, Manchester United
profile: Son of shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), he and his five siblings own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers (bought for $192M in 1995, now worth ~$5.2B) and a controlling stake in Manchester United (bought 2005; a quarter of their stake sold to Jim Ratcliffe in 2023). He has helped run the Bucs since 1995, including the new stadium and brand redesign, and the team has won Super Bowls XXXVII and LV.
interesting_fact: Under Glazer ownership the Buccaneers won Super Bowl LV (2021), the first time a team played the Super Bowl in its own home stadium.
deep_cut_fact: He majored in broadcast communications at American University before earning a law degree at Whittier; in 2016 he gave $4M to convert Tampa's historic Fort Homer W. Hesterly Armory into the Bryan Glazer Family Jewish Community Center.

public_contacts.value: https://www.buccaneers.com/ (Tampa Bay Buccaneers; route via team communications)

notes: The Glazers rarely give interviews, especially about Manchester United, so avoid United fan-protest topics. Best route is the Buccaneers communications department. He was a key figure in the design of Raymond James Stadium and the Bucs' logo redesign.

name: Edward Glazer
current_role: Owner/Co-Chairman, Tampa Bay Buccaneers; co-owner and director, Manchester United
profile: One of six children of mall magnate Malcolm Glazer, who bought the Buccaneers in 1995 and Manchester United in 2005; the siblings jointly control both clubs. Entering his 32nd season with the Bucs, Edward is co-chairman involved in strategy and business operations, oversees real-estate acquisitions for First Allied Corp., and founded US Property Trust and US Auto Trust.
interesting_fact: He and his wife Shari funded Glazer Arena at his alma mater Ithaca College (class of '92), a 6,700-seat venue with a 200-meter six-lane indoor track that opened in fall 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Glazer Arena has become the largest sports and events venue for the Elmira-Corning-Ithaca region, hosting concerts, trade shows and graduations as well as the Bombers' indoor track team.

public_contacts.value: https://www.buccaneers.com/team/contact-us (Buccaneers front office, One Buccaneer Place, Tampa)

notes: Man Utd ownership is a sensitive topic with fans - keep outreach on Bucs/real estate/auto dealerships. Best route: Buccaneers front office/communications.

name: Joel Glazer
current_role: Co-Chairman, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (NFL) and Co-Chairman, Manchester United
profile: Rochester-born (1967) son of shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer. He helped his father buy the Buccaneers in 1995 ($192m; now worth about $5.2bn) and Manchester United in 2005. He co-chairs both clubs with his brothers. In 2023 the six siblings sold a quarter of their United stake to Jim Ratcliffe at a valuation of about $5.4bn.
interesting_fact: The Buccaneers won Super Bowl XXXVII (January 2003) and Super Bowl LV (2021) under the Glazers. With brother Bryan, Joel built local support for what became Raymond James Stadium.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the NFL's International Committee, which oversees the league's games abroad, and sits on its Finance, Media and Sports Betting committees. The Glazer Family Foundation gave $5m toward the Glazer Children's Museum in Tampa (opened 2010).
notes: He almost never gives interviews, especially to UK media. Manchester United ownership is a sensitive topic with fans, so avoid it. The best route is Buccaneers communications (media site above); I didn't find a published press email.

name: Huang Jianjun
current_role: Director and General Manager, Suzhou Semight Instruments (联讯仪器, SSE STAR: 688808); one of its three joint actual controllers
profile: Huang Jianjun (黄建军, b. 1981) is GM of Semight Instruments, a Suzhou maker of optical-communication and semiconductor test equipment for 400G/800G/1.6T optical modules used in AI data centers. He holds ~7.2% directly and, with chairman Hu Haiyang and VP Yang Jian, controls ~55%. Semight listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 24 Apr 2026 and closed day one at ~RMB 82B market cap.
interesting_fact: Semight is described as the world's second company to offer a full suite of core test instruments for 1.6T optical modules; on its April 2026 IPO day the stock closed at RMB 799 vs an RMB 81.88 issue price.
deep_cut_fact: An optical-module insider before he tested them: after a 2006 optical-engineering master's at Beijing University of Technology he worked at O-Net and JDSU in Shenzhen, then spent nearly a decade (2008-2017) at Finisar's Shanghai unit, rising from senior engineer to engineering director, before joining Semight as GM in Jan 2018.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. IR contact is the board office (board secretary Liao Jin, securities rep Zhang Jinping; office line 0512-68780583 published in filings). Strong fit for AI data-center optics/1.6T interconnect topics.

name: Lawrence Ho
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Melco International Development and Melco Resorts & Entertainment (Nasdaq: MLCO); founder of family office Black Spade Capital
profile: Lawrence Ho, eldest living son of the late Stanley Ho, left investment banking in 2001 to take a 26% stake in Melco International and built Melco Resorts into a major integrated-resort operator: City of Dreams and Studio City in Macau, City of Dreams Manila and Europe's largest integrated resort, City of Dreams Mediterranean in Cyprus (2023). His Black Spade Capital invests in SPACs, tech and green energy.
interesting_fact: His Black Spade SPAC merged with Vietnamese EV maker VinFast in a $23 billion Nasdaq listing in 2023; Black Spade's remit also covers green energy and, reportedly, space-sector deals.
deep_cut_fact: Before casinos he began in September 1999 in Jardine Fleming's Asia derivatives group (then Citibank), and in 2003 Melco's Mocha Clubs pioneered café-style slot parlours in Macau.
notes: Media-friendly CEO who speaks at conferences; Black Spade Capital (family office, Hong Kong) is a second route for non-gaming topics such as green energy and SPACs. Toronto-educated (Upper Canada College, U of T BCom 1999).

name: Niu Yishun
current_role: Listed by Hurun as the principal behind Hixih (华勤集团, Hixih Rubber Industry Group), Shandong; exact title not verified
profile: Hurun lists Niu Yishun (牛宜顺), jointly with Niu Teng, as the owner of Hixih. Hixih Rubber Industry Group was founded in 1989 and centers on high-end rubber: tires, engineering rubber and steel cord. It has expanded into power, new energy, metal products, property, capital operations and healthcare, and employs over 10,000 people.
interesting_fact: Hixih has formed joint ventures with Italy's Pirelli and Germany's Continental, and is a repeat entrant in China's Top 500 Enterprises.
notes: The company was matched via its 'Hixih' name, but the group site does not name Niu Yishun, so his role and the Niu Teng relationship are unverified (web search budget used up). Possible energy angle through the group's new-energy and power businesses. Very low international profile.

name: Niu Teng
profile: Listed by Hurun (China 2017-2026, Global 2018-2026) with Niu Yishun, with wealth attributed to 'Hixih' in auto components. The underlying company and Chinese name could not be confirmed with the available sources.
notes: Identity not confirmed: 'Hixih' looks like a Hurun romanisation, and hixih.com is a parked domain. Web search quota ran out before Chinese-language searches (e.g. 牛腾 牛奕顺 汽车零部件) could be run. Needs a follow-up pass.

name: Zhang Ronghua
current_role: Chairwoman of the board, Tianjin Rockcheck Xiangtai Investment Holding Group (Rockcheck Group / 荣程集团)
profile: Tangshan-born (1969) self-made steel entrepreneur who co-founded Rockcheck in Tangshan in 1989 and moved it to Tianjin in 2001. She has chaired it since 2014. The private group now spans Rockcheck Steel, commodities trading, digital tech, new energy and culture/health. She is a 14th National People's Congress deputy for Tianjin and a vice-chair of the Tianjin federation of industry and commerce.
interesting_fact: Rockcheck has set up a dedicated new-energy arm (荣程新能科技集团, Rockcheck New Energy Technology Group) as part of a 'hundred-year green Rockcheck' push, and its steel bars now carry green-product certifications.
deep_cut_fact: Rockcheck, which she co-founded, donated RMB 100 million to relief after the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake. That was one of the largest private donations at the time, from founders who had themselves come out of Tangshan, the city devastated by the 1976 earthquake.
notes: Mandarin-only route; the group site lists a switchboard but no email. Steel decarbonisation and the new-energy unit are a natural podcast hook. Her co-founder husband Zhang Xiangqing died in 2014; do not raise this.

name: Li Shuibo
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Kunshan Kinglai Hygienic Materials (新莱应材, SZSE: 300260)
profile: Taiwan-born engineer Li Shuibo (Li Shui-po, b.1956) rose to factory director at a steel mill in Dajia, Taichung, then co-founded Kinglai with his wife in 1991, moving it to Kunshan in 2000. Kinglai makes clean and ultra-high-purity stainless components (valves, pipes, vacuum parts) for food, biopharma and chip fabs; listed in Shenzhen in 2011.
interesting_fact: Kinglai went from food-grade stainless fittings (its first mainland order came from dairy giant Yili) to ultra-high-purity gas and vacuum components favoured by semiconductor makers.
deep_cut_fact: Kinglai's very first customer was a US buyer who placed a US$40,000 order in 1991, landed thanks to his wife's background in international trade; the 2000 move to Kunshan was his father-in-law's suggestion.
notes: Known in English as Li Shui-po; company 新莱应材 / Kinglai Group. IR emails belong to the board secretary (Zhu Mengyong) and securities rep (Wang Mengdie) per the 2025 annual report summary. Tagged 'Green Energy' but the business is ultra-clean materials for semiconductor/biopharma - a chip supply-chain angle.

name: Zhou nanfang
profile: Zhou Nanfang (周南方) has appeared on the Hurun China Rich List every year from 2012 to 2026, with wealth attributed to 'Nanfang' in the metals industry. The specific company and his role could not be verified.
notes: Unverified: the web search budget ran out before the 'Nanfang' metals company could be identified. Look up his Hurun China 2026 entry for the company name and province, then the company's own site or filings for an IR/press contact.

name: Ding Feng
current_role: Non-executive director and co-controlling shareholder, Wanbang Digital Energy (Star Charge), Changzhou
profile: Ding Feng is the husband of Star Charge founder Shao Danwei; together they control about 87% of Wanbang Digital Energy (Star Charge), a Changzhou-based maker of EV chargers, microgrid and storage systems that has shipped 2M+ chargers to ~70 countries and filed for a Hong Kong IPO in Jan 2026. He keeps a low profile behind his wife.
interesting_fact: Per the 2026 HK prospectus, Ding and Shao each hold 1.36% directly and own 50/50 the Wanbang Investment Group, which holds 84.44%; the loss-making charging-network operation was spun out to another company they control before the IPO.
notes: Common name; identity inferred from Hurun 'shared with Shao Danwei' + Star Charge. Reports call him a behind-the-scenes adviser; some say he earlier founded a Wanbang auto business (unverified). Shao Danwei is the public face; approach via Star Charge corporate contact.

name: Shao Danwei
current_role: Founder, executive director and CEO, Wanbang Digital Energy (Star Charge / 星星充电), Changzhou; chairman since Dec 2017
profile: Changzhou-born founder (age ~43, Nanjing University of Finance & Economics) of Star Charge, China's No. 2 public EV-charging network (15.7% share, Nov 2025) with 2M+ chargers delivered to ~70 countries. She and husband Ding Feng control ~87% of parent Wanbang Digital Energy, which filed for a Hong Kong IPO in January 2026 after earlier listing attempts.
interesting_fact: Before starting Star Charge in 2014 she ran a car-dealership business, serving as executive director and CEO of Jiangsu Wanbang Jinzhixing auto investment group (2012-2014); she has been vice chair of the Jiangsu General Chamber of Commerce since July 2022.
deep_cut_fact: She says Star Charge began after an August 2014 dinner in Laoshan with TELD chairman Yu Dexiang: she wanted to buy his chargers, his quote was too high, so she built her own - joking in 2024, 'If you had given me a cheaper price, there would be no runner-up today.'
notes: No personal channels found; route via Star Charge corporate/international team. Company is mid-IPO process in Hong Kong (filed Jan 2026), which may limit media availability. Chinese-language outreach likely more effective.

name: Huang Xiaonan
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, DeepZero (深演智能, HKEX: 2723), Beijing
profile: Peking University alumna and ex-McKinsey manager who cofounded ad-tech firm iPinYou (品友互动) with Xie Peng in April 2009. Renamed DeepZero, it now sells decision-AI agents for marketing and sales to large enterprises and listed in Hong Kong in May 2026, where the retail tranche was ~5,480x oversubscribed and shares nearly tripled on debut.
interesting_fact: DeepZero's Hong Kong IPO in May 2026 was ~5,480x oversubscribed in the public tranche; shares priced at HK$55.5 opened at HK$155 (+179%), turning a 2009 ad-tech startup into one of the year's hottest AI listings.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding iPinYou she worked at Procter & Gamble in the 1990s, running decisions on Nielsen retail-audit 'small data', then was a project manager at McKinsey Beijing; her cofounder Xie Peng was a P&G Guangzhou regional sales manager.

public_contacts.value: marketing@ipinyou.com (company contact email listed on DeepZero site)

notes: Gives media interviews (e.g. Shanghai Securities News, Sept 2026) on enterprise AI agents - a natural fit for the podcast. Her name is sometimes romanized Huang Xiaonan / Xiao Nan Huang; some sources render it 黄晓楠.

name: Folorunsho Alakija
current_role: Executive Vice Chairman, Famfa Oil Ltd; Group Managing Director, Rose of Sharon Group
profile: Nigerian businesswoman who moved from secretarial and banking jobs into fashion (Supreme Stitches, later Rose of Sharon House of Fashion), then won an oil prospecting licence in 1993 for the offshore block containing the Agbami field, developed with Chevron. Now focused on philanthropy, ministry and writing; served as Chancellor of Osun State University 2016-2026.
interesting_fact: In 2025 she funded and donated a 250-bed teaching hospital (the Modupe and Folorunso Alakija Medical Research and Training Hospital) to Osun State University, reportedly worth N34 billion.
deep_cut_fact: Her career began in 1974 as an executive secretary at Sijuade Enterprises in Lagos after secretarial studies at Pitman Central College, London; she later served as president of the Fashion Designers Association of Nigeria and remains a trustee.
notes: Name often spelled Folorunso. Her official site has a 'Let's Talk' contact form and a Press section; she is publicly active as an author and Christian minister, so the personal site is the best route.

name: Oran Holtzman
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, Oddity Tech (Nasdaq: ODD)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who, with sister Shiran Holtzman-Erel (Chief Product Officer), bought the 1972 New York makeup brand Il Makiage and relaunched it as a digital-first business, forming Oddity Tech in 2018. Oddity uses AI/computer vision to match shoppers to products across Il Makiage, SpoiledChild and METHODIQ; it IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2023 at ~$2.7B and is HQ'd in New York with R&D in Tel Aviv.
interesting_fact: Oddity sells only online to 50M+ customers and runs its own biotech lab in Boston after acquiring AI molecular-discovery startup Revela in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Il Makiage was founded in 1972 by New York makeup artist Ilana Harkavi; L Catterton took a $29M minority stake in 2017, a year before the Holtzman siblings' digital relaunch.
notes: Data/AI-driven consumer company - good fit for an entrepreneurship/data podcast. Best route: press@oddity.com. Forbes lists him as UK-based.

name: Antonio Marcegaglia
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Marcegaglia (steel), Gazoldo degli Ippoliti/Mantua
profile: Co-owner, with his sister Emma, of Marcegaglia, one of Italy's largest steel processors and the world's largest maker of welded tubes. His father Steno founded it in Mantua in 1959. Antonio joined full-time after graduating from Bocconi in 1987, led its internationalisation from 1989 (plants in the US, Brazil, Poland, China and elsewhere) and has chaired it since Steno's death in 2013.
interesting_fact: He steered Marcegaglia's diversification beyond steel into tourism and renewable energy. From 2017 he promoted the relaunch of the Ilva steelworks through AM Investco, a joint venture with ArcelorMittal.
deep_cut_fact: He was named 'Stainless Steel Executive of the Year 2010' at the 9th Stainless & Special Steel Summit in Rome, and won Forbes Italia's CEO Italian Award 2024 in the Industry category.
notes: The Marcegaglia newsroom explicitly invites journalists to write to the newsroom address. Energy angle: the group's renewables/energy arm (a euroenergygroup contact appears on its site). Wikipedia flags his page for promotional tone, so the facts above come from that page and should be checked.

name: Liang Yanfeng
current_role: Chairman/leader of Zhonggeng Group (中庚集团), Fuzhou, per Forbes (profile last updated 2021)
profile: Forbes describes Liang Yanfeng (梁衍锋) as the self-made head of Fuzhou-based Zhonggeng Group, which has interests in real estate, industrial parks and financial investments. He dropped off the Forbes and Hurun lists after 2021-22, and I could not confirm his current status.
notes: Very little verifiable public information. The Forbes profile has not been updated since April 2021, the company domain zhonggeng.com shows 'site under construction', and Baidu Baike blocked access. The web-search budget was exhausted, so current status (and whether he dropped off the lists due to wealth loss) is unverified. Low priority.

name: Rosely Schweizer
current_role: Shareholder (~12.5%) of Dr. August Oetker KG; former advisory board chair (until 2010)
profile: Born Rosely Oetker in Hamburg in 1940, eldest daughter of Rudolf-August Oetker, she studied economics in Innsbruck (1964), was a general partner and advisory board chair at sparkling-wine maker Henkell & Soehnlein, and chaired the Oetker parent company's advisory board from 2007 to 2010. She owns about 12.5% of the food, beverage and hotel group; her son Rudolf Louis Schweizer became board chairman in 2019.
interesting_fact: In 2001 she co-founded, with the German association of women entrepreneurs, the Kaete-Ahlmann-Foundation, named after her grandmother, to support female entrepreneurs.
deep_cut_fact: Besides business she had a long political career: Murrhardt town councillor 1984-2006 and CDU member of the Baden-Wuerttemberg state parliament 1992-2001 for the Backnang constituency, where she was the party's economic-policy spokesperson.
notes: Aged ~86; no death reported on German Wikipedia (alive status not freshly confirmed). Lives in Murrhardt area; very private. Holds the Bundesverdienstkreuz (Federal Cross of Merit). Avoid her father's wartime past in outreach.

name: Ong Beng Seng
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Hotel Properties Limited (SGX-listed); chairman of Singapore GP (F1 race promoter)
profile: Born 1946 in Teluk Anson, Perak, and raised in Singapore, Ong started in shipping insurance, joined trader Kuo International in 1975, then built Hotel Properties Ltd, which owns or holds stakes in Four Seasons, Hilton, Hard Rock and other hotels in Asia and Europe. With wife Christina (Como hotels, Club 21) they are among Singapore's most influential couples.
interesting_fact: As chairman of race promoter Singapore GP he is credited with bringing Formula One to Singapore; the inaugural 2008 Singapore Grand Prix was F1's first-ever night race.
deep_cut_fact: His career began at a firm insuring ships; he met his future wife Christina at Kuo International, the trading company founded by her father Peter Fu Yun Siak, which he joined in 1975.
notes: Caution: he was charged in 2024 and in 2025 pleaded guilty to abetting obstruction of justice in the case of former minister S. Iswaran (fined) - a sensitive topic; avoid in outreach. HPL website (hpl.com.sg) did not load from this session; corporate route via HPL investor relations/SGX filings.

name: Sergey Lomakin
current_role: Co-founder and (per Forbes) chairman and controlling shareholder, Fix Price Group (Russian fixed-price discount retailer)
profile: Co-founded Fix Price in 2007 with Artem Khachatryan. It grew to more than 4,000 stores across Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Uzbekistan and other countries, and went public in 2021. In December 2023 he bought nearly all of Khachatryan's stake for $990m, becoming the dominant shareholder.
interesting_fact: In December 2023 Lomakin paid $990m to buy almost all of co-founder Artem Khachatryan's stake. The chain has expanded to more than 4,000 stores in seven countries.
notes: Russia-based; there may be sanctions and reputational issues to check before outreach. Forbes moved him to its 'former' list in 2026. Very low personal media profile, and his current board role in 2026 is unverified. The company's 2026 news covers GDR conversion into shares and a new distribution centre in Belarus.

name: Stefan Schoerghuber
profile: Owner and CEO of Munich's Schörghuber Unternehmensgruppe (construction/real estate, brewing via Paulaner/BrauHolding, hotels), which he took over after his father Josef died in 1995. Died unexpectedly 25 November 2008 aged 47; widow Alexandra Schörghuber later led the group.
notes: Deceased (25 Nov 2008, per Wikipedia and Brauwelt https://brauwelt.com/en/international-report/europe-russia/626074-brewer-and-hotelier-stefan-schrghuber-dies-at-47). Skip.

name: Eugenio Garza Laguera
notes: Eugenio Garza Laguera, longtime chairman of FEMSA and of the Tec de Monterrey board, died May 24, 2008 in Monterrey at age 84. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenio_Garza_Lag%C3%BCera ; https://www.femsa.com/en/press-room/press-release/fundacion-paz-es-a-b-p-recognizes-the-life-and-legacy-of-eugenio-garza-laguera/

name: Thyssen-Bornemisza family
profile: A 1999 Forbes family entry. The family fortune descends from the Thyssen steel dynasty via Baron Hans Heinrich 'Heini' Thyssen-Bornemisza, who inherited TBG (Thyssen-Bornemisza Group) Holdings in 1947 and assembled one of the world's great private art collections, now in Madrid's Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum. The patriarch died on 27 April 2002.
interesting_fact: Heini Thyssen's art collection, housed in Madrid's Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, stays in Spain under a settlement reached before his death.
notes: A family entry rather than an individual. Hans Heinrich died in 2002, and the current family members and holdings (e.g. TBG Holdings; Thyssen Petroleum, reportedly chaired by son Lorne) were not verified. Not a practical outreach target without first naming a specific living family member.

name: Peter Peterson
current_role: Deceased (co-founder of Blackstone, 1985); died 20 March 2018 in New York, aged 91
notes: Died 20 March 2018. His legacy organisation is the Peter G. Peterson Foundation (fiscal policy), led by his son Michael Peterson; not a route to him.

name: Frank Stronach
current_role: Founder of Magna International (no role since 2011); thoroughbred owner/breeder (Adena Springs)
profile: Austrian-born (1932, as Franz Strohsack) industrialist who started Multimatic in a Toronto garage shop in 1956. It won its first auto-parts contract in 1969 and became Magna International in 1973, one of the world's largest auto-parts makers. deep_cut_fact: Before finance, Wilson earned a civil engineering degree and spent three years working the oilfields of Western Canada for Imperial Oil, then did an MBA in entrepreneurship at the University of Calgary (1985) and started at McLeod Young Weir.
notes: Hurun $2B figure looks inflated (other estimates far lower). Very active and outspoken on social media; has had public controversies over posts (2018, 2020) - be aware. Prolific philanthropist (prostate cancer, domestic-abuse research, mental health) and regular podcast guest, so likely receptive.

name: Mark Dixson
current_role: Executive Chair, International Workplace Group plc (IWG, owner of Regus); was CEO until June 2026
profile: Mark Dixon (name usually spelled Dixon) is a British entrepreneur who founded Regus in Brussels in 1989. It grew into International Workplace Group (IWG), the world's largest flexible-workspace operator, with brands like Regus and Spaces in 120+ countries. In June 2026 he handed the CEO job to Christian Schmitz and became Executive Chair.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for Regus in the late 1980s in Brussels, after seeing business travellers with nowhere professional to work. That first Brussels business centre grew into a network in more than 120 countries.
deep_cut_fact: He left school at 16 and started Dial-a-Snack, a sandwich business that delivered on a butcher's bicycle. After that came a hot dog van in 1983 and The Bread Roll Company in 1986, all before Regus.
notes: The input spells the name 'Dixson'; the correct spelling is Mark Dixon. IWG's head office is in Zug, Switzerland. In the June 2026 leadership-change RNS, Richard Manning (Head of IR) is the named contact. I found no published press email for him.

name: Didier Domange
current_role: Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Fidoma SAS (Domange family holding); former Chairman of Zodiac Aerospace Supervisory Board
profile: Didier Domange is the Domange family patriarch, and the family was long Zodiac Aerospace's reference shareholder. He chaired Zodiac's Supervisory Board until Safran acquired the company in 2018. He then sat on Safran's board (2018-2022) and now runs the family holding Fidoma.
interesting_fact: After Safran bought Zodiac Aerospace for about EUR 10bn, Domange joined Safran's board of directors from 2018 to 2022. The family's stake became Safran shares.
notes: Very private and has almost no public profile. Insider-profile sites disagree on his dates. Alive status is unverified after his Safran board term ended in May 2022. Any route to him would go through Safran's corporate office, though Safran has no link to him today.

name: Tatiana Santo Domingo
current_role: Co-founder and creative director, Muzungu Sisters (ethical fashion brand)
profile: Born 1983 in New York and raised in Geneva and Paris, she is a granddaughter of Colombian magnate Julio Mario Santo Domingo, whose Bavaria brewery fortune passed into SABMiller; she inherited a share on his 2011 death. She co-founded the ethical slow-fashion label Muzungu Sisters with Dana Alikhani (launched 2011) and is married to Andrea Casiraghi of Monaco.
interesting_fact: Muzungu Sisters works with around 41 artisan communities worldwide; 'muzungu' is a Swahili word for wanderer/traveller.
deep_cut_fact: She studied photography and visual communications at the American University in London, and before Muzungu Sisters worked at AEFFE in New York, for art director Giovanni Bianco (GB65) and at Vanity Fair.
notes: Also known as Tatiana Casiraghi (Monaco royal family by marriage); very private. Business link is fashion, not energy; best route is via Muzungu Sisters general contact.

name: Ronald Mc Aulay
current_role: Director, Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons Ltd (Kadoorie family office); former long-time director of CLP Holdings and Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels
profile: Ronald McAulay (b. 1935/36), a Scottish-born Hong Kong businessman, married into the Kadoorie family. His wealth stems mainly from a roughly 10% stake, held through trusts, in CLP Holdings, Hong Kong's biggest power utility. He sat on CLP's board 1968-2016 and on Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels' board 1972-c.2017.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of CLP, Hong Kong's main power utility, in 1968 at age 32 and served nearly half a century, leaving on 1 October 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the Kadoorie businesses he trained as an accountant: he is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Scotland, holds a master's degree from the University of Glasgow, and was schooled at Gordonstoun.
notes: Very private and about 90 years old. I found no death report, and Wikipedia (edited 2026) lists him as living. No published personal contact; the only route is via the Kadoorie family office (Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons, Hong Kong) or CLP corporate communications. Input lists the country as China (Hong Kong); he is a British citizen.

name: Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani
current_role: Emir of Qatar (since June 2013); oversees the Qatar Investment Authority
profile: Born 1980 in Doha, Tamim became Emir in 2013 when his father abdicated, after a decade as heir apparent. As head of state he oversees Qatar's sovereign wealth fund, the Qatar Investment Authority; his listed wealth reflects that role rather than a business he built. His reign is defined by the 2022 FIFA World Cup, Qatar National Vision 2030 and Qatar's role as a diplomatic mediator.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he founded Oryx Qatar Sports Investments, the vehicle that later bought Paris Saint-Germain F.C.
deep_cut_fact: He was elected an IOC member at the 113th IOC Session in February 2002, aged 21. He also chaired the organising committee of the 2006 Doha Asian Games, which was the first edition attended by every member country.
notes: Reigning head of state, so a podcast request would realistically go through the Amiri Diwan or Qatar's Government Communications Office (gco.gov.qa). A more practical guest from QIA might be its CEO. His net worth figure is an old Hurun 2016 estimate.

name: Catherine Lozinck
profile: Catherine Lozick (correct spelling), daughter of Swagelok co-founder Fred A. Lennon, inherited a majority stake in the Solon, Ohio valve and fittings maker. Forbes reports she died in January 2025 at age 79. Swagelok is now led by Fred Lennon's grandson Thomas F. Lozick as chairman and CEO.
notes: Deceased January 2025 per Forbes profile (https://www.forbes.com/profile/catherine-lozick/). Input name is misspelled ('Lozinck'). Family remains very private; Swagelok is run by Thomas F. Lozick (https://swagelok.com/en/about/news/swagelok-announces-election-of-directors).

name: Sarah Chaney
current_role: Cargill heir (no known operating role); listed as Sarah MacMillan on LA Business Journal's 2017 Wealthiest Angelenos
profile: Cargill-MacMillan family heir, one of four daughters of the late W. Duncan MacMillan; media reports estimated each daughter inherited roughly a 3% stake in Cargill, the largest privately held US company. Appears to be the same person as 'Sarah MacMillan' (LABJ #49, 2017, $1.35B). Keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: She is a great-great-granddaughter of W.W. Cargill, who started Cargill as a single grain storage business in Conover, Iowa, in 1865.
notes: Very private; no public role, accounts or published contacts found. Identity link Chaney = MacMillan rests on LABJ and a LittleSis listing rather than a primary source; LABJ's stated age (28 in 2017) looks inconsistent. Not a good podcast target.

name: Li Guoxiang
current_role: Listed by Hurun as linked to Heaven-Sent Capital (Beijing PE firm); role not verified
profile: Appeared on the Hurun Global/China lists in 2015-2016 with about $2bn, with wealth attributed to Heaven-Sent Capital Management, a Beijing private-equity firm founded in 2006. Searches in English and Chinese did not confirm his role at the firm, or any current activity.
interesting_fact: Heaven-Sent Capital Management is a Beijing-based private equity firm founded in August 2006 that focuses on venture capital and buyouts.
notes: Identity not confirmed: searches did not tie the name Li Guoxiang (李国祥) to Heaven-Sent Capital. He dropped off the Hurun lists after 2016. Check the Chinese business registry before any outreach.

name: Stephen Hilbert
profile: The Hurun 2017 entry ties a 'Stephen Hilbert' to Menards, but Menards is owned by John Menard Jr. The likely match is Stephen C. Hilbert, Conseco founder, who was a 20% partner with Menard in investment firm MH Equity until Menard pushed him out in 2013. This looks like a list attribution error.
interesting_fact: Hilbert was a former investment partner of Menards owner John Menard Jr. in MH Equity (Indianapolis).
notes: Probably a data error: no evidence Hilbert owns Menards or is a billionaire. The MH Equity split involved litigation, so avoid that topic. Don't confuse him with Ithaca College mathematician Stephen R. Hilbert. Low priority.

name: Yin Tongyue
current_role: Chairman, Chery Automobile Co. / Chery Holding Group (Wuhu, China)
profile: Anhui-born engineer (b. 1962) who left a fast-track career at FAW-Volkswagen in 1996 to lead Wuhu city's new car project, which became Chery in 1997. He has run Chery for nearly three decades, building it into China's top car exporter; Chery listed in Hong Kong (9973.HK) in September 2025.
interesting_fact: Chery started with about RMB 300,000 in the bank (roughly the price of one VW Santana), and Yin set up shop in an abandoned brick factory with no heating or air conditioning.
deep_cut_fact: Yin bought Ford's retired Kent engine line from Wales for ~US$30M, sent the British installation engineers home, and his own team translated the manuals and installed it themselves; Chery's first engine came off the line on 27 April 1999.
notes: No published personal/press email found; best route is Chery Group corporate communications or HK-listed company secretary (HKEX filings). Chery 'founder' label is loose: company was set up by Wuhu officials with Yin as first technical director.

name: Maria del Carmen Sundblad Beccar Varela
current_role: Matriarch and shareholder of the Perez Companc Family Group (Argentina); founder of Munchi's ice cream and driving force behind Temaikèn.
profile: Born 1942, 'Munchi' Sundblad is the widow of Gregorio Pérez Companc (d. 2024), whose family controls Pecom (oil & gas services/production, expanding in Argentine upstream), Molinos Río de la Plata food and farmland. She built her own businesses: the Munchi's ice-cream chain, a Jersey dairy herd, and the Temaikèn bioparque in Escobar.
interesting_fact: She personally decided to build Temaikèn in Escobar, which opened in 2002 as Latin America's largest theme/bioparque, and she weighed in on the family's historic 2002 sale of Pecom Energía to Petrobras for about US$1bn.
deep_cut_fact: Her ice-cream brand Munchi's is named after her own childhood nickname; she also raises prize Jersey cattle at the family's San Isidro Labrador cabaña in Escobar, which she visited weekly, and La Nación wrote she only raises her voice when her bulls win at a rural show.
notes: Extremely private family ('extremists of anonymity'); no personal channels. Alive status presumed (on Hurun Global 2025-26 lists, no obituary found; would be 84). Contacts are company forms only (Munchi's, Pecom). Husband Gregorio died June 2024.

name: Giannis Vardinogiannis
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Motor Oil (Hellas) Corinth Refineries; Chairman & CEO, Avin Oil
profile: Eldest son of the late Vardis Vardinoyannis and head of the Vardinoyannis group, which controls Greek refiner Motor Oil Hellas. CEO since 2021 and chairman since Nov 2024, he has pushed the refiner into renewables (2.2 GW via the 2024 Anemos RES deal), waste/circular economy and banking (Optima Bank, listed 2023), with interests in shipping, upstream and hospitality.
interesting_fact: He ran Panathinaikos FC from 2000, taking the club to the Champions League quarter-finals in 2001-02, and was a founding member and later president of Greece's Super League.
deep_cut_fact: A Vassar economics graduate, he won the Greek Rally championship six straight times (1987-1992) in a Lancia Delta with co-driver Kostas Stefanis, and in 2024 founded the private team Cyclon Rally Sport.
notes: Also spelled Yannis/Ioannis Vardinoyannis. No published personal or press email verified (moh.gr blocked automated access); Motor Oil IR officer listed as Mary Psyllaki on market-data sites.

name: Robin Khuda
current_role: Founder and CEO, AirTrunk
profile: Dhaka-born accountant who moved to Sydney at 18, worked at Fujitsu, PIPE Networks and NEXTDC (as CFO), then founded hyperscale data-center operator AirTrunk in 2015. Blackstone and CPP Investments bought AirTrunk in 2024 in a A$24B (~US$16B) deal; he remains CEO and is expanding across APAC, the Middle East and India (a ~US$30B India plan announced in 2026).
interesting_fact: In AirTrunk's early days he dipped into his retirement savings to keep it afloat and came close to bankruptcy; in 2024 he was named AFR Business Person of the Year. In 2025 he gave A$100M to the University of Sydney for a 20-year women-in-STEM program.
deep_cut_fact: Right before founding AirTrunk he left NEXTDC to become CEO of Mint Wireless, a telecom payments company; he says he had been watching the cloud boom since 2010-11 and planning his own data-center business.
notes: Elected Fellow of ATSE in 2026. Runs the Khuda Family Foundation (women in tech, mental health). Also founded luxury developer Ondas. Excellent fit for the data-center podcast; route via AirTrunk media.

name: Amjad Masad
current_role: Cofounder and CEO, Replit
profile: Jordan-raised son of refugees who moved to the US in 2012 as an early engineer at Codecademy, then worked on Facebook's JavaScript infrastructure before cofounding Replit in 2016 with his wife Haya Odeh. Replit became a leader in AI 'vibe coding' agents and was valued at $9bn after a $400m round in March 2026.
interesting_fact: As a teenager in Jordan he made money building software management systems for local internet cafes; Replit's backers now include a16z, Coatue, Shaquille O'Neal, Jared Leto and Qatar's QIA.
deep_cut_fact: Before Replit he was tech lead on Facebook's JavaScript infrastructure team, which built or maintained the Babel compiler, Jest and the React Native packager; before that he was Codecademy's #1 employee, briefly at Yahoo, and worked in cybersecurity while in college.
notes: Very active and accessible on X (@amasad); has done many podcasts, so a direct X reply/DM plus press@replit.com is the best route. Strong AI/data-center angle (compute-hungry coding agents).

name: Sandeep Engineer
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Astral Ltd (Ahmedabad, India)
