profile: Chemical engineer (L D College, 1981) who began in pharma at Cadila before running his own bulk-drug ventures. After studying polymers in the US in 1997, he launched Astral in 1999 as India's first CPVC pipe maker, convincing plumbers to switch from metal; Astral now also makes adhesives, sealants and other building products.
interesting_fact: Astral was India's only CPVC pipe manufacturer when it started production in 1999, and had a hard time convincing customers that plastic pipes could outperform metal ones; it later used film stars as brand ambassadors.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture (1982) was Shree Trading, a pharma-formulation trading business run from a rented spot on Biscuit Gali off Ahmedabad's Relief Road with Rs 40,000, marketing GDCL's Isabgol products. He had joined Cadila in 1981 on Rs 850 a month. His motto: 'If we think we can, we will.'
notes: Contact is Astral's general corporate email (also listed on the investors page). He has given interviews to The CEO Magazine (theceomagazine.com) and is reasonably accessible to business media.

name: Chen Jiancheng
current_role: Founder and group chairman, Wolong Holding Group (Shangyu, Zhejiang)
profile: Founder of Wolong Group (born Shangyu 1959), a global maker of electric motors, generators and drive controls with interests in renewables. Its listed units include Wolong Electric Drive (600580.SH), Wolong New Energy and Brook Crompton. His daughter Chen Yanni is chairman and CEO of Wolong Holding, and his son-in-law Pang Xinyuan chairs Wolong Electric Drive.
interesting_fact: He was named China's EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year in 2019. His stated strategy is 'European technology, Chinese cost, global market', which he built through acquisitions such as Austria's ATB motors.
deep_cut_fact: Wolong began in 1984, when Chen and five partners pooled just over 50,000 yuan. They set up the Shangyu Multi-Speed Micro Motor Factory in a rented, run-down workshop at the foot of Wolong Mountain in Haobi township, which gave the company its name.
notes: Day-to-day leadership has passed to his daughter Chen Yanni (Wolong Holding) and son-in-law Pang Xinyuan (Wolong Electric Drive). Wolong is relevant to energy and storage topics: it has a Wolong Energy Storage unit and is pursuing a Hong Kong listing of Wolong Electric Drive. The IR email belongs to the listed company's board-secretary office.

name: Wang Jianfeng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ningbo Joyson Electronic Corp. (Joyson Electronics), listed in Shanghai (600699) and Hong Kong
profile: Wang founded Ningbo-based Joyson in the early 2000s and turned it into a global auto-parts group through a series of overseas acquisitions after its 2011 listing, including Germany's Preh, US-based KSS and the assets of Japan's Takata. Joyson makes airbags, seatbelts, steering wheels and automotive electronics, and has added a Hong Kong listing and a push into robotics.
interesting_fact: Between 2011 and 2019 Joyson bought nine overseas auto-parts companies, including Preh and KSS, which made a regional supplier into one of the world's largest automotive safety groups.
deep_cut_fact: Wang is an avid photographer whose work has been exhibited at the Ningbo Museum of Art. Before Joyson he was general manager of TRW (Ningbo) Electronic Components Fastener Co. and Ningbo Yongxing Vehicle Parts Co.
notes: Also known in English as Jeff Wang. The photography detail comes from the Forbes bio; the TRW/Yongxing career detail comes from the GlobalData executive profile (https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/ningbo-joyson-electronic-corp/executives/). Sources disagree on Joyson's founding year (2001 vs 2004). The robotics push is relevant to the podcast's tech angle.

name: Vivek Chand Burman
current_role: Patriarch of the V.C. Burman branch of the Dabur promoter family; former chairman of Dabur India (1998-2007)
profile: The oldest member of the Burman clan behind Dabur, the Ayurvedic consumer-goods company his great-grandfather S.K. Burman founded in Kolkata in 1884. He joined Dabur in 1954, chaired it from 1998 for about a decade, then handed over to nephew Anand Burman; his son Mohit became Dabur chairman in 2022. The family also holds a stake in battery maker Eveready Industries.
interesting_fact: Dabur began as a physician's home dispensary of Ayurvedic medicines in 1884; 360 ONE ranks the 'VC Burman and Family' #39 among India's wealthiest families (about $5.5bn) on Dabur shares, with brands like Dabur Chyawanprash, Honey and Amla Hair Oil leading their categories.
notes: Very elderly and low-profile (joined Dabur in 1954); alive status inferred from current Forbes listing, no death reports found. Realistic route is via Dabur corporate communications or son Mohit Burman's offices. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast except via the Eveready (batteries) stake.

name: Peter Jackson
current_role: Filmmaker; founder of WingNut Films (Wellington, NZ); producer of 'The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum' (2027)
profile: New Zealand director behind the 'Lord of the Rings' and 'Hobbit' trilogies, which grossed about $6bn worldwide. He became a billionaire in 2021 after selling Weta Digital's tech to Unity for $1.6bn in cash and stock. He is now producing 'The Hunt for Gollum' (directed by Andy Serkis), writing a Tintin sequel with Fran Walsh, and has invested in de-extinction firm Colossal Biosciences.
interesting_fact: He owns more than 40 airworthy WWI-era aircraft, kept at Hood Aerodrome near Masterton, and his firm The Vintage Aviator restores and builds WWI/WWII fighters. He received an Honorary Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He left school at 16 to work for seven years as a photo-engraver at Wellington's Evening Post, living with his parents to save for film gear. He shot his debut 'Bad Taste' mostly at weekends with unpaid friends, and played two roles in it, including a cliff-top fight with himself.
notes: Weta Workshop's FAQ names reception@wingnutfilms.co.nz for all enquiries about Peter Jackson and WingNut Films. He is a big fan of aviation history and tech (Weta, de-extinction), which could be a good podcast angle. He rarely does interviews outside film promotion.

name: Zhu Gongshan
current_role: Founder, chairman and joint CEO of GCL Technology Holdings (3800.HK); chairman of GCL Group (Golden Concord)
profile: Born 1958 in Funing, Yancheng, Jiangsu, Zhu founded GCL in Hong Kong in 1990, first building cogeneration power plants, then moving into solar-grade polysilicon from 2006. GCL Tech became one of the world's largest polysilicon makers and is now pushing low-energy FBR granular silicon. He also chairs the Asian Photovoltaic Industry Association and the Global Green Energy Industry Council.
interesting_fact: Zhu trained as a power engineer, graduating from Nanjing Electric Power College (now Nanjing Institute of Technology) in 1981. GCL's first business was thermal and cogeneration power plants, years before it became a solar-materials giant.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding GCL he worked ordinary jobs from 1978, including as a shop sales clerk. He later chaired the SNEC Hydrogen Energy Industry Alliance Council and was named one of the 'Ten Outstanding Contributors to New China's New Energy Industry' in its 70th year.
notes: ESG@gcl-power.com is the corporate contact printed in GCL Tech's 2025 annual/ESG report (Suzhou HQ, tel +86 512 6853 3900); no dedicated press email was found. He speaks often at SNEC and global solar forums, so a conference is a plausible route. The sales-clerk detail comes from an ifeng profile (https://finance.ifeng.com/people/comchief/zhugongshan.shtml); the award and hydrogen role from the HKEX annual report.

name: Anju Agarwal
current_role: Shareholder and promoter-group member, Macleods Pharmaceuticals (Mumbai); no public executive role found
profile: Anju Agarwal is the widow of Dr. Rajendra Agarwal, who co-founded Macleods Pharmaceuticals in 1986 with his brothers Girdharilal and Banwarilal Bawri to make anti-TB medicines. Macleods is privately held and among India's leading generics makers. She is listed in the promoter group of its 2022 draft IPO prospectus, and her husband died in November 2025.
interesting_fact: Macleods is named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks. The company grew into one of the world's major suppliers of affordable TB drugs.
notes: Very private; I found no public biography or interviews. She is a recently widowed shareholder, not an operating executive, and the bereavement is recent, so she is a poor podcast fit. The only route is through the Macleods corporate office.

name: Mitchell Jacobson
current_role: Non-executive Chairman of the Board, MSC Industrial Direct Co. (MSC Industrial Supply), Melville, NY
profile: Mitchell Jacobson joined MSC, the industrial-supply distributor his father Sidney founded, in 1976. He became president in 1982 and CEO in 1995, and he took the company public that year. He stepped back as CEO in 2005 and has been non-executive chairman since 2013. He and his wife Kathy give through the Jacobson Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: MSC took its name from Manhattan Supply Company, a cutting-tool marketer his father bought in 1970. It grew into one of the largest industrial distributors in North America.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer (Brandeis, then NYU Law) and worked at MSC on summers and holidays. When he joined full time in 1976, his first big project was a research tour of other industrial supply houses to find best practices to bring back to MSC.
notes: Low public profile. The published IR contact is Ryan Mills, VP Investor Relations. Avoid mentioning his parents' 2005 deaths.

name: Ilona Herlin
current_role: Chair of the Board, Kone Foundation (2026–); Docent in Finnish language, University of Helsinki; major Cargotec shareholder (via Pivosto Oy)
profile: Daughter of Kone chief Pekka Herlin and great-granddaughter of Harald Herlin, who invested in Kone in 1924. After the 2005 Kone/Cargotec demerger she and her brothers became leading owners of Cargotec (cargo-handling machinery). She is an academic linguist and long-time board member of the Kone Foundation, a major Finnish arts and science funder, which she now chairs.
interesting_fact: She is a working linguist (PhD, University of Helsinki) whose research has prompted debate about simplifying Finnish; she still publishes, e.g. a 2025 Virittäjä article on 'responsibility for language, responsibility for nature'.
deep_cut_fact: Her doctoral dissertation was on Finnish subordinating conjunctions, and in the 2010s she published a study of the much-debated 'alkaa tekemään' construction (using the 3rd infinitive after 'alkaa').
notes: Low-profile; academic email is published (obfuscated) on the University of Helsinki research portal. Kone Foundation chair since 2026, on its board since 1995. Also listed on board of an electrosensitivity foundation per fi.wikipedia.

name: Shi Yonghong
current_role: Chairman, Yihai International (HK:1579); co-founder and director of Haidilao International
profile: Co-founded Sichuan hot pot chain Haidilao in Jianyang in 1994 with Zhang Yong and their wives, each pair putting in a small share of an 8,000-yuan start. Haidilao listed in Hong Kong in 2018; Shi and wife Li Haiyan also hold stakes in spun-off condiment maker Yihai International, which he chairs.
interesting_fact: Haidilao is known for extreme service touches such as free manicures for waiting customers, and has expanded to the US, Japan, South Korea and Singapore.
deep_cut_fact: Shi met his future co-founder Zhang Yong as a schoolmate at a vocational school in Jianyang, Sichuan, where Zhang was studying electric welding; that friendship became the four-person founding team of Haidilao's first four-table shop in March 1994.
notes: Low public profile compared with Zhang Yong; Yihai chairman role per etnet company page (https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=1579). Best route is Haidilao/Yihai IR or media office. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Evan Williams
current_role: Co-founder and chairman of Mozi (private social app); founder of Medium; co-founder of Obvious Ventures
profile: Nebraska farm kid and college dropout who created Blogger (sold to Google), co-founded Twitter (CEO 2008-2010; on the board until 2019), and founded Medium in 2012 (CEO until 2022). Through Obvious Ventures he backs 'world positive' companies; Beyond Meat was one of its big wins. In late 2024 he co-founded Mozi with CEO Molly DeWolf Swenson, an app built to help friends meet in person.
interesting_fact: He is credited with coining the term 'blogger', and in the mid-1990s he sold tutorial videos that explained the Internet.
deep_cut_fact: Before Pyra and Blogger, he moved to Sebastopol, California in 1996 to work in marketing at O'Reilly Media, later freelancing as a coder (with clients including Intel and HP). While there he started his personal blog, EvHead.com.
notes: His current focus is Mozi, an anti-algorithm social app for meeting in person. For the energy/climate angle, Obvious Ventures' sustainability investing fits. His personal handles (@ev on X and Medium) are widely known, but I did not verify them against a source here.

name: Ruslan Rahimkulov
current_role: Private investor (family holdings in OTP Bank, MOL, real estate), Budapest
profile: Ruslan Rahimkulov (47, Russian citizen living in Budapest) and his older brother Timur inherited the fortune of their father Megdet in 2020. Megdet ran Gazprom's Hungarian office and a Gazprom-MOL JV, and built big stakes in MOL and OTP Bank. The brothers still hold large OTP and MOL stakes and have been setting up Hungarian companies in real estate, energy, construction and tourism.
interesting_fact: Their father Megdet Rahimkulov was the richest person in Hungary before he moved back to Russia in 2008.
notes: Very private, with no public profile or official contact channels. Hungarian press coverage is often critical (Russia ties, Sopron property deal), so approach carefully. Weak fit for the podcast apart from the energy-holdings angle (MOL).

name: William Koch
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Oxbow Corporation / Oxbow Carbon (West Palm Beach, Florida)
profile: William 'Bill' Koch, one of the four sons of Koch Industries co-founder Fred Koch, founded Oxbow in 1983 after leaving the family business; it grew into a major trader and processor of petroleum coke, coal, sulphur and other carbon products. He remains chairman, and is also a big collector of art, wine and Old West memorabilia.
interesting_fact: He won the 1992 America's Cup with his America3 syndicate, then in 1995 entered 'Mighty Mary', a boat crewed mostly by women, in the next Cup.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2011 he paid about $2.3m at Brian Lebel's Old West auction in Denver for the 'Upham tintype', the only authenticated photo of Billy the Kid; it joined his Wild West collection that includes Custer's rifle and Remington bronzes.
notes: Born 1940; listed on Forbes real-time 2026, no death reports found. Oxbow is private; a 2015 Oxbow press release listed a Corporate Communications Office in West Palm Beach (phone 561-907-5422, Director Corporate Affairs Brad Goldstein) - may be outdated. oxbow.com did not respond to direct fetch. Avoid the Koch-brothers feud and Oxbow litigation topics.

name: Tom Persson
current_role: Film and media entrepreneur (founder of CoMade); H&M family shareholder
profile: Tom Persson (b. 1985), youngest child of H&M chairman Stefan Persson and grandson of founder Erling Persson, is a third-generation heir to the H&M fortune. After studying at the Met Film School in London he moved into film production in Stockholm, starting media company CoMade in 2016.
interesting_fact: He was a producer of Jens Assur's 2017 feature Ravens (Korparna), made via Film and Art Affairs II, the company Assur ran with Persson.
deep_cut_fact: He is credited as executive producer on Tarik Saleh's The Nile Hilton Incident (2017), which won the World Cinema Grand Jury Prize (Dramatic) at Sundance and five Guldbagge Awards including Best Film.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Not in an H&M executive role, so H&M press office is not a route to him. Nile Hilton award detail: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Nile_Hilton_Incident

name: Mariarosa Lavelli
current_role: Major shareholder (~11%) of Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan); co-founder of the Fondazione Mariarosa e Giuseppe Crippa
profile: Widow of Giuseppe Crippa (d. July 2025), an ex-STMicroelectronics engineer who founded Technoprobe, now a global leader in probe cards for chip testing used by Nvidia, Apple, TSMC and others. She handled the administration from the start and was still reported in 2022 to follow the family company's accounts. Owns ~11% since the 2022 IPO.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco). In 1993 the nucleus was Giuseppe, son Cristiano, Mariarosa on administration and two employees. It moved to its first building in 1996 with about 10 staff.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2023 she and Giuseppe set up the Fondazione Mariarosa e Giuseppe Crippa to give structure to the family's and Technoprobe's philanthropy. Il Giorno noted she 'still follows the accounts' of the family firm even after it made Giuseppe a billionaire at 87.
notes: Recently widowed (July 2025), so be sensitive. Never gives interviews; route via Technoprobe press office. The family (son Cristiano Crippa, CEO Stefano Felici) is the public face. The foundation's start date is given as May 2023 in Technoprobe materials.

name: Li Jianli (励建立)
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen Kedali Industry Co. (科达利, SZSE 002850)
profile: Ningbo-born mould designer who co-founded Kedali in Shenzhen in 1996 with his brother using ~RMB 20,000 of savings. Kedali moved from stamping dies to phone-battery parts and, from 2007, to precision structural parts for EV batteries; it listed in Shenzhen in 2017 and supplies CATL, BYD, CALB, EVE, Panasonic and LG, with ~32% global share in 2023.
interesting_fact: In 2007, as iPhone-era pouch cells threatened his phone-battery parts business, he put more than half its profits into EV battery structural parts; R&D succeeded by 2010 and the segment grew from RMB 66m revenue (2013) to RMB 930m (2016).
deep_cut_fact: He studied mould design at a technical secondary school, graduated in 1991 and went to Shenzhen as a die designer at a Hong Kong-owned firm. Kedali's break came in 1999 when BYD asked it to co-develop phone-battery parts: after 20+ attempts in a year it matched Japanese imports at about a third of the price.
notes: Low media profile; Chinese-language outreach advisable. No published email found on company site; best route is Kedali's investor-interaction page (cninfo IRM, linked from its website) or the company contact page https://www.kedali.com.cn/contact.html. Brother Li Jianju (励建炬) is president.

name: Airat Shaimiev
current_role: Head (CEO) of JSC Tatavtodor, Tatarstan's state road-construction company; co-owner of TAIF shareholders' stake in Sibur
profile: Son of Tatarstan's first president, Mintimer Shaimiev. He built his fortune as a co-owner of TAIF Group, a Tatarstan holding with refining and petrochemical assets that merged into Sibur in 2021; TAIF shareholders received 15% of Sibur. He still runs Tatavtodor, the regional road builder, which reported 2025 contracts worth billions of rubles.
interesting_fact: With his brother Radik and his son Timur he also owns MNKT, a small oil producer in Tatarstan (per Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: He practiced karate in Soviet times, when the sport was banned in the USSR. After it was legalised he won the Kazan championship, then took up motor racing; he and his brother raced in the first events at the Vysokaya Gora autodrome in 1996.
notes: He is under UK sanctions (OpenSanctions entry gb-hmt-15608), so outreach may raise compliance and reputational issues. The only published contact is Tatavtodor's general company email. He gives few interviews.

name: Wang Nan
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Puya Semiconductor (普冉股份, Shanghai STAR Market 688766)
profile: Born 1976; SJTU physics graduate who spent 14 years at Hua Hong NEC (engineer to senior director) before founding Puya in 2012/2016. Puya makes NOR Flash, EEPROM and MCUs, listed in 2021, bought SLC-NAND maker SkyHigh Memory, saw H1 2026 profit jump ~19x on AI-driven memory demand, and plans a Hong Kong listing.
interesting_fact: He bet on an unfashionable process: Puya was the first to build general-purpose NOR Flash on the SONOS charge-trap process (instead of incumbents' ETOX), whose low power and tiny die size rode the TWS-earbud boom into Xiaomi, Samsung, OPPO and vivo products.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a double bachelor's in physics and applied electronics from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and, while still at Hua Hong NEC, earned an EMBA (2011) from Washington University in St. Louis' Olin Business School.
notes: Low-profile; few personal interviews. Route via board secretary / IR (ir@puyasemi.com). Hurun lists name as Wang Nan (王楠). Company announced H-share HK listing plans in Nov 2026.

name: Yao Lijun
current_role: Founder, Chairman (and CTO), Konfoong Materials International Co. (SZSE: 300666), Yuyao/Ningbo, Zhejiang
profile: Materials scientist with doctorates from Harbin Institute of Technology and Hiroshima University who returned from abroad and in 2005 co-founded Konfoong Materials with six partners in Yuyao, Zhejiang. Konfoong makes ultra-high-purity metal sputtering targets used by 100+ chip fabs worldwide, a key domestic supplier in China's semiconductor supply chain; he aims for a 30% global share.
interesting_fact: Konfoong's sputtering targets are used by more than 100 chip factories worldwide, and Yao has said his goal is a 30% global market share in target materials.
deep_cut_fact: He launched Konfoong in April 2005 alongside returned Chinese scientists plus Japanese and American experts, shipping in 20 containers of imported equipment to Yuyao; he credits reform and opening-up with 'four opportunities' including his Japanese doctoral scholarship.
notes: Thousand Talents Program recipient; won Zhejiang provincial science & technology award (2018). No published IR email found; Konfoong's board secretary (Zou Junwei, appointed 2025) and securities dept. handle investor queries via SZSE Interactive (irm.cninfo.com.cn). Company site was not reachable from here; URL taken from public listings.

name: Farris Wilks
current_role: Co-owner, Wilks Brothers LLC (family investment office, Cisco, Texas); 10%+ shareholder in ProFrac Holding Corp. (ACDC)
profile: Texas stonemason-turned-fracking billionaire: with brother Dan he founded Wilks Masonry (1995) and Frac Tech (2002), selling to a Temasek-led group in 2011 for $3.5bn pretax. Via Wilks Brothers they invest in oilfield services (ProFrac, U.S. Well Services, Dawson Geophysical) and own ~672,000 acres in six states.
interesting_fact: Farris is pastor of his own church, the Assembly of Yahweh Seventh Day Church near Cisco, Texas - the congregation his father Voy led from 1952.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil, the brothers were bricklayers like their father and ran Wilks Masonry; they launched Frac Tech in 2002 out of tiny Cisco, Texas (Eastland County), where both still live, and grew it into one of the largest US fracking firms in under a decade.
notes: Very private; Wilks Brothers site publishes no contact. ProFrac (chaired by Dan's son Matt Wilks) is an indirect route only - Farris is a shareholder, not an executive. Politically prominent (major conservative donor), so expect media caution.

name: Tseng Shin-yi
profile: Most likely Cheng Hsin-yi (鄭信義, b. 1928), one of three cofounders in 1949 of Taiwan's Chang Chun Group, the island's No. 2 petrochemical group after Formosa Plastics. Chinese Wikipedia records his death on 28 January 2016.
notes: Caproasia's 2017 Forbes-based list has 'Tseng Shin-yi', 90, Chang Chun Group; this matches cofounder 鄭信義, who died 28 Jan 2016 per https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%84%AD%E4%BF%A1%E7%BE%A9 and https://www.cmoney.tw/notes/note-detail.aspx?nid=49860. Romanization match not 100% confirmed; treat as deceased.

name: Vladimir Gridin
current_role: Retired co-founder of Siberian Business Union (SDS) holding, Kemerovo; exited the business from 2016 to 2019
profile: Vladimir Gridin co-founded Siberian Business Union (SDS) with Mikhail Fedyaev in the mid-1990s and built it into a large Kuzbass coal, chemicals and engineering holding (registered 2004). He was a State Duma deputy for Kemerovo region from 2011. He later stepped back, reportedly moved to Monaco, and from about 2016 to 2019 sold his stakes to Fedyaev and Roman Trotsenko.
interesting_fact: SDS grew into Russia's third-largest producer of thermal (power-station) coal, with interests in mining, rail transport, chemicals, machine building and radio stations.
deep_cut_fact: The partners' first major asset in the mid-1990s was the Chernigovets open-pit coal mine in Kuzbass. When SDS was formally registered in Kemerovo in 2004, it already brought together more than 20 businesses in coal, machinery, building materials and utilities.
notes: Out of public life since around 2015; last on the Forbes list in 2013. He has largely exited SDS and reportedly lives in Monaco (dataset says UK). No current public contact found; alive status is unconfirmed, with no death reports found. Russian coal ties carry sanctions sensitivity, so check before outreach.

name: George Hearst, Jr.
current_role: Deceased (was Chairman of the Board, Hearst Corporation, 1996-2012)
profile: George Randolph Hearst Jr., eldest grandson of William Randolph Hearst, chaired Hearst Corporation from 1996 until his death on June 25, 2012, aged 84, at Stanford University Medical Center after complications from a stroke.
notes: Died June 25, 2012 (Hearst Corporation press release, globenewswire, June 26, 2012). Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Roberto Gonzalez Barrera
current_role: Deceased (died 25 Aug 2012, Houston, Texas); was chairman of Gruma and lifetime honorary chairman of Grupo Financiero Banorte
notes: Died 25 August 2012 aged 81. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Gonz%C3%A1lez_Barrera ; https://expansion.mx/negocios/2012/08/25/fallece-roberto-gonzalez-barrera . Son Juan Antonio Gonzalez Moreno now leads Gruma.

name: Tuncay Ozilhan
current_role: Former Chairman of Anadolu Group (handed the chair to Kamil Süleyman Yazıcı on 21 April 2025); Chairman of the Anadolu Foundation per the group's board page
profile: Born in Kayseri in 1947, Özilhan is the son of Anadolu Group co-founder İzzet Özilhan. He was the group's CEO from 1984 to 2017 and its chairman from 2007 to April 2025, building it into a conglomerate spanning Anadolu Efes beer, Coca-Cola İçecek bottling, Migros retail and Isuzu/Honda automotive. He handed the chair to the third generation in 2025.
interesting_fact: Under the group's founding 'constitution', Anadolu donates 1-5% of profits to the Anadolu Foundation before any dividends are paid. The foundation runs a hospital, a school and dormitories.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1977 as general director of Erciyas Brewery in his home region and held posts at Toz Metal and Turkish Airlines before joining Anadolu Group in 1984. He later served as chairman of the business association TÜSİAD (2001-2003).
notes: Stepped down as group chairman in April 2025, so 'current role' may be limited to foundation and board posts. Sources differ between 'chairman' and 'president' of TÜSİAD and give 2001-2003 or 2001-2004 for the term. No dedicated press email found; Kaan Ünver is named as the group's corporate communications coordinator.

name: Jess Jackson
current_role: Deceased (founder of Kendall-Jackson / Jackson Family Wines)
profile: Jess Stonestreet Jackson Jr. (1930-2011), founder of Kendall-Jackson and Jackson Family Wines, died on April 21, 2011 at age 81 at his home in Geyserville, California.
notes: Died April 21, 2011 (source: https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/wine-icon-jess-stonestreet-jackson-passes-away-120361079.html). The business is now run as Jackson Family Wines by his family; profile skipped per instructions.

name: Chaijudh Karnasuta
current_role: Co-founder of Italian-Thai Development (ITD), Thailand; MarketScreener also lists him as chairman of Siam Steel Syndicate. Current status unverified.
profile: Forbes listed him in 1996 with about $1.9bn and no source of wealth. He is most likely the Thai co-founder (also spelled Chaiyudh) of Italian-Thai Development, which he started with Italian Giorgio Berlingieri in 1958. ITD became one of Thailand's largest construction groups and is now led by Premchai Karnasuta.
interesting_fact: Before founding ITD, he and Giorgio Berlingieri worked together in 1954 on a venture to salvage five sunken ships. ITD was incorporated on 15 August 1958.
notes: Only one Forbes listing (1996) with no source of wealth, so the ITD match is likely but not certain. He would be very elderly now and I could not confirm whether he is alive. ITD is currently led by Premchai Karnasuta, who faces criminal charges over a 2025 building collapse. Treat this lead with caution.

name: Mary Alice (Dorrance) Malone
profile: Died June 16, 2025, aged 75. She was a Campbell Soup heiress, Campbell's longest-serving director (35 years) and the founder of Iron Spring Farm, an equestrian breeding centre.
notes: Deceased (June 2025) per Campbell's press release and the Philadelphia Inquirer obituary (https://www.inquirer.com/obituaries/mary-alice-dorrance-malone-death-campbells-equestrian-20250624.html). Skipped.

name: Mike Lazaridis
current_role: Managing Partner & Co-Founder, Quantum Valley Investments (Waterloo, Ontario); founder of Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics
profile: Mike Lazaridis was born in Istanbul and grew up in Windsor, Ontario. He dropped out of the University of Waterloo in 1984 to found Research In Motion, the maker of the BlackBerry, and was co-CEO until 2012. He has since put hundreds of millions into Waterloo's quantum ecosystem: the Perimeter Institute, the Institute for Quantum Computing, and the $100M Quantum Valley Investments fund he co-founded with Doug Fregin.
interesting_fact: Before the BlackBerry, he won an Emmy (1994) and an Academy Award for Technical Achievement (1999) for a high-speed barcode reader used in film editing.
deep_cut_fact: At age 12 he won a prize from the Windsor Public Library for reading every science book in the library.
notes: Strong angle for an energy and data-center show: quantum computing and quantum-safe technology. Perimeter Institute marked its 25th anniversary in 2025, and he founded it. The library prize is cited on Wikipedia to an old CRN article, so verify it if possible.

name: Zhou Xiaoguang
current_role: Founder/former chairman, Neoglory Holdings Group (新光控股集团), Zhejiang — group in bankruptcy restructuring since 2019
profile: Born 1962 in Zhuji, Zhejiang, Zhou built Neoglory from a jewellery/ornament trading business in Yiwu into a conglomerate with large real estate holdings, and was a National People's Congress deputy (10th and 11th NPC). Neoglory defaulted on bonds in 2018 and entered bankruptcy proceedings in 2019; she no longer appears on rich lists after 2018.
interesting_fact: In 2018, shortly before its debt crisis, Neoglory sought to spend over RMB 8bn acquiring Hong Kong-listed China High Speed Transmission, a wind-turbine gearbox maker, to enter the wind-power market.
deep_cut_fact: She started out at 17 as a street-stall vendor ("地摊妹") with no capital, a rags-to-riches story that made her a celebrated model entrepreneur in China; she later studied economic management at Zhejiang University.
notes: Sensitive: Neoglory's 2018 bond default and bankruptcy; in Dec 2019 regulators imposed a 10-year securities-market ban on her and her husband (wallstreetcn.com/articles/3519767, nbd.com.cn). No recent public activity found; not a good podcast prospect. No published contact found.

name: Gu Jiangsheng
current_role: Director (former chairman) of Kuka Home (顾家家居, SSE:603816)
profile: Built Hangzhou upholstered-furniture maker Kuka Home out of his father Gu Yuhua's furniture business, rebranding it as 'Kuka' around 2000 and listing it in Shanghai in 2016. In 2023-24 the Gu family sold ~29% to Midea heir He Jianfeng's Infore group (~8.9bn yuan), and Gu stepped down as chairman in Sept 2024 while staying on the board.
interesting_fact: Control of Kuka Home passed in January 2024 from the Gu family to He Jianfeng, son of Midea founder He Xiangjian, with ex-Midea executive Kuang Guangxiong taking over as chairman.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking over the family furniture business from his father around 2000 and renaming it 'Kuka Craft Sofa', Gu was a physical education teacher (Yicai describes him as a former university PE teacher; other profiles say he studied in Hangzhou University's PE department).
notes: No longer controls the company; no IR email found in quick search (check latest 603816 annual report on sse.com.cn). Avoid the 2020 CSRC probe topic.

name: Wang Shusheng
current_role: Founder and chairman, Tianjin DTW Group (大田集团); chairman, Huatian Investment (per older profiles)
profile: Tianjin-born (1954) founder of DTW Group, which he started in 1992 as an air-cargo forwarding and charter business. In 1999 DTW formed a China express joint venture with FedEx. FedEx bought DTW's 50% stake and its domestic network in 2006 for about $400m. He later expanded into logistics (a DTW-Geodis JV), real estate and tourism through Huatian Investment.
interesting_fact: DTW's joint venture with FedEx (1999) gave FedEx its China express network; in early 2006 FedEx bought DTW's 50% of the JV together with its domestic express network.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked at the Tianjin Public Security Bureau. He started DTW in 1992 with 60,000 yuan he had raised himself.
notes: Profile sources are mostly from around 2006. He was off the Hurun lists after 2020, and I found no recent confirmation that he still chairs DTW. The DTW site (dtw.com.cn) returned 403. He has also been a Tianjin CPPCC member. He is low-profile, so a Chinese-language approach via DTW Group is the likeliest route.

name: Zhang Shengfei
profile: Listed by Hurun (China list 2006-2019, Global 2018-2020) as the founder behind 'Shenghua' (manufacturing). Searches could not confirm which Shenghua company this is or find a sourced biography of Zhang Shengfei.
notes: Unverified. Several Chinese companies are called Shenghua (升华/胜华/盛华), and none of the sources found named Zhang Shengfei as owner or chairman. He has been off the Hurun lists since 2020. Needs a Chinese-language company registry check before any outreach.

name: G Amarender Reddy
current_role: Founder and Chairman, GAR Corporation (Hyderabad)
profile: G. (Gavva) Amarender Reddy founded GAR Corporation in 1982, which grew into a developer and single owner of Grade-A office parks in Hyderabad (10M+ sq ft, incl. the GAR Infobahn campus in Kokapet) leased to IT, BFSI and pharma tenants. Day-to-day leadership has passed to his son Abhinav Ram Reddy as managing director.
interesting_fact: The 2021 Grohe-Hurun India Real Estate Rich List ranked him the richest real estate developer in Hyderabad, with family wealth of about Rs 15,000 crore, built on a lease-and-hold office model rather than selling property.
notes: Low public profile; son Abhinav Ram Reddy (MD) is the public face and a Milken Institute speaker. Company's only published email is the leasing inbox leaseinfo@garcorp.in (https://www.garcorp.in/contactus), not a press address. Data-center angle: Hyderabad office/GCC landlord.

name: Sanjeev Soosaipillai
current_role: Founder, chairman & CEO of Prax Group (UK oil refining/fuel group); key UK units in administration since June 2025
profile: Sanjeev Kumar (Winston) Soosaipillai cofounded Prax with his wife Arani in 1999, growing from petrol retailing into wholesale fuel (2002), then buying the Lindsey Oil Refinery on the Humber and a stake in South Africa's Natref refinery. Parent State Oil and the Lindsey refinery entered administration/liquidation in June 2025; retail, upstream and international arms continue to trade.
interesting_fact: Prax grew from a two-person operation in 1999 into the owner of one of the UK's six major refineries (Lindsey), a rare case of a privately held, founder-owned UK refiner.
notes: Sensitive: Prax's UK refining collapse (June 2025) is under Insolvency Service investigation, with a reported asset freeze. The only press contact is the administrators' (Teneo) media desk, not him personally. Most bio coverage is sponsored content. Probably not a suitable guest now.

name: Arani Soosaipillai
current_role: Co-owner (with husband Sanjeev Kumar/Winston Soosaipillai) of Prax Group, UK oil refining and trading group now in insolvency
profile: Arani Soosaipillai and her husband built London-based Prax Group (founded 1999), an oil trading, distribution and refining group that bought the Lindsey oil refinery. Reports name her as joint ultimate controlling party alongside her husband, who was sole director. Prax's main companies entered administration/liquidation in mid-2025 and Lindsey refinery ceased operations.
interesting_fact: Prax grew from a 1999 London fuel-trading start-up into an integrated group owning the Lindsey refinery in Lincolnshire, one of only a handful of UK refineries.
notes: Not a good outreach target: Prax collapsed in June 2025 (administration/liquidation, refinery closure, UK government demands for investigation, High Court asset freeze on her husband). Hurun $1.9bn figure is pre-collapse and stale. No public role or contact for her found.

name: Wang Junshi
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder, Ginlong Technologies (Solis inverters); stepped down as director/deputy GM in 2021
profile: Wang Junshi (age ~77, Ningbo) co-founded Ginlong Technologies in 2005 with his wife Lin Yibei and son Wang Yiming; the company, sold under the Solis brand, became one of the world's largest string solar-inverter makers and listed in Shenzhen (300763) in 2019. He left the board in 2021; his son now chairs the firm, which has expanded into energy storage.
interesting_fact: Ginlong/Solis says it was only the second inverter company worldwide to obtain the UK's G83 grid-connection certification, in 2006, a year after its founding, an early bet on export markets.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding a multibillion-dollar solar-inverter business, Wang Junshi worked as a high school teacher.
notes: Very low public profile; elderly and retired from management. Best route is via Ginlong/Solis corporate (son Wang Yiming is chairman and the public face). No published press/IR email found on Solis site (only sales/service addresses).

name: Tan Dong
current_role: Director (non-independent), Guangdong Kingshine Electronic Technology Co. (科翔股份, SZSE: 300903); GM of subsidiary Huayu Huayuan
profile: Tan Dong (b. 1969, postgraduate degree) co-founded Huizhou-based PCB maker Kingshine (Dayawan Kexiang) in 2001 with Zheng Xiaorong, now chairwoman; the pair are its controlling shareholders and share the Hurun fortune. Kingshine listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in Nov 2020 and makes HDI, multilayer, flex and ceramic-substrate boards for autos, servers, optical modules and mmWave radar.
interesting_fact: Before Kingshine, Tan Dong was general manager (1996-2001) of Shenzhen Shunjiaxing Electronics, where Zheng Xiaorong was executive director; they then moved together to found Dayawan Kexiang in July 2001, the origin of today's listed group.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1993 as an engineer in the technical department of Guangdong Macro (Wanjiale) Communication Equipment Co., before moving into PCB manufacturing.
notes: Hurun English name 'Kingshine' = 科翔股份 (not Kinwong/景旺). Low public profile; no interviews found. Company securities dept (board secretary Zheng Haitao) is the formal route; IR email published in company filings (shown via Eastmoney F10).

name: Zheng Xiaorong
current_role: Chairwoman, Guangdong Kingshine Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (科翔股份, SZ:300903), a Huizhou PCB maker
profile: Zheng Xiaorong (b. 1972) and her husband Tan Dong are the controlling shareholders of Kingshine Electronic (科翔股份). The company makes high-density PCBs, including HDI boards for AI servers and 800G optical modules, at plants in Huizhou and Jiangxi. She has run the business since 2001 and was general manager until October 2025. She holds about 15% directly.
interesting_fact: In 2009 she bought a near-bankrupt factory, turned it profitable within three months, and passed RMB 100M in output the next year. Around 2012 she set up an HDI division while most peers held back, and that bet now underpins Kingshine's AI-server boards.
deep_cut_fact: She began her career in 1992 as marketing department manager at Shenzhen Kerong Electronics' subsidiary factory. In 1997 she became executive director of Shenzhen Shunjiaxing Electronics, before founding Daya Bay Kexiang (Kingshine's predecessor) in 2001.
notes: The Hurun 'Kingshine' entry is Guangdong Kingshine Electronic (科翔股份), not Jingsheng/晶盛. The board secretary is Zheng Haitao, and the IR route is the securities affairs inbox. Her motto from a 2026 Shanghai Securities News interview: 'bend down to dig into technology, look up to see the direction clearly' (俯身深耕技术、抬头看清方向).

name: Zhang Yanxia
current_role: Co-founder and Deputy General Manager (joined 2013 as deputy GM and board secretary), Gpixel / Changchun Changguang Chenxin Microelectronics (長光辰芯), HKEX-listed
profile: Zhejiang University applied-electronics graduate with a PhD from TU Delft; co-founded Gpixel with her husband Wang Xinyang, an incubatee of the CAS Changchun Institute of Optics. Gpixel makes industrial and scientific CMOS image sensors (ranked ~3rd globally in both niches). The couple held ~49.5% pre-IPO; the company listed in Hong Kong in April 2026, jumping ~75% on day one.
interesting_fact: Gpixel avoided the smartphone-sensor market dominated by Sony and Samsung and targeted industrial/scientific imaging (<3% of the CIS market); in 2015 it launched what it calls the world's first back-illuminated scientific CMOS image sensor.
deep_cut_fact: She and her husband were classmates in Zhejiang University's applied electronics program; she did her master's at Concordia University in Canada (he went to Southampton) before both earned PhDs at TU Delft. She gave up a job abroad to join Gpixel in its second year.
notes: Fortune shared with husband Wang Xinyang (chairman/GM). Her exact current board title post-IPO not verified; check the HKEX prospectus. Media contact form is the best press route.

name: Zhou Xunwei
current_role: Founder & Chairman, JoulWatt Technology (杰华特, SSE STAR: 688141), Hangzhou
profile: Zhou Xunwei (周逊伟) is a Zhejiang University and Virginia Tech-trained power-electronics engineer who spent years at US analog-chip firms before co-founding JoulWatt in Hangzhou in March 2013. JoulWatt designs analog/power-management ICs, including power chips for servers and data centers, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in Dec 2022; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: JoulWatt was founded on 18 March 2013 by Zhou and co-founder Huang Biliang and IPO'd on the STAR Market in December 2022, part of China's push for domestic analog/power-management chips.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding JoulWatt he was a senior design engineer at Linear Technology in the US (2001-2007) and then VP of engineering at Helix Micro; he earned his PhD at Virginia Tech after bachelor's and master's degrees at Zhejiang University.
notes: Deep-cut career details come from a single Chinese profile site (maigoo); verify against the STAR Market prospectus director bios before use. IR contact is board secretary Ma Wenwen's office. Reported US nationality.

name: Dou Baibing
current_role: Supervisor, Hangzhou Jinjiang Group; legal representative of family holding companies (Hangzhou Yande Industrial, Zhejiang Kangrui Investment)
profile: Dou Baibing (钭白冰) is a next-generation member of the family behind Hangzhou Jinjiang Group (founded by Dou Zhenggang and Wei Xuefeng), a Zhejiang private group in waste-to-energy, alumina/aluminium and chemicals. Hurun's 2023 Self-Made Women list ranks her jointly with Wei Xuefeng (Jinjiang, energy & chemicals). She holds board-level and holding-company roles in the group.
interesting_fact: She was profiled in a 2021 '浙商接班人 TOP50' (Top 50 Zhejiang business successors) audio series as one of Jinjiang Group's successor generation.
deep_cut_fact: She is legal representative of Hangzhou Yande Industrial (杭州延德实业, est. 2013), one of the shareholder vehicles of Sanmenxia Aluminum, the alumina business Jinjiang is folding into listed Jiaozuo Wanfang.
notes: Identity tied via Hurun API (2023 Self-Made Women: '尉雪凤、钭白冰 / Wei Xuefeng & Dou Baibing, Jinjiang') and corporate registry snippets (aiqicha/qcc list her as supervisor of Hangzhou Jinjiang Group from 2022). Very private; no interviews or social accounts found. Route via Jinjiang Group.

name: Fan Caiping
current_role: Wife of JA Solar founder/chairman Jin Baofang; former co-owner of JA Solar's controlling holding company Jingtaifu (stake transferred within the family in 2023)
profile: Fan Caiping (范彩平) is the wife of Jin Baofang, who built Jinglong Group and JA Solar (晶澳科技, 002459.SZ) in Ningjin county, Xingtai, Hebei, into one of the world's largest solar-module makers. She co-owned the family holding company Jingtaifu, which controls JA Solar. Hurun listed her with Jin Junmiao on its Self-Made Women lists (2022-2023).
interesting_fact: JA Solar is controlled through a single family vehicle, Jingtaifu, which held about 47.6% of the company as of March 2023; Hurun ranked Fan Caiping and Jin Junmiao jointly at No. 30 on its 2022 Self-Made Women list (RMB 21.5bn).
deep_cut_fact: Jingtaifu, now JA Solar's controlling shareholder, started out as Ningjin County Jingtaifu Technology, owned by Jin Baofang and Fan Caiping in their home county of Ningjin, Hebei, where JA Solar and Jinglong are based.
notes: Identity confirmed via Hurun API (2022 women list: 范彩平、靳军淼, 晶澳科技, mother & daughter) and Chinese press naming her as Jin Baofang's wife. Per Sina (Aug 2026) her Jingtaifu stake went to the family in 2023, so her current holding may be small or nil. No public role or interviews. Route only via JA Solar IR.

name: Jin Junmiao
current_role: Shareholder (25%) of Jingtaifu, the controlling shareholder of JA Solar Technology; former JA Solar assistant president and procurement head. Current title unconfirmed.
profile: Younger daughter of JA Solar founder Jin Baofang. Her wealth comes from a 25% stake in Jingtaifu, the holding company that owns about 48% of JA Solar, one of the world's largest PV module makers. She was assistant president and ran procurement, and has a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: In June 2021 her father transferred 25% of Jingtaifu, the vehicle controlling about 47.77% of JA Solar, to her. That makes her the only one of his daughters with a direct stake in the controlling shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2019 she was 'godmother' at the naming ceremony for a new COSCO Shipping vessel, the 'COSCO Shipping Aquarius'. She named the ship, cut the rope and broke the champagne bottle in the traditional launch rite.
notes: Hurun calls her 'self-made', but her stake came from her founder father. She is very private and I found no personal channels; go through JA Solar IR. Her husband Tao Ran is a JA Solar director.

name: Alfons Doblinger
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder and managing director, Doblinger Unternehmensgruppe (incl. DIBAG Industriebau AG), Munich; major shareholder of Bauer AG
profile: Bavarian builder-turned-landlord who founded the Munich-based Doblinger group (design, construction and management of property) and remains one of Munich's largest property owners, with roughly 19,600 apartments and a large commercial portfolio. Still running the group in his 80s; he is also the largest shareholder of foundation-engineering firm Bauer AG.
interesting_fact: He first came to public attention in 1990 when he bought the Bavarian portfolio of the trade-union housing company Neue Heimat - more than 32,500 apartments - for just under 1 billion D-Mark.
deep_cut_fact: Born and raised in the Bavarian Forest (an 'Oberpfälzer'), he started his business at 23 in 1967 according to Börsen-Zeitung (Forbes dates it to 1962 at 17), and was still the group's Geschäftsführer at 78.
notes: Described by Börsen-Zeitung as 'der scheue' (the shy one): avoids publicity and declined to answer the paper's questions. Expect low responsiveness; corporate email via DIBAG is the only published route.

name: Philip O'Doherty
current_role: Chairman and owner of Derry City FC; founder and former CEO of E&I Engineering (now part of Vertiv)
profile: An engineer and Queen's University Belfast graduate, O'Doherty founded E&I Engineering in Burnfoot, Co. Donegal in the 1980s. It made switchgear and power-distribution equipment, much of it for data centres. In 2021 he sold it with affiliate Powerbar Gulf to Vertiv for about $1.8bn upfront plus up to $200m earnout, in cash and Vertiv stock. He now bankrolls Derry City FC.
interesting_fact: At the time of the sale E&I had about 2,100 employees, roughly $460m in sales and over 1,000 staff at its rural Burnfoot HQ, making it one of the largest private employers in the Donegal/Derry border region and a key supplier of data-centre power infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting E&I he spent five years as an engineer at DuPont's plant in Campsie, Co. Derry. He has long been the financial backbone of his hometown club Derry City FC and in recent seasons set an explicit target of winning the club's first league title in decades.
notes: Forbes data says 'Vertix'; the acquirer is Vertiv. Highly relevant to a data-centre/energy podcast. Sources give the founding year as 1986 or 1987; the DuPont detail is from the Forbes bio (https://www.forbes.com/profile/philip-odoherty/). Low media profile outside football; the club is the most realistic route. No published personal or office email found.

name: Casey Foyt
current_role: Owner & Executive Vice President, Indianapolis Colts (since June 2025)
profile: Middle daughter of the late Jim Irsay and granddaughter of Robert Irsay, who bought the Colts in 1972. She and sisters Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Kalen Jackson inherited equal ~33.3% stakes in the franchise after their father's death in May 2025; she became Owner & EVP after 13 seasons as vice chair/owner, focusing on marketing and community relations.
interesting_fact: Before joining the Colts in 2007, she worked for the NFL in London planning the league's first regular-season game outside North America - Giants vs. Dolphins at Wembley in October 2007.
deep_cut_fact: An Indiana University sports-marketing graduate, she helped revitalize the Indianapolis Colts Women's Organization and planned the group's first major fundraiser in 2007; as a high-schooler she answered phones at the Colts' front desk.
notes: Low public profile compared with sister Carlie (CEO). Best route is the Colts' communications/front office. Family is active in mental-health campaign Kicking the Stigma (led by sister Kalen). Little energy/data-center angle.

name: Kalen Jackson
current_role: Owner and chief brand officer, Indianapolis Colts; president, Indianapolis Colts Foundation
profile: Youngest daughter of the late Colts owner Jim Irsay; she and her two sisters each inherited about a third of the NFL franchise after his death in May 2025. She joined the team in 2010 after graduating from Indiana University in sports management and marketing. She now runs the Colts' brand and philanthropy, including the Kicking The Stigma mental health initiative.
interesting_fact: Kicking The Stigma, which she leads, has put more than $32m into mental health grants and programs since 2020. It won the Colts the 2025 ESPY for Sports Humanitarian Team of the Year.
deep_cut_fact: She worked with the Indiana High School Athletic Association to promote girls' flag football and get it made an official Indiana high school sport. She also helped set up the Irsay Institute at IU Bloomington, which researches mental health stigma. She chairs the NFL's employee benefits committee.
notes: She speaks publicly and often about mental health (GMFB, Up & Adam, BizVoice), so a podcast pitch tied to Kicking The Stigma is the most natural route, via Colts communications. There is no energy or data-center link. The official_website entry is the Colts front-office page, not her own site.

name: Sandro Veronesi
current_role: Founder and President, Oniverse (formerly Calzedonia Group), Verona
profile: Veronesi founded Calzedonia in the mid-1980s as a side business while still working at Golden Lady, Nerino Grassi's hosiery company. He built it into Oniverse, a group with Calzedonia, Intimissimi, Tezenis and Falconeri, more than 5,600 stores in 57 countries, and 2025 revenue of about EUR 3.7bn. The group has since added wine (Signorvino, wineries) and yachts (Pardo, Grand Soleil, VanDutch).
interesting_fact: He started Calzedonia as a side business while still employed at Golden Lady, then the world's leading tights maker. He later expanded into wine with Signorvino and into yacht building.
deep_cut_fact: When Calzedonia Group renamed itself in December 2023, the new name 'Oniverse' was chosen partly because it is an anagram of the Veronesi surname.
notes: hello@oniverse.it is the group's general contact address, not his personal one. The family also runs Fondazione San Zeno. Not to be confused with the Italian novelist of the same name.

name: Olivia Holding
current_role: President, E & F Properties Inc. and Twin States Farming Inc. (Smithfield, NC); President, Ella Ann L. & Frank B. Holding Foundation; major shareholder, First Citizens BancShares
profile: Olivia (Britton) Holding is one of four sisters of First Citizens chairman and CEO Frank Holding Jr. With her siblings she owns about 20% of First Citizens BancShares, the Raleigh bank her grandfather led from 1935. She runs the family's commercial-property and farming companies in Johnston County and the family foundation, and serves on North Carolina conservation and civic boards.
interesting_fact: Her family has run First Citizens since 1935. In 2023 the bank bought the collapsed Silicon Valley Bank, which turned it into a national player and put it on the Fortune 500.
deep_cut_fact: She once considered the Foreign Service but became an elementary-school guidance counselor (M.Ed., George Washington University, 1990), and later served as personnel director for YMCA Camp Seafarer. She sits on the boards of the NC Coastal Federation, NC Aquarium Society and the Research Triangle Park Foundation.
notes: Private passive shareholder, not a First Citizens executive. The bank's media address reaches the company, not her directly. Her environmental and coastal board work (NC Coastal Federation, EDF NC office) could be a hook for an energy show. Bio details date from a 2016 RTP profile.

name: Hui Wing Mau
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Shimao Group Holdings (HK:0813); chairman until Sept 2024, when son Jason Hui reportedly took over as chairman
profile: Hui Wing Mau (Xu Rongmao), born 1950 in Shishi, Fujian, founded Shimao, a Hong Kong-listed developer with projects across dozens of Chinese cities, and chaired it from 2004. Shimao defaulted on bonds in 2022 and has been restructuring its offshore debt; leadership has passed to his son Jason, with daughter Carol at Shanghai Shimao.
interesting_fact: Shimao's portfolio has long mixed residential development with hotels and landmark commercial towers; Hui describes 34+ years in property development, property investment and hotel operation.
deep_cut_fact: Before Shimao, Hui moved to Hong Kong in the 1980s, says he made his first fortune in the local stock market, lived for a time in Australia (he holds an MBA from the University of South Australia), then returned to invest in Shanghai and Beijing property.
notes: Also known as Xu Rongmao. Sensitive context: Shimao's 2022 defaults and ongoing debt restructuring; trading suspended into 2023. Chair handover per Webb-site officer records (webbsite.renavon.com) – verify. Very unlikely to do media; IR email is the only published route.

name: Alexander Isaev
current_role: CEO of Elga coal managing company (Elgaugol / UK Elga) and minority co-owner (~20%) of the Elga coal project via Energogroup
profile: Russian coal executive, formerly co-owner and CEO of VostokCoal, who in 2020 became CEO of Elgaugol, the operator of the Elga coking-coal deposit in Yakutia (Russia's largest, ~2.2bn t reserves) bought by Albert Avdolyan's A-Property. He holds roughly a 20% stake alongside Avdolyan; the pair also bought and later sold Sibanthracite. Forbes added him to its billionaire list as a newcomer in 2025.
interesting_fact: Elga sits in remote, frozen southern Yakutia; its owners set out to lift output from ~4m tonnes in 2019 to tens of millions of tonnes, mostly exported to China, building a private railway to reach the Pacific coast.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2022 Isaev's Energogroup and Avdolyan's AP Holding registered a new company, A-Steel, to produce pig iron, steel and ferroalloys (Avdolyan 75%, Isaev 25%) - a first sign of interest in moving downstream from coal.
notes: Very low public profile; no official site, press contact or social accounts found for him or Elgaugol. Russian coal sector — check Western sanctions status of Elga/A-Property entities before any outreach. Common name: confirm identity via Elga link.

name: Brad Keywell
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Gigawatt AI (AI-native operating system for utilities, founded Aug 2025); Director, TKO Group Holdings
profile: Detroit-born serial founder who co-founded Groupon, Echo Global Logistics and Mediaocean with Eric Lefkofsky, plus VC firm Lightbank. His fortune rests largely on being a founding investor in Tempus AI. He founded industrial-AI firm Uptake (2014; sold to Bosch in 2026) and now runs Gigawatt AI, building AI software for energy and water utilities.
interesting_fact: Named overall 2019 EY World Entrepreneur of the Year (chosen from 44 country winners); he also founded Chicago Ideas and the immersive WNDR Museum, and signed the Giving Pledge in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first business at age 7, a greeting-card company called Key Creations. As a University of Michigan freshman he met Sam Zell and spent summers interning at Zell's Equity Group Investments; Zell mentored him for 35 years. He is also an adjunct professor of entrepreneurship at Chicago Booth.
notes: Strong podcast fit: Gigawatt AI targets utilities (energy/grid). Personal site has a press kit (bradkeywell.com/files/Brad-Keywell-Bio-2026.pdf). Gigawatt's published media route is marketing@gigawatt.ai. Avoid divorce topic.

name: Zhou Xiaoping
current_role: Chairwoman and CEO, Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems (SSE:601799)
profile: Founded Xingyu in 1993 with her late father Zhou Bajin, growing it into China's leading private auto-lamp maker supplying VW, Mercedes-Benz, BMW and GM; it listed in Shanghai in 2011. 2025 revenue was about 15.3bn yuan; the company filed for a Hong Kong 'A+H' listing in 2026 and set up a robotics JV with Jaka in 2025.
interesting_fact: Xingyu was the first private Chinese auto-lighting company to list on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (2011).
deep_cut_fact: She trained as a doctor (Norman Bethune University of Medical Sciences, 1990) and was vice principal of Wujin Health School in Changzhou before leaving at 32 to start an auto-lamp factory on about 112,000 yuan of borrowed money.
notes: IR contact (board secretary Gao Peng) is listed in Xingyu's SSE filings; no email captured here. Chinese-language outreach via company IR advisable.

name: Hope Welker
current_role: Beneficiary of the Hope Margaret Hancock Trust (stake in Hancock Prospecting); no executive role found
profile: Third child of Gina Rinehart. With her siblings she is a beneficiary of a family trust that holds a large stake in Hancock Prospecting, the Pilbara iron-ore group. She has no public operating role in the business and keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: She went to boarding school at Switzerland's Institut Le Rosey.
notes: Very private passive heiress with no operating role in mining, energy or data centres, so a poor fit for the podcast. Most of her press coverage concerns the family trust dispute; avoid it. A search found nothing recent. If approached at all, go through Hancock Prospecting media relations, though they represent the company rather than her.

name: Stephane Bonvin
current_role: Founder, CEO and director, Investis Holding SA (SIX: IREN), Zurich
profile: Stéphane Bonvin founded Investis in 1994 and built it into a Swiss residential landlord with 3,000+ apartments around Lake Geneva. He listed it on SIX in 2016 and still holds a large majority stake. He co-founded private equity firm Patrimonium in 2006/07, ran it until 2015 and sold his stake in 2022. Investis has since sold its real estate services segment to focus on owning property.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Patrimonium in 2006, ran it until 2015 and sold his stake in 2022 to focus on Investis. In a 2026 interview he set a target of CHF 100m in rental income.

public_contacts.value: laurence.bienz@investisgroup.com (Laurence Bienz, Head Investor & Media Relations, +41 58 201 72 42)

notes: Low public profile, with few interviews and no personal social accounts found. Best route is Investis media/IR. Investis is residential real estate only, so energy/data-centre relevance is limited.

name: Mehmet Sinan Tara (Tara family)
current_role: Head of the Tara family / ENKA group (Tara Holding largest ENKA shareholder); passed ENKA İnşaat board chair to son Agah Mehmet Tara in 2022
profile: Mehmet Sinan Tara is the son of ENKA co-founder Şarık Tara and the largest shareholder of ENKA İnşaat, the Istanbul-listed engineering, construction, power-generation and real-estate group (580 projects in 58 countries). He ran ENKA for decades before handing the listed company's chairmanship to his son Agah in 2022; ENKA now also operates data centers near Istanbul.
interesting_fact: ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. embassy and consular buildings over roughly the past 20 years, with projects from Algeria and Nepal to the Netherlands.
deep_cut_fact: The name ENKA comes from the first syllables of the Turkish words 'enişte' and 'kayınbirader' (brother-in-law), reflecting its 1957 founding by Şarık Tara and his brother-in-law Sadi Gülçelik.
notes: enka@enka.com is ENKA's general corporate address. Sources differ on whether Sinan took over in 1984 (Forbes US) or 1994 (Forbes Türkiye). Podcast angle: ENKA is Turkey's leading private power producer and runs EDS data centers (IST 01 Tuzla, IST 02 Gebze); son Agah Mehmet Tara is the operational leader and likelier guest.

name: Deng Weiming
current_role: Chairman and President, CNGR Advanced Material Co. (中伟股份; Shenzhen 300919 / HKEX-listed)
profile: Born 1968 in Shaoyang, Hunan, Deng founded the Zhongwei group in 1995 around coal chemicals and trading, pivoted to new energy by buying a lithium-battery precursor maker in 2013, and spun out CNGR in 2014 in Tongren, Guizhou. CNGR makes nickel/cobalt precursor materials for cathodes supplied to Tesla, LG Chem and CATL; it listed in Shenzhen in 2020 and Hong Kong in 2025.
interesting_fact: After its 2020 Shenzhen ChiNext listing, CNGR at one point became the second-most valuable listed company in Guizhou province, behind only Kweichow Moutai.
deep_cut_fact: Deng studied organic chemistry at Taiyuan University of Science and Technology and began his career as a technician at a state-owned coking plant in Shaodong, Hunan, before quitting to try property trading in Hainan during the early-1990s boom.
notes: Chinese-language outreach recommended. He and his wife Wu Xiaoge jointly control ~56% of CNGR. Early-career details come from a Chinese media summary (Touzijie, reposted on Bilibili) of the HK IPO prospectus.

name: Said Gutseriev
current_role: Russian-British investor; founder of Larnabel Ventures; shareholder in SFI holding (Europlan leasing, VSK insurance) - reportedly exited M.Video board in 2025
profile: Said Gutseriev (b. 1988, Moscow) is the son of oligarch Mikhail Gutseriev and was educated in the UK from age 8. After an analyst stint at Glencore he took board roles in family oil, refining and coal businesses from 2014, then built holdings in retailer M.Video and investment group SFI. Reports say he left M.Video's board in 2025 after signalling plans to sell.
interesting_fact: He holds an Oxford master's degree in geology and an MA in oil & gas management from the University of Plymouth.
deep_cut_fact: He started out (2012-2014) as an analyst in Glencore's London structured-financing department for oil projects, later moving to the trader's finance office.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK (28 June 2022) and EU over his SFI directorship - check legal/sanctions implications before any outreach or featuring. No published personal contact or official social accounts found. M.Video ownership in flux in 2025 (interfax.ru/business/860507).

name: Massimo Moratti
current_role: Private investor; former chairman/CEO of Saras (Italian oil refiner) and former owner/president of Inter Milan
profile: Son of Angelo Moratti, who founded Sardinian refiner Saras in 1962, Massimo ran the company with brother Gian Marco and took it public in 2006. In 2024 the Moratti family sold about 35% of Saras to trader Vitol at EUR 1.75/share, triggering a takeover and delisting. He is best known for owning Inter Milan for ~two decades, selling his last shares in 2016.
interesting_fact: His Inter Milan tenure included five straight Serie A titles and the 2010 treble (Serie A, Coppa Italia and Champions League), plus that year's Club World Cup.
deep_cut_fact: As Inter president he conceived Inter Campus, the club's social project that since 1997 has used youth football to help children in need, starting in Recife, Brazil; it now reaches thousands of kids worldwide.
notes: Forbes bio is outdated: family sold its Saras control to Vitol (closed June 2024; Vitol press release https://www.vitol.com/members-of-the-moratti-family-enter-into-an-agreement-to-sell-approx-35-of-saras-to-vitol/). No personal channels; reachable mainly via Italian press/football world. Brother Gian Marco died 2018.

name: Grigory Berezkin
current_role: Owner and Chairman of the Board, ESN Group and RBC Group (Russian media holding)
profile: Moscow-born chemist-turned-investor Berezkin made his fortune in Russian oil and power: he arranged the sale of KomiTEK to Lukoil (~$600m+) and built Rusenergosbyt, an electricity trader supplying Gazprom, Russian Railways and Transneft, selling ~half to Enel in 2006. He later moved into media (Komsomolskaya Pravda, Metro Moscow) and has controlled RBC since 2017.
interesting_fact: In 2000-2003 his group ran Kolenergo, a power system operating largely above the Arctic Circle, building cross-border links to Finland and Norway that let it export electricity and trade on the Nord Pool exchange.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in chemical sciences (1993) from Moscow State University, where he was a junior research fellow until 1994. He backs the International Chemistry Olympiad and in 2022 created the Viktor Berezkin Prize for young chromatography researchers, named for his chemist father.
notes: No published personal/office contact found; ESN Group site appears defunct. Route, if any, would be via RBC Group corporate office. He was on EU sanctions list Apr 2022-Sep 2023 (delisted); journalist should check current US/UK sanctions status before any engagement.

name: Arthur Mensch
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Mistral AI (Paris)
profile: Polytechnique graduate with an ML PhD (Paris-Saclay), ex-DeepMind Paris (early Gemini work), who co-founded Mistral AI in 2023. Mistral builds open-weight LLMs and raised $2bn at a $14bn valuation in Sept 2025; it is now building its own compute, including a debt-financed site near Paris and a 1 GW target by 2030.
interesting_fact: Mistral is turning into an infrastructure player: it borrowed $830m to build a 44 MW Nvidia GB300 data centre at Bruyeres-le-Chatel near Paris, targets 200 MW by end-2027 and 1 GW by 2030; Mensch has put the cost of a gigawatt of compute at about $50bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before LLMs he was a neuroimaging researcher: his PhD (Inria Parietal team, supervised by Bertrand Thirion) was 'Apprentissage de representations en imagerie fonctionnelle' - learning representations of human cognition from fMRI brain scans, including fast dictionary learning for massive matrix factorisation.
notes: Highly relevant for a data-centre/energy podcast (Mistral Compute, French nuclear power as AI advantage). press@mistral.ai is the official press/events route. X handle @arthurmensch is widely attributed to him but the profile page itself was not fetched directly.

name: Guillaume Lample
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Mistral AI (Paris)
profile: French AI researcher (École Polytechnique, CMU master's) who spent years at Meta's FAIR, co-authoring the original LLaMA paper. In April 2023 he co-founded Mistral AI with Arthur Mensch and Timothée Lacroix; it builds open-weight LLMs and raised ~$2B at a ~$14B valuation in Sept 2025. He leads its science work.
interesting_fact: Mistral's $113M raise in 2023, weeks after founding, was then Europe's largest-ever seed round.
deep_cut_fact: As a CMU student he co-built 'Arnold' with Devendra Chaplot, a deep-RL agent that played Doom from raw pixels; at the 2016 Visual Doom AI Competition it placed second in both tracks but had the fewest deaths and best kill-to-death ratio by a wide margin.
notes: Active on X and does tech podcasts (e.g. Latent Space-style episodes on Voxtral in 2026), so a good podcast candidate for AI/compute. Mistral is also building its own data-center capacity in France, a natural hook. Route via press@mistral.ai or X.

name: Timothy Dunn
current_role: CEO, CrownQuest Operating (Midland, Texas)
profile: Texas Tech chemical engineer (b. 1955) who worked at Exxon Production Research, ran oil-and-gas lending at First City National Bank and was CFO of Parker & Parsley before founding CrownQuest in 1996. Early Permian Basin leases made CrownRock, his venture with Lime Rock, a major producer; Occidental agreed to buy CrownRock for about $12B in Dec 2023. He is also one of Texas's largest conservative political donors.
interesting_fact: Some of Dunn's fortune came from acquiring cheap Permian Basin leases years before fracking made the oil there economical to extract; CrownQuest was Texas's eighth-largest oil producer in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He played lead guitar in a rock band from high school through Texas Tech, says making Eagle Scout is the early achievement he is proudest of, and scrapped plans for law school to take a job at Exxon Production Research, which sent him to the Middle East three times.
notes: Politically prominent and frequently profiled critically by Texas media; keep outreach on energy/entrepreneurship. His own site directs people to his Yellow Balloons Bible-teaching podcast; the contact form is for that ministry. CrownQuest's website lists no contact email.

name: Timothée Lacroix
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Mistral AI (Paris)
profile: French AI researcher who spent years at Meta's FAIR lab in Paris (co-author of the original LLaMA paper) before co-founding Mistral AI in 2023 with Arthur Mensch and Guillaume Lample. As CTO he leads Mistral's technical work on open-weight models (Mistral 7B, Mixtral, Magistral, Voxtral) and its European compute build-out; Bloomberg reported the trio became France's first AI billionaires in 2025.
interesting_fact: He is a co-author of Meta's 2023 'LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models' paper, published months before he co-founded Mistral.
deep_cut_fact: Long before LLMs, he co-authored TorchCraft (2016), a library connecting the game StarCraft to machine-learning research, and later PyTorch-BigGraph (2019) and HyperTree Proof Search for neural theorem proving (2022); his ICML 2018 work was on tensor decomposition for knowledge-base completion.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Arthur Mensch; technical framing (inference efficiency, compute/data centers like Mistral Compute) likely to resonate. Route via Mistral press.

name: Christopher Cline
current_role: Deceased (died 4 July 2019); was founder of Foresight Energy / Cline Group coal operations
profile: Chris Cline was a West Virginia-born coal entrepreneur who built Illinois Basin coal producer Foresight Energy. He died on 4 July 2019 in a helicopter crash in the Bahamas; per instructions the rest of the profile is skipped.
notes: Died 4 July 2019 (Miami Herald; Wikipedia 'Chris Cline'). Not a viable podcast guest.

name: Sit Kwong Lam
current_role: Reportedly chairman of Shenzhen Brightoil Group and founder of Marine Online (Singapore); former chairman of HK-listed Brightoil Petroleum (left 2019) - current status unverified
profile: Hong Kong oil entrepreneur who founded Brightoil in 1993 and built Brightoil Petroleum into a HK-listed marine-fuel bunkering, oil-tanker and upstream oil & gas group, serving as chairman (and CEO 2008-2014). He left the board in 2019 and returned briefly as strategic adviser; Brightoil later spun up Marine Online, a maritime e-commerce platform.
interesting_fact: Brightoil was among the largest marine-fuel suppliers in Asian ports and launched Marine Online, an early one-stop e-commerce platform for shipowners and charterers to buy bunkers and services.
notes: Low priority: his billionaire status (Forbes 2011-2017, Hurun to 2018) ended after Brightoil's 2019 restructuring and a personal bankruptcy order; avoid referencing that. No published personal/office contacts found and no 2025-26 news located; alive status not confirmed.

name: David Chow
current_role: Macau businessman; co-founder and former co-chairman of Macau Legend Development (developer of Macau Fisherman's Wharf); no longer on its board
profile: Hong Kong-born (1950) Macau entrepreneur and former legislator (13 years, until 2009) who developed Macau Fisherman's Wharf, the themed waterfront complex opened 2005-06, and co-founded Macau Legend Development in 2006, which ran the Babylon and Pharaoh's Palace casinos under SJM's licence. He has since exited the board and cut his stake to a fraction of a percent.
interesting_fact: Fisherman's Wharf was built partly on reclaimed land (about 40% of its area) and once housed Macau's first roller coaster, inside an artificial volcano topped by a Potala Palace replica.
deep_cut_fact: Besides his gaming and tourism businesses, he has served as Honorary Consul of the Republic of Cape Verde to the Macau SAR.
notes: Full name Chow Kam Fai, David (周錦輝). Fortune largely eroded: GGRAsia reported in April 2025 he held only ~0.39% of Macau Legend after a debt settlement. Forbes listing is from 2014 only. No personal published contact found; outreach would have to go via Macau business channels.

name: Alexander Shchukin
profile: Kuzbass coal magnate and co-founder of the Sibuglemet coal holding (Kemerovo region, Russia); former Forbes-list billionaire. Died in Novokuznetsk in July 2021, aged 70.
notes: Deceased: Kommersant (20 Jul 2021) reports Sibuglemet co-founder Alexander Shchukin, a former Forbes-list member and coal magnate, died in Novokuznetsk aged 70 (https://kommersant.ru/doc/4909362). Identity match is by coal/Russia/Forbes-list profile; rest skipped per instructions.

name: Vladimir Melnichenko
current_role: Former co-owner of Sibuglemet (Kuzbass coking-coal holding, incl. OAO Mezhdurechye); no current public role found
profile: Russian coal businessman from Kemerovo (Kuzbass), one of the co-owners of coking-coal producer Sibuglemet with Anatoly Skurov, Valentin Bukhtoyarov and Alexander Shchukin. Kommersant calls him an ex-owner of Sibuglemet and of its Mezhdurechye mine. His only Forbes listing is 2011 (coal, about $1.8bn); his stake was reportedly sold around 2013-14.
interesting_fact: Sibuglemet, one of Russia's larger coking-coal suppliers from the Kuzbass basin, was held by four roughly equal partners; Kommersant photographed and named him as an ex-owner in 2014.
notes: Not Andrey Melnichenko (SUEK/EuroChem). Kommersant confirms a Vladimir Melnichenko as ex-Sibuglemet/Mezhdurechye owner, but no source ties that person to Forbes' 2011 entry, so identity stays 'uncertain'. Forbes.ru's 2011 list is JS-rendered and English/Russian searches found nothing more. He was named in a 2014 Kemerovo criminal case (avoid). No published contacts; not a realistic guest.

name: Valentin Bukhtoyarov
current_role: Former co-founder, shareholder and VP for finance/economics of Sibuglemet coal holding (Kuzbass); no current public role found
profile: Valentin Petrovich Bukhtoyarov (b. 1955, Kemerovo region) is a Kuzbass coal-mining engineer who in 1995 co-founded Sibuglemet, a coking-coal producer, with Anatoly Skurov, Anatoly Smolyaninov and Vladimir Melnichenko, later serving as its VP for finance. Forbes Russia ranked him #52 in 2011 at $1.8B; the founders sold the holding to Akhmet Palankoev in 2013 after a shareholder dispute.
interesting_fact: Ranked 52nd among Russia's 200 richest businessmen by Forbes in 2011 with an estimated $1.8B, from coking coal used in steelmaking.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from the Siberian Metallurgical Institute in 1978 he was assigned to the Kalinin mine of Prokopyevskugol and rose to become director of the Yesaulskaya mine before moving to Kuznetskugol as supply director in 1994.
notes: Very private; only on Forbes list in 2011. Sibuglemet was sold in 2013 and its successor is under US/Canadian sanctions (2022) - outreach to Russian coal interests may carry sanctions/compliance considerations. No death reported; alive status not confirmed. No published contacts found (sibuglemet.ru unreachable).

name: Mario Brescia Cafferata
current_role: Deceased (died 16 May 2013, Lima); was co-chairman of Grupo Breca and chairman of BBVA Continental
notes: Died May 2013. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Brescia_Cafferata ; https://www.mch.cl/fallece-empresario-peruano-mario-brescia-presidente-del-holding-breca-dueno-de-cemento-melon-y-pinturas-tricolor/ . Grupo Breca is now run by the next generation of the Brescia family.

name: Qin Hui
current_role: Former controlling shareholder of Stellar Megamedia / SMI Holdings Group (星美控股), a Chinese cinema chain; no confirmed current role
profile: Qin Hui (覃辉), a Chongqing-born businessman, built the Stellar (星美) cinema and media group, one of China's larger theatre circuits in the 2010s, listed in Hong Kong as SMI Holdings. His brother Qin Hong ran day-to-day operations. Forbes listed him at #1339 on its 2018 billionaires list (Media & Entertainment). The group fell into a debt and cash-flow crisis from late 2018.
interesting_fact: Stellar was among the earliest private cinema chains to expand nationwide after China's film-distribution reforms. In 2010 SMI agreed to buy 25 cinemas directly from Qin Hui for HK$55m.
notes: The Forbes profile (forbes.com/profile/qin-hui) links him to SMI Holdings Group; he is NOT the historian Qin Hui (秦晖).
