She built stakes in Angolan banking and telecoms (Unitel, BFA) and Portuguese companies such as NOS, and was once called Africa's richest woman. Since 2020 Angola and other states have pursued fraud and money-laundering cases and asset freezes against her, all of which she denies; Forbes dropped her from its billionaire list in 2021.
interesting_fact: Her father appointed her to head Sonangol, Angola's state oil company, in June 2016; the next president removed her in November 2017. She is nicknamed 'the princess' in Angola.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as an electrical engineer at King's College London before going into business.
notes: HIGH REPUTATIONAL RISK: she faces an Interpol notice, a UK worldwide asset freeze (appeal rejected 2024), a Dutch court finding over Sonangol funds and ongoing Angolan charges (some dropped in November 2025). She denies wrongdoing. Recommend not approaching her for an entrepreneurship podcast. Reported Instagram handles are inconsistent, so none are listed. No longer a billionaire per Forbes.

name: Carson Brice
current_role: Major (10%+) shareholder, First Citizens BancShares (FCNCA); private individual, Raleigh, NC
profile: Carson Holding Brice is the youngest of the four sisters of Frank Holding Jr., chairman and CEO of Raleigh-based First Citizens Bank. With her siblings she owns about 20% of the bank and close to half the voting power, a stake from a family that has led the bank since 1935. SEC Form 4 filings show she is a passive holder who mostly makes gifts and trust transfers.
interesting_fact: The Holding family controls First Citizens, which acquired Silicon Valley Bank in 2023 and has since grown into a national bank on the Fortune 500.
notes: Very private and has almost no public profile beyond SEC filings. A UNC page says she is a UNC and UNC business school graduate (https://ie.unc.edu/people/f-bryan-brice-jr). The bank media address reaches the company, not her.

name: Yang Jian
current_role: Co-founder, director and deputy general manager, Semight Instruments (苏州联讯仪器, 688808.SH); one of its three actual controllers
profile: Yang Jian (杨建, b. 1980, Jinan) co-controls Suzhou-based Semight Instruments with Hu Haiyang and Huang Jianjun. Semight makes high-speed optical-communication and semiconductor test equipment; its customers include Innolight, Eoptolink and Lumentum, so it is tied to the AI data-center optics boom. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2026, opened up more than 800% and later traded above RMB 2,000 a share.
interesting_fact: Semight's STAR Market debut in April 2026 rose about 876% and briefly valued the company at RMB 82bn; by mid-2026 its shares topped RMB 2,000, making it the A-share 'stock king', and the three controllers' stakes were worth about RMB 55bn.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a 2006 communications-engineering master's from Huazhong University of Science & Technology, worked in technical support at Qingdao Lucent, then was a sales manager at Agilent/Keysight (2011-17), the test-instrument giant Semight now competes with, before joining Semight at its founding in March 2017.
notes: Input record looks merged: Forbes' 'yang-jian' profile (2020-22, real estate, Wenzhou) is a different person, likely Zhongliang Holdings' Yang Jian (杨剑). The 杨建 / optical-semiconductor-test identity matches Hurun 2026 (联讯仪器 Semight; Jinan-born; HUST master's). Strong fit for a data-center optics angle. Route via Semight IR.

name: Gretel Packer
current_role: Chair, Packer Family Foundation; private investor; arts philanthropist (Art Gallery of NSW, Sydney Theatre Company Foundation)
profile: Daughter of media mogul Kerry Packer and elder sister of James Packer, she became a billionaire after the family fortune was divided in 2015, giving her investments including a Crown Resorts stake. Famously low-profile, she drove the creation of the A$160m National Philanthropic Fund (2014) and chairs the Packer Family Foundation, focusing on arts, education and environmental science.
interesting_fact: She was one of five women donors credited with championing the Art Gallery of NSW's Sydney Modern expansion, and served as vice-president of the gallery's board of trustees.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2020 she and the Packer Family Foundation pledged A$240,000 to a philanthropist-backed rescue of Sydney's Carriageworks arts centre when it went into administration during COVID.
notes: Very private; no published personal, office or foundation contact found. Avoid family-settlement topics. Only plausible route is via arts institutions she serves (AGNSW, Sydney Theatre Company Foundation). Appointed AM (2020) per Wikipedia. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so contacts not exhaustively checked.

name: Liang Changlin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Dingdong Maicai (Dingdong Fresh); stepped down as CEO in 2026 after Meituan agreed to acquire the company
profile: Army veteran (12 years' service) turned serial entrepreneur in Shanghai's Zhangjiang: built video software, then mother-and-baby community Yaya.com (sold to TAL in 2016), then founded fresh-grocery e-commerce platform Dingdong Maicai in 2017, listing it on the NYSE in 2021. In 2026 Meituan agreed to buy Dingdong for about US$717m; Liang handed the CEO role to CFO Wang Song and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Named on China's 2020 national honour roll of veteran entrepreneurs ('全国退役军人创业光荣榜') for job creation.
deep_cut_fact: His first pot of gold came from a piece of software: shortly after leaving the army in 2002 he wrote 'Easy Video Joiner & Splitter', billed as the first video cut-and-join tool, and sold about 50,000 copies worldwide for roughly US$800,000.
notes: Meituan deal and CEO change per Jiemian (https://www.jiemian.com/article/14091669.html); IR mailbox may change once Dingdong is absorbed into Meituan. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Brandt Louie
current_role: Chairman and CEO, H.Y. Louie Co. Ltd. and London Drugs Ltd. (Vancouver)
profile: Fourth-generation head of the Louie family business, founded when his grandfather H.Y. Louie opened a Chinatown store in 1903. Brandt worked as a chartered accountant before joining in 1972 and has led the business since 1998. The Vancouver-based group runs the London Drugs chain and IGA grocery operations and is one of BC's largest private companies. He was SFU's chancellor for six years and was named to the Order of Canada in 2024.
interesting_fact: H.Y. Louie's first store, originally called the Kwong Chong Company, sold seed, fertilizer and wholesale groceries. The family has been in the Vancouver area since the 19th century.
deep_cut_fact: He is a keen fisherman who supports ocean conservation and works with First Nations on preserving fish stocks. In 2023 he spoke in the Senate Chamber in Ottawa about families affected by the 1923 Chinese Exclusion Act, and he was a major catalyst for a national strategy on anti-Asian racism.
notes: Honours include the Order of Canada (2024), the Order of BC and the BC Business Laureates. Former RBC board member. He is approachable through community and civic channels in Vancouver. Older London Drugs press releases list Hartley PR as the media agency, but those contacts date from 2013-15 and may be stale.

name: Harvey Jones
current_role: Managing Partner, Square Wave Ventures; NVIDIA director since 1993 (Nvidia's board page lists him as Chair of the Board, plus audit and nominating/governance committees)
profile: EDA pioneer: co-founded Daisy Systems in 1981 (president/CEO to 1987), then led Synopsys 1987-1998 as CEO and executive chairman, and co-founded processor-IP firm Tensilica in 1997 (chairman until Cadence bought it in 2013). An Nvidia director since its 1993 founding, he became a billionaire from his Nvidia stake and invests via Square Wave Ventures.
interesting_fact: He has sat on Nvidia's board since the company was founded in 1993, and is a billionaire almost entirely from director compensation and stock, owning about 0.03% of Nvidia.
deep_cut_fact: In high school he discovered a teletype link to a timesharing system, taught himself BASIC, and 'sold my chemistry homework to my classmates' - his first entrepreneurial exercise. He then nearly took an IBM job on Allegheny Airlines' reservations system before joining CAD firm Calma.
notes: Georgetown math/CS and MIT Sloan MS. Gave a 2009 Computer History Museum oral history (good prep material). No personal social accounts or published Square Wave contact found; Nvidia corporate PR is the formal route. Chair title taken from nvidia.com board page (not independently re-verified).

name: Fu Guangming
current_role: Chairman, Fujian Sunner Development Co. (SZSE: 002299), Guangze, Fujian
profile: Fu Guangming founded what became Sunner Group, China's largest white-feather broiler producer and a major chicken supplier to KFC and McDonald's in China. He started with a small hatchery in Guangze county, Fujian, in 1983. He still chairs listed Fujian Sunner Development, which now produces over 600 million broilers a year, and he shares the fortune with his wife and his daughter Fu Fenfang, a company director.
interesting_fact: Sunner grew from a single flock and about 10 staff into a vertically integrated poultry group that produces over 600 million white-feather broilers a year.
deep_cut_fact: In 1983, aged 30, he quit a secure job at the Guangze County People's Armed Forces Department and borrowed RMB 20,000 to open a chicken farm. He told Yicai the idea came from his childhood: with so many siblings, the family's chickens were saved for his mother after childbirth.

public_contacts.value: snljj@sunnercn.com (Board Secretary Liao Junjie, Fujian Sunner Development)

notes: Rarely talks to Western media, so expect to work in Chinese. Best route is the board secretary's office (IR). Daughter Fu Fenfang is involved in management. Podcast angle is limited apart from the entrepreneurship story.

name: Femi Otedola
current_role: Chairman and largest shareholder (~27.7% as of Aug 2026), First HoldCo Plc (parent of First Bank of Nigeria)
profile: Lagos businessman who built Zenon Petroleum into a dominant diesel supplier, later controlled Forte Oil and then Geregu Power, whose majority stake he sold in 2025 for about $750M. He has since redeployed capital into First HoldCo, steadily raising his stake toward a stated goal of over 51%, and published the memoir 'Making It Big' in 2025.
interesting_fact: At one point he was Nigeria's largest private ship owner; one of his vessels, a flat-bottomed 16,000-tonne bunker ship, was reported as the first of its kind in Africa.
deep_cut_fact: In his memoir he recalls that while he was in A-levels his father set up Impact Press, a printing company in Surulere, Lagos; he became fascinated with the machines, skipped Upper Sixth to join the business, and became its MD at about 25 before founding Centre Force in 1994.
notes: Best route: the official memoir site's contact form, which has 'Media Inquiry' and 'Speaking Engagement' options. Active on social media; news reports cite X @realFemiOtedola, but I did not verify it from an official page, and reports give conflicting Instagram handles. First HoldCo site was unreachable from here. His memoir 'Making It Big' (Aug 2025) is a natural outreach hook.

name: Wang Zhenhua
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Seazen Group (formerly Future Land Development, HK:1030) / Seazen Holdings (SH:601155); no current formal executive post found
profile: Wang Zhenhua founded the Shanghai-headquartered property developer now called Seazen Group (formerly Future Land Development, HK-listed) after entering property development in 1993, building it into one of China's large developers. He resigned his posts after his 2018 detention; the group is now chaired by Wang Xiaosong, and 2025 filings still describe Wang as controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: He earned an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business in July 2005.
notes: CAUTION: Wang was detained in 2018 and sentenced in June 2020 to 5 years in prison over the molestation of a 9-year-old girl (reported by Caixin). Not recommended as a podcast guest. Forbes bio (still calling him chairman) is outdated. Release date and current status not confirmed. Conviction source: https://www.caixinglobal.com/company-info/seazen-7712.html

name: Filippo Ghirelli
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Infracorp (infrastructure, energy, AI and space investment group); founder of family office Sophrance Global
profile: Monaco-based Italian engineer-entrepreneur (mid-40s). Built real estate businesses in Italy/North Africa, founded energy-efficiency firm Genera Group in 2009 (sold to SUSI Partners in 2024), and in 2023 bought a 25% stake in India's Nayara Energy refinery from Trafigura for $169M - the deal behind most of his ~$1.5B fortune. Infracorp (2024) targets airports, energy, data centres, AI and orbital modules.
interesting_fact: He bought Trafigura's 25% stake in Nayara Energy (India's second-largest refinery) for $169M, a 42% discount to Trafigura's 2017 price; Forbes estimates it is now worth at least $1.1B. Infracorp's plans include data centres in outer space.
deep_cut_fact: Right after graduating from college in Rome he left for Africa, starting his career as an engineer on infrastructure projects in Guinea and Mali.
notes: Strong fit for energy + data-center podcast (Infracorp plans ~600M in airports, data centres and space; AI lab 'Manthica'). Speaks publicly (Forbes interviews, SuperReturn Private Wealth speaker, appears on a Buzzsprout podcast). Nayara is EU-sanctioned due to Rosneft co-ownership - sensitive. Confirm sophrance.com is his Sophrance Global before using.

name: Steven Meisel
current_role: Managing member of Pencross Energy, LLC (Dallas), an early investor in Fermi America (Fermi Inc., Nasdaq: FRMI)
profile: Steven Meisel is a Dallas investor whose fortune comes from Fermi America, the Amarillo, Texas REIT co-founded by Rick Perry and Toby Neugebauer to build 'Project Matador', a gigawatt-scale private power and AI data-center campus. Through Pencross Energy he held 56.25m Fermi shares (9.41%) at the October 2025 IPO, making him a billionaire on Forbes' real-time list. He had sold down to about 4.5% by March 2026.
interesting_fact: Fermi's October 2025 Nasdaq debut ($682.5m raised at $21/share, up about 54% on day one) instantly minted several billionaires; Meisel's Pencross Energy was then a 9.41% holder of a company with no revenue yet, planning nuclear, gas and solar power for AI data centers.
notes: Not the fashion photographer Steven Meisel. Identity from SEC 13G filings (Pencross Energy LLC / Steven Meisel, Fermi Inc.) and Fermi's 2026 proxy contest filings, which describe him as a close associate of Griffin Perry. He is caught up in the 2026 Neugebauer-board fight and related petitions (avoid). Some outlets link him to 'FG1 Capital'; unverified. No published contacts.

name: Wang Kunxiao
current_role: Director (formerly vice chairman and chairman), Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group (002353.SZ)
profile: Wang Kunxiao (王坤晓, b. 1969) is a co-founder of Jereh Group, founded in Yantai in 1999 with Sun Weijie and others; Jereh grew from oilfield equipment trading into fracturing fleets, gas compression, oil and gas engineering, new energy and power. He was vice chairman then chairman of the listed Jereh Oilfield Services and remains a board director.
interesting_fact: Jereh now runs a dedicated 'Data Center & Power' segment and markets PowerVEGA, a power-generation product built for AI data centers ('No waiting, power for AI now'), launched at RE+ 2026.

name: Somphote Ahunai
current_role: Founder and former CEO of Energy Absolute PCL (Thailand); resigned as director/executive effective July 2024
profile: Thai entrepreneur and former stockbroker/financier who founded Energy Absolute in 2006, turning a biodiesel plant into a SET-listed renewable group spanning solar and wind farms, a battery gigafactory (Amita) and electric buses/boats (Mine Mobility), earning it the nickname 'Tesla of Thailand'. He held roughly 30-40% of EA; he stepped down in 2024 and dropped off Forbes' list after 2024.
interesting_fact: Energy Absolute was dubbed the 'Tesla of Southeast Asia' as it expanded from renewables into EVs and a lithium-ion battery gigafactory in Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: He had planned to retire at 36 as a millionaire stockbroker, but was drawn into an unprofitable biodiesel factory his family had invested in; with an electrical-engineering background, he taught himself mechanical and chemical engineering from books and rebuilt the plant from scratch - the seed of EA. In 2020 he still wore a Uniqlo suit and rode the MRT.
notes: Sensitive: he and a deputy resigned from EA in July 2024 after Thailand's SEC filed a criminal complaint alleging fraud (see https://www.caproasia.com/?p=44424); approach with care and do not route via EA. MBA from Univ. of Pittsburgh (Katz), undergrad Chulalongkorn. No personal published contact found.

name: Neha Narkhede
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Oscilar (AI risk decisioning / fraud prevention); co-founder and former CTO of Confluent
profile: Pune-born engineer who, at LinkedIn, co-created Apache Kafka, the open-source streaming system now underpinning real-time data pipelines worldwide. In 2014 she co-founded Confluent to commercialize Kafka; it IPO'd in 2021 at ~$9.1B. Since 2021 she has run Oscilar, an AI-native risk and fraud-decisioning platform for fintechs and banks, and angel-invests in startups.
interesting_fact: She co-wrote the O'Reilly book 'Kafka: The Definitive Guide' (2017) with Gwen Shapira and Todd Palino, and Oscilar won a 2025 Banking Tech Award while she made Inc.'s 2025 Female Founders 500.
deep_cut_fact: Her fascination with computing began when her parents bought her a computer at age eight; after a BE from the University of Pune and an MS at Georgia Tech, her first job was at Oracle before she joined LinkedIn's Kafka team.
notes: Active public speaker (Money20/20, Fintech Meetup, Slush) and on X/LinkedIn - good podcast prospect for a data-infrastructure angle. Another Oscilar release routed media to an outside rep (Tim Granholm, Shallot). Input net worth is from 2022 Hurun; she dropped off Forbes' real-time list.

name: Sait-Salam Gutseriev
current_role: Russian businessman; co-owner of Gutseriev-family oil assets (took control of Neftisa and his brother Mikhail's RussNeft stake after 2021 EU sanctions on Mikhail); long-time head of PFC BIN
profile: Younger brother of Safmar founder Mikhail Gutseriev, born 1959 in Akmolinsk (now Astana). An oil engineer from Grozny, he ran the BIN industrial-financial company from 1993, sat on BIN bank and RussNeft boards, and served two terms in the State Duma (1999-2007). He became a key holder of the family's oil assets after Mikhail was sanctioned.
interesting_fact: He was a two-term State Duma deputy (1999-2007) and holds both a doctorate in economics (2003) and a candidate degree in law (2000).
deep_cut_fact: He started at the bottom of the oil-products business: in 1978 he was an operator at the Grozny oil distribution depot, becoming its workshop chief in 1983, after graduating from the Grozny Oil Institute in chemical-production machinery.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK in June 2022 - check sanctions rules before any outreach. Only on Forbes lists 2016-2017; no English Wikipedia page, very low public profile, no published personal or office contacts found. Web search budget ran out during this profile, so current holdings were not re-verified beyond Wikipedia.

name: Su Weizhong
current_role: Former co-founder and senior shareholder of CEFC China Energy (中国华信能源); former actual controller of Huaxin International (002018.SZ); no current public role found
profile: Su Weizhong (苏卫忠, b. Sept 1968) co-founded, with Ye Jianming, the Fujian trading business that grew into CEFC China Energy, a Shanghai oil-trading conglomerate that briefly ranked among China's biggest private firms (Hurun: 华信石油, oil & chemicals; Forbes 2016-18). He ran Shandong Huaxin and was actual controller of listed Huaxin International. CEFC collapsed in 2018.
interesting_fact: In 2015 Hurun ranked him No. 65 in China with RMB 26bn, at the height of CEFC's global oil-trading and acquisition spree.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000 he co-founded Fujian Huaxin Import & Export with Ye Jianming and Ye Xiangdong; Fujian Huaxin Holdings followed in 2005, the seed of what became CEFC China Energy.
notes: Identity confirmed via Hurun API (苏卫忠, 华信石油, Shanghai, 2015/2017) and Chinese press. CEFC collapsed in 2018 after Ye Jianming's detention; in 2019 Su was put on a court consumption-restriction list as Huaxin International's controller (Sina, Sept 2019). Sensitive; not a realistic podcast guest. No published contacts.

name: James Kim
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Amkor Technology (retired as Executive Chairman 31 Oct 2024); family remains a major AMKR holder
profile: James Joo-Jin Kim, eldest son of ANAM founder Hyang-Soo Kim, studied at Penn and taught at Villanova before founding Amkor Electronics in Philadelphia in 1968 to sell ANAM's chips in the US. Amkor became a top outsourced semiconductor packaging and test (OSAT) firm (IPO 1998) and now does advanced packaging for AI chips, incl. a new Arizona plant.
interesting_fact: Amkor (America + Korea) grew from a Philadelphia sales office for his father's ANAM, whose 1970 metal-can transistor shipments were Korea's first recorded semiconductor export. Kim also chaired retailer Electronics Boutique, sold to GameStop in 2005.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Amkor he taught at Villanova, which later gave him an honorary Doctor of Commercial Science (1990). A Penn alumnus (W'59, G'61, GR'63), he endowed Penn's James Joo-Jin Kim Center for Korean Studies and a Wharton professorship; he won the 1998 Semiconductor Industry Award as a pioneer of merchant packaging.
notes: Born c.1935-36 and retired from operating roles; no personal public channels found. Kim family trusts remain major AMKR holders. ir@amkor.com was reported in Amkor's Jan 2026 Investor Day release (Business Wire); not independently fetched here. Strong AI-chip advanced-packaging angle via Amkor.

name: Johnathan Oringer
current_role: Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman, Shutterstock (NYSE: SSTK) - back as CEO since October 2026
profile: Programmer-photographer Jon Oringer founded Shutterstock in 2003 with his own savings and about 30,000 of his own photos, built it into a global stock-media marketplace and took it public in 2012, becoming known as New York's first tech billionaire. He was executive chairman from 2020; after the planned Getty Images merger was terminated in July 2026, he returned as CEO in October 2026.
interesting_fact: To seed Shutterstock he bought a Canon Rebel and shot about 100,000 photos himself in six months, launching with a culled set of 30,000 images, a 600 sq ft office and a $49/month unlimited-download subscription.
deep_cut_fact: As a Stony Brook student in the 1990s he wrote and sold thousands of copies of one of the web's first pop-up blockers and ran about ten one-person subscription software startups (personal firewalls, cookie blockers, trademark managers); he is also a certified commercial helicopter pilot.
notes: Very current: per the Nov 2026 proxy (DEF 14A) he became CEO and Chairman in October 2026 after the Getty Images merger agreement was terminated on July 7, 2026. Shutterstock's AI data-licensing business (selling training data to AI labs) is a natural podcast angle.

name: Yao Xinquan
current_role: Vice president, DunAn Holding Group (盾安控股, Hangzhou/Zhuji); chairman of Sichuan Yangzi Mining and director of other DunAn-linked firms per corporate registry
profile: Yao Xinquan (姚新泉) is the younger brother and long-time partner of Yao Xinyi, who founded DunAn in Zhuji, Zhejiang in 1987 with RMB 900. DunAn grew from air-conditioner shut-off valves (world No. 1) into central air-conditioning, precision parts, civil explosives/chemicals, property and food. Hurun listed Yao Xinquan separately in 2008-2017 (manufacturing & energy). Gree later took control of the listed DunAn Environment.
interesting_fact: DunAn's core product began in 1992 as shut-off valves made for Hangzhou Dongbao air-conditioner factory; the small Zhuji parts maker grew into the world's largest maker of air-conditioner valves.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2013 he represented DunAn at a Sichuan ceremony where it funded two 'Red Army primary schools' for old revolutionary areas; Sichuan's party committee named him a 'Sichuan Hope Project Caring Ambassador', and he was also named one of China's 'Top 10 Public-Spirited Young Entrepreneurs'.
notes: Identity confirmed: Hurun API (姚新泉, 盾安控股 DunAn, Hangzhou, 2015/2017) plus registry listings (qcc/aiqicha) naming him DunAn Holding VP. Very low profile. Avoid DunAn's 2018 debt crisis and family topics. No published personal contact; DunAn Holding's corporate channels are the only route.

name: Ali Wakrim
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Afriquia Gaz; Vice-president/co-owner, Akwa Group (Casablanca)
profile: Moroccan businessman who co-owns Akwa Group - Morocco's large fuel, LPG and industrial-gas conglomerate (Afriquia fuel brand) - with the family of Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch; their fathers co-founded the business in 1959. He has chaired LPG distributor Afriquia Gaz (listed in Casablanca) since 1992 and also chairs industrial-gas maker Maghreb Oxygene.
interesting_fact: Akwa is a two-family partnership: his father Ahmed Wakrim and Ahmed Akhannouch founded Afriquia SMDC in Casablanca in 1959, and in 1977 the partners started Maghreb Oxygene, producing industrial gases at a factory in Berrechid.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the family business in the late 1980s, at the same time as Aziz Akhannouch, after earning a graduate degree from the Universite de Pau in France.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal channels. Only corporate route is Afriquia Gaz/Akwa financial communication. IR email reported in Afriquia Gaz 2025-2026 communiques (site blocks automated fetch, so not re-verified directly). Politically sensitive: business partner is the Moroccan PM's family.

profile: Lu Pingfang (卢萍芳) is a major shareholder of Shenzhen-listed Minglida Precision, which she was previously listed alongside Tao Cheng as co-controlling. name: Geraldo Werninghaus
profile: Co-founder of WEG (founded 1961 in Jaraguá do Sul, Brazil, with Eggon João da Silva and Werner Ricardo Voigt), where he ran production. Died in a traffic accident on 10 February 1999. The 2014 Hurun entry presumably reflects his family's inherited WEG stake.

name: Govindbhai Laljibhai Dholakia
current_role: Founder and chairman, Shree Ramkrishna Exports (SRK), Surat; Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha (BJP, Gujarat) since April 2024
profile: Born 1949 into a farming family in Dudhala, Amreli district, Gujarat, Dholakia moved to Surat in 1964 to work as a diamond polisher and went on to found Shree Ramkrishna Exports, one of India's largest diamond manufacturers/exporters. Known as 'Kaka', he entered the Rajya Sabha in 2024 and remains a prominent philanthropist.

As a sitting MP, official contact details also appear on sansad.in. Hurun 2022 named SRK 'Most Respected Family Business'.

name: Tom Steyer
current_role: Co-founder, Galvanize Climate Solutions (took leave in 2025 to run for California governor; conceded after June 2026 primary)
profile: Founded hedge fund Farallon Capital in 1986 and grew it to about $20bn before leaving in 2012 to focus on climate and politics. Co-founded climate investor Galvanize with Katie Hall in 2021, ran for president in 2020 and for California governor in 2026, finishing third in the June 2026 top-two primary. Author of 'Cheaper, Faster, Better: How We'll Win the Climate War' (2024).
interesting_fact: In 2008 he and his wife Kat Taylor gave $41 million to create the TomKat Center for Sustainable Energy at Stanford; they also founded Beneficial State Bank, whose stock is held by a foundation.
deep_cut_fact: He captained the Yale soccer team, and named Farallon after the Farallon Islands off the Bay Area coast; Yale's endowment, after first turning him down, became an early client in 1987 with Farallon managing its money at no fee.
notes: Very media-accessible and a natural energy/climate-investing guest. Galvanize lists the press address for media inquiries. Primary result: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/billionare-tom-steyer-ends-california-governor-campaign-falling-short-jungle-primary.print ; post-campaign role at Galvanize not confirmed.

name: Mariana Voigt Schwartz Gomes
current_role: Interior designer in Florianópolis; individual shareholder of WEG S.A. (no board or executive role)
profile: Granddaughter of WEG co-founder Werner Ricardo Voigt and one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, Latin America's largest maker of electric motors. WEG is a listed multinational with factories in more than ten countries and about $7bn in annual revenue. She holds no board seat or executive role at WEG and works as an interior designer in Florianópolis, Brazil.
interesting_fact: WEG was founded in 1961 in Jaraguá do Sul by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt with Eggon João da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus; the name WEG comes from their first initials.

name: Charles Cohen
current_role: President and CEO, Cohen Brothers Realty Corp.; Chairman, Cohen Media Group
profile: Charles S. Cohen (born 1952) bought out his father and uncle and grew the family's Cohen Brothers Realty into roughly 12M sq ft of Manhattan offices and design centres (750 Lexington, Pacific Design Center). A lifelong film buff, he founded Cohen Media Group in 2008, built a classic-film library of 800+ titles and bought Landmark Theatres in 2018. Since 2024 a Fortress loan default has led to foreclosure auctions, and Forbes now lists him as a former billionaire.
interesting_fact: He produced the Oscar-nominated 'Frozen River' (2008) and distributed Asghar Farhadi's Oscar-winning 'The Salesman'. In 1985 he wrote the movie quiz book 'Trivia Mania'.
deep_cut_fact: At 16 he made his first short film, which won an honourable mention at the Kodak Teenage Movie Awards. He went on to major in English at Tufts (1974) and graduate from Brooklyn Law School (1977).
notes: Ongoing financial and legal trouble: the Fortress $534M loan default, a 2024 foreclosure auction and a 2026 court deadline. Avoid the subject, and note his billionaire status is doubtful now. The best hook is film and cinema restoration. Contact through Cohen Media Group publicity; no verified published email found.

name: Lucio Co
current_role: Chairman, Cosco Capital Inc.; director of Puregold Price Club (Philippines)
profile: Manila-born (1953) Lucio Co grew up around his family's Atlantic Glassware store in Divisoria and moved from oil and minerals (Alcorn Gold, later Cosco Capital) into retail, co-founding Puregold with wife Susan in 1998; it now spans hundreds of hypermarkets and supermarkets plus S&R membership warehouses. In Dec 2025 his Crystal Bridges Holding acquired water utility PrimeWater (renamed Hiraya Water).
interesting_fact: Puregold was born out of the 1997 Asian financial crisis: the first store opened on 12 December 1998 at Liberty Center on Shaw Boulevard, Mandaluyong, partly to support employees of his Puregold Duty Free store in Clark.
deep_cut_fact: Cosco Capital, his holding company, started life as Alcorn Gold Resources, an oil and mineral exploration company, only renamed Cosco Capital in 2012; his family's original business was the Atlantic Glassware store in Santo Cristo, Divisoria.
notes: IR email is the published address of Cosco Capital's VP Investor Relations (John Marson T. Hao). Couple is low-profile; son Vincent Co (Puregold president) is the public face. Energy/infrastructure angle: Hiraya Water (ex-PrimeWater) acquisition.

name: Dean Solon
current_role: Founder, CEO & President, Create Energy (Portland, Tennessee); founder of Shoals Technologies Group
profile: Tennessee solar-hardware entrepreneur who founded Shoals Technologies in 1996 (electrical gear for utility-scale solar) and took it public on Nasdaq in 2021. Left Shoals' board around 2022 and in 2023 founded Create Energy, a U.S. maker of solar, storage and tracker products that announced a $78M, 1,000-job Tennessee expansion in 2026.
interesting_fact: Since the 1970s he has visited Disney World at least twice a year and says his favourite movie is Beauty and the Beast; he holds about two dozen solar-gear patents.
deep_cut_fact: Shoals began making auto parts for Bosch; when Bosch wanted suppliers to move to Mexico after NAFTA he refused to leave Tennessee, and his first solar customer was an upstart First Solar needing junction boxes. Despite billionaire status he says he still drives a 2017 Chevy Bolt.
notes: Press email is Create Energy's published media contact (Joseph Fahrney, Chief of Staff). Solon is colourful and talkative with media (Canary Media, Clean Power Hour podcast) - a strong podcast candidate.

name: Dmitry Nikolaev
current_role: Controlling owner and general director, Stroyservis (coal producer, Kemerovo, Kuzbass)
profile: Siberian businessman who controls Stroyservis, founded in 1994, which traded metals and pipes in the early 1990s before buying coal mines in the Kuzbass; it is now one of Russia's top coal producers (coking and thermal coal, coke chemistry), headquartered in Kemerovo. On Forbes' billionaire list since 2023.
interesting_fact: Stroyservis is the main sponsor of the Muay Thai Federation of Russia and publishes employees' production 'world records' on its website; it signs annual social-economic cooperation agreements with the Kemerovo region.
deep_cut_fact: Stroyservis was general partner of the free open-air 'Heroes of World Rock' festival in central Kemerovo on 27 July 2019, staged for the company's 25th anniversary, with Accept, Within Temptation, HammerFall and Royal Hunt; a 2018 edition in Novokuznetsk marked the city's 400th anniversary.
notes: Very low public profile; little English-language coverage. Russian-language approach via Stroyservis press service (pr@) is the only published route. Russia-based coal business: check any sanctions/compliance status before engaging.

name: Aloke Lohia
current_role: Founder & Group CEO, Indorama Ventures PCL (Bangkok)
profile: Kolkata-born (1958), Bangkok-based founder of Indorama Ventures, the world's largest PET resin producer by capacity (~$13.6B revenue in 2025), built through a long string of acquisitions since 2014 including Brazil's Oxiteno ($1.3B, 2022). He is the younger brother of Indonesia-based Sri Prakash Lohia. In March 2026 Indorama agreed to merge its Indian unit Indovida India with Blackstone-backed EPL in a $2B deal.
interesting_fact: Indorama Ventures has recycled more than 50 billion PET bottles since 2011 and targeted recycling 50 billion a year by 2025; Lohia also lunches with his wife Suchitra, who works alongside him, nearly every day.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture after moving to Thailand in 1988 was Indorama Chemicals (now Aurus Specialty), which turned corncobs into furfural alcohol with backing from Germany's DEG; he then started Thailand's first wool business (1994) and first PET business, Indorama Polymers (1995).
notes: Started as finance director of P.T. Indorama Synthetics, Indonesia (1979-87). Reasonably accessible to media (Forbes Thailand interview 2018 posted on IVL site). Wikipedia article is thinly sourced; deep-cut also described on IVL's own leadership bio per Wikipedia citation. IR phone +66 2661 6661 is published on the IR page.

name: Wang Bing
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Chongqing Genori Technology Co. (重庆臻宝科技, STAR Market 688797)
profile: Wang Bing (王兵, b. 1980) studied mechatronics at East China Jiaotong University and spent a decade selling semiconductor and display-panel parts in Shanghai. In 2016 he founded Genori, which makes silicon, quartz, SiC and ceramic parts for the vacuum chambers of chip-making and panel tools, along with surface-treatment services. Genori listed in Shanghai in June 2026.
interesting_fact: Genori's June 2026 STAR Market IPO was more than 6,000x oversubscribed by retail investors, and its shares jumped almost 1,200% within days. Forbes put his fortune at about $4.7B at that point.

name: Jin Baofang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, JA Solar Technology Co. (Shenzhen: 002459), Beijing
profile: Born 1952, Jin founded JA Solar in 2005 and built it into one of the world's largest solar-module makers, with plants in China and Southeast Asia and a planned factory in Phoenix, Arizona. JA listed on Nasdaq in 2007, went private in 2018 and relisted in Shenzhen in 2019. He is a former vice president of the China Photovoltaic Industry Association.

deep_cut_fact: Before founding JA Solar he was an official at the electricity bureau in Ningjin County, a background that predates his move into photovoltaics.

profile: Wang Suqin (王素勤) is the wife of Weiming founder-chairman Xiang Guangming and one of four acting-in-concert actual controllers of Weiming Environment Protection, a Wenzhou-based waste-to-energy incineration operator and equipment maker. Husband Xiang Guangming (chairman) is the company's public face; route via company IR.

name: Sun Xiangbang
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (~1.96% direct; acting in concert with Sun Qinghuan) of MLS Co., Ltd. (Muliansen, SZSE: 002745); holds no executive post
profile: Sun Xiangbang is listed with Sun Qinghuan as joint actual controller of MLS, the Zhongshan-based LED packaging and lighting group that owns LEDVANCE (former Osram general lighting; LEDVANCE and SYLVANIA brands). The family fortune derives from MLS, founded by Sun Qinghuan in 1997. MLS's 2025 annual report says Sun Xiangbang is currently studying and has not taken up a role.
interesting_fact: MLS's global brand cluster is built on LEDVANCE and SYLVANIA, acquired via the takeover of Osram's former general-lighting business; the Suns jointly control ~39% of MLS.
notes: MLS 2025 annual report states he is 'currently in the study stage and has not yet taken office' - effectively a passive family shareholder, likely a poor podcast target. The active figure is Sun Qinghuan (founder, chairman & GM of MLS). Only route found is MLS IR.

name: Wang Yutian
current_role: Chairman & General Manager (controlling shareholder), Hongrida Technology Co., Ltd. (鸿日达科技, SZSE: 301285), Kunshan
profile: Mold-design engineer who built Hongrida, a Kunshan maker of precision connectors for phones and consumer electronics, listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext. He is the controlling shareholder; Hurun lists his wealth jointly with director Shi Zhangqin. He is moving into chip-package heat sinks, liquid-cooling plates and optical parts.
interesting_fact: Hongrida says its semiconductor-package metal heat-sink business is in mass production on four lines with two more being added, and it is sampling liquid-cooling plates and microchannel cooling with customers. That links a phone-connector maker to AI and data-center thermal management.
deep_cut_fact: Wang, born in 1979, studied mold manufacturing and design at Shaoyang University in Hunan (2001). He began as an R&D engineer at Shenzhen Longteng computer factory and Kunshan Jiehuang Electronics, then ran Shanghai Xiergai Electronics' connector division before building Hongrida.
notes: Country is blank in the input but the person is in mainland China (Kunshan, Jiangsu). The IR email is the board-secretary/securities-affairs inbox from the 2025 annual report summary. Outreach should be in Chinese. Hurun's 'Hongrida' is 鸿日达.

name: Shi Zhangqin
current_role: Director and co-controlling shareholder, Hong Ri Da Technology Co. (鸿日达科技, SZSE ChiNext: 301285), Kunshan, Jiangsu
profile: Co-actual controller (with chairman/GM Wang Yutian) of Hongrida, a Kunshan maker of precision electronic connectors (SIM/card, I/O, USB Type-C, battery and board-to-board connectors) and metal structural parts that has expanded into photovoltaic products. The company listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in September 2022; she has been a director since 2020, re-elected in 2026.
interesting_fact: Hongrida is a nationally recognized 'specialized and sophisticated little giant' and holds patents on products such as a stacked three-in-one hot-swappable phone SIM card holder and a double-waterproof USB Type-C connector.
deep_cut_fact: She started in 2004 as an administrative assistant at Kunshan Jiehuang Electronic Precision (Hongrida's predecessor) and between 2008 and 2013 ran two small hardware shops of her own in Kunshan before rejoining the connector business.
notes: Input 'Hongrida' = 鸿日达 Hong Ri Da Technology. Very low public profile; best route is the board secretary's office (IR email from 2025 annual report summary). Board secretary as of mid-2026: Zhou Yi.

name: Lu Haodong
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Wuxi Rich Intelligent Equipment (理奇智能, 301599.SZ); re-elected chairman Nov 2026
profile: Lu Haodong (陆浩东, b. 1974, Wuxi) founded Rich Intelligent Equipment in 2018. It makes automated material-handling systems (batching, dispersion, mixing) for lithium-battery slurry, with CATL, BYD and Sunwoda as customers, and had 43% of China's battery-slurry feeding-system market in 2024. Rich listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext on 30 April 2026, jumping 245% at the open. He controls about 85%.
interesting_fact: Rich grew revenue from RMB 619m in 2022 to RMB 2.17bn in 2024 supplying CATL, BYD and Sunwoda, and Lu's first Hurun appearance (2026) put him at No. 735 with RMB 10.5bn.
deep_cut_fact: He started at 20 as an export salesman for a Wuxi county trading company. He then became East Asia sales manager for US mixer maker Charles Ross & Son, ran its Wuxi subsidiary, and after founding Rich bought control of Wuxi Ross, his former employer.
notes: Identity confirmed: Hurun API 2026 (陆浩东, 理奇智能 'Rich', Wuxi, New Energy) plus IPO prospectus bio (CEIBS EMBA 2008). Prior pass couldn't decode 'Rich' = 理奇智能. Good energy/battery-manufacturing angle. Best route: board secretary Yu Dakui via IR email.

name: Chris Lin
current_role: Chairman and President, ASPEED Technology (Taiwan; TPEx: 5274)
profile: Chris Lin founded ASPEED Technology in 2004 after working at IC designer Silicon Integrated Systems. ASPEED, a fabless chip designer, is the world's largest maker of baseboard management controller (BMC) chips, which run in almost every server. It listed on the Taipei Exchange in 2013, and AI data-center demand has sent its revenue soaring.
interesting_fact: ASPEED became the world's largest BMC SoC supplier after buying Broadcom's Emulex Pilot BMC business in 2016. Its chips sit in servers at nearly every hyperscaler.
deep_cut_fact: Lin has quantified the AI effect on his niche: he said an Nvidia GB200 NVL72 rack uses 87 BMCs versus 12 in an H100-based rack. At Computex 2026 he said ASPEED's constraint was supply-chain capacity, not orders.
notes: The input's SEC insider link (TSMC VP and CIO) is a DIFFERENT Chris Lin and is not this person. Very relevant to a data-center podcast: ASPEED BMCs are in most AI servers. Lin speaks to press at Computex every year, so that is a good hook.

name: Ahmet Calik
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Çalık Holding (Istanbul)
profile: Born 1958 in Malatya to a textile family, Çalık started out in 1981 and built Çalık Denim into a supplier to Levi's, Diesel and Gap. From the 1990s he expanded into Central Asia and diversified into energy distribution and generation, construction, mining, banking and telecom under Çalık Holding.
interesting_fact: Çalık Holding's pipeline of construction and energy projects is worth around $7 billion; its long partnership with Mitsubishi Corp. dates to 1990s plant-building in Central Asia.
deep_cut_fact: At about 20 he asked his father for start-up capital and was told: 'Son, if you have been raised well enough to start your own business, then that is your capital.' He 'picked up his jacket' and went into denim because jeans were fashionable but hard to find.
notes: No published press email found; Çalık Holding contact page lists HQ switchboard and a web contact form. The Ahmet Çalık Foundation is listed on the group site. Energy angle: Çalık Enerji (YEDAŞ distribution, Kosovo's KEDS).

name: Cesar Mata Pires
current_role: Deceased (founder and largest shareholder of Brazilian construction group OAS)
profile: César de Araújo Mata Pires (born Salvador, Bahia, 19 Jan 1950), civil engineer and founder of the construction group OAS, died in São Paulo on 22 August 2017, aged 67.
notes: Died 22 August 2017 (Portuguese Wikipedia). Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Robert Mouawad
current_role: Head of the Robert Mouawad real-estate group and Robert Mouawad Foundation/Private Museum; former president of Mouawad jewellers (retired 2010)
profile: A third-generation jeweller, Mouawad took over the house his grandfather founded in Beirut in 1890. He moved its headquarters to Geneva in the 1970s and built it into a global high-jewellery and watch brand known for buying some of the world's largest diamonds. He handed the business to his sons in 2010 and now focuses on real estate, including Reef Island in Bahrain and a 2024 Riyadh project with Dar Global, and on his museum.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he opened the Robert Mouawad Private Museum in a neo-Gothic Beirut palace built in 1891 by collector Henri Philippe Pharaoun. It displays Roman and Byzantine antiquities, Islamic woodwork, icons and rare books, and reopened after the 2020 Beirut port explosion.
deep_cut_fact: He originally studied in Europe to become a doctor, until his father persuaded him to join the family business, where he started as a salesman. The Gemological Institute of America's Carlsbad, California campus is named in his honour for his support of GIA.
notes: Born c.1944 and still listed by Forbes; there is no death report, but this was not separately verified. The mouawad.com site blocked automated reads, so no press contact was captured. The company (now run by his sons Fred, Alain and Pascal) is the likely route. The Bahrain/Riyadh real-estate projects are the most podcast-relevant angle.

name: Park Dong-suk
current_role: Founder and chairman/CEO, Sanil Electric (KOSPI-listed transformer maker)
profile: Korean engineer-entrepreneur who founded Sanil Electric after working at rival transformer maker Yuil Electric. He has spent 38 years on industrial special transformers and reactors. Sanil earns over 60-80% of revenue abroad, mainly from US utilities and grid players such as GE Vernova, PG&E and Duke Energy, and listed on KOSPI in 2024 on the grid and AI-power boom.
interesting_fact: Sanil Electric is a direct beneficiary of the US power-grid and data-center build-out. Most of its sales are exports of special transformers to US utilities and energy companies, and it won Korea's $100m Export Tower award.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2025 IBK Industrial Bank inducted him as the 22nd member of its Business Leaders' Hall of Fame. His guiding motto, as cited there, is 'Opportunity comes to those who are prepared' (기회는 준비된 사람에게 온다).
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast: transformers are a key grid bottleneck for AI data centers. Korean press says he started the business at 26 (founded Aug 1987); Forbes says 1994, so the founding year is unclear. The company website did not load, so no IR contact was captured; try Sanil Electric IR via KRX/DART filings.

name: Eric Hémar
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, ID Logistics (Euronext Paris: IDL)
profile: Hémar started his career in the French civil service, at the Cour des comptes (supreme audit court) and then the transport ministry. He founded contract-logistics group ID Logistics in 2001 and floated it in Paris in 2012. The group made EUR 3.7bn of revenue in 2025 across 450 sites in 20 countries with 55,000 staff. He owns over 50% and has also chaired the TLF union of French transport and logistics firms since 2019.
interesting_fact: In November 2026 ID Logistics announced a partnership with Terra Robotics to pilot humanoid robots (Unitree G1 units nicknamed 'IDA' and 'Heinz') on sorting tasks at its German sites.
deep_cut_fact: Although ID Logistics is an SBF 120 company operating on five continents, its head office is in Orgon, a small village in the Provence countryside (Bouches-du-Rhône), rather than in Paris.
notes: A good podcast fit (warehouse automation, robotics, logistics energy use). The press agency Rumeur Publique is the best route. Web-search quota ran out partway through this lane, so the profile relies on Forbes and company documents.

name: Daniel Dines
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, UiPath (NYSE: PATH), New York
profile: Daniel Dines is a self-taught programmer from Onești, Romania. He started DeskOver in Bucharest in 2005 and built it into UiPath, the robotic-process-automation company that IPO'd on the NYSE in 2021. He handed the CEO job to Rob Enslin in early 2024 but returned as CEO in June 2024. He is now steering UiPath toward 'agentic' AI automation.
interesting_fact: Forbes dubbed him the 'Boss of the Bots', the first 'bot billionaire'. UiPath was bootstrapped in Bucharest for about a decade before raising venture money and became one of software's biggest IPOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding UiPath he spent 2000-2005 at Microsoft in Seattle, then went home to Bucharest to start DeskOver, a small outsourcing shop that became UiPath. In April 2019 he donated EUR 1 million to help rebuild Notre-Dame de Paris.
notes: Talks about his story readily: Sequoia 'Crucible Moments' episode and a 2019 Forbes cover. Good fit for an AI and automation angle. Avoid the 2019 layoffs.

name: Lord Grantchester
current_role: Labour life peer, House of Lords (from 15 June 2026); dairy farmer near Crewe, Cheshire
profile: Christopher John Suenson-Taylor, 3rd Baron Grantchester (b. 1951; known as John Grantchester), is a grandson of Sir John Moores, founder of the Littlewoods retail and football-pools empire, and a former Littlewoods director. Educated at Winchester and the LSE (economics), he sat as an elected hereditary peer from 2003 and was made a life peer in 2026 after hereditary seats were abolished.
interesting_fact: He is a former Everton FC director and long-time shareholder (8.5% as of 2015), and a trustee of the Everton Collection, a large open-access archive of club memorabilia.
deep_cut_fact: A working dairy farmer, he runs a farm near Crewe, chairs the South West Cheshire Dairy Association and sits on the council of the Royal Agricultural Society of England; he has been a Labour frontbench voice on agriculture in the Lords.
notes: Rich-list entry is for the wider Moores family fortune. Parliamentary email is the clear published route. Note: he chaired Dairy Farmers of Britain when it collapsed in 2009 — avoid as an opener.

name: Antti Aarnio-Wihuri
current_role: Chairman, Wihuri Oy (Wihuri Group), Helsinki
profile: Born in Turku in 1940, he heads the Wihuri Group, a 120-year-old Finnish family conglomerate (packaging, technical trade incl. Caterpillar dealerships, Metro wholesale, aviation, jet charter and air ambulance) with about 5,000 staff. He is also the largest shareholder of Canadian packaging maker Winpak.
interesting_fact: A former racing driver and team principal: his AAW Racing Team won the European Interserie championship three times in the early 1970s with driver Leo Kinnunen.
deep_cut_fact: He raced himself in the 1960s, taking class wins at Finnish circuits Artukainen, Keimola and Rovaniemi in 1966 and entering the 1000 km Nürburgring four years running (1967-70); he later backed young drivers including Valtteri Bottas.
notes: Aged 86, private. Board role per Finnish registry (https://www.asiakastieto.fi/yritykset/fi/wihuri-oy/25578562/paattajat). Group general mailbox is the only published route.

name: Konstantin Sixt
current_role: Co-CEO (Co-Chairman of the Management Board), Sixt SE
profile: Third-generation member of the Sixt car-rental family. With his brother Alexander he controls about 56% of Sixt SE, and the two have been co-CEOs since June 2021, when their father Erich moved to chair the supervisory board. Konstantin built out Sixt's online business from 2005 and later ran global sales and e-commerce. He has also led marketing, franchise development and the SIXT+ car subscription.
interesting_fact: Sixt was founded in Munich in 1912 by Martin Sixt. Konstantin's father Erich took over in 1969, when it had about 200 vehicles, and with his wife Regine built it into a global brand operating in over 100 countries.
deep_cut_fact: After an MSc in International Accounting and Finance at Cass Business School in London, he took charge of Sixt's online operations in 2005. He joined the management board in 2015.
notes: Contact through Sixt corporate communications (press contact Johannes Gunst, per Sixt corporate news releases) or IR. Possible podcast angle: Sixt's EV fleet, charging and digital mobility platform.

name: Winai Teawsomboonkij
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (with family), Thaifoods Group PCL (SET: TFG); resigned as CEO and director in late 2025
profile: Winai Teawsomboonkij founded Thaifoods Group in 1987 with a 20,000-bird chicken farm. He expanded into pig breeding and animal feed, took the company public in 2015, and with his family still holds a majority stake. TFG is a major Thai chicken and pork producer and runs 600+ Thaifoods Fresh Market shops. He stepped down as CEO and director after Thai SEC civil sanctions for insider trading in late 2025.
interesting_fact: Thaifoods grew from a single 20,000-chicken farm in 1987 into a listed integrated poultry and pork group with more than 600 retail outlets.
notes: Sensitive: he resigned after 2025 Thai SEC insider-trading sanctions and holds no formal role now. Not a strong fit and probably unreceptive. The IR page loads via JavaScript, so I couldn't extract an email.

name: Pieter van der Does
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Adyen (Amsterdam), sharing the role with Ingo Uytdehaage since May 2023
profile: Amstelveen-born (1969) economist who worked at ING and Elsevier, then was commercial director at e-payments firm Bibit (sold to RBS in 2004). In 2006 he co-founded Adyen with Bibit colleague Arnout Schuijff, building a single global payments platform used by merchants like Spotify, Netflix and Booking.com; Adyen listed in Amsterdam in 2018 and he owns about 3%.
interesting_fact: He started his first business in his early teens, refurbishing broken mopeds in his parents' backyard; he is also an avid rock climber and mountaineer.
deep_cut_fact: A 2020 Business Insider Netherlands profile noted that, despite being a billionaire, he drove a 15-year-old Volvo and preferred to repair his central-heating boiler himself. Earlier in his career he worked for Elsevier in New York, Oxford and Amsterdam.
notes: Accessible, engineering-minded founder who does occasional interviews. Media requests should go through Adyen's press-and-media page; ir@adyen.com is the investor address.

name: Pantas Sutardja
current_role: Director, Credo Technology Group (Nasdaq: CRDO); founder & CEO of LatticeWork.
profile: Indonesian-born engineer (UC Berkeley EE/CS PhD, ex-IBM Almaden) who cofounded Marvell in 1995 with his late brother Sehat and Weili Dai, serving as VP engineering and CTO until 2014. He backed Credo's 2015 Series A and sits on its board (~3% stake); Credo's high-speed connectivity chips/AECs are now a key AI data-center supplier. He also runs consumer-storage firm LatticeWork.
interesting_fact: Marvell's name came from the founders' plan to 'do marvelous things' plus the observation that successful chip firms' names ended in -el/-ell (Intel, Novell, Nortel); the three incorporated it on 10 Feb 1995.
deep_cut_fact: Drawing on his IBM hard-drive work, Pantas defined the architecture of Marvell's first all-CMOS read-channel chip. Designed for 180 Mb/s, it was already running near 240 Mb/s when Seagate asked for 240 - Seagate became Marvell's first customer. As boys in Singapore he and Sehat built a Van de Graaff generator from surplus copper wire.
notes: Strong data-center angle via Credo (AI interconnect). Credo contacts are company IR/media (published in FY2026 earnings release), not personal. Avoid Marvell 2016 accounting-probe ouster topic (concerned his brother/sister-in-law).

name: Hwang Chul-joo
current_role: Founder and chairman, Jusung Engineering (co-CEO, overseeing R&D since the April 2025 switch to three co-CEOs)
profile: Former Hyundai Electronics and ASM International engineer who founded Jusung Engineering in 1993 and listed it in 1999. Jusung makes thin-film deposition tools (notably atomic layer deposition) for chips, displays and solar cells, selling heavily to SK Hynix. Since 2025 he focuses on R&D, pitching next-generation ALD for 3D and AI memory chips.
interesting_fact: Jusung was the first company in the world to succeed in mass-production atomic layer deposition (ALD) equipment, and Hwang founded it when Korea imported virtually all of its chip-making equipment.
deep_cut_fact: Born in 1958 in Goryeong, North Gyeongsang and an Inha University engineering graduate, he served two terms as chairman of the Korea Venture Business Association and was founding chairman of the Korea Youth Entrepreneurship Foundation, which runs startup mentoring and competitions.

public_contacts.value: https://www.jusung.com (IR section incl. IR-letter form at /write/ir_Letter)

notes: Gives long interviews to Korean press (Hankyung, Herald); also chairman of the Korea Invention Promotion Association (20th). Son Hwang Eun-seok became co-CEO in 2025.

name: Ignacio Torras
current_role: Founder and CEO, Tricon Energy (Houston)
profile: Barcelona-born, dual Spanish-American trader who took over his ailing father's small chemicals trading business in Brazil, worked at Holland Chemical in Houston, then cofounded Tricon Energy in 1996. Tricon is now one of the world's largest distributors and traders of chemicals and plastics; he briefly handed off the CEO job in 2016 and took it back a year later.
interesting_fact: His Houston restaurant BCN Taste & Tradition earned a Michelin star in 2024, and in 2024 he launched the Genuine Cup, a soccer tournament for neurodivergent players.
deep_cut_fact: His restaurants began on a 2008 family holiday: renting a house in Fonteta, Spain, he met its house chef Luis Roger and recruited him to Houston. Their restaurants BCN and MAD are named after the Barcelona and Madrid airport codes.
notes: Goes by 'Nacho'. Devout Catholic; passionate about neurodiversity inclusion (Genuine Cup, SEMILLAS preschool opening 2026). Privately held company, no IR; general Tricon inbox is the published route.

name: Peter Ludwig
current_role: Cofounder and CTO, Applied Intuition (Sunnyvale, CA)
profile: Detroit-raised University of Michigan engineer who worked at Google on Maps and Android Automotive, then cofounded Applied Intuition with Qasar Younis in 2017. The company sells simulation tools and vehicle operating systems/autonomy software to carmakers (GM, Nissan, VW) and defense customers; valued at $15bn after a $600m round in June 2025.
interesting_fact: Applied Intuition started in a rented space above a bar on Murphy Avenue in Sunnyvale; Ludwig now oversees 1,000+ engineers and, with Younis, still personally interviews leadership hires.
deep_cut_fact: A third-generation auto guy (his grandfather spent 30+ years at GM), Ludwig's first job, in high school, was as a software engineer at an automotive tooling company; he and Younis first explored starting a self-driving company back in 2013 before deciding against it.
notes: Less public than CEO Qasar Younis; route via press@applied.co. Good AI/physical-AI and defense-autonomy angle.

name: Qasar Younis
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Applied Intuition (Sunnyvale, CA)
profile: Born in Punjab, Pakistan and raised in Detroit, Younis studied at GMI/Kettering and Harvard Business School. He founded TalkBin (bought by Google in 2011), worked on Google Maps and was COO of Y Combinator. In 2017 he co-founded Applied Intuition with Peter Ludwig; it makes simulation and autonomy software for cars, trucks and defence, valued at $15bn in 2025.
interesting_fact: After years of publicly calling X a distraction, he joined in late 2025 as @qasar. He wrote that 'almost nobody talks about AI in the real world', meaning cars, trucks, tanks and fighter jets, and that the self-driving debate should be about more than Waymo vs Tesla.
deep_cut_fact: As a Kettering co-op student he rotated through General Motors tech centres and factories. Kettering gave him an honorary Doctor of Engineering and made him its 2026 commencement speaker. His site's About page quotes Andy Grove: 'I am an engineer by training and a manager of a high technology company by profession... work is worship.'
notes: He keeps a personal site (qy.co) with essays, a reading list (Krishnamurti, Hayek) and travel photos, e.g. Salar de Uyuni in 2024. He now sees being a spokesperson as part of his role, so he is likely receptive to a podcast about physical AI and autonomy. Company site: applied.co.

name: Azalia Mirheseini
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Ricursive Intelligence; Assistant Professor of Computer Science, Stanford University
profile: Azalia Mirhoseini (Forbes spells it Mirheseini) is an AI researcher who co-created AlphaChip, Google's deep-RL chip floorplanning system used on TPUs, and worked at Google Brain, Anthropic and Google DeepMind. In Dec 2025 she co-founded Ricursive Intelligence with Anna Goldie to automate chip design with AI; it raised $335m at a ~$4bn valuation within four months.
interesting_fact: She and co-founder Anna Goldie have moved in lockstep: they started at Google Brain on the same day, left the same day, joined and left Anthropic the same day, rejoined and left Google the same day, then founded Ricursive together.
deep_cut_fact: Her Stanford lab's 'Intelligence Per Watt' work found local on-device models already handle most real-world queries, motivating OpenJarvis, an open-source framework treating energy, latency and cost as first-class constraints. She also won Rice University's Best ECE Thesis Award.
notes: Correct spelling is Mirhoseini. Strong fit for an AI/data-center podcast (chips + energy efficiency of AI). Accessible academic; press via JConnelly. Forbes lists her as a 'former' billionaire in real-time data; her equity stake is undisclosed.

name: Wang Wenbiao
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Elion Resources Group (亿利资源集团), Inner Mongolia/Beijing (last confirmed listings 2024-25)
profile: Inner Mongolian entrepreneur known in China as the 'Son of the Desert'. In 1988 he took over a struggling saltworks in the Kubuqi Desert and built Elion into a conglomerate spanning chemicals, clean energy (Elion Clean Energy, SH:600277), large desert solar farms and ecological restoration, greening thousands of km² of Kubuqi.
interesting_fact: In 2017 he won the UN Environment 'Champions of the Earth' Lifetime Achievement award for Kubuqi desert restoration, the first Chinese citizen to receive it.
deep_cut_fact: Elion began in 1988 when Wang took over the Hanggin (Hangjinqi) Banner Saltworks in the middle of the Kubuqi in his home district. He told UNEP: 'I was haunted by hunger and sand in my childhood.'
notes: Elion Resources Group has faced debt and bond defaults since about 2021. The listed arm Elion Clean Energy is now led by Wang Ruifeng (2025 interim report). Wang's current executive status is unclear and no 2025-26 confirmation was found. elion.com.cn did not resolve. WEF profile: https://cn.weforum.org/people/wang-wenbiao. No published personal contact.

name: Anna Goldie
current_role: Co-founder and CEO (co-CEO per Forbes), Ricursive Intelligence
profile: AI researcher (MIT BS/MEng, Stanford NLP PhD) who co-founded Google Brain's ML for Systems team and co-led AlphaChip, an RL chip-layout method published in Nature and used in four TPU generations. She was an early Anthropic employee (Constitutional AI co-author) and a Google DeepMind staff scientist. Ricursive, an AI-for-chip-design lab, raised $335M at a $4B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: Her AlphaChip work with cofounder Azalia Mirhoseini (Nature, 2021) has been used to lay out four generations of Google's TPU, datacenter CPUs and other Alphabet chips; she was named to MIT Technology Review's 35 Innovators Under 35 in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: She gave keynote talks at Google Developer Day China in 2017, 2018 and 2019 in Mandarin, livestreamed to 10M+ viewers. Her 2011 MIT master's thesis was 'CHATTER', a spoken-dialogue system for language learning.
notes: Very relevant for data-center/AI chip angle. Her own site and links list X/LinkedIn. Forbes lists her as former billionaire-list member (net worth ~ $1.5B). Thesis on MIT DSpace: https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/66420.

name: Tang Rui
current_role: Founder & CEO, ZongMu Technology (纵目科技, Shanghai), and founder of its robotics unit Cancong Robotics (蚕丛机器人)
profile: Tang Rui (唐锐, RUI TANG; holds US citizenship) founded ZongMu Technology in 2013. ZongMu makes ADAS and automated-parking systems and raised over RMB 2.2bn from investors including Qualcomm Ventures; Forbes listed him as a $1.5bn billionaire in 2023. In 2024 he launched Cancong Robotics, which makes AI-driven mobile EV-charging robots (FlashBot) for the smart-energy market.
interesting_fact: He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in electronic engineering from Tsinghua. He spent about 20 years in Silicon Valley automotive electronics before returning to China to found ZongMu.
deep_cut_fact: Before ZongMu he was global senior engineering director of the automotive group at UK chipmaker CSR (later bought by Qualcomm), running about $230m a year of auto chip products. The in-car navigation platform he led there helped create China's market for car navigation and infotainment systems, now over 10m units a year.
notes: Caution: ZongMu was in serious financial distress in early 2025, with unpaid wages, social insurance stopped and most staff gone. Tang said he was abroad seeking funding (https://m.jiemian.com/article/12405750.html). He has dropped off Forbes' list. Forbes spells his name 唐睿, but Chinese sources use 唐锐. No public contact found.

name: Azalia Mirhoseini
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Ricursive Intelligence; Assistant Professor of Computer Science, Stanford (directs the Scaling Intelligence lab)
profile: Rice PhD who co-created AlphaChip at Google Brain (RL chip floorplanning used on several TPU generations) and worked at Anthropic and Google DeepMind on Claude and Gemini. In late 2025 she co-founded Ricursive Intelligence with Anna Goldie to build AI that designs chips; it raised $300M at a $4B valuation in Jan 2026, with Nvidia investing.
interesting_fact: She and co-founder Anna Goldie have moved in lockstep: they started at Google Brain on the same day, left on the same day, joined and left Anthropic on the same day, rejoined and left Google on the same day, then started Ricursive together. Both turned down 'crazy' offers from Zuckerberg.
deep_cut_fact: Because she and Goldie worked out together doing circuit training, Jeff Dean nicknamed their AlphaChip project 'chip circuit training'; internally the pair were known as 'A&A'. She is also a co-author of the early Mixture-of-Experts work now standard in frontier LLMs.
notes: Listed as former Forbes real-time billionaire (~$1.5B). Her personal site has a Contact page. Ricursive recently released an open-weight model (Ripple-65B preview). Very relevant for data-center/AI-hardware angle.

name: Joseph Craft, III.
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Alliance Resource Partners, L.P. (ARLP), Tulsa; director, BOK Financial
profile: Hazard, Kentucky native (b. 1950) with UK accounting and law degrees who started at Tulsa energy firm Mapco, ran its coal division from 1986, led a 1996 management buyout to form Alliance Coal and took it public in 1999. He still runs Alliance, the third-largest coal producer in the eastern U.S. (now also in oil & gas royalties), and became board chairman in 2019.
interesting_fact: UK's basketball practice facility, the $30M Joe Craft Center (opened 2007), is named for him after a $6M pledge, then the largest private gift in UK Athletics history; UK football's training facility also bears his name.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 his Joseph W. Craft III Foundation gave $3M to UK's Gatton College Institute for the Study of Free Enterprise, funding faculty positions and doctoral fellowships for research on how markets affect people's lives.
notes: Married to Kelly Craft (former U.S. ambassador to the UN). Politically prominent coal-industry figure; ARLP IR contact is CFO Cary P. Marshall per 2026 releases. Relevant to energy/data-center power demand angle (coal supply to utilities).

name: Suzan Sabanci Dincer
current_role: Chairperson, Akbank; board member, Sabancı Holding
profile: Third-generation member of Turkey's Sabancı family (b. 1965; now goes by Suzan Sabancı), a treasury and risk-management banker who joined Akbank in 1989 as EVP for treasury and has chaired the bank since March 2008. She also sits on the boards of Sabancı Holding, the Institute of International Finance, and Blackstone's international advisory board.
interesting_fact: Queen Elizabeth II appointed her a CBE in 2012 for developing Turkey-UK relations (she chaired the Turkish-British Business Council 2010-14), and King Felipe VI awarded her Spain's Order of Civil Merit in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: She served as Honorary Consul of Luxembourg in Istanbul for 17 years (2005-2022), and is a founding member and board member of Endeavor Turkey, the high-impact entrepreneurship network - a natural hook for an entrepreneurship podcast.
notes: Now uses the name Suzan Sabancı (dropped 'Dinçer'). Akbank IR page also lists individual IR team emails; no personal channel published. Endeavor Turkey is a possible warm route.

name: Alfred Mann
current_role: Deceased (died 25 February 2016, Las Vegas, aged 90)
profile: Alfred E. Mann was an American physicist and serial medical-device entrepreneur. He founded Spectrolab (solar cells), Pacesetter Systems (pacemakers), MiniMed (insulin pumps), Advanced Bionics (cochlear implants) and Second Sight, and led MannKind. He died in 2016.
notes: Deceased; source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_E._Mann. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Family Jahr
current_role: Hamburg publishing family; heirs of Gruner + Jahr co-founder John Jahr Sr.; held stake via Jahr Holding until 2014
profile: Very likely the Hamburg family of John Jahr Sr., who co-founded magazine publisher Gruner + Jahr (Stern, Brigitte, Geo) in 1965 with Richard Gruner and Gerd Bucerius. The family kept a 25.1% stake through Jahr Holding until Bertelsmann bought it out in November 2014. Family members have also held significant Henkel shares.
interesting_fact: At G+J's founding in 1965, John Jahr held 32.3%. After Gruner left in 1969, Jahr and Bucerius briefly owned the publisher 50/50 before Bertelsmann bought in.
notes: This is a family entry from a single 1996 Forbes listing; no individual is named. John Jahr Sr. died in 1991. The family sold its last G+J stake to Bertelsmann in 2014. Not an actionable outreach target without first picking a specific living family member.

notes: Deceased in 1997 per German Wikipedia (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Hilti). Skipped. The Hilti group is now controlled by the Martin Hilti Family Trust.

current_role: Family behind E. A. Juffali & Brothers (Jeddah); chairman Khaled bin Ahmed Al Juffali
profile: This 1996 Forbes entry covers the Juffali family of Saudi Arabia, owners of E. A. Juffali & Brothers. The Jeddah group was founded in 1946 and is one of the kingdom's largest private conglomerates, with about 59,000 employees, spanning Mercedes-Benz vehicles, power, construction, insurance and telecoms. The group is now chaired by Khaled Juffali.
interesting_fact: The Juffali group developed Saudi Arabia's first electricity generation and telecommunications, as well as early television concessions.
notes: A family, not an individual. Key earlier figures Ahmed Juffali (d. 1994) and Walid Juffali (d. 2016) are deceased. For outreach, research the chairman Khaled Juffali separately. The power-generation history fits an energy show.

name: Margaret Cargill
profile: Margaret Anne Cargill (1920–2006), granddaughter of Cargill founder W. W. Cargill and heir to the grain-trading fortune, died on August 1, 2006 in La Jolla, California; her estate endowed Margaret A. Cargill Philanthropies.
notes: Deceased (d. 2006, per Wikipedia / LA Times obituary). Skipped further research.

name: Theodore Lerner
profile: Deceased. Washington-area real estate developer (Lerner Enterprises, founded 1952) and founding principal owner of the Washington Nationals; died 12 February 2023 at age 97.
notes: Died 12 Feb 2023 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Lerner). Skip.

name: Daniel Harrison, III.
current_role: Principal of the family's Houston-based oil & gas company (Harrison Interests) and Harrison Quarter Horses / Harrison ranches (Fulshear and Piloncillo Ranch, Texas)
profile: Dan J. Harrison III is a third-generation Texas oil and ranching heir. His wealth jumped after his family leased the ~100,000-acre Piloncillo (Harrison) Ranch in Dimmit/Webb counties, atop the Eagle Ford shale, to a Shell unit around 2010, putting him on Forbes' billionaire list in 2013 (age ~65, $1.1bn). The 'Royal Dutch Shell' label reflects the lessee, not ownership.
interesting_fact: Shell's Eagle Ford position was built largely around the Harrisons' Piloncillo Ranch; Forbes added him as a new Houston billionaire in 2013 largely on the strength of that lease.
deep_cut_fact: His family has bred American Quarter Horses since the 1930s (registered with AQHA since 1941); the AQHA gave his father and grandfather its Legacy Award in 1997, and Harrison-bred horses have competed in every timed event at the National Finals Rodeo. He and wife Rosemary run the program from Fulshear, west of Houston.
notes: Very private; no published personal, office or press contact found. No obituary found but he has not appeared on rich lists since 2021 (born c.1947-48), so confirm he is alive before outreach. Ranching/Quarter Horse world (TSCRA, AQHA) is the most natural rapport angle.

name: Chen Jinsong
current_role: Founder of Shenzhen Worldunion Group (世联行, SZ:002285); former chairman, later co-chairman/director (current board status unverified)
profile: Founded Worldunion, the Shenzhen real-estate consultancy and agency that became one of China's largest property-services firms and listed in Shenzhen in 2009. Hurun lists him jointly with Tong Jie. In 2020 his holding vehicle sold about 202m shares to the Zhuhai state-owned Da Hengqin Group. He then stepped down as chairman in favour of Da Hengqin's Hu Jia and became co-chairman.
interesting_fact: In the 2020 deal his holding company World Union China sold a stake to Zhuhai's state-owned Da Hengqin Group, bringing a state-owned shareholder into the private property-services firm he founded. He stayed on as co-chairman.
notes: Known in China as an outspoken property-market commentator. As of 2025-26 Worldunion is chaired by a Da Hengqin executive. His current board status is unclear; check the latest 002285 announcements. Not an energy or data-centre fit.
