profile: Hurun listed Qi Jianhong (綦建虹) in 2005-2019 with wealth from Sparkle Roll, a Beijing-based group known for luxury car dealerships (premium British and Italian marques) and lifestyle and cinema businesses. He has been off the Hurun lists since 2019, and I couldn't confirm his current role or holdings.
notes: Research incomplete: the lane's web search budget ran out and Baidu/Wikipedia/company pages couldn't be fetched, so nothing here is sourced. Verify through HKEXnews filings for Sparkle Roll Group before using. Weak fit for an energy/data-centre podcast.

name: Jayashree Ullal
current_role: Chairperson and CEO, Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET)
profile: London-born, New Delhi-raised engineer (SFSU BSEE, Santa Clara MS) who built Cisco's Catalyst switching business into a multibillion-dollar line, then became Arista CEO in 2008 and took it public in 2014. Arista's Ethernet switching now underpins AI and cloud data centers; she owns roughly 5% of the company.
interesting_fact: She joined Crescendo Communications in 1992; its 1993 sale to Cisco was Cisco's first-ever acquisition and its entry into switching, which she helped grow to a $5B business by 2000. In 2026 Arista posted its first $3B quarter and joined the S&P 100.
deep_cut_fact: Before networking she was a chip engineer: she started at Fairchild Semiconductor and then at AMD designed high-speed memory chips for IBM and Hitachi (quoted in Electronics magazine in 1987 as an AMD senior strategic development engineer). She was schooled at Convent of Jesus and Mary, Delhi.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center theme (AI networking). Media contact per Arista releases is Corporate Communications (Amanda Jaramillo); ir@arista.com seen in 2026 Business Wire release (could not load page directly, verify). Also active on LinkedIn/X as public CEO.

name: Hoyt R. Barnett
current_role: Retired; former Vice Chairman and director of Publix Super Markets (director 1985-2019)
profile: Hoyt R. 'Barney' Barnett spent about four decades as a Publix officer, serving as Vice Chairman and an ESOP trustee and on the board from 1985 until April 2019. He was married to Carol Jenkins Barnett, daughter of Publix founder George W. Jenkins (she died in 2021); the family fortune derives from Publix stock.
interesting_fact: Publix's 2017 proxy noted his 39 years as a company officer and 31 on the board; the board waived its age-72 retirement policy for him for continuity after his wife's resignation.
deep_cut_fact: Florida Southern College's Barney Barnett School of Business and Free Enterprise is named for him, a Florida Southern graduate, funded by a 2011 gift from Carol Jenkins Barnett in his honor.
notes: Identity caveat: the list's Chinese name field refers to Carol Jenkins Barnett (d. Dec 2021), so the Hurun entry likely reflects the couple's combined Publix stake. Hoyt R. Barnett and 'Barney Barnett' appear to be the same person (SEC proxy: brother-in-law of Howard Jenkins), but confirm. Alive status not verified (search budget exhausted); born c.1943.

name: Michael P Scarpelli
current_role: Independent Director and Audit Committee Chair, ClickHouse (since Sept 2026); former CFO of Snowflake (2019-2025)
profile: Mike Scarpelli is one of tech's best-known CFOs. He was CFO of Data Domain, ServiceNow (2011-2019) and Snowflake (2019-2025), taking each through its IPO, including Snowflake's record 2020 software IPO; his Snowflake equity made him a billionaire. He retired as CFO in 2025 (succeeded by Brian Robins) and joined the ClickHouse board in September 2026.
interesting_fact: He worked alongside Frank Slootman through three companies (Data Domain, ServiceNow, Snowflake) and took all three public. ClickHouse credits him with helping generate more than $100bn in shareholder value over his career.
deep_cut_fact: Scarpelli holds an economics degree from the University of Western Ontario in Canada. He also has a strong view on AI data infrastructure: on joining ClickHouse he said 'Every generation of infrastructure has a company that redefines the category' and that every CFO and CIO he knows is consolidating data platforms.
notes: Post-retirement, Snowflake press is a weak route; the ClickHouse board role (data infrastructure for AI) is the timely hook. He is known as blunt and data-driven on earnings calls. No personal social accounts were verified.

name: Robert Coyuito jr
current_role: President & COO, Oriental Petroleum and Minerals Corp.; Chairman & CEO, Prudential Guarantee and Assurance (PGA)
profile: Robert G. Coyiuto Jr. (spelled 'Coyiuto') is a Filipino-Chinese tycoon whose holdings span insurance (Prudential Guarantee), luxury car distribution (PGA Cars: Porsche, Audi, Lamborghini, Bentley), oil exploration (Oriental Petroleum) and a stake in the national power grid operator NGCP. He left the board of NGCP parent Synergy Grid (SGP) in Oct 2025 after 13 years.
interesting_fact: Through PGA Cars, his group is the Philippine importer and distributor for Porsche, Audi, Lamborghini and Bentley, alongside its insurance and energy businesses.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2017 President Duterte named him presidential adviser on capital market development.
notes: Name usually spelled 'Robert Coyiuto Jr.' (input has 'Coyuito'). Role at Oriental Petroleum confirmed on its officers page (https://opmc.com.ph/about/company-officers/). Synergy Grid exit per InsiderPH (https://insiderph.com/tycoon-robert-coyiuto-jr-leaves-synergy-grid-board-after-13-years-amid-maharlika-investment-talks). Low media profile; no personal social accounts found.

name: Chen Youxing
current_role: Listed as Vice Chairman / director, StarPower Semiconductor Ltd (SSE: 603290), Jiaxing (per third-party profiles)
profile: Chen Youxing appears on Hurun lists (2020-23) for his stake in StarPower Semiconductor, China's leading IGBT power-module maker, founded in Jiaxing in 2005 by US returnees Shen Hua and Hu Wei. Insider-data sites list him as a director/vice chairman holding ~13% (31.1m shares) as of 2023; the stake appears to be held via Zhejiang Xingdeli Textile, StarPower's No.2 shareholder.
interesting_fact: StarPower's IGBT modules are core power components in EV inverters, solar/wind converters and industrial drives; it has been added to the SSE 180 and FTSE All-World indices.
notes: Very little public information; not named in StarPower's 2025 annual report summary, so current board role is unverified. Link to Xingdeli Textile (11.32% holder in 2025) is an inference, not confirmed. IR email is the company board secretary's (Zhang Zhe). Better podcast target at StarPower is founder/chairman Shen Hua.

name: Hock E. Tan
current_role: President and CEO, Broadcom Inc.; Director, Meta Platforms (since 2024)
profile: Penang-born Hock Tan came to MIT on a scholarship, worked in finance at GM and PepsiCo, then ran Integrated Circuit Systems before becoming Avago CEO in 2006. Through serial M&A (Broadcom, CA, Symantec enterprise, VMware) he built today's Broadcom, a key supplier of custom AI accelerators and data-center networking chips.
interesting_fact: In 2017-18 he led a $117B bid for Qualcomm, which would have been the largest tech deal ever, until the US government blocked it; Broadcom then moved its legal home from Singapore back to the US.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 he pledged $4M to MIT to endow the Nam P. Suh Professorship in mechanical engineering, honoring his former MIT professor (first holder: quantum-computing pioneer Seth Lloyd). He earned both his MIT BS and MS in mechanical engineering in 1975.
notes: Notoriously media-shy; rarely does interviews beyond earnings calls. Major philanthropy with ex-wife K. Lisa Yang on autism/disability research (MIT Yang Tan Collective, Cornell). Avoid family topics. Net worth in input (~$1.5B, Hurun 2022-23) is likely understated given Broadcom stock run-up.

name: Xiang Ping
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hunan Goke Microelectronics (国科微, SZSE: 300672), Changsha
profile: Xiang Ping (b. 1971) has led Goke Microelectronics, a Changsha-based fabless chip designer founded in 2008, serving as chairman and general manager since 2015 (earlier a supervisor). Goke listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2017 and makes direct-broadcast-satellite HD chips, 4K/8K ultra-HD decoder and display chips, AI vision SoCs and automotive AI chips, including its own in-house NPU.
interesting_fact: Goke developed China's direct-broadcast-satellite HD decoder chips and has since built its own neural processing unit (NPU) for edge-AI SoCs, pitching itself as a supplier of domestic 'China chips' for on-device AI.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as a journalist, not an engineer: chief editor of the South China edition of 'Network News' (1995-97), then head of the Shenzhen bureau of the Chinese Academy of Sciences' newspaper Science Times (1997-2000) and deputy GM of its business centre (2000-04).
notes: Former journalist turned chip CEO — the media background could be a good outreach hook. IR email published in company filings (via Eastmoney F10); board secretary is Huang Ran.

name: Huang Zezhong
current_role: Director and General Manager (and co-controlling shareholder), Quanzhou Jiadeli Electronics Material Co., Ltd. (嘉德利, SH:603435)
profile: Huang Zezhong and his cousin Huang Yanhuang each own about 47.9% of Quanzhou Jiadeli, a Fujian maker of BOPP electrical film. That film is the core dielectric in the film capacitors used in EVs, solar and wind inverters and HVDC grid equipment. The pair took control in 2010, and Jiadeli listed on the Shanghai main board on 22 May 2026, putting him on the 2026 Hurun list.
interesting_fact: Jiadeli's niche is an energy-transition chokepoint. BOPP film for capacitors depends on electrical-grade polypropylene resin that is still mostly imported (about 80% of Jiadeli's comes from Borouge). The film goes into the capacitors used in EV drivetrains, renewable inverters and flexible HVDC transmission.
notes: The 'Jiadeli' in the dataset is Quanzhou Jiadeli Electronics Material (嘉德利). He is general manager, not chairman; the chairman is Huang Huanming. Board secretary is Huang Shengquan, reachable via ir@jdlxcl.com. He keeps a very low profile and I found no English-language coverage.

name: Huang Yanhuang
current_role: Director and Deputy General Manager; co-controlling shareholder, Quanzhou Jiadeli Electronic Materials (嘉德利, SSE: 603435)
profile: Huang Yanhuang (黄炎煌, ~41) and his cousin Huang Zezhong (general manager) each own ~43% of Jiadeli, a Quanzhou, Fujian maker of BOPP electrical film, the dielectric used in film capacitors for EVs, solar/wind inverters and grid equipment. Jiadeli (founded 2002) listed on the Shanghai main board on 22 May 2026, raising ~RMB 725m for a new Xiamen plant.
interesting_fact: Jiadeli is a national 'little giant' specialised SME; its BOPP film makes up over 75% of the insulation in film capacitors, a niche long dominated by overseas suppliers, so it is a domestic-substitution play for EV and renewables power electronics.
notes: Low public profile; nearly no interviews or English-language coverage. Company chairman is his father Huang Huanming (no shareholding). IR email from a June 2026 shareholder-meeting notice in China Securities Journal. Best route: company board-secretary office.

name: Mori Arkin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Arkin Capital (Israeli multi-asset investor; formerly Arkin Holdings); controlling shareholder of Sol-Gel Technologies
profile: Born in Ramat Gan in 1952, Arkin took over his father's small pharmaceutical importer Agis at 19 after his father's death in 1972. He turned it into a generic-drug manufacturer and sold it to Perrigo in 2004 for about $818m. He now runs Arkin Capital, which manages over $2.5bn across health, tech, private equity and real estate, and controls Nasdaq-listed dermatology firm Sol-Gel.
interesting_fact: He was a 19-year-old serving soldier when he inherited the running of Agis. Forbes later dubbed him a 'pharma kingpin-turned-VC' when he joined the billionaires' club in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He started university at Tel Aviv studying Old Testament and archaeology before switching to psychology (BA with honours), then did graduate work in physiological psychology and philosophy of science. He is also an art-history buff who composes music as a hobby.
notes: The music/art hobby comes from Forbes facts (https://www.forbes.com/profile/mori-arkin/). Arkin Capital (formerly Arkin Holdings; the old domain redirects) is his own office, so its contact form is the best route. Also co-founder and chairman of Accelmed. Avoid family/children topics.

name: Anas Sefrioui
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Douja Promotion Groupe Addoha (Casablanca-listed); founder of Ciments de l'Atlas (CIMAT)
profile: Fès-born (1957) Moroccan developer who founded Addoha in 1988 and built it into Morocco's largest homebuilder through low-cost and social housing, often on government programmes. Addoha listed in Casablanca in 2006. He also built cement maker Ciments de l'Atlas, with plants in Morocco and West/Central Africa. The record's country (Macao) is wrong; he is Moroccan.
interesting_fact: Beyond housing, he built cement plants in Settat and Beni Mellal and 500,000-ton plants in Cameroon, Gabon, Ivory Coast and Guinea, expanding Addoha's model across francophone Africa.
deep_cut_fact: He left secondary school early to work in his father Haj Abdeslam Sefrioui's business making a clay product used to wash the body and hair (traditional Moroccan ghassoul). He used the savings from that to start his property group in 1988.
notes: The input country 'Macao' is wrong; he is Moroccan. He is media-shy, and his daughter Kenza is deputy chair. The listed contacts are Addoha's company channels and LinkedIn, not personal ones.

name: Aziz Akhannouch
current_role: Majority owner/head of Akwa Group (Morocco); mayor of Agadir; Prime Minister of Morocco 2021-Sept 2026
profile: Aziz Akhannouch controls Akwa Group, the Moroccan conglomerate founded by his father in 1932, with fuel (Afriquia), gas (Afriquia Gaz) and industrial-gas (Maghreb Oxygene) businesses. He was agriculture minister 2007-2021 and prime minister from 2021 until King Mohammed VI named Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri PM after the 23 Sept 2026 election.
interesting_fact: In March 2020, via Akwa's Afriquia subsidiary, he donated about 1 billion dirhams (~$100m) to the King's COVID-19 pandemic management fund.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in 1961 in Aguerd Oudad, a village near Tafraout in the Anti-Atlas, into the Ammeln Amazigh tribe, and earned a management diploma from Canada's Université de Sherbrooke in 1986 before returning to run the family business.
notes: Country field 'Macao' in input is wrong; he is Moroccan. Just left the premiership (Sept/Oct 2026) after RNI came second to PAM; stepped down as RNI leader Feb 2026. Politically sensitive figure; route via Akwa Group corporate communications. No published direct email found.

name: Stephen Winn
current_role: Founder and former CEO of RealPage (stepped down after the 2021 sale to Thoma Bravo); private investor, Dallas
profile: Winn, an electrical engineer (BA UT Austin, MS Stanford), began at his father's accounting software firm, Computer Language Research, and became its CEO. He founded RealPage in 1998 to sell property-management software to landlords, took it public in 2010 and sold it to Thoma Bravo in April 2021 (reported at about $10.2bn). He stepped down as CEO shortly afterwards and is now about 80 and based in Dallas.
interesting_fact: RealPage grew out of 'Little Buddy', a side venture inside a tax-software business Winn had acquired to expand Computer Language Research.
notes: Retired from operating roles with a low public profile, and I found no personal or family-office contact channel. RealPage is the subject of DOJ and state antitrust litigation over rent-pricing software, a sensitive topic. Web-search quota ran out before deeper research on this person.

name: Polys Haji-Ioannou
current_role: Founder/owner, Polyar Tankers; major shareholder, easyJet
profile: Polys Haji-Ioannou is the elder brother of easyJet founder Stelios and the son of Cypriot tanker magnate Loucas Haji-Ioannou (d. 2008). Much of his wealth comes from a large easyJet stake. He carries on the family shipping legacy with his own tanker fleet, Polyar Tankers, and invests in commercial and residential property in Cyprus, Greece, Monaco and London.
interesting_fact: His yacht 'Esmeralda' is named after one of the world's largest tortoises.
deep_cut_fact: His father Loucas, whose shipping business Polys continues, once owned the world's largest private tanker fleet, which he built up from the 1950s. Polys remains involved in the philanthropic foundation his father started.
notes: Do not confuse him with Polys V. Hajioannou, chairman and CEO of NYSE-listed Safe Bulkers and a relative from another branch of the family. Wikipedia currently merges the two, so check any Safe Bulkers claim before using it. Very private and based in Monaco. No published personal or office contact was found, and the web-search budget ran out before Polyar Tankers' site could be checked.

name: Francisco Jose Riberas Mera
current_role: Executive Chairman, Gestamp Automoción (Madrid-listed)
profile: Francisco José Riberas Mera and his brother Juan María each own about 25% of Gestamp, the autoparts maker he founded in 1997 from the family steel business started by their father in 1958; the family holds its stake via holding company ACEK. Gestamp makes body-in-white, chassis and battery-box components in 20+ countries and reported €11.3bn revenue in 2025. The brothers are also top shareholders in CIE Automotive.
interesting_fact: In March 2026 Gestamp signed a 10-year renewable-energy PPA with Iberdrola for 660,000 MWh of electricity for its European plants, and it supplies scrap via Gescrap to Hydnum Steel's green-hydrogen steelmaking.
deep_cut_fact: For Gestamp's 25th anniversary in 2023, Riberas personally guided King Felipe VI around the Palencia plant that makes structural bodywork and chassis parts.
notes: Good energy-transition angle (PPAs, green steel, EV battery boxes). Gestamp press office is the published route. Web search budget ran out before checking personal social accounts.

name: Suh Kyung-bae
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Amorepacific Group
profile: Second-generation head of Amorepacific, South Korea's largest cosmetics maker (Sulwhasoo, Laneige, Innisfree), founded by his father Suh Sung-whan in 1945. Took over in 1997 and rode the K-beauty/Hallyu wave into global markets; Forbes Asia named him Businessman of the Year in 2015. Also funds basic life-science research through his own foundation.
interesting_fact: Amorepacific traces its roots to his grandmother, who sold camellia oil as a hair treatment across the Korean peninsula; in the 1960s the company built a door-to-door saleswomen network, some of them Korean War widows.
deep_cut_fact: His Suh Kyungbae Science Foundation (founded 2016) backs young Korean life scientists with long-term grants (31 SUHF Fellows by 2025); in his chairman's message he cites the phrase 'Beyond the sky there is another sky' (天外有天), which also names the foundation newsletter 'Beyond the Sky'.
notes: Foundation mailbox (he chairs it) is the most personal published route; corporate PR via Amorepacific. Bio details: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suh_Kyung-bae. Foundation history: https://www.suhf.org/introduce/history.do

name: Zhang Xingang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Shaanxi Yuanjie Semiconductor Technology (STAR Market: 688498)
profile: Born 1970; Tsinghua materials grad, USC materials-science PhD, US citizen. Worked on optical chips at Luminent from 2001, then in 2013 founded Yuanjie in Xianyang, Shaanxi, an IDM making laser (DFB/EML) chips for optical transceivers. AI data-center optics demand sent the stock up ~780% in a year, making him a billionaire in 2026.
interesting_fact: Yuanjie's laser chips transmit data as light inside AI data centers. In March 2026 its shares broke RMB 1,000, the first new A-share 'thousand-yuan stock' of 2026, valuing the company at ~RMB 96B.
deep_cut_fact: Yuanjie's first product, launched after about a year of lab work, was a 2.5G 1310nm DFB laser chip. By 2018 it had shipped 10 million DFB chips, becoming China's first IDM to mass-produce optical chips at scale. He chose Xianyang because the city had just launched tech-startup support policies.
notes: Highly relevant to the data-center/AI optics theme. Forbes said the company did not respond to its request for comment. The board secretary (Cheng Shuo) is the published IR contact.

name: Dan Gertler
current_role: Israeli mining investor (Fleurette Group), active mainly in the Democratic Republic of Congo
profile: Israeli businessman who built a fortune from mining and oil interests in the DRC, starting with diamonds in 1997. In 2017 he sold his stakes in two Congo copper/cobalt mines to Glencore for $960m, netting an estimated $400m. He has been under US sanctions since December 2017 over alleged corrupt deals; Forbes says the sanctions have been eased in recent years.
interesting_fact: His grandfather, Moshe Schnitzer, co-founded the Israel Diamond Exchange in 1947 and was its long-time president.
notes: HIGH-RISK SUBJECT: under US Treasury sanctions (2017, expanded 2018), with ongoing legal and reputational controversy over Congo mining. A spokesman typically declines to comment. He is relevant to cobalt/copper supply chains, but any podcast contact needs legal and editorial review. I did not verify his current sanctions status because the search budget was exhausted.

His twin sons now run them, Anurang Jain at Endurance and Tarang Jain at Varroc, and he retains stakes in both listed companies.

notes: Low public profile; operating roles are held by his sons Anurang (Endurance) and Tarang (Varroc), who are better outreach targets. Company websites (endurancegroup.com, varroc.com) blocked automated access; IR contacts are in their stock-exchange annual reports. Search budget was exhausted before a deep-cut could be sourced.

name: Vadim Vikulov
current_role: Owner, Aston (Rostov-on-Don agricultural exporter)
profile: Sole owner of Aston, one of Russia's largest grain and sunflower-oil traders, founded by his father Ivan in 1992 as a sea/river transport business. A maritime-trained logistics man, he worked at Soviet shipping agency Sovfracht, then set up a freight and trading firm in Germany before building Aston into grain storage, oil plants, tankers, bulk carriers and a marine terminal.
interesting_fact: In March 2011 he was elected chairman of Russia's newly formed National Association of Agricultural Products Exporters, whose members then controlled over 60% of the country's grain exports.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering grain, he trained as a shipping specialist (master's, Admiral Makarov State University of Maritime and Inland Shipping) and worked at Sovfracht, the USSR's foreign-trade shipping agency, until 1992.
notes: Russia-based; Aston website (aston.ru) not reachable from here and no published press contact found. Consider sanctions/compliance context before any outreach to Russian agribusiness owners.

name: Lucy Guo
current_role: Founder of creator platform Passes. The Blast (Oct 2026) reported she stepped down as CEO; Passes has not confirmed it publicly. Also founder of Backend Capital.
profile: Born 1994 in California, Guo left Carnegie Mellon as a Thiel Fellow, worked at Facebook, Snapchat and Quora, and cofounded Scale AI in 2016. She left in 2018 but kept about 3%, which became a billionaire stake after Meta's $14bn deal in 2025. She founded Passes in 2022 and invests through Backend Capital.
interesting_fact: As a teenager she taught herself to code by building bots for the online game Neopets and selling the in-game items. From April to December 2025 she was the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire, displacing Taylor Swift.
deep_cut_fact: In 2018 she built 'Apply to Date', a public 'dating resume' site. It started when she made a page to find a date for a holiday party and turned it into an 'actionable about.me' that let anyone screen applicants from their own network.
notes: Very public on social media. X handle @lucy_guo appears only in aggregator sources, so verify before using. Sensitive context: Passes faces a lawsuit, and in 2026 there was press about her exit as CEO and a personal dispute. Avoid these in outreach. She also started a DJ/music side career in 2026.

name: Andrei Kosogov
current_role: Member of Alfa Group's supervisory board overseeing its investment units; co-founder and reportedly largest shareholder of LetterOne (left L1 board in March 2022)
profile: Estonian-born Russian financier (b. 1961), a power-engineering graduate who joined Mikhail Fridman in 1992 to set up a privatization investment fund and then ran Alfa Capital. He became a long-time Alfa Group partner, co-founded Luxembourg-based LetterOne in 2013 (Wintershall Dea, VEON/Vimpelcom, Turkcell, Holland & Barrett) and stepped off L1's board after his partners were sanctioned in 2022.
interesting_fact: After the 2022 EU/UK sanctions on Fridman, Aven and Khan, Bloomberg reported their stakes moved toward Kosogov, the low-key partner who had never been sanctioned, making him the largest shareholder of Alfa-Bank and LetterOne.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he graduated from the Moscow Power Engineering Institute in 1987 and first worked at a small firm founded with the institute's help; he received Russia's Medal of Honour for charitable work on childhood mental and neurological illnesses.
notes: Very private, rarely gives interviews. He no longer sits on the LetterOne board, so the L1 media contact is indirect. Alfa-linked entities face Western sanctions; check compliance before outreach. Energy angle: L1 Energy (formerly Wintershall Dea stake, now sold to Harbour Energy).

name: Timothy Headington
current_role: President & sole shareholder, Headington Resources / Headington Companies (Dallas); co-founder, Ley Line Entertainment
profile: Dallas-born, Oklahoma City-raised oilman who founded Headington Oil in 1978 (moved to Dallas in 1984) and in 2008 sold North Dakota Bakken acreage to XTO Energy for $1.85B. His Headington Resources spans oil & gas, Dallas real estate and hotels (The Joule), private equity and entertainment; he's also a prolific film and theatre producer.
interesting_fact: Ley Line Entertainment, which he co-founded in 2018 with Theresa Steele Page, backed the Best Picture winner 'Everything Everywhere All at Once' and the Broadway/West End musical '& Juliet'; he earlier co-produced 'Hugo' and was EP on 'Rango'.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil, he lettered in tennis at the University of Oklahoma, then earned graduate degrees in theology and psychology at Fuller Theological Seminary and did his psychology internship at Los Angeles County Hospital. He co-founded the Headington Institute, which provides psychological care for humanitarian aid workers.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Headington Companies (Dallas) is the only family-office-style public presence (website lists only an office address/phone). Headington Energy Partners (co-founded with Pat L. Smith & William Johnston) has a general contact form. Ley Line does not accept unsolicited submissions.

name: Charles Liang
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman, President and CEO, Super Micro Computer Inc. (Supermicro), San Jose
profile: Born in Chiayi, Taiwan; EE degrees from National Taiwan University of Science & Technology and UT Arlington. Co-founded Supermicro in 1993 with his wife Sara Liu as a five-person motherboard shop; it is now a leading builder of Nvidia-based AI server and liquid-cooled rack systems for data centres. Holds several server patents and founded the Green Earth Foundation.
interesting_fact: His Green Earth Foundation bought nearly 200 acres in Milpitas, California (the former Rancho Higuera) for reforestation and backs planting drought-resistant trees for the Sahara's Great Green Wall.
deep_cut_fact: Supermicro's green-computing push began in 2004 when Liang took his kids to see 'The Day After Tomorrow'; his back-of-envelope sum showed slightly more efficient server power supplies could save the output of 30 fossil-fuel plants, so Supermicro built its own.
notes: Ideal fit for a data-centre/energy-efficiency episode (green computing, liquid cooling). Go via Supermicro PR. Company has been under heavy media scrutiny over governance and export matters, so expect a cautious comms team.

name: Jared Smith
current_role: Cofounder and former president, Qualtrics; private investor (Provo, Utah)
profile: Jared Smith cofounded survey-software firm Qualtrics in Provo, Utah in 2002 with brother Ryan (CEO) and father Scott, serving as president; it started in their parents' basement and avoided VC money for a decade. SAP bought it for $8B days before its 2019 IPO, when Jared owned ~14%; Silver Lake and CPP took it private at $12.5B in 2023. He now invests, mostly at seed stage.
interesting_fact: Qualtrics was acquired by SAP for $8 billion in cash just three days before its scheduled January 2019 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Jared was the engineer of the founding trio: he wrote Qualtrics' code while Ryan sold it, and Ryan had to convince him to quit his job as a product director at Google to run the technical side.
notes: Low public profile compared with brother Ryan Smith (Utah Jazz owner, Qualtrics chairman). No published personal contact or verified social accounts found; Qualtrics press office or Ryan Smith's network are indirect routes.

name: Zong Yanmin
current_role: Chairman, general manager and controlling shareholder, SICC Co., Ltd. (Shandong Tianyue Advanced Technology; SSE STAR 688234 / HKEX 2631)
profile: Jinan native (b. 1964) and serial entrepreneur. After a construction-machinery dealership, in 2010 he bought the silicon carbide single-crystal research of Shandong University academician Jiang Minhua and founded SICC, now a top-three global maker of SiC substrates used in EVs, power electronics and RF chips. SICC listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022 and added a Hong Kong listing in 2025.
interesting_fact: SICC took Jiang Minhua's lab-grown SiC crystal to mass production (4-inch in 2015, 6-inch in 2017) and by 2020 held ~30% of the global semi-insulating SiC substrate market, behind only II-VI and Cree; Huawei, CATL and SAIC are among its backers.
deep_cut_fact: A silicate-engineering graduate of Shandong Institute of Light Industry, he spent 15 years as a process engineer at the Jinan Bulb Factory; when it closed he started over at 38 (2002) with Jinan Tianye, a Volvo excavator dealership that grew into Shandong's leading construction-machinery seller.
notes: No personal channels found. Company website www.sicc.cc (as listed in HKEX filings, e.g. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0327/2026032704444.pdf); approach via SICC's board office/IR. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Satya Nadella
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Microsoft
profile: Hyderabad-born engineer who joined Microsoft from Sun Microsystems in 1992, became CEO in 2014 and chairman in 2021. He built Azure into a leading cloud platform, bought LinkedIn and Activision Blizzard, and made Microsoft a central AI player via its multibillion-dollar OpenAI investment and Copilot; his billionaire status comes from Microsoft stock awards despite owning ~0.01%.
interesting_fact: He announced that all profits from his 2017 book 'Hit Refresh' would go to Microsoft Philanthropies and on to nonprofits.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong cricket fan who played on his school team and credits the sport with shaping his leadership, he is part of the investor group (with Soma Somasegar, GMR Group and others) that owns the Seattle Orcas of Major League Cricket; he and his wife are also part-owners of MLS club Seattle Sounders FC.
notes: Highest-profile person in this lane; direct outreach is unrealistic without a strong hook - requests go through Microsoft corporate communications (news.microsoft.com; site blocked automated fetches so no press email was captured). Very relevant to data-center/energy theme (Azure capex, nuclear/clean-power PPAs). Also posts frequently on LinkedIn.

name: Li Xuhui
current_role: Shareholder of Foshan Haitian Flavouring and Food; former director and vice president (left 2016)
profile: Li Xuhui is a long-time executive and shareholder of Foshan Haitian Flavouring & Food, China's largest soy-sauce maker. She was a director and vice president until 2016, and her fortune comes from her Haitian stake. Haitian chairman Pang Kang and vice chairman Cheng Xue are also billionaires.
interesting_fact: She managed Haitian's oyster-sauce factory from 1999 to 2010 before serving as a company director and vice president.
notes: Very private, with no public role since 2016. Her Chinese name was not verified (search budget exhausted). Haitian's IR office (SSE 603288 / HKEX filings) is the only institutional route, but she no longer works there. Low priority.

name: Shao Peisheng
current_role: One of the four actual controllers (with Shao Shuwei, Shao Qiuping, Shi Xuping) of Jiangsu Lettall Electronic Co. (利通电子, 603629.SH); no executive title found
profile: Shao Peisheng (邵培生) is one of the controlling family shareholders of Jiangsu Lettall Electronic, a Shanghai-listed maker of precision metal structural parts and components for LCD TVs. Since 2023 the company has pivoted into AI computing-power rental via its Century Lettall subsidiary, and the resulting share surge put the family on Forbes' 2026 rich list. Chairman is Shao Shuwei.
interesting_fact: Lettall entered AI compute in June 2023 by injecting RMB450m for 90% of 'Century Lettall' and now rents out all its own GPU servers via cloud delivery, turning a TV-bracket maker into a dual-business AI-compute stock.
notes: Very low public profile; no biography, age or executive role found for Shao Peisheng himself (listed alongside chairman Shao Shuwei in the IPO prospectus as an actual controller). Best route is the company securities office (board secretary Ding Ajing). Alive status not confirmed from a source.

name: Vladimir Bogdanov
current_role: Director General, PJSC Surgutneftegas (Russia); powers reportedly extended in 2026
profile: Career Siberian oilman (b. 1951) who has run Surgutneftegas, one of Russia's largest oil producers, since 1984 and through its 1993 privatisation. His wealth stems from a stake in the famously opaque company. He remains director general and has sat in the Khanty-Mansi regional legislature since 1996.
interesting_fact: He has led Surgutneftegas for over four decades - since 1984, in the Soviet era - making him one of the longest-serving chief executives of any major oil company worldwide; he was named a Hero of Labour of the Russian Federation in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in the village of Suerka in Tyumen Oblast's Uporovsky District and graduated in oil and gas from the Tyumen Industrial Institute in 1973, spending essentially his entire career in the West Siberian oilfields (Yuganskneftegaz 1978-80, then Surgutneftegas).
notes: IMPORTANT: sanctioned by the US (OFAC, April 2018), the EU (April 2022) and the UK (2022) - check legal/compliance implications before any outreach or paid arrangement. Extremely press-shy. Surgutneftegas website (surgutneftegas.ru) was unreachable from this environment, so no corporate press contact was verified.

name: Wang Linpeng
profile: Former chairman of Beijing Easyhome (居然之家 / 居然智家), the home-furnishings retail chain he took over in 1999 and built into a national leader. Chinese Wikipedia reports he died on 27 July 2025, aged about 56.
notes: Deceased (July 27, 2025), per https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/汪林朋, which cites The Paper (澎湃新闻). Forbes now lists him as 'former'. Do not contact.

name: Huang Zelan
current_role: Chairman and ultimate controlling shareholder, Chongyi Zhangyuan Tungsten Co. (SZSE: 002378), Ganzhou, Jiangxi
profile: Huang Zelan (黄泽兰) is the founding shareholder and chairman of Zhangyuan Tungsten, based in Chongyi county, Jiangxi, China's tungsten heartland. The company runs the whole tungsten chain, from its own mines and concentrate through APT, tungsten and carbide powders to cemented-carbide tools. He controls it through Chongyi Zhangyuan Investment Holding, of which he owns 94%.
interesting_fact: Zhangyuan has moved into high-strength tungsten wire built for diamond-wire cutting of solar silicon wafers, a fast-growing replacement for steel wire in PV manufacturing, and is building a smart-manufacturing project for it.
deep_cut_fact: Zhangyuan was originally set up by Huang Zelan with a small group of individual co-founders and is still headquartered in Chongyi county town rather than a big city. The group also includes a local power company, Chongyi Niubilong Electric Power.
notes: Very low public profile and Chinese-language only. Tungsten is a critical mineral, and the PV tungsten-wire business gives an energy angle. Day-to-day operations are run by the vice-chairman and GM, a younger family member. The deep-cut fact is company-level rather than personal.

name: Xianbao Chen
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Qiaqia Food Co. (ChaCha Food, SZSE: 002557), Hefei; controls parent Hefei Huatai Group
profile: Chen Xianbao was born in Hefei in 1959 and graduated from Wuxi Institute of Light Industry (now Jiangnan University) in 1982. He worked at a state-run Anhui sugar, tobacco and wine company before quitting in 1995 to found Huatai, which first sold ice pops. In 1999 he launched Qiaqia sunflower seeds, which became one of China's biggest snack-seed and nut brands; the company listed in Shenzhen in 2011.
interesting_fact: Qiaqia sales jumped from RMB 30m in its first year (1999) to RMB 1bn by 2006, helped by an early RMB 4m bet on CCTV advertising.
deep_cut_fact: The brand name 洽洽 comes from the cha-cha dance, and the 'water' radical in the character reflects his key product idea: boiling the seeds with herbal seasonings instead of roasting them, so they leave the eater's fingers clean.
notes: The input's SEC link (Gaotu Techedu CEO) is a name collision: Gaotu's CEO is Chen Xiangdong, not this person, so ignore it. The Qiaqia website (qiaqiafood.com) did not load. The SZSE investor-relations disclosures would be the route for an official contact.

name: Xu Jingnan
current_role: Chairman, Peak Sport Products (匹克体育), Quanzhou, Fujian
profile: Xu Jingnan (许景南) is the founder and chairman of Peak Sport, a Quanzhou-based basketball-focused sportswear and footwear brand founded in 1989; he and his family held about 65% of the company when it was listed in Hong Kong (taken private in 2016). Peak now sells in about 110 countries, and his son Xu Zhihua is CEO.
interesting_fact: Peak built its brand on basketball, signing NBA players such as Tony Parker and Dwight Howard and sponsoring FIBA and the WTA; its in-house 'TAICHI' adaptive-cushioning shoe tech had sold over 40 million pairs by end-2022.
notes: Low international media profile; son Xu Zhihua (CEO) is the public face of Peak. No published press email for the chairman found (only a consumer customer-service address for the overseas webstore). Web search budget ran out before a deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Li Xiande
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, JinkoSolar Holding (NYSE: JKS) and Jinko Solar Co. (Shanghai STAR)
profile: Born in 1975 in Shangrao, Jiangxi; in 2006 co-founded Jinko with his brother Li Xianhua and brother-in-law Chen Kangping (now CEO) with ~RMB10M. He grew it into one of the world's largest solar-module makers (NYSE IPO 2010, STAR Market listing 2022). His fortune has shrunk sharply amid the solar price war, but he remains among Jiangxi's richest people.
interesting_fact: Early on, Jinko funded expansion with customers' money: in 2007 he raised nearly RMB200M in prepayments from downstream buyers, and in 2009 bought Zhejiang cell maker Solar Valley (Taiyanggu) for ~RMB300M to integrate into cells.
deep_cut_fact: He wasn't the family's first solar entrepreneur: before Jinko he worked in construction engineering, and Jinko began as a wafer supplier to ReneSola (Yuhui Solar), the company founded by his eldest brother Li Xianshou.
notes: Very low-profile and rarely appears in public; outreach should go through JinkoSolar IR/corporate communications. The IR email is as listed in JinkoSolar's Dec 2025 press releases (found via search; the IR site blocks direct fetch). Avoid leading with the fortune decline.

name: Wu Meirong
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Wang Lubao) of Jiangsu Meike Solar Technology via Jiangsu Huantai New Materials Development Group, which she controls 100%
profile: Wu Meirong (吴美蓉) is the wife of Meike founder Wang Lubao; the couple control Jiangsu Meike Solar Technology (美科股份, Yangzhong, Jiangsu), an upstream maker of monocrystalline silicon ingots and wafers founded in 2004, through holding companies she owns. Meike passed its ChiNext IPO hearing in 2022 but withdrew the listing in Feb 2025.
interesting_fact: The family entered solar in 2003 after Wang Lubao, then running a compound-fertilizer business, was introduced to Suntech founder Shi Zhengrong, who persuaded him of the industry's prospects; the couple's holding vehicle is an agricultural company, Yangzhong Changke Agriculture.
notes: Very low public profile; virtually all coverage is about husband Wang Lubao and the company. Best route is via Meike Solar's general inbox (hello@meikesolar.com). Meike also operates a large Baotou (Inner Mongolia) ingot-pulling base.

name: Ren Daode
profile: Listed by Hurun (2021-2026) with wealth attributed to Taikang (insurance). Could not confirm his role or relationship to Taikang Insurance Group in the time available.
notes: Identity unverified (web search quota exhausted; Baidu Baike blocked). Taikang Insurance's founder/chairman is Chen Dongsheng; Ren is presumably a significant shareholder. Needs a follow-up check before any outreach.

name: Yang Xia
current_role: Founder and chairwoman, Shanxi Jinbo Bio-Pharmaceutical (锦波生物, Beijing Stock Exchange-listed), per Hurun listing; not independently re-verified this session
profile: Listed by Hurun (2023-2026, including Hurun Self-Made Women 2025) for wealth from Jinbo, a Taiyuan, Shanxi biotech known for recombinant humanized collagen used in medical-aesthetic and medical products. She is a self-made scientist-entrepreneur. The company's stock rally on the Beijing Stock Exchange lifted her onto the rich lists.
notes: The search budget ran out before I could verify details, and the company site (jinbobio.com) was unreachable. The role and company description come from the Hurun listing and general knowledge, so verify them against Jinbo's annual report (BSE 832982) before using. Biotech is not an energy or data-centre fit.

name: Ma Guolin
current_role: Shareholder of controlling holder Zhejiang Satellite Holding; vice chairman of Satellite Chemical (002648.SZ) per 2022 filing (current board seat not re-confirmed)
profile: Ma Guolin (马国林) is one of three shareholders, with chairman Yang Weidong and Yang Yuying, of Zhejiang Satellite Holding, controlling shareholder of Jiaxing-based Satellite Chemical (formerly Zhejiang Satellite Petrochemical), a C2/C3 petrochemicals maker. He was director & GM around the 2011 IPO and vice chairman in 2022.
interesting_fact: Satellite Chemical won approval in 2020 for a $4.2bn complex in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, built to crack ethane shipped from the United States - one of China's first large imported-ethane-to-ethylene projects.
notes: Very low profile; no personal bio found. Filings: 2011 listing doc https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2011-12-27/6f36d255-4c86-47d6-b9fa-66ccfd2d780d.PDF ; 2022 ESOP draft (vice chairman) https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk03/finalpage/2022-05-09/7ffef110-50b2-4022-8de2-d3c65108683a.PDF. Route: company IR/board secretary.

name: Zhang Hao
current_role: Co-founder/shareholder, Lilith Games (Shanghai); exact title not verified
profile: Hurun lists Zhang Hao (张昊) as a sub-40 billionaire from Lilith Games, the Shanghai developer founded in May 2013 whose public face is CEO Wang Xinwen (Kenny Wang). Lilith made its name with 'Dota Legends' (刀塔传奇, 2014) and later global hits 'Rise of Kingdoms' (2018) and 'AFK Arena' (2019). I couldn't verify Zhang Hao's specific role.
interesting_fact: Lilith's first hit, 'Dota Legends' (刀塔传奇, later renamed 小冰冰传奇), launched on the App Store in 2014, about a year after the company was founded in May 2013.
notes: Very low profile; Wang Xinwen is Lilith's spokesperson. The name is very common, so confirm identity before outreach. Research was cut short because the lane's web search budget ran out. Weak fit for an energy/data-centre podcast.

name: Xie Peng
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, Beijing DeepZero Technology (深演智能, HKEX: 2723)
profile: Xie Peng (谢鹏) co-founded DeepZero, the Beijing decision-AI marketing company formerly known as iPinYou (品友互动), alongside CEO Huang Xiaonan. DeepZero sells ad-execution, CRM/data and AI-agent software to brands and listed in Hong Kong in May 2026; Xie held about 13% per the prospectus and acts in concert with Huang.
interesting_fact: DeepZero, which began as iPinYou, one of China's early programmatic/behavioural-targeting ad-tech firms, listed on HKEX in May 2026 rebranded as a 'decision-making AI' company with an AI-agent suite (Deep Agent).
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he worked at Shanghai Johnson & Johnson and holds an MBA from CEIBS; 36Kr's iPinYou profile also lists him as chairman and GM of a firm called 能量工程 (Energy Engineering) when he co-founded the company.
notes: Hurun's 'Deepzero' = 深演智能 (ex-iPinYou), not DeepSeek. Very low English-language profile. Some aggregators list execs under English names (Grace Huang CEO, 'Mark Xie' COO). Best route: DeepZero IR.

name: Gu Tie
current_role: Founder/controlling shareholder of SeeYA Technology (视涯科技, SSE STAR: 688781), Hefei, per Hurun; exact title not independently verified
profile: Gu Tie (顾铁) is listed by Hurun (China 2026) as the source of a fortune in SeeYA Technology, a Hefei-based maker of OLED-on-silicon (OLEDoS) micro-displays for AR/VR headsets founded in October 2016. SeeYA listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 25 March 2026, raising 100 million shares at RMB 22.68, which created his paper wealth.
interesting_fact: SeeYA is one of the few plants worldwide producing OLEDoS micro-displays on 12-inch silicon wafers; its Hefei base exceeds 53,000 m² and it holds 300 granted patents.
deep_cut_fact: SeeYA lit up its first-generation demo display in June 2018 and its factory demo in December 2018, just over two years after founding; in 2026 the company received a second-class National Science and Technology Progress Award.
notes: New 2026 billionaire via STAR IPO. Company site does not name him; his chairman/GM title should be confirmed in the STAR prospectus. IR contact is the board office (董事会办公室). Deep-tech hardware angle relevant to AR/VR and semiconductor manufacturing.

name: Joseph Steinberg
current_role: Chairman, Jefferies Financial Group (NYSE: JEF); director, Vitesse Energy
profile: Harvard MBA (1970) who, with partner Ian Cumming, took over Talcott National in 1979 and turned it into Leucadia National, a 'mini-Berkshire' known for buying messy undervalued assets (National Beef, WilTel, Berkadia JV with Buffett). He drove Jefferies' 2012-13 merger into Leucadia, chairs the combined Jefferies and remains its largest shareholder (~10%).
interesting_fact: Leucadia's holdings put him on the board of Vitesse Energy, the oil and gas company spun out of Jefferies in 2023; since 2015 he and wife Diane have given over $15m via their trust to museums, colleges and community centers.
deep_cut_fact: Jefferies' CEO Rich Handler wrote that Steinberg convinced Andrew Whittaker to start his banking career at Drexel, mentored both via 'tough love', and in 2000 personally delivered the anchor $100m order for Jefferies' first high-yield fund; Jefferies did its first HY, IG, equity and convert deals with Leucadia.
notes: Jefferies describes him as 'an incredibly private person'. Best route is via Jefferies corporate/media relations (contact listed on the IR page). Note Jefferies warns of impersonators; genuine Jefferies email comes only from jefferies.com.

name: Ziyavudin Magomedov
current_role: Former owner of Summa Group (ports, gas/energy engineering, telecoms); currently imprisoned in Russia
profile: Dagestan-born Ziyavudin Magomedov (b. 1968, Moscow State University) built Summa Group into a conglomerate spanning ports (FESCO, Novorossiysk Commercial Sea Port), oil and gas engineering and construction. Arrested in 2018 and convicted in 2022, he lost his Summa and FESCO stakes to confiscation and was declared bankrupt by a Moscow court in November 2025.
interesting_fact: Summa was an early backer of Hyperloop One, and Magomedov publicly championed building a hyperloop link for Moscow and Russian freight corridors in the mid-2010s.
notes: NOT a viable outreach target: serving a long prison sentence in Russia after a 2022 embezzlement/organized-crime conviction (contested), assets confiscated, personal bankruptcy Nov 2025 (https://www.interfax.ru/russia/1097484). Sensitive/political (Medvedev-era oligarch). No published contacts.

name: Viren Doshi
current_role: Director, Waaree group (Waaree Renewable Technologies board; non-executive director, Waaree Indosolar); minority shareholder in Waaree Energies
profile: Mumbai-based co-promoter of the Waaree group, India's largest solar-module maker by capacity, founded by his brother Hitesh Doshi. Waaree Energies listed in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price, making Viren and his three brothers billionaires. He sits on group boards and has overseen the group's engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) business.
interesting_fact: The Waaree group his brother started with a Rs 5,000 (~$60) loan in the mid-1980s making pressure gauges is now India's largest solar-panel manufacturer, with five module plants; its 2024 IPO turned four Doshi brothers into billionaires.
notes: Low personal profile; brother Hitesh Doshi (CMD) is the public face of Waaree. Sources differ on his exact current title (Waaree Energies WTD vs. Waaree RTL director/WTD from Aug 2025) - confirm via latest BSE/NSE filings. Investor-relations address investorrelations@waaree.com is cited by third-party sites only.

name: Li Hejun
current_role: Founder of Hanergy Holding Group (former chairman); reportedly detained by police in Jinzhou, Liaoning since Dec 2022 - no current public role
profile: Li Hejun (李河君, b. 1967, Heyuan, Guangdong) is a Beijing Jiaotong University mechanical-engineering graduate who built Hanergy from hydropower into a thin-film solar group, briefly becoming China's richest man in 2015 (Forbes: $21.1B). Hanergy's Hong Kong-listed arm later collapsed; Li was barred from HK directorships and was reported detained by police in December 2022.
interesting_fact: In 2013 he published 'New Energy Revolution' (English ed. 'China's New Energy Revolution', 2014), arguing future energy competition would be over core technology rather than resources, and that thin-film solar plus the internet would drive a third industrial revolution.
deep_cut_fact: He was one of the primary sponsors and the first executive director-general of the China Red Ribbon Foundation, a special fund for HIV/AIDS prevention and treatment in China.
notes: NOT a viable outreach target: reportedly in police custody since Dec 2022 (Caixin/SCMP Jan 2023); no trial outcome found. Hanergy is defunct as a public company; HK SFC 8-year director ban. Avoid.

name: Malone Mitchell
current_role: Chairman & CEO, TransAtlantic Petroleum LLC (Turkey/Bulgaria E&P, now private); owner of Mitchell Group / Longfellow Energy
profile: West Texas oilman N. Malone Mitchell 3rd built Riata Energy (1985-2006) into one of the largest private US energy companies, then sold control to Tom Ward for about $500M; it became SandRidge Energy. He then founded Mitchell Group (Riata Management, Longfellow Energy) and has led TransAtlantic Petroleum, which produces oil and gas in Turkey.
interesting_fact: He is one of America's biggest landowners: the Land Report ranked him No. 22 with 384,000 acres, including the 350,000-acre Longfellow Ranch near his hometown of Sanderson, Texas, known for elk and mule deer hunts.
deep_cut_fact: Before Riata he worked in oilfield services and in his family's ranching and aviation businesses; he graduated from Oklahoma State University in 1983 and, while running TransAtlantic, spent much of his time on the ground in Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania.
notes: Formally N. Malone Mitchell 3rd (some filings: Noah Malone Mitchell). TransAtlantic is now an LLC (taken private), so there is no IR team; a 2013 Wall Street Transcript CEO interview exists. Last on Forbes in 2010-2011.

name: Mohammed Al Barwani
current_role: Founder and Chairman, MB Holding Company LLC (Muscat, Oman)
profile: Omani petroleum engineer (b. 1951) who founded MB Holding in 1982 as an oilfield-services firm, then expanded into oil & gas E&P (Petrogas), engineering and mining (Mawarid). He owned superyacht builder Oceanco 2010-2025 and was named Oman Air chairman in 2020.
interesting_fact: He bought superyacht builder Oceanco in 2010 after first visiting it in 2009, and sold it in 2025 to Valve founder Gabe Newell; MB's Mawarid Mining was the first private company to explore for copper and gold in Oman.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding MB he spent a decade (1976-86) as a reservoir engineer at Petroleum Development Oman (the Shell/government JV); he studied at Miami University (Ohio), UT Austin (chemical engineering) and Heriot-Watt, which gave him an honorary doctorate in petroleum engineering in 2010.
notes: mboman@ is MB Holding's general corporate inbox, not personal. Sons run MB's mining and E&P arms (Usama Al Barwani listed as CEO). Current Oman Air chair status not re-verified.

name: Donald Graham
current_role: Chairman and majority owner, Graham Holdings Company (NYSE: GHC)
profile: Donald E. Graham (b. 1945), son of Katharine Graham, was publisher of The Washington Post (1979-2000) and led the company until selling the Post to Jeff Bezos in 2013; the renamed Graham Holdings is now a diversified conglomerate (Kaplan education, TV stations, healthcare, manufacturing, auto dealerships). He was also Facebook's lead independent director (2009-2015).
interesting_fact: An early backer and mentor of Mark Zuckerberg, he served as lead independent director of Facebook's board from 2009 to 2015.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family paper he was president of The Harvard Crimson (1965), volunteered for the Army and served in Vietnam with the 1st Cavalry Division (1967-68), then worked as a patrolman in the D.C. Metropolitan Police Department from January 1969 to June 1970.
notes: Contact is the media contact named on Graham Holdings' press releases (Nov 2026). He co-founded TheDream.US (college scholarships for immigrant 'Dreamers') - not verified in this pass, but a known philanthropic route. Known as approachable to journalists.

name: Malav Ashwin Dani
current_role: Managing Director, Hitech Corporation Ltd (Dani family plastic-packaging group); member of the Asian Paints promoter (Dani) family
profile: Malav Dani is the son of the late Ashwin Dani, a long-time leader of Asian Paints, the paint company co-founded in a Mumbai garage in 1942 by four friends including his grandfather Suryakant Dani. His wealth derives mainly from the family's Asian Paints stake. He runs Hitech Corporation, a rigid plastic packaging maker founded in 1991 with 13 locations in India and a technology centre in Pune.
interesting_fact: Asian Paints began in February 1942 in a garage in Girgaon, Mumbai, started by four friends: Champaklal Choksey, Chimanlal Choksi, Suryakant Dani and Arvind Vakil. Their families still hold the controlling promoter stake.
deep_cut_fact: On Hitech's website Malav Dani sums up his management philosophy as: 'Adopting Six Sigma, we enhance customer satisfaction while embracing sustainability and global unity through Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the Sanskrit idea that 'the world is one family').
notes: His Asian Paints board status was not verified (search budget exhausted). His father Ashwin Dani died in September 2023. contact@hitechgroup.com is Hitech's general corporate inbox, not a personal address. Hitech's chairperson is his mother, Ina Dani (Hitech Specialities).

name: He Qi
current_role: Associated with 'Junhe' (trading), per Hurun; not independently verified
profile: Hurun Global listed He Qi (何旗) of China at about $1.4bn (2019-2025), with wealth from 'Junhe' in trading. I could not verify which Junhe company this is or confirm any biographical details.
notes: Unverified: the lane hit its web-search budget before this person, and Baidu Baike blocked automated access. Needs a follow-up search, e.g. Hurun profile '何旗 君和'. The name is common, so be careful matching.

name: Lu Keping
current_role: Founder/patriarch of Jiangsu Sunshine Group (wool textiles), Jiangyin; current formal title not confirmed
profile: Lu Keping (陆克平, born November 1944, Jiangyin, Jiangsu) became director of the Jiangyin Wool Mill in 1986 and built it into Sunshine Group (阳光集团), one of China's largest worsted-wool fabric and apparel makers. Its listed arm is Jiangsu Sunshine (SSE: 600220). He appeared on Hurun lists from 2005 to 2023 together with Yu Qinfen.
interesting_fact: He took over the small Jiangyin Wool Mill as factory director and party branch secretary in 1986 and grew it into Sunshine Group, often described in Chinese media as a 'wool-textile giant'.
notes: Now in his 80s and only covered in Chinese. In 2019 the CSRC fined him RMB 27.34m and imposed a lifetime securities-market ban over undisclosed control of Sihuan Bio (per Wikipedia), and the listed company is now flagged 'ST'. A reputational concern and a poor podcast fit. I could not find or verify an official group website or contact.

name: Vineet Jain
current_role: Managing Director, Bennett, Coleman & Co. Ltd (The Times Group), India
profile: Vineet Jain was born in Kolkata in 1966 and is managing director of Bennett, Coleman & Co. (The Times Group), publisher of The Times of India and The Economic Times and owner of Times Now, and India's largest media group. He joined in 1987 and, with his elder brother Samir, built it into a print, TV, digital and entertainment conglomerate. He oversees the group's day-to-day entertainment and TV businesses.
interesting_fact: He is the great-grandson of Ramkrishna Dalmia, founder of The Times Group and the Dalmia Group. His grandfather Shanti Prasad Jain, father Ashok Jain and mother Indu Jain all chaired BCCL before him.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the American College of Switzerland before joining the family business in 1987. He received the Art Karat Award in 2018.
notes: He is the public face of the Times Group, while his brother Samir is reclusive. Ken Auletta's 2012 New Yorker profile 'Citizens Jain' is the definitive long read. No published personal or office contact was found, and the web-search budget ran out before the group's corporate contact pages could be checked. He is said to post on X, but the account was not verified.

name: Vladimir Evtushenkov
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder (~49%) of AFK Sistema; stepped down from Sistema's board in April 2022
profile: Vladimir Yevtushenkov (b. 1948, Smolensk), a chemical engineer by training, left Moscow city government in 1993 to build Sistema into a conglomerate spanning telecoms (MTS), banking, retail and other assets, taking it public in London in 2005 in a then-record $1.35bn Russian IPO. After UK and Australian sanctions in 2022 he cut his stake below 50% and left the board.
interesting_fact: Sistema's 2005 London IPO, at $1.35bn, was the largest ever by a Russian company at the time.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he trained as a chemist (Mendeleev Moscow Chemical Engineering Institute, 1973) and worked as an engineer at the Karacharovo Plastics Works, then as chief engineer of the Polymerbyt research-and-production association.
notes: Under UK (Apr 2022) and Australian sanctions — journalist should check legal/compliance implications before any engagement. Sistema websites are geo/WAF-blocked from here; no published contact retrieved. Not recommended as a podcast guest.

name: Lin Wei $ family
profile: Listed by Hurun (2020-2022) with family wealth from CIFI Holdings (旭辉, HK:0884), the Shanghai-based developer founded in 2000 by the Lin family (chairman Lin Zhong). CIFI announced a suspension of US-dollar bond payments in November 2022, after which the family dropped off rich lists.
notes: Could not confirm Lin Wei's exact role at CIFI or relationship to Lin Zhong (web search quota exhausted; CIFI sites blocked). Developer is in debt restructuring: sensitive topic, low podcast fit. CIFI background: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/旭辉控股

name: Dou Wenwei
current_role: Unverified; Hurun 2021 attributes wealth to Ping An Healthcare and Technology (Ping An Good Doctor, HK:1833)
profile: Appeared only on the 2021 Hurun Global and China lists, at about $1.4bn, with wealth attributed to Ping An Healthcare and Technology (Ping An Good Doctor), the Hong Kong-listed online-health platform. I could not confirm his specific role (founder, early shareholder or executive) because the search budget ran out and no Wikipedia entry exists.
notes: Low-confidence identity. He dropped off the lists after 2021, probably because Ping An Good Doctor's share price fell sharply. Check HKEX disclosure-of-interests filings for 1833 to establish his role.

name: Liao Rongjiu
profile: Hurun (China 2014-2021, Global 2021) lists Liao Rongjiu (廖榕就), with Chen Lianying, as the owners of 'Sun City', a Chinese property developer. I couldn't identify which developer this is or find a sourced biography.
notes: Unverified: the lane's web search budget ran out and no Wikipedia page exists. Off Hurun lists since 2021, possibly because of China's property downturn. Needs a Chinese-language check before any outreach; low priority.

name: Lim Kuang Sia
current_role: Founder, Group Managing Director and CEO, Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd (Malaysia)
profile: Tan Sri Dato' Lim Kuang Sia, a chemical engineer, founded Kossan in 1979 making technical rubber parts such as cutlass bearings, moving into gloves in 1989. Kossan is now one of the world's largest makers of latex and nitrile examination gloves (capacity ~32bn pieces a year); the COVID-19 glove boom briefly made him a billionaire in 2020-21. He still runs the company as group MD/CEO.
interesting_fact: In November 2020 Kossan donated RM50 million to the Malaysian government's COVID-19 fund.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a Nanyang University chemistry degree (1975) and a master's in chemical engineering from Imperial College London (1977), and chairs the Pulau Ketam Art Association, a small fishing-island art society off Klang.
notes: Wealth has dropped since the 2021 peak (only on Hurun 2021). Active in Chinese-Malaysian chambers of commerce and Chinese independent schools; founder of Yayasan Kossan foundation. Company HQ line published: +603 5626 0888 (corporate switchboard).

name: Kang Qiao
current_role: Former actual controller of Searainbow Holding (海虹控股, 000503.SZ, now China Reform Health/国新健康); no current public role found
profile: Kang Qiao (康乔, b. ~1982, Haikou) became actual controller of Hainan-based Searainbow Holding in 2011 by buying 99% of Baijing Consulting, then the listed company's parent. Searainbow ran medical e-commerce and pharmacy-benefit services, digital entertainment (Ourgame) and chemical fiber. Hurun named Kang Hainan's richest person in 2016 (RMB 10bn, age 34). Control passed to state-owned China Reform Holdings in 2017-18.
interesting_fact: At 34 Kang topped Hainan's 2016 Hurun ranking; Searainbow, originally the state Hainan Chemical Fiber Factory, listed in Shenzhen in 1992 and owned Ourgame (联众), once among the world's largest online-game sites and an MSN Games partner.
deep_cut_fact: Kang became Searainbow's actual controller in September 2011 at just 29, when Baijing Consulting's largest holder Lin Zongqi transferred a 66% stake, giving Kang 99% of the parent; China's CNTV ran it as an '80s-generation' new rich-list entry.
notes: Identity confirmed: Hurun API (康乔, 海虹控股 Searainbow, Haikou, 2015/2017) plus CNTV/Sina. Gender conflict: Hurun says male, CNTV calls Kang 'Hainan's richest woman'; verify before outreach. Former Searainbow head Kang Jian is likely related (not verified). No longer linked to the company (now 国新健康); no published contacts.

name: Armon Dadgar
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, HashiCorp (an IBM company, within IBM Software)
profile: Co-founded HashiCorp in 2012 with University of Washington classmate Mitchell Hashimoto, building infrastructure-automation tools Terraform, Vault, Consul and Nomad. HashiCorp IPO'd in 2021 and was acquired by IBM for $6.4B in Feb 2025; Dadgar stayed on as CTO, working on Terraform/Ansible integration within IBM Software.
interesting_fact: He co-founded HashiCorp at about 24; the company name is a portmanteau of co-founder Hashimoto's surname and 'Corp', and it sold to IBM for $6.4B in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: As a student he interned at Amazon Web Services when it had only ~250 people and 'the whole thing fit on one floor' (Andy Jassy welcomed the interns). He first learned to program from a Visual Basic box set with five install CDs and a 600-page book.
notes: Press email is from 2024 HashiCorp releases (pre-IBM); post-acquisition press may route through IBM communications. Before HashiCorp he was an academic researcher at the University of Washington. Frequent podcast guest (Logan Bartlett Show ep. 102, Open Source Underdogs ep. 58).

name: Daniel Jaeggi
current_role: Co-founder & President, Mercuria Energy Group (Geneva)
profile: Swiss commodities trader (also spelled Jäggi) who co-founded Geneva-based Mercuria with Marco Dunand in 2004; it has grown into one of the world's five largest independent energy traders, spanning crude, products, gas, LNG, power and increasingly energy-transition assets. He and Dunand control the majority of the privately held firm.
interesting_fact: Mercuria's 2014 purchase of JPMorgan's physical commodities business vaulted the then 10-year-old firm into the elite club of global commodity trading houses alongside Vitol, Glencore and Trafigura.
deep_cut_fact: Jaeggi and Dunand began their careers together at Cargill International, then moved through trading roles at Goldman Sachs's J. Aron unit, Salomon Brothers (Phibro) and Sempra Energy before launching Mercuria together in 2004 - a partnership spanning roughly four decades.
notes: Very low public profile; rarely gives interviews (Dunand is the usual public face). Mercuria's contact page lists a Geneva switchboard; 2025 releases name Matt J. Lauer as press contact (no email published). Best route is Mercuria corporate communications via the contact form.

name: Marco Dunand
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Mercuria Energy Group (Geneva)
profile: Swiss commodities trader and University of Geneva economics graduate who co-founded Mercuria in Geneva in 2004 with Daniel Jaeggi after stints at Cargill, Goldman Sachs' J. Aron and Phibro/Salomon. Mercuria grew into one of the world's largest independent energy traders and is pushing into critical minerals and energy-transition assets; Dunand speaks frequently at FT, Reuters and WEF events.
interesting_fact: Bloomberg in 2014 dubbed Mercuria 'the $100 billion commodity empire that few know'; it went from startup to one of the top five independent oil traders within a decade.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Daniel Jaeggi started their careers together at Cargill in Geneva, then both moved into oil trading at Goldman Sachs' J. Aron unit, decades before founding Mercuria together.
notes: Accessible on the conference circuit (FT Commodities Summit, Reuters Events, WEF, World Government Summit) — a good podcast candidate on energy trading and transition. Mercuria site was not reachable from this session to confirm a press email; use contact form or Geneva HQ switchboard.

name: Eugene Shvidler
current_role: Private investor and owner of Château Thénac winery (France); formerly chairman of Millhouse LLC (stepped down March 2022)
profile: Born in Ufa (1964), Gubkin-trained mathematician and Fordham MBA who worked at Deloitte in New York before partnering with Roman Abramovich. He was president of Sibneft from 1998 until its $13bn sale to Gazprom in 2005, later held about 5% of steelmaker Evraz and chaired Abramovich's Millhouse. He holds British and US citizenship.
interesting_fact: As Sibneft president (1998-2005) he ran what was, for most of his tenure, Russia's fastest-growing oil company by production and its most profitable per barrel, before Gazprom bought it for $13bn.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious winemaker: in 2000 he bought Château Thénac near Bergerac, built on the ruins of a monastery founded in 1109, and told The Guardian he wanted 'first-class wine that will rival anything neighbouring Bordeaux has to offer'.
notes: High-risk outreach: under UK sanctions since March 2022 (High Court 2023 and Court of Appeal 2024 rejected his challenges). Does not like being called an oligarch. Very private; no personal press office found. The winery is the only published channel. Listing says energy/Evraz but he is no longer active in Russian energy.

name: Ge Zhiyong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Wuxi Autowell Technology (ATW; Shanghai STAR Market 688516)
profile: Ge Zhiyong (葛志勇) is the controlling shareholder (with concert party Li Wen), chairman and GM of Wuxi Autowell, founded 2010. It makes automation equipment for solar module and cell production (notably cell stringers), plus lithium-battery and semiconductor equipment. Hurun listed him as a billionaire 2021-23 at the peak of the solar boom.
interesting_fact: Autowell only entered the PV business in 2012, yet its flagship multi-busbar (MBB) cell soldering stringer now claims over 70% market share, with customers including Jinko, JA Solar, Trina, Longi, Tongwei and India's Tata and Adani (company claim).
notes: Low media profile; no sourced personal biography found online. Not on Hurun since 2023 (solar equipment downturn). Best route: company IR mailbox (listed in the 2024 annual report summary; board secretary Zhou Yongxiu).

name: Rusteem Sulteev
current_role: Former co-owner and first deputy general director of TAIF Group (Kazan); TAIF was merged into SIBUR in 2021 (now Sibur-RT) - current formal role unclear
profile: Kazan-born (1954) civil engineer who joined TAIF as first deputy general director in 1995 and became a co-owner, alongside Albert Shigabutdinov and Radik Shaimiev, of the Tatarstan oil, gas and petrochemicals group (Kazanorgsintez, Nizhnekamskneftekhim, TGK-16). Through TAIF's 2021 combination with SIBUR he became a SIBUR shareholder; he also co-owns Kazan's Avers Bank.
interesting_fact: TAIF, which he co-owned, was one of Russia's largest private petrochemical groups before its 2021 merger with SIBUR; its shareholders received a stake in SIBUR Holding in the deal.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as a construction foreman after graduating from the Kazan Institute of Civil Engineering in 1976; one of his first major projects was building a factory for the bread and baking industry, and in 1984 he was deputy director for construction of Kazan's second bakery plant.
notes: Name usually spelled Rustem Sulteev. Very private; no public contact channels found. Listed in sanctions databases (OpenSanctions: https://opensanctions.org/entities/Q55759794) - check legal/sanctions implications before any outreach. Alive status not confirmed by recent news (no death reports found).

name: Tang Jinkui
current_role: Vice Chairman, Shenghong Group (盛虹集团), Suzhou; shareholder in Jiangsu Eastern Shenghong (SZSE: 000301)
profile: Suzhou-based self-made businessman (age ~71) and long-time No. 2 to chairman Miao Hangen at Shenghong Group, which grew from a Shengze silk-weaving/dyeing mill into a polyester-fibre and petrochemicals conglomerate. Its fibre arm backdoor-listed in Shanghai/Shenzhen in 2018 as Jiangsu Eastern Shenghong.
interesting_fact: Eastern Shenghong now runs a 16 Mt/yr integrated refining-petrochemical complex plus methanol-to-olefins and propane dehydrogenation units, and markets itself as moving into 'new energy new materials' such as EVA for solar panels.
notes: Very low public profile; Forbes lists him as 'Tang Jinkui & family', vice chairman of Shenghong Group (Forbes profile). Miao Hangen is the group's public face. Only realistic route is Eastern Shenghong's securities-affairs mailbox. No verifiable personal anecdotes found.

name: Roland Duchatelet
current_role: Non-executive director, X-FAB Silicon Foundries SE; co-controlling shareholder (via Elex) of Melexis and X-FAB
profile: Belgian engineer-entrepreneur (b. 1946, Merksem) who in 1989 formed holding Elex with Rudi De Winter and Francoise Chombar, taking over automotive-sensor maker Melexis (1994) and specialty foundry X-FAB (1999); the families still jointly control both listed firms. He founded the Vivant party, was a senator 2007-10, and has owned several football clubs.
interesting_fact: He has owned a string of football clubs - Sint-Truiden, Standard Liege, Charlton Athletic, AD Alcorcon and Ujpest - and remains main shareholder of Germany's FC Carl Zeiss Jena.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Elex he was a marketing manager at German chipmaker Elmos Semiconductor (1985-89); his 1993 book 'NV Belgie, verslag aan de aandeelhouders' (Belgium Inc., a report to the shareholders) spent ten weeks in Belgium's non-fiction top ten and argued for a basic income.
notes: X-FAB's published IR & PR contact (Uta Steinbrecher) is the cleanest corporate route; Melexis also has an IR page (melexis.com/en/investors). Avoid leading with his football-ownership era, which was contentious with fans (Charlton, Standard).

name: Liu Jianfang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Jiangsu Gao Kai Precision Fluid Technology (Shanghai STAR: 688835)
profile: Former Jilin University mechanical engineering professor who founded Gao Kai in Wujin, Changzhou in 2013 to commercialise piezoelectric drive and precision fluid-control technology (flow controllers, jet dispensing, coating) used in chip and electronics manufacturing; customers include BYD, CATL and Foxconn. Gao Kai listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in Aug 2026, jumping ~240% on debut.
interesting_fact: He left a tenured professorship at 38, taking several graduate students with him, and started the company with just 2 million yuan of registered capital to attack a market then almost monopolised by foreign piezo-jet dispensing brands.
deep_cut_fact: During his PhD (Jilin, 2002-05) he spent a year at Yamagata University in Japan studying piezoelectric drive and vibration control under Katsumi Watanabe and Katsuyoshi Suzuki; his research line traces to his mentor Prof. Yang Zhigang, who pioneered Jilin's piezo-drive work in 1992.
notes: Newly minted billionaire (Aug 2026 IPO). No personal/press contact found in this pass; company IR/board-secretary contacts should be in the STAR Market prospectus or SSE filings for 688835. Some English sources call the company 'Gaoke'/'Gaokai'.

name: Aluru Jagadish Prasad
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, HBL Engineering Ltd (formerly HBL Power Systems), Hyderabad
profile: Dr. Aluru Jagadish Prasad founded what is now HBL Engineering in 1977 in Hyderabad, starting with aircraft batteries for the Indian Air Force. The company now makes specialised batteries (for aircraft, data centres, submarines, missiles and tanks), defence electronics, e-mobility drivetrains and the Kavach train collision-avoidance system for Indian Railways; he remains CMD.
interesting_fact: HBL's batteries go into aircraft, data centres, submarines, missiles and battle tanks, and the company also builds train collision-avoidance systems for Indian Railways - a mix of defence, rail and backup-power tech that started with one IAF aircraft battery in 1977.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting HBL he worked at the Administrative Staff College of India in Hyderabad; he holds a B.Tech from IIT Kharagpur, an MS in Management from MIT and a doctorate in international business from Columbia University (per HBL's 2023-24 annual report).
notes: Aged about 78 in 2024. HBL's battery energy storage (BESS) and data-centre battery lines fit the podcast's energy/data-centre angle. Best route is the company's general address contact@hbl.in or investor@hbl.in (company secretary).

name: Wu Ming
current_role: Co-founder and part of the controlling shareholder group of Fourth Paradigm (4Paradigm, HKEX-listed AI company); not listed in current executive team
profile: Wu Ming (吴茗, Phairy Wu) co-founded enterprise-AI company Fourth Paradigm in 2014 with her husband Dai Wenyuan (ex-Baidu, Huawei Noah's Ark) and AI scholar Yang Qiang. It listed in Hong Kong in 2023. Before the IPO, Dai, Wu and affiliated vehicles controlled about 41% of the company.
interesting_fact: Fourth Paradigm was the first AI startup to win investment from all five of China's big state banks (ICBC, ABC, BOC, CCB and BoCom), and raised a $700M Series D in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Fourth Paradigm she studied at Huazhong University of Science and Technology in Wuhan and worked at Baidu, the same company where Dai Wenyuan ran the Fengchao ad-ranking system.
notes: Low public profile; 36Kr marks her as a former co-founder who has left operating roles. Her husband Dai Wenyuan (chairman/CEO) is the public face. Approach via Fourth Paradigm PR/IR. One source describes her as also an investment partner at Sequoia China, but the wording is ambiguous and unverified.

name: Tong Yongsheng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical Co. (SZSE: 002851)
profile: Power-electronics engineer (b. 1964) who left senior roles at Huawei Electric and Emerson Network Power to take over loss-making Megmeet in 2005, turning it into a profitable maker of power supplies, industrial automation, EV and smart-appliance controls. Megmeet says it helped design power systems for NVIDIA's Blackwell platform and is building plants in Thailand, India and the US.
interesting_fact: Megmeet announced in 2024 that it participated in designing NVIDIA's Blackwell system, making it one of NVIDIA's 40-plus equipment suppliers for data centers.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in aviation electrical engineering from Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and did a power-electronics postdoc at Zhejiang University; he was a vice president of Shenzhen Huawei Electric (1996-2001) and stayed on as VP at Emerson Network Power (2001-05) after Emerson bought that unit.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center/energy podcast (AI server power supplies for NVIDIA). IR email from the 2025 annual report summary. The Huawei-to-Emerson detail reflects Emerson's 2001 acquisition of Huawei Electric (Avansys); his own resume confirms the role sequence.

name: Zhang Shengwei
current_role: Founder and majority owner, Shenzhen iMiracle Technology (maker of Elf Bar and Lost Mary vapes)
