profile: Zhang Shengwei founded Shenzhen iMiracle Technology, part of the Heaven Gifts group, whose Elf Bar brand (launched 2018) became the world's best-selling disposable e-cigarette by 2023, alongside sister brand Lost Mary. He also holds stakes in the firms behind Air Bar and Geekvape. He keeps an extremely low public profile.
interesting_fact: iMiracle was expected to generate up to $4bn in revenue in 2023. In the UK alone, Elf Bar and Lost Mary sold more than £900m of vapes in 12 months, according to NielsenIQ.
deep_cut_fact: Before vaping, Zhang was a cross-border e-commerce seller who sold kitchenware and clothing on eBay.
notes: Very private, with almost no interviews. The brand's PR inbox is the only published route. The vaping industry is under heavy regulatory scrutiny (UK disposable-vape ban, US FDA actions); be mindful of framing in outreach.

name: Adrian Paval
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Dragoș), Dedeman and Pavăl Holding, Romania
profile: Adrian Pavăl and his brother Dragoș founded DIY and building-materials retailer Dedeman in Bacău in 1992. It grew into Romania's market leader, overtaking Praktiker in 2010, and now has about 60+ stores, over 12,000 staff and roughly $2bn in sales. Through Pavăl Holding they invest in offices in Bucharest and Cluj, listed Romanian stocks (Romgaz, Transelectrica, Banca Transilvania) and a private equity fund.
interesting_fact: Dedeman had just 11 employees in 1994 and over 12,000 today. About 85% of its 60,000+ in-store products come from Romanian suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: Their holding launched Grunman Energy to put solar power on the rooftops of Dedeman's seven logistics centres. They also hold stakes in grid operator Transelectrica and gas producer Romgaz, a quiet energy angle in a retail fortune.
notes: The Pavăl brothers are famously media-shy and rarely give interviews. The only published channel is Dedeman's corporate contact page. The energy holdings (Transelectrica, Romgaz, rooftop solar) offer a podcast hook.

name: Jordi Rubiralta
current_role: Board member (former President 2012-2019), Werfen; head of family office Yukon Capital
profile: Jordi Rubiralta's fortune comes from Werfen, the Barcelona-based in-vitro diagnostics group (hemostasis, acute care, autoimmunity, transfusion) that his father José María Rubiralta founded as Izasa in 1966. He became president in 2012 and led acquisitions of TEM (Germany, 2016) and Accriva Diagnostics (US, 2017), before handing the presidency to Marc Rubiralta in 2019. He remains on the board, and his family office Yukon Capital is active in Spanish real estate.
interesting_fact: Werfen began in 1966 as Izasa, a small Barcelona distributor of clinical diagnostic products. It moved into manufacturing in 1973 with Biokit and became a global player in 1991 by buying Boston-based Instrumentation Laboratory.
deep_cut_fact: Werfen's own timeline marks his 2012 appointment as president as its official 'Generational Change' milestone. During his presidency the company built a new Iberian logistics centre in Cuenca (2016) and new Biokit facilities near Barcelona (2017).
notes: Werfen is headquartered in L'Hospitalet de Llobregat (Barcelona), not Madrid as Forbes states. He keeps a low profile. No press email is published, so the contact form is the route; Yukon Capital might also be reachable. Web-search quota ran out, so this relies on Forbes and the Werfen site.

name: Yasseen Mansour
current_role: Chairman, Palm Hills Developments (EGX: PHDC); shareholder, Mansour Group
profile: Yasseen Mansour is the youngest son of Loutfy Mansour, who founded Egypt's Mansour Group in 1952. The group is the exclusive distributor of GM vehicles and Caterpillar equipment in Egypt and several other countries and holds Egypt's McDonald's franchise. He shares ownership with his billionaire brothers Mohamed and Youssef. He co-founded the Mansour-Maghraby real-estate partnership and chairs Palm Hills Developments, one of Egypt's biggest real-estate developers.
interesting_fact: Mansour Group is the sole McDonald's franchisee in Egypt as well as the exclusive distributor of GM vehicles and Caterpillar equipment.
deep_cut_fact: A George Washington University graduate, he joined the family's Mansour Motors in 1986. He later co-founded Mansour & Maghraby Investment Development, a 60:40 venture with his cousin's Maghraby Group, which became majority owner of Palm Hills.
notes: The Palm Hills site has an online inquiry form but shows no published IR email. His Wikipedia page notes 2011 legal issues and the Suisse Secrets leak, so avoid those. Some reports have linked him to Al Ahly club leadership, but this was not verified, so check before mentioning.

name: Jenny Lindén Urnes
current_role: Chair and owner, Lindéngruppen AB (Höganäs, Sweden)
profile: Born 1971, Lindén Urnes inherited Lindéngruppen from her father Ulf G. Lindén, an ex-Volvo executive who bought Beckers and built a stake in Höganäs AB. The family group now owns Beckers (coil and industrial coatings), Colart (Winsor & Newton, Liquitex), Alex Begg (cashmere) and parts of Höganäs (world's largest metal-powder maker) and oat-ingredient maker cReal; combined 2025 turnover was about SEK 19.5bn.
interesting_fact: Höganäs is the world's largest producer of metal powder (about a third of the global market), used in components and to remove contaminants from drinking water; in 2013 she and a Wallenberg-linked foundation took it private.
deep_cut_fact: She studied art history (BA, Heythrop College, University of London, 1995), chairs the Färgfabriken contemporary-art foundation in Stockholm, and in 2015 was made an honorary doctor of Lund University School of Economics and Management.
notes: Forbes says she majored in philosophy; Swedish Wikipedia says art history at Heythrop (a philosophy/theology college) — wording kept neutral. Group has a sustainability focus ('lead the transformation to a sustainable world'), a good podcast hook. Also breeds horses (Forbes).

name: Katie Rodan
current_role: Co-founder, Rodan + Fields; adjunct clinical professor of dermatology, Stanford University
profile: Stanford-trained dermatologist who, with partner Kathy Fields, created acne treatment Proactiv (1995) and later launched skincare company Rodan + Fields (2002), which Estée Lauder bought in 2003 and the founders bought back in 2007. TPG bought a 25% stake in 2018 for $1bn. She also teaches at Stanford and has practiced dermatology in the East Bay.
interesting_fact: She and Fields sold their Proactiv royalties in 2016 to a Guthy-Renker/Nestlé joint venture, two decades after inventing the product.
deep_cut_fact: She met Kathy Fields as a Stanford dermatology resident in 1984 and finished the residency in 1987 as chief resident; the pair later co-wrote four consumer skincare books, including 'Unblemished' (2008).
notes: No personal published contact found; route via Rodan + Fields corporate. Avoid MLM-criticism topic. Dropped off Forbes lists after 2020.

name: Liu Zhiqiang
current_role: Chairman, Heung Kong Group (香江集团), Guangzhou-based conglomerate
profile: Co-founded Heung Kong Group in 1990 with his wife Zhai Meiqing, who is its president and chairs the listed Shenzhen Heungkong Holding. The Guangzhou-based group grew in real estate and furniture and home-goods retail, then expanded into finance and health care. He has appeared on Hurun's China list continuously since 2004.
interesting_fact: The couple's philanthropy is unusually prominent for a Chinese developer family: his co-founder and wife Zhai Meiqing received the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy in New York in 2017.
notes: His wife Zhai Meiqing is the group's public face and runs its charity work, so she is the more accessible contact. The corporate sites I tried (heungkong.com.cn and others) did not respond, and the search budget ran out before I could find a verified press contact or a sourced deep-cut fact.

name: Clelia Haji-Ioannou
current_role: Private investor (easyJet shareholder, European real estate); board member, Cyprus Marine Environment Protection Association (CYMEPA)
profile: Born in Athens in 1970, Clelia Haji-Ioannou is the daughter of Greek Cypriot tanker magnate Loucas Haji-Ioannou and the sister of easyJet founder Stelios and of Polys. Her fortune comes from her inherited easyJet stake plus European property in London, Monaco and Greece. She lives in Monaco, collects art (her gallery outside Athens shows Picasso, Warhol and Dalí) and serves on CYMEPA's board.
interesting_fact: She oversaw publication of a biography of her father, 'Loucas Haji-Ioannou: The King of the Tankers'.
deep_cut_fact: She studied Banking and International Finance at City, University of London. Its Bayes Business School now offers a master's scholarship in her name, the Clelia Haji-Ioannou Scholarship.

public_contacts.value: https://www.cymepa.org.cy/en/history (CYMEPA, the marine-protection NGO on whose board she sits)

notes: Very private, with no personal social accounts or office contact found. The marine-environment (CYMEPA) and art-collecting angles are the best hooks. Scholarship page: https://www.bayes.citystgeorges.ac.uk/study/masters/funding-your-study/scholarships/the-clelia-haji-ioannou-scholarship (blocked by bot protection, not read).

name: Cheng Wei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, DiDi Global (Beijing Xiaoju Technology)
profile: Cheng Wei (程维, b. 1983, Shangrao, Jiangxi) spent about eight years at Alibaba, rising to a deputy GM role in Alipay's B2C unit, before founding ride-hailing app Didi Dache in 2012 at age 29. Didi merged with Kuaidi, drove Uber out of China in 2016 and expanded into robotaxis, EV and mobility services; it delisted from NYSE in 2022 and trades OTC.
interesting_fact: Didi famously 'tamed Uber': in 2016 Uber sold its China business to Didi in exchange for a stake in the combined company, after a costly subsidy war.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alibaba he drifted through odd jobs, including as an assistant to the head of a foot-massage chain; he was ill on the day of China's gaokao but still won a place at Beijing University of Chemical Technology, studying administration.
notes: Input's SEC link (TSMC Chairman & CEO) is a mismatch: that is C.C. Wei (Wei Che-chia) of TSMC, a different person. Cheng Wei keeps a low media profile post-2021 regulatory crackdown; route via DiDi corporate/IR.

name: Hu Wei
current_role: Director and Vice General Manager, StarPower Semiconductor (Jiaxing; SSE: 603290)
profile: Hu Wei (female) co-founded StarPower Semiconductor in Jiaxing, Zhejiang, in 2005 with husband and chairman Shen Hua after both returned from the US. StarPower makes IGBT and SiC power-semiconductor chips and modules for EVs, solar/storage and industrial drives; listed in Shanghai in 2020. The couple jointly control ~41.7%.
interesting_fact: StarPower was ranked fifth in the global IGBT module market by Omdia (2023), a field that was dominated by foreign firms when the couple started the company in 2005.
deep_cut_fact: She earned a master's in Engineering-Economic Systems from Stanford in 1994, then spent 1995-2001 at US credit-card issuer Providian Financial as marketing director, assistant to an executive SVP and corporate strategy manager before co-founding StarPower.
notes: Wealth is shared with husband Shen Hua (chairman/GM, the public face). Both reportedly hold US nationality. Route via StarPower board secretary/IR (Jiaxing HQ). Highly relevant to EV/solar/data-center power electronics.

name: Zhong Fenghao
current_role: Director and early co-founding shareholder, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology Co., Ltd. (300604.SZ)
profile: Zhong Fenghao (钟锋浩) is a director and long-time major shareholder (~5%) of Hangzhou Changchuan Technology, founded in 2008 by Zhao Yi, which makes semiconductor test equipment (testers and handlers) used by Chinese packaging/test houses such as JCET and Tongfu. The company's market value surged in 2025-26 on chip/AI demand and it is pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: Changchuan's equipment sits at the last step of chip mass production: every chip is tested and sorted before shipping, and Changchuan builds the machines for both steps; four of its original six non-independent directors came from Silan Microelectronics.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Changchuan, he was manager of the test-equipment development department at Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics, the chipmaker where founder Zhao Yi was production director; Silan later became a Changchuan customer.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Not the chairman (founder Zhao Yi controls the company). Best route is company IR/board secretary. Sold ~0.97m shares in Jan 2026, dropping below 5%; not relevant to outreach.

name: brother
current_role: Unnamed brother of Mikhail Gutseriev in Forbes' family listing; most likely Sait-Salam Gutseriev, who took over family oil/coal stakes (e.g. Russneft via Vemonar Holdings) in 2021-22
profile: Forbes' 'mikhail-gutseriev-brother' entry (Forbes 2021; real-time 2023) does not name the brother, and the slug now resolves to Mikhail Gutseriev's own profile (Safmar Group: oil, coal, real estate, retail). Reporting shows Mikhail's younger brother Sait-Salam received his 37.15% Russneft stake in Aug 2021 via Cyprus-based Vemonar Holdings and was beneficial owner of Russian Coal until Aug 2022.
interesting_fact: The family's Safmar Group also owns Moscow's Hotel National, where Donald Trump stayed on his first Russia visit in 1987 (from Forbes' facts on Mikhail Gutseriev).
notes: Not a separate, named person in Forbes; treat as part of the Mikhail Gutseriev family fortune. Sait-Salam link is inferred from Russneft/Russian Coal ownership reports (e.g. https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/90211/), not from Forbes. Mikhail is sanctioned by the UK/EU (2021) over ties to Lukashenko; reputational risk is high and no contacts are appropriate.

name: Joachim Goldbeck
current_role: CEO / managing director, GOLDBECK SOLAR GmbH (Hirschberg an der Bergstrasse); co-owner (~1/3) of the Goldbeck construction group
profile: Son of Ortwin Goldbeck, founder (1969) of Bielefeld-based Goldbeck, one of Germany's largest builders of factories, warehouses, offices and car parks; he and his two brothers (the group's co-CEOs) each own about a third. Joachim himself runs GOLDBECK SOLAR, an international EPC, developer and operator of utility-scale, commercial-roof and agri-PV solar plants plus battery storage, which describes itself as one of Europe's most valuable solar companies.
interesting_fact: GOLDBECK SOLAR runs its own engineering podcast, 'Inside Solar Engineering'; in episode 1 Joachim Goldbeck discussed large-scale PV construction challenges, storage, inverter selection and grid connection.
deep_cut_fact: Rather than joining the family construction business's management, he built his own solar company, which now also does O&M for battery storage, PPAs and agri-PV with dynamic trackers - and built an agri-PV park at its own Hirschberg headquarters; it works with Fraunhofer on research projects.

public_contacts.value: Inside Solar Engineering (GOLDBECK SOLAR company podcast)

notes: Top-priority fit for an energy podcast: he is CEO of a large solar/BESS EPC (not just a passive heir as Forbes implies) and already does podcasts. The company's press kit offers his official photos. Imprint lists him and COO Tobias Schüßler as legal representatives.

name: Gao Xingjiang
current_role: Chairman, Yongxing Special Materials Technology (永兴材料, SZSE: 002756), Huzhou, Zhejiang
profile: A former PLA Navy serviceman (1981-87), he founded Yongxing in July 2000 as a maker of stainless steel and nickel-alloy bars and wire rods. It is a top-3 Chinese supplier, listed in 2015. He then pivoted the company into lithium: Yongxing mines lepidolite in Yichun, Jiangxi, is a leading Chinese producer of battery-grade lithium carbonate from mica, and also makes lithium-titanate batteries for storage.
interesting_fact: Yongxing has invested in 超磁新能 (Chaoci Xinneng, Shanghai), a high-temperature-superconducting magnet startup for fusion. It built its first HTS pancake coil and is working toward a 25-tesla toroidal-field model magnet for controlled fusion.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an industrialist, Gao served six years in the People's Liberation Army Navy (1981-1987).
notes: Strong energy angle: lithium carbonate, energy storage batteries and a fusion-magnet investment. The company site has an online message form; investor contact is also available via the SZSE interactive platform (互动易). Little English-language coverage of him personally.

name: Liu Zhenfeng
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group Co., Ltd. (002353.SZ)
profile: Liu Zhenfeng (刘贞峰, b. 1961) co-founded Jereh in 1999 with Sun Weijie and Wang Kunxiao, and has served as its vice president, director and 'meritorious adviser'. Jereh grew from a parts trader into a major maker of fracturing and oilfield equipment, listed in Shenzhen in 2010, and is now selling gas-fired power generation to data centers. He was re-elected to Jereh's board in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Jereh, best known for oilfield fracturing equipment, won a US$100 million order for generator sets from a North American data center in November 2025, a sign of oilfield-equipment makers moving into AI power.
deep_cut_fact: Liu trained in computer science at the University of Science and Technology Beijing. Jereh started in 1999 as Yantai Jereh Equipment, a small trader in imported mining spare parts, long before it built its own oilfield machinery.
notes: Low public profile. The computer-science detail comes from his exchange-filed resume (Eastmoney F10: emweb.securities.eastmoney.com ... code=SZ002353). zqb@jereh.com is Jereh's registered securities-affairs office email. Chairman is Li Zhiyong and president is Sun Weijie.

name: Jack Cogen
current_role: Private investor; early backer and director of CoreWeave from Sept 2017 until he chose not to stand for re-election at the June 8, 2026 annual meeting
profile: Jack D. Cogen founded and ran Natsource Asset Management (1994-2014), one of the largest private greenhouse-gas/environmental-markets asset managers. Two later CoreWeave cofounders (incl. CEO Michael Intrator) worked at Natsource and at gas hedge fund Hudson Ridge, where he was a director; he became an early CoreWeave investor and board member, owning ~5% at its 2025 IPO.
interesting_fact: CoreWeave started in 2017 as a crypto-mining operation run by former natural-gas/carbon traders before pivoting to GPU cloud for AI customers such as Microsoft and OpenAI; Cogen backed and served on its board for more than eight years.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the International Emissions Trading Association (IETA) from 2008 to 2011 and remains an IETA Fellow; academically he holds an M.S. in Mathematics as well as an MBA from NYU, plus a B.A. from Rutgers.
notes: Left CoreWeave's board in June 2026, so CoreWeave channels are now indirect; no personal/family-office contact published. Great podcast angle: carbon markets -> natural gas -> AI data centers. Low public profile.

name: Lim Kaling
current_role: Non-executive director and major shareholder, Razer; head of the Lim Teck Lee family group (Singapore)
profile: Lim Kaling (62, Singapore; BBA, UC Berkeley) was an early backer of gaming-hardware brand Razer, co-founded by Min-Liang Tan in 2005, and is its non-executive director. Razer listed in Hong Kong in 2017, raising $529m, and Lim and Tan took it private in 2022 at a $3.2bn valuation. He also runs the Lim Teck Lee group, a family business in real estate, manufacturing and trading.
interesting_fact: He and Razer co-founder Min-Liang Tan took Razer private in 2022, five years after its $529m Hong Kong IPO, in a deal valuing it at $3.2bn.
notes: Very private and rarely interviewed; Min-Liang Tan is Razer's public face. Razer's press office is the only published route and will only answer press. Web-search quota ran out before I could find a sourced personal deep-cut fact.

name: Wang Aiguo
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Qingdao Gon Technology (国恩股份; SZSE 002768, HKEX-listed 2025); Chairman, Baotou Dongbao Bio-tech
profile: Wang Aiguo founded and runs Qingdao Gon Technology, a Qingdao group set up in December 2000 that makes modified and composite engineering plastics for home appliances, cars, electronics and new-energy uses. It listed in Shenzhen in 2015 and in Hong Kong in 2025. He also chairs Baotou Dongbao Bio-tech, a maker of gelatin, capsules and collagen, part of Gon's second 'big health' pillar.
interesting_fact: Gon runs on 'two wings': chemical new materials (including new-energy and display materials and artificial sports turf) and biomedical health (pharmaceutical gelatin, hollow capsules, collagen peptides).
notes: His name is very common and Chinese Wikipedia lists only unrelated people called 王爱国, so identify him by the company. No published email was found; the company's A-share and H-share investor-relations pages, linked from the site, are the formal route. The new-energy materials business is a possible angle for an energy show.

name: Burhan Karim
current_role: Director, Musim Mas Holdings (Singapore-based integrated palm oil group)
profile: Burhan Karim (Lim Ek Kian) runs Musim Mas with his brothers Bachtiar and Bahari. Their late father Anwar founded the Nam Cheong Soap Factory in Medan in 1932; the family opened Indonesia's first palm oil refinery in 1970 and set up Musim Mas in 1972. The group now operates in 14 countries across plantations, refining, oleochemicals, biodiesel and consumer products.
interesting_fact: Musim Mas says it was the first major oil palm group to have all its Indonesian plantations with mills 100% RSPO-certified (2012) and the first palm oil major verified by the Palm Oil Innovation Group (2019); it also runs what it calls Indonesia's largest smallholder programme.
notes: Very private family; brother Bachtiar Karim is the more visible family member. Energy angle: Musim Mas makes biodiesel and has a net-zero commitment. No published press email found. Web search budget ran out before a personal deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Li Wa
current_role: Chairman, Excellence Group (卓越集团), Shenzhen (per Forbes; not re-verified)
profile: Shenzhen property developer whose Excellence Group has built commercial and residential projects in 14 Chinese cities since he entered real estate in 1992; he owns about 95% of Cayman-registered Excellence Real Estate Group. He dropped off Forbes' list after 2024.
interesting_fact: Excellence Group develops both office towers and housing across 14 Chinese cities, with brother Li Xiaoping as a vice president.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into property in 1992, he spent the first five years of his career, in the mid-1980s, working for the Communist Youth League.
notes: Very private; no official website or contact verified (web search quota exhausted). Avoid the 2019 investigation episode. Low podcast fit.

name: Bhikhabai Virani
current_role: Co-founder and director, Balaji Wafers Pvt. Ltd. (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: One of the Virani brothers (also spelled Bhikhubhai) who built Balaji Wafers from a wafer stall at Rajkot's Astron Cinema into one of India's largest regional snack makers, dominant in Gujarat and western India. The family has run it with brothers Chandubhai and Kanubhai/Kanjibhai. Selling a minority stake to General Atlantic in January 2026 made them billionaires.
interesting_fact: The business began in 1974 in the canteen of Astron Cinema in Rajkot, and the brand is named after a Balaji temple next to the cinema. Wafers were made at the family home until 1989.
deep_cut_fact: Before snacks, the brothers put the 20,000 rupees their father gave them from selling ancestral farmland into a farm-equipment venture, and it failed. They opened their first wafer factory at Aji GIDC near Rajkot in 1989 and incorporated Balaji Wafers Pvt Ltd in 1992.
notes: The email is the company's general contact address published on its homepage, not a dedicated press line. Chandubhai Virani is the public face of the business. The brothers speak mainly Gujarati, so expect a Gujarati-language approach. Spellings vary: Bhikhabhai/Bhikhubhai. Not an energy fit; better as a classic bootstrapped-entrepreneur story.

name: Réal Plourde
current_role: Co-founder and Corporate Director, Alimentation Couche-Tard (Circle K)
profile: Engineer (Université Laval, HEC Montréal MBA) who joined Couche-Tard in 1984. He helped build it from a Quebec convenience chain into the global Circle K operator with 17,000+ stores and about $73B in revenue, serving as COO and EVP and as chairman 2011-2014. He retired from management in 2011 and still sits on the board. One of four co-founders made billionaires by the company.
interesting_fact: Couche-Tard has made four of its co-founders billionaires: Alain Bouchard, Richard Fortin, Jacques D'Amours and Plourde.
deep_cut_fact: Before Couche-Tard he worked on engineering projects in Canada and Africa. In 2018 he and his wife Ariane Riou received the Lieutenant Governor's Seniors Medal for volunteer work, notably at the palliative care home in Laval.
notes: Low-profile Quebec engineer, so his engineering background and EV-charging/fuel-retail transition are natural podcast hooks (Circle K runs EV chargers). Route through Couche-Tard corporate communications.

name: Wang Lekang
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Shenzhen Sunmoon Microelectronics (明微电子, SSE STAR: 688699); re-elected Oct 2025
profile: Born 1966, Wang Lekang is a senior electronics engineer who founded Shenzhen Sunmoon Microelectronics in October 2003, a fabless designer of LED display/lighting driver ICs now listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. He controls about 38% of the company directly and via holding company Shenzhen Mingwei Technology, and was re-elected chairman and GM in October 2025.
interesting_fact: He remains both founder-chairman and general manager more than two decades after starting Sunmoon, holding ~9.8% directly and ~27.9% indirectly as actual controller.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Sunmoon he worked as an engineer at SAST Shenfei Laser Optical Systems (先科深飞激光光学系统), then at Guowei Technology (国微科技) as office director, sales director and assistant to the GM.
notes: Low public profile; best route is the board secretary/IR office (Ir@chinaasic.com). Company website domain chinaasic.com.

name: Liu Chengyu
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Kstar Science & Technology (科士达, SZSE: 002518)
profile: Liu Chengyu joined Kstar's predecessor in 1993 and rose to run and control it. Kstar, listed in Shenzhen since 2010, makes UPS systems, data-center power and cooling infrastructure, solar inverters and energy-storage systems. He remains chairman and GM, and was renominated to the board in late 2025.
interesting_fact: Kstar sits right at the podcast's intersection: it supplies uninterruptible power, precision cooling and modular data-center infrastructure, and also builds PV inverters and battery storage.
deep_cut_fact: After university he taught at Xiapu No. 6 Middle School in Fujian. Kstar began as Fujian Xiapu Kstar Electronics in that coastal county before moving to Shenzhen. He later earned an EMBA at Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

public_contacts.value: stock@kstar.com.cn (company IR mailbox; board secretary Fan Tao fantao1@kstar.com.cn, tel 0755-86168479)

notes: Fellow director Liu Ling (also a former Xiapu schoolteacher) is co-controller. Low media profile; IR mailbox/board secretary is the formal route. Data-center power angle makes him a strong fit.

name: Andrei Kuzyaev
current_role: President and CEO, ER-Telecom Holding (Dom.ru); main owner and chairman of Luch Capital (formerly Perm Financial and Industrial Group)
profile: Perm-born economist turned oil and telecom magnate. In the 1990s his Perm Financial and Industrial Group bought into Permneft, and he ran Lukoil-Perm before selling the stake to Lukoil in 2003. He then led Lukoil Overseas, Lukoil's international upstream arm, and was a Lukoil vice-president. Since 2015 he has run ER-Telecom, Russia's third-largest broadband provider (Dom.ru).
interesting_fact: He was a Lukoil veteran who ran its international upstream division, Lukoil Overseas, from December 2000 and was a Lukoil vice-president. In 2015 he switched to running ER-Telecom full time.
deep_cut_fact: As a Perm State University economics student he set up his own student work brigade, 'Sever', which collected logs washed onto the banks of the Vishera river and shipped them to a pulp mill. He also created Perm's first student research squad doing contract research, and graduated in 1987 with honours.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK since Feb 2025 under the Russia regime, and earlier by Ukraine; outreach may raise compliance issues. ER-Telecom's press pages render in JavaScript and list no email. A 2020 release named a Dom.ru press secretary, but that contact is outdated and personal, so it is not listed. He also founded Perm's Stroganov Club and chaired the Russia-Venezuela business council.

name: Wang Yuxian
current_role: Investor; controlling partner (~72%) of Xinrui Jicheng (Xiamen) Venture Capital LP, a founding shareholder of Semight Instruments (688808.SH)
profile: Wang Yuxian (王育贤) is a Fujian-linked private investor whose wealth comes from Semight Instruments, the Suzhou maker of optical-communication and semiconductor test gear that soared after its 2026 STAR Market IPO. He holds it through Xinrui Jicheng (Xiamen) VC LP, one of Semight's promoter shareholders at its 2022 conversion to a joint-stock company. Hurun 2026 values him at RMB 8.8bn.
interesting_fact: Semight, his main holding, supplies test equipment to AI-optics leaders such as Innolight and Eoptolink, and its shares passed RMB 2,000 in 2026, making it the most expensive stock on the A-share market.
deep_cut_fact: His vehicle Xinrui Jicheng (Xiamen) Venture Capital is named among Semight's original promoter shareholders in the company's articles of association, alongside founders Hu Haiyang, Huang Jianjun and Yang Jian.
notes: Identity resolved: Hurun API 2026 (王育贤, 联讯仪器 Semight, Suzhou); corporate registry (aiqicha) shows he holds 72% of Xinrui Jicheng (Xiamen), a Semight promoter shareholder. He is not an executive; no interviews or bio found. Also invests in Shenzhen Chengguangxing Optoelectronic and a Quanzhou property firm per aiqicha. Semight IR is an indirect route only.

name: Houshan Bai
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ningbo Ronbay New Energy Technology (688005.SH); Chairman, Beijing Ronbay Investment Holding
profile: Bai Houshan (白厚善) is a metallurgical engineer who founded two Chinese lithium-battery cathode makers. He built Beijing Easpring into a ChiNext-listed company (IPO 2010) and left in 2013. That year he started Ronbay, which became China's leading high-nickel cathode supplier and listed on the STAR Market in 2019.
interesting_fact: After leaving Easpring in 2013, he built Ronbay into a company that overtook his former employer within a few years. By 2021 Ronbay held close to half of China's high-nickel cathode shipments, and its market value approached RMB 60B.
deep_cut_fact: His career as a founder began in 1992, leading a research group at Beijing's BGRIMM. The group first made electronic-ceramic additives and only moved into lithium cobalt oxide in 2001, becoming Easpring. Before that he was a technician at the Shenyang Research Institute of Mining & Metallurgy.
notes: The website is the company's, not his personal site, and I found no published email. In April 2026 the Ningbo office of the CSRC warned and fined him RMB 3M over misleading contract disclosures by Ronbay (csrc.gov.cn). Be aware of this before outreach. The formal route is the Ronbay board secretary office.

name: Yu Bangping
current_role: Chairman, executive director and controlling shareholder, Perennial Energy Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 2798), Guizhou coal miner
profile: Guizhou coal entrepreneur with 30+ years in mining who built the Hongguo, Baogushan and Xiejiahegou underground coal mines in Panzhou, Guizhou, grouped under Perennial Energy (久泰邦达), listed in Hong Kong in 2019. He was CEO 2018-2023 and remains chairman; Forbes listed him as a billionaire in 2021 on the coal-price boom.
interesting_fact: In Feb 2024 the group's Baogushan mine won Guizhou safety permits to double annual capacity from 600,000 to 1.2 million tonnes, with a similar expansion planned for the Hongguo mine.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the Hongguo coal mine back in November 1990, then the Baogushan mine in April 2004 - long before the 2019 Hong Kong IPO of the group.
notes: Very low profile; no media/social presence found. Company website listed in filings did not return content; best route is via company secretary / HK office listed in HKEX filings. Deep-cut source is a data aggregator quoting the company bio (not independently verified in a filing).

name: Lim Oon Kuin
current_role: Former founder of Hin Leong Trading (collapsed 2020); serving a prison sentence in Singapore
profile: Lim Oon Kuin ('OK Lim') founded Hin Leong Trading in 1963 and built it into one of Singapore's largest independent oil traders, with the Ocean Tankers fleet. Hin Leong collapsed in 2020 with billions in debt. He was convicted of abetting cheating and forgery, and in March 2026 the High Court cut his sentence on appeal to 13.5 years.
interesting_fact: He started Hin Leong in 1963, at age 20, with a single truck delivering diesel to fishermen and small rural power producers. 'Hin Leong' means 'prosperity' in Chinese.
notes: Not suitable for outreach: he is in prison (see SCMP, March 2026: https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3345339/singapore-court-reduces-oil-tycoon-ok-lims-prison-sentence-13-1/2-years-appeal). The Forbes bio is outdated; Hin Leong no longer operates. No public contact routes.

name: Gao Don
current_role: Founder and President, Positec Group (Worx, Kress)
profile: Don Gao founded Positec in Suzhou in 1994 as an OEM power-tool maker for brands like Black & Decker, then built his own brands, launching Worx in 2004 and later Kress. Positec now sells cordless tools, battery outdoor equipment and robotic mowers in ~70 countries with 4,000+ staff; in April 2026 it took a strategic investment from Bain Capital.
interesting_fact: Positec once shipped 700,000 angle grinders in a single year to Black & Decker; when the tool giant decided to make them in-house, Gao resolved to 'control his own destiny' and build branded products.
deep_cut_fact: Gao hired Vicenza, Italy-based designer Paolo Andriolo to style Positec tools, and the company's Australian design office originated the JawSaw, a 'safe chainsaw' whose chain is exposed only when cutting.
notes: Forbes lists him as 'Gao Don'; he uses Don Gao. Low public profile. Bain Capital deal (Apr 2026) press release: https://positec-europe.com/es/news/positec-gibt-strategische-partnerschaft-mit-bain-capital-bekannt/ . Energy angle: battery platforms and electrification/robotics of outdoor equipment. No published press email found.

name: Manoj Bhargava
current_role: Founder/owner, Innovation Ventures / Living Essentials (5-hour Energy); founder, Stage 2 Innovations & Billions in Change
profile: Lucknow-born (1953) entrepreneur who spent over a decade at an Indian ashram, ran his family's plastics business, then launched 5-hour Energy in 2004 and made it the dominant US energy shot. Giving Pledge signatory; funds Stage 2 Innovations/Billions in Change (Free Electric bike, water purifiers) and India's Hans Foundation.
interesting_fact: Through Stage 2 Innovations he developed the HANS Free Electric bike, a pedal generator meant to supply off-grid households with electricity, alongside the 'Rain Maker' water purifier — pitched as inventions for 'the unlucky third of the world'.
deep_cut_fact: Long before 5-hour Energy, his first venture's early product was 'Chaser', an anti-hangover pill; he had earlier won a scholarship to The Hill School for maths and spent one year at Princeton (1972) before leaving for India.
notes: Reclusive ('mystery monk'). Journalist should be aware of reputational issues: WSJ (Oct 2024) and CNBC reported a US federal tax probe involving him and his philanthropy, plus past 5-hour Energy regulatory suits and the 2023 Arena Group/Sports Illustrated dispute. Energy angle = Free Electric/off-grid power inventions.

name: Rama Prasad Goenka
current_role: Deceased (died 14 April 2013, Kolkata)
profile: R. P. Goenka founded the RPG Group (RPG Enterprises, 1979), the diversified Indian conglomerate now chaired by his son Harsh Goenka; the group later split with the separately run RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group. He died in 2013.
notes: Deceased; source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama_Prasad_Goenka. Rest skipped. The successor groups (RPG Enterprises: Harsh Goenka; RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group: Sanjiv Goenka) are separate potential targets.

name: Els Blokker
current_role: Shareholder/heir in the Blokker family retail holding (Blokker Holding / Mavaro); art patron
profile: Els Blokker-Verwer is the widow of Jaap Blokker (1942-2011), who ran Dutch retailer Blokker Holding from 1976 to 2010 and co-owned it with his brother Albert. She inherited a large stake and ranked 7th on the Quote 500 in 2013. The family later sold off most chains in the group.
interesting_fact: In April 2018 she donated the couple's Nardinc Collection of 117 Dutch modernist paintings to the Singer Laren museum. It includes about 40 works by Jan Sluijters plus Van Dongen, Gestel, Toorop and Willink, and the gift also funded a new museum wing.
deep_cut_fact: The collection's name, 'Nardinc', and a book about it, 'De gezamenlijke kunstliefde van Jaap en Els Blokker' ('Jaap and Els Blokker's shared love of art'), reflect that the couple built the collection together around Jan Sluijters.
notes: Very private, with no published contacts; Singer Laren is the only public link. I could not confirm whether she is alive. Not on recent rich lists after 2015. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Lilian Werninghaus
current_role: Heir/shareholder in the WEG founding-family holdings (presumed); no public role found
profile: Lilian Werninghaus appeared once on the Forbes billionaires list (2014) under 'industrial machinery', Brazil. This almost certainly reflects a stake in WEG, the Jaraguá do Sul electric-motor and power-equipment maker co-founded in 1961 by Geraldo Werninghaus with Werner Ricardo Voigt and Eggon João da Silva. Geraldo died in 1999, and her exact relationship to him and current holdings could not be verified.
interesting_fact: WEG's name combines the first letters of its three founders' names: Werner, Eggon and Geraldo. Geraldo Werninghaus later served as a Santa Catarina state deputy (1995-1999).
notes: Identity is only partly confirmed: the WEG link is inferred from the surname and Forbes category. Very private, and on the list only in 2014. WEG (motors, transformers, solar and storage, grid equipment) is highly relevant to energy and data centres, but the family's public faces are other WEG founder-family members. The WEG name etymology is from my general knowledge; the source confirms only the three founders.

name: Alexander Vagin
current_role: Former co-owner and chairman of Raspadskaya (Kuzbass coking-coal miner); exited 2012-2013, current activity unknown
profile: Alexander Stepanovich Vagin (Kuzbass State Technical University, 1981) rose from the mine floor to co-control Raspadskaya, a top Russian coking-coal miner, with partner Gennady Kozovoi after its 1991 privatisation; partnered with Evraz from 2004 and IPO'd in 2006. Forbes put him at $1.3B in 2011. In 2012 the pair sold out to Evraz for $202M plus 11% of Evraz.
interesting_fact: Raspadskaya was one of the first Soviet 'people's enterprises', corporatised in December 1991 with miners as shareholders; Vagin, then the mine's production director, was elected chairman of the shareholders' council and with Kozovoi gradually bought out the miners' shares.
deep_cut_fact: Forbes estimated that Vagin and Kozovoi, who started at the mine in the 1970s as mechanics (slesari), took about $1.8B gross out of Raspadskaya over two decades through asset swaps, its 2006 IPO, dividends and the 2012 Evraz deal.
notes: Appears only on Forbes 2011 list; essentially no public profile since exiting Raspadskaya (MarketScreener lists his chairmanship ending 2013). No published contacts found; Russian national, so sanctions/compliance context may matter. Raspadskaya had a fatal 2010 mine disaster; avoid as an opener.

name: Choy Kam Lok
profile: Choy Kam Lok appeared once on the Forbes billionaires list (2011) as a Hong Kong pharmaceuticals billionaire. Wikipedia sources could not identify the company behind the listing, and the web-search budget ran out before other sources could be tried.
notes: Unresolved identity, with only one list appearance (Forbes 2011). Needs a follow-up search, e.g. HKEX shareholding disclosures or the Forbes 2011 list entry, to identify the pharmaceutical company. Low priority.

name: Erol Tabanca
current_role: Chairman and co-founder, Polimeks Holding (Istanbul); founder of Odunpazarı Modern Museum (OMM), Eskişehir
profile: An architect from Eskişehir, Tabanca co-founded Polimeks in 1995 with Cem Siyahi and Abdullah Gözener. It became a major contractor in Turkmenistan (Ashgabat International Airport, a ~$2bn+ contract, then the largest project by a Turkish firm abroad) and built Russia's first Ritz-Carlton in Moscow (2007). Polimeks now describes itself as an investment holding in tourism, real estate and renewable energy.
interesting_fact: Polimeks' 2013 contract to build Ashgabat International Airport was reported as the largest construction project ever undertaken abroad by a Turkish company.
deep_cut_fact: An art collector, he founded the Odunpazarı Modern Museum (OMM) in his hometown Eskişehir, designed by Kengo Kuma with stacked timber evoking the district's old wood market; it opened in September 2019.
notes: Received the Turkish Foreign Ministry's Distinguished Service Award (2002). Renewable-energy pivot at Polimeks is a podcast hook. OMM press office (basin@omm.art) is a softer route via his arts philanthropy. Only on Forbes list in 2018.

name: Dominique Heriard Dubreuil
current_role: Former chair/CEO of Rémy Cointreau; family shareholder (current board titles not re-verified)
profile: Born in Paris in 1946, she joined the family Cognac house Rémy Martin in 1988, became its president in 1998 and led Rémy Cointreau as CEO (2001) and board chair (2004) before handing over to her brother François in 2013. She has sat on boards including Vivendi, Wendel, Baccarat and Stora Enso, and chaired the Comité Colbert luxury association (1994-98).
interesting_fact: Promoted to Grand Officier of the Légion d'honneur by decree of 15 January 2025; Fortune once ranked her the 42nd most influential businesswoman in the world (2008).
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family Cognac business she was a PR professional: a press attaché at Havas, then at Ogilvy & Mather, Hill & Knowlton and McCann Erickson, and in 1978 she founded her own PR agency, Infoplan.
notes: Aged ~80; no personal published contact. Route via Rémy Cointreau corporate communications. French-language outreach advisable.

name: Enrique Cueto
current_role: Former CEO of LATAM Airlines Group (2012-2020); later a board member and member of the Cueto controlling family (current board status unverified)
profile: Chilean business engineer (b. 1959, PUC Chile) whose family built its fortune in aviation. He joined the small cargo carrier Fast Air in 1982, ran LAN Chile from 1994 as it expanded and listed in New York, and co-negotiated the 2010-12 LAN-TAM merger. He then ran the combined LATAM Airlines Group as CEO until 2020.
interesting_fact: He was one of the main negotiators of the 2010-2012 LAN-TAM merger, which created LATAM Airlines Group, Latin America's largest airline group.
deep_cut_fact: His aviation career began in 1982 at Fast Air Carrier, a small Chilean cargo airline founded in 1978, where he became VP of finance within a year. He later served as president of ALTA, the Latin American and Caribbean airline association.
notes: The Spanish Wikipedia article is flagged as outdated (2020), so verify his current LATAM board seat against LATAM's latest governance filings. Possible podcast angle: sustainable aviation fuel and airline energy use. I found no verified personal channels, so go through LATAM corporate communications.

name: Lu Qianfang
current_role: Co-owner (with Chen Zhuolin) of Agile Group Holdings stake; role not verified
profile: Hurun lists Lu Qianfang (陆倩芳) with Chen Zhuolin, chairman and president of Guangzhou-based developer Agile Group Holdings (HK: 3383), as co-owners of the Agile fortune. Chen founded Dynasty Furniture in Zhongshan in 1985 and Agile Property in 1992. Her own role and relationship to Chen couldn't be confirmed from sources fetched (lane search budget exhausted). She dropped off Hurun after 2024 amid China's property slump.
interesting_fact: The Agile fortune began with furniture: Chen Zhuolin founded Dynasty Furniture in Zhongshan in 1985, seven years before starting Agile Property in 1992.
notes: Private, with no public statements found. Agile is under financial stress like other Chinese developers, so avoid the topic. Verify her role (reportedly a family member) before outreach. Weak podcast fit.

name: Li Xipeng
current_role: Deceased (died 15 April 2023, Zhengzhou, aged 60); was founder and chairman of Henan Shengrun Holding Group (盛润控股)
profile: Li Xipeng (李喜朋), founder of Zhengzhou-based Henan Shengrun Holding Group (est. 2001; healthcare and elderly care, water/power/heat supply, expressways, energy & chemicals, textiles, property), died on 15 April 2023 aged 60, according to Shengrun's announcement as reported by Dahe Caifang.
notes: Identity confirmed: Hurun API (李喜朋、舒蒲娟, 盛润控股 Shengrun, Zhengzhou; b. Zhoukou, Henan). Death reported by Dahe Caifang citing Shengrun's website, and repeated by Sohu (https://news.sohu.com/a/674681900_121124575). Remainder skipped per instructions. Co-listed spouse Shu Pujuan is a separate record.

name: Shu Pujuan
current_role: Co-owner (49% shareholder) of Henan Shengrun Holding Group (河南盛润控股集团), Zhengzhou
profile: Shu Pujuan (舒蒲娟, b. ~1965) is the wife and business partner of Li Xipeng (李喜朋), founder of Zhengzhou-based Shengrun Holding (盛润控股), a group in real estate, power/energy and urban infrastructure (toll expressways). Hurun listed the couple jointly (2013-2020). She keeps no public profile of her own.
interesting_fact: A 2011 SEC filing by Nasdaq-listed China Infrastructure Investment Corp (CEO/chairman Li Xipeng, which ran the Pingdingshan-Linru expressway in Henan) states that Li owns 51% and his wife Shu Pujuan 49% of Henan Shengrun.
deep_cut_fact: Shengrun's ties to US markets: through China Infrastructure Investment Corp, the family's toll-road business (Pingdingshan Pinglin Expressway) was listed on Nasdaq, and in 2011 a Shengrun subsidiary, Zhengzhou Simian Real Estate, was folded into the listed company via VIE agreements.
notes: Hurun romanises husband's name as Li Xipeng (李喜朋, not 李西鹏). Hurun data: Shengrun Holding, Zhengzhou, Henan; Shu b. 1965. Company site www.srkg.com.cn did not respond. No personal public channels found; any outreach would go via Li Xipeng / Shengrun Holding. Baidu/Sogou blocked automated access, so Chinese news coverage was only partly checked.

name: Cai Di'e
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2022-2024) jointly with Wang Mingwang as a source of Sunwoda wealth; personal role at Sunwoda not confirmed
profile: Appears on the Hurun Global list 2022-2024 together with Wang Mingwang, co-founder (with Wang Wei) of Shenzhen-based Sunwoda Electronic (SZSE: 300207), a major lithium-ion battery maker for phones/laptops, EVs and energy storage. Her own role and relationship to the company could not be confirmed from public sources checked.
interesting_fact: Sunwoda, the source of this fortune, was the world's largest supplier of batteries for smartphones, laptops and tablets by 2024 shipments, with a 34.3% share of mobile-phone batteries.
notes: Identity uncertain: could not find a public bio or Chinese name for Cai Di'e (web-search budget exhausted mid-lane). Any approach would go through Sunwoda corporate/IR; Wang Mingwang or chairman Wang Wei are the public faces. Energy-storage/EV battery fit is good.

name: Vladimir Shmunis
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, RingCentral (NYSE: RNG)
profile: Ukraine-born engineer (SF State BS/MS in computer science) who founded RingCentral in 1999 and built it into a cloud business-communications company with over $2B in revenue. After a brief stint as executive chairman in 2023 he returned as CEO in December 2023 and has pushed AI-focused products; supports Stanford cancer research and Tel Aviv University's Shmunis School of Biomedicine.
interesting_fact: UC Today dubbed him 'the godfather of UCaaS'; RingCentral has been a Gartner Magic Quadrant leader for UCaaS for 12 straight years, and he received the Ellis Island Honors Society Award in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before RingCentral he founded Ring Zero Systems, a pioneer of desktop business-communications software that shipped more than 25 million copies bundled by PC makers such as IBM, HP, Sony and Toshiba, and was later acquired by Motorola.
notes: Goes by 'Vlad'. Best route is RingCentral media relations (named PR contact on 2026 releases). Named inventor on several US patents.

name: Lin Jiangwei
current_role: Founder and largest individual shareholder (~13.4%), Suzhou Jolywood (Zhonglai) Photovoltaic New Materials (300393.SZ); no longer a director or executive
profile: Lin Jianwei (林建伟; listed as Lin Jiangwei) founded Jolywood (Zhonglai) in Suzhou, Jiangsu in 2008, building it into the world's top solar-backsheet maker and an early mass producer of n-type TOPCon cells. In Feb 2023 state-owned Zhejiang Energy's listed arm Zheneng Electric Power took control; he remains the largest individual holder alongside Zhang Yuzheng (~2.75%).
interesting_fact: Jolywood's FFC double-sided coated backsheet broke a foreign technology monopoly in China, and the company says it was No.1 globally in PV backsheet shipments four years running (2021-2024), with over 210 GW shipped cumulatively.
notes: Correct Chinese spelling is 林建伟 (Lin Jianwei). Not on Jolywood's current board (chairman Zhang Chengyu); company now controlled by Zhejiang SASAC via Zheneng. Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Alive status not independently confirmed (still listed as shareholder at 30 Sep 2026). Web search budget exhausted before deep-cut research.

name: Zhang Yuzheng
current_role: Co-founder of Suzhou Jolywood (Zhonglai) Photovoltaic (300393.SZ); no current board or management role found
profile: Zhang Yuzheng (张育政) co-founded the predecessor of Jolywood/Zhonglai, Suzhou Zhonglai Solar Materials Technology, in Changshu in March 2008. The company grew from PV backsheets into N-type TOPCon cells and modules and listed on ChiNext in Sept 2014. Hurun listed this wealth jointly (to 2022) with Lin Jianwei. Control has since passed to state-owned Zhejiang Zheneng Electric Power, and Lin waived his voting rights in 2026.
interesting_fact: Jolywood went from a 2008 backsheet start-up to a ChiNext listing in only six years (Sept 2014), then became an early mass producer of N-type bifacial cells before Zhejiang Energy took control.
deep_cut_fact: Company filings name her as one of just two founding investors (with Dai Enqi) of Suzhou Zhonglai Solar Materials Technology, registered in Changshu on 7 March 2008.
notes: Very private; no interviews found. The founding family no longer controls Jolywood (Zheneng Electric is now the controlling shareholder), so the company is not a route to Zhang. Last Hurun appearance was 2022; current wealth probably much lower. Avoid the change of control and losses as topics.

name: Zang Jianjun
current_role: Unknown; formerly Executive Chairman of SGX-listed CEFC International Ltd and a senior executive of the Huaxin/CEFC China Energy group
profile: Zang Jianjun (臧建军, b. ~1974) is a petrochemical-trading executive from the Huaxin/CEFC China Energy group (founder Ye Jianming). He ran Hua Xin Energy Holdings 2006-11, then became CEO (2012) and Executive Chairman (2013) of SGX-listed CEFC International. CEFC collapsed in 2018 and went bankrupt in 2020. His current activity is not public.
interesting_fact: He joined CEFC International's board in January 2012, became CEO in December 2012 and Executive Chairman in December 2013, handing the CEO role to ex-PetroChina finance manager Lu Dachuan in February 2015.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in Hebei trading: business manager at Hebei Baoding International Trading Co (1995-96), international trading manager at Hebei Lixiang Corp (1996-99), then chemical business unit GM and deputy GM at DaGang Petro Chemical (1999-2006) before Huaxin.
notes: Identity: Hurun 2015/2017 entries list 臧建军, b. 1974, Shanghai, company 华信石油 / Huaxin (oil & chemicals), which matches the CEFC (华信) group. The CEFC group collapsed after chairman Ye Jianming was detained in 2018 (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEFC_China_Energy). No current role, channels or contacts found. Approach with care given the group's history.

name: Lin Haifeng (林海峰)
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Risen Energy Co. (东方日升, SZSE: 300118)
profile: Born 1975, founder of Risen Energy, a Ningbo (Ninghai)-based solar manufacturer founded in 2002 that makes PV cells and modules and builds solar plants, with sales offices in Australia, India, the US and Japan; listed in Shenzhen in 2010. Chairman since at least 2021 and holds ~283M shares; the company is pushing heterojunction (HJT) modules.
interesting_fact: Risen set up a 'Global PV Research Institute' in Nov 2023 to drive integrated cell/module R&D, and its 2023 revenue reached about RMB 35.3bn with net profit up ~46%, helped by its heterojunction technology.
deep_cut_fact: His official company bio notes he holds an EMBA from Ningbo University and has been named one of Ningbo's 'Ten Outstanding Young People' and 'Ten Charity Stars', as well as a 'Changzhou Star Entrepreneur'.
notes: Low international profile; no personal accounts found. Board secretary is Zhou Yinning. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so profile relies on exchange-data and company pages. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Zhang Jinfang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Chipone Technology (Beijing) Co. (集创北方); since Jan 2026 also actual controller of Silicon-valley display-chip firm Analogix/硅数股份
profile: Born 1985 in Shuozhou, Shanxi; PhD in circuits and systems from Beijing Jiaotong University. Founded display-driver chip designer Chipone in 2008 while a first-year master's student; it became a ~RMB 31B unicorn backed by Xiaomi, vivo, Huawei Hubble and BOE, and is preparing a STAR Market IPO. In 2026 he took control of display-chip maker Analogix (硅数股份).
interesting_fact: Chipone's chips are behind the 16K wraparound LED display of the Las Vegas Sphere, and it holds over 45% of the global LED display-driver chip market.
deep_cut_fact: He started Chipone in 2008 with four classmates in a ~40 sqm rented room in Zhongguancun; within a year the five-person team shipped its first product, a phone-charger power-management chip, before moving into LED driver and touch chips.
notes: Young (b. 1985) chip founder; IPO-in-preparation context means company may limit his media. Best route: Chipone public affairs (pr@). Display-chip focus is more consumer electronics than data center.

name: Radik Shaimiev
current_role: Businessman, Kazan; one of the main shareholders of the TAIF group (Tatarstan petrochemicals, merged into SIBUR in 2021); long-time Tatneft board member
profile: Son of Tatarstan's first president Mintimer Shaimiev (listed spelling 'Shaimev'). Trained as a civil engineer, he joined Kazan investment firm TAIF in 1992; TAIF became the holding company for Tatarstan's big petrochemical, refining and power assets, and he has sat on Tatneft's board since 1998. Also an internationally ranked rally/autocross driver and was named president of FC Rubin Kazan in 2017.
interesting_fact: A Master of Sport (international class) in motorsport, he won the 2003 European Autocross Championship in the touring-car class, with his own brother Airat as main title rival, and still competes in classic rallies, including World Championship rounds.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he trained as an architect-engineer: after Marine service in Vladivostok (1982-84) and graduating from the Kazan Civil Engineering Institute in 1989, he worked as an engineer in architectural-planning workshop No. 2 of the Kazgrazhdanproekt institute.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Sanctioned by Ukraine (Oct 2022) and Canada (June 2025), which makes outreach/booking legally and reputationally sensitive for a Western podcast. Only data point is Hurun 2014; TAIF has since been folded into SIBUR.

name: Herbert Sy
current_role: Adviser to the board, SM Investments Corp.; director, SM Prime Holdings (Philippines)
profile: Second-youngest of the six children of the late SM founder Henry Sy Sr., who all hold posts in the conglomerate spanning retail, banking (BDO, China Bank), property, mining and hotels. Herbert is closely involved in the group's supermarket operations and sits on the SM Prime board. He holds a management degree from De La Salle University.
interesting_fact: In 2022 SM Investments agreed to buy Philippine Geothermal Production Co. in a $304m all-share deal to cut its carbon footprint, a notable energy move for a retail-and-property group.
notes: Low-profile Sy sibling who rarely gives interviews; the realistic route is SM Investments corporate communications/IR. The SM sites blocked automated access, so no contact was captured. The geothermal deal is the energy hook.

name: Ranga Raju Kanumuri
current_role: Chairman, Sai Life Sciences (Hyderabad; NSE/BSE-listed CRDMO)
profile: Dr. K. Ranga Raju, a pharmaceutical scientist turned entrepreneur, founded Sai Life Sciences in Hyderabad in 1999 as a medicinal-chemistry partner to US biotechs. It is now an integrated contract research, development and manufacturing organisation (CRDMO) with sites in India, the UK and the US. Sai Life listed in India in December 2024, raising about INR 30.4bn; his son Krishna Kanumuri is MD and CEO.
interesting_fact: He holds a Doctor of Pharmacy plus bachelor's and master's degrees from the Massachusetts College of Pharmacy in Boston, after a first pharmacy degree from the University of Mysore.
deep_cut_fact: Sai Life Sciences was originally founded in 1999 as 'Sai Dru Syn Laboratories'. It began as a small medicinal-chemistry services provider for US biotechs and was renamed later to reflect a broader life-sciences focus.
notes: Low personal profile; CEO Krishna Kanumuri is the company's public voice and may be the easier guest. Route requests via IR or general inquiries.

name: Mikhail Fedyaev
current_role: Co-owner and president of Siberian Business Union (SDS) holding, Kemerovo (coal, fertilizers, engineering, transport)
profile: Kemerovo businessman (b. 1962, Prokopyevsk) who started as a car-factory mechanic. With partner Vladimir Gridin he won control of the Chernigovets coal pit in 1999 and in 2004 formed Siberian Business Union (SDS), now spanning coal mining, fertilizers/chemicals, engineering, transport and construction in Kuzbass. He has been SDS president since 2007.
interesting_fact: He was elected chairman of a production-and-construction cooperative in 1989, one of the first Soviet-era private ventures, and in the 1990s ran the Kemerovo office of MirInvest, where he met his long-time partner Vladimir Gridin.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer in 'Automobiles and motor transport' at the Kuzbass Polytechnic Institute (1985), rose to deputy head of a truck column, and in 1996 was general director of Partner-Grundfos, a Kemerovo venture tied to the Danish pump maker, before going into coal.
notes: Sensitive: owner of the Listvyazhnaya mine where a 2021 methane explosion killed 51; he was arrested in 2021 and given a suspended sentence in 2025. No published personal or press contact found. Russian-language, regionally focused; likely a poor fit for outreach.

name: Gao Jifan
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Trina Solar Co., Ltd. (SSE STAR: 688599), Changzhou
profile: Gao Jifan, a Changzhou native with chemistry degrees from Nanjing University and Jilin University, founded Trina Solar in 1997. Trina listed on the NYSE in 2006, went private in 2017 and relisted on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020; it is now one of the world's largest PV module makers and has expanded into energy storage, trackers and digital energy services, with plants in China, Vietnam and Thailand.
interesting_fact: Trina was named the first solar 'Industry Shaper' by the World Economic Forum in Davos, and was the first PV and energy-storage company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market.
deep_cut_fact: Trina says Gao was inspired to found the company by the Kyoto Protocol and the US 'Million Solar Roofs' initiative (both 1997); academically he is a physical chemist - MSc in physical chemistry from Jilin University (1988) after a Nanjing University chemistry BSc (1985).
notes: Frequent Davos/industry-forum speaker, so conference panels are a natural route. Son Gao Haichun became co-chairman in 2025 (succession under way). Could not verify a published press/IR email (web-search budget exhausted).

name: Tang Xiuguo
current_role: Director & President, Sany Group; rotating chair (alternating six-month terms with Xiang Wenbo since 2023)
profile: Tang Xiuguo is one of four co-founders, with Liang Wengen, Mao Zhongwu and Yuan Jinhua, of Sany Group, China's largest construction-machinery maker and among the biggest in the world. He has been president since 2002. When Liang retired in 2023, Sany moved to a rotating chair, with Tang and Xiang Wenbo alternating every six months as leader of daily operations.
interesting_fact: Sany started in 1986 as Lianyuan Welding Material Ltd in the town of Maotang, Hunan, with RMB 60,000 of capital. The four founders quit their jobs to start it, renamed it Sany in 1991 and moved to Changsha.
deep_cut_fact: He studied metallic materials at Central South University (bachelor's, 1983), which fits Sany's origins as a welding-materials factory before it moved into concrete pumps and excavators.
notes: Sany has a big energy business: listed subsidiary Sany Heavy Energy (wind turbines) and hydrogen and battery equipment, which makes it a strong energy-show angle. Only sales and service emails are published, with no press email. Rotating-chair source: https://www.yicaiglobal.com/news/2023051611-sanys-founding-chairman-retires-chinese-heavy-equipment-maker-to-adopt-rotating-chair-system

name: Igor Yakovlev
current_role: Founder and owner, Kari (Russian footwear, accessories and household-goods retail chain)
profile: Igor Nikolaevich Yakovlev (b. 1965, Makhachkala) founded the Eldorado consumer-electronics chain in 1994 and sold it to Czech group PPF in 2008–2011. In 2012 he founded Kari, now about 1,500 stores in 600+ cities across Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Armenia. He also holds a stake in Kazakh electronics retailer Sulpak.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he returned to Forbes' global billionaires list 16 years after first dropping off it, this time on the back of Kari rather than Eldorado.
deep_cut_fact: Before retail he studied at the Dagestan Polytechnic Institute and the St Petersburg University of the Russian Interior Ministry, moving to Moscow in the 1990s where he launched Eldorado.
notes: Very low public profile; Kari website blocked automated fetch so no press email verified. Russia-based retail; check sanctions/compliance status before outreach. Forbes bio says he owned 50% of FC Anzhi Makhachkala in 2008–2011.

name: Thomas Bailey
profile: Deceased. Founder (1969) and long-time CEO of Denver mutual fund firm Janus. Forbes now marks his profile 'Deceased'; Wikipedia's infobox gives a death date of 30 Aug 2025 (unsourced).
notes: Forbes profile labelled Deceased (https://www.forbes.com/profile/thomas-bailey/); exact date per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_H._Bailey not independently confirmed. Skip.

name: Juan Maria Riberas Mera
current_role: Co-owner of Gestamp Automoción (with brother Francisco); widely reported as chairman of Gonvarri Industries (not re-verified this session)
profile: Known as Jon. He and his brother Francisco each own just over 25% of Gestamp, the listed Spanish auto-parts maker, through the family holding Acek. Their father Francisco Riberas Pampliega founded the steel processor Gonvarri in 1958, and the group diversified into auto parts in 1997. Jon trained in law and business and joined the company in junior management in 1992.
interesting_fact: Gonvarri started in 1958 as a small steel trading business founded by Francisco Riberas (1932-2010). Today it runs a Gonvarri Solar Steel unit making steel structures for solar plants, a link to the energy transition.
deep_cut_fact: Gonvarri's first site was Gonvarri Burgos (1958), followed by Hiasa in Asturias (1972) and Gonvarri Valencia (1978). The group's stated founding values are 'Honesty, Humility, Tenacity and Hard Work'.
notes: Good energy angle: Gonvarri Solar Steel makes solar mounting and tracker structures, and the family's Acek group also has renewables interests (not verified this session). info@gonvarri.com is Gonvarri's general corporate address, not a dedicated press line. He keeps a low public profile.

name: Wang Dong
current_role: Co-founder and Executive President, Moore Threads Technology (Beijing GPU maker; STAR Market 688795)
profile: Per Forbes, Wang Dong spent more than a decade as a sales director at Nvidia before co-founding Moore Threads in 2020 with former Nvidia China head Zhang Jianzhong. Moore Threads designs full-function GPUs for AI training/inference and graphics as a domestic Chinese alternative to Nvidia; it listed in Shanghai in December 2025, raising about $1.1B.
interesting_fact: Moore Threads' shares jumped about 468% on their Shanghai trading debut on 5 Dec 2025, with DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng's High-Flyer reported among institutional investors.
deep_cut_fact: At the July 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai he argued the inference market has no 'universal chip' - only combinations of solutions - because inference scenarios are highly fragmented and no single company can monopolize them; he also noted Chinese frontier models' cost advantage.
notes: Common name; matched via Forbes URL (wang-dong-1 = Moore Threads cofounder, $1.4B on 2026 list). Input's 'Hurun China 2007-2021' entries predate Moore Threads (2020) and likely belong to another Wang Dong. Public speaker at WAIC - route via Moore Threads marketing (mkt@) or IR.

name: Vincent Lo
current_role: Chairman, Shui On Group and Shui On Land (HK: 272)
profile: Vincent Lo Hong-sui (born 1948, Hong Kong) founded the Shui On construction and building-materials group and its property arm Shui On Land. Shui On Land is best known for turning a run-down Shanghai neighbourhood into the Xintiandi shopping and entertainment district. He has chaired the HK Airport Authority (2014-15) and the HK Trade Development Council (2015-19), and is handing day-to-day leadership to his daughter Stephanie, vice chairman of Shui On Land.
interesting_fact: He was an early mover into mainland China: he began investing in Shanghai in 1984, building a hotel there with the Communist Youth League, long before Xintiandi made Shui On famous.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating (reportedly from the University of New South Wales), he started his first business with HK$100,000 borrowed from his father, property tycoon Lo Ying-shek, rather than joining the family firm Great Eagle. He received Hong Kong's highest honour, the Grand Bauhinia Medal, in 2017.
notes: Prominent HK establishment figure. Avoid the family trust feud and the Trump lawsuit. The best route is Shui On Land corporate communications or IR; the contact page is JS-rendered, so I couldn't extract an email. Shui On has low-carbon and urban-regeneration angles.

name: Cao Zheng
current_role: Major shareholder (wealth shared with chairman Cao Ji) of Zhejiang Hangke Technology (688006.SH); director and VP of the company until Dec 2021
profile: Cao Zheng (b. 1983) built his career inside Hangke, the Hangzhou maker of formation and grading equipment used in the back-end of lithium-ion battery production lines, rising from purchasing staff to director, deputy GM and head of sales. Hangke listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in July 2019; Hurun lists his fortune jointly with Cao Ji, Hangke's founder and chairman.
interesting_fact: Hangke was one of the first batch of companies to list on Shanghai's STAR Market (July 2019), and its post-processing equipment for EV battery cells is sold to major battery makers in China and abroad.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he spent 2005-2008 as an assistant engineer at STATS ChipPAC, the Singapore-based semiconductor packaging and test company; he holds Singapore permanent residency and a master's degree.
notes: No longer on Hangke's board (term ended Dec 2021), so current role is unclear; alive status not independently confirmed (no reports of death found, but web search budget ran out). The IR email is the company's board-secretary mailbox. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Li Chen
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (founding-shareholder group with Li Zhen and Guoxuan Holding) of Gotion High-Tech (国轩高科, SZSE: 002074); holds ~1.57% directly and sits on boards of group-related companies
profile: Li Chen (李晨) is the son of Gotion High-Tech founder-chairman Li Zhen and, with him and Nanjing Guoxuan Holding, one of the company's acting-in-concert controlling shareholders. Hefei-based Gotion (formerly Anhui Guoxuan) makes LFP and other lithium-ion cells for EVs and grid energy storage, with Volkswagen China as a major strategic shareholder.
interesting_fact: Although Volkswagen (China) is a top shareholder, under its shareholder agreement VW irrevocably waives part of its voting rights so that its voting power stays at least 5 points below that of the founding shareholders - Guoxuan Holding, Li Zhen and Li Chen.
notes: Wealth listing is shared with father Li Zhen, the public face of Gotion; Li Chen keeps a low profile and his executive title (if any) is not confirmed in the 2026 interim report. Strong energy-storage fit, but the better interview target is likely Li Zhen. Contact via Gotion IR/board office.

name: Lu Weidong
current_role: Deputy General Manager, Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources Co. (鄂尔多斯, SSE: 600295 / 900936); previously a company director
profile: Lu Weidong is a long-serving senior executive of the Erdos group in Ordos, Inner Mongolia, whose listed arm Erdos Resources spans cashmere (the Erdos brand), coal, power and ferroalloy/chemicals. He sat on the listed company's board (still a director in mid-2025) and is listed as Deputy GM in the 2025 pay disclosure; Hurun ranks him for his group shareholding.
interesting_fact: The Erdos group combines one of China's best-known cashmere brands with an energy-and-metallurgy business (coal, power, silicon/ferroalloys) in Ordos, one of China's main coal regions.
notes: Role confirmed in Erdos Resources' Apr 2026 notice on executive pay (Lu Weidong, Deputy GM, 2025 pay RMB1.96M): https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604141821185338_1.pdf . Chairman is Wang Zhen. No personal channels; formal route would be the board secretary listed in Erdos Resources' annual report.

name: Huang Biliang
current_role: Co-founder, director & general manager, JoulWatt Technology (Hangzhou); co-controlling shareholder with chairman Zhou Xunwei
profile: Huang Biliang (b. 1971, Macau resident) earned BS/MS degrees at Tsinghua and a PhD at Virginia Tech, then spent 2001-2013 at Linear Technology as a design engineer and R&D center manager. He co-founded power-management chipmaker JoulWatt in Hangzhou in 2013 (GM since 2016); it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market and serves data-center/server power.
interesting_fact: Both JoulWatt founders, Huang and Zhou Xunwei, earned PhDs at Virginia Tech under power-electronics pioneer Fred C. Lee, and both later worked at Linear Technology before co-founding JoulWatt; Huang is the named inventor on 99 granted invention patents there.
deep_cut_fact: Per JoulWatt's IPO prospectus, he was the first to propose using coupled inductors to improve power modules' static and dynamic performance, an idea widely adopted by industry, with the work cited 2,000+ times; in 2015 his team was named a Zhejiang 'leading innovation and entrepreneurship team'.
notes: Technical founder, low media profile. Coupled-inductor/VRM power-delivery work is directly relevant to AI server power, a strong podcast angle. JoulWatt filed for a Hong Kong H-share listing in Jan 2026.

name: Vitali Machitski
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Vimetco NV, owner of 84% of Romanian aluminium smelter Alro Slatina; developer of Moscow's Rostec-City complex
profile: Russian businessman who traded timber and oil in the 1990s, sold refinery assets to Yukos and others in the early 2000s, and took control of Romania's privatised Alro aluminium smelter in 2002 via Marco Industries, later Vimetco. Vimetco also held stakes in China's Zhongfu Industrial. His companies developed the Rostec-City business complex in Moscow.
interesting_fact: Alro, his main asset, is Romania's single largest electricity consumer, using about 8% of national power. In 2007 it was the largest primary aluminium producer in Central and Eastern Europe outside the CIS.
notes: Very private, with no published personal contacts. Forbes notes he is a friend of Rostec head Sergey Chemezov, so check sanctions exposure before any outreach. Alive status was not confirmed independently but he is on the 2026 Forbes real-time list. Energy angle: aluminium smelting and power intensity.

name: David Chen
current_role: Chief Product Officer, Shopee (Sea Ltd, NYSE: SE); Sea co-founder
profile: David Chen (45, Singapore; BSc, National University of Singapore) co-founded Sea in 2009 with Forrest Li and Gang Ye. Sea is the Singapore group behind Garena's hit mobile game Free Fire, e-commerce platform Shopee and the digital-finance arm Monee. He was previously Sea's COO and chief of staff and now runs product for Shopee.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding Sea, Chen trained as a computer engineer and worked at PSA Corp, the Temasek-owned Singapore port operator.
notes: Low profile compared with Forrest Li. Forbes marks him as 'former' on the real-time list, so his net worth is near the $1bn threshold. Common name: make sure outreach targets the Sea/Shopee co-founder. Web-search quota ran out before deeper research.

name: Herriot Tabuteau
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Axsome Therapeutics (NASDAQ: AXSM), New York
profile: Herriot Tabuteau is a Haitian-born, Yale-trained physician who worked in healthcare investing, including as a partner at Healthco/S.A.C. Capital. He founded Axsome Therapeutics in 2012 to develop treatments for brain disorders and took it public in 2015; he owns about 15%. Axsome sells the depression drug Auvelity and the migraine drug Symbravo, and is advancing AXS-05 for Alzheimer's agitation. He is named inventor on more than 200 patents.
interesting_fact: He is named as inventor on more than 200 patents, covering potential medicines for depression, Alzheimer's agitation and narcolepsy. Forbes includes him among the world's Black billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: He emigrated from Haiti at nine, grew up on Manhattan's Upper East Side near Rockefeller University, and attended Xavier High School, a Jesuit school. He calls himself 'forever grateful to New York City's Catholic school system', credits his mother for his love of Motown, and names Citymeals and Success Academy as favorite charities.
notes: Business Insider has called him an 'elusive doctor'; he gives few interviews. His personal site has a contact page and a 'Call for Grants' section, which may be the best direct route. Avoid the S.A.C. Capital association.

name: Joe Kiani
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Willow Laboratories (Irvine, CA); CEO of Like Minded Labs (since July 2025)
profile: Iranian-born engineer (b. 1964, Shiraz) who founded Masimo in 1989 and, with Mohammed Diab, invented pulse oximetry that reads through motion and low perfusion, making Masimo the hospital leader. He left Masimo in Sept 2024 after a proxy fight (Danaher agreed to buy Masimo in Feb 2026) and now runs diabetes/metabolic-health startup Willow Labs and media-tech firm Like Minded Labs. He served on Biden's PCAST.
interesting_fact: He finished high school at 15 after arriving from Iran at nine speaking almost no English, and earned BS and MS degrees in electrical engineering from San Diego State by 22; he holds 500+ patents and patent applications.
deep_cut_fact: In 1988, while consulting for Newport Medical Electronics on a low-cost pulse oximeter, he discovered the motion-artifact problem and pitched a fix; when they declined, he returned all the pay they had given him in exchange for a release, then founded Masimo. His first engineering job was a 1984 co-op at Burroughs in Rancho Bernardo.

public_contacts.value: https://medium.com/@JoeKiani (Medium blog linked from his site)

notes: Founded the Patient Safety Movement Foundation (goal: zero preventable hospital deaths). Avoid Masimo proxy fight/litigation topics. joekiani.com looks like a personal/reputation site (also links Threads @joe.kiani) – treat as semi-official. Willow Labs general email is the best published route.

name: Li Zhigang
current_role: Chairman, Wuhan DR Laser Technology (帝尔激光, SZSE:300776)
profile: Founder-chairman of Wuhan DR Laser, a maker of laser processing equipment for solar cells (e.g. PERC/TOPCon/BC laser doping and grooving) that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2019. Customers include LONGi, Trina Solar, Tongwei and Canadian Solar.
interesting_fact: DR Laser's laser equipment is used by leading Chinese solar cell and panel makers including LONGi, Canadian Solar, Tongwei and Trina Solar.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (solar manufacturing equipment). dr@ is the company's general mailbox. The company works closely with Huazhong University of Science and Technology (site news, Feb 2026). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Jassim Al-Kharafi
current_role: Deceased (died 21 May 2015)
profile: Kuwaiti businessman and politician (1940-2015) from the family behind the M.A. Kharafi & Sons conglomerate. He served five terms as Speaker of Kuwait's National Assembly (1999-2011, briefly again in 2012). He died on 21 May 2015.
interesting_fact: He served as Speaker for five terms, the most in Kuwait's history.
notes: Deceased (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jassem_Al-Kharafi). The family wealth sits with the M.A. Kharafi & Sons group.

name: Li Baoyuan
current_role: Honorary Chairman and non-executive Director, Hebei Construction Group (HKEX: 1727); chairman, Hebei Baocang Expressway; GM, Qianbao Investment
profile: Li Baoyuan (李宝元) has spent over 50 years at Hebei Construction Group, a Baoding-based general contractor descended from 1950s state construction units.
