He rose from trainee to lead it, took it public in Hong Kong, and controls it through Qianbao Investment. He is now honorary chairman, chairs the Baoding-Cangzhou expressway company and leads the SME Committee of the China Construction Industry Association.
interesting_fact: Hebei Construction Group traces its roots to two central-ministry construction companies founded in 1952-53 (Ministry of Light Industry's Northeast Engineering Co. and the Textile Ministry's North China construction company).
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1970 as a trainee and budget planner at No. 1 Construction Engineering Company of Hebei Province. He worked his way up through the site teams, heading 'Team 2 of Division I' and then the '101 Engineering Team', before running the whole group.

public_contacts.value: hebjs.hk@pordahavas.com (Porda Havas International Finance Communications, media enquiries for Hebei Construction)

notes: Aged about 71+ and semi-retired (honorary chairman); his brother Li Baozhong is executive chairman. Chinese-language outreach is best. Moderate fit through construction and infrastructure.

name: Kim Sang-beom
current_role: Chairman, ISU Group (ISU Chemical, ISU Petasys, ISU Specialty Chemical), South Korea
profile: Chairman of ISU Group since 2000, succeeding his late father Kim Joon-sung (founder of Daegu Bank, ex-chairman of Samsung Electronics and Daewoo). He became a billionaire in 2025 as AI demand sent shares of ISU Petasys - a Daegu maker of high-layer printed circuit boards for AI servers and 800G switches used by Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft and Cisco - up more than 200%; he holds ~17% directly and indirectly.
interesting_fact: ISU Petasys's most advanced product is 40+-layer multilayer boards for AI network switches; JPMorgan analysts forecast that mix rising from 22% of networking sales in 2025 to 43% in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the family group he was a New York lawyer at Debevoise & Plimpton; he holds a JD and an MBA from the University of Michigan and a business degree from Seoul National University.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. Route would be via ISU Group / ISU Petasys corporate communications (Korean company sites not reachable from this environment, so no published email verified). Strong data-center/AI-hardware angle (PCBs for AI servers).

name: Wang Xinyang
current_role: Chairman, Gpixel Changchun Microelectronics (长光辰芯, HKEX: 3277)
profile: Wang Xinyang (王欣洋) chairs Gpixel, a Changchun-based fabless maker of high-performance CMOS image sensors for machine vision, scientific, medical and professional imaging, founded in 2012 with subsidiaries in Antwerp and Tokyo. Gpixel listed on the Hong Kong main board on 17 April 2026 (HK$39.88 offer price), which made him a billionaire on Forbes' real-time list.
interesting_fact: Gpixel's very first product, the GMAX3005, was at launch the world's highest-resolution CMOS image sensor (150 megapixels), and it later built the first back-illuminated scientific CMOS sensor, the GSENSE400BSI.

public_contacts.value: info@gpixel.com (general/media contact; media inquiry form on site)

notes: Forbes profile now 404s (dropped off list). Personal bio details not verified from a public source; web-search budget ran out during this lane. Gpixel Europe (Antwerp) handles English-language inquiries: info@gpixel.eu.

name: Cao Kanyu
current_role: Director and President (CEO since April 2023), CXMT Corporation / ChangXin Memory Technologies, Hefei
profile: PhD-trained chip engineer (born 1971) who worked at Philips Semiconductors in the U.S., founded two Beijing chip startups, then ran a NAND flash unit before joining CXMT in 2017. Rose through R&D to CEO/President of CXMT, China's leading DRAM maker and world No.4 by share, which raised about $8.6B in its July 2026 Shanghai STAR Market IPO.
interesting_fact: In October 2026 he publicly unveiled CXMT's progress on a 4F2 DRAM cell architecture at China's Integrated Chips and Chiplets conference, with next-gen DDR5 RDIMM products targeted for year-end.
deep_cut_fact: Before CXMT he was a serial founder: between 2005 and 2013 he set up Beijing Kuntian Kewei Microelectronics and Beijing Fandaxun Technology, then was GM of the NAND flash division at NoVoMem Inc. (2013-17), per CXMT's IPO prospectus.
notes: Chinese state-linked strategic chip company; executives rarely give Western media interviews. Route via board office / IR (board secretary Yuan Yuan). Company is subject to U.S. export-control scrutiny.

name: Daniel Roberts
current_role: Co-Founder, Co-CEO and Director, IREN Ltd (Nasdaq: IREN)
profile: Sydney-based co-founder, with brother Will, of IREN (formerly Iris Energy, founded 2018), which began as a renewable-powered bitcoin miner and now builds AI/HPC data centers, including a 2GW campus in Sweetwater, Texas. IREN signed a five-year, ~$9.7bn AI cloud contract with Microsoft in 2025. Before IREN, Daniel helped grow Palisade Investment Partners in infrastructure.
interesting_fact: The brothers deliberately sought 'stranded' renewable power: their first site was a data center beside a shut pulp mill in Canal Flats, British Columbia, using surplus hydro and rehiring local mill workers.
deep_cut_fact: Daniel first bought bitcoin in 2013 at about US$1,000 and sold at US$500 ('What nonsense is this?'), then joined the Ethereum presale. Scouting sites for Iris Energy, the brothers backpacked through Europe, Iceland and the US, and still laugh about a scuzzy windowless New York hostel.
notes: Wealth shared with brother/co-CEO William Roberts. Forbes AU says Daniel was co-owner of Palisade Investment Partners (helped grow it to ~$6bn infrastructure AUM) while Will was a Macquarie VP, slightly contradicting the Forbes profile that both worked at Macquarie. Highly relevant to energy/data-center podcast.

name: William Roberts
current_role: Co-Founder & Co-CEO, IREN Ltd (Nasdaq: IREN), Sydney
profile: Will Roberts and his older brother Daniel co-founded Iris Energy (renamed IREN in 2024), which listed on Nasdaq in November 2021 as a renewable-powered bitcoin miner and has pivoted to AI cloud/HPC data centers. IREN is building a 2GW, 1,800-acre campus in Sweetwater, Texas, and in 2025 signed a five-year, $9.7B AI cloud contract with Microsoft. Before IREN, Will was a vice president at Macquarie Group, where he co-founded its digital assets team.
interesting_fact: The brothers deliberately named the company Iris Energy rather than something like 'Iris Data' - they measure compute in gigawatts, not gigabytes - and IREN's sites span Texas, Oklahoma and British Columbia.
deep_cut_fact: Will and Daniel first bought bitcoin in 2013 at around US$1,000, sold at US$500 after it crashed ('What nonsense is this?'), then got into the Ethereum presale for next to nothing - years before founding Iris Energy.
notes: Shares Forbes profile with brother Daniel (the more public-facing co-CEO). Ideal podcast fit (bitcoin-to-AI-data-center pivot, 2GW Texas campus, Microsoft deal). Best route: IREN media@iren.com. Avoid referencing Daniel's 2023 health scare mentioned in Forbes AU.

name: Tang Jie
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Scientist, Zhipu AI (Z.ai); Professor of Computer Science, Tsinghua University
profile: Tang Jie (唐杰) is a Tsinghua professor and an ACM, AAAI and IEEE Fellow. He co-founded Zhipu AI in 2019 out of his Knowledge Engineering Group and, as chief scientist, leads its GLM/ChatGLM large-language-model family. Zhipu went public in Hong Kong in January 2026, which made him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: He invented AMiner.org, an academic search and social-network mining system he has built since 2006, which grew to over 30 million users in 220 countries and regions. It became Zhipu's technical foundation.
deep_cut_fact: As a grad student he interned in Microsoft Research Asia's NLC group (2004-05) and at IBM China Research Lab (2004). He was later a visiting scholar at Cornell with John Hopcroft and Jon Kleinberg. His research won the SIGKDD Test-of-Time (ten-year best paper) award.
notes: He is an accessible academic who publishes his own email and gives many keynotes in English. Forbes estimates of his net worth vary widely with Zhipu's share price. For data-center/AI topics, frame the pitch around open models (GLM) and AGI.

name: Yan Junjie
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, MiniMax Group (HKEX-listed Chinese foundation-model/AI company, Shanghai)
profile: Born 1989 in Xiayi County, Henan, Yan earned a PhD at the CAS Institute of Automation, did a Tsinghua postdoc in deep learning, then rose from intern (2015) to vice president at SenseTime. He left in 2021 to found MiniMax (LLMs, Hailuo video, Talkie, speech/music models); its January 2026 Hong Kong IPO made him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he joined a symposium hosted by Premier Li Qiang, only the second founder of a Chinese foundation-model developer (after DeepSeek's Liang Wenfeng) to attend such a meeting.
deep_cut_fact: A devoted Dota 2 player, he goes by the alias 'IO' (a pun on input/output and the Dota wisp hero); watching OpenAI's bots beat top Dota players in 2019 pushed him from computer vision toward language models. As a PhD student he said his goal was to be a Java developer at IBM.
notes: MiniMax name comes from the minimax algorithm. Gave a Bloomberg Q&A in Jan 2026 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-08/minimax-founder-was-once-dismissed-as-a-fraud-by-big-tech-q-a), so open to English-language press. Gaming link: knows miHoYo CEO Cai Haoyu, an early backer.

name: Oleg Misevra
current_role: Controlling owner and chairman, East Mining Company (VGK / Vostochnaya Gornorudnaya Kompaniya), Sakhalin, Russia
profile: Former USSR/Russian Internal Troops officer who became a top manager and minority partner at MDM Group and president of SUEK (2002-04). In 2004 he bought SUEK's Sakhalin assets, building East Mining Company around the Solntsevsky open-pit coal mine and Shakhtersk port, now one of Russia's fastest-growing thermal coal exporters to Asia.
interesting_fact: He was named Russia's 'Exporter of the Year' in 2019 in the All-Russian People-2019 competition, as VGK ramped Sakhalin coal exports and expanded its Shakhtersk port.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 interview he explained that VGK was then Russia's only exporter of brown (lignite) coal, so its real competitor is Indonesia rather than Australia, and that the business is fully self-contained: 'We have everything of our own: the mine, the port, the conveyor line.'

public_contacts.value: https://www.eastmining.ru/en/ (East Mining Company; was unreachable from our network when checked)

notes: Very low public profile; no published personal or press contacts found. Russian coal exporter: sanctions/compliance considerations for any outreach. Interviews exist only in Russian regional/business media (EastRussia, PortNews).

name: Ji Wei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, Wasion Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 3393), Changsha
profile: Ji Wei founded Wasion in Changsha in 2000 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2005 - the first Chinese energy-metering company listed overseas and Hunan's first overseas main-board listing. Wasion makes smart electricity/water/gas/heat meters, distribution equipment and energy-efficiency systems, with subsidiaries in Mexico, Brazil, Tanzania and Hungary; its unit Willfar listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020.
interesting_fact: Wasion was the first professional energy-metering and energy-efficiency group from China to list overseas (HKEX, Dec 2005), and has since won large smart-meter contracts in emerging markets across Latin America, Africa and Europe.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an energy-tech founder he was a trader: business manager at Hunan Province Minerals Import & Export Co. (1980-85) and import-export manager at Hunan International Economic Development Group (1985-89). He has received the 'Top Ten Educational Entrepreneur' award and the Chinese Red Cross Dedication Medal.
notes: The listed email is the shareholder-enquiry address for the attention of the Company Secretary (spelled 'enquires@' in the 2023 annual report). Wasion IR site: http://website.wasionholdings.wisdomir.com/. Ji is ~69; low international media profile.

name: Hitesh Doshi
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Waaree Energies Ltd (NSE: WAAREEENER); head of the Waaree Group, Mumbai
profile: Founder of the Waaree Group, which began in 1990 making thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers and moved into solar modules in 2007 with a 30 MW plant in Surat. Waaree Energies is now India's largest solar-panel maker by capacity and listed in Mumbai in October 2024 at a 70% premium. He is expanding into cells, US manufacturing and other clean-energy businesses.
interesting_fact: On listing day in October 2024, Waaree shares jumped about 56% after a $514M IPO, roughly doubling the Doshi family's fortune to about $5.2B, according to Bloomberg as reported by Fortune.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Tunki, a village in Maharashtra, Doshi moved about 600 km to attend Shri Chinai College of Commerce and Economics in Mumbai in 1985. He borrowed Rs 5,000 (about $60) from a relative to trade hardware, electronics and instrument gauges, which paid his college fees (he told the Economic Times in 2014).
notes: waaree@waaree.com is the company's general/customer-service inbox, not a personal or press address; no dedicated press or IR email was confirmed (the web-search budget ran out). The X account is the company's (@waareegroup). Strong fit for an energy podcast.

name: Zhu Shunquan
current_role: Director and General Manager, Hubei Dinglong Co. (鼎龙股份, SZSE: 300054), Wuhan; also director of Wuhan Zhongyuan Huadian since Dec 2025
profile: Co-founder (in 2000, with his elder brother, chairman Zhu Shuangquan) and co-controlling shareholder of Hubei Dinglong, which grew from printer-toner chemicals and consumables into one of China's leading semiconductor-materials makers: CMP polishing pads and slurries, wafer photoresists, display materials and advanced-packaging materials.
interesting_fact: Dinglong entered CMP polishing pads in 2012, a market long dominated by Dow and Cabot, and says it is now China's only supplier with full-process, self-controlled pad technology (including its own prepolymers and microspheres); CMP pad sales grew 52% to RMB 795M in 9M 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His motto for chips materials, from a Feb 2026 Securities Times interview: 'There is no overtaking on the curve in semiconductor materials - slowest is fastest' (慢就是快). Before Dinglong he was a department manager at China Hubei International Economic & Technical Cooperation Co. (1997-2000); he is a member of Hubei's 13th CPPCC.
notes: Career details (CPPCC, prior job) from company executive bio at https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/300054/company.html. Board secretary: Yang Pingcai. Gives occasional interviews to Chinese financial press (Securities Times).

name: Pankaj Doshi
current_role: Promoter-shareholder, Waaree Energies Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Pankaj Doshi is one of four Doshi brothers whose family controls Waaree Energies, India's largest solar-module maker by capacity. Waaree's October 2024 listing, which debuted ~70% above its IPO price, made him and his three brothers billionaires. He holds a minority stake; the company is run day-to-day by his brother Hitesh Doshi (chairman & MD).
interesting_fact: Waaree started in 1990 not in solar but as a maker of thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers before pivoting to become India's largest solar-panel manufacturer.
notes: Low public profile; not on Waaree Energies' board per company site. Brother Hitesh Doshi is the public face of Waaree, so outreach likely goes through the company. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so no deep-cut fact found.

name: Liu Shiqi
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hubei Wanrun New Energy Technology Co. (688275.SH)
profile: Liu Shiqi controls Hubei Wanrun New Energy, founded in December 2010 in Shiyan, Hubei. The company makes lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials and precursors for EV and energy-storage batteries. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in September 2022, and Liu still runs it as chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: Liu personally chairs Wanrun's board-level Sustainability Committee. The company has joined the CDP carbon-disclosure programme two years running, scoring B-, and is developing technology to recover lithium carbonate and iron phosphate from waste.
deep_cut_fact: Wanrun funds the 'Wanrun Class' (万润班) at Yunyang High School in Shiyan, the company's hometown: 40 students a year from low-income families get study and living stipends through all three years of high school.
notes: The input's SEC insider link (UMC Vice President) is a different person and does not match. Low public profile, with little personal biography online. The email is Wanrun's general ESG/company contact from its 2024 ESG report; outreach in Chinese is advisable.

name: Li Fei
current_role: Co-founder, co-controlling shareholder and director (per 2024 filings), Hubei Wanrun New Energy Technology (SSE STAR: 688275)
profile: Li Fei (李菲) and her husband, chairman Liu Shiqi, founded and jointly control Hubei Wanrun New Energy, a top-three global lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode maker based in Shiyan, Hubei. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022, it supplies LFP for EV and energy-storage batteries.
interesting_fact: Wanrun grew revenue at a 324% CAGR from 2020 to 2022, reaching RMB 12.35bn in 2022, as LFP displaced other EV battery chemistries and lithium carbonate prices spiked.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wanrun, Li Fei worked at Dongfeng Motor and Shenzhen Zhonghuang Industrial; the founders' first firm, Wanrun Gongmao (2003), made iron-phosphate cathode precursors and got into the supply chain of US battery pioneer A123 before Wanrun New Energy was set up in 2010.
notes: Low public profile; husband Liu Shiqi is chairman and public face (re-elected chairman Dec 2025). Board secretary is Gao Wenjing. Unconfirmed whether Li Fei remained a director after the Dec 2025 board re-election. Best route: board office email.

name: Colette Kress
current_role: Interim CEO (since 12 Nov 2026) and EVP & Chief Financial Officer, NVIDIA.
profile: Kress joined Nvidia as CFO in 2013 after ~25 years in tech finance (Texas Instruments, 13 years at Microsoft, CFO of a Cisco division). She steered its finances as sales rose from $4.3bn to $215.9bn and it became the first $5tn company. On 12 Nov 2026 she was named interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigned, while remaining CFO.
interesting_fact: She joined Nvidia partly at the urging of her two young sons, avid gamers who knew the company from the chips in their favourite video games.
deep_cut_fact: Jensen Huang interviewed 22 candidates before hiring her; in her first week she asked how long he'd want her in the role and he answered, 'For as long as we shall live and death do us part.' She holds a finance B.Sc. from the University of Arizona and an MBA from SMU.
notes: Very timely: just became interim CEO amid Huang's sudden 12 Nov 2026 resignation (personal-conduct reports) - avoid that topic; expect heavy media demand. Best route is Nvidia corporate PR (press@nvidia.com). Q3 FY27 earnings 17 Nov 2026.

name: Lidiya Mikhailova
current_role: Co-owner (about 15%) of Cherkizovo Group, Russia's largest meat producer; her sons Evgeny (chairman) and Sergei (CEO) run it
profile: Ex-wife of Cherkizovo founder Igor Babaev. He built the Moscow Cherkizovsky meat plant into Cherkizovo Group, which listed in London and Moscow in 2006, and later passed his shares to their sons. She holds about 15% alongside sons Evgeny and Sergei Mikhailov (about 28% each). The group has over 20,000 employees and about $3.4bn in 2025 revenue.
interesting_fact: Cherkizovo became a major poultry and pork producer through acquisitions; after buying LISKO Broiler in 2014 its poultry capacity reached about 550,000 tonnes a year. It trades on the Moscow Exchange as GCHE.
notes: Passive shareholder with no public profile; Forbes lists her as 'former' (2024). The company site blocked automated access, so no IR contact was captured. Russian-sanctions context applies, and this is not a useful podcast guest.

name: Bastian Nominacher
current_role: Co-founder & Co-CEO, Celonis (Munich/New York)
profile: Bastian Nominacher co-founded Celonis in 2011 with Alexander Rinke and Martin Klenk, straight out of the Technical University of Munich. Celonis makes process-mining software that analyses companies' system data to find inefficiencies and is now pitched as a 'process intelligence' layer for enterprise AI. It was valued at $13bn in 2022, and Nominacher, co-CEO alongside Rinke, owns about 16%.
interesting_fact: Celonis reached a $1bn valuation in 2018 and $11bn in 2021, making it then Germany's and New York's most valuable startup. It was SAP's process-mining reseller partner from 2015.
deep_cut_fact: Celonis grew out of a student consulting gig. As members of Academy Consult, Munich's largest student consultancy, the three founders analysed internal IT service processes for broadcaster Bayerischer Rundfunk, the work that became the first Celonis product.
notes: Rinke is the more public face; Nominacher focuses on operations and finance. The Celonis newsroom lists only a general info@ address. A good AI-and-operations angle.

name: Xu Yuejuan
current_role: Supervisor, Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding Group (Hangzhou)
profile: Hangzhou-based shareholder and supervisor of Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding Group, the private parent of Shenzhen-listed Rongsheng Petrochemical (002493), one of China's largest refining, petrochemical and polyester-fibre groups. She is the sister-in-law of Rongsheng chairman and cofounder Li Shuirong; Forbes lists her wealth source as petro fibre.
interesting_fact: She has appeared on Forbes' billionaire rankings for years as one of the family shareholders behind Rongsheng, which grew from a 1989 Xiaoshan textile mill into a refining-to-polyester giant.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal channels found. Only route is via Rongsheng Petrochemical's board secretary/IR (tel 0571-82520189 per 2025 annual report summary).

name: Ken Kendrick
current_role: Managing General Partner and principal owner, Arizona Diamondbacks (MLB)
profile: Born 1943 in Princeton, West Virginia, Kendrick started at IBM, then founded higher-education software maker Datatel (merged with SunGard Higher Education into Ellucian, sold to TPG for $3.5bn in 2015) and became principal investor in Texas-based Woodforest National Bank in 1989. A Diamondbacks owner since the 1995 expansion, he has run the club since 2004, including its 2023 World Series run.
interesting_fact: A lifelong collector, he owns the T206 Honus Wagner card once owned by Wayne Gretzky; it and other cards from his 'D-backs Collection' were displayed at the Baseball Hall of Fame, on whose board he has sat since 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He owns Bumble Bee Ranch in Arizona, which hosts western-lifestyle experiences for children's charities, as well as the Ironbridge Golf Club in Glenwood Springs, Colorado.
notes: Best route is the Diamondbacks communications office via the team's official contact page (no media email published there). Also chairs the Arizona Diamondbacks Foundation. Tech angle: founded Datatel/Ellucian; he was personally part of the 2021 investor group that bought Collectors (PSA).

name: Blair Hull
current_role: Founder, Hull Investments (family office) and Hull Tactical Asset Allocation, Chicago
profile: Former blackjack card counter turned options market maker who founded Chicago's Hull Trading Company in 1985, a pioneer of computer-driven trading, and sold it to Goldman Sachs in 1999 for $531m. Since then he has run his family office Hull Investments and quant ETF adviser Hull Tactical, and is a Democratic donor.
interesting_fact: In the 1970s he was one of the 'Big Players' on Al Francesco's blackjack card-counting team (chronicled in Ken Uston's 'The Big Player') and was inducted into the Blackjack Hall of Fame in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before trading he worked on a cannery line and taught high-school math and physics; after leaving blackjack with $25,000 he leased a seat on the Pacific Stock Exchange and built his own options-pricing model without knowing about Black-Scholes.
notes: Aged 84. Hull Investments mailbox is his family office. Avoid the 2004 Senate race divorce-records issue.

name: Tseng Sing-ai
current_role: Shareholder (inherited stake), Chang Chun Group, Taiwan; no public executive role found
profile: Taipei-based heiress who inherited her stake in Chang Chun Group from her father Tseng Shin-yi (d. 2016), who cofounded the company in 1949 with classmates M.K. Liao and Lin Shu-hong. Chang Chun is one of Asia's largest petrochemicals-and-plastics makers, with plants in Taiwan, mainland China and Southeast Asia. Forbes previously listed her jointly with her brother Tseng Cheng.
interesting_fact: Chang Chun Group was founded in 1949 by three classmates, including her father Tseng Shin-yi, and remains privately controlled by the three founding families (Liao, Lin, Tseng).
notes: Very private; no public profile, interviews or official accounts found. Any approach would have to go through Chang Chun Group corporate (ccp.com.tw, site blocked automated access). Forbes listed her jointly with sibling Tseng Cheng until recent years.

name: Zhou Wei family
current_role: Chairman, Winning Health Technology Group (卫宁健康, SZ:300253) as of Forbes' April 2021 profile; current status unverified
profile: Self-made Shanghai software entrepreneur who chairs Winning Health Technology Group, a supplier of IT systems to Chinese hospitals and health institutions (more than 6,000 clients). Demand for digital-health systems during COVID-19 pushed him onto the Forbes and Hurun billionaire lists in 2020-2021. He fell off them as the share price dropped.
interesting_fact: Winning Health's software supports more than 6,000 medical and health institutions in China, and the business got a boost from the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
notes: Forbes' profile was last updated April 2021, and he has not been on the lists since 2022. The search budget ran out and winning.com.cn was unreachable, so I could not confirm his current role. Check recent 300253 announcements before outreach. Healthcare IT is a weak fit for the podcast.

name: Henrik Fisker
current_role: Independent automotive designer and advisor (strategic advisory, board-level and special projects); founder of Fisker Inc. (Chapter 11 in June 2024)
profile: Danish-born car designer (b. 1963, ArtCenter Vevey 1989) who shaped the BMW Z8 and the Aston Martin DB9 and V8 Vantage, and did early design work on the Tesla Model S. He founded Fisker Automotive (Karma plug-in hybrid, 2011) and later Fisker Inc. (Ocean EV, SPAC listing in 2020), which filed for bankruptcy in 2024. He is no longer a billionaire and now takes selective design and brand advisory work.
interesting_fact: He styled the BMW Z8 roadster that James Bond drove in 'The World Is Not Enough'. The Fisker Karma, launched in 2011, was the first premium extended-range electric performance car to reach production.
deep_cut_fact: Besides road cars, he designed a race car for the Formula BMW open-wheel series. His own site says he is particularly interested in turning historic brand designs into iconic timepieces, along with motorsport heritage and F1.
notes: Very reachable: his site openly invites advisory and special-project contact. Avoid dwelling on the Fisker Inc. bankruptcy and the 2013 Fisker Automotive collapse. Design, EV and entrepreneurial-resilience angles suit the podcast. No longer on billionaire lists.

name: Wang Wenjian
current_role: Founder, honorary chairman and non-executive director, Sunny Optical Technology (Group) Co. (HKEX: 2382)
profile: Wang Wenjian (王文鉴, b. ~1947) founded what became Sunny Optical in Yuyao, Zhejiang, in 1984, serving as chairman and CEO before moving to non-executive director in 2012. Sunny is now a global leader in phone camera lenses and modules (1.32bn lenses shipped in 2024) and automotive/AR optics. His son Wang Tan Jiong became board chairman in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Sunny's largest shareholder is an employee trust (Sunny Group Overseas Employee Trust, ~35.5%) co-administered by Wang, a structure designed to avoid family control; the company pivoted to phone optics in 2000 when phones had no cameras of note.
deep_cut_fact: In 1984 he started the business as a small township optical-instrument factory in Yuyao with just eight high-school graduates and a RMB 60,000 loan; he has also been honorary president of the Yuyao Charity Federation (2003) and a guest professor at Zhejiang University (2005).
notes: Age ~78-79; low public profile. Board bio: https://www.irasia.com/listco/hk/sunnyoptical/onlinereport/2025/e_annual/47/ . Best route is Sunny IR office. Shares the Sunny fortune with co-founders such as Ye Liaoning (P07144).

name: Dasari Uday Kumar Reddy
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Tanla Platforms Ltd (Hyderabad)
profile: Uday Reddy founded Tanla in 1999 as an SMS-centre provider for telecom operators and listed it in 2006. Tanla is now a leading Indian CPaaS and enterprise-messaging company, with blockchain-based anti-spam (Trubloq) and anti-phishing (Wisely ATP) platforms. He first joined the Forbes billionaires list in 2022 after Tanla's shares more than doubled in 2021.
interesting_fact: The name 'Tanla' contains his wife's initials. He told LBS he has no family office and no passive investments, and reinvests everything in his own businesses.
deep_cut_fact: At 11 he sold sweets to his whole school. In the late 1980s he sold his only possession, his motorbike, to start a paging business in Hyderabad, camping outside a hardware maker's site in Singapore until he had mastered the technology. He charged per message rather than for hardware.
notes: Not the same person as YuppTV founder Uday Reddy; avoid YourStory or FPJ articles about that Uday Reddy. He did an MBA at Manchester Business School, where seeing UK text-messaging use inspired Tanla. Forbes also notes his first venture was real estate in 1993.

name: Tang Zhuang
current_role: Co-founder, Director, Deputy GM & CTO of Jiangsu Maxscend Microelectronics (SZSE: 300782); Chairman of Wuxi Xinzhuo Huguang Semiconductor
profile: Tang Zhuang (b. 1973) is a co-founder and CTO of Maxscend (卓胜微), a Wuxi-based maker of RF front-end chips (switches, LNAs, filters) for smartphones that listed in Shenzhen in 2019. He has led its shift from fabless to IDM via the 'Xinzhuo' fab project, with 6-inch SAW filter and 12-inch silicon-based lines now in volume production.
interesting_fact: Under his technical lead Maxscend built its own 6-inch SAW filter wafer line in just 14 months and by end-2024 had shipped over 100,000 6-inch and 20,000+ 12-inch wafers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied physics at Peking University and earned his MS/PhD in electrical engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; in his first-ever media interview (2025) he said of heterogeneous integration: 'we have waited for this opportunity for at least 10 years.'
notes: Input lists source as 'Guide Electrics', which does not match; the semiconductor billionaire Tang Zhuang on Forbes 2021/Hurun 2019-21 appears to be Maxscend's co-founder (Maxscend's founders made those lists), but the label mismatch is unresolved. Board secretary Liu Liqiong; IR mailbox info@maxscend.com.

name: Wu Daohong
current_role: Founder and former chairman/controlling shareholder, Shenwu Technology Group (神雾集团), Beijing; current role unclear
profile: Combustion engineer who did postdoctoral research at China University of Petroleum (1995) and founded Shenwu in 1996 to commercialise energy-saving industrial furnace and burner technology. Shenwu grew into a group with two listed arms (Shenwu Environmental, Shenwu Energy Saving) before a 2017-18 liquidity crisis.
interesting_fact: China Daily credits Wu with inventing a 'third-generation' combustion technology in 2001, behind Shenwu's high-efficiency regenerative burner, which it says cuts energy use by over 30% on average.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually hands-on for a billionaire, Wu is a named inventor on many Shenwu patents (e.g. CN104848220A on regenerative combustion devices for heating furnaces) and co-authored a 2015 Energy Procedia paper on double-preheating regenerative burners.
notes: Low priority and sensitive. The Shenwu group collapsed in a 2017-18 debt crisis (shares frozen, executives left). In Nov 2025 the Shenzhen Stock Exchange proposed a public reprimand of Shenwu Environmental and Wu over past violations (https://finance.eastmoney.com/news/1354,202511043554848524.html). Last on rich lists in 2018. No current public contact found.

name: Clayton Riddell
current_role: Deceased (died September 15, 2018, aged 81); was founder, president and CEO of Paramount Resources, Calgary
notes: Died Sept 15, 2018 (Globe and Mail obituary, Sept 25, 2018: https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-clay-riddell-81-was-a-billionaire-and-philanthropist-who-thrived-in/ ; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_Riddell). Paramount Resources (Calgary) continues as a listed company if an energy-guest angle is wanted.

name: Daisy Igel
profile: Brazilian architect and heiress (born 1927), daughter of Ernesto Igel, who founded Ultragaz/Ultrapar. Reported to have died in 2019.
notes: Deceased. Wikipedia gives her death as 2019, citing a 2024 UNIFESP dissertation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daisy_Igel). This fits her dropping off Forbes after 2018. I found no Brazilian obituary to confirm the exact date. Skipped.

name: Kenneth Adams, Jr.
profile: K.S. 'Bud' Adams Jr. (1923-2013), founder and chairman/CEO of Adams Resources & Energy and founding owner of the AFL's Houston Oilers (now NFL Tennessee Titans). Died October 21, 2013.
notes: Deceased 21 Oct 2013 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Adams). Not a candidate for outreach; Titans now owned by his heirs.

name: Marguerite Harbert
profile: Died March 17, 2015 in Mountain Brook, Alabama, aged 91. She was Alabama's only billionaire, having inherited the fortune of her husband John M. Harbert III, founder of Harbert Corporation, in 1995.
notes: Deceased (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marguerite_Harbert ; Birmingham News obituary 'Marguerite Harbert, Alabama's only billionaire, dies at 91', al.com, March 19, 2015). Remove from outreach list. Her son Raymond J. Harbert runs Harbert Management Corp. if the family/firm is of interest.

name: Ural Rakhimov
current_role: No known current corporate role; former chairman of Bashneft (until 2009); reported to live in Austria
profile: Russian (Bashkir) businessman, b. 1961 in Ufa, son of ex-Bashkortostan president Murtaza Rakhimov. He headed the Bashkir oil complex (Bashneft and refineries), sold to AFK Sistema in 2005-2009. He left Russia after being charged in absentia in 2014; an Austrian court declined extradition in 2016.
interesting_fact: In March 2016 the Vienna Regional Criminal Court refused Russia's extradition request, citing political motives behind the case against him.
deep_cut_fact: A trained petroleum engineer: he graduated from Ufa State Petroleum Technological University in 1984, then earned an MSc at the French Petroleum Institute (IFP) and a second master's in the US; he briefly owned KHL hockey club Salavat Yulaev Ufa (2009-10).
notes: Not a suitable outreach target: wanted in Russia since 2014 on embezzlement/laundering charges (contested as political), living abroad (Austria) with no public presence or published contact. Alive status based on Wikipedia 'living people' and no death reports; not independently confirmed recently.

name: David Yakobashvili
current_role: President, Orion Heritage Co. (private Museum 'Collection', Moscow); founder of InOil (GreenBooster fuel additive)
profile: Tbilisi-born (1957) entrepreneur who cofounded Russian dairy-and-juice giant Wimm-Bill-Dann and chaired it 2001-2010; it sold to PepsiCo for ~$5.7B in 2010-11, netting him ~$600M for his ~10% stake. He later moved into energy: InOil's GreenBooster fuel additive, Bioenergy Corp, and African mineral trading.
interesting_fact: The 'Wimm-Bill-Dann' name was coined to sound like 'Wimbledon'; in 2002 the company became the first Russian food company to IPO on the NYSE.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious collector of self-playing musical instruments and automatons: his Moscow museum 'Collection' grew from his ~2000 purchase of Swedish collector Bill Lindwall's ~460 mechanical instruments and now holds over 20,000 items, including wax cylinders and perforated piano rolls.
notes: Holds Swedish citizenship per Wikipedia. Left RSPP board and AFK Sistema board in 2022. No personal press channel found; museum is the only organisation-published route. Energy angle: GreenBooster fuel additive and Bioenergy Corp.

name: Mokhzani Mahathir
current_role: President, Motorsports Association of Malaysia (MAM); owner of Kencana Capital Sdn Bhd
profile: Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir (b. 1961), son of ex-PM Mahathir, is a petroleum engineer who founded Kencana Petroleum. It merged with SapuraCrest in 2012 to form SapuraKencana (now Sapura Energy). He now invests via Kencana Capital and leads Malaysian motorsport as MAM president.
interesting_fact: He chaired Sepang International Circuit for over a decade. As MAM president he said in October 2026 that Sepang has the capability and experience to host Formula 1 again.
deep_cut_fact: He is a racer as well as an administrator. Driving a Porsche 911 GT3 RSR for Team Hong Leong-Kencana Racing with Sven Herberger and Lars Erik Nielsen, he won the 2007 Merdeka Millennium Endurance race (Sepang 12 Hours). He earned his engineering degree at the University of Tulsa.
notes: No published personal or office email found. The most likely official route is the Motorsports Association of Malaysia (mam.org.my; site is JS-rendered and no email could be extracted). He left all Opcom positions in 2019 and retired from politics (quit UMNO in 2008). Motorsport is the strongest rapport angle.

name: Zhou Wenyu
profile: Listed once (Forbes 2018) as a Chinese real-estate billionaire worth ~$1.2bn; no company, Chinese name or Forbes profile could be found to pin down which Zhou Wenyu this is.
notes: Ambiguous: no company or Chinese characters in source data and searches return no matching tycoon. Needs the company name (or Chinese name) before any outreach.

name: Yang Jianxin
current_role: Former chairman/actual controller of Global Top E-Commerce (KJT, 跨境通, SZSE 002640); executive director of Shanxi Baiyuan Trousers
profile: Shanxi entrepreneur who built Baiyuan Trousers (百圆裤业), a budget trousers retail chain listed in Shenzhen in 2011. In 2014 it bought Shenzhen cross-border e-tailer Huanqiu Yigou (Gearbest, Zaful) for RMB1bn and became KJT, briefly making Yang Shanxi's richest man. He sold control to a Guangzhou state fund in 2019; Huanqiu Yigou went into bankruptcy in 2021.
interesting_fact: The 2014 RMB1bn acquisition of Huanqiu Yigou turned a Taiyuan trousers retailer into one of China's first listed cross-border e-commerce players, and made Yang the richest person in Shanxi.
deep_cut_fact: Before cross-border e-commerce, his business was Baiyuan Trousers, a Shanxi chain of budget men's trousers stores, which he grew into a Shenzhen-listed company in 2011.
notes: Probably no longer a billionaire: 2025 Chinese media report he is under 5 court consumption-restriction orders (about RMB2.2bn enforced) and his shares are being judicially auctioned; he is also in a public dispute with Huanqiu Yigou founder Xu Jiadong. Not a good podcast target; no published personal contact found.

name: Chen Jianming
profile: Listed by Hurun (2007-2021) and Forbes (2018) as a property developer whose wealth comes from 'Guangda', shared with Chen Runguang. Several searches in English and Chinese (陈建铭 / 陈润广 / 光大) did not establish which 'Guangda' company this is; it is not the state-owned China Everbright (光大) Group.
notes: Identity not confirmed: Chen Jianming is a common name and Guangda (光大) is a common company name. Needs a lookup of the Hurun China Rich List entry (e.g. the 2019 list) to pin down the company and city before any outreach.

name: Carlos Fernández González
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO of Grupo Finaccess (Mexico/Spain); Honorary Chairman of AmRest (majority owner via Finaccess)
profile: Mexican businessman (b. 1966, Mexico City) who ran Grupo Modelo, maker of Corona, as CEO from 1997 and chairman from 2005 until its 2013 sale to AB InBev. He then built investment group Finaccess, which controls Europe-based restaurant operator AmRest (KFC, Pizza Hut, Burger King franchises) and holds stakes in Spanish firms such as Colonial and Prisa.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Grupo Modelo became one of the world's largest brewers before its 2013 sale to AB InBev; Finaccess later became AmRest's controlling shareholder (about two-thirds of the shares).
deep_cut_fact: An industrial engineer from Universidad Anáhuac, he also took a beer-brewing course at the University of California, Davis, before leading Modelo. He founded the Mexico chapter of Fundación Carolina and the Academia Mexicana de la Comunicación.
notes: Wikipedia education details are flagged as lacking citations; verify the UC Davis detail before using. He left the AmRest board in May 2023 (now honorary chairman); José Parés chairs AmRest. Finaccess is the more relevant route.

name: Li Yiping (李一萍)
current_role: No executive role found; spouse of Times China Holdings (HKEX:1233) founder/chairman Shum Chiu Hung (岑钊雄)
profile: Li Yiping appears on Hurun rich lists jointly with her husband Shum Chiu Hung, founder of Guangzhou developer Times China Holdings (listed in Hong Kong in 2013). HKEX filings describe her as his wife and a connected person who co-owned Guangzhou property used by the company. No public business profile of her own was found.
interesting_fact: Times China's 2013 HKEX disclosure records that the company occupied Guangzhou premises owned by Li Yiping and the Shum family's Times Development group, making her a 'connected person' of the listed company.
notes: Very private; wealth is via husband Shum Chiu Hung's Times China stake (Hurun lists them jointly). Hurun's 2018 'self-made women' listing suggests she was treated as co-founder, but no independent profile found. Any approach should go via Times China corporate channels; live status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Chizuko Matsui
current_role: Shareholder of Matsui Securities (former controlling shareholder); no executive role found
profile: Chizuko Matsui (松井千鶴子) was the largest and controlling shareholder of Tokyo online broker Matsui Securities, holding about 58% of voting rights (directly and indirectly) in 2015. In 2016-17 she transferred shares to Maruroku Ltd, the founding family's asset-management company, after which she ceased to be a major/controlling shareholder. Wealth is shared with longtime president Michio Matsui.
interesting_fact: Matsui Securities, founded in 1931 as a tiny brokerage, reinvented itself in the mid-1990s as one of Japan's first online brokers; in Nov 2026 Japan Post Bank agreed to buy shares from Maruroku and become its largest shareholder.
notes: Extremely private; no public profile, interviews or role beyond shareholder filings (JPX disclosures e.g. https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/86280/140120161104430973.pdf). Exact family relationship to Michio Matsui not confirmed in sources. Not a podcast-likely guest; any approach would be via Matsui Securities/Maruroku.

name: Michio Matsui
current_role: Advisor (former President & Representative Director, 1995-2020), Matsui Securities Co., Ltd.
profile: Michio Matsui (b. 1953, born Mutai) married into the Matsui family and ran Matsui Securities as president for 25 years (1995-2020). He turned a tiny Tokyo broker into a pioneer of Japanese online brokerage, entering internet trading in earnest in 1998. He handed the presidency to Akira Warita in June 2020 and now serves as an advisor.
interesting_fact: Before finance he spent 11 years at shipping line NYK (Nippon Yusen) after graduating from Hitotsubashi in 1976; he joined Matsui Securities in 1987 as a mid-career hire and became president just eight years later.
deep_cut_fact: As a Tokyo high-school student he hung out in jazz cafes, was friends with singer Tatsuro Yamashita, and was in the art club aiming for Tokyo University of the Arts until a teacher talked him out of it.

public_contacts.value: https://www.matsui.co.jp/company/history/essay/ (Matsui Securities page hosting his memoir as former president)

notes: Wealth shared with wife Chizuko Matsui (daughter of the previous president). Retired from management; best route is likely via Matsui Securities corporate office. Speaks/writes in Japanese.

name: Fan Meihua
current_role: Co-shareholder (with husband Yang Jianxin) in KJT / Global Top E-Commerce (跨境通, SZSE: 002640); no confirmed executive role
profile: Fan Meihua (樊梅花) is the wife and concert party of Yang Jianxin, founder of Shanxi-based Baiyuan Trousers, which became cross-border e-commerce group KJT (跨境通) after acquiring export e-retailers Globalegrow (环球易购) and Patozon. The couple were controlling holders; from 2019 they ceded voting control to a Guangzhou state-backed fund (unwound 2021) and sold down stakes. Little else is public.
interesting_fact: SZSE filings describe Yang Jianxin and Fan Meihua as legal spouses and formal 'persons acting in concert' who jointly controlled KJT until a 2019 voting-rights delegation to a Guangzhou Development District fund.
notes: Very private; no public profile found. Hurun listing (2016-2020) was via the couple's KJT stake, which has since shrunk sharply, so she is likely no longer a billionaire. Only route would be KJT board secretary (Wang Yuedi per 2025-26 IR records) via cninfo filings / ir.p5w.net.

name: Zheng Jianming
current_role: Chairman, Asia Pacific Resources Development Investment (APRD); former controlling backer of Shunfeng International Clean Energy (HK:1165, in liquidation since Nov 2025)
profile: Hong Kong-based tycoon (Cantonese name Cheng Kin Ming) who made his money in China/HK real estate, then from 2012 built a clean-energy portfolio through APRD: Shunfeng (which bought bankrupt Wuxi Suntech in 2013), Nobao geothermal, Lattice Power LEDs, GreenWheel EV and US battery maker Boston-Power. Shunfeng later ran into debt problems and entered liquidation in 2025.
interesting_fact: He bankrolled Shunfeng's 2013 rescue of Wuxi Suntech, once the world's largest solar-panel maker, after it went bankrupt.
deep_cut_fact: Long described as reclusive, he made a rare public debut on a 2014 US tour (a NYC solar-finance conference, then Goldman Sachs' EcoSummit), pledging 50 GW of clean energy in 10 years and saying geothermal firm Nobao would replace coal heating in Beijing and Tianjin.
notes: Very private, little coverage since about 2019. No reports of death found, but nothing recent confirms his status. Shunfeng (01165.HK) is in liquidation (shares suspended 19 Nov 2025) and its only contacts are the liquidators. He is a creditor (via APRDIL). No published personal or office contact found. Probably a low-yield outreach target.

name: Chung Mong Jin
current_role: Chairman (and CEO), KCC Corporation / KCC Group, South Korea
profile: Eldest son of KCC founder Chung Sang-young (youngest brother of Hyundai founder Chung Ju-yung), he has led KCC, Korea's leading paint, building-materials and silicone maker, since the 2000s. He steered KCC's 2019 consortium buyout of US silicones maker Momentive Performance Materials from Apollo (~$3bn) and in 2024 moved KCC to full ownership.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership KCC bought Momentive Performance Materials from Apollo in 2019 for about $3.1bn, turning a Korean paint company into one of the world's largest silicone producers; in 2024 it agreed to buy out partner SJL Partners for 100% ownership.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is KCC corporate communications via the company website. Brother Chung Mong-ik is vice chairman.

name: Khaleefa Butti bin Omair Al-Muhairi
current_role: Emirati investor; former vice-chairman and major shareholder of NMC Health (resigned Feb 2020); listed as chairman of Travelex Holding
profile: Abu Dhabi businessman (name also spelled Khalifa Butti Omeir Bin Yousef) who, with partners, built a stake of roughly 40% in UAE hospital group NMC Health, partly by buying shares from founder B.R. name: Paul Salteri

name: Hirokazu Sugiura
current_role: Founder and adviser (non-executive), Sugi Holdings; chairman of the council of the Sugiura Memorial Foundation
profile: Pharmacist Hirokazu Sugiura (b. 1950, Nishio, Aichi) founded Sugi Pharmacy in 1976 and built it into Sugi Holdings, one of Japan's largest drugstore/dispensing chains (~¥1 trillion revenue). name: Zhang Tianren

name: Edward W. Stack
current_role: Executive Chairman, DICK'S Sporting Goods, Inc. (since Feb 2021; CEO 1984-2021)

name: Xiu Laigui
current_role: Founder and chairman, Xiuzheng Pharmaceutical Group (修正药业), Tonghua, Jilin
profile: Born 1955 in Tonghua, Jilin, Xiu studied law at Jilin University and spent about 20 years in the Tonghua public security system. name: Bhaskara Rao Bollineni
current_role: Founder & Chairman (Managing Director), KIMS Hospitals (Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd)
profile: Cardiothoracic surgeon who founded KIMS Hospitals in 2000, starting with a 200-bed hospital in his hometown of Nellore, Andhra Pradesh. KIMS is now a listed chain of about 25 hospitals with roughly 8,300 beds across five southern and western Indian states. His son Dr. Abhinay Bollineni is CEO, and he remains chairman and a practising surgeon.

name: Sir Dennis Gillings
current_role: Non-Executive Chair and Founder, GHO Capital (healthcare investment firm); retired IQVIA lead director (2018)
profile: British-born statistician (b. 1944, London) who co-founded Quintiles in Durham, NC, growing it from UNC biostatistics consulting into the world's largest clinical-research organisation; Quintiles merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form IQVIA. Now an investor/chair at London-based GHO Capital and a dementia-research advocate.
interesting_fact: In 2014 David Cameron appointed him World Dementia Envoy; he helped found and became first chairman of the World Dementia Council, and was knighted in 2020 for services to dementia and life-sciences research.
deep_cut_fact: Quintiles traces back to a single 1974 project: Hoechst hired the UNC biostatistics professor to analyse trial data for a new diabetes drug; his analysis showed which patients to exclude, letting Hoechst bring it to market. The company was only incorporated in 1982 with fellow professor Gary Koch.
notes: Lane name 'Sir Dennis' = Sir Dennis Gillings (wealth shared with wife Mireille Gillings, per Sunday Times). Son of a London fishmonger (Wikipedia). Best route likely via GHO Capital (ghocapital.com) — no published personal contact found.

current_role: Founder, CEO & Executive Chair, HUYABIO International; Co-founder & Non-Executive Vice Chair, GHO Capital
profile: Montreal-born neurobiologist (PhD Radboud Nijmegen, postdocs at Bordeaux and Scripps) who founded San Diego-based HUYA Bioscience International in 2004 to in-license and develop novel drugs discovered in China. She co-founded London healthcare private-equity firm GHO Capital. Married to Sir Dennis Gillings, founder of Quintiles (now IQVIA), source of the shared family fortune.

notes: Styled Lady Mireille Gillings. Listed as UK on Sunday Times Rich List but based in San Diego. Healthcare/biotech focus; best route is HUYABIO contact form.

current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shijiazhuang Shangtai Technology (SZ:001301)
profile: Born 1966, Ouyang is a carbon-materials engineer who built Shangtai Technology in Hebei into a major maker of graphite anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. He owns about 36.5% of the company, which listed in Shenzhen in 2022. H1 2026 revenue rose 33% to RMB 4.5bn.

current_role: Honorary chairman (and vice chairman) of Tongfu Microelectronics (002156.SZ); son Shi Lei is chairman & president
profile: Nanjing University physics graduate and engineer (b. 1945) who in 1990 took over the debt-ridden Nantong Transistor Factory and turned it into Tongfu Microelectronics, now the world's No.4 chip packaging & test group. notes: Hurun lists wealth shared with son Shi Lei (current chairman). Strong AI/data-center angle via AMD advanced packaging. Gave a long interview to Shanghai Securities News in Feb 2026, so open to press; approach via board secretary office (Jiang Shu).

current_role: Founder, Chairman, President and CEO, VeriSilicon Microelectronics (688521.SH), Shanghai
profile: Dai Weimin (Wayne Dai) earned his BS and PhD in EECS at UC Berkeley, taught computer engineering at UC Santa Cruz and founded chip-design-software firms Ultima and Celestry (bought by Cadence in 2002).
