profile: Dr. Weiwei Luo, China's 'Queen of Gallium Nitride', holds an applied-math PhD from Massey University (NZ) and spent ~15 years at a NASA-affiliated institute before founding Innoscience in 2015; it built China's first 8-inch GaN-on-silicon line and listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024. In 2022 she also founded Micro LED startup Xingyue Semiconductor.
interesting_fact: In 2025 Innoscience was named the youngest company on NVIDIA's partner list for its 800V DC data-center power architecture, supplying GaN power solutions from 800V input down to the GPU.
deep_cut_fact: She described starting Innoscience as 'Difficult, really difficult, extremely difficult': only one employee followed her back from the US, and she bet on an 8-inch GaN process when rivals used 4-6 inch, after rising from senior project manager to chief scientist at a NASA-affiliated institute.

public_contacts.value: https://www.innoscience.com/contact-us (general company email IS@innoscience.com listed there)

notes: Highly relevant to data-center power (GaN for AI server PSUs, NVIDIA 800V DC). Speaks English; approach via Innoscience corporate channels.

name: Zhu Shuangquan
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and Executive Director, Hubei Dinglong Holding (鼎龙股份, 300054.SZ); also Chairman of Wuhan Zhongyuan Huadian (300018.SZ) since Dec 2025
profile: Zhu Shuangquan (朱双全) co-founded Wuhan-based Dinglong in July 2000 with his brother Zhu Shunquan (general manager); together they hold ~29%. Dinglong began in printing/imaging consumables and became a key Chinese supplier of semiconductor materials: CMP polishing pads and slurries, display materials, photoresists and advanced-packaging materials. It filed for a Hong Kong listing in July 2026.
interesting_fact: Dinglong is one of China's few domestic makers of CMP polishing pads, a chokepoint material in chipmaking; 2025 revenue reached RMB2.47bn with profit of ~RMB796m.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Dinglong he was a cadre at the Hubei Provincial Federation of Trade Unions doing labour-union theory research; he holds a 1987 Wuhan University diploma in the history of the Chinese revolution and a 2012 Peking University Guanghua MBA.
notes: hbdl@dl-kg.com is Dinglong's general corporate inbox. Investor Q&A is run through the 'Tougua Yi' (投关易) WeChat mini-program; board secretary is Yang Pingcai. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Michael Tojner
current_role: Founder/CEO, Montana Tech Components and Global Equity Partners (Vienna); chairman of supervisory board, Montana Aerospace; major shareholder of Varta
profile: Austrian serial entrepreneur (b. 1966) who bought microbattery maker Varta in 2007 for ~$40m and floated it in 2017; his Montana Tech Components group also built Montana Aerospace and Aluflexpack (sold 2024). He runs Global Equity Partners and developer WertInvest. Varta is in restructuring; he reportedly wants to keep its microbattery arm.
interesting_fact: He co-founded the online betting company bwin with university friend Manfred Bodner; the pair had earlier run a mail-order business that sold 40,000 Chinese-made mixers into newly opened Hungary after the fall of the Iron Curtain.
deep_cut_fact: The son of a plumber, he made his first million schillings as a 20-year-old WU Vienna student selling ice cream: he talked a bank into a 300,000-schilling loan, won a concession at Schonbrunn Palace and ran carts there and at Kahlenberg, Laxenburg and Belvedere, selling up to 5,000 cones a day.

public_contacts.value: office@gep.at (Global Equity Partners, his investment firm, Vienna)

notes: Best route is probably Global Equity Partners' published office email. Varta filed for insolvency/protective-shield proceedings in 2026 - a sensitive topic; avoid leading with it. Holds doctorates in business (WU Vienna) and law (Univ. of Vienna) per trend.at.

name: Manfred Gorvy
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hanover Acceptances Limited (London)
profile: South African-born (1938) chartered accountant based in London who founded the private investment group Hanover Acceptances in 1974. The group focuses on real estate (Dorrington, African Realty Trust), agribusiness (Letaba citrus in South Africa) and venture capital (Fresh Capital); it formerly backed drinks bottler Refresco Gerber.
interesting_fact: In 2014 Gorvy rejected a Blackstone approach for Refresco Gerber, then one of Europe's largest juice and soft-drink bottlers.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife Lydia funded the 2011 refurbishment of a Victoria and Albert Museum lecture theatre, now the Lydia and Manfred Gorvy Lecture Theatre; they also support the National Theatre, Tate, RSC and Donmar Warehouse.
notes: Aged 88 and private; day-to-day CEO of Hanover Acceptances is now Sean Gorvy. Only route is the group's general reception address.

name: Sanjeev Shah
current_role: Chairman, Everest Food Products Pvt Ltd (Everest Spices), Mumbai
profile: Sanjeev Shah chairs Everest, the Mumbai spice brand his father Vadilal Shah registered in 1967 with three masalas sold from a 200 sq ft shop. He joined in 1981 and built the sales and distribution network; brother Rajiv joined in 1992. Everest calls itself India's largest maker of pure and blended spices, exports to 80+ countries and has added herb seasonings and ginger/garlic pastes since 2021.
interesting_fact: Everest's first three products in 1967 were Milk Masala, Garam Masala and Tea Masala; by 2005 it held about 30% of India's branded spice market.
deep_cut_fact: The year after Sanjeev joined to build distribution, Everest held its first dealer meet, 'Everest Ki Yadgaar Raat' (1982), and in 1983 launched its first TV ad on Doordarshan with producer Harish Bhimani.
notes: Private, low-profile family; very few interviews. Corporate contact form/customer-care email on the website is the only published route. Avoid the 2024 Singapore/Hong Kong ethylene oxide recall topic.

name: Stefania Triva
current_role: President & CEO and largest shareholder, Copan Italia S.p.A. (Brescia)
profile: CEO and ~48% owner of Copan, founded by her father Giorgio in 1979. Her late brother Daniele invented the flocked swab there in 2003, making Copan a world leader in diagnostic swabs and lab automation. She became CEO in 2014, led it through the Covid demand surge, and keeps it family-owned despite buyout offers.
interesting_fact: Flocked swabs made up more than 80% of Copan's $445M revenue in 2021. The Covid-19 testing boom made Triva a billionaire.
deep_cut_fact: In 2023 President Mattarella named her a Cavaliere del Lavoro (Knight of Labour) for the medical-devices industry. She started out as a teenager in the 1980s packing boxes at her father's company.
notes: info@copangroup.com is Copan's general address, published in a 2020 press statement signed by Triva. Copan is private and keeps a low profile; the best route is the corporate contacts page. Copan is now based in Brescia. The box-packing detail comes from a Forbes profile reprinted in Forbes Middle East ('Nose for Business', 2022).

name: Huh Jae-myung
current_role: Private investor; former CEO and largest shareholder of Iljin Materials (now Lotte Energy Materials); still holds stakes in Iljin Display and Iljin Steel
profile: Second son of Iljin Group founder Huh Jin-kyu. As CEO and 53.3% owner of Iljin Materials he built it into a leading maker of elecfoil (thin copper foil) for EV batteries. He sold that stake to Lotte Chemical for 2.7 trillion won in a deal agreed in October 2022 and closed in March 2023. Afterwards he founded the investment firm Company H, stepping down as its representative in 2025.
interesting_fact: He sold his 53.3% stake in Iljin Materials, a world-leading maker of copper foil for EV batteries, to Lotte Chemical for about 2.7 trillion won (about $1.9bn). The deal closed in 2023 and the company was renamed Lotte Energy Materials.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Iljin in February 2023 he set up a private investment firm, Company H (an LLC), as its sole executive. In July 2024 it signed a strategic partnership with NH Investment & Securities to co-invest in acquisition and project-financing deals.
notes: Romanised as Heo Jae-myeong in some outlets. Very low public profile, and no published contacts found. Avoid family topics: reports mention little contact with his brother. Forbes lists him as a former billionaire.

name: Kavita Singhania
current_role: Shareholder (~5%) in J.K. Cement Ltd; director of Express Infrastructure (Chennai real-estate developer)
profile: Kavita Yadupati Singhania holds a stake in listed J.K. Cement, run until his 2020 death by her husband Yadupati Singhania as chairman & MD. She briefly served as a non-executive director of J.K. Cement (2020-21) and is a director of Chennai developer Express Infrastructure; she has no operating role in the cement business.
interesting_fact: She is a granddaughter of newspaper baron Ramnath Goenka, founder of the Indian Express media group.
notes: Low public profile. Stake (~5.01% as of June 2023) and 2020-21 directorship per MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/KAVITA-Y-SINGHANIA-A0CFTB). Only route found is via J.K. Cement corporate/IR channels.

name: Michael Rees
current_role: Co-President and board member, Blue Owl Capital; Head of GP Strategic Capital platform
profile: Rees spent 2001-09 at Lehman Brothers (head of asset management strategy 2003-06), moved to Neuberger Berman in its 2009 management buyout as first COO of its alternatives unit, and founded Dyal Capital there, pioneering buying minority stakes in private equity firms. Dyal merged with Owl Rock in 2021 to form NYSE-listed Blue Owl, where he co-presides and runs GP Strategic Capital.
interesting_fact: Dyal/Blue Owl GP Strategic Capital has bought minority stakes in 60+ private equity firms and runs a sports fund with pieces of the NBA's Phoenix Suns, Sacramento Kings and Atlanta Hawks.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he holds a BS in mechanical engineering and a BA in political science from the University of Pittsburgh plus MIT master's degrees in mechanical engineering and technology policy; his family backs the Rees Chancellor Scholarship program at Pitt. He calls himself a proud Pittsburgh 'Yinzer'.
notes: Has done podcasts (Capital Allocators ep. 278, CAIS Live) and a PEI 'Off-duty' interview on how Dyal got its name and Guns N' Roses (https://www.privateequityinternational.com/off-duty-blue-owls-michael-rees-on-how-dyal-got-its-name-guns-n-roses-and-being-a-yinzer/, paywalled). Blue Owl is a major data-center financier, relevant to the podcast. Route via Blue Owl media.

name: Chen Wenping
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Sailvan Times Co., Ltd. (赛维时代, SZSE ChiNext: 301381)
profile: Chen Wenping (陈文平) founded Shenzhen-based Sailvan Times in 2012 as a cross-border e-commerce seller and built it into a brand incubator selling fashion and lifestyle products to overseas consumers via Amazon and other platforms. Sailvan listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in July 2023; Chen is the controlling shareholder with roughly 37% and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Sailvan describes itself as a technology-driven 'smart commerce platform' organised as a 'small front-end + big middle platform' structure, combining product design, brand incubation and supply-chain integration for global online shoppers.
notes: Very low public profile; little personal biography online in English. Country blank in input but he and the company are mainland China (Shenzhen). Route via Sailvan investor relations / board secretary.

name: Gina Vecchiarelli
current_role: Co-heir and principal shareholder (with sister Terry Leprino) of Leprino Foods, Denver; no public executive role
profile: Daughter of James Leprino, who built his father's 1950 Denver cheese shop into the world's largest mozzarella maker (supplier to Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's). After his death in June 2025, she and her sister inherited a ~90% stake in the private company. She keeps a very low profile; her father said in 2016 she ran a program for Make-A-Wish.
interesting_fact: Leprino Foods makes more than 1 billion pounds of cheese a year; her father pioneered the technology to manufacture pizza mozzarella at industrial scale.

public_contacts.value: No email published; Leprino Corporate Communications media line 720-295-4815 (company press line)

notes: Very private, no public footprint found. Forbes says her husband Dan Vecchiarelli became chairman/CEO c.2023, but Leprino's own site names Lance FitzSimmons President & CEO (Oct 2024) and does not mention Vecchiarelli - verify before outreach. Only route is via Leprino corporate communications.

name: Holger Timm
current_role: Chairman of the management board, Berliner Effektengesellschaft AG; CEO, Tradegate AG Wertpapierhandelsbank
profile: A Berlin stockbroker who founded Berliner Effektengesellschaft (BEG) in 1986 and remains its majority shareholder. BEG holds about 57% of Tradegate AG, which runs the Tradegate trading platform (launched 2000) and co-owns Tradegate BSX exchange with Deutsche Börse; BEG also holds a stake in Quirin Privatbank.
interesting_fact: Tradegate, launched in 2000 as one of the first electronic trading systems for German online brokers, became a full exchange (Tradegate BSX) co-owned with Deutsche Börse and is now a key venue for retail traders and neobrokers; Timm chairs its exchange council.
notes: Low media profile. BEG ownership ~56.6% of Tradegate per 2025 half-year report (Forbes' 88% figure refers to his stake in BEG). Generic company inboxes only.

name: Simón Pedro Barceló Vadell
current_role: Executive chairman and CEO, Barceló Group (Barceló Corporación Empresarial), Palma de Mallorca
profile: Born in Palma in 1966, he studied law at the University of the Balearic Islands and joined the family tourism group in 1993. He co-chaired it with his cousin Simón Barceló Tous from 2000 and now leads it alone after his cousin's age-limit retirement in 2025. The group, founded in 1931, runs 300+ hotels in about 30 countries plus the Ávoris travel business.
interesting_fact: Barceló started in 1931 as a bus/transport company in Mallorca and opened its first hotel only in 1962. Hosteltur named Simón Pedro Barceló its 2023 Tourism Personality of the Year, marking 30 years at the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he was a senator for the Partido Popular from 1989 to 1993, entering the Spanish Senate in his early twenties.
notes: He gives Spanish-media interviews fairly often (Hosteltur, Exceltur forums) and is a former president of the Exceltur tourism lobby. The best route is the group communications office.

name: Tang Ye
current_role: Chairman (since 2007) and CEO, Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) Electronic Technology (SSE STAR: 688188)
profile: Tang Ye co-founded Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) Electronic Technology in September 2007 in Shanghai's Zizhu high-tech zone, near Shanghai Jiao Tong University, where he earned a master's in engineering management. The company makes control systems and software for fiber laser cutting machines and listed on the STAR Market in August 2019; he remains its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: Friendess was one of China's first private companies developing fiber laser cutting control systems and now supplies control systems to more than 400 laser equipment makers.
notes: Low international profile; communicates in Chinese. Investor posts relaying a SJTU video interview say the five co-founders took tiny salaries early on and never raised outside capital, but this is unverified so it is not used as a fact.

name: Nikita Mishin
current_role: Founder, Dar Charitable Foundation for the Promotion of Education; private investor (former Globaltrans co-owner)
profile: Nikita Mishin (b. 1971) built his fortune in Russian freight logistics with partners Konstantin Nikolaev and Andrei Filatov, co-founding rail operator Globaltrans and port group Global Ports. He exited ports in 2017 and sold his Globaltrans stake around 2024; UK-based, he now devotes himself largely to education philanthropy through his Dar foundation.
interesting_fact: His Dar foundation opened Moscow's New School in 2017 with needs-blind admission and fees about half those of other private schools; it gets roughly 600 applicants for ~48 entry places a year.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Moscow State University, earning a degree that qualified him to teach or research the subject, and has said: 'I was never absolutely happy being just an entrepreneur.' He reportedly still sits in on New School classes via Zoom.
notes: Best angle is education philanthropy (Dar / New School). Dar foundation is based in Moscow; he lives in the UK (dual UK citizenship since 2024 per Forbes). Wikipedia also notes Cypriot citizenship (2015).

name: Edwin Soeryadjaya
current_role: Co-founder and President Commissioner, PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya (also President Commissioner of Merdeka Copper Gold)
profile: Son of Astra founder William Soeryadjaya; USC business graduate who joined Astra in 1978 and led its restructuring and IPO. After the family lost Astra in the 1990s, he co-founded Saratoga with Sandiaga Uno (1997-98), building stakes in Adaro, Tower Bersama, Merdeka Copper Gold and ~40 firms. His son Michael now runs Saratoga.
interesting_fact: He was one of the consortium (with his father, Garibaldi Thohir, Sandiaga Uno and Teddy Rachmat) that bought into Adaro in 2005, now one of Indonesia's largest coal and energy groups; EY named him Indonesia Entrepreneur of the Year in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: His comeback after Astra started with a Rp15 million loan to bid for a PT Telkom operational-cooperation (KSO) tender, drawing on telecom experience from his Astra days; his firm became one of five winners. He also chairs the foundation behind Universitas Kristen Indonesia (UKI) in Jakarta.
notes: Born 1949; low public profile. The IR email comes from a broker's company-profile page (last updated 2023), not Saratoga's own site, so verify it. His exact current board title is per MarketScreener and secondary sources. Deep-cut detail is from a secondary Indonesian profile (Cermati). Avoid the Bank Summa backstory.

name: Xia Xinde
current_role: Chairman, Guangzhou Great Power Energy & Technology (鹏辉能源, SZ300438)
profile: Xia Xinde (夏信德, b. 1964), a Central South University materials graduate with a master's in electrochemistry, founded Guangzhou-based lithium battery maker Great Power Energy in 2001 and owns roughly half of it; he was president until 2021 and has been chairman since 2011. The company has pivoted strongly to energy-storage batteries and filed for a Hong Kong 'A+H' listing in January 2026.
interesting_fact: Great Power's energy-storage battery revenue reached RMB 4.84bn in the first three quarters of 2025, up from RMB 3.03bn a year earlier, as the company swung back to profit and filed to list in Hong Kong.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Great Power, Xia spent 1988-1994 as deputy director of the Guangzhou 555 Battery Research Institute, then ran Guangzhou Weili Power Supply Co. (1994-2001).
notes: Low-profile technical founder; route via Great Power's general inbox or IR/board secretary office (HK listing application filed 30 Jan 2026, status of debut not confirmed).

name: Rubens Ometto Silveira Mello
current_role: Chairman of the Board and controlling shareholder, Cosan S.A.; chairman of Raízen
profile: Born 1950 in Piracicaba, grandson of Italian immigrant sugar-mill owner Pedro Ometto, he joined the family business in 1986 and built Cosan into Brazil's largest sugar and ethanol producer, listing it in São Paulo (2005) and New York (2007), buying Esso Brazil's assets and forming Raízen with Shell in 2011. A 2025-26 deal with BTG Pactual and Perfin keeps him Cosan chairman until 2031.
interesting_fact: Raízen, the joint venture he formed by merging Cosan's sugar, ethanol and fuel assets with Shell's Brazilian business, became one of Brazil's largest energy companies by revenue (about US$45.5bn in the 2023/24 harvest year).
deep_cut_fact: Before entering the family mill business he trained as a mechanical production engineer at USP's Escola Politécnica, worked at Unibanco (1971-73), then became finance director of Grupo Votorantim in 1974 under his mentor Antônio Ermírio de Moraes.
notes: Cosan is restructuring/deleveraging (2025-26) and Raízen is under pressure - avoid as outreach angle. Chairmanship to 2031 per shareholder pact: https://fusoesaquisicoes.com/acontece-no-setor/rubens-ometto-assina-acordo-de-acionistas-com-btg-pactual-e-perfin-na-cosan/. Route via Cosan IR/corporate communications.

name: Zhong Peifeng
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Amlogic (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (晶晨股份, SSE STAR: 688099)
profile: Zhong Peifeng (John Zhong, b. 1963, US citizen) is a Georgia Tech-trained electrical engineer who co-founded Amlogic in Silicon Valley in 1995 and moved its base to Shanghai's Zhangjiang in 2003. Amlogic designs SoCs for smart TVs, set-top boxes and AIoT devices; it listed on the STAR Market in 2019 and in late 2026 was pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: Amlogic is the 'hidden king' of set-top-box chips: roughly one in three smart set-top boxes and one in five smart TVs worldwide reportedly use its silicon.
deep_cut_fact: Amlogic's first products in the mid-1990s were self-developed VCD decoder chips, riding China's VCD boom; before founding it Zhong worked at North American firms including Nortel after his Georgia Tech EE master's. Amlogic was in the first batch of STAR Market listings in Aug 2019.
notes: Goes by John Zhong in English. Forbes lists residence Beijing, citizenship US; company is HQ'd in Shanghai. Low media profile; route via Amlogic IR / board secretary office (IR@amlogic.com from SSE announcements).

name: Li Guoqing
current_role: Supervisor (board of supervisors), Rongsheng Petrochemical (SZSE: 002493); shareholder of Rongsheng Holding
profile: One of the original founding shareholders of Rongsheng Petrochemical, the Hangzhou (Xiaoshan, Yinong town)-based group that grew from textiles and chemical fiber into polyester feedstocks and refining; Forbes lists him as a supervisor of the listed company. His brother Li Yongqing, a Rongsheng director, is also a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Rongsheng controls 51% of Zhejiang Petroleum & Chemical (ZPC), an 800,000 bpd integrated refinery-petrochemical complex; in 2023 Saudi Aramco paid about $3.4bn for 10% of Rongsheng and agreed to supply ZPC with 480,000 bpd of crude.
deep_cut_fact: He was one of seven founding promoters when Rongsheng Petrochemical was set up as a joint-stock company ahead of its 2010 Shenzhen IPO, holding 7.15 million shares (1.43%) alongside Li Shuirong and Li Yongqing.
notes: Name is ambiguous: not the Dangdang co-founder Li Guoqing. Very low public profile; no interviews found. IR emails are those of the board secretary (Quan Weiying) and securities affairs rep (Hu Yangyang) as published in Rongsheng's annual-report summary; Chinese-language outreach advised. Deep-cut fact from the 2010 IPO prospectus-era filing (search-summarised; verify).

name: Scott Smith
current_role: Co-founder of Qualtrics; Professor Emeritus of Marketing, BYU Marriott School of Business
profile: Scott M. Smith is a longtime BYU marketing-research professor who co-founded Provo, Utah-based Qualtrics in 2002 with sons Ryan and Jared Smith and Stuart Orgill, starting in his basement. Qualtrics was bought by SAP for $8B in 2018, spun out in a 2021 IPO and taken private by Silver Lake in 2023. He is now professor emeritus and lives in Provo.
interesting_fact: Qualtrics grew out of his academic work: as a BYU professor he wanted an online survey tool that could handle sophisticated research yet stay easy to use. In the early days he took no paycheck so the company could pay employees.
deep_cut_fact: Colleagues say he 'still pours his own cement'; he once spotted an employee's car with bald tires in the Qualtrics lot and paid for new ones. He calls his Qualtrics experience a 'magic pony ride' and left the company in 2014 to serve a mission in Hong Kong with his wife.
notes: Name is common: this is Scott M. Smith of Provo, Utah (Qualtrics). Low public profile; academic author (Basic Marketing Research). No personal channels found. Best route: Qualtrics press, or via BYU Marriott School. Not an energy/data-center figure, though Qualtrics is a cloud company.

name: Kazim Turker
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Türkerler Holding (Ankara)
profile: Ankara-based founder of Türkerler Holding, a group of ~137 companies in construction, real estate, energy and healthcare. Türkerler owns 534 MW of hydro, wind and geothermal plants plus an electricity distributor serving 828,000 subscribers, and built Ankara's Etlik City Hospital with Italy's Astaldi as a $1.3B public-private partnership.
interesting_fact: He started out at 19 running a small clothing store in Ankara before moving into construction; one of his first projects was the Police Moral Education Center in Istanbul.
deep_cut_fact: The 'Kazım Türker Art Gallery' bears his name: opened in January 2018 at Dokuz Eylül University's Faculty of Fine Arts in İzmir, created jointly with the university through Türkerler's Mahall Bomonti İzmir real-estate project. Türkerler also won a best geothermal project award at the 2018 ICCI Energy Awards.
notes: Strong energy angle (geothermal, hydro, wind, power distribution). Rarely gives English-language interviews; approach via Türkerler Holding head office in Ankara (Mahall Ankara).

name: Danilo Iervolino
current_role: Entrepreneur/investor; controlling shareholder of BFC (AI) Media (publisher incl. Forbes Italia) and owner of US Salernitana (stepped down as club president Aug 2024)
profile: Born 1978 in Palma Campania, Iervolino founded online university UniPegaso in 2006 at 28 and grew it into Italy's largest, then sold parent Multiversity to CVC in 2021 for about $1.3bn. Since then he bought Salernitana football club and media group BFC Media (briefly also L'Espresso), and invests in Italian tech startups and VC, e.g. a 6.2% stake in Vertis SGR via his holding IDI Srl.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for an all-digital university after time in the US, where he became interested in dotcoms and online education, after developing online master's programmes at the University of Salerno.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote a book on the digital economy: 'Now! Strategie per affrontare le nuove frontiere del web' (Mondadori, 2015).
notes: Best route is via BFC Media (his media company). No verified personal social accounts found. Background check: Italian Wikipedia reports a first-instance conviction (2019 case re Ministry of Labour hiring) - verify before approaching. Don't confuse with film producer Andrea Iervolino.

name: Zhang Jianguo
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Jiangxi JOVO Energy Co. (九丰能源, SSE: 605090)
profile: Zhang Jianguo (张建国, ~63, Guangzhou) chairs JOVO Energy, a natural-gas/LNG and LPG distributor founded in Zhuhai in 1990, which listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in May 2021. He and his wife Cai Lihong are the company's controlling shareholders; Forbes ranked 'Zhang Jianguo & family' #2052 on its 2026 billionaires list.
interesting_fact: JOVO's international partners include Malaysia's Petronas and Norway's Skaugen Group; the company grew from a 1990 Zhuhai gas trader into a listed LNG/LPG importer.
notes: Very common name - identity tied to Forbes profile zhang-jianguo-1 (JOVO Energy). Low media profile; board secretary listed as Huang Bo - IR channel is the best route. 'Forbes annual 2001-2025' in input likely merges other people of the same name.

name: Lai Miao
profile: Listed on the Hurun China and Global lists (2021-2026) with wealth from Ganten (景田), the Shenzhen bottled-water company behind the Baisuishan (百岁山) mineral-water brand, founded in 1992. Searches did not find public material naming 赖苗 or describing their role at Ganten.
interesting_fact: Ganten's Baisuishan leads China's natural mineral water category, and Hurun valued Ganten at RMB 26B in 2025, top-three among Chinese bottled-water companies.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or bios found. Their role (founder, co-owner or family shareholder) is unconfirmed. Ganten is private, so the only route is likely the company's corporate channels.

name: Joseph Baratta
current_role: Global Head of Private Equity, Blackstone; member of Blackstone's Board of Directors and Management Committee
profile: Joined Blackstone in 1998 and moved to London in 2001 to help build its European private equity business. He has run Blackstone's global private equity business since 2012, overseeing deals such as Medline, Ancestry and Merlin Entertainments. His wealth comes from carried interest and Blackstone equity. Earlier he worked at Morgan Stanley M&A, Tinicum and McCown De Leeuw.
interesting_fact: He is one of very few non-founder private equity executives to reach billionaire status; Forbes lists him for his Blackstone stake and carried interest.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up with modest means in Sacramento. He champions Blackstone's Career Pathways programme, which hires people from underserved communities into portfolio companies, and sits on the board of the youth-employment nonprofit Year Up. He is also a trustee of the Tate Foundation.
notes: Comfortable with media: he appeared on Masters in Business, the Goldman Sachs Exchanges podcast and Bloomberg TV. Approach through Blackstone press inquiries. The Sacramento detail comes from a Money & Wealth podcast page (bryantgroupventures.com/money-wealth-podcast-joe-baratta/).

name: Manny Stul
current_role: Co-owner of Moose Toys (Melbourne); former chairman/co-CEO — current formal title not confirmed (stepson Paul Solomon became Executive Chairman, Ronnie Frankowski CEO, Oct 2025)
profile: Born in a German refugee camp to Polish-Jewish Holocaust survivors, Stul grew up in Western Australia, built and listed giftware firm Skansen, then in 2000 took over struggling Moose Toys and grew sales ~7,000% on hits like Shopkins (1bn+ units sold) and Mighty Beanz. Moose remains Melbourne-headquartered and family-owned.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he became the first Australian to win EY World Entrepreneur of the Year, aged 67. During the pandemic logistics crunch he chartered an entire ship to bring Moose products from China.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of university and worked in construction to fund his first business, giftware company Skansen, founded in 1973 and publicly listed 20 years later for over A$15m. As a toddler he spent three years in the Northam migrant camp in Western Australia.
notes: Moose leadership reshuffle Oct 2025 (https://globaltoynews.com/2025/10/09/moose-names-frankowski-ceo-other-management-changes/). Wife Jacqui Tobias is a long-time Moose product lead. Northam camp detail from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manny_Stul).

name: Jacques Merceron-Vicat
current_role: Honorary Chairman (Président d'honneur) and director, Vicat SA
profile: Born 1938, Jacques Merceron-Vicat is the patriarch of the family that controls Vicat, the listed French cement group founded in 1853 near Grenoble by Joseph Vicat, son of cement pioneer Louis Vicat. He led the group as chairman/CEO for decades before handing operations to son-in-law Guy Sidos (CEO 2008, chairman 2014); he remains honorary chairman with a board mandate running to 2030.
interesting_fact: The family's ancestor Louis Vicat discovered the principle of hydraulic binders in 1817 (the basis of modern cement), and Joseph and Louis Vicat built the world's first concrete bridge at Grenoble's Jardin des Plantes in 1855.
deep_cut_fact: When Guy Sidos became chairman in March 2014, the board named Jacques Merceron-Vicat honorary chairman; he had stepped back from operational control around age 70, passing the CEO role to his son-in-law in 2008, keeping the 170-year-old company under sixth-generation family control.
notes: Aged ~88, low public profile. Company now active in cement decarbonisation and alternative fuels (energy angle). Better podcast guest may be CEO Guy Sidos; approach via Vicat press office (named press officer as published in Vicat's July 2026 release).

name: Hiroyuki Inoue
current_role: Chairman (Director), Yamato Kogyo Co., Ltd. (TSE: 5444)
profile: Hiroyuki Inoue (井上浩行, b. 1945) is the son of Yamato Kogyo founder Asaji Inoue and spent his entire career at the Himeji electric-arc-furnace steelmaker, joining in 1969 and serving as president for about 36 years (1981-2017). He internationalised the company into the US, Thailand, Korea and the Middle East, and has been chairman since 2017 while remaining its largest shareholder (~12%).
interesting_fact: Yamato Kogyo makes rails and switches for Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains, and earns the majority of its sales overseas.
deep_cut_fact: In 1987, under his presidency, Yamato Kogyo formed a joint venture with US steelmaker Nucor, Nucor-Yamato Steel in Arkansas, taking the company into North American H-beam (structural steel) production; it later added JVs in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.
notes: Re-elected director at June 2025 AGM (94.4% approval). Electric-arc-furnace (low-carbon) steel is a possible energy angle. Japanese-language approach via corporate office recommended.

name: Yao Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, LUSTER LightTech (凌云光, SSE STAR: 688400)
profile: Yao Yi founded Beijing-based LUSTER LightTech in 2002; it makes configurable machine-vision systems, intelligent vision equipment and optical-communication/fiber-optic products and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. He owns roughly 44% of the company and runs it as chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: LUSTER began supplying configurable vision systems to Apple in 2016 and became one of its preferred suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he earned bachelor's and master's degrees at Xidian University (1986, 1989) and a doctorate from Beijing Jiaotong University in 1994, eight years before founding LUSTER.
notes: Board secretary is Gu Baoxing (per 2025 annual report summary). Machine vision for AI/electronics manufacturing is the podcast angle. Education details come from one MarketScreener profile.

name: Jet Jie Li
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, J&T Global Express (HKEX: 1519)
profile: Li spent 15+ years at OPPO, leading its expansion into Indonesia and other Asian markets, then founded J&T Express in Jakarta in 2015. J&T became Southeast Asia's parcel-volume leader, entered China in 2020 (riding Pinduoduo's growth) and listed in Hong Kong in 2023; it now also operates in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Mexico, Brazil and Egypt.
interesting_fact: The 'J&T' name and brand were born in Indonesia, not China: Li launched it in Jakarta in June 2015 and only later took it back to China, now the group's largest market.
deep_cut_fact: OPPO's headquarters created the 'Jet Lee' award, named in his honour, to reward top salespeople across its global sales agencies. He holds a 1998 marketing degree from the University of Science and Technology Beijing and began at OPPO selling audiovisual products in 1999.
notes: Goes by 'Jet Lee' (李杰) in Indonesia. Rarely gives interviews; route via J&T IR/corporate communications.

name: Igor Kudryashkin
current_role: Commercial director and co-owner, Ural Mining and Metallurgical Company (UMMC); executive board member, Svyatogor
profile: Long-time commercial director of Iskander Makhmudov's UMMC, a major Russian copper, zinc, coal and gold producer, who received a UMMC stake when the business was reorganised in 2013. His family also controls a majority of European Media Group, a large Russian radio-station network.
interesting_fact: Besides metals, Kudryashkin's family holds more than two-thirds of European Media Group, whose eight radio stations reach roughly 35 million listeners a week.
notes: UK-sanctioned since Feb 2024 (listed for his Svyatogor/UMMC role, updated Apr 2025; see opensanctions.org/entities/NK-TCxUTL6L7fKzsmG7XVhB22). Not a suitable outreach target; no published contacts found.

name: Warren Chen
current_role: Chairman, DynaColor Inc. (TPEx: 5489); cofounder and shareholder of Chroma ATE
profile: Warren Chen co-founded Chroma ATE (TWSE: 2360) in 1984 with other National Chiao Tung University alumni, including billionaire Leo Huang. Chroma makes automated test equipment for power electronics, EVs and semiconductors, and AI data-center power demand has lifted its shares. In 1991 he founded DynaColor, a Taipei maker of video-surveillance and machine-vision cameras, which he chairs.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes that Chroma's power-testing equipment is increasingly used worldwide as the AI boom drives up electricity demand, which makes him a direct fit for an energy and data-center podcast.
notes: Investing.com and StockAnalysis list a Warren Chen as DynaColor chairman/CEO. MarketScreener names the chairman 'Chun Sheng Chen' (an NCTU graduate), probably his formal name, but I could not confirm that link. He is low-profile, with almost no English press. DynaColor's contact page lists only sales emails; reach him via the company or through Chroma ATE.

name: Kuan Kam Hon
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hartalega Holdings Bhd (Malaysia)
profile: High-school dropout who started in his father's KL home-building firm in 1969, founded label maker Timol Weaving in 1978, then pivoted into medical gloves in 1988 as Hartalega, now one of the world's largest nitrile glove makers. He acts as mentor and spokesman, leaving operations to his sons.
interesting_fact: In 2005 Hartalega launched the world's first lightweight nitrile glove (4.7g vs an industry norm of 6g+), a product most rivals doubted could work.
deep_cut_fact: The name Hartalega combines two Malay words meaning 'relief assets'; he converted his struggling woven-label and badge plant into a latex glove factory as demand rose in the early AIDS-epidemic years.
notes: Also known as Kwan Kam Onn; wealth shared with brother Kuan Kam Peng. Glove sector is cyclical; avoid wealth-decline framing. Route via Hartalega corporate/IR (Sepang, Selangor); no published IR email verified.

name: Wang Minwen
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Hangzhou Lion Electronics (Hangzhou Lion Microelectronics, SSE: 605358); chairman of Xianhe Holding
profile: Chinese executive (b. 1963) who chairs Hangzhou Lion Electronics, a maker of semiconductor silicon wafers, power-device chips and compound-semiconductor RF/optoelectronic chips, listed in Shanghai in 2020. He and four siblings also control specialty-paper maker Xianhe Co. via Zhejiang Xianhe Holding.
interesting_fact: Lion runs a wafer-to-chip platform spanning silicon wafers (via subsidiary Zhejiang Jinruihong), power semiconductors and GaAs/GaN-on-SiC chips, making it one of China's few vertically integrated silicon-wafer-plus-chip groups.
deep_cut_fact: Before semiconductors he spent ~two decades at Shanghai energy group Shenergy: joining Shenergy Co. in 1988 in its investment department and rising to board secretary and director, then running Shenergy Asset Management and serving as Shenergy Group VP (2005-07). He is also a trustee of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics.
notes: Low public profile; bio from company filings. Energy-industry background (Shenergy) is a natural podcast hook. Investor email published in Lion's site (investors section).

name: René Holeček
current_role: Majority shareholder and Vice-chairman of the Supervisory Board, Colt CZ Group SE (per company corporate-affairs page)
profile: René Holeček (b. 1966), a Czech engineer-turned-banker, invested in ailing Česká zbrojovka Uherský Brod in 2001, took control in 2014 and listed it in Prague in 2020. He turned it into Colt CZ Group, buying US icon Colt (2021) and ammunition maker Sellier & Bellot (2024), and has since added an Amsterdam listing.
interesting_fact: Before guns he was a banker in the early 1990s (senior roles at Komerční banka and Pragobanka) and helped privatize the giant Třinec ironworks with long-time partner Rudolf Ovčaří.
deep_cut_fact: Forbes Czech lists his 'obsession' as golf, and with partner Rudolf Ovčaří he invested heavily in building golf courses and leisure resorts. His Holeček Family Foundation (Nadace rodiny Holečkových) funds education, health, science, crisis intervention and culture.
notes: Extremely low media profile (Forbes CZ calls him the 'mysterious owner'); rarely gives interviews. Best route is Colt CZ media relations. Defence/ammunition manufacturing angle may fit energy/industrial episodes.

name: Xu Guangfu
current_role: Chairman, Daqo Group (since 1984); director of Daqo New Energy Corp. (NYSE: DQ), whose board he chaired 2007-Aug 2023
profile: Born 1942 in Yangzhong, Jiangsu, Xu joined the township enterprise Xinba General Company in the 1960s and turned it into Daqo Group, a major Chinese maker of electrical systems and equipment. Daqo spun out polysilicon producer Daqo New Energy (NYSE-listed); his son Xu Xiang now leads much of the business while Xu remains Daqo Group chairman.
interesting_fact: He was named a National Township and Village Entrepreneur by China's Ministry of Agriculture in 2001 and 2002 and a 'Pioneer in Electricity Industry' in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He started as an agricultural technician at the Xinba farm-tech station; the township factory he later ran made grinding wheels and bakelite goods, and its breakthrough came in 1990 when it won a contract to supply electrical products to 17 venues of the Beijing Asian Games.
notes: In his early 80s; son Xu Xiang (co-listed) is the more active executive. Best route is Daqo New Energy IR (ir@daqo.com; full list at dqsolar.com/IR-Contacts). Deep-cut fact from a Chinese brand-profile site, moderate reliability.

name: Xu Xiang (徐翔)
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Daqo New Energy Corp. (NYSE: DQ); President, Daqo Group
profile: Son of Daqo Group founder Xu Guangfu, Xu Xiang runs the family's Jiangsu-based Daqo (大全) empire, which spans electrical equipment and solar-grade polysilicon. He has been a Daqo New Energy director since its 2007 founding, president of Daqo Group since 2006, and became CEO and chairman of the NYSE-listed polysilicon maker in August 2023.
interesting_fact: Daqo New Energy is one of the world's lowest-cost producers of high-purity polysilicon for solar panels, with 305,000 metric tons of nameplate capacity.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Daqo Group he was general manager of Jiangsu Changjiang Electric Co. (a Daqo electrical-equipment subsidiary) from 2000 to 2006, and earned his EMBA from Nanjing University in 2004; he holds directorships at 25 Daqo Group subsidiaries.
notes: Wealth shared with father Xu Guangfu (Daqo founder). Low English-language media profile; IR team is the practical route. Relevant to energy angle (polysilicon/solar supply chain; Daqo Group also makes power equipment).

name: Qian Ke
current_role: Chairman, General Manager & CEO, Tolerance Precision Manufacturing (Jiangsu) Co. (托伦斯, SZSE ChiNext: 301583); actual controller
profile: Qian Ke (钱珂, b. 1973; Chinese national with US permanent residency; software degree) ran US-based UFO Engineering, a maker of semiconductor vacuum chambers, before taking over its Shanghai affiliate Tolerance in 2015. He moved production to Qidong, Jiangsu, in 2017 and built it into a key chamber/precision-parts supplier to NAURA and AMEC. Tolerance listed on ChiNext in July 2026.
interesting_fact: Tolerance's ChiNext debut on 10 July 2026 opened up ~1,054% (intraday high +1,070%) from its ¥22.6 IPO price, briefly valuing the ~¥720m-revenue parts maker at nearly ¥50bn - one of the year's hottest A-share listings.
deep_cut_fact: Tolerance's core edge is multi-layer vacuum brazing: it can braze 7-layer semiconductor vacuum chambers in one piece (most domestic peers manage 3-4), a technique Qian brought over from his years running UFO Engineering in the US.
notes: Hurun's 'Tolerance' = 托伦斯精密制造（江苏）股份有限公司 (Qidong, Jiangsu). Newly listed; very little English coverage, no personal social presence found. No IR email located in sources I could open; IPO issuance announcement lists contact person Xu Hongyan, tel 0513-83393785 (https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2026-06/26/A14/zqA1426.pdf). Check the 2026 interim report on cninfo for the board-secretary email.

name: Gao Denghua
current_role: Chairman and co-controlling shareholder (with Xie Yun), Hubei Doti-Micro Technology (东田微, 301183.SZ)
profile: Chairman and legal representative of Doti-Micro, founded July 2009, which makes precision optical components: GPON filters, TO caps, WDM filters and optical-isolator assemblies for optical transceivers, plus camera optics. He and Xie Yun are the actual controllers. AI-driven optical-module demand lifted earnings in 2026 and put him on the Hurun China list for the first time.
interesting_fact: Doti-Micro guided H1 2026 net profit of RMB85-95m, up 68-87% year on year, as its optical-isolator and filter components for transceivers rode the AI data-center optics boom.
notes: Very low public profile; no biography found in public sources. Contact would be via the company's board secretary (Li Guanghua, also CFO, per July 2026 IR record https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202607091826847628_1.pdf); no published IR email located from this session (cninfo unreachable).

name: Xie Yun
current_role: Director and General Manager, Hubei Doti-Micro Technology (东田微, 301183.SZ); co-controlling shareholder with husband Gao Denghua
profile: Xie Yun and her husband, chairman Gao Denghua, control Hubei Doti-Micro Technology (founded 2009, listed on ChiNext), which makes precision optical components for smartphone cameras and high-speed optical modules. She has been with the company since founding and is its general manager and a director (re-nominated July 2026).
interesting_fact: Doti-Micro runs an 'imaging optics + communication optics' twin strategy; with AI data-centre build-outs driving optical-module demand, 2025 revenue rose 46.9% to RMB 877m and net profit 80.2% to about RMB 101m.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal accounts found. Hurun lists her jointly with Gao Denghua. Route: company board-secretary office (secretary Li Guanghua). Some data providers list her as CEO/general manager since July 2009.

name: Yang Yuying
current_role: Vice Chairwoman and employee-representative director, Satellite Chemical Co. (formerly Zhejiang Satellite Petrochemical; Shenzhen 002648)
profile: Yang Yuying (杨玉英, b. 1961) is the elder sister of Satellite Chemical founder-chairman Yang Weidong and a shareholder of controlling holder Zhejiang Satellite Holding. The Jiaxing-based group grew from a small chemicals plant into a major Chinese maker of ethylene, acrylics and polymers; she is vice chairwoman and the company's Party secretary.
interesting_fact: Satellite Chemical cracks imported US ethane rather than naphtha: it locked in supply through a long-term deal with Energy Transfer and runs its own fleet of very large ethane carriers (VLECs), giving roughly 80% ethylene yield vs ~30% for naphtha cracking.
deep_cut_fact: Outside the boardroom she is a prominent volunteer organiser: executive president of the Jiaxing Volunteers Association and president of the Nanhu District Charity Volunteers Association, and a winner of the 6th Zhejiang Province Charity Award and a Jiaxing 'moral model' title.
notes: Company website is the corporate site, not hers. Low media profile; her charity/volunteer work is the warmest angle. Route via the board-secretary/IR mailbox listed in the 2025 annual report.

name: Pan Jian
current_role: Co-Chairman and Executive Director, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. (CATL; SZ 300750 / HK 3750)
profile: Hong Kong permanent resident (b. 1976, University of Chicago master's); a CATL director since 2015, later vice chairman, and co-chairman since Dec 2024. His wealth comes from his CATL stake, and he is CATL's frequent international face, e.g. at Davos and the 2025 Hong Kong listing.
interesting_fact: At Davos 2025 he said China's industry no longer talks about 'EVs' but 'EIVs' - the I for 'intelligent' - crediting China's software engineers from the smartphone/internet boom for its edge over Western automakers.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a battery executive he sat on the boards of non-battery companies including Shanghai M&G Stationery (the pen maker), Luye Pharma and French animal-health group Ceva Sante Animale.
notes: Speaks English and is CATL's main voice at global forums (Davos, WEF) - a realistic podcast guest via CATL IR/corporate communications. IR email from 2024 interim report; verify against latest filing.

name: Wu Xiaoge
current_role: Co-actual controller (~16% holder) of CNGR Advanced Material (中伟股份, SZSE: 300919 / HKEX); former director & VP (stepped down 2023)
profile: Chengdu-based co-founder of CNGR, a Hunan-headquartered maker of nickel/cobalt precursor cathode materials for EV batteries, alongside her husband, chairman Deng Weimin. CNGR listed in Shenzhen in 2020 and dual-listed in Hong Kong in 2025. She left the board in 2023 but remains a joint controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: CNGR has become one of the world's largest suppliers of ternary battery precursors and now also makes sodium-ion and solid-state-battery precursor materials, as well as precursors marketed for the 'low-altitude economy' (drones/eVTOL).
notes: Forbes lists her as 'formerly' on its real-time list (age 54, Tsinghua MBA). Very low public profile since leaving management; husband Deng Weimin is the public face. Route via CNGR IR mailbox.

name: Chen Yuantai
current_role: Secretary of the Communist Party committee, Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) - per Forbes; not independently confirmed
profile: Per Forbes, Chen Yuantai is party committee secretary at CATL, the Ningde, Fujian-based battery maker that is the world's largest EV-battery supplier, and his fortune stems from CATL shares. He holds no board seat and has almost no public footprint beyond Forbes's listing.
interesting_fact: CATL, whose stake underpins his fortune, is headquartered in Ningde, a once-remote Fujian city now dubbed a global lithium-battery powerhouse.
notes: English and Chinese searches found no independent confirmation of his role (he is not among CATL directors in the Dec 2024 board slate or named in the 2025 annual report summary). Treat as a very low-profile insider; the only published route is CATL's board-office/IR email.

name: Anna Margaret Smedvig
current_role: Vice Chair, Smedvig Family Office (Stavanger); formerly chairman of London-based Smedvig Capital
profile: Norwegian-born, London-based fourth-generation heir (b. 1983) to the Smedvig shipping and offshore-drilling fortune founded by great-grandfather Peder Smedvig in 1915; the family sold Smedvig ASA's rig business and redeployed into venture capital (Smedvig Capital, est. 1996), funds and Stavanger real estate. Sunday Times Rich List has valued her and father Peter at ~GBP 850m-1bn.
interesting_fact: Smedvig Capital, which she chaired from 2016, has invested over GBP 1bn in British and Nordic companies, pivoting an oil-services dynasty into tech venture investing.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking over the family investment arm she worked at luxury stationer Smythson, consumer private-equity firm L Catterton and EC Hambro Rabben; she holds an MA in Psychology and Business from the University of Edinburgh and lists fashion, film, architecture and design as interests.
notes: Private; rarely gives interviews. Smedvig contact form has a 'Smedvig family office' department option, which is the most direct published route. The family also runs Peder Smedvigs Stipendiefond (since 1992) funding Norwegian students' study abroad - a possible warm angle.

name: Dou Zhenggang
current_role: Chairman and owner, Hangzhou Jinjiang Group (environmental energy, alumina/aluminium, non-ferrous metals, trade and logistics)
profile: Dou Zhenggang (钭正刚) started in textiles in Zhejiang in 1983 and built Hangzhou Jinjiang Group into a conglomerate spanning waste-to-energy, power, alumina/aluminium, non-ferrous metals and logistics. His family's China Jinjiang Environment became a leading waste-to-energy operator; the group now runs large alumina projects in China and Indonesia.
interesting_fact: His Hangzhou Jinjiang Group signed an MoU to supply alumina to Aluminium Bahrain (Alba), one of the world's largest smelters, and has built alumina refineries from Shanxi to West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
deep_cut_fact: The World Bank's IFC backed his early power business: it lent up to $20 million to China Green to consolidate Jinjiang's plants, including a 12 MW waste-to-energy plant in Yuhang, Hangzhou, burning municipal solid waste, and plants fired by bone coal and low-grade coal.
notes: Low public profile; no official group website or published contact found. A possible indirect route is via Zheneng Jinjiang Environment (SGX-listed, formerly China Jinjiang Environment) investor relations, but the Dou family's stake there has been reduced. Name sometimes romanised 'Tou Zhenggang'.

name: Pan Shiyi
current_role: Co-founder and board member, SOHO China (stepped down as chairman in 2022)
profile: Born 1963 in Gansu, Pan co-founded SOHO China with his wife Zhang Xin in 1995 and built it into a leading developer of landmark commercial property in Beijing and Shanghai, listed in Hong Kong. In 2022 the couple left management (remaining on the board) to focus on the arts and philanthropy, and are now based mainly in the US.
interesting_fact: He had a film role: he starred as a lonely real-estate developer, 'Li Wenqing', in the 2006 romantic film Aspirin (阿司匹林).
deep_cut_fact: On 14 Nov 2019 (his 56th birthday) he announced on Weibo 'I'm going to learn Python', calling it the 'best-evolved' computer language. The post went viral in China's tech community.
notes: Once one of China's most-followed Weibo users; now low-profile and US-based. No current published office/press contact found (SOHO China site pages 404). Best route is probably via SOHO China's HKEX-listed company secretary/IR or via Zhang Xin's arts/philanthropy channels.

name: David Capobianco
current_role: CEO & Managing Partner, Five Point Infrastructure (formerly Five Point Energy); Chairman of LandBridge (NYSE: LB) and PowerBridge
profile: Founded Five Point Energy (now Five Point Infrastructure) in 2012 after co-founding Vulcan Capital's private equity group. Five Point built Permian water business WaterBridge and land platform LandBridge (IPO 2024, 270k+ acres). Its new PowerBridge unit is developing gigawatt-scale powered data-center campuses, including 2 GW in Reeves County, TX.
interesting_fact: He pitches the Permian Basin as a rival to Northern Virginia as a data-center hub, citing its land, cheap gas, fiber, and produced water for cooling. He has argued that nuclear power, possibly small modular reactors sited at data centers, is the only route to fully renewable data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vulcan he worked in Salomon Brothers' Energy Corporate Finance Group and on the investment teams of Harvest Partners and Greenhill Capital Partners. He later chaired Vulcan Energy Corp. (formerly Plains Resources) and chaired the compensation committee of Plains All American Pipeline. Duke BA, Harvard MBA.
notes: A strong fit for an energy and data-center podcast: he has spoken on the Cool Vector podcast/Substack and speaks publicly about the Permian, powered land and data centers. For media, go through Kekst CNC (LandBridge's PR firm) or the LandBridge IR address. The Kekst address appeared in older releases, so check that it is still current.

name: Alexander Dzhaparidze
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Eurasia Drilling Company; London-based investor (reported exit from all Russian assets in 2022)
profile: Russian-Georgian oilfield-services entrepreneur. He bought used seismic gear abroad in the 1990s, built PetroAlliance and sold it to Schlumberger. In 2004 he bought Lukoil's drilling arm for $130M and turned it into Eurasia Drilling, Russia's biggest onshore driller. Schlumberger's bids for EDC were blocked, and he reportedly exited Russian assets in 2022.
interesting_fact: He collects ancient daggers. In 2016 he bought a yacht and renamed it 'Here Comes the Sun' after the Beatles song.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Makhachkala, Dagestan in 1955, holds a Doctor of Science from Moscow's Gubkin oil and gas university, and early on ran MD SEIS, a seismic-survey joint venture.
notes: Very private, with no personal website or social accounts found. EDC's website (eurasiadrilling.com) no longer resolves. Forbes now lists him as a former billionaire (real-time 2023). Wikipedia mentions a 2015-16 UK SFO probe into his Soma Oil & Gas, closed in 2016 with no action. Avoid the topic.

name: Valery Kustov
current_role: Chairman of the board and main shareholder (~42%) of EFKO Group (Russia); under arrest in Moscow since July 2026
profile: Russian entrepreneur (b. 1961) who co-founded EFKO with partners in 1994 on the base of an essential-oils plant in Alekseyevka, Belgorod region. EFKO grew into one of Russia's largest food companies, with sunflower oil, mayonnaise, industrial fats and brands such as Sloboda, Altero and DeOlio, and in 2025 it bought Bunge's former Russian oilseed assets.
interesting_fact: EFKO started as a small perfume and essential-oil producer privatised in the 1990s and was repurposed to make sunflower oil and mayonnaise. Today it also works in biotech, including sweet proteins.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1980s he worked at the 'Deviz' electronics plant in Alekseyevka. He then founded the business on the town's 'Efirnoye' essential-oil plant together with colleagues, bringing over former Deviz staff.
notes: CAUTION: detained in Moscow on 30 July 2026 on large-scale fraud charges over a drone project ('Transport of the Future', spun off from EFKO), with a court-ordered arrest until at least 29 Sept 2026. Unsuitable for outreach at present. The RBC deep-cut source sits behind a paywall or login; the detail was seen via search snippet.

name: Michaela Herz
current_role: Managing director and ~45% owner, Mayfair Vermögensverwaltungs SE (Herz family holding, Hamburg)
profile: Granddaughter of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz and daughter of Günter Herz, who ran Tchibo for ~35 years. After Günter and his sister sold their Tchibo stake in 2003 they founded Mayfair, a Hamburg family holding investing in companies, bonds and real estate; Michaela owns about 45% and helps steer investment decisions.
interesting_fact: Mayfair's first big deal was a 17% (later 27%) stake in Puma in 2004, sold to PPR at €330/share; it then bought Germanischer Lloyd for €575m, which expanded into oil & gas and renewable-energy services before merging into DNV GL in 2013 (stake sold 2017).
notes: Extremely private — almost no public footprint under her own name. Energy angle for the podcast: Mayfair's Germanischer Lloyd/DNV GL investment. Aunt Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel's branch has exited Mayfair (Forbes). Mayfair website did not load; no published contact found.

name: Anton Fedun
current_role: Hotel owner / managing director, The Ampersand Hotel (South Kensington) and Vintry & Mercer (City of London); Lukoil shareholder
profile: Anton Fedun's fortune stems from Lukoil, Russia's No. 2 oil producer, where his father Leonid Fedun was a long-time controlling shareholder and in 2018 transferred part of his stake to him. A dual Russian-UK citizen living in London, he runs his own boutique hotels: The Ampersand in South Kensington and Vintry & Mercer, a 92-room City hotel opened in 2019.
interesting_fact: He is hands-on in hospitality rather than oil: he is managing director of Vintry & Mercer, built on the City site where medieval Vintners unloaded wine and Mercers traded silks and textiles, hence the name.
deep_cut_fact: In an Oct 2020 Boutique Hotel News video interview he discussed repurposing Vintry & Mercer and The Ampersand during the pandemic, courting London's local market and designing distinctive concepts; Vintry & Mercer's design deliberately references its City neighbourhood's history.
notes: Private; no personal channels found. Best route is via the hotels (Ampersand / Vintry & Mercer, an SLH member). Russian oil-wealth links (Lukoil) mean sanctions sensitivity should be checked before outreach. SLH journal Q&A (journal.slh.com, post 7096) describes him as MD of Vintry & Mercer.

name: Judith Neilson
current_role: Founder and director, White Rabbit Gallery (Sydney); philanthropist and Platinum Asset Management shareholder
profile: Zimbabwe-born former graphic designer and Sydney philanthropist whose fortune stems from her stake in Platinum Asset Management, the global equities manager co-founded by her ex-husband Kerr Neilson (divorced 2015). She founded and solely funds the White Rabbit Gallery of post-2000 Chinese contemporary art, backed the Phoenix arts spaces in Chippendale, and set up the A$100M Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas.
interesting_fact: White Rabbit holds one of the world's largest collections of 21st-century Chinese art; in 2024 she said it held work by around 800 artists and 'there were 4,000 pieces the last time I counted'. Her interest began on trips to Beijing in the late 1990s.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 she endowed a Chair of Architecture at UNSW to develop housing solutions for displaced people such as climate refugees and disaster or conflict victims, and in 2017 a Chair of Contemporary Art at UNSW. She was made a Member of the Order of Australia (AM) in 2016.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed. Note: neilson.org.au (contact@neilson.org.au) is the Neilson Foundation run by ex-husband Kerr Neilson, NOT her - do not use. Best route is via White Rabbit Gallery or the Judith Neilson Institute. Arts/journalism focus rather than energy.

name: Peter-Alexander Wacker
current_role: Chair of the Supervisory Board, Wacker Chemie AG (since 2008; re-elected 2023)
profile: Great-grandson of founder Alexander Wacker, he owns roughly 10% of Munich-based Wacker Chemie. After ten years at BMW he joined Wacker's board in 1993, became CEO when it went public in 2005, and moved to chair the supervisory board in 2008. Wacker is a major maker of silicones and of hyperpure polysilicon for solar cells and semiconductors.

deep_cut_fact: He collects elephant figures from around the world because elephants symbolize strength to him, which is why his holding company is named Blue Elephant. He was also named Germany's family businessman of the year in 2006.

public_contacts.value: Manuela.Dollinger@wacker.com (Wacker Media Relations, as listed in company profile)

name: KR Sridhar
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE)
profile: Tamil Nadu-born engineer (MS nuclear engineering, PhD mechanical engineering, UIUC) who directed the University of Arizona's Space Technologies Laboratory, building Mars oxygen-generation tech for NASA. After NASA shelved its Mars Surveyor 2001 lander he co-founded Ion America (2001), renamed Bloom Energy, whose solid-oxide fuel cells now supply on-site power to AI data centers; IPO 2018.
interesting_fact: Bloom has become an on-site 'bring your own power' supplier for AI data centers, including a 2025 collaboration with Oracle to deliver power to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure sites at the speed of AI build-outs.

Bloom's fuel cell is essentially that Mars device run in reverse. Fortune named him one of five young innovators in 2000.

name: Wang Jianyi
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, Futong Group Co., Ltd. (Hangzhou); deputy to the 14th National People's Congress

Futong became a major maker of optical fibre, cable and fibre preforms. Since 2024 the group has faced debt problems and its listed unit was delisted.

Official site futong.com.cn did not load. Former CPPCC member; senior figure in the Zhejiang federation of industry and commerce.

name: Oleg Misrevra
current_role: Controlling owner (and former president) of East Mining Company (VGK / EMCO), Sakhalin coal miner

name: Qiu Minxiu
current_role: Director and co-actual controller (with chairman Cao Jianwei), Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical (Shenzhen: 300316)
profile: Born in 1945, Qiu is a research fellow and doctoral supervisor in fluid power and electro-hydraulic control who turned academic engineering into an equipment business. name: Anatoly Skurov
current_role: Private investor; owner of the Uvalnaya coal-mining project (Kuzbass), per Forbes
profile: Russian mining engineer (b. 1952, Tula Oblast) who designed Soviet coal-mining machinery, then in 1995 co-founded coal producer Sibuglemet, which he ran until 2003. notes: Very private; no published personal, office or press contact found. Russia-based coal investor - check sanctions/reputational issues before any outreach. Web-search quota ran out, so current Uvalnaya ownership is per Forbes only.

name: Sung Kyu-dong
current_role: Founder and CEO (co-CEO with Park Jong-goo), EO Technics (KOSDAQ: 039030), Anyang, South Korea
profile: Sung Kyu-dong (성규동) founded EO Technics in 1989 and listed it on KOSDAQ in 2000. The company makes laser equipment for memory-chip production: laser markers that etch traceability codes onto chips and laser annealing (LA) tools, plus dicing/grooving systems; it is reported to supply laser annealing tools to Samsung. Ranked #49 on Forbes' 2026 Korea's 50 Richest.
interesting_fact: EO Technics' flagship laser markers etch an ID code onto each chip so manufacturers can trace the source of any defect; its LA tools use targeted laser heat to activate the electrical pathways inside chips.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding EO Technics he worked at the Goldstar (now LG) Central Research Center, Daewoo Heavy Industries and Korea Laser, the company that pioneered industrial laser technology in South Korea.
notes: Low-profile engineer-founder. Company site publishes only a sales address (sales@eotechnics.com) and a Q&A form; no press/IR email found. Good fit for AI-memory/HBM supply-chain angle. Korean-language outreach likely needed.

current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu JieJie Microelectronics Co., Ltd. (Shenzhen: 300623)
profile: Huang Shanbing (黄善兵) founded the predecessor of JieJie Microelectronics in Qidong, Jiangsu in 1995 and chairs the company, which makes power semiconductor discrete devices such as thyristors (triacs/SCRs) and protection devices; it listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in 2017.

current_role: Venture Partner, New Enterprise Associates (NEA); director and audit committee chair of Nvidia, Tenable and GoodLeap
profile: Brooke Seawell has sat on Nvidia's board since 1997, joining while EVP at NetDynamics (sold to Sun Microsystems a year later). current_role: Founder & CEO, Social Capital; co-host, All-In podcast

current_role: Deputy Group Chairman, Fung Group (Li & Fung parent), Hong Kong

profile: Xia Feng (夏风, b. ~1968) co-founded Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (晶丰明源) in 2008 with chairman Hu Liqiang; the fabless analog/mixed-signal chip designer makes LED-lighting driver, power-management and motor-control ICs. current_role: Probable match: non-independent director (since Jan 2024) of Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources Co. (SSE: 600295), the listed arm of Erdos Group
profile: Hurun China (2025-26) lists a Zhang Xiaohui with wealth from Erdos (cashmere, coal, real estate). name: Ajay Puri
current_role: Executive Vice President, Worldwide Field Operations, NVIDIA (still listed with this title on an Aug 2026 SEC Form 4)
profile: Ajay 'Jay' Puri runs NVIDIA's global sales and field organisation, which sells the GPUs and systems behind the AI data-center boom. He joined NVIDIA in 2005 after 22 years at Sun Microsystems in sales, marketing and general management. His wealth comes from NVIDIA stock (about 0.02% stake), and he remains in the role as of 2026.

He holds electrical engineering degrees from the University of Minnesota (BS) and Caltech (MS) as well as a Harvard MBA, so he is an engineer by training, not a career salesman.

name: Eddy Sugianto
current_role: President Commissioner, PT Prima Andalan Mandiri Tbk (IDX: MCOL, 'Mandiri Coal'); controlling shareholder of Mandiri Herindo Adiperkasa (Mandiri Services)
profile: Indonesian coal magnate behind the Mandiri group, whose PT Mandiri Intiperkasa mine in North Kalimantan sells coal under the 'Mandiri Coal' brand, with in-house mining contracting and barging units. He took Prima Andalan Mandiri public in 2021 and the coal-services arm in 2023; his family controls ~70% of MCOL. Brother Handy Glivirgo is president director.

name: Cao Yuhua
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, Wuxi Best Precision Machinery (贝斯特, SZSE ChiNext 300580)
profile: A Wuxi native born in 1954, Cao spent nearly 30 years at a Wuxi machine-tool factory before co-founding Wuxi Best in 1997. It makes precision auto-parts components (turbocharger parts), tooling, fixtures and intelligent equipment used in new-energy vehicles, industrial machinery and robots, and went public in Shenzhen in 2017. More than a third of revenue comes from overseas; his daughter Cao Yi is vice chairman.
interesting_fact: Wuxi Best started in 1997 with registered capital of just RMB500,000, split 50/50 between Cao and co-founder Pan Zhiyu. It is now a ChiNext-listed precision manufacturer worth about RMB8bn.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the Wuxi Machine Tool Factory as a 16-year-old shop-floor worker in 1970 and rose to head its non-standard design office. While there he spotted the chance to localise motorcycle-engine tooling fixtures, which became Best's first business.
notes: Also a Jiangsu Provincial Model Worker and Wuxi People's Congress deputy (per Sina). Chinese-language only; route via the company securities-affairs (IR) office. Angle: NEV and robotics component supply chain.

name: Yang Xuegang
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director & CEO, China Risun Group (1907.HK)
profile: Founded Xingtai Risun Coking in Hebei in 1995 and built it into China Risun Group (1907.HK), China's largest independent coke producer and a major coke-based chemicals maker. Risun is expanding into hydrogen, new energy and new materials. He has been chairman since 1996 and leads Hebei's coking industry association.
interesting_fact: Frost & Sullivan ranked Risun the world's largest independent coke producer and supplier by volume in 2020. Its production bases include Xingtai, Dingzhou, Laoting and Cangzhou.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a hydraulic engineer (Hebei Hydraulic College, 1985) and spent about 10 years at Handan's Dongwushi Reservoir Management Center, becoming deputy director in 1988. He still keeps a water link as a director of Beijing Automic, a water-conservancy IT firm.
notes: Relevant to the energy theme: Risun produces hydrogen from coke-oven gas and is pursuing new-energy materials. The best route is Risun IR. Bio details come from the 2025 annual report (published April 2026).

name: Roy Vagelos
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Merck (1985–1994) and longtime Chairman of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (1995–c.2024); philanthropist
profile: Physician-scientist (b. 1929) who moved from NIH and Washington University to Merck's research labs, then ran Merck as CEO and chairman until 1994. He chaired Regeneron for nearly 29 years from 1995 and co-founded Theravance. His fortune comes largely from Regeneron stock, and he and his wife Diana are major donors to Columbia, Penn and Barnard.
interesting_fact: As Merck's CEO he had the company give its river-blindness drug ivermectin (Mectizan) free to governments and patients. Over two decades the programme reached more than 55 million people.
deep_cut_fact: The son of Greek immigrants, he grew up during the Depression working in his family's small restaurant in Rahway, New Jersey, the town where Merck's labs were based. He left on a partial scholarship to Penn, where he earned a chemistry BA (Phi Beta Kappa, 1950).
notes: Aged 97 and living in New Jersey. Columbia's medical school is named the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons, and the couple gave $400m to Columbia in 2024. No personal contact published; Regeneron or Columbia communications offices are the likely routes (pages blocked automated fetches).

name: Zelimkhan Mutsoev
current_role: Deputy of the Russian State Duma (United Russia), serving his 6th convocation (8th Duma, elected 2021)
profile: Tbilisi-born (1959) Russian businessman-politician of Yazidi heritage. He moved to Moscow in the early 1990s, ran a foreign-trade association, became a co-owner of Pervouralsk New Pipe Plant in 1998 and later built holdings in fertilizers (Uralkali stake) and real estate, while serving in the Duma almost continuously since 1999.

current_role: Founder and Chairman, Apex Dynamics (Taichung, Taiwan)
profile: Chang Chung-Hsing (張重興) founded Taichung-based Apex Dynamics in 1987 as a maker of robotic arms and built it into one of the world's largest suppliers of high-precision planetary gearboxes used in automation and machine tools. Apex listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 2022, making him a billionaire on Forbes' 2025 list.

name: Larry Silverstein
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Silverstein Properties (New York)
profile: Brooklyn-born developer (b. 1931) who co-founded Silverstein Properties with his father in 1957. He leased the World Trade Center in July 2001, seven weeks before 9/11, and spent two decades rebuilding 7, 4 and 3 WTC. The firm also owns LA's U.S. Bank Tower and downtown Manhattan's tallest residential tower, 30 Park Place.
interesting_fact: He usually held breakfast meetings at Windows on the World atop the North Tower, but on the morning of 9/11 his wife insisted he keep a medical appointment, which likely saved his life.
deep_cut_fact: Before real estate he was a music kid: he played piano, loved classical music and attended New York's High School of Music and Art; he met his wife Klara while working at a summer camp in college. Brooklyn Law School named him its 2026 Alumnus of the Year.

public_contacts.value: mgrace@Rubenstein.com (Rubenstein, listed as media contact on Silverstein news releases)

name: Lee Chae-yoon

January 1976, master's degree) at Do-Fluoride, a Jiaozuo, Henan-based maker of fluorine chemicals and lithium-battery materials such as lithium hexafluorophosphate electrolyte salt. profile: Ye Liaoning (叶辽宁, b. ~1965) joined the Yuyao Chengbei optical-instrument factory that became Sunny Optical in 1984 and is counted among the group's founders. name: Hartono Kweefanus
current_role: Chairperson Emeritus and director, Monde Nissin Corporation (Philippines); chairman, PT Khong Guan Biscuit Indonesia
profile: Indonesian businessman whose late father co-founded Philippine food maker Monde Nissin (Lucky Me! noodles, SkyFlakes, Quorn meat substitutes) in 1979 with Betty Ang, his sister-in-law. A Monde director for 45 years and long its chairman, he is now Chairperson Emeritus, while also chairing Indonesia's PT Khong Guan Biscuit and other family companies. current_role: President and co-founder, Monde Nissin Corporation (PSE: MONDE)
profile: Betty T. Ang, an Assumption College business graduate, co-founded Monde Nissin in 1979 with her late father-in-law Hidajat Darmono and built it into the Philippines' leading biscuit and instant-noodle maker (Lucky Me!, SkyFlakes, Fita). Monde Nissin's June 2021 IPO raised 55.9 billion pesos, then the country's largest, and it owns UK meat-alternative brand Quorn.
