name: Ivan Müller Botelho
current_role: Patriarch of the controlling Botelho family of Energisa S.A. and its long-time former chairman; he is not listed on the board elected in April 2026
profile: An electrical engineer (University of Miami) from Leopoldina, Minas Gerais, Ivan Botelho is the third generation of the family that has controlled Brazilian utility Energisa since 1905. He built it from a regional Cataguases utility into a group with nine state distribution companies, transmission and gas, serving more than 20 million customers. His sons Ricardo (CEO) and Maurício (CFO) now run it.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Energisa, the underdog bidder, won the 2013 creditors' vote for the bankrupt Grupo Rede over CPFL, a deal that changed the group's scale. In 2026, at 92, he published a memoir, 'A jornada da Energia para o futuro', based on his testimony to journalist Plínio Fraga.
deep_cut_fact: He started on the front line, in the lines and power plants. His memoir recalls installing Brazil's first photoelectric cell to switch street lighting on automatically, and a safety-glove demonstration that ended up shutting down power to the whole town. He was also an early backer of the Instituto Liberal think tank.
notes: He is about 92 (per JB, March 2026), so the realistic route is via Energisa IR or his sons; CEO Ricardo Botelho is the active public face. The new memoir (2026) is a natural hook for outreach. Confirm his current board status in Energisa's Formulário de Referência.

name: Andrea Della Valle
current_role: Vice Chairman, Tod's S.p.A. (Tod's, Hogan, Roger Vivier, Fay)
profile: Born 1965 in Sant'Elpidio a Mare in the Marche shoe district, Andrea and brother Diego control Tod's, the luxury shoe and leather-goods group grown from their grandfather's early-1900s workshop. In 2024 they took Tod's private with L Catterton and LVMH at a ~$1.5bn valuation. The brothers also hold stakes in Piaggio and RCS MediaGroup; Andrea chaired ACF Fiorentina 2004-09.
interesting_fact: Tod's group funded the restoration of Rome's Colosseum; Andrea also led Fiorentina's revival after its previous owner's bankruptcy and remained honorary president until the club was sold to Rocco Commisso in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: On 31 May 2024 the Marche mountain town of Arquata del Tronto, devastated by the 2016 earthquake, made him an honorary citizen 'for the social and civil commitment shown after the 2016 earthquake'.
notes: Brother Diego Della Valle is the public face of Tod's; Andrea is lower-profile. todsgroup.com blocked automated access, so press contact not extracted - check its Media/Contacts section manually. Web search budget exhausted at this point.

name: Max Turnauer
current_role: Deceased (died November 2020)
profile: Son of Constantia group founder Herbert Turnauer; inherited Constantia Industries (Fundermax, Isovolta) in the family split. Died in 2020 aged 90; his son Stanislaus Turnauer now chairs and owns the group.
notes: Death reported by Industriemagazin on 9 Nov 2020: https://industriemagazin.at/industrie/der-industrielle-max-turnauer-verstorben/ . Listing is stale; relevant living person is Stanislaus Turnauer (Constantia Industries).

name: Vladimir Melnikov
current_role: Founder, owner and chairman of the board, Gloria Jeans (Moscow)
profile: Melnikov founded the Gloria cooperative in Rostov-on-Don in 1988 and the Gloria Jeans retail company in 1997. The business also manufactured for Western brands such as Levi's and H&M. After Inditex, H&M and Uniqlo left Russia in 2022 it expanded rapidly into their vacated space and now runs 700+ stores in Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan. HQ moved to Moscow in 2016.
interesting_fact: In 2022 he gave 1 million rubles to each employee who had worked at Gloria Jeans for at least 10 years.
deep_cut_fact: His 1988 Gloria cooperative in Rostov-on-Don became the first officially recognised jeans maker in the Soviet Union.
notes: Russia-based. Check sanctions and reputational considerations before outreach. The Gloria Jeans site renders via JavaScript, so I could not extract a press email. The web-search budget ran out before this profile.

name: Louis Bacon
current_role: Founder, Chairman and principal investment manager, Moore Capital Management; Founder and Chairman, The Moore Charitable Foundation
profile: North Carolina-born macro trader who profited in the 1987 crash and founded Moore Capital in 1989, becoming one of Wall Street's best-known macro managers. He returned outside capital in 2019 and now runs Moore mainly as a family/employee investment firm, while focusing heavily on land, water and wildlife conservation through the Moore Charitable Foundation (founded 1992).
interesting_fact: He named Moore Capital after his own middle name, and launched Moore Global Investments in 1990 with $25,000 inherited from his family.
deep_cut_fact: His Wall Street start came from a summer job: while working on a fishing boat on Long Island he met NYSE specialist Walter Frank, who gave him a clerking job at Walter N. Frank & Co. during his college summers. He later ran a floor 'runner' job at the New York Cotton Exchange.
notes: Energy angle: has written publicly against Drax biomass sourcing (Daily Mail op-ed linked from louisbacon.com) and on wildfire/forest health and offshore drilling. Ann Colley, Moore Capital's Director of Public Relations and Charitable Giving and Foundation Executive Director, is the published PR lead (https://www.moorecharitable.org/leadership/ann-colley/).

name: Irvine Laidlaw, Lord Laidlaw
current_role: Chairman, Irvine Laidlaw Foundation (Laidlaw Foundation); private investor
profile: Irvine Laidlaw (b. 1942, Keith, Banffshire) built the Institute for International Research from a small US publisher bought in 1973 into the world's largest conference organiser, selling it in 2005 for about £768m; he also founded Abbey Business Centres. A former Conservative life peer (2004-2010), he now focuses on education philanthropy via the Laidlaw Foundation.
interesting_fact: A keen historic racer, he owned and raced a Le Mans-winning 1950s Jaguar and a 1962 Ferrari 250 GTO before stopping racing in 2013. Wikipedia also says he part-owns a $2.1bn wind-farm project.
deep_cut_fact: His £9m gift to the University of Leeds, where he studied economics in the 1960s, was its largest ever and funded the £26m Laidlaw Library (opened 2015). His Laidlaw Scholarships for undergraduate research and leadership now run at about 19 universities including Oxford, Cambridge, Columbia and EPFL.
notes: Contacts are for his foundation, not him personally. Possible energy angle via reported wind-farm investment (unverified detail). Left the House of Lords in 2010.

name: Muhammed Aziz Khan
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Summit Group (Bangladesh); based in Singapore
profile: Bangladesh-born, Singapore-based Muhammed Aziz Khan (b. 1955, Dhaka IBA MBA) started out as a trader and founded Summit in 1985; it built Bangladesh's first independent power plant (Khulna, 1998) and its first private off-dock port, and now spans power, LNG, ports, fibre optics and real estate. Japan's JERA owns 22% of Summit Power International, run by his daughter Ayesha.
interesting_fact: He told Nikkei Asia Summit plans Bangladesh's first data centre using Summit Power's gas-fired capacity: 'Summit Group's next phase focuses on integrating energy and data, leveraging our LNG and fibre-optic expertise.'
deep_cut_fact: Singapore's Prime Minister's Office awarded him the Public Service Medal (COVID-19) for financially helping Bangladeshi workers in Singapore during the pandemic; he and his wife were also the first Bangladeshis named UNICEF International Council members.

public_contacts.value: enquiry@summitpowerinternational.com (Summit Power International, One Raffles Place, Singapore)

notes: Very good fit: energy + data-centre angle (gas-to-data-centre plan, fibre/LNG). Gives interviews to Bangladeshi press and Nikkei. Best route: Summit Power International Singapore enquiry form (press category).

name: Gennady Kozovoy
current_role: Shareholder (~5.7%) of Evraz plc; former CEO and board member of Raspadskaya coal company (Mezhdurechensk, Kuzbass)
profile: Siberian coal executive who rose through Russia's Raspadskaya mine. In 1993 he was elected general director and, with partner Alexander Vagin, gained control of the company as workers' shares were bought up. Raspadskaya listed in 2006. In 2012 they sold control to Evraz for cash plus Evraz shares, his main asset today. He stepped down as CEO in July 2014.
interesting_fact: Kozovoy and Vagin turned Raspadskaya, once a 'people's enterprise' owned by its miners, into one of Russia's biggest coking-coal producers. They sold their stake to Evraz for about $202M plus roughly 11% of Evraz.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 36 years at Raspadskaya, starting as an electrician-fitter (elektroslesar) at the mine and rising to general director, as the company noted when he handed over the CEO role in 2014.
notes: Very private and gives virtually no press. Russia-based. Evraz was sanctioned by the UK in 2022 (Abramovich link) and is no longer LSE-traded, so outreach may be impractical. Patronymic Ivanovich. No published contact found.

name: Mikhail Abyzov
current_role: None; former Russian Minister for Open Government Affairs (2012-2018), now serving a prison sentence in Russia
profile: Minsk-born Russian energy and engineering businessman (b. 1972) who built his fortune via fuel supply and power assets such as Novosibirskenergo, and chaired engineering group E4. He was Russia's Minister for Open Government Affairs 2012-2018. Arrested in 2019, he was sentenced in Dec 2023 to 12 years; a later RVC-related conviction raised the total to 14 years.
interesting_fact: He set up his first company, Intershops, in 1990 at about 18, selling Turkish consumer goods and later office equipment, before moving into fuel supply and Siberian power utilities.
notes: NOT a viable outreach target: imprisoned in Russia (12-year sentence Dec 2023 per Moscow Times https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2023/12/22/former-russian-minister-sentenced-to-12-years-for-embezzlement-a83522; further cases since, incl. 14-year combined sentence reported by Current Time). He denies the charges. No public contacts; deep-cut fact left empty deliberately.

name: Kirill Shamalov
current_role: Shareholder of PAO SIBUR Holding (about 4% per Forbes); listed by the UK sanctions register as Deputy Chairman of SIBUR's Management Board (current status unverified)
profile: Russian petrochemicals investor and son of Rossiya Bank co-owner Nikolai Shamalov. He joined Sibur as a vice president in 2008, became deputy CEO in 2012 and built up a stake that made him briefly Russia's youngest billionaire. He later sold most of it and is believed to keep about 4% of Sibur. He is under US (2018), UK and EU sanctions.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes he became a vice president of Sibur, Russia's largest petrochemicals company, at age 26, after studying law at Saint Petersburg State University.
deep_cut_fact: According to a Sibur biography cited by Bloomberg, in 2002, at about 20 and still a law student, he was named Gazprom's chief legal counsel for foreign economic activity. He later became chief legal counsel at Gazprombank before joining Sibur in 2008.
notes: High risk: he is sanctioned by the US, UK and EU, and most coverage concerns his former marriage to Putin's daughter and how he got his Sibur shares. He is very private and gives no interviews. The only route is Sibur's corporate press office, and it is unclear whether he still holds a Sibur post. Probably not a suitable podcast guest.

name: Cesar Maklary
current_role: Co-founder and President, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, HQ New York)
profile: French co-founder (with Gary Wu and Jamie Cox) of Fluidstack, which grew from an Oxford-born GPU marketplace into a builder/operator of large AI data centers for customers including Anthropic, Google and Meta. A ~$1.5B round led by Jane Street in 2026 valued Fluidstack at over $18B, making the three co-founders billionaires at around 30; he joined in 2020.
interesting_fact: Maklary was the face of Fluidstack's Feb 2025 deal, announced by Emmanuel Macron at the Paris AI Action Summit, to help build an $11.5B AI data center in France ('Nvidia has told me that they will send those chips when we need them'); later that year Jensen Huang signed a Lego model of an Nvidia chip for him and Wu at GTC.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he worked on aerodynamics for a Formula One team. He has explained Fluidstack's origin as matching PhD friends starved for compute with 'hardcore cloud gaming friends' whose rigs sat idle most of the week.
notes: Great fit for data-center podcast. Speaks at conferences (e.g. RAISE Summit Paris). France data-center project was reportedly scrapped in 2026 in favour of US sites (avoid framing as failure). Fluidstack declines to comment on valuation/net worth.

name: Gary Wu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, New York)
profile: Most likely the Gary Wu who co-founded Fluidstack in 2017 while studying economics at Oxford. It began renting idle gamers' GPUs to AI researchers and now builds gigawatt-scale AI data centers, incl. Anthropic's planned $50B build-out on Google TPUs. A Sept 2026 round valued it above $18B, making Wu (31) a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Fluidstack's backers project it managing up to 1.3 GW across 10+ sites in 2026 and aspire to 17+ GW by 2030; it appears to be the first publicly known operator of Google TPU data centers outside Google.
deep_cut_fact: Fluidstack started in 2017 helping gamers make 'beer money' by renting out their idle GPUs to AI researchers; the company never disclosed raising any outside funding until July 2026.
notes: Identity uncertain only because the input lists country 'China' while Fluidstack is UK-founded and now New York-HQ; source of wealth ('AI datacenter builder') and new-billionaire status match strongly. Founders give few interviews; Fluidstack declines press comment. Note Anthropic is a major customer (research compiled by Claude, an Anthropic model).

name: James Dacombe
current_role: Founder & CEO, Olix (OLIX Computing, London AI-inference chip startup); founder & CEO, CoMind (brain monitoring)
profile: British serial founder (b. ~2001) who dropped out of school at 17 to build CoMind, a non-invasive brain-monitoring company, then in 2024 founded Olix (formerly Flux Computing), which designs chips and systems for AI inference. Olix raised $312m in August 2026 at ~$3.3bn, making him Europe's youngest self-made billionaire per Forbes (~30% of Olix, ~12% of CoMind).
interesting_fact: Forbes counts him as one of only 11 self-made billionaires worldwide under 30 - and one of four based outside the US; Olix tripled in value between February and August 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He started programming apps and websites at 13 while at Ashville College in Harrogate, North Yorkshire, then became a Thiel Fellow. He told the Sunday Times in 2024: 'An advantage of starting my business so young was naivety... you just try a lot of things.'
notes: Highly relevant for data-center/AI-infrastructure angle (Olix pitches a 'token factory' rebuild of the datacentre). Olix and CoMind did not respond to Forbes/Fortune comment requests in Aug 2026, so expect a press-office gate; press@olix.com is the best route.

name: Jamie Cox
current_role: Cofounder, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, now HQ'd in New York)
profile: British cofounder (with Gary Wu, later Cesar Maklary) of Fluidstack, started in 2017 as a marketplace renting idle gamer GPUs to AI researchers and now a builder/operator of large AI data centers, including custom sites for Anthropic in New York and Texas and a planned 1GW campus in France. A 2026 Jane Street-led $1.5B round valued it at $18B+, making Cox (29) a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Forbes reported Fluidstack appears to be the first publicly known operator of Google TPU data centers outside Google; Macron announced its ~EUR10B, 1-gigawatt French AI data center project in Feb 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He was reading classics at Oxford when he met economics student Gary Wu; he dropped out in 2018 to become a Thiel Fellow, and in 2020 he and Wu started Treecard, a cashback card that funded tree planting, alongside Fluidstack.
notes: Prime fit for the data-center podcast. Specific exec title not published (Wu is CEO, Maklary President). Company declined comment to Forbes on funding; route via press@fluidstack.io.

name: Baoshen Zhong
current_role: Chairman and President (General Manager), LONGi Green Energy Technology Co. (SSE: 601012)
profile: Zhong Baoshen chairs LONGi Green Energy, a global leader in monocrystalline solar wafers, cells and modules. He first built Fushun Magnetic Equipment, then joined Lanzhou University classmate Li Zhenguo at LONGi in 2006 as chairman, adding the CEO role in 2025. He is now steering LONGi through a PV downturn and into energy storage and hydrogen.
interesting_fact: LONGi bet early on monocrystalline silicon when multicrystalline was the industry mainstream, and that bet made mono the dominant solar technology. In 2026 Zhong set a goal of growing LONGi's energy-storage business to a scale close to its PV business within five years.
deep_cut_fact: LONGi's origin story starts with a phone call. In September 2005 Zhong was sightseeing at the Petronas Twin Towers after a business trip to Malaysia when Li Zhenguo, his 1986-entry Lanzhou University physics classmate and fellow Henan native, called about buying used US mono-crystal pullers. Zhong replied: 'Wait for me to come back' (等我回来).
notes: Very visible: NPC deputy, Boao and UN energy forum speaker, regular earnings-call commentator. Best route is LONGi PR (PR@longi.com). Topical hooks: solar-plus-storage ('光储融合') and the anti-'involution' push in Chinese PV. Sources differ on his major (Forbes says metallurgy, Chinese media say physics).

name: Zhang Xuezheng
current_role: Founder and actual controller (via Wentianxia Technology Group) of Wingtech Technology (600745.SH); former chairman of Wingtech (to 2025) and CEO of Nexperia (suspended by Dutch order, Sept 2025)
profile: Born 1975, studied at Guangdong University of Technology, then worked at STMicroelectronics and ZTE before founding Wingtech in 2006. Wingtech became China's top phone ODM (it made Xiaomi's Redmi line), then bought Dutch chipmaker Nexperia in 2019. In 2025 the Dutch government took control of Nexperia, suspending him as CEO; he remains Wingtech's controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Wingtech designed and built Xiaomi's Redmi 1, the first smartphone to retail for under 1,000 yuan (799 yuan), which sold more than 30 million units.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he reportedly started Wingtech in Jiaxing with about 30 staff and 100,000 yuan, then went door-to-door in Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei with three salespeople to sell its first phone mainboard, the W100. It went on to ship 18 million units.
notes: Highly sensitive: Nexperia/Dutch government dispute (2025-26), a 2024 CSRC fine, and 2026 share freezes tied to an arbitration. Wingtech denied 'fled' rumours in Sept 2026. Rarely gives interviews. No published press/IR email found on the Wingtech English site. Career timeline (ST 1997-98, ZTE 1998-2002) per https://www.maigoo.com/mingren/24826.html.

name: William Moncrief-jr
current_role: Deceased (died 29 December 2021, Fort Worth, aged 101); formerly head of Moncrief Oil
profile: William Alvin 'Tex' Moncrief Jr., Fort Worth wildcatter who with his father 'Monty' built the Moncrief oil and gas business over 70+ years, died on 29 December 2021 aged 101.
notes: Deceased - death reported by NBC DFW and Hart Energy (Dec 2021). Source for death: https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/local/texas-oil-billionaire-william-tex-moncrief-jr-dead-at-101/2848207/ ; also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Moncrief

name: Zhang Yuxiang
current_role: Chairman, Nanji E-Commerce (南极电商, formerly Nanjiren; SZSE 002127), Shanghai
profile: Zhang founded Nanjiren in Shanghai in 1997-98 selling thermal underwear, then turned it into a brand-licensing business. After selling its fibre, dyeing and weaving units in 2014-15 it became an asset-light 'e-commerce brand services' company that licenses Nanjiren, Cartelo and other labels to thousands of suppliers selling on Chinese platforms. He shares the wealth with Zhu Xuelian.
interesting_fact: Nanjiren became one of China's biggest apparel brands by sales while making almost nothing itself: it sold its factories by 2015 and now earns brand-service fees from licensed suppliers and distributors.
notes: Fell off Forbes/Hurun lists after 2021-22 as the stock declined. Couldn't confirm in this session that he is still chairman (web search budget exhausted). The contact_form is the SZSE investor-interaction platform linked from the company site; HQ phone is published on the site.

name: Sergey Shnayder
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner, Svetofor Group (Svetofor/Mayak hard-discount supermarkets; operating companies 'Torgservis')
profile: Siberian entrepreneur (also spelled Schneider) who co-founded Svetofor with his brother Andrei in 2009. Modelled on Aldi and Walmart, its bare-bones stores price at least 20% below rivals, and the chain now has 2,000+ stores in Russia and abroad. He started in the 1990s distributing beer, then ran a beer-store chain from 2004.
interesting_fact: Svetofor deliberately opens stores in run-down suburbs that rivals avoid and buys stock close to its expiry date. It became Russia's fastest-growing supermarket chain and expanded into Germany, the Baltics, Poland and Serbia.
deep_cut_fact: Before discount groceries, Shnayder was a 1990s beer and low-alcohol drinks distributor; in 2004 he and partners launched a chain of stores selling mainly beer, the precursor to Svetofor.
notes: Extremely secretive: the brothers never give interviews and ignore approaches made through intermediaries (The Bell). OpenSanctions lists him on a Lithuanian (LTFIU) sanctions list, so check legal and reputational risk before any outreach. No published contact found. Low relevance to energy/data centers.

name: Randal Nardone
current_role: Director and major shareholder, New Fortress Energy (Nasdaq: NFE); co-founder of Fortress Investment Group
profile: Lawyer-turned-investor Randal Nardone co-founded Fortress Investment Group in 1998, was its CEO 2013-2017 and became a billionaire on its 2007 IPO; SoftBank bought Fortress in 2017. He sits on the board of Wes Edens' LNG-to-power firm New Fortress Energy (~9.6% holder per 2025 proxy).
interesting_fact: Fortress was the first major US private-equity/hedge-fund manager to go public (Feb 2007), which put Nardone on the Forbes billionaires list that year.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, Nardone was a partner and member of the executive committee at New York law firm Thacher Proffitt & Wood, then a principal at BlackRock Financial Management; he holds a BA from UConn and a JD from Boston University School of Law.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Wes Edens (NFE CEO) is the public face. NFE has been through financial stress/refinancing in 2025-26, so avoid wealth/stock topics. Power-for-data-centers angle: NFE's Oct 2026 300MW turbine lease.

name: Vlad Vendrow
current_role: Co-founder of RingCentral (longtime CTO); major Class B shareholder. Not listed among executive officers in the 2026 proxy, so his current title is unconfirmed
profile: Engineer who co-founded RingCentral with Vlad Shmunis in 1999 and served as its CTO, building the cloud phone and communications platform, which listed on the NYSE in 2013 and passed $1bn in revenue in 2020. Before that he was director of engineering at Motorola and at Ring Zero Systems. His wealth comes from his RingCentral stake.
interesting_fact: Entities tied to him still hold about 30% of RingCentral's super-voting Class B shares, roughly 17% of total voting power, second only to co-founder Vlad Shmunis (2026 proxy).
deep_cut_fact: RingCentral began life as 'RingZero', focused on small-business communications on Microsoft Windows, following on from Ring Zero Systems, where he had been director of engineering. He is named on more than 40 software patents.
notes: Very low public profile. The patent count and Motorola/Ring Zero detail come from the Forbes bio (https://www.forbes.com/profile/vlad-vendrow/). Confirm whether he is still CTO before outreach.

name: Yousuf Mohammad Salah Jamjoom
current_role: Founder and ~42% shareholder, Jamjoom Pharmaceuticals Factory Co. (Tadawul-listed, Jeddah); no longer listed on the current board
profile: Jeddah businessman who ran pharmaceutical distributor Jamjoom Medicine Store as CEO from 1965 to 2005 and founded Jamjoom Pharmaceuticals Factory, one of Saudi Arabia's largest makers of OTC and generic medicines, listed on the Saudi exchange in 2023. His sons now run the board: Mahmoud is chairman, Ahmed vice-chairman.
interesting_fact: He earned a diploma in commerce from the University of Wales back in 1947, and led Jamjoom Medicine Store for 40 years (1965-2005).
deep_cut_fact: The company he founded was the first in Saudi Arabia to build a complete soft-gelatin capsule manufacturing facility and pioneered Blow-Fill-Seal technology for sterile eye-care products in the Kingdom.
notes: Likely in his mid-90s (1947 diploma); 2025-26 board list on company site names only his sons (Mahmoud chairman, Ahmed vice-chair, Waleed/Alaa/Mohammed members). Alive status not confirmed by a recent source; approach via the family/chairman's office.

name: Tran Ba Duong
current_role: Founder and Chairman, THACO (Truong Hai Group), Vietnam
profile: Born in Huế in 1960, Tran Ba Duong trained as a mechanical engineer, worked his way up from an auto repair factory, and founded Truong Hai Auto (THACO) in 1997. It grew from selling cars to assembling Kia, Mazda and Peugeot models, gaining Jardine Cycle & Carriage as an investor in 2008, and is now a conglomerate spanning autos, real estate, agriculture and logistics. He stepped down as CEO in 2013 but remains chairman.
interesting_fact: He won the EY ASEAN Entrepreneurial Excellence Award in 2020, and is known for controlling every detail, often calling management meetings on evenings and weekends.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in mechanical engineering from Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology in 1983 and began as a repair technician at the Dong Nai auto repair factory before rising to management, so he literally went from fixing cars to building Vietnam's largest carmaker.
notes: THACO sites were unreachable (503/proxy errors) during research and web-search budget was exhausted, so no press email verified. Also linked to Dai Quang Minh real estate (Thu Thiem). Industrial/EV-manufacturing angle may suit podcast.

name: Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Chairman and CEO, King Power International (Thailand); Chairman, Leicester City FC
profile: 'Top' (b. 1985) took over Thailand's dominant airport duty-free operator King Power, founded by his late father Vichai in 1989, after Vichai's death in an October 2018 helicopter crash; the family fortune is shared with his mother and siblings. He chairs Leicester City (family-owned; reported in Aug 2026 to be up for sale) and the family also owns OH Leuven and a stake in Bangkok's MahaNakhon tower.
interesting_fact: The family name was a gift: Thailand's late King Bhumibol Adulyadej gave Vichai the surname Srivaddhanaprabha; Aiyawatt was born Aiyawatt Raksriaksorn.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious polo player who represents Thailand: he won gold in mixed 2-4 goals polo at the 2025 SEA Games in Thailand, and team silver at the 2017 SEA Games in Kuala Lumpur.

public_contacts.value: https://www.lcfc.com (Leicester City FC; chairman statements published here)

notes: Sensitive moment: Leicester relegated to League One (Apr 2026) and reportedly put up for sale (Aug 2026) — avoid in outreach. Only customer-service emails are published by King Power/LCFC; no press contact for him found. Energy-focus tag in input looks weak (duty-free retail).

name: Mukand Lal Dua
current_role: Whole Time Director, Relaxo Footwears Ltd (NSE: RELAXO), Delhi
profile: Mukand Lal Dua and his younger brother Ramesh Kumar Dua control Relaxo Footwears, India's largest footwear maker by volume, known for affordable brands Sparx, Bahamas, Flite and Schoolmate. He has about 51 years in footwear manufacturing and, as whole-time director, leads new product development and quality control; Relaxo's eight factories can make about a million pairs a day.
interesting_fact: Relaxo's capacity is roughly one million pairs of footwear per day, and its brands have been endorsed by Bollywood stars Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar and Katrina Kaif.
deep_cut_fact: Relaxo's own board page credits him with 51 years in footwear manufacturing and describes his role as 'providing cutting edge impetus to new product development and quality control', the hands-on factory side of the brothers' partnership.
notes: Low public profile; brother Ramesh Kumar Dua is chairman & MD and the more public face. Route via Relaxo corporate office in New Delhi.

name: JoeBen Bevirt
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chief Architect, Joby Aviation (NYSE: JOBY)
profile: Raised off-grid in Santa Cruz County, Bevirt studied mechanical engineering at UC Davis and Stanford, co-founded lab-robotics firm Velocity11 (sold to Agilent 2007) and Joby Inc. (GorillaPod tripod), then founded Joby Aviation in 2009. Joby, backed by Toyota and others, went public via SPAC in 2021 and is working to certify and launch an all-electric air-taxi service.
interesting_fact: He is named after JoeBen, a character in Ken Kesey's novel 'Sometimes a Great Notion' - his father was one of Kesey's Merry Pranksters.
deep_cut_fact: While still at Santa Cruz High School (class of 1991) he built one of the world's first full-suspension mountain bikes; during COVID-19 he also co-founded SummerBio with UC Santa Cruz geneticists to offer affordable PCR testing.
notes: Strong podcast fit (electric aviation, batteries, energy). Holds 160+ US patents and has testified to Congress on aviation noise. Also ran Joby Energy (airborne wind turbines) - a good energy-angle hook.

name: Bernard Charles
current_role: Co-founder and former Executive Chairman, Dassault Systèmes (stepped down from board Feb 21, 2026)
profile: Breton-born engineer who joined Dassault Systèmes in 1983, ran it as CEO from 1995 to 2023 and built it into a global 3D design/PLM software leader (CATIA, SolidWorks, 3DEXPERIENCE). He became chairman in 2022 (executive chairman from 2024, when Pascal Daloz took over as CEO) and stepped down in February 2026 for personal reasons, saying he would apply his experience to AI-driven transformation of industrial production.
interesting_fact: In 1989 he initiated the 'digital mock-up', a complete virtual 3D model replacing physical prototypes, which underpinned the shift to fully digitally designed products such as aircraft. HBR ranked him the world's 13th best-performing CEO in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he earned the French 'agrégation' in mechanical engineering, the country's most senior teaching qualification, plus a PhD in automation engineering from ENS Cachan; in 1986, three years after joining, he founded Dassault Systèmes' New Technologies, Research and Strategy department.
notes: Left Dassault board Feb 2026 but 'remains available' to the company; his stated next focus is AI for industrial production ('Generative Economy'), a good podcast hook. Company contacts may not route to him personally now.

name: Ina Chan
current_role: Private investor; shareholder in SJM Holdings, STDM and Macau Legend
profile: Ina Chan (Chan Un-chan), born in Macau, was a nurse hired to care for Stanley Ho's first wife after a 1971 car accident and is recognised as the late casino magnate's third wife. Her wealth comes from stakes in Macau casino operator SJM and Ho's former vehicle STDM, plus a holding in Macau Legend.
interesting_fact: She met Stanley Ho while working as a nurse caring for his first wife, Clementina Leitão.
notes: Very private, with no public role or published contact. She left the Forbes list after 2021. I found no death report but could not verify current status (the web-search budget ran out). Her wealth is tied to Ho family estate matters, so she is a poor fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast and I do not recommend outreach.

name: Xu Shijun
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Haili Wind Power Equipment Technology Co., Ltd. (海力风电, SZ:301155)
profile: Xu Shijun (b. 1963) controls Jiangsu Haili Wind Power, a Nantong-based maker of wind-turbine towers, monopiles and other offshore foundation structures, which listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in 2021. A trained mechanical engineer and senior economist, he joined Haili in 2009 and has chaired it since. He shares the Hurun listing with Xu Chengchen, a fellow director.
interesting_fact: Haili builds the giant steel towers and pile foundations that hold up China's offshore wind turbines. That made Xu one of the few billionaires whose fortune comes directly from the build-out of offshore wind in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea.
deep_cut_fact: Before wind power he worked his way up at the Rudong County Cotton Machinery Factory (如东县棉机厂) in Jiangsu, first as head of supply and sales and then as factory director. He also still chairs Longteng Machinery (龙腾机械).
notes: 'Haili' here is Jiangsu Haili Wind Power, not the unrelated NEEQ-listed Zhejiang Haili (835787). Xu is low-profile and the IR inbox is the only published route. The listed sector 'Energy' fits: offshore wind supply chain.

name: Sebastian Siemiatkowski
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Klarna (NYSE: KLAR)
profile: Swedish son of Polish immigrants who co-founded Klarna in 2005 at 23 after selling accounts-receivable services and seeing how painful e-commerce payments were for small merchants. Klarna pioneered buy-now-pay-later, became a licensed European bank and listed on the NYSE in September 2025, the year's largest NYSE IPO. He is a prominent voice on AI replacing corporate headcount.
interesting_fact: He met one of his Klarna co-founders while the two were flipping burgers at a Burger King in Sweden.
deep_cut_fact: He credits Sweden's late-1990s policy of subsidising home-computer ownership for his career, since it let his family buy their first computer; his early business heroes were Richard Branson and IKEA founder Ingvar Kamprad.
notes: Very active publicly on X (widely cited as @klarnaseb) and LinkedIn, posting about AI and Klarna; could not verify the handle from an official page here. Good podcast fit for AI/compute-demand angle (Klarna's 'AI can do all the jobs' stance).

name: Wu Peifu
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Shuangxing Color Plastic New Materials Co. (SZSE: 002585), Suqian, Jiangsu (per Forbes)
profile: Wu Peifu (about 65 per Forbes 2022) founded and chairs Jiangsu Shuangxing Color Plastic New Materials, founded in 1997 in Suqian and listed in Shenzhen in 2011. Starting in packaging film, it has become a major Chinese maker of polyester functional films, including optical films (a Samsung VD supplier since 2019), new-energy materials and energy-saving window films; the wealth is held with his family.
interesting_fact: The 'Chairman's message' on Shuangxing's website sets out a personal creed: 'do one practical thing a day, one new thing a month, one big thing a year, and one meaningful thing in a lifetime.'
notes: Forbes bio misspells him 'Wang Peifu'; not to be confused with warlord Wu Peifu (1874-1939). Company name is Shuangxing ('Shuangxin' in input). New-energy films offer an energy angle. Very low public profile; Chinese-language outreach via company/IR office. Web-search budget exhausted before a deep-cut fact could be sourced; the motto is from the chairman's page and not explicitly signed by him.

name: Mehmet Rustu Basaran
current_role: Chairman, HABAŞ Group (Habaş Sınai ve Tıbbi Gazlar İstihsal Endüstrisi); chairman and part-owner of Anadolubank
profile: Turkish industrialist (b. ~1946/47) who heads Habaş, founded by his father Hamdi Başaran in 1956 in Istanbul as the Topkapı oxygen plant. Habaş grew from industrial/medical gases into one of Turkey's largest steel producers, with LPG/LNG/CNG distribution, storage, shipping and port operations; he also controls Anadolubank.
interesting_fact: Per Forbes, he is a serious car collector whose collection has included a Ferrari 288 GTO, Ferrari F40, McLaren F1, Porsche Carrera GT and Hennessey Venom GT.
notes: HIGHLY SENSITIVE / timing: on 10 Nov 2026 he was reported detained in Istanbul in the probe into a deadly explosion at Habaş's Aliağa (İzmir) steel plant (reported 18 dead). Source: https://www.timeturk.com/habas-patronu-mehmet-rustu-basaran-kartalda-gozaltina-alindi. Forbes says he seldom appears in public and doesn't talk to press. Outreach not advisable now.

name: Yao Lisheng
current_role: Non-independent director and major shareholder, Maxscend Microelectronics (卓胜微, SZSE: 300782), Wuxi
profile: Yao Lisheng (姚立生) is a co-founding shareholder and long-time board member (since 2017) of Maxscend Microelectronics, a Wuxi-based fabless maker of RF front-end chips (switches, LNAs, modules) for smartphones that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in June 2019. His fortune tracks his Maxscend stake; he dropped off Forbes/Hurun lists after 2022 as the shares fell.
interesting_fact: Maxscend's predecessor was set up in August 2012 with RMB10m registered capital by just three backers: CEO Xu Zhihan, Yao Lisheng and Tianjin Xundu.
deep_cut_fact: He studied as an undergraduate at Tsinghua University and did graduate work at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
notes: Very low public profile; not an executive (chairman/CEO is Xu Zhihan). Education detail comes from an aggregator (MarketScreener); verify against Maxscend's annual report director bios. Route via company general/IR inbox.

name: Ghan Djoe Hiang
current_role: Family shareholder, Baramulti Group (Indonesian coal; listed arm PT Baramulti Suksessarana Tbk, IDX: BSSR)
profile: Jakarta-based widow, about 86, of Athanasius Tossin Suharya (d. 2020), who started the Baramulti group in 1971 as general contractor PT Ensicon Indonesia and moved into coal trading in 1988. Her wealth comes from the family's coal holdings; the group owns 11 coal concessions in Kalimantan and Sumatra. Forbes listed her as a billionaire only in 2023.
interesting_fact: Baramulti grew from a 1971 construction contractor into the owner of 11 coal concessions in Kalimantan and Sumatra; its listed unit BSSR mines near Samarinda, East Kalimantan.
notes: Extremely private: no interviews or public role found. The group's site lists only phone numbers, no email. She dropped off Forbes' list after 2023, and no recent news was found to confirm she is alive (Forbes gave her age as 83 in 2023). Family members such as Daniel Suharya appear on the BSSR board; the company is a better route than her personally.

name: Dai Wenyuan
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director & CEO, 4Paradigm (Beijing Fourth Paradigm Technology, HKEX-listed)
profile: AI researcher-turned-founder who started 4Paradigm in 2014 after serving as chief architect of Baidu's Phoenix Nest ad system and principal scientist at Huawei's Noah's Ark Lab. 4Paradigm sells enterprise machine-learning/AI platforms and is HK-listed; he holds degrees from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and HKUST.
interesting_fact: He is a former ACM-ICPC (international collegiate programming contest) world champion, per 4Paradigm's leadership page, and was named to MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35 (China) and Fortune's 40 Under 40.
deep_cut_fact: He is first author of 'Boosting for Transfer Learning' (ICML 2007, with Qiang Yang, Gui-Rong Xue, Yong Yu), which introduced TrAdaBoost, the first boosting-based transfer-learning algorithm and a widely cited classic in the field.
notes: Data-center/AI angle: 4Paradigm builds enterprise AI platforms and compute solutions. Best route is 4Paradigm PR (pr_co@4paradigm.com).

name: Kenshin Oshima
current_role: Former founder/chairman of SFCG (formerly Shohkoh Fund), a Japanese SME lender that went bankrupt in 2009; no current role found
profile: Born 1948, Oshima graduated top of his class from Keio's commerce faculty and worked at Mitsui & Co. (including Jakarta) before founding Shohkoh Fund in 1978 to lend to small businesses. It listed in 1989 and on the TSE First Section in 1999, and he ranked 61st on Forbes' 1997 list. SFCG collapsed in 2009.
interesting_fact: While at Mitsui & Co. in Jakarta, a Singaporean banker entertained him and thanked him 'for borrowing'. Oshima said that moment made him decide to go into finance himself.
deep_cut_fact: His father ran the 'Dance Hall Shinseiki' in Tokyo, the ballroom used as a setting in the 1996 film 'Shall We Dance?'.
notes: Not a suitable guest: SFCG went bankrupt in 2009; he was arrested that year and finally fully acquitted by the Tokyo High Court in 2016. The trustee won a ~JPY71.7bn damages ruling. He is almost certainly no longer a billionaire. Alive status not confirmed (no death reported on ja.wikipedia). No public contacts.

name: Roberto Rocca
notes: Roberto Rocca, longtime head of Argentina's Techint group and first chairman of Tenaris, died in Milan on 10 June 2003 aged 81 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Rocca). The group is now led by his son Paolo Rocca.

name: Adolf Merckle
profile: German industrialist who founded generics maker Ratiopharm (1973), ran the family firm Merckle GmbH and held large stakes in HeidelbergCement. He died on 5 January 2009 in Blaubeuren, aged 74.
notes: Deceased 5 Jan 2009 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Merckle). The family business continues under the Merckle family. Handle sensitively.

name: Jose Cutrale
current_role: Deceased — most likely José Luís Cutrale (1946-2022) of Sucocítrico Cutrale, the orange-juice giant; his father and company founder José Cutrale Jr. died in 2004
notes: Forbes 1999-2000 entry 'Jose Cutrale' refers to the Cutrale orange-juice family (Araraquara, Brazil). José Luís Cutrale died in London on 17 Aug 2022 (https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Lu%C3%ADs_Cutrale); his father José Cutrale Jr., who founded the company in 1967, died in 2004. Either way, deceased. Company now run by the next generation (José Luís Cutrale Jr. et al.).

name: Hinduja, Srichand, Gopichand
profile: Combined 1999 Forbes listing for brothers Srichand (S.P.) and Gopichand Hinduja, co-chairmen of the Hinduja Group. Both have died: S.P. Hinduja on 17 May 2023 and Gopichand Hinduja on 4 November 2025.
notes: Both deceased. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._P._Hinduja and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopichand_Hinduja . Surviving brothers Prakash and Ashok Hinduja and the next generation run the Hinduja Group (energy interests incl. Hinduja Renewables, power), if the journalist wants a living contact.

name: Lee Family
profile: A generic 'Lee Family' (Hong Kong) entry from Forbes' 1996-2001 lists with no source of wealth recorded. Several Hong Kong Lee families could match (e.g. the Lee Hysan family behind Hysan Development, or the Lee Kum Kee sauce family), so the record cannot be tied to a specific family or person.
notes: Ambiguous family entry; identity could not be determined from the input. Needs the original Forbes 1996-2001 listing text (source of wealth) to resolve before any outreach.

name: Gaston Vidigal
current_role: Deceased (d. 7 Aug 2001, São Paulo)
profile: Most likely Gastão Eduardo de Bueno Vidigal (1919-2001), longtime head of Banco Mercantil de São Paulo, which he chaired 1962-1985 and grew to ~250 branches. He died in São Paulo on 7 August 2001, aged 82.
notes: Input has no source of wealth; matched on name/country/Forbes 1999-2000 listing to the Banco Mercantil de São Paulo banker Gastão Vidigal (died 2001, per Portuguese Wikipedia). Not a viable outreach target.

name: Zhu Wenchen
current_role: Founder/controller, Furen Pharmaceutical Group (Henan); also owns Songhe Liquor (status uncertain)
profile: Henan-based pharmaceutical entrepreneur, founder and long-time chairman of Furen Pharmaceutical Group, which took control of listed Shanghai Minfeng Industrial in 2006; he also owns Songhe Liquor. Publicity-shy; few current details available.
notes: Identity match to Forbes 'pharmaceuticals' listing is likely Furen's founder but not confirmed from Forbes. Per Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Wenchen), regulators found Furen had falsified results and banned him from the securities market for 10 years in 2020; not a recommended outreach target.

name: Anastasia Soare
current_role: Founder and CEO, Anastasia Beverly Hills (ABH)
profile: Born 1957 in Constanța, Romania, Soare emigrated to Los Angeles in 1989 speaking little English and worked as an aesthetician. She developed a brow-shaping method based on facial bone structure, opened her Bedford Drive salon by 1997 and built Anastasia Beverly Hills, sold in about 2,000 stores. TPG invested in 2018. Known as the 'Eyebrow Queen', she still runs the company.
interesting_fact: She has said her first eyebrow clients were Cindy Crawford and Naomi Campbell. She had to rent a room in a Beverly Hills salon after her manager doubted there was a market for eyebrow shaping.
deep_cut_fact: Before emigrating she studied art history and architecture in Romania. She based her brow-shaping method on proportions from that training, fitting brows to each person's bone structure.
notes: The Instagram and X accounts belong to the company, not to her personally. Forbes listed her as a billionaire only in 2019; its 2023 estimate valued ABH at about $500M, so she may no longer be a billionaire. She is a frequent podcast and interview guest on immigrant-founder stories. The web-search budget ran out before this profile, so it relies on Wikipedia and company sites.

name: Kenny Park (Park Eun-kwan)
current_role: Founder and CEO, Simone Accessory Collection (Seoul; KOSPI-listed)
profile: Yonsei graduate who founded Simone Accessory in 1987 and built it into one of the world's largest contract makers of designer handbags, supplying brands such as Michael Kors, Coach, Kate Spade, Marc Jacobs and DKNY from factories in Vietnam, Cambodia, Indonesia and China (about 18m bags and small leather goods a year).
interesting_fact: For decades he quietly manufactured luxury handbags for famous labels while staying almost unknown himself, until joining the Forbes Korea rich list in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: After university he first worked at his father's fishing company, then at handbag maker Chungsan, before starting Simone in 1987. His own description of the craft: 'My canvas was small, but I could paint the drawing I liked, the painting I wanted.'
notes: Low-profile; Simone's website could not be reached during research and no official contact was verified. Route via Simone Accessory Collection corporate office in Seoul / its KRX disclosures.

name: Patricia Matte
current_role: Honorary councillor, Sociedad de Instrucción Primaria (SIP Red de Colegios); member of the Matte family (CMPC shareholders)
profile: Patricia Matte Larraín (b. 1943, Santiago) is the eldest child of industrialist Eliodoro Matte Ossa and shares in the Matte family fortune built on forestry/paper giant Empresas CMPC. A sociologist (Universidad Católica, 1969), she worked on social and anti-poverty policy and later concentrated on education through the SIP network of free schools.
interesting_fact: She focused much of her career on the Sociedad de Instrucción Primaria, a Chilean network of tuition-free schools founded in 1856 that celebrated 170 years in 2026; she now sits on its council of honorary members.
deep_cut_fact: A trained sociologist, she started her career at the UN's Economic Commission for Latin America (CEPAL) and later helped design poverty-reduction programmes at the national planning office (Odeplan); she received Chile's Premio Bicentenario in 2007.
notes: Low profile, ~83 years old; wealth is shared family wealth (CMPC). Her role in the Pinochet-era government is politically sensitive; avoid in outreach. SIP communications is the only published channel found.

name: Bryan Sheffield
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Formentera Partners (Austin, TX)
profile: Son of Pioneer Natural Resources CEO Scott Sheffield. In 2008 he founded Parsley Energy on his grandfather's old Midland wells, listed it in 2014 and sold it to Pioneer in 2021 for about $7.6bn including debt. Since 2020 he has run Formentera Partners ($2.8bn+ commitments, about 70,000 boe/d), which is developing Australia's Beetaloo Basin with INPEX.
interesting_fact: Parsley Energy started in 2008 with 109 old wells his grandfather Joe Parsley had drilled around Midland. Bryan had no energy experience, only 'family connections' and a 'trader's taste for risk', per Forbes.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 he founded the Drop Shot Series, Austin's first professional tennis tournament series, with former world-ranked pro Christo van Rensburg. It grew into the ATX Open, a WTA 250 event and Austin's largest women's pro sporting event. He is also a co-owner of Austin FC.
notes: Good podcast fit: shale plus Australian gas/LNG, with first Beetaloo gas sales in Sept 2026. He speaks at Hart Energy conferences. Firm news goes out via BusinessWire; I found no published press email. The LinkedIn link is the company page, not his own.

name: Liu Fuhai
current_role: Founder/chairman, Shandong Dahai Group (山东大海集团), Dongying (as last reported by Forbes, 2018)
profile: Liu Fuhai (刘福海, b. ~1954) is the self-made founder of Shandong Dahai Group (est. 1988, Guangrao/Dongying, Shandong), a conglomerate spanning textiles, new energy (including PV and copper/energy materials), new materials and trade. Forbes listed him with family at about US$1bn (2017-2018). Hurun listed him 2008-2018.
interesting_fact: Dahai grew into a ~RMB40bn-revenue group by 2017, built on a 'circular economy' model that links textiles with energy and new-materials businesses.
deep_cut_fact: Outside business, Liu is president of the Shandong Shanglian Calligraphy and Painting Academy (山东尚联书画院), according to Forbes.
notes: Forbes profile 'Liu Fuhai & family': textiles, energy; residence Dongying; married, 2 children; age 72. The Dahai group reportedly went through court-supervised debt restructuring after 2019 (not verified here), so his current role and wealth are uncertain. No official website or contacts found. Not to be confused with a USTB metallurgy researcher of the same name.

name: Ajay Kalsi
current_role: Founder of Indus Gas Ltd (Guernsey; Rajasthan gas producer, being cancelled from AIM) and chairman of operator Focus Energy Ltd
profile: Delhi-based LSE (BSc Econ) and Cambridge (MPhil Econ) graduate who inherited a family shoe business in Kanpur and built a portfolio spanning oil & gas, premium footwear, commodity trading, real estate and BPO. His wealth stems mainly from Indus Gas, which he founded and listed on London's AIM in 2008.
interesting_fact: Indus Gas holds a 90% participating interest in Block RJ-ON/6, a ~4,026 sq km onshore gas block in Rajasthan's mid-Indus basin, under a production sharing contract first signed in 1998; his Focus Energy is the operator.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond gas, his footwear holdings include the English heritage shoemaker Barker (and Barker Black) of Earls Barton, Northamptonshire; UK Companies House records show him as a Barker Shoes director from 2000 to 2010.
notes: Low public profile. Indus Gas has proposed cancelling its AIM admission and its exec chairman is Jonathan Keeling, so Kalsi's exact current title is uncertain. Best route is Indus Gas's London representative office (info@indusgas.com). Avoid company financial difficulties as a topic.

name: Thomas Kaplan
current_role: Chairman and CIO, The Electrum Group LLC (New York natural-resources investment firm); Chairman, NOVAGOLD Resources
profile: New York-born, Oxford-educated (BA/MA/DPhil in history) resource investor. He founded Apex Silver in 1993 (San Cristobal mine, Bolivia) and Leor Exploration, whose Texas gas assets sold to Encana for $2.55B in 2007, then pivoted to gold and silver via Electrum (NovaGold, Sunshine Silver). Also co-founded big-cat charity Panthera and built The Leiden Collection.
interesting_fact: He is the world's largest private collector of Rembrandt; The Leiden Collection, named for Rembrandt's birthplace, lends works to museums such as the Louvre and Louvre Abu Dhabi as a 'lending library'.
deep_cut_fact: His Oxford doctorate, supervised by Sir Michael Howard and Robert O'Neill, examined the Malayan counterinsurgency and how commodities shape strategic planning; he reportedly impressed his first boss, Avi Tiomkin, by predicting Iraq's invasion of Kuwait years before 1990.
notes: Energy angle: Leor Exploration was a large US natural-gas E&P (sold 2007). Articulate, frequent conference speaker (Milken, mining events). Also founder/chair of Panthera (panthera.org).

name: Billy Kan
current_role: Chairman, China HK Power Smart Energy Group Ltd (0931.HK; formerly China LNG Group), Hong Kong
profile: Billy Albert Kan Che-kin (b. ~1951, Hong Kong) studied at La Salle College, Cotton College in England and the University of East Anglia (BSc maths), then worked as an executive at Deloitte and KPMG before going it alone. He built China LNG Group (renamed China HK Power Smart Energy in 2023), an LNG/natural-gas and energy business, and remains its chairman as of June 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he donated 30 million of his shares to a church, and the same year received an honorary doctorate from his alma mater, the University of East Anglia.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining why he left the Big Four accounting world, he told The CEO Magazine he realised he was wasting time mingling to get ahead: 'If I wanted to succeed, I needed to take destiny into my own hands and work for myself.'
notes: Billionaire status dated (Forbes 2015-2017); company is now small-cap. Chairman role confirmed in HKEX announcement of 12 June 2026 (https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0612/2026061200670.pdf). No published press email found; company office in St. John's Building, Central HK.

name: Jon Huntsman
profile: Jon M. Huntsman Sr. (1937-2018), founder of chemicals maker Huntsman Corporation, died on 2 February 2018 in Salt Lake City, aged 80. The company is now led by his son Peter R. Huntsman.
notes: Deceased (d. 2 Feb 2018) - skip. Not to be confused with son Jon Huntsman Jr. (ex-governor/ambassador). If the podcast wants the family, Peter R. Huntsman (Huntsman Corp CEO) is the active figure.

name: Steven Allen Spielberg
current_role: Film director and producer; co-founder and principal of Amblin Entertainment / Amblin Partners
profile: Spielberg (born 1946) is the highest-grossing film director of all time (Jaws, E.T., Jurassic Park, Schindler's List). His wealth comes from directing, producing and profit participations, Amblin, and co-founding DreamWorks in 1994. He still directs and produces through Amblin, and founded the USC Shoah Foundation's archive of Holocaust survivor testimony.
interesting_fact: He used his profits from Schindler's List to start the Shoah Foundation, which recorded over 50,000 Holocaust survivor testimonies; the archive moved to USC in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: He became an Eagle Scout at 13 and earned his photography merit badge by making a 9-minute 8mm Western, 'The Last Gunfight'. He later helped the Boy Scouts of America create a cinematography merit badge, launched at the 1989 National Jamboree.
notes: Input name says 'Allen'; his middle name is Allan. Entertainment billionaire, off-theme for an energy/data-center podcast. Very hard to reach; any approach would go through Amblin or his talent agency/publicist (not verified in this session). Possible tech angle: early adopter of digital filmmaking/VFX (Jurassic Park CGI).

name: Carl Ray Pohlad
notes: Carl Pohlad, Minnesota financier and Minnesota Twins owner from 1984, died 5 January 2009 aged 93 (source: https://www.mprnews.org/story/2009/01/05/pohlad1). The family business continues as Pohlad Companies.

name: Georg ("Heini Jr.") Thyssen-Bornemisza
profile: Georg Heinrich, Baron Thyssen-Bornemisza (b. 1950, Lugano), eldest son of industrialist and art collector Hans Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza. He chaired TBG AG, the family investment arm that bought weather-data firms DTN and MeteoGroup, and founded the NOMIS Foundation. He died in Zürich on 30 September 2022.
notes: Deceased 30 Sep 2022 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_Heinrich_Thyssen-Bornemisza). TBG AG and the NOMIS Foundation continue; the TBG/DTN weather-data angle could interest an energy podcast through other TBG executives.

name: Robert (Bob) Oatley
current_role: Deceased (died 10 January 2016, aged 87); founder of Rosemount Estate winery, former owner of Hamilton Island and yacht Wild Oats XI
notes: Death confirmed via Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Oatley). Family (Oatley Family Holdings / Hamilton Island, Oatley Wines) continues the business.

name: Ramesh Chandra
current_role: Founder of Unitech Group (no current executive role found; Unitech has been under a government-appointed board since 2020)
profile: IIT Kharagpur-trained structural engineer who in 1972 co-founded United Technical Consultants, a Delhi soil-investigation firm that became Unitech, once India's second-largest listed real-estate developer. He moved into civil engineering (including projects in Libya) and then housing, with Forbes putting his fortune at over $11B at its 2007 peak; he was a billionaire through 2011.
interesting_fact: Unitech began in 1972 as a soil-testing consultancy started by five partners before becoming a property giant building in Gurgaon and the Middle East.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Farrukhabad, Uttar Pradesh, the son of a banker, he worked briefly at the Bridge and Roof Company in Kolkata after IIT Kharagpur, then went to the University of Southampton to study structural engineering before co-founding his soil-investigation firm with four friends.
notes: Born c.1939-41; alive status not confirmed (no death reported on Wikipedia). Heavily entangled in legal cases (company and family) since 2011; Unitech under government-appointed management. Low suitability for outreach; no published personal contact found.

name: Lloyd Dorfman
current_role: Founder of Travelex; Chair of the Royal Opera House; Vice President, King's Trust International
profile: Sir Lloyd Dorfman (b. 1952) started Travelex in 1976 as one London bureau de change and built the world's largest non-bank FX retailer, sold to Abu Dhabi owners in 2014. He then chaired co-working pioneer The Office Group (sold to Blackstone, 2017) and co-founded Doddle; today he is a leading arts and youth philanthropist.
interesting_fact: His £10 million gift to the National Theatre's redevelopment led to the Cottesloe being renamed the Dorfman Theatre in 2013; Travelex also pioneered the National's cheap-ticket season.
deep_cut_fact: He never went to university; after a year studying for the Bar at Lincoln's Inn he dropped out, and in 1986 won Travelex the landmark contract to be the first non-bank currency exchange at the newly opened Heathrow Terminal 4. His business motto: 'fire before you aim'.
notes: Writes occasional op-eds (City AM) and gives interviews to the Jewish press; approachable via his philanthropic roles (Royal Opera House, King's Trust International). Avoid Travelex's later 2020 collapse/ransomware topic. No direct published personal or office email found.

name: Ioan Niculae
current_role: Founder/owner, InterAgro group (agribusiness and fertilizers), Romania; owner of FC Astra Giurgiu
profile: Born 1954 in Buturugeni, Giurgiu County, Niculae traded chemical fertilizers in the 1980s, co-founded trader Interaction after 1990 and set up InterAgro in 1995, building one of Romania's largest grain and fertilizer groups (~50,000 ha farmed, large silo capacity). He also profited from stakes in insurer Asirom and the Astra Română refinery. Forbes listed him 2010-2015.
interesting_fact: In Forbes' 2010 list he was the third-richest Romanian, behind Dinu Patriciu and Ion Tiriac; his group farms roughly 50,000 hectares, making him one of Romania's largest grain growers.
deep_cut_fact: He has owned the football club Astra Giurgiu since 1996, and planted about 170 hectares of vineyards whose first harvest came in 2008.
notes: Caution: convicted in 2015 (illegal campaign financing, 2.5 years) and 2021 (InterAgro corruption case, 5 years); acquitted in another case in 2024 per Romanian Wikipedia. Wealth has likely fallen well below $1bn. Poor fit for outreach; no published contacts found.

name: Silvio Scaglia
current_role: Founder, SHS A.M. (quant asset manager, 2020); owner of Freedom Holding / Pacific Global Management (Elite World Group parent)
profile: Swiss-born Italian engineer and telecom entrepreneur who launched Omnitel (Italy's second mobile operator) as CEO in 1995, then founded e.Biscom/Fastweb in 1999, the world's first all-IP fibre-to-the-home operator, selling his 18.7% stake to Swisscom in 2007. He later bought Elite World modelling agencies (2011) and La Perla (2013), and in 2020 founded AI-driven asset manager SHS.
interesting_fact: Fastweb was the first company in the world to build a fully IP-based network and the first public consumer fibre-optic network; e.Biscom's 2000 IPO was the second most successful in Italian history, and Time named him among 2003's 'tech survivors'.
deep_cut_fact: Fresh out of Turin Polytechnic (electronic engineering, cum laude, 1983) his first job was at Aeritalia Spazio, where he worked on the Tethered Satellite project with NASA and Martin Marietta, before stints at Andersen Consulting, McKinsey and Piaggio.
notes: His 'Freedom Holding' (ex-Pacific Global Management) is unrelated to Nasdaq-listed Freedom Holding Corp (Timur Turlov). Ongoing high-profile litigation with ex-wife Julia Haart over Elite World since 2022; avoid. Acquitted in the Fastweb/Telecom Italia Sparkle case (2013, upheld 2017). No published contact found.

name: Mian Mohammad Mansha
current_role: Chairman, MCB Bank Ltd; head of the Nishat Group (Pakistan)
profile: Born in Chiniot, Punjab, and educated at Hendon College in London, Mansha built his family's cotton-ginning business into the Nishat Group. It spans Nishat Mills (textiles), MCB Bank (acquired in 1992 privatisation), cement, insurance, hotels and power generation. In 2010 Forbes listed him as Pakistan's first billionaire.
interesting_fact: Forbes listed him in 2010 as the first Pakistani on its billionaires list. His group also bought two power plants in the late 2000s, adding an energy angle to its textile and banking base.
deep_cut_fact: He went to school at Sacred Heart Convent in Faisalabad before studying at Hendon College, London. In 1979 he built the textile complex at Nishatabad near Faisalabad that became the group's industrial base.
notes: Received the Sitara-e-Imtiaz in 2004 and has sat on the Atlantic Council board. The MCB and Nishat websites blocked automated access, so I could not pull a published IR/press email. MCB's investor-relations page and annual report should list one. The web-search budget ran out before this profile.

name: Patrick Bowlen
profile: Longtime owner of the NFL's Denver Broncos (from 1984), winning three Super Bowls. Died June 13, 2019, aged 75; team later sold to the Walton-Penner group in 2022.
notes: Deceased 13 June 2019 per PBS NewsHour https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/denver-broncos-owner-pat-bowlen-dies-at-age-75

name: Richard Farmer
profile: Richard T. Farmer (Nov 22, 1934 - Aug 4, 2021), founder and long-time CEO/chairman of uniform company Cintas, died in 2021 aged 86.
notes: Deceased (August 2021) per Wikipedia; skipped further research. Legacy: Farmer School of Business at Miami University (Ohio).

name: Alexander Putilov
current_role: Co-owner, Eurasia Drilling Company (EDC), Russia's largest onshore/Caspian drilling contractor
profile: Alexander Putilov (b. 1952, Tyumen) is a Russian oil veteran who ran Urayneftegaz, then served as president of state oil company Rosneft (1993-1998) and later as BP/Amoco's special representative to Sidanko. In 2004 he became co-owner of the drilling company founded by Alexander Djaparidze (ex-LUKOIL Burenie), now Eurasia Drilling, which drills in Russia, the Caspian Sea and Iraq.
interesting_fact: He was appointed president of Rosneft in April 1993, the first years of the then state-owned oil company's post-Soviet existence, and led it until 1998.
deep_cut_fact: A former mechanic: after graduating from the Tyumen Industrial Institute in 1974 he started out as a fitter/repairman in the oil fields, then rose to deputy head of a plant shop and chief mechanic.
notes: Forbes lists him as a Russian citizen living in Moscow, age 74. Wikipedia (single-source stub) calls him Czech. His exact current EDC stake is unclear (reportedly 25-28% at various points). EDC's site eurasiadrilling.com was unreachable from here. No personal public channels. Given Russia sanctions and compliance issues, check before any outreach.

name: Benny Subianto
current_role: Deceased (died 4 January 2017); formerly Commissioner, PT Adaro Energy and founder of PT Persada Capital Investama
profile: Benny Subianto (Soebianto), an ITB-trained mechanical engineer, helped found United Tractors (Astra group), served as its president director, founded Persada Capital Investama in 2003 and was a co-owner and commissioner of coal miner Adaro Energy. He died in January 2017; his daughter Arini Subianto now leads the Persada group.

name: Mehmet Sepil
current_role: Founder and former president of Genel Energy (retired Oct 2015); private investor and former Göztepe SK chairman/owner
profile: Turkish entrepreneur who moved from construction into oil, founding Genel in 2002 and signing the first production-sharing agreement in Iraqi Kurdistan (Taq Taq). He was CEO until Genel merged with Tony Hayward's London-listed Vallares in 2011, then president until retiring in 2015. He later owned İzmir football club Göztepe, selling a 70% stake to Sport Republic in 2022.
interesting_fact: The 2011 Genel-Vallares deal paired his Kurdistan assets with former BP CEO Tony Hayward's cash shell; Sepil called it 'a marriage between the asset and the money', and Hayward insisted on keeping the Turkish name Genel.
deep_cut_fact: He was already working in Iraqi Kurdistan with his own construction company in 2002 when Jalal Talabani, later Iraq's president, suggested he try the oil business, which led to the Taq Taq field.
notes: Appeared only on Forbes 2011; wealth largely from Genel shares (major insider sales ~2015). No longer an executive; low-profile. I found no published personal or office contact; Genel Energy's corporate site (genelenergy.com) could pass on a message. Also chaired Turkey's Club Association (Kulüpler Birliği) c. 2019.

name: Jiang Yu
current_role: Co-owner (with father Jiang Yehua) of Chongqing Huayu Group (重庆华宇集团), real estate; no public executive title found

name: Apichet Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Assistant COO and Acting Chief Resource Management Officer, King Power Group (per The Nation, Dec 2025); Vice-Chairman, Leicester City FC
profile: Apichet Srivaddhanaprabha is a son of the late Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha, who built Thailand's King Power airport duty-free empire, and shares in the family fortune. He holds senior management roles at King Power and has sat on the board of Leicester City FC since the 2010s, becoming vice-chairman when his brother Aiyawatt ('Top') took over as chairman.

deep_cut_fact: The Dec 2025 final, played at VS Sports Club & Siam Polo Park in Samut Prakan, gave Thailand its first-ever SEA Games polo gold; the sport only entered the Games in 2007 (Thai bronze) thanks to the Thailand Polo Association his father set up, and the brothers dedicated the win to him.
notes: Not the same person as brother Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha (King Power CEO, Leicester chairman), who is the family's public face. Apichet is private; no personal social accounts found. kingpower.com contact is a general/customer-service address; Leicester City club contact page is an alternative. Energy/data-centre link is weak.

name: Aroonroong Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Executive at King Power Group (Thailand); listed in 2019 company materials as assistant to the CFO - current title unverified
profile: Daughter of the late King Power founder Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha and part of the family that controls King Power, Thailand's dominant duty-free retailer, and Leicester City FC. She sits on the group's executive team alongside siblings Apichet and Voramas; her brother Aiyawatt is chairman and CEO. Hurun listed her as a billionaire 2019-2021.

name: Voramas Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Senior executive (reported as Group Vice Chairman / Chief Marketing Officer) at King Power International, Thailand
profile: Voramas Srivaddhanaprabha is the eldest daughter of the late King Power founder Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha and sister of chairman/CEO Aiyawatt. The family's wealth comes from King Power, Thailand's dominant airport duty-free retailer, plus holdings including Leicester City FC and OH Leuven. She sits on King Power's executive team overseeing commercial and marketing functions.
interesting_fact: She is reported as a minority shareholder of English football club Leicester City (about 10%), the club her father bought in 2010 and which won the 2015-16 Premier League as 5000-1 outsiders.
notes: Very private; no interviews or personal channels found. Exact current title varies across aggregator profiles. Retail (duty-free) wealth, not energy: weak fit for the podcast's energy focus. Route via King Power corporate contact.

name: Zeki Zorlu
current_role: Honorary Chair (board of management), Zorlu Holding; chairs various group textile, energy and property companies
profile: Born 1939 in Babadağ, Denizli, Zeki Zorlu co-founded Turkish conglomerate Zorlu Holding with his younger brother Ahmet Nazif Zorlu, growing a family weaving trade into a group spanning textiles, Vestel electronics, Zorlu Energy (geothermal, wind, hydro, gas) and property such as Zorlu Center. He founded Korteks in Bursa in 1976, the group's first manufacturing company.
interesting_fact: He and his brother were 'masterful weavers' by primary-school age, working the family's household loom in Babadağ that their parents ran day and night; their father's Yükselen company (1953) is the root of today's Zorlu Holding.
deep_cut_fact: Before manufacturing, he took the family weaving trade into commerce by running the first Zorlu store, opened in Trabzon on the Black Sea; HQ moved to Istanbul in 1970 and he launched Korteks yarn in Bursa in 1976.
notes: Aged ~87 and largely retired from day-to-day roles. His brother and co-founder Ahmet Nazif Zorlu reportedly died on 2 Nov 2026 - be sensitive with timing of outreach. Next generation (e.g. Olgun Zorlu) more active publicly. Energy angle: Zorlu Enerji is a major Turkish geothermal/renewables producer.

name: Alicia Fentener Van Vlissingen
current_role: Heir / family shareholder in SHV Holdings (Fentener van Vlissingen family); no public executive role found
profile: Member of the Dutch Fentener van Vlissingen family that owns SHV Holdings, one of the world's largest private trading groups (energy distribution/LPG, industrial services). Reported as a daughter of former SHV chairman and conservationist Paul Fentener van Vlissingen (d. 2006); Hurun listed her at ~$1B (2014-2020). No public biography, business role or interviews found.
interesting_fact: Her family's Letterewe estate on Loch Maree in north-west Scotland, bought in 1978, was the subject of the 1990s 'Letterewe Accord', a pioneering public-access agreement that predated Scotland's 2003 land reform.
notes: Extremely private heiress; only a passing Wikipedia mention (uncited) links her as Paul Fentener van Vlissingen's daughter. Not an operator - no podcast angle beyond SHV's energy business. Better SHV-family interlocutor would be Annemiek Fentener van Vlissingen (SHV supervisory board chair). Identity marked uncertain due to thin sourcing.

name: Mahdi Al-Tajir
current_role: Owner, Highland Spring Group (Scottish bottled water); private investor in finance and property
profile: Mohammed Mahdi Al Tajir, born in Bahrain around 1932-33 and educated at Preston Grammar School, was a key adviser to Dubai's ruler and the first UAE ambassador to the UK (1971-1987). He made his fortune in Dubai's development era, and owns Highland Spring, the Blackford and Keir estates in Scotland, London's Sheraton Park Tower hotel and Mereworth Castle in Kent.
interesting_fact: He was the UAE's first ambassador to the UK, serving 16 years from the federation's founding in 1971, and was a thinly disguised character in Robin Moore's 1976 novel 'Dubai'.
deep_cut_fact: A serious silver collector, he paid a then-record auction price for silver in 1993: GBP2.27m at Christie's Monaco for a 1736 silver chandelier by Balthasar Friedrich Behrens.
notes: Now about 93; very private and avoids media. Still on Hurun Global 2026, but no confirmation he is alive. Wikipedia also covers old Dubai Aluminium court cases; avoid those. Highland Spring press office is the only published route. Unlikely guest.

name: Mahmud Kamani
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Vice Chair, Debenhams Group plc (formerly boohoo group)
profile: Manchester entrepreneur who co-founded online fashion retailer boohoo with Carol Kane in 2006 and floated it in 2014. The group grew to include PrettyLittleThing, Nasty Gal, Debenhams, Dorothy Perkins and Burton, and is now renamed Debenhams Group. In February 2026 he became executive vice chair and invested £8M in a £40M raise.
interesting_fact: His father Abdullah, a Gujarati-heritage Kenyan who moved to north-west England in the 1960s, started out selling handbags on a market stall. He then built a textile business supplying New Look and Primark, which became the springboard for boohoo.
deep_cut_fact: He supports Kibera Kids, a Nairobi-based non-profit, a link back to his family's years in Kenya. He was Entrepreneur of the Year at the 2013 English Asian Business Awards.
notes: The group is in a turnaround and there is ongoing shareholder pressure from Frasers Group, so outreach is best kept to his entrepreneurial story. Go through the in-house press office or its agencies (Threesixty, Sodali). Little energy/data-center relevance.

name: Peter Harris
current_role: Founder of Bourne Leisure (Haven, Warner); his family trust owns Butlin's (bought back in 2022)
profile: British former accountant (b. 1934) who co-founded Bourne Leisure in 1964 with David Allen. It grew into the UK's largest holiday-park group (Haven, Butlin's, Warner Leisure Hotels). In 2021 he sold the majority to Blackstone in a deal valuing the business at about £3bn, keeping a minority stake. In 2022 the Harris Family Trust bought Butlin's back for about £300m.
interesting_fact: He and his partners built and sold the business twice: they floated Leisure Caravan Parks in 1972 and sold it to Rank for £20m in 1975, started again, then bought Rank's holiday arm, including Butlin's and Haven, for £700m in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: He found his way into holiday parks while working as an accountant, after auditing a caravan park; in 1964 he bought the Alberta caravan park in Whitstable, Kent. From 1977 he bought land at Tring, Hertfordshire, where racehorses were trained until 2004. He was inducted into the British Travel & Hospitality Hall of Fame in 2013.
notes: Aged about 92; Wikipedia lists no death, but recent status was not independently verified. Extremely private. Butlin's, owned by his family trust, is the most direct organisational route.

name: Rishi Shah
current_role: None — former co-founder, chairman & CEO of Outcome Health (resigned 2018); sentenced in June 2024 to 7.5 years in prison for fraud
profile: Oak Brook, Illinois-born (1986) Northwestern dropout who co-founded ContextMedia (later Outcome Health) in 2006 to put health-education screens in doctors' waiting rooms; it hit a $5.6bn valuation in 2017. After a WSJ investigation he resigned, and in 2023 he was convicted of mail, wire and bank fraud and money laundering.
interesting_fact: Outcome Health's May 2017 round of 500m+ dollars led by Goldman Sachs, CapitalG and Pritzker Group valued it at $5.6bn, then the largest single round since Groupon's in 2011.
notes: NOT SUITABLE for outreach: convicted in April 2023 of fraud tied to a ~$1bn scheme and sentenced June 2024 to 7.5 years (Wikipedia). Rich-list wealth figure is stale.

name: Robert Tsao Hsing-Cheng
current_role: Founder and former chairman of United Microelectronics Corp (UMC); civil-defence philanthropist and activist in Taiwan
profile: Born in Beijing in 1947 and raised in Taiwan, Tsao studied electrical engineering at NTU, worked at ITRI, and in 1980 founded UMC, Taiwan's first private chipmaker. He held Singapore citizenship 2011-2022 (hence the Singapore listing), then regained Taiwanese citizenship in 2022 and pledged NT$3B toward Taiwan's civil defence; he advised President Lai's Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee (2024-25).
interesting_fact: After the 2019 Yuen Long attack in Hong Kong, Tsao vowed never to return to China, Hong Kong or Macau, and in 2022 pledged funds to train civilians and build a million combat drones for Taiwan's defence.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious art collector who started in the 1990s with jadeite before moving on to archaic Chinese bronzes, and he recorded an oral history on the founding of UMC for the Computer History Museum.
notes: Outspoken and media-accessible (interviews with FT, RFA, Globe and Mail), so a podcast fit on semiconductors/geopolitics. No verified published contact found in budget; UMC press office (umc.com) is not his personal channel. Jadeite/bronze detail sourced via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Tsao (Christie's interview).

name: Salman Al-Hokair
current_role: Co-owner of the Alhokair family retail group (Fawaz Abdulaziz Alhokair & Co., later Cenomi Retail / AFG retail); current title not verified
profile: Listed by Hurun (2018-2021) with wealth from Fawaz Abdulaziz Alhokair & Co., the Riyadh retail franchise group founded in 1989 by the Alhokair brothers from two menswear stores. It became Saudi Arabia's largest fashion franchisee (Zara, Gap, etc.) and is linked to mall developer Cenomi. His current personal role was not verified.

profile: Listed by Hurun (2014-2020) as a member of the Dutch Fentener van Vlissingen family, whose wealth comes from privately held SHV Holdings in Utrecht (energy distribution via SHV Energy/LPG, plus industrial and other businesses). No public biography or interviews for her could be found.
