name: Yan Junbo
current_role: Chairman, Sichuan Haoji Group (濠吉集团), per Chinese Wikipedia (last updated 2020)
profile: Yan Junbo (严俊波, b. 1958, Nanchong, Sichuan) founded Haoji (豪吉), a leading Chinese chicken-bouillon brand. In 2001 his group sold a stake in Haoji Foods to Nestlé while keeping a minority, then diversified into property, education and restaurants under the renamed Haoji Group. He served as a Sichuan deputy to the 11th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: His Haoji chicken-essence brand was attractive enough that Nestlé bought into Haoji Foods in 2001, with Yan's group retaining a minority stake.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he moved into instant noodles with a non-fried, mixed-grain product, '玖玖爱六粮面' (Jiujiu'ai six-grain noodles).
notes: Hurun 'Haoji' = 豪吉 chicken bouillon, not 好记星. Very low international profile; no current (post-2020) information or published contacts found. Web search budget was exhausted, so alive status not confirmed.

name: Pratap Reddy
current_role: Founder and executive chairman, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd (Chennai)
profile: Born 1933 in Aragonda (now Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh), Dr Prathap C. Reddy trained as a cardiologist in the UK and US before returning to India. In 1983 he founded Apollo Hospitals in Chennai, India's first corporate hospital chain, which grew into one of Asia's largest integrated healthcare groups. In his 90s he remains chairman, with his four daughters in senior roles.
interesting_fact: Apollo's first hospital in Chennai (1983) was inaugurated by then-President Zail Singh. Reddy received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian honour, in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: After Stanley Medical College he did a fellowship at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston and then ran research programmes at the Missouri State Chest Hospital before returning to India.

name: Deepak Chimanlal Mehta
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Deepak Nitrite Ltd (Vadodara, India)
profile: Son of Deepak Nitrite founder Chimanlal Khimchand Mehta, a Gujarat chemical trader who incorporated the company in 1970. Deepak Mehta has built it from a sodium nitrite maker into a diversified chemicals group, notably via subsidiary Deepak Phenolics, which makes phenol and acetone at Dahej, Gujarat; his son Maulik Mehta is CEO.
interesting_fact: Deepak Nitrite's 1971 IPO was oversubscribed 20 times, and its first sodium nitrite/nitrate plant at Nadesari, Vadodara started production in 1972.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 he took the company into large-scale petrochemical intermediates by promoting Deepak Phenolics, building a phenol and acetone plant at Dahej, Gujarat that also makes pharmaceutical-grade isopropyl alcohol.
notes: Company site was unreachable (503) during research, so no IR/press email verified; Deepak Nitrite's stock-exchange filings list the company secretary/investor contact. Web-search budget ran out before a more personal deep-cut could be found.

name: Kunal Shah
current_role: Head of WhatsApp, Meta (since June 2026); founder of CRED (stepped down as CEO)
profile: Kunal Shah (b. 1979, Mumbai) co-founded recharge/payments app FreeCharge in 2010, sold it to Snapdeal in 2015 for roughly US$400m, then founded members-only credit-card rewards platform CRED and became one of India's most prolific angel investors (200+ deals). In June 2026 Meta named him head of WhatsApp, succeeding Will Cathcart, while investing $900m in CRED for ~20%.
interesting_fact: Mark Zuckerberg hired him to run WhatsApp, the world's biggest messaging app, saying he 'built CRED into one of India's most important technology companies'; Meta simultaneously took a ~20% stake in CRED for $900m.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Wilson College, Mumbai, worked from his teens, and dropped out of a part-time MBA at NMIMS in 2004; FreeCharge grew out of a pivot of his earlier cashback start-up PaisaBack (2009). ET named him 'Comeback Kid of the Year' in 2016.
notes: Very active on X (@kunalb11) where he posts frequently on consumer behaviour and India; now a senior Meta executive so interview requests likely go via Meta/WhatsApp comms. X handle is widely known but source here is the account itself.

name: Chen Kangping
current_role: Co-founder, JinkoSolar; resigned as vice chairman and director of Jinko Solar Co., Ltd. (SSE: 688223) in July 2026 - no new role announced
profile: Born 1973, Chen co-founded JinkoSolar, one of the world's largest solar-module makers, serving as CEO of NYSE-listed JinkoSolar Holding from 2008 to 2020 and then general manager of the Shanghai-listed operating company. He moved to vice chairman in a March 2026 reshuffle and resigned all Jinko posts for personal reasons in July 2026.
interesting_fact: He stepped down as general manager in March 2026 to focus on strategy as vice chairman, then left Jinko entirely in July 2026, ending nearly two decades leading the solar giant he co-founded.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he was CFO of Zhejiang Supor, the cookware and small-appliance maker, from 2003 to 2006.
notes: Left Jinko in July 2026, so the company IR route is indirect at best; no personal channels found. 2026 resignation timeline from PV Tech / Deep News reports.

name: Nikhil V Merchant
current_role: Managing Director, Swan Corp Limited (formerly Swan Energy Ltd; BSE 503310 / NSE SWANCORP)
profile: Mumbai industrialist who took over century-old textile firm Swan Mills in the early 1990s and turned it into a conglomerate spanning textiles, real estate, LNG and shipbuilding. Swan Energy won NCLT approval to acquire Anil Ambani's Reliance Naval and Engineering, relaunched as Swan Defence and Heavy Industries (Pipavav Shipyard); the parent was renamed Swan Corp.
interesting_fact: After the takeover, Pipavav (described by the company as India's largest shipyard) won India's first-ever chemical tanker order: six 18,000 DWT vessels for Norwegian owner Rederiet Stenersen.
deep_cut_fact: His Swan LNG unit built an FSRU-based LNG terminal at Jafrabad, Gujarat, and took delivery of the first Indian-flagged Floating Storage and Regasification Unit, built by Hyundai Heavy Industries. Swan's realty arm also built Hyderabad's Technova Business Park, leased to Google.
notes: Corporate office emails (Swan Corp / SDHI) are general enquiry addresses; Swan's site also has a Media Centre. Strong energy angle: Jafrabad LNG terminal/FSRU. Company was renamed from Swan Energy to Swan Corp.

name: Ghanshyam Sarda
current_role: Listed shareholder (~1.8%) of Sarda Energy & Minerals Ltd (NSE: SARDAEN); no executive or board role found
profile: A 'Ghanshyam Sarda' appears in Sarda Energy & Minerals' shareholder register with ~1.82% of the Raipur-based steel, ferro-alloy, coal and hydro/thermal power company. The company is run by promoter-chairman Kamal Kishore Sarda and MD Pankaj Sarda; Ghanshyam Sarda's own role and relationship could not be confirmed.

Hurun's $1bn SEML-linked fortune more plausibly belongs to the K.K. Sarda promoter family; verify against Hurun's entry before outreach. Kept minimal per instructions.

name: Qu Xiaohua (Shawn Qu)
current_role: Founder, Executive Chairman and Chief Technology Officer, Canadian Solar Inc. (NASDAQ: CSIQ) — handed CEO role to Colin Parkin in May 2026
profile: Tsinghua physics graduate with a U of Toronto PhD who founded Canadian Solar in Ontario in 2001 and listed it on NASDAQ in 2006. It has shipped ~177 GW of PV modules and, via e-STORAGE, 20+ GWh of battery storage, while Recurrent Energy develops utility-scale solar and storage. In May 2026 he moved from CEO to Executive Chairman and CTO to focus on the technology roadmap and US manufacturing.
interesting_fact: Canadian Solar's storage arm e-STORAGE had shipped 20+ GWh of battery systems by March 2026 with a $3.5bn contracted backlog; Qu says the company is shifting 'from volume-driven expansion to value-driven leadership'.
deep_cut_fact: His 1995 U of Toronto PhD (supervised by Prof. Harry Ruda) focused on semiconductor super-lattices and optical effects; he then worked as a research scientist on Ontario Hydro's solar commercialization team before founding Canadian Solar. U of T Engineering gave him a Hall of Distinction award in 2019.
notes: Wealth shared with Zhang Hanbing (Canadian Solar co-founder/shareholder). Strong podcast fit (solar + storage + US manufacturing). Speaks publicly at investor forums; IR route is the published channel.

name: Zhang Hanbing
current_role: Shareholder of Canadian Solar (CSIQ) / CSI Solar (688472.SH) alongside husband Dr. Shawn Qu (founder, chairman & CEO); no current executive title found
profile: Hanbing Zhang is the wife of Shawn Qu, who founded Canadian Solar in Ontario in 2001; Hurun lists the couple's fortune jointly. Canadian Solar's 20-F filings show she was an early employee who received options at the 2006 IPO, and SEC 13D filings show her holding shares as part of Qu's group. name: Fred Mannix
current_role: Chairman/owner, The Mancal Group (Mancal Corporation), Calgary
profile: Frederick Philip Mannix (b. 1942, Calgary), OC, AOE, is the third-generation heir of the Mannix construction and coal dynasty (Loram, Manalta Coal). After the family businesses were split with brother Ron (Coril Holdings), he built the private Mancal Group, active in oil and gas (Mancal Energy), coal, real estate, private capital and ranching; Steve Letwin is CEO.

deep_cut_fact: Troubled by inaccurate media coverage of the 1990s Balkans conflict, he created a 10-day military journalism course at the University of Calgary and Universite de Montreal, saying 'good reporting and strong democracy depend on an informed public.' He also completed National Defence College Course 32 as a civilian in 1979.
notes: Input lists 'Fred and Ron Mannix' jointly; this profile is Fred P. Mannix (Mancal). Brother Ron runs separate Coril Holdings. Very private family. Strong interest in military history, defence/foreign affairs (founder of Canadian Defence and Foreign Affairs Institute) and journalism, a good hook for a journalist. Not to be confused with son Fred Mannix Jr., the polo player.

name: Massimo Moratti
current_role: Former CEO of Saras (sold to Vitol in 2024) and former president/owner of FC Internazionale; private investor
profile: Massimo Moratti (born 16 May 1945, Milan) was a long-time executive and shareholder of Saras, the Sardinian oil refiner his father Angelo founded in 1962. He owned and presided over Inter Milan (1995-2013), winning the 2010 treble. The family sold its remaining 35% of Saras to Vitol in 2024, and he still gives interviews on Inter and Milan life.

notes: Name in input is misspelled 'Moratty'. Saras is now owned by Vitol, so no corporate route remains, and I found no published personal or family-office contact. He is open to press interviews (Italian sports/business outlets); Inter's media office has published his interviews (inter.it). He was hospitalised briefly in 2025; avoid mentioning health.

current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, Pony AI Inc. (Nasdaq: PONY; also Hong Kong-listed)

name: Vinod Kumar Agarwal
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Agarwal Coal Corporation Pvt. Ltd. (Indore); Chairman, Emerald Developers

profile: Yu Faxin (郁发新), a Zhejiang University aerospace-electronics professor since 2006, turned chip entrepreneur. name: G Ravindra Rao (G. Ravender Rao)

name: Namit Malhotra
current_role: CEO of DNEG; founder and non-executive chairman of Prime Focus Ltd; film producer (Ramayana)
profile: Namit Malhotra (b. 1976, Mumbai), from a film family, started an editing studio in 1995 that became Prime Focus (listed 2006). He expanded globally, pioneered 3D conversion and in 2014 merged Prime Focus World with London's Double Negative to form DNEG, the multi-Oscar-winning VFX studio behind Interstellar, Tenet and Dune. He also produces films, including the big-budget 'Ramayana' (2026).
interesting_fact: DNEG, which he leads, has won Academy Awards for Best Visual Effects for films including Inception, Interstellar, Ex Machina, Blade Runner 2049, First Man, Tenet, Dune and Dune: Part Two.

notes: High-profile in Indian and Hollywood media; currently promoting Ramayana. DNEG PR is the best route. Data-center angle: VFX rendering is compute-heavy (DNEG runs large render farms).

name: Jony Ive

Fit is AI hardware/design rather than energy. Fun aside: LoveFrom's bear mascot 'Montgomery' is named after Montgomery Street, SF.

Moore Threads IPO'd in Shanghai in Dec 2025 raising ~$1.1B, makes AI-training/data-center GPUs (MTT S4000/S5000, KUAE clusters) and in Aug 2026 announced plans for a Hong Kong H-share listing.

Profile follows Forbes. Strong AI/data-center GPU angle.

name: Lim Chai Hock
current_role: Director & Chief Operating Officer, PT Bayan Resources Tbk (Indonesia)
profile: Malaysian cofounder of the Bayan Group, one of Indonesia's largest coal producers, controlled by billionaire Low Tuck Kwong. He has been a director of PT Gunungbayan Pratamacoal since 1998 and of PT Bayan Resources Tbk since 2006, where he serves as COO; his shareholding in Bayan is the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: Before coal, Lim spent 1983-1998 at Low Tuck Kwong's coal-mining infrastructure firm PT Jaya Sumpiles Indonesia, rising to regional manager, then cofounded Bayan with him. He also sits on the board of PT Kariangau Power, Bayan's power-plant unit, since 2010.
deep_cut_fact: His formal training is in land surveying: after his 1977 Malaysian Certificate of Education he earned a Certificate in Land Surveying in 1981 from Lembaga Jabatan Ukur, Peninsular Malaysia - a surveyor who became a coal billionaire.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Bayan's corporate secretary. Note Bayan warns of imposters using its name - verify any replies come from bayan.com.sg.

name: Takanori Nakamura
current_role: Founder, Representative Director & President, RAKUS Co., Ltd. (TSE Prime: 3923), Tokyo
profile: Born 1973, Kobe University graduate and ex-NTT employee who founded IT Boost (now RAKUS) in November 2000. RAKUS grew into a leading Japanese SaaS company for SMB back-office work, best known for the Rakuraku Seisan expense-management cloud and email-marketing tools; Nakamura remains president and its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: RAKUS's cloud products (the 'Rakuraku' series such as Rakuraku Seisan and Rakuraku Meisai) made it one of the fastest-growing listed SaaS companies in Japan, and Nakamura now argues small SaaS players will struggle as the market consolidates.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, Infocast, was founded in January 2000 and sold to Rakuten within the year; he founded IT Boost (now RAKUS) that November. He has named Jim Collins' 'Great by Choice' (Visionary Company 4 in Japan) as his most memorable book.
notes: Media inquiry form exists on rakus.co.jp (contact/media). Interviews mostly in Japanese business press (Toyo Keizai, President, ITmedia).

name: Liu Ming Hui
current_role: Chairman (and cofounder), China Gas Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 384)
profile: Hong Kong-based cofounder and chairman of China Gas Holdings, one of China's largest private piped natural gas distributors, which supplies gas to cities and industrial parks across mainland China and has expanded into LPG and value-added services. Forbes lists him at about $1B (2026).
interesting_fact: Liu's brother Liu Mingxing and daughter Liu Chang also sit on China Gas Holdings' board, making it a family-led utility platform.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond his science degree from Hebei Normal University, Liu holds both a master's and a doctorate from Renmin University of China.
notes: Web search budget ran out mid-lane; company site is a JS app, so no published IR/press email was verified. China Gas IR contact should be in its HKEX annual report. Age 63 per Forbes (2026).

name: Wang Qiang
current_role: Chairman & President and actual controller, Shenzhen Leading Semiconductor Industry Co. (深圳市领先半导体科技产业, 'Zhizheng', 603991.SH)
profile: Wang Qiang (王强) is a Shenzhen investor who controls Shanghai-listed Zhizheng (至正股份, now Shenzhen Leading Semiconductor) through Shenzhen Zhengxin Tongchuang and affiliates. In 2025 it completed a restructuring that brought in AAMI, ASMPT's former semiconductor lead-frame business, and spun off its legacy cable-polymer (plastics) unit. deep_cut_fact: Beyond chips, Wang's holdings include Shenzhen Tourism (Group) Co. (深圳市旅游(集团)股份有限公司), where he sits on the board, plus the Shenzhen tourist-taxi company and the Qiaoshe industrial company, per the listed company's 2025 related-party disclosures.
notes: Hurun 2026: 王强 / 领先 / Leading Semiconductor, Shenzhen, industry listed as 'plastic products' (the legacy cable-materials business). A very common name, but the filing and Hurun company match. The 2025 annual report gives no personal bio (age/education). He was also acting board secretary from Mar 2026. Board office phone 0755-29618132 (company line, in the annual report).

name: Mark Armenante
current_role: Private investor; early backer and former director of Veeva Systems (2007-2015); co-founder/board member of Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce 2020) per aggregator listings
profile: A veteran of enterprise sales in pharma software, Armenante worked at Information Resources Inc. and Oracle, ran PharmaSystems, and spent over ten years as a Siebel Systems group VP. In 2007 he became one of Veeva's first outside backers and directors. He held about 13% of Veeva before its 2013 IPO, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: Veeva's 2013 S-1 shows he owned 14.8 million shares (13.2%) before the IPO, nearly as many as CEO Peter Gassner's 15.2 million. That made him one of the company's largest individual holders.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Veeva, he was President of PharmaSystems, Inc., a pharmaceutical sales-force management company, from 1991 to 1994. That is essentially the market Veeva later dominated. He also holds a biology degree from Case Western Reserve University.
notes: He was about 74 in 2026 (61 at the S-1 in 2013), and I found no recent public activity or confirmation that he is alive. He has no public social or website presence, and some aggregator claims (e.g., 'founder' of Veeva) are imprecise. He was a Series A investor and director rather than an operating co-founder.

name: Ray Irani
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Occidental Petroleum (1990-2011); reported as chairman/CEO of private investment firm Ray Investment, LLC
profile: Lebanese-born chemist (b. 1935) who worked at Monsanto and was president/COO of Olin before Armand Hammer brought him to Occidental in 1983; Hammer named him heir in 1990 and he led Oxy for two decades, growing it into a major US oil producer. He stepped down as CEO in 2011 and as chairman in 2013 and has since kept a low profile.
interesting_fact: Armand Hammer, then 91, picked Irani as his successor at Occidental in February 1990; by 1988 Irani's team was already running day-to-day operations for the nonagenarian founder.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a chemistry BS from the American University of Beirut in 1953, moved to Los Angeles at 18 and had a USC physical-chemistry PhD by 1957; USC named its life sciences building Ray R. Irani Hall in 2007, and he was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2012 for work on particulate systems.
notes: Aged ~91; no death reported in searches as of Nov 2026 (Wikipedia lists him as living) - verify before outreach. No published personal or office contact found. Possible routes: AUB trustees emeriti page (https://www.aub.edu.lb/AboutUs/bot/emeriti/Pages/irani.aspx) or USC. Avoid executive-pay and tax-shelter controversies.

name: Cao Jianwei
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical (SZSE: 300316); co-actual controller with founder Qiu Minxiu
profile: Cao Jianwei (曹建伟, b. 1978), an engineering PhD, has run Jingsheng since its early years (GM from 2010, chairman since 2016). Founded in 2006 by Zhejiang University professor Qiu Minxiu, it makes crystal-growth furnaces for solar and semiconductor silicon plus sapphire and SiC substrates; listed in Shenzhen in 2012.
interesting_fact: Jingsheng's founder, his co-controller Qiu Minxiu, was a Zhejiang University professor who retired at 60 to start the company and rang the bell for its ChiNext IPO at 67.
deep_cut_fact: A researcher in hydraulic transmission and electromechanical control, he has won two first-class Zhejiang Provincial Science & Technology awards, and was named one of Shaoxing's Top Ten Outstanding Young People and a recipient of the Chinese Red Cross Humanitarian Service Medal.
notes: Engineer-chairman; few English-language interviews. Data-center/AI angle via semiconductor equipment and SiC substrates (power electronics). Route via company securities office.

name: Kiki Barki
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, PT Harum Energy Tbk (IDX: HRUM); owner of private coal miner Tanito Harum
profile: Indonesian coal pioneer Kiki Barki (Ji Qihui) founded Tanito Harum in 1988 and Harum Energy in 1995, listing Harum in 2010. His sons now run Harum, which has diversified from Kalimantan thermal coal into nickel, including a stake in ASX-listed Nickel Industries with nickel pig-iron plants in Indonesia.
interesting_fact: Then-mining minister Ginandjar Kartasasmita recalled that Barki spoke Mandarin better than Indonesian, having lived and studied in China for more than 10 years before returning to set up Tanito Harum, one of the few Indonesian-owned coal miners of the late 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Bandung in 1939 to a Hokchia (Fujian) family, he finished secondary school in Beijing and trained at a mining academy there; before coal he helped run his father's textile, hotel and banking businesses, and in 1993 his interests backed PT Vietmindo Energitama, a coal mine in northern Vietnam.
notes: Aged ~87; alive status based on Forbes' 2026 profile wording, not independently confirmed (web-search budget ran out). Very private; day-to-day leadership is with his sons at Harum. harumenergy.com is behind bot protection, so its IR/corporate secretary contact could not be extracted - check its Investor Relations page manually.

name: Wu Ying
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~49.6%) of Yangling Metron New Material (300.861.SZ); retired as chairman Nov 2024
profile: Wu Ying founded and chaired Yangling Metron New Material, a Shaanxi-based maker of electroplated diamond wire used to slice silicon wafers for the solar industry (clients include LONGi, Jinko, GCL). Listed on ChiNext in 2020. He stepped down as chairman in Nov 2024 on reaching retirement age, but remains controlling shareholder and actual controller.
interesting_fact: Metron's diamond wire - diamond micro-powder fixed on high-strength metal wire - is a key consumable for cutting solar-grade silicon wafers, tying his fortune directly to the PV boom.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career he was director of the computer lab at the China Academy of Machinery Science and Technology Group.
notes: Resigned all company posts 18 Nov 2024 (retirement); Liu Haiying is now chairman. Company board-secretary office is the only published route. Resignation notice: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202411181640941995_1.pdf

name: Cho Hyun-sang
current_role: Vice Chairman & CEO, HS Hyosung (holding company spun off from Hyosung in July 2024)
profile: Youngest son of late Hyosung chairman Cho Suck-rae. Brown economics grad who started at Bain & Co. and joined Hyosung in 2000; after the 2024 split he leads HS Hyosung (advanced materials incl. tire cord, carbon fiber; pushing into AI, batteries and chip materials) while brother Cho Hyun-joon runs Hyosung.
interesting_fact: He chaired the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) for 2025, presenting its report to APEC leaders at the Gyeongju summit; AI cooperation was a core agenda item.
deep_cut_fact: Between Bain and his Hyosung career he worked at Japan's NTT Communications, leading wired/wireless strategy projects and helping set up its Korean branch.
notes: Romanized also as Jo Hyun-sang / Hyun Sang Cho. In Dec 2025 HS Hyosung named Kim Kyoo-young as first non-family chairman; Cho remains vice chairman. Best route: HS Hyosung corporate communications.

name: André Street
current_role: Co-founder of StoneCo (left board April 2024); angel/'late co-founder' investor in ~20 startups
profile: Brazilian fintech entrepreneur who sold his first payments company, Braspag, then co-founded StoneCo in 2012 with Eduardo Pontes; Stone broke the Cielo-Rede card-machine duopoly and IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2018. He left Stone's board in 2024 and now runs a personal VC operation (portfolio NAV ~US$200m) from the LTS (Lemann/Telles/Sicupira) office.
interesting_fact: Brazil Journal (Nov 2026) calls him probably Brazil's largest individual VC: ~40 startups backed incl. Brex, Cora, On Running and QI Tech; his Brex bet returned ~100x after he met its founders as teenagers when Stone bought Pagar.me.
deep_cut_fact: He says he personally took part in recruiting Stone's first 1,000 employees and for some years interviewed ~900 candidates a year; today he keeps mornings for sport and family and meets founders only 2pm-7pm.
notes: No longer at StoneCo management/board, so the Stone IR address is a weak route. His VC work runs out of the LTS family office in São Paulo; a warm intro via portfolio founders (e.g. QI Tech) is likely the best route. Some profiles also tie him to Teya (Europe), founded by Eduardo Pontes.

name: Andrew Paradise
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, FIRY Inc. (NYSE: FIRY; rebranded from Skillz Inc. in 2026)
profile: Paradise cofounded Skillz with Casey Chafkin in 2012 (originally as Lookout Gaming), creating real-money skill-based mobile gaming; it went public via SPAC in Dec 2020. In 2026 Skillz was rebranded FIRY, a Las Vegas-based holding company spanning Skillz, AI ad-tech platform RZR (Aarki) and developer backend Beamable. He earlier sold mobile-checkout startup AisleBuyer to Intuit in 2012.
interesting_fact: Skillz employees were required to play at least 35 games per week on the platform. FIRY says Paradise personally holds more than 90 issued patents covering matchmaking, fraud detection and real-time competition systems.
deep_cut_fact: He has said he learned to program at age 7 by editing a video game's configuration file with a hex editor, later writing his first game in Pascal; before startups he worked in private equity at Boston-area buyout firm The Watermill Group.
notes: Company renamed from Skillz to FIRY in 2026; HQ Las Vegas. FIRY blog has an 'Andrew Paradise' category with his letters/shareholder addresses (good prep material). Holds ~86% voting power via dual-class shares.

name: Mark Miller
current_role: President and Chief Operating Officer, Constellation Software (CSI); director, CSI board; executive chairman of Volaris Group
profile: Canadian software executive who co-founded transit-software firm Trapeze Group in 1988; it became Constellation Software's first acquisition in 1995. He built Volaris Group, a CSI operating group that has bought 200+ vertical-market software companies, and now serves as CSI President/COO and board member. Owns ~1% of CSI plus Topicus and Lumine shares.
interesting_fact: Trapeze, the transit-planning software company he co-founded, was the very first company Constellation Software ever acquired (1995); its name came from the tagline 'Transit Planning Made Easy'.
deep_cut_fact: Studied math and statistics at McMaster; spent summers coding on mainframes at the Canada Centre for Inland Waters (Great Lakes water research). He and co-founder Ian Keaveny taught themselves C from the Kernighan & Ritchie book to build Trapeze; first sale was in St. John's, Newfoundland, where he coded on site.
notes: Input SEC insider data (UHS CEO / Premier director) belongs to a different person (Marc D. Miller of Universal Health Services) - ignore. CSI management page lists Miller as President and COO; corporate email info@csisoftware.com is generic.

name: Michelle Xia
current_role: Co-founder, Chairwoman, President and CEO, Akeso Inc. (HKEX: 9926)
profile: Biochemist (Sun Yat-sen University) who spent ~12 years in U.S. research and biotech (University of Louisville, Bayer, Crown Bioscience) before returning to China in 2008 and co-founding Akeso in 2012. Akeso's PD-1/VEGF bispecific ivonescimab, licensed to Summit Therapeutics in 2022, beat Merck's Keytruda in a 2024 Phase 3 trial.
interesting_fact: Akeso's ivonescimab outperformed Merck's blockbuster Keytruda in a head-to-head Phase 3 lung cancer trial in 2024; Summit Therapeutics paid $500M upfront (up to $5B in milestones) for rights in the U.S., Europe and Japan.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech she earned postgraduate degrees at Newcastle and Glasgow universities in the UK, then moved to the U.S. in 1996 to do cancer immunotherapy research at the University of Louisville. Akeso is named after the Greek goddess of healing.
notes: Company site only; no published press/IR email found on akesobio.com. Akeso press releases go out via PR Newswire. She also sits on Summit Therapeutics' board (smmttx.com).

name: Bancha Ongkosit
current_role: Founder and Chairman, KCE Electronics PCL (Thailand)
profile: Former advertising executive who founded KCE Electronics (originally Kuang Charoen Electronics, named after his father) in 1982; it is now Southeast Asia's largest printed-circuit-board maker and a top global PCB supplier to the auto industry. The firm rebuilt after the 1997 crisis; his Cornell-educated son Pitharn has been CEO since 2013.
interesting_fact: KCE is described as the largest PCB manufacturer in Southeast Asia and among the top five global PCB suppliers for the automotive industry; Bancha became a billionaire in 2021 as auto-electronics demand surged.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in advertising and launched KCE in 1982 with just 12 million baht of capital.
notes: Low public profile; son Pitharn Ongkosit (CEO) is the public face of KCE. Best route is company IR. Chairman title per MarketScreener listing; deep-cut figures from Forbes 2021 coverage (forbes.it page blocked to direct fetch, verify before use).

name: Zuo Zongshen
current_role: Founder & chairman, Zongshen Industrial Group; chairman, Chongqing Zongshen Power Machinery (SZSE: 001696), re-elected Sept 2025
profile: Chongqing-born entrepreneur (b. 1952) who turned a 1982 motorcycle repair shed known as 'Master Zuo' into Zongshen Industrial Group, a major Chinese motorcycle and engine maker with 20,000+ staff. In September 2025 he was re-appointed chairman of the listed Zongshen Power Machinery board.
interesting_fact: He learned motorcycle repair working under his brother-in-law, opened his own shop in 1982 in a street-front room in Banan, Chongqing, and in 1992 borrowed 300,000 yuan to register Chongqing Zongshen Motorcycle Technology Development Co., the start of the group.
deep_cut_fact: Before the repair shop, after quitting his 'iron rice bowl' job as a kiln worker at a Chongqing porcelain factory in the early 1980s, he tried peddling martial-arts (wuxia) novels in Hebei and then fruit and clothing in Shandong, without success.
notes: No personal contacts published. Best formal route is the board secretary/IR office of Chongqing Zongshen Power Machinery (SZSE 001696; board secretary Lin Yi per Sept 2025 filing: https://filingreader.com/news-wire/shenzhen/2025-09-10/zongshen-power-names-new-chairman-general-manager-in-leadership-reshuffle). Daughter Zuo Ying described as successor running group investments.

current_role: Co-founder and major (5%+) shareholder of Wangsu Science & Technology (ChinaNetCenter), Shenzhen-listed 300017; not an executive
profile: Chen Baozhen co-founded the predecessor of Wangsu Science & Technology, a Shanghai CDN/edge-computing and internet infrastructure provider, in 2000 after ~30 years at a Fujian electrical-instrument factory. She sold much of her stake in 2018-2020 and further reductions were announced in 2024; she remains a 5%+ holder.
