profile: Yao Sanjun (姚三俊) is a member of Shanxi's Yao coking family, one of seven family shareholders of Meijin Energy Group, with a reported 12.5% stake; the group is led by Yao Junliang. The family business grew from a road-transport start into a Taiyuan coal, coke and coal-chemical group whose listed arm, Meijin Energy, has since pushed into hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles.
interesting_fact: The Meijin group started with the family buying two used trucks to run a haulage business and grew into a coal, coking and coal-chemical group that at one point supplied over 40% of Taiyuan city's town gas.
notes: Almost no public information about Yao Sanjun as an individual. He is identified only as one of seven Yao family shareholders of Meijin Energy Group, an old listing. The public face of the business is Yao Junliang and his son Yao Jinlong (chairman of Meijin Energy). The IR email is Meijin Energy's board-secretary address. Last appeared on Hurun in 2021.

name: Yao Sijun
current_role: Co-owner (12.5% family shareholder) of Shanxi Meijing Energy Group, controlling shareholder of Shenzhen-listed Shanxi Meijing Energy (000723.SZ)
profile: Yao Sijun (姚四俊) is the fourth son of Meijing founder Yao Juhuo and one of seven Yao family shareholders of Meijing Energy Group. Meijing was Shanxi's largest private coking group. Its listed arm, Meijing Energy, is now a major Chinese hydrogen fuel-cell player, making hydrogen from coke-oven gas.
interesting_fact: The business began in 1981, when his father Yao Juhuo, then 50, and eldest son Yao Junliang borrowed 16,000 yuan to buy two used trucks, becoming Qingxu county's first private haulage household, before moving into coal processing and coking.
notes: Minor public profile: he appears in press mainly as a family shareholder and group spokesman in old loan-guarantee disputes (avoid). The listed company is chaired by Yao Jinlong, of the family's next generation,, who is the better-known hydrogen figure. Only route found is Meijing Energy's board-secretary email. Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Du Jiangbo
current_role: Shareholder (30%) of Wuhai Junzheng Technology Industry Group, the No. 2 holder of Inner Mongolia Junzheng Energy & Chemical (601216.SH); long-time chairman of Junzheng's supervisory board (not on the board elected July 2026)
profile: Du Jiangbo (杜江波) is the elder brother of Junzheng founder and controller Du Jiangtao, often Inner Mongolia's richest man. Junzheng, based in Wuhai, runs coal mining, power, calcium carbide, PVC/caustic soda, ferrosilicon, coke, methanol and BDO, plus a chemical-logistics arm. Du Jiangbo's wealth comes from his stake in the family holding company and his supervisory role at the listed group.
interesting_fact: Junzheng is a vertically integrated 'coal-to-chemicals' play: it mines coal and limestone, generates its own power, and turns it into carbide, PVC and cement clinker from carbide slag, and also controls a chemical tanker fleet of ~1.1M dwt.
notes: Very low profile; almost no personal coverage. Not listed among Junzheng's 7th board or executives in its July 2026 announcement (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202607241827321470_1.pdf), so his supervisory-board role likely ended with China's 2026 governance changes. Best route via Junzheng Group corporate/IR.

name: Cai Tianzhen
current_role: Former founder-chairman of Titan Petrochemicals Group (泰山石化, HKEX 1192); no current role found
profile: Cai Tianzhen (蔡天真, Tsoi Tin Chun, b. c.1962), an oil trader, founded Hong Kong-listed Titan Petrochemicals in 2002 and controlled ~56% through Singapore-registered Titan Oil Pte. Titan ran oil tankers, bunkering and oil-storage logistics in Asia. He stepped down as chairman in July 2012, left the board in Feb 2013, and later sold control to Guangdong Zhenrong.
interesting_fact: By 2006 he had over 20 years in the oil business, meaning he started trading oil in his early twenties, in the mid-1980s.
deep_cut_fact: He held his Titan stake through Titan Oil Pte. Ltd., owned 95% by him and 5% by his wife, via an intermediate company aptly named Great Logistics Holdings, and chaired Titan from its May 2002 inception until July 2012.
notes: Out of the public eye since 2013. Avoid: Titan went through a debt restructuring and the HKEX Listing Committee later censured him as a former director. No published contact. Resignation source: https://en.portnews.ru/news/140198

name: Li Zhantong
current_role: Actual controller (approx. 70%) of Tianjin Datong Investment Group (天津大通投资集团); current activity unclear
profile: Li Zhantong (李占通) controls Tianjin Datong Investment Group, a Tianjin conglomerate spanning pharmaceuticals, gas, real estate, environmental services and media that once held about 20 companies, including control of listed Chase Sun Pharmaceutical (红日药业) and Sichuan Datong Gas (000593). In 2018-19 he sold down both stakes; Datong Gas passed to steel magnate Ding Liguo.
interesting_fact: Datong Group was founded in Tianjin by a team largely made up of former teachers from well-known Tianjin universities, and was seen as the leading 'Tianjin university-faction' investment house.
deep_cut_fact: In March 2005 Datong Group bought 55 million legal-person shares of Baoguang Pharmaceutical from Langjiu Group and others, became its largest shareholder and swapped in its gas business, a backdoor listing that created listed Datong Gas.
notes: Very little public information; no recent (post-2019) news found, so alive status and current role are unverified. Hurun last listed him in 2020. Has exited the gas business, so weak fit for an energy podcast. No official contact channel found.

name: Wang Wenliang
current_role: Chairman and executive director, Zhongyu Energy Holdings Ltd (formerly Zhongyu Gas, HKEX: 3633)
profile: Wang Wenliang (王文亮; input has 王文良), 55, has been executive director of Zhongyu since 2003 and chairs the Hong Kong-listed city-gas and energy distributor, controlled through his Hezhong Investment Holding. Over 30 years he has also invested in securities, internet services, building materials, property, energy and infrastructure.
interesting_fact: Before joining Zhongyu, Wang was briefly an executive director of China Gas Holdings (Jan-Jun 2003), one of China's biggest piped-gas distributors.
deep_cut_fact: Wang is deputy chairman of the fourth council of the China Foundation for Justice and Courage, which honours civilians who act bravely. He is a Hong Kong Justice of the Peace, did postgraduate finance at CASS's Graduate School (2001) and a Peking University EMBA (2019).
notes: Correct Chinese name per HKEX filings is 王文亮. Hurun lists wealth shared with Feng Haiyan. The company was renamed from Zhongyu Gas to Zhongyu Energy. Best route is company IR in Hong Kong (Shun Tak Centre).

name: Liu Han
profile: Liu Han (刘汉), founder and chairman of Sichuan-based Hanlong Group (mining, energy, chemicals, property), died in February 2015.
notes: Deceased: executed in China in February 2015 (Hanlong Group Wikipedia article, citing BBC/Reuters/SMH; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanlong_Group). Do not contact. Hanlong Group has been dissolved. Remove from outreach list.

name: Ma Yongsheng
current_role: Founder/chairman of Yunnan Haolong (Haolong) Group, Ludian County, Zhaotong (current status after 2021 not confirmed)
profile: Ma Yongsheng (马永升; not Sinopec's Ma Yongsheng 马永生) left a prosecutor's-office job in 1988 to revive a bankrupt cement plant, then in 1998 founded Ludian Haolong Industrial, growing it into a Yunnan group in lead-zinc mining, cement, hydropower and Kunming real estate. He was once called Yunnan's richest man and its top philanthropist; on Hurun lists 2008-2021 with Suo Fang.
interesting_fact: From 2005 Haolong built a string of small hydropower stations in Yunnan (Heishihe, Pudu River, Qingshui River, Guanhe) and won rights to Huangjiaoshu, the largest cascade on the Niulan River.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999, ignoring an official survey that said the Lehong deposit was unfit for large-scale mining, he led his team in winter to measure cliff profiles by tape, sometimes roped to trees on the summit, and proved large lead-zinc reserves. Earlier, as a 1988 graduate, he carried cement sacks alongside workers to revive the idle Dashuijing plant.
notes: Hurun spells the company 'Haolong' (昊龙). Little coverage after the 2010s; current role and well-being unverified. Fortune shared with Suo Fang. Do not confuse with Sinopec chairman Ma Yongsheng. No published contact found; regional Yunnan private group with minimal web presence.

name: Suo Fang
current_role: Second-largest shareholder (6.36%) of Yunnan Haolong Industrial Group (云南昊龙实业集团, Zhaotong); wife of group president Ma Yongsheng
profile: Suo Fang (锁芳) is the wife of Ma Yongsheng, founder of Yunnan Haolong (昊龙) Industrial Group, set up in 1998 in Zhaotong and focused on non-ferrous metal mining and processing, with utilities and property interests. Registry data cited by the press show Ma with 89.1% and Suo Fang 6.36%. She has acted as the family's public spokesperson in recent years.
interesting_fact: Hurun's 2009 list made Ma Yongsheng 'Yunnan's richest man' (RMB3bn), 11 years after founding the group; Haolong says it has paid RMB5.13bn in cumulative taxes and ranks among Yunnan's top 100 private firms.
notes: Hurun romanises the firm as 'Haolong' but the Chinese is 昊龙 (not 浩龙). Sensitive: Ma Yongsheng was detained in April 2022 and a 1990 assault case against him was reopened in 2023; Suo Fang has spoken to media about it. Avoid in outreach. No published contact found.

name: Ji Jing
profile: Hurun's 2018 list ranks Ji Jing (纪静, Yinchuan-based) No.902 with RMB4.5bn from Bao Ta Petrochemical (宝塔石化, Yinchuan; petrochemicals and education). Baota's actual controller in filings was Sun Hengchao (孙珩超); we found no public source naming 纪静 as owner, director or relative.
notes: Hurun record: https://www.hurun.net/zh-CN/Rank/HsRankDetailsList?num=DFW1O34E&search=%E7%BA%AA%E9%9D%99&offset=0&limit=20 . Tried: 纪静 + 宝塔石化/孙珩超/银川能源学院; Baota Industry (000595) 2016 annual report. Baota later collapsed (finance arm licence revoked). Unresolved.

name: Sun Jiangyan
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016-21) with Wang Fuxiang as holding wealth through Shanghai Sinyang Semiconductor Materials (300236.SZ), a Songjiang-based maker of chip electroplating and cleaning chemicals and photoresists. Wang Fuxiang, the founder, held about 14% directly in 2025, and the company is now led by Wang Su. I found no public filing or profile describing Sun Jiangyan's role.
notes: Identity not confirmed: probably a family member or co-holder alongside founder Wang Fuxiang, but no source confirms it. The company IR email comes from the 2018 annual report summary (April 2019) and may be out of date. A better route is probably via Wang Fuxiang or chairman Wang Su. Low priority.

name: Feng Haiyan
current_role: Substantial shareholder (non-executive) of Zhongyu Energy Holdings Ltd. (HKEX: 3633, formerly Zhongyu Gas); co-owner of Hezhong Investment Holding
profile: Feng Haiyan (冯海燕) is the wife of Zhongyu Energy chairman Wang Wenliang, and Hurun lists them together. She owns 49% of Hezhong Investment Holding, the couple's vehicle; with Wang's direct holding, they control about 29% of Zhongyu. Zhongyu is a Hong Kong-listed city-gas distributor in mainland China, and China Gas Holdings is its other major holder. She holds no board or executive role.
interesting_fact: Under Hong Kong disclosure rules she holds 10.9M Zhongyu shares directly and is deemed interested in 800M shares (29.12%) through Hezhong and her husband's holdings.
notes: Private, passive shareholder with no public profile; Hurun listed her only in 2021, jointly with Wang Wenliang. For a podcast, Wang Wenliang (chairman since 2003) is the more natural guest. The company's Hong Kong office is at China Merchants Tower, Shun Tak Centre (from the annual report). Company secretary: Lui Siu Keung.

name: Yu Dehai
current_role: Co-actual controller of Kede Numerical Control (科德数控, SSE STAR: 688305) via Dalian Guangyang Science & Technology (光洋科技), its controlling shareholder
profile: Dalian industrialist behind Guangyang Science & Technology, the parent of Kede Numerical Control, one of China's leading makers of high-end five-axis CNC machine tools with in-house CNC systems, servo drives and motors. Kede listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; Yu Dehai and Yu Benhong are named together as controllers in its IPO commitments.
interesting_fact: Kede is one of the few Chinese companies to build both five-axis machining centres and their CNC control systems in-house, serving aerospace and power-generation turbine-blade machining, a field long dominated by Swiss/German suppliers.
notes: Very low public profile; Yu Benhong is Kede's chairman and day-to-day face. Web-search budget ran out, so Yu Dehai's personal bio and current status were not verified. Route via Kede board secretary/IR email.

name: Yu Benhong
current_role: Chairman, Kede Numerical Control (科德数控, SSE STAR:688305), Dalian; member of the 14th CPPCC National Committee
profile: Yu Benhong (b. ~1977) has chaired Kede CNC since 2015; the Dalian company makes five-axis CNC machine tools, high-end CNC systems and key components (servo drives, motors, spindles) aimed at replacing imports, serving aerospace/defence and civil markets. Wealth is shared with Yu Dehai, the founder of the Dalian Guangyang group from which Kede emerged.
interesting_fact: Kede is one of China's few makers of both five-axis machine tools and their own high-end CNC control systems, including blade-machining and blisk centres used for turbine parts.
deep_cut_fact: Before chairing Kede he ran Dalian Guangyang's international industrial-control technology-transfer centre for 16 years (2004-2020); in January 2023 he became a member of the 14th CPPCC National Committee.
notes: Hurun listing shared with Yu Dehai. Relevant to advanced manufacturing/turbine machining. IR email from the 2025 annual report.

name: Zhang Hebing (张和兵)
current_role: Co-founder, joint controlling shareholder and Special Assistant to the Chairman, Porton Pharma Solutions (博腾股份, SZSE: 300363); chairman & GM of Chongqing Juxin Investment
profile: Zhang is one of three co-founders and joint actual controllers (with chairman Ju Nianfeng and Tao Rong, under a joint-control agreement) of Chongqing-based Porton Pharma Solutions, a contract development and manufacturing organisation founded in 2005. Porton makes APIs and drug products for global pharma across small molecules, peptides/oligos, biologics and ADCs; he holds about 7.7%.
interesting_fact: Porton has grown from a 2005 Chongqing start-up into a global CDMO with 4,400+ staff, 1,500+ customers and about 6,000 delivered projects.
deep_cut_fact: Porton's three founders signed a formal joint-control agreement before the 2014 IPO and still act in concert; besides Porton, Zhang chairs the supervisory board of Runsheng Pharmaceutical and runs Chongqing Yixin Investment Management.
notes: Low public profile; chairman Ju Nianfeng is the spokesman. Facts from Porton 2025 annual report (cninfo) and company site. Web search budget exhausted, so personal background (education/early career) not researched.

name: Zhao Guanlong
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2020-2021 (赵关龙) with wealth from 'RongSheng', a chemical-fibre business. The specific company could not be pinned down in this pass; it should not be assumed to be Rongsheng Petrochemical (controlled by Li Shuirong).
notes: Identity unconfirmed: web search budget was exhausted and no Wikipedia/Baike entry was reachable. Needs a Chinese-language follow-up search (赵关龙 荣盛 化纤) before any outreach.

name: Chuo Yung-Tsai
current_role: Founder and Group President, HIWIN Technologies (上銀科技, TWSE: 2049), Taichung, Taiwan; also founder of HIWIN Mikrosystem
profile: Chuo Yung-Tsai (卓永財, b. 1942), a Hakka from a tenant-farming family in Zhubei, Hsinchu, was a Bank of Communications executive who turned around Taiwan's largest nut maker in 1983, then bought ball-screw maker Ho Feng Precision and in 1989 founded HIWIN, now the world's second-largest ball-screw maker with motion-control and robotics units worldwide. His son Eric Chuo is chairman.
interesting_fact: HIWIN bought German ball-screw maker Holzer in 1993, just four years after founding, giving the Taiwanese company an early European manufacturing base; it is now the world's No. 2 ball-screw maker.
deep_cut_fact: He once posted on Yahoo! Kimo Knowledge+ under the alias '猛男一號' ('Macho Man No. 1'), chatting about the machinery industry and encouraging female students to study mechanical engineering. He also funded a library at Liujia Elementary School in memory of his elder brother.
notes: Accounting graduate of Tamkang University with a management master's from University of San Francisco; author of a book on foreign-exchange practice. Honorary chairman of Taiwan's machine tool & accessory builders' association. Best route is HIWIN corporate/IR.

name: Zuo Guojun
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology Corp. (捷佳伟创, 300724.SZ)
profile: Co-controller and chairman (since November 2023) of S.C New Energy, a major Chinese maker of solar-cell production tools (PECVD, diffusion, wet-chemistry) that also supplies semiconductor wet-process equipment. He acts in concert with Yu Zhong and Liang Meizhen and held 7.5% directly in March 2026.
interesting_fact: S.C equipment underpins much of China's solar-cell manufacturing build-out. In March 2026 Zuo and fellow pre-IPO holders took part in an inquiry-based share transfer, when Zuo held 26.16M shares (7.51%).
notes: 'S.C' in the source data refers to S.C New Energy (捷佳伟创). Little personal biography is public. The board secretary is Tan Xiangping. Company site was unreachable from this environment.

name: Liu Daojun
current_role: No current public role found; former director (2004-2022) and co-founding shareholder of Jiangxi Zhengbang Technology (SZSE: 002157)
profile: Liu Daojun (legal name Liew Kenneth Thow Jiun, Canadian national, b. Oct 1972) co-founded the listed Zhengbang Technology with Lin Yinsun's Zhengbang Group, a Jiangxi feed and hog-farming giant, and sat on its board from 2004 to 2022 as a large non-controlling shareholder (169.6m shares at end-2019). Zhengbang has since been restructured under new control; his current activities are not public.
interesting_fact: Though listed by Hurun as a Chinese billionaire, filings identify him as a Canadian citizen named Liew Kenneth Thow Jiun - unrelated to Zhengbang's controlling family, yet a founding promoter of the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before and alongside Zhengbang he chaired Jiangxi Zhengbang Industrial, Yunnan Guanglian Livestock & Poultry and Nanchang Guanglian Industrial, and took no pay from the listed company as a director.
notes: Left Zhengbang board in 2022; the company went through court restructuring in 2023 and is now controlled by the Twins Group - avoid that topic. No personal channels found. Very low profile.

name: Jabbok Schlacks
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, EquipmentShare.com Inc (Nasdaq: EQPT), Columbia, Missouri
profile: Jabbok Schlacks co-founded EquipmentShare in 2015 with his brother Willy and three others, after the brothers ran construction and contracting businesses from their teens. The company grew from a peer-to-peer equipment marketplace into a national construction equipment rental, sales and telematics business with 448 locations, and raised about $747m in its January 2026 Nasdaq IPO.
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare's T3 cloud platform tracks over 397,000 construction assets with telematics, GPS and keypads. In 2025 the company opened a $100m Technology and Development Center at its Columbia, Mo. headquarters.
deep_cut_fact: The company began as a weekend pitch: in October 2014 the brothers won Startup Weekend Columbia with a peer-to-peer equipment-sharing idea, then joined Y Combinator's Winter 2015 batch.
notes: Strong fit for the podcast: a Midwest founder story (YC alum, Columbia MO) in construction tech, with exposure to data-center construction demand. Personal social accounts not verified. Web-search quota ran out mid-lane, so press/IR emails were not extracted.

name: Abel Matutes
current_role: President, Grupo Empresas Matutes (owner of Palladium Hotel Group), Ibiza
profile: Ibiza-born (1941) businessman and former politician: mayor of Ibiza (1970-71), senator, MEP, European Commissioner (1986-94) and Spain's foreign minister (1996-2000). His family group, Grupo Empresas Matutes, owns Palladium Hotel Group (formerly Fiesta Hotel Group), behind Ushuaia Ibiza and Hard Rock Hotel Ibiza, with banking, real estate and energy interests.
interesting_fact: In 1993-94 he was the European Commissioner responsible for Transport, Energy and the Euratom Supply Agency under Jacques Delors -- a direct link to an energy-focused podcast.
deep_cut_fact: While studying law and economics in Barcelona he played professional football for RCD Espanyol, and reportedly turned down an offer from FC Barcelona to pursue business instead.
notes: Aged 85; his son Abel Matutes Prats now runs much of the group day-to-day. Also taught public finance at the University of Barcelona. Palladium HQ contacts page: palladiumhotelgroup.com/en/contact/oficinas-centrales; no dedicated press email found.

name: Christopher R Gordon
current_role: Partner, Global Head of Private Equity and Global Head of Healthcare, Bain Capital (Boston); former Kestra Medical director (2021 to Sept 2025)
profile: Chris Gordon joined Bain Capital in 1997 after consulting at Bain & Company and now leads its global private equity and healthcare investing. He has sat on boards of HCA, Quintiles (IQVIA), Waystar, Surgery Partners, Stada and Kestra Medical (wearable defibrillators), which Bain controls via West Affum Holdings. The SEC-derived net worth likely reflects Bain-held Kestra shares attributed to him, not personal holdings.
interesting_fact: He has served on the boards of a who's-who of healthcare buyouts, including HCA, Quintiles Transnational (now IQVIA), Grupo NotreDame Intermedica and Cerevel Therapeutics.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Baker Scholar (top of class distinction) at Harvard Business School, graduated magna cum laude in economics from Harvard College, and is a founding Director of the Healthcare Private Equity Association.
notes: Net worth figure ($646M) is likely an artefact: Kestra proxy lists his address c/o Bain Capital and shows no personal beneficial ownership; the 10% stake belongs to Bain funds. He left Kestra's board Sept 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1877184/000119312526320956/ck0001877184-20260727.htm). Member, Council on Foreign Relations.

name: Oleg Tinkov
current_role: Founder of Tinkoff Bank (now T-Bank); no current executive role - divested his stake in 2022
profile: Siberian-born Oleg Tinkov built and sold a string of consumer businesses (Petrosib electronics, Daria frozen foods, Tinkoff beer, sold to InBev in 2005) before founding branchless Tinkoff Bank in 2006, which listed in London in 2013. After publicly condemning the war in Ukraine he sold out in 2022, renounced Russian citizenship and is now a Cypriot citizen living abroad.
interesting_fact: Tinkov owned a UCI World Tour cycling team - Tinkoff-Saxo/Tinkoff, bought from Bjarne Riis in 2013 - and earlier ran the Tinkoff Restaurants and Tinkoff Credit Systems pro teams.
deep_cut_fact: Before business, Tinkov was a serious road cyclist from age 12 and earned the Soviet title 'Candidate for Master of Sports' in 1984; he started trading goods during cycling training camps in Central Asia, and later studied at the St Petersburg Mining Institute.
notes: Sensitive: UK-sanctioned (March 2022), designated a 'foreign agent' by Russia (2024), outspoken political critic; outreach could be politically delicate. Active on Instagram/X but handles not verified from an official source. No published office/press contact found.

name: Gao Naize
current_role: Legal representative/chairman (last reported), Shaanxi Xingmao Jurassic Coal & Magnesium Power Group (陕西兴茂侏罗纪煤业镁电集团), Yulin, Shaanxi
profile: Shaanxi coal entrepreneur behind the Yulin-based Xingmao Jurassic coal, magnesium and power group; once Shaanxi's richest man and on Hurun China lists 2010-2015 (Forbes China #198 in 2011). In March 2020 Shaanxi's supervisory commission opened a bribery investigation into him linked to the case of a former Yulin party secretary; no later outcome found.
interesting_fact: He was a prominent donor in his heyday, ranking as high as 15th on the Hurun China Philanthropy List.
notes: Not a good outreach target: under a 2020 bribery investigation (status/verdict unknown, may be detained). No public contacts found. Keep minimal.

name: Peng Jiahua
profile: Listed as a Chinese billionaire with wealth from 'HJS'. English and Chinese searches (彭家华) could not identify the company behind 'HJS' or find any biography, interview or rich-list entry matching this name.
notes: Identity could not be confirmed and the Chinese characters of the name are unknown. Hurun PDFs could not be fetched from this environment. We need the full company name behind 'HJS' (or a Forbes/Hurun profile link) to go further.

name: Zhang Yingcen
current_role: Controlling shareholder (via family trust) of China Tian Lun Gas Holdings (1600.HK); retired as chairman Jan 2025
profile: Zhang Yingcen (张瀛岑) founded and long chaired China Tian Lun Gas, one of China's early private city-gas operators, rooted in Henan and listed in Hong Kong in Nov 2010. It grew to ~67 urban gas projects in 16 provinces plus pipelines, LNG plants and filling stations. He stepped down as chairman in January 2025 (succeeded by Xian Zhenyuan) and placed his majority stake in a family trust.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he bought out the IFC's stake in Tian Lun Gas and sold an 11.96% block to state-owned Zhuhai Port, which became the No. 2 shareholder and signed a 5-year new-energy cooperation pact with the company.
notes: Retired from the board Jan 2025; low public profile, Chinese-language only. Best route would be Tian Lun Gas company secretary/IR via HKEX filings; no published IR email found in the sources checked. Hurun pairs him with Sun Yanxi.

name: Sun Yanxi
current_role: Shareholder (20% of controlling holding company Gold Shine Development) of Tian Lun Gas Holdings (HKEX: 1600); no executive role
profile: Wife of Zhang Yingcen, chairman and controlling shareholder of Zhengzhou-based Tian Lun Gas, a Henan city-gas distributor (piped gas, CNG/LNG refuelling, integrated energy) listed in Hong Kong. Per the 2023 annual report she owns 20% of Gold Shine Development, which controls Tian Lun Group, and holds 5.7m Tian Lun shares directly. No public profile beyond filings.
interesting_fact: Tian Lun Gas grew from Zhengzhou into a multi-province city-gas network and is controlled through Gold Shine Development, owned 60/20/20 by Zhang Yingcen, Sun Yanxi and Zhang Daoyuan.
notes: Passive family shareholder, not an operator; Hurun listings stopped after 2021. Better podcast target is husband Zhang Yingcen (chairman). Only route is Tian Lun Gas IR.

name: Wang Xingchun
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Winsway Coking Coal (now E-Commodities Holdings, HKEX 1733); no current board seat found
profile: Wang Xingchun (王兴春) built Winsway into the largest importer of Mongolian coking coal into China, with its own cross-border logistics, and listed it in Hong Kong in 2010 as chairman and CEO (it also had a Mongolian JV with Peabody). The company was renamed E-Commodities Holdings; filings since 2023 show others chairing the board.
interesting_fact: Before coal, he spent 15+ years building cross-border logistics: in 1995 he invested in and became vice chairman of Manzhouli Haitie Yonghui, which runs oil and petrochemical transshipment facilities at the Manzhouli railway port on the Russian border.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1990 as an agent for Hong Kong Management Service (Chemicals), part of the Landmark Chemicals trading group; he had earned a diploma in mechanical manufacturing from Beijing Open University (1984-87), per Winsway's IPO prospectus.
notes: Low profile; last on Hurun China list in 2021. No longer a director of the listed company; no published personal or press contacts found. Hurun calls the source 'Winsway Coking Coal'.

name: Chen Jinyue
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Ningbo Baosi Energy Equipment (Shenzhen: 300441)
profile: Born 1964 in Fenghua, Zhejiang, Chen ran small local alloy-materials and machinery workshops before founding Baosi in 2005. Baosi makes screw-compressor parts, compressors, vacuum pumps and hydraulic pumps and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2015; he controls roughly 40% of the company.
interesting_fact: Baosi is headquartered in Fenghua, Ningbo, which the company itself promotes as Chiang Kai-shek's ancestral home and a Maitreya Buddhist holy site, and it builds its corporate culture around Maitreya ideals of openness and harmony.
deep_cut_fact: Before Baosi he ran two small Fenghua workshops, the Fenghua Daqiao Chengli alloy-materials factory and Fenghua Jingda machinery factory; he also serves as a director of China's compressor industry association and a Fenghua district people's congress deputy.
notes: The IR email is the company's published securities-affairs contact (board secretary Xu Bin), not Chen personally. Very low international profile; Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Zhou Lina
current_role: Spouse of founder-chairman Chen Jinyue and related party of Ningbo Baosi Energy Equipment (鲍斯股份, SZSE ChiNext 300441), Fenghua, Ningbo
profile: Zhou Lina (周利娜) is the wife of Chen Jinyue (b. 1964), founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Ningbo Baosi Energy Equipment, which makes screw compressor and blower air-ends and complete compressor sets (plus precision tooling). Hurun lists the couple jointly (2015-2021). Filings show she and her husband personally guarantee the company's bank credit lines.
interesting_fact: Before Baosi, Chen Jinyue ran two small Fenghua workshops - Daqiao Chengli Alloy Materials Factory and Fenghua Jingda Machinery - then built Baosi into a listed screw-compressor maker; he chairs it and has also been general manager since 2016.

name: Tony Buckingham
current_role: Owner (reported CEO), Albion Energy Ltd, holder of Malta offshore exploration study licence for Areas 2 and 7 (2023); founder & ex-CEO of Heritage Oil
profile: Tony Buckingham, a former British SAS officer, founded Heritage Oil in 1992 to explore in Angola; Heritage later made big finds in Uganda's Lake Albert basin and Iraqi Kurdistan, listed in London in 2008 and was sold in 2014. He now explores via privately owned Albion Energy, which won a Maltese offshore licence in 2023.
interesting_fact: Heritage Oil found hundreds of millions of barrels in Uganda and up to ~3bn barrels recoverable in Kurdistan; Heritage's prospectus says he advised Angola's government from 1989 and helped set up Sonangol, the national oil company.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in the oil industry as a North Sea diver in the 1970s before launching Heritage Oil in 1992.
notes: Very private; no website or published contact found for Albion Energy (UK Companies House: Albion Energy Limited 09187547). Press coverage routinely references his past links to private military firms Executive Outcomes/Sandline - sensitive; avoid in outreach. Alive status inferred from 2023 Malta licence news; no death reports found.

name: Claiborne P Deming
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Murphy Oil Corporation (since 2012); Director, Murphy USA Inc.
profile: Louisiana-born lawyer (Tulane BA 1976, JD 1979) and nephew of Murphy Oil's longtime head Charles H. Murphy Jr. He joined Murphy Oil as a staff attorney and was President & CEO from 1994 to 2008, tripling production and reserves, expanding into Malaysia and starting the Walmart gas-station tie-up that became Murphy USA. He is now board chair of Murphy Oil and a Murphy USA director.
interesting_fact: He conceived the El Dorado Promise, a $50M Murphy Oil-funded pledge (2007) covering in-state college tuition for every El Dorado (Ark.) High graduate. By 2016, 84% of eligible students went to college and AP offerings grew from 3 to 19 classes.
deep_cut_fact: After Hurricane Katrina in 2005 he had Murphy hire a security firm to rescue employees trapped in its flooded New Orleans office; 83 people were brought out that Friday. Earlier, Murphy's exploration under him found the ~500M-barrel Kikeh field off Borneo (2002), the largest reserve add in company history.
notes: Inducted into the Arkansas Business Hall of Fame. Former chair of the National Petroleum Council. Also a senior advisor to TPH Partners (energy PE). Wealth estimate comes from SEC insider holdings. Approach via Murphy Oil corporate communications/IR in Houston.

name: Lin Guofang
current_role: Chairman & General Manager (controlling shareholder), Shenzhen Fuanna Bedding & Furnishing Co. (富安娜, SZSE: 002327)
profile: Shenzhen home-textile entrepreneur (b. 1954, high-school education) who ran Shenzhen Yahao home-decor before founding Fuanna's predecessor in 1994. Fuanna grew into one of China's leading premium bedding and home-textile brands and listed in Shenzhen in 2009; he remains chairman, GM and actual controller per the 2025 annual report.
interesting_fact: He personally funded about RMB200m to build the Lufeng city cultural centre plus a township hospital and middle school in Tanxi, Lufeng, earning the 'New Rural Worthy of South Guangdong' (南粤新乡贤) honour in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before Fuanna he was general manager of Shenzhen Yahao Home Décor (深圳雅豪家饰精品); he founded Fuanna in 1994 as 'Shenzhen Fuanna Home Decoration & Health Products Co.' and has run it for over 30 years.
notes: Hometown philanthropy in Lufeng (Shanwei, Guangdong) is a good warm angle. Route via Fuanna board office email.

name: Gao Zhendong (高振东, Don Gao)
current_role: Founder and CEO/president, Positec Group (宝时得, Suzhou), maker of WORX, Rockwell and Kress tools (latest confirmed reporting ~2016)
profile: Founder of Suzhou-based Positec (Chinese name 宝时得), started in 1994 as a power-tool exporter. He opened a Suzhou factory in 1995 making OEM tools for Sears, B&Q, OBI and Black & Decker, then built own brands: WORX (launched 2004) and the acquired US brand Rockwell. Positec, a major cordless and robotic-mower player, sells via Home Depot, Lowe's, Walmart and Costco.
interesting_fact: He chose to build Chinese-owned global brands rather than stay an OEM, deciding in 1999 to launch his own brand even though old customers would become competitors; WORX products were later reported to outsell Bosch in some German categories.
deep_cut_fact: The name 'Positec' is a play on 'Positive Technology'. To launch WORX he hired Vicenza-based Italian designer Paolo Andriolo for ergonomic products; the flagship was the WORX GT trimmer. He has said: 'Consumers don't care about the technology you put into products. They only care about whether it works well.'
notes: Identity: Hurun lists 高振东 of 宝时得 (Positec); English sources call Positec's founder 'Don Gao'. Same company, very likely the same person, but the Chinese/English name link isn't explicitly confirmed. Private company, little recent press; current title and status not confirmed after ~2016. Quote is from China Daily (2016). Energy angle: cordless battery platforms (Power Share).

name: Bao Wendong
current_role: Unverified; listed by Hurun (2010-2021) for Dongxing Aluminium (东兴铝业), mining/aluminium
profile: Appeared on Hurun China Rich Lists 2010-2021 for Dongxing Aluminium, jointly with Wu Kaihui. No reliable public profile was found to confirm his current role.
notes: Chinese name 包文东. Dongxing Aluminium not found as a listed issuer on cninfo; Baidu Baike blocked automated access and the lane's web-search budget ran out. Potentially relevant to an energy podcast (aluminium smelting is power-intensive), but needs manual identity check first.

profile: Listed on Hurun China 2010-2021 (jointly with Bao Wendong) with wealth from 'Dongxing Aluminium' (mining/aluminium). No accessible source could be found to confirm her/his role or the company's details.
notes: Not researched in depth: web search budget was exhausted before this record and Baidu Baike was unreachable. Needs a follow-up pass (search 东兴铝业 / 吴开慧 / 鲍文东).

name: Li Jiaxuan
current_role: Former director and early shareholder, Canaan Inc. (Nasdaq: CAN); current role not found
profile: Jiaxuan Li (李佳轩) is a chip designer who joined Canaan, the bitcoin-mining ASIC maker founded by N.G. Zhang, and became a director in December 2015. At the 2019 Nasdaq IPO he was its largest shareholder by share count (~16%, via the trust vehicle Ouroboros Ltd.). He no longer appears among directors in Canaan's latest 20-F.
interesting_fact: Canaan's IPO prospectus named him, alongside founder Nangeng Zhang, as one of the two senior managers the company's future depended on.
deep_cut_fact: Before Canaan he spent 2010–2013 as an IC engineer at Vimicro, the Chinese fabless multimedia-chip company. He holds a computer-science BS from Harbin Institute of Technology (2008) and a software-engineering master's from Beihang University (2010).
notes: Very low profile. He has apparently left Canaan's board, so the company is probably not a route to him. Relevant to the energy/data-center theme (bitcoin-mining hardware). Around 41 in 2026 (age 34 in the 2019 prospectus).

name: Tang Yuxiang
current_role: Chairman, Yutong Bus Co. / President, Zhengzhou Yutong Group (verify current title in latest annual report)
profile: Born 1954 in Yixing, Jiangsu, Tang joined the state-run Zhengzhou Bus Factory as a technician in 1981, rose to deputy director and from 1993 led its successor Zhengzhou Yutong Bus, which he and management later took private via a buyout. Yutong is one of the world's largest bus makers and a major producer of electric buses; he has served as a National People's Congress deputy since 2008.
interesting_fact: Yutong traces back to the Zhengzhou Bus Repair Factory founded in 1963 and now sells e-buses and e-coaches worldwide; in 2019 Tang used his NPC seat to propose government-backed pilot cities for autonomous-driving firms.
deep_cut_fact: As a 'sent-down' youth in Dec 1970 he worked on a May Seventh youth farm in Jicheng commune outside Zhengzhou, studied construction machinery at Jiyuan 531 Machinery School, and was a factory worker at Jiaozuo Zhongzhou Machinery Plant before joining the bus factory.
notes: Chinese name 汤玉祥; named 2005 National Model Worker. Yutong (SSE: 600066) is highly relevant to EV/energy. Only a sales inbox is published; Yutong also lists official Facebook/LinkedIn/X accounts on its contact page. Age ~72 -- check whether he has handed over the chairmanship.

name: Zhu Long
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and largest shareholder, YITU Technology (依图科技), Shanghai
profile: Computer-vision scientist (Leo Zhu) who co-founded YITU Technology in Shanghai in 2012. YITU became one of China's 'four AI dragons' in face recognition and later moved into medical AI and AI chips (its QuestCore inference chip) and large models. He holds a statistics PhD from UCLA under Alan Yuille and was a postdoc at MIT's AI lab before teaching at NYU.
interesting_fact: YITU's early break came from recognising cars with cloned licence plates before faces. Staff photographed about 50 vehicles a day on Shanghai streets to build a vehicle database, which won the company its first police client in Suzhou.
deep_cut_fact: He and YITU co-founder Lin Chenxi (an ACM ICPC world champion and Alibaba Cloud architect) were childhood friends. Both were born in 1978 and attended the same primary, middle and high school, Fuzhou's Yinghua school, for 12 years, then reconnected at a class reunion in late 2011.
notes: Keeps a low public profile. YITU is on the US Entity List (since 2019) over surveillance in Xinjiang, which makes outreach sensitive. Its STAR Market IPO was suspended and a Hong Kong IPO has been mooted. No sourced 2025-26 update on his role.

name: Sun Yanbin
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2020-2021) as sharing a fortune with Feng Kang from Aofei Data (奥飞数据, Shenzhen 300738), a Guangzhou-based IDC/data-center operator. Aofei's controlling shareholder and chairman is Feng Kang; no public role for Sun Yanbin at Aofei could be found in filings or press.

public_contacts.value: liuhy@ofidc.com (Aofei Data board secretary Liu Haiyan; securities rep fangmh@ofidc.com)

notes: Could not confirm who Sun Yanbin (孙彦彬) is or their link to Aofei Data beyond the Hurun joint listing with Feng Kang; possibly a family co-holder. Not in current management. If pursuing the Aofei story, Feng Kang (chairman/GM) is the relevant person, via the board secretary.

name: Jin Yong
current_role: Majority limited partner (55.33%) of Tianjin Xundu Venture Capital, a founding shareholder of Maxscend (卓胜微, SZSE 300782)
profile: Jin Yong (金勇) is a private investor whose Maxscend wealth comes through Tianjin Xundu Venture Investment Partnership, in which he held 55.33% as LP. Xundu co-founded Maxscend's Jiangsu operating company with Xu Zhihan and Yao Lisheng and held 7.77% before the 2019 IPO; the RF front-end chip stock's surge put him on Hurun's 2020-2021 lists.
interesting_fact: Tianjin Xundu was one of the three original cash investors that set up Jiangsu Maxscend (卓胜有限), alongside chairman Xu Zhihan and Yao Lisheng; it still held 1.81% of Maxscend at end-2025.
notes: Identified via Maxscend's 2019 IPO prospectus (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2019-06-03/1206323462.PDF) and Xundu's 2020 equity-change report: Jin Yong = 55.33% LP of Tianjin Xundu (GP: Wuxi Yuandu Venture Consulting, rep Wang Xuefeng). Hurun 2020-21 matches. Purely a financial investor with no public profile or role at Maxscend; not the novelist Jin Yong. Maxscend contact is only an indirect route.

name: Luo Chuankui
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Shanghai Nenghui Technology Co., Ltd. (能辉科技, SZSE ChiNext: 301046)
profile: Luo Chuankui (罗传奎, b. Sept 1966) is a Tsinghua-trained environmental engineer who founded Shanghai Nenghui in 2009, building it into a new-energy engineering and products firm (solar, wind, storage, EV heavy-truck battery swapping, power-plant environmental systems). He controls it via Shanghai Nenghui Investment Holding and holds ~35.4m shares directly.
interesting_fact: Nenghui's founding team all came from provincial power design institutes; the company has recently added data-centre infrastructure operation and AI/computing services to its registered business scope alongside storage and battery-swap equipment.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in environmental engineering from Tsinghua and is a professor-level senior engineer; before founding Nenghui he was chief design engineer and branch GM at the Zhejiang Electric Power Design Institute (1995-2002), then VP of Shandong Sanrong Environmental Engineering (2002-2008). He is rotating chairman of the Shanghai New Hushang Federation.
notes: Chinese-language outreach via company email/board secretary (罗联明) is the realistic route. Good fit for energy-storage and data-centre-power angle.

name: Shen Xueru
current_role: Chairman, Aoyang Group Co. (Zhangjiagang, Jiangsu); former actual controller of Jiangsu Aoyang Health (002172.SZ)
profile: Shen Xueru (沈学如, b. 1954) built Zhangjiagang-based Aoyang Group from wool textiles into viscose fibre (Aoyang Technology, listed 2007), hospitals and pharma logistics (now Aoyang Health). In Sept 2025 Aoyang Group agreed to sell 20% of Aoyang Health to a Zhangjiagang development-zone vehicle, handing control to local government.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he took Aoyang Technology public on the Shenzhen exchange, making viscose staple fibre the core of the 'Aoyang system', which later pivoted into private hospitals and healthcare.
notes: Aged ~72 and stepping back from the Aoyang listed companies (control of Aoyang Health passing to Zhangjiagang ETDZ). No personal/public channels found; the only route is Aoyang Health's board-secretary office via its Shenzhen exchange filings (cninfo). Low relevance to energy/data centers beyond Aoyang Shunchang link.

name: Shen Qing
current_role: Shareholder and acting-in-concert party to her father Shen Xueru in the Aoyang group; has worked in Aoyang Group's financial management centre
profile: Shen Qing (沈卿, b. 1979) is the daughter of Shen Xueru, founder of Zhangjiagang-based Aoyang Group (chemical fibres/viscose, later healthcare via Aoyang Health, SZSE: 002172). Hurun listed the family's wealth from 2011 to 2020. In September 2025 the family sold a controlling 20% stake in Aoyang Health to a Zhangjiagang ETDZ-backed vehicle, and control passed to the zone's management committee.
interesting_fact: The Aoyang group grew from viscose fibre in Zhangjiagang into listed businesses in healthcare (Aoyang Health) and metals and logistics (Aoyang Shunchang, 002245, now Shunchang). In 2025 the family handed control of Aoyang Health to the local development zone.
notes: Private family member with no public profile or interviews found. Weak fit for the podcast: textiles and healthcare, despite the data_center_ai tag. The IR email belongs to Aoyang Health, which the family no longer controls. Her father Shen Xueru (b. 1954) is the public figure.

name: Chen Haoyue
current_role: Early individual shareholder of Maxscend Microelectronics (卓胜微, SZSE 300782); holds no position at the company
profile: Chen Haoyue (陈皞玥, male, b. 1975) was an early shareholder of Maxscend's Cayman holding company and in 2015 moved his stake onshore, buying 4.5% of Jiangsu Maxscend for RMB500,000 at par. He held 4.09% before the 2019 Shenzhen IPO; the RF chipmaker's rise put him on Hurun's 2021 list (~US$530m).
interesting_fact: His roughly 4.5% Maxscend stake was acquired for just RMB500,000 in 2015 as part of the company unwinding its offshore Cayman structure, years before Maxscend became one of China's most valuable chip designers.
notes: Confirmed via Maxscend IPO prospectus and lawyer's work report on cninfo (listed as a natural-person shareholder, 'no position held'). Not in Maxscend's 2025 top-10 holders, so he has likely sold down. No public profile, background or role found; passive investor. Low priority for outreach.

name: Liang Dazhong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Chippacking Technology / Qipai Technology Co. (SSE STAR: 688216), Dongguan
profile: Liang Dazhong, a veteran chip-packaging engineer, is the controlling shareholder of Qipai (Chippacking) Technology, an integrated-circuit packaging and testing company headquartered in Shipai, Dongguan and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. He built it with Bai Ying (fellow director and co-holder) through a series of Shenzhen chip firms from 1997 onward.
interesting_fact: In late 2024 he sold a 5% block of Qipai and pledged to lend the after-tax proceeds back to the company to fund its development.
deep_cut_fact: He started as an engineer at Huayue Microelectronics (1984-1990), then spent seven years trading in the Shenzhen electronics market before founding Shenzhen Tianguang Microelectronics in 1997 - the forerunner of Qipai.
notes: Bai Ying (listed as co-holder) also worked at Huayue Microelectronics and the Shenzhen electronics market and is a Qipai director. IR email is the board secretary's (Wen Zhengguo). Small-cap; Hurun listing only in 2021.

name: Bai Ying
current_role: Non-independent Director, China Chippacking Technology (Qipai Technology, 688216.SH); director of its Hong Kong subsidiary
profile: Bai Ying co-controls Shenzhen-founded China Chippacking Technology (气派科技) with husband Liang Dazhong (chairman/GM). It is one of South China's largest domestic IC packaging-and-test firms and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. She has been a director since 2013.
interesting_fact: Qipai defined its own chip package formats (Qipai and CPC series, and CDFN/CQFN) that shrink traditional DIP/SOP/SOT packages, and developed plastic packaging for GaN RF power amplifiers used in 5G MIMO base stations.
deep_cut_fact: Her chip career began in September 1983 at Huayue Microelectronics, where she worked until 1992 (her husband was an engineer there too) before the couple moved into sales in Shenzhen's electronics market and later founded their own packaging businesses.
notes: Low profile; husband Liang Dazhong is the public face. Company board secretary: Wen Zhengguo. Wealth is shared with Liang Dazhong. Contacts sourced from Eastmoney's F10 company data (exchange-filed info).

name: Tan Guanghua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou Raycloud Technology (光云科技, SSE STAR: 688365)
profile: A Central South University software-engineering graduate (class of 2004) and ex-Alibaba software engineer (2008-09), Tan Guanghua co-founded Raycloud in 2009 as one of China's first e-commerce SaaS vendors. Its tools (Chaoji Dianzhang, Kuaidi Zhushou, Kuaimai ERP) serve 4M+ merchants on Taobao, Tmall, JD, Pinduoduo and Douyin, and it is building DingTalk-based enterprise SaaS.
interesting_fact: When Raycloud listed on 29 April 2020 it was the 100th company on Shanghai's STAR Market, billed as A-shares' first e-commerce SaaS stock, and at 35 Tan became the STAR Market's youngest chairman.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2015, years before the IPO, his company gave RMB 1 million to his alma mater Central South University to set up the 'Raycloud Fund' at its School of Software, backing students in tech competitions and entrepreneurship.
notes: Only on Hurun lists in 2021; wealth now likely below the original threshold. IR email from company filings (via Eastmoney F10); board secretary Liu Yu.

name: Gary L. Carano
current_role: Executive Chairman of the Board, Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (Nasdaq: CZR), since July 2020
profile: Reno casino-family executive (age ~64) who ran Eldorado Resorts as CEO and chairman from 2014, then became Executive Chairman of Caesars Entertainment when Eldorado combined with Caesars in July 2020. He is also President of Recreational Enterprises Inc., the family holding company that partly owns G PEG I, operator of six casinos in Reno and Carson City.
interesting_fact: Before leading the public company, he was President and COO of Eldorado Resorts LLC (2004-2014); the Reno family business he helped build ended up acquiring Caesars, the largest US casino operator, with Carano as executive chairman.
deep_cut_fact: He was the General Manager and CEO of Reno's Silver Legacy Resort Casino from its opening in 1995 until September 2014, nearly two decades running a single property before the Caesars era.
notes: Media contact (Kate Whiteley) and IR contact (Brian Agnew) are as published in Caesars' Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Ex. 99.1). Carl Icahn's funds secured two board seats in March 2025. He has served on several Nevada charitable boards.

name: Pan Qi (潘琦)
current_role: Shareholder and ultimate controller of Yinhe Tiancheng Group (银河天成集团), Beihai, Guangxi (per last available filings)
profile: Pan Qi built the Beihai-based Yinhe (Galaxy) group, which spanned power transmission and distribution equipment and biotech; through it he controlled listed Beihai Yinhe Biological Industry Investment (000806, formerly Yinhe Technology) and Guizhou Changzheng Tiancheng Holding. He appeared on Hurun China lists 2005-2017.
interesting_fact: Its listed flagship combined a power-equipment arm making large transformers (up to 330kV, incl. rectifier transformers for metal smelters) with biomedicine, which it named as its strategic transformation direction.
notes: Caution: the group fell into financial distress; filings from 2019 record court enforcement against Pan Qi and the group, and 000806 has since been delisted ('银河退'). Wealth figure is stale (last Hurun 2017). No current contact channel; likely not a suitable outreach target.

name: Xing Libin
profile: Deceased. Xing Libin, the former coal magnate of Liulin, Shanxi, who controlled Liansheng Energy/Group, died in Shanghai in January 2023, according to Jiemian News. Liansheng filed for bankruptcy restructuring in 2013 and was reorganised as Jinliu Energy.
notes: Died January 2023 in Shanghai (source: https://m.jiemian.com/article/11268445.html). His former company was restructured as Jinliu Energy, and the remaining coverage is mostly negative (bankruptcy, detention, litigation). Not a podcast candidate.

name: Rui Fubin
current_role: Chairman and President, Jiangnan Group (江南集團), power-cable maker based in Guanlin, Yixing, Jiangsu (status after 2023 privatisation not re-verified)
profile: Founder-chairman of Jiangnan Group, which designs, makes and sells power cables and electrical-equipment wires from Yixing's Guanlin town, a Chinese cable-making hub. He took the company public on the Hong Kong main board in April 2012 (raising roughly HK$546-789M) and later led its privatisation, with the shares delisted on 23 May 2023.
interesting_fact: Jiangnan Group listed in Hong Kong in April 2012 and was taken private again 11 years later, delisting in May 2023 - putting a major Chinese grid-cable supplier back under founder control.
notes: Relevant to energy/grid angle (power cables). Company now private; website sits behind bot protection and no published contact was found. Web search budget exhausted, so only Wikipedia was checked.

name: Song Yuqing
current_role: Founder of Zhongdeng Group (中登集团), Xi'an; formally exited the group's shareholding and board in 2015 but reported to still run it; current status unclear
profile: Song Yuqing (宋玉庆, b. c.1960-62, Nantong, Jiangsu) started in petrochemicals and moved Zhongdeng into Xi'an real estate in 2001, building a 'petrochemicals + property' group that later spread into finance, tourism and film. A Hurun regular 2009-2015 and often in Shaanxi's top ten, he saw the group hit a debt crisis after taking on four urban-village redevelopment projects.
interesting_fact: Zhongdeng's first big Xi'an move was winning a 71-mu plot in the Economic & Technological Development Zone at auction in 2003 for RMB98m, billed then as 'the north city's first auction'; it became the Zhongdeng Jiayuan estate.
notes: Sensitive: NBD (Nov 2018) reports Zhongdeng became a court-listed defaulter (30+ enforcement cases, >RMB2bn) and Xi'an Intermediate Court searched its HQ in Oct 2018; in 2015 Song and family transferred group shares to his brother Song Yu (88%) and Shen Weiding (12%). Wealth likely much reduced. Searches found no recent (post-2018) news or official contact. Avoid as outreach target or approach with care.

name: Xun Jianhua
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of EGing PV (亿晶光电, 600537.SH); co-controller with family of Huayao PV (华耀光电)
profile: Xun Jianhua (荀建华, b. 1962) founded Changzhou-based EGing Photovoltaic in 2003, building an integrated wafer-cell-module chain and taking it public via a 2011 backdoor listing billed as one of the first A-share solar plays. He sold control in 2017 to Shenzhen property developer Gu Yaoming for a reported ~3bn yuan; his family now runs solar maker Huayao PV.
interesting_fact: He entered solar after China's 2001 'Brightness Program' rural electrification push, putting in 30m yuan in 2003 to found EGing, which added wafer (2005), cell (2006) and module (2007) lines in quick succession.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he took over a struggling local enterprise, overhauled its equipment, talent and products, and grew annual sales to nearly 100m yuan by 1999, earning a local reputation as a turnaround 'nengren' (go-getter).
notes: Off Hurun lists since 2017. Alive status not explicitly confirmed (no reports of death; family co-controls Huayao PV per its 2023 ChiNext prospectus, which named him a co-controller). Was publicly reprimanded by regulators in 2018 over EGing disclosures; avoid. No published personal/office contact found.

name: Zhong Cong
profile: Listed by Hurun China 2014–2017 as 钟葱, with wealth from 'King1' (gold products). That matches Beijing King1 Culture (金一文化, SZSE: 002721), a gold and jewellery company, but his role and current status could not be verified before the web-search quota ran out.
notes: Unverified. He has been off the Hurun list since 2017, and King1's control reportedly changed hands later. Check his current status before any outreach. Low priority.

name: Zhu Danfeng
current_role: Exercises the shareholder rights over Qiu Yibo's 26.19% stake in Zhejiang Hengyi Group (controlling holder of Hengyi Petrochemical, SZSE 000703); her family controls Hangzhou Xiaoshan Hehe Textile
profile: Zhu Danfeng (朱丹凤) is part of the Qiu family circle behind Hengyi, the Hangzhou polyester-to-refining group founded by Qiu Jianlin. Hengyi filings state that Qiu Yibo (Qiu Jianlin's son, now Hengyi Petrochemical chairman) assigned the rights of his 26.19% Hengyi Group stake to her, which is why Hurun's 2010-2012 lists showed the wealth jointly under her and Qiu Yibo.
interesting_fact: Hengyi Petrochemical classes Hangzhou Xiaoshan Hehe Textile, controlled by Zhu Danfeng and her family, as a related party precisely because she votes Qiu Yibo's 26.19% Hengyi Group stake; the textile firm has bought polyester from Hengyi.
notes: Confirmed via Hengyi Petrochemical 2020 bond prospectus (cninfo). Her exact family relationship to Qiu Jianlin/Qiu Yibo is not stated in filings (likely close family, not verified - don't assume). No public profile. The relevant outreach target is Qiu Yibo (Hengyi Petrochemical chairman) via the company IR email.

name: Dong Li
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Executive Director, Leoch International Technology (HKEX: 842)
profile: Dong Li founded Shenzhen-born battery maker Leoch in 1999 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2010. Leoch is China's top lead-acid battery exporter (100+ countries, ~$1.4B+ turnover) and has added lithium and energy-storage products for telecom, data-centre and grid use; he was re-elected executive director in 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he announced a 4GW/yr lithium battery factory in Anhui aimed partly at telecoms and data centres, while backing bipolar lead technology via US startup Gridtential - insisting lithium 'will not kill lead.'
deep_cut_fact: At the gala of Leoch's first Global Battery Innovation Conference in Zhaoqing (Oct 2024, 1,500+ attendees) he surprised delegates by singing 'Auld Lang Syne' on stage, as reported by Batteries International.
notes: Strong fit for energy/data-center podcast (data-centre UPS batteries, UL 9540 energy storage). Frequent speaker at industry conferences (Asian Battery Conference, BCI) - conference organisers are a good route. enquiry@leoch.com is the general company enquiry address; IR site leochir.com.

profile: Guo Jinlin (郭金林; Hurun romanises it 'Guo Jinglin') and his brother Guo Jindong built Nanjing Gpro (Jinpu) Group, with interests in petrochemicals, titanium dioxide (listed Gpro Titanium) and real estate. notes: Could not identify which 'Kunlun' entity this is (many unrelated Chinese firms use the name). Needs Chinese business-registry lookup (e.g. Qichacha) to confirm; no public contacts found.

name: Ye Jian
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2014-2021 (with Ye Zhehua) with wealth from 'Kunlun' in real estate and investment (~US$470m). Searches could not tie this name to a specific Kunlun-branded company; there are several unrelated Kunlun groups (Kunlun Tech, Kunlun Energy, etc.).
notes: Identity not confirmed: the Kunlun entity behind this Hurun listing could not be identified; do not assume a link to Kunlun Tech or Kunlun Energy. No public contacts found.

name: Hu Zuliu
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Primavera Capital Group; non-executive chairman, Yum China
profile: Fred Hu Zuliu is a Harvard-trained economist who worked at the IMF, then became Goldman Sachs' Partner and Chairman of Greater China. In 2010 he founded Primavera Capital, an Asia growth-equity firm that backed Alibaba, Ant Group, ByteDance, Kuaishou, Xpeng and Yum China; he still runs it and chairs its investment committee.
interesting_fact: Primavera initiated or led investments in Alibaba, Cainiao, Ant Group, Yum China, ByteDance, Xpeng, Kuaishou and SenseTime; Hu also sits on the boards of UBS Group and ICBC.
deep_cut_fact: Before economics he trained as an engineer, earning a Master in Engineering Science at Tsinghua before his Harvard PhD; he is also a trustee of Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study and co-chairs The Nature Conservancy's Asia Pacific Council.
notes: Frequent speaker at WEF, Milken and HKU AsiaGlobal events; conference circuit is a natural route. Writes WEF agenda pieces.

name: Xu Jie
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Phoenix Healthcare Group (now China Resources Medical, HKEX: 1515); current role not publicly reported
profile: Xu Jie (徐捷) founded Phoenix Healthcare, which grew from private hospitals into China's largest private hospital group by beds and visits and listed in Hong Kong in 2013 as the 'first private-hospital stock'. In 2016 China Resources took control; her family vehicle SpeedKey exited and she stepped down as chair. No public role since.
interesting_fact: Phoenix Healthcare's 2013 Hong Kong IPO made it the first listed private-hospital operator from mainland China; it pioneered investing in and managing public and SOE-owned hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Per the 2013 IPO prospectus, she bought the Jilin City Trauma Hospital (吉林市创伤医院) in 1988 and personally served as its legal representative and hospital director until 1995, before investing in hospitals in Dalian and Wuxi and founding Beijing Phoenix in 2007 with RMB45m of her own capital.
notes: Very low public profile since the 2016 China Resources takeover; company contacts (China Resources Medical) no longer represent her. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Huang Mingsong
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (about 24.6%), CSG Smart Science & Technology (科大智能, 300222.SZ), Shanghai
profile: Huang Mingsong (黄明松), born 1971, holds a master's degree. He leads CSG Smart Science & Technology, founded in Shanghai in 2002 with links to the University of Science and Technology of China. Listed in 2011, it makes smart power-distribution automation, EV charging and energy management systems, industrial robots and logistics automation; JD Logistics is a strategic investor.
interesting_fact: CSG Smart combines grid tech (distribution automation, EV energy management) with industrial robots and logistics automation; JD Logistics invested about RMB 618m as a strategic investor in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before scaling CSG Smart he ran a cluster of USTC-linked ventures, including Anhui Keda Luneng Technology and Anhui Keda Smart Grid Technology. He also sits on the board of the Shanghai Fuke Intelligent Robot Research Institute.
notes: 'CSG Smart' = 科大智能 (not China Southern Grid). A 2026 report says Wang Tingting succeeded him as president (CEO) ahead of a Hong Kong listing application; he remains chairman per the latest board filings we found. IR email is the board-secretary address from the Jan 2025 board-election notice.

name: Huang Ruohong
current_role: Executive Director and Chairman, Redco Properties Group (HKEX: 1622)
profile: Huang Ruohong (Wong Yeuk Hung, 黄若虹) founded Redco Properties, a Shenzhen-headquartered residential developer listed in Hong Kong, and is its controlling shareholder (about 40%). He has chaired the board since March 2017. The company, like many Chinese developers, has been working through a difficult property market.
interesting_fact: He became Redco's board chairman and an executive director in March 2017 in his capacity as controlling shareholder, after building the developer from its Fujian/Jiangxi roots into an HKEX-listed group.
deep_cut_fact: He holds the Hong Kong title of Justice of the Peace (JP), is a member of a national CPPCC committee and serves as vice chairman of the Hong Kong Federation of Fujian Associations.
notes: Known in HK filings as Wong Yeuk Hung. No published IR email found; check latest HKEX annual report for company secretary / IR contact. Avoid referencing the company's debt situation in outreach.

name: Mo Shuming
current_role: Co-founder (and long-time vice chairman) of Guangdong Mingcrown Group, Dongguan
profile: Dongguan-born entrepreneur who co-founded Guangdong Mingcrown Group (名冠集团) in 1994 with Mo Zhiming. The family conglomerate spans construction, real estate, steel/new materials (Huaguan), Xinhui Port logistics, hotels, schools and a golf club; it is now chaired by Mo Guanliang and ranks among Guangdong's top 500 companies.
interesting_fact: Mingcrown is pivoting into culture-tourism: in March 2026 it won Dongguan's first land auction of the year for RMB 730m to build the Mingcrown Oasis theme-park project, and signed a strategic deal with Tencent Cloud in April 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; the group site names him only as co-founder. A 2012 Xinhui district government page called him vice chairman of Mingcrown. Day-to-day leadership is now Mo Guanliang (chairman) and Mo Guanjing (president). Hurun listed him jointly with Yao Hesong. Best route is the group's corporate email.

name: Xia Hua
current_role: Chairwoman, Eve Group (依文集团), Beijing; founder of Eve China Handmade; vice chair, All-China Chamber of Commerce (ACFIC); NPC deputy
profile: Xia Hua (夏华) left a law lectureship at China University of Political Science and Law to found menswear company Eve (依文) in 1994, building it into a leading Chinese menswear brand. She now focuses on Eve China Handmade, which links rural ethnic-minority embroiderers in Guizhou, Yunnan and Sichuan with global fashion through digital pattern libraries and IP licensing.
interesting_fact: Her China Handmade platform works with more than 25,000 rural embroiderers; she cites a Miao artisan, 'Grandma Pan', whose family embroidery business earns over 1.8 million yuan a year.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Eve she quit her teaching post and became a shop-floor salesperson at a Xidan mall in Beijing, becoming its top seller within a month by studying which stores' bags shoppers carried. She later funded an 'Eve Distinguished Professor' fund at her alma mater CUPL (2003).
notes: High-profile public figure in China (NPC deputy, ACFIC vice chair, frequent Xinhua interviewee); best route is via Eve Group corporate office. Hurun listing 'Eve' = 依文.

name: Gong Sheng
current_role: Standing Executive Director and President, Jiangsu Shagang Group (Zhangjiagang)
profile: Gong Sheng is the long-serving president of Jiangsu Shagang Group, China's largest private steelmaker (about 40m tonnes of crude steel in 2023). He took over as president from founder Shen Wenrong in 2011, after serving as vice president, and holds a shareholding in the group. He still runs operations under chairman Shen Bin.
interesting_fact: He succeeded founder Shen Wenrong as Shagang's president in 2011 and has run day-to-day operations of China's biggest private steelmaker for more than a decade.
deep_cut_fact: In October 2026 he personally led a site visit to Shagang's Huaigang special-steel subsidiary, which reflects his hands-on, plant-floor management style.
notes: Low public profile, and there is almost no personal biography online. The best route is the Shagang Group board office (集团董事局 常委办公室) email. Listed arm: Jiangsu Shagang Co (002075.SZ).

name: Wan Jie
current_role: Chairman, Artron Art Group (雅昌文化集团), Shenzhen
profile: Beijing-born (1962) founder-chairman of Artron, set up in Shenzhen in 1993 as a high-end art printer. He expanded it into China's largest art-data and online art portal (artron.net) with bases in Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen. A long-time CPPCC National Committee member, he also served as a vice-president of the Palace Museum Academy.
interesting_fact: Artron grew from fine-art book printing into a digital art database business; in 2022 Wan used his CPPCC proposals to push metaverse and digital-culture infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2014 'Two Sessions' he proposed a national copyright-registration system for Chinese calligraphy and paintings to clean up forgery in the art market.

public_contacts.value: help@artron.net (general Artron portal helpdesk, not personal)

notes: Best route is via Artron Group corporate channels; little English-language coverage. Industry listed as Print but now primarily art data/culture.

name: Zhang Yaping
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shanxi Donghui Energy Group (coal, coking, non-ferrous metals, new materials, cultural tourism)
profile: Shanxi entrepreneur Zhang Yaping (张亚平) started in coal trading and mine acquisitions, then founded Donghui in 2003. It was once China's largest stamp-charged coke producer and now has about 19bn yuan in assets. The group spans coal, non-ferrous metals, new materials and tourism, and holds 7.5% of Shanghai-listed Kexin Development.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Donghui paid A$160M for an Australian copper-gold miner, making it the first private Shanxi company to buy mines overseas. The group has since added Wutai Mountain tourism, a Marriott hotel, EV in-wheel motors and modern agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: Hurun's 2017 business-jet owners report listed him with an Embraer Legacy 650, then the only private jet owned by a Shanxi tycoon. He first built capital as a coal trader and by buying the Dengjiazhuang mine in Liulin county.
notes: Very private; no official group website or press contact found. In June 2026 Shanxi securities regulators fined Donghui's investment arm over undisclosed share buying in Kexin Development. Approach cautiously, in Chinese. Hurun's 'Donghui Coal Coking & Chemicals' (2010-12) now trades as Shanxi Donghui Energy Group.

name: Chen Jianxing
current_role: Shareholder associated with Wens Foodstuff Group (per Hurun listing); no current public role found
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016-2021) as sharing a Wens Foodstuff fortune with Wen Xiaoqiong, one of the Wen family members named as actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (Guangdong pig and poultry producer). No public filings or press found naming a 陈建兴 in a Wens director or executive role.
interesting_fact: Wens grew from a 'seven households, eight shares' rural partnership in 1983 into a company with thousands of employee-shareholders, after introducing an all-employee shareholding scheme in 1986.
notes: Could not confirm identity or role from public sources; appears to be a passive family shareholder rather than an executive. Contact only via Wens corporate channels (website/IR). Very low public profile.

name: Wen Xiaoqiong
current_role: Member of the Wen family group named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (SZSE: 300498); no executive role disclosed
profile: Wen Xiaoqiong (温小琼) is one of the Wen family members named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group, China's largest hog and broiler producer. Wens was founded by her father Wen Beiying (per press reports) in 1983. She was among the top pre-IPO individual shareholders and is a passive shareholder rather than a manager.
interesting_fact: Wens began in 1983 when Wen Beiying raised 8,000 yuan from seven village families in Xinxing, Guangdong to start a chicken farm; it became China's largest livestock company, listing in Shenzhen in 2015.
notes: Very private; no public profile. Listed among Wens actual controllers in the 2023 annual report. Only route is the Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn). Hurun listing was shared with Chen Jianxing (also a listed controller).

name: Wen Junsheng
current_role: One of the 10 actual controllers (Wen family concert group) of Wens Foodstuff Group (300498.SZ)
profile: Wen Junsheng (温均生) is a member of the founding Wen family behind Wens Foodstuff Group, China's large pig/poultry producer founded by his father Wen Beifen in 1983. He remains on the 10-person actual-controller group named under the family's renewed concert-party agreement (2025), per the company's 2026 interim report.
interesting_fact: Per Jiemian, he is Wen Beifen's eldest son and the father of Wen Jiaolong, the first third-generation family member added as an actual controller and to the Wens board.
notes: No personal profile/executive post found; low public profile. Approach via Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn, tel published 0766-2292926). Alive status not explicitly confirmed, but listed as controller in Aug 2026 filing.

name: Yan Shengjun
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, China Tianying Inc. (000035.SZ)
profile: Yan Shengjun (严圣军) built Tianying from Jiangsu into a listed environmental-energy group (China Tianying, Shenzhen-listed) focused on waste-to-energy incineration, sludge and food-waste treatment. Under him it has pivoted into new energy, licensing Energy Vault's technology to build a 25MW/100MWh gravity energy storage plant in Rudong, Jiangsu, connected to the grid in 2024.
interesting_fact: China Tianying's Rudong plant is billed as the world's first commercial-scale gravity battery: cranes lift composite blocks made partly from waste (soil, coal ash, fibreglass from retired wind blades) when power is cheap and lower them to generate power later.
deep_cut_fact: At the March 2022 groundbreaking Yan said the project would help Rudong become a Yangtze Delta 'zero-carbon industrial centre'; Tianying's deal with Rudong county also covers tidal-flat solar, offshore wind, hydrogen and a zero-carbon data centre.
notes: Strong energy/data-center fit (gravity storage, zero-carbon data centre plans). Low personal media profile; no personal channels found. Company site ctyi.com.cn was unreachable from here; route via China Tianying IR / board office. Hurun listed wealth jointly with Mao Hongju.

name: Mao Hongju
current_role: Director and Vice President, China Tianying Inc. (SZSE: 000035), Hai'an, Jiangsu; joint actual controller with husband Yan Shengjun
profile: Mao Hongju (b. 1968) and husband Yan Shengjun, the chairman, control China Tianying via two Nantong holding companies. Tianying grew from waste-to-energy and environmental services into a 2014 reverse-merger listing spanning wind, solar, green hydrogen/ammonia and gravity storage. She has been a director and VP since 2014.
interesting_fact: China Tianying is Energy Vault's partner on the 25 MW/100 MWh gravity energy storage system in Rudong, Jiangsu, next to a wind farm; it was connected to the State Grid in Dec 2023 and billed as the first commercial utility-scale non-pumped-hydro gravity storage plant.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike many founder-spouses listed as passive shareholders, she holds professional titles as a senior engineer and senior economist, and has served as Tianying's vice president since its 2014 listing (per her 2026 board nomination resume).
notes: Husband Yan Shengjun (chairman) is the public face. IR email is that of board secretary Lu Ping as published in the 2026 interim report (securities rep: zhangmma@cnty.cn). IR email is the reliable route.

name: Lu Hongping
current_role: Major individual shareholder (~2.35% at end-2025) of GoodWe Technologies (688390.SH); controller of Kunshan-based precision-electronics firms
profile: Lu Hongping (卢红萍, b. 1969) is a passive top-10 shareholder of GoodWe, the Suzhou maker of solar inverters and energy-storage systems founded in 2010. Her stake came largely from husband Tu Haiwen, one of GoodWe's five founding shareholders, who transferred his 8.76m shares to her in 2018. She also controls precision-electronics and investment firms in Kunshan and Shenzhen.
interesting_fact: GoodWe was set up in November 2010 by five individuals including chairman Huang Min and Tu Haiwen (who put in 4m yuan for 20%), and grew into one of China's leading PV inverter and home energy-storage brands, listing on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond GoodWe, GoodWe's IPO prospectus lists her as actual controller of Kunshan Tianyaze Precision Electronics, Shenzhen Tianyaze Precision Electronics and Anhui Deying Electrical Technology, plus investment vehicles Kunshan Hanzetai and Kunshan Handing.
notes: Not an executive or director of GoodWe; a passive investor with no public profile. GoodWe chairman/CEO Huang Min is the more relevant guest for an energy podcast. She has been reducing her GoodWe stake (sold ~3.6m shares in 2025). Only route found is GoodWe IR.

name: Shen Jie
current_role: Largest shareholder (about 8.75%, about 10.7% with concert party Beijing Hongyu Rongji VC) of Jiangsu Nata Opto-electronic Material Co. (南大光电, SZSE: 300346)
profile: Shen Jie (沈洁) is a pre-IPO investor and the largest shareholder of Nata Opto-electronic, a Jiangsu maker of MO sources, electronic specialty gases (e.g. phosphine/arsine) and ArF photoresists for chipmakers. Nata has no controlling shareholder. She appears to be a passive investor rather than an executive.
interesting_fact: Nata, where she is the top shareholder, said its ArF photoresist was the first domestically made one to pass customer certification (tested on 50nm flash memory, 2020), challenging an import-dominated market.
notes: Very private; no interviews or bio found. Exchange filings (June 2026, https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202606291826547570_1.pdf) confirm her as Nata's largest 5%+ shareholder. Common name, so be careful with other 'Shen Jie's. The company website lists a general inbox, natainfo@natachem.com, which is a company contact, not hers.

name: Zhu Guangping
current_role: Private investor based in Shenzhen; actual controller of Dangtu Xinshi Emerging Industry Fund, an early ~4.25% shareholder of Trina Solar (688599.SH)
profile: Zhu Guangping (朱广平) is a Shenzhen businessman and investor. Trina Solar's 2021 convertible-bond prospectus names him as actual controller of Dangtu Xinshi Emerging Industry Fund, which held about 4.25% of Trina after its 2020 STAR Market listing. That stake explains his single 2021 Hurun listing. Filings link him to duty-free retail, Guowei Electronics, microfinance and food-import companies in Shenzhen.
interesting_fact: His Trina stake came through a private fund, not a solar company. Trina's prospectus lists more than 20 firms he controlled or helped run, from China Duty Free joint ventures in Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Urumqi to Comvita Food (China), the mainland arm of the New Zealand manuka-honey brand.
deep_cut_fact: For years he was listed as the legal representative of Shenzhen China Duty Free Merchandise Co. and Zhuhai China Duty Free Merchandise Co., joint ventures in which state-owned China International Travel Service (now China Tourism Group Duty Free) held 30-50%.
notes: Identity resolved via cninfo filings. Not a Trina executive; he was a financial investor whose fund had sold down to under 5% by 2021. Other filings (Focus Media 2025-26 deal documents) show him as an indirect LP investor via Shenzhen Guangliwei Investment. Very private; no personal or office contact published. Common name: check before outreach. Hurun 2021 entry: 朱广平 | 天合光能 | RMB 3.0bn, rank 2122 (hurun.net). Hurun gives his residence as Changzhou, but the filings link his companies to Shenzhen.

name: Luo Jianqiang
current_role: Chairman & GM of Zhejiang Xinghuo Chemical; chairman of Zibo Zhongda Chemical; majority LP of Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (per 2015 filing)
profile: Luo Jianqiang (骆建强, b. 1965) is a Hangzhou chemicals entrepreneur and investor. He held 61.3% of Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (上海辰祥投资中心), which took 300 million shares (11.89%) in the 2014 court-led rescue of bankrupt Shanghai Chaori Solar.
