Chaori was relaunched under GCL as GCL System Integration (002506.SZ), which explains Hurun's 2015 solar listing.
interesting_fact: His vehicle was the second-biggest investor, after GCL, in the nine-member consortium that rescued Shanghai Chaori Solar. Chaori's March 2014 missed coupon was China's first onshore corporate bond default.
deep_cut_fact: His day job is chemicals, not solar: GCL System's 2015 filing lists him since 2012 as chairman and general manager of Zhejiang Xinghuo Chemical Co. and chairman of Zibo Zhongda Chemical Co. in Shandong.
notes: Resolved via cninfo: Hurun's 'Chenxiang' is 上海辰祥投资中心 (not 晨祥). Chaori default background: https://thediplomat.com/2014/03/its-official-chinas-chaori-defaulted. Other filings show a 骆建强 as a 2011 Joyson Electronics (600699) asset vendor and a shareholder of Haixing (603115); not confirmed as the same man. Private; no published contact.

name: Frank Hurst Lin
current_role: General Partner, DCM (venture capital); independent director of Vipshop; board/major holder positions in 51Talk and GigaCloud
profile: Hurst (Frank) Lin, 林欣禾, co-founded SINA (now Weibo) and served as its COO, then joined VC firm DCM as a general partner in 2006. His investments include Kuaishou, Vipshop, 58.com, GigaCloud (US IPO 2022), QuantaSing and 51Talk; he now focuses on AI and consumer-internet companies, splitting time between the US and Asia.
interesting_fact: SINA, which he co-founded and ran as COO, was the first venture-backed Chinese internet company to go public in the US; he oversaw its global business development and M&A.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in New York City, earned an engineering degree at Dartmouth, worked as an Ernst & Young management consultant in Silicon Valley, and co-founded SINA's predecessor SinaNet in 1995 after his Stanford MBA.
notes: Goes by Hurst Lin professionally (SEC filings: Frank Hurst Lin). Data-center/AI angle: DCM AI investing; GigaCloud is B2B e-commerce logistics. Best route via DCM or LinkedIn.

name: Vitaliy Khomutynnik
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Cascade Investment Fund (Ukraine); President, Ukrainian Golf Federation
profile: Ukrainian entrepreneur and former MP (Verkhovna Rada 2002-2019) from Makiivka who founded Cascade in the 1990s and built holdings in gas production (Ukrnaftoburinnya, JKX Oil & Gas), insurance and agriculture (Kernel stake, Cascade-Agro). Between 2020 and 2023 he exited oil, gas and farmland, and he now runs Cascade as an investor in VC funds, European tech and Kyiv real estate (Respublika Park mall).
interesting_fact: He has pivoted from gas to tech. Cascade sold its JKX Oil & Gas, Ukrnaftoburinnya, Kernel and Cascade-Agro stakes (2020-23) and now invests via Cascade Ventures in funds and startups such as Wefox, McMakler and Discord.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000, at age 24, he served as 'Minister of Fuel and Energy' in Ukraine's Youth Government, years before he owned gas-production assets. He later backed mobile-game startup Playco, which was valued at about $1bn in 2020.
notes: Former Party of Regions/Opposition Bloc MP, often described in the press as an oligarch. He was sanctioned by Russia in 2018 and reportedly lives abroad. I found no published contact for Cascade Investment Fund. cascadeventures.com looks like an unrelated company, so don't use it. Energy angle: a gas-to-venture pivot.

name: Shengwei (Sean) Da
current_role: Chairman & CEO, AMC Robotics Corp. (Nasdaq: AMCI; formerly AlphaVest Acquisition Corp.); Executive Chairman, Kami Vision
profile: Sean Da is a Tsinghua- and UC Davis-trained electrical engineer who ran YI Technology (Xiaomi-ecosystem action/security cameras) as chairman & CEO from 2014 to 2021, then became executive chairman of AI camera firm Kami Vision. He founded AMC Corp. in 2021 and took it public via a SPAC merger with AlphaVest, listing on Nasdaq as AMC Robotics (AMCI) in December 2025; his reported wealth is largely those insider holdings.
interesting_fact: AMC Robotics builds AI security robots, including the Kyro quadruped robot shown at CES and Tokyo Security Show 2026, and the NovaArm system now running in a live warehouse with Sunward Logistics.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a chip designer: a staff design engineer in Analog Devices' Power Management Group (2002-05), then CTO of Rock Semiconductor and engineering director at Intersil, after a PhD in electrical engineering at UC Davis.

public_contacts.value: AMCRoboticsIR@allianceadvisors.com (Alliance Advisors IR - investors and media contact)

notes: Paper wealth from a small-cap de-SPAC (AMCI); actual value volatile. Power-electronics background makes him a plausible fit for an energy/data-center angle. Best route: Alliance Advisors IR/media contact.

name: Alisa Moussaieff
current_role: CEO & Creative Director, Moussaieff Jewellers (London)
profile: Austrian-born Alisa Moussaieff heads Moussaieff Jewellers, the London high-jewellery house she built with her husband Shlomo Moussaieff (d. 2015), known for rare coloured diamonds. She runs it with her daughters, with salons in London, Geneva and Hong Kong, and is regarded as a doyenne of the coloured-diamond trade.
interesting_fact: She married Shlomo Moussaieff in Jerusalem in 1948, two weeks before he was taken captive for a year during the Arab-Israeli war; together they built a gem business and he amassed one of the largest private collections of Biblical-era antiquities (~60,000 artefacts).
deep_cut_fact: Jewellery historian Vivienne Becker traces the Moussaieff family's gem-dealing lineage roughly 800 years back to Bukhara, the Silk Road city of gem merchants; Becker called Alisa the 'matriarch' of the global diamond industry.
notes: Very private; seldom seeks publicity (per Phillips). Best route is the house's published press contact. She is likely in her 90s; no death report found, but confirm before outreach. Mother of Dorrit Moussaieff (former First Lady of Iceland).

name: Michael J. Angelakis
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Atairos (private investment firm he founded with Comcast backing)
profile: Former Comcast Vice Chairman & CFO (joined 2007 from Providence Equity; earlier CEO of State Cable TV and Aurora Telecom, banker at Manufacturers Hanover). Founded Atairos in 2015/16 to provide long-term strategic capital. Director at ExxonMobil, American Express (since Mar 2025), Clarivate, TriNet and Lucky Strike Entertainment.
interesting_fact: Named 'Best CFO in Media' on Institutional Investor's 2013 All-America Executive Team while Comcast CFO; also sits on the ExxonMobil board (energy angle for the podcast).
deep_cut_fact: Served on the national board of directors of Big Brothers Big Sisters of America, with which Comcast ran a mentoring initiative; a Babson College grad who spent years in London building Manufacturers Hanover's acquisition-finance business.
notes: Best route is Atairos media contact at FGS Global. Babson/London detail sourced from wict.org/littlesis bios as well.

name: Charles A Davis
current_role: Chairman and Co-CEO, Stone Point Capital; Chair of the Board, BETA Technologies (since Feb 2021); director, Progressive Corp.
profile: Chuck Davis spent 23 years at Goldman Sachs (head of investment banking services worldwide, general partner) and was vice chairman of Marsh & McLennan before founding Stone Point Capital in 1998, a financial-services-focused investor with $65bn+ AUM. He chairs Vermont electric-aircraft maker BETA Technologies and has been a Progressive director since 1996.
interesting_fact: He chairs BETA Technologies, the Vermont electric aircraft and charging-network company, and was previously chairman of The Hershey Company's board.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Vermont graduate, he served on the board of Vermont's Merchants Bancshares from 1985 to 2008 and is credited as chief architect of Stone Point's 'Elephant Process' investment philosophy.
notes: Strong fit for energy/aviation electrification angle via BETA. Also on AXIS Capital and Fibrolamellar Cancer Foundation boards (Stone Point bio).

name: Thomas E Gottwald
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, NewMarket Corporation (NYSE: NEU), Richmond, Virginia
profile: Thomas E. 'Teddy' Gottwald is third-generation leader of the Gottwald family's Richmond chemicals business. He joined Ethyl in 1984, became NewMarket president/CEO in 2004 and chairman in 2014, succeeding his father Bruce. NewMarket owns Afton Chemical (petroleum additives) and in 2025 bought Calca Solutions, a maker of aerospace/defense propellants.
interesting_fact: His grandfather Floyd D. Gottwald Sr. ran Albemarle Paper, which in 1962 bought the much larger Ethyl Gasoline company, a famous early leveraged deal. Ethyl later became NewMarket.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Virginia Military Institute graduate and a former rector of VMI's Board of Visitors. He also chairs VMI's Jackson-Hope Board of Overseers.
notes: Low-profile CEO. Best route is NewMarket Corporate Communications in Richmond. The Calca propellants deal and the additives business are natural energy-podcast angles.

name: Gert-Rudolf Flick
current_role: Private investor, art historian and collector; visiting professor in the history of art, University of Buckingham (as of 2019)
profile: Grandson of German industrialist Friedrich Flick, born 1943; holds a law doctorate from LMU Munich. Joined the Flick firm in 1971 and, with his siblings, sold his stake in 1975, the source of his wealth. Since then he has lived in London as an art historian, author and collector of Italian old masters and vedute.
interesting_fact: He was publisher of Apollo, the London fine-art magazine, in the 1990s, and kept a collection of early silver and Italian vedute, including a Canaletto of fireworks over Venice, at Park House, Kensington.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote 'Missing Masterpieces: Lost Works of Art 1450-1900' (2003), a study of lost artworks, and 'Masters & Pupils' (2008), which traces an 'apostolic succession' of teacher-pupil training through European art history.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contacts found. Probably best reached through the University of Buckingham's art history department. Not in energy or data centres, so a weak fit for the podcast. I could not confirm recent activity, so 'alive' is set to unknown (no death report found). His family history is a sensitive topic.

name: Corinne Flick
current_role: Founder and head of the Convoco Foundation (think tank, Berlin/London/Salzburg); general partner of Vivil GmbH & Co. KG, Offenburg
profile: Dr Corinne Michaela Flick, a lawyer trained at LMU Munich (doctorate 1989), is married to Gert-Rudolf Flick of the Flick industrial dynasty and comes from the family behind Vivil confectionery. She founded the interdisciplinary think tank Convoco in 2004, runs its Salzburg forum, London/Berlin lectures, podcast and the Convoco Edition book series.
interesting_fact: Before founding Convoco she worked as a lawyer at Bertelsmann Buch AG in London and at Amazon.com in Munich; she has also been a general partner of Vivil (Offenburg) since 1998.
deep_cut_fact: The Jewish Museum Berlin gave her its Prize for Understanding and Tolerance (alongside Wolfgang Ischinger); the jury noted that every Convoco topic takes the German Basic Law as its reference point.
notes: Wealth is via the Flick family (husband Gert-Rudolf Flick) and Vivil. Very relevant fit: she hosts a think-tank podcast and her council includes energy-sector figures; approach via Convoco's general inbox.

name: Jonathan Hiscock
current_role: Founder, GSA Capital Partners LLP (London quant hedge fund)
profile: British quant hedge fund manager (b. 1974), Oxford maths graduate. Ran Deutsche Bank's Global Statistical Arbitrage prop-trading team, then spun it out in 2005 as GSA Capital with ~$500m and 15 colleagues. GSA now runs systematic strategies across all asset classes with a team of ~150 and repeated EuroHedge awards; Sunday Times put his wealth at £350m (2019).
interesting_fact: GSA's name literally comes from 'Global Statistical Arbitrage', the Deutsche Bank desk he ran; the Independent said he modelled the firm on idiosyncratic tech outfits like Google rather than traditional finance houses.
deep_cut_fact: When he spun GSA out of Deutsche Bank in Jan 2005, it launched with two funds and ~$500m under management; in 2021 the firm deliberately returned investor capital in its scalable 'alt beta' strategies to refocus on its core.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Pitch via GSA press enquiries; quant/compute angle (systematic trading infrastructure) could fit a data-center theme.

name: Sir Elton John
current_role: Singer-songwriter; founder, Elton John AIDS Foundation; co-owner of Rocket Entertainment
profile: English singer, pianist and composer (born Reginald Dwight, 1947) whose catalogue, touring and Rocket Entertainment business built his fortune. His Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour sold 6m+ tickets over 330 shows (2018-2023); he returned for Rock in Rio (Sept 2026) and two final Mexico City shows in October 2026. He is an EGOT winner and runs the Elton John AIDS Foundation.
interesting_fact: His Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour (2018-2023) sold over six million tickets across 330 shows, ending in Stockholm in July 2023, before he announced two extra 'farewell' shows in Mexico City for October 2026.
deep_cut_fact: At 15 he got his first paid gig as the pub pianist at the Northwood Hills Hotel near Pinner, playing Thursday to Sunday nights; he left Pinner County Grammar School just before his A-levels to pursue music.
notes: Musician rather than entrepreneur/energy figure; best route is the EJAF media office (foundation emails are for the foundation, not him personally) or Rocket Entertainment management.

name: Sir Philip Hulme
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder, Computacenter plc; philanthropist (founder, The Hadley Trust)
profile: Born 1948, Imperial College engineer and Harvard MBA who was a Boston Consulting Group VP before co-founding IT services group Computacenter with Harvard classmate Peter Ogden in 1981. He chaired it 1998-2001 after its LSE flotation and remains a large shareholder; also a substantial shareholder in Dealogic and a major philanthropist.
interesting_fact: After Computacenter's 1998 London flotation he gave much of his share-sale proceeds to charity, and was knighted in 2016 for services to technology and philanthropy.
deep_cut_fact: Before Computacenter he graduated with a first in engineering from Imperial College, went to Harvard Business School on a Harkness Fellowship, and became a Vice-President and Director of Boston Consulting Group in 1979.
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Route likely via The Hadley Trust (his charitable trust) or Computacenter corporate communications (computacenter.com).

name: Charles Odell Schiff
current_role: Director, Cincinnati Financial Corp (CINF); EVP, secretary & treasurer, John J. & Thomas R. Schiff & Co. Inc.
profile: Charles O. 'Charlie' Schiff is a nonindependent director of Cincinnati Financial (since Aug 2020, investment committee) and an executive of John J. & Thomas R. Schiff & Co., the privately owned Cincinnati independent insurance agency bearing the names of CINF's founding-era Schiff family. His wealth reflects a large CINF stake (~1.1M+ shares).
interesting_fact: He joined the CINF board in 2020 as Thomas R. Schiff stepped down under the director age guideline; the company said he would give insight into how CINF serves its primary customer, the independent agent.
deep_cut_fact: A Fordham history graduate (magna cum laude), he has served on the boards of The Children's Theater of Cincinnati and The Cincinnati Observatory, among other local nonprofits.
notes: Low public profile; contacts are Cincinnati Financial corporate (2020 release, may have changed). Insurance industry, not energy-related.

name: Wen Kaifu
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Holitech Technology (合力泰, SZSE: 002217); no current executive role found
profile: Wen Kaifu built Holitech, a Shandong-based maker of touch screens, LCD modules and other display components for smartphones. In 2018 he handed control (via a voting-rights proxy and share transfers) to the state-owned Fujian Electronics & Information Group, which now controls the company.
interesting_fact: Holitech grew into one of China's larger suppliers of touch-display modules for smartphone brands before Fujian Electronics & Information Group took control around 2018.
notes: Not a good outreach target: in June 2026 Holitech disclosed a regulator's preliminary penalty notice naming the company and Wen Kaifu over 2017-2021 financial misreporting, and reports say he faces a lifetime securities-market ban and his shares are judicially frozen (news.10jqka.com.cn/20260901/c679501996.shtml). No personal public channels found.

name: Chai Huijing
profile: Chai Huijing (柴慧京) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2008 to 2018 with real-estate wealth tied to a company listed as 'Guodu' (国都). I could not find any public profile, company page or press coverage to confirm her role or what she is doing now.
notes: Very low public footprint; searches for the exact Chinese name returned nothing relevant. Not the Taiwanese general Chai Hui-chen (柴惠珍). Verify via Chinese corporate registries (Qichacha/Tianyancha) before outreach.

name: Li Qinfu
current_role: Former chairman and major shareholder of Jiulongshan / 九龙山 (SH600555, later renamed HNA Innovation 海航创新); current role unknown
profile: Li Qinfu (李勤夫) built the Jiulongshan (Nine Dragon Hill) resort and real-estate business, listed in Shanghai as 九龙山 (600555), and appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2001-2016. In 2011 he sold a 29.9% stake to HNA-affiliated companies; by 2016 HNA had taken board control and the company was renamed 海航创新. No recent public activity found.
interesting_fact: After selling a 29.9% stake to HNA units in March 2011 (reported value ~RMB1.69bn), he kept about 19% and remained chairman for several years, favouring a real-estate focus while HNA pushed for a tourism-plus-finance platform.
notes: Very low recent profile; most coverage is from 2012-2016 and concerns a control dispute with HNA, so avoid that topic. Country field blank in the input; nationality not confirmed. No published contacts found.

name: Zhang Xinming
current_role: Formerly chairman, Shanxi Jinye Coal Coking Group (山西金业煤焦化集团); no verified current role
profile: Zhang Xinming was chairman of Shanxi Jinye Coal Coking Group and was described as Shanxi's richest energy tycoon, appearing on Hurun China from 2005 to 2010. Reports since 2010 concern legal matters rather than business activity.
notes: Do not approach. Chinese media reported in Oct 2010 that he fled and was wanted by police (https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2010-10-26/400513.html); later reports cite organised-crime allegations. Off rich lists since 2010; current status unverified.

name: Zhang Tongsheng
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, C&U Co., Ltd. (人本股份) and controlling shareholder of C&U Group (人本集团), Wenzhou
profile: Wenzhou entrepreneur who co-founded the Wenzhou Bearing Factory in 1991 with three partners; it became C&U Group, China's largest bearing maker, plus the Renben (人本) supermarket and Shizu retail chains. He controls ~60.8% of the votes of C&U Co., which re-filed for a Shanghai main-board IPO in late 2025.
interesting_fact: C&U has ranked No.1 in China by bearing output and sales every year since 2013 and is described as the only Chinese company in the global top 10 bearing makers; it employs ~19,000 people.
deep_cut_fact: He started the bearing business at age 24 with a junior-middle-school education; the Wenzhou Bearing Factory was registered in July 1991 with RMB 4 million of capital, and he has led it as chairman ever since.
notes: Low public profile; little personal press. Route via C&U corporate office or the IPO sponsor/IR once listed. Bearings for wind turbines/EVs could be an energy angle.

name: Sun Guomin
current_role: Early shareholder of Zhejiang Netsun Co. (生意宝, 002095.SZ); no executive role found
profile: Listed by Hurun alongside Sun Deliang, founder and chairman of Hangzhou-based Netsun (China Chemical Network / 生意宝), a B2B e-commerce pioneer listed in Shenzhen in 2006. Exchange filings show a pre-IPO 5%+ holder named 孙国明 (Sun Guoming), possibly the same person as Hurun's 孙国民, who held 9.25% and sold down to 4.83% by 2014.
interesting_fact: Netsun says it was the first Chinese company to build and run an industry-specific B2B website (ChemNet / China Chemical Network); it listed in Shenzhen in late 2006.
notes: Identity unclear: Hurun's 孙国民 may be a rendering of filings' 孙国明, a passive pre-IPO holder (9.25%, cut to 4.83% by 2014). Their link to Sun Deliang is unconfirmed. The public face of the business is founder-chairman Sun Deliang. Not a good outreach target.

name: Zhou Jianhe
current_role: President, Junefield (Holdings) Ltd (Hong Kong); chairman, Prime Century Investments Ltd (per MarketScreener, undated)
profile: Hong Kong-based businessman (also styled Zhou Chu Jian He) behind Junefield Group, whose interests span Beijing property, hospitality and trade. Was chairman of HKEX-listed Junefield Department Store Group (stock 758), based at Beijing Junefield Plaza on Xuanwumen Wai Street. Appeared on Hurun China lists 2003-2005.
interesting_fact: His group developed Beijing Junefield Plaza on Xuanwumen Wai Street, the PRC base of his HK-listed department-store company in the mid-2000s.
notes: Low public profile; most info from 2005 HKEX filings and aggregator data. No official Junefield website or contacts found. Verify current role via HK Companies Registry.

name: Hong Jiangyou
current_role: Chairman and President, Honz Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (康芝药业, SZSE: 300086), re-elected Dec 2025
profile: Born 1964 in Puning, Guangdong; pharmacy graduate (Guangdong College of Pharmacy, 1988) who left a state pharmacist job in Shenzhen to found Hainan-based Honz Pharmaceutical, a children's-medicine maker listed on ChiNext. He controls ~20% of the company and was re-elected chairman for a three-year term in December 2025.
interesting_fact: He has pitched Honz around a single mission, 'children's great health' (儿童大健康), and has said he won't retire until it is complete; the firm specialises in paediatric drugs.
deep_cut_fact: A keen Go player since university, he chairs the Hainan Provincial Go Culture Promotion Association and says Go's opening stage shapes how he makes business decisions; Honz sponsored a children's Go training camp in Guangzhou.
notes: Also chairs the International Teochew (Chaozhou) Business Federation 21st council and the Hainan overseas-Chinese business federation. Company has been loss-making in 2024-25. Best route: the board secretary (Lin Dexin) through the IR email.

name: Li Shiyong
current_role: Associated with Shandong Ensign Industry (formerly Weifang Ensign), Changle, Weifang; current title not confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2012-2018) for wealth from Ensign, a citric-acid and alcohol producer. Shandong Ensign Industry (named Weifang Ensign until 2020) is reported to be the world's largest citric-acid producer, with ~600,000 t/a capacity and an upgrade planned to 700,000 t/a. Recent annual reports list Li Jian as company head; Li Shiyong's current role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Shandong Ensign has been described as the world's largest citric acid producer, planning to lift capacity from 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes a year.
interesting_fact_source: https://www.cnchemicals.com/Press/91863-Shandong Ensign: Citric acid capacity expansion proposal and refined citric acid project completion.html
notes: Very low public profile; no biography found in English or Chinese web search, and Baidu Baike was not accessible. A 'Shiyong Li' appears as an inventor on Weifang Ensign patents (goodip.io). No published contact or company website found.

name: Luo Weidong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Aurora Mobile Ltd (Nasdaq: JG), Shenzhen
profile: Luo Weidong (Chris Luo) co-founded Shenzhen-based Aurora Mobile (JPush / Jiguang) in 2011 and has been chairman and CEO since May 2012. The mobile developer-services and big-data company, backed by IDG, Fidelity and Goldman Sachs, listed on Nasdaq in 2018; his stake (~30%) is the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: PolyU says Aurora Mobile was the first company of its kind to list on Nasdaq (2018); Luo holds an MPhil in computing from PolyU and won its Outstanding Alumni Award for entrepreneurial achievement in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: During COVID-19, Luo led a research team behind a data platform that PolyU credits with supporting epidemic-containment work in 334 Chinese cities. Before Aurora he was GM of Shenzhen Zhiwo Information Technology (2007-2010).

public_contacts.value: Christensen Advisory - Xiaoyan Su, Xiaoyan.Su@christensencomms.com (IR agency named in Aurora Mobile press releases)

notes: Goes by Chris Luo. Some IR pages list ir@aurora-mobile.com instead of ir@jiguang.cn (company rebranding of IR domain). Named 2025 Greater Bay Area Strategic Emerging Industry Youth Leader (Feb 2026 release).

name: Yang Zhen
current_role: Founder and (per 2024 reports) actual controller of Jiajia Food Group (加加食品, SZSE: 002650); no longer chairman
profile: Yang Zhen (杨振, b. 1962, Ningxiang, Hunan) founded Jiajia soy sauce in 1996 and took it public in 2012 as China's first listed soy-sauce maker, earning the nickname 'soy sauce king'. He later stepped back from management to focus on outside investments; a cousin, Yang Xudong, now chairs the company.
interesting_fact: In 2003 he spent RMB 48m, nearly all of Jiajia's profits from its first seven years, to win CCTV's prime-time 'ad king' slot for two months; revenue hit a record RMB 500m in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he trained at Yiyang Normal College and worked as a Chinese-language teacher. He is credited with inventing the built-in pull-ring soy-sauce bottle cap, and he founded Jiajia in 1996 after Hunan factories turned down his offer to sell the patent for RMB 500k.
notes: Sensitive. Since 2022, Yang and his holding company have repeatedly been listed as debt defaulters, and Jiajia has been ST-flagged over guarantees he arranged. Approach with care, if at all. No personal or office contact published. Go through the Jiajia Food board secretary listed in SZSE filings.

name: Ye Jiahao
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2016-2020) as founder/owner of Qixin Construction; current role not verified
profile: Ye Jiahao (叶家豪) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2016-2020 with wealth attributed to 'Qixin Construction' (construction sector). Web searches in Chinese and English found no public coverage linking him to a specific company, so identity and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Very low public profile; company name 'Qixin' may be a romanisation of 祺鑫/启鑫/奇信 etc. Verify via Chinese business registry (e.g. Qichacha) before outreach.

name: Wang Jinglian
profile: Listed on the 2008 Hurun China Rich List with Jinsheng Group (copper). No reliable online source found linking the name 王景连 to a specific Jinsheng group or role, so identity could not be confirmed.
notes: Could not verify. A copper business called Shandong Jinsheng Nonferrous Group (Linyi) went through a court-supervised restructuring/settlement in 2022-23 (https://www.zhonglun.com/news/trade/15361.html), but no source names Wang Jinglian in connection with it. Treat as unverified; low priority.

name: Luo Lin
current_role: Founder and chairman, Anton Oilfield Services Group (3337.HK)
profile: Petroleum engineer (Southwest Petroleum University; Tsinghua MBA, per MarketScreener) who left a secure job at state-owned CNPC in 1999 to found Anton Oilfield Services in the Tarim Basin. Anton grew into one of China's largest private oilfield-service firms, once dubbed 'China's Halliburton', and listed in Hong Kong in 2007. It now works for international clients in Iraq and elsewhere.
interesting_fact: Caixin reported that Anton was once dubbed 'China's Halliburton' and was a major player during the 'golden decade' of China's petroleum sector.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as an employee of state oil giant CNPC. In 1999 he gave up that 'iron rice bowl' job to start a private company selling services to CNPC itself, one of the first private entrants into China's state-dominated oilfield-services market.
notes: IR email from irasia.com (2015) and a 2011 company release; antonoil.com did not load, so currency is unverified. Hurun listing (2013-14) is old; his stake is now far smaller (~$90M per MarketScreener). Good oilfield-services angle; the 'China's Halliburton' line comes from a sector ups-and-downs piece, so keep framing positive.

name: An Yong
profile: Hurun China listed An Yong (安勇) in 2014-2017 at about $450M, with wealth from 'Tianyu' (coal and property). Searches in Chinese and English could not establish which Tianyu company this is (Shaanxi Tianyu Mineral Industry Group is one candidate) or confirm his role there.
notes: Identity unresolved and no public footprint found. He has not been on Hurun since 2017, possibly because coal-sector wealth fell. Not a viable outreach target without more identifying information.

name: An Mei
current_role: Private investor; former 5%+ shareholder of Beijing Ultrapower Software (神州泰岳, 300002.SZ)
profile: An Mei (安梅) is a private shareholder of Ultrapower, a Beijing IT-operations and software company founded in 1998 and listed on ChiNext in 2009. Her stake (6.47% in 2016) came from a 2013 property-division agreement, and its voting rights were entrusted to chairman Wang Ning. She sold down in 2016-2018 and fell below 5% in June 2018. She has no known operating role.
notes: Private individual, not an entrepreneur or executive, and her wealth derives from a personal settlement. I would not recommend outreach. Her only appearance on a rich list is Hurun China 2015. Not a fit for an entrepreneurship podcast.

name: Sun Jie
current_role: CEO and Director, Trip.com Group (Nasdaq: TCOM; HKEX: 9961)
profile: Jane Jie Sun (孙洁) is the CEO of Trip.com Group (formerly Ctrip), one of the world's largest online travel companies. She was an audit manager at KPMG in Silicon Valley and then head of SEC reporting at Applied Materials. She joined Ctrip as CFO in 2005, became COO in 2012 and has been CEO since November 2016. She is also a director of iQIYI.
interesting_fact: She spent her pre-Ctrip career in Silicon Valley. After five years as a KPMG audit manager there, she ran the SEC and external reporting division at chip-equipment maker Applied Materials from 1997 to 2005.
deep_cut_fact: She did her first two undergraduate years at Peking University before finishing at the University of Florida's Fisher School of Accounting with high honors (1992). In 2010, already a Ctrip executive, she went back to Peking University Law School for an LL.M.
notes: Known in English as Jane Sun. She is a high-profile CEO who speaks often at travel-industry forums (Skift, PATA), which makes conference organisers or Trip.com corporate comms a plausible route. Trip.com press releases now date from Singapore. Data-center angle: Trip.com is a large-scale tech platform.

name: Zhang Zhen
profile: Zhang Zhen (张真) appeared once on the Hurun China Rich List (2017) with wealth attributed to 'Youfu' (investment sector). Searches in Chinese and English found no verifiable profile linking this person to a company named Youfu (友富); the name is very common.
notes: Could not identify which Zhang Zhen this is or the full name of 'Youfu'. Needs the Hurun 2017 list entry (city/company full name) or a corporate-registry lookup before any outreach.

name: Qian Sujin
current_role: Co-founder and largest individual shareholder (5.21%) of Beijing E-Techstar Co., Ltd. (恒实科技, 300513.SZ); no longer chairman
profile: Qian Sujin (钱苏晋) co-founded Beijing E-Techstar (北京恒泰实达) in 2000 and long served as chairman/GM, building it into a digital-energy and IoT solutions provider for power grids, telecoms and smart cities, listed in Shenzhen in 2016. Kang Jinsheng now chairs the company; Qian remains a co-controlling shareholder with Zhang Xiaohong.
interesting_fact: E-Techstar's core business is digitising the power grid and telecom networks: big-data/IoT platforms for utilities, plus smart-energy, smart-city and smart-transport applications - squarely in the energy-data space.

public_contacts.value: huangzijian@techstar.com.cn (board secretary Huang Zijian, company IR contact)

notes: Hurun pairs him with Zhang Xiaohong (co-controller). Wealth now much reduced vs. 2016 listing (5.21% stake, Q3 2026). Relevant to energy/grid-digitisation theme. Low public profile; English-language coverage minimal. Web search budget ran out, so no deep-cut fact was found.

name: Zhang Xiaohong
current_role: Director, Beijing E-Techstar Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300513) (per third-party data)
profile: Listed as a board director of Beijing E-Techstar since 2012 with roughly a 3.6% direct stake (about 11.2M shares). E-Techstar is an IT/software and power-grid information services company; chairman listed as Qian Sujin.
notes: Name is common; match is based on the company name only and the modest stake makes the wealth link unclear. Verify in latest E-Techstar annual report before outreach.

name: Liang Jianhua
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Super Telecom Co., Ltd. (SH:603322; renamed 超讯科技 in June 2026)
profile: Liang Jianhua (b. 1969), a senior engineer, founded Guangzhou Super Telecom in 1998 to build, maintain and optimise telecom networks; it listed in Shanghai in 2016. He has chaired the board since 2011 and holds about 20% of the shares; the company was renamed Super Telecom Technology (超讯科技) in 2026.
interesting_fact: He is president of the Guangzhou Software Association and a Standing Committee member of the Tianhe District People's Congress.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1992 as an engineer at the Ministry of Posts & Telecommunications' Guangzhou Communications Equipment Factory, then spent 1995-98 at the Guangdong Posts & Telecom Technology Research Institute before founding Super Telecom.
notes: Board-office email is the published route. Relevant to podcast: telecom network infrastructure; check recent 2026 filings for new business lines after the rename.

name: Zhu Xiande
current_role: Listed with Deng Yingping as owner of 三德控股 (Sande Holdings; medical services and internet finance) on the Hurun China list (2016). Current role not verified.
profile: Zhu Xiande (朱先德) appeared on the 2016 Hurun China Rich List with an estimated $450M, shared with Deng Yingping, from 三德控股 (Sande Holdings), a group active in medical services and internet finance. No accessible sources confirm further details about the company or his current activities.
notes: Appeared on Hurun only once (2016). No verifiable English or Chinese sources were found (Baidu Baike was blocked). Treat identity as unconfirmed.

name: Deng Yingping
profile: Hurun China 2016 lists Deng Yingping (邓应平) with Zhu Xiande (朱宪德) as the source of wealth behind '三德控股' (Sande Holdings), in medical services and internet finance. Searches found no reliable public record that identifies this person or company.
notes: Could not identify. Searches returned a namesake ophthalmology professor at West China Hospital (Sichuan), and nothing links him to Sande Holdings, so do not use that. Appeared on Hurun only once (2016). Business-registry research in China would be needed to identify this person.

name: Dmitriy Zaporozhets
current_role: GitLab co-founder; left his Engineering Fellow role in Nov 2021; describes himself as a software developer (no confirmed current executive role)
profile: Kharkiv-born engineer who wrote the first version of GitLab in October 2011 as an open-source, self-hostable GitHub alternative with Valery Sizov, then co-founded GitLab Inc. with Sid Sijbrandij (CTO, later Engineering Fellow). He rang the Nasdaq bell at the October 2021 IPO and stepped away a month later, having fulfilled his 10-year commitment.
interesting_fact: The GitLab name was an accident: he and Valery Sizov were hunting for a cheap short 'git' domain and found gitlabhq.com for sale for $12.
deep_cut_fact: He studied computer-aided diagnosis of motor vehicles at Kharkiv National Automobile and Highway University, hoping to design cars, and taught himself C by writing a clone of two levels of Mario for Windows.
notes: Low-key engineer, not a media personality; he publishes his own email on his personal site, so a direct, technical note is the best route. Spells his name Dmytro in recent profiles.

name: Deepak Babani
current_role: Managing Director, Satguru Holdings Ltd (Dubai real-estate developer); former Executive Vice Chairman/CEO, Eros Group (Dubai)
profile: Dubai-based Indian executive who spent ~43 years at Eros Group, the UAE electronics/consumer-tech distributor and retailer (a major Samsung distributor), rising to CEO and Executive Vice Chairman. Left at end-2021 and now develops residential property in Dubai via Satguru Holdings, starting with a G+14 tower in Al Furjan.
interesting_fact: He says he is not actually a shareholder of Eros despite the common assumption; he built the business as its long-time executive, including a Huawei partnership creating the 'IdeaHub' B2B device destination.
deep_cut_fact: He landed in the UAE in April 1978 aged 27, got his first job (assistant manager at Jumbo Electronics) via a walk-in interview at a starting salary of Dh2,000/month; his favourite book is 'Buffett: The Making of an American Capitalist'.
notes: Listing says 'Eros / Media & Entertainment' (Hurun India 2015), which could be confused with Eros International (Lulla family, films). This Deepak Babani is Eros Group Dubai (electronics); he has publicly said he is not an Eros shareholder, so the wealth attribution is uncertain. Featured in Entrepreneur ME 'The 100 NRIs 2026'.

name: Nick Leslau
current_role: Partner, Prestbury Capital Partners Ltd; chairman/CEO, Prestbury Investment Holdings (London)
profile: London commercial property investor (b. 1959, Cricklewood) who built Burford Holdings with Nigel Wray, then Prestbury Group, Max Property Group (sold to Blackstone 2014) and Secure Income REIT (Travelodge hotels, private hospitals, theme-park freeholds), which merged with LXI REIT in 2022. He now runs Prestbury Capital Partners with long-time partners Ben Walford and Sandy Gumm.
interesting_fact: Secure Income REIT, his long-income vehicle listed in 2014, owned 20 private hospitals and 55 Travelodge hotels before its 2022 merger with LXI REIT at a 16.5% average annual return.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of a German degree at Warwick to study quantity surveying, qualified as a chartered surveyor, and became CEO of Burford Estate & Property at just 23.
notes: Low media profile but gave an FT 'My money' interview (2015). Prestbury's general enquiries inbox is the published route.

name: Paul Day
current_role: Owner and head of Turners (Soham) Ltd, haulage, warehousing and property group, Newmarket, Suffolk
profile: Paul Edwin Day runs Turners (Soham), the family haulage and logistics business founded in 1930 by his grandfather Wallace Turner and great-uncle Frank. Under him it grew into one of the UK's largest privately owned hauliers (about 1,000 trucks, temperature-controlled warehousing, tankers) with a sizeable property portfolio, all headquartered on a 40-acre site in Newmarket.
interesting_fact: Turners' Newmarket HQ holds 500,000 sq ft of temperature-controlled storage for 80,000 pallets; in 2010 it bought container haulier Dart Distribution.
deep_cut_fact: He is a former national table tennis champion and England international; his parents built a table tennis facility in their grounds for him where the Soham team played home premier-division matches. He also chairs the Soham and District Sports Association charity.
notes: Very private family-business owner; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Turners (Soham) head office contact page. Name is common: confirmed via Turners website ('Wallace Turner's grandson, Paul Day') and Companies House (Paul Edwin Day).

name: Peter Dawson
profile: Most likely Peter Michael Dawson (1938-2024), executive chairman and owner of Dawsongroup, the UK truck/trailer/equipment rental group grown from his father Ted's one-lorry Leighton Buzzard haulage firm (1935). He launched Dawsonrentals in 1974. He died in 2024 after a short illness.
interesting_fact: In 1994 Commercial Motor reported he topped the Sunday Times list of richest truck-industry figures, owning 75% of Dawsongroup, then valued at £100m.
notes: Deceased (2024), source: https://dawsongroup.co.uk/peter-michael-dawson-1938-2024/ . Identity inferred from 'Transport' + UK Rich List; Dawsongroup is the only UK transport Peter Dawson with Rich List coverage found.

name: Sir Martyn Arbib
current_role: Founder of Perpetual (now Invesco); philanthropist via the Arbib Foundation
profile: Sir Martyn Arbib (b. 1939, Hendon) founded fund manager Perpetual in 1973 in a small office on Hart Street, Henley-on-Thames, and sold it to AMVESCAP in 2001 for over £1bn; it became Invesco Perpetual. He left Perpetual's board in 2015 and focuses on philanthropy through the Arbib Foundation (est. 1987), which sponsors schools in Slough including Langley Academy.
interesting_fact: He was knighted in 2003 for services to charity, especially education; his foundation sponsors academies in Slough including The Langley Academy.
deep_cut_fact: His 1994 backing of Henley's River and Rowing Museum was what allowed the founders to commission architect David Chipperfield for the building, which opened in 1998 (and later won a Royal Fine Art Commission Building of the Year award).
notes: Very private, now in his late 80s; no personal website or social accounts found. Alive status assumed (no death notice found). The River and Rowing Museum closed in September 2025, so avoid framing it as current. Best route is likely via the Arbib Foundation (registered charity) or Langley Academy.

name: Steve Parkin
current_role: Founder and former executive chairman of Clipper Logistics (sold to GXO in 2022); private investor through Knaresborough Investments
profile: Leeds entrepreneur who left school at 16 and founded Clipper Group in 1992. He built it into a listed e-commerce and retail logistics firm (LSE IPO 2014) serving retailers such as John Lewis. GXO Logistics bought Clipper for about £965m in 2022, netting Parkin over £100m in cash plus GXO shares. He now invests privately in Yorkshire businesses.
interesting_fact: Clipper began in 1992 with a single van delivering clothing to fashion stores. Thirty years later it sold for roughly £965m.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 his private-equity vehicle Knaresborough Investments took a 25% stake in a small Leeds electric-heating business. He likened it to Clipper in its early days.
notes: Not to be confused with David Parkin (Yorkshire business journalist with a Substack). Clipper was a Leeds United sponsor and Parkin is a known Leeds fan. He is also reported to own racehorses, but I could not open a source to confirm it. No published personal or office contact found; Clipper is now part of GXO, so its press office is no longer relevant. Best route is probably Yorkshire business networks.

name: The Queen
profile: Queen Elizabeth II, UK head of state 1952-2022, listed on the Sunday Times Rich List 2020. She died on 8 September 2022 at Balmoral.
notes: Deceased 8 Sep 2022 (source: https://www.royal.uk/her-majesty-the-queen). Skip for outreach.

name: Howard S Jonas
current_role: Chairman, IDT Corp; Chairman, Genie Energy; Executive Chairman, CEO & President, Rafael Holdings; director, Zedge
profile: Bronx-born serial entrepreneur (b. 1956, Harvard '78) who founded IDT in 1990 as an international call-back service and spun off Genie Energy (retail energy/solar), Zedge, Rafael Holdings and Straight Path (sold to Verizon for $3.1B in 2017). He chairs the group and leads Rafael's pharma efforts.
interesting_fact: He sold Straight Path Communications, a long-struggling spectrum company spun out of IDT, to Verizon for $3.1 billion in 2017 after a bidding war over its 5G-suitable millimeter-wave licenses.
deep_cut_fact: Asked about his first job, he said he had little jobs at the Bronx Zoo and a butcher shop, but his first real 'business' was a hot dog stand he opened at 14 near a local hospital - the origin of his 1998 memoir 'On a Roll: From Hot Dog Buns to High-Tech Billions'.
notes: Author of 'On a Roll' (1998) and 'I'm Not the Boss, I Just Work Here' (2006); generally open to media. Genie Energy is the energy hook (retail power/gas, solar). IDT contact emails are general corporate inboxes.

name: Brian F. Sullivan
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, Celcuity Inc. (Nasdaq: CELC), Minneapolis
profile: Serial Minnesota med-tech founder: co-founded filtration firm Recovery Engineering (sold to P&G for $265M, 1999), then ran Sterilmed (sold to J&J for $330M, 2011). Co-founded Celcuity in 2012, took it public in 2017; in July 2026 the FDA approved its first drug, Revtorpyk (gedatolisib), for advanced HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
interesting_fact: Revtorpyk (approved July 14, 2026) is the first FDA-approved drug to inhibit all class I PI3K isoforms plus mTORC1/mTORC2; in Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 the triplet gave 9.3 months median PFS vs 2.0 months for fulvestrant.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he built a water-filtration business (Recovery Engineering) that he took public and sold to Procter & Gamble; he holds 11 U.S. patents and graduated magna cum laude with distinction in economics from Harvard College.

public_contacts.value: Sam Brown LLC - Laura Morgan, lauramorgan@sambrown.com

notes: Sullivan lists himself as an investor contact in Celcuity press releases (published email). Biotech, not energy, but a strong serial-founder story. Not to be confused with Brian F. Sullivan of Entegris.

name: Dmitry Korzhev
current_role: Non-executive director and major shareholder, O'KEY Group S.A. (Russian grocery retailer, O'KEY hypermarkets / DA! discounters)
profile: St. Petersburg entrepreneur who, with long-time partner Dmitry Troitsky, built car dealer Mega-Avto, then juice maker Multon (sold to Coca-Cola in 2005), and in 2001 co-founded the O'KEY hypermarket chain, floated in London in 2010. He still sits on O'KEY's board and audit and remuneration committees.
interesting_fact: Multon, the juice business he co-founded in 1995 in a workshop of a former defence plant and grew into one of Russia's largest juice makers (Nico brand), was sold to Coca-Cola in 2005 for about $500m.
deep_cut_fact: He and partner Dmitry Troitsky are both graduates of St. Petersburg State Marine Technical University. Their first venture as young partners was Mega-Avto, selling cars from the Volga Automobile Plant (AvtoVAZ/Lada) in St. Petersburg.

public_contacts.value: Natalya.Belyavskaya@market-da.ru (Head of IR, O'KEY Group; tel +7 495 664-40-42)

notes: Input lists industry as 'fashion-retail', but Forbes's Korzhev is the O'KEY grocery co-founder (confirmed on O'KEY's board page). Very low media profile. The only published route is O'KEY's investor relations. Russian business: check sanctions and compliance before outreach.

name: Dmitry Troitsky
current_role: Co-owner and board director, O'KEY Group / DA Group (Russian grocery retail; re-elected to board May 2026)
profile: St Petersburg entrepreneur, Leningrad Shipbuilding Institute graduate, who with longtime partner Dmitry Korzhev co-founded juice maker Multon (sold to Coca-Cola) and in 2001 the O'KEY supermarket chain, listed in London in 2010. After O'KEY sold its hypermarkets in 2025 the group runs the DA! discounter and is being renamed DA Group.
interesting_fact: He and Korzhev built Multon juice plant from 1995 and sold it to Coca-Cola about ten years later for roughly $500m, funding the O'KEY supermarket chain.
deep_cut_fact: He and Korzhev began working together as students; their first venture was selling cars, which became Mega-Auto (1993), one of St Petersburg's largest car dealers.
notes: Low media profile; Russia-based, sanctions/compliance context worth checking before outreach. Board re-election: https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/117810/ . Input lists 'fashion-retail' but he is grocery retail (O'KEY).

name: Prakash P Chhabria
current_role: Executive Chairman, Finolex Industries Ltd (PVC pipes, fittings and resin), Pune
profile: Son of Finolex Group founder Pralhad P. Chhabria (group founded 1958). He joined the Finolex Industries board in 1992 and became Executive Chairman in 2012, building it into one of India's leading PVC pipe brands with a backward-integrated resin plant near Ratnagiri. He also holds a stake in Finolex Cables, the group's original business.
interesting_fact: Finolex Industries is backward-integrated: it runs its own PVC resin plant near Ratnagiri (set up 1994) supplied through an open-sea jetty it operates for raw materials; he is also a director of Pawas Port Ltd.
deep_cut_fact: He studied international business at the University of Evansville in Indiana, USA, and in FY2021-22 received an honorary D.Litt. from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth, Pune, for his contributions to society.
notes: Source_of_wealth says Finolex Cables, but his executive role is at Finolex Industries; Finolex Cables is run by another branch of the family, so avoid conflating them. CSR is via Mukul Madhav Foundation. marcom@ is the company marketing-communications address.

name: Dharam Pal Gulati
profile: Founder/owner and face of MDH spices; died 3 December 2020 in New Delhi aged 97 (post-COVID cardiac arrest).
notes: Deceased 3 Dec 2020 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharampal_Gulati, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/owner-of-mdh-masala-dies-at-97-179362). Business now run by son Rajiv Gulati.

name: Raman Gupta
current_role: Promoter/long-time director of Metenere group (Metenere Limited, Metenere (Global) Ltd), Delhi; MD role at Metenere Limited reportedly ceased Oct 2024
profile: Raman Gupta is the Delhi-based promoter of Metenere, a non-ferrous metals group producing lead, lead alloys and oxides, aluminium products and tin. He has been a director of Metenere Limited since its 1997 incorporation; registry aggregators indicate a board change/amalgamation in Oct 2024. Hurun India listed him in 2017-2018.
interesting_fact: Metenere describes itself as one of India's biggest lead producers and the only producer of pure tin in India.
notes: Very little public coverage; sources are company-registry aggregators (Tofler, Qorpiq). Company website metenere.com appears to be parked/for sale. No published contact found; any outreach would need a verified company channel.

name: Dinesh Kumar Goel
current_role: Founder Chairman & Chief Mentor, FIITJEE Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: D.K. Goel, an IIT Delhi mechanical engineering graduate, founded FIITJEE (Forum for IIT-JEE) in 1992, building it into one of India's largest coaching chains for IIT-JEE and science olympiads, with centres in India, Bahrain and Qatar. Since late 2024 the company has faced centre closures and regulatory investigations.
interesting_fact: FIITJEE's name is an acronym: 'Forum for Indian Institute of Technology - Joint Entrance Examination'; the company was incorporated as FIITJEE Limited in 1997, five years after Goel started it.
notes: Caution: in 2024-25 FIITJEE shut multiple centres; Delhi Police EOW cheating case and Enforcement Directorate raids (April 2025) over student fees, which Goel denies; also a 2024 leaked staff-meeting video. Reputational risk for a podcast guest.

name: Sushil Kumar Kalyanji Parekh
current_role: Promoter-family shareholder of Pidilite Industries; director of family holding companies (e.g., Pidichem, Pargro Investments)
profile: Younger brother of Pidilite founder Balvant Parekh and part of the promoter family that controls Pidilite Industries, maker of Fevicol, M-Seal and Dr. Fixit. He worked with Balvant in the family's early dye and chemicals trading and served as Pidilite's Vice Chairman from 1969 to 2014. He now holds directorships in family investment companies.
interesting_fact: Pidilite's Fevicol, launched in 1959, became so widespread that 'Fevicol' is effectively India's generic word for white glue.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Vice Chairman of Pidilite Industries for 45 years, from 1969 to 2014.
notes: Elderly and very low-profile. No death report found, but there are no recent public appearances, so his status is unconfirmed. Sources disagree on whether he co-founded Pidilite in 1959 or joined early. The Pidilite investor-relations inbox is a company channel, not his own; Narendrakumar and Apurva Parekh are the family's public faces.

name: Maroš Grund
current_role: Senior Research Fellow and Member of the Board, ESET (Bratislava)
profile: Slovak software engineer and co-owner of cybersecurity firm ESET, maker of NOD32 antivirus. He became a co-owner in 2005 alongside Richard Marko and co-authored ESET's new-generation detection engine; he stepped back from day-to-day management in 2011 but remains on the board as Senior Research Fellow.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he and fellow ESET shareholder Peter Kusý bought Bratislava's landmark Carlton Hotel building in a joint venture with developer Erik Mikurčík.
deep_cut_fact: ESET's own 30th-anniversary history credits him (with Richard Marko) as co-author of the new generation of ESET's detection engine, the core of its products.
notes: Low public profile; engineer rather than spokesperson. Best route is via ESET's newsroom/press team. Owners stepping back from daily management in 2011: https://www.virusbulletin.com/blog/2011/01/all-change-top-eset/

name: Colin T. Moran
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Abdiel Capital (Abdiel Capital Advisors, LP), New York
profile: Hedge fund manager who co-founded Abdiel Capital with Geoffrey Gentile in 2006 after stints at Goldman Sachs and as a partner at Chieftain Capital. Abdiel is a concentrated, long-term investor and long-time 10%+ holder of low-code software firm Appian (APPN); in 2025 it also took a ~12% stake in Rise Gold (RYES), which is reviving California's Idaho-Maryland gold mine.
interesting_fact: Abdiel has reported as a 10%+ owner of Appian for years, filing more than 40 amendments to its Schedule 13D on the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before running money he trained as a historian and lawyer: a summa cum laude B.A. in History and Economics from Duke, an MSt in Modern History from Oxford, and a law degree from Stanford Law School (Order of the Coif).
notes: Low-profile investor; no published personal or firm contact email found. Rise Gold stake per Form 3 (Oct 2025): https://www.secform4.com/filings/1424864/0001193125-25-261127.htm. Education details from MarketScreener aggregator; worth double-checking.

name: Cui Lianguo
current_role: Chairman, Inner Mongolia Jiutai Group (last confirmed 2013; current status not verified)
profile: Cui Lianguo (崔连国) heads Jiutai Group, an Inner Mongolia coal-chemicals company producing methanol and downstream materials in Ordos and Hohhot. He appeared on Hurun's China rich list 2009-2020 for the petrochemical business. Little recent English or Chinese coverage of him personally was found.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Jiutai chose GE's high-pressure coal gasification technology to double methanol capacity at its Ordos (Zhungeer Banner) plant to 1.5 million tonnes a year, which Cui pitched as a cheaper, cleaner way to make methanol.
notes: Very low profile; no official website or IR contact found for him (Jiutai Group is unlisted; HK-listed 2798 is a different company, Perennial/Jiutai Bangda coal). Current role and status should be checked before outreach.

name: Keith Kepler
current_role: Vice President (副总经理) & Head of Research Institute, Farasis Energy (Ganzhou) Co. (SSE STAR: 688567); director & CTO of Farasis Energy USA
profile: US battery scientist (b. 1967) who co-founded Farasis Energy in California in 2002 with Yu Wang and served as its CTO; the company moved manufacturing to Ganzhou, China, and became a major pouch-cell supplier for EVs (Daimler/Mercedes was an anchor customer), listing on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He was reappointed VP and head of Farasis' research institute in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Farasis started in Silicon Valley in 2002 and is now a Chinese STAR Market-listed EV battery maker; Kepler is a named inventor on many of its lithium-ion cell patents.
deep_cut_fact: Before Farasis he was a scientist at Argonne National Laboratory (1996-98) and then senior R&D director and scientist at early lithium-ion startup PolyStor Corp (1999-2001); he holds a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
notes: US citizen despite 'China' country tag. In 2025 he and co-founder entities agreed to sell a combined 5% Farasis stake to Guangdong state investors (Hengjian/Guangzhou Industrial). Technical, low-profile; IR route via board secretary Pan Lian.

name: Gao Jinna
current_role: Former major shareholder of Lander Sports Development (莱茵体育, SZSE: 000558, now 天府文旅), acting in concert with Lander Holding Group. No current executive role found.
profile: Gao Jinna (高靖娜) is linked to Hangzhou's Lander (莱茵达) group, founded and chaired by Gao Jisheng, with whom Hurun lists her. In 2012 Lander Holding transferred 100m shares of the listed Lander company (a property developer that later pivoted to sports) to her. Lander Holding sold control to Chengdu Sports Investment Group in 2019, and the company is now Tianfu Cultural Tourism.
interesting_fact: The Lander listed vehicle she held shares in made one of China's more unusual pivots, from Hangzhou property developer to 'Lander Sports Development' (sports venues and events). After its 2019 sale to Chengdu's state sports-investment group it became Tianfu Cultural Tourism.
notes: Private, with no public profile. The listed company is now Chengdu-state-controlled, so its IR inbox is not a route to her. lander.com.cn did not respond. Any approach would go via Lander Holding Group (Hangzhou, chaired by Gao Jisheng), for which I found no published contact. Web search budget was exhausted.

name: Xu Mingbo
current_role: Chairman & general manager, Beijing SL Pharmaceutical Co. (双鹭药业, SZSE: 002038)
profile: Xu Mingbo (徐明波, b. 1964) is a genetic-engineering scientist who co-founded Beijing SL Pharmaceutical, has run it as general manager since December 1994 and later became chairman. The Shenzhen-listed company makes biotech and chemical drugs (recombinant proteins, peptides, generics); his wealth comes from his controlling stake. He still chaired the board through 2025-26.
interesting_fact: Before going into business he was a research group leader at the Academy of Military Medical Sciences, led four national high-tech research projects, published 40+ papers and won a National Science and Technology Progress Award (2nd class).
deep_cut_fact: He earned his PhD at China's Academy of Military Medical Sciences and was described as one of the first young experts in 'mid- and downstream' genetic-engineering process technology trained entirely in China; he also serves on the council of the Chinese Society of Biotechnology.

public_contacts.value: lsj@slpharm.com.cn (board secretary Liang Shujie); securities rep yitingjing@slpharm.com.cn; IR tel +86 10-88627635

notes: Low public profile, Chinese-language only. In May 2026 the SZSE publicly reprimanded the company and Xu over unrecovered trust investments (company blamed alleged embezzlement by a former finance employee) - context to be aware of, sensitive. Best route: board secretary's office.

name: Xu Zhiming
current_role: Chairman, Hong Kong Jiahao (Ka Ho) Group; former chairman and controlling shareholder of Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical (HKEX 346, later Sino Union Energy Investment) (last reported)
profile: Xu Zhiming (许智明), born 1964 in Gaozhou, Guangdong, moved to Hong Kong in the late 1980s and built Jiahao Group in property, finance and trade, then became an oil tycoon via Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical ('Sunpec'), which bought overseas oilfields. In 2009 he bought five coal mines for HK$3.66B, steering it toward coal and chemicals.
interesting_fact: A major poverty-relief donor (over HK$300M per his profile), he was honoured by China Post with a 7-envelope commemorative cover set, 'Xu Zhiming and China's Guangcai poverty relief', and received Hong Kong's Gold Bauhinia Star.
deep_cut_fact: He single-handedly financed the development of Fangji Island (放鸡岛), dubbed the 'Pearl of the South China Sea' off Guangdong, and was awarded an honorary doctorate and the Lomonosov Medal by the Russian Academy of Sciences.
notes: 'Sunpec' appears to be the abbreviation of Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical (中联石化). Little news after ~2010; last on Hurun list 2021. No published contacts found. Former CPPCC national committee member and Hong Kong JP.

name: Shao Jianming
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Highsun Group Co., Ltd. (海印股份; reappointed March 2025)
profile: Shao Jianming (邵建明) founded Guangzhou's Highsun (海印) group in 1991, growing it from a leasing business into theme malls, wholesale markets, shopping centres and urban complexes, with a later push into finance (payments, a rural-bank stake, Huacheng Bank). He is a co-controller with Shao Jianjia (president) and Shao Jiancong.
interesting_fact: Highsun was one of the few privately controlled commercial-property companies listed in Guangzhou (Shenzhen listing 2008) and pioneered themed specialist malls in the city; it also helped found Huacheng Bank (花城银行).
deep_cut_fact: He served as a non-executive director of Guangzhou Rural Commercial Bank from 2009 to 2019.
notes: Company now trades on the NEEQ delisted-securities board ('海印5') and faces regulatory/financial issues; avoid financial topics. Deep-cut fact comes from an aggregator (MarketScreener), so verify it. Not a natural fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Gao Tianle
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Zhejiang Tengen Electrics Co., Ltd. (SHSE: 605066)
profile: Founder-chairman of Tengen (天正电气), founded 1999 in Yueqing, Zhejiang, which makes low-voltage electrical products and industrial control solutions; company listed in Shanghai in 2020.
interesting_fact: Tengen's low-voltage switchgear and power-distribution products sit directly in the power infrastructure chain relevant to energy and data-center build-outs.
notes: Chinese name 高天乐 inferred from romanization. No public personal channels found; route via company IR/board secretary.

name: Chen Guangbiao
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Jiangsu Huangpu Renewable Resources (Nanjing)
profile: Born 1968 to a farming family in Sihong, Jiangsu, Chen trained in Chinese medicine, patented a medical device, then in 2003 found he could profit from reselling steel from a demolition job. That became Jiangsu Huangpu Renewable Resources, a demolition and construction-waste recycling firm. He is best known as a flamboyant, highly publicized philanthropist.
interesting_fact: After the 2008 Sichuan earthquake he arrived early with 100+ staff and 60 excavators and hoists, personally rescued 13 survivors, and was named one of Forbes Asia's 48 leading Asia-Pacific philanthropists in 2008 and 2009.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, at age 10, was selling water in his village, earning about 0.3 yuan a day (nearly half an adult's daily wage at the time); at 13 he moved on to selling frozen food.
notes: Highly media-seeking (stunts like a 2014 bid to buy The New York Times); his philanthropy has been questioned by Chinese media, so vet claims. Last on Hurun lists in 2019. No verified official contact found; he historically courts press via his company in Nanjing. Recycling/demolition is only loosely related to energy.

name: Li Yuping
notes: Hurun China 2009-2017 (real estate, 'Nature'). Could not identify the company or any public record of 厉育平; web-search budget ran out. No facts or contacts recorded.

name: Wang Dafu
current_role: Listed as owner of Visun, a real-estate group, on the Hurun China list (2009-2021). Current role not verified.
profile: Wang Dafu (王大富) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List for over a decade (2009-2021), most recently at about $430M, with wealth attributed to the property group 'Visun'. No accessible English or Chinese source could confirm the company's full name, location or his current role.
notes: Unverifiable from this environment (Baidu Baike blocked, no Wikipedia page). Long Hurun tenure suggests an established regional developer, but treat identity as unconfirmed. Real estate is not a strong podcast fit.

name: Lin Kaiwen
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO (legal representative), Shanghai Kaiquan Pump (Group) Co., Ltd.
profile: Lin Kaiwen (林凯文) founded Shanghai Kaiquan Pump in the mid-1990s; it was registered in July 1996 and is headquartered in Jiading, Shanghai. It grew into one of China's largest private pump groups, designing and making pumps, water-supply equipment and pump control systems. He has been on Hurun's China rich list every year since 2006 and still leads the group.
interesting_fact: Kaiquan sells through its own direct-sales model and has been recognised as a 'National Enterprise Technology Centre', claiming more than 700 technology patents. Large pumps like its products run municipal water, power plants and cooling systems.
notes: Very low media profile; I found no interviews. The company site (kaiquan.com.cn) did not load from here. Note that kaiquan.com is a different, unrelated pump company. Pumps for power plants and cooling are a possible energy/data-centre angle. Data aggregators disagree on the founding year (1995 vs 1996).

name: Wang Chunming
current_role: Founder/controller of Sichuan Guodong Construction Group (Chengdu); former chairman of Guodong Construction (SSE: 600321, now Zhengyuan Co.)
profile: Wang Chunming built Chengdu-based Sichuan Guodong Construction Group and was legal representative and chairman of its listed arm, Sichuan Guodong Construction Co., which IPO'd in Shanghai in 2001. In 2016 Guodong Group agreed to sell control (about RMB 2.5bn at RMB 7/share) to Zhengyuan Real Estate (Fu Yanbin). Guodong Group and an affiliate still held ~22.9% in 2023 as second-largest holder.
interesting_fact: Guodong Construction's March 2001 Shanghai IPO sold 70m shares at RMB 12.28 each (about 28x earnings), lifting its share capital from 105.2m to 175.2m shares.
notes: Very low public profile and little personal coverage; no published personal or office contact found. Control sale source: https://stock.stockstar.com/SS2016101100001192.shtml; 2023 stake: https://paper.cnstock.com/html/2023-04/10/content_1746133.htm. Not an obvious podcast fit.

name: Dai Wei
current_role: Founder, ofo (defunct Beijing dockless bike-sharing company); since COVID has run small US ventures (Seattle power-bank rental; About Time Coffee, New York)
profile: Peking University graduate who co-founded ofo in 2014 with fellow PKU cycling-club members; it pioneered dockless smartphone bike-sharing, raised money from Didi, Xiaomi, Alibaba and DST and became a $1bn+ unicorn by 2017 before collapsing in 2018-19. He has since split time between China and the US, launching a power-bank rental startup in Seattle and the About Time Coffee chain in New York.
interesting_fact: The name 'ofo' was chosen because the word visually resembles a cyclist riding a bicycle; ofo grew from 2,000 bikes on the PKU campus in 2015 to a global unicorn in under two years.
deep_cut_fact: He spent a year as a volunteer teacher in Qinghai Province during his postgraduate studies; the 'ofo' name was reportedly born on 15 Feb 2014 while he was still teaching there. He met co-founders through a PKU Cycling Association outdoor trip.
notes: Sensitive history: ofo's collapse left large unrefunded user deposits and he was placed on China's debtor ('laolai') list; avoid in outreach. No published personal contact; US coffee venture largely wound down per 2023 reports. Was a WEF Young Global Leader-type profile; best route likely via mutual tech/VC contacts.

name: Mo Jianrong
current_role: Linked by Hurun to Boee Group (保亿集团), Hangzhou property developer; exact current title not confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2012-2018) for Boee, i.e. Boee Group (保亿集团), a Hangzhou-based private developer founded on 16 Sept 1991 as Huarong home-appliance trading company in Taizhou that moved into real estate in the late 1990s. The group now spans property development, property management, trading and industrial investment. A third-party profile names a Mo Jianrong as chairman of its property-service arm.
interesting_fact: Boee began in 1991 as Zhejiang Huarong, a home-appliance trading firm, and switched to property; its first project, Boee Mingzhu in Taizhou (2001), made its name. Its property arm sent butlers to train in Europe for a 'platinum butler' service.
notes: Chairman's name on Boee's site is shown only as an image; a third-party site (altss.com) names founder Mo Jianhua as group chairman and Mo Jianrong as chairman of Zhejiang Boee Property Service - unverified. Group HQ: Boee Center, Qianjiang Century City, Hangzhou. Very private; Chinese-language media is the likely route.

name: Chen Yunqin
current_role: Deceased (founder of Ningbo David Medical Device Co., SZSE: 300314)
profile: Founder, controlling shareholder and one of the actual controllers of Ningbo David Medical Device (founded 1992). The company announced he died of illness on 20 September 2024, aged 82; he held about 21.12% of the company at the time.
notes: Died 20 Sept 2024 per company announcement filed with Shenzhen Stock Exchange: https://disc.static.szse.cn/download/disc/disk03/finalpage/2024-09-23/15a7f1c9-2396-4e01-b537-99518cc845e2.PDF . Company is now led by Chen Zaihong (legal representative/chairman).

name: Liao Dinghai
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Guangzhou Hi-Target Navigation Tech Co. (SZSE 300177)
profile: Liao Dinghai (b. 1963), a naval hydrographic surveyor turned entrepreneur, founded Hi-Target (中海达), a Guangzhou maker of GNSS/BeiDou surveying, mapping and marine-survey equipment that listed on ChiNext in 2011. He has chaired it since 2009 and was re-elected for a three-year term in May 2024; son Liao Wen is a director and VP.
interesting_fact: He graduated from the Dalian Naval Academy's marine surveying department and spent nearly 20 years in the PLA Navy as a unit leader and senior engineer doing marine surveying before running Hi-Target.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2015 he and Hi-Target's executives have funded a RMB10m 'Hi-Target Love Fund' (中海达爱心基金) that supports employees and their families facing serious illness or accidents.
notes: Hurun co-listee Liao Wen is his son. Relevant to podcast via BeiDou/GNSS positioning tech. Contact via board secretary office.

name: Liao Wen
current_role: Pre-IPO shareholder of Hi-Target Navigation Tech (中海达, SZSE: 300177); no executive role found
profile: Liao Wen appears on the Hurun list jointly with Liao Dinghai, founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Guangzhou-based Hi-Target, a maker of high-precision GNSS receivers, CORS stations, total stations, 3D laser scanners and drones. Liao Wen was named as a shareholder in Hi-Target's 2011 IPO lock-up undertakings; the exact relationship to Liao Dinghai is not stated in the filings found.
interesting_fact: Hi-Target, founded in Guangzhou in 1999, is one of China's main makers of BeiDou/GNSS high-precision surveying equipment.
notes: Low public profile; the wealth figure is shared with Liao Dinghai, the public face of the company. Any outreach is better aimed at Liao Dinghai via Hi-Target's board secretary/IR. Relationship between Liao Wen and Liao Dinghai not confirmed.

name: Hu Dong
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and CFO, Ebang International Holdings (Nasdaq: EBON), Hangzhou
profile: Born 1973; founded Hangzhou-based Ebang, which started out making communications network access equipment and around 2014 pivoted into bitcoin-mining ASIC machines, listing on Nasdaq in 2020. Holds most of the voting power; Ebang has since expanded into crypto exchange, payments and mining businesses.

current_role: Founder of Weidai (微贷网), Hangzhou; current role/status unclear since the platform wound down in 2020-21
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur (born c.1980) who founded Weidai in 2010, a P2P lender that pivoted to car-collateral loans in 2012 and listed on the NYSE in 2018. The platform exited online lending in 2020 and came under a Hangzhou police illegal-deposit-taking investigation; Weidai reported repaying all outstanding investor principal by mid-2021. No recent public information on him.

notes: Sensitive: Weidai has been under police investigation since July 2020 (https://m.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_17363197). Status unknown; Hurun listings ended 2019. Not a good outreach target; no public contacts found.
