name: Shen Haiyin
current_role: Founder and CEO, Zhiche Youxing Technology (智车优行, brand Singulato / 奇点汽车), Shanghai/Beijing; current status unclear
profile: Shen Haiyin (沈海寅) is an internet executive turned EV entrepreneur: a former VP at Kingsoft and Qihoo 360 and angel investor, he founded Zhiche Youxing in Oct 2014 to build smart EVs under the Singulato (奇点) brand, which raised at least seven rounds through 2020 and made him a Hurun unicorn founder.
interesting_fact: He decided to build cars after driving a Tesla in 2014: 'After experiencing a Tesla, I felt the auto industry was bound to change' (体验过特斯拉的车后，我就感觉汽车行业一定会变天).
deep_cut_fact: Not a total auto outsider: his first job after university was at Shanghai Delphi Automotive Air Conditioning, making car A/C components; in 2000 he moved to Japan and founded three companies there before ~15 years in China's internet industry.
notes: Singulato faced funding/wage-arrears problems and was reported heading toward bankruptcy around 2023 - avoid as a hook. No recent (2024-26) public activity found; no published contact.

name: Guo Xiangwen
current_role: Founder and former chairman/Party secretary of Shanxi Kangwei Group (Qinyuan County coal and coke); 65% sold to Yongtai Energy (600157.SH) in 2012; current role unverified
profile: Guo Xiangwen (郭向文) built Shanxi Kangwei Group from Qinyuan Kangwei Coal & Coke, set up in 2000 with him as legal representative. In 2012 Yongtai Energy paid RMB 2.895bn for 65% of Kangwei (a RMB 1.5bn capital injection plus RMB 1.395bn for 31% from Guo and employee share funds). He then held Yongtai shares (about 70m in 2014), and still appeared in its top-10 holders in 2020.
interesting_fact: Kangwei was a rural collective turned private company. Until 2012 three employee share-fund associations, one with about 420 worker members, owned about 36% of the group alongside Guo.
deep_cut_fact: Kangwei began as the Nanshan coal mine in Baizi town, Qinyuan County. It was restructured in 2000 into Qinyuan Kangwei Coal & Coke with registered capital of only RMB 820,000. Twelve years later Yongtai valued the group at billions.
notes: Identity confirmed via Yongtai Energy filings on cninfo (2012 acquisition report; 2015 notice that Guo personally paid the 2014 profit-guarantee shortfall: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2015-06-24/1201186581.PDF). That payment is neutral but avoid it in outreach. Very local, low-profile Shanxi coal owner; no published contact. Kangwei is now a Yongtai subsidiary.

name: Pan Huarong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Focus Lightings Technology (聚灿光电, SZSE: 300708), Suzhou
profile: Pan Huarong (潘华荣) built Focus Lightings from a small plant in Suzhou Industrial Park (founded 2010, ChiNext IPO 2017) into a leading LED epitaxial-wafer and chip maker, expanding counter-cyclically through three downturns. He is steering it toward a compound-semiconductor platform: Mini/Micro LED, auto lighting, AR, optical interconnect and space PV.
interesting_fact: Focus Lightings has taped out prototype Micro LED CPO (co-packaged optics) array chips with a strategic customer; Pan says AI data-center expansion will accelerate commercial optical interconnects.
deep_cut_fact: Known for a low-key, almost obsessive 'product-first' style, he told Shanghai Securities News in 2026: 'We don't chase being No. 1 in scale, but we pursue leadership in profitability' (我们不追求规模上的第一，但追求盈利能力上的领先).
notes: Good data-center angle (CPO/optical interconnect Micro LED chips; joint lab with CAS Suzhou Nano institute on optical interconnect and space PV). Company email is a general corporate address; IR materials at stocknotice.asp. Chinese-language approach advised.

name: Xie Yunkai
current_role: No current listed-company role found; formerly director of Dalian Energas Gas-System Co. (派思股份, SSE: 603318), now Shuifa Energas
profile: Xie Yunkai (谢云凯) was a board director of Dalian Energas Gas-System (natural-gas processing and gas-system equipment maker) from 2014 to 2019 and again 2020-2021, alongside chairman Xie Bing (谢冰). Hurun counted him among China's rich in 2015-2016, around Energas's 2015 Shanghai listing; control of the company later passed to Shandong's Shuifa Group.
notes: Low-profile; little coverage beyond board records (source: https://vip.stock.finance.sina.com.cn/corp/go.php/vCI_CorpManager/stockid/603318.phtml). Family relationship to chairman Xie Bing not verified. The Energas business is now under state-owned Shuifa Group, so there is no obvious current corporate route. Low priority.

name: Marc Murphy
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Micron Technology
profile: Mark Murphy (listed here as 'Marc') has been Micron's CFO since 2022, running finance, treasury, tax, audit and investor relations as AI-driven demand for high-bandwidth memory pushed Micron to record results. He was previously EVP and CFO of Qorvo and held senior roles at Delphi Automotive, MEMC Electronic Materials and Praxair; his wealth stems from Micron equity.
interesting_fact: His career has spanned nearly every layer of the chip supply chain: semiconductor materials (MEMC), capital equipment, fabrication, and assembly and test, before landing at memory maker Micron.
deep_cut_fact: He is a U.S. Marine Corps veteran (Marquette BBA in finance, Harvard MBA) and serves on the Advisory Council of Boise State University's College of Business and Economics, in Micron's hometown.
notes: Name is spelled Mark Murphy by Micron. The 'Hurun Unicorn founders (2021)' tag in the input likely belongs to a different Marc Murphy; ignore. Press/IR contacts are Micron's media (Mark Plungy) and IR (Satya Kumar) leads named in the Sept 2026 earnings release.

name: Lord Alliance
profile: David Alliance, Baron Alliance (born 1932, Kashan, Iran) was a Lib Dem peer, founding shareholder and former chairman of mail-order group N Brown, and co-founder of textiles group Coats Viyella. He died on 18 July 2025, aged 93.
notes: Died 18 July 2025 (N Brown announcement, reported by FashionUnited and The JC). Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Stephen J Hemsley
current_role: Chairman & CEO, UnitedHealth Group (returned as CEO May 2025)
profile: Stephen Hemsley (b. 1952) is a Fordham-trained accountant who rose to CFO of Arthur Andersen, joined UnitedHealth in 1997, and was its CEO from 2006 to 2017, building Optum into the health-services giant it is today. After serving as chairman, he returned as CEO in May 2025 to lead a turnaround; his wealth comes from decades of UNH equity awards.
interesting_fact: He is widely credited as the architect of Optum, now the largest employer of physicians in the US; in 2026 he said UnitedHealth was on track to invest $1.5 billion in AI in a single year.
deep_cut_fact: Outside UnitedHealth he has sat on Cargill's board since 2015, is a trustee of the University of St. Thomas in Minnesota, serves on the Boy Scouts of America's National Executive Board, and in 2019 founded his own investment firm, Cloverfields Capital Group.
notes: Famously media-shy; rarely gives interviews. Company under heavy scrutiny (DOJ probes, litigation) - outreach should go through UHG corporate communications. Healthcare focus, weak fit for energy/data-center unless angle is AI investment.

name: Daniel Levy
current_role: Co-founder, Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI), Palo Alto / Tel Aviv (assumed match for the AI-unicorn listing)
profile: This record merges two different men. The AI-unicorn Daniel Levy is a former OpenAI researcher (led its Optimization team) who co-founded Safe Superintelligence (SSI) with Ilya Sutskever and Daniel Gross in June 2024; SSI reached a $30B valuation in March 2025 and announced a long-term compute partnership with Nvidia in July 2026. The 'Football' / Sunday Times 2020 entry is ex-Tottenham Hotspur chairman Daniel Levy (b. 1962).
interesting_fact: SSI calls itself the 'world's first straight-shot SSI lab' with one product (a safe superintelligence) and no product cycles; it uses Google Cloud TPUs and, from 2026, a strategic Nvidia partnership.
deep_cut_fact: (SSI Levy) He did the French prepa at Lycee Louis-le-Grand, then Ecole Polytechnique (applied maths/CS), an MS at Stanford with Stefano Ermon and a PhD with John Duchi on optimization and privacy; in 2017 he interned at Google Brain with Jascha Sohl-Dickstein and Matt Hoffman.
notes: IDENTITY MERGE: Sunday Times 2020 'Football' wealth (GBP ~421M) belongs to Tottenham's Daniel Levy, while the Hurun AI-unicorn listing is SSI's Daniel Levy; the profile above covers the SSI one given the data-center/AI focus. SSI is very low-profile; comms@ssi.inc is the only published press route. The Stanford email is self-published but from his PhD days and may be stale.

name: Andrew T. Kaplan
current_role: Partner (Healthcare), Bain Capital Private Equity, Boston; Director, Kailera Therapeutics (KLRA)
profile: Andrew Kaplan is a Bain Capital healthcare partner (joined 2009, ex-Goldman Sachs banker) who joined the board of obesity-drug developer Kailera Therapeutics with its $600m Series B in Oct 2025. The SEC '10% owner' holdings attributed to him reflect Bain Capital fund stakes in Kailera, not necessarily personal wealth.
interesting_fact: Kailera was launched in 2024 with $400m to develop GLP-1/GIP obesity drugs in-licensed from China's Jiangsu Hengrui, which took a 19.9% stake; it later went public as KLRA.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded EngagedHealth, LLC, a post-hospitalization service for chronically ill, low-income patients aimed at cutting readmissions; he was a Baker Scholar at Harvard Business School and studied economics at Wharton.

public_contacts.value: Kailera media/IR: maura.gavaghan@kailera.com (Maura Gavaghan, VP Corp Comms & IR, as of Oct 2024)

notes: Net worth figure is an artifact of SEC Form 4 aggregation of Bain Capital fund holdings; he is a PE partner, not a founder billionaire. Middle initial 'T.' not confirmed on Bain's page; distinct from Andrew Gary Kaplan (another Bain director). Best route: Bain Capital media office.

name: Shi Zhengrong
current_role: Founder, Sunman Energy (上迈新能源, Shanghai), maker of ultra-light flexible solar modules; founder and former chairman/CEO of Suntech Power
profile: Shi Zhengrong (施正荣, b. 1963, Yangzhong, Jiangsu) earned a solar PhD at UNSW, became an Australian citizen and returned to Wuxi in 2001 to found Suntech Power; its 2005 NYSE listing briefly made him China's richest man and helped spark China's solar boom. After leaving Suntech in 2013 he built Sunman Energy, which makes ultra-light solar panels, and still speaks widely on PV.
interesting_fact: Academic Lan Xiaohuan argues Shi's overnight wealth after Suntech's 2005 NYSE IPO had a 'strong demonstration effect' that prompted local governments across China to pour money into solar - seeding the industry China now dominates.
deep_cut_fact: He did his doctorate at UNSW's School of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering under Professor Martin Green, the 'father of photovoltaics'; in 2009 he was elected a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering and won the Oslo Business for Peace Award.
notes: Great podcast fit (solar pioneer, Australia-China story) and historically media-friendly. Avoid Suntech's 2013 bankruptcy in outreach. No published email found (Sunman site is JS-only); route via Sunman's website contact page or conference organisers where he keynotes. Holds Australian citizenship.

name: Jin Ming
current_role: Former President of Suning Appliance / Suning Commerce Group (2010 to about 2015); current role not publicly known
profile: Jin Ming (金明) is a long-time Suning executive who joined founder Zhang Jindong's appliance retailer in 1993, became a director and shareholder, and in July 2010 replaced Sun Weimin as president. He was widely seen as a possible successor to Zhang. His wealth comes from his Suning shareholding; he was on the Hurun China list from 2007 to 2011.
interesting_fact: He spent his whole early career at Suning, joining straight out of university in 1993 when it was still a Nanjing air-conditioner retailer, and rose to president of what became one of China's largest electronics retailers.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Suning in 1993 straight after graduating, three years after Zhang Jindong founded it as a single air-conditioner shop in Nanjing, and in July 2010 succeeded Sun Weimin as company president.

Suning.com's IR office is the only institutional route, and he may no longer be connected to it. A common name, so double-check identity before any outreach.

name: Qiao Tianming
current_role: Former chairman of Sichuan Jiannanchun (JNC) Group, the Mianzhu baijiu maker; no active public role since c.2016
profile: Qiao Tianming spent more than 30 years at Jiannanchun, one of the 'Mao-Wu-Jian' baijiu brands. He became chairman in 2001 and led its 2003 restructuring from state ownership, which made him a major owner. He largely vanished from public view around 2016, and in 2023 a Leshan court convicted him in a case tied to that restructuring.
interesting_fact: In 2012 he announced the RMB 2bn Datang Guojiu eco-park to add 20,000+ tonnes of base-liquor capacity; it was only formally unveiled in 2022, a decade later.
notes: Not a viable podcast guest. He was reported missing from public view around 2016, and in 2023 the Leshan Intermediate Court sentenced him to 5 years for bribery and illegally dividing state assets, with a RMB 400m fine (per media reports). Some reports say his son Qiao Yu took on management. Source: https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2018-07-24/1238247.html and tmtpost.

name: He Yan
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Chengdu GoldTel (Guoteng) Electronics Group and, since Jan 2025, actual controller of Chengdu Zhenxin Technology (300101.SZ, BeiDou satellite-navigation chips)
profile: Chengdu-born (1961) computer engineer turned entrepreneur. Founded Chengdu Guoteng (GoldTel) Communications in 1995 and in 2003 Guoteng Microelectronics, forerunner of Zhenxin Technology, often called China's 'first BeiDou navigation stock'. After years of legal disputes over the parent group, courts confirmed her control and she was reinstated as Zhenxin's actual controller in Jan 2025.
interesting_fact: Her group built an early Chinese satellite-navigation chip business (BeiDou), with GoldTel spanning communications, power, tax/finance equipment, satellite comms and IC design.
deep_cut_fact: She studied computer science at Nanjing Institute of Technology (now Southeast University), started her career in 1983 at Dongfang Electric, and is an adjunct professor at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC).
notes: Highly sensitive: arrested in 2013-14 in connection with the Li Chuncheng corruption case and served prison time; long control fight with Zhenxin management continues. Not a recommended podcast target; no published contact found.

name: Wang Yangang
current_role: Former chairman and CEO, China Animal Healthcare Ltd (HKEX: 0940); no current public role found
profile: Controlling shareholder, chairman and CEO of China Animal Healthcare, a veterinary-vaccine and animal-drug maker (incl. Inner Mongolia Bigvet Bio-tech) that listed via Singapore in 2007 and moved to Hong Kong in 2010. Hurun listed him with Li Chunhua (2014-2016). He stepped down from all board roles in July 2017; the shares were suspended in 2015 and the listing cancelled in January 2020.
interesting_fact: China Animal Healthcare was one of the few Chinese veterinary-vaccine makers to list overseas, first via a 2007 reverse takeover in Singapore before transferring to the Hong Kong main board in 2010.
notes: Name also romanised Wang Yan Gang in HKEX filings. Company delisted (2020) after a long suspension, and he has kept no public profile since leaving in 2017; no published contacts. Probably a poor podcast target.

name: Li Chunhua
current_role: Former ultimate controlling shareholder, China Animal Healthcare Ltd (HKEX-listed; in provisional liquidation since 2019)
profile: HKEX filings name Madam Li Chunhua as the ultimate controlling party and a controlling shareholder of China Animal Healthcare, a Chinese veterinary drugs and vaccines maker; she is described as the spouse of former chairman and CEO Wang Yangang. The company's shares were suspended and provisional liquidators appointed in 2019, so her current business activity is unclear.
notes: Essentially no public profile; source: HKEX filings (e.g. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2018/0517/ltn20180517013.pdf). Company in liquidation; Forbes wealth figure likely stale. Not a good outreach candidate.

name: Dou Qiling
current_role: Chairwoman and controlling shareholder, Guizhou Yibai Pharmaceutical Co. (SSE 600594)
profile: Dou Qiling (窦啟玲, b. 1960), a co-founder of Guizhou Yibai Pharmaceutical in Guiyang, has led the company as chair, vice-chair and general manager over the years; it makes traditional-Chinese-medicine and oncology drugs (e.g. Aidi injection). Her daughter Dou Yaqi is now vice-chair and general manager.
interesting_fact: She holds a doctorate in business administration and is one of the few women founder-chairs of a listed Chinese drugmaker; the family runs Yibai as a two-generation team.
notes: Pharma, not energy. Company has had several regulatory warnings (2019, 2024) - avoid in outreach. Contact via board secretary email.

name: Zhang Shiquan
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Zhejiang Shibao Co. (浙江世宝, SZSE: 002703 / HKEX: 1057)
profile: Zhang Shiquan (b. c.1950) co-founded Zhejiang Shibao in Yiwu in 1993 and, with family members, controls it. Shibao designs and makes automotive steering gears and steering-system components, with subsidiaries such as Siping Steering Gear and Wuhu Sterling Steering Systems. He was CEO until December 2017 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Shibao is dual-listed in Hong Kong and Shenzhen and is one of China's main independent steering-system suppliers, now developing electric power steering for new-energy and intelligent vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Shibao's chief executive for over 24 years, from its founding in June 1993 until December 2017, before handing the CEO job on while staying chairman.
notes: Low media profile; the controlling group includes several Zhang family members. Best route is via the company's board secretary / IR (HKEX 1057 filings list company secretary contacts).

name: Sheng Faqiang
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman, Toread Holdings (探路者); no current executive role found
profile: Sheng Faqiang (盛发强) co-founded Beijing outdoor-gear brand Toread in 1999. In 2009 it listed on ChiNext, where it was called the 'first outdoor stock', and he served as chairman during its mid-2010s diversification. In 2021 the founders transferred control to an investor group led by chip-industry executive Li Ming, and Sheng stepped down as chairman.
interesting_fact: Toread was one of the first companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext growth board when it launched in 2009, and was dubbed China's 'first outdoor stock'.
deep_cut_fact: Before outdoor gear he was in printing: around 1993 he quit a state railway survey-and-design institute, worked as a salesman for a printing plant in Beihai, Guangxi, and then set up his own small printing company.
notes: Since 2021 Toread has been controlled by Li Ming's group, so the company website is no longer a direct route to Sheng. Low recent public profile; I found no personal channels.

name: Chen Fucheng
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller (43.82%) of Shanghai Songz Automobile Air Conditioning Co. (SZ002454); holds no executive post
profile: Hong Kong-resident Chen Fucheng (陈福成) is the actual controller of Songz (松芝股份), a Shanghai maker of bus and passenger-car air-conditioning and thermal-management systems founded in 1998 and listed in Shenzhen in 2010. He owns about 43.8% of the company; day-to-day leadership is with chairman Chen Huanxiong. He was on the Hurun China list 2010-2021.
interesting_fact: Songz is a leading supplier of large and mid-size bus air conditioners and has moved into battery thermal-management systems for new-energy buses and passenger cars.
notes: 2024 annual report lists him as a Hong Kong (China) natural person with 'no' principal occupation/position - a passive owner with no public profile. Route via the board secretary / securities affairs office (IR email). Alive inferred from his continued listing as shareholder in the April 2025 filings.

name: Gu Qingwei
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Beijing Dinghan Technology Group (鼎汉技术, SZSE: 300011)
profile: Born 1972, a Jiangxi University of Finance & Economics graduate who spent 1996-2002 in Huawei's finance organisation before founding Dinghan in 2002. Dinghan makes rail-transit power systems (signal, platform-door and traction power supplies, train electrical equipment) and was among the first ChiNext listings (2009). Guangzhou state investor GIIC's capital arm is now controlling shareholder; Gu remains chairman and a 5%+ holder.
interesting_fact: Dinghan carries code 300011 - it was in the very first batch of 28 companies to list on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in October 2009; it supplies power systems for metro and high-speed rail across China.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Dinghan he was a Huawei finance man for six years: section chief in finance management, CFO of Shandong Huawei, director of Huawei's Beijing financial shared-services centre and CFO of North Huawei. He holds EMBAs from both Peking and Tsinghua universities.
notes: Good energy/power-electronics angle (rail power supply). Board secretary office (ir@) is the formal route. Source is Dinghan 2024 annual report (bio section).

name: Xu Xianda
current_role: Deceased; was a controlling shareholder and actual controller of Guangdong Delian Group (002666.SZ, automotive fine chemicals)
profile: Xu Xianda (徐咸大) and his children Xu Tuanhua and Xu Qingfang were the controlling shareholders of Guangdong Delian Group, a Shenzhen-listed maker of automotive fluids and fine chemicals. A September 2024 company filing says he has died and his shares await inheritance.
notes: Deceased per Delian Group's Shenzhen exchange filing: https://disc.static.szse.cn/download/disc/disk03/finalpage/2024-09-09/77909eab-e7f8-4ba9-9d40-9d4c142dbee8.PDF (the family relationship is in the 2016 filing: https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2016-03-28/9262a952-b6b2-4e19-81ad-213be012b88d.PDF). Exact date of death not found. The business is now run by his son Xu Tuanhua (chairman).

name: Chen Zhifeng
current_role: Chairman, Yema (Wild Horse) Group Co., Ltd., Urumqi, Xinjiang
profile: Xinjiang entrepreneur whose Yema Group grew from trade with Central Asia into finance, property and tourism (Hurun China 2008-2014). He is best known as the man who brought Akhal-Teke 'heavenly horses' from Central Asia to China in numbers, running a breeding and exhibition base in Urumqi (Xinjiang Paleo-ecology Park).

notes: Hurun 2015 entry (hurun.net): 刘海祥 | 恒东 | 煤炭 | residence Ordos | RMB 2.6bn. Identity tied via Yitai Coal's 2014 related-party notice naming him as Hengdong's legal representative. Company-promo and GEM pages say Hengdong runs 7 mines (~13.2 Mt/yr design capacity, after a 2011 consolidation), but those are unverified. No personal profile or published contact found.

name: Miguel Matias Galuccio
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Vista Energy (NYSE/BMV: VIST); board director, SLB
profile: Argentine petroleum engineer (b. 1968, Paraná; ITBA 1994) who rose through Schlumberger's international ranks, then led state oil company YPF as chairman/CEO from its 2012 renationalization to 2016. In 2017 he founded Vista, the first NYSE-listed independent focused on Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale, which he still runs.

name: Jack Hightower
current_role: Founder and former Chairman/CEO, HighPeak Energy (NASDAQ: HPK); retired 15 Sept 2025, remains a major shareholder
profile: Texas oilman with 50+ years in E&P who founded HighPeak Energy, a Midland Basin (Permian) producer formed in 2020 via his SPAC Pure Acquisition Corp. He serially built and sold E&P companies: Enertex (1991-94), Titan Exploration (1995), which became Pure Resources (taken in by Unocal in 2002), Celero Energy I and II, and Bluestem Energy. He retired as CEO/chairman in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: Pure Resources, which grew out of the Titan Exploration he founded in 1995, became the 11th-largest publicly traded independent E&P company in North America before Unocal bought out minority shareholders in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: A 1970 Texas Tech graduate (BBA degrees in Administrative Finance and in Money, Banking & Investments), he chaired both Pure Resources (until Unocal's 2002 buyout) and, 15 years later, Pure Acquisition Corp. (2017), the SPAC that took HighPeak public.
notes: Retired from HighPeak in Sept 2025 (CEO now Michael Hollis). No personal public channels found; company contact is the only published route and may not forward. Not to be confused with the late Texas congressman Jack Hightower (d. 2013).

name: Manish Mahendra Choksi
current_role: Non-Executive Vice Chairman (Promoter), Asian Paints Ltd
profile: Manish Choksi (58), a member of the Choksi promoter family of Asian Paints - India's largest paint maker, founded in a Mumbai garage in 1942 by four friends including Chimanlal Choksi - joined the company in 1992 and rose through sales, supply chain, IT, chemicals, HR and international business. He became a non-executive director in 2018 and is now Vice Chairman.
interesting_fact: As President of International Business, IT, HR and Chemicals he led Asian Paints' digital transformation and its entry into home improvement, and was instrumental in restructuring its joint ventures with US coatings giant PPG Industries.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MBA and a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from the University of Houston; a recognised IT leader, he has served on the advisory boards of IBM and SAP and is an active angel investor.
notes: Data said 'Chemicals/Petrochemicals'; his wealth is from Asian Paints (paints/coatings). Angel investor and IT/digital background make him a decent podcast fit. Route via Asian Paints investor relations / company secretary.

name: Wu Jianlong
current_role: Actual controller of Zhejiang Sunflower Great Health (300111.SZ, formerly Zhejiang Sunflower Light Energy / 'Sunowe'); chairman of Zhejiang Longhua New Century Real Estate
profile: Wu Jianlong (吴建龙, b. 1967, Shaoxing) founded Zhejiang Sunflower Light Energy (向日葵光能, brand Sunowe), a solar-cell and module maker that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2010 with him as chairman. In 2019-20 the company sold its PV assets and bought his Beide Pharmaceutical, becoming Sunflower Great Health. He remains controller via Hong Kong Youchuang International; Wu Shaoqin is now legal representative.
interesting_fact: Rather than ride out the solar shakeout, he turned his listed solar company into a pharmaceutical business. The PV unit went to his private Shaoxing Sunflower Investment, and the listed company took over Zhejiang Beide Pharma, which he had already chaired since at least 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked for the Huashe town government in Shaoxing County. He later earned an EMBA from Zhongnan University of Economics and Law and was a Shaoxing County people's congress deputy (2010 annual report bio).
notes: Hurun 2021: 吴建龙 | 向日葵光能 | b.1967 Shaoxing | RMB 2.6bn. 'Sunowe' is Sunflower's English brand/domain, not a separate firm. The IR email belongs to board secretary Li Lan (published in the annual report). 'Alive: yes': he is named as actual controller in the 2025 annual report and in a Sept 2026 share-pledge release. He holds Hong Kong residency. Not the Taiwanese basketball coach.

name: Li Lianjie (Jet Li)
current_role: Martial-arts film star; founder of the One Foundation (Shenzhen One Foundation charity)
profile: Li Lianjie (Jet Li, b. 1963, Beijing), a five-time Chinese national wushu champion, became an international film star (Once Upon a Time in China, Hero, Fearless). notes: Identity inferred from Hurun pairing with 'Li Zhi' (Nina Li Chi) and investments/entertainment; Hurun's 'Yuandong' label could not be matched to a company. Facebook/YouTube/TikTok also linked from jetli.world. Book tour suggests a publisher publicity route.

profile: Xu Baojin (徐宝金, b. July 1960, Shaoxing) built Jinhui Holding Group, a Shaoxing private group in chemical fibre, property and investment; he owned 90% of it in 2015. The Yang family took full ownership by 2005 and listed it among the first 28 ChiNext stocks in 2009 (code 300004). In Dec 2022 he and son Yang Zijiang sold 32m shares, exiting as 5%+ holders.

profile: Li Yuzhen (李玉珍; input romanisation 'Li Yuzheng') controls Guangzhou-based Jinyi Cinemas (金逸影视), one of China's larger cinema chains, listed in Shenzhen in 2017, alongside co-controller Li Genchang. profile: Teng Daochun (滕道春, b. Jan 1970) is a Xuzhou industrialist. profile: Founder-controller of Suzhou Doson Pressure Control, a maker of oil and gas drilling/wellhead pressure-control equipment that listed in Shanghai in Dec 2015. name: Terry Smith

Zhongrong Xinda, formerly Shandong Coking Group, grew from coking coal into coal chemicals, mining, glass/building materials and logistics. He is legal representative of its Binzhou subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Zhongrong Xinda put six people on the 2018 Hurun list: Wang Qingtao plus Zhang Yigui (RMB 8.1bn), Liang Kai, Tian Tongbao, Guo Yan and Wang Weijie. That made the company a 'rich-list factory' for Qingdao.

A 2024 Zibo court ruling put 128 Zhongrong Xinda firms, including his 滨州市友康建材, into consolidated restructuring, so avoid the topic. Common name; the website is the group's, not his.

name: Damodar Prasad Choudhary
current_role: Co-founder and promoter-family member of Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd (Kolkata). He holds no current board position; MarketScreener lists him as chairman 2010-2013.
profile: Damodar Prasad Choudhary co-founded Himadri Speciality Chemical (formerly Himadri Chemicals & Industries) in Kolkata in 1987 with six other family members. Himadri began as a coal-tar pitch maker and has grown into specialty carbon black, naphthalene derivatives and lithium-ion battery materials. The company is now run by Chairman/MD/CEO Anurag Choudhary.
interesting_fact: The company he co-founded has turned a steel-industry byproduct (coal tar) into an energy-transition business, making advanced battery materials such as anode materials and LFP cathode chemicals. Its CMD was named BT India's Best CEO 2026 in chemicals.
notes: I found no recent news on him personally and no obituary, so alive is marked unknown. He appears to have stepped back years ago, and Anurag Choudhary (CMD) is the public face and better podcast guest. He was on the Hurun India list only in 2017-18.

name: Manish Satyanarayan Nuwal
current_role: Managing Director & CEO, Solar Industries India Ltd (Nagpur)
profile: Son of founder Satyanarayan Nuwal; joined the family explosives business in the mid-1990s when it began manufacturing, and has been MD & CEO since ~2012. He has steered Solar from bulk/packaged explosives for mining into defence: propellants, warheads, ammunition, 'Nagastra' loitering munitions and counter-drone systems, with a large new defence/aerospace hub in Nagpur.
interesting_fact: Solar supplies 'Nagastra' loitering-munition drones to the Indian Army, and PM Modi inaugurated its loitering-munition test range in Nagpur in March 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A qualified chartered accountant, he says Solar's defence breakthrough was multi-mode hand grenades co-developed with DRDO over nearly three years, which he calls a watershed for private-sector defence in India; asked if 'playing with fire' is fun, he laughed.
notes: Hurun net-worth figure is from 2019 and well out of date; the Nuwal family is now multi-billionaire as Solar's market cap soared on defence orders. Strong energy/defence-manufacturing angle. Chartered-accountant credential per company website.

name: Liu Haifeng
current_role: Executive Chairman and co-founder, DCP Capital (德弘资本)
profile: Liu Haifeng (David H. Liu) is a veteran China private-equity investor. He co-headed Morgan Stanley Private Equity Asia, then was a KKR partner, co-head of KKR Asia PE and CEO of KKR Greater China. In 2017 he left with Julian Wolhardt to co-found DCP Capital, a China-focused PE firm. His deals include Mengniu Dairy, Ping An, Haier, Belle and Nanfu Battery.
interesting_fact: He was KKR's first local hire in Asia, and he backed some of China's best-known private-equity deals, including Mengniu Dairy and Ping An Insurance.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer. He graduated as Class Salutatorian from Columbia with a B.S. in Electrical Engineering, was a Tau Beta Pi member, and won the Edwin Howard Armstrong Memorial Award for Columbia's top electrical engineering student.
notes: Uses the English name David H. Liu. A low-profile PE investor. The best route is DCP Capital's general inbox (info@dcpcapital.com). The site also has a Charity section.

current_role: Founder and former Chairman, Beijing Lirr High-temperature Materials Co. (SZSE: 002392); his son Zhao Wei has been chairman since July 2024
profile: Zhao Jizeng (赵继增), born 1955, is a professor-level senior engineer and former executive vice-president of the Ministry of Metallurgy's Luoyang Institute of Refractories Research. In 2000 he founded Beijing Lier (now Lirr) Refractory Materials, which supplies refractories and full-service furnace-lining contracts to steel, non-ferrous, petrochemical and building-materials plants. It listed in Shenzhen in 2010.

deep_cut_fact: He was one of the first startup mentors in Zhongguancun's 'Golden Seed Project' (金种子工程), sits on the board of and teaches part-time at Wuhan University of Science and Technology, and serves on the council of the World Refractories Association (WRA).
notes: Web search quota ran out mid-lane; data comes from Sina Finance filings pages. His board role after July 2024 is unconfirmed (Zhao Wei is now chairman). Refractories for steel furnaces give an angle on heavy-industry energy use and decarbonisation.

name: Tang Faling
current_role: Founder of Wuxi Qiaolian Group (无锡桥联集团), maker of wind-turbine castings and components, Huishan, Wuxi; handed day-to-day control to son Tang Ming in 2008
profile: Tang Faling (唐法林) founded Wuxi Qiaolian (Hurun's 'Qiaolian'), a hardware maker that switched to wind-turbine components in 2004: hubs, nacelles, bearing housings and main shafts for 1.5-2.4MW turbines. He and his son Tang Ming were on Hurun's list in 2011-2013. Registry data still show him as legal representative of several Wuxi machinery companies; no recent press coverage found.
interesting_fact: In 2007 Qiaolian Wind raised US$70m from foreign funds including Avenue Capital, France's NBP and Tsing Capital, aiming for a New York listing. That took a family firm with RMB 20-30m in sales past RMB 1bn within a few years.
deep_cut_fact: Before building Qiaolian he had farmed, worked as a carpenter, designed furniture and made hardware; his son described him as a '拼命三郎' (workaholic) always travelling to scout markets.
notes: Hurun's 'Qiaolian' = 桥联 (Wuxi Qiaolian Wind Power Technology / Qiaolian Group), not 侨联. The planned US IPO never happened, and there is no news coverage after about 2013. Private company with no IR channel; no published contact found. Very low profile.

name: Tang Ming
current_role: Chairman of Wuxi Qiaolian Wind Power Technology Group (无锡桥联风电科技集团), as of last press coverage; legal representative of Wuxi Qiaolian Investment
profile: Tang Ming (唐明), son of founder Tang Faling, took over Wuxi Qiaolian Group in 2008 after it pivoted from hardware to wind-turbine castings and components in 2004 (Qiaolian Wind was set up in Nov 2006). He brought in US$70m of foreign private equity in 2007 and pursued a planned New York IPO; Yicai put his wealth at RMB 1.7bn in 2011.
interesting_fact: Tang rejects the label 'fu er dai' (rich second generation): 'to be precise, I'm a chuang er dai (second-generation founder)', saying he earned it through 20 years of his own hard work.
deep_cut_fact: To pick investors for the 2007 round he set criteria: a mature US fund for a New York listing (Avenue), a fund with clean-energy listing experience (France's NBP), and Tsing Capital for its government background. More than 200 VCs had been tracking the company.
notes: Hurun's 'Qiaolian' = 桥联 (not 侨联). In 2009, as chairman, he signed a RMB 2bn deal in Deyang, Sichuan to expand component supply to Dongfang Electric (https://mobile.epaper.routeryun.com/index.php/home/article/index/appkey/192/date/2009-06-23/page/390414/aid/1924365.html). No news coverage after about 2013; the company is private and no published contact was found.

deep_cut_fact: The Mrs. Kavita Vinod Saraf Foundation (KVSF), a registered public charitable trust bearing her name, is consolidated into Vinati Organics' financial statements and is a vehicle for the company's CSR work.
notes: Not an operating executive; the public faces of Vinati are founder-chairman Vinod Saraf and MD Vinati Saraf Mutreja. The listed email is Vinati's general corporate inbox. Industry tag 'petrochemicals' fits only loosely (specialty chemicals). Alive status not confirmed by a dated source.

name: Rahul Dhanuka
current_role: Managing Director, Dhanuka Agritech Ltd (NSE: DHANUKA), since August 2024
profile: Second-generation leader of Gurugram-based crop-protection company Dhanuka Agritech, on its board since 2002 and previously COO; became MD in Aug 2024 as the company was handed to him and Harsh Dhanuka. Dhanuka's model relies on tie-ups with Japanese and US agrochemical majors to bring patented and exclusive molecules, and increasingly biologicals, to Indian farmers.
interesting_fact: As COO he committed Dhanuka to launching two new exclusive products every year, built on licensing partnerships with Japanese and American agrochemical firms.
deep_cut_fact: In a Sept 2026 interview he said Dhanuka was launching a new range of crop-nutrition products to help farmers recover from El Niño stress and depleted soil moisture, with the goal of 'making 2027 a more resilient and healthier year' for Indian agriculture.
notes: Agrochemicals rather than energy despite the 'Chemicals & Petrochemicals' tag; weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Gives trade-press interviews (AgroPages, Indian Chemical News). Company also publishes groupchairmanoffice@dhanuka.com, which serves the group chairman rather than him.

name: Ayman Asfari
current_role: Co-founder, The Asfari Foundation (London); former CEO (2002-2020) of oilfield-services group Petrofac
profile: Syrian-born British engineer (b. 1958; Villanova, Penn, Wharton MBA) who joined Petrofac in 1991, bought it out in 2001 and floated it in London in 2005, building a major oil & gas engineering contractor. He stepped down as CEO at end-2020. Since Assad's fall he has become a prominent diaspora investor and philanthropist re-engaging with Syria.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 he returned to Syria via Idlib and laid the foundation stone for the Dr. Mohammad Adeeb Asfari Maternity and Children's Hospital, named after his father; in 2025 he met Syria's energy minister about oil and gas investment and was floated as a possible transitional PM.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was in Oman as a consulting engineer doing soil testing; when he joined Petrofac in 1991 it was essentially a single plant in Tyler, Texas. He won the UK EY Entrepreneur of the Year award in 2011.
notes: Sensitivities: he was questioned in the SFO's Unaoil-related inquiry (Petrofac itself pleaded guilty in 2021; he was not charged) and was a large Conservative donor - avoid. His personal site aymanasfari.com (listed on Wikipedia) did not load. Great angle: post-war Syrian energy reconstruction. Foundation is the cleanest route.

name: Brian P Friedman
current_role: President and Director, Jefferies Financial Group (NYSE: JEF); Director, Vitesse Energy (NYSE: VTS)
profile: Brian P. Friedman (70) has been President and a director of Jefferies Financial Group since 2013, after joining legacy Jefferies Group in 2005. A former Wachtell Lipton lawyer, he spent 17 years at Furman Selz (head of investment banking) and ran Jefferies Capital Partners. He sits on the board of Vitesse Energy, the oil and gas company Jefferies spun off in 2023.
interesting_fact: About 70% of his pay since joining Jefferies has come in equity; counting all earned and unearned deferred shares and options, he would own about 6.8 million Jefferies shares, roughly 3.2% of the firm.
deep_cut_fact: He is co-chairman of the board of Strive, a workforce-training nonprofit, and a board member of the HC Leukemia Foundation. He graduated summa cum laude in economics from Wharton, also took a Wharton M.S. in Accounting, and holds a Columbia Law J.D.

public_contacts.value: https://www.jefferies.com/contact-us/ (directs investor, media and general inquiries to Jefferies Investor Relations)

notes: Energy angle: Vitesse Energy (non-operated oil and gas interests, spun off by Jefferies in 2023). Jefferies' IR pages are behind a bot wall, so no published email was captured. Route via Jefferies IR/corporate communications.

name: Sun Gengwen
current_role: Former chairman (until Dec 2018) of LandOcean Energy Services (SZ: 300157, now renamed New JCM Group); current role unclear - listed as director of some former subsidiaries
profile: Founder and long-time chairman of Beijing-based LandOcean Energy Services (Hengtai Aipu), a ChiNext-listed provider of oil and gas exploration software, geophysical services and oilfield equipment, which put him on the Hurun China list in 2011-2014. He stepped down as chairman in Dec 2018; the company was later renamed New JCM Group under new management (chairman Wang Lifei since 2022).
interesting_fact: LandOcean was among the early oilfield-technology companies listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext growth board (2010) and expanded through acquisitions such as Jinzhou New JCM Machinery and Sichuan Chuanyou Engineering Survey & Design.
notes: Low public profile; no verifiable biography or personal contacts found. No longer runs the listed company, so its IR channel is not a route to him. ChiNext listing year from general knowledge of ticker 300157 - verify. Consider low priority.

name: Chen Huinan
profile: Chen Huinan (陈惠南) appeared on the Hurun China list from 2005 to 2012 with wealth attributed to Fa Run Group (glass). He has not been listed since 2012. I could not verify the company, his current status or role before the web search budget ran out.
notes: Off Hurun since 2012 and has no listed company I could identify, so this needs a follow-up Chinese-language search. Not researched further.

name: Lin Youyao
profile: Lin Youyao (林友耀) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List in 2005-2006 with wealth attributed to Baohua Group (宝华集团), listed under insurance. No verifiable current information was found in this pass.

name: Wang Yingyan
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with Xu Jing, ~17.9%) of Misho Ecology & Landscape (美尚生态, 300495.SZ); not on current management
profile: Wang Yingyan (王迎燕) founded Wuxi-origin Misho Ecology & Landscape, an ecological restoration, landscape engineering and nursery company listed on ChiNext in 2015. She and Xu Jing remain recorded as actual controllers, but the company is now under *ST risk-warning status and run by chairman Wu Tianhua.
interesting_fact: Misho specialised in ecological restoration and sponge-city/landscape engineering projects in eastern China.
notes: Company is *ST (financial distress), so avoid financial topics; low priority. Hurun pairs her with Xu Jing. Limited research because the web search budget was exhausted.

name: Sha Yunlong
current_role: Founder & Chairman/CEO, Puxin (Puxin Ltd / Puxin Education); also listed as Chairman & CEO of Prepshine Holdings
profile: Former president of Beijing New Oriental School who left New Oriental in 2014 to found Puxin, a consolidator of after-school education businesses in China that listed on the NYSE (ticker NEW) in 2018.
interesting_fact: Rose through New Oriental, serving as president of Beijing New Oriental School, before founding Puxin; holds an MBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

public_contacts.value: ir@pxjy.com (Puxin IR, published 2019; may be outdated)

notes: Puxin's listing status after China's 2021 tutoring crackdown not verified; contacts may be stale.

name: Zeng Zhijun
current_role: Non-executive director and co-actual controller, Richinfo Technology (SZ:300634); owner of Beijing Honghuaweiye Investment
profile: Zeng Zhijun (b. 1971), a PhD in management from Hong Kong PolyU, is co-controller with Yang Liangzhi of Richinfo, an industrial-internet tech and services firm (enterprise messaging, cloud). He holds ~20% via Shenzhen Bailong and other vehicles and wholly owns Beijing Honghuaweiye Investment (Hurun's 'Honghuaweiye').
interesting_fact: His career runs from IBM China systems engineer to Merrill Lynch investment banking to chairing Beijing Huaya Hexun before backing Richinfo.
deep_cut_fact: He started as an IBM China systems engineer and account manager (1993-96), then was a systems analyst and project manager at International Rectifier (1996-2000).
notes: Identity confirmed via Richinfo convertible-bond prospectus (2026). Low personal profile.

name: Zhang Limin
current_role: Listed as owner of Qibu (children's supplies) on the Hurun China list (2018-2020), presumably Qibu Co. (起步股份), a Zhejiang children's footwear and apparel company. Current role not verified.
profile: Zhang Limin (章利民) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2018 to 2020 with about $350M from Qibu, a children's products company. That is presumably Qibu Co., Ltd. (起步股份), the Zhejiang children's shoe and clothing brand listed in Shanghai, but the link was not verified in this session.
notes: The identity link to the listed Qibu company is an unverified assumption. Web-search budget was exhausted. Consumer goods, so a weak fit for the podcast.

name: Chen Zhenbiao
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Petpal Pet Nutrition Technology Co. (SZSE: 300673), Pingyang, Wenzhou
profile: Chen Zhenbiao (陈振标), born 1961, is a senior economist with a master's degree. In 2002 he co-founded Wenzhou Peidi Pet Products with family members including Chen Zhenlu and Zheng Xianglan, and built it into Petpal, a leading Chinese maker of pet chews and pet food, much of it exported. It listed on ChiNext in 2017, and he still runs it as chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Petpal is based in Shuitou town, Pingyang, historically China's leather-processing hub. He also chairs the Zhejiang Import & Export Pet Food and Supplies Association and is vice-president of the China Animal Agriculture Association's pet industry branch.
deep_cut_fact: Before pet food he spent a decade (1992 to 2002) as director of the Pingyang Peidi Leather Goods Factory (平阳县佩蒂皮件制品厂). The Peidi name and the leather know-how carried straight into the pet-chew business he founded in 2002.
notes: Hurun co-lists Zheng Chunlan; the company's co-founder in filings is Zheng Xianglan (郑香兰), possibly the same person under a different romanisation, which I could not verify. Web search quota ran out mid-lane; data comes from Sina Finance filings. Weak fit for the energy/data-centre theme.

name: Chen Yongrui
current_role: Founder and former chairman/GM, Shenzhen Shengxunda Technology (盛讯达, 300518.SZ; now renamed Guangxi Xinxunda Technology); ceded control in Sept 2022
profile: Guangzhou-born (1984) MBA who founded Shengxunda in Dec 2006 and took it public on ChiNext in June 2016 while holding ~60%. The firm began making mobile-phone hardware, then pivoted fully to mobile games (standalone and cross-platform titles) by 2014; it now focuses on casual/social card games for Southeast Asia. Control passed to new owners in 2022.
interesting_fact: Shengxunda started as a mobile-handset hardware company and completely exited hardware in Aug 2014 to become a pure mobile-game developer, two years before its IPO, when he was 31.
notes: Exchange filings write his name as 陈湧锐. Sensitive: shares frozen in 2021, control changed 2022 (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2022-09-30/1214721820.PDF), and a CSRC administrative penalty against the company and its then controller in Dec 2024. No current public role or contact found; not a recommended target.

name: Ma Xiaoming
current_role: Founder/controlling shareholder (reported chairman), Xin Point Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 1571), Huizhou
profile: Hurun-listed (2017-2018) founder behind Xin Point, established in Huizhou in 2002 and listed in Hong Kong in 2017. Through Huizhou Keen Point Precision Plastics it supplies electroplated and painted plastic trim ('one-stop surface decoration') to global automakers, with ~4,700 staff and production in China, Malaysia and Mexico.
interesting_fact: Xin Point has expanded from Huizhou into a global auto-parts supplier with 13 locations; in 2026 its Malaysian plant passed a Tier-1 audit and it is building out in Mexico.
notes: His chairman title was not verifiable on the company site during this run (management pages returned 404); confirm via HKEX annual report. IR manager Cui Haoran is the published media/IR contact.

name: Li Songxiao
current_role: Former chairman and controlling shareholder of Neo-China Land Group (now Shanghai Industrial Urban Development, 0563.HK); no current role found
profile: Li Songxiao (郦松校) led Neo-China Land, a property developer founded in 1999 and listed in Hong Kong in 2003. After aggressive land buying in 2007 and a 2008 suspension, he sold 500 million shares to Shanghai Industrial (SIIC) in 2010 as SIIC took about 45% control. The company was renamed Shanghai Industrial Urban Development.
interesting_fact: In 2010 Shanghai Industrial bought about 45% of Neo-China Land for HK$2.746bn, including 500 million existing shares from Li at HK$2.32 each, ending his control.
notes: Exited control in 2010; no current public role found. Low suitability for outreach. Web search budget ran out during this lane, so this is minimal; worth a re-run with Chinese-language search (company filings, Qichacha).

name: Yu Haifeng
current_role: Founder of Fanhua Puyi / Puyi Inc. (Chengdu wealth management); no longer a principal shareholder of the listed successor (now Maase Inc., Nasdaq: MAAS)
profile: Chengdu-based financier who founded Fanhua Puyi Investment Management in November 2010, a third-party wealth manager for China's mass-affluent and emerging middle class, and took it public on Nasdaq as Puyi Inc. in 2019. He handed the CEO role to Yong Ren in Sept 2019 while staying chairman. The listed company was later renamed Highest Performances and then Maase, and it disposed of the Puyi wealth business in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: Puyi's US listing structure was a VIE: Yu personally held the onshore operating company Puyi Bohui under contractual arrangements that lasted from 2018 until the business was spun out of the listed group in September 2025.
notes: Current activities unclear; he is absent from Maase's 2025 principal-shareholder table. Source for founder/chairman role: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1750264/000121390019018722/f6k092319ex99-1_puyi.htm. No personal contacts found.

name: Zou Guoying
current_role: Founder-era owner of Sacon (帅康) kitchen appliances, Yuyao, Zhejiang; current role unknown (Sacon now part of listed Sunrise East, 603366)
profile: Listed on the 2007 Hurun China list for 'cooking sets' wealth from Sacon (Zhejiang Sacon Electric, 帅康), a Yuyao range-hood and kitchen-appliance maker founded in 1984 as a TV tuner-parts factory. Sacon joined the listed Sunrise East group (日出东方, 603366) in 2017; its chairman is now Xu Xinjian. Zou's present activities could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Sacon began in 1984 as the Yuyao Tuner Parts Factory and in 1993 launched what it calls China's first deep-type range hood; its water heaters were installed at the Bird's Nest and Water Cube for the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
notes: Sacon's site does not name Zou; link rests on Hurun's company attribution. brand@sacon.cn is the company brand department, not his office. Sold control to Sunrise East in 2017, so company is no longer a direct route.

name: Rakesh Malhotra
current_role: Co-founder and head of SAR Group (Livguard, Livfast, Livpure, Lectrix EV, Ncubate), Gurugram
profile: Engineer-entrepreneur who founded Luminous Power Technologies in 1988 and built it into one of India's leading home inverter/UPS and battery brands before selling it to Schneider Electric (74% in 2011, the rest later). He then relaunched SAR Group around clean energy, founding Livguard (inverters, batteries, solar, storage) in 2014, plus EV and venture-incubation arms.
interesting_fact: He started Luminous at 26 with just Rs 40,000 in a 600 sq ft workshop in South Delhi; after the Schneider exit he built a second energy company, Livguard, reported to be worth about Rs 3,500 crore.
deep_cut_fact: Luminous's first big break was an order from Modi Xerox for 28 UPS units worth Rs 4.2 lakh; the company closed its first year with just Rs 8 lakh in revenue.
notes: SAR Group co-founded with Navneet Kapoor (per Livguard 'About us'). Good fit for an energy-storage / Indian power-backup episode. No personal social accounts verified; Livguard's published mailbox is marketing, so it is a fallback rather than a press desk.

name: Chimanlal Khimchand Mehta
profile: Deceased: C.K. Mehta, founder and chairman emeritus of the Deepak Group (Deepak Nitrite, 1970; Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals, 1979), died on 3 July 2023 at age 91 in Vadodara.
notes: Died 3 July 2023 (sources: Business Today; Deepak Fertilisers BSE filing https://bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/695923ed-fd4a-490e-b542-8873a97405a4.pdf). His son Sailesh C. Mehta (P14423) chairs Deepak Fertilisers.

name: Muhammad Raghib Hussain
current_role: CEO, Altera (Intel's FPGA business, majority-owned by Silver Lake) since May 2025; director, Cirrus Logic
profile: Pakistani-American chip executive who co-founded Cavium (networking/security processors) with Syed Ali in 2000, took it public in 2007 and sold it to Marvell for ~$6bn in 2018. He then ran Marvell's products and technology as president, helping build its data-center/custom AI silicon business, before being named Altera CEO when Silver Lake bought 51% of the FPGA maker from Intel.
interesting_fact: Intel picked him to lead Altera as part of the April 2025 deal valuing the FPGA pioneer at $8.75bn, making him the first CEO of Altera as a standalone, PE-backed company.
deep_cut_fact: A NED University (Karachi) computer-systems engineering grad, he began his career at Karachi firms Zelin (Pvt.) Ltd. and ITIM Associates before moving to Silicon Valley (Cisco, Cadence); he later earned an MS from San Jose State.
notes: Input lists him as Marvell president, but he moved to Altera in May 2025. Strong fit for data-center/AI theme (FPGAs, AI infrastructure). Altera media contact is Stephen Gabriel via the newsroom email. NED University awarded him a citation (neduet.edu.pk).

name: Miao Liansheng
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Yingli Green Energy (Baoding); no current role confirmed after the 2020-21 court restructuring
profile: Miao Liansheng (苗连生), from Hebei, left the military, ran a cosmetics trading business in Baoding, and in 1998 founded Yingli, which became one of the world's largest solar module makers and listed on the NYSE in 2007. Heavy debts led to a 2020-21 court restructuring in which the Baoding government became the largest shareholder; his role since then is not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Under Miao, Yingli became the first Chinese company to sponsor the FIFA World Cup (2010, renewed for Brazil 2014), and by 2013 it was described as the world's largest PV module maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he was in the military, then ran the 'Yingli' cosmetics trading company in Baoding. The solar business took the same Yingli name when it was founded in 1998.
notes: Yingli went through court restructuring in 2020-21 and is now controlled by Baoding state investors, so Yingli company channels are probably not a route to him. No personal or office contact found. He last appeared on Hurun in 2011. Avoid the debt and restructuring history in outreach. Living status is unconfirmed: no recent coverage found either way.

name: Sun Hongyuan
current_role: Party secretary, chairman and president of Shanxi Qinxin Energy Group (山西沁新能源集团), Qinyuan, Changzhi, Shanxi (registry data now also list him as director)
profile: Sun Hongyuan (孙宏原, b. 1964), a delegate to the 17th and 18th National Party Congresses, turned a little-known local coal mine in Qinyuan county into Qinxin Group. It is now a 31-company energy group spanning coal, coke, power, metallurgy, materials, machinery, logistics and agro-forestry, with two circular-economy industrial parks. Revenue is near RMB 10bn and it employs about 12,000 people.
interesting_fact: Qinxin is a national foundry-coke production base and a top-10 Chinese corundum maker, a five-star supplier to CITIC Pacific Special Steel and FAW's Changchun foundry. It has given about RMB 250m to education, poverty relief and charity.
deep_cut_fact: A 2012 Sina profile notes that on a hot 25°C afternoon in Qinxin's Taiyuan office, the 'Confucian-merchant' Sun kept the air conditioning off, practising the energy saving he preaches.
notes: Hurun 'Qinxin Group' = 山西沁新能源集团 (unlisted). In 2021 he was named a national 'advanced individual of private economy in fighting COVID-19', the only Shanxi private entrepreneur so honoured. Still called chairman in Oct 2026 coverage. Search autocomplete hints (arrest/funeral) are unsupported by any reports. No published contact.

name: Cao Mingfang
current_role: Founder of Jiangyin Mould & Plastic Group (Jiangnan Mould & Plastic Technology, 000700.SZ); historically chairman, current role unconfirmed
profile: Cao Mingfang (曹明芳, b. 1944, Jiangyin, Jiangsu), a former township official, founded Jiangnan Mould & Plastic in 1984 as a $320k joint venture with a Hong Kong plastics firm. It became a major supplier of car bumpers to Shanghai VW, Citroen and GM and listed in Shenzhen in 1999. Wealth listed jointly with Cao Kebo, who has chaired the listed company.
interesting_fact: The company that became a leading bumper maker started out making decorative candles; its break came in 1988 with an order for front and rear bumpers for 30,000 Santana sedans.
deep_cut_fact: A farmer's son with a middle-school education, he started in 1960 as an apprentice at the township-run Jiangyin No. 2 Textile Machinery Factory and by 25 had risen to head its technical section.
notes: Input's SEC link (TSMC VP) is a mismatch; unrelated person. Industry tag 'wooden floor' also seems wrong (auto parts/moulding). Born 1944; last on Hurun 2020; no death notice found but current status unconfirmed. Very low profile; route only via the listed company's board office. Weak fit for energy/data-center podcast.

name: Chen Zhongxiao
current_role: Chairman and legal representative of Shanxi Lu'an Changping Group (山西潞安常平集团), Huguan county, Changzhi, Shanxi; chairman of Shanxi Dongzhuang Coal and Shanxi Huai'an Coal (per business registries)
profile: Chen Zhongxiao (陈忠孝, b. Aug 1953 in Changping village, Huguan county) built Changping Group, an industrial group of coal, coking and steel ('Changping' in Hurun), out of his poor mountain village and founded the Changping Economic Development Zone. A national model worker, he served on the 11th CPPCC National Committee (2008) and in the Shanxi people's congress.
interesting_fact: He made his home village a showcase of Shanxi's 'new countryside' push: Changping New Village of villas, tree-lined streets and a stream circling the village, while the group spent six straight years in China's top-500 private enterprises.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture was a machine-made brick kiln in Changping village; he grew from there step by step into coal and industry, with the stated aim of lifting the old revolutionary base area out of poverty.
notes: Hurun 'Changping' = 山西(潞安)常平集团, now partly tied to state-owned Lu'an Group. Business registries (aiqicha/qcc, Nov 2026) still list him as chairman of Dongzhuang Coal, so he appears active, but no recent personal news was found to confirm he is alive. Search autocomplete hints at an old dispute with a 'Li Quanxin'; not verified, so avoid. Unlisted company; no published contact.

name: Zhou Licheng
current_role: Legal representative / head of New United Group (新誉集团有限公司), Changzhou, Jiangsu
profile: Zhou Licheng (周立成) heads New United Group, a private equipment-manufacturing group founded in 2002 in Wujin, Changzhou, listed by Hurun together with Ge Yaqin. The group makes rail-transit traction and electrical systems (a key supplier to China Railway rolling stock), wind-power equipment, CNC machines, office equipment, aerospace parts and logistics, with 4,000+ staff and about 10.3bn yuan in assets.
interesting_fact: New United runs a provincial wind-power equipment research institute and a ground test bench that can full-performance test wind turbines up to 3.8 MW before they leave the factory, plus a 3 MW traction-drive lab and a national-level EMC lab.
notes: 'New United' = 新誉集团 (Xinyu Group). Hurun listed him 2009-2021 jointly with Ge Yaqin. Very little personal information online; no recent personal news found, so alive status marked unknown. Email is the group's general address published on its own website.

name: Li Fengyi
current_role: Long-time Erdos Group (鄂尔多斯集团) senior executive and shareholder (vice president in the 1990s); current title not confirmed
profile: Li Fengyi (李凤义) is one of the Erdos Group management shareholders, along with Yang Zhiyuan, Hou Yongwang, Wang Junfeng and Zhang Yinrong, who joined Hurun's list from 2008 on the value of their stakes in Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources (SSE: 600295). The company grew from cashmere into coal, ferroalloy/silicon smelting and power. Yicai's 2010 A-share wealth ranking put his holding at about RMB 1.41bn.
interesting_fact: Hurun 2008 counted a cluster of Erdos managers (Yang Zhiyuan, Hou Yongwang, Li Fengyi, Wang Junfeng, Zhang Yinrong) among Inner Mongolia's 21 rich-listers. All made their wealth from a company that began in cashmere and expanded into coal, power and smelting.
deep_cut_fact: As Erdos Group vice president during the 1998 floods, he framed the company's relief effort as a 'battle' by a group whose mission is 'to warm the whole world', and said it acted without waiting or hesitating. The statement is preserved in an Inner Mongolia tax-records compilation (1996-1998).
notes: Identity confirmed via the Inner Mongolia DRC write-up of Hurun 2008 (lists Li Fengyi among Erdos executives) and Yicai's 2010 A-share 1000 list (https://m.yicai.com/news/602679.html). Could not open SSE annual reports (bot challenge) or lixinger (blocked) to confirm his current board seat. Low profile; any approach would go via Erdos Group / Erdos Resources investor relations.

name: Ge Yaqin
profile: Hurun China (2012-2021) lists Ge Yaqin (戈亚琴) with Zhou Licheng as owners of 'New United', i.e. New United Group (新誉集团), a private Changzhou, Jiangsu group founded in 2002. It makes rail-transit traction/equipment and wind-power equipment, plus CNC and aerospace businesses. No public source describing Ge Yaqin's own role was found.
interesting_fact: New United Group, founded in 2002 in Wujin, Changzhou, is a key supplier of locomotive and rolling-stock components to China's national railway and has been recognised as a national 'single-champion' manufacturer, with about 4,000 staff.
notes: Wealth is shared with Zhou Licheng, New United's founder/chairman, who is the more public figure. Her personal role is unconfirmed. The company website (newunited.com.cn) was unreachable during research. A third-party brand directory lists nug@newunited.com.cn, but that listing is unclaimed and not official, so it is not included as a contact. She dropped off Hurun after 2021.

name: Ding Wenxiang
current_role: Chairman, Inner Mongolia Tehong Coal & Power Group (内蒙古特弘煤电集团), Jungar Banner, Ordos; vice chairman, Inner Mongolia Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese; president, Inner Mongolia Market Development Promotion Association
profile: Ding Wenxiang (丁文祥) chairs Tehong Coal & Power (Hurun's 'Tehong'), a private Ordos group founded in 2000 that runs coal mines in Jungar Banner (e.g. Laiyegou, Guanbanwusu) plus power generation and haulage. He is executive VP of the Inner Mongolia Ordos Chamber of Commerce and was active in charity events in Dec 2025.

He described Tehong's ethos of 'taking from society, giving back to society' and urged firms to help disabled people find work in rural revitalisation.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond coal, he heads the Inner Mongolia Market Development Promotion Association. In Jan 2025 it opened an online/offline showroom for Inner Mongolian specialty foods under the slogan 'Inner Mongolia Flavour'.
notes: Hurun 'Tehong' = 内蒙古特弘煤电集团 (unlisted). In 2018, as a federation vice chairman, he hosted a China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese research visit to Tehong (https://3g.163.com/dy/article/E14KN3RO05129BH0.html). Do not confuse him with namesakes (e.g. the elderly Professor Ding Wenxiang, a doctor). No published contact; possible routes are the Ordos Chamber of Commerce or the overseas-Chinese federation.

name: Wang Zhihua
profile: Wang Zhihua (王志华) appeared on the Hurun China list from 2017 to 2021 with wealth attributed to China Guardian (investments, auction). The name is common, and I could not confirm his role at China Guardian or any related Hong Kong-listed entity before the web search budget ran out.
notes: Ambiguous: a common name, and the link to China Guardian Auctions is unverified. Needs a follow-up search (HKEX filings for China Guardian-related listed companies). Not researched further.

name: Wang Junyang
current_role: Executive director & chairman, Guangdong Kanghua Healthcare Group (康华医疗, HKEX: 3689), Dongguan
