interesting_fact: Main Street's predecessor funds co-founded Quanta Services (NYSE: PWR), the specialty contractor that has become a key builder of transmission lines and power infrastructure for the AI data-center boom; Foster sat on its board from its 1998 IPO until 2025.
deep_cut_fact: At Arthur Andersen he specialised in 'roll-ups' - companies consolidating fragmented industries - the playbook behind Quanta; he was a founding director of the Texas TriCities chapter of the National Association of Corporate Directors and won EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2008 (Houston, financial services). He holds a JD from Wayne State.
notes: Main Street publishes his direct work email on its board page - the best route. Strong podcast angle: the origin story of Quanta Services, now central to US grid and data-center power build-out. Michigan State BBA.

name: Brian E. Lane
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Comfort Systems USA (NYSE: FIX); Director, Main Street Capital (NYSE: MAIN)
profile: Brian Lane has been CEO of Houston-based Comfort Systems USA, a large US mechanical and electrical contractor, since December 2011, after joining in 2003 and rising through regional operations to COO. Under him the company became a major builder of data-center and semiconductor-fab HVAC/electrical systems, with technology work reaching ~45% of 2025 revenue and backlog near $12bn.
interesting_fact: Comfort Systems' technology segment (mostly data centers) grew from about a third of revenue in 2024 to roughly 45% in 2025, making it one of the biggest picks-and-shovels winners of the AI build-out.
deep_cut_fact: A chemistry graduate of Notre Dame, Lane spent 15 years at Halliburton (leaving as Regional Director, Europe & Africa) and was also a Regional Director at Capstone Turbine, the microturbine distributed-power maker - real on-site power experience now relevant to data centers.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast. Gave up the President title in Dec 2025 (remains CEO) - possible succession planning. Corporate general inbox is the published route; IR is handled by the CFO's office.

name: Martin Tuchman
current_role: CEO, The Tuchman Group / Kingstone Capital V; director of FTAI Aviation and Princeton Bancorp; chair of the Tuchman Foundation
profile: Martin 'Marty' Tuchman (NJIT '62, Seton Hall MBA '68) co-founded the container lessor Interpool in 1968 and later the chassis lessor Trac Lease. Interpool listed on the NYSE in 1993 and was sold to Fortress in 2007 for about $797M. He now runs the Tuchman Group (real estate, banking, shipping) and Kingstone Capital V, sits on the FTAI Aviation board and is a large Princeton Bancorp holder.
interesting_fact: NJIT's business school, the Martin Tuchman School of Management, is named after him. As an engineer at Railway Express Agency he helped create the intermodal container and chassis standard that lets boxes move between rail, truck and ship, and it is still in use.
deep_cut_fact: At 25 he was on the Railway Express Agency team that developed the container twist lock. He got the idea for Interpool while on vacation in Bermuda, seeing containers chained to chassis, and later said of the container business: 'This isn't rocket science, it's a hole.'

public_contacts.value: See FTAI Aviation investor relations (board-member page)

notes: Longtime Princeton, NJ resident and active local philanthropist (TASK soup kitchen trustee, Seton Hall and TESU scholarships, YingHua International School). Central Jersey reports he long owned Princeton's PJ's Pancake House (https://archive.centraljersey.com/?p=684317). I could not open that article to verify it. Avoid opening with his Parkinson's philanthropy unless it is relevant. I found no direct email; best route is the Tuchman Group office or FTAI IR.

name: Carl M. Eschenbach
current_role: Former CEO of Workday (2022-2026; co-founder Aneel Bhusri is CEO again); director of Palo Alto Networks per SEC filings
profile: Carl Eschenbach is a veteran enterprise-software operator. After sales roles at 3Com, Lucent, Inktomi and EMC, he spent 14 years at VMware (2002-16), rising to President and COO. He then became a partner at Sequoia Capital, joined Workday's board in 2018, was named co-CEO in Dec 2022 and sole CEO in Feb 2024. Workday's leadership page now lists Bhusri as CEO, and Fortune calls Eschenbach 'former Workday CEO'.
interesting_fact: He began as a competitive wrestler and says the sport shaped his business outlook. His leadership motto: 'By serving others, somehow success will follow you.'
deep_cut_fact: His first credential was an Electronics Technician diploma from DeVry, not an elite university degree. He worked his way up through hands-on tech sales roles before running VMware's go-to-market operations.

public_contacts.value: media@workday.com (Workday media relations; he is no longer CEO)

notes: The exact date and terms of his Workday exit were not verified because the web-search budget ran out. Some reports say February 2026, possibly moving to a strategic-adviser role. Palo Alto Networks board seat is from SEC insider data and was not re-verified. The DeVry diploma comes from his former Workday bio (that page no longer renders). Relevant to AI/enterprise-software discussions; Sequoia alumnus.

name: Michael E. Hurlston
current_role: President & CEO and director, Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE); board member of Flex Ltd. and Astera Labs
profile: Michael Hurlston (59) is a semiconductor/optics executive who became CEO of Lumentum - a key supplier of lasers and optical transceivers for AI data-center interconnect - in February 2025. He was previously CEO of Synaptics (2019-25) and Finisar (2018-19), after 16 years at Broadcom running its wireless connectivity division and later worldwide sales. He also sits on the boards of Flex and AI-connectivity chipmaker Astera Labs.
interesting_fact: He has now run three public tech companies; at Finisar he led the agreed sale to II-VI (now Coherent) - Lumentum's chief optical rival - before moving to Synaptics and then Lumentum.
deep_cut_fact: He is a triple UC Davis Aggie - BS and MS in electrical engineering plus an MBA - and spent the 1990s in marketing and engineering roles at small chip firms including Exar, MicroPower Systems, IC Works, Avasem and Oren Semiconductor before joining Broadcom in 2001.
notes: Highly relevant to the data-center/AI optics theme; regularly speaks on earnings calls and at investor conferences. SEC insider wealth ~US$248M. Best route is Lumentum IR/communications.

name: Neil Utley
current_role: Private investor; director of several private property/investment vehicles (e.g. Tiptree Property Company, NU Twyford Ltd); former director of Markerstudy Group Holdings (2021–2022)
profile: Neil Utley appears on the Sunday Times Rich List (2020) with an insurance fortune. UK Companies House records show a Neil Alan Utley (b. 1962), apparently the same man, as a director of insurer Markerstudy Group Holdings (2021–22). He holds dozens of past and present appointments in property and investment vehicles, some of them registered from the UAE.
interesting_fact: He has held more than 70 UK company appointments over his career, ranging from insurance holding companies to property, motor and even a music venture (Nusic Sounds LLP).
notes: Low-profile insurance entrepreneur. Identity rests only on Companies House plus the Rich List 'Insurance' tag, and the original insurer behind his fortune was not confirmed before the web-search budget ran out. No published contacts found; Markerstudy's corporate press office is a possible indirect route.

name: Michael Kirban
current_role: Co-Founder and Executive Chairman, The Vita Coco Company (Nasdaq: COCO)
profile: Michael Kirban co-founded Vita Coco with Ira Liran in 2004 and built it into the leading US coconut-water brand. Vita Coco also sells Copra, private-label coconut water and other drinks, IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2021, and is a public benefit corporation and Certified B Corp. As executive chairman he continues to steer the company, whose sales and EBITDA grew strongly in 2026.
interesting_fact: The company began after a 2003 conversation in a New York bar with two Brazilian women who said coconut water was what they missed most from home. Liran later married one of them and moved to Brazil, and Kirban's visit there sparked the business.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days Kirban roller-skated through New York neighbourhoods selling Vita Coco and handing out samples himself.
notes: IR is handled by ICR, Inc. He is a relatively media-friendly founder who often speaks at consumer/entrepreneurship events. The web-search budget ran out, so personal social accounts were not verified.

name: Anastasios Gianakakos
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chair, Kardigan, Inc. (Nasdaq: KARD), South San Francisco
profile: Anastasios 'Tassos' Gianakakos (MIT engineering & economics; Northwestern biotech; Harvard MBA) was CEO of MyoKardia, sold to Bristol Myers Squibb for $13.1bn in 2020. He then co-founded Prolaio (connected cardiac care) and Kardigan, a cardiovascular drug developer with three late-stage programs that listed on Nasdaq.
interesting_fact: Kardigan folds Prolaio's AI and real-world-data platform into drug development, aiming to cut the time and cost of cardiovascular trials; MyoKardia's $13.1bn exit was one of the largest cardiology biotech deals.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in vaccine development at Merck & Co. before helping start and scale several biotech companies.
notes: Goes by 'Tassos'. Contact form has a 'Media' inquiry option. Company website is kardigan.bio (kardigan.com is an unrelated parked domain).

name: Ronald David Miller
current_role: Co-Founder & Chairman of the Board, StartEngine Crowdfunding, Inc. (STGC)
profile: Ron Miller is a lawyer-turned-serial entrepreneur who founded, built and sold five companies (including Disability Group, Inc., a large Social Security disability advocacy firm) before joining Howard Marks in 2014 to turn StartEngine from an accelerator into an equity-crowdfunding portal. He chairs StartEngine and, via his trust, holds tens of millions of its shares.
interesting_fact: A four-time Inc. 500/5000 honoree and EY Entrepreneur of the Year finalist, Miller founded the San Diego chapter of the Entrepreneurs' Organization (EO) and served on the YPO/WPO executive committee.
deep_cut_fact: He sits on the board of West Coast Care, a nonprofit helping homeless individuals get off the street, and advises USC's Greif Center for Entrepreneurial Studies.
notes: Good fit for an entrepreneurship/fundraising angle. Only company general contact found; no personal published contact. Disability Group detail comes from aggregator profiles (village.ai), not primary.

profile: Listed on the Sunday Times Rich List 2020 with wealth from property (approx. USD247m). Company and background not identified this session.

name: Aart J. de Geus
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chair, Synopsys Inc. (SNPS); director, Applied Materials (AMAT)
profile: Dutch-born electrical engineer (b. 1954) and a pioneer of logic synthesis / electronic design automation, who co-founded Synopsys in 1986 out of GE and led it as CEO until January 2024, building the leading chip-design software company (including the Ansys acquisition). He now serves as executive chair, alongside board roles at Applied Materials and industry groups.
interesting_fact: He is lead guitarist of the Silicon Valley blues band 'Legally Blue', and speaks English, German, Swiss-German, French and Dutch.
deep_cut_fact: At GE he led the team behind SOCRATES, a rule-based logic-synthesis expert system, finishing his SMU PhD at night; when GE exited semiconductors he persuaded GE vice chair Ed Hood to back a spin-off with $400,000 for equity, which became Synopsys.
notes: Highly relevant to AI/data-center chip design theme; gives a long Computer History Museum oral history (2009). Route via Synopsys corporate PR.

name: Randolph L Marten
current_role: Chairman of the Board and CEO, Marten Transport Ltd. (NASDAQ: MRTN), Mondovi, Wisconsin
profile: Randy Marten joined the family trucking firm founded by his father Roger in 1946, became president at its 1986 Nasdaq IPO and CEO in 1993, turning a Wisconsin milk-route business into a ~3,500-truck temperature-controlled carrier operating from Mexico to Canada. He moved to executive chairman, then resumed the CEO role after Timothy Kohl retired in September 2025.
interesting_fact: Marten Transport began in 1946 when Roger Marten, aged 17, bought a milk-delivery route from the Modena Co-op Creamery with a $400 loan from his mother.
deep_cut_fact: Randy won Ernst & Young's Entrepreneur of the Year award for transportation in the Wisconsin region in 2005; for the company's 50th anniversary in 1996 Marten opened the Roger Marten Community Center in Mondovi.
notes: Low media profile; best route is corporate office in Mondovi, WI via contact page or IR. Energy angle: fleet fuel efficiency (APUs, $16m commitment in 2007), refrigerated/intermodal logistics.

name: Jack M Huynh
current_role: Senior Vice President and General Manager, Computing and Graphics Group, AMD
profile: AMD lifer who joined in 1998 and now runs the Computing and Graphics Group (PC, Radeon graphics and semi-custom businesses), responsible for strategy, business and engineering for CPUs, GPUs and NPUs in end-user devices. He previously led AMD's semi-custom group as SVP/GM and was CVP/GM of the mobile business unit. Wealth (~$240M) is from AMD equity per SEC insider filings.
interesting_fact: Before running PCs and graphics he led AMD's semi-custom group, which designs bespoke high-performance chips for individual customers, and earlier ran AMD's mobile business unit.
deep_cut_fact: He started at AMD in 1998 as a microprocessor design engineer, straight out of an electrical-engineering B.S. at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and has spent his entire 25+ year career at the company.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; frequent keynote presenter (Computex/CES) for AMD client products. Route via AMD Communications (Carolyn Guss listed as press contact in Q3 2026 release).

name: Ren Tiezhu
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Shanxi Tongzhou Coal & Coking Group (Qinyuan County, Changzhi, Shanxi) - placed under official control in May 2026 (see notes)
profile: Self-made Shanxi coal and coke entrepreneur from a farming family in Qinyuan County. Starting with coal haulage in 1978, he built Qinyuan's first coking plant in 1992 and formed Shanxi Tongzhou Coal & Coking in 1995, which later consolidated several local mines under Shanxi's coal-industry restructuring. Former Shanxi provincial people's congress deputy and National May Day Labour Medal recipient.
interesting_fact: He went from herding sheep for his production team (1971) and working as a township cook and livestock broker to founding Qinyuan County's first coking plant and a regional coal-coke group.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, in 1978, was hauling coal with a single donkey-drawn rubber-tyred cart; within about six months he had upgraded to a large cart pulled by three mules. (Workers' Daily profile, 2014, as cited by Wikipedia.)
notes: IMPORTANT: after the 22 May 2026 explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine (Shanxi), Ren was taken into official custody on 23 May 2026 as actual controller of Tongzhou Group. Not appropriate for podcast outreach at present. Hurun-listed only 2008-2010; no published contacts found.

name: He Fangying
current_role: Chairman, Shaanxi Huabin Energy Group and Binxian Coal Co., Ltd. (彬县煤炭有限责任公司, 'Bin Coal'), Binzhou, Shaanxi
profile: Correct name is He Wanying (何万盈). A technician-turned-coal boss, he led the 1998 ownership reform of the near-bankrupt Baizigou mine in Bin county and has chaired 'Bin Coal' since, growing it into a Fortune China 500 private group (coal, chemicals, trade, hotels). He is now pushing into fine chemicals (adiponitrile in Ningdong) and lithium/potash tech with Xi'an universities.
interesting_fact: He spent RMB422m over three years lifting the Xiagou mine from 0.45 to 3 Mt/yr with full mechanisation; the China Coal Industry Association branded the approach the 'Shaanxi Binxian model', alongside the Shenhua and Yankuang models.
deep_cut_fact: In 2020 Bin Coal's Jiangjiahe mine went live with a 5G smart-mine system, billed as the first private coal company in China to apply 5G to mine safety; he has also donated >RMB160m, incl. six Hope primary schools, and plans a company charity fund.
notes: Dataset romanisation 'He Fangying' is wrong; Chinese name 何万盈 = He Wanying. 2010 National Model Worker; VP of Shaanxi Coal Industry Association. No company website or published press/IR email found; Bin Coal is unlisted. Bin county was renamed Binzhou city.

name: Ashwin Ramanlal Gandhi
current_role: Member of the promoter group of Asian Paints Ltd (India's largest paint maker), per company shareholding filings
profile: Ashwin Ramanlal Gandhi belongs to the Asian Paints promoter group (with the Dani, Choksi and Vakil founding families), which holds ~52.6%. Trendlyne showed him with ~4.33m shares (0.45%) in mid-2019, when Hurun India listed him; by 2024-26 his direct stake was 91,860 shares (0.01%), the family holding having moved to relatives and holding companies.
interesting_fact: Asian Paints was founded in 1942 in a Mumbai garage by four friends (Champaklal Choksey, Chimanlal Choksi, Suryakant Dani and Arvind Vakil) and grew into India's paint market leader; the extended promoter families still control just over half the company.
notes: Identity confirmed only as a promoter-group shareholder (Asian Paints shareholding pattern, 31 Mar 2026, lists 'Ashwin Ramanlal Gandhi', promoter group, since 08-02-2019 in SBO disclosure). Holds no board/executive role; no biography, interviews or personal contacts found. Very private; IR email is a corporate route only.

name: Rita Mahendra Choksi
current_role: Listed as an Asian Paints promoter-family shareholder (Hurun India 2018-19)
profile: Rita Mahendra Choksi appeared on the Hurun India Rich List (2018-2019) through holdings in Asian Paints, India's largest paint maker, which was founded in 1942 by four families including the Choksis. No personal public profile was found.
notes: Private passive shareholder; no public role found. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Only corporate IR contact available. Research limited: shared web-search budget exhausted.

name: Kanhaiya Lal Jain
current_role: Founder and Group Chairman, KLJ Group (New Delhi)
profile: Commerce graduate who started KLJ in 1967 as a one-man proprietorship making PVC compounds and built it into South Asia's largest maker of plasticizers and polymer compounds (and the world's largest maker of chlorinated paraffin), with plants in India, Thailand and Qatar (2.3M+ tpa), petrochemical distribution, Delhi NCR real estate and a Qatar chlor-alkali JV.
interesting_fact: KLJ's Qatar chlor-alkali joint venture involved over $125M of investment, and the group recently moved into edible oils and plant-based protein manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: His company profile says his personal passion is improving processes by self-designing plasticizer/PVC machinery; he runs two non-profit schools in Delhi and has donated schools to the Rajasthan government. His guiding motto is 'Shubh Labh' - prosperity through ethical means.
notes: Founder is elderly (career began 1967); day-to-day the group is run by the next generation as managing directors of KLJ Resources and KLJ Polymers & Chemicals, who may be more accessible podcast guests. Petrochemicals, moderate energy fit.

name: Jon Moulton
current_role: Private equity investor; founder of Better Capital and Alchemy Partners; principal behind Perscitus LLP family office (London/Guernsey)
profile: Jon Moulton (b. 1950, Stoke-on-Trent) is a veteran British private-equity investor who ran Citicorp Venture Capital in London, Schroder Ventures (now Permira) and Apax's buy-out group before founding Alchemy (1997) and turnaround fund Better Capital (2009). Now Guernsey-based, he invests privately via the Perscitus family office and writes a regular column.
interesting_fact: He named Better Capital after apologising to Alchemy investors for 'too many investment and people errors' and promising to invest again 'but better'.
deep_cut_fact: A Lancaster chemistry graduate (honorary doctorate 2022), his Jon Moulton Charity Trust funds non-commercial clinical trials - 170+ trials and about £53m committed so far, yielding 100+ published papers.
notes: Famously outspoken and media-friendly (frequent commentator, writes 'Jon Moulton's Diary'-style columns hosted on the Perscitus site) - a good podcast prospect. Perscitus has an EA to the principal; route via info@ inbox.

name: Michael Wright
current_role: Founder (retired) of Riviera Travel, Burton-on-Trent; private investor and philanthropist
profile: Michael Wright founded Riviera Travel in 1984. It began as cheap escorted coach tours to France and grew into the UK's largest escorted-tour operator, adding Eurostar tours and, from 2008, river cruises on its own ships. He and his wife Claire sold control to Phoenix Equity Partners in 2014 (about £130M to them), and Riviera was later sold on to Silverfleet for about £250M. He is now retired and manages his own investments, including stakes in Phoenix funds.
interesting_fact: By 2014 Riviera served 110,000+ customers a year on about £130M turnover. Wright chose a private-equity buyer over larger trade rivals partly to protect his staff.
deep_cut_fact: After hating a bank job his mother suggested, he went to work at a campsite in France. There he sold iced, nicely garnished melons on the beach ('crinkle cut lemons... a 600% markup') and built up a fleet of about 120 rental caravans before switching to coach tours.

name: Tommy Dreelan
current_role: Team principal/driver, Celtic Speed (historic motorsport team); Aberdeen-based oil-services entrepreneur (co-founder of Qserv)
profile: Wexford-raised Tommy Dreelan moved to Aberdeen in 1977 and with his three brothers started an oil-related company in 1986, sold for ~£45.5m. The brothers then built Qserv (well intervention, pipeline and process services, founded 2001), sold to Norway's Aker in 2008 for a reported £100m-£165m. He now focuses on historic motor racing through his Celtic Speed team.
interesting_fact: His Celtic Speed team owns the Williams FW08 that carried Keke Rosberg to the 1982 F1 world title, plus a 1976 March F1 car and an ex-Kremer Leyton House Porsche 962 that won the Classic 24 Hours of Daytona in 2014, 2017 and 2018.
deep_cut_fact: He restored and raced the very Spice C2 Group C car that won the 1986-87 Group C2 world championship with Gordon Spice, and is a dedicated Japanese martial-arts student who received a 'Scottish Samurai (Shogun)' award at Knockhill in recognition of sponsoring young drivers.
notes: Best hook is motorsport (historic F1/Group C, Daytona Classic wins) and the Aberdeen oil-services story. Celtic Speed cars are managed by Scott Sport (Aaron Scott). Qserv sale figures vary by source (£100m-£165m). 'Alive' inferred from Celtic Speed site noting his rally plans from 2021; no recent news found.

name: Jonathan Turner
current_role: Owner and head (MD/CEO) of Bayford Group, Bowcliffe Hall, Wetherby, West Yorkshire
profile: Yorkshire entrepreneur running the century-old family firm Bayford & Co (MD from 2000; family buy-out 2004). Bayford spans fuel distribution, retail energy (E Gas and Power, 340,000+ customers), EV charging (RAW Charging), utility networks (Fulcrum), software (Jumptech), property and hospitality (Bowcliffe Hall, The Yorke Arms).
interesting_fact: Bayford has been in the energy business since 1919 and has ridden every transition since - from coal merchant to fuel cards, retail gas and electricity, and now EV charging and grid connections; its supplier E was named by Which? in 2026 as the UK's No.1 energy supplier.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Newcastle Business School he started in 1986 literally selling coal for the family firm; he describes himself as a 'calculated risk taker', and the 2004 family buy-out (FAMBO) he led is cited as a textbook example of succession planning.
notes: Accessible regional entrepreneur: Connect Yorkshire 'entrepreneur in residence' and listed as an EY Entrepreneur of the Year (North) judge, so business-community networks are a warm route. Bowcliffe Hall (HQ) is also an events venue.

name: Tom Cross
current_role: Executive Chairman, The Parkmead Group plc (Aberdeen-based oil, gas and renewable energy group)
profile: Aberdeen petroleum engineer and North Sea entrepreneur who founded Dana Petroleum in 1994 with under GBP300k of seed capital, listed it in 1996 and ran it until Korea National Oil Corp bought it in 2010 for about GBP1.7bn. He then took over Parkmead, which he called 'Dana Mach 2', building oil and gas assets plus an onshore renewables division.
interesting_fact: Dubbed the North Sea's 'man with the Midas touch' after the Dana sale; he was 2007 Grampian Industrialist of the Year and chaired BRINDEX, the association of British independent oil explorers, from 2005.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Dana he worked for Conoco, Thomson North Sea and Louisiana Land and Exploration, was Director of Engineering at the UK Petroleum Science and Technology Institute, and later served as an adviser to the BBC on energy affairs.
notes: Name is common; identity matched via Sunday Times 'oil, gas and property' listing and Dana/Parkmead background (Thomas Patrick Cross). Accessible, has given many interviews to Energy Voice/Press and Journal. Route via Parkmead's Aberdeen office.

name: John T Chambers
current_role: Founder and CEO, JC2 Ventures; Chairman Emeritus, Cisco; Director, Bloom Energy
profile: John Chambers (b. 1949, raised in Charleston, West Virginia) led Cisco as CEO from 1995 to 2015 and then as executive chairman, growing it into a networking giant through dozens of acquisitions. After IBM sales (1976-83) and Wang Laboratories, he joined Cisco in 1991. Since 2018 he has run JC2 Ventures, a Palo Alto firm that backs and mentors startups, and he sits on Bloom Energy's board.
interesting_fact: In 2018 West Virginia University renamed its business school the John Chambers College of Business and Economics, after the alumnus who earned his business degrees and law degree (JD) there.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 India awarded Chambers the Padma Bhushan, one of its highest civilian honours (trade and industry), for his work building US-India business ties; he chairs the US-India Strategic Partnership Forum. Early JC2 investments included Aspire Food Group, an insect-protein startup.
notes: Very accessible, frequent speaker and an author ('Connecting the Dots', 2018). Best route is JC2's PR agency, Ruder Finn (jc2ventures@ruderfinn.com). Strong energy and AI angle via the Bloom Energy board and his startup portfolio. The @JohnTChambers handle is sourced from a 2018 speaker bio; confirm it is still active.

name: Gary S Winemaster
current_role: CEO, NEXIO Power (propane/alternative-fuel commercial vehicles), per his self-published bio; founder and former CEO of Power Solutions International (PSI)
profile: Illinois-born Wharton graduate who cofounded Power Solutions International in 1985 with his father William, building it into a major maker of alternative-fuel (propane/natural gas) industrial and on-highway engines shipped to OEMs such as Navistar, Hyster-Yale and Caterpillar. He retired from PSI in 2019 and now leads NEXIO, which is developing propane-powered commercial trucks.
interesting_fact: In 2026 the Propane Education & Research Council committed $6M to NEXIO to advance certification of propane commercial vehicles; NEXIO showed a propane truck at the 2026 NPGA Southeastern Propane Expo.
deep_cut_fact: He cofounded PSI in 1985 as a family business with his father, William Winemaster, and stayed 34 years until retiring in 2019.
notes: Sensitive: charged by SEC/DOJ in 2019 over PSI revenue accounting. Acquitted at trial (Sept 2021), and the SEC dropped fraud claims in a 2022 settlement (https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/following-an-acquittal-sec-settles-with-gary-s-winemaster-cleared-of-all-allegations-of-intentional-wrongdoing-301577376.html). Avoid. NEXIO role is from self-published bios only.

name: Rupert Hambro
profile: British banker (Hambros Bank chairman 1983-86; co-founder of J O Hambro Capital Management; Hambro Perks co-founder) who died on 19 February 2021, aged 77.
notes: DECEASED 19 Feb 2021 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Hambro). Sunday Times 2020 entry predates his death.

name: Katherine Littlefield Hagedorn
current_role: Vice Chair of the Board (since 2013) and Finance Committee Chair, The Scotts Miracle-Gro Company; general partner, Hagedorn Partnership L.P.
profile: Katherine Hagedorn Littlefield (b. c.1955) has been a Scotts Miracle-Gro director since 2000 and Vice Chair since 2013. She is a general partner and former chair of the Hagedorn Partnership, Scotts' largest shareholder (about 23%). The family stake comes from the 1995 merger of Miracle-Gro, co-founded by her father Horace Hagedorn, with Scotts. She also serves on the Hagedorn Family Foundation board.
interesting_fact: Miracle-Gro was formed in 1950 by Horace Hagedorn and nurseryman Otto Stern, with a formula developed by a Rutgers professor. Hagedorn's wife Peggy named the product.
deep_cut_fact: She has long worked on Scotts' innovation side. She was on the Innovation Advisory Board from its formation in 2001 until it was retired in 2014, has sat on the board's Innovation and Technology Committee since 2004, and gave up her director pay for 2024 and 2025.
notes: The name in the input is reordered: she is listed as Katherine Hagedorn Littlefield. Very private, non-executive family shareholder. The formal route is Scotts corporate or the Hagedorn Partnership via company IR. Her brother Jim Hagedorn is Chairman and CEO of Scotts.

name: Suresh Kumar
current_role: Executive Vice President, Global Chief Technology Officer and Chief Development Officer, Walmart Inc.
profile: Suresh Kumar leads Walmart's global technology, data, cloud, infrastructure and security organisations. He spent 15 years at Amazon (VP of technology for retail systems), then was corporate VP of Microsoft's cloud infrastructure and operations, then a Google VP/GM over display, video, app ads and analytics. He holds a Princeton engineering PhD and a B.Tech from IIT Madras.
interesting_fact: At Microsoft he ran all physical cloud infrastructure: data centers, network, servers, fiber, supply chain, energy, construction and leases. During his tenure Azure's global reach doubled and its capacity tripled.
deep_cut_fact: Before Amazon he was a research staff member at IBM's T.J. Watson Research Center, working on collaborative supply-chain planning and on shock modelling to protect portable hard-disk drives.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center/energy podcast: he ran Microsoft's data-center, energy and construction build-out. Contact through Walmart corporate communications.

name: Kamalkumar Shivkishan Agrawal
current_role: Director in the Nagpur arm of the Haldiram's group (Haldiram Foods International / Haldiram's India Pvt Ltd), part of the Shiv Kishan Agrawal family
profile: Kamal Kumar Agrawal is a son of Shiv Kishan Agrawal, who leads the Nagpur branch of Haldiram's. The snack and sweets business was founded in Bikaner in 1937 by his great-grandfather Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal. In the 2022–25 restructuring, the Nagpur family took a 44% stake in the merged packaged-snacks company Haldiram Snacks Food, which Temasek invested in in 2025 at about a US$10bn valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's began in 1937 as a single sweets-and-namkeen shop in Bikaner. In 2017 it overtook PepsiCo to become India's largest snack company, and in 2025 Temasek bought a 9%+ stake at about a US$10bn valuation.
notes: Very low media profile; the family speaks through patriarch Shiv Kishan Agrawal. His exact current title was not verified in filings. Not an energy fit, though the Temasek deal and the family-business transition could make a story. Avoid older family legal matters.

name: Patanjali Govind Keswani
current_role: Chairman and Executive Director, Lemon Tree Hotels Ltd (NSE: LEMONTREE); Neelendra Singh is now MD
profile: Patu Keswani (IIT Delhi electrical engineering, IIM Calcutta) spent 17 years at the Taj Group, rising to SVP (special projects), then worked at A.T. Kearney as a director. He founded Lemon Tree Hotels in 2002, opened its first 49-room hotel in 2004 and built it into one of India's largest mid-market chains (brands include Aurika). He remains chairman after handing the MD role to Neelendra Singh.
interesting_fact: Lemon Tree is known for large-scale hiring of people with disabilities, and Keswani chairs India's Skill Council for Persons with Disability.
deep_cut_fact: He calls himself an 'entrepreneur by chance': he left a long corporate career (Taj, then A.T. Kearney) to start Lemon Tree. He was inducted into the FHRAI Hall of Fame in 2010 and received IIM Calcutta's Distinguished Alumnus Award in 2012.
notes: sectdeptt@ is the address the company publishes for the Chairman & MD in its SEBI disclosure-contacts document; gm_cs@ is the Company Secretary. 'Entrepreneur by chance' is the title of a 2011 article listed on Lemon Tree's media page, not a verified direct quote. Media-friendly founder.

name: Arun K Chittilappilly
current_role: Managing Director, Wonderla Holidays Ltd (India's largest amusement-park chain); promoter shareholder of V-Guard Industries
profile: Arun K. Chittilappilly is the elder son of V-Guard founder Kochouseph Chittilappilly and a promoter-shareholder of V-Guard Industries, the Kerala-based maker of voltage stabilisers, inverters, wires and appliances. He co-promoted and runs listed Wonderla Holidays, which grew from the Veegaland water park in Kochi (2000) to parks in Bengaluru (2005), Hyderabad (2016), Bhubaneswar (2024) and Chennai (2025).
interesting_fact: Wonderla started as 'Veegaland' in Kochi in 2000; Arun and his father then built the 82-acre Wonderla Bengaluru for about INR105 crore in 2005, and the Kochi park was rebranded Wonderla in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: In January 2018 he personally launched 'Recoil', a reverse-looping roller coaster that is Wonderla Hyderabad's signature ride, alongside CEO D.S. Sachdeva.
notes: Hurun lists his wealth under V-Guard (family holding); his operating role is at Wonderla. Confirm he is still MD before outreach (search budget ran out in this pass).

name: Hemant Kanoria
current_role: Founder and former Chairman & MD, Srei Infrastructure Finance; founder, Kanoria Foundation
profile: Kolkata entrepreneur Hemant Kanoria ran two family flour mills in West Bengal before founding, with brother Sunil Kanoria, Srei - an infrastructure and construction-equipment financier that became one of India's largest NBFCs in its sector. Srei's board was superseded by the RBI in 2021 and the companies went through insolvency resolution; Kanoria remains active in philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Before Srei he operated two family-owned flour mills in West Bengal, then pivoted into financing construction equipment for India's infrastructure build-out; he later chaired FICCI's National Committee on Infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: In 2014 he set up the Kanoria Foundation, which runs Suryodaya schools for underprivileged children and created the Acid Survivors and Women Welfare Foundation for treatment and rehabilitation of acid-attack survivors.
notes: Sensitive: Srei was taken over by RBI in 2021 and went through IBC insolvency - avoid as outreach topic. No published contact found; Kanoria Foundation would be the most appropriate route (site not verified). Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemant_Kanoria

name: Sunil Kanoria
current_role: Co-founder, Srei Infrastructure Finance; Honorary Consul of Spain in Kolkata; Kanoria Foundation
profile: Kolkata-born (1965) chartered-accountant-turned-financier who co-founded Srei Infrastructure Finance with brother Hemant in 1989, building it into a leading infrastructure-equipment financier. He set up a JV with BNP Paribas (2007) and co-created telecom-tower firm Viom Networks with Tata Teleservices (2009), later sold to American Tower; he was ASSOCHAM president from 2015.
interesting_fact: In 2009 he formed Viom Networks with Tata Teleservices, one of India's big telecom-tower companies; Srei's stake was acquired by American Tower Corporation in 2016 - a digital-infrastructure angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He serves as Honorary Consul of Spain in Kolkata, and his Kanoria Foundation has hosted a series of global 'Confluence' gatherings on humanity, power and spirituality since 2009, alongside its Suryodaya Schools for underprivileged children.
notes: Wikipedia article is flagged for undisclosed paid editing; verify facts. Srei entered RBI-initiated insolvency proceedings in 2021, so avoid framing around Srei's current status; infrastructure/telecom-tower history is the better hook.

name: Pratul K Shroff
current_role: Founder and former CEO, eInfochips (now an Arrow Electronics company); venture investor and philanthropist (Dr. K. R. Shroff Foundation)
profile: Pratul Krishnakant Shroff (BITS Pilani, IIM Ahmedabad) worked at Intel, co-founded Daisy Systems in Silicon Valley, then returned to found Ahmedabad's eInfochips (1994/95), a chip-design, embedded and IoT services firm sold to Arrow Electronics in 2018 (reported ~$300m+). He now invests in start-ups and runs a rural-development foundation.
interesting_fact: He was one of the founders of Daisy Systems, a Silicon Valley computer-aided-engineering pioneer that hit about $125m in sales and ~1,200 staff within five years of founding.
deep_cut_fact: He started eInfochips with one office, one engineer and Rs 5.5 lakh, and in the late 1990s deliberately skipped the Y2K/COBOL gold rush to bet on embedded systems and chip-verification IP.
notes: Anchor trustee of ISDM (Indian School of Development Management): https://www.isdm.org.in/our-people/pratul-shroff-anchor-trustee . No published personal or foundation contact found. Gujarat tech-ecosystem elder statesman; good fit for semis/engineering-services angle.

name: Vikram Indrajit Shah
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Shalby Ltd (Shalby Hospitals), Ahmedabad
profile: Ahmedabad orthopaedic surgeon (b. 1962) who trained in joint replacement in the UK (Wrightington/Ormskirk), Switzerland, Germany and the US, then founded Shalby in 1994 as a six-bed knee-replacement unit. It grew into a listed multispecialty hospital chain with 2,000+ beds and over 100,000 joint replacements performed.
interesting_fact: He set a record of 3,000 knee replacement surgeries at a single centre in 2008, and his 'Zero Technique' cut total knee replacement time to roughly 7-12 minutes.
deep_cut_fact: He invented the 'OS Needle' (Orthopaedic Surgeons' Needle), able to pass through both bone and soft tissue, for which he received an award from Johnson & Johnson; he was also the only Indian surgeon on Zimmer's Board of Designers.
notes: His personal site drvikramshah.com routes to info@shalby.org. Note Shalby's Wikipedia page is tagged as promotional; surgery-count claims are company-sourced.

name: Suresh Tyagi
current_role: Vice Chairman & Whole-Time Director, Gold Plus Glass Industry Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: Suresh Tyagi is vice chairman of Gold Plus Glass, the family glass group led by his brother, chairman Subhash Tyagi. It grew from a 1985 glass-trading business into architectural glass processing (Sonepat, Kala Amb) and, from 2009, float glass manufacturing in Roorkee; Gold Plus now claims about 26% of India's float-glass capacity and is the country's second-largest maker.
interesting_fact: In 2009 Gold Plus began float-glass production at Roorkee, describing itself as the first fully Indian-owned company to do so, and added a 700 TPD second float line in 2018. Its tagline is 'Apna Desh, Apna Glass'.
deep_cut_fact: The group's origin story: Subhash Tyagi started in 1985 as a glass trader with Rs 5,000 of capital and became India's largest glass trader by the early 1990s before moving into processing in 1996.
notes: Few personal details published about Suresh himself; deep-cut fact is about the family business (his brother's founding story). info@ is the general corporate inbox. Energy angle: float glass is an input for solar panels and energy-efficient buildings.

name: Ashish Bharat Ram
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, SRF Limited (India)
profile: Cornell MBA Ashish Bharat Ram, of Delhi's Shriram business family, apprenticed at SRF for over five years before becoming MD in 2007 and later Chairman & MD. He transformed SRF from a nylon tyre-cord maker (70% of revenue) into a diversified fluorochemicals, specialty chemicals and packaging-films group, with chemicals now the growth engine and heavily export-led.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership SRF shifted from a business where nylon tyre cord was ~70% of revenue to one where technical textiles were ~20%, with chemicals and packaging films making up the rest; in specialty chemicals, exports exceed 90% of sales.
deep_cut_fact: Reflecting on why he reinvented SRF, he told Business Standard: 'There were limited buyers for nylon tyre cord. The only differentiator was cost... We had to change SRF's business model.' He spent 5+ years as an understudy inside SRF before taking over in 2007.

public_contacts.value: cs@srf.com (company secretary; listed as authorised KMP contact)

notes: Hosts quarterly earnings calls, so accessible to media via SRF IR. Energy angle: SRF makes refrigerant gases and fluorochemicals, and battery-chemical/fluoropolymer expansion. Avoid Shriram family split history. cs@srf.com reported via search of SRF investor page; I could not load the page directly.

name: Kartik Bharat Ram
current_role: Joint Managing Director, SRF Ltd (reappointed to 31 March 2031); Chairman, KAMA Holdings
profile: Third-generation member of the Shri Ram family that controls SRF, the Gurugram-based chemicals (fluorochemicals, refrigerants, agrochemical intermediates), packaging-films and technical-textiles group. He served as Deputy MD for decades before becoming Joint MD alongside his brother, Chairman & MD Ashish Bharat Ram, and chairs KAMA Holdings, SRF's majority shareholder.
interesting_fact: Under his watch SRF approved ~Rs 1,100 crore for new plants at Dahej, Gujarat to make fourth-generation refrigerants with much lower global-warming potential, part of a Rs 1,500 crore capex round in Oct 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He has served as President of the Indian Blind Sports Association; he is also a Fellow of the Aspen Institute India's India Leadership Initiative, chaired CII's Delhi State Council in 2007-08, and studied at Santa Clara University before a Cornell MBA.
notes: Also on the SRF Foundation board; active in education philanthropy (Shri Educare, Ashoka University per MarketScreener — unverified on primary site). SRF is relevant to energy via refrigerants/fluorochemicals for cooling.

name: Arshia A. Lalljee
current_role: Director (listed as Managing Director in some registry data), Süd-Chemie India Pvt. Ltd.
profile: Arshia Altaf Lalljee has been a director of Süd-Chemie India since 2006, alongside Iskander Altaf Lalljee, and the Lalljee family are the company's Indian promoters. Founded in 1969 and registered in Kerala, Süd-Chemie India makes catalysts for refineries, petrochemicals, synthesis gas/ammonia, sulfuric acid plants and vehicle emission control. It has plants in Kochi and Vadodara and an affiliation with Clariant Catalysts.
interesting_fact: Süd-Chemie India is a 50-year-old catalyst maker serving energy and petrochemicals. Its products include ReforMax low-pressure-drop catalysts for ammonia/syngas, ShiftMax shift catalysts and EnviCat BS6 low-PGM catalysts for vehicle emissions.
notes: Very private; the company is unlisted and has no press office. Titles come from registry aggregators (tofler/qorpiq), which differ on whether she is MD or director. CEO Prakash Babu Surya runs operations. She appeared only on the 2019 Hurun India list.

name: Michael W Bokan
current_role: Independent Director, Wolfspeed, Inc. (since Sept 2025); retired SVP Worldwide Sales, Micron Technology (2018-May 2025)
profile: Micron lifer who joined in 1996 and rose through sales to lead worldwide sales from Oct 2018, reporting to CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, building relationships with OEM, hyperscale and distribution customers through the AI-driven memory (HBM) boom. Retired in May 2025 and joined the board of silicon-carbide maker Wolfspeed on its emergence from Chapter 11.
interesting_fact: He took over Micron's global sales organisation in Oct 2018 from 30-year veteran Steve Thorsen, the year Micron passed $30B in annual revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his Micron career he was General Manager of the Crucial division, Micron's consumer memory/SSD brand, before moving into OEM sales; he is a Colorado State University business graduate.
notes: Low public profile, no personal channels found. Net worth reflects SEC-reported Micron/Wolfspeed holdings. Best route is via Wolfspeed IR/corporate secretary. Good data-center memory angle (HBM/hyperscaler sales).

name: Chen Jianlong
current_role: Probable match: Chairman, Highsun / Hengshen Holding Group (恒申控股集团), Fuzhou (Changle), Fujian - caprolactam, nylon chemical fibres, new materials
profile: Most likely Chen Jianlong (陈建龙), Fujian's 'chemical-fibre king': he began in 1984 with a workshop making nylon rope and built Hengshen into an integrated caprolactam-nylon group (Shenyuan New Materials, Hengshen Synthetic Fibre, Liheng Nylon). Hurun's 2005-09 'Hengli Chemical Fibre' label may reflect Hengshen/Liheng; it is not Chen Jianhua's Jiangsu Hengli Group.
interesting_fact: Hengshen bought Fibrant, the caprolactam business spun out of Dutch group DSM, giving it plants in Lianjiang, Nanjing and Europe and making it the world's largest caprolactam producer with an eight-step integrated chain.
deep_cut_fact: His caprolactam push was personal: when a few foreign chemical giants monopolised the nylon feedstock, the seller's-market pain 'left a lasting mark' on him, so he went abroad to buy capacity; in 2017 Hengshen's RMB40bn, 1 Mt/yr polyamide complex in Lianjiang started up.
notes: Link to Hurun 'Hengli Chemical Fibre' not confirmed: Hurun naming not found online; Jiangsu Hengli Group is Chen Jianhua's (different person). Chen Jianlong of Hengshen fits name + chemical fibre + era and, via Liheng Investment, controls SZSE-listed Meida (000782). Treat as probable; verify before outreach.

name: Zhao Jianchang
current_role: Chairman & general manager, Zhejiang Fuling Holding Group (浙江富陵控股集团), Shaoxing - plastic packaging films and petrochemicals
profile: Zhao Jianchang (赵建昌, b. Nov 1956, Shaoxing) grew Fuling from plastic packaging film into petrochemicals: in 2002 he committed RMB2.68bn to a 600kt/yr polypropylene plant, an early large private project. The group has two petrochemical firms, two film makers and a trading arm (~RMB10bn assets); he owns ~95.8% and is VP of the Zhejiang Packaging Federation.
interesting_fact: His 2002 RMB2.68bn bet on a 600kt/yr polypropylene project to feed his own film plants was among the first large private-sector petrochemical investments in China.
notes: Dataset's 'Fulin Group' (富林) matches Zhejiang Fuling Holding (富陵) by person, packaging + petrochemicals and era. Facts from an All-China Federation of Industry & Commerce profile (2014) and Shuidi credit registry (legal rep, ~95.79% stake), seen via search; ACFIC page not reachable here for full read. No published contacts found.

name: Zhang Er
current_role: Former chairman & CEO, Honghua Group (宏华集团, HKEX 0196), Chengdu land-drilling-rig maker; now controlled by Dongfang Electric (chair since 2022: another executive)
profile: The Honghua Group chairman is Zhang Mi (张弭); dataset's 张珥/'Zhang Er' appears to be a character error. He led Chengdu-based Honghua - one of the world's largest land drilling-rig makers, HK-listed in 2008 - as chairman and president, expanding into shale-gas equipment, electric frac fleets and offshore. Honghua later passed to state-owned Dongfang Electric.
interesting_fact: Under him Honghua shipped nearly 60 land rigs to the US shale-gas industry, and developed a 6,000-hp AC electric fracturing pump - billed as the world's highest-horsepower frac pump - where six units replace 18 conventional diesel pumps.
deep_cut_fact: In Sept 2015 he presented to the US Energy Association in Washington on 'Efficient and environmental solutions of shale gas exploitation', arguing China's shale bottleneck was not resources or technology, and pitching grid/hydro-powered electric frac fleets for Sichuan.
notes: Name: confirm as Zhang Mi (张弭); English sources (Drilling Contractor 2013, PR Newswire 2015-16, USEA 2015) call him Honghua chairman/president/CEO. Current role unknown - Honghua board since 2022 led by a Dongfang Electric appointee; Zhang not in recent director lists. Company site hh-gltd.com.

name: Zhou Hanping
current_role: Co-founder, former vice-chairman and director, Oriental Energy (东华能源, SZ:002221); current role unconfirmed
profile: Born May 1951, Zhou co-built Oriental Energy, a Zhangjiagang/Nanjing LPG importer and trader that grew into a major propane-dehydrogenation (propylene and polypropylene) producer. He was vice-chairman at its 2008 Shenzhen IPO. In 2013 he and his daughter Zhou Yifeng, later chairman, together controlled about 52% of the company.
interesting_fact: Oriental Energy began in 1996 as Zhangjiagang Donghua Unocal Energy, a joint venture with foreign partners including US oil company Unocal, and later became one of China's leading LPG and propylene players.
notes: Born 1951 and low profile; the last Hurun listing was 2010. The IR email is Oriental Energy's board-secretary contact (2025 annual report summary). Company leadership has since passed to others (Zhou Yifeng; recent reports name Yang Wei as chairman).

name: Daniel M. Friedberg
current_role: Managing Partner/co-founder of 325 Capital (NYC small-cap activist investor); Chairman of Quest Resource Holding (QRHC); director of TransAct Technologies and MultiSensor AI
profile: Ex-Bain & Company partner who ran Sagard Capital Partners (Power Corporation of Canada's PE arm) from 2005-2016, then co-founded 325 Capital in 2016 to take constructive stakes and board seats in under-covered small caps. He chairs Quest Resource, sits on the TransAct and MultiSensor AI (industrial thermal sensing) boards, and is CEO of Hampstead Park Capital and EV startup Roundtrip EV Solutions.
interesting_fact: He sat on the boards of four Roth CH SPACs, which merged with PureCycle Technologies (plastic recycling), Reservoir, QualTek and, in 2023, solar optimizer maker Tigo Energy.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2019 he has served on the Board of Directors of USA Field Hockey; he holds a BSc from the University of Manchester Institute of Science & Technology (UMIST) and an MBA from Cornell's Johnson School.
notes: Wealth figure reflects 325 Capital fund holdings reported as 10% owner (APEI, QRHC, MSAI, TACT), not purely personal. Partner Laura Laufer is listed as 325's head of IR. Good fit for energy/AI-sensing angle (MultiSensor AI, Tigo SPAC, Roundtrip EV).

name: Ross M Cummings
current_role: Trustee of family trusts that held ~11.6% of Sterling Check Corp. (filing address c/o Bluewater Systems, Austin, TX)
profile: SEC filings show Ross M. Cummings reported as a 10%+ holder of background-screening firm Sterling Check Corp. (IPO 2021; acquired by First Advantage in 2024) solely in his capacity as trustee of three family trusts linked to Sterling's founding Greenblatt family, with sole voting/dispositive power over 11.07m shares. He does not appear to be the economic owner of that stake.
notes: Likely a FALSE POSITIVE for a UHNW list: the ~$189m is trust assets he controls as trustee, not his own wealth (Schedule 13G, 14 Feb 2022: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1645070/000119312522039906/d316664dsc13g.htm). No public bio or contact found. Recommend dropping.

name: David Stinnett
current_role: Partner, Trive Capital (Dallas); Chairman of Karman Holdings (NYSE: KRMN); director of Lyntris Inc. (LYNX)
profile: David Stinnett (about 43) is a partner at private-equity firm Trive Capital, which he joined at its founding in 2012. He focuses on aerospace, defense, government services and industrial technology. He has been on the Karman Space & Defense board since 2020 and chairs it; Karman IPO'd in February 2025 at about $4B. He joined the board of defense-tech company Lyntris in May 2026, and also sits on the boards of Robinson Helicopter and Field Aerospace.
interesting_fact: Karman, the Huntington Beach space and defense fabricator he chairs, came out of Trive's portfolio and listed on the NYSE in February 2025 at roughly a $4B valuation.

Forbes Ukraine ranked him No. 59 among the richest Ukrainians in 2021 (~$180m).
interesting_fact: Before crypto he spent 2006-2014 manufacturing and distributing payment/trade terminals, and he holds a PhD in law.
deep_cut_fact: He served in Ukraine's armed forces in 2001-2003 in the radiation, chemical and biological reconnaissance troops, and graduated from Kharkiv Automobile and Highway University in 2009 in 'roads and airfields' engineering.
notes: Caution: Ukrainian Wikipedia records fraud allegations against his crypto projects and criticism over alleged Russia/criminal links - reputational due diligence advised before featuring. No published personal contact found.

name: Forrest Eugene Norrod
current_role: Executive Vice President & General Manager, Data Center Solutions Business Group, AMD; board member, Intuit
profile: Forrest Norrod runs AMD's data-center business - EPYC server CPUs, Instinct AI GPUs, Pensando networking and rack-scale AI systems - having joined AMD in 2014 after 14 years at Dell, where he ended as VP/GM of the server business (2009-2014). His wealth (~$176M per SEC insider holdings) comes from AMD equity as the data-center unit became AMD's largest growth engine.
interesting_fact: AMD's data-center group under Norrod powers El Capitan and Frontier, which hold top places among the world's supercomputers, and is now pushing 'Helios' rack-scale AI systems against Nvidia.
deep_cut_fact: He is a chip designer by training: Virginia Tech BS/MS in electrical engineering, worked at x86 challenger Cyrix (1993-97), led National Semiconductor's integrated x86 CPU business (1997-2000), and holds 11 US patents in computer architecture, graphics and system design.
notes: Highly relevant for data-center/AI angle; frequent keynote speaker (AMD Advancing AI, Hot Chips, etc.). Interview requests should go via AMD corporate communications (media contact emails on AMD's contacts page are rendered dynamically and were not captured).

name: Richard Higham
current_role: Former Group CEO (to June 2020), later non-executive director and senior adviser, Acteon Group (subsea services, Norwich UK)
profile: Most likely the Richard Higham who spent about 30 years building Acteon Group, a Norwich-based subsea services company formed from UWG Group (Acteon brand since 2004), whose backers have included KKR. He handed the CEO role to Carl Trowell in June 2020 and stayed on the board as a non-executive director and senior adviser.
interesting_fact: Acteon grew by acquisition into a group of specialist subsea businesses (moorings, cables, survey, decommissioning) serving both oil and gas and offshore wind; in 2024 it was acquired by Buckthorne and One Equity Partners.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the business in 1989, when it was still UWG Group, and led it for three decades through its 2004 rebranding as Acteon and its shift to a subsea focus.
notes: The Sunday Times 2020 entry only says 'oil and gas services'; the link to Acteon is my inference (no other UK oil-services Richard Higham found), so verify before outreach. The UWG/1989 detail rests on secondary profiles. No published personal contact found; route via Acteon.

name: Daniel S Shugar
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nextpower Inc. (Nasdaq: NXT; formerly Nextracker)
profile: Solar pioneer who co-founded PowerLight (sold to SunPower for $332M in 2007; he became SunPower president), then co-founded Nextracker in 2013 as its CEO. It became the top utility-scale solar tracker maker, IPO'd in 2023 and rebranded as Nextpower in 2025, adding power conversion and battery storage.
interesting_fact: Under Shugar the company had shipped trackers for 100+ GW of solar capacity in 40 countries by 2024, and in Dec 2024 shipped the first US-made solar trackers with 100% domestic content after reshoring manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: An RPI electrical-engineering grad from New Jersey, he started in the late 1980s in PG&E's R&D department; in 2023 the American Solar Energy Society gave him its Hoyt Clarke Hottel Award, and S&P Global Platts named him Chief Trailblazer of the Year.
notes: Very media-friendly CEO and frequent conference speaker; excellent fit for an energy podcast. Pitch via media@nextpower.com (global media contact Brandy Lee).

name: Mark Allen McFarland
current_role: President and CEO, Talen Energy Corp. (NASDAQ: TLN) since May 2023; Director, California Resources Corp.
profile: Known as 'Mac', a veteran power-industry executive who has run Luminant (2013-16), GenOn Energy (2017-18) and California Resources Corp. (2020-23) before taking over Talen Energy. At Talen he pivoted the independent power producer toward data centers, selling the Cumulus campus beside the Susquehanna nuclear plant to AWS and signing a large nuclear power deal with Amazon.
interesting_fact: In March 2024 Talen sold its 960 MW Cumulus data-center campus next to the Susquehanna nuclear station to AWS for $650m - one of the first big nuclear-to-data-center co-location deals; McFarland argued 'around-the-clock nuclear power matches very well with around-the-clock data center power needs.'
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer: a B.S. in Civil Engineering with an environmental concentration from Virginia Tech (plus an MBA from the University of Delaware), and spent 1999-2008 at Exelon, rising to SVP of Corporate Development.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast (nuclear + hyperscaler deals). Media contact is Talen's Director of Corporate Communications as listed in 2026 press releases.

name: Anton Bilton
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Deputy Chairman, The Raven Property Group (formerly Raven Russia); non-executive Chairman, Sabina Estates (Ibiza)
profile: Anton Bilton is a third-generation British property developer who co-founded Raven Russia (now The Raven Property Group), which built a large portfolio of Russian logistics warehouses, and has founded three other AIM-floated companies. He chairs Sabina Estates, a luxury-villa development on Ibiza, and funds consciousness/psychedelics research.
interesting_fact: After a mystical experience at 15, he co-founded the Tyringham Initiative in 2015, hosting multidisciplinary symposia on DMT research at his Buckinghamshire home; its documentary 'ENTITIES' completes production in 2026. He also wrote a novel, 'Soul Searcher', about a Wall Street LBO dealmaker's near-death experience.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded the UK charity Standing Voice, which supports people with albinism in Tanzania and East Africa, and through the Bilton Charitable Foundation helped establish The Bilton High School in Hlabekisa, South Africa.
notes: Unusually open public persona (own website, blog, book, documentary) - good prospect, best via his site's contact form. Raven's Russian warehouse business is a sensitive topic post-2022; the Raven role on his site may be dated. Do not confuse with the unrelated US 'RAVEN Property Group' (Pacific Northwest).

name: Gary Dutton
current_role: Retired founder of Synseal Extrusions (UK PVC-U window, door and conservatory-roof systems); no current executive role found
profile: Gary Dutton MBE founded Synseal in 1980 and built it into a leading UK maker of conservatory roof kits and PVC-U window/door profiles, run from a 34-acre site in Sutton-in-Ashfield, Nottinghamshire, with 500+ staff. He exited in 2010 when H.I.G. Europe backed a management buyout, retiring after a two-year wind-down 'to pursue his hobbies'.
interesting_fact: Synseal's turnover reached £76.3M in the year to March 2009, shortly before its private-equity sale.
deep_cut_fact: As Synseal chairman he was ranked Britain's 23rd best entrepreneur by Management Today, on the strength of 200% turnover growth in five years to £66M.
notes: Private retired individual; no published contact found. Weak fit for energy/data-center focus (window/insulation products only). Last rich-list appearance was 2020; no recent public information.

name: Mark Bailey
profile: Listed on the Sunday Times Rich List 2020 with Rhianon Bailey, with wealth from car sales. I could not identify which UK car-retail business this is before my web-search budget ran out.
notes: Common name. Identity unresolved; needs another search pairing 'Mark and Rhianon Bailey' with the dealership group name.

name: The Duke of Roxburghe
current_role: 11th Duke of Roxburghe (Charles Innes-Ker), owner of Floors Castle and the Roxburghe Estates in the Scottish Borders
profile: Charles Innes-Ker (b. 1981), the 11th Duke, succeeded his father Guy, the 10th Duke, in August 2019. He inherited Floors Castle near Kelso, about 60,000 acres around the Cheviot Hills and River Tweed, and hotels in the area. Educated at Eton, Newcastle University and Sandhurst, he served as a captain in the Blues and Royals, including in Iraq, and now runs the family estate business.
interesting_fact: The title was created in 1707, and the estate's wealth was boosted by the 8th Duke's 1903 marriage to American heiress May Goelet. When the 10th Duke died in 2019, The Times estimated his wealth at £132m.
deep_cut_fact: As Lord Bowmont, he and fellow Army officer Rob Bassett-Cross founded Capstar, a chauffeur company with a fleet of black Jaguar XJs that mostly employed ex-servicemen and women.
notes: The 2020 Rich List entry fits the 11th Duke, who inherited in 2019 (the 10th Duke, Guy, died in 2019). For podcast angles, landed estates often host renewables, though no Roxburghe energy projects were verified here. Contact via the Floors Castle/estate office. Avoid personal and marital topics.

name: Doug Black
current_role: Chairman and CEO, SiteOne Landscape Supply (NYSE: SITE)
profile: Doug Black (61) has been CEO of SiteOne Landscape Supply since 2014, when it was carved out of Deere & Co, and chairman since 2017. He took it public in 2016 and built it, largely through acquisitions, into the largest US wholesale distributor of landscape supplies. Before SiteOne he spent 18 years at CRH's Oldcastle, rising to President and COO, after starting at McKinsey.
interesting_fact: A West Point graduate (math/civil engineering), he served as a US Army Engineer Officer from 1986 to 1990, leading construction projects in the southeastern US, Central America and South America.
deep_cut_fact: At West Point he was an AP All-American fullback and an NCAA Scholar-Athlete. He later earned his Duke Fuqua MBA as a Fuqua Scholar.
notes: Public-company CEO based in Roswell, Georgia. Best route is SiteOne investor relations.

name: Nandlal Valecha
current_role: Co-founder of Regent Group / Regent Gas (London commercial gas supplier); stepped down from all group directorships in June 2019
profile: Nandlal Mulchand Valecha (b. 1938), a British Indian entrepreneur, co-founded Regent Gas in 1995 with his son Deep Valecha; the Acton-based group supplies natural gas, connections and metering to businesses across Great Britain and has expanded into water and power. He resigned his Regent directorships in 2019; Deep now runs the group as CEO.
interesting_fact: In 2024 the Valecha-owned Regent Group agreed to take private TClarke - the 1889-founded building-services firm that once wired Windsor Castle and lit up the Shard - for £90.56m, after building a ~21.5% stake from 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Regent Gas Ltd was incorporated in October 1995; Companies House shows Nandlal Valecha appointed a director in January 1996 and serving for more than 23 years until June 2019.
notes: Shared fortune with son Deep Valecha (Sunday Times Rich List 2020). Nandlal is ~88 and no longer active; status since 2019 not publicly confirmed. Deep Valecha (CEO, Regent; director of TClarke) is the realistic interview target. Email is Regent Gas's general company inbox.

name: Deep Valecha
current_role: Owner of Regent Group (Regent Gas); director, Regent Gas Ltd and Regent Acquisitions Ltd; non-executive director of TClarke plc since June 2024
profile: UK businessman behind Regent Gas, a family-owned supplier of gas and metering services to industrial and commercial customers, set up in 1995 (with family incl. Nandlal Valecha) and trading as a licensed supplier since 1996. After building a ~21.5% stake from 2018, Regent bought London building-services/electrical contractor TClarke for ~£90m in 2024, taking it private.
interesting_fact: Regent's 2024 takeover of TClarke — an electrical and building-services contractor founded in 1889 that works on data centres and large commercial buildings — moved a gas-supply family business into construction services.
deep_cut_fact: Regent Gas started trading as a licensed gas supplier in April 1996, an early independent entrant in the newly liberalised UK gas market, and remains privately owned.
notes: Private; no personal or press contacts published (Regent Gas website unreachable from this session). Route via TClarke corporate office or Regent Gas. TClarke angle (data-centre electrical contracting) is a good podcast hook.

name: William Asprey
current_role: Founder, William & Son (Mayfair luxury jeweller, gunmaker and outfitter)
profile: A seventh-generation member of the Asprey dynasty (Asprey, the Bond Street luxury house founded 1781 by his ancestor of the same name), William Asprey founded William & Son in Mayfair in 1999. The business sells fine jewellery, timepieces, leather and homeware plus a gun room and field sports range, largely made by British craftsmen, and holds a Royal Warrant.
interesting_fact: His ancestor William Asprey founded Asprey in 1781 as a silk-printing business in Mitcham, Surrey; the family sold the group to Prince Jefri Bolkiah's Amedeo in 1995 for GBP244m.
deep_cut_fact: William & Son was set up in 1999 by William Asprey as the seventh generation of the family, with a stated mission of keeping traditional British crafts alive by working with artisans and designer-makers.
notes: Current status/involvement in William & Son not re-verified (web search budget exhausted). Not an energy/tech figure; luxury retail angle.

name: Sun Shuhua (孙树华)
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China list in 2004 (about $170m) with wealth from Hualin Group, a business in PE piping, plastic film and spinning mills. No current information could be verified before the lane's web search budget ran out.
notes: Only a 2004 Hurun listing; current status unknown. Needs Chinese-language research (孙树华 华林集团).

profile: Listed on Hurun China 2007 (shared with Qian Yunbao) with wealth from Hengbao Group (Jiangsu Hengbao, smart cards/SIM and communication equipment, 002104.SZ). No published biography or current role found.
