name: Brian Long
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, Atlantic Bridge (growth-equity tech investor, Dublin/London/Palo Alto); director of Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) since ~2015
profile: Irish engineer-entrepreneur (Trinity College Dublin, BA/MSc in electronic engineering and semiconductor microelectronics) who founded chip-IP firm Parthus in 1993 and ran it until 2003, taking it public on Nasdaq and London. In 2004 he co-founded Atlantic Bridge, now managing over EUR 1bn across eight funds, which backed GaN/SiC power-chip maker Navitas from early on.
interesting_fact: Navitas, the GaN/SiC power-chip company whose board he sits on, is supplying devices for NVIDIA's 800 VDC power architecture for next-generation AI-factory data centres; Atlantic Bridge's fund fully exited its Navitas stake in Dec 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before VC, he built Dublin's Parthus Technologies (founded 1993), a chip-IP licensor for mobile/Bluetooth/GPS that floated on Nasdaq and the LSE in 2000 and became today's CEVA after merging with DSP Group's Ceva unit.

public_contacts.value: https://www.abven.com (Atlantic Bridge; contact page lists offices)

notes: Investor rather than operator - good guest on European deep-tech / power-semis for AI. Navitas board status in late 2026 not re-verified after Atlantic Bridge's exit. Common name: confirm via Atlantic Bridge. Parthus->CEVA merger detail is from general knowledge plus Navitas bio (which says 'Parthus-CEVA').

name: Charles Alvin Meloy
current_role: Director, Diamondback Energy (Nasdaq: FANG) since September 2024; retired President & CEO, Endeavor Energy Resources
profile: Charles A. 'Chuck' Meloy (65) is a Permian Basin veteran. He ran Kerr-McGee's exploration and production as a VP, was EVP of US Onshore E&P at Anadarko until 2015, and was President & CEO of Endeavor Energy Resources from 2016 to 2020. After Diamondback's 2024 merger with Endeavor he joined Diamondback's board as one of four directors designated by Endeavor's Stephens family stockholders.
interesting_fact: He is one of four Diamondback directors whom the Stephens family stockholders, legacy owners of Endeavor, have the right to designate under the 2024 Endeavor-Diamondback merger, which created one of the largest Permian Basin producers.
deep_cut_fact: He is an engineer by training: a 1982 Texas A&M chemical-engineering graduate and member of the Society of Petroleum Engineers and Texas Professional Engineers. He was also on the API Upstream Committee and the boards of Western Gas Equity Partners and the Independent Producers of America Association.
notes: Retired executive, now a board member; no personal public channels found. Diamondback's own IR pages block automated access. Its quarterly press releases list an investor-relations contact, so check the latest release for the current address. Route via Diamondback IR (Midland, TX).

name: Marshall S McCrea Iii
current_role: Co-CEO and director, Energy Transfer LP (NYSE: ET); retiring as co-CEO at end of 2026, remaining on the board (Tom Long becomes sole CEO)
profile: Known as Mackie McCrea, he has spent ~30 years at Energy Transfer, joining its predecessor in 1997 as SVP of business development and producer services, then serving as president of ETP (2008), group COO/chief commercial officer (2015-18), president and CCO (2018-20) and co-CEO since Jan 2021. He has led ET's commercial push into supplying gas to AI data centers (e.g. CloudBurst in Texas).
interesting_fact: On AI-driven gas demand he said: 'The data centers - especially around AI - it's going to happen... We're believers like everybody else,' and after the CloudBurst deal noted that tech companies 'are in a hurry.'
deep_cut_fact: He joined Energy Transfer's predecessor in 1997 - when it was a small Texas gas gatherer - and has served on the partnership's board since December 2009, making him one of the longest-tenured executives in its rise to a top US midstream company.
notes: Goes by 'Mackie'. Retirement as co-CEO announced June 2026 (8-K), effective ~Dec 31 2026 - post-retirement he may be freer for a podcast. Energy Transfer media relations is by phone (Vicki Granado, 214-840-5820) per 2026 press releases; no current published email confirmed. Strong data-center/gas angle.

name: N Jagan Mohan Reddy
current_role: Vice Chairman, Rain Industries Ltd (Hyderabad; NSE: RAIN) and CEO of Rain Carbon Inc.
profile: Hyderabad industrialist (Jagan Mohan Reddy Nellore - not the Andhra politician Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy) who built Rain from an Indian calcined-petroleum-coke maker into Rain Carbon, a global producer of calcined pet coke, coal-tar pitch and advanced carbon materials for aluminium smelting, batteries and chemicals, via acquisitions of US-based CII Carbon (2007) and Germany's RÜTGERS (2013).
interesting_fact: Rain is one of the world's largest producers of calcined petroleum coke and coal-tar pitch, two key inputs for aluminium smelter anodes; he addresses shareholders as Vice Chairman at its AGMs.
deep_cut_fact: A Purdue University industrial-engineering graduate, he was founder-MD of Rain Calcining, which began producing calcined petroleum coke in Visakhapatnam in 1998, before leading its globalisation through the CII Carbon buyout (renamed Rain CII Carbon).
notes: Name collision risk with Andhra Pradesh politician Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy - always use 'Jagan Mohan Reddy Nellore / Rain Carbon'. Purdue degree field comes from Crunchbase (secondary); confirm before quoting. Only published company channel is the company secretary mailbox.

name: Sailesh Chimanlal Mehta
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corp. (DFPCL), Pune; chairman, Fertiliser Association of India (elected 2025)
profile: Sailesh C. Mehta, son of founder C.K. Mehta, has run Deepak Fertilisers since the 2010s (chairman since 2012/13), steering it from commodity fertilisers and chemicals toward ammonia self-sufficiency (a new greenfield ammonia plant), technical ammonium nitrate for mining, and branded crop nutrition. He was elected chairman of the Fertiliser Association of India in June 2025.
interesting_fact: He was a winner in the Natural Resources category of the 2024 BT-PwC India's Best CEOs ranking, credited with a strategy shift 'from customer to consumer' and backward integration into ammonia instead of relying on Middle East imports.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining DFPCL's move into branded crop nutrition, Mehta cited the insight that a 1% rise in sugarcane sucrose content is worth about Rs 35 crore to a sugar mill: 'If people see value, they will not speak about the price.'
notes: Accessible, media-friendly CEO (Zee Business, Outlook Business, Business Today interviews). Best route: Anuradha Bose, EVP Group Branding & Corporate Communications, listed as media contact in the Q1 FY27 results (July 2026); CFO Subhash Anand is the IR contact. His father C.K. Mehta (P11922) died in July 2023.

name: Jigish Shailesh Choksi
current_role: Managing Director, ELF Trading & Chemicals Manufacturing Ltd; Asian Paints promoter-group member (non-executive director of Asian Paints 2019-2025)
profile: Member of the Choksi family, one of the four founding promoter families of Asian Paints (est. 1942), India's largest paint maker; his wealth stems mainly from that inherited stake. He runs agro-chemical trader ELF Trading & Chemicals, works in the family's Navbharat Packaging corrugated-box business, and oversees a family office investing in equities, debt and startups.
interesting_fact: Despite being a promoter heir, he started at Asian Paints in 2010 as a regular sales hire and served on the company's board from April 2019 until 2025.
deep_cut_fact: An RIT (Rochester Institute of Technology) business grad, he spent three years as an Area Manager in project sales at Asian Paints, then moved to marketing, where he was in charge of several product launches in the waterproofing range; his board profile also calls him a sports enthusiast.
notes: Low-profile heir; no personal channels found. Asian Paints IR email is a weak route since he left the board in 2025 (email appears in the filing footer, OCR-garbled as 'mvestor.relations'). Industry tag in input (petrochemicals) is loose; paints/chemicals.

name: Varun A Vakil
current_role: Chairman and Non-Executive Director, Elcid Investments Ltd; Assistant General Manager - Supply Chain New Products, Asian Paints Ltd (promoter group)
profile: Varun Amar Vakil is a member of the Vakil family, one of the four founding promoter families of Asian Paints, and is in its promoter group. He chairs Elcid Investments, a Vakil-family holding company whose main asset is an Asian Paints stake, and works in Asian Paints' supply-chain function for new products.
interesting_fact: Elcid Investments, which he chairs, became India's most expensive stock overnight in October 2024: a special price-discovery auction re-rated it from about Rs 3.53 to roughly Rs 2.36 lakh per share, reflecting the value of its Asian Paints stake.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BBA from Michigan State University and an MBA in entrepreneurship and global marketing from Babson's F.W. Olin Graduate School. He began with an internship at Asian Paints, then worked at Piramal Glass before rejoining Asian Paints in supply chain.
notes: vakilgroup@gmail.com and the Worli office are Elcid Investments' published company contact (also the Vakil group office). He is a working manager rather than a public-facing founder, so keep the outreach low-key. His link to energy/chemicals is weak (paints). His father Amar Vakil, a former Asian Paints promoter director, died in 2021/22.

name: Shyam Sunder Jindal
current_role: Promoter and head (described in group materials as chairman) of the B.C. Jindal Group (Jindal Poly Films, Jindal India, Jindal India Thermal Power); not on the current Jindal Poly Films board
profile: Shyam Sunder Jindal leads the Delhi-based B.C. Jindal Group, founded in 1952 as a steel-pipe maker; Hurun India listed him in 2016-17 via Jindal Poly Films. The group expanded into polyester yarn, BOPET and BOPP packaging films (it bought ExxonMobil's BOPP business in 2013) and a 1,200 MW coal power plant in Angul, Odisha.
interesting_fact: Jindal Poly Films runs what the group calls the world's largest single-location plant for polyester (PET) and polypropylene (OPP) films, at Nashik, Maharashtra, and in 2013 bought ExxonMobil's BOPP films business.
notes: Do not confuse him with the O.P. Jindal/JSW family. Very low media profile. Several unofficial 'personal' sites (odoo.com, netlify) appear in search but are unverified or offline, so ignore them. The group's energy angle is Jindal India Thermal Power (2x600 MW, Odisha). Approach via the group's corporate office.

name: Matthew J Murphy
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Marvell Technology (MRVL)
profile: Matt Murphy spent 20+ years at Maxim Integrated, rising to EVP of business units, sales and marketing, before becoming Marvell's CEO in 2016 (chairman since 2023). He turned Marvell from a storage/consumer chip vendor into a data-infrastructure company built around custom AI silicon, optical DSPs and data-center connectivity for hyperscalers.
interesting_fact: He is the first executive to have chaired both the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA, 2018) and the Global Semiconductor Alliance (GSA), and sat on eBay's board 2019-2022.
deep_cut_fact: Not an engineer by degree: he holds a BA from Franklin & Marshall College, and outside chips he is a Trustee of the U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Foundation; he also set up Marvell's formal global philanthropy program.
notes: Excellent fit for data-center/AI angle (custom AI accelerators, optical interconnect). Frequent conference/podcast speaker (e.g. OFC 2026 Optica Executive Forum). Net worth in input is from SEC holdings only. Franklin & Marshall BA per https://www.semiconductors.org/board/matt-murphy/.

name: Marc Worth
profile: Co-founder (with brother Julian) of fashion trend-forecaster WGSN, sold to Emap for £140m in 2005, and later founder of Stylus. Died of a heart attack on 13 January 2023, aged 61.
notes: DECEASED 13 Jan 2023 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Worth). Rich-list entry was shared with brother Julian Worth, who could be researched separately if relevant.

name: Kaveh Alamouti
current_role: Hedge-fund manager and trader, London; current firm not verified (former CEO, Citadel Asset Management Europe)
profile: Kaveh Alamouti (b. 1954) is an Iranian-British trader with an Imperial College engineering degree and an MBA and PhD in finance from London Business School, where he also taught. He set up Tokai Bank Europe's global arbitrage group in 1990, founded Optimum Asset Management in 1999, traded at Moore Capital, and reportedly ran Citadel's European asset-management arm from 2008 to 2014.
interesting_fact: He moved from academia to markets: he was on London Business School's finance faculty before becoming head of trading at Tokai Bank Europe.
notes: Most of his Wikipedia biography is uncited, so verify his career details and current firm before outreach. Very private. I found no published contact; web-search budget was exhausted.

name: Lawrence Tomlinson
current_role: Chairman, LNT Group (Ginetta Cars, Ideal Carehomes, LNT Construction, LNT Software, LNT Solutions), Leeds
profile: Lawrence Tomlinson (b. 1964, Batley) is an engineer-turned-entrepreneur. In 1988 he bought his parents' single care home and built the Tricare/Orchard Care Homes group, selling it for £175m in 2007. LNT Construction has built roughly a fifth to a quarter of all new UK elderly care homes. He now runs LNT Group, which spans care homes, care software (CoolCare), rail and aviation de-icing chemicals, and Ginetta sports and race cars.
interesting_fact: He won the GT2 class at the 2006 Le Mans 24 Hours driving the Team LNT Panoz Esperante. He also drew up the base specification for the Ginetta G50 race car, which was built in six months.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he wrote care-home management software on an Amstrad 8256 for his parents' new care home, the seed of the CoolCare software now used in 1,000+ homes. He bought LNT Solutions, which makes leaf-fall and third-rail de-icing chemicals for Network Rail, from his motor-racing instructor over a pub conversation after a track day.
notes: Was BIS 'Serial Entrepreneur in Residence' in 2013-14 (author of the Tomlinson Report on bank lending to SMEs) and IoD Director of the Year 2013. Holds honorary doctorates from Huddersfield, Bradford and Leeds Met. Sunday Times 2025 put his wealth at £525m. Strong entrepreneurship guest; LNT Solutions offers an energy/infrastructure angle.

name: Fatma Kiamil
current_role: Co-owner (with Mustafa Kiamil) of JJ Food Service; stepped down as a director of the JJ group companies in Dec 2016/Jan 2017
profile: Fatma Kiamil and her husband Mustafa Kiamil built JJ Food Service, a UK independent foodservice wholesaler founded in 1988 by a former restaurateur. It supplies restaurants, takeaways, schools and caterers from 14 branches with 4,000+ products. Companies House shows she was a director of JJ Food Service from 1991 until she resigned in early 2017.
interesting_fact: JJ began in 1988 as a supplier to takeaway and restaurant owners, founded on the idea that 'suppliers should make life easier for customers'. It now sells through online, app, phone and self-service kiosk channels across 14 UK branches.
deep_cut_fact: She was a director of JJ Food Service Ltd from December 1991, effectively from the company's first years, until January 2017. She also served on the board of the group's Falcon Fast Food Supplies business.
notes: Very private; Mustafa Kiamil is the founder figure. No press email found on the JJ site (only an export sales address). She is no longer a director, so approach via the JJ head office. Not an energy fit.

name: Roger Ames
current_role: Former record-industry executive (London Records, Warner Music Group, EMI); no current role verified
profile: Roger Ames is a veteran music executive who ran London Records as a semi-independent label inside PolyGram. After the 1998-99 PolyGram/Universal merger he took the label with him to Warner Music Group, where he became a top executive, and he later held senior roles at EMI. His rich-list wealth comes from music.
interesting_fact: When he left PolyGram for Warner Music Group around the 1999 PolyGram-MCA/Universal merger, he took London Records with him.

deep_cut_fact: Jutal's 2006 Hong Kong IPO priced at just HK$1.50 a share, raising HK$150M from 100 million shares; the group began in 1995 as a small Shenzhen machinery-equipment firm, adding a Hong Kong engineering arm in 1996.
notes: Very low personal profile; no personal bio found. market@jutal.com is the company's listed general/marketing email (not a dedicated press desk). Energy-transition angle: oil and gas modules plus offshore wind. Hurun wealth figure (2007) is dated.

name: Mike F Chang
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and EVP of Strategic Initiatives, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor (Nasdaq: AOSL)

name: Gary Hromadko
current_role: Independent Director, Equinix Inc. (since June 2003); private investor

name: Randall J Weisenburger
current_role: Managing Member, Mile 26 Capital LLC; Presiding Director and Senior Independent Director, Carnival Corp & plc; director of Valero Energy, MP Materials and Corsair Gaming
profile: Finance executive (age 67) who was EVP and CFO of advertising giant Omnicom Group from 1998 to 2014, after a decade (1988-98) as a founding member of boutique bank Wasserstein Perella, where he ran its merchant-banking arm Wasserstein & Co. Since 2014 he has run private investment firm Mile 26 Capital and serves on major public boards, including Valero (since 2011) and rare-earths producer MP Materials (since 2020).
interesting_fact: He has served on Carnival's boards since 2009 and is now its Presiding Director and chair of the compensation committee, while also sitting on the boards of refiner Valero Energy (since 2011) and rare-earths producer MP Materials (since 2020).
deep_cut_fact: In 1988 he was a founding member of Bruce Wasserstein and Joseph Perella's boutique investment bank Wasserstein Perella, serving as president and CEO of its merchant-banking subsidiary Wasserstein & Co. and as an executive of several of its portfolio companies before joining Omnicom.

Valero/MP Materials board seats give energy/critical-minerals angle.

name: Padmakar Haribhau Mulay
current_role: Chairman, Ajeet Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (PM Group), Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra
profile: Padmakar Mulay founded Ajeet Seeds in Aurangabad in 1986 and built it into a hybrid-seed company covering 22 crops. It is the flagship of the PM Group, which also includes construction (Gangamai Industries & Construction), sugar and other seed businesses. His son Sameer Mulay runs it day to day as managing director.
interesting_fact: Ajeet Seeds' first big hit was the Ajeet-11 cotton hybrid, launched in 1992. The company says it was the first private seed company in India to introduce a proprietary wheat variety, Ajeet-102.
deep_cut_fact: Ajeet Seeds set up its own Plant Biotechnology Research Center in Hanumantgaon (Gangapur taluka) in 2003. Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University recognises it as a research centre, and it launched three Bt cotton hybrids in kharif 2006.
notes: Elder founder. A Feb 2025 Lokmat obituary of his brother lists him (as Padmakarrao Mulay) among the surviving brothers. MD Sameer Mulay is the public face of the company. The email is the company's general address, and the X account belongs to the company, not to him personally.

name: Gautam N Mehra
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Savita Oil Technologies Ltd (re-appointed MD to Sept 2028)
profile: Chemical engineer with a UC Berkeley MBA, Gautam N. Mehra leads Savita Oil Technologies, the Mumbai petroleum-specialties firm his father N.K. Mehra co-founded in 1961. Savita leads India in transformer oils, white oils and waxes, sells in 75+ countries, owns wind farms, and now markets data-center immersion-cooling and BESS fluids.
interesting_fact: Savita says it set up India's first private-sector R&D centre in the petroleum industry, was the first Indian private petroleum company to earn ISO 9001, and commissioned its first windmill in Maharashtra around 1999-2002 - an early oil-company move into renewables.
deep_cut_fact: Savita began in 1961 at Sakinaka, Mumbai, making liquid paraffin as an import substitute; in his chairman's message Mehra says founder N.K. Mehra 'drew inspiration from the sun' and coined the company motto 'Bonds Build Businesses'.
notes: legal@savita.com is the published registered-office (Nariman Point) email, likely routed via company secretary. Good podcast angle: Savita now sells 'Data Center Fluids' (immersion cooling) and transformer oils for grid/BESS.

name: Vijay Sankeshwar
current_role: Founder & Chairman, VRL Logistics / VRL Group (Hubballi, Karnataka)
profile: Born 1950 in Gadag, Karnataka. He started a cargo business in 1976 with one truck and built VRL Logistics into one of India's largest commercial-vehicle fleet owners. He also founded the Kannada newspaper Vijaya Karnataka (sold to the Times Group in 2007) and later Vijaya Vani, and was a BJP MP for Dharwad North. He is chairman, and his son Anand runs VRL as MD.
interesting_fact: His life story, from a single truck to India's largest logistics fleet, became the 2022 multilingual biopic 'Vijayanand'. He received the Padma Shri in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1976 with one truck bought on a Rs 2 lakh loan and took heavy early losses from accidents and competition. In 1978 the family moved to Hubballi and added three more trucks. His father ran a printing press, B G Sankeshwar & Co., in Gadag.
notes: Both emails appear in VRL's FY2025-26 BRSR filing on NSE. The filing also lists the Company Secretary, Aniruddha Phadnavis (aniruddha@vrllogistics.com), as compliance contact. Better known in Karnataka media and politics. Family-owned Kannada media (Vijaya Vani, Digvijay 24x7) are another route.

name: KP Ramasamy
current_role: Founder and Chairman, KPR Mill Ltd and KPR Group (Coimbatore, India)
profile: Born into a farming family in Kalliampudur village, Erode district, he started as a power-loom cloth maker in 1971 and, with his brothers, built KPR Mill into one of India's largest vertically integrated apparel makers, with sugar, ethanol, power and education arms. He still chairs the group and appears on Forbes India's rich lists.
interesting_fact: KPR Mill runs an in-house higher-education program for its mostly rural women workers. The company says about 27,000 employees have earned degrees (computing, management, nursing, teaching) while working there, through tie-ups with Annamalai, Alagappa and Tamil Nadu Open universities.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first power-loom business in 1971 with a borrowed Rs 8,000, which some profiles say came from his mother's uncle.
notes: Also appears as Palanisamy Ramasamy Kalliampudur on data sites. The published email is the company's investor-grievance address, not a press line, so the corporate office in Coimbatore is the realistic route. The group also has an energy angle: windmill/solar and sugar-ethanol cogeneration.

name: KPD Sigamani
current_role: Managing Director and promoter, K.P.R. Mill Ltd (Coimbatore); heads the apparel division
profile: KPD Sigamani is a founding promoter of the KPR Group, the Coimbatore textile conglomerate begun by K.P. Ramasamy as a power-loom business in 1971. As MD of K.P.R. Mill he runs the export-focused apparel division of a yarn-to-garment maker that also has sugar, ethanol, wind and solar power. Re-appointed MD in 2025.
interesting_fact: KPR Mill runs a long-running in-factory education programme (since 1998) that lets its mostly women workers earn school-level, degree, vocational and nursing qualifications while employed; tens of thousands have completed courses.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mathematician: the group describes him as a postgraduate in mathematics, and he is credited with a major role in project execution for KPR's expansions.
notes: The published email is KPR Mill's investor grievance-redressal address (company secretary), not a personal contact. Chairman K.P. Ramasamy is the group's public face; Sigamani gives few interviews.

Sigamani) behind KPR Mill, one of India's largest vertically integrated textile/apparel makers. As MD he oversees finance, cotton procurement and yarn marketing, and fronts the company's earnings calls.

deep_cut_fact: Despite being a CA, Nataraj's remit at KPR has long included the hands-on job of cotton procurement and yarn marketing, not just finance.
notes: Low public profile; route via company secretary/IR. Family also runs KPR Institute of Engineering and Technology trust.

name: Ajay Relan

profile: Ajay Relan is Managing Director of Sharda Motor Industries, an Indian auto-components maker (exhaust/emission-control systems, suspension) founded by the Relan family. He oversees manufacturing, plants, R&D and product development; wealth is shared with family member Rohit Relan.

A chartered accountant, he has run engineering companies since 1986 and leads Bharat Seats, a seating-systems JV of Suzuki Motor Corp, Maruti Suzuki and the Relan family, which recently opened a Gujarat plant.

Wind-energy angle may suit the energy podcast. Best route: company website/office in Coimbatore.

name: Nara Bhuvaneswari
current_role: Vice Chairperson & Managing Director, Heritage Foods Ltd; Managing Trustee, NTR Memorial Trust
profile: Runs Heritage Foods, the Hyderabad-based listed dairy company, which she joined in 1994 as a whole-time director before becoming Vice Chairperson & MD; she is its largest individual shareholder (~24%). She also leads the NTR Memorial Trust (healthcare, blood banks, education, clean water) and is the daughter of N. T. Rama Rao.

notes: Wife of Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu; politically high-profile family, so outreach is best via Heritage Foods corporate office or NTR Trust. Heritage's site blocks some automated fetches.

name: Nemish S Shah
current_role: Co-founder, ENAM Holdings (manages treasury and proprietary capital); Governing Body member, FLAME University
profile: Mumbai investor who co-founded ENAM with Vallabh Bhanshali in 1984. ENAM began as a broking firm, then grew into a leading IPO investment bank. ENAM's banking and broking businesses were merged into Axis Bank. Shah now runs ENAM Holdings' treasury and long-term proprietary investing in Indian equities, using bottom-up fundamental research.

notes: Very low public profile and no personal social media found. ENAM founders also set up FLAME University in Pune, which may be a warmer route in. No published office email found.

profile: Bathina Umapathy Reddy co-founded BGR (originally B Girijapathi Reddy & Co.) in 1988 with Girijapathy Reddy and I. Sudhakara Reddy. It is now a Hyderabad-based contract-mining and Mine Developer & Operator (MDO) group running coal and mineral projects for NTPC, CCL, Vedanta and Hindalco. He still leads the group alongside the second generation.

deep_cut_fact: BGR began in 1988 as a small partnership firm, B Girijapathi Reddy & Co., set up by three co-founders including Umapathy Reddy. It became a company only in 2011, and by FY2022-23 it was moving about 29 million tonnes of coal a year.

profile: Uday Jayant Desai is listed as founder director and managing director of Frost International Ltd, a Mumbai commodity-trading company (incorporated 1995, also with a Kanpur presence) that traded a large portfolio of agri and other commodities. current_role: Member of the Board of Directors, Cloudflare (NYSE: NET); former Cloudflare CTO (to March 2025)

name: Sharad V Parekh
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Nilkamal Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Co-founded Nilkamal in 1981 with elder brother Vamanrai Parekh, leaving the family's metal-button business to make plastic household goods in Powai, Mumbai. He led marketing and pioneered India's plastic material-handling (crate) business; Nilkamal is now a Rs 2,000+ cr furniture, materials-handling and retail (@home) group. He became chairman in 2020 after years as MD.
interesting_fact: Nilkamal's roots go back to a one-machine metal-button factory shed set up by the family in 1934; the brothers switched to plastics in 1981 and 'crate' became almost synonymous with the Nilkamal brand.
deep_cut_fact: Spotting that Operation Flood was spawning dairies, Sharad Parekh, then 37, followed a milk van all the way to Mumbai's Worli Dairy to pitch plastic crates; by 1983 Nilkamal won its first crate order, launching its material-handling business.
notes: Low-profile family business founder; company bio says he is active in several charitable trusts and educational institutions. Route via corporate office.

name: Jayendra H Kharawala
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Jay Chemical Industries Pvt Ltd (JCIL), India (listed as chairman on the company website)
profile: Founder of Jay Chemical Industries, started in 1967 as a small dye and dye-intermediate unit. JCIL is now one of the world's top reactive-dye producers, with more than 15% of India's market, sales in over 40 countries and revenue above $200M. It has expanded into digital textile inks, construction chemicals and garments.
interesting_fact: JCIL makes more than half of its own raw-material inputs (over 50% backward integration). That is a deliberate self-reliance strategy that Kharawala built into a dye business started when international firms dominated Indian dyes.
deep_cut_fact: Jay Chemicals marked its 50th anniversary on 9 March 2017. The company credits its founding to Kharawala's vision 'to do business that would not only provide for his family but would better society as well'.
notes: Private company with a low profile. Day-to-day operations are run by Managing Director Greeven Kharawala. Alive status is not independently confirmed (the company site still lists him as chairman). The links are corporate, not personal. Industry is textile dyes, so the fit with energy and data centers is weak.

name: Ramesh Vinayak Vaze
current_role: Not on the current board of S H Kelkar and Company (Keva); current status unconfirmed
profile: Member of the Vaze promoter family behind S H Kelkar and Company (now branded Keva), a Mumbai fragrance, flavour and aroma-ingredients maker that began as an industrial perfume manufacturer in British India and is now one of India's largest fragrance companies. The family's third generation, Kedar Vaze, is Group CEO; Prabha Vaze is a non-executive director.
interesting_fact: Keva started as S H Kelkar & Company, a maker of industrial perfumes in British India, and grew organically and via acquisitions into an Indian fragrance multinational.
notes: Hurun India 2018-2019 listing. He does not appear on Keva's current board/leadership page; his current role and whether he is alive could not be verified (web search budget exhausted). Contacts are company-level (Keva). Industry is fragrances/chemicals, weak fit for energy focus.

name: Arvind Domadia
current_role: Managing Director, Kunal Structure (India) Pvt Ltd, Ahmedabad (per company registry aggregators)
profile: Gujarat infrastructure contractor. Kunal Structure (India) Pvt Ltd was incorporated in 2006 and builds roads, canals and buildings. A registry aggregator reported operating revenue above INR 500 crore for FY2021. Registry listings name Arvindbhai Amrutlal Domadia as managing director, with his son Kunal A. Domadia as co-director.
interesting_fact: The company carries his son's name, Kunal, who sits on the board with him. Kunal Structure is privately held and was incorporated in April 2006 with registered offices in Bodakdev, Ahmedabad.
notes: Identity based on registry listings only (Arvindbhai Amrutlal Domadia, DIN 01608844). No press coverage, official website or published contacts found. Very private. Kunal Structure also appears in Gujarat tender records.

name: Kulanthaivel Vinayagam
current_role: Managing Director, SCM Group / The Chennai Silks; Group MD, Space Textiles Pvt Ltd
profile: K. Vinayagam (also spelled Vinayakam) is one of the brothers who run SCM Group, the family textile empire founded by A. Kulandaivel Mudaliar, best known for the South Indian retail chain The Chennai Silks. The group also spins yarn, exports hosiery and garments to brands such as Decathlon and Hanes, and runs precast-construction, school and hospital ventures.
interesting_fact: In 2007 The Chennai Silks set a Guinness record for the world's most expensive silk saree, worth about Rs 41 lakh. It reproduced 11 Raja Ravi Varma paintings and took around 4,760 hours to design.
deep_cut_fact: The business began as a Khadi shop, Kasthuribhai Khadi Vasthralayam in Madurai (1962). Today it is run jointly by eight brothers, four sisters and their children, about 130 family members, and spins roughly 130 tonnes of yarn a day on 170,000 spindles.
notes: Low individual media profile; family-run group led publicly by chairman T.K. Chandiran. His son V. Vikram Narayen is Executive Director. The best route is the corporate office via the official website. Spelling varies (Vinayagam/Vinayakam).

name: Shantaben P Jain
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder, Kewal Kiran Clothing Ltd (Mumbai; 'Killer' jeans) - no executive role found
profile: Shantaben P. Jain is a member of the Jain promoter family of Kewal Kiran Clothing, the Mumbai apparel maker behind the Killer, Lawman Pg3 and Integriti brands run by the Pukhraj Jain brothers (CMD Kewalchand P. Jain). Exchange filings show the largest promoter block (~30.8m shares) held in her name jointly with Kewalchand and Hemant P. Jain.
interesting_fact: The promoter group reported no pledged or encumbered shares for FY26; her name heads the joint holding with Kewalchand and Hemant Jain.
notes: Private family shareholder with no public profile, interviews or biography found; relationship to the Pukhraj Jain brothers not stated in sources (name suggests family matriarch, unverified). Approach would realistically be via the company / CMD Kewalchand Jain.

name: Sonal Yatin Kakodkar
current_role: Listed shareholder/family member associated with Parle Products (per Hurun India 2018-2019); no public executive role found
profile: Appears on Hurun India 2018-2019 (about US$132m) with wealth attributed to Parle Products, the Mumbai biscuit maker (Parle-G) founded in 1929 and controlled by the Chauhan family. No public biography, interviews or executive role were found; she appears to be a passive family shareholder.
interesting_fact: Parle Products, the source of her listed wealth, became India's first packaged-food company to pass US$2bn in annual revenue (FY22).
notes: Very private; family relationship to the Parle Products Chauhans not publicly documented. Not a public-facing figure; only route is via Parle Products corporate.

name: Rita Kishore Sinha
current_role: Non-Executive Director, SIS Limited (Security and Intelligence Services India)
profile: Rita Kishore Sinha is a long-time director and major shareholder (~16%) of SIS Ltd, the Patna-founded security, facility-management and cash-logistics group started by her husband, journalist-turned-politician RK Sinha. SIS is now one of India's largest private employers, with FY2026 revenue of about ₹15,982 crore; her son Rituraj Sinha is Group MD.
interesting_fact: SIS grew from a small Patna security agency into a multinational group; the company says revenue rose from ₹25 crore in 2002 to ₹15,982 crore in FY2026, with operations including Australia (MSS) and a cash-logistics JV with Prosegur.
deep_cut_fact: She is a lawyer by training: she holds a BA in Hindi and an LLB from Ranchi University, has around 32 years of legal experience and is enrolled with the Supreme Court Bar Association.
notes: Low personal media profile; the public face of SIS is son Rituraj Kishore Sinha (Group MD). Best route is SIS media relations.

name: Bharat Naresh Oberoi
current_role: Joint Managing Director and Promoter, Powerica Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Bharat Oberoi is a promoter and Joint MD (since 2003) of Powerica, the Mumbai power-solutions firm his father Naresh Chander Oberoi founded in 1984. Powerica builds diesel generator sets and medium-speed large generators for standby/prime power (a key data-center backup market) and since 2008 has been a wind IPP and wind EPC/O&M contractor. He joined in 1994 and leads its marketing side.
interesting_fact: Powerica began as a diesel-generator business in 1984, added medium-speed large generators in 1996, and in 2008 moved into wind energy as an independent power producer, later adding wind EPC and O&M services.
notes: Low public profile; last on Hurun India in 2018. Backup-power gensets for Indian data centers plus wind IPP make a natural energy/data-center angle. Route via company. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so no sourced personal deep-cut.

name: Vasant Laxminarayan Rathi
current_role: Promoter and Non-Executive Director, Advanced Enzyme Technologies Ltd (NSE: ADVENZYMES); heads its US subsidiaries
profile: V. L. Rathi, a pharmacist turned enzyme entrepreneur, co-founded Rathi Papains (1978), set up Cal-India Foods in the US (1985) and has been with Advanced Enzyme Technologies since 1993. The Thane-based enzyme and probiotics maker listed in India in 2016; from the US he runs its American subsidiaries.
interesting_fact: Advanced Enzymes grew from a family papain business into one of India's largest enzyme makers, with US and European arms. It owns Germany's evoxx technologies in Monheim am Rhein.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture, Rathi Papains (1978), made enzymes from papain, the protein-digesting enzyme taken from papaya latex. He trained as a pharmacist (B.Pharm, Nagpur University) and earned an MS at the University of Hawaii.
notes: Categorized as Chemicals/Petrochemicals 'energy', but the business is industrial and nutritional enzymes, so the fit for an energy podcast is weak (enzymes are used in biofuel/biogas, which could be an angle). Low media profile; route via the US subsidiaries (Cal-India Foods / AST Enzymes in California) or the company's general email.

name: Suresh Harakchand Parakh
current_role: Chairman, Parakh Agro Industries Ltd (Samrat flour brand), Parakh Group, Pune
profile: Younger son of Parakh Group founder Harakchand K. Parakh (1930-2015), Suresh Parakh is a flour-milling veteran who chairs Parakh Agro Industries, maker of Samrat atta, besan and oil. The family's Parakh Foods built the Gemini edible-oil brand, sold to Cargill in 2004-05; the Pune group now spans FMCG, flexible packaging, real estate (Gemini Housing) and wind power.
interesting_fact: Parakh Group's energy arm, Parakh Energy, runs 8.3 MW of wind turbines (4 Suzlon, 2 Vestas) in Dhule, Maharashtra, feeding the western regional grid.
deep_cut_fact: He drove the adoption of Swiss Bühler milling technology in the group's flour mills, which combine traditional stone chakkis with Bühler machinery, and personally heads the bulk flour sales business, with some customers loyal for 25+ years. B.Com, Maharashtra Mandal College, Pune.
notes: Primarily a food/FMCG businessman; the energy link is the family's wind assets and former edible-oil refining (Gemini sold to Cargill: https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2011/03/29/Acquisition-boosts-Cargill-brand-portfolio-in-India). Elder brother Prakash Parakh led group expansion. Low-fit for energy podcast.

name: Sureshbhai Jayantibhai Patel
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Bodal Chemicals Ltd (NSE: BODALCHEM), Ahmedabad.
profile: Suresh J. Patel founded Bodal Chemicals in Ahmedabad around 1989-90 as a small vinyl sulphone maker and built it into a vertically integrated producer of dye intermediates, textile/leather/paper dyestuffs and basic chemicals (sulphuric acid etc.), exporting to 40+ countries. He has been chairman & MD since 2006, the year the company went public.
interesting_fact: Bodal is one of very few dye makers integrated from basic chemicals through intermediates to finished dyestuffs; by 2015 it ran eight Gujarat plants with ~2,500 staff and sales above Rs 1,000 crore, exporting 80% of its dyestuff output.
deep_cut_fact: Bodal began in 1989 as 'JK Pharma', a two-man partnership of Suresh Patel and Ramesh Patel with capacity of just 60 tonnes a year of vinyl sulphone; it became Bodal Chemicals Pvt Ltd in 1994.
notes: Chemicals, not energy/data-center; modest wealth (Hurun India 2017 only). Director Bhavin Patel runs the dyestuff division. Best route: company secretarial/info email.

name: Madan Mohan Dhanuka
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, I G Petrochemicals Ltd (Dhanuka Group), Mumbai (per Simply Wall St/Investing.com; some sites list Nikunj Dhanuka as chairman)
profile: Senior figure of the Dhanuka Group and a director of I G Petrochemicals since its incorporation in October 1988. IGPL, set up in technical collaboration with Germany's Lurgi, is India's largest maker of phthalic anhydride (used in plasticisers, paints and resins), with plants at Taloja, Maharashtra; he also sits on the board of Mysore Petro Chemicals.
interesting_fact: He has served on IGPL's board for more than 35 years, since the company's founding in 1988, as it grew into India's largest phthalic anhydride producer.

public_contacts.value: ssingh@igpetro.com (Company Secretary Sudhir R Singh, published company contact)

notes: Chairman title conflicts across data sites; confirm in latest IGPL annual report. Day-to-day leadership by younger family members (Nikunj, Mayank Dhanuka). Low public profile.

name: Abhay Vithaldas Udeshi
current_role: Chairman, Jayant Agro-Organics Ltd (Mumbai; BSE/NSE listed)
profile: Mumbai industrialist who succeeded his father Vithaldas Udeshi as chairman of Jayant Agro-Organics, a castor-oil and castor-derivatives company with an estimated 35-40% share of the global castor oil market. The group runs JVs with France's Arkema and a Japanese partner, plus hybrid castor seed and pharma-grade oil operations.
interesting_fact: He notes India produces nearly 90% of the world's castor oil; Jayant says it was the first company in India to process castor seeds into oil, starting in 1952.
deep_cut_fact: He helped create the Sustainable Castor Association (with Arkema, BASF and NGO Solidaridad), which runs a sustainable castor farming code and certification for Indian farmers and had grown to 31 global members by 2024.
notes: University of Baroda graduate; director of the Sustainable Castor Association. Energy relevance is modest (company has a power-generation segment; castor-based bio-chemicals). Family-run board.

name: Brij Bhushan Agarwal
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd (and subsidiary Shyam SEL and Power); President, Indian Chamber of Commerce
profile: Kolkata-based industrialist (B.Com, University of Calcutta) who has led Shyam Metalics since its inception in 2001, building it into an integrated metals producer (ferroalloys, iron and steel, aluminium foil) with captive power plants in West Bengal and Odisha; listed on NSE/BSE in 2021. He owns roughly 9.5% directly, with the promoter family holding the majority.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Shyam Metalics became India's largest producer of ferroalloys (per CRISIL, as of Feb 2021); its integrated plants run partly on captive power, hence 'Energy' in the name.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the Indian Chamber of Commerce's National Expert Committee on Minerals and Metals in 2019 and that October won Zee Business's 'Inspirational Leader of the Year' award in the 'Dare to Dream' category, before rising to ICC Senior VP and then President.
notes: Hurun India figure ($132m, 2019) is stale; promoter-family stake is worth much more today. Head of IR Pankaj Harlalka appears on earnings calls; IR partner is EY (per call transcripts). ICC presidency gives a second route via Indian Chamber of Commerce, Kolkata.

name: Sridhar Vembu
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Zoho Corporation (stepped down as CEO in January 2025)
profile: Sridhar Vembu co-founded AdventNet with his brothers in 1996. It was renamed Zoho in 2009 and grew into a bootstrapped SaaS company with no outside investors. He has an IIT Madras degree and a Princeton PhD and started his career as a wireless engineer at Qualcomm. He handed the CEO role to Shailesh Davey in January 2025 to focus on R&D as Chief Scientist, and he runs Zoho's rural-development work from Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu.
interesting_fact: He moved from the Bay Area to the village of Mathalamparai in Tenkasi district in 2019, and Zoho set up offices there to bring product development to rural India. He received the Padma Shri in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In 2004 he started Zoho Schools (originally Zoho University), which trains rural students in software as an alternative to college. Zoho says 15-20% of its engineers have no college degree.
notes: Very active on X (@svembu) and accessible to podcasters, especially on deep tech, rural R&D and Indian manufacturing; Zoho is also building chips and its own data-centre infrastructure. Hurun's figure is outdated: Forbes put Vembu and his siblings at about $6B in October 2025. Avoid personal topics, as his divorce litigation is public.

name: Sultan Ali
current_role: Founder & Chairman, IB Group (Abis Exports India Pvt Ltd), Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh
profile: Co-founded IB Group (Indian Broiler Group) in Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh, with his younger brother Bahadur Ali. It grew from a small poultry farm in the mid-1980s into one of India's largest integrated poultry, feed and protein groups. Abis Exports, incorporated in 1998, was the group's backward-integration arm. He chairs the group and oversees its CSR.
interesting_fact: IB Group says it began with a small poultry farm (500 chicks) in 1984, started on the advice of a veterinarian. Some company sources date it to 1985. It became an integrated protein group running contract farming with thousands of rural farmers.
deep_cut_fact: According to his brother's account on the IB Group site, Sultan Ali started the poultry venture in Rajnandgaon with 500 chicks in 1984 after a veterinarian suggested poultry. The company calls 1984-1996 its formative growth period.
notes: Low personal media profile. His brother Bahadur Ali (MD) is the group's public face and does more interviews. The IB Group site was unreachable (503) during research, so no published email was confirmed. Try the group's corporate site or investor-relations page.

name: Sumitra Agarwal
current_role: Director in the Delhi-branch Haldiram's companies (e.g. Haldiram Marketing Pvt Ltd), per company-registry aggregators; current status unclear
profile: A member of the Delhi-based Agarwal family behind Haldiram Snacks, who appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2019. Registry aggregators list her (DIN 00011417) as a director of Haldiram Marketing, Haldiram Ethnic Foods and Haldiram Snacks entities. No public biography or media profile was found.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to a sweets shop opened in Bikaner in 1937 by Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal. Hurun has named Haldiram Snacks India's most valuable unlisted company (about Rs 63,000 crore, 2024).
notes: Very private, with no interviews or social accounts found. Her exact place in the family and her current directorships could not be confirmed: aggregators disagree, and one shows her Haldiram Marketing role ending in Jan 2026. Any contact would go through the Haldiram's corporate office. Low priority.

name: Umesh Agarwal
current_role: Director, Haldiram Snacks Pvt Ltd (Delhi branch of Haldiram's); also director of Haldi Ram Products and Haldiram's Marketing
profile: Umesh (Kumar) Agarwal is a member of the Delhi branch of the Agarwal family behind Haldiram's, the snack brand that grew from a 1937 Bikaner sweet shop. Company filings list him (DIN 00011472) as a director of Haldiram Snacks and related entities; the Delhi business has since merged into Haldiram Snacks Food, which took investment from Temasek in 2025.
interesting_fact: In an October 2026 interview he argued that 'consistency is not created by writing a standard' and that food safety at Haldiram's has to be a daily culture rather than something prepared for before inspections.
notes: Several Umesh Agarwals are linked to Haldiram's in press (Umesh Kumar Agarwal of Haldiram's Marketing; 'Umesh Madhu Agarwal', interviewed by Zomato's Deepinder Goyal in 2024). Filings tie DIN 00011472 to Haldiram Snacks; confirm which person Hurun means before outreach. Family is private; corporate channel is the realistic route.

name: Y Kasyap Reddy
current_role: Managing Director, Medha Group (Medha Servo Drives Pvt Ltd), Hyderabad
profile: Kasyap Reddy Yadavelli runs Medha, a privately held Hyderabad rail-technology group founded in 1984 that supplies propulsion electronics, traction motors and signalling systems to Indian Railways. Under him Medha has moved into full rolling stock (Vande Bharat propulsion, train sets) and opened a 100-acre coach factory near Hyderabad in 2023.
interesting_fact: Medha's Kondakal plant, inaugurated in June 2023, was billed as India's largest private rail coach factory, with planned capacity of 500 coaches and 50 locomotives a year; Medha also has a JV with Swiss maker Stadler Rail.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond rail, Medha has worked on solar inverters, battery-electric vehicle propulsion and canal automation, and signed an MoU to develop large propulsion motors for the Indian Navy.
notes: Private company, low-profile MD. marketing@ is the general sales/marketing address (no dedicated press address found). Relevant energy angle: electrification/propulsion, solar inverters.

name: Y Swetha
profile: Listed (~US$132m) with wealth from Medha Servo Drives, a privately held Hyderabad maker of rail propulsion/traction systems, signalling and, more recently, solar inverters and EV drives. No public source found identifying Y Swetha's role at the company; public director lists name other Yadavelli/Nookala family members.
interesting_fact: Medha Servo Drives (founded 1984, Hyderabad) supplies rail propulsion equipment to 50+ countries and has diversified into solar string inverters (250 kW unit launched at Intersolar India 2024).
notes: Identity/role could not be confirmed; likely a family shareholder of a private company with no public profile. Company itself is relevant (rail electrification, solar inverters). Approach via company only.

name: Mark D. McClain
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Director, SailPoint, Inc. (Nasdaq: SAIL), Austin, Texas
profile: Serial identity-security founder: started Waveset Technologies in 2000 (sold to Sun Microsystems in 2003) and co-founded SailPoint in 2005. He took SailPoint public in 2017, sold it to Thoma Bravo for $6.9bn in 2022, and led it back to public markets in February 2025; he remains CEO as SailPoint pushes into securing AI agent identities.
interesting_fact: He wrote a leadership book, 'Joy and Success at Work: Building Organizations that Don't Suck the Life Out of People' (ForbesBooks, 2020), critiquing perk-driven 'pseudo-cultures'.
deep_cut_fact: After selling Waveset to Sun Microsystems he served as Sun's VP of Software Marketing, then carried Waveset's 'Four I's' core values (integrity, innovation, impact, individuals) into SailPoint.
notes: Accessible, media-friendly founder CEO who speaks often on culture and leadership (book, podcasts). The 'Four I's' values are also described in an Austin Technology Council post: https://www.austintechnologycouncil.org/?p=484

name: Matthew H. Peltz
current_role: Partner and Co-Head of Research, Trian Fund Management; Wendy's director (non-exec Vice Chairman since Nov 2021; verify current board status)
profile: Son of activist investor Nelson Peltz, Matt Peltz joined Trian's investment team in 2008 after two years as a Goldman Sachs investment-banking analyst, and is now a partner and co-head of research. He has sat on Wendy's board since December 2015 and served as non-executive Vice Chairman from 2021; Trian and the Peltzes hold a roughly 15% stake.
interesting_fact: He previously served on the board of ARG Holding Corporation, the former parent of Arby's, from 2012 to 2015, one of several restaurant brands in the Peltz family's orbit.
deep_cut_fact: Outside finance he is a trustee of the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York.
notes: MarketScreener lists his Wendy's director/vice-chair role as ending in 2025 while Wendy's bio page still shows him; check the latest proxy. Media route is via Trian or Wendy's corporate communications.

name: Darren M Rebelez
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Casey's General Stores (CASY)
profile: West Point graduate and former Army Ranger who built a career in fuel and convenience retail. He spent time at ExxonMobil and Thornton Oil, was COO of 7-Eleven, and served as president of IHOP. He became Casey's CEO in 2019 and Chair in 2023. Casey's is the third-largest US convenience-store chain and is known for its pizza, and it joined the S&P 500 in 2026.
interesting_fact: Before his civilian career he was an Army Ranger and Gulf War veteran. He is a San Diego native and earned a BS in Foreign Area Studies at West Point.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil and c-stores, his early civilian jobs were at Fuddruckers and PepsiCo. He told CSP Daily he spent his whole post-military career 'either in the restaurant business or the' convenience business.

public_contacts.value: Casey's media relations: Katie Petru, (515) 446-6772 (company line)
Casey's investor relations: Sam James, (515) 446-6506 (company line, Aug 2026 release)

notes: Casey's press releases list phone contacts but no email. Energy angle: Casey's is a large fuel retailer, roughly 2,900 stores across the Midwest/South.

name: Scott H. Baxter
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Kontoor Brands (Wrangler, Lee, Helly Hansen); director at Lowe's
profile: Has led Kontoor Brands since August 2018, when it was spun out of VF Corp as the home of Wrangler and Lee. He has been chairman since 2021. Before VF (2007-2018, including group president roles over The North Face and Vans) he spent about 20 years at Nestle, PepsiCo and Home Depot, where he was SVP running the services division.
interesting_fact: Spent the first half of his career in suits at consumer and retail companies. He now wears denim to work and says he often gives away Wrangler and Lee clothes when someone compliments them: 'It shocks people, but 99% of the time, they take it.'
deep_cut_fact: A history graduate, he turned down a job offer from the US Secret Service to start his career at Nestle.
notes: Kontoor is based in Greensboro, NC. The Brunswick Review interview (2023) is a good source of rapport material.

name: Glade M. Knight
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Apple Hospitality REIT, Inc. (APLE), Richmond, VA
profile: Utah-born, BYU-educated (BA, MBA) real estate entrepreneur who built the 'Apple' family of non-traded REITs and earlier ran Cornerstone Realty Income Trust (1993-2005). He founded Apple Hospitality, a lodging REIT owning Marriott- and Hilton-branded select-service hotels, was CEO until 2014 when his son Justin took over, and remains Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: He is the founding figure of Southern Virginia University, which he reorganised in the 1990s and chaired from 1996 to 2015; its stadium bears the Knight name.
deep_cut_fact: A competitive horseman with ranches in Virginia and Texas, he offered SVU students a yearly 'Cowboy Up' scholarship honouring his father 'Mac' Knight, whom he calls 'my champion and the real cowboy'; the campus knight statue bears Mac's likeness.
notes: Born 1944; low media profile. Wikipedia notes an LDS patriarch role and close friendship with Bill Marriott. Avoid referencing the 2014 SEC disclosure fines.

name: Michael Pompeo
current_role: Director, VEON Ltd. (since May 2024) and Kyivstar board member; founder, Pompeo Foundation; former US Secretary of State
profile: West Point graduate and Harvard Law alumnus who built and sold Wichita aerospace-parts maker Thayer Aerospace, ran oilfield-equipment firm Sentry International, then served as Kansas congressman, CIA director (2017-18) and US Secretary of State (2018-21). He now sits on the boards of VEON and its Ukrainian unit Kyivstar and runs the Pompeo Foundation.
interesting_fact: He graduated first in his class at West Point in 1986, majoring in engineering management.
deep_cut_fact: In 1996 he and West Point classmates bought three Wichita aircraft-parts shops and a St. Louis tool-and-die firm and named the company Thayer Aerospace after Sylvanus Thayer, the 'father of West Point'; he later ran Sentry International, an oilfield equipment manufacturer – relevant energy-industry roots.
notes: High-profile political figure; likely routed through a speakers bureau or his foundation. Kyivstar board role was framed as safeguarding US investors in Ukraine's largest mobile operator.

name: Mark A Goldsmith
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Revolution Medicines (Nasdaq: RVMD)
profile: Mark A. Goldsmith, MD, PhD (Princeton; UCSF) has led Redwood City-based Revolution Medicines since 2014, building it around RAS(ON) inhibitors for RAS-addicted cancers. Its lead drug daraxonrasib showed a major overall-survival benefit in the Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer and was reported FDA-approved (as RASONQUE) in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 Revolution reported daraxonrasib met all primary and key secondary endpoints, including overall survival, in a pivotal Phase 3 trial in metastatic pancreatic cancer, one of the hardest-to-treat cancers.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech management he was an academic HIV researcher: a UCSF School of Medicine faculty member who ran a research lab at the Gladstone Institute of Virology and Immunology; he later founded and led Cogentus Pharmaceuticals (2006-09) and ran Constellation Pharmaceuticals.
notes: Biotech, not energy; podcast angle would be entrepreneurship/company-building. Deep-cut source (The Org) is marked unverified; career history is corroborated by MarketScreener bio pages. Aug 2026 FDA approval taken from company release summarized in search results.

name: William D. Banfield
current_role: Chief Business Officer, Rocket Companies (RKT), Detroit
profile: Bill Banfield is a 25+-year Rocket Mortgage veteran who joined in 1999 and rose through capital markets, serving as Chief Risk Officer and EVP of Capital Markets before becoming Chief Business Officer in March 2024. He oversees capital markets, mortgage servicing and government affairs - a remit that grew with Rocket's acquisition of servicing giant Mr. Cooper.
interesting_fact: He sits on the Mortgage Bankers Association board of directors, giving him a voice in national housing-finance policy alongside his Rocket role.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Rocket (then Quicken Loans) in 1999, he worked at two smaller Michigan-area lenders, MCA Mortgage and Lambrecht Mortgage Company; he holds a finance degree from Western Michigan University.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; low personal public profile. IR email seen via search snippet of Rocket's IR page (site is bot-protected) - verify before use. Route media requests via Rocket's press room.

name: Russell Craig Ellwanger
current_role: CEO (since May 2005) and director, Tower Semiconductor Ltd (Nasdaq/TASE: TSEM), Migdal HaEmek, Israel
profile: An American-born semiconductor veteran, Ellwanger spent 1980–92 at Philips Semiconductors and 1992–96 at Novellus. He then held senior roles at Applied Materials from 1996 to 2005, including running its Metal CVD, CMP/electroplating and global services units. Since 2005 he has turned Tower into a profitable specialty foundry; it now has big silicon-photonics and SiGe contracts for AI data-centre optical modules, including work with NVIDIA.
interesting_fact: Tower reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $460m (+24%), and Ellwanger raised the 2028 target to $3.6bn revenue and $1.2bn net profit. Growth is driven by silicon photonics for data-centre optics; Tower signed customer contracts for about $1.3bn of 2027 silicon-photonics revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He started wrestling at 11 and his family picked a Las Vegas high school for its wrestling programme. While studying physics at BYU he joined Philips Semiconductors' Utah site, partly because it was one of the few companies offering students health insurance, and was later sent to Philips' main lab in the Netherlands.
notes: Articulate and quotable: Globes says he quotes management gurus, William Faulkner and Alice in Wonderland. A strong data-centre/AI-optics guest. The IR contact is Liat Avraham (+972-4-6506154). A media contact (oritsha@towersemi.com) appears in some releases but I didn't verify it. The $1.3bn photonics-contracts figure comes from a Finviz headline.

name: Aaron Cowen
current_role: Founder, CIO and Managing Partner, Suvretta Capital Management (New York); director of Veradermics and Benitec Biopharma
profile: Aaron Cowen is a hedge-fund manager who founded Suvretta Capital Management in 2011-12 after stints at Lehman Brothers, Baupost, Karsch Capital, SAC Capital (CIO) and Soros. Suvretta runs generalist and healthcare/biotech long-short funds (the Averill funds). He holds large stakes in and sits on the boards of several biotechs, including Veradermics, Benitec and ProKidney.
interesting_fact: By mid-2023 Suvretta's biotech/healthcare-focused Averill funds had grown to double the size of its flagship generalist funds.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Seth Klarman's Baupost Group in 1997 as an analyst for two years after starting as an associate at Lehman Brothers. He then spent 6+ years as a managing director at Karsch Capital before becoming SAC's CIO.
notes: Low-profile hedge-fund manager. No published press contact or personal social accounts found; Suvretta has no informative public website. Best route is likely via the IR/press contacts of portfolio companies where he is a director (e.g. Veradermics, Benitec). Biotech focus, so limited fit with an energy/data-center theme.

name: Dominic Frederico
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Assured Guaranty Ltd (NYSE: AGO)
profile: Has led bond insurer Assured Guaranty since December 2003, taking it public in 2004 and building it into the leading municipal bond insurer and financial guarantor, notably by buying FSA in 2009 (renamed Assured Guaranty Municipal). Before that he was President/COO of ACE Limited and spent about 13 years at AIG. More recently he pushed into alternative asset management and, in Jan 2026, annuity reinsurance (Assured Life Re).
interesting_fact: In January 2026 Assured Guaranty entered annuity reinsurance by acquiring a life and annuity reinsurer it renamed Assured Life Re; by mid-2026 he reported record per-share book value metrics.
deep_cut_fact: At ACE (1995-2003) he was the deal executive behind ACE's purchase of CIGNA's property-casualty business and the Capital Re acquisition. That Capital Re platform later became the core of Assured Guaranty, the company he has run since 2003.
notes: Media contact is Ashweeta Durani (Director, Media Relations, 212-408-6042) and IR contact is Robert Tucker; both are listed in the Q2 2026 earnings release. Little personal or public-profile information exists beyond earnings calls. Assured Guaranty insures infrastructure bonds such as JFK New Terminal One, which could be a relevant hook for energy and infrastructure topics.

name: Rocco A Ortenzio
current_role: Deceased (October 2024); was Chairman Emeritus & Co-Founder, Select Medical
profile: Healthcare entrepreneur who founded or co-founded four healthcare companies, including Continental Medical Systems (sold to Horizon Healthcare in 1995 for $502m) and Select Medical (co-founded 1996), now a Fortune 500 company. Died October 26, 2024.
notes: Deceased: died Oct 26, 2024 per Harrisburg University tribute (https://www.harrisburgu.edu/news/2024-10-28-remembering-rocco-ortenzio/) and APTA in-memoriam notice (https://apta.org/article/2024/11/20/rocco-ortenzio-in-memoriam). Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Zheng Dingping
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guangdong Great Impression (Dayinxiang) Group, Shantou
profile: Shantou entrepreneur, born 1955 in Chaoyang, who founded Great Impression (大印象) in 1988 and has chaired the group since 1996. The company is best known for health and slimming teas and also makes health products, wine and medicine. It took over Shantou Brewery in 2003 to move into brewing.
interesting_fact: Great Impression expanded beyond health teas by merging with Shantou Brewery in 2003, entering beer brewing. Its range now runs to more than 100 product series.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics by correspondence at Jinan University (1976–77), and in 1994 the Ministry of Agriculture gave him a personal award for scientific and technological progress. He was named a Guangdong Model Worker in 2003.

name: Li Shujun
current_role: Founder, Trustbridge Partners (挚信资本), Shanghai-based China-focused private equity firm
profile: Li Shujun (Shujun Li) is the former CFO of Shanda Interactive who founded Trustbridge Partners in 2006. Via Trustbridge and Inspiration Partners he was the Series A investor and a board director of Yingli Green Energy, holding ~9.9% before its 2007 NYSE IPO - the basis of his Hurun listing. name: Liu Binguo
current_role: Co-owner of Jinglong Group (BVI), a founding shareholder group of JA Solar (Ningjin, Hebei); limited partner in JA Solar investor vehicle Xingtai Jingjun Ningyu
profile: Liu Binguo (刘彬国) is one of the ten Chinese individual co-owners of Jinglong Group, the Ningjin, Hebei silicon business led by Jin Baofang that spawned JA Solar. He held 9.58% of Jinglong Group BVI, the joint-largest stake after Jin, which held JA Solar shares through its 2007 Nasdaq IPO, 2018 take-private and 2019 Shenzhen relisting (JA Solar Technology, 002459).
interesting_fact: JA Solar, which Jinglong's shareholders co-founded, listed on Nasdaq in Feb 2007, was taken private in 2018 by Jin Baofang and Jinglong BVI, then relisted in Shenzhen via a reverse merger with Tianye; Liu also holds 21.22% of LP vehicle Xingtai Jingjun Ningyu, which invested in that deal.
deep_cut_fact: JA Solar's SEC filings list 'Mr. Binguo Liu (9.58%)' among Jinglong Group BVI's owners, level with Huixian Wang and behind only chairman Jin Baofang (32.96%).
notes: Identity confirmed via JA Solar 20-F (2008) and the 2019 Tianye/JA Solar reverse-merger legal opinion. Liu is a passive co-founder/shareholder with almost no public profile; no executive title found. Best route is via JA Solar IR or Jinglong Group. Earlier pass missed him because Chinese web search yields nothing; SEC full-text search on 'Binguo Liu' does.

current_role: Unknown; early shareholder of Jinglong Group (晶龙集团, Ningjin, Hebei), the founding parent of JA Solar

name: Stefan A Dyckerhoff
current_role: Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures; independent director, Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB) since Nov 2019
profile: Networking executive turned VC. He ran Cisco's Edge Routing unit and Juniper's Platform Systems Division before joining Sutter Hill Ventures in 2012. An early backer and director of AI-connectivity chipmaker Astera Labs (IPO 2024), he also has board seats at SiFive and Enfabrica.
interesting_fact: His board seats cover much of the AI data-center 'plumbing' stack: Astera Labs (PCIe/CXL retimers and scale-up switches), Enfabrica (AI networking silicon) and SiFive (RISC-V processor IP).
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he ran routers himself. From 2007 to 2009 he was VP & GM of Cisco's Edge Routing Business Unit, and he then ran the Platform Systems Division at rival Juniper. He has a Duke BSE in electrical engineering and computer science and a Stanford MSEE.
notes: Low public profile. Sutter Hill is famously quiet, and its website is a placeholder with no contact details. The Astera Labs media contact reaches the company, not him. A warm intro through the Astera Labs or Sutter Hill network is likely the best route.

name: Jack Hartung
current_role: Independent director, Tesla (since 2025, Audit Committee); also on boards of The Honest Company, Portillo's, Wonder Group and ZocDoc. Retired from Chipotle March 2026
profile: John R. 'Jack' Hartung, 68, spent 18 years at McDonald's before joining Chipotle in 2002 as CFO (20 years), later CFAO and President & Chief Strategy Officer. He delayed retirement after Brian Niccol left for Starbucks, retired as senior advisor in March 2026, and now sits on the boards of Tesla, Honest Company, Portillo's and others.
interesting_fact: He was persuaded to delay his retirement when CEO Brian Niccol made a surprise move to Starbucks in 2024; he has been named 'CFO of the Year' by the Orange County Business Journal and 'Best CFO' (restaurants) by Institutional Investor.
deep_cut_fact: Portillo's 2026 proxy lists his favorite menu item as the Italian Beef with Hot Peppers. He holds a B.S. in accounting and economics and an MBA from Illinois State University, and is a (non-practicing) CPA and CMA.
notes: Tesla board seat gives an energy/AI angle (Tesla Energy, Megapacks). Low social-media profile; route via board/IR channels or Chipotle alumni network.

name: Theodore Blegen
current_role: Retired EVP & CFO (Feb 2026), Monolithic Power Systems; remains with MPS in a transition role
profile: T. Bernie Blegen joined power-chip maker Monolithic Power Systems in 2011 as corporate controller and served as CFO from 2016 until retiring after the FY2025 10-K in Feb 2026, a decade in which MPS grew into a major supplier of power-management chips for AI servers and data centers. Earlier he held finance roles at Xilinx and Credence Systems; UC Santa Barbara graduate.
interesting_fact: CEO Michael Hsing credited him with helping MPS grow 'consistently at an above-market growth rate' during his ten years as CFO, after joining in 2011 'when MPS was relatively small and only beginning to strategically diversify'.
deep_cut_fact: Before semiconductors he worked in publishing and software finance, including at Times Mirror's higher-education group, Shutterfly and Micro Focus, per his executive profile; his 10-K bio cites 25+ years across the semiconductor, software and publishing industries.
notes: Goes by 'Bernie'. Now retired as CFO, so the company IR route is indirect; Rob Dean is interim CFO. Specific employers Times Mirror/Shutterfly/Micro Focus come from MarketScreener profiles (not the 10-K, which confirms only the publishing/software background).

name: Joseph W Gorder
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Valero Energy (CEO 2014-June 2023, Executive Chairman until 31 Dec 2024)
profile: Joe Gorder ran Valero, the largest US independent refiner, as CEO (May 2014-June 2023) and chairman (from end-2014), then executive chairman until retiring at end-2024. He rose through Diamond Shamrock/Ultramar Diamond Shamrock (sales, treasury, IT, business development) before Valero's 2001 acquisition of UDS.
interesting_fact: When he became CEO, UMSL noted he was one of only two undergraduate alumni of the University of Missouri-St. Louis running a Fortune 500 top-20 company (with Express Scripts' George Paz) - a distinction otherwise shared only by Cornell.
deep_cut_fact: A Pattonville High School (Maryland Heights, Mo.) grad, he chose UMSL because he could work 30-40 hours a week and still graduate on time (BSBA, marketing, 1979). His leadership line: 'I believe that a leader is one who serves... give them the latitude to do their jobs without micromanaging them.'
notes: Retired from Valero's board at end-2024, so Valero IR is only an indirect route; no personal social accounts found. SEC-derived wealth (~$125m). UMSL alumni network is a possible warm connection.

name: William J McMorrow
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Kennedy Wilson (taken private in June 2026 by a consortium he led with Fairfax Financial)
profile: Bill McMorrow, a former banker, bought the small real-estate auction firm Kennedy-Wilson in 1988, when it had one office and 11 employees. He grew it into a global real estate investor with about $16B of assets under management across the US, UK, Ireland, Spain and Japan. In June 2026 he and Fairfax completed a take-private at $10.90 a share. He keeps operational control while Fairfax holds the majority economic interest.
interesting_fact: He has taken three companies public in three countries: Kennedy-Wilson on the NYSE, Kennedy Wilson Japan in Tokyo, and Kennedy Wilson Europe Real Estate in London. The London company's $1.7B IPO was the second-largest real-estate IPO in the London Stock Exchange's 200-year history.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 17 years in banking before buying Kennedy-Wilson. That included eight years as a Senior VP at Fidelity Bank in Pennsylvania, followed by EVP and chair of the Credit Policy Committee at Imperial Bank in Los Angeles. In 2011 Kennedy Wilson led the recapitalisation of Bank of Ireland, which was its entry into Europe.
notes: The company is now private, so the SEC-derived net worth is out of date: he cashed out or rolled over his stake in the take-private. The best route is Emily Heidt, MD Communications, the media contact on the June 2026 release; she is a company contact, not his personal one. His bio page also has an 'Open contact form' link. He has appeared on podcasts (ceointerviews.ai lists interviews).

name: James J Filler
current_role: Lead Independent Director, ServisFirst Bancshares (NYSE: SFBS), Birmingham, Alabama
profile: Birmingham businessman who spent 44 years in metals recycling with Jefferson Iron & Metal and its brokerage affiliate, then retired in 2006 to invest privately. He has been a director of ServisFirst Bank since its 2005 founding and of the holding company since 2007, and has been Lead Independent Director since 2019. His wealth is mostly early ServisFirst shares.
interesting_fact: He was an original director when ServisFirst Bank was founded in Birmingham in 2005 and has stayed on the board as it grew into a multi-state commercial bank with roughly US$17bn+ in assets.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking he spent 44 years in scrap-metal recycling with Jefferson Iron & Metal, Inc. and its brokerage affiliate, which he led, before retiring in 2006. He attended Samford University.
notes: Private investor in his 80s with no personal media presence. The only published route is ServisFirst investor relations (Davis Mange). Proxy statements say board communications can go by mail to the corporate secretary.

name: Avishai Abrahami
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Wix.com Ltd (Nasdaq: WIX). Director, monday.com.
profile: A Jerusalem-born serial entrepreneur and IDF Unit 8200 veteran who co-founded Wix in 2006 with his brother Nadav and Giora Kaplan, after the founders were frustrated by how hard it was to build websites. He has grown Wix into a global website-building platform for tens of millions of users and is now pushing it into AI-built sites. He was also an early backer and board member of monday.com.
interesting_fact: Wix was monday.com's first customer, and Abrahami was an early investor who owned about 4% of monday.com at its 2021 IPO. Founder Roy Mann credits him with helping them 'identify the challenge of harnessing people at work.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Wix he founded the software company AIT in 1994 and sold it in 1997, then co-founded Sphera Corporation (1998), which was later acquired by SWsoft. Wikipedia also says he practices ninjutsu.
notes: Wix PR (pr@wix.com) is the best route. The ninjutsu detail rests on Wikipedia only, so treat it lightly. Strong entrepreneurship guest.

current_role: President & CEO, VIAVI Solutions (NASDAQ: VIAV); director, Avnet
profile: Semiconductor and network-test executive who has led VIAVI since February 2016. Previously CEO of International Rectifier (2008 until its 2015 sale to Infineon) and a senior advisor at Silver Lake. VIAVI now pitches heavily into AI/data-center optical and high-speed Ethernet test (e.g. 1.6T validation, hollow-core fibre testing).
