notes: Strong data-center fit: VIAVI sells test gear for AI-fabric/optical interconnects. Best route is VIAVI PR (Grand Bridges).

name: Mario A Harik
current_role: Chairman (since Dec 2025) and CEO, XPO, Inc.; Director, QXO, Inc.
profile: Mario Harik is chairman and CEO of XPO, the North American LTL trucking carrier. A founding executive of Brad Jacobs' XPO in 2011, he was CIO, built its tech platform, ran LTL from 2021 and became CEO in 2022 after the GXO/RXO spin-offs. He also sits on the board of Jacobs' QXO.
interesting_fact: As XPO's CIO he ran the technology integrations of 17 acquisitions in four years, then spent six years building digital tools for the Con-way LTL business he later took over.
deep_cut_fact: Engineer by training: computer & communications engineering from the American University of Beirut and an MIT master's in IT; early in his career he co-founded G3 Analyst as chief architect of web and voice applications, and was CTO of Tallan.
notes: Media contact Cole Horton listed on XPO press releases (mid-2026). Tech-heavy CEO (AI in freight ops) - good podcast angle; spoke at Northwestern in 2026.

name: Brent M Stevens
current_role: Founder/Manager of Peninsula Pacific and Chairman of Peninsula Pacific Entertainment (P2E); Director, Concrete Pumping Holdings
profile: Los Angeles investor and former Jefferies investment banker (1990-2010; EVP and Head of Capital Markets). He co-founded Peninsula Gaming (sold to Boyd Gaming for $1.45bn in 2012) and P2E, which sold most assets incl. Colonial Downs to Churchill Downs for ~$2.8bn in 2022. Peninsula Pacific also backed Brundage-Bone, now Concrete Pumping Holdings, where he is a ~10%+ holder and director.
interesting_fact: His gaming empire started in 1999 with a single Mississippi riverboat casino, the Diamond Jo in Dubuque, Iowa, bought for $77m; P2E's later assets sold to Churchill Downs for ~$2.8bn in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before gaming and concrete, he spent 20 years at Jefferies, rising to Head of Capital Markets and a seat on its Executive Committee; he holds a B.A. in Accounting from USC and a Wharton MBA.
notes: Low media profile. Avoid referencing a past Iowa campaign-contribution legal matter. P2E still pursuing Iowa casino development (Cedar Rapids).

name: Edward Smolyansky
current_role: Founder, Pure Culture Naturals (kefir brand); largest individual shareholder of Lifeway Foods (LWAY)
profile: Son of Lifeway Foods founders Michael and Ludmila Smolyansky, Edward worked at the family kefir company for two decades as controller, CFO, COO and director until 2022. He remains Lifeway's largest shareholder (~16%) and has led a public campaign for board change, and in 2025 launched his own kefir brand, Pure Culture.
interesting_fact: After leaving Lifeway he started a direct kefir competitor, Pure Culture, unveiled at Natural Products Expo West 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His family brought kefir to the American mainstream after emigrating from the Soviet Union; Lifeway was founded in Morton Grove, Illinois in 1986, and Edward grew up speaking Russian at home.
notes: Ongoing, contentious shareholder dispute with Lifeway's board (CEO is his sister Julie Smolyansky); avoid that topic in outreach. Best route is likely via Pure Culture or the press contacts on his shareholder-campaign press releases (e.g. https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2361215/).

name: G. Zachary (Zack) Gund
current_role: Managing Partner, Coppermine Capital (Concord, MA)
profile: Member of the Cleveland Gund family, longtime major Kellogg shareholders. He founded the private-capital firm Coppermine Capital in 2002 and still runs it. He was a Kellogg/Kellanova director from Dec 2014 and later lead independent director of the WK Kellogg Co spin-off. Both board seats likely ended when Ferrero bought WK Kellogg (2025) and Mars bought Kellanova.

deep_cut_fact: Coppermine's portfolio includes B2U, which builds grid storage from second-life EV batteries, and Little Leaf Farms, a controlled-environment lettuce grower. These are useful hooks for an energy-focused podcast.

name: Bruce C. Bruckmann
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director, Bruckmann, Rosser, Sherrill & Co. (BRS), New York; Director, Mohawk Industries
profile: Harvard College and Harvard Law graduate who practised at Patterson Belknap, then spent 1983-94 at Citicorp Venture Capital before co-founding middle-market private equity firm BRS in 1995 with Harold Rosser and Stephen Sherrill. BRS backed consumer, retail and restaurant companies such as B&G Foods and AMF Bowling; he sits on Mohawk's board and was a long-time H&E Equipment director (H&E was acquired by Herc in 2025).
interesting_fact: The three BRS founders had worked together at Citicorp Venture Capital since as early as 1983 before spinning out their own firm in 1995 and putting their surnames on the door.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was a lawyer: an associate at New York firm Patterson, Belknap, Webb & Tyler after Harvard Law School.
notes: Very private PE investor; no published personal or press email found. Best route is via BRS's main office or Mohawk Industries' corporate secretary. Current BRS title not reconfirmed on brs.com (site blocked automated access).

name: Aaron Rosenberg
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, BeOne Medicines Ltd. (formerly BeiGene; Nasdaq: ONC) since July 2024
profile: Pharma finance executive who spent more than two decades at Merck, rising to Senior Vice President and Corporate Treasurer, before becoming CFO of oncology company BeiGene (renamed BeOne Medicines after redomiciling to Switzerland in 2025) in July 2024.
interesting_fact: He joined BeiGene just ahead of its transformation into BeOne Medicines, a Swiss-domiciled global oncology company known for the blood-cancer drug Brukinsa.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Merck in 2003 and, before becoming corporate treasurer, ran finance for Merck Animal Health (2015-18) and led Merck's corporate strategy and planning (2018-21). University of Florida finance BS, NYU Stern MBA.
notes: Corporate executive rather than founder; best route is BeOne investor relations.

name: Arthur G. Sulzberger
current_role: Chairman, The New York Times Company, and Publisher of The New York Times
profile: A.G. Sulzberger (b. 1980), fifth-generation member of the Ochs-Sulzberger family, became publisher of The New York Times in 2018 and company chairman in 2021. A former reporter (Providence Journal, The Oregonian, NYT Kansas City bureau), he led the 2014 Innovation Report and has steered the Times' shift to a subscriber-first digital business.
interesting_fact: He was lead author of the Times' 97-page 2014 Innovation Report, a blunt internal assessment of how the paper was losing ground to digital rivals that leaked to BuzzFeed and became a widely read industry document.
deep_cut_fact: The 2017 film 'Kodachrome' (Ed Harris, Jason Sudeikis, Elizabeth Olsen) was inspired by his 2010 NYT article on Parsons, Kansas, the last place in the world to develop Kodachrome film. As a Providence Journal intern he exposed a Narragansett Lions Club's men-only membership; it began admitting women months later.
notes: booking@nytimes.com is listed by NYTCo as the 'Press: Media Requests' address (for booking Times people on outside media), the natural route for a podcast invitation. Media-business rather than energy angle; he speaks publicly on press freedom and AI/copyright.

name: Aaron Jagdfeld
current_role: President and CEO, Generac Holdings (NYSE: GNRC), Waukesha, Wisconsin; director, Hillman Solutions
profile: Jagdfeld joined Generac in its finance department in the mid-1990s and became CFO in 2002. As CFO he helped sell the company to CCMP for about $2bn in 2006. He became CEO in 2008 at 36 and took Generac public in 2010. He has turned Generac into the leading US home-standby generator maker and now a fast-growing supplier of backup power for data centers.
interesting_fact: In Q3 2026 Generac signed a long-term supply deal for backup generators for Amazon data centers, with initial deliveries of about $2.4bn in 2027-28. Jagdfeld said the data-center backlog had reached about $4.5bn.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Deloitte & Touche auditor in Milwaukee when Generac, one of the manufacturers he audited, offered him a job. Years later he said of the business: 'We don't have a company jet.'
notes: Top fit for an energy/data-center podcast: Generac is pivoting hard into data-center backup power (Amazon deal, capacity expansion). He regularly does earnings calls and trade-press interviews. Route via Generac IR/communications.

name: Donald G Macpherson
current_role: Chairman & CEO, W.W. Grainger (NYSE: GWW); Director, DuPont de Nemours
profile: D.G. Macpherson has been CEO of industrial MRO distributor Grainger since October 2016 and Chairman since October 2017. He joined Grainger in 2008 from Boston Consulting Group, where he was a partner and managing director, and previously ran global supply chain and international operations before serving as COO. He has led Grainger's push into high-touch and endless-assortment (Zoro, MonotaRO) e-commerce models and, more recently, AI.
interesting_fact: Under his tenure Grainger has split into two models: 'High-Touch Solutions' for large customers, and an 'Endless Assortment' online business (Zoro in the US, MonotaRO in Japan). At the April 2026 AGM he highlighted the company's AI push.
deep_cut_fact: Before running a distributor he advised them: at BCG (2002-2008) he was on the firm's Industrial Goods leadership team. He holds a Stanford bachelor's degree and a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Goes by 'D.G.'. IR head is Kyle Bland (VP Investor Relations). Data aggregators (MarketScreener) say he was earlier an operations manager at Rain Bird Sprinkler Manufacturing, but no primary source was found, so verify before using it. Grainger sells MRO supplies to data-center builders and utilities, which is a possible podcast angle.

name: Vincent Pilette
current_role: CEO, President & Chair of the Board, Gen Digital Inc. (Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion)
profile: Belgian-born (1972) finance executive who was CFO of Electronics for Imaging (2011) and Logitech (2013-19) before joining Symantec as CFO in 2019. He led the sale of Symantec's enterprise business, became CEO of the consumer remainder, NortonLifeLock, merged it with Avast in 2022 to form Gen Digital, and added the Board chair role in 2025.
interesting_fact: Pilette says he arrived at Symantec as CFO on the very day its CEO was fired, then led the split and sale of half the company within a year and was named CEO months later, despite never having CEO aspirations.
deep_cut_fact: As a young financial analyst at a Fortune 500 IT company he told the CFO he wanted her job; when she laid out a 15-year succession plan he left ('I don't have that much time') and chased CFO roles through 'hundreds of nos', including an initial rejection from EFI, which later hired him as CFO.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Gen press office. Has spoken publicly about CFO-to-CEO path and consumer cyber safety/AI-era scams, good podcast angles.

name: Dan O Dinges
current_role: Former Chairman, President and CEO of Cabot Oil & Gas (2002-2021); Coterra Energy director until the May 2026 Devon-Coterra merger
profile: Dan Dinges ran Cabot Oil & Gas for about 20 years. He took over in 2002 after more than 20 years at Noble Energy/Samedan and built Cabot into a leading Marcellus Shale gas producer. He led the 2021 merger with Cimarex that created Coterra Energy and then served on Coterra's board. Coterra merged into Devon Energy in May 2026, and Dinges was not named to the combined board.
interesting_fact: He chaired the American Exploration & Production Council, the trade group of the largest US independent oil and gas producers, from 2015. He has also served on the boards of U.S. Steel and the American Petroleum Institute.
deep_cut_fact: Dinges started out as a Mobil Oil landman covering Louisiana, Arkansas and the central Gulf of Mexico. He holds a BBA in Petroleum Land Management from the University of Texas, a niche degree. He is a member of the All-American Wildcatters and served on the executive committee of UT Austin's Kay Bailey Hutchison Center for Energy, Law and Business.
notes: Retired from executive roles and Houston-based, with no personal website or social accounts found. Coterra no longer exists independently (merged into Devon, May 2026), so there is no current corporate press route. Industry associations (AXPC, All-American Wildcatters) or UT's KBH Energy Center are possible intro paths.

name: Emil D Kakkis
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical (NASDAQ: RARE); founder of the EveryLife Foundation for Rare Diseases
profile: Physician-scientist (MD/PhD, UCLA) who developed Aldurazyme, an enzyme replacement therapy for MPS I, at Harbor-UCLA. As BioMarin's CMO he steered further rare-disease drugs to approval. He founded the EveryLife Foundation in 2009 and Ultragenyx in 2010, and Ultragenyx has built a portfolio of rare and ultra-rare disease therapies.
interesting_fact: Drug companies turned down his MPS I therapy as too complex and too costly for so few patients. The family of a young patient, Ryan Dant, set up the Ryan Foundation and raised the money for the trial, and the drug went on to win FDA approval in 2003.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Montebello and Long Beach, graduated from Pomona College, and did his early MPS enzyme work with Dr. Elizabeth Neufeld. In 2019 he won BIO's Henri A. Termeer Biotechnology Visionary Award.
notes: A frequent public speaker on rare-disease policy, so the EveryLife Foundation is another route. Ultragenyx had an FDA complete response letter for UX111, so check recent company news before outreach. The latest release found (Sept 2025) still listed him as CEO.

name: Theresa E Wagler
current_role: EVP & CFO, Steel Dynamics (becomes President & CEO on 1 Jan 2027); Director, CF Industries
profile: Theresa Wagler is a former Ernst & Young CPA who joined steelmaker Steel Dynamics in 1998, when it was still a fast-growing startup. She became CFO in 2007 and built her wealth through the company's stock. In August 2026 SDI named her its next President & CEO, effective 1 January 2027, succeeding co-founder Mark Millett, who becomes Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: She will become CEO of one of the largest US steelmakers, an electric-arc-furnace producer that has expanded into aluminum (Aluminum Dynamics). That puts her squarely in industrial energy and decarbonisation themes.
deep_cut_fact: She is an avid rock climber who books several climbing trips at the start of each year and tells her team in advance. She nearly took a Chicago consulting job before a mentor steered her to Steel Dynamics to set up its financial reporting.
notes: Strong podcast fit (steel, energy-intensive industry, newly named CEO from Jan 2027). Taylor University accounting graduate; Trine University trustee and 2022 Woman of Distinction honoree. Route through SDI investor relations / corporate office, Fort Wayne (260-969-3500).

name: Michael C Morgan
current_role: Co-founding partner & Chairman, Triangle Peak Partners; Lead Director, Kinder Morgan Inc.
profile: Former president of Kinder Morgan (pipelines and energy infrastructure) who co-founded Triangle Peak Partners, a venture/growth investor in energy and technology, and runs the Portcullis Partners investment partnership. He is lead director at Kinder Morgan and has served on the boards of residential-solar firm Sunnova and AI-driven storage company Stem.
interesting_fact: He spans both ends of the energy transition: lead director of one of North America's largest natural-gas pipeline operators while backing solar, storage and clean-tech companies through Triangle Peak.
deep_cut_fact: A 2022 Stanford Distinguished Careers Institute fellow (billed as 'Energy & Technology Geek/Investor'), he co-chaired the Precourt Institute for Energy's advisory council, won the Stanford Associates Governors' Award, and once taught as an adjunct professor at Rice's Jones School.
notes: Kinder Morgan contacts are corporate routes, not personal. No working Triangle Peak website found. Sunnova filed for Chapter 11 in 2025, so avoid that topic. Education: Stanford BA econ & MA sociology, Harvard MBA. Stanford energy-network ties could make a warm intro.

name: Chinh Chu
current_role: Founder and Senior Managing Director, CC Capital (New York private equity); director of Getty Images and other portfolio companies
profile: Vietnamese-born American dealmaker who spent ~25 years at Blackstone (joined 1990), rising to senior managing director and co-chair of private equity. He left in 2015 to found CC Capital, which led deals including Dun & Bradstreet's take-private, Utz Brands' SPAC listing, E2open and Getty Images' listing.
interesting_fact: Chu summited Mount Everest on 17 May 2023, guided by record-holding Sherpa Kami Rita.
deep_cut_fact: To pay for college at the University at Buffalo he sold educational books door-to-door for Southwestern Co., building a sales team and becoming a top seller; he also worked as a telemarketer raising funds for UB. After a 1999 flood he co-founded Vietnam Relief Effort with his sister.
notes: Fled Saigon at age 8 in 1975 on one of the last US military refugee flights. Best route is CC Capital's published media contacts (Karv / Joele Frank).

name: Girish Saligram
current_role: President, CEO and Director, Weatherford International plc (NASDAQ: WFRD), Houston
profile: Engineer-turned-oilfield-services executive who has run Weatherford since October 2020, leading its post-bankruptcy turnaround and return to profitability. Previously COO of Exterran (from 2016) and spent about 20 years at GE, in GE Healthcare and later GE Oil & Gas. His wealth comes largely from Weatherford equity awards.
interesting_fact: He spent roughly 12 years at GE Healthcare in engineering, services and operations before moving into oil and gas, an unusual route into the CEO seat of a major oilfield services firm.
deep_cut_fact: Before Exterran he ran GE Oil & Gas's Contractual Services business from Florence, Italy; he holds an engineering degree from Bangalore University, an MS in computer science and a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Frequent energy-conference speaker (ADIPEC, CERAWeek-type events); writes occasionally for SPE's JPT. Good fit for an energy podcast; route via Weatherford corporate communications (media contact Kelley Hughes per releases).

name: Rene R. Joyce
current_role: Director, Targa Resources Corp. (NYSE: TRGP); founding CEO (2005-2011)
profile: Rene Joyce is the founding CEO of Targa Resources, the Houston midstream natural-gas and NGL company he led from its 2005 formation until 2011, then served as executive chairman (2012-2014) and remains a director. Earlier he ran Tejas Gas pipeline subsidiaries and Shell's Coral Energy units, and has sat on the boards of Apache and Core Labs.
interesting_fact: Targa, which he built from a 2005 private-equity-backed startup, is now one of North America's largest independent midstream companies; in 2026 it signed 20-year integrated midstream agreements with ExxonMobil in the Permian Delaware Basin.
deep_cut_fact: He is both an engineer and a lawyer: BS in mechanical engineering from LSU (1970) and a JD from Loyola University New Orleans (1974); he sits on the LSU Foundation National Board and is a member of LSU's Society for Engineering Excellence.
notes: Highly relevant to energy theme (natural gas midstream, Permian). Low personal media profile; route via Targa corporate/investor relations or LSU engineering network. A Targa proxy noted a planned board retirement at an annual meeting—confirm current board status in latest proxy.

name: Xue Yongmin
current_role: Chairman of the supervisory board (earlier chairman), Shanxi Dongfang Resources Development Group (山西东方资源, ex-Dongfang Ferro Alloy), Jishan, Shanxi; head of the manganese committee of China's ferroalloy industry association
profile: Xue Yongmin (薛永民) built Shanxi Dongfang Resources Development, founded in 2002 in Jishan county, Yuncheng, Shanxi, into China's largest high-carbon ferromanganese producer. It is an integrated 'circular economy' plant covering coal washing (1.2 Mt), coking (0.6 Mt), sintering, blast-furnace smelting and power generation. By 2016 it had about 550,000 t/yr of ferromanganese capacity, which it put at over half the national market.
interesting_fact: In 2016 the company lit what it called China's largest-volume, highest-output high-carbon ferromanganese blast furnace (No. 6, 120m yuan). It said it carried no bank debt even in that downturn and had been Jishan county's top taxpayer for 13 straight years.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership the company publicly adopted a 'low-key, rigorous, frugal' (低调、严谨、节约) management creed, and in Jan 2016 he personally lit the ceremonial 'blessing fire' to start the No. 6 ferromanganese furnace.
notes: Hurun 'Dongfang Ferro Alloy' matches the company's own domain and Xue Yongmin as chairman (2016). Site unreachable from here; a snippet says it lists him as 监事长 and head of the ferroalloy association's manganese committee. 2016 GM was Xue Guodong. Facts come from trade press reposted on Sina Blog. Hurun's 'iron mine' not confirmed.

name: Yang Huaijin
current_role: Unknown; formerly founder/CEO of JA Solar (2005-2009) and later CEO and largest shareholder of Hareon Solar
profile: Yang Huaijin (Samuel Yang) founded JA Solar in 2005 with partner Jinglong Group (Jin Baofang) and ran it as CEO until July 2009 through its Nasdaq IPO, which put him on Hurun's 2008 list. He then became CEO and top shareholder of Shanghai-listed Hareon Solar, later selling his stake (~6.6%) to Huajun Industrial; his current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: He founded JA Solar, now one of the world's largest solar cell and module makers, in 2005 and led it as CEO through its 2007 Nasdaq listing.
deep_cut_fact: Before JA Solar, he also helped found Suntech Power, the company that made Shi Zhengrong China's first solar billionaire (per JA Solar's own website, as cited by Reuters).
notes: Hard to reach; no current company role or published contact found. Hareon Solar later went through severe distress, so avoid that topic. Wealth figure (Hurun 2008) is very dated. Uses English name Samuel Yang.

name: Hari Krishna Chaudhary
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Vikram Solar Ltd (NSE/BSE); Director, Vikram (India) Ltd; chairman of the Kolkata-based Vikram Group
profile: Patriarch of the Kolkata Vikram Group, whose businesses began in 1974 with tea-processing machinery and spread into CTC tea, sponge iron and textiles. The group's solar arm, Vikram Solar (founded 2005 and led by MD Gyanesh Chaudhary), now has ~9.5 GW of module capacity and listed on the BSE/NSE on 26 Aug 2025 after a Rs 2,079 crore IPO; he serves as non-executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Vikram Solar commissioned India's first floating solar plant, a 10 kW pilot in Rajarhat, Kolkata, in 2013-14, and grew from 12 MW of module capacity in 2009 to about 9.5 GW by January 2026.
deep_cut_fact: The family's solar business grew out of tea: he is a director of Vikram (India) Ltd, a Kolkata company founded in 1974 that makes tea-processing machinery, the original business of the Vikram Group.
notes: Low public profile; the public face of Vikram Solar is MD Gyanesh Chaudhary. Only a sales@ address is published on the site; for formal contact use the company-secretary/investor channels listed on vikramsolar.com investors pages. Exact titles vary across sources (some call him Vikram Group chairman).

name: Jyotsna Gautam Kulkarni
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder, Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd (NSE: KIRLOSENG); no executive role found
profile: Jyotsna Gautam Kulkarni belongs to the Kirloskar promoter group of Pune-based Kirloskar Oil Engines (KOEL), which makes diesel and gas gensets, engines, and power and water-management equipment. A March 2023 SEBI takeover-regulation disclosure shows she held about 13 million KOEL shares (~8.97%) before that transaction. She has no public executive profile.
interesting_fact: Kirloskar Oil Engines is one of India's largest makers of diesel and gas generator sets, the backup-power equipment that data centres and industry depend on. That makes the family shareholding indirectly relevant to the energy and data-centre theme.

public_contacts.value: https://www.kirloskaroilengines.com (company; investor contacts via Company Secretary)

notes: She is a passive shareholder and I found no public profile or interviews. Alive status is inferred from her 2023 SEBI filing. The only route is via KOEL's Company Secretary (Farah Irani, per 2026 filings). Search results cite investors@kirloskar.com, but I could not verify it on a primary page. Executive family members (e.g. Gautam Kulkarni, former KOEL executive vice chairman) are more natural guests.

name: Atul Chandrakant Kirloskar
current_role: Retired as Chairman of Kirloskar Oil Engines on 31 Mar 2026 (age 70); remains on boards incl. Kirloskar Industries and Kirloskar Pneumatic (non-executive)
profile: Fourth-generation member of Pune's Kirloskar family. Joined the group in 1978 and led Kirloskar Oil Engines (engines, gensets, pumps) for decades as vice-chair, chair, CMD and executive chair; brother Rahul succeeded him as KOEL chair in April 2026. Former MCCIA president; past chair of CII's National Committee on Defence.
interesting_fact: He stepped down from KOEL in a two-line letter citing only that he had reached 70, handing the chair to his brother Rahul, with Gauri Kirloskar as vice-chair.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1978 as a trainee at Kirloskar Cummins, and by December 1981 was Chief Executive of Cummins Diesel Sales and Services; he became EVP of Kirloskar Oil Engines in Nov 1984 and MD the following year.
notes: Now retired from KOEL chair; good elder-statesman voice on Indian engines/backup power (gensets relevant to data centers). Education sources conflict (COEP/IIM-C vs. other listings), so don't cite his degrees.

name: Rahul Chandrakant Kirloskar
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd (from April 2026); Chairman, Kirloskar Pneumatic Co.
profile: Rahul C. Kirloskar is a fourth-generation member of India's Kirloskar engineering family with 34+ years in the group. He became MD of Kirloskar Pneumatic in 1993 and its chairman in 1998, ran exports for Kirloskar Oil Engines 2001-2012, and succeeded his brother Atul as KOEL chairman when Atul retired on 31 March 2026.
interesting_fact: He took over the KOEL chair from his brother Atul Kirloskar, who retired at 70 in March 2026, with Gauri Kirloskar becoming vice-chairperson alongside her MD role; KOEL makes gensets and engines widely used for backup power.
deep_cut_fact: He personally founded Kirloskar Chillers (HVAC/refrigeration) and has chaired both the CII Pune Council and the Maharashtra State CII Council; from 2001-2012 he led KOEL's push to expand exports for the whole Kirloskar Group.
notes: Good energy/data-center angle: KOEL gensets are used for data-center backup power. Kirloskar Pneumatic (where he is chairman) is a separate listed company with its own IR. Route via KOEL corporate inbox.

name: C Selvam
current_role: Whole-time Director, Asvini Fisheries Pvt. Ltd., Chennai, per company-registry aggregators (likely Chandrasekaran Selvam)
profile: C Selvam is linked to Asvini Fisheries, a Chennai seafood processor and exporter incorporated in 1986 that runs a raw-fish freezing unit at Tuticorin. Registry data lists Chandrasekaran Selvam as whole-time director since 1994. He is also a director of Asvini Hatcheries, Selvam Exports, Emerald Fishing and Meridian Fisheries, and is listed on the Seafood Exporters Association of India.
interesting_fact: His directorships cover much of the seafood chain: hatcheries (Asvini Hatcheries), fishing (Emerald Fishing Co.), processing and exports (Asvini Fisheries, Selvam Exports).
notes: Very low public profile. The identity rests only on registry aggregators (Tofler/Qorpiq) matching 'C Selvam' to Chandrasekaran Selvam at Asvini Fisheries; this is plausible but not confirmed by a primary source. I found no company website or published contact. The search budget ran out before a fuller check.

name: Arjun Juneja
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Mankind Pharma Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: Second-generation leader of Mankind Pharma, founded in 1995 by his father Ramesh C. Juneja and uncle Rajeev Juneja. He studied business at the University of Bradford, got an MBA from Strathclyde, and joined Mankind in 2008, starting in business development. As COO he helped lead its 2023 IPO and its expansion into one of India's largest pharma companies by domestic sales.
interesting_fact: He cold-called his way into Mankind's first big pharma partnership, a marketing deal with Belgium's UCB, which led to Mankind taking over UCB's India business. He also led the 2012 R&D push on fertility drug Dydroboon.
deep_cut_fact: He was a serious cricketer: a leg-spinner from grade 4 who played up to state level. Fortune India links that to Mankind's cricket-heavy marketing with Sourav Ganguly and Anil Kumble. His line on the UCB deal: 'Cold calling randomly got us the first break with UCB.'
notes: investor.relations@ is the institutional-IR desk (Head of IR). investors@ is the secretarial/shareholder address. Fortune India 40 Under 40 (2024) honoree. He has given interviews to Hurun, Business Today and Entrepreneur India, so he is reasonably media-accessible.

name: Vijay Biyani
current_role: Unclear. Formerly Managing Director of Future Retail (from May 2016) and a senior executive at Future Enterprises.
profile: Vijay Laxminarayan Biyani is a brother of Kishore Biyani and one of the Biyani family members who built the Mumbai-based Future Group (Big Bazaar, Pantaloons heritage), India's former retail giant. He served as Managing Director of Future Retail and on the boards of group companies, and appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2018-19.
interesting_fact: Future Retail redesignated Vijay Biyani as its Managing Director in May 2016, during the group restructuring in which Kishore Biyani became vice chairman.
notes: Future Retail and the group's listed companies went through insolvency proceedings from 2022, so there is no working corporate press channel. No personal public presence was found. Avoid the group's financial troubles in any outreach. Low priority.

name: Gundavaram Vanaja Devi
current_role: Whole-time Director and co-promoter, Kaveri Seed Company Ltd (Secunderabad); re-appointed for 2026-2031
profile: G. Vanaja Devi is a co-promoter of Kaveri Seed Company, the Hyderabad-area hybrid seed maker (cotton, maize, rice, vegetables) led by chairman and MD G.V. Bhaskar Rao. She has been on the board since the company was incorporated in 1986 and oversees CSR and community development while assisting the MD with administration; shareholders were asked in 2026 to extend her term to 2031.
interesting_fact: Kaveri Seed has been named six times by Forbes Asia among its 'Best Under a Billion' companies.
deep_cut_fact: She has been a director since the company's incorporation on 27 August 1986 and heads Kaveri's CSR and community-development work, which the board credits for its rural-empowerment programmes.
notes: Company contacts only (company secretary and general info). Very low media profile; chairman G.V. Bhaskar Rao is the public face.

name: Vrajmohan Shah
current_role: Founder, GSP Crop Science (Ahmedabad); no current directorships on MCA record
profile: Vrajmohan Ramanlal Shah founded GSP Crop Science in Ahmedabad in February 1985; it began in phosphate sales before moving into agrochemicals (crop-protection formulations and technicals). The company is now run by his son Bhavesh Shah (Chairman & MD) with the next generation (Executive Director Tirth Shah).
interesting_fact: GSP started out selling phosphates in 1985 before pivoting into agrochemicals around 1988, growing into one of India's larger privately held crop-protection makers.
notes: One aggregator profile refers to 'his demise', and the MCA register shows his DIN deactivated with zero current appointments, but no obituary was found, so alive status is unverified. If contacting, route via the company/Bhavesh or Tirth Shah (Tirth has given trade-press interviews, e.g. agribusinessglobal.com). Web-search budget ran out before contact research.

name: Mahabir Prasad Jalan
current_role: Chairman Emeritus (founder), Ramkrishna Forgings Ltd, Kolkata
profile: Mahabir Prasad Jalan founded Ramkrishna Forgings in Kolkata in 1981, initially making forged parts for Indian Railways; the firm moved into commercial-vehicle components around 2000 and is now a major listed forging/casting exporter. He chaired it until 2023 and is now Chairman Emeritus, with son Naresh Jalan as MD and grandson Chaitanya Jalan in management.
interesting_fact: RKFL began in 1981 as a railway forging supplier and only entered the automotive market around 2000, later becoming a key supplier of heavy-truck components globally.
deep_cut_fact: Has said: 'Honesty, dedication, and customer engagement are the three cardinal mantras that RKFL believes in' - and blamed India's early forging struggles on outdated techniques and low volumes.
notes: Now semi-retired (emeritus); for a podcast the active family leaders (Naresh / Chaitanya Jalan) may be more accessible. Alive status inferred from 2025-26 board listings naming him Chairman Emeritus.

name: Simran Lal
current_role: CEO, Good Earth (Eicher Goodearth) and co-founder/creative director, Nicobar; Eicher Motors promoter-family shareholder
profile: Daughter of Eicher Motors patriarch Vikram Lal and sister of Royal Enfield/Eicher chairman Siddhartha Lal; her Hurun wealth reflects family Eicher Motors holdings. Rather than join Eicher, she joined her mother Anita Lal's luxury design house Good Earth in 2002, became CEO, took it online in 2013, co-founded resortwear brand Nicobar (2016) with husband Raul Rai and later launched luxury label Paro.
interesting_fact: Nicobar is named after the Nicobar Islands in the Indian Ocean; the brand draws on the Spice Route and an island aesthetic, and fabric-hunting and factory visits are among her favourite parts of the job.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Good Earth she had a brief stint at a homewares label; after Good Earth and Nicobar she launched Paro, a luxury brand spanning apparel, jewellery, bed linen and a botanical range.
notes: Design/retail entrepreneur rather than auto executive; some 2024 sources call her 'former CEO' of Good Earth, so confirm current title. Podcast angle: building heritage luxury brands, D2C.

name: Tara Lal
profile: Listed by Hurun India (2018) with wealth from Eicher Motors, the Royal Enfield parent controlled by the Vikram Lal family. Authoritative Eicher sources do not name a Tara Lal; one data aggregator links a 'Tara Lal Vikram' to Eicher's promoter holding company, so she is likely a passive Lal-family shareholder.
notes: Could not confirm identity or role from reliable sources. Not a public figure; the operating family leader is Siddhartha Lal (Executive Chairman, Eicher Motors) https://eicher.in/about-us/siddhartha-lal

name: Gaurav Swarup
current_role: Co-Chairman, Paharpur Cooling Towers Ltd (Kolkata); long-time Chairman, KSB Ltd (India)
profile: Third-generation leader, with brother Vikram Swarup (Chairman), of Paharpur Cooling Towers, India's market leader in industrial cooling towers and air-cooled heat exchangers for power, petrochemical and steel plants; MD from 1993. In July 2024 Paharpur bought control of thyssenkrupp Industries India, renamed TKIL Industries.
interesting_fact: Paharpur took control of thyssenkrupp's Indian engineering arm (cement, mining, energy and sugar equipment) in 2024. He and Vikram called TKIL 'a highly successful and well-regarded entity'.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2016 he became President of the All India Organisation of Employers (AIOE), the FICCI-allied employers' body, at its 82nd AGM. He has also chaired pump maker KSB Ltd's Indian board since 2009.
notes: Paharpur also makes dry/air-cooled systems (SPG Dry Cooling), which fit the data-center cooling theme. The contact page lists only general and regional company inboxes, none specific to him. The KSB chairmanship dates from 2009 (marketscreener) and should be rechecked before citing.

name: Vikram Swarup
current_role: Chairman, Paharpur Cooling Towers Ltd (Kolkata)
profile: Vikram Swarup chairs family-owned Paharpur Cooling Towers (est. 1949, Kolkata), a major global maker of wet, dry and adiabatic cooling towers for power plants, HVAC, oil & gas, chemicals and heavy industry, alongside co-chairman Gaurav Swarup. A director since 1993, he has expanded the group into engineering; in 2024 Paharpur took majority control of thyssenkrupp's Indian unit, renamed TKIL Industries.
interesting_fact: In 2024 Paharpur Cooling Towers became majority shareholder of thyssenkrupp Industries India, which was renamed TKIL Industries - a supplier of equipment for cement, mining, energy and sugar plants.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts or interviews found. Strong energy/data-center fit (industrial and power-plant cooling, dry/adiabatic coolers). Company HQ switchboard and support@paharpur.com are the published routes. Don't confuse with author/diplomat Vikas Swarup.

name: Tulsi Tanti
profile: Founder and chairman of Suzlon Energy, India's wind-turbine pioneer (founded 1995). He died of cardiac arrest on 1 October 2022, aged 64.
notes: Deceased 1 Oct 2022 (per Suzlon's stock-exchange filing). Source: https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/suzlon-energy-founder-tulsi-tanti-passes-away-due-to-cardiac-arrest-348768-2022-10-02. Suzlon is now run by the Tanti family and professional management; if relevant, approach the company directly, not this profile.

name: Rupal Anant Bhat
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder of Asian Paints Ltd (India); no executive or board role found
profile: Member of the Asian Paints promoter group (the founding Choksi/Dani/Vakil families) who holds about 0.20% of Asian Paints directly and is listed as a significant beneficial owner through promoter investment companies Doli Trading and Investments and Elf Trading and Chemical Manufacturing. Asian Paints is India's largest paint maker. Appeared on Hurun India 2018-2019.
interesting_fact: Asian Paints' September 2026 filing lists her as holding 1,923,770 shares directly (0.20%), plus beneficial interests via Doli Trading & Investments (0.98%) and Elf Trading & Chemical Manufacturing (0.22%), recorded since February 2019.
notes: Private individual with no public profile; only appears in shareholding disclosures. Weak fit for energy/data-center podcast (paints/chemicals). Company contacts are indirect; low-priority target.

name: Vinod Vyas
current_role: Founder & Joint Managing Director, Standard Greases and Specialities Pvt Ltd (Mumbai); Director, Tide Water Oil Co. (India) Ltd (Veedol)
profile: Vinod S. Vyas, a science graduate with 48+ years in lubricants and greases, founded Mumbai-based Standard Greases & Specialities (est. ~1983), described as India's largest private-label grease manufacturer. Through Standard Greases he became a co-promoter and the largest shareholder of listed Tide Water Oil, maker of Veedol lubricants, and sits on its board.
interesting_fact: In 2015-16 his privately held Standard Greases ran an open offer for Tide Water Oil (Veedol) and overtook the state-owned Andrew Yule group as its largest shareholder, after which the board named it co-promoter.
deep_cut_fact: His directorships reach well beyond India: he sits on the boards of Granville Oil & Chemicals in the UK and Geotic Company in New Zealand, plus Tarapur Grease Industries and Royal Castor Products at home.
notes: Contact is Tide Water Oil (Veedol India) corporate office, where he is a director; no Standard Greases website found online. Business partner D.S. Chandavarkar is CMD of Standard Greases and chairman of Tide Water Oil. Low public profile.

name: Sajja Kishore Babu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Managing Director, Power Mech Projects Ltd (Hyderabad; NSE/BSE-listed)
profile: Power-plant engineer who spent 14 years building and maintaining thermal power plants before founding Power Mech in 1999. The company grew into one of India's largest erection, testing and commissioning (ETC) and O&M contractors for power plants, and has expanded into civil works, mining (MDO), railways and the Middle East.
interesting_fact: Power Mech moved from maintenance into large builds within three years, doing its first ETC job on 1x63 TPH and 2x165 TPH fluidised-bed boilers for BHEL, then units at Raigarh, Chhattisgarh. It went on to commission generating units for every fuel type.
deep_cut_fact: Power Mech's very first contract in 1999 was the overhaul and maintenance of gas turbines for Tata Power at Trombay, Mumbai. His company bio also notes he is known for remembering employees by name.
notes: Hurun India 2018-19 listing; Power Mech's market value has risen sharply since, so his wealth is likely higher now. A good fit for India power-buildout themes. Route via corporate office or company secretary.

name: Rajesh Agarwal
current_role: Co-founder, Micromax Informatics Ltd (Gurugram, India)
profile: A mechanical engineer and former IT salesman (Pertech, Xerox), Rajesh Agarwal co-founded Micromax with Rahul Sharma, Sumit Arora and Vikas Jain, growing it from an IT/training business into India's top domestic phone brand in the late 2000s on cheap dual-SIM handsets. Micromax has since pivoted toward electronics manufacturing and memory chips (MiPhi JV with Phison) under Rahul Sharma.
interesting_fact: Micromax broke into handsets with dual-SIM phones when critics predicted it would 'end up losing big time'; Agarwal says 'We wouldn't be in business had we not created a category.'
deep_cut_fact: In 1991 he sold his Maruti 800 for Rs 80,000 to fund his first venture, a PC-assembly firm called Micromax Technologies; he later co-founded Micromax Informatics with Rahul Sharma, his neighbour of 35 years.
notes: Low public profile versus co-founder Rahul Sharma. No published personal/press email found; route via Micromax corporate. Current executive role not confirmed in 2026 sources.

name: Sumeet Kumar
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Micromax group; director of MiPhi Semiconductors, Micromax Biofuels, YU Televentures and Bhagwati Products
profile: Co-founded Micromax in 2000 (with Rahul Sharma, Rajesh Agarwal and Vikas Jain) as an embedded-systems startup and grew it into India's largest home-grown phone brand. The group now spans electronics manufacturing (Bhagwati Products), enterprise SSDs (MiPhi, a JV with Taiwan's Phison), solar modules (Startup Energy) and ethanol (Micromax Biofuels).
interesting_fact: MiPhi Semiconductors, the Micromax-Phison JV (55/45) on whose board he sits, became the first Indian brand to design and manufacture enterprise SSDs aimed at data centres and AI workloads.
deep_cut_fact: Besides chips, he is a director of Micromax Biofuels, which runs a 100 KLPD ethanol plant in Bihar supplying fuel-grade ethanol under India's Ethanol Blending Programme; the group also makes solar modules via Startup Energy.

public_contacts.value: https://micromaxinfo.com/micromax-biofuels (group 'Contact the group' form on site pages)

notes: Sometimes listed as Sumeet Kumar Arora. Strong energy/data-center angle (MiPhi SSDs, solar, ethanol). Low public profile; co-founder Rahul Sharma is the usual spokesperson. Studied B.Tech mechanical engineering at Jamia Millia Islamia per a Naukri company profile (https://companies.naukri.com/micromax-jobs/executive-team).

name: Vikas Jain
current_role: Co-founder, World of Play (PLAY wearables/audio brand); co-founder of Micromax Informatics
profile: Vikas Jain is one of the four co-founders (with Rahul Sharma, Rajesh Agarwal and Sumeet Kumar) of Micromax, the Gurgaon company that grew from an IT venture into one of India's largest budget phone brands. He later co-founded World of Play, which sells affordable smart wearables and audio products aimed at young Indian consumers.
interesting_fact: In a DNA interview he said the Micromax founders 'never thought we would sell 1.8 million handsets a month', a volume the company reached at its peak.
deep_cut_fact: He was the fourth partner to join Micromax Informatics in its pre-phone era as a computer-training/IT venture; co-founder Rajesh Agarwal recalled: 'Later on, Vikas too joined us, chipping in his share of capital.'
notes: Consumer electronics, not energy. Micromax's fortunes declined after ~2016; avoid that topic. Hurun appearances 2015-2018 only. No published press email found for World of Play.

name: Ashok Kumar Chaturvedi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, UFlex Ltd (Noida, India)
profile: First-generation entrepreneur Ashok Chaturvedi started a tiny manufacturing unit in 1985 that became UFlex, India's largest multinational flexible-packaging group (films, pouches, chemicals, holography, aseptic packaging, printing cylinders and packaging machines) with film plants in the US, Mexico, Poland, Egypt, UAE, Russia, Hungary and Nigeria and >US$1bn turnover. He was reappointed CMD from Feb 2024 for five years; son Anantshree is Vice Chairman/CEO of Flex Films.
interesting_fact: He is widely called the 'Father of Flexible Packaging' in India (title conferred at the Global Conference on Plastic & Packaging 2019) and also won the ET Polymers Lifetime Achievement Award 2018.
deep_cut_fact: He promises customers '3 Q's' - Quality, Quantity & Quickness - and is a cricket enthusiast who funds education and sports facilities for under-privileged children and youth.
notes: Best route is UFlex Global Corporate Communications (corpcomm@). UFlex's recycling/biodegradable packaging and energy-intensive film plants could be podcast angles.

name: Mukesh Chimanlal Gandhi
profile: Co-founder, Whole-time Director and CFO of MAS Financial Services (Ahmedabad NBFC founded 1995). Died January 19, 2021, according to the company's founders page.
notes: Deceased (Oct 20, 1957 - Jan 19, 2021), source: https://mas.co.in/about/#our-founders. The surviving founder is co-founder Kamlesh Gandhi (Chairman & MD); company contact mfsl@mas.co.in is published at https://www.mas.co.in/.

name: Jyoti Agarwal
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder, AU Small Finance Bank; co-founder, Sanjay & Jyoti Agarwal Foundation
profile: Wife of AU Small Finance Bank founder and MD/CEO Sanjay Agarwal. She holds about 3.2% of the Jaipur-based bank (roughly 3.8% in FY21) as part of the promoter group. She was an early director of the group (appointed 2003, since ceased). Her Hurun wealth comes from that stake. AU is moving toward universal bank status.
interesting_fact: AU grew from a Jaipur vehicle-finance NBFC into one of India's first small finance banks and has been asked by the RBI to move the promoter family's ~22% stake into a non-operative holding company before final approval as a universal bank.
deep_cut_fact: She co-founded the Sanjay and Jyoti Agarwal Foundation, which works on education for underprivileged children, road safety and digital empowerment.
notes: Private individual with almost no public profile of her own. Shareholding source: AU Bank MGT-9 FY2020-21 (https://www.au.bank.in/pdfs/other-reports/mgt-7---mgt-9/MGT-9-2020-21.pdf). Best route is via AU Bank corporate communications or the family foundation.

name: Shakuntala Agarwal
current_role: Promoter shareholder, AU Small Finance Bank Ltd (no executive or board role found)
profile: Listed by Hurun India for AU Small Finance Bank, the Jaipur-based lender founded by Sanjay Agarwal (AU Financiers, 1996) that converted to a small finance bank in 2017. AU's filings list her in the promoter group, holding ~1.86 crore shares (~2.5%) as of late 2025. No public profile, interviews or operating role found.
interesting_fact: AU's promoter group (Sanjay Agarwal, Jyoti Agarwal, Shakuntala Agarwal, MYS Holdings) built the bank from a Jaipur vehicle-finance NBFC into one of India's largest small finance banks, which has since sought RBI approval to become a universal bank.
notes: Very private passive promoter shareholder; relationship to founder Sanjay Agarwal not confirmed in sources found. Only realistic route is via AU Small Finance Bank corporate/IR office; consider approaching Sanjay Agarwal instead.

name: Madhu N Jain
current_role: Director, IIFL Foundation (CSR arm of IIFL Group); promoter shareholder in IIFL with husband Nirmal Jain
profile: Wife of IIFL founder Nirmal Jain. Together they are promoters of the IIFL financial-services group (IIFL Finance, IIFL Capital, 360 ONE), which Bloomberg has valued their stake in at over $1B. She leads IIFL Foundation, whose flagship Sakhiyon Ki Baadi programme teaches out-of-school girls in rural Rajasthan.
interesting_fact: IIFL Foundation's Sakhiyon Ki Baadi programme has brought about 36,000 out-of-school girls in rural Rajasthan into education, making it one of India's largest girl-literacy efforts. In December 2024 the Foundation adopted 102 government girls' high schools in the state.
deep_cut_fact: She personally received a 'CSR Leadership Award', and the Foundation's work has been recognised by the United Nations. In April 2026 the Foundation opened revitalised government schools in Rajasthan, inaugurated on Mahavir Jayanti.
notes: Her public profile is almost entirely philanthropic (girls' education in Rajasthan). The IIFL Foundation email is the most natural route. Not an operating business executive.

name: Archana H Mariwala
current_role: Director, Ascent India Foundation; Marico promoter-group shareholder
profile: Archana Mariwala is the wife of Harsh Mariwala, founder and chairman of Marico (Parachute, Saffola). Her wealth comes from her promoter-group stake in Marico. She has kept a low public profile and has sat on the board of ASCENT, the entrepreneur peer-learning foundation set up by Harsh Mariwala, since 2015.
interesting_fact: ASCENT Foundation, on whose board she sits, is funded by Harsh Mariwala and runs peer-learning groups for growth-stage Indian entrepreneurs. That ties directly to the podcast's entrepreneurship theme.
notes: Very private; no interviews found. Her board role comes from registry data (tofler). Don't confuse her with Archanna Das, ASCENT's CEO. Best route is via the ASCENT Foundation or Harsh Mariwala's office; Harsh is the far more natural podcast guest.

name: Prakash Harakchand Parakh
current_role: Managing Director, Parakh Agro Industries Ltd (Parakh Group, Pune); heads group real estate arm Gemini Housing
profile: Second-generation leader of Pune's Parakh Group, a Maharashtra trading house that moved into wheat flour, pulses and edible oil in the 1980s. He drove the edible-oil business, sold to Cargill in 2005, then refocused on atta/pulses, flexible packaging (Parakh Flexipacks), wind power and real estate; the group re-entered oil refining in 2017.
interesting_fact: Parakh pioneered flexible pouches for edible oil in India and claims the first 10 kg atta pack; Fortune India named it the fastest-growing mid-size FMCG company in 2017-18.
deep_cut_fact: Per the group's own site, he set up what it calls Asia's largest edible-oil refinery under one roof at Kurkumbh in 1999, and was appointed a non-executive director of Bank of Maharashtra on the recommendation of Maharashtra's Chief Minister.
notes: Privately held family group; MD listing per MCA-based directories (DIN 00337188). Brother Suresh Parakh and third-generation Harshal Parakh also active. Web search budget ran out mid-research; Cargill deal details from packaging trade press only.

name: Reena Kamalkumar Agrawal
current_role: Family shareholder associated with Haldiram's Nagpur business (per Hurun India 2018-2019); no public executive role found
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2018-2019 (about US$120m) with wealth from Haldiram Foods International, the Nagpur arm of the Haldiram's snacks empire built by Shivkisan Agrawal, who moved the business base to Nagpur in 1970. Her name pattern suggests she is linked to executive director Kamalkumar Agrawal, but no public source confirms her role. In 2025 the Nagpur and Delhi Haldiram FMCG businesses merged into Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's began as a small sweet shop in Bikaner; the Nagpur and Delhi family branches completed a merger in 2025 to form Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd, one of India's largest packaged-snack companies.
notes: Very private, no public profile found; relationship to Kamal Agrawal inferred from the patronymic only and unconfirmed. Outreach would go via Haldiram's corporate; Kamal Agrawal is the more visible family member.

name: Rashmita Patnaik
current_role: Director/promoter, Falcon Marine Exports Ltd (Bhubaneswar, Odisha)
profile: Rashmita Patnaik is a long-serving director and promoter of Falcon Marine Exports, a Bhubaneswar-based seafood (mainly shrimp) processor and exporter founded in 1986 by Tara Ranjan and Prava Ranjan Patnaik. She also holds directorships in group companies such as Falcon Drinks, Falcon Real Estate and Falcon Holdings. Listed on Hurun India 2018-2019 (~US$120m).
interesting_fact: Falcon Marine Exports, set up in Odisha in 1986, grew into one of India's leading shrimp exporters and has been recognised in MPEDA's export awards (2018-19 awardee list).
notes: Non-executive, very private; company's public face is chairman Tara Ranjan Patnaik (Priyanka Mohanty named Joint MD in 2026). Board data from third-party MCA aggregators (qorpiq.com). No published company email found on falconmarine.in.

name: Manish Ramprakash Bubna
current_role: Whole-time Director and co-founder/promoter, Sharda Cropchem Ltd (NSE: SHARDACROP), Mumbai
profile: Manish Bubna, a chemical engineer from Mumbai's UDCT (now ICT), is a promoter-director of Sharda Cropchem, the generic agrochemicals company founded by his father Ramprakash Bubna and run by the family. Sharda sells generic fungicides, herbicides and insecticides across Europe, the US and Latin America; he also sits on the boards of group firms incl. Sharda Europe BV.
interesting_fact: Sharda is 'asset-light': it owns no big factories, instead identifying off-patent molecules, building regulatory dossiers and winning product registrations in high-barrier markets like Europe and the US, then sourcing from third-party manufacturers.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chemical engineer at the University Department of Chemical Technology (UDCT), Bombay University - the institute now known as ICT Mumbai, alma mater of many Indian chemical-industry founders.
notes: Hurun India 2017 only; agrochemicals rather than energy. Low personal profile; father Ramprakash Bubna (CMD) is the public face. Education detail comes from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener).

name: Ashish Ramprakash Bubna
current_role: Whole-Time Director and co-founder/promoter, Sharda Cropchem Ltd (Mumbai; NSE: SHARDACROP), reappointed through Dec 2028
profile: Ashish R. Bubna co-founded Mumbai-based Sharda Cropchem with his parents Ramprakash and Sharda Bubna and brother Manish. The company runs an asset-light model: it owns regulatory registrations for generic agrochemicals across Europe, the Americas and elsewhere and outsources manufacturing. A University of Mumbai commerce graduate, he heads marketing, procurement, registrations and logistics.
interesting_fact: Sharda Cropchem's moat is paperwork, not plants: rather than manufacturing, it builds and owns registration dossiers that let it sell off-patent crop-protection chemicals in heavily regulated markets, with production sourced largely from third parties.
deep_cut_fact: Per the company's annual report, he was 'instrumental in strategizing early investment in product registrations and building the library of product dossiers' - the strategy that became Sharda's core competitive advantage - and has 30+ years in chemicals marketing.
notes: Low public profile. Sector is agrochemicals (Hurun tags it chemicals/petrochemicals), so energy/data-center fit is weak. Company site: shardacropchem.com.

name: Anil Chaudhary
current_role: Director of Kolkata-based Vikram group companies (e.g. Vikram Financial Services, Vikram India); listed as a past director of Vikram Solar
profile: Anil Chaudhary was ranked by Hurun India (2017) for wealth tied to Vikram Solar, the Kolkata-based solar module maker that listed on Indian exchanges in 2025. Company-registry data show an Anil Chaudhary (DIN 00897159) as a long-time director of several Vikram group entities and a past director of Vikram Solar; Vikram Solar itself is led by Gyanesh Chaudhary.
interesting_fact: Vikram Solar is one of India's largest solar PV module manufacturers, part of the Kolkata Vikram group whose roots go back to Vikram India Ltd (1980) and Vikram Financial Services (1982).
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or bio found. Identity link to the Hurun listing rests on company-registry data (aggregator sites), not a primary source. The public face of Vikram Solar is CMD Gyanesh Chaudhary - he may be the better podcast guest.

name: Sasikala Raghupathy
current_role: Chairperson (promoter), BGR Energy Systems Ltd, Chennai (since October 2013)
profile: Sasikala Raghupathy is the widow of BGR Energy founder B.G. Raghupathy and became chairperson of the Chennai-based power-plant engineering company after his death in 2013. BGR (NSE: BGRENERGY) builds balance-of-plant and EPC packages for thermal and gas power plants and makes oil and gas equipment; her son Arjun Govind Raghupathy is managing director. Hurun listed her in 2017.
interesting_fact: BGR began in 1985 as a joint venture with Germany's GEA Energietechnik making on-line condenser tube cleaning systems, debris filters and rubber cleaning balls for thermal and nuclear power plants, before the Raghupathy family bought out the partner in 1993 and grew it into a turnkey power-plant contractor.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal bio, education or philanthropy found. Hurun wealth (2017) likely stale - BGR has been under financial stress in recent years, so check the company's current status before outreach. Son Arjun Govind Raghupathy (MD) is the operational face of the company.

name: Manoj Agarwalla
current_role: Director and shareholder, Dhansar Engineering Company Pvt. Ltd. (per Tofler registry listing)
profile: Manoj Agarwalla is a director of Dhansar Engineering, a family mining contractor incorporated in 1955. It does overburden removal, coal extraction, drilling and blasting, and coal transport, mainly in the Dhanbad coalfield. Harsh Agarwalla is also listed as a director. The firm wins large hiring contracts from Coal India's Bharat Coking Coal Ltd (BCCL).
interesting_fact: Dhansar Engineering dates back to 1955 and does open-cast mining work: site levelling, overburden removal, drilling and blasting, coal extraction, wagon loading and transport. A BCCL award notice reported in search results gave it a roughly Rs 64.5 crore, 36-month contract in the Kustore area.
notes: Do not confuse him with Manoj Kumar Agarwal, CMD of BCCL since Sept 2025, who is a different person. The identity link rests on the Tofler registry listing, and I found no company website or published contact. Relevant to the energy (coal) theme, but very private. I could not open the BCCL contract PDF to verify the Rs 64.5 crore figure (bcclweb.in was unreachable), so treat it as unverified.

name: Mayankutty C
current_role: Director of several Malabar Group companies (probably Mayan Kutty Cholakkal, DIN 00017550), Kozhikode, Kerala
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2019 (~US$120m) as a shareholder in Malabar Gold, the Kozhikode-based jeweller founded in 1993 by M.P. Ahammed with a group of Kerala investors. Registry data shows a Mayan Kutty Cholakkal as a long-standing director of Malabar Gold Ltd (since 2004), Malabar Gold Palace and other Malabar entities. That is probably this person, but no source confirms it.

name: N Nagaraju
profile: Listed on the Hurun India Rich List 2019 with wealth attributed to 'personal investment'. No public source was found that identifies which N. Nagaraju this is, so no profile was compiled.

profile: Dr. N. Sitaram (Narayana Sitaram) Shetty leads the board of Shankaranarayana Constructions, a Bengaluru infrastructure contractor that builds dams, power plants, aqueducts, tunnels and canals. With over three decades in construction, he is credited with steering SNC towards energy and water projects; Vybhav Shetty is Managing Director.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership SNC repositioned itself around energy and water, building dams, power plants, tunnels and irrigation canals.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a construction magnate he trained as a medical doctor; the company describes him as 'a professional Doctor'.
notes: Good fit for energy/water infrastructure theme. Company website currently carries injected gambling spam (appears hacked), so verify contacts before use. sncbgr@ is the published general company inbox.

current_role: Managing Director, Virchow Laboratories Ltd (Hyderabad) - per company-registry aggregators
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2019 via Virchow Laboratories, a Hyderabad pharmaceutical/API maker incorporated in January 1982 at the Jeedimetla industrial estate (group also includes Virchow Biotech). Registry aggregators list a Venkata Reddy Nandigala as MD and Craft lists 'N. Venkata Reddy, MD (Commercial)', likely the same person, but not confirmed by a primary source.

name: Nav Ratan Goenka
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director (founder), Diamond Beverages Pvt Ltd, Kolkata
profile: Nav Ratan Goenka founded Diamond Beverages, a Kolkata-based Coca-Cola franchise bottler incorporated in 1995 that bottles Coca-Cola soft drinks, Maaza, Minute Maid and Kinley water for eastern India. Registry records list him as a director since 1995; day-to-day leadership is with MD Hemant Goenka and director Abhyuday Goenka.
interesting_fact: Diamond Beverages is one of Coca-Cola's franchise bottlers in India, producing carbonated drinks, fruit beverages (Maaza, Minute Maid Pulpy Orange) and Kinley packaged water.
notes: Private family business with no public website found (diamondbeverages.in is parked). Not to be confused with Shiv Ratan Goenka of Bengal Beverages. Alive status not confirmed from a dated source.

name: Padmaja Gangireddy
current_role: Managing Director/CEO, Keertana Finserv Pvt Ltd (gold and housing loans); Director, Caspian Financial Services (per MarketScreener; unverified with company)
profile: Padmaja Reddy Gangireddy founded Spandana in 1998 and built it into Spandana Sphoorty Financial, one of India's largest listed microfinance lenders. She stepped down as CEO in November 2021 and left the board in 2023; she now runs Keertana Finserv, a Hyderabad-area NBFC focused on gold and housing loans for low-income borrowers.
interesting_fact: Before becoming a lender she worked in the development sector at ASSIST, an NGO serving marginalised rural communities in Andhra Pradesh, and studied at Acharya Nagarjuna University.
notes: Web-search budget ran out mid-lane; profile is based on MarketScreener plus earlier knowledge. Company sites (spandanaindia.com, Keertana) did not load. Avoid the 2021 exit dispute with Spandana's PE investor (Kedaara). Re-check current role and look for a Keertana Finserv contact.

name: Percy Sorabji Chowdhry
current_role: Executive Director and promoter, Keystone Realtors Ltd (Rustomjee Group), Mumbai
profile: One of the three promoters of Mumbai developer Keystone Realtors, which builds under the Rustomjee brand, alongside chairman-MD Boman Irani and Chandresh Mehta. He has been on Keystone's board since January 1999, making him its longest-serving director; the company listed on Indian exchanges in 2022.
interesting_fact: He is the longest-serving director on Keystone Realtors' board, appointed 3 January 1999.
notes: Very low public profile; Boman Irani is the group's public face. Approach via Rustomjee corporate communications/investor relations.

name: Piyoosh Goyal
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Worlds Window Group (New Delhi)
profile: Indian businessman who founded Worlds Window Group in New Delhi in 1993, a multi-division group described as offering logistics and trading/manufacturing-related services. He appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2019 (~$120M). He also served as an independent non-executive director of Prakash Industries (steel and power) from 2011 to 2013.
interesting_fact: He sat on the board of Prakash Industries, a steel and captive-power producer, as an independent director from 2011 to 2013.
notes: Not to be confused with Piyush Goyal, India's Commerce Minister; searches are heavily polluted by him. Input calls it 'World Window Group'; the company styles itself Worlds Window. All profile data comes from MarketScreener insider pages; the company site is behind a Cloudflare check and wasn't readable. Very low public profile.

name: Pranay Godha
current_role: Managing Director & CEO, Ipca Laboratories Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Pranay Godha leads Ipca Laboratories, the Indian drugmaker (APIs, formulations, notably anti-malarials and pain management) his father Premchand Godha has steered since 1975. Ipca posted FY26 revenue of about Rs 9,646 crore with over half earned abroad; Premchand is executive chairman and brother Prashant is an executive director.
interesting_fact: Ipca was rescued from losses in 1975 by a group including chartered accountant Premchand Godha (Pranay's father) and actor Amitabh Bachchan's family; the Bachchans sold their 36% stake to the directors in 1997, leaving the Godhas in control.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.Sc. from the University of Bombay and an MBA from the New York Institute of Technology, and came up through marketing and general management at Ipca.
notes: Low media profile; company comms via Ipca corporate (Kandivli, Mumbai). Investor-relations email is published in Ipca's annual reports/stock-exchange filings but could not be extracted (search budget exhausted).

name: Prashant Godha
current_role: Executive Director, Ipca Laboratories Ltd (since August 2011)
profile: Member of the Godha family that controls Mumbai-based drugmaker Ipca Laboratories, a major producer of APIs and formulations (notably anti-malarials and pain management). A commerce graduate with a PGDBM, he has worked in pharma marketing and general management and has been an Ipca executive director since 2011.
interesting_fact: Ipca's turnaround began in 1975 when his father, chartered accountant Premchand Godha (then managing Amitabh Bachchan's finances), and the Bachchan family acquired the struggling company; the Bachchans exited in 1999 and Ipca is now worth roughly Rs 28,000 crore.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Ipca's board he spent 12 years (May 1999 - Aug 2011) as wholetime/executive director of Makers Laboratories, a smaller listed pharma company later linked to the Ipca group.
notes: Low public profile; Executive Chairman Premchand Godha and MD & CEO Pranay Godha are the public faces of Ipca. Also non-executive director at Lyka Labs and Resonance Specialties per MarketScreener.

name: Preetha Reddy
current_role: Executive Vice Chairperson, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd
profile: Dr. Preetha Reddy, eldest daughter of Apollo founder Dr. Prathap C. Reddy, has spent nearly four decades building Apollo Hospitals, India's largest private hospital group, joining management around 1989 and later serving as managing director before becoming executive vice chairperson. She shares the family's stake in the listed company with her sisters.
interesting_fact: She brought proton therapy to India: the Apollo Proton Cancer Centre in Chennai (2019) was the first such facility in South East Asia and the Middle East and has treated over a thousand patients.
deep_cut_fact: She championed India's first Joint Commission International (JCI) hospital accreditation, won by Apollo Indraprastha in Delhi in 2006, and credits her father's lesson that 'any aspect will be a problem, only if you decide to see it as one.'
notes: Healthcare, not energy. Has appeared on ET's 'Corner Office Conversation' podcast with sister Suneeta Reddy (https://omny.fm/shows/corner-office-conversation/corner-office-conversation-with-apollo-s-dr-preetha-and-suneeta-reddy). Apollo's website blocked automated access, so no corporate press/IR email could be verified; route via Apollo corporate communications.

name: Radhe Shyam Dixit
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Ananda Group / Gopaljee dairy business (Ananda Dairy), Noida, Uttar Pradesh
profile: Dr. Radhey Shyam Dixit founded the Gopaljee/Ananda dairy group, starting with a plant at Siyana, Bulandshahr (UP) in 1989. It grew into a major North Indian dairy brand selling 50+ products (paneer, ghee, milk, sweets), sourcing from 2.5 lakh+ farmers across 5,000+ village societies, with turnover of Rs 1,725 crore in FY2017-18.
