name: Zhu Zhangjin
current_role: President (总裁) of Kasen Group / Kasen International Holdings (HKEX: 0496), Haining, Zhejiang; chairman of its Cambodian special economic zone
profile: Zhu Zhangjin built Kasen from a small tannery (1988) into a leather and sofa exporter, listed in Hong Kong in 2005. The group expanded into property and resorts in Hainan and Changbaishan. Since 2019 Kasen has repositioned as a Belt-and-Road special-economic-zone operator in Cambodia and an international power developer. It builds thermal, solar, hydro and wind projects in Mongolia, Cambodia and Zimbabwe.
interesting_fact: Kasen now develops power projects (coal, solar, hydro, wind, district heating) in Mongolia, Cambodia and Zimbabwe with Chinese state builders. It also runs the 15,000-mu Koh Kong Zhejiang Special Economic Zone in Cambodia, launched 2022-23.
deep_cut_fact: Kasen began in 1988 as the Qingyun Huafeng tannery, making pigskin and sheepskin garment leather. By 2001 its leather sofas were exported to Europe and the US and, per the company, 'placed in the White House'.
notes: Listed (Wikipedia) among Zhejiang delegates to the National People's Congress. He accompanied President Hu Jintao on a 2008 state visit to the Americas. Strong energy/infrastructure angle (overseas power plants). Chinese-language outreach advised; the HK email is the listed company's IR mailbox (via IMS).

name: D James Bidzos
current_role: Executive Chairman, President & CEO, VeriSign Inc.
profile: Jim Bidzos is a pioneer of commercial internet security. He ran RSA Data Security from 1986 to 1999, co-founded RSA Laboratories, created the RSA Conference in 1991 and founded VeriSign in 1995. He has chaired VeriSign since 2007 and been CEO since 2011. Verisign now runs the authoritative .com and .net registries and two of the internet's 13 root servers.
interesting_fact: He started the RSA Conference in 1991 as a small cryptography gathering; it grew into one of the world's largest cybersecurity events. In the mid-1990s he publicly led the industry campaign against the US government's Clipper chip.
deep_cut_fact: When he joined RSA Data Security on 1 Feb 1986, he later said the company was 'a complete failure'. A toolkit deal with Iris Associates (makers of Lotus Notes) helped turn it around, and by 1993 about 100 companies were using RSA's encryption toolkit.
notes: Rarely gives interviews these days. Strong fit for internet-infrastructure / data-center themes (DNS root operations). Route via Verisign media relations, using the contacts published in the Q3 2026 earnings release.

name: Jane Nind Fraser
current_role: Chair (since Oct 2025) and CEO (since 2021), Citigroup Inc.
profile: Scottish-born banker (b. 1967, St Andrews) who became the first woman to run a major US bank when she took over as Citigroup CEO in 2021, adding the chair role in October 2025. A former McKinsey partner, she joined Citi in 2004 and ran Citi Private Bank, CitiMortgage, US consumer banking and Latin America; she is leading Citi's multi-year simplification and restructuring.
interesting_fact: Fortune ranked her No. 1 on its 2026 Most Powerful Women list; she was made a Dame (DBE).
deep_cut_fact: Before banking leadership, she co-authored the 1999 book 'Race for the World: Strategies to Build a Great Global Firm' with three McKinsey colleagues, and early on worked as a brokerage associate at Asesores Bursátiles in Madrid (1990-92).
notes: Very high-profile CEO; requests go through Citi Corporate Communications (US media hotline 212-793-0710 published on the same page). Educated at Girton College, Cambridge and Harvard Business School.

name: Enrique Selva Bellvis
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Turbo Energy S.A. (Nasdaq: TURB); Chairman & CEO, Umbrella Global Energy S.A. (formerly Umbrella Solar Investment, BME Growth)
profile: Valencia-based solar entrepreneur who built IM2 Energía Solar (founded ~2003) into the Umbrella group of PV development, O&M and equipment businesses. Its subsidiary Turbo Energy, maker of the SunBox all-in-one solar-plus-storage system and AI-driven energy management, listed on Nasdaq in 2023; he moved from CEO to chairman at end-2023 and Turbo now focuses on C&I battery storage in Europe.
interesting_fact: Turbo Energy pitches itself as AI applied to renewables: its software optimises battery storage for industrial sites, and in 2026 it brought 62.5 MWh of intelligent storage online across three industrial sites.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture, Valencia's IM2 Energía Solar, had installed some 152,000 solar panels generating ~79 million kWh a year by 2018, when he regrouped its businesses (incl. Solar Rocket, Thunder Energy and Turbo Energy) into the Umbrella Capital holding.
notes: Small-cap (net worth figure derives from SEC insider holdings). Speaks Spanish; quoted regularly in Valencian business press (Valencia Plaza). Turbo's CEO is Mariano Soria; communications contacts have changed through 2026, so IR inbox is the stable route.

name: Thomas E. Long
current_role: Co-CEO and director, Energy Transfer LP (set to become sole CEO when Mackie McCrea retires by end-2026); chairman, USA Compression Partners; director, Texas Capital Bancshares
profile: Dallas-based midstream finance executive. CFO of Regency Energy Partners (2010-15), joined Energy Transfer when it bought Regency, was ET's CFO 2016-2020 (overseeing the 2018 ETE/ETP merger), and co-CEO since Jan 2021. In June 2026 ET said he will become sole CEO on McCrea's retirement. Wealth reflects his ET equity per SEC insider filings.
interesting_fact: Long sits on the board of the new Texas Stock Exchange (since July 2024), and in Sept 2026 Energy Transfer announced it would move its listing from the NYSE to TXSE — the exchange's first primary listing transferred from the NYSE.
deep_cut_fact: Before Energy Transfer he spent 1998-2005 in executive roles at Duke Energy subsidiaries, then was CFO of DCP Midstream Partners and of Matrix Service Co.; he also serves on the Dallas Fed's Energy Advisory Council.
notes: Energy Transfer press releases list Media Relations (Vicki Granado) and Investor Relations contacts with phone numbers only, no email. Speaks at industry events (Hart Energy Super DUG). Strong energy/data-center-gas fit.

name: Fang Jin
current_role: Founder and Chairman/General Manager, Fujian Scud Co. (飞毛腿, Fuzhou) - per company-profile sources (undated)
profile: Fujian entrepreneur who founded Scud (飞毛腿) in Fuzhou's Mawei district in 1997, building one of China's best-known mobile-phone battery and power-bank brands and listing Scud Group in Hong Kong in late 2006. The group later spun its power-battery business into a separate unit (2016) and expanded into energy storage.
interesting_fact: Scud ('飞毛腿', literally 'fleet-footed') grew from phone batteries into a group of 10+ companies making mobile batteries, power banks and EV/storage power batteries, and appeared on Hurun's China Rich List in 2007 after its 2006 Hong Kong IPO.
deep_cut_fact: In 2010 Scud set up its own vocational school, the Fujian Scud Senior Technical School (福建省飞毛腿高级技工学校), which has since graduated nearly 10,000 skilled workers.
notes: Only appeared on Hurun in 2007; very little recent coverage, and no official company contact page could be verified (scudbattery.com is a parked domain). Alive status not confirmed by a dated source. Low-priority lead.

name: Tao Guoping
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Jiangsu Jiangnan High Polymer Fiber (Shanghai 600527); transferred control in 2023 (no current executive role found)
profile: Tao Guoping (陶国平) founded Jiangsu Jiangnan High Polymer Fiber in Suzhou's Xiangcheng district, listed in Shanghai in 2003, and remained controlling shareholder (22.57%) until July 2023, when he passed control to the next generation of the family. The company says it is China's largest maker of bicomponent (ES) staple fibre and polyester tops.
interesting_fact: Jiangnan High Polymer Fiber's ES bicomponent staple fibres (230,000 t/yr capacity) are a main raw material for nonwovens used in disposable hygiene products such as diapers, and its polyester tops are blended with wool for worsted fabrics.
notes: Hurun-listed only in 2007. Polyester fibres, not data centers/AI, so a weak fit for the podcast's focus. He stepped back in 2023 (control-transfer notice: https://paper.cnstock.com/html/2023-07/22/content_1798337.htm). 'Alive' is based on that 2023 transaction. Route via the IR mailbox.

name: Jagdeep Singh
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO/Chairman of QuantumScape; retired from the board at the end of 2024. I could not verify a current role.
profile: Jagdeep Singh is a serial deep-tech founder. He founded and ran optical-networking company Infinera as CEO from 2001 to 2009, then co-founded solid-state battery maker QuantumScape in 2010 with Tim Holme and Stanford professor Fritz Prinz. He was CEO until February 2024, when Siva Sivaram took over after a year-long succession plan, and he left the chairmanship and board at the end of 2024.
interesting_fact: He planned his own exit: QuantumScape's 8-K says Siva Sivaram's appointment as CEO in Feb 2024 was the culmination of a year-long succession plan that Singh started as chairman and outgoing CEO. Before that he had led the company since founding it in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He has three degrees from three schools: a B.S. in computer science from the University of Maryland, an M.S. in computer science from Stanford, and an MBA from UC Berkeley Haas. He also sat on the boards of the SPACs Khosla Ventures Acquisition Co. and Slam Corp. in 2021-22.
notes: A strong fit for the energy theme (batteries). He started the QuantumScape CEO succession himself, so it was not an ouster. The SEC net-worth figure dates from 2024, before his equity awards terminated when he retired. I found no personal site or published contact; LinkedIn is the likely route but I did not verify it.

name: Rehan Jaffer
current_role: Founder and Managing Member, H Partners Management LLC (New York investment firm). Director, Six Flags Entertainment Corp since May 2026.
profile: Founder of H Partners Management, a concentrated, long-term public-equity investor. He joined the Six Flags board after the 2026 annual meeting under a cooperation agreement with the company, replacing H Partners' previous representative Arik Ruchim, and sits on its Audit and Finance Committee.
interesting_fact: According to Six Flags' filing, H Partners had been a significant Six Flags investor for more than 15 years and long had a seat on its board before Jaffer took it himself in 2026.
notes: Low-profile hedge fund founder. The listed contacts are Six Flags company channels, not his own. A better route would be H Partners itself, but no official website or contact for it was confirmed (web search quota ran out). The 8-K URL was built from the filing's accession number.

name: J Scott Kirby
current_role: CEO, United Airlines Holdings; director, CVS Health
profile: Scott Kirby is CEO of United Airlines (since May 2020), after serving as United's president from 2016 and earlier as president of US Airways and American Airlines. An Air Force Academy graduate in computer science and operations research, he began as a Pentagon budget analyst and at Sabre before joining America West in 1995. He also chairs the Star Alliance chief executive board.
interesting_fact: He has led three major US airlines as president (US Airways, American, United) and in December 2020 became chairman of the Star Alliance chief executive board.
deep_cut_fact: As an Air Force Academy cadet he learned he would never be a military pilot when an instructor had him close his eyes and fly straight and level in an F-4 over the Gulf of Mexico; when he opened them he was in a 30-degree left bank.
notes: High-profile, heavily handled by United corporate communications; route via United media relations newsroom.

name: Sohit Khurana
current_role: Co-owner/controller (with Manoj Jain) of Maso Capital Partners, Hong Kong; SEC reporting person for FiscalNote (NOTE)
profile: Hong Kong-based hedge-fund principal. SEC Form 4 filings (June 2025) state Maso Capital Partners, an Asia-focused event-driven/activist manager founded in 2013, is beneficially owned and controlled by Manoj Jain and Sohit Khurana. Maso sponsored the SPAC Duddell Street Acquisition, which merged with FiscalNote in 2022, hence the 10%+ stake (fund holdings).
interesting_fact: The FiscalNote shares are held via Duddell Street Holdings, named after Maso's office address at 6 Duddell Street in Central, Hong Kong.
notes: Very low profile: not listed on Maso's current leadership page (which shows Manoj Jain and Allan Finnerty), so his current day-to-day role is unclear. 'Net worth' reflects fund holdings he is deemed to control, not personal wealth.

name: Mauad Bruno Sousa
current_role: Partner & equities portfolio manager, Kapitalo Investimentos (Sao Paulo); Independent Director, Aura Minerals (AUGO) since 2020
profile: Bruno Sousa Mauad is a Brazilian investor - partner in charge of equities strategies at Sao Paulo hedge fund Kapitalo Investimentos (executive committee since 2019) - and an independent director of gold/copper miner Aura Minerals. His SEC-reported holdings largely reflect Kapitalo-managed Aura shares. Earlier he was at Ashmore Brasil and Patria Investimentos.
interesting_fact: Started his career at Patria Investimentos in 2005, later a senior PM at Ashmore Brasil before joining Kapitalo in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: Public Administration graduate of FGV-EAESP (Sao Paulo) and a CFA charterholder.
notes: Low public profile; bio facts are from aggregator (MarketScreener) rather than primary filings. Route via Aura IR or Kapitalo.

name: Satish Chitoori
current_role: Chief Operations Officer, Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE)
profile: Operations executive who joined Bloom Energy in 2019 as SVP of global supply chain and became COO (around end-2023/April 2024), overseeing supply chain, manufacturing, installations and facilities as Bloom scales solid-oxide fuel-cell production to power AI data centers onsite. His SEC-reported wealth comes from Bloom stock, which surged on data-center demand.
interesting_fact: He is the operations lead behind Bloom's rapid capacity ramp for AI data-center customers (e.g. Oracle, AEP, Brookfield deals) - Bloom pitches being able to deliver onsite power in months rather than the years needed for grid connections.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bloom he spent 22 years in semiconductor and electronics operations - process engineering, quality, product and program leadership - and holds a mechanical engineering degree plus an MBA in operations.
notes: Low public profile operator rather than founder; great for a 'how do you build fuel cells fast enough for AI' segment. Route via Bloom media relations (Katja Gagen, press@bloomenergy.com). Interesting_fact customer names from general Bloom news, not his bio page.

name: David D Dallas
current_role: Chairman, Unity Bancorp / Unity Bank (Clinton, NJ); CEO, The Dallas Group of America, Inc.
profile: New Jersey industrialist and banker (age 71) who has been on Unity Bancorp's board since 1991 and is its Chairman and a 10%+ holder alongside his brother Robert H. Dallas II. His operating business is The Dallas Group of America, a family-founded (1959) maker of adsorbent and edible-oil filtration products for restaurant fryers, food, beverage and industrial purification, with plants in North America, Europe and Asia.
interesting_fact: The Dallas Group's adsorbent powders and filtration programs extend the life of commercial frying oil in restaurants worldwide, an unglamorous niche the family has built since Robert H. Dallas founded the business in 1959.
deep_cut_fact: He and his brother Robert have both sat on Unity's board since 1991, more than three decades of continuous oversight of the community bank, which they combine with running a global specialty-chemicals business.

public_contacts.value: info@dallasgrp.com (Dallas Group of America general inbox)

notes: Private, low-profile family businessman. Best route is the Dallas Group general inbox or the Unity Bank corporate secretary. No current Unity press contact found (a 2017 release used Yankee PR).

name: Clinton Bybee
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director (listed by some sources as Emeritus), ARCH Venture Partners
profile: Clint Bybee co-founded ARCH Venture Partners, the early-stage firm spun out of the University of Chicago/Argonne tech-transfer effort, and has invested in advanced materials, semiconductors, photonics and infrastructure tech. His SEC-reported 10% stakes in Neumora, Lyell and Boundless Bio reflect ARCH funds' biotech holdings rather than personal operating roles.
interesting_fact: He is an organizing member and the first President of the Texas Venture Capital Association, and has served on boards including RFID chipmaker Impinj.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he worked as a production engineer at Amoco, and he managed a venture fund for the State of Illinois before co-founding ARCH; he holds a Texas A&M engineering degree and a University of Chicago MBA.
notes: Relevant to energy/infrastructure-tech angle (advanced materials, photonics, semiconductors). Ownership filings are as ARCH fund manager. Based in Austin per Crunchbase.

name: Chris Diorio, Ph.D.
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Vice Chair, Impinj, Inc. (PI), Seattle
profile: Caltech-trained electrical engineer (BA physics, Occidental) who co-founded Impinj in 2000 with his PhD adviser Carver Mead, commercialising their research. Impinj makes RAIN (UHF RFID) chips and readers that tag billions of retail and logistics items. CEO since 2014, he reported record endpoint IC revenue in Q3 2026 on its M800 chips; he remains an affiliate professor of CSE at the University of Washington.
interesting_fact: The company name is a technical acronym: Impinj stands for 'Impact-ionized hot-electron injection', the semiconductor effect behind the Caltech research by Mead and Diorio.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Impinj he consulted for it (2000-04) and served as VP Engineering and CTO; he also chaired the RAIN Alliance industry group and sits on GS1's Innovation Board and the EPCglobal Board of Governors that set RFID standards.

public_contacts.value: comms@impinj.com (Bassil Elkadi, Sr Director Communications & PR, +1 206-517-5300)
ir@impinj.com (Andy Cobb, VP Corporate Finance & IR)

notes: Technical founder-CEO; good for deep-tech/IoT angle. Media requests via comms@impinj.com (from Q3 2026 earnings release, Oct 28, 2026).

name: Wilmot H Kidd
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Central Securities Corporation (NYSE American: CET)
profile: Long-time steward of Central Securities, a New York closed-end investment company: director since 1972, President 1973-2018, CEO 2018-21 and now Chairman (age 84 per the 2026 proxy). He owns about 7% of the fund directly, with a further ~32.5% held by The Endeavor Foundation, giving the Kidd circle effective control of a ~$2bn concentrated, long-horizon portfolio.
interesting_fact: Central Securities' largest holding is a private stake in insurer The Plymouth Rock Company, first bought in 1982 at a cost of $0.7m and valued at about $503m (25.6% of net assets) at 30 Sept 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He has served as a Central Securities director continuously since 1972 – over five decades – and was its President for 45 years (1973-2018); the fund still holds positions it first bought decades ago, e.g. Analog Devices since 1987 and Motorola Solutions since 2000.

public_contacts.value: Corporate office: Central Securities Corporation, 630 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10111 (shareholder reports state 'Stockholders' inquiries are welcome')

notes: Very private, old-school value investor; no social media. Best route is a letter to Central Securities' corporate office (business address). John C. Hill is now CEO/President. No published email found (company site blocked automated access).

name: John Kent Walker
current_role: President, Global Affairs and Chief Legal Officer, Google & Alphabet
profile: Kent Walker (Harvard BA 1983, Stanford JD) has been Google's top lawyer since 2006 and President of Global Affairs since 2021, overseeing legal, policy, government affairs and trust & safety. He oversaw creation of Google's 2018 AI Principles and is a leading voice on AI regulation, digital sovereignty and the energy/infrastructure needs of AI.
interesting_fact: In a March 2026 post he argued AI developers should compete on demonstrable privacy techniques, calling it 'not just privacy by default, or even privacy by design - it's privacy by innovation.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Google he was a federal prosecutor (Assistant U.S. Attorney for five years), then a lawyer at AirTouch Communications and deputy general counsel at Netscape (1997-2001) during the browser wars, followed by Liberate Technologies and eBay.
notes: Strong fit for data-center/energy policy topics (Google's AI infrastructure and power advocacy). Best route is Google's press team; he publishes regularly on blog.google.

name: Sean McNealy
current_role: Co-Founder & Advisor, Abacus Global Management, Inc. (NYSE: ABX); 10% owner
profile: Sean McNealy is one of the co-founders (with Matthew Ganovsky and Scott Kirby) of Abacus, a life-settlements firm that went public and is now Abacus Global Management, a longevity-focused alternative asset manager with divisions in life settlements, asset management, data/tech (Abacus Intel) and lifespan-based wealth planning. He now serves as Co-Founder & Advisor and is a 10%+ shareholder.
interesting_fact: Abacus has turned life-insurance settlements - buying policies from people typically over 65 - into an institutional asset class marketed as uncorrelated with traditional markets.
notes: No longer an operating executive; low personal profile. Contact via Abacus IR. Personal biography details not verified because web search budget was exhausted.

name: Kevin Scott Kirby
current_role: Co-founder and ~13% shareholder of Abacus Global Management (Nasdaq: ABX), Orlando, Florida; former President after the 2023 SPAC listing
profile: K. Scott Kirby co-founded Abacus Settlements in 2004 with Sean McNealy and Matthew Ganovsky, and served as a managing partner building the life-settlements market. Abacus buys and trades life-insurance policies for institutional investors. It went public via a SPAC merger in 2023 and has since expanded into asset management. He served as President after the listing and remains one of its largest holders.
interesting_fact: Abacus's 2023 merger proxy says its three managing partners co-founded the firm in 2004 and 'helped build the institutional and broker market for the entire industry' of life settlements.
deep_cut_fact: He is a University of Central Florida business-management graduate (BSBA) and has held a Florida life and annuity license since 2006.
notes: The April 2026 proxy lists him only as a 5%+ holder (13.1%), not among executive officers, so he may have stepped back from day-to-day management. Low public profile. Route via Abacus PR. Weak fit for an energy/data-center theme.

name: Emanuele Lauro
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Scorpio Tankers (Monaco); Vice Chairman, Cadeler A/S
profile: Emanuele Lauro joined the Monaco-based Scorpio group of shipping companies in 2003 and founded Scorpio Tankers, one of the world's largest product-tanker owners, which he has led as Chairman and CEO since its April 2010 IPO. He also co-founded Eneti (formerly Scorpio Bulkers), which pivoted into offshore-wind installation vessels and merged with Cadeler in December 2023.
interesting_fact: He steered Eneti from dry-bulk shipping into building offshore-wind turbine installation vessels. After its 2023 merger with Cadeler, the world's leading wind-installation vessel operator, he became Cadeler's Vice Chairman, a strong energy-transition angle.
deep_cut_fact: He studied international business at the European Business School, London. He is Vice President of the Monaco Chamber of Shipping and sits on Fordham University's London Advisory Council.
notes: Based in Monaco; brother Filippo Lauro is a Scorpio VP. Very good fit for the energy theme (oil-product shipping plus offshore wind via Cadeler). Route via Scorpio IR.

name: Mark W Begor
current_role: CEO and director, Equifax Inc. (since April 2018); director, Raymond James Financial
profile: A 35-year GE veteran who ran GE Energy Management, GE Capital Real Estate and GE Capital Retail Finance (now Synchrony) and was CFO of NBCUniversal, then a Warburg Pincus managing director. He took over Equifax after its 2017 breach, led a ~$3bn cloud rebuild and grew revenue from $3.4bn (2018) to about $6.1bn (2025).
interesting_fact: Equifax has completed 15 acquisitions totalling nearly $4bn since 2021 under his leadership.
deep_cut_fact: Outside Equifax he chairs the board of trustees of Dartmouth Health and is a trustee of the U.S. Ski and Snowboard Foundation; earlier he led GE's investor-relations function.
notes: Syracuse University BA, RPI MBA. Left the NCR Atleos board in May 2025 per Equifax bio. Route via Equifax media relations.

name: Michael J Hennigan
current_role: Director, The Cigna Group (since Jun 2025) and Kayne Anderson Energy Infrastructure Fund (KYN, since May 2026); retired as MPC/MPLX Executive Chairman on 1 Jan 2026
profile: Veteran downstream/midstream executive who spent 30+ years at Sunoco, rising to CEO of Sunoco Logistics, then briefly ran crude/NGL/refined products at Energy Transfer before joining MPLX in 2017. He was CEO of Marathon Petroleum (largest US refiner) from March 2020 and executive chairman from Aug 2024 until retiring on 1 Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: He took over as Marathon Petroleum CEO in March 2020, right as COVID crushed fuel demand, and led the period in which MPC sold Speedway to 7-Eleven for $21bn; MPC's board later credited him with 'a period of significant value creation'.
deep_cut_fact: A Drexel University chemical engineering graduate (Philadelphia), he started his career at Sunoco Inc. and stayed more than three decades, an unusually long single-company run before becoming CEO of its pipeline arm, Sunoco Logistics.
notes: Now retired from MPC, so outreach via MPC is weak; MPC media line (419) 421-3577 is published in the Nov 2025 8-K exhibit. Speedway sale detail is widely reported but not in the cited 8-K - verify before quoting. Input listing (MPC exec chairman) is outdated.

name: He Xianshu
current_role: Chairman, Houying Group (海城市后英经贸集团), Haicheng, Liaoning (as of 2019)
profile: He Xianshu (何宪恕) chairs Houying Group, a private conglomerate founded in 1984 in Yingluo town, Haicheng, Liaoning ('world magnesium capital'), spanning magnesite mining and refractories, iron ore and steel (Houying Group Haicheng Iron & Steel), building materials and, earlier, soybean/edible-oil processing. The group reported 2020 sales of 14bn yuan and about 10,000 staff.
interesting_fact: Houying mines over 1.8m tonnes of magnesite a year and makes close to 1m tonnes of refractories (magnesia bricks, fused magnesia), plus 1.5m tonnes of steel; it ranks among China's top refractory and magnesium-oxide brands.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 he told reporters that after Haicheng consolidated its magnesite mines, Houying's 2018 profit equalled the previous several years combined; the group spent ~200m yuan on new kilns and another 100m yuan in 2018 on pollution control, refilling mined areas and replanting.
notes: Confirmed: chairman He Xianshu quoted by China Nonferrous Metals News (2019); registry snippets show him holding ~84.6% of Houying Haicheng Iron & Steel. Baidu Baike (blocked; seen via snippet only) reportedly gives b. June 1977, US business degree, 2015 National Model Worker - unverified. Group legal rep is now Liang Biao. Contact is a company phone.

profile: Appears only on the 2006 Hurun China Rich List (~$100m) under 'Shengda Group' in energy processing. Searches in English and Chinese (陈永洪 盛达集团) found no biography or company record clearly matching; several unrelated Chinese firms use the Shengda name.

name: Cao Ruiying
current_role: Shareholder (7.18%) of Jinglong Industrial Group, Ningjin, Hebei; the original parent of JA Solar. No public executive title found
profile: Cao Ruiying (曹瑞英) owns 7.18% of Jinglong Group, alongside Jin Baofang (78.45%), Liu Binguo and Ren Bingyan. Jinglong began in 1996 as a county power-bureau silicon plant, became employee-owned in 2003 and co-founded JA Solar. After moving its PV assets into JA Solar, it now focuses on hotels, property and finance.
interesting_fact: Jinglong started in 1996 when the county power bureau chief Jin Baofang heard of a Hebei University of Technology process for making monocrystalline silicon by neutron-transmutation doping. The plant later became one of the world's largest monocrystalline-silicon producers and gave rise to JA Solar.
notes: Identity confirmed via Jinglong's registry shareholding (7.18%), reported by Beijing News (https://m.bjnews.com.cn/detail/160517055515260.html). No personal public profile, role or contact found, and she appears only on Hurun 2008. The Jin Baofang family fronts JA Solar and Jinglong; approach via Jinglong Group, in Chinese.

No public source found for anyone named Liu Rongrui (刘容蕊) at Jinglong; the group is led by founder Jin Baofang (靳保芳). Likely a minor early shareholder or executive with no public footprint.
notes: Could not confirm identity or current status; kept minimal. Single 2008 Hurun appearance (~$100M). If useful for the solar angle, Jinglong/JA Solar founder Jin Baofang is the better-documented figure (https://www.pv-magazine.com/2010/07/07/ja-solar-buys-out-shanghai-jinglong-solar-technology_1000373/).

name: Liu Huiqiang
current_role: Co-owner of Jinglong Group (BVI), a founding shareholder group of JA Solar (Ningjin, Hebei)
profile: Liu Huiqiang (柳辉强) is one of the ten Chinese individual co-owners of Jinglong Group, the Ningjin, Hebei silicon group led by Jin Baofang that founded JA Solar. He held 7.18% of Jinglong Group BVI, which kept a JA Solar stake through its 2007 Nasdaq IPO, 2018 take-private and 2019 Shenzhen relisting as JA Solar Technology (002459).
interesting_fact: JA Solar grew out of Jinglong's mono-silicon business in Ningjin county, Hebei; its predecessor, Jinglong Zhong'ao, was renamed JA Solar in December 2005 and went to Nasdaq barely 14 months later.
deep_cut_fact: JA Solar's SEC filings list 'Mr. Huiqiang Liu (7.18%)' among Jinglong Group BVI's owners, alongside Jicun Yan, Rongrui Liu and Ruiying Cao with equal 7.18% stakes.
notes: Identity confirmed via JA Solar 20-F (2008) and the 2019 Tianye/JA Solar reverse-merger legal opinion (柳辉强持股7.18%). Passive co-founder/shareholder with almost no public profile; no executive title found. Best route is via JA Solar IR or Jinglong Group.

name: Yan Jicun
current_role: Unknown; historically a co-owner (7.18%) of Jinglong Group Co., Ltd. (BVI), founding largest shareholder of JA Solar
profile: Yan Jicun (闫计存) appears in JA Solar's SEC filings as one of 11 individual owners of Jinglong Group Co., Ltd. (7.18%), the BVI holding company of Hebei Ningjin's Jinglong silicon/solar group and JA Solar's largest shareholder when it listed on NASDAQ in February 2007. That stake underpinned his single Hurun appearance (2008). No current role or recent news found.
interesting_fact: Jinglong Group, led by Jin Baofang in Ningjin County, Hebei, was the parent behind JA Solar, now one of the world's largest solar-module makers; Yan was among the small circle of Jinglong insiders who co-owned its offshore holding vehicle at the 2007 NASDAQ IPO.
notes: Identity marked uncertain: SEC filings confirm a 'Mr. Jicun Yan' as Jinglong Group BVI shareholder (2007-2014), consistent with Hurun's 'Jinglong Group' attribution, but no biography or current role is public. Only appeared on Hurun in 2008. Very low profile; no contact route found.

name: Campos Vicente Falconi
current_role: Chairman of the Board (independent), AXIA Energia S.A. (formerly Eletrobras); founding partner and board chairman, Falconi Consultores de Resultado
profile: Vicente Falconi Campos is a Brazilian engineer and management thinker who founded Falconi, one of Brazil's largest management consultancies, over 40 years ago. He spent 25 years on AmBev's board and also sat on Unibanco, Sadia, BRF, Cyrela and Qualicorp boards. He now chairs AXIA Energia (ex-Eletrobras), Latin America's largest power utility.
interesting_fact: Falconi introduced Japanese-style Total Quality Control to Brazilian industry in the 1980s-90s; his book 'TQC: Controle da Qualidade Total (no estilo japonês)' became a standard management text in Brazil.
deep_cut_fact: Before consulting he was an academic: he earned his Master's and PhD in engineering at the Colorado School of Mines and taught engineering for about three decades at UFMG in Belo Horizonte, which made him Professor Emeritus.
notes: Input name is inverted; he is known as Vicente Falconi. Board role confirmed on AXIA's IR governance page (https://ri.axia.com.br/en/?p=1043). Best route is the Falconi consultancy press page or AXIA IR. Individual AXIA IR staff emails are also listed on the IR page, but ri@ is the general inbox.

name: Richard E Muncrief
current_role: Retired President & CEO of Devon Energy (to March 2025); Director, Williams Companies (since 2022) and OGE Energy (since Aug 2026)
profile: Rick Muncrief (Oklahoma State petroleum engineering, 1980) spent about 45 years in oil and gas, including at Continental Resources. He became CEO and chairman of WPX Energy in 2014, led its 2021 merger with Devon, and ran Devon as CEO until retiring in March 2025. He now sits on the boards of pipeline giant Williams and Oklahoma utility OGE Energy.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 he and former Noble Energy CEO Chuck Davidson received the Energy Workforce & Technology Council's Platinum Award, its highest honour, which is not given every year. He is also in Hart Energy's Hall of Fame (2023).
deep_cut_fact: Muncrief took his first oilfield job at 17. He grew up in the Texas and Oklahoma oil fields of the '60s and '70s listening to his father's and grandfather's stories, including his granddad's stint on a pulling unit in southern Oklahoma.

public_contacts.value: Williams board communications via the Corporate Secretary, The Williams Companies, Inc., One Williams Center, Tulsa, OK (details on the Investors page of williams.com)

notes: Retired from Devon, so outreach via Devon is no longer appropriate. Best published routes are the board-communication channels at Williams or OGE Energy. Age 68 per OGE's Jul 2026 8-K. Good podcast fit: he spans upstream gas, midstream pipelines and a utility facing data-center load growth in Oklahoma.

name: Pablo Manuel Vera Pinto
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Vista Energy S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE/BMV: VIST), since Aug 2017
profile: Argentine executive Pablo Vera Pinto (48) is a founding member of Vista Energy, the Vaca Muerta shale producer launched in 2017 by ex-YPF CEO Miguel Galuccio as a SPAC, and has been CFO since. Before that he ran business development at YPF (2012-2017), after restructuring work, McKinsey in Europe and Credit Suisse First Boston in New York.
interesting_fact: He has been involved with Vista since its incorporation on March 22, 2017 - the company was created as a Mexican-listed blank-check vehicle that bought Argentine oil assets and became one of Vaca Muerta's leading shale producers.
deep_cut_fact: At YPF he was Director of Transformation in 2012 and sat on the boards of fertilizer JV Profertil (with Agrium), power generator Central Dock Sud (with Enel) and gas distributor MetroGAS. He studied economics at Universidad Torcuato Di Tella and holds an INSEAD MBA.
notes: Listed name order 'Pinto Pablo Manuel Vera' is SEC-insider style; he goes by Pablo Vera Pinto. Regularly speaks on Vista earnings calls, so IR is a natural route. Wealth (~$98m) is from Vista insider holdings.

name: Marshall T Reynolds
current_role: Chairman, First Guaranty Bancshares (FGBI); Chairman, Champion Industries; Director, Energy Services of America (ESOA)
profile: Huntington, West Virginia businessman who built printing/office-products firm Champion Industries (Nasdaq IPO 1993) from Chapman Printing, bought in 1964; took control of First Huntington National Bank in the early 1980s and has chaired Louisiana's First Guaranty Bank since 1996. Also a director of utility contractor Energy Services of America.
interesting_fact: He remains an active buyer of his own bank's stock: he was chairman and proxy holder at First Guaranty's 2026 annual meeting and bought about $250k of FGBI shares in October 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Chapman Printing in Huntington as a 1950s clean-up boy, rose to delivery boy and top salesman, ran it when owner John Chapman fell ill, and in 1964 bought the company from his former boss; he attended Marshall University but never finished his degree.
notes: Born late 1930s; long-time Huntington power broker, featured repeatedly in Huntington Quarterly. Inducted into WVU Business Hall of Fame (business.wvu.edu). Energy angle: Energy Services of America (gas/water/electric utility contracting). Route via company IR/corporate secretary.

name: R. Lane Riggs
current_role: Chairman, CEO and President, Valero Energy Corporation (NYSE: VLO)
profile: Lane Riggs is a chemical engineer who has spent his whole career at Valero, joining in 1989 and rising through refining operations, crude supply and trading to President & COO. He became CEO in June 2023 and added chairman in Dec 2024, leading the largest independent US refiner, which also has major renewable diesel and ethanol businesses.
interesting_fact: A rare lifer CEO: 35+ years at one company, from process engineer to chairman. He holds a chemical engineering BS from the University of Oklahoma and an MBA from West Texas A&M.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Valero as a process engineer at the McKee refinery in the Texas Panhandle. He also writes bylined pieces for the San Antonio Report on Valero's giving culture, e.g. 'Valero's legacy of giving and culture of caring' (Oct 2026).

public_contacts.value: Media relations: Lillian Riojas, Executive Director - Media Relations and Communications, 210-345-5002 (no email published)

notes: Engineer-operator, not a founder; SEC-insider wealth ~US$98m. Best route is Valero media relations. Byline archive: https://sanantonioreport.org/author/lane-riggs/

name: Nguyen Duc Tai
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Mobile World Investment Corporation (MWG; Thegioididong, Dien May Xanh, Bach Hoa Xanh)
profile: Nguyễn Đức Tài (born 1969, Nam Định) studied finance and accounting at the University of Economics HCMC and earned an MBA from the French-Vietnamese CFVG programme. In 2004 he and four partners founded Thegioididong, which grew into MWG, Vietnam's largest electronics and phone retailer, with the Bach Hoa Xanh grocery chain and the EraBlue venture in Indonesia. He was CEO until 2019 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: MWG started in March 2004 as a basic e-commerce site that only displayed product information, backed by three tiny shops on Hoàng Văn Thụ street in HCMC. It became profitable after moving to a bigger store on Nguyễn Đình Chiểu that October.
deep_cut_fact: Thegioididong had five co-founders, not one: Tài, Trần Lê Quân, Đinh Anh Huân, Điêu Chính Hải Triều and Trần Huy Thanh Tùng. Before founding it, Tài had trained in finance and accounting and earned a French-Vietnamese (CFVG) MBA.
notes: The $96M Wikidata net-worth figure probably understates his MWG holding. He is well known in Vietnam for blunt speeches at MWG shareholder meetings. Outreach in Vietnamese via MWG IR is the most practical route; I found no personal contact. The search budget ran out, so I could not find an English-language deep cut.

name: Keith Stuart Liddell
current_role: Founder and Chair of the Board, Lifezone Metals Ltd (NYSE: LZM)
profile: A metallurgical engineer who has worked only in minerals and metals since 1981, taking nickel, copper and PGM projects from exploration through to production. He founded the Lifezone group, which listed on the NYSE via a SPAC in 2023. As chair he focuses on its Hydromet refining technology and the Kabanga Nickel Project in Tanzania. He and his family hold about 28% of Lifezone.
interesting_fact: Lifezone's pitch is its own hydrometallurgical ('Hydromet') process, offered as a lower-emission alternative to smelting, which it plans to use to refine nickel from the Kabanga project in Tanzania.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a minerals engineer, with an honours BSc in Minerals Engineering from the University of Birmingham and an MSc in Engineering from the University of the Witwatersrand. Lifezone also retains him as a consultant for hands-on metallurgical engineering.
notes: Good fit for an energy-transition and critical-minerals (battery nickel) episode. The company's general info@ address is the only published channel found.

name: H Andrew DeFerrari
current_role: Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (also Principal Accounting Officer), Dycom Industries
profile: Drew DeFerrari has been CFO of Dycom Industries, the Florida-based contractor that builds and maintains fiber, wireless and utility networks for telecom carriers, since April 2008. He joined Dycom in 2004 as Controller from Ernst & Young, became Chief Accounting Officer in 2005, and added Principal Accounting Officer duties in January 2024.
interesting_fact: He has been Dycom's CFO since April 2008, succeeding Richard Dunn: roughly 18 years in the role, an unusually long tenure for a public-company CFO.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Dycom in July 2004 as Controller after a stint as a senior audit manager at Ernst & Young, rising to CFO less than four years later.
notes: Fiber/telecom infrastructure angle (Dycom builds fiber networks, relevant to data-center connectivity). info@ is the company's general inbox; the IR contact page blocks automated access, check it manually.

name: Patrick Connor Haley
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner/CIO, Alta Fox Capital Management (Fort Worth, Texas)
profile: Connor Haley is the activist/value investor who launched the Alta Fox Opportunities Fund in 2018 after working at a New York long/short fund. Alta Fox is a 10%+ holder of LED-display maker Daktronics (DAKT), where it has been an engaged/activist shareholder; the SEC 'net worth' reflects fund holdings.
interesting_fact: He founded Alta Fox in Fort Worth rather than New York, and its flagship fund hunts 'overlooked and under-the-radar' opportunities across any asset class, market cap or geography.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Alta Fox he graduated magna cum laude from Harvard College with an A.B. in Government, not economics or finance.

public_contacts.value: Longacre Square Partners (media link on Alta Fox contact page points to gmarose@longacresquare.com)

notes: SEC name is Patrick Connor Haley; goes by Connor Haley. Active on X/fintwit historically but handle not verified here. Media inquiries routed via Longacre Square.

name: Charles Lynn Hamilton
current_role: Chief Site Development Officer, Fermi Inc. (Fermi America, NASDAQ/LSE: FRMI)
profile: Charles 'Charlie' Hamilton is Chief Site Development Officer of Fermi America, which is building Project Matador, a nuclear/gas-powered 'HyperGrid' AI data-center campus in the Texas Panhandle near Amarillo. He leads site development and has testified to the Texas House on the campus's water strategy; his wealth stems from Fermi insider shares.
interesting_fact: In June 2026 he told the Texas House Natural Resources Committee that Project Matador's four-pillar water strategy (dry/hybrid cooling, closed-loop reuse) would use ~80% less water than conventional data-center cooling.
deep_cut_fact: A sixth-generation Texan who grew up on a cow-calf and peanut farm; his family has worked the Panhandle for more than 130 years.
notes: Goes by Charlie Hamilton. Highly on-topic (AI power campus, nuclear, water). Fermi has had executive turnover (CEO/CFO departures, interim CFO) in 2026. Earlier career not verified (search budget exhausted).

name: Joseph Patrick Daly
current_role: Founder & CEO, Essig Research, Inc. (Cincinnati); Lead Independent Director and 10%+ holder, Butler National Corp; Director, Autoscope Technologies
profile: Joe Daly is an engineer-entrepreneur who founded Essig Research (1993), an engineering and manufacturing services firm specialising in aircraft powerplants and also serving locomotive, energy and government clients. He invests in small-cap industrials: he was largest shareholder of Kreisler Manufacturing (sold to Arlington Capital 2016) and since 2024 has been a director, now lead independent director, of Butler National (aerospace plus Boot Hill Casino, Kansas).
interesting_fact: Essig Research marked 30 years in business in 2023; it grew from aircraft-engine engineering into a global PLM software practice with teams in the US, Puerto Rico, Mexico, the Philippines and Barcelona.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 he bought the PLM (product lifecycle management) business of SofTech, Inc., and in 2017 opened Essig PLM in Barcelona, Spain to serve European customers. He trained as a mechanical engineer (B.S.M.E., Rensselaer) before a Northeastern MBA/MSF.
notes: Education and board roles are from Butler National's 2026 proxy: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/15847/000001584726000032/buks-20260817.htm. He joined the Butler board after a 2024 shareholder campaign, so avoid that topic. Aerospace and engineering angle.

name: Andrew C Dodson
current_role: Managing Partner, Parthenon Capital; Director, loanDepot, Inc. (NYSE: LDI)
profile: Andrew Dodson is a managing partner and investment-committee member at growth-equity firm Parthenon Capital, which he joined in 2005 and where he heads the San Francisco office. He represents Parthenon, an early backer of loanDepot, on the lender's board.
interesting_fact: He has served on the board of loanDepot's operating company, loanDepot.com LLC, since December 2009, when the mortgage lender was a young startup, well before its 2021 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Before Parthenon he was a consultant at Bain & Company (2004-2005); he is a Duke graduate with a Harvard MBA.
notes: Private-equity investor with low public profile; route via Parthenon Capital.

name: John W. Childs
current_role: Chairman, J.W. Childs Associates, FL L.P. (West Palm Beach); Director, Biohaven Ltd. and VeraDermics
profile: Yale and Columbia MBA who spent 17 years in investments at Prudential, then was a Senior MD at Thomas H. Lee (1987-95), leading buyouts such as Snapple and GNC. He founded J.W. Childs Associates in 1995; at 84 its focus has shifted to early-stage biotech, pharma and health consumer investments, and he sits on the Biohaven and VeraDermics boards.
interesting_fact: At Thomas H. Lee he arranged the leveraged buyout of Snapple, one of the landmark consumer LBOs of the early 1990s.
deep_cut_fact: A conservationist and wine investor: he serves on the boards of Delta Waterfowl, the Waterfowl Research Foundation and the Wild Salmon Center, chaired cult Pinot Noir producer Kosta Browne before its sale, and served as a 1st Lieutenant in the US Army.
notes: Age 84 (2026 Biohaven proxy). Major Republican donor. Avoid the 2019 Florida charge he denied (noted on Wikipedia). Firm email published on its own site.

name: Richard M Beyer
current_role: Retired semiconductor CEO; Micron Technology director 2013 to January 2026 (chaired its Compensation Committee)
profile: Veteran chip-industry CEO who ran Elantec Semiconductor (2000-02), Intersil (2002-08) and Freescale Semiconductor (chairman and CEO, 2008-12), after senior roles at National Semiconductor and VLSI Technology. He served on Micron's board from 2013 and retired at the January 2026 annual meeting; earlier he was also a director of Dialog Semiconductor.
interesting_fact: EE Times named him Executive of the Year at its 2012 ACE awards for his time leading Freescale.
deep_cut_fact: Before his semiconductor career he served three years as an officer in the US Marine Corps. He holds BS and MS degrees from Georgetown and an MBA from Columbia Business School.
notes: Left Micron's board in January 2026 (announced Oct 2025), so Micron IR is no longer a relevant route. Age about 77 (76 in the Nov 2024 proxy). He has no public personal channels, so the best route is probably a warm introduction through semiconductor-industry networks. Good guest for memory, chip and AI-supply-chain history.

name: Martin Roper
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, The Vita Coco Company (Nasdaq: COCO); Chairman, MGP Ingredients
profile: Cambridge-trained engineer and Harvard MBA who spent 24 years at Boston Beer (Samuel Adams), as COO and then CEO from 2001-2018, building out Twisted Tea, Angry Orchard and Truly Hard Seltzer. He joined Vita Coco as President in 2019 and has been CEO since May 2022; in 2026 Vita Coco bought premium coconut-water brand Copra.
interesting_fact: During his 17 years as Boston Beer CEO, revenue roughly quadrupled as the company diversified beyond Samuel Adams into Twisted Tea, Angry Orchard and Truly Hard Seltzer.
deep_cut_fact: He holds BA, MA and MEng degrees from Trinity Hall, Cambridge – an engineer by training – and before Vita Coco sat for years on the board of the maker of Power Crunch energy bars (2019-25); since May 2025 he also chairs whiskey/spirits supplier MGP Ingredients.
notes: Consumer-beverage operator; entrepreneurship angle via scaling Boston Beer and Vita Coco. Co-founder Michael Kirban is Executive Chairman. Route via investor relations.

name: Kathryn A Mikells
current_role: Former SVP and CFO, Exxon Mobil (Aug 2021 - retired effective 1 Feb 2026)
profile: Kathryn Mikells was ExxonMobil's Senior Vice President and CFO from August 2021 until her retirement on 1 February 2026, succeeded by Neil Hansen. She joined Exxon from Diageo plc, where she was CFO and a board director (2015-2021); earlier CFO roles reportedly included Xerox, Nalco and United Airlines.
interesting_fact: She was recruited to ExxonMobil's CFO job from consumer-goods group Diageo (Johnnie Walker, Guinness), where she had been CFO and a main-board director for nearly six years.
notes: Retired from Exxon Feb 2026 for personal reasons (per Exxon 8-K, Dec 2025: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408825000122/xom-20251208.htm); outreach should be gentle and should not raise the reason. Not currently in an executive role; earlier CFO roles (Xerox, Nalco, United) not verified in this pass.

name: Richard M Demartini
current_role: Director, Victory Capital Holdings (VCTR); Vice Chairman, Crestview Partners
profile: Richard DeMartini spent 26 years at Morgan Stanley/Dean Witter (co-president of Dean Witter, chairman of Discover Card, chairman/CEO of the international private client group), then ran Bank of America's ~$400bn wealth and asset management group (2001-04). He joined private-equity firm Crestview Partners in 2005 - which bought Victory Capital from KeyCorp in 2013 - and became vice chairman in 2021.
interesting_fact: He has served as chairman of the board of the Nasdaq Stock Market and vice chairman of the NASD, and was a founding member of Partners Capital.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trustee and former President and chairman of the Whitney Museum of American Art; his degree is a BA from San Diego State University.
notes: Board member, not an operator at Victory; Crestview Partners is an alternative route. Press email is Victory Capital's published media contact (Director, Global Communications).

name: Steven A J Salamon
current_role: Co-founder and Portfolio Manager, Rosalind Advisors (life-sciences investment manager, Toronto); director of Delcath Systems since May 2020
profile: Steven Salamon co-founded Rosalind Advisors in 2006. The life-sciences fund's Rosalind Master Fund and Rosalind Opportunities Fund are large holders in small-cap biotech and medtech. He was earlier an equity analyst at HSBC Securities and RBC Capital Markets. He joined Delcath's board under a board-appointment agreement with the Rosalind funds.
interesting_fact: Before finance he was a product engineer at Chrysler. He holds a University of Toronto Engineering Physics degree and an Ivey MBA.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a product engineer at Chrysler Corporation before his Ivey MBA, then moved to equity research at RBC Dominion Securities and HSBC before co-founding Rosalind in 2006.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Engineering background (Chrysler, engineering physics) could be a hook. Weak fit with an energy/data-center theme. Route via Delcath IR or Rosalind Advisors.

name: Badrinarayanan Kothandaraman
current_role: President, CEO and Director, Enphase Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ: ENPH)
profile: Badri Kothandaraman has run solar microinverter and home-battery maker Enphase Energy since September 2017, after joining as COO in April 2017. Before that he spent 21 years at Cypress Semiconductor, rising from process technology and chip design to EVP of its Data Communications Division (2011-16). Enphase is now also pitching power products for AI and data-center infrastructure.
interesting_fact: He is an engineer by training (IIT Madras B.Tech; UC Berkeley MS in materials science) and holds eight U.S. patents.
deep_cut_fact: At Cypress he also served as executive director of its Indian subsidiary, Cypress Semiconductor Technology India (2012-16). He attended the Stanford Executive Program in 2008, the year he became VP of Cypress's Asynchronous SRAM business.
notes: Hands-on, data-driven CEO who speaks often on earnings calls and at events. Enphase's 2026 releases cover AI-infrastructure and data-center power products (OCP Foundation, IQ SST power modules), which fits the podcast's energy and data-center theme. The press email comes from the contact blocks of Enphase's own 2026 releases; their PDFs block curl, so it was confirmed through search snippets only.

name: Jean X. Hu
current_role: EVP, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, AMD; Director, Fortinet
profile: Jean Hu has been AMD's CFO since January 2023, running finance, investor relations and corporate services during AMD's push into AI data-center GPUs. She was previously CFO of Marvell (2016-2023), CFO of QLogic (2011-2016) and a senior executive at Conexant. She has sat on Fortinet's board since 2019. Her listed wealth reflects AMD and Fortinet stock holdings.
interesting_fact: At QLogic she twice served as acting CEO (May 2013 to February 2014, and August 2015 to August 2016) while also acting as CFO.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as an engineer before finance. She holds a BS in chemical engineering from Beijing University of Chemical Technology and a PhD in economics from Claremont Graduate University.
notes: Corporate CFO, not a founder. Media access goes through AMD corporate communications. She regularly appears at investor conferences and could speak to AI data-center capex and economics.

name: Martha S. Spurlock
current_role: Director, Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. (NASDAQ: CBK) and Commercial Bank (Harrogate, TN); manager, Unified Shares, LLC
profile: Martha Spurlock is a director and roughly 9% beneficial owner of Commercial Bancgroup, the Harrogate, Tennessee parent of Commercial Bank, which listed on Nasdaq in 2025. Her stake is held largely through Unified Shares, LLC, which she has managed since 2014. She has sat on the bank's board since 2016 and the holding company's since 2023.
interesting_fact: Before her bank board career she spent years as a claims service representative at Underwriters Safety & Claims, a workers' compensation insurer, retiring in 2015. She also managed rental properties around Harrogate, Tennessee.

public_contacts.value: ir@cbtn.com (Commercial Bancgroup IR, attn. CFO Philip Metheny)

notes: Private, non-executive shareholder-director of a small Appalachian community bank. No media presence. Weak fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast; reachable only via the company's IR.

name: Juan Maria Garoby
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Vista Energy (NYSE/BMV: VIST); previously COO until Jan 2025
profile: Argentine petroleum/industrial engineer (ITBA) who co-founded Vista Oil & Gas with Miguel Galuccio in 2017 after stints at Baker Hughes, SLB and YPF. As COO he built Vista's Vaca Muerta shale operation at Bajada del Palo, focusing on new drilling and completion technology to cut well costs; since 2025 he is CTO of what is now Argentina's largest independent oil producer.
interesting_fact: Vista claims its Vaca Muerta wells are around 25% more productive than comparable Permian wells - a result of the drilling and completion approach Garoby's team developed.
deep_cut_fact: He met Miguel Galuccio at Buenos Aires' ITBA when both were studying petroleum engineering; after ten years working abroad he returned to Argentina in 2012 to join the management of the newly renationalised YPF under Galuccio.
notes: Technical operator rather than public figure; good guest for Vaca Muerta shale tech. IR is led by co-founder Alejandro Cherñacov.

name: Jason Wilk
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Dave Inc. (Nasdaq: DAVE)
profile: Los Angeles entrepreneur who sold video ad network AllScreen (Y Combinator, Mark Cuban-backed) for a reported $85m in 2015, then founded Dave in 2016 as an overdraft-fee-free banking app. Dave grew past 10 million members, went public via SPAC in January 2022, and he still runs it as CEO.
interesting_fact: He says he took more than 120 VC meetings to fund Dave, which was inspired by his own frustration with overdraft fees; he testified to a Senate Banking subcommittee in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: A Loyola Marymount golfer who once aimed to turn pro, his first venture was golf-equipment site 1DaySports.com, which he sold for $100,000 and used to fund a multi-continent backpacking trip; he also co-founded WriteyBoard, selling stick-on whiteboards to startups.
notes: Founder-CEO with an open, story-driven public persona (fintech/overdraft disruption) - good podcast fit. Media contact Dan Ury per Nov 2026 earnings release.

name: David J Lubar
current_role: President & CEO, Lubar & Co. (Milwaukee); director and 10%+ owner of Hallador Energy (HNRG)
profile: Milwaukee investor who has led Lubar & Co., a family office/private investment firm founded in 1977 that buys middle-market companies for long-term ownership; he joined in 1983 and led investments in 20+ companies. A Hallador Energy director since 2018; also on the Milwaukee Brewers and Baird Funds boards.
interesting_fact: Hallador, where he is a director and major holder, owns Indiana's ~1 GW Merom coal plant and signed a commitment agreement with a global data-center developer in 2025 as it repositions the plant to serve data-center demand.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1977 at Norwest Bank (now Wells Fargo) in Minneapolis, spending six years in commercial and correspondent banking before joining Lubar & Co. in 1983. He holds a BA from Bowdoin College and an MBA from the University of Minnesota.
notes: Strong energy and data-center angle through Hallador and Merom. He is a prominent Milwaukee civic leader (past chair of Froedtert-ThedaCare Health, the Greater Milwaukee Committee and United Way). No published email found; lubar.com blocks scripted access, so check its contact page manually.

name: Robert E Switz
current_role: Retired; former Chairman of Micron Technology (2012-Jan 2025) and Marvell director (2016-June 2025)
profile: Bob Switz was CFO and then Chairman/President/CEO of ADC Telecommunications (CEO 2003-2010) until its sale to Tyco Electronics. He went on to chair Micron's board from 2012 and sat on the boards of Marvell, Broadcom (lead independent director), FireEye/Mandiant, Gigamon and GT Advanced. He left Micron in early 2025 and did not stand for re-election at Marvell in June 2025.
interesting_fact: He chaired Micron's board for over a decade (2012-2025), spanning its rise to become a key supplier of AI-data-center HBM memory.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he did finance roles at Olin (1971-79), AMF (1979-85), PepsiCo and Gulfstar, then was CFO of Tucson chipmaker Burr-Brown (now part of TI), where he oversaw five startup ventures. CFO magazine gave him its CFO Excellence Award in 1999.
notes: Retired from public boards in 2025 (Marvell announcement: https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/99/marvell-announces-changes-to-its-board-of-directors). No personal public contact found; Minnesota-based executive historically. Alive assumed (no obituary found, active through 2025).

name: Gregory M. Shepard
current_role: Private investor; ~6.2% shareholder of Atlas Energy Solutions (NYSE: AESI); former AESI director (appointed Sept 2023)
profile: Florida investor who chaired Union Insurance Group (1985-2004) and was a long-time activist investor in listed insurers. An early backer of Permian frac-sand supplier Atlas Sand (2017), he joined successor Atlas Energy Solutions' board in 2023 and holds ~7.65m shares; recent Form 4s list him as 'Other', not director.
interesting_fact: From 1996 to 2019 he ran activist campaigns at publicly traded subsidiaries of mutual insurers, including Meridian Insurance Group, State Auto Financial, Donegal Group and EMC Insurance Group.
deep_cut_fact: Before backing Atlas, he was sole owner and founder of Wisconsin Northern White Sands Holdings (2014-2019), which explored building frac-sand (proppant) mines in Illinois, Wisconsin, Oklahoma and Texas.
notes: No published contact; SEC filings list counsel Amundsen Davis LLC (Chicago) as authorized to receive notices - not an outreach channel. Dec 2025 he entered a UBS prepaid variable forward on 532,500 AESI shares. Atlas IR is the only corporate route.

name: Steven Sell
current_role: Former President and CEO of agilon health (2020 to Aug 2025); advisor to early-stage healthcare companies. I could not verify a current role.
profile: Steven J. Sell is a managed-care executive. He ran Health Net's Western Region from 2008 to 2016 and was President, CEO and Chairman of Health Net from 2016 to 2019, the period of its sale to Centene. He led value-based primary-care company agilon health from 2020 through its 2021 IPO, then stepped down as CEO and director in August 2025, when co-founder Ron Williams became Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: agilon health, which he led for five years, partners with independent primary-care physician groups to move them into full-risk Medicare Advantage contracts, a model built around doctors rather than insurers.
deep_cut_fact: He is a liberal-arts graduate (B.A. from Swarthmore College) who went on to a Stanford GSB MBA. While running agilon he also advised several early-stage healthcare startups.
notes: He is no longer at agilon, so the agilon press (media@agilonhealth.com) and IR contacts no longer reach him. name: Kim R Cocklin
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Atmos Energy Corporation (NYSE: ATO), Dallas

name: William D. Watkins
current_role: Chairperson of the Board, Nextpower Inc. (formerly Nextracker, NASDAQ: NXT); director (reported chair since 2024) of Flex Ltd.

deep_cut_fact: He earned three degrees at RPI (BS Mech. Eng. 1987, MS Mech. Eng. 1991, MS Mathematics 1992) before a Stanford PhD, and ran the first computer simulations of blood flow in patient-specific models built from medical imaging data.
notes: Academic-founder; HeartFlow is heavy AI/compute user (digital twins). Best route is via UT Austin Oden Institute / Dell Med communications, or HeartFlow media contact (Elliot Levy). Sources differ on his current HeartFlow title (some list CTO/director).

name: Christopher K. Zarins
current_role: Co-founder, HeartFlow, Inc. (Nasdaq: HTFL); Professor Emeritus of Surgery, Stanford University
profile: Latvian-born vascular surgeon (b. 1943) who chaired vascular surgery at the University of Chicago and then Stanford, where he moved in 1993. In 2007 he co-founded HeartFlow with biomedical engineer Charles Taylor to turn coronary CT scans into non-invasive blood-flow (FFR-CT) models; he left full-time faculty in 2010 to focus on the company, now Nasdaq-listed.
interesting_fact: HeartFlow was the first company to come out of Fogarty Innovation, and its FFR-CT technology uses computational fluid dynamics to tell doctors whether a coronary blockage actually restricts blood flow, without a catheter.
deep_cut_fact: With his siblings he founded the Honorary Foundation of Richard Zarins (2013), named for their Lutheran-pastor father, which has given $105,000+ to the University of Latvia for scholarships and books on 20th-century Latvian history; he fled Latvia as an infant in 1944 via Sweden.
notes: Age ~82; academic, publishes widely (350+ papers). Also on the board of the Latvian Medical Foundation. HeartFlow contacts are the company's named IR (Nick Laudico) and media (Elliot Levy) leads from Nov 2026 release. Bio: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Zarins

name: Peter Lipka
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Improbable (London) — last confirmed Oct 2025; an unverified 2026 directory lists him as CEO of Somnia
profile: Imperial College computing graduate (first-class MEng, 2011) who worked at Goldman Sachs before co-founding London virtual-worlds company Improbable in 2012 with Herman Narula and Rob Whitehead. He led its fabric, engineering and commercial teams before becoming COO; Improbable raised $502M led by SoftBank in 2017 and has since pivoted to a venture-builder model in web3, AI and the metaverse (incl. the Somnia blockchain).
interesting_fact: Improbable's 2017 SoftBank-led $502M round valued it at over $1B just five years after founding; it later spun out ventures such as Somnia, whose token reached a ~$1B valuation.
deep_cut_fact: For his Imperial final-year project (supervised by Prof. Andrew Davison of the Dyson Robotics Lab) he built an AI program that learned to understand and play a video game from screen pixels alone — years before DeepMind's Atari work made that famous.
notes: Current title uncertain (COO of Improbable vs. Somnia role) — verify before outreach. Note: the DeepMind comparison in deep_cut is editorial framing; the sourced fact is the pixels-to-gameplay project. Web search budget ran out before a press email could be found.

current_role: Co-founder, Improbable (leads new venture creation); CEO of Improbable spin-out MSquared
profile: Rob Whitehead co-founded London-based Improbable in 2012 with Cambridge computer-science classmate Herman Narula. They built SpatialOS, a cloud platform for massive simulations and multiplayer games, which drew a $502M SoftBank-led investment. Improbable has since become an AI/web3 venture builder, and Whitehead leads MSquared, its metaverse-interoperability network.

public_contacts.value: UKTN podcast appearance: 'What has become of the metaverse' (Aug 2025)

name: Moshe Yanai
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Infinidat (stepped down as CEO 2020; Infinidat agreed to be acquired by Lenovo in 2025); storage-industry inventor
profile: Israeli electrical engineer (b. 1949, Technion 1975) and one of enterprise storage's legends: he led development of EMC's Symmetrix from the late 1980s to 2001, then founded XIV (sold to IBM in 2008 for ~$300m) and in 2011 Infinidat, which reached unicorn status after a TPG-led $150m round in 2015. He is an EMC Fellow, IBM Fellow and holds ~40 US storage patents.
interesting_fact: The Symmetrix remote replication (SRDF) his team built was called 'the true hero of 9/11' by Barron's, because it kept NYSE and bank data intact after the attacks - EMC had 25 customers in the World Trade Center.
deep_cut_fact: He is a licensed helicopter pilot - in 2010 TheMarker reported his 'new job' was flying businessmen by helicopter; he also won the 2010 IEEE Reynold B. Johnson Information Storage Systems Award.
notes: No longer runs Infinidat; no published personal contact found. Blocks and Files (Jan 2026) reported personal insolvency proceedings in Tel Aviv - Hurun 'unicorn founder' wealth is likely outdated; be sensitive. Former IDF tank commander per storage press.

name: David Elkington
current_role: Founder & CEO, Atonom (AI 'Cloud Employees' for sales, support, marketing and HR), Silicon Slopes, Utah
profile: Utah entrepreneur who founded InsideSales.com in 2004 (rebranded XANT, later back to InsideSales), an AI sales-acceleration platform that raised nearly $400M from backers incl. Salesforce and Microsoft, reached a ~$2B valuation and 1,000+ staff. He now runs Atonom, building autonomous AI agents that do full jobs, and is a co-founder of the Silicon Slopes tech community.
interesting_fact: InsideSales' 'Neuralytics' self-learning engine had analysed more than 80 billion sales interactions by 2016, the year he was named one of Utah's top 10 entrepreneurs in the Peak 100 awards.

notes: Accessible, public-facing founder who keynotes Utah events (Silicon Slopes STACKED, Aug 2026); Atonom PR contact is Pete Ketchum via the EIN Presswire release form. X/LinkedIn listed are Atonom company accounts, not personal. Good AI-agents angle.

current_role: Chairperson and CEO of JUSDA; Chief Logistics and Trade Compliance Officer and Global Chief Campus Operation Officer, Hon Hai (Foxconn); rotating group CEO Apr 2025-Mar 2026

name: Gerald Blackie
current_role: Former CEO and co-founder of Kaseya; later launched Pilixo (MSP remote-control software), reportedly in a chairman role. No current role confirmed.
profile: Gerald Blackie became CEO of Kaseya in 2003, merging in his own startup. Kaseya, founded in 2000 by Mark Sutherland and Paul Wong, created the remote-monitoring and management category for managed service providers (MSPs). Kaseya counts him as a founder. He left after Insight Venture Partners took control in June 2013 and named Yogesh Gupta CEO; he then launched Pilixo.

Kaseya's VSA remote monitoring platform became core infrastructure for thousands of IT service providers, and the company later became a multi-billion-dollar business under Insight.

name: Wang Yulin
current_role: Former founding president/CEO of Kingsoft Cloud (Nasdaq: KC; HKEX: 3896), stepped down in 2022; current role not found
profile: Wang Yulin (王育林) built Kingsoft Cloud within Lei Jun's Kingsoft group from 2012, growing it into one of China's largest independent cloud providers. name: Paolo Cerruti
current_role: Northvolt co-founder; stepped down as CEO of Northvolt North America in Jan 2025 (stayed chairman of the Canadian entity); current main role not publicly confirmed

current_role: Co-founder and chairman, Aris Machina AB (agentic AI operating system for manufacturing, Sweden); former co-founder and CEO of Northvolt
profile: Swedish supply-chain executive (CPO at Sony Ericsson, NXP and Tesla) who co-founded Northvolt in 2016 to build Europe's largest lithium-ion battery factory, raising billions (Hurun valued it at ~$20B). He stepped down as CEO in Nov 2024 when Northvolt entered restructuring. In 2025 he co-founded Aris Machina with Northvolt's former AI lead Siddharth Khullar.

Aris Machina's general contact is a sales inbox. A sodium-ion venture (Sonder Labs) is also linked to him in Swedish press (unverified).

name: Daisuke Okanohara
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Preferred Networks, Inc. (since Nov 2025); CEO, Matlantis Inc.
profile: University of Tokyo computer-science PhD (2010) who co-founded Preferred Infrastructure as a grad student in 2006 and Preferred Networks (PFN) in 2014 with Toru Nishikawa. As CTO he led generative AI, the PLaMo LLM and Matlantis atomistic simulator; became CEO in Nov 2025. PFN builds the full stack from apps and models down to its own MN-Core AI chips, and agreed a capital alliance with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries in 2026.

notes: Excellent fit for data-center/AI-chip angle (energy-efficient AI chips, sovereign Japanese AI stack). Contact form is PFN's official Media/PR inquiry form (also handles speaker requests). Active on X (@hillbig), mostly in Japanese.

name: Toru Nishikawa
current_role: Co-Founder and Chairman, Preferred Networks Inc. (PFN), Tokyo (Daisuke Okanohara is now CEO)
profile: Toru Nishikawa co-founded Preferred Infrastructure (2006) and then Preferred Networks (2014) with Daisuke Okanohara. PFN is one of Japan's most valuable AI startups, working on deep learning, its own MN-Core AI accelerator chips and supercomputers, and LLMs (PLaMo), with partners such as Toyota, Fanuc and Mitsubishi. He led PFN as president/CEO and is now its chairman.

name: Louay Eldada
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Quanergy Systems (stepped down Jan 2020); current role not publicly confirmed
profile: Louay Eldada, a Columbia electrical-engineering PhD, is a photonics and solar technologist. He built telecom photonics at Honeywell/AlliedSignal, founded Telephotonics (bought by DuPont), was CTO at thin-film solar maker HelioVolt and chief science officer at SunEdison, then co-founded lidar company Quanergy in 2012, which was valued around $2B. He left Quanergy in 2020.

By then he had published 170+ technical papers, filed 39 patents and won 43 technical awards, starting at Honeywell, where he launched the Telecom Photonics unit later acquired by Corning.

ReNew is one of India's largest clean-energy firms (solar, wind, storage, manufacturing, green hydrogen; ~28 GW pipeline). name: Bradley Keywell
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Gigawatt AI (AI-native operating system for energy and water utilities); director, TKO Group

Founding investor in Tempus AI. In Aug 2025 he founded Gigawatt AI to build AI software for utilities.

name: Dmitri Gaskin
current_role: Co-founder, Branch (Branch Metrics, mobile deep-linking); current title unclear — previously Head of Engineering
profile: Dmitri Gaskin co-founded Branch in 2014 with Alex Austin, Mada Seghete and Mike Molinet at age 19, building the deep-linking platform that routes users to specific pages inside mobile apps; Branch reached a ~$4B valuation in 2022.
