name: Nugroho Herucahyono
current_role: Co-founder, Init6 (early-stage venture fund, Indonesia); former co-founder and CTO, Bukalapak
profile: Indonesian engineer who co-founded e-commerce marketplace Bukalapak in 2010 with Achmad Zaky (later joined by Fajrin Rasyid) and served as its CTO. He stepped down around Zaky's late-2019/2020 exit and the two founded Init6 to back early-stage start-ups. Bukalapak later raised up to US$1.5B in Indonesia's then-largest IPO (2021).
interesting_fact: Bukalapak ('open a market stall') was built to digitise small Indonesian merchants and in its early days rode the fixie-bike craze, becoming known for a time as a bike marketplace.
notes: Low public profile; no verified personal site or published contact found. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so research is thinner than ideal; best route likely via Init6 or Achmad Zaky's network. Current Init6 role not independently confirmed beyond Wikipedia.

name: Nevada Sanchez
current_role: EVP of Engineering, Science Corporation (since July 2026); co-founder, Butterfly Network
profile: Nevada Sanchez co-founded Butterfly Network with Jonathan Rothberg in 2011 and helped develop its ultrasound-on-a-chip, the basis of the handheld Butterfly iQ whole-body scanner. He spent about 15 years there, most recently as SVP and Chief Innovation Officer. In July 2026 he joined Max Hodak's brain-computer-interface company Science Corp. to lead engineering.
interesting_fact: Butterfly's chips integrate about 9,000 silicon ultrasound transducers, each not much bigger than the tip of a human hair, which turns a phone into a whole-body imaging device.
deep_cut_fact: At 22, as a 2011 Hertz Fellow, he deferred his PhD to join Rothberg. Rothberg had asked MIT physicist Max Tegmark for his most brilliant students, and Sanchez had been working in Tegmark's lab. He holds three MIT degrees (EECS S.B., Math S.B., EECS M.Eng.).
notes: Recently moved from Butterfly to Science Corp. (neurotech), so this is a good angle for a deep-tech conversation. The Hertz Foundation is also a possible warm route.

name: Patricia House
current_role: Cofounder of C3 AI and Siebel Systems; Chairman, Mary Mae Foundation (left the C3 AI board in Feb 2023)
profile: Pat House cofounded Siebel Systems with Tom Siebel in the 1990s, building it into a ~$2B-revenue CRM pioneer and serving as Vice Chairman and EVP until the 2006 Oracle merger. She then cofounded C3.ai (enterprise AI) and was its board Vice Chairman from 2009 until resigning in February 2023. Her wealth comes mainly from her C3 AI stake.
interesting_fact: Before Siebel she held managerial and executive roles at Verbatim, Oracle and Frame Technology. Fortune named her one of its 50 Most Powerful Women.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as a teacher, with a BA in Education from Western Michigan University, and chairs the Mary Mae Foundation, a nonprofit that provides affordable housing for teachers.
notes: Her C3 AI board resignation (Feb 24, 2023) is documented in an 8-K: https://sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1577526/000162828023006047/ai-20230224.htm. She has served on the Hewlett Foundation and Carnegie Endowment boards. No published personal or office contact found; low public profile since leaving C3.

name: Adrian Merino
current_role: Early team member / co-founder-listed at Cabify (Madrid); current role not verified
profile: Spanish tech entrepreneur listed among Cabify's founders. Cabify was started in Madrid in May 2011 by Juan de Antonio; Adrián Merino joined the founding team in its first months alongside CTO Samuel Lown and Michael Koper. Cabify became Spain's first unicorn, operating ride-hailing across Spain and Latin America.
interesting_fact: Cabify's first service, called 'Executive', used only high-end cars priced slightly above taxis; by February 2012 it had 20,000 users and nearly 3,000 rides in Madrid.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Cabify in about September 2011, two months after CTO Samuel Lown, when the company was only a few months old.
notes: Identity marked 'uncertain' only because his exact title and current activity could not be confirmed. A web-search budget limit cut research short. Cabify's sole formal founder per Wikipedia is Juan de Antonio; Merino is an early team member often listed as co-founder.

name: Francisco Montero
current_role: Co-founder, Cabify (Maxi Mobility); last publicly listed as Global Head of Settings / Global Ops (current role unverified)
profile: Francisco 'Paco' Montero is one of five co-founders of Madrid-based ride-hailing company Cabify (with Juan de Antonio, Vicente Pascual, Sam Lown and Adrian Merino), founded in 2011 and later valued at over $1B under parent Maxi Mobility. He worked across marketing, operations and 'excellence' functions and played a key role in Cabify's expansion into Latin America.
interesting_fact: Cabify founder Juan de Antonio gave the co-founder title to everyone who was there at the start of the company; Montero helped lead its early push into Latin America, which became Cabify's main market.
notes: Very low public profile; only brief mentions in Spanish press and Wellfound. No current role or contact verified. Route via Cabify press office if needed.

name: Dave Baxter
current_role: Co-founder and VP Hardware Engineering, ChargePoint (per company leadership page; current status not re-verified)
profile: Dave Baxter co-founded Coulomb Technologies in 2007 in Campbell, California, alongside Richard Lowenthal, Harjinder Bhade and others; it became ChargePoint, one of the largest EV-charging networks, and went public via SPAC in 2021. He has led hardware engineering for the charging stations and is a named inventor on many Coulomb/ChargePoint patents.
interesting_fact: ChargePoint started in 2007 as Coulomb Technologies, years before mass-market EVs, betting on networked public charging stations.
deep_cut_fact: A Cornell engineering grad, before ChargePoint he was VP of Engineering at Jetstream Communications, where he led work on an early carrier-grade voice-over-DSL system, after engineering roles at 3Com and Adept Technology.
notes: Low-profile engineer co-founder; no personal socials found. Deep-cut source is Crunchbase (summarised via search, page paywalled) so verify before use. ChargePoint leadership page (https://www-aws.chargepoint.com/at-de/node/2548) lists him but is undated.

name: Harjinder S. Bhade
current_role: Chief Technology Officer, Blink Charging (Nasdaq: BLNK) (appointed April 2021; still listed on Blink's site)
profile: Silicon Valley networking engineer who co-founded Coulomb Technologies (now ChargePoint) in 2007 with Richard Lowenthal and Dave Baxter, serving as VP of Software Engineering and helping develop the IP behind networked EV charging. He then spent 6+ years as CTO/SVP Engineering at ENGIE Storage (built its GridSynergy battery-storage platform) before joining Blink as CTO.
interesting_fact: He is credited with helping create the intellectual property behind networked EV charging infrastructure at ChargePoint, now one of the world's largest charging networks.
deep_cut_fact: At ENGIE Storage (formerly Green Charge Networks) he built the GridSynergy behind-the-meter battery storage software platform from the ground up, and he is named inventor on roughly 28 US patents from his ChargePoint/Coulomb days.
notes: Patent count from patentleaderboard.com (https://www.patentleaderboard.com/chargepoint/harjinder-bhade/225012). Gave a 2024 interview to Renewable Energy World on EV charging infrastructure - useful hook. Hurun unicorn-founder listing; personal wealth not disclosed. Current 2026 role not re-confirmed via filings.

name: Milton T. Tormey
current_role: Co-founder of ChargePoint (founded 2007 as Coulomb Technologies); current role not publicly documented
profile: Milton 'Tom' Tormey is one of five co-founders (with Richard Lowenthal, Harjinder Bhade, Praveen Mandal and Dave Baxter) of Coulomb Technologies, launched in 2007 in Campbell, California, to build networked EV charging before many EVs were on the road. Renamed ChargePoint, it became one of the largest EV charging networks and went public via SPAC in 2021.
interesting_fact: Stanford GSB's ChargePoint case credits the five founders with seeing the need for an expansive charging network 'even before many electric vehicles were on the road'; early backers included Voyager Capital and Rho Ventures.
deep_cut_fact: He is a named inventor on ChargePoint's networked-charging patents, including 'Authorization in a networked electric vehicle charging system' (US 12,068,620, issued Aug 2024), and an early Coulomb patent on a self-powered charging-connector locking system.
notes: Lesser-known co-founder (Wikipedia lists only three founders). Very low public profile; no interviews, website or social accounts found. ChargePoint's public face is co-founder Richard Lowenthal.

name: Praveen Mandal
current_role: Senior Founding Connection Science Fellow, MIT Connection Science; fractional CTO to startups (CTO of NovaCHARGE from June 2022)
profile: Praveen K. Mandal co-founded Coulomb Technologies in 2007, which became EV-charging network ChargePoint (NYSE: CHPT, listed 2021), and served as its president until about 2011. A veteran of seven start-ups, he also founded Pipal Systems (sold to Riverstone Networks) and data-science firm 2predict (sold to Volta Charging), was Volta's CTO from 2019, and joined NovaCHARGE as CTO in 2022.
interesting_fact: He is credited with inventing the networked charging-station concept: he put a processor with a CDMA cell-phone chipset inside a charger and linked it to a client-server back end. That enabled the driver notifications, reservations and billing found on almost all chargers today.
deep_cut_fact: He calls himself 'an R&D guy' and says 'I'm all about cross-bubble pollination', meaning progress comes from stepping out of your professional bubble. He is co-inventor on 10 patents, holds a BSCE from Santa Clara University, and earlier was VP of R&D for Carrier Ethernet at Lucent and SVP/GM of SGI's Emerging Technologies Group.

public_contacts.value: connectionscience@mit.edu (MIT Connection Science group contact, not personal)

notes: Strong fit for an EV/energy-infrastructure episode. Current day job unclear: MIT page says fractional CTO to startups, and an unverified me.sh profile lists Chief Product & Technology Officer at Phorum.AI. Not shown as a current ChargePoint insider. No personal verified social account confirmed; LinkedIn is likely the best route but wasn't verified here.

name: Richard Lowenthal
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of ChargePoint (founded as Coulomb Technologies); former ChargePoint director - current role not verified
profile: Co-founded Coulomb Technologies in 2007 with Dave Baxter and Harjinder Bhade and led it as CEO; Coulomb's 'ChargePoint Network' of smart public charging stations became ChargePoint, one of the largest EV-charging networks, which went public via SPAC in 2021 (NYSE: CHPT). He remained on the board and as a shareholder through the 2021 listing.
interesting_fact: In 2010, as Coulomb's CEO, he won a federal stimulus-backed program to give away free home and public chargers - about 11,200 across nine U.S. regions - to seed EV adoption.
deep_cut_fact: Coulomb's very first chargers (July 2008, from an office in Campbell, CA) were called 'Smartlets' and used 802.15.4 mesh wireless; his launch pitch was that the U.S. had 247M cars but only 54M garages, so most drivers would need public charging.
notes: No longer appears to be a ChargePoint officer/director, so the company press team is an indirect route; I couldn't verify a personal site or social accounts (web-search quota exhausted). He is widely reported to be a former Cupertino mayor, but I couldn't source it. Good EV-infrastructure/grid founder story.

name: Lee Holloway
current_role: Cloudflare cofounder and original lead engineer; no longer with the company (left in 2015)
profile: Lee Holloway cofounded Cloudflare on July 26, 2009 with Matthew Prince and Michelle Zatlyn and was its original technical lead, building much of the early network that became one of the internet's largest edge/CDN and security platforms (NYSE: NET, IPO 2019). He stepped away from the company in 2015.
interesting_fact: Before Cloudflare, Holloway and Matthew Prince collaborated on Project Honey Pot, an anti-spam effort by Unspam Technologies that partly inspired the idea for Cloudflare.
notes: Do not approach: he left Cloudflare in 2015 because of a serious illness that was widely reported (Wired, 2020) and is not a viable interview subject; current status not verified. For the Cloudflare story, approach Matthew Prince or Michelle Zatlyn instead.

name: Kris Gale
current_role: Co-founder of Clover Health (left the company in 2017); current role not verified
profile: Kris Gale co-founded Clover Health, a data- and software-driven Medicare Advantage insurer, with Vivek Garipalli in 2014, leading its technology side. He left in 2017; Clover later went public via a SPAC in 2021.
interesting_fact: Clover's pitch was to use data analytics and software to spot health risks early and cut costs for Medicare Advantage members, including a home-based primary-care program for homebound members launched in 2017.
notes: Left Clover nearly a decade ago; no verified current role, website or social accounts found, and the web search budget ran out before more could be checked. 'Artificial Intelligence' industry tag is loose (health-insurance tech). Low priority for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Vivek Garipalli
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairperson, Clover Health (Nasdaq: CLOV); runs family-office investment arm Wormhole Capital
profile: Vivek Garipalli (47) co-founded Medicare Advantage insurer Clover Health in 2014 and was CEO until Dec 2022, taking it public via SPAC in 2021; he has been Executive Chair since Jan 2023. Earlier he co-founded New Jersey hospital system CarePoint Health and Ensemble Health, and after finance roles at CSFB, J.P. Morgan Partners and Blackstone became an early backer of Flatiron Health.
interesting_fact: Clover pitches itself as a tech company first: its in-house clinical software gives doctors data-driven prompts at the point of care, e.g. for earlier detection of diabetes and chronic kidney disease.
deep_cut_fact: He was an early investor in Flatiron Health, advised on its business model, led its acquisition of the Altos data platform and sat on its board from 2012 until Roche bought it in 2018; he holds a BBA in entrepreneurship from Emory.
notes: Input tag 'Artificial Intelligence' reflects Clover's AI-assisted care software; weak fit for an energy/data-centre podcast unless angled on healthcare AI. Route via Clover press inbox.

He led the company as CEO as it built an automated machine-learning ('AutoML') platform and reached a ~$6B valuation (Hurun unicorn list 2019-2024), before Dan Wright took over as CEO around 2020. name: Solomon Hykes
current_role: Co-founder of Dagger (dagger.io), a programmable CI/CD and AI-agent workflow engine; Docker founder
profile: New York-born, France-raised engineer (b. 1983) who co-founded dotCloud in Paris in 2008, went through Y Combinator in 2010, and open-sourced Docker in 2013, popularising Linux containers that now underpin cloud and data-center software. He left Docker's CTO role in 2018 and launched Dagger in 2022.
interesting_fact: Docker was first shown publicly in a roughly five-minute lightning talk, 'The future of Linux Containers', at PyCon 2013 in Santa Clara, and was open-sourced that same month.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to France at age 4, entered the Epitech coding school in 2001, started his career in 2006 at an IT-security firm, and in 2008 set up dotCloud as a small SARL in Montrouge with fellow Epitech alum Sébastien Pahl. His story was cited around François Hollande's 2014 Silicon Valley 'brain drain' visit.
notes: Approachable, active in open-source communities and on conference stages (KubeCon keynote, Dagger blog demos). His personal X handle is widely known as @solomonstre but I could not verify it from an official page here; company X/Discord are verified. Docker 'valued $2B' refers to Hurun unicorn list.

name: Wu Jingzhuan
current_role: CEO (co-founder), Dtdream / Hangzhou Dtdream Technology (数梦工场), per 36Kr company profile; current status not re-confirmed
profile: Wu Jingchuan (吴敬传; Hurun romanises as 'Wu Jingzhuan') is a veteran Chinese networking executive: ~7 years at Huawei, then a founding executive of H3C, where she became CEO in 2012 before leaving in Feb 2015. She is listed as CEO of Dtdream, the Hangzhou digital-government cloud/data platform company set up in 2015 by ex-H3C staff with Alibaba ties.
interesting_fact: Dtdream was founded in March 2015 in Hangzhou's Yunqi (Cloud Town) by a team of ex-H3C executives led by Wang Wei, shortly after the H3C leadership exodus; it focuses on 'digital government' platforms, e.g. Zhejiang's 'run at most once' reform.
deep_cut_fact: In China's IT industry she was nicknamed the 'Iron Lady' (铁娘子); before taking over as H3C CEO from Zheng Shusheng in 2012 she ran H3C's global marketing, sales and channels, and at Huawei had been VP of domestic marketing and head of datacom marketing.
notes: Chinese name 吴敬传 (Wu Jingchuan). 36Kr PitchHub (https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1678465091859458) lists her as Dtdream CEO and Wang Wei (王巍) as founder; no 2024-26 news found confirming she is still CEO. dtdream.com was unreachable from this session, so no published press contact captured. Low public profile; approach via Dtdream corporate channels.

name: Zhai Xuehun
current_role: Founder & CEO, G7 E6 (G7易流; formed from the 2022 merger of G7 and E6/易流), Beijing
profile: Zhai Xuehun (翟学魂), a Tsinghua physics graduate, founded G7 around 2010 to put IoT devices and a SaaS platform into Chinese truck fleets; by 2018 it had raised 500M+ USD and connected 800k+ vehicles. After merging with E6 it became G7易流, a digital-logistics/IoT platform serving tens of thousands of SME carriers, now pushing hard into logistics AI.
interesting_fact: In April 2018 G7 co-founded an autonomous-trucking company together with NIO Capital and GLP (Inceptio Technology), as Zhai pursued his vision of logistics becoming a self-operating, algorithm-driven industry.
deep_cut_fact: Despite running a 'dirty, hard work' logistics business, he studied physics at Tsinghua and has said he still regrets not pursuing theoretical physics; on stage he introduces himself simply as 'G7's Lao Zhai' (老翟). In 2017 he set a target of one logistics manager per 50 trucks, vs. the industry's 1:5.
notes: Chinese name 翟学魂. Frequently speaks at TMTPost ITValue / T-EDGE and G7's annual Digital Logistics Conference (2025 launch of logistics AI hardware; 2026 talk on token usage) - conference/media route is the most realistic. g7.com.cn was unreachable from this session so no published press email captured. 36Kr interview: https://www.36kr.com/p/1721664929793

profile: Hurun's unicorn index names 崔晶晶 (Cui Jingjing) as founder of GEO (集奥聚合, Beijing GeoTMT Co.), founded around 2011-12. name: Monish Darda
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Mentor (board member), Icertis
profile: Pune/Seattle-based enterprise-software entrepreneur who co-founded contract-lifecycle-management company Icertis with Samir Bodas in 2009 after launching BladeLogic's India R&D operation (BladeLogic was acquired by BMC). As long-time CTO he built the Icertis Contract Intelligence platform used by Airbus, Daimler, J&J, Microsoft and Sanofi; he now serves as Co-founder & Chief Mentor while Jim Moffatt and Rajat Bahri are co-CEOs.
interesting_fact: He led Icertis's AI and blockchain work, which landed the company on Forbes' AI 50 list two years running, and he is co-inventor on two patents in cloud resource management and provisioning.
deep_cut_fact: He is an avid PlayStation 4 gamer (especially Call of Duty: Warzone), a Formula 1 fan and an Isaac Asimov science-fiction reader; he trained as a mechanical engineer and earned a master's from Florida Atlantic University.
notes: No longer CTO/operational lead; title is Chief Mentor. LinkedIn is linked from his official company bio. Wikipedia's Icertis article is outdated (lists Bodas as CEO).

name: Samir Bodas
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO, Icertis (current role unconfirmed; Icertis now led by interim co-CEOs, Jim Moffatt chairs the board)
profile: Former CEO of Indian IT-services firm Aztecsoft who co-founded Icertis in 2009 (Pune roots, Bellevue, WA HQ) and built it into a leading AI-powered contract lifecycle management platform valued around $5B. Anand Subbaraman joined in 2024 and later led the company; in July 2026 Icertis appointed interim co-CEOs and a new board chair.
interesting_fact: Icertis grew from a Pune-based startup into a top-ranked enterprise contract-intelligence vendor whose customers include Microsoft and Accenture; its board's lead independent director is Penny Pritzker.

profile: Guilherme Bonifácio is one of four co-founders of iFood (2011), Brazil's dominant food-delivery app, which grew out of the phone-and-fax ordering service Disk Cook. He later ran sister company Rapiddo, was the last founder to sell his iFood stake, and has since co-founded neighbourhood-commerce startup Mercê do Bairro and invests in pre-seed/seed startups.

current_role: Co-founder (former CTO), Illumio — current role not confirmed; no longer listed on Illumio's leadership page
profile: Silicon Valley engineer who co-founded zero-trust segmentation company Illumio in 2013 with CEO Andrew Rubin, serving as its founding CTO. Illumio (Sunnyvale) raised ~$558M, including a $225M Thoma Bravo-led Series F at a $2.75B valuation in 2021, and now sells breach-containment products (Illumio Segmentation, Illumio Insights).

name: Abhay Singhal
current_role: Co-Founder, InMobi & CEO, InMobi Advertising
profile: IIT Kanpur graduate Abhay Singhal co-founded InMobi in 2007 with Naveen Tewari, Mohit Saxena and Amit Gupta. It started as the SMS search engine mKhoj, pivoted to mobile advertising, and in 2011 became India's first unicorn. He now runs InMobi Advertising from the San Francisco Bay Area; the platform reaches over 1.3B people in 190+ countries.
interesting_fact: InMobi began in 2007 as mKhoj ('mobile khoj', Hindi for search), an SMS search service run from a residential apartment in Bangalore. It was renamed partly because 'InMobi' was easier to pronounce outside India.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming CEO of InMobi Advertising and Chief Revenue Officer, he served as InMobi's Head of Human Resources, an unusual stint for a technical co-founder. He made the Economic Times 40 Under Forty list in 2018.
notes: He is based in the SF Bay Area. Mobile ad-tech, with InMobi's sister company Glance, is a possible data/AI angle. For press, use InMobi's press page (https://www.inmobi.com/press).

name: Mohit Saxena
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, InMobi (Bengaluru/Singapore)
profile: Indian technologist who co-founded mKhoj in 2007 with Naveen Tewari, Amit Gupta and Abhay Singhal; it began as an SMS-based search engine, pivoted to mobile advertising and rebranded as InMobi in 2008. InMobi became India's first unicorn in 2011 and also spawned the lock-screen content platform Glance. Saxena remains InMobi's CTO.

name: James Hom
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Product Officer and Interim CFO, SoundHound AI (Nasdaq: SOUN)
profile: Stanford computer-science graduate who cofounded voice-AI company SoundHound (whose first product was the Midomi music-search app) in 2005 with Keyvan Mohajer and Majid Emami. As CPO he leads product development for the SoundHound AI platform, SoundHound services and consumer apps reaching hundreds of millions of users; the company listed via SPAC in 2022.
interesting_fact: SoundHound's voice-AI platform powers voice assistants in cars, TVs and restaurant ordering systems; Hom's products reach hundreds of millions of end users.

name: Keyvan Mohajer
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SoundHound AI (Nasdaq: SOUN)
profile: Iranian-born, Canada-raised engineer with a Stanford PhD in electrical engineering who co-founded SoundHound in 2005 from his Stanford dorm. Known first for its music-recognition app, SoundHound now sells voice and agentic AI to carmakers, restaurants (e.g. Five Guys), insurers and telcos, and went public via SPAC in 2022.
interesting_fact: SoundHound was started in a Stanford dorm room and Mohajer has described it as an 18-year road to a billion-dollar voice-assistant business, built on proprietary speech tech rather than licensed models.
deep_cut_fact: He immigrated to Canada as a teenager without fluent English yet aimed to finish top of his high-school class, and had already started three companies by the time he was in college - all inspired by a childhood love of science fiction and talking computers.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (Voicebot, Fox News Radio, Stratospheric Leaders), so receptive to audio interviews. PR email appears in 2026 press releases (IR site blocked direct fetch here; confirmed via search snippet). Edge-AI/on-device angle (NVIDIA GTC 2026).

name: Majid Emami
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Science Officer and SVP Engineering, SoundHound AI (Nasdaq: SOUN)
profile: Majid Emami co-founded SoundHound in 2005 with Keyvan Mohajer and James Hom; the three met in Stanford's electrical-engineering PhD programme. He was VP of Engineering from the founding and became Chief Science Officer and SVP Engineering in 2022. SoundHound, known for its music-recognition app and the Houndify voice-AI platform, now sells voice and agentic AI to carmakers, restaurants and enterprises.
interesting_fact: SoundHound's voice-AI origins go back to a project he and his co-founders started as Stanford EE doctoral students. Its technology now ranges from in-car voice commerce (CES 2026) to restaurant ordering agents.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a Stanford PhD in electrical engineering and is named on 16 patents in voice AI, per SoundHound's investor-relations biography.
notes: A technical, low-profile co-founder; CEO Keyvan Mohajer is the public face. Some sources say his undergraduate degree is from the University of Toronto, but I couldn't verify this. The Hurun listing is as a unicorn founder; SoundHound is now public. A good angle is on-device and edge voice AI versus data-centre inference.

name: Josh Luber
current_role: Co-founder, StockX; co-founder (Chief Vision Officer) of Fanatics Collectibles. 2026 status not re-verified
profile: Philadelphia-born Josh Luber turned his sneaker-data side project Campless into StockX, the 'stock market for things' resale platform. He co-founded it in Detroit in 2015-16 with Dan Gilbert, Greg Schwartz and Chris Kaufman, and it later reached a roughly $4B valuation. He stepped down as CEO in 2019, then co-founded Fanatics Collectibles with Michael Rubin, securing trading-card rights from MLB, NBA and NFLPA and overseeing the purchase of Topps.
interesting_fact: He gave a 2015 TED Talk, 'Why sneakers are a great investment', on the data behind the sneaker resale market, years before StockX became a unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He started Campless, a sneakerhead-data company, while working as an IBM consultant. Before that he briefly practiced as a bankruptcy attorney (he holds a BA, MBA and JD from Emory) and had founded and run three earlier startups.
notes: No personally published contact was verified, and the search budget ran out before his current (2026) role could be checked. Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Luber. The TED bio links @Campless, a legacy account.

name: Jonathan Neman
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Sweetgreen, Inc. (NYSE: SG), Los Angeles
profile: Co-founded Sweetgreen in November 2006 with Georgetown classmates Nicolas Jammet and Nathaniel Ru, opening the first salad shop in Washington, D.C. in August 2007, three months after graduating from Georgetown's McDonough School of Business. As CEO he moved HQ to Los Angeles (2016), took the chain public in November 2021 and pushed restaurant automation via the 2021 acquisition of robotics startup Spyce (the 'Infinite Kitchen').
interesting_fact: Sweetgreen bought MIT-founded robotic-kitchen startup Spyce in 2021 and has been rolling out automated 'Infinite Kitchen' restaurants, an unusual bet on robotics for a salad chain.
deep_cut_fact: From 2011 to 2016 Sweetgreen ran its own music and food festival, Sweetlife, at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Maryland; headliners included The Strokes (2011) and Avicii and Kid Cudi (2012).
notes: Confirmed still CEO in an Aug 2026 SEC 8-K. Active on LinkedIn and does frequent founder interviews, so a good entrepreneurship guest; route through press@sweetgreen.com.

name: Nathaniel Ru
current_role: Co-founder and Board Director, Sweetgreen, Inc. (NYSE: SG); retired as Chief Brand Officer effective January 1, 2026
profile: Co-founded salad chain Sweetgreen with Georgetown classmates Jonathan Neman and Nicolas Jammet, opening the first store in 2007; it grew to 280+ restaurants and listed on the NYSE in 2021. As Chief Brand Officer for ~20 years he led campaigns, collaborations and school programs; he retired from the role in January 2026 but remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Ru led Sweetgreen's sweetlife music and food festival and was named one of Fast Company's Most Creative People in Business and to Forbes' Next 50 CMOs list.
deep_cut_fact: Sweetgreen's first store, opened in August 2007 within three months of the founders' Georgetown graduation, was a tiny ~560-square-foot space on M Street; Ru also ran 'sweetgreen in schools' healthy-food education programs.
notes: Now has more free time after stepping back as CBO in Jan 2026; avoid the stock-decline framing some coverage used. Route via Sweetgreen press.

name: Cristina Fonseca
current_role: Co-founder of Talkdesk (left operations 2016); last confirmed role Head of AI at Zendesk (2023); also linked to Lisbon VC Indico Capital Partners (venture partner from 2018)
profile: Portuguese engineer (Instituto Superior Tecnico) who co-founded call-centre software firm Talkdesk with Tiago Paiva in 2011; it became one of Portugal's first unicorns and was later valued at $10bn. She left day-to-day work in 2016, co-founded AI customer-service startup Cleverly (acquired by Zendesk in 2021) and became Zendesk's Head of AI; she is also an angel/VC investor.
interesting_fact: Talkdesk began in 2011 when she and Tiago Paiva built the first version of the product for a developer contest run by Twilio.
deep_cut_fact: Despite co-founding a $10bn company, she has said 'Zendesk was my first corporate job, so I've always been biased towards startups' - Zendesk came to her via its 2021 acquisition of her second startup, Cleverly.
notes: Current (2025-26) role not confirmed; check LinkedIn before outreach. Frequent conference speaker (Web Summit, MWC, SaaStock) - event organisers are a viable route. Forbes 30 Under 30 (2016) per Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristina_Fonseca. Indico Capital press contact (press@indicocapital.com) exists but her current affiliation there is unverified.

name: Tiago Paiva
current_role: Founder & CEO, Talkdesk (AI-powered cloud contact-center software, San Francisco/Lisbon)
profile: Portuguese engineer who built the first Talkdesk prototype in 10 days in 2011 for a Twilio hackathon, won TwilioCon, joined 500 Startups' third batch and moved to the US. He grew Talkdesk into a contact-center-as-a-service leader valued at $10B in 2021, now centred on AI agents for customer service, and remains CEO.
interesting_fact: He entered Twilio's 2011 contest because, aged 24 with an old PC and no money, he wanted the MacBook Air prize. He won it, then won TwilioCon's $10,000 first prize, which started Talkdesk.
deep_cut_fact: He got the email inviting him to present at TwilioCon on a Sunday night while watching Benfica play at the stadium. With no passport, he fast-tracked one and flew to San Francisco Monday night. Earlier he had a part-time job at Procter & Gamble, which convinced him he 'wasn't built for the 9-5 life.'
notes: Accessible, story-friendly founder with frequent interviews (SaaStr, CEO Magazine). Talkdesk has had layoffs and valuation pressure since 2022, so avoid valuation talk. The $10B figure is the 2021 Series D valuation. Strong AI angle (agentic customer service).

name: Abhishek Rai
current_role: Reportedly Senior Director of Engineering (compute platform), Databricks (aggregator profile, unconfirmed); co-founder of ThoughtSpot
profile: IIT Kharagpur/Stony Brook-trained engineer who worked at VMware and Google (2007-12), then co-founded ThoughtSpot (search/AI analytics, valued ~$4B) as VP Engineering. He then co-founded NetSpring (warehouse-native analytics, acquired by Optimizely 2024) and reportedly now leads compute-platform engineering at Databricks.
interesting_fact: He has co-founded two analytics startups from the same team: ThoughtSpot (2012), which pioneered search-style natural-language queries over enterprise data, and NetSpring (2019), sold to Optimizely in 2024.

Current Databricks role and NetSpring co-founder title come only from aggregator profiles (humantic.ai, MarketScreener), so verify on LinkedIn before outreach. Common name: several unrelated people named Abhishek Rai exist.

name: Ajeet Singh
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, ThoughtSpot
profile: Serial enterprise-software founder. He co-founded Nutanix as Chief Products Officer (its 2016 IPO was the largest tech IPO that year), then co-founded ThoughtSpot in 2012. ThoughtSpot pioneered search-based analytics and has since moved into AI agents for data analysis (Spotter, AgentSpot). He moved from CEO to executive chairman and remains its public face on AI analytics.
interesting_fact: He has built two multibillion-dollar companies from scratch: Nutanix, which created the hyperconverged-infrastructure market, and ThoughtSpot, valued at about $4bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding companies he was at Oracle, on the team that first launched Oracle Database on Amazon EC2. He studied chemical engineering at IIT Kanpur, where he graduated top of his class, and earned an MBA from IIM Calcutta.
notes: An approachable, frequent podcast guest (DealMakers, ThoughtSpot's own Data Chief podcast). Good for AI and data-infrastructure topics. Pitch through ThoughtSpot's press team; Russell Dougan, Director of Corporate Communications, is named on recent releases.

name: Amit Prakash
current_role: CEO and co-founder, AmpUp (formerly A79.ai; AI sales-coaching startup, Palo Alto); co-founder and former CTO of ThoughtSpot
profile: Ex-Microsoft Bing engineer and Google ads ML lead who co-founded ThoughtSpot with Ajeet Singh in 2012 as CTO; the AI analytics firm reached a ~$4B+ valuation and he architected its natural-language-to-SQL agent. Since 2024 he has run AmpUp (ex-A79.ai), building real-time AI coaching for sales and frontline teams.
interesting_fact: ThoughtSpot co-founder Ajeet Singh (also a Nutanix co-founder) has written that he recruited all his co-founders, Amit included, in Starbucks coffee shops around the Bay Area.
deep_cut_fact: He is a co-author of 'Elements of Programming Interviews' (with Adnan Aziz and Tsung-Hsien Lee), the cult coding-interview prep book used by thousands of software engineers.

public_contacts.value: https://intro.co/AmitPrakash (paid advisory calls he lists himself)

notes: No published personal net worth; on Hurun unicorn-founder list via ThoughtSpot. Accessible founder: active on LinkedIn and offers paid intro.co calls. Good AI/data angle.

profile: IIT Kanpur (B.Tech) and Stanford (MS CS) engineer who worked on search and ads technology at Google before co-founding search-driven analytics company ThoughtSpot in 2012 (valued ~$4B). In 2019 he and fellow ThoughtSpot founders started warehouse-native analytics firm NetSpring as CTO; Optimizely bought it in 2024, and he has reportedly since joined Snowflake.

name: Sanjay Agrawal
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Revefi (AI data-operations / data observability startup, founded 2021)
profile: Database researcher-turned-founder: after a decade-plus at Microsoft (incl. Research work on self-tuning databases) he co-founded ThoughtSpot in 2012 (AI/search analytics, ~$4bn valuation), leading engineering. In 2021 he co-founded Revefi, which raised a $20m Series A and was a 2025 Gartner Cool Vendor.
interesting_fact: At ThoughtSpot he pushed the decision to build a specialised in-memory database for analytics and a push-based data-recommendation system, foundations of its 'search your data' product.
deep_cut_fact: At Microsoft Research he co-authored the VLDB 2000 paper 'Automated Selection of Materialized Views and Indexes in SQL Databases' with Surajit Chaudhuri and Vivek Narasayya - the AutoAdmin work behind SQL Server 2000's index/view tuning tool; Revefi says he earned two 'Test of Time' awards at Microsoft.
notes: Hurun unicorn-founder listing (ThoughtSpot); personal wealth not confirmed as $1bn+. Technical founder - deep database/AI-for-data angle. Name is common: confirm via ThoughtSpot/Revefi context. Best route is Revefi's website/contact.

name: Shashank Gupta
current_role: Cofounder and CTO, Revefi (AI/data FinOps and observability); cofounder of ThoughtSpot
profile: IIT Delhi / UT Austin-educated engineer who cofounded search-driven analytics firm ThoughtSpot in 2012, building its search engine and leading engineering for three years. After leading data quality for Meta's exabyte-scale warehouse, he cofounded Revefi in 2021 with ThoughtSpot cofounder Sanjay Agrawal to cut AI and cloud-data spend.
interesting_fact: Revefi's RADEN agent targets AI/data cost control across Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and LLM apps; in Nov 2026 it launched closed-loop 'AI FinOps' to budget and enforce enterprise AI spend.
deep_cut_fact: While working on an EdTech startup venture, he went back to school for a master's degree in education to understand learners from the inside; earlier he worked on distributed systems and search at Amazon and Yahoo.
notes: Revefi media contact is Girish Bhat (published on press releases). Revefi runs its own 'Deep Dive' podcast. Good AI-cost/compute-efficiency angle.

name: Vijay Ganesan
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of NetSpring (acquired by Optimizely, 2024); now leads NetSpring analytics within Optimizely (exact current title unverified)
profile: Vijay Ganesan, an IIT Madras graduate, co-founded AI-search analytics firm ThoughtSpot (2012; valued at about $4.2bn) and led product there until 2019. He then co-founded NetSpring, a warehouse-native analytics platform, which Optimizely acquired in late 2024. He now works on bringing that analytics across Optimizely One.
interesting_fact: Before founding companies he spent eight years at Oracle as technical lead for its flagship business-intelligence product. He has now built two analytics startups on that foundation: ThoughtSpot and NetSpring.
deep_cut_fact: NetSpring was built on his thesis that 'event data' from sensors, devices, phones and product instrumentation was outgrowing traditional reporting tools. Its answer was analytics that sit directly on the customer's data warehouse rather than copying data out. Dell Technologies Capital backed it at seed and led its Series A.
notes: The press contact is Optimizely's VP of Global Communications as listed on the 2024 NetSpring acquisition release, so it may be outdated. He appears on marketing and analytics podcasts (e.g. Agile Brand), so he is open to podcast appearances. Not a billionaire; the Hurun unicorn-founder listing relates to ThoughtSpot.

name: Hao Jianan
current_role: Co-founder, COO & Director, CreateAI Holdings (formerly TuSimple; OTC: TSPH); legal representative of Beijing TuSimple
profile: NTU PhD in parallel/distributed systems and ex-Temasek Labs researcher who cofounded autonomous-trucking firm TuSimple in 2015 as COO, running its China engineering. After TuSimple froze US operations and delisted, it rebranded in Dec 2024 as CreateAI, pivoting to generative AI for games and animation.
interesting_fact: CreateAI open-sourced its 'Ruyi' image-to-video model (Ruyi-Mini-7B, a DiT model trained on ~200M clips) on Hugging Face and licensed Jin Yong's martial-arts IP and The Three-Body Problem for AI-made games and animation.

No working CreateAI/TuSimple press or IR email found (ir.tusimple.com returns 403; createai.com unreachable from here). The pi record claim comes from the company's own 36Kr team bio.

name: Sebastian Thrun
current_role: Co-founder, Cresta (AI for contact centers); founder, Sage AI Labs; adjunct professor, Stanford University
profile: Sebastian Thrun (b. 1967, Solingen) led Stanford's Stanley to win the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge, led Google's self-driving project (now Waymo) and co-founded Google X. He co-founded Udacity, ran eVTOL firm Kitty Hawk, co-founded $2bn AI contact-center unicorn Cresta (2017) and recently founded agentic-AI start-up Sage AI Labs.
interesting_fact: Larry Page reportedly disguised himself to watch a driverless-car race in order to scout and recruit Thrun to Google, where he went on to found the moonshot lab Google X.
deep_cut_fact: Long before self-driving cars he built museum tour-guide robots: Rhino at the University of Bonn (1994) and Minerva, which guided thousands of visitors at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History in 1998 - the same museum that now houses his DARPA-winning car Stanley.
notes: Hurun lists him for Cresta. Very accessible public speaker and podcast guest (recent appearances on AI, flying cars, education). Active on X (posted 2025 about hiring for an agentic-AI start-up) but handle not verified here.

name: Liang Jia'en
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CTO, Unisound AI Technology (HKEX: 9678)
profile: Liang Jia'en (梁家恩), a USTC graduate with a CAS Institute of Automation PhD, led speech-recognition R&D at CAS before co-founding Unisound in 2012. Unisound makes voice AI, AI chips and its 'Shanhai' large model for IoT and healthcare, and listed in Hong Kong on 30 June 2025.
interesting_fact: Unisound's work on what it called the world's first AI chip for IoT voice interaction won the Wu Wenjun AI Science & Technology Progress Award; its medical knowledge-graph work won a Beijing Science & Technology Progress first prize.
deep_cut_fact: At CAS in 2008-2010 his biggest project put machine scoring into the English oral middle-school entrance exams for all of Jiangsu province and Wenzhou, reaching millions of students. He calls it China's first large-scale AI scoring deployment; it was hard to commercialise inside CAS, which pushed him toward entrepreneurship.
notes: Self-described 'engineer at heart': all four Unisound founders are AI PhDs, and he is the one who stayed on R&D. Quote: tech founders must not 'succeed by technology and then fail by technology', since tech is only a third of the business chain. CEO Huang Wei is the commercial face. Mostly Chinese-language media.

name: Paul Nguyen
current_role: Unknown; co-founder of View, Inc. (formerly eChromics/Soladigm), no longer with the company
profile: Paul Nguyen co-founded electrochromic smart-glass maker eChromics with Mike Scobey in April 2007 in Santa Rosa, California; it became Soladigm and in 2012 View, Inc., whose dynamic glass tints to cut building heat and glare. Rao Mulpuri took over as CEO in 2008. View reached a $1B+ valuation, listed on Nasdaq via SPAC (2021) and went private again in 2024. No public record of Nguyen's current role was found.
interesting_fact: The company he co-founded makes 'dynamic' electrochromic windows that tint electronically to control sunlight and heat, an energy-efficiency play for buildings; it was valued above $1 billion in 2017.
notes: Common name — don't conflate with other Paul Nguyens. His exit from the company led to a 2010 lawsuit/arbitration (ruled in his favour in 2015); avoid the topic. View itself had financial trouble and went private in 2024. Current whereabouts unknown; very low profile.

name: Craig Ramsey
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman/board member of Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce in 2020); former Salesforce director (to 2014)
profile: Craig D. Ramsey is a veteran enterprise-software sales executive. He worked at Oracle (1986-94), nCUBE and Siebel Systems, where he became SVP Worldwide Operations in 1996, and sat on Salesforce's board until 2014. In 2014 he co-founded Vlocity, an industry-specific cloud CRM built on Salesforce, which Salesforce bought for about $1.33B in 2020.
interesting_fact: He was part of the Oracle-to-Siebel-to-Salesforce sales lineage that built the enterprise CRM industry. He sat on Salesforce's board in its early public years, then co-founded Vlocity, which Salesforce later acquired.
deep_cut_fact: Siebel's 1996 IPO filing shows he joined from parallel-computing pioneer nCUBE, where he was SVP of worldwide sales, marketing and support. Before that he spent eight years at Oracle, rising to VP of US Commercial Sales. He holds a BA in economics from Denison University.
notes: Low public profile, with no published contact or social accounts found. MarketScreener lists a Glide Foundation (San Francisco) directorship. He has been out of the news since the 2020 Vlocity sale; alive status not confirmed. Fit with the podcast theme is weak (cloud CRM, not infrastructure).

name: David Schmaier
current_role: President & Chief Strategy Officer, Salesforce (per Salesforce media bio, June 2025)
profile: Founding executive and EVP at Siebel Systems, then co-founder/CEO of Vlocity (industry cloud apps on Salesforce), sold to Salesforce for $1.33B in 2020. At Salesforce he ran Salesforce Industries, then was Chief Product Officer driving agentic AI, and now oversees strategy, M&A, Salesforce Ventures and philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Salesforce acquired Vlocity for about $1.33B in 2020 and immediately made Schmaier CEO of the new Salesforce Industries division.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer (B.S., Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute) before his Harvard MBA, and today sits on the cabinet board of Harvard's Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences and on Genstar Capital's strategic advisory board.
notes: Title has shifted several times (CEO Industries -> President & CPO -> President & Chief Strategy Officer); confirm current title before outreach. Also oversees Salesforce's Office of Ethical and Humane Use of technology.

name: James Ramsey
current_role: Co-founder & former board member, Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce 2020); LP at Stage 2 Capital; private investor
profile: James (Burr) Ramsey co-founded Vlocity in 2014 with Craig Ramsey, David Schmaier, Mark Armenante and Young Sohn to build industry-specific cloud CRM apps on Salesforce. Salesforce bought Vlocity in 2020 for about $1.33bn in cash. A long-time enterprise-software sales executive, he sat on SPS Commerce's board 2014-May 2025 and is now an LP with go-to-market VC Stage 2 Capital.
interesting_fact: Vlocity was built entirely on top of Salesforce's own platform, and Salesforce ended up acquiring it for ~$1.33bn in 2020, folding it into Salesforce Industries.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vlocity he was SVP of Worldwide Sales & Distribution at NetSuite, after starting out at Oracle, and he served about 11 years as an independent director of supply-chain software firm SPS Commerce, leaving in May 2025.
notes: Do not confuse with co-founder Craig D. Ramsey (Vlocity chairman, ex-Salesforce director). SPS board exit confirmed in SPS 2026 proxy: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1092699/000109269926000029/spsc-20260413.htm. Data-center angle is indirect (cloud software).

name: Young Sohn
current_role: Founding Managing Partner, Walden Catalyst Ventures; Chairman, HARMAN International; Chairman, Samsung Semiconductor Advisory Board
profile: Seoul-born, Maryland-raised Silicon Valley executive (Penn EE, MIT Sloan). Intel, Quantum, Agilent Semiconductor and Oak Technology, then took Inphi public in 2010 as CEO. As Samsung President/CSO (2012 on) he drove the $8B HARMAN deal and created the Samsung Catalyst Fund. He now invests in deep tech, AI and semis at Walden Catalyst (with Lip-Bu Tan).
interesting_fact: He has been a seed investor in Zoom, Ring, Noom, SambaNova, AI21 Labs and Berkeley Lights, and has sat on the boards of Arm, Cadence and Cymer (ASML).

He also co-founded the Extreme Tech Challenge, a startup competition tied to the UN SDGs.
notes: Identity is clear (well-known executive), but Hurun's label 'Vlocity founder' could not be verified. Vlocity's known founders are other people, so he may have been an early investor or board member; avoid calling him its founder. Strong fit for an AI/semis/data-center podcast and a frequent conference speaker (CES, Web Summit).

name: David A. Steinberg
current_role: Co-Founder, Chairman & CEO, Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who spent ~17 years in wireless (Sterling Cellular, then InPhonic) before co-founding XL Marketing - now Zeta Global - with former Apple CEO John Sculley in 2007. Zeta, an AI/data-driven marketing cloud, listed on the NYSE in 2021; he now pushes its 'Athena' AI agent, including a partnership with OpenAI.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Zeta Global (originally XL Marketing) with former Apple CEO John Sculley shortly after leaving InPhonic.
deep_cut_fact: His first real company, at 16 or 17, was a nightclub production business in New York City and the Hamptons; after college (1990) Goldman and Morgan Stanley turned him down, so he worked on telecom issues on Capitol Hill before entering wireless.
notes: Very media-friendly; does many podcasts/interviews (Adam Mendler, ICE House, Alejandro Cremades). Best route: press@zetaglobal.com. Zeta's valuation is now well above the $1B in the source field.

name: Wang Xiaogang
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director, CTO and EVP, SenseTime (HKEX: 0020); Chairman, ACE Robotics (since Dec 2025)
profile: Computer-vision scientist who co-founded SenseTime in 2014 from Tang Xiaoou's CUHK lab, whose DeepID face recognition beat human accuracy. SenseTime became one of China's largest AI firms and runs big AI compute (SenseCore). Since Dec 2025 he has also chaired ACE Robotics, a SenseTime embodied-AI spinout behind the open 'Kairos' world model.
interesting_fact: DeepID, from his CUHK team, was the first method to exceed 99% face-verification accuracy on the Labeled Faces in the Wild benchmark, beating human performance. That result helped launch SenseTime.
deep_cut_fact: He studied in USTC's famous 'Special Class for the Gifted Young' (BEng 2001), took an MPhil at CUHK under Tang Xiaoou, and on Tang's recommendation did his PhD at MIT (2009). He returned that year to teach electronic engineering at CUHK.
notes: Strong fit for AI and data-center topics: SenseTime runs large AI compute (SenseCore AIDC), and he is now leading on embodied AI and world models. He speaks often to media (Yicai, CnTechPost); in 2026 he predicted robotics' 'ChatGPT moment' is about two years away. SenseTime is on the US Entity List.

name: Tang Wenbin

name: Feng Shicong
current_role: Founder and CEO, Bailian Intelligence (百炼智能, AI-driven B2B marketing/lead generation); co-founder and former President/CTO of Mininglamp (明略)
profile: Feng Shicong (冯是聪) earned a Peking University computer science PhD (2003) under Prof. Li Xiaoming, worked at Lucent and HP Labs China, then joined Wu Minghui's AdMaster/Miaozhen as tech director and VP and co-founded Mininglamp Data as CTO. notes: Hurun lists him as a Mininglamp unicorn founder, but his current company is Bailian Intelligence; in May 2026 he spoke publicly about AI shifting B2B SaaS from 'selling tools' to 'selling results' (https://cj.sina.com.cn/articles/view/2311077472/89c03e6002002khka). No published contact found; route via Bailian Intelligence.

name: Kunle Olukotun
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technologist, SambaNova Systems; Cadence Design Systems Professor of EE and CS, Stanford University
profile: London-born Nigerian computer architect known as the 'father of the multi-core processor' for Stanford's Hydra chip-multiprocessor project. His startup Afara Websystems (2000) was bought by Sun in 2002 and became the Niagara/UltraSPARC T1 line. In 2017 he co-founded AI-chip company SambaNova (dataflow RDU chips for inference), which raised $1B at an $11B valuation in July 2026.
interesting_fact: The Niagara multicore design from his startup Afara went on to power Oracle's SPARC servers and generate billions of dollars of revenue; he was an architect of Sun's 2005 UltraSPARC T1.
deep_cut_fact: He did his undergraduate degree at Calvin College in Grand Rapids, Michigan, before a Michigan PhD (1991) under Trevor Mudge; his mid-1990s paper 'The Case for a Single-Chip Multiprocessor' argued for multicore years before industry adopted it. He won the 2023 Eckert-Mauchly Award.
notes: Funding source: https://www.ai-infra-summit.com/press-releases/ai-chip-startup-sambanova-valued-at-11-billion-in-1-billion-funding-round. Intel's ~$1.6B acquisition talks collapsed in early 2026, replaced by an Intel partnership/investment. Academic, approachable; Stanford route also possible.

name: Rodrigo Liang
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SambaNova Systems (AI inference chips and systems, Palo Alto)
profile: A chip executive from Sun/Oracle, Rodrigo Liang co-founded SambaNova in 2017 with Stanford professors Kunle Olukotun and Christopher Ré to build dataflow AI chips. In 2026 it launched the SN50 chip with Intel collaboration and closed a $1B round led by General Atlantic at an $11B valuation, selling inference racks for power-constrained data centres.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 SambaNova partnered with TEPCO Systems to supply energy-efficient AI infrastructure to Japan's power sector, squarely at the energy/data-centre intersection.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Taipei but raised in Brazil, Liang chose the company's name himself: SambaNova is Portuguese for 'new dance'. 'It's time for us to do something new in the world of technology,' he told SoftBank Vision Fund.
notes: Very media-friendly; frequent podcast/conference speaker (Bloomberg Open Interest, theCUBE, HumanX). Strong fit for the AI data-centre/energy angle. Intel acquisition talks reportedly stalled in early 2026; Intel remains investor/partner.

name: Daniel Yanisse
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Checkr (San Francisco)
profile: French-born engineer who co-founded Checkr with Jonathan Perichon in 2014 (YC) after seeing, at delivery startup Deliv, how slow background checks held up gig hiring. Checkr's API-first, AI-assisted screening platform serves thousands of employers and was valued at $4.6bn in 2021.
interesting_fact: Checkr launched Checkr.org in 2022 to push 'fair chance' hiring of people with criminal records, a mission Yanisse says crystallised from the founders' first conversations with job applicants.
deep_cut_fact: Before Checkr he was a software engineer who helped develop prototypes of the Mars rover for NASA; he was also on Forbes 30 Under 30.

public_contacts.value: Guest on 20VC (Harry Stebbings) discussing hiring and fundraising

notes: Podcast-friendly founder (20VC, SafeGraph, Battery Ventures interviews). Best route: Checkr press team. AI/HR-tech angle rather than energy/data-center.

name: Jonathan Perichon
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of Checkr (San Francisco); reported as board director
profile: Jonathan Perichon is a software engineer who co-founded Checkr in 2014 with Daniel Yanisse, building an API-first background-check platform that took off with gig-economy customers. Checkr went through Y Combinator (S14), was valued at $5B in 2022 and reported about $800M in 2025 gross revenue with 120,000+ customers. Recent research profiles list him as former CTO.

deep_cut_fact: He and Yanisse met in 2012 as coworkers at LA startup Mogreet; when it failed less than a year later they moved together to Deliv, where the Checkr idea emerged. At Y Combinator they landed Checkr's first 10 customers.

profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Trax with Dror Feldheim in 2010 to digitize retail shelves with computer vision.
