current_role: Co-founder, Hive (thehive.ai, AI content-moderation and deepfake-detection APIs); historically CTO
profile: Dmitriy Karpman co-founded San Francisco AI company Hive with CEO Kevin Guo; Hive sells cloud-hosted ML models via API for content moderation, AI-generated-content and deepfake detection, trained with data labelled by ~700,000 gig workers on its Hive Work app. Hive raised $85M at a $2B valuation in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Hive built its training-data pipeline on a crowd workforce of around 700,000 people labelling data through its Hive Work app, and early on raised $30M+ from Peter Thiel's Founders Fund and others.
notes: Very low public profile; Kevin Guo is the public face. Input 'Hive' means Hive AI (thehive.ai), not Hive project-management software. Web search budget ran out before a deep-cut fact or press contact could be found; his current title is unverified.

name: Kenny Rueter
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Kajabi (Irvine, California) — per Wikipedia; stepped back from CEO in 2021
profile: Software engineer who co-founded creator-economy platform Kajabi with Travis Rosser in Irvine, CA in 2010, giving course creators and coaches tools to sell online courses, memberships and coaching. Kajabi took its first outside capital only in 2019 (Spectrum Equity) and was valued at $2B after a $550M round in May 2021, when Ahad Khan became CEO and Rueter moved to executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Kajabi grew for nearly a decade before raising any outside capital (first minority investment from Spectrum Equity in Nov 2019), then hit a $2B valuation in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Kajabi came from a homemade PVC sprinkler toy he built: it took off on YouTube via a how-to video, and his frustration at being unable to monetize that video led him to build a platform for creators to sell their knowledge.
notes: Kajabi site publishes no press email; no verified personal channels confirmed (web search budget exhausted mid-lane). Origin story is a natural, friendly outreach hook; avoid details about his family.

name: Travis Rosser
current_role: Co-founder, Kajabi (current role not verified)
profile: Travis Rosser co-founded Kajabi in Irvine, California in 2010 with software engineer Kenny Rueter. Kajabi is a SaaS platform that lets creators sell online courses, memberships and podcasts. It bootstrapped for nearly a decade before taking Spectrum Equity's minority investment in 2019, then raised $550M at a $2B valuation in 2021, led by Tiger Global. Little public information on Rosser's current activities was found.
interesting_fact: Kajabi traces back to a toy: co-founder Kenny Rueter built a PVC sprinkler toy for his sons, and when he struggled to monetize a how-to video about it on YouTube, the founders built a platform for selling digital content.
notes: Very low profile. Wikipedia confirms him only as co-founder. The search budget ran out, so his current role was not verified and the record is minimal; the company contact is not his own.

name: Johannes Schildt
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board (styrelseordforande), Kry
profile: Swedish entrepreneur who co-founded Kry, the Stockholm-based digital healthcare provider (video consultations with doctors, psychologists and nurses, plus physical clinics; known as Livi in some markets), which reached a $1B+ valuation. He led it as CEO and is now board chair, with Kalle Conneryd Lundgren as CEO.
interesting_fact: He remains one of Kry's official spokespeople as board chair, alongside the CEO and chief medical officer, per the company's press page.
notes: Kry press page lists him as a company spokesperson (styrelseordforande), so press office is a good route. Web-search budget ran out before a sourced deep-cut fact could be found.

name: Mario Kohle
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Enpal (Berlin)
profile: Mario Kohle is a serial Berlin founder who co-founded home-improvement marketplace Käuferportal (now Aroundhome) in 2008, then Enpal in 2017 with Jochen Ziervogel and Viktor Wingert to rent rooftop solar to German homeowners. Enpal expanded into batteries, heat pumps, EV charging and energy supply, and in Jan 2026 reported its first year above EUR1bn revenue with positive free cash flow.
interesting_fact: Enpal popularised a 'solar system for rent' model in Germany, passed 100,000 customers, and in early 2026 reported over EUR1bn annual revenue and its first full year of positive free cash flow.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Strausberg (Brandenburg), he went straight from business-studies student to CEO when he started Käuferportal in 2008; he has called Enpal 'so etwas wie mein Lebenswerk' (something like my life's work).
notes: Media-friendly founder (many interviews with EU-Startups, OMR, pv-magazine, McKinsey case study). Strausberg birthplace from gruender.de (https://www.gruender.de/gruendung/enpal-gruender-mario-kohle/); 2008 student-to-CEO detail from KfW (https://www.kfw.de/stories/economy/start-ups/enpal/). Best route: Enpal press office.

name: Krste Asanovic
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect, SiFive; Chief Architect, RISC-V International; Professor Emeritus, UC Berkeley EECS
profile: Computer architect (born 1965; Berkeley PhD 1998; MIT faculty 1998-2007) who has led Berkeley's open RISC-V instruction-set project since its 2010 start. He co-founded the RISC-V Foundation (now RISC-V International) and in 2015 SiFive to commercialize RISC-V cores. He co-directs Berkeley's SLICE lab (Chipyard, FireSim, Gemmini).
interesting_fact: RISC-V, the free and open instruction set he co-created at Berkeley in 2010, is now a global alternative to Arm and x86, used from microcontrollers to AI accelerators. He was elected an ACM Fellow in 2018 for 'the open RISC-V instruction set and Agile hardware'.
deep_cut_fact: His 1998 Berkeley PhD thesis, under John Wawrzynek, was titled 'Vector Microprocessors', foreshadowing the RISC-V vector extension. He was tenured at MIT in 2005 before returning to Berkeley in 2007 to co-found the Par Lab, the parallel-computing lab where RISC-V was born.
notes: His university email is published on his own Berkeley page as 'krste at berkeley dot edu'. SiFive PR is an alternative route. A strong fit for a data-center/AI-silicon episode (RISC-V in AI accelerators).

name: Yunsup Lee
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Technology Officer, SiFive
profile: Yunsup Lee co-created the open RISC-V instruction set and the first RISC-V processors as a UC Berkeley PhD student, then co-founded SiFive in 2015 with Andrew Waterman and Krste Asanovic to commercialize RISC-V core IP. SiFive's cores ship in 2B+ devices; it raised a $400M Series G in 2026 (~$3.65B valuation) to push into AI data centres, including NVIDIA NVLink Fusion support.
interesting_fact: He was one of the original authors of the RISC-V spec 'from Day 1' and co-designed the first RISC-V microprocessors at Berkeley; SiFive is now targeting AI data-centre CPUs.
deep_cut_fact: His 2016 Berkeley PhD thesis introduced the Hwacha 'decoupled vector-fetch' architecture (committee included David Patterson), and at Hot Chips 2015 he presented Raven3, a 28nm RISC-V vector chip with on-die switched-capacitor DC-DC converters.
notes: Strong data-center fit (RISC-V for AI data centres, $400M 2026 round). Press email is SiFive Corporate Communications (David Miller) as listed on 2026 press releases. Hot Chips slides: https://old.hotchips.org/wp-content/uploads/hc_archives/hc27/HC27.25-Tuesday-Epub/HC27.25.70-Processors-Epub/HC27.25.731-RISC-V-Lee-UCB-V4.with-backup.pdf

name: Tan Zaixing
current_role: Chairman, Beiqing Clean Energy Investment Co. (北清清洁能源投资, renamed Tianjin Beiqing Power Smart Energy / 天津北清电力智慧能源, 'Beiqing Smart'), per MarketScreener; former executive director of Beijing Enterprises Clean Energy (HKEX: 1250) to May 2022
profile: Tan Zaixing (谭再兴) was an executive director of Beijing Enterprises Clean Energy (now Shandong Hi-Speed New Energy, HKEX: 1250) from at least 2019 to May 2022, and a director of Beiqing Huanneng (000803). He is listed as chairman of Tianjin-based Beiqing Clean Energy Investment, which controlled 000803 until 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2022 Shandong Hi-Speed Group took control of BE Clean Energy through a large share subscription, renaming it Shandong Hi-Speed New Energy; Tan and other Beijing Enterprises Water-nominated directors stepped down on 16 May 2022. He then held 60M shares plus 340M share options.
notes: Matched to 谭再兴/譚再興 via Hurun 2026 (谭再兴 / 北清智慧 / Beiqing Clean Energy / Tianjin). Beiqing Huanneng's 2021 annual report (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2022-03-05/1212511577.PDF) confirms 北清智慧 = 天津北清电力智慧能源 (formerly 北清清洁能源投资). His director role at 000803 is in its Aug 2021 equity-change report. Education (China University of Petroleum BA/MBA) and China Development Bank stint (2007-12) come only from MarketScreener, so they're unverified. No official contact found; private, low profile.

name: Ye Jun
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Zhaoxin Semiconductor (兆芯集成; STAR Market IPO filed June 2025) and Chairman, Shanghai Alliance Investment (联和投资)
profile: Ye Jun (叶峻, b. 1972) has worked at Shanghai Alliance Investment, the city-owned tech investor he now chairs, since 1996. He has chaired Zhaoxin since its 2013 founding as a JV with VIA Technologies; it is China's leading x86-compatible CPU designer, with six generations in mass production. Also on Hua Hong and Bank of Shanghai boards.
interesting_fact: Zhaoxin is one of very few companies anywhere designing x86-compatible CPUs (the architecture behind ~90% of PCs and servers, per its prospectus); it began by 'introducing, digesting, absorbing and re-innovating' VIA's x86 technology and has shipped six generations.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond chips, his portfolio of chairmanships includes MetLife's China life-insurance JV (中美联泰大都会人寿), sensor maker Shanghai QST (矽睿科技) and pharma firm Shanghai Xuantai (宣泰医药); he was Zhaoxin's legal representative from day one, when it was registered in April 2013 with US$100M capital.
notes: Identity confirmed by Hurun 2026 (叶峻 / 兆芯集成 / Zhaoxin Semiconductor) and Zhaoxin's STAR prospectus (June 2025 filing). He is a state-investment executive (Lianhe is under Shanghai SASAC) rather than a private wealth-holder. Route via Zhaoxin IR / board office (contact person Du Mengmeng per prospectus).

name: Joshua Motta
current_role: CEO & Co-Founder, Coalition, Inc. (cyber insurance / 'Active Insurance')
profile: Former CIA officer, Goldman Sachs and Francisco Partners alum and early Cloudflare executive (CXO, head of special projects) who co-founded Coalition with Lookout founder John Hering in 2017. Coalition pairs cyber insurance with continuous risk scanning and incident response, was valued at $5B in 2022, and partners with Allianz for capacity.
interesting_fact: He joined Cloudflare in 2010 as employee No. 20, at the CEO's request, before leaving to start Coalition.
deep_cut_fact: At 12 in Olathe, Kansas he ran a website-building business for local realtors with a junior-high friend; at 15 he was hired as a software developer at Microsoft's Redmond HQ (Building 18), reportedly the youngest hire in Microsoft's history, where posters dubbed him 'Microsoft's Wonder Boy'.
notes: Recruited to the CIA from a University of Chicago career fair; ex-intelligence background makes him somewhat reticent. Input tags him 'energy' focus but Coalition is cyber insurance; the angle could be cyber risk to energy/critical infrastructure. Press route: press@coalitioninc.com.

name: Alexi Robichaux
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, BetterUp (digital and AI-powered coaching platform)
profile: USC political-science graduate who worked as a product manager at Socialcast and became a VMware product executive at 25 after its 2011 acquisition. In 2013 he co-founded BetterUp with Eduardo Medina to bring evidence-based professional coaching to whole workforces; it reached a ~$4.7-5B valuation in 2021 and now pairs human coaches with AI coaching.
interesting_fact: BetterUp grew out of Youth Leadership America, a nonprofit Robichaux co-founded in 2003 as a teenager, where he and Medina coached and mentored high-school students.
deep_cut_fact: He taught himself to code and build websites as a high-school freshman in England with his brother. Before founding BetterUp he went searching for better coaching, trying executive coaching and the Landmark Forum and even walking the Camino de Santiago in Spain.
notes: Comfortable with media and writes on BetterUp's blog and the WEF site. BetterUp lists offices in Austin and Toronto. No press email is published, so LinkedIn or X is the best direct route. Weak energy/data-centre angle beyond AI-coaching products.

name: Eddie Medina
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, BetterUp
profile: Eduardo 'Eddie' Medina cofounded BetterUp, the coaching and 'human + AI' leadership-development platform, with CEO Alexi Robichaux in 2013. As COO he runs coaching, operations and delivery for enterprise clients; BetterUp was valued at ~$4.7B in 2021 and now sells AI coaching, incl. inside Microsoft 365 Copilot. He was earlier at Bain and Altamont Capital.
interesting_fact: In March 2021 BetterUp hired Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, as its first Chief Impact Officer - after he had been using the coaching platform himself for a couple of months.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated summa cum laude in business from USC, and BetterUp highlights him as an advocate for education, economic access and workplace equity who actively mentors emerging leaders.
notes: Goes by Eduardo or Eddie. Speaks at ASU+GSV and writes on the BetterUp blog/Benefit News - reachable via BetterUp press office. Fits the AI/entrepreneurship angle more than energy.

name: Samuel Ellis
current_role: Early-stage software investor; partner at Scout Ventures (per 2022 interviews; current status not confirmed)
profile: Sam Ellis is a West Point graduate (operations research) and former Army intelligence officer at U.S. Cyber Command who co-founded Dutchie, the cannabis e-commerce/POS platform later valued at about $3.75B. He built Dutchie's first software version, then moved into venture investing as a partner at Scout Ventures, leading SaaS pre-seed and seed deals.
interesting_fact: He single-handedly wrote the first version of Dutchie's online cannabis marketplace software while coming out of a military cyber role, coding in his spare time.
deep_cut_fact: Before Dutchie he served as a software developer and intelligence leader at U.S. Cyber Command after studying operations research and applied statistics at West Point; he has said he spotted great engineers as people who 'love the game'.
notes: Low public profile; the less-visible co-founder next to Ross and Zach Lipson. Veteran-focused VC (Scout Ventures) is the natural route; current Scout role unverified on its team page. Podcasts: Travis Makes Money #717 (2022), Those Who Dare (May 2022).

name: Zach Lipson
current_role: Investor/advisor, Lightweight Ventures (former co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Dutchie)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who co-founded Dutchie in 2017 with his younger brother Ross; as chief product officer he helped build it into the leading cannabis e-commerce/point-of-sale platform (valued ~$3.75B in 2021). The brothers left Dutchie in early 2023; he has since invested in and advised early-stage startups.
interesting_fact: Dutchie started in Bend, Oregon; within two years it served 450 dispensaries in 18 states and was pitched as 'a Shopify of the cannabis space maybe meets DoorDash'. Ross described Zach as the methodical one: 'Zach is the one who wants to make sure that we're doing everything right.'
notes: No longer at Dutchie (left Feb 2023; the founders later filed suit against company leadership, so avoid framing outreach around Dutchie's current management). Low public profile; LinkedIn is the likely route. Appeared on the 'To Be Blunt' cannabis podcast (ep. 020).

name: Felix Ohswald
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, GoStudent (Vienna)
profile: Austrian mathematician-turned-founder who co-founded GoStudent with Gregor Müller in 2016, building a one-to-one online tutoring platform that became Europe's first edtech unicorn (valued ~$3.5B in 2022). After a post-boom restructuring, GoStudent reported full-year operational profitability in 2025.
interesting_fact: Studied maths in Vienna and at Cambridge (BA Hons 2014), then a master's in quantitative finance at ETH Zurich, before quitting a finance path to start GoStudent.
deep_cut_fact: GoStudent began in 2015 when Ohswald, then 20 and at ETH Zurich, ran an online group answering schoolchildren's homework questions after helping his younger brother's friends with their schoolwork.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (ASU+GSV, 4GameChangers). Best route is the GoStudent press team.

name: Ferdinand von Hagen
profile: Listed by Hurun as a GoStudent founder, but public sources name Felix Ohswald and Gregor Müller as GoStudent's founders (Vienna, 2016). A CB Insights entry lists a Ferdinand von Hagen as former CTO of Studienkreis (a German tutoring firm acquired by GoStudent), with GoStudent, Deloitte, ETH Zurich and Airbus in his work history.
notes: Founder attribution looks wrong: he appears to be a tech executive (ex-CTO at Studienkreis, a GoStudent group company), not a co-founder. His current role isn't confirmed. Source: https://www.cbinsights.com/company/studienkreis/people. For GoStudent, the founders are Felix Ohswald (CEO) and Gregor Müller.

name: Gregor Muller
current_role: Co-founder & COO, GoStudent (Vienna)
profile: Austrian entrepreneur who co-founded online/hybrid tutoring platform GoStudent in Vienna in 2016 with CEO Felix Ohswald. GoStudent has raised over EUR 675m (Prosus, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Left Lane) at a peak valuation around EUR 3bn, and has expanded via acquisitions (Seneca Learning, Tus Media, Studienkreis, Berlitz Germany sites).
interesting_fact: GoStudent Group reported its first full year of operational profitability in 2025, after a period of rapid post-pandemic expansion and restructuring.
deep_cut_fact: Before it was a platform, GoStudent began in 2016 as a WhatsApp chat through which pupils could go over their homework with tutors.
notes: Common name: a different Gregor Mueller (health economist, Thieme RECOM) exists - don't confuse. Lower public profile than CEO Felix Ohswald; GoStudent press office is best route.

name: Cliff Click
current_role: CTO, CRATUS Technology (lidar machine perception / industrial IoT automation), since Feb 2019; co-founder of H2O.ai
profile: Compiler engineer Cliff Click (Texas A&M BS/MS, Rice PhD 1995) was primary architect of Sun's HotSpot JVM server compiler (C2), co-founded Azul Systems (2002), and co-founded H2O.ai (2012), designing its distributed in-memory math engine. He later was CTO of fintech Neurensic and since 2019 CTO of CRATUS; he also hosts the open 'Coffee Compiler Club'.
interesting_fact: His Rice PhD work produced the 'sea of nodes' intermediate representation, which became the basis of HotSpot's C2 JIT - code that still optimizes much of the world's Java.
deep_cut_fact: He describes himself as having been 'writing compilers since age 15', holds 20+ patents, and runs a weekly 'Coffee Compiler Club' video call open to anyone interested in language design.
notes: Hacker/engineer personality, approachable in the compiler/PL community; technical deep-dives (JIT, GC, sea of nodes, ML infra) would land well. Coffee Compiler Club recordings are on YouTube (link via https://lists.puremagic.com/pipermail/digitalmars-d-announce/2021-December/058199.html).

name: Sri Satish Ambati
current_role: Founder and CEO, H2O.ai (Mountain View, CA)
profile: Sri Ambati co-founded H2O.ai in 2012 (originally 0xdata, with Java veteran Cliff Click) to build the open-source H2O ML platform, later adding Driverless AI and enterprise GenAI/agent products. He earlier co-founded Platfora and led engineering at DataStax. In 2026 H2O launched the tabH2O tabular foundation model and expanded an AI lab in Singapore.
interesting_fact: H2O.ai's open-source ML platform is used by tens of thousands of organizations; in July 2026 its 'H2O AI Super Agent' ranked #2 on the FutureX overall leaderboard.
deep_cut_fact: Before H2O he was a partner and performance engineer at Java multi-core startup Azul Systems, built a NoSQL trie-based index for semi-structured data at in-memory startup RightOrder, pursued theoretical neuroscience at Berkeley, and worked on scaling R over big data with Purdue and Stanford researchers.
notes: Very accessible, prolific speaker and poster (handle @srisatish). Press contact is the named contact in H2O's site metadata. Company is private; 'unicorn' valuation dates from 2021 funding.

name: Rishi Singh
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Harness; founder & CEO, SapientAI / BaseRock.ai (AI software testing)
profile: IIT Delhi-trained engineer who spent five years at Apple leading its deployment-automation platform, then co-founded Harness (AI software delivery platform) with Jyoti Bansal and served as CTO until 2021. He remains on Harness's board and now runs an AI test-generation startup (SapientAI, launched May 2023 with $5M seed from 8VC; BaseRock.ai).
interesting_fact: SapientAI emerged from stealth in May 2023 with a $5M seed led by 8VC to build an 'AI Test Coder' that writes unit tests automatically.
deep_cut_fact: Before Harness he spent five years at Apple leading development of its internal deployment automation platform, and says he learned from Steve Jobs the importance of constantly talking about what you believe in.
notes: Not the founder-CEO of Harness (that is Jyoti Bansal); he is the technical co-founder. Best route likely via his current AI-testing startup.

name: Andy Katz-Mayfield
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Mammoth Brands (formerly Harry's Inc.; owns Harry's, Flamingo, Lume, Mando)
profile: Duke and Stanford GSB (MBA 2011) alum who worked at Bain & Company and Charlesbank Capital before co-founding Harry's with Jeff Raider in 2012. Harry's grew into a ~$750M-revenue DTC/retail razor business; in April 2025 the parent was renamed Mammoth Brands, which he still co-leads with Raider.
interesting_fact: In January 2014, barely a year after launch, Harry's bought the century-old German blade maker Feintechnik (Eisfeld, founded 1920) for $100M so it could control manufacturing; in 2019 Edgewell agreed to buy Harry's for $1.4B before the FTC sued to block it.
deep_cut_fact: His first paying job was as a banquet waiter at a country club, which taught him that great service 'isn't that hard'; he has every Harry's employee spend a day each quarter working in customer experience, and says he wants to build a brand that lasts 100 years.
notes: Co-CEO with Jeff Raider (also Warby Parker co-founder). Best route is Mammoth Brands press email. LinkedIn listed is the company page, not his personal profile.

name: Israel David
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, HiBob (Tel Aviv / New York / London)
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded HiBob with CEO Ronni Zehavi in 2015; HiBob makes 'Bob', a cloud HR/people platform for mid-sized companies, and has been valued at about $2.7B+ (Hurun lists $3B). Before HiBob he held senior technology roles at companies including Kenshoo and VMware (per third-party profiles). He continues to lead HiBob's technology as CTO.
interesting_fact: HiBob was founded in 2015 by Ronni Zehavi and Israel David on the idea that 'the employee experience and role of HR needed to evolve'; it opened its first US HQ in New York in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining as co-founder, David was Ronni Zehavi's neighbor in Silicon Valley; Bessemer's account of HiBob's rise notes Zehavi brought on 'his former Silicon Valley neighbor, Israel David.'
notes: Low public profile compared with CEO Ronni Zehavi, who does most media. Earlier career details (Kenshoo, VMware, 48Upper) come from third-party profiles; verify before citing. HiBob's US PR has been handled by 5W Public Relations (5wpr.com/practice/hibob.cfm) but no verified press email was found.

name: Ronni Zehavi
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, HiBob (HR software, London/Tel Aviv/New York)
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur who co-founded HiBob in Tel Aviv in 2015, maker of the 'Bob' cloud HR/HCM platform for mid-sized, distributed companies. HiBob has raised several $150M rounds (valued ~$2.7B in 2023) and has added payroll (Pento, 2024) and FP&A (Mosaic, 2025) via acquisitions. He remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Before HiBob he co-founded content-delivery startup Cotendo in January 2008 (backed by Sequoia and Benchmark), which Akamai bought in March 2012 for over $300M - he calls HiBob his third company.
deep_cut_fact: Cotendo was founded by three former Commtouch (later Cyren) colleagues - Zehavi, Udi Trugman and David Drai - with R&D in Netanya, Israel and HQ in Sunnyvale; it set out to challenge Akamai and ended up being acquired by it.
notes: No published press email found on hibob.com; press page and general Contact Us form are the official routes. Frequent podcast guest on HR/future-of-work topics (Josh Bersin, Digital HR Leaders, DealMakers).

name: Arseniy Vershinin
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect (formerly CTO), Personio
profile: Russian-born software engineer who co-founded Munich HR-software company Personio in 2015 with Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher and Ignaz Forstmeier, serving as CTO as it grew into Europe's leading SMB HR platform (valued up to $8.5B). In a 2024 leadership change he moved from CTO to Chief Architect, leading technology projects.
interesting_fact: He met his three Personio co-founders in 2014 at Munich's Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), a one-year startup program for TUM/LMU students.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Ulan-Ude and raised in the small Siberian town of Ust-Ilimsk, he spent a year in the US as a teen on the FLEX exchange program, then studied at MIPT ('Phystech') and did iOS development for Moscow startups before moving to Munich for 'an international atmosphere'.
notes: Low public profile; listed as a Founders Pledge member (https://www.founderspledge.com/members/2681). Best route is Personio press office. Could not directly re-verify the press email in the PDF (download blocked); also seen as press@personio.de on older releases.

name: Hanno Renner
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Personio (Munich)
profile: German entrepreneur who co-founded HR-software company Personio in Munich in 2015 with fellow CDTM classmates. Personio grew into one of Europe's most valuable startups (valued ~$8B in 2022), serving SMEs with HR and payroll software; Renner continues to lead it as CEO.
interesting_fact: Personio started with about $200 in the bank and reached a $6.3B valuation within six years, making Renner one of Europe's youngest unicorn CEOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Personio he trained as a sailing skipper and spent semester breaks taking tourists out on sailing boats; he studied industrial engineering at HTWG Konstanz and Management & Technology at TUM.
notes: Press releases also list press@personio.de; best route is Personio's comms team.

name: Ignaz Forstmeier
current_role: Co-founder and former CMO, Personio; now with 3VC (Vienna software VC) and an angel investor
profile: One of four TU Munich/CDTM alumni who founded Munich HR-software company Personio in 2015 (with Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher and Arseniy Vershinin); he served as CMO as it grew to an $8B valuation. Having left Personio's operations, he is based in Vienna, works with Series A fund 3VC and has angel-invested in 25+ startups.
interesting_fact: Personio grew out of the Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM) programme in Munich, which all four founders attended; Forstmeier was there 2013-2015.
deep_cut_fact: In Personio's early days, while hunting for their EUR 2.1M seed round, the founders went unpaid for a while; Forstmeier said fundraising is usually a full-time job for at least one founder. In 2016 customers grew from ~20 to 100+ purely through referrals, with no marketing budget.
notes: No longer operational at Personio; LinkedIn shows current affiliation with 3VC, Vienna. Low public profile.

name: Roman Schumacher
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Personio (former Chief Product Officer; moved to a strategic role in late 2022)
profile: Roman Schumacher co-founded Munich HR-software company Personio in 2015 with Hanno Renner, Arseniy Vershinin and Ignaz Forstmeier, and ran product as CPO for about seven years. Personio grew into one of Europe's most valuable SaaS startups (valued at about $8.5B). In Nov 2022 he handed product to ex-Meta exec Maria Angelidou-Smith, moving into a strategic role and staying on Personio's board.
interesting_fact: Personio grew out of the founders' time at Munich's Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), where Schumacher met CEO Hanno Renner.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of his studies to build Personio and had no prior work experience. On handing over product leadership as the company scaled, he told t3n: 'Die Zügel aus der Hand zu geben, war schon hart für mich' ('Handing over the reins was really hard for me').
notes: Low public profile since leaving the CPO role (Nov 2022, per Munich Startup). Reach him through Personio press. One unverified profile says he later started a venture called Studio Sonntag; not confirmed.

name: Anastasia Zamyshlyaeva
current_role: VP Engineering, GitKraken (per 2025/26 speaker bio); co-founder and former Chief Architect of Reltio
profile: Russian-born software architect who co-founded master-data-management company Reltio with CEO Manish Sood in 2011, serving as technical co-founder, Chief Architect and VP Platform Product Management. She has since held engineering leadership roles at Redpanda Data and is now VP Engineering at developer-tools company GitKraken.
interesting_fact: Won the 2018 Aragon Research Women in Technology Award (CIO category) as Reltio's Chief Architect.
deep_cut_fact: Before Reltio she designed core components of the Informatica MDM tool; she holds an MS in CS from Chelyabinsk State University (research in distributed graph computing), and Reltio's earliest brainstorms took place in Mountain View coffee shops.
notes: Appears to have left Reltio; current role at GitKraken per SF Engineering Leadership Community speaker page (https://sfelc.com/speaker/anastasia-zamyshlyaeva-2). Low public profile; no published contacts found. Best route likely via conference speaking circuits (LeadDev/SFELC).

name: Manish Sood
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Reltio (sources differ; has also been listed as CTO & Chairman 2020-2022)
profile: Indian-born engineer who founded Reltio in 2011 (with Anastasia Zamyshlyaeva) after leading MDM product strategy at Siperian and Informatica. Reltio sells a cloud master-data-management / 'data unification' platform, valued around $1.7-2B, and now pitches it as the data foundation for enterprise AI.
interesting_fact: Before enterprise software, Sood was educated as a mechanical engineer (Andhra University, graduated 1995) in India.
deep_cut_fact: He told interviewer Adam Mendler that he began his career working on the automation of large-scale power plants, a natural hook for an energy/data-center podcast.

public_contacts.value: reltio@allisonpr.com (Allison + Partners, media and analyst inquiries)

notes: Press contacts per Reltio press releases (Kevin Keenan, VP Communications, listed in 2026 release); verify current contact on latest release. Frequent podcast guest (Modern CTO, DataVersity).

name: Drew Durbin
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Wave Mobile Money (Dakar, Senegal)
profile: American entrepreneur who co-founded remittance app Sendwave (YC, sold to WorldRemit for ~$500M in 2020) and then Wave, a low-fee mobile money network that launched in Senegal and became Francophone Africa's first unicorn after a $200M Series A in 2021. He continues to run Wave as it expands across West Africa.
interesting_fact: Wave's flat 1% transfer fee undercut incumbents by roughly 70%, forcing Orange Money and others to slash their prices; Wave reached about 70% of Senegal's mobile-money users.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Sendwave came from his own frustration with fees and unreliable transfers when sending money to an NGO he ran in Tanzania; he and co-founder Lincoln Quirk met as freshman hallmates at Brown University.
notes: Low public profile; no published press email found on wave.com. Best route is via Wave corporate channels.

name: Lincoln Quirk
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Product, Wave Mobile Money
profile: Co-founded Sendwave (low-fee US/UK-to-Africa remittances, sold to WorldRemit in 2020) and then Wave, a mobile money company that has grown into one of francophone West Africa's largest fintechs, starting in Senegal and valued around $1.7-2B. He met CEO Drew Durbin as a freshman hallmate at Brown and still leads product at Wave.
interesting_fact: Says he and his co-founders build Wave 'primarily for EA reasons'; he attended his first effective altruism gathering in 2013 (about 50 people in an Oakland house) and says he has had more impact through direct work at Wave than through donations.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2020 EA Forum AMA with CTO Ben Kuhn he said he personally wrote much of the original code for both Sendwave and Wave; Sendwave's pitch was sending money by phone number at a 3% fee vs the typical 8-12%.
notes: Low-profile; active in effective altruism circles (EA Forum). Best route likely via Wave or EA community. No published personal email found.

name: Peng Yi
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of YBM (药帮忙 / Xiaoyaoyao, Wuhan-based B2B pharmaceutical e-commerce platform connecting drugmakers with pharmacies and clinics; valued ~$2B). Could not confirm in public sources that Peng Yi is a founder; business registration lists Li Meng as legal representative of Wuhan Xiaoyaoyao.
notes: Identity unverified; English and Chinese searches did not link Peng Yi to YBM/Xiaoyaoyao. Verify via company registry (shareholders) or Hurun list before outreach.

name: Huang Tingting
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of YBM (Yaobangmang/药帮忙), the B2B pharmaceutical procurement platform run by Wuhan Xiaoyaoyao Pharmaceutical Technology (founded Dec 2015). Public sources found name Peng Yi (彭裔) as founder and Li Meng (李萌) as founder/CEO; no source tying a Huang Tingting to the company was found.
notes: Could not confirm identity. Searches for 'Huang Tingting' mostly return an unrelated SNH48 idol singer. Company sources: https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1679729594749704 and https://finance.ifeng.com/c/87KuE7F91Ne. Verify via Hurun or company registry before outreach.

name: JC Glancy
current_role: Co-founder, ZenBusiness; Venture Partner, Fluent Ventures
profile: JC (James) Glancy co-founded ZenBusiness, the Austin-based all-in-one platform that helps small businesses form, run and grow (LLC formation, compliance, banking, accounting), valued around $1.7B in 2021. He brought in HomeAway founding CTO Ross Buhrdorf as investor and later CEO. He is now a venture partner at Fluent Ventures and an angel/advisor.
interesting_fact: ZenBusiness took roughly a 10-year journey to become an 'overnight success'; Glancy says his drive came from wanting to make life easier for small-business owners like his father.
deep_cut_fact: Glancy deliberately hired his own boss, bringing in Ross Buhrdorf as CEO, summing up the trade-off as: "You can either be rich or be king." He also noted ZenBusiness customers who use its banking churn at half the rate of those who don't.
notes: Low public profile; Ross Buhrdorf is ZenBusiness's public face. Fluent Ventures (Alex Lazarow) is a warm route - Glancy is a venture partner there.

name: Rafael Lopez
current_role: Listed as a ZenBusiness founder/'Product Director' on an insider-data aggregator; not named on ZenBusiness's current leadership page
profile: Rafael Lopez is named as one of several ZenBusiness co-founders (alongside Ross Buhrdorf, Shanaz Hemmati, JC Glancy and Art Flores) in a secondary source and as a founder/Product Director on MarketScreener. ZenBusiness, an Austin-based small-business formation and compliance platform founded in 2015, was valued around $1.7B. No independent biography was found.
interesting_fact: ZenBusiness is a public benefit corporation (ZenBusiness PBC) in Austin that helps small-business owners form LLCs, stay compliant and manage finances; a 2025 CNBC piece described it as a $1.7 billion startup.
notes: Very low public profile; company's official founder list (website, Wikipedia) names only Buhrdorf and Hemmati. 'Rafael Lopez' is a common name - verify identity (e.g. via the Forbes listing) before outreach. Best route is via ZenBusiness press.

name: Ross Buhrdorf
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, ZenBusiness (Austin, Texas)
profile: Nebraska-born technologist who was founding CTO of HomeAway (vacation rentals), acquired by Expedia for $3.9B in 2015. That year he co-founded ZenBusiness with Shanaz Hemmati, a public-benefit SaaS platform for business formation and compliance that has served 1M+ entrepreneurs and reached a ~$1.7-2B valuation.
interesting_fact: He met his ZenBusiness co-founder Shanaz Hemmati when both worked at Excite.com, one of the internet's earliest web portals; EY named him Entrepreneur of the Year (Gulf South) in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: His personal motto, published on ZenBusiness's site: "Fear is a liar that holds us back... Don't let fear dictate your actions - go for it."
notes: Best route is ZenBusiness press team. Company is a PBC; Hemmati is also co-founder.

name: Andreas Bittner
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder of Solaris (formerly solarisBank), Berlin; left the management board in February 2020 - current executive role not confirmed
profile: Co-founded Berlin banking-as-a-service platform solarisBank (now Solaris) in 2015 and, as COO and board member, built its operations. He left the board in Feb 2020. Solaris became a fintech unicorn before a 2025 rescue by Japan's SBI Holdings, whose takeover he and other ex-shareholders have challenged in a Berlin court.
interesting_fact: As founding COO he built solarisBank's banking and back-office processes from scratch - a fully licensed bank designed to be plugged into other companies' apps via APIs; by 2020 it had nearly 300 staff and had raised over EUR100m.
notes: Hurun tags him 'energy' but Solaris is a fintech (banking-as-a-service), not solar - weak fit for an energy/data-centre podcast. He is in active litigation against Solaris/SBI (2025), so Solaris's press office is not an appropriate route. An insider-data site links him to finCraft AG (unconfirmed). No published personal contact found.

name: Marko Wenthin
current_role: Co-founder of Solaris (formerly solarisBank, Berlin); current role unconfirmed (former CCO of solarisBank, CEO of Penta Fintech 2019-2021)
profile: German banker-turned-fintech founder who co-founded Berlin banking-as-a-service platform solarisBank (Solaris) with Andreas Bittner in 2015-16, serving as co-managing director/Chief Commercial Officer. He later ran Solaris-owned SME neobank Penta (2019-21). Solaris reached unicorn status (~$2B) before a 2025 SBI-led rescue round. His Hurun listing comes from that founder stake.
interesting_fact: Solaris pioneered 'banking-as-a-service' in Europe, giving fintechs and brands such as Vivid, Tomorrow and ADAC the regulated bank licence underneath their apps.
deep_cut_fact: Before solarisBank he founded GroupPlatina and created Sofort Bank, the banking sister of Sofortüberweisung, Germany's big online-payment brand. Earlier he was COO and board member of Deutsche Bank PBC in Poland and worked for Deutsche Bank in Argentina.
notes: Fintech, not energy; weak fit for the podcast's focus. Current activity unclear after Penta (2021). Solaris valuation collapsed and co-founder Bittner is litigating against SBI, so avoid. I found no verified personal site or social account; LinkedIn is the likely route but unverified.

name: Xu Hui
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and CEO, AInnovation Technology Group (创新奇智, HKEX: 2121)
profile: Xu Hui (徐辉), a former Microsoft Greater China vice president with earlier enterprise-software roles at SAP, co-founded AInnovation in April 2018 with Kai-Fu Lee's Sinovation Ventures (Lee is non-executive chairman). The company builds industrial AI and large-model applications, mainly for manufacturing; it listed in Hong Kong and in FY2025 grew revenue 23.8% to RMB 1.51bn, with manufacturing over 80%.
interesting_fact: Under his 'One Model, One Body, Two Wings' strategy AInnovation pivoted almost entirely to AI-for-manufacturing: manufacturing revenue reached RMB 1.22bn (80.9% of the total) in 2025 and he described operations as at a 'historically optimal level'.
notes: Strong fit for the AI/industrial angle. The published inbox is for business cooperation; IR contact via HKEX filings. Third-party profiles also mention IBM, Wanda Network and a Honma Golf INED seat, which could not be verified from primary sources here.

name: Gustavo Sapoznik
current_role: Founder of ASAPP (CEO 2014-2024, now reportedly founder/advisor); per Crunchbase, founder & CEO of Conquest Labs (Bozeman, MT) - unverified by primary source
profile: University of Chicago math graduate who founded New York-based ASAPP in 2014 to build AI that makes contact-center agents 'radically' more productive rather than replacing them; backers included John Doerr and John Chambers and it reached unicorn status. He stepped back as ASAPP CEO in 2024 (Katie Stein is now CEO) and has reportedly started a new venture, Conquest.
interesting_fact: ASAPP built its pitch on augmenting rather than replacing humans: 'If we can automate half of this thing away, we can get to the same place by making people twice as productive.' Its speech tech came from a team led by a founding member of Apple's Siri speech group.
deep_cut_fact: He is a licensed pilot with a fondness for classical music, and before ASAPP he first applied his coding skills to his family's real-estate and financial business in Miami, building machine-learning systems to trade markets - which he found unfulfilling.
notes: Facts source is a repost of Alan Ohnsman's 2020 Forbes AI 50 profile (original on forbes.com). Conquest Labs info only from aggregators (https://crunchbase.com/person/gustavo-sapoznik). ASAPP PR may not reach him now that he's not CEO; LinkedIn likely the best direct route (not verified).

name: Marcus Westin
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of ASAPP; later co-founder/CTO of Aldyn (closed 2022); current role unclear (profiles say he now builds software for writers)
profile: Marcus Westin is a software engineer who co-founded New York AI customer-experience company ASAPP with Gustavo Sapoznik in 2014 and served as its founding CTO; ASAPP was valued at about $2bn per Hurun. Earlier he was a senior engineer at Meebo (2008), a founding engineer at Clover (2011) and founder of Flutterby Labs (2012). He no longer appears on ASAPP's leadership roster.
interesting_fact: ASAPP, which he co-founded, builds AI systems for large enterprise contact centres and was one of New York's early AI unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote WebViewJavascriptBridge, a widely used open-source iOS/OSX library for passing messages between Objective-C and JavaScript in web views; its README lists Facebook Messenger and Facebook Paper among apps that used it.
notes: Engineer-founder, low media profile; his GitHub is the most reliable self-published presence (search results also indicate @marcuswestin on X, not verified here). Not involved in ASAPP's current management (CEO is Gustavo Sapoznik), so ASAPP press is not a good route.

name: Ma Zheren
current_role: Founder and CEO, Inceptio Technology (Shanghai autonomous heavy-truck developer)
profile: Julian Ma (Ma Zheren), a veteran of Motorola, Tencent (corporate VP) and fleet-IoT firm G7 (president), founded Inceptio Technology in Shanghai in 2018. It builds full-stack L3 autonomous driving for heavy trucks, put series-production L3 trucks on the road with OEMs in 2021, and opened a German office in 2024.
interesting_fact: Inceptio's autonomous trucking system has logged over 500 million km in commercial operation on Chinese freight routes; in Feb 2026 Ma joined the China-Germany Economic Advisory Committee symposium with the Chinese premier and German chancellor.
deep_cut_fact: He started Inceptio at about 47 after three decades spanning China and the US in tech, consulting and strategy; he told IMD: 'The essence of entrepreneurship is to do what no one else has done in the past, whether it is technological innovation or business model innovation.'
notes: Goes by Julian Ma in English. Company also lists partner@inceptio.ai for business partnerships. Hurun unicorn founder (company ~$2bn); personal wealth not disclosed.

name: Qiu Yujing
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SemiDrive (芯驰科技), Nanjing
profile: Qiu Yujing (Maggie Qiu, 仇雨菁) co-founded Nanjing-based automotive chip designer SemiDrive in June 2018 with chairman Zhang Qiang, after leading automotive-grade chip R&D in China for NXP (and earlier Freescale). SemiDrive makes cockpit, ADAS, gateway and MCU chips for Chinese and overseas carmakers and is valued at about $2B as a Hurun unicorn.
interesting_fact: SemiDrive taped out China's first 16nm automotive-grade chip and broke into a cockpit-chip market where domestic firms had almost zero share; it has since won cockpit-chip supply deals with a European carmaker.
deep_cut_fact: SemiDrive was effectively a team spin-out: when rumours of Qualcomm's planned takeover of NXP threatened to break up her automotive-chip R&D team in 2018, Qiu and dozens of veteran colleagues walked out together and founded the company that June.
notes: English name Maggie Qiu. No published press/IR email found (private company). Possible route via SemiDrive's website or its investors. Automotive semiconductor angle; tangential to AI/data centers.

name: Yu Liang
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2021-2024) as the person behind CASICloud / 航天云网 (Casicloud Technology Development Co., Beijing); role not independently confirmed
profile: Hurun names 於亮 (Yu Liang) as founder of CASICloud (航天云网), the industrial-internet company set up in June 2015 by state aerospace group CASIC and affiliates to run the INDICS platform (INDICS 2.0 launched June 2021). As a CASIC subsidiary, its leaders are state-appointed executives, not private founders.
interesting_fact: CASICloud's INDICS platform is billed as one of China's leading national industrial-internet platforms and underpins CASIC's 'Digital Aerospace' strategy; INDICS 2.0 was unveiled at the International Industrial Internet Conference on 15 June 2021.
notes: Chinese name 於亮 per Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2021 and 2024 (hurun.net list data). Searches in Chinese (於亮/于亮 + 航天云网/航天科工 + 董事长/总经理) and English (Yu Liang + CASICloud) found no news or filing confirming his title; casicloud.com was unreachable from this session. Many unrelated 'Yu Liang's exist (Guilin Fuda, Guangzhou Finance Holdings, etc.), so don't conflate. Treat as unverified.

name: Pedro Castillo
current_role: Founder of Onum, now Falcon Onum inside CrowdStrike (deal announced Aug 2025, reported ~$290M); co-founder of Devo
profile: Spanish engineer Pedro (del) Castillo co-founded Devo (originally Logtrust) in Madrid in 2011, a cloud-native security data analytics platform that became Spain's first cybersecurity unicorn; he served as CEO and then about 11 years as CTO. In 2022-23 he founded Onum, a real-time security data pipeline company, which CrowdStrike agreed to buy in 2025 to feed its Falcon Next-Gen SIEM.
interesting_fact: CrowdStrike's 2025 purchase of Onum (reported at $290M) gave Castillo a second security exit after Devo; he said pipelines should 'transform data into real-time intelligence', not just move it.
deep_cut_fact: Before Devo he was security tech director, then CTO and head of tech innovation at Bankinter, where back in 2001 his team built an on-prem system to collect all the data the bank generated, the seed of the Devo idea. Devo spent two years building product before launching and came within days of running out of cash.

public_contacts.value: https://www.crowdstrike.com (onum.com now redirects to CrowdStrike's Falcon Onum page)

notes: Also appears as Pedro del Castillo / Pedro Muros Castillo. Since the CrowdStrike deal, CrowdStrike press relations is likely the route; his post-acquisition title not verified. MWC Barcelona speaker. Do not confuse with Peru's former president Pedro Castillo.

name: Sammy Krikler
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Insurance Officer and board member, Earnix
profile: Israeli statistician and co-founder (2001) of Earnix, whose AI-driven pricing and rating software is used by insurers and banks to price policies and loans. He is the only one of the three co-founders still at the company, which became a unicorn in 2021 after a $75M round led by Insight Partners.
interesting_fact: Earnix's CEO Udi Ziv has called Krikler 'the brains of the product'; of the three 2001 co-founders (with Yoni Cheifetz and Shai Fogel) he is the one who stayed for two decades-plus.
notes: Very low media profile. Aggregator profiles say he studied statistics at the Hebrew University and was R&D manager at Eventus Software before Earnix (unverified primary source). Route via Earnix press/marketing or LinkedIn.

name: Yoni Cheifetz
current_role: Partner, Lightspeed Venture Partners (heads Israel investment team); co-founder of Earnix
profile: Israeli software entrepreneur who co-founded insurance/banking pricing-analytics firm Earnix in 2001 with Sammy Krikler (valued ~$1B after Insight Partners' 2021 investment). Also co-founded or chaired Demantra (sold to Oracle), Agentics and Traiana; since 2006 he has led Lightspeed's Israel investing across AI, enterprise, fintech, climate and deep tech.
interesting_fact: A serial founder of nearly a dozen software companies before VC, including Demantra (acquired by Oracle), Agentics (acquired by Mercado) and Traiana (acquired by ICAP).
deep_cut_fact: Holds an MSc in applied mathematics and computer science from the Weizmann Institute, ran product management at ClickSoftware, and unwinds by kayaking and rowing: 'Somehow that makes me a better, or at least calmer, person.'
notes: Also listed as Jonathan Cheifetz in some filings. Says he tries to meet as many entrepreneurs as possible. Work email is the 'Get in Touch' link on his Lightspeed bio.

name: Chen Yuqi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Hai Robotics (Shenzhen)
profile: Chen Yuqi (Richie Chen) co-founded Hai Robotics in Shenzhen in 2016. The company makes autonomous case-handling robots (ACRs) for warehouse automation and was later valued at about $2B. He still runs it as CEO. Its HAIPICK and HaiClimber systems are deployed worldwide for customers such as DHL and Philips.
interesting_fact: Hai Robotics launched HAIPICK, billed as the world's first autonomous case-handling robot. The company says it raises warehouse storage density by 80-130%. Chen was named to Fortune China's 40 Under 40 in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Chen earned a BEng in Electronic and Information Engineering from Hong Kong PolyU in 2012. PolyU calls Hai Robotics the first unicorn nurtured under its entrepreneurship ecosystem.
notes: Known in English as Richie Chen. The company PR inbox is the best route.

name: Ben Christensen
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Handshake
profile: Michigan Tech alum ('14) who co-founded Handshake, the college-to-career recruiting network, with Garrett Lord and Scott Ringwelski in Houghton, Michigan. Handshake now connects ~20M students and alumni with 1M+ employers (valued ~$3.5bn) and has pushed into supplying expert talent for AI training work.
interesting_fact: Christensen nearly took a cybersecurity job at a Michigan company instead; the founders gave themselves three years to sign five schools or give up.
deep_cut_fact: He met Garrett Lord in a Michigan Tech outdoor adventure group; on early sales trips they often slept in a Ford Focus in McDonald's parking lots and once drove to Virginia and back for a single school visit.
notes: Low-profile co-founder (Crunchbase lists Denver base; previously Arbor Networks ASERT security research). Press office or Michigan Tech alumni connection are natural routes.

name: Garrett Lord
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Handshake
profile: Michigan native who co-founded Handshake, the college career network, in 2014 with Michigan Tech classmates Ben Christensen and Scott Ringwelski, leaving school a few credits short to raise capital. Handshake was valued at $3.5B (Series F, 2022). Since late 2024 he has pushed a 'refounding' via Handshake AI, which recruits domain experts to train AI models.
interesting_fact: He conceived Handshake AI at the company's 2024 Christmas party; the unit was projected to hit about $100M in annual recurring revenue, and he calls the pivot the 'refounding of Handshake'.
deep_cut_fact: At Michigan Tech he worked as a ski patroller at Mont Ripley, played broomball, and scavenged campus dumpsters for parts for his IT side business; he also cold-emailed recruiters to land a Palantir internship and won its summer hackathon.

public_contacts.value: Notion 'First Block' interview with Garrett Lord

notes: Very accessible founder with lots of interviews; Handshake AI (data-for-AI) angle relevant to a data-center/AI podcast.

name: Scott Ringwelski
current_role: Co-founder, Handshake (former CTO; current operating title not publicly stated)
profile: Traverse City, Michigan native and Michigan Tech software-engineering grad ('14) who co-founded Handshake, the college career network, with Garrett Lord and Ben Christensen in 2014 and served as its CTO. Handshake was valued at $3.5B in 2022; Ringwelski keeps a low public profile and is listed today simply as co-founder.
interesting_fact: Handshake was born at a small engineering school in Houghton, Michigan: the founders saw the opportunity gap versus Ivy League students; the platform grew to 18M students and 1,200 schools by 2021.
deep_cut_fact: While Lord and Christensen pitched colleges on the road, he stayed in Houghton building the product; he took the call from Wabash College that became Handshake's first client ('my first and only sales call'), and the first HQ was a rental house with a hole where a basement window should be.
notes: Very low public profile; co-founders call him 'the smartest person in all our CS classes'. Current role unclear (Handshake now lists a different CTO). Route via Handshake press or Michigan Tech alumni network.

name: Blake Hall
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, ID.me (McLean, Virginia)
profile: Former US Army Ranger and Harvard MBA who co-founded ID.me in 2010 (originally TroopSwap, a military deals site) with fellow Ranger Matt Thompson; renamed ID.me in 2013, it became a leading digital identity-verification network used by federal and state agencies and companies, valued around $2B. He remains CEO and a frequent voice on identity fraud policy.
interesting_fact: As a battalion reconnaissance platoon leader in Iraq he led some 450 combat patrols with no casualties in his platoon and received two Bronze Star medals before leaving the Army in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He applied to Harvard Business School on his battalion commander's push; Hall recalled deciding to 'apply to the best of the best if I'm going to do this.' ID.me began life as TroopSwap, a Groupon-style deals site for service members.

public_contacts.value: ID.mePR@rhstrategic.com (Raffetto Herman Strategic Communications, listed in 2022 release)

notes: Comfortable with media and podcasts (veteran-entrepreneur story). PR agency contact is from a 2022 release and may be outdated; check ID.me's newsroom for current press contact.

name: Matthew Thompson
current_role: President & Chief Commercial Officer, Socure (identity verification), since Dec 2025
profile: Former Army Ranger and Harvard MBA who co-founded ID.me (begun 2010 as TroopSwap, a military deals site) with HBS classmate Blake Hall and served as its COO/president; left in 2015. Later ran IDEMIA's North America identity business and held an identity role at Capital One, then joined Socure, building its public-sector business before becoming CRO and, in Dec 2025, President & CCO.
interesting_fact: ID.me began as an HBS project: Hall and Thompson, both Army veterans, struggled to claim veteran discounts online. Thompson had gone to Goldman Sachs in Los Angeles after his MBA but came back when Hall opened shop near D.C. in early 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three patents spanning mobile biometric liveness detection and tiered and third-party authentication, and was Socure's first public-sector leader, launching its government business.
notes: No longer at ID.me (left 2015 per Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ID.me); best route is via Socure's PR agency (Highwire). Common name - confirm via ID.me/Socure context.

name: Tanel Suurhans
current_role: Co-founder and Distinguished Engineer, ID.me (CTO 2014-2024)
profile: Estonian engineer who joined veterans' discount startup TroopSwap as co-founder in 2013 and helped rebuild it as ID.me, the digital identity wallet used by US federal and state agencies (valued ~$2B in 2021). He was CTO from 2014 until September 2024, when Scott Meyer succeeded him and he moved to Distinguished Engineer.
interesting_fact: Tallinn's city government celebrated ID.me as 'yet another unicorn co-founded by an Estonian', citing it as proof of Estonia's world-leading unicorn-per-capita record.
deep_cut_fact: ID.me began in 2010 as TroopSwap, a service founded by two former Army Rangers to verify veterans for discounts; Suurhans was brought on in 2013 as the Estonian technical co-founder who helped turn that log-in flow into a general identity network.
notes: Very low public profile; no published personal or press email found for ID.me (media seems routed through staff contacts). CTO transition source: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/idme-appoints-scott-meyer-as-chief-technology-officer-302242142.html

name: Lisa Riolo
current_role: Co-founder and advisor, impact.com (Santa Barbara)
profile: Affiliate-marketing veteran who was SVP of Business Development at Commission Junction before co-founding Impact Radius (now impact.com) in Santa Barbara in 2008. impact.com became a leading partnership-automation platform valued at ~$2B+; Riolo is described as co-founder and advisor and remains an industry speaker.
interesting_fact: She has 25+ years in affiliate/partnership marketing and was among impact.com's 2008 founding team alongside Per Pettersen, Roger Kjensrud, Todd Crawford and Wade Crang.
deep_cut_fact: Mixergy's Andrew Warner titled his interview with her 'The woman who paid me $1 million in affiliate revenue' from her Commission Junction days; she also co-founded workzones, a Santa Barbara co-working business.
notes: Low public profile; current operating role at impact.com unclear (listed as co-founder/advisor). Workzones detail is from Crunchbase bio.

name: Per Pettersen
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Strategy Officer and Board Director, impact.com
profile: Serial ad-tech entrepreneur who co-founded Commission Junction (an early affiliate network, sold to ValueClick), then Leadpoint and Savings.com. In 2008 he co-founded Santa Barbara-based Impact Radius (now impact.com), a partnership-automation platform later valued at ~$2B. He was CEO until 2017, when he became executive chairman and CSO; impact.com now lists him as CSO.
interesting_fact: Impact Radius was founded by a group of Commission Junction alumni: Pettersen, Wade Crang, Todd Crawford, Lisa Riolo and Roger Kjensrud (now impact.com's CTO). In effect, the team that built one of the first affiliate networks rebuilt the category a decade later.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he holds a BS in electrical engineering and an MS in computer engineering from UC Santa Barbara. impact.com's own bio says he 'was building partnership businesses before the industry had a name for what he was doing.'
notes: Santa Barbara-based. No personal channels or published press email found; the impact.com contact page or press-releases section is the route in. The UCSB degrees appear in aggregated bios (e.g. a 2026 impact.com release, per search snippets); the full bio text could not be fetched directly.

name: Roger Kjensrud
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, impact.com (Santa Barbara, CA)
profile: Norwegian-born engineer who co-founded partnership-marketing platform impact.com (founded 2008 as Impact Radius) and has led its engineering and product teams as CTO ever since; the company was valued at about $2B+. Earlier he was Director of Engineering at affiliate pioneer Commission Junction and co-founded Savings.com and Leadpoint.
interesting_fact: At Commission Junction he led the move of the original affiliate network onto a scalable Java-based infrastructure, before co-founding impact.com with fellow CJ alumni.
deep_cut_fact: His Dark Reading author bio notes that he is a former Norwegian ice fishing champion.
notes: Very low public profile and a technical (non-CEO) founder. Ice-fishing fact comes from the Dark Reading bio as shown in search snippets (page is bot-blocked, so I couldn't read it directly). Media contact is from a 2024 release and may be stale. Also linked to the Estalea venture vehicle with co-founder Per Pettersen.

name: Todd Crawford
current_role: Co-Founder and VP Strategic Initiatives, impact.com
profile: Affiliate-marketing pioneer who was on the founding team of Commission Junction (CJ) in 1998, later guided strategy for Digital River's OneNetworkDirect, and in 2008 co-founded Impact Radius (now impact.com), the Santa Barbara partnership-automation platform. He remains VP of Strategic Initiatives and co-hosts the company's Partnership Economy podcast.
interesting_fact: Industry peers call him the 'Godfather of Affiliate'; he was named to PartnerCentric/Hello Partner's Hero100 2025 as 'The OG Hero'.

current_role: Co-founder/board member, LandSpace; founder and chairman, MinoSpace; Chair Professor and Executive Dean, School of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

name: Shu Congxuan
current_role: Founder of Laoxiangji (Home Original Chicken), Hefei, Anhui (chairman in 2020; current formal title not confirmed)
profile: Former soldier who began raising chickens in Feixi, Anhui in 1982 and became one of the province's largest free-range chicken farmers. The chain now has about 1,400 stores and has repeatedly attempted an IPO; his children hold most of the stake.

notes: Chinese-language media only; reach via Laoxiangji corporate (Hefei). Reported to have transferred his direct shareholding to his children; daughter Shu Wen is an executive director.

name: Eric Larchevêque
current_role: Manager (gérant) and largest shareholder of TBSO (listed AI/fintech group); co-founder and former CEO/chairman of Ledger
profile: French serial entrepreneur since 1996 (Montorgueil, Prixing). Founded La Maison du Bitcoin in Paris, which merged with BTChip and Chronocoin in 2014 to form Ledger, the hardware crypto-wallet maker he led as CEO until 2019. Now an angel investor, TV investor on M6, and head of TBSO, which in 2026 dropped a bitcoin-treasury plan to build an AI/fintech group.

notes: Very public in French media and podcasts; best route is likely via TBSO investor relations or the M6 show/press. No published personal contact found in this pass. Recent interview: https://www.toutsurmesfinances.com/actualites/?p=799

name: Joel Pobeda
current_role: Co-founder of Ledger (former COO); no current public title confirmed
profile: French entrepreneur and one of four co-founders of Ledger, the Paris-based crypto hardware-wallet maker, alongside Eric Larchevêque, Thomas France and Nicolas Bacca. He served as COO in Ledger's early years, helping build its operations. His current activities are not publicly documented.

notes: Very low public profile; sources are mostly profile aggregators. Alive status assumed (no death reports found). Best route likely via Ledger press/comms or LinkedIn.

name: Nicolas Bacca
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, ZKNox (hardware security & zero-knowledge cryptography); angel investor
profile: French hardware-security engineer who co-founded Ledger (2014), the Paris crypto hardware-wallet unicorn, serving as CTO and from 2019 chief innovation officer until leaving in 2023. After briefly launching smart-wallet project Smoo.th, he co-founded ZKNox in 2025 with cryptographers from Ledger and Thales, and angel-invests in French crypto startups (Bitstack, Spiko, Bubblemaps, Hyli).
interesting_fact: He read the Bitcoin whitepaper in 2012 while holding a smart-card design that could store secrets but had no business model: 'Bitcoin gave me that. So I'm very grateful for Satoshi.'
deep_cut_fact: As a child he printed his own fake banknotes and 'paid' his parents with them ('I was kind of my own central bank'); today he's invested in a champagne house that pays dividends in bottles, and says he's famous for bringing champagne to every party.
notes: Long known in crypto by the handle 'btchip' (on Devcon profile) - personal X not independently verified here. Speaks regularly at Paris Blockchain Week, EthCC, Devcon; conference circuit is a natural route. Ledger's Recover controversy preceded his exit - avoid.

name: Thomas France
current_role: Co-founder of Ledger (board advisor per profile aggregators); founder/managing partner of Cygni Capital (crypto/trust-tech VC)
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Ledger, the Paris-based maker of crypto hardware wallets, in 2014 (Ledger later raised $380M in 2021 at unicorn valuation). Earlier he co-founded the shopping app Prixing. After stepping back from operations around 2019 he co-founded Cygni Capital, investing in blockchain, privacy and AI, and is an active angel investor.
interesting_fact: Ledger, which he co-founded in 2014, became one of France's best-known crypto unicorns, building secure hardware wallets for digital assets and raising $380M in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2014, with Eric Larcheveque, he opened La Maison du Bitcoin on rue du Caire in Paris, a physical venue for training in and buying cryptocurrencies, often described as Europe's first bitcoin space and a precursor to Ledger.
notes: Ledger press email is for the company, where he is no longer an operator. Cygni Capital has no confirmed official website; dates from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener, Dealroom) are inconsistent. Low media profile; appeared on the 'Can't Be Done' podcast (ep. 58).

name: Assaf Eisenstein
current_role: Co-Founder & President, Lusha
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Lusha, a B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform, with developer Yoni Tserruya in 2016. Lusha bootstrapped to profitability before raising a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation; Eisenstein oversees business operations (legal, finance, investment strategy) as president.
interesting_fact: Lusha began as a side project aimed at recruiters, but salespeople quickly became its main users; it grew from a Chrome extension into a data platform with 515M+ data entries and now an MCP/API layer for AI agents.
deep_cut_fact: Before Lusha he was an HR-tech founder (Lusha's own site calls him 'an HR tech creator'), having built employee-referral software in Tel Aviv - which is why Lusha was first pitched as a recruiting tool.
notes: Low public profile compared to CEO Yoni Tserruya. No published press email found; LinkedIn (linked from Lusha's About page) is best route. Lusha's name comes from a family nickname (avoid in outreach per rules).

name: Han bing
current_role: Legal representative, Rongxin Semiconductor (Ningbo) Co. (荣芯半导体, 'RSMC'); title (chairman/CEO) not confirmed
profile: Han Bing (韩冰) is listed by Hurun as founder of RSMC (荣芯半导体) and by registry data as legal representative of Rongxin Semiconductor (Ningbo), founded April 2021. Rongxin is a privately financed 12-inch foundry on 28-180nm specialty processes, with a Huai'an fab (producing since 2022) and a RMB 16B Ningbo line begun in 2025.

Ex-SMIC/Wuhan Xinxin chief Yang Shining chairs its technical committee.

No interviews, bio or press quotes found; company statements are issued in the company's name. Very low profile; no published contact found.

name: Allon Bloch
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, K Health (AI-powered primary care); independent director, Wix.com
profile: Israeli-American serial entrepreneur who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Ran Shaul. It uses AI models trained on large clinical datasets to power virtual primary care and has partnerships with health systems such as Northwell, Cedars-Sinai and Penn Medicine. Earlier he was co-CEO and president of Wix.com (2008-2010) and CEO of online car retailer Vroom (2014-2016).

name: Israel Roth
current_role: Co-founder (former CTO) of K Health; reported in 2023 to have stepped back from the CTO role to work as a chef

K Health builds AI-driven primary care (symptom checking and virtual clinicians) and was valued as a unicorn. Earlier he co-founded print-personalisation software firm XMPie and Labgoo.

name: Ran Shaul
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, K Health (New York / Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur (Tel Aviv University) who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Allon Bloch, Israel Roth and Adam Singolda. K Health uses AI trained on millions of anonymised medical records to power a symptom checker and virtual primary care, partnering with health systems such as Cedars-Sinai; it reached unicorn status. Shaul leads product.
interesting_fact: K Health's pitch is 'a doctor in your pocket': its AI compares a user's symptoms against millions of patient records to show how doctors diagnosed similar people, before routing them to a clinician - Shaul has explained the approach on podcasts such as The MAML Podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 he co-founded Pursway, an audience-targeting startup that mapped real-life relationships among 150m+ North American consumers using machine-learning and techniques borrowed from anti-terrorism link analysis; it was acquired by Interpublic (IPG) in 2015.
notes: Has done podcast interviews before (MAML podcast) - receptive to podcast format. Route via K Health press team.

name: Augusto Marietti
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kong Inc. (API and AI connectivity platform, San Francisco)
profile: Rome-born entrepreneur who started Mashape with schoolmate Marco Palladino in a rented Milan garage in 2009, moved to San Francisco after failing to raise money in Italy, and pivoted to an API marketplace. Mashape became Kong, whose open-source API gateway grew into an enterprise API/AI-gateway platform; Kong reached unicorn status (~$2B valuation).
interesting_fact: He and his co-founders lived on about $1,000 a month in Silicon Valley, gave themselves '90 days to make it or break it', and got their first break after cold-emailing hundreds of contacts from a Stanford entrepreneurship event list.

name: Marco Palladino
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Kong Inc. (San Francisco)
profile: Italian-born, self-taught engineer who co-founded API marketplace Mashape in Milan (2009-10) with Augusto Marietti, moved to San Francisco in 2011, and pivoted it into Kong, the open-source API gateway (2015) that became a cloud-native API and AI-connectivity platform. Kong passed $100m ARR and raised at a ~$2bn valuation in 2024; as CTO he now focuses on APIs for AI agents.

profile: Israeli engineer who co-founded cyber insurer At-Bay in 2016 with Rotem Iram and Roman Itskovich, serving as its first CTO; At-Bay pairs insurance with active security monitoring and reached unicorn status. profile: Israeli-born co-founder of At-Bay (2016, with CEO Rotem Iram), a cyber insurer that pairs policies with active security monitoring ('insure-sec'). As Chief Risk Officer he runs underwriting/risk and speaks publicly on cyber-market pricing discipline.
interesting_fact: At-Bay made Forbes' Fintech 50 list in 2023; Itskovich has publicly warned that 'irresponsible' competition in the cyber insurance market is unsustainable as threats rise.
deep_cut_fact: Before insurance he was VP of Financial Products at FX fintech Ebury, on Bain Capital's investment team, and a McKinsey consultant; he holds a BA in Economics and Accounting from Tel Aviv University and an HBS MBA.
notes: Has appeared on insurance podcasts (Behind the Growth, Making Risk Flow) - receptive to talking about cyber risk. Route via press@at-bay.com.

name: Rotem Iram
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, At-Bay (acquired by Munich Re, Aug 2026)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded cyber-insurance company At-Bay in 2016 with former McKinsey colleague Roman Itskovich; it pioneered 'InsurSec', pairing insurance with security scanning and monitoring, and hit a $1.35B valuation in 2021. Munich Re bought At-Bay for $575M in August 2026; Iram is based in Tel Aviv again after a decade in Palo Alto.
interesting_fact: He first ran into the cyber-insurance problem while at risk consultancy K2 Integrity after the Target data breach, which led to At-Bay's model of underwriting using external scans of client systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before McKinsey he was an officer in IDF Unit 8200 and a software engineer at RAD Data Communications, holds a computer-engineering BSc from the Hebrew University, and grew up in Herzliya after a childhood stint at Kibbutz Lehavot HaBashan.
notes: Recent exit to Munich Re (Calcalist, Oct 2026) was below peak valuation - avoid framing around valuation. WEF contributor (https://weforum.org/stories/authors/rotem-iram).

name: Tilli Kalisky-Bannett
current_role: Managing Partner, Pinegrove Venture Partners (formerly SVB Capital); co-founder, At-Bay
profile: Venture investor and co-founder of At-Bay, the cyber-insurance insurtech founded in 2016 and valued at ~$1.35B. She spent about 10 years as a partner at Greylock IL (now 83North) backing European and Israeli startups and now co-leads Pinegrove, a ~$10B multi-strategy venture platform spun out of SVB Capital.
interesting_fact: At-Bay, which she co-founded, insures companies against losses from cyberattacks and made the Forbes Fintech 50 in 2023 and 2024, with 35,000+ policyholders.
deep_cut_fact: Before investing she earned a magna cum laude BA in Psychology at Hebrew University, then an MBA at MIT; she now lives in Palo Alto.
notes: Investor-founder rather than At-Bay operator; one source says she is not in an active At-Bay leadership role. Best route is via Pinegrove (general inquiries address). Milken Global Conference 2025 speaker.

name: Adam Hotchkiss
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Plume (Palo Alto); interim CEO until April 2025
profile: Co-founded Plume at the end of 2014 with Fahri Diner, Aman Singla and Sri Nathan. Plume is a cloud-managed 'adaptive WiFi' and smart-home services platform sold through ISPs such as Comcast, Charter and Vodafone, reaching 65M+ locations, and was valued at ~$3B. He was interim CEO, then became CPO when ex-Comcast exec Daniel Herscovici was hired as CEO in April 2025.
interesting_fact: Plume's founding idea was to deconstruct the home router: move its 'brains' into the cloud and scatter small low-power pods around the home, an approach Plume calls 'Adaptive WiFi'.
deep_cut_fact: Before he became CPO, Plume's own technical whitepaper on its Adapt WiFi system listed him as 'Co-Founder, VP Product'. He has been the product mind behind the pods since day one.

public_contacts.value: ted_miller@tedmillergroup.com (Ted Miller Group, listed as Plume media contact)

notes: Low personal profile; best route is Plume corporate comms. Plume has done media interviews with him (e.g. plume.com interview on consumer engagement). The deep-cut fact is from search-result snippets of the whitepaper; the PDF itself was not opened.

name: Aman Singla
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Immersa (AI/data startup); co-founder of Plume Design
profile: Wireless-systems engineer who co-founded Plume Design (2014), the cloud-managed home Wi-Fi platform used by ISPs and valued at about $2.6–3B. Profiles list him as Plume's co-founder & CTO (2015–2020). Before that he was VP of Engineering at Qualcomm Atheros, after joining Atheros early. After a stint as an EIR at Mayfield he co-founded Immersa (2021), which applies AI to data.
interesting_fact: Plume's pitch was cloud-controlled, hardware-independent home Wi-Fi sold through ISPs, a natural next step from years building Wi-Fi chip software at Atheros/Qualcomm.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his PhD at Georgia Tech in 1997 under distributed-systems professor Umakishore Ramachandran, whose lab built experimental systems such as Beehive; earlier he studied at IIT Delhi and was on the technical staff at Silicon Graphics.
notes: Low public profile, and sources are mostly aggregators. Titles conflict: MarketScreener says 'Head-Engineering' at Plume, other profiles say CTO. TheOrg says he co-founded Plaksha University, but I couldn't confirm that on Plaksha's founders page (only page 1 checked). Don't confuse Immersa with Leia's 'Immersity'. No published direct contact found.

name: Fahri Diner
current_role: Co-founder (and longtime CEO) of Plume Design; Executive Chairman of Aliro (quantum networking) since June 2026
profile: Telecom entrepreneur who founded optical-networking firm Qtera, sold to Nortel in 2000 for $3.25B, then became a VC (Applied Materials Ventures, Sigma Partners). He co-founded Plume in 2014-15, building a cloud SaaS platform for smart home Wi-Fi sold through broadband providers, and in 2026 became executive chairman of quantum-networking startup Aliro.
interesting_fact: His first startup, Qtera (ultra-long-haul photonic networking), was acquired by Nortel Networks for about $3.25 billion at the height of the optical boom.
deep_cut_fact: In November 2002, after Qtera, he joined Applied Materials Ventures in Menlo Park as a general partner investing in early-stage communications companies.
notes: Whether he is still Plume CEO in 2026 is unclear (one profile lists CEO 2014-2024). Crunchbase lists his self-styled title as 'Chief Servant of Plume's people, Customers & Stakeholders'. Aliro press office is another route.

name: Sri Nathan
current_role: Co-founder, Plume Design (listed variously as Head of Business Development / VP Major Accounts)
profile: Networking-industry executive credited, with Fahri Diner, Adam Hotchkiss and Aman Singla, as a co-founder of Palo Alto-based Plume Design (founded 2014), the cloud-managed home Wi-Fi/smart-home platform sold through internet service providers and valued around $2-3B. Earlier he was president & CEO of Jasmine Networks and held roles at Menara Networks and other networking firms.
interesting_fact: Plume sells its 'pods' and cloud Wi-Fi software mainly through ISPs (e.g. Comcast, Charter) rather than directly to consumers.
notes: Very little public information; identity and current title based only on insider-data aggregators and job-board listings. Holds a doctorate from UT Austin and undergraduate degree from University of Madras per MarketScreener (unverified elsewhere). Route via Plume corporate comms.

name: Rajesh Ramanand
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Signifyd
