profile: Payments-risk veteran who co-founded Signifyd with Michael Liberty in 2011 after leading emerging-markets risk at PayPal. Signifyd sells guaranteed-fraud-protection and commerce-protection software to online retailers and reached unicorn status; Ramanand still leads it as CEO.
interesting_fact: Signifyd's model guarantees merchants against chargebacks on orders it approves, shifting fraud liability from the retailer to Signifyd.
deep_cut_fact: Before PayPal he spent years at FedEx working on payments and shipping risk; at Signifyd's 2013 launch he argued that 'a lot of merchants are declining good transactions' because of mismatched identity data.
notes: Goes by 'Raj'. Speaks at Signifyd's FLOW summit and on podcasts; no published press email found on signifyd.com.

name: Evan Doll
current_role: Rejoined Apple in 2016 as Director of Health Software Engineering (current role not confirmed by recent sources)
profile: Stanford 2003 grad who joined Apple as an engineer and worked on the original iPhone software (2003-2009). In 2010 he co-founded Flipboard, the magazine-style news app, with Mike McCue and led engineering/product; he left in 2015 for an EIR stint at Redpoint Ventures and returned to Apple in 2016 to direct health software engineering.
interesting_fact: Helped build the original iPhone's software as a senior iPhone engineer at Apple before leaving to co-found Flipboard, one of the breakout iPad apps of 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Healdsburg, California (Healdsburg High class of 1999, senior class president). While at Apple he taught an iPhone app programming class on the side and persuaded management to let him keep teaching: 'Teaching is a way to gain mastery.'
notes: Low public profile since returning to Apple; no recent interviews or published contacts. Apple employees rarely do outside media without Apple PR approval.

name: Mike McCue
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Flipboard
profile: American tech entrepreneur who never attended college: founded Paper Software (sold to Netscape for $20M in 1996), co-founded voice-browser Tellme Networks (acquired by Microsoft in 2007), then co-founded the Flipboard news-magazine app in 2010, which he still leads and has pushed into the open social web/fediverse.
interesting_fact: He gave up a congressional nomination to the US Air Force Academy to support his family after his father died, joined IBM on a six-month temp contract in 1986 and stayed three and a half years.
deep_cut_fact: His Netscape project to turn Navigator into a web-based desktop OS was codenamed 'Constellation' after a boat his father helped restore; he later bought a 48-foot classic wooden sailboat and named it Constellation too. His first app was a space-shuttle flight simulator written in TI-BASIC in 1981.
notes: Media-friendly; frequent podcast guest on the open social web. Press contact is the 'Contact Us' link on Flipboard's press page.

name: Martin Tolar
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Alzheon Inc. (Framingham, MA)
profile: Czech-born neurologist and neuroscientist who founded Alzheon in 2013 to develop ALZ-801, an oral tramiprosate-prodrug anti-amyloid Alzheimer's drug licensed from Bellus Health. Before that he was Yale neurology faculty, worked in business development at Pfizer, and ran CoMentis, NormOxys and Knome. He also founded Tolion Health, an AI brain-health company.
interesting_fact: He received his M.D. from Charles University in Prague, did a Ph.D. on apolipoprotein E in Alzheimer's, and was on The Medicine Maker's Power List 2016-2019.
deep_cut_fact: As a medical student in Prague he helped organize and lead the November 1989 Velvet Revolution that ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia; he later received the Czech Laurels Award (2021).
notes: Company email is a general corporate inbox, not a personal one. He sits on the CERGE-EI Foundation board, another possible warm route.

name: Eli Broverman
current_role: Co-founder, Treasury (early-stage fintech venture fund); co-founder of Betterment
profile: Securities lawyer who co-founded robo-advisor Betterment with Jon Stein in 2008, serving as President/COO and building its legal/regulatory structure, broker-dealer and 401(k) business. He stepped back from day-to-day operations in 2017 (staying on the board/advisory) and co-founded Treasury, an early-stage fintech fund with Acorns founders, which led Betterment's 2021 $60M Series F.
interesting_fact: Betterment's founders needed a lawyer willing to take risk: Stein realised automated advice needed a regulatory structure built from scratch, and Broverman, a lawyer who 'had been wanting to start something', built it at Stein's kitchen table.
deep_cut_fact: He first met Betterment co-founder Jon Stein at a poker table around 2003 - 'Little did I know that we would soon be working together at his kitchen table building a company...' He calls himself a masochist who loves a company's 'formative period'.
notes: Low public profile; no longer operational at Betterment so company press is an indirect route. Treasury fund (with Jeff Cruttenden/Acorns) is a better angle; Milken Institute speaker profile exists.

name: Jon Stein
current_role: Founder and chairman, Betterment (CEO 2008–Dec 2020); angel investor/advisor
profile: American fintech entrepreneur (Harvard BA, Columbia MBA) who founded Betterment, the pioneering robo-advisor, in 2008 after ~4 years at First Manhattan Consulting Group. He was CEO until December 2020, when ex-Viacom COO Sarah Levy succeeded him; he remains founder/chairman and advises and invests in startups.
interesting_fact: He launched Betterment on stage at TechCrunch's 2008 Startup Battlefield in the middle of the financial crisis, betting big banks would be distracted by lost trust; he was named to Fortune's 40 Under 40 in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: For the TechCrunch launch pitch he memorized his speech and practiced it about 50 times (he says he never memorized a speech again), overdressed, and got teased by Michael Arrington about his tie; Betterment's servers went live for the first time that day.
notes: Current day-to-day activities after stepping down as CEO are not well documented; a profile site mentions a new venture called 'Warmer' but this is unverified. In 2020 he said his next startup would not be in finance.

name: Eric Cheng
current_role: Co-Founder, Chairman & Group CEO, CARSOME (Kuala Lumpur)
profile: Malaysian entrepreneur who co-founded CARSOME in 2015 with Innity colleague Teoh Jiun Ee. It grew into Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform (Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore) and Malaysia's first tech unicorn, valued around $1.7B in 2021. He leads group strategy and sits on Endeavor Malaysia's board.
interesting_fact: An accounting-degree dropout, Cheng says he 'wasn't the smartest kid in the family'; Carsome was his third company after two short-lived ventures. He was EY Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year Malaysia 2019.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he started Clicks Communications, an ad network and creative agency, but sold his stake back to his co-founders within a year because he felt he had left Innity too soon - and went back to lead Innity's digital ad team before founding Carsome. His first venture (2008) was a print magazine with college friends.
notes: Active in SEA startup community and Endeavor Malaysia; Endeavor is a possible warm route.

name: Yin Jing
current_role: Founder and CEO, Cloudwise (云智慧, Beijing) - AIOps / IT operations and observability software
profile: Listed by Hurun as 'Yin Jing', the Cloudwise founder is Yin Jin (殷晋, 'Andy Yin'), CEO since 2010. Cloudwise began with the Jiankongbao (监控宝) website-monitoring SaaS for small businesses and grew into an AI-driven IT-operations platform for large enterprises; Sequoia China led its US$150m Series E in 2021, valuing it at about US$1bn.
interesting_fact: Cloudwise now pitches itself as 'Reliability for AI Infrastructure', selling AI agents for alert triage and autonomous incident resolution to 2,000+ enterprises.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cloudwise became an enterprise AIOps vendor, Yin co-founded and ran Jiankongbao (监控宝), one of China's early SaaS tools for monitoring small-business websites.
notes: Name discrepancy: Hurun 'Yin Jing' vs filings/press 'Yin Jin' (殷晋) / Andy Yin; same Cloudwise founder. The marketing mailbox is the international (Singapore) arm's published address; the Chinese site cloudwise.com was unreachable from here.

name: Lv Shijie
current_role: Founder, Cloudwise (云智慧), Beijing-based AIOps/observability software company
profile: Lv Shijie (吕士杰, Shijie Lyu) founded Cloudwise in Beijing in 2009, starting in application performance monitoring and growing into an AI operations platform (observability, incident resolution, ITSM/CMDB) used by 2,000+ enterprises. Hurun counted him among unicorn founders in 2021 when Cloudwise was valued at ~$1bn; the company now markets itself as 'reliability for AI infrastructure'.
interesting_fact: Cloudwise has repositioned from classic APM to AIOps for AI infrastructure, pitching AI agents that find root causes of IT incidents in seconds, a direct play on data-center reliability.
notes: Founder identity per CB Insights (lists Shijie Lyu as founder); some databases give other founder names (Yin Jin co-founder). Little English-language coverage of him personally; current title not confirmed. Company contact form is the published route.

name: Ren Yuancheng
current_role: Executive director (formerly chairman and CEO), Xinmai Semiconductor Technology (Hangzhou) Co. (芯迈半导体), which is seeking a Hong Kong IPO
profile: Ren Yuancheng (任远程), about 50, a power-electronics engineer, founded Xinmai Semiconductor in Hangzhou in 2019-20: a 'virtual IDM' power-chip firm backed by CATL and Xiaomi and valued around RMB 20bn (~$3bn). He was chairman/CEO until June 2025 (now executive director); the firm filed for a Hong Kong IPO a third time in July 2026.
interesting_fact: Xinmai's valuation went from a RMB 100m pre-money in August 2020 to RMB 5bn less than a month later, and reached about RMB 20bn within roughly three years, with CATL and Xiaomi among its investors.
deep_cut_fact: He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in engineering from Zhejiang University and a 2005 Virginia Tech PhD in electrical engineering. He ran a China subsidiary of Monolithic Power Systems (2006-13), then was VP at JoulWatt, and was named a provincial 'leading talent' by Hangzhou's Binjiang high-tech zone in 2014.
notes: Identity match is inferred: Hurun lists 'Jupiter' as a $3B semiconductor unicorn. Ren Yuancheng = 任远程, founder of Xinmai Semiconductor (valued about RMB 20bn, roughly $3B). I could not confirm 'Jupiter' as Xinmai's English name, so verify before outreach. No published contact found; the HKEX prospectus would list company contacts.

name: Kannan Muthukkaruppan
current_role: Co-founder and President of Yugabyte (distributed PostgreSQL database); some profiles list him as co-CEO with Karthik Ranganathan
profile: Database engineer. He spent 13 years on Oracle's PL/SQL compiler, then at Facebook built the HBase storage behind Messages, then worked on distributed storage at Nutanix. In 2016 he co-founded Yugabyte, maker of the open-source distributed SQL database YugabyteDB, with ex-Facebook colleagues Karthik Ranganathan and Mikhail Bautin, and was its founding CEO.
interesting_fact: He was the founding CEO of Yugabyte. In 2020 he handed the CEO role to Pivotal's ex-president Bill Cook and moved to President, Product Development. Before Yugabyte he spent about 13 years on Oracle's PL/SQL compiler and virtual machine team.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote Facebook's 2010 engineering post 'The Underlying Technology of Messages'. It explained why the team picked HBase over MySQL and Cassandra after weeks of benchmarking, to serve 350M users sending 15B+ messages a month.
notes: A technical founder who speaks at developer conferences (QCon, AsiaTechX). Sources conflict on his title (President vs co-CEO) and on whether Karthik Ranganathan is now sole CEO (May 2026 release), so confirm before outreach. The PR address was found through search excerpts of Business Wire releases; the pages themselves were blocked.

name: Karthik Ranganathan
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Yugabyte (previously CTO)
profile: Karthik Ranganathan (BS IIT Madras, MS UT Austin) was one of Facebook's early database engineers from 2007, working on Cassandra and as an Apache HBase committer. In 2016 he co-founded Yugabyte with ex-Facebook colleagues Kannan Muthukkaruppan and Mikhail Bautin to build YugabyteDB, an open-source, Postgres-compatible distributed SQL database for cloud-native and AI workloads.
interesting_fact: When he joined Facebook in 2007 it had roughly 30-40 million monthly users; by the time he left about six years later it had passed one billion, an experience that shaped YugabyteDB's focus on scale.
deep_cut_fact: He worked on Facebook's inbox-search store before it was open-sourced and is credited with naming it 'Cassandra'; he has been quoted saying he was 'fortunate enough to have given it its name'.
notes: Very accessible technical founder; frequent conference speaker (QCon, PGConf, Postgres Conference) and podcast guest (Last Week in AWS). Cassandra-naming claim comes from secondary profiles, so verify or soften before quoting it to him. Good data-infrastructure fit.

name: Mikhail Bautin
current_role: Engineer at Google Cloud (Cloud SQL), reportedly since Nov 2024; co-founder and former software architect of Yugabyte
profile: Stony Brook CS PhD and Apache HBase committer at Facebook (ran HBase for Facebook Messages and search indexing). Co-founded Yugabyte in Feb 2016 with Kannan Muthukkaruppan and Karthik Ranganathan; YugabyteDB is an open-source, PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL database (unicorn in 2021). After ~8 years building it he reportedly joined Google Cloud to work on Cloud SQL in Nov 2024.
interesting_fact: Called the quietest of Yugabyte's three ex-Facebook founders, he was the architecture-focused one who understood at code level where HBase and Cassandra diverged and broke under load, knowledge that shaped YugabyteDB.
deep_cut_fact: Before databases he worked on NLP: as a Stony Brook PhD student he co-authored 'International Sentiment Analysis for News and Blogs' (ICWSM 2008, with Lohit Vijayarenu and Steven Skiena), machine-translating news in nine languages and scoring entity sentiment with the Lydia text-analysis system.
notes: Low public profile; per a 2025/26 origin-story article he left Yugabyte in Nov 2024 for Google Cloud (Cloud SQL) via a LinkedIn update only (not independently confirmed). Yugabyte's PR agency (Inkhouse) is listed but is unlikely to route to him now. Hurun lists no net worth for him.

name: Mike Murchison
current_role: Co-founder of Ada; becoming Chief AI Officer of the combined Dialpad-Ada company (deal announced Nov 4, 2026, expected to close ~Nov 12, 2026)
profile: Toronto serial entrepreneur (U of T cognitive science/HCI) who co-founded Ada with David Hariri in 2016 after their previous startup, Volley, was swamped by support requests. As CEO he built Ada into a $1bn+ AI customer-service agent platform (clients incl. Pinterest, Square, monday.com). In Nov 2026 Ada agreed to combine with Dialpad; Craig Walker becomes CEO and Murchison Chief AI Officer.
interesting_fact: Before building Ada, he and co-founder David Hariri worked as customer-service reps at several fast-growing tech companies to understand the problem first-hand; Ada then went through the AI stream of the Creative Destruction Lab at U of T's Rotman School.
deep_cut_fact: As a U of T cognitive-science and human-computer-interaction student he was regularly inspired by Geoffrey Hinton's research and by Steve Mann's wearable-computing lab; he was also in an early cohort of The Next 36 entrepreneurship program and is a Forbes 30 Under 30 alum.
notes: Role change: as of mid-Nov 2026 Ada is merging into Dialpad; use 'co-founder of Ada, Chief AI Officer at Dialpad' once closed. pr@ada.cx and PAN agency contact came via search of Ada's media center (site blocks scripted fetch); pr@dialpad.com verified on the deal release. Articulate, podcast-friendly AI-agents founder.

name: Aaron Kalb
current_role: Co-founder, Alation (data catalog / data intelligence); recent profiles list him as Chief Strategy Officer (title unconfirmed for 2026)
profile: Aaron Kalb co-founded Alation in 2012 with Satyen Sangani, Venky Ganti and Feng Niu, bringing design and linguistics to a team of database/ML researchers. The company pioneered the modern enterprise data catalog and reached unicorn status. Kalb has been Alation's head of product, its first Chief Data Officer (2019) and Chief Data & Analytics/Innovation Officer.
interesting_fact: In 2019 Kalb became Alation's first Chief Data Officer, a co-founder 'drinking his own champagne' by running the company's internal data governance and analytics, and he went on a global tour to collect best practices from other CDOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alation, Kalb was a designer and researcher in Apple's Siri Advanced Development Group. He studied Symbolic Systems (BS and MS) at Stanford, and Alation's own history describes him as the 'designer and linguist' of its founding team.
notes: Current title is inconsistent across sources (CSO vs CDAO vs Chief Innovation Officer; one profile says the CDAO role ended Aug 2023), so confirm on LinkedIn before outreach. Also linked to Alchemist Accelerator as a partner/mentor. Alation's media center lists marketingwebrequest@ for marketing/media requests.

name: Feng Niu
current_role: Co-founder of Alation (2012) and Lattice Data (acquired by Apple); current role not confirmed from a primary source
profile: Feng Niu is a database and machine-learning researcher (Tsinghua CS; UW-Madison PhD) who co-founded data-catalog company Alation in 2012 with Satyen Sangani, Venky Ganti and Aaron Kalb. Alation reached about a $1.7-2B valuation. He also co-founded Lattice Data (DeepDive-based dark-data extraction) with Chris Ré, which Apple acquired in 2017; profiles say he then worked at Apple.
interesting_fact: Niu is a co-author, with Ben Recht, Chris Ré and Stephen Wright, of 'Hogwild!' (2011), the lock-free parallel SGD paper that won the NeurIPS 2020 Test of Time Award and shaped how large ML models are trained.
deep_cut_fact: Hogwild! was written while Niu was a UW-Madison PhD student in the optimization group of the Wisconsin Institute for Discovery, which was in its first months of operation at the time. Alation's founding story credits him and Ganti with seeing data-discovery problems first-hand in research and at Google.
notes: Low public profile, with no verified personal site or social accounts. Secondary profiles claim Apple Research Scientist (2017-2020) and later CEO of a startup called Evidently, but neither is verified. The Alation founding-team description is at https://www.alation.com/about. Good AI-infrastructure/data angle for the podcast.

name: Satyen Sangani
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Alation, Inc. (Redwood City, CA)
profile: Satyen Sangani, an economist by training and former Oracle VP for financial-services analytical applications, co-founded Alation in 2012 with Aaron Kalb (ex-Apple Siri), Feng Niu and Venky Ganti. Alation pioneered the enterprise data catalog and was valued around $1.7-2B; in 2026 it relaunched its platform as AIOS, aimed at governing data and AI agents.
interesting_fact: Alation's founding idea combined Sangani's economics/Oracle view that big-company users can't find or trust data with Kalb's Siri-era natural-language work; its first 2015 product let employees query enterprise data in plain English.
deep_cut_fact: He has hosted Alation's podcast since 2022: launched as 'Data Radicals', it was relaunched in July 2026 as 'AI Radicals' for its fourth season, with biweekly interviews of data and AI leaders.
notes: A fellow podcast host, so a podcast-swap or guest invitation could land well. Fit: data/AI infrastructure rather than energy. ashley.womack@alation.com is Alation's named media contact (Sr. Director, Corporate Marketing).

name: Venky Ganti
current_role: Snowflake (Head of Migrations, per Snowflake blog author page, 2026); co-founder of Alation
profile: Venky Ganti co-founded data-catalog company Alation and served as CTO, helping define the 'data catalog' category. He later co-founded Mesh Dynamics, worked at Google, and was SVP Product & Engineering at AI startup Numbers Station (acquired by Alation in 2025). He now works on data migrations at Snowflake.
interesting_fact: Before Alation he worked on Google's Dynamic Search Ads, building web-scale ML/data-enrichment pipelines, and at Microsoft Research he initiated and productized several projects.
deep_cut_fact: He holds more than 35 granted patents from his Microsoft Research years and earned his PhD in machine learning and databases at the University of Wisconsin-Madison after a BTech from IIT Madras.
notes: Hands-on technical founder; good fit for a data-infrastructure/AI episode. Current Snowflake title taken from search snippet of snowflake.com blog author page (could not fetch directly). No net-worth figure; Hurun lists him via Alation's valuation.

name: Alex Cornell
current_role: Director of Design, Generative AI, Meta (per his own website)
profile: Alex Cornell is a San Francisco interface designer, filmmaker and musician. In 2011 he co-founded Firespotter Labs, which built UberConference and became Dialpad; he was creative director and design lead there. He later founded Cocoon (acquired by Substack in 2021), designed the Substack and Linear mobile apps, and now leads generative-AI design at Meta.
interesting_fact: Firespotter won TechCrunch Disrupt in 2012. Outside product design, his music has over 25M plays on Spotify/YouTube, and his best-known photos are of a flipped iceberg in Antarctica.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups he spent three years as an apprentice to Scott Hansen (ISO50 / Tycho), writing for the ISO50 blog and running the studio. In 2012 he published a book with Princeton Architectural Press.
notes: A designer-cofounder, not a typical UHNW profile; Hurun lists him as a Dialpad founder. Very approachable: he publishes a personal email. Angle: designing generative-AI products at Meta and the UberConference/Dialpad origin story.

name: Brian Peterson
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Dialpad
profile: Software engineer who co-founded Dialpad (originally UberConference) in 2011 with CEO Craig Walker, after both worked on Google Voice. He led engineering as SVP and in April 2021 became Dialpad's first CTO, overseeing its AI-powered calling, meetings and contact-center platform. In November 2026 Dialpad agreed to combine with the AI customer-service firm Ada in an all-share deal.
interesting_fact: Dialpad has pushed AI into its own engineering: in a 2026 HumanX interview he described a company-wide AI mandate, including that engineers should not write code without AI assistance.
deep_cut_fact: Before Dialpad he was a senior software engineer at Google and built the front end of Google Voice, the product that grew out of Craig Walker's startup GrandCentral, which Google acquired.
notes: Hurun lists him as a Dialpad unicorn co-founder. The Dialpad-Ada merger was announced on 4 Nov 2026 (https://www.dialpad.com/press/dialpad-and-ada/), so his title may change. The HumanX page now returns 404; the AI-mandate detail is from search snippets. Common name: be sure to reference Dialpad. A good engineering-leader guest on AI adoption.

name: Craig Walker
current_role: Founder and CEO, Dialpad (AI-powered business communications / contact center)
profile: Craig Walker is a former M&A lawyer turned three-time founder. He ran the first Dialpad Communications (sold to Yahoo) and co-founded GrandCentral, which Google bought in 2007 and relaunched as Google Voice. After leaving Google he founded today's Dialpad in 2011, an AI-native communications and contact-center platform valued at about $2B with roughly 1,500 staff. It is now pushing agentic AI with Google Gemini integrations.
interesting_fact: He co-founded GrandCentral, the startup Google acquired in 2007 that became Google Voice.
deep_cut_fact: His career started in door-to-door dictation-equipment sales, which he credits for his grit. He then worked at Apple, went to law school, and did M&A at Wilson Sonsini before becoming a founder.
notes: A frequent podcast guest and open about founder lessons, so likely receptive. A June 2026 Dialpad release also lists pr@dialpad.com. His LinkedIn is linked from his official Dialpad author page.

name: John Rector
current_role: Unclear. Former co-founder, VP Engineering and board director, Dialpad; aggregator profiles disagree on his current role (VP Engineering at Warp vs. Sr Director of Engineering at Reddit).
profile: Listed as a technical co-founder of Dialpad (founded around 2011 as UberConference/Switch, with Craig Walker and Brian Peterson), where he was VP Engineering (telephony) and a board director. Dialpad became an AI cloud-communications company valued at about $2B. He reportedly studied CS at Stanford and is named on several Dialpad patents.
notes: Low public profile, and all biographical data comes from aggregator sites (theorg, zerogtalent, patentleaderboard). Treat the details as unverified. Some profiles also claim earlier GrandCentral/Yahoo work, which I could not verify. dialpad.com was unreachable from this environment. The likely route is a professional network or Dialpad press.

name: Matt Vincett
current_role: Longtime CEO of LifeMiles / Avianca Chief Loyalty Officer (2010 to at least late 2023); current role unverified after Avianca named new LifeMiles leadership in 2025
profile: Matt Vincett built LifeMiles, the Avianca-TACA frequent-flyer programme, as its CEO from 2010, launching it in March 2011 and leading its 2015 carve-out and partial sale to Advent International at a valuation of about $1B+. Avianca bought the whole business back in 2020. LifeMiles had more than 11 million members in 2023 and earns most of its money selling miles to banks and retailers.
interesting_fact: He describes LifeMiles as a business that sells miles to banks, partners and retailers more than an airline perk; by 2023 it had 11M+ members and co-branded cards in 10 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Before LifeMiles he was an airline man at TACA, serving as Commercial VP, VP of TACA's regional airlines and Director of Strategy & Business Development (per Avianca IR management bio).
notes: In Feb 2025 Avianca named Valeria Yglesias SVP Loyalty & managing director of LifeMiles, and later Jaime Manso to lead LifeMiles, so Vincett has probably moved on; his bio is gone from Avianca's current IR page (the TACA background came from an earlier version). Very low public profile; LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Felipe Delgado
current_role: Co-founder (CFO/President), Merama; partner and board member, Beetmann Energy
profile: Mexican finance executive who co-founded Merama in 2020, a Mexico City/São Paulo group that acquires and scales leading Latin American e-commerce brands; its 2022 Series B valued it at $1.2B. Before that he was CEO/CFO of Beetmann, a Mexican wholesale-electricity supplier and renewable-energy developer using AI/IoT to optimise energy use.
interesting_fact: He has an energy background unusual for an e-commerce founder: he ran Beetmann Energy, a qualified supplier in Mexico's wholesale electricity market that develops renewable plants, and remains a partner and board member there.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in J.P. Morgan's US Oil & Gas investment-banking group, holds a UT Austin BBA (Walter B. Smith Scholar) and a Harvard MBA, and is a keen runner who has completed two marathons; Quién named him a 'Titan of Business' among its 50 people transforming Mexico (2022).
notes: Strong energy-podcast angle via Beetmann. Titles vary by source (CFO vs President). Low media profile; LinkedIn or Merama is the route.

name: Guilherme Nosralla
current_role: Co-founder, Merama (São Paulo / Mexico City)
profile: Brazilian growth/marketing executive who co-founded Merama in 2020, a Latin American e-commerce group that takes majority stakes in leading online consumer brands and scales them across marketplaces. Merama became a unicorn about a year after founding, valued at ~$1.2B after a $60M Series B extension led by Advent and SoftBank in Dec 2021.
interesting_fact: Merama hit a US$1.2B valuation roughly one year after launch, one of the fastest unicorn runs in Latin America; the round also funded Merama Labs, an in-house unit for building new businesses.
notes: Low public profile; founding-team lists vary (Sujay Tyle is CEO; Renato Andrade, Felipe Delgado, Olivier Scialom also cited). A Web Summit Rio 2025 speaker page (now 404) said he was previously Growth Strategy Director at mobile-game maker Wildlife Studios; unverified. No published press email found; reach via Merama website/LinkedIn.

name: Olivier Scialom
current_role: Co-founder, Merama (role since 2021 not confirmed)
profile: French entrepreneur Olivier Scialom co-founded Merama in December 2020 with Sujay Tyle, Felipe Delgado, Renato Andrade and Guilherme Nosralla. Merama is a Latin American e-commerce roll-up that buys majority stakes in leading online brands while their founders keep running them. It raised a $60M Series A and a $225M Series B in 2021 and became a unicorn.
interesting_fact: Merama raised its $225M Series B only about five months after its first round, becoming one of Latin America's fastest e-commerce unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: Before Merama, Scialom co-founded Petsy, a Mexican pet-focused e-commerce site that was sold to Maskota.
notes: Very low public profile and his current role isn't confirmed. Sujay Tyle is the company's public face. No published contact was found. Merama's website (merama.io) returned almost no content.

name: Renato Andrade
current_role: Co-founder, Merama; reportedly CEO of Omniteca since 2025 (directory listing only, unverified)
profile: Brazilian ex-McKinsey consultant (USP business degree, INSEAD MBA) who co-founded Merama in Dec 2020 with Guilherme Nosralla and others. Merama buys majority stakes in independent brands selling on Amazon/Mercado Libre across Latin America and became a unicorn in Dec 2021 at a $1.2bn valuation after Advent and SoftBank-backed rounds.
interesting_fact: Merama reached unicorn status less than a year after founding, with a $60m Series B extension valuing it at US$1.2bn.
deep_cut_fact: He and Nosralla met at McKinsey (Renato spent 5+ years there serving retail/consumer clients); the Merama idea came after they read about a funding round for US brand aggregator Perch and found nothing similar in Latin America.
notes: Current role uncertain: theofficialboard.com lists him as CEO of Omniteca (joined 2025) - verify via LinkedIn before outreach. Common name in Brazil; match via Merama/McKinsey/INSEAD. No published direct contact found.

name: Sujay Tyle
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Merama (Latin American e-commerce brand builder/aggregator)
profile: US-born serial founder who entered Harvard at 15, left as a 2011 Thiel Fellow, and worked at Scopely before moving to Berlin to co-found Frontier Car Group (emerging-market used-car marketplaces), acquired by OLX/Naspers in 2019. He then co-founded Merama, which acquires and scales consumer brands selling on Mercado Libre and Amazon across Latin America, reaching unicorn status.
interesting_fact: He was a freshman at Harvard by age 15 and left in his junior year to become one of Peter Thiel's original '20 Under 20' fellows.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008, as a teenager, he co-founded ReSight with his older brother Sheel, a venture aimed at democratizing eye-care services.
notes: No published personal/press contact found; Merama's website has no press email. Route via Merama or Frontier Car Group investors.

name: Deepak Diwakar
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, Mindtickle (revenue-enablement software; HQ San Francisco, engineering in Pune)
profile: IIT Bombay computer-science grad (2008) who started as a machine-learning/platform engineer at ad-tech startup PubMatic, then co-founded Mindtickle in Pune in 2011-12 with Krishna Depura, Nishant Mungali and Mohit Garg. Mindtickle became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1.2B) selling sales-readiness and revenue-enablement software; he runs technology and operations as COO.
interesting_fact: Mindtickle helped define the 'sales readiness' software category and was named a Leader in the Forrester Wave for Revenue Enablement Platforms (Q3 2024).
deep_cut_fact: At IIT Bombay he wrote three of the four Performing Arts Festival (PAF) productions during his time there; he is a keen cyclist and nature lover whose mantra is 'Truth, honesty, and transparency build trust, and trust builds transformation.'
notes: Some sources list him as CTO; Mindtickle's own leadership page says COO. Older press releases cite a pr@ Mindtickle mailbox but I could not verify it on a live page, so it is omitted. Recognised by IIT Bombay alumni awards page.

name: Krishna Depura
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mindtickle (San Francisco / Pune)
profile: Indian-born engineer and ISB MBA (Class of 2006) who co-founded Mindtickle in 2011 with former PubMatic colleagues Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali. Mindtickle grew from a gamified employee-learning tool into a revenue-enablement and sales-readiness platform, valued at over $1B; he leads it as CEO, now pushing AI coaching and role-play products.
interesting_fact: Before Mindtickle he spent about five years at startups building photonic and semiconductor chips, then worked at Infinera, Microsoft (program manager) and ad-tech firm PubMatic (Director of Products until 2010).
deep_cut_fact: In a 2012 ISB alumni profile he said Mindtickle came 'after ten years of trying, failing and learning,' wished he'd started his entrepreneurial journey during his ISB days, and named his fondest ISB memory as alumni worldwide making the 'world's first wiki movie' Sapney.
notes: Also writes occasional TechCrunch contributor pieces (techcrunch.com/author/krishna-depura). Personal interests per ISB profile: travel and water sports.

name: Mohit Garg
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, OLOID (passwordless workforce identity, Sunnyvale CA); co-founder of Mindtickle
profile: One of four co-founders (with Krishna Depura, Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali) of Pune-born Mindtickle, which pivoted from gamification to onboarding to sales enablement and became a unicorn in Aug 2021. In 2018 he co-founded OLOID, a passwordless/physical-identity platform for frontline workers, which has raised ~$23M Series A/A1 from Dell Technologies Capital, Honeywell, Okta Ventures and Yaletown.
interesting_fact: Mindtickle was the product of three pivots: it began in 2011 as a gamification platform, moved to employee onboarding, then to sales-rep productivity before reaching a $1B+ valuation.
deep_cut_fact: The Mindtickle idea began with online 'treasure hunts' the founders ran for fun - they later converted those treasure hunts into a way to engage and onboard new employees.
notes: Now focused on OLOID rather than Mindtickle (listed as Mindtickle co-founder/advisor). Appeared on Founder Thesis podcast ('Once Tickled, Twice OLOID'). No dedicated press email found; OLOID site has Contact Us form/newsroom.

name: Nishant Mungali
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Mindtickle
profile: Indian product designer-turned-founder who co-founded Mindtickle (Pune/San Francisco) in 2011 with Krishna Depura, Mohit Garg and Deepak Diwakar. The company grew from gamified onboarding into a sales-readiness and revenue-enablement platform, reaching unicorn status in 2021 (~$1.2B); he leads product.
interesting_fact: He recalls that at launch Mindtickle 'had difficulty landing one client, let alone five' and leaned on its network and a pilot program for its first referenceable customers.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Almora in the Kumaon hills of Uttarakhand, he studied at IIT Guwahati and took his first job at investment firm D. E. Shaw in Hyderabad (as a UX designer) before the four co-founders started dabbling with the Mindtickle idea in 2010.
notes: Mindtickle 2025 releases name individual media contacts without emails; older releases show a generic pr(at)mindtickle address that I could not confirm on a live page, so not listed. Route via Mindtickle newsroom (https://www.mindtickle.com/blog/news_tax/news).

name: Darpan Sanghvi
current_role: Founder, CoFounder Circle (AI-native startup acceleration/venture studio platform, India)
profile: Mumbai-based entrepreneur who founded MyGlamm in 2015 and built it into the Good Glamm Group, a content-to-commerce beauty conglomerate valued at $1.2B in 2021 (backers incl. Warburg Pincus, L'Occitane, Amazon). After the group was broken up by lenders in 2025, he launched CoFounder Circle, an AI-native accelerator for startups and MSMEs, and judges on JioHotstar's 'Pitch To Get Rich'.
interesting_fact: He is credited with pioneering the 'content-to-commerce' model in India's beauty industry, buying media/influencer platforms POPxo, Plixxo and ScoopWhoop to sell MyGlamm products; the group later launched Wyn Beauty with Serena Williams.
deep_cut_fact: While studying engineering at MIT Pune he worked at Baazee.com, the Indian auction site later bought by eBay; he later did a dual MBA at ESADE (Barcelona) and UT Austin.
notes: Sensitive: Good Glamm Group collapsed in July 2025; he pledged part of future earnings/CoFounder Circle equity to make stakeholders whole. Avoid as an opener. Likely official site cofoundercircle.com (unconfirmed link to him); LinkedIn is his main public channel.

name: Priyanka Gill
current_role: Founder & CEO, COLUXE (lab-grown diamond jewellery brand, launched 2025); co-founder, Good Glamm Group (MyGlamm)
profile: A former London-based journalist, Gill turned her blog eStylista into POPxo, a digital community for Indian women, after moving back to India in 2014. POPxo/Plixxo merged with MyGlamm in 2020 and became part of the Good Glamm Group in 2021, where she ran the media and content arm. She was later a venture partner at Kalaari Capital, then left in early 2025 to found COLUXE.
interesting_fact: COLUXE pitches AI-powered personalisation, virtual try-ons and modular jewellery, and has backers including Ajai Chowdhry (HCL co-founder) and Startup Sherpas.
deep_cut_fact: Born in a village in Punjab and an English Literature graduate of Lady Shri Ram College, she wrote for The Guardian, The Independent and Vogue India in London. She co-chaired the Pratham Gala (2009-10), which raised over GBP 3M. Her early collection of modern Indian art later sold at Christie's first auction in India.
notes: Media-friendly and active on social media. Her current focus is COLUXE (consumer/luxury), not the Good Glamm Group, so lead with COLUXE or her founder journey rather than Good Glamm's recent difficulties.

name: Michael Dombowsky
current_role: Co-founder, co-inventor and (per TheOrg) SVP Building Technology, Nexii Building Solutions; current status after Nexii's 2024 restructuring unclear
profile: Saskatchewan-born builder and inventor who co-founded Vancouver green-construction company Nexii (2017/18) with Ben Dombowsky and Stephen Sidwell. He invented its 'Nexiite' panelised low-carbon building system, which carried a unicorn valuation in 2021. Profiles credit him with 40+ years of designing and building residential, commercial and institutional projects.
interesting_fact: He is described as the inventor behind Nexii's whole-building system: prefabricated panels made of 'Nexiite', a concrete alternative pitched as cutting building emissions and construction time.
notes: Sensitive: Nexii entered CCAA creditor protection in Jan 2024 and was sold and relaunched under interim CEO Bill Tucker (SBIZ, Aug 2024); his role since then is unconfirmed. The 'unicorn' valuation is historical. A profile claim that he designed the Tunnels of Moose Jaw could not be verified, so I left it out. Very low public profile.

name: Ed Felten
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Offchain Labs (developer of Arbitrum); Robert E. Kahn Professor of CS and Public Affairs emeritus, Princeton
profile: Princeton computer scientist and security researcher who was the FTC's first Chief Technologist (2011) and Deputy US CTO in the Obama White House (2015-17). In 2018 he co-founded Offchain Labs with former Princeton students Steven Goldfeder and Harry Kalodner; its Arbitrum rollup became the largest Ethereum layer-2. He served on the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board until January 2025 and still keynotes events like EthCC 2026.
interesting_fact: As the US government's witness in United States v. Microsoft, he demonstrated in court a tool built with two students that removed Internet Explorer access from Windows 98, rebutting Microsoft's claim that it couldn't be done.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a physicist: after a Caltech BS in physics (1985) he spent three years as a staff programmer on a Caltech parallel-supercomputer project before his CS PhD at the University of Washington, where his thesis was on communication protocols between parallel processors.

public_contacts.value: Freedom to Tinker (blog he founded/writes for): https://freedom-to-tinker.com

notes: Princeton email is from his (older) self-published faculty homepage, written as 'felten at cs dot princeton dot edu'; may be less monitored now. Frequent podcast guest and conference speaker, so a podcast invitation fits him well. Also a NAE member and former EFF board member.

name: Harry Kalodner
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, Offchain Labs (Arbitrum)
profile: Princeton computer-science PhD researcher who co-founded Offchain Labs in 2018 with Ed Felten and Steven Goldfeder to commercialise their Arbitrum research. Arbitrum became the most widely used Ethereum layer-2 rollup; Kalodner leads Offchain's engineering and technical vision.
interesting_fact: Arbitrum began as an academic project: the three founders developed the technology at Princeton and published it as a 2018 paper before forming the company.
deep_cut_fact: As a Princeton PhD student he was lead author of BlockSci, an open-source blockchain analysis platform (2017 paper 'BlockSci: Design and applications of a blockchain analysis platform').
notes: Technical founder; appears on crypto podcasts (e.g. Masters of Web3).

name: Steven Goldfeder
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Offchain Labs (now branded Offchain), developer of Arbitrum
profile: Computer scientist who earned a Princeton PhD in cryptocurrency security and, after a Cornell Tech/IC3 postdoc, co-founded Offchain Labs in 2018 with Ed Felten and Harry Kalodner to commercialise the Arbitrum research project. Arbitrum became the largest Ethereum layer-2 rollup; he continues to lead the company as CEO.
interesting_fact: Arbitrum began as an academic research project at Princeton before being spun out as Offchain Labs, which raised at a $1.2B valuation in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: As a Princeton PhD student advised by Arvind Narayanan, he co-authored the widely used textbook 'Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies' (Princeton University Press) alongside Narayanan, Bonneau, Felten and Miller.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (Bankless, Castle Island, Fintech Blueprint) - receptive to long-form interviews.

name: Avi Shua
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Innovation Officer and board member, Orca Security
profile: Israeli cybersecurity veteran (Unit 8200/IDF, then a decade-plus at Check Point, rising to Chief Technologist for threat prevention). Co-founded Orca Security in 2019 and was CEO until March 2023, building its agentless 'SideScanning' cloud security platform to a ~$1.8B valuation; he now leads innovation (SideScanning, Unified Data Model) as CIO.
interesting_fact: Orca's core idea, 'SideScanning', reads cloud workloads' block storage via the cloud provider's APIs instead of installing agents, giving full-stack visibility without touching running workloads.
deep_cut_fact: On CyberWire's 'Career Notes' he said he has been excited about cybersecurity since age 13, when he started probing his high school's network, and advised 'try to do things by yourself'.
notes: info@orca.security is Orca's general company email, not personal. Frequent conference speaker/podcast guest on cloud security, so a podcast invite fits his pattern.

name: Ety Spiegel Hubara
current_role: Co-founder, Orca Security (listed on org charts as Head of SRE)
profile: Israeli engineer and one of eight co-founders of Orca Security, the agentless cloud-security platform founded in 2019 (largely by ex-Check Point colleagues) and valued at about $1.8B in 2021. She has kept a low public profile, working on the site-reliability/engineering side rather than as a company spokesperson.
interesting_fact: Orca Security was founded by eight co-founders and reached unicorn status within about two years, joining the Israeli unicorn club in late 2020/2021.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Orca's About page publishes a general info@orca.security address; better route may be via CEO Gil Geron or Orca PR.

name: Gil Geron
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Orca Security
profile: Israeli cybersecurity executive who co-founded Orca Security in 2019 with Avi Shua, serving as chief product officer before becoming CEO in 2023. Orca pioneered agentless cloud security (its patented SideScanning approach). Before Orca he spent nearly 11 years at Check Point.
interesting_fact: Orca was co-founded by a group of senior Check Point veterans; Geron was promoted from CPO to CEO in 2023 to drive 'efficient growth'.
deep_cut_fact: His last role at Check Point (2017-2019) was overseeing its cybersecurity gateway and cloud products, capping nearly 11 years at the company before he left to start Orca.
notes: Frequent conference and podcast guest on cloud/AI security; reachable via Orca comms.

name: Hadas Amitay
current_role: Listed co-founder of Orca Security (current role not publicly documented)
profile: Hadas Amitay appears (sometimes as 'Amitay Hadas') in founder lists of Orca Security, the Tel Aviv-founded agentless cloud-security (CNAPP) company started in 2019 by eight colleagues largely from Check Point, which reached a $1.8B valuation in 2021. No public biography, title or current role was found.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by eight co-founders - unusually large for a startup - most of them former Check Point colleagues, and pioneered 'SideScanning', agentless cloud-workload scanning.
notes: Very low public footprint; only insider-data aggregators (MarketScreener) list the name. Name order/spelling inconsistent. Public faces of Orca are CEO Avi Shua and Gil Geron - route via them/company press.

name: Liran Antebi
current_role: Co-founder and (founding) Chief Architect, Orca Security; current title not confirmed
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded cloud-security company Orca Security in 2019 with Avi Shua, Gil Geron and Matan Ben Gur, all Check Point Software veterans. Orca's agentless 'SideScanning' cloud-security platform raised large rounds and reached a ~$1.8B valuation. Antebi keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by a team of former Check Point executives and architects; Antebi and Matan Ben Gur were the founding 'chief architects' when the company emerged from stealth with a $6.5M seed round in 2019.

public_contacts.value: Inkhouse on behalf of Orca Security: orcasecurity@inkhouse.com (per a 2026 Orca press release; verify)

notes: Not listed on Orca's current leadership page (orca.security/about), so he may have stepped back from an executive role. No interviews found. Aggregators claim ~16 years at Check Point before Orca, unverified by a primary source. Route via Orca press.

name: Jia Jiaya
current_role: Founder and Board Chairman, SmartMore (思谋科技); Chair Professor, HKUST and Dean of its von Neumann Institute
profile: Hunan-born computer-vision scientist (b. 1978; PhD HKUST 2004), ex-CUHK tenured professor and head of Tencent YouTu X-Lab, who founded SmartMore in 2019. SmartMore sells AI vision 'industrial agents' for inspection in EV batteries, autos, rail and electronics; a unicorn within two years, it filed for a Hong Kong IPO in March 2026.
interesting_fact: His lab produced LongLoRA (2023), a widely used technique for extending LLM context length, and the open-source multimodal model DreamOmni2 (2025); he has 200+ papers and over 100,000 citations.
deep_cut_fact: A keen photographer, in 2002 as an HKUST student he spent scholarship money on one of the early digital cameras; frustrated by the image quality, he wondered if algorithms could dehaze, deblur and denoise photos - the question that launched his computer-vision career.
notes: Accessible academic-founder; day-to-day SmartMore CEO is co-founder Shen Xiaoyong. SmartMore is in an HKEX IPO process (filed Mar 2026) - may limit what he can say. global@smartmore.com is a general company inbox; academic route via HKUST also possible.

name: Shen Xiaoyong
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, SmartMore (思谋科技)
profile: Chinese AI entrepreneur and CEO of SmartMore, an industrial machine-vision and AI company founded in 2019 with his former CUHK doctoral supervisor, Prof. Jia Jiaya, and a core team from Tencent's YouTu Lab. SmartMore sells AI inspection and smart-manufacturing systems to clients such as Bosch, Canon and P&G. It raised about US$200M in 2021 and reached a ~$1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: SmartMore's founding team largely came from Tencent YouTu Lab, which Jia Jiaya joined from CUHK in 2017; Shen was one of Jia's CUHK students before becoming CEO of the spin-out.
notes: global@smartmore.com appears on the company's international site and is a general company inbox, not his personal one; sales@ and product@ are on smartmore.com/contact. Sources differ on whether Jia Jiaya or Shen is called 'founder'. Mostly covered in Chinese media (36Kr, QbitAI).

name: Liu Shu
current_role: Co-founder and technology lead (CTO), SmartMore (思谋科技)
profile: Liu Shu (刘枢) co-founded Shenzhen/Hong Kong industrial-AI company SmartMore with CUHK professor Jia Jiaya and Shen Xiaoyong, and leads its R&D, including the IndustryGPT multimodal industrial model and AI visual-inspection equipment for manufacturing. SmartMore became a unicorn after large early funding rounds; he was named to Hurun's Under-30 entrepreneurs lists in 2020 and 2021.
interesting_fact: His R&D team at SmartMore has an average age under 30 and builds industrial-model-powered AI inspection machines that the company says reach 99.99% accuracy.
deep_cut_fact: Colleagues nickname him 'Co哥' ('Brother Co') because, as a PhD student, he won five MS COCO competition titles; his PANet paper (CVPR 2018, with Jiaya Jia) took 1st place in the COCO 2017 instance-segmentation challenge.
notes: 'Co哥' nickname and 5-title claim from Shenzhen Special Zone Daily (sznews, May 2025; page not directly fetchable here, quoted via search). PANet authorship/COCO 1st place verified on arXiv. global@smartmore.com is a general company inbox on the site, not specifically press. Chinese outreach preferred.

name: Li Ruiyu
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of SmartMore (思谋科技); a company directory lists a 'Ruiyu Li' as co-founder & head of product - not confirmed by an official source
profile: Hurun names Li Ruiyu among the founders of SmartMore, the Hong Kong/Shenzhen industrial-AI unicorn founded in 2019 by CUHK professor Jia Jiaya with former students including CEO Shen Xiaoyong, which sells machine-vision and AI inspection systems to manufacturers. No official bio of Li was found on SmartMore's site or in press coverage.
interesting_fact: SmartMore was founded in 2019 by CUHK computer-vision professor (and ex-Tencent YouTu X-Lab head) Jia Jiaya and his former PhD students, and has been dubbed Hong Kong's new hi-tech poster child.
notes: Could not confirm Chinese name or role from an official source; possibly the CUHK PhD 'Ruiyu Li' who co-authored with Jia Jiaya, but unverified - do not use in outreach without confirming. global@smartmore.com is SmartMore's general company inbox.

name: Wu Gansha
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, UISEE Technology (驭势科技; listed in Hong Kong, 2026)
profile: Wu Gansha (吴甘沙), born 1976 in Nantong, Jiangsu, holds a Fudan CS master's and spent 16 years at Intel, ending as head of Intel Labs China, before co-founding UISEE in 2016. UISEE skipped robotaxis to focus on L4 autonomy in closed sites like airports, factories and mines, and listed in Hong Kong in 2026 at ~RMB 10B.
interesting_fact: UISEE's contrarian bet on commercial vehicles in closed scenarios paid off: H1 2026 revenue was about RMB 163M (+64.9% YoY) with a ~53% gross margin; Wu says his main daily question is simply how to 'stay alive'.
deep_cut_fact: He likes to argue autonomy in unit economics: how expensive a driver is in Europe and how many drivers one unmanned vehicle replaces, pitching the near-zero marginal cost of an 'AI driver' sold like software.
notes: Articulate, media-friendly founder who speaks at conferences (World Robot Conference etc.); good fit for AI/autonomy angle. UISEE's site lists pr@uisee.com for media and an IR site (ir.uisee.com).

name: Peng Jinzhan
current_role: Co-founder, deputy general manager and head of innovation business division, UISEE Technologies (驭势科技, HKEX: 1511)
profile: Peng Jinzhan (彭进展) is one of five co-founders of UISEE (驭势科技), a Beijing L4 autonomous-driving company focused on closed scenarios such as airports and factories. Ex-Intel engineer; co-founded UISEE in Feb 2016 with Wu Gansha. UISEE listed on HKEX (1511.HK) in May 2026; Peng is a controlling shareholder (~2% stake) and part of the acting-in-concert founder group.
interesting_fact: UISEE was started in February 2016 in a garage in Beijing's Fangshan district by ex-Intel colleagues Wu Gansha, Zhou Xin and Peng Jinzhan plus Zhao Yong and Jiang Yan; in 2019 it began the world's first routine driverless baggage-logistics operation at Hong Kong International Airport.
deep_cut_fact: Before UISEE, Peng was lead system architect for Intel's Edison chip platform, which won four awards at CES 2014, and directed the Robotics System Lab at Intel China Research Institute. He studied computer science at Huazhong University of Science and Technology (1999) and Beihang (master's, 2002).
notes: Chinese name 彭进展. Identity confirmed via HKEX prospectus (May 12, 2026), Directors and Senior Management section. Not a board director; low public profile. Spoke at TIC 2021 as co-founder/chief system architect. Business contact on site: winfuture@uisee.com.

name: Jiang Yan
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of UISEE (驭势科技, HKEX 01511); current role not verified - he is not named on UISEE's current board or management page
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder lists (2021-2025) name Jiang Yan as a founder of UISEE Technology, the Beijing autonomous-driving company led by co-founder, chairman and CEO Wu Gansha. UISEE focuses on driverless logistics in airports and factories (tractors, shuttles, delivery vehicles), passed 11.2M km of fully driverless operation by Oct 2026, and listed in Hong Kong in May 2026.
interesting_fact: UISEE says it was the first company to run commercial 'truly driverless' operations (no safety driver) at airports and factories, starting in 2019, and passed 11.2M km of such operations by October 2026.
notes: Common name; I could not confirm his current role from an official source (web-search quota exhausted), and UISEE's site now names only Wu Gansha as co-founder. Verify before outreach; route via UISEE media mailbox pr@uisee.com. Autonomous-logistics rather than energy/data-center fit.

name: Hitesh Sheth
current_role: President and CEO, Vectra AI (San Jose, CA)
profile: Networking veteran who leads AI threat-detection company Vectra AI (formerly Vectra Networks) as president and CEO, building it into a $1B+ unicorn. Previously COO of Aruba Networks, EVP/GM of switching at Juniper, and a senior switching executive at Cisco (metro Ethernet), after roles at Liberate Technologies and Oracle.
interesting_fact: Vectra bills itself as the team behind 'the world's first AI-based cybersecurity platform'; its threat labs showed in 2016 that consumer Wi-Fi webcams could be reprogrammed into persistent network backdoors.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a Unix programmer at the Santa Cruz Operation (SCO) after earning a BA in Computer Science from the University of Texas at Austin.
notes: Hurun lists him as founder; Vectra's own bio describes him as president & CEO (he joined early rather than being a day-one founder). Best route: Vectra media room / InkHouse PR. Security-for-AI and data-center network angle.

name: Marc Rogers
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, nbhd.ai (AI observability startup); Head of Security, DEF CON
profile: British security researcher and white-hat hacker who co-founded Bay Area security startup Vectra (now Vectra AI; formerly TraceVector/Vectra Networks). Career spans a decade at Vodafone, Lookout, Cloudflare (head of security) and Okta (VP cybersecurity strategy). Now co-founder/CTO of nbhd.ai and senior technical advisor at the Institute for Security and Technology.
interesting_fact: His research hacks include Apple's TouchID (iPhone 5 and 6), Google Glass and, with Kevin Mahaffey in 2015, the Tesla Model S; in 2020 he co-founded the COVID-19 CTI League of volunteer hackers protecting hospitals, and received a President's Volunteer Service Award in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Most of the DEF CON community knows him simply as 'CJ'. He has been hacking since the 1980s, was once a CISO in South Korea, and as technical advisor helped create the on-screen hacks for USA's 'Mr. Robot' and the BBC's 'The Real Hustle'.
notes: Vectra co-founder status confirmed by his own bio (marcrogers.org) and Wikipedia's Vectra AI infobox; one career profile shows him as Vectra VP Security/CISO 2013-2014. He is no longer at Vectra (CEO is Hitesh Sheth). His site invites people to reach out via social media. Beware confusion with Purdue professor Marcus K. Rogers.

name: Chris Lynch
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Arsenal Collective (defense-hardware venture fund); co-founder and former CEO, Rebellion Defense
profile: Seattle serial entrepreneur hired by Defense Secretary Ash Carter in 2015 to found the Pentagon's Defense Digital Service. Left DDS in April 2019 and co-founded AI/software firm Rebellion Defense with Oliver Lewis and Nicole Camarillo; it hit a $1B valuation in 2021. Now runs Arsenal Collective, a VC fund for weapons, munitions and defense manufacturing startups, with Capital Factory's Joshua Baer.
interesting_fact: At DDS he created Hack the Pentagon, the first federal bug bounty program, and helped launch the JEDI cloud program; Ash Carter called him the Pentagon's resident hoodie-wearer.
deep_cut_fact: Arsenal's bio credits him with building and fielding the first man-packable counter-drone hardware for CENTCOM and INDOPACOM. In 2019 he said: 'If the nerds don't show up and work on the mission of national defense...then I'm not sure who will.'
notes: Arsenal fund launched at Capital Factory's FSN 2026 event. He did a Nov 2025 interview on 'The Briefing Room' podcast about DDS, Rebellion and Arsenal. Common name, so make sure you have the defense-tech Chris Lynch (LinkedIn handle lynchseattle). Rebellion's later troubles (reported by Forbes, 2023) are best avoided in outreach.

name: Nicole Camarillo
current_role: Listed as a co-founder of Rebellion Defense (Washington, DC defense-AI software); current role not verified
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder list (2021-2024) names Nicole Camarillo as a founder of Rebellion Defense, a defense-tech software company started in 2019 by former Pentagon Defense Digital Service people that builds AI and cybersecurity software for the U.S. and UK militaries, valued at ~$1B in 2021. Her current position could not be verified.
notes: Thin record: the web-search quota ran out and Rebellion's site has no team page, so her role and background could not be sourced. Company-level inquiries email only (she may no longer be with the company). Verify her current role before outreach.

name: Xie Xiaoliang
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2021-2025) as a co-founder of CalmCar (天瞳威视, Suzhou); not on CalmCar's current management team
profile: Hurun's Global Unicorn Index 2021-2025 named Xie Xiaoliang (谢晓靓) alongside Wang Xi and Li Hao as founders of CalmCar, a Suzhou-based (est. 2016) software-centric ADAS/autonomous-driving company valued at ~US$1.1B. CalmCar supplies L2-L2+ driving/parking and cockpit-monitoring solutions to 23 car brands and runs L4 Robobus/Robotaxi pilots. Hurun's 2026 list dropped her name.
interesting_fact: CalmCar says it was China's second-largest software-centric provider of combined highway-driving and parking ADAS in 2024, serving 23 car brands and nearly 200 models, and launched ConnectOne, billed as the first L4 robotaxi on Horizon Robotics' Journey 6 chip.
notes: Her role could not be verified: CalmCar's management page lists Wang Xi (chairman/CEO), Wang Ruoyu, Yuan Jin, Xu Jie, Tao Zhiheng and others, but not Xie; Hurun 2026 replaced her with Wang Ruoyu. Company appears to be preparing a listing (IR pages 'coming soon'). Contacts are the company's. Auto-ADAS, weak data-center fit.

name: Jochen Ziervogel
current_role: Co-founder of Enpal (Berlin); Crunchbase lists him as Co-Founder and Head of Partner Management (Mario Kohle is CEO)
profile: WHU alumnus and one of three co-founders (with Mario Kohle and Viktor Wingert) of Enpal, the Berlin solar company founded in 2017 that sells and rents rooftop PV, batteries and heat pumps to households. Enpal became Germany's first greentech unicorn in 2021, reached about EUR 960M revenue in 2023 and has installed ~115,000 solar systems; the company says it is still founder-led.
interesting_fact: Enpal was founded in 2017 under the name 'Evergreen' and drew early backing from Princeville's climate fund, which is supported by Leonardo DiCaprio; in 2021 it became Germany's first greentech unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2021, as Enpal was scaling, he was the guest on Tech.eu Podcast #219, 'The photovoltaic expansion', discussing solar panels and the future of green energy in Europe.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Mario Kohle; reach via Enpal press office. Prior career (per Crunchbase) included banking and BMW roles, not independently verified. Enpal restructured in 2026 (layoffs, Hamburg site closure); avoid that topic.

name: Viktor Wingert
current_role: Co-founder and managing director (board member), Enpal B.V., Berlin
profile: Co-founded Berlin solar company Enpal in 2017 with Mario Kohle and Jochen Ziervogel. Enpal sells/rents rooftop solar, batteries, wallboxes and heat pumps to German households, reached ~EUR 960M revenue in 2023, and is building what it calls Europe's largest virtual power plant by trading customers' flexible demand on the power exchange.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Enpal became Germany's first green-tech 'unicorn'; an early backer was Princeville's climate fund supported by Leonardo DiCaprio - its first-ever investment in a German company.
deep_cut_fact: Enpal was founded in 2017 under the name 'Evergreen Energy'; the founders started small, installing their first solar systems themselves before scaling into a heat-pump and virtual-power-plant business.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Mario Kohle; route via Enpal press office. Virtual power plant / grid flexibility angle fits the energy podcast. Personal social accounts not verified this pass (search budget exhausted).

name: Avi Baum
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Hailo (Tel Aviv-based edge-AI processor company)
profile: Israeli chip architect who co-founded Hailo in 2017 after serving as CTO for Wireless Connectivity at Texas Instruments and in senior architecture roles in the Israel Defense Forces. Hailo designs low-power AI accelerators and vision processors (Hailo-8, Hailo-10H with on-device generative AI, Hailo-15) used in cameras, cars, PCs and the Raspberry Pi AI HAT; it reached a ~$1B unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Hailo's chips power the official Raspberry Pi AI Kit/AI HAT add-ons, putting dedicated neural-network accelerators in the hands of hobbyists, and its Hailo-10H brings LLMs/VLMs onto edge devices.
deep_cut_fact: He argues TOPS is no longer the right yardstick for edge AI: for generative models, memory bandwidth matters more, and each product needs its own 'power-cost-latency working point' (Unite.AI interview, Aug 2025). He also writes on the DRAM shortage's effect on edge AI.
notes: Accessible technical leader who regularly blogs and gives interviews (hailo.ai/blog). LinkedIn is linked from Hailo's own leadership page. Edge-AI counterpoint to data-center AI; good on power-efficiency and memory-bandwidth topics.

name: Hadar Zeitlin
current_role: Listed as a co-founder of Hailo (Tel Aviv edge-AI chipmaker); not on Hailo's current leadership team page
profile: Hurun (2021-2024) lists Hadar Zeitlin as a founder of Hailo, the Israeli maker of edge AI processors (Hailo-8, Hailo-10 and vision processors), founded in 2017 and valued at about $1B. Hailo's current leadership team (CEO Orr Danon, CTO Avi Baum) does not include him; his current role could not be verified.
interesting_fact: Hailo says it was founded in 2017 to bring deep-learning compute, then largely confined to costly, power-hungry data centers, onto small edge devices - the opposite of the data-center build-out trend.
notes: Personal bio not verified (web search quota exhausted; no Hailo page names him). Company contacts reach Hailo, not necessarily him - he may have left the company. Check LinkedIn manually before outreach.

name: Orr Danon
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Hailo Technologies (Tel Aviv edge-AI chipmaker; acquired by Microchip Technology, completed Sept 2026)
profile: Orr Danon co-founded Hailo in Tel Aviv in February 2017 with Avi Baum, Hadar Zeitlin and Rami Feig, and became CEO after Feig's passing. Hailo designs low-power AI processors for edge devices - the Hailo-8 accelerator, Hailo-15 vision processors and Hailo-10H generative-AI module - and became a unicorn with its $136M Series C in 2021. Microchip Technology agreed to buy Hailo in July 2026 and closed the deal on 21 Sept 2026.
interesting_fact: Hailo went from a $3.5M seed round in 2017 to a $1B valuation in 2021, and its Hailo-10H powers what ASUS billed as the world's first USB edge-AI accelerator.
deep_cut_fact: At Calcalist's AI Conference in Sept 2025 he argued AI's next frontier is embodied systems: 'What's really big in AI today is undoubtedly the cloud, but the issue of AI entering the physical world is a revolution no less significant,' adding that China's robot competitions 'feel like the moments before ChatGPT.'
notes: Hailo's site still lists him as CEO, but his role post-Microchip acquisition (Sept 2026) should be checked. Strong fit for an edge-vs-datacenter AI compute conversation; regular conference speaker (CES, Calcalist). info@ is a general company inbox.

name: Jeffrey Spector
current_role: Co-founder and President, Karat (technical-interviewing and workforce-intelligence company, Seattle)
profile: Co-founded Karat in 2014 with Mo Bhende (now CEO) to re-engineer the technical interview for software engineers, outsourcing structured interviews to professional 'Interview Engineers'. Karat, valued around $1B, now pitches AI-native simulations and workforce intelligence for engineering leaders in the 'human + AI era'; Spector serves as President.
interesting_fact: Karat says it works with 7 of the 25 largest public companies in the world, 4 of the 7 largest payment companies and all 4 of the largest UK banks, having run hundreds of thousands of technical interviews.
deep_cut_fact: Spector and Bhende were friends who founded Karat around a shared belief that access to career growth is too often limited by where a person went to school, who their friends and family are, or past work experience - so they set out to make the technical interview itself more objective.
notes: Fit for data-center/AI podcast is indirect (hiring/talent in the AI era). Route via press@karat.com.

name: Mohit Bhende
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Karat (Seattle technical-interviewing / Human+AI hiring platform)
profile: Mohit 'Mo' Bhende co-founded Karat in 2014 with Jeffrey Spector to re-engineer how software engineers are interviewed; Karat runs technical interviews for large enterprises and reached unicorn valuation in 2021. Before Karat he was a senior director at Microsoft working on Xbox product strategy (including in China), and a strategy consultant at Oliver Wyman.
interesting_fact: Karat built a professional class of 'Interview Engineers' who conduct technical interviews on behalf of client companies, and in 2025 it pushed into AI-era hiring with products such as Partner Talent Solution for grading contractor engineers.
deep_cut_fact: He was in the very first cohort of Gates Cambridge Scholars (2001), doing an MPhil in Economics at Trinity Hall. In 2024 he spoke at a Gates Cambridge/Cambridge in America event in Seattle about purposeful leadership.
notes: Press contact in Karat releases: Gordie Hanrahan, Sr. Director Communications (press@karat.com). He also co-founded Seattle-based Topic Magazine (per secondary profiles, not verified). Gates Cambridge annual report 2024 lists him as a 2001 first-cohort scholar. Don't confuse Karat with Karat Packaging or Karat Financial.

name: Oleg Rogynskyy
current_role: Founder and Board Member, Backstory (formerly People.ai); Jason Ambrose is now CEO
profile: Oleg Rogynskyy founded People.ai in 2016, an AI platform that automatically captures sales activity (emails, meetings, calls) into CRM data and turns it into revenue insights; it reached unicorn status (~$1B valuation per Hurun). The company has since rebranded as Backstory, an 'AI answers platform for sales teams'; Rogynskyy remains founder and board member while Jason Ambrose runs it as CEO.
interesting_fact: People.ai, now Backstory, says it has spent more than a decade training AI models on billions of sales interactions, and was named a Challenger in Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Revenue Action Orchestration.
notes: No longer CEO, so company PR may not route to him; his own domain olegrogynskyy.com redirects to his LinkedIn, the best direct route. Current new ventures not verified (web-search quota exhausted mid-lane). Fit: AI/sales data, not energy.

name: Jonathan Webb
current_role: Co-founder of Pharmapacks (later renamed Packable); co-founder and CEO of Packable per directory profiles; current activity unverified
profile: Jonathan Webb is one of five co-founders of Pharmapacks (2010, New York), which grew from a Bronx pharmacy operation into one of Amazon's largest US third-party sellers of health and beauty products and was valued at about $1B. It was renamed Packable, an e-commerce enablement company, and he is listed as its co-founder and CEO. His background is in spirits and luxury marketing and sales.
interesting_fact: Pharmapacks went from a Bronx retail pharmacy to one of the biggest sellers on Amazon in the US, built by a small group of friends.
deep_cut_fact: Before e-commerce, he co-founded LeSutra, a sparkling liqueur launched in 2012 with music producer Timbaland and Grey Goose co-founder Tom Bruno, with fellow future Pharmapacks co-founder Adam Berkowitz.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Packable (ex-Pharmapacks) went through Chapter 11 in 2022 after a planned SPAC deal fell through, so avoid framing outreach around the company's valuation. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Jordan Feldman
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Rightway (New York)
profile: Harvard-educated former Goldman Sachs banker who co-founded Rightway (c.2017), a New York healthcare-navigation and pharmacy-benefits company combining clinician-led support with an app to help members find high-quality, cost-efficient care. Rightway reached a unicorn valuation and Feldman remains CEO.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Rightway with his father, physician Dr. Theodore Feldman (its chief medical officer); his father's experience as a doctor inspired the clinician-led model.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he worked on Goldman Sachs' Mortgage Trading and Investment Banking teams, then left to help found RedBird Capital Partners, Gerry Cardinale's private-equity firm; he holds an A.B. in Government and Economics from Harvard.
notes: Speaks at Conference Board events; reachable via Rightway's press/marketing team or LinkedIn.

name: Theodore Feldman
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Medical Officer, Rightway (New York)
profile: Dr. Ted Feldman is a Miami cardiologist who co-founded Rightway in 2017 with his son, CEO Jordan Feldman, to give employees physician-backed help navigating healthcare. Rightway has since become a transparent pharmacy-benefits (PBM) alternative valued at over $1B, and was reported in Sept 2026 to be eyeing an IPO after new funding.
interesting_fact: Rightway's founding story is a family one: Jordan Feldman grew up with a cardiologist father at his side and saw how transformative expert clinical guidance could be, so the two set out to give every member that access.
deep_cut_fact: A Harvard College and Albert Einstein College of Medicine graduate, he trained in cardiology at the University of Miami/Jackson Memorial and has served as medical director of the South Miami Heart Center and Baptist Health South Florida's Center for Healthy Living.
notes: Practising physician with low media profile; son Jordan Feldman (CEO) is the public face. Rightway's about page says media inquiries go to info@rightwayhealthcare.com; press page also lists press@. Deep-cut bio is from a CME faculty page (Miami cardiologist Theodore Feldman) - matches but not explicitly linked to Rightway there.

name: David Cummings
current_role: Founder, Atlanta Tech Village; founder/CEO, Atlanta Ventures
profile: Atlanta serial entrepreneur David Cummings co-founded marketing-automation firm Pardot, which was sold to ExactTarget (later Salesforce) for $95M in 2012. He then co-founded SalesLoft with Kyle Porter. Salesloft reached a $1B+ valuation before Vista Equity bought it. He now runs the Atlanta Tech Village startup hub and the Atlanta Ventures fund.
interesting_fact: Atlanta Tech Village, which he founded, is billed as the Southeast's largest tech entrepreneur center. Its alumni include SalesLoft, Calendly and Terminus. He was an early investor in Calendly.
deep_cut_fact: A Tallahassee, Florida native with an economics degree from Duke, he has founded 10+ companies. Besides software, they include Intown Golf Club, an Atlanta indoor golf venture.
notes: Very accessible. He has blogged on davidcummings.org for years and is active on X. Atlanta Tech Village and Atlanta Ventures are natural routes in.

name: Kyle Porter
current_role: Founder and board member/former chairman, Salesloft (now merged with Clari); LP at Stage 2 Capital
profile: Atlanta entrepreneur who co-founded sales-engagement platform Salesloft in 2011 out of Georgia Tech's ATDC and led it as CEO through Vista Equity's ~$2.3bn acquisition (2021). He stepped down as CEO in 2023 (David Obrand succeeded him) and stayed on the board; Salesloft agreed to merge with Clari in 2025.
interesting_fact: Porter insisted Salesloft stay an 'Atlanta unicorn', refusing investor pressure to relocate; early culture perks included rotating a Porsche 911 to the top sales rep each month.
deep_cut_fact: Salesloft killed its original, most profitable product, the lead-scraping tool Prospector, because customers were using it for spam, betting the company on Cadence, then a tiny ~$75k business, which became the flagship.
notes: Active in Atlanta startup ecosystem (Endeavor Atlanta board per directories) and appears on podcasts; LinkedIn is the most direct published route.

name: Rob Forman
current_role: CEO coach (listed with Scalebound); independent board member (e.g., Grayscale); co-founder & former President, Salesloft
profile: Atlanta software engineer-turned-founder who co-founded Salesloft, the sales engagement platform, serving as head of technology and later President & Chief Strategy Officer. Vista Equity Partners acquired Salesloft in December 2021 for $2.3B. He now coaches CEOs on organizational health and execution and sits on company boards.
interesting_fact: Salesloft, which he co-founded and served as President, was acquired by Vista Equity Partners in December 2021 for $2.3B.
deep_cut_fact: Before Salesloft he co-founded HireIQ, a call-center hiring and machine-learning analytics company, serving as its CTO; it was later acquired by Verint Systems.
notes: Faith-driven entrepreneur active in the Praxis network; LinkedIn is the best published route. Board roles (Grayscale, Hubstaff) per aggregators, unverified on primary sources.

name: Tim Dorr
current_role: Co-founder of Salesloft; Atlanta startup investor/engineer (Techstars Atlanta MD 2022-24, later co-chair; current employer reported inconsistently)
profile: Georgia Tech-rooted Atlanta engineer who co-founded sales-engagement platform Salesloft (2011, with Kyle Porter and Rob Forman) and served as its original technical architect/CTO; Salesloft reached unicorn status and was sold to Vista Equity in 2021. In March 2022 he became Managing Director of Techstars Atlanta (with Cox Enterprises), backing local founders.
interesting_fact: On taking the Techstars Atlanta job he said he wanted to 'pay back into the ecosystem that has gotten me this far' and that he looks for 'the less-than-perfect founder, that 95% founder.'
deep_cut_fact: He is a long-time open-source maintainer of Redux, the JavaScript state-management library used by millions of web apps; his npm handle 'timdorr' sits on the Redux package maintainer list alongside creator Dan Abramov (gaearon) and Mark Erikson.
notes: Current day job unclear: aggregator profiles mention a principal-engineer role at 8th Light (2025) and Techstars Atlanta co-chair; verify before outreach. Very approachable in Atlanta tech circles (ATDC EIR, Atlanta Tech Village advisor). No published email found.

name: Jacob Boudreau
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Stord (Atlanta)
profile: Co-founded Atlanta-based Stord in 2015 with CEO Sean Henry out of Georgia Tech's CREATE-X student incubator; Stord started as a peer-to-peer storage idea and pivoted into an on-demand warehousing network and now a 'cloud supply chain' (fulfillment, OMS, software) for consumer brands. A 2025 Series F valued it around $3B. Boudreau leads technology as CTO.
interesting_fact: Stord came out of Georgia Tech's CREATE-X student startup program, and Atlanta security entrepreneur Chris Klaus (ISS founder), who backs CREATE-X, became one of Stord's early investors; Henry met him at Georgia Tech.
deep_cut_fact: Boudreau and Henry were named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2018, then picked as 'All-Star Alumni' on the 2020 Manufacturing & Industry list, which recognizes those 'creating the products, methods and materials of tomorrow.'
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Sean Henry is the public face. Recent Stord releases (2025-26) list David Packman as media contact.

name: Sean Henry
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Stord (commerce enablement / fulfillment, Atlanta)
profile: Atlanta native who co-founded Stord with Jacob Boudreau in 2015 as a Georgia Tech freshman, dropping out at 19.
