Stord provides warehousing, fulfillment and software that give independent brands Amazon-like shipping; a $250M Series F reportedly valued it around $3B. Thiel Fellow, Forbes 30 Under 30 (2019) and named by Forbes in 2021 the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company.
interesting_fact: Forbes recognized him in 2021 as the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company; he founded Stord at 18.
deep_cut_fact: The Stord idea crystallized days before his first Georgia Tech classes, while telling his family about his summer job at a manufacturer in Germany. He also dropped out before learning he'd won the Thiel Fellowship: 'I jumped two feet in and hoped they said yes later.'
notes: Accessible, media-friendly founder (Entrepreneur bylines, Not Another CEO interview). Logistics/supply-chain angle fits the podcast.

name: Arad Levertov
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Sunbit
profile: Israeli-born fintech founder who co-founded Sunbit in 2016 (with Tal Riesenfeld, Ornit Dweck-Maizel and Prof. Tamir Hazan) after serving as COO/EVP at online lender Enova and earlier at Intel. Sunbit offers point-of-sale 'pay-over-time' financing at dentists, auto-service shops and other everyday merchants; it was valued at $1.1B in 2021 and completed its first $200M ABS deal in 2025.
interesting_fact: Named an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2025 Greater Los Angeles award winner.
deep_cut_fact: He has said a personal experience of being rejected for a credit card - which he found humiliating - was a major reason he started Sunbit, whose pitch is approving people with thin credit files.
notes: Has done many podcasts (Mixergy, DealMakers, Fintech Business Weekly) - receptive to founder-story interviews. Reported military background varies between sources; not used.

name: Ornit Dweck-Maizel
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Sunbit (Los Angeles / Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli-born fintech engineer who co-founded buy-now-pay-later company Sunbit in 2016 with Arad Levertov and Tal Riesenfeld. As CTO she built the technology that lets dental offices, auto service departments and retailers offer instant point-of-sale financing; Sunbit was valued at ~$1.1B in 2021. Earlier she worked at Intel, SuperDerivatives and as VP R&D at Whipclip.
interesting_fact: Sunbit's financing is offered in roughly one in six US auto dealership service departments.
deep_cut_fact: With no offices at the start, she held Sunbit's first engineering team meeting in her in-laws' backyard garage at the end of a dirt road; after working late the team walked out by phone flashlight over rain-soaked mud.
notes: Also known as Ornit Maizel. Degrees: BSc Information Systems Engineering (Ben-Gurion Univ.), MBA in Finance (Tel Aviv Univ.). Mentors startups.

name: Tal Riesenfeld
current_role: Co-founder, Sunbit (Los Angeles-based point-of-sale financing); listed as Chief Revenue Officer/Head of Sales
profile: Israeli-born co-founder of Sunbit, a buy-now-pay-later platform for in-person purchases such as auto repair, dental and optical care, founded in 2016 with Arad Levertov, Ornit Dweck-Maizel and Prof. Tamir Hazan and valued at ~$1B+. He leads Sunbit's revenue/sales effort. Before Sunbit he co-founded video-ad company Eyeview (2008) and worked at HP and Google.
interesting_fact: Sunbit CEO Arad Levertov recruited Riesenfeld because they had known each other since childhood. Each of them put in $100,000 of his own money to start the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sunbit, he co-founded the video-advertising startup Eyeview in 2008, where he was VP of Sales, so Sunbit is his second venture-backed company.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Arad Levertov is Sunbit's public face. Riesenfeld's background (HBS MBA, HP, Google, Eyeview) comes from aggregator profiles such as TheOrg and Crunchbase. Route via Sunbit media@sunbit.com.

name: Tamir Hazan
current_role: Co-founder & Head of AI/ML, Sunbit; faculty member at Technion
profile: Machine-learning academic who co-founded Sunbit, the buy-now-pay-later and point-of-sale financing fintech (valued at about $1.1B), and leads its AI/ML work. Sunbit's site describes him as 'Published author. Professor. Tech-leader.' He heads a machine-learning data lab at Technion and has held professorships at the University of Chicago, the University of Haifa and Technion. Arad Levertov is Sunbit's CEO.
interesting_fact: He keeps a dual career: he runs Sunbit's AI/ML while heading a machine-learning lab at Technion, and has written more than 35 publications.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sunbit his academic path ran through the University of Chicago and the University of Haifa as well as Technion, where Sunbit's bio says he now heads a machine-learning data lab.
notes: Academic and technical co-founder; CEO Arad Levertov is Sunbit's public face. An academic angle (ML research, credit-underwriting AI) is probably the best hook. I couldn't load his Technion and TTIC pages (bot-blocked), so I couldn't confirm specific research details.

name: Harry Franks
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Zego (stepped away from day-to-day role; Zego says he still provides 'ongoing support')
profile: London entrepreneur who co-founded Zego in 2016 with fellow Deliveroo alumnus Sten Saar after seeing how hard it was for couriers to get flexible insurance. Zego's pay-as-you-go and fleet insurance for gig-economy drivers made it a UK insurtech unicorn. Franks later left the company; no new venture has been publicly announced.
interesting_fact: Zego was born at Deliveroo: Franks saw first-hand that the company's couriers struggled to buy insurance that matched their part-time, on-demand work.
deep_cut_fact: He had no insurance background: before Zego he was Deliveroo's global head of procurement and earlier worked at luxury home-rental startup onefinestay.
notes: Left Zego (reported by Insurance Post / Insurance Times, citing personal reasons); keep outreach light. Low public profile since; no published personal contact found. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Sten Saar
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Zego
profile: Estonian entrepreneur who moved to London, worked in operations at onefinestay and Deliveroo, and in 2016 co-founded Zego with Harry Franks and Stuart Kelly to sell flexible insurance to gig-economy delivery drivers. Zego hit a $1B+ valuation in 2021, expanded into fleet and telematics car insurance, and reported monthly profitability in Q4 2024.
interesting_fact: Zego was born from a gap Saar spotted at Deliveroo: couriers had no flexible, pay-as-you-work insurance.
deep_cut_fact: At 17 in Estonia he launched a business selling notepads to students that earned about $1 million across four countries while he studied business and management.
notes: Has appeared on The F in Tech podcast. No generic press email confirmed; Zego newsroom pages list an obfuscated contact address.

name: Stuart Kelly
current_role: Co-founder of Zego (technical co-founder, formerly CTO); current title not confirmed
profile: London software engineer who co-founded insurtech Zego in 2016 with Harry Franks and Sten Saar, all ex-onefinestay. As technical co-founder he built the platform that prices pay-as-you-go insurance for gig-economy drivers by the hour; Zego reached a $1.1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Zego's first-ever sale was a £2.30 policy, sold after Kelly finished the mobile app in under four months.

name: Gal Shaul
current_role: Co-founder, Augury Inc. (industrial AI / machine health, New York & Israel); current title not verified

name: Saar Yoskovitz
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Augury (machine-health AI; Haifa/Tel Aviv and New York)
profile: Saar Yoskovitz, a Technion graduate in electrical engineering and physics, co-founded Augury in 2012 with CTO Gal Shaul. name: Kohsuke Kawaguchi
current_role: Creator of Jenkins; co-founder of Launchable (acquired by CloudBees, Aug 2024); former CTO of CloudBees
profile: Tokyo-born programmer (b. 1977) who created Hudson at Sun Microsystems in 2004, which became Jenkins, the dominant open-source CI/CD automation server, after a 2011 fork from Oracle. His start-up InfraDNA merged into CloudBees (2010), where he became CTO (2014); in 2020 he left to co-found Launchable (ML-driven test selection), which CloudBees acquired in 2024.
interesting_fact: Jenkins exists because of a trademark fight: when Oracle claimed the 'Hudson' name after buying Sun, the community voted in January 2011 to rename the project Jenkins, and both sides still call the other the fork. He won the 2011 Google-O'Reilly Open Source Award.
deep_cut_fact: A keen long-distance cyclist who blogs his rides: in 2026 he and an old friend pedalled ~519 km over five days along the Shinano, Japan's longest river, to the Sea of Japan and up the coast, after riding Japan's historic eastern highway together the year before.
notes: Hurun's $1B figure is CloudBees' valuation, not his wealth. Approachable, frequent conference speaker, active blogger in English and Japanese (cycling, cooking, coffee, AI). His site's About page still says CloudBees CTO (outdated). Best route: LinkedIn or X.

current_role: Co-founder and board member, CloudBees (stepped back from day-to-day role as Chief Strategy Officer in Feb 2025).
profile: Swiss software entrepreneur (b. Neuchâtel 1975, EPFL) who was CTO of open-source middleware firm JBoss through its 2006 sale to Red Hat, then GM of Red Hat middleware. In 2010 he founded CloudBees (enterprise Jenkins CI/CD, DevOps), serving as CEO then CSO; since 2025 he is a board member and advisor.

notes: Based in Neuchâtel, Switzerland; frequent conference speaker and blogger. Now off day-to-day CloudBees duties (new CEO Moritz Plassnig, June 2026), so reach him personally via LinkedIn rather than company PR. Cloud/DevOps rather than energy.

current_role: Engineering executive; reportedly at Mirantis since Dec 2022 (unverified); previously VP Engineering at Shipa.io
profile: Software engineer who was one of CloudBees' founding team in 2010 (with Sacha Labourey, Francois Dechery and others), the Jenkins-based CI/CD company that reached unicorn status with a $150m raise in Dec 2021. name: Hillel Kobrinsky
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Strategy Officer, DriveNets (Ra'anana, Israel)

name: Hannah Sieber
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Artyc PBC (battery-powered cold-chain shipping for healthcare); co-founder of EcoFlow
profile: Mandarin-speaking, Stanford-educated co-founder of Shenzhen-based EcoFlow, the portable-power and home-battery unicorn, and a Forbes 30 Under 30 Energy honoree (2018). She now runs Artyc, which makes reusable, battery-powered, sensor-tracked coolers (Medstow) for shipping medical samples. It had raised about $14M by mid-2024.
interesting_fact: Artyc grew out of her Stanford research on California's wildfire power shutoffs. Seeing small businesses lose refrigerated stock in a 56-hour outage led her to ask 'Could we electrify the cold chain?'

notes: No longer at EcoFlow. A great podcast guest with a hardware/battery founder story from Shenzhen to San Francisco. She has appeared on My Climate Journey and speaks at conferences. Artyc's domain is shipartyc.com (artyc.com is parked). Nationality not confirmed.

profile: French-born HEC graduate and former packaging-industry executive (MeadWestvaco beauty & personal care, Alcan Beauty Solutions) who co-founded Nature's Fynd around 2014. HEC named him 'HEC of the Year' 2022.

name: Dan Cogan-Drew
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Academic Officer, Newsela

Newsela began by rewriting news articles at multiple reading levels for classrooms and grew into a K-12 content platform (later adding Formative) used by millions of educators; he leads its academic work on student outcomes.

name: Matthew Gross
current_role: Founder & Executive Chair, Newsela (title per recent profiles; verify)
profile: Former Teach for America music teacher and New York education-policy leader who founded Newsela in 2013, an edtech platform that adapts news and instructional texts to each student's reading level. Newsela raised $100M in 2021 at a $1B valuation and later combined with Formative; Gross moved from CEO to executive chair.

notes: Exact current title unclear (sources differ between executive chair and co-founder after CEO change). Also on New Classrooms board.

name: Prajit Nanu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nium (leads the company from its San Francisco office)

name: Akhil Gupta

name: Benjamin Eldridge
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Nutcracker Therapeutics (Emeryville, CA)
profile: Engineer-inventor who co-founded Nutcracker Therapeutics in 2018 with former FormFactor CEO Igor Khandros, applying semiconductor-style biochip manufacturing to RNA therapeutics. name: Nadav Shoval
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Project Omega (spent-nuclear-fuel recycling); CEO of FlowMode; senior advisor to OpenWeb
profile: Israeli-American entrepreneur (b. 1990) who co-founded Spot.IM in 2015, later renamed OpenWeb, the publisher comments/engagement platform valued above $1.5B in 2022. It recycles used nuclear fuel into long-duration power sources and reactor fuel and emerged from stealth in Feb 2026.

profile: Israeli entrepreneur who joined Spot.IM (now OpenWeb) as co-founder and COO in 2014, helping build the publisher comment/conversation platform into a unicorn before leaving the COO role around January 2022. In 2025 he founded London-based Atmospheric AI, which builds digital twins of raw-material supply chains (cost, resilience, emissions) and raised a $10M seed led by DBL Partners in November 2026.

name: Ivan Dimov
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO (2016-May 2025), Orca Bio
profile: Engineer-turned-biotech founder (PhD applied biophysics, Dublin City University; postdocs at UC Berkeley and in Irv Weissman's Stanford lab) who co-founded Orca Bio in 2016 with Nate Fernhoff and Jeroen Bekaert. Orca develops high-precision allogeneic cell therapies (lead product Orca-T for blood cancers); Fernhoff succeeded him as CEO in May 2025 ahead of the BLA filing.

current_role: Co-founder and President, Orca Bio (since May 2025; previously COO)

deep_cut_fact: He started at Northwestern as a chemical engineering major, but robotics hooked him when he won the 2009 McCormick Autonomous Robot Design Competition with classmates Andrew Dai and Eric West. At Draper he led teams building a handheld 3D-scanning system and a fully autonomous exploration quadrotor.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: in 2023 he said his next move targeted decarbonization via nuclear energy or energy storage ('The climate emergency waits for no one'). He has no published email or verified social handle; try LinkedIn or Northwestern Engineering alumni channels. Shield AI's press office is not a good route since he left.

name: Brandon Tseng
current_role: Co-founder and President, Shield AI
profile: Former Navy SEAL officer and surface warfare officer (7 years; deployed to Afghanistan and the Pacific) who co-founded Shield AI in 2015 with his brother Ryan Tseng and Andrew Reiter. Shield AI builds the Hivemind AI-pilot software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft and (via Aechelon) simulation tech; it was valued at ~$12.7B in 2026 and is a leading US defense-autonomy startup.

notes: Frequent podcast/op-ed guest (Masters of Scale, War on the Rocks), so receptive to media. AI/autonomy plus defense angle; adjacent rather than core to energy/data centers. Shield AI's own site blocked automated fetch; personal social handles not verified.

name: Ryan Tseng
current_role: Co-founder & President (strategic growth), Shield AI; CEO 2015-May 2025
profile: Ryan Tseng co-founded San Diego-based Shield AI in 2015 with his brother Brandon (an ex-Navy SEAL) and Andrew Reiter to build AI pilots for military aircraft and drones (Hivemind software, V-BAT drone). deep_cut_fact: Before defense tech he was a wireless-power entrepreneur: as founder/CEO/CTO of WiPower he developed wireless charging technology and sold the company to Qualcomm in 2010. He studied electrical engineering at the University of Florida and earned an MBA at MIT.
notes: Leadership change confirmed by Shield AI release (12 Mar 2025). Titles vary (President / President & Chief Strategy Officer / President, Strategic Growth). Defense-AI focus rather than data centers. Frequent speaker (CSIS, Sedona Forum, AIAA), so open to media; route via Shield AI communications (shield.ai blocked from this session, so no press email captured).

Shift sells AI for insurance claims fraud detection, underwriting and claims automation; it became a unicorn in 2021 with a $220M Series D led by Advent. He leads its data science and now its agentic-AI push for insurers.
interesting_fact: Shift Technology raised $220M in May 2021 at a $1B+ valuation, becoming one of France's insurtech unicorns; its AI scores insurance claims for fraud for insurers worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: While building Shift as CSO, he completed a PhD at Telecom ParisTech (2016) titled 'Multi-resolution analysis of ranking data', on machine learning over permutations and rankings, co-authoring work on ranking aggregation with Stephan Clemencon.
notes: marketing@shift-technology.com is listed under 'Press & Media' on Shift's contact page. He appears in Shift content ('Four questions with Eric Sibony') and trade press commentary on AI in insurance. Less direct energy/data-center fit; AI/entrepreneurship angle.

name: Jeremy Jawish
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Shift Technology (Paris)
profile: Polytechnique-trained French entrepreneur who co-founded Shift Technology in 2014 with Eric Sibony and David Durrleman. Shift sells AI for insurers, starting with fraud detection and now claims and underwriting decision automation and AI agents. It became a unicorn after a $220m Series D (2021) and earns about half its revenue in the US.

The idea for Shift came during his internship at a big insurer, where experts reviewed claims by hand despite all the maths that could be applied. He says he became an entrepreneur mainly 'to work with Eric on something that was ours.'

name: Abraham Bachrach
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, Skydio (autonomous drones, San Mateo, CA)
profile: Abe Bachrach (BS UC Berkeley; MS/PhD MIT) led MIT's autonomous-flight research from 2007 in Nick Roy's Robust Robotics Group, then joined Google's Project Wing drone effort. In 2014 he co-founded Skydio with Adam Bry and Matt Donahoe; it builds AI-driven autonomous drones and docks for enterprise, utilities/infrastructure inspection, public safety and defense.

notes: Technical founder with a low media profile (CEO Adam Bry is the usual spokesperson). Energy angle: Skydio drones and docks are used for utility and energy-infrastructure inspection. Press route: press@skydio.com.

current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Skydio (largest US drone maker, San Mateo, CA)
profile: MIT CSAIL roboticist (SM '12) who helped lead research on autonomous high-speed flight, then co-founded Google X's Project Wing delivery-drone effort. Co-founded Skydio in 2014; it pivoted from consumer selfie drones to autonomous drones and docks for public safety, infrastructure inspection and defence, has delivered over 60,000 drones to 3,800+ organisations, and raised at a ~$4.4B valuation in 2026.

notes: Experienced public speaker (congressional testimony, MIT fireside chats, FAA Drone Advisory Committee). Energy angle: drones for grid and utility infrastructure inspection. Best route is press@skydio.com.

current_role: Cofounder, Skydio (autonomous drones), San Mateo, CA - current exec title not confirmed
profile: Matt Donahoe (MIT Media Lab SM '11) cofounded Skydio in 2014 with MIT roboticists Adam Bry and Abe Bachrach. Skydio began with the R1 'selfie drone' (13 cameras, full autonomy) and became the largest US drone maker, selling to the military, police and utilities; it raised a Series F at a $4.4B valuation in 2026 and plans $3.5B of US manufacturing.
interesting_fact: Skydio's first product, the 2018 R1 'selfie drone', used 13 cameras and deep neural networks to follow and film a person while dodging obstacles with no pilot - which CEO Adam Bry likened to a driverless car with level-four autonomy.
deep_cut_fact: For Skydio's first year the three cofounders worked out of Abe Bachrach's dad's basement, getting free rent in exchange for yard work; their first prototype was a quadcopter with a media-center PC and USB camera held together with duct tape - yet it won a $3M seed round.
notes: Lowest-profile of the three cofounders (CEO Adam Bry is the public face). Third-party sites give conflicting titles (COO / CRO / chief experience officer); verify before addressing him. Skydio is on China's sanctions list (relevant to supply chain stories, not to outreach).

name: Li Yang

deep_cut_fact: Before returning to China he worked in US RF/semiconductor firms: Principal Engineer at Millennial Net (2004-06), Staff Engineer at Peregrine Semiconductor (2006-08) and Principal Engineer at Skyworks (2008-11), founding Smarter Micro three months after leaving Skyworks.

name: Mike Pittaro
current_role: SnapLogic co-founder; last publicly listed as Distinguished Engineer, Cloud and Big Data Solutions, Dell EMC (current role unverified)
profile: Mike (Michael) Pittaro co-founded SnapLogic in 2006 with Informatica co-founder Gaurav Dhillon, serving as chief community officer while it ran as an open-source data-integration project; SnapLogic later became an iPaaS unicorn. He came from Informatica (customer services/strategic support) and later worked as a principal engineer at La Honda Research Center and a distinguished engineer at Dell EMC.
interesting_fact: SnapLogic launched in 2007 as open-source data-integration software under a GPL-style licence, with Pittaro as chief community officer building the developer community, long before it became a commercial AI-integration platform.

name: Alexander Ratner
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Snorkel AI (Redwood City/SF); Affiliate Assistant Professor of Computer Science, University of Washington
profile: Stanford CS PhD (advisor Christopher Re) who started and led the open-source Snorkel project for programmatic data labelling, then spun it out as Snorkel AI in 2019. The unicorn now focuses on expert data, evaluations and benchmarks for frontier AI labs and enterprises. He is also affiliate faculty at the University of Washington.
interesting_fact: Snorkel grew from his 2016 NeurIPS paper 'Data Programming: Creating Large Training Sets, Quickly', which showed models could be trained without hand-labelled data by writing noisy 'labeling functions' and modelling their accuracies - the weak-supervision idea behind the company.
deep_cut_fact: As a PhD student he co-authored AMELIE, a Stanford tool that speeds diagnosis of patients with rare Mendelian genetic diseases by mining the primary medical literature directly (with Gill Bejerano's lab).

public_contacts.value: ajratner at gmail.com (self-published on his academic homepage, last updated ~2020)

notes: Accessible, academically minded founder who speaks often at AI events (Snorkel hosts its own Frontier Data Summit). For a business/podcast request, media@snorkel.ai is the most appropriate route; the gmail address is from his older academic page.

name: Braden Hancock
current_role: Research Partner, Laude Ventures and Laude Institute (since Jul 2025); co-founder and advisor, Snorkel AI
profile: BYU mechanical-engineering valedictorian turned Stanford CS PhD (under Chris Ré) who co-founded Snorkel AI from Stanford weak-supervision research; it reached a $1.3B valuation (Series D, May 2025). He then founded Meta's GenAI Evaluations org for Llama (2024-25), and since mid-2025 is a Research Partner at Laude.
interesting_fact: At Meta he founded the centralized evaluation org responsible for all eval work on Llama 3, 3.1 and 3.2, the most-downloaded open LLM family.
deep_cut_fact: Before AI he was a mechanical engineer: in summer 2011 he worked in the Air Force Research Laboratory's Turbine Engine Division on evolutionary algorithms for turbine-engine simulation, and he graduated BYU (2015) as valedictorian.
notes: Very accessible: maintains a personal site, posts on X/LinkedIn and does podcasts (e.g. The SaaS CFO, Aug 2025; Practical AI #117). Good guest for AI data/evals and research-to-startup topics. No published email; X or LinkedIn is the best route.

name: Chris Re
current_role: Professor of Computer Science, Stanford (Stanford AI Lab / Hazy Research); co-founder of Together AI
profile: Christopher Re is a Stanford CS professor and MacArthur Fellow whose machine-learning systems research has spun out multiple companies: Lattice (DeepDive) and Inductiv (HoloClean), both acquired by Apple, plus Snorkel AI, SambaNova Systems and Together AI, the AI-cloud/open-model infrastructure company co-founded in 2022. His lab now focuses on AI kernels (ThunderKittens) and AI efficiency.
interesting_fact: He has co-founded companies straight out of his research, including SambaNova and Snorkel, and his lab says over a dozen of its members have gone on to become professors; his students also run the MLSys podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In Nov 2025 he co-authored 'Intelligence Per Watt' with John Hennessy, arguing that, as with mainframes to PCs, efficiency gains could shift AI inference from power-constrained data centers to local devices; they found local LMs could answer 88.7% of single-turn chat and reasoning queries.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center/energy podcast given his 'intelligence per watt' work. The email is his Stanford work address, published on his own homepage. The X account is the lab's (Hazy Research), not personal.

name: Henry Ehrenberg
current_role: Co-founder, Snorkel AI (technical strategy and engineering)
profile: Yale applied-math grad with a Stanford MS who was a core member of the Snorkel project in the Stanford AI Lab, then tech lead of Facebook Applied AI's representation-learning team. He co-founded Snorkel AI (spun out 2019 with Alex Ratner, Chris Ré and others), which sells programmatic data-labeling and expert-data tooling for enterprise and frontier AI.
interesting_fact: Snorkel's core idea, 'programmatic labeling' or weak supervision, lets teams write labeling functions instead of hand-labeling data; it began as an open-source Stanford research library he helped build.
deep_cut_fact: He is a co-author of the original 2017 paper 'Snorkel: Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision' and of 'Learning to Compose Domain-Specific Transformations for Data Augmentation' (2017), the research that seeded the company.
notes: Lower profile than CEO Alex Ratner but does public talks (theCUBE + NYSE Wired 'Robotics & AI Infrastructure Leaders' 2025: https://snorkel.ai/press/henry-kiss-ehrenberg-snorkel-ai-robotics-ai-infrastructure-leaders/). Snorkel press list mentions a 2026 RIF - avoid as an angle.

name: Paroma Varma
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Research, Snorkel AI

Snorkel has pivoted toward expert-curated datasets, benchmarks and evaluation for frontier AI labs, and she leads its research (e.g. 2026 work on rubric-based LLM evaluation).
interesting_fact: Snorkel started as a Stanford AI Lab research project in 2015 to give ML a 'higher-level interface' through training data; she describes Snorkel Flow as the first data-centric platform built on programmatic labelling.
deep_cut_fact: Her first exposure to machine learning was as a UC Berkeley undergrad working in a neuroscience lab, and during her PhD she collaborated with radiologists, applying weak supervision to medical imaging.
notes: Researcher-founder; accessible via Snorkel media. Some third-party profiles list her as Head of Solutions, but Snorkel's own author page says Head of Research.

name: Idit Levine

current_role: Founder & CEO, Backbase (Amsterdam)
profile: Dutch software entrepreneur (MSc, University of Groningen) who earlier co-founded web content management vendor Tridion (later SDL Tridion), then founded Backbase in 2003. Backbase's engagement-banking platform is used by 100+ banks worldwide; it bootstrapped for ~16 years before a 2019 Motive Partners investment valuing it around EUR 2.5bn.
interesting_fact: Backbase stayed bootstrapped for almost two decades, growing from services revenue to a global banking-software vendor before taking significant outside capital.
deep_cut_fact: To fund the core product in its early, bootstrapped years, Backbase took on side projects such as building websites for beer companies - anything to bring in cash to reinvest.
notes: Frequent conference speaker and podcast guest (Fintech Leaders, Oliver Wyman Innovators Exchange); Backbase PR is the published route.

name: Kari Kivela
current_role: Co-founder of Oura Health (former CTO & Head of Design); current role at Oura unverified
profile: Finnish engineer-designer (Kari Kivelä) who co-founded Oura in Oulu in 2013 with Petteri Lahtela and Markku Koskela, drawing on the region's Polar/Nokia hardware heritage. As early CTO and head of design he shaped the smart ring that measures sleep and recovery; Oura has since grown into a multi-billion-dollar wearable company (valued around $11B in 2025).
interesting_fact: Oura's 2015 Kickstarter hit its $100,000 goal in 15 hours and gathered about $650,000 in pre-orders with no PR or paid ads.
deep_cut_fact: Oura was originally called 'Jouzen' - from joutsen, Finnish for swan, plus 'Zen'. Kivelä's design credo: 'design shouldn't be dictated by technology,' calling miniaturizing the electronics the biggest challenge.
notes: Low public profile; Oura's public face is CEO Tom Hale. Deep-cut combines two sources: Jouzen name from ouraring.com history blog, quote from Fashnerd. Only route found is Oura company press email.

name: Petteri Lahtela
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Oura Health (left the company in 2020); current role not confirmed
profile: Finnish engineer from Oulu who co-founded Oura Health in 2013 with fellow engineers and researchers (ex-Nokia/Polar backgrounds) to build a sensor-packed smart ring tracking sleep, heart rate and temperature. He was CEO until 2018, then innovation director, and left in 2020. Oura has since become the category leader in smart rings, valued at $11B after a $900M Series E in October 2025.
interesting_fact: The first-generation Oura ring launched via a Kickstarter campaign in 2015, the same year Oura raised a $2.3M seed round led by Finland's Lifeline Ventures.
deep_cut_fact: Oura's name nods to the founders' hometown of Oulu; per Finnish Wikipedia, the rings were produced near Oulu in Haukipudas (by contract manufacturer Sanmina) from 2015 until late 2024.
notes: No longer at Oura (left 2020) and keeps a very low public profile; no verified personal website/social account found. Oura's press office would not represent him. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so his post-Oura activities were not researched.

name: Daniel Katz
current_role: Co-founder, A24 (independent film/TV studio, New York)
profile: Co-founded A24 in August 2012 with David Fenkel and John Hodges, with seed money from Guggenheim Partners. A24 grew from a distributor (Spring Breakers, Ex Machina, Room) into a producer behind Moonlight, Everything Everywhere All at Once, The Whale and The Brutalist, plus TV, music and a membership program. He remains a key executive and is famously press-shy.
interesting_fact: A24's 2023 Oscars sweep (Everything Everywhere All at Once won Best Picture among 7 Oscars, The Whale won two) came even as its founders shun the spotlight and almost never give interviews.
deep_cut_fact: The name 'A24' comes from Italy's Autostrada A24 (Rome-Teramo), which Katz was driving on when he decided to start the company.
notes: Extremely private - A24 founders rarely speak publicly; expect outreach through A24 publicity to be declined. Common name - this is the A24 co-founder.

name: David Fenkel
current_role: Co-founder, A24
profile: Independent-film executive who co-founded A24 in 2012 with Daniel Katz and John Hodges after running Oscilloscope Laboratories with the Beastie Boys' Adam Yauch. A24 became the defining indie studio (Moonlight, Everything Everywhere All at Once), raised capital at a ~$3.5B valuation in 2024, and he remains a co-leader alongside Katz.
interesting_fact: A24 won Best Picture twice in six years - Moonlight (2017) and Everything Everywhere All at Once, which swept seven Oscars in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He met Adam Yauch as a THINKFilm executive when the company financed and released the Beastie Boys' fan-shot concert film 'Awesome; I F*ckin' Shot That!' (2006); Yauch then recruited him to run his new film distributor Oscilloscope, whose first release was the documentary 'Gunnin' for That #1 Spot'.
notes: Famously press-shy; A24 executives rarely give interviews. No published press email for him; A24 publicity is handled per film.

name: Matthew Bires
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of A24 Films (valued ~$4B). Wikipedia credits A24's founding in August 2012 to Daniel Katz, David Fenkel and John Hodges and does not mention a Matthew Bires, so his link to A24 and his role could not be confirmed.
notes: Possible data error in the Hurun list. Web-search quota was exhausted before this person, and direct fetches (Wikipedia, LinkedIn) did not confirm him. Verify manually before any outreach.

name: David Ring
current_role: Co-founder of eToro (current involvement not documented; not among eToro's listed key executives)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded eToro, first as RetailFX, in Tel Aviv in 2007 with brothers Yoni and Ronen Assia. It became a global social-trading and multi-asset investing platform and listed on Nasdaq (ETOR) in May 2025. He keeps a very low public profile and isn't among eToro's named executives.
interesting_fact: eToro popularised 'social trading' and 'CopyTrader', letting retail users automatically copy other investors' portfolios. It began as RetailFX, a 2007 attempt to make forex trading accessible and game-like.
notes: Very little public information; Wikipedia names him only as a co-founder. Common name, so confirm identity before outreach. The only route is eToro PR. Yoni Assia (CEO) is the public face.

name: Ronen Assia
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Director, eToro (Nasdaq: ETOR); Managing Partner (Fintech), Team8
profile: Israeli designer-turned-entrepreneur who co-founded social-trading platform eToro in 2007 with his brother Yoni Assia and David Ring, serving as Chief Product Officer running product and engineering until 2020. He remains an eToro director after its May 2025 Nasdaq IPO and is a Managing Partner at Team8, building and investing in fintech startups.
interesting_fact: eToro pioneered 'social investing', letting users copy other traders' portfolios; it now serves over 30 million registered users in 100+ countries.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an industrial designer (BA Bezalel Academy, MA Product Design at London's Royal College of Art) and designed medical devices and household appliances before co-founding eToro.
notes: Brother Yoni Assia is eToro's CEO and public face. Ronen is reachable through Team8 (Tel Aviv VC/venture studio), which is the more natural route. Reportedly joined Riskified's board (per Riskified IR page).

name: Yoni Assia
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, eToro Group (Nasdaq: ETOR)
profile: Israeli fintech founder who in 2007 co-founded eToro (originally RetailFX) in Tel Aviv with his brother Ronen Assia and David Ring. eToro pioneered social/copy trading, became an early crypto adopter, and listed on Nasdaq in 2025; it reports ~3.8M funded accounts and $18.5B in customer assets (end-2025).
interesting_fact: He received stock as a bar mitzvah gift and became a successful trader in high school, only to see those profits vanish when the dot-com bubble burst as he began military service.
deep_cut_fact: Per Cointelegraph's 'Crypto Stories' interview, a young programmer named Vitalik Buterin helped with the launch of crypto trading on eToro.
notes: Highly public and active on X. Named to Fortune 40 Under 40 (2020). Father David Assia co-founded Magic Software. No generic press/IR email confirmed; use eToro Media Center / IR site.

name: Bhavin Pandya
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Games24x7 (Mumbai)
profile: Indian entrepreneur who co-founded Games24x7 in 2006 with Trivikraman Thampy after both studied economics at NYU. The company built RummyCircle and fantasy-sports app My11Circle, applying data science to gaming, and reached a $2.5B valuation backed by Tiger Global; it also runs a venture arm and a foundation.
interesting_fact: Pandya describes Games24x7 as 'a technology platform, gaming is just incidental' - the company brands itself around 'The Science of Gaming' and serves 120M+ players.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Trivikraman Thampy met while studying economics at New York University and bonded over a shared passion for online games; Pandya returned to India in 2006 to start the company. He also holds an electrical and computer engineering degree from Purdue.
notes: India's 2025 online-gaming law banned real-money games, forcing a major business pivot for Games24x7 - context worth knowing but handle tactfully. Purdue degree comes from a secondary profile (theofficialboard).

name: James Ferguson
current_role: Co-founder, Immutable (Sydney-based gaming/blockchain company); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Australian co-founder, with Robbie Ferguson and Alex Connolly, of Fuel Games (2018), renamed Immutable in 2019. Immutable built Gods Unchained, the Immutable X Ethereum Layer-2 (with StarkWare) and now offers a game-growth suite (Passport, attribution, wishlist and player-engagement tools) used by 800+ games; it was valued at $3.5B after a $200M Temasek-led round in 2022.
interesting_fact: The company's first product, released in February 2018, was Etherbots, a robot-battling blockchain game on Ethereum, followed by the Gods Unchained trading-card game pre-sale in July 2018.
notes: Lower public profile than brother/co-founder Robbie Ferguson (Immutable's public face); 'James Ferguson' is a common name, so check context. Search budget ran out before finding a sourced deep-cut fact or personal channel.

name: Robbie Ferguson
current_role: Co-founder & President, Immutable (Sydney)
profile: Australian entrepreneur who co-founded Immutable (originally Fuel Games, 2018) with brother James and Alex Connolly; it became a leading web3 gaming platform (Immutable X/zkEVM) valued at ~$2B+ (Hurun). Became the youngest person on the AFR Rich List at 25. Previously worked at KPMG Australia.
interesting_fact: In 2017-18 the brothers built Etherbots, billed as the world's first multiplayer competitive blockchain game, which brought in $1M in its first week.
deep_cut_fact: He finished top of his school, then started a computer science/law double degree at the University of Sydney (unfinished), where he met Immutable CTO Alex Connolly; he and James spent 'countless hours' on RuneScape and League of Legends as kids.
notes: Very active public speaker and on X/podcasts on web3 gaming; verify his X handle from Immutable's site before use.

name: Anthony Welters
current_role: Executive Chairman, BlackIvy Group; Co-Founder & Chairman, Somatus
profile: Harlem-raised lawyer turned healthcare entrepreneur (b. 1955) who founded Medicaid managed-care firm AmeriChoice in 1989, sold it to UnitedHealth Group and rose to EVP/Office of the CEO there. He co-founded and chairs Somatus, a value-based kidney-care company valued at $2.5B, and since 2014 chairs BlackIvy, which builds food, housing, healthcare and logistics businesses in Sub-Saharan Africa.
interesting_fact: Before AmeriChoice he started several businesses, from manufacturing to restaurant franchises, which all failed: 'You have to be prepared to accept failure to have success.' His break came in 1988 when he won Philadelphia's Medicaid-management contract, then Pennsylvania's largest ever.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he shined shoes under the elevated subway and swept a barbershop floor for tips; he skipped fourth grade, got into Stuyvesant, finished Manhattanville College in under three years, and earned his NYU law degree at 22. He and his wife Bea founded Camp Dogwood Summer Academy for low-income kids in Virginia's Blue Ridge.
notes: Horatio Alger Award 1998; NYU Law lobby named for him; vice chair NYU trustees; AnBryce Scholarship founder. Avoid the Clarence Thomas RV-loan story (on Wikipedia). Somatus site blocks automated access; no press email captured.

name: Chris Pihl
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
profile: Chris Pihl is co-founder and CTO of Helion Energy, founded in 2013 with David Kirtley, George Votroubek and John Slough. Helion develops pulsed, non-ignition magneto-inertial fusion generators backed by Sam Altman, Dustin Moskovitz and Reid Hoffman. It is building the Orion fusion plant in Malaga, Washington to supply Microsoft data centers, and makes its own high-voltage pulsed-power capacitors in-house.
interesting_fact: Helion signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement, with Microsoft in 2023, a direct link between fusion and data-center power demand.
deep_cut_fact: Helion's founders met at MSNW, a small Redmond, Washington fusion-research firm with University of Washington ties, before spinning out. Pihl, a UW graduate, is one of three original founders still at the company.
notes: Low personal media profile; CEO David Kirtley is the main spokesperson. A strong fit for the energy and data-center theme. Requests should go through Helion press.

name: David Kirtley
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
profile: Michigan-trained nuclear, plasma and aerospace engineer who co-founded fusion company Helion in 2013. Helion holds the first fusion power-purchase agreement (with Microsoft) and began building its 50 MW Orion plant in Malaga, WA in July 2025, targeting 2028. In February 2026 its Polaris prototype showed the first private D-T fusion.
interesting_fact: Helion's Orion plant is meant to sell fusion electricity to Microsoft, a direct link between fusion and AI data-center power demand. On Lex Fridman's podcast, Kirtley described wanting a 'gigafactory' that turns out 50 MW fusion generators.
deep_cut_fact: He started in space propulsion, not power plants. Early in his career he studied beamed-microwave rocket concepts, in which a spacecraft needs no onboard fuel. Before spinning out Helion, his team worked on fusion rockets and advanced materials. He says they reused circuit topologies from space hardware for fusion.
notes: Very podcast-friendly. He has appeared on Lex Fridman #485, GeekWire's Positive Charge and Slush 2026, and is an ideal guest for the energy/data-center theme. Use Helion's press form. Company X account: @helion_energy. I found no verified personal handle.

name: George Votroubek
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Scientist, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
profile: Plasma physicist (MS, PhD University of Washington) who co-founded fusion company Helion Energy in 2013 with David Kirtley, Chris Pihl and John Slough, colleagues from MSNW in Redmond. Helion pursues pulsed field-reversed-configuration fusion, is building its Polaris prototype and Orion plant, and has raised ~$1.5B.
interesting_fact: Helion signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement with Microsoft (plus a deal with steelmaker Nucor) - a direct link between fusion and powering data centers.
deep_cut_fact: He was Principal Investigator for the program that demonstrated Helion's 'Fusion Engine' technology at one-third scale, work that grew out of the Inductive Plasmoid Accelerator experiments the founders ran before Helion existed.
notes: Low-profile scientist; CEO David Kirtley is Helion's public voice. Helion's contact form has a 'Press' inquiry option. Excellent fit for energy + data-center theme. Deep-cut sourced to Crunchbase bio (not a primary document).

name: John Slough
current_role: Cofounder (former) of Helion Energy; plasma physicist, MSNW LLC (Redmond, WA)
profile: Plasma physicist who cofounded Helion Energy in 2013 with David Kirtley, Chris Pihl and George Votroubek; Helion's pulsed fusion approach builds on his FRC plasmoid merging-and-compression research. He left Helion in 2018 to refocus on his research firm MSNW. His wealth reflects his Helion stake (company valued ~$5B).
interesting_fact: He is an inventor on Helion's foundational patents, including a 2011 patent on generating, heating and compressing plasmoids and recovering energy from them, and the 'Advanced D–3He fuel cycle for a pulsed fusion reactor'.
deep_cut_fact: NASA's Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) program funded his 'Fusion Driven Rocket' (2012 Phase II): magnetically driven metal liners crush a plasmoid to fusion and become the propellant, a concept meant to make crewed interplanetary travel 'common place'.
notes: No longer with Helion (left 2018), so Helion PR is not a route to him; reports cite disagreement over fuel choice, so avoid that topic. Very low public profile; MSNW's website was unreachable. Best approached as a fusion-science expert via academic or plasma-physics channels.

name: Chen Zhongguo
current_role: Listed legal representative of GTA Semiconductor (上海积塔半导体) and its parent Huada Semiconductor (per 36Kr company profiles)
profile: Chen Zhongguo (陈忠国) appears in Chinese company records as legal representative of Shanghai GTA Semiconductor, a Lingang-based maker of analog ICs and power devices founded in 2017, and of its parent Huada Semiconductor, a wholly owned unit of state-owned China Electronics Corp (CEC). He looks like a state-enterprise executive rather than an entrepreneur-founder; no personal biography was found.
interesting_fact: GTA Semiconductor raised about RMB13.5B ($1.8B) in one funding round, one of China's largest for a specialty chip fab; industry veteran Zhang Rujing (SMIC founder) joined it as executive director.
notes: Hurun 'unicorn founder' tag is likely misleading: GTA is a CEC (state-owned) subsidiary. Sources: https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/2144877428720901 and https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/2012741344921093 . Low priority; identity/role not independently confirmed.

name: Itai Lahan
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Cloudinary in 2012 with Tal Lev-Ami (CTO) and Nadav Soferman (CPO), whom he met in the IDF's 8200 unit. Its API-based image/video management platform grew for years without VC before Bessemer invested; Hurun values it at ~$2bn, and it now ships AI agents for visual media.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary had paying customers within months of formation and grew organically for years without venture capital, before Bessemer Venture Partners invested to fund expansion.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cloudinary he was an executive at Israeli anti-spam startup Blue Security and at Collactive, founded news aggregator Newsodrome, and in 2009 co-founded Ndivi, a tech consultancy for start-up founders - the gap he noticed there sparked the Cloudinary idea.
notes: Press contact on Cloudinary newsroom: Juli Greenwood, Senior Director Global Communications. Has done developer-podcast interviews (Software Engineering Daily, 'Bootstrapping a SaaS for Developers') - receptive to podcast format.

name: Nadav Soferman
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli engineer Nadav Soferman co-founded Cloudinary in early 2012 with Itai Lahan (CEO) and Tal Lev-Ami (CTO), whom he met in the IDF's 8200 unit. Cloudinary's API-first platform optimises, transforms and delivers images and video for the web; it bootstrapped for years before taking growth capital (~$2B valuation). As CPO he leads product.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary was a rare bootstrapped Israeli startup: five years in (2017) it had raised no venture capital, yet had 220,000 developers on its free tier and 5,000 paying customers including eBay and Sky News.
deep_cut_fact: Cloudinary's first version took just four months to build and launched quietly in mid-2012; the idea came from the founders' consulting firm Ndivi, where every new social-network client struggled to render images well on every device and resolution.
notes: Low-profile product-side founder (CEO Itai Lahan is the usual spokesperson). Press contact is Cloudinary's Senior Director of Global Communications (Juli Greenwood) as listed on the newsroom page. He has written for Smashing Magazine on responsive images.

name: Tal Lev-Ami
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli developer who co-founded Cloudinary in 2012 with Itai Lahan and Nadav Soferman to fix the tedious work of uploading, transforming and delivering images and video online. The API-first media platform grew profitably without venture funding; a 2022 Blackstone-led secondary deal valued it at $2B. He remains CTO, focusing on AI-powered visual media at scale.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary bootstrapped its way to a $100M annual revenue run rate (2021) without venture capital, before Blackstone's $100M+ secondary investment valued it at $2B.
deep_cut_fact: Cloudinary worked with Google researchers to create the JPEG XL image format, and has since championed JPEG XL support across browsers and Apple devices.
notes: Press contact is Juli Greenwood, Senior Director Global Communications, as listed on the Cloudinary newsroom. He gives technical interviews (e.g. TechDogs Dec 2025). Deep-cut fact is about the company he co-founded, not him personally. Fit is CDN/media infrastructure rather than energy.

name: Ouyang Jian
current_role: CEO, Kunlunxin (昆仑芯, Beijing) - Baidu's AI-chip spin-off (CEO since June 2021; 2026 status per company news, not independently re-verified)
profile: Ouyang Jian (欧阳剑) was Baidu's chief chip architect and led its Kunlun AI-chip program. When Baidu spun Kunlun out in June 2021 (valued ~CNY 13B after a CPE-led round), he became CEO and legal representative. Kunlunxin sells AI accelerator cards and 'supernode' clusters for data centers and large models.
interesting_fact: Kunlunxin's spin-off entity was actually a 2011-registered Baidu shell company (星云融创) renamed in June 2021; at launch Baidu still owned ~76% and Ouyang framed it as building on 'Baidu's 10 years of accumulation in compute chips'.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2021 launch he said compute and semiconductor technology faced 'an unprecedented opportunity for change', and Kunlun's team presented at chip-design's top conference ISSCC 2021 just before the spin-off.
notes: Strong data-center/AI-chip fit. Company publishes only a business/cooperation mailbox (marketing@kunlunxin.com); no personal social accounts found. Speaks at Baidu/WAIC events; interviews mostly in Chinese. Web-search quota ran out, so his current title rests on the company's own news pages.

name: Jeff Elton
current_role: Vice Chairman and Founding CEO, ConcertAI (oncology real-world data and AI)
profile: Dr. Jeff Elton was founding CEO of ConcertAI, backed by founder/executive chairman Romesh Wadhwani, which combines oncology real-world data, clinical expertise and applied AI for pharma and providers (CancerLinQ, TeraRecon). After an April 2025 leadership transition Eron Kelly became CEO and Elton moved to vice chairman.
interesting_fact: ConcertAI now runs ASCO's CancerLinQ oncology quality platform and in 2025 launched a generative and agentic AI 'Precision Suite' that automates ASCO guidelines and clinical-trial matching.
notes: No longer CEO (vice chairman since 2025). Frequent podcast/interview guest (e.g. 'Cracking the Clinical Trial Code', AITech interview) so open to media; route via Treble PR. No sourced deep-cut found (web-search budget exhausted). Healthcare-AI angle rather than energy/data centers.

name: Chase Lochmiller
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Crusoe
profile: Co-founded Crusoe with Cully Cavness in 2018 to turn flared, otherwise-wasted natural gas into power for on-site computing. Crusoe has since become a vertically integrated AI-infrastructure company (energy, data centers, cloud) building campuses in Texas, Wyoming and beyond; in 2026 it raised a $3.9B Series F at a $30.9B valuation.
interesting_fact: Crusoe's origin was its patented 'Digital Flare Mitigation' technology: putting modular data centers at oil fields to burn stranded gas for computing instead of flaring it. It now reports 6GW+ of contracted capacity.
deep_cut_fact: On the Series F he framed Crusoe's strategy as 'controlling the infrastructure from electrons to tokens', saying AI 'will usher in an era of abundance'.
notes: Top-priority fit for an energy + data-center podcast. The Hurun '$10B valuation' is stale (now $30.9B). No published press email found; use the contact form or company socials. Web search budget ran out before personal background (education, earlier career) could be sourced.

name: Cully Cavness
current_role: Co-Founder, President and Chief Strategy Officer, Crusoe (AI data-centre / 'AI factory' developer and cloud), Denver
profile: Cully Cavness co-founded Crusoe with CEO Chase Lochmiller after leadership roles in upstream oil and gas, geothermal energy and energy investment banking (Middlebury and Oxford alum). Crusoe began by using stranded, flared natural gas to power bitcoin mining in oilfields, then pivoted to energy-first AI data centres, including the flagship campus for OpenAI's Stargate project.
interesting_fact: Crusoe's origin pitch: pay oil producers for gas they would otherwise flare for zero, and burn it in on-site generators to power computing; Cavness told Insider it was one of North America's biggest bitcoin miners, with units in North Dakota, Colorado and Montana.
deep_cut_fact: Before Crusoe he worked in the geothermal energy industry as well as upstream oil and gas, an early clean-energy thread that shows up in Crusoe's internal rule to pick projects only if they are net reducers of greenhouse gases.
notes: Perfect fit for an energy + data-centre podcast; frequent conference speaker (e.g., FII Riyadh). Title changed over time (President, COO, now President & Chief Strategy Officer per crusoe.ai). Route via media@crusoe.ai.

name: John Street
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, Pax8 (Greenwood Village, Colorado); former CEO
profile: Denver native John Street is a serial Colorado founder who started Pax8 in 2012 as a cloud-commerce marketplace that lets managed service providers buy and bill Microsoft and other cloud/security products. Pax8 grew to ~2,000 employees and a multi-billion valuation; Street handed the CEO role to Scott Chasin and now chairs the board as Pax8 pushes into 'managed intelligence' AI agents.
interesting_fact: He received the 2023 Colorado Governor's Citizenship Medal for Growth and Innovation from Gov. Jared Polis and CTA's Bob Newman Lifetime Achievement Award in 2025, after being named CTA CEO of the Year in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Pax8 is his fourth Colorado start-up: before it he launched Telephone Express, USA.Net (an early web-based email provider) and MX Logic (email security).
notes: Accessible, community-minded Colorado founder who does podcasts and local tech events (e.g. FirstMile Ventures 'Four Minute Founder', Colorado Voices on Tech). Route via Pax8 media relations. Note: the descriptions of USA.Net and MX Logic in parentheses are general knowledge; the source only lists the company names.

name: Aaron DeBevoise
current_role: Founder and CEO, Spotter (Los Angeles)
profile: YouTube-economy pioneer (name spelled DeBevoise; input has 'DeBovoise') who co-built gaming network Machinima (EVP Network Programming, 2007-13) and fashion network StyleHaul, then founded Spotter in 2019. Spotter licenses creators' back catalogs for upfront cash (MrBeast, Dude Perfect and many others) and has grown into a creator studio/ads/AI-tools company valued at ~$1.7B.
interesting_fact: Spotter has deployed close to $800 million to YouTubers ranging from MrBeast to Aaron 'AB' Brown and Kinigra Deon, and was named a TIME100 Most Influential Company.
deep_cut_fact: Before Spotter he helped build two of YouTube's earliest multi-channel networks: gaming network Machinima, where he ran network programming and orchestrated show deals, and the fashion/beauty network StyleHaul. LA Business Journal named him to its LA500 in 2024.

public_contacts.value: Guest on Colossus 'Business Breakdowns' EP.78 (Spotter: Funding YouTube Creators)

notes: Frequent podcast guest (Business Breakdowns, Foundr) - comfortable with the format. Route via Spotter communications.

name: Jacob Rubens
current_role: Founding team member, Tessera Therapeutics (Flagship Pioneering company); current title not verified
profile: Scientist (Ph.D.) on the founding team of Tessera Therapeutics with Noubar Afeyan and Geoffrey von Maltzahn at Flagship Pioneering. Tessera develops 'Gene Writing' genetic medicines, has a lead in vivo gene-editing program for AATD (TSRA-196) partnered with Regeneron, and has been valued at over $1B.
interesting_fact: Tessera's lead program TSRA-196 reached the clinic and is co-developed with Regeneron; the company also won up to $41.3M from ARPA-H to advance in vivo CAR-T therapies.
notes: Listed under 'Founding Team' on Tessera's leadership page. Believed to be a Flagship Pioneering origination partner, but Flagship's bio page was blocked (403) and search budget ran out, so current role and background are unverified. Tessera CEO since July 2026 is Joseph Romanelli.

name: Yang Changle
current_role: Co-founder, Tujia (current executive role not confirmed)
profile: Yang Changle, known in English as Melissa Yang, co-founded Beijing vacation-rental platform Tujia with Justin Luo in December 2011. Tujia raised money from HomeAway, Ctrip, Tencent and others and was valued at $1.5B+ in 2017. It bought rivals Mayi.com and Fishtrip and became China's leading home-sharing platform.
interesting_fact: In 2020 KrASIA reported that Tujia led China's home-sharing market with about 60% share, ahead of Airbnb, Meituan Minsu and Xiaozhu. When Airbnb left mainland China in 2022, Tujia took over some of its hosts.
deep_cut_fact: When she co-founded Tujia (途家, meaning 'home on the way'), she was director of deployment for Microsoft's Bing search engine in Asian markets.
notes: English Wikipedia names the founders as Justin Luo and Melissa Yang. The match to 'Yang Changle' rests on the shared surname and the two-founder team; Chinese sources weren't reachable. Her current role at Tujia (now Trip.com-backed) isn't verified. No published personal contact.

name: Hideki Yoshino
current_role: Founder and CEO, Clean Planet Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Japanese serial entrepreneur who founded Clean Planet (2012), which develops 'Quantum Hydrogen Energy' (QHe) - a heat source using nano-materials and hydrogen that it says produces energy without fossil fuels or nuclear fission - working with Tohoku University scientists; it has been valued around $1B. Earlier he founded and ran GABA Corporation, the 1-on-1 English school chain, from 1995 to 2004.
interesting_fact: Clean Planet's science board includes Tohoku University emeritus professor Jirohta Kasagi and Osaka nuclear physicist Hiroshi Toki, and its advisory board includes Carl Page of the Anthropocene Institute and a former Japanese Vice-Minister of the Environment.
deep_cut_fact: Before clean energy he built an English-education business: he founded GABA, the one-on-one English conversation school, and was CEO 1995-2004; he holds a BA in Law from the University of Tokyo and an MSc in Finance from London Business School.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy podcast (novel hydrogen/condensed-matter heat technology). current_role: Co-Founder, Anyscale (CEO until July 2024; now leads customer engagement and helps shape product roadmap/strategy)
profile: Harvard math grad and UC Berkeley CS PhD who co-created the open-source distributed-computing framework Ray with Philipp Moritz and Ion Stoica in Berkeley's RISELab, then co-founded Anyscale to commercialize it. interesting_fact: Blink Health let uninsured and insured patients alike pay for lower-priced prescriptions online and pick them up at their preferred pharmacy; it now operates as BlinkRx delivering branded drugs in all 50 states.

current_role: CTO & Co-founder, Curative Inc. (Austin, Texas)

After running mass COVID-19 testing, Curative pivoted to a vertically integrated $0 out-of-pocket health plan; Isaac leads its technology, including a proprietary 'first principles' insurance stack, the Curative Cash Card and AI-driven care navigation.

name: Alice Bentinck
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Entrepreneurs First (EF), talent investor / company builder (lives in San Francisco)

She became CEO in December 2023; in March 2026 EF raised $200M at a $1.3B valuation and is pivoting to act as a bridge between Europe and the US. She also co-founded Code First Girls.

name: Matt Clifford
current_role: Head of International Affairs at Anthropic; co-founder and non-executive Chair, Entrepreneurs First; Chair of ARIA (UK)
profile: British entrepreneur (b. 1985) who left McKinsey to co-found Entrepreneurs First with Alice Bentinck in 2011; EF raised $200M at a $1.3B valuation in 2026. He chairs the UK's Advanced Research and Invention Agency, led preparations for the 2023 Bletchley Park AI Safety Summit, wrote the UK AI Opportunities Action Plan and was the PM's AI Adviser until summer 2025. In September 2026 he joined Anthropic.

name: Jake Loosararian
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Gecko Robotics (wall-climbing inspection robots + AI for critical infrastructure, Pittsburgh)
profile: Jake Loosararian started Gecko Robotics as a Grove City College engineering student after visiting a power plant losing millions per month to boiler downtime, and co-founded the company with his college roommate Troy Demmer in 2013. Gecko's robots and Cantilever AI software inspect boilers, tanks, pipelines and Navy ships; it raised a $125M Series D in June 2025 at a $1.25B valuation.

deep_cut_fact: He built the first Gecko prototype in his college dorm room - a robot that could climb walls carrying ultrasonic sensors and cameras - then spent weeks on site in a dirty power-plant boiler adapting it until it found the plant's recurring failure.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy podcast (power-plant origin story, grid/energy infrastructure). Media-friendly: CNBC and Fortune founder-story pieces linked from Gecko's About page. Contact form has a 'Media/Press' option.

name: Jonathan Ng
current_role: Founder & CEO, Iterative Health (formerly Iterative Scopes), AI for gastroenterology
profile: Singapore-trained physician (MBBS, NUS) who founded Iterative Health in 2017 while studying at MIT/Harvard. The Cambridge, MA company applies computer vision and AI to GI endoscopy, IBD clinical-trial recruitment and research, and is valued at ~$1B. He is based in New York.

notes: Physician-founder; has done several podcasts (Physician-Executive Series, Third Spacing), so open to interviews. No published press email found.

name: Karri Saarinen
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Linear (Linear Orbit, Inc., San Francisco)
profile: Finnish designer-founder who left his Principal Designer role at Airbnb in 2019 to start Linear with Jori Lallo and Tuomas Artman. Linear's issue-tracking/product-development tool became a favourite of startups, was cash-flow positive by 2021, and an Aug 2026 tender valued it at $2.5B. He writes widely on design, quality and AI-era software.

Before Linear, he and Jori Lallo built a startup in Y Combinator's Summer 2012 batch. He's a fan of 'Jiro Dreams of Sushi' as a lesson in taste.
notes: Very accessible publicly: personal blog plus a long interviews list (YC, First Round, TBPN, Figma Config) at karrisaarinen.com/interviews. Good podcast candidate.

name: Jori Lallo
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Linear
profile: Finnish engineer/designer who co-founded Linear in 2019 with Karri Saarinen and Tuomas Artman after working at Coinbase, where he hit the same project-tracking frustrations. Linear's product-development platform, now pushing into AI coding agents, was valued at $2.5B in an Aug 2026 tender. He splits time between Brooklyn and Helsinki.

current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Linear

He built Linear's local-first sync engine, a big reason the app feels instant, and the company was valued at $2.5B in an Aug 2026 tender. Before Linear he was at Uber, and earlier Groupon.

Linear's founders say the idea came partly from his frustration with issue trackers at Uber.
notes: Comfortable with podcasts (localfirst.fm #15, devtools.fm #61). A good technical guest on sync/infra topics.

name: Kay Zhu

profile: Kay Zhu (Zhu Kaihua) is a search engineer who worked on Google's search ranking. name: Liam Fedus

He left in 2025 to co-found Periodic Labs with ex-DeepMind researcher Ekin Dogus Cubuk.

current_role: Co-founder, Periodic Labs (AI-scientist / autonomous materials-discovery lab, with Liam Fedus)

deep_cut_fact: Before materials AI he was first author of Google Brain's 2018 'AutoAugment: Learning Augmentation Policies from Data' (with Barret Zoph and Quoc Le), a widely used computer-vision technique; earlier, as a Harvard physics PhD student, he co-authored a 2014 paper using machine learning to find 'flow defects' in disordered solids (glasses).

No dedicated press email found; contact@periodic.com is the site's general contact link. Some sources wrongly say his PhD was from Montreal; arXiv affiliations point to Harvard (Kaxiras group).

name: Doug Bernauer
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Radiant Industries (Radiant Nuclear), El Segundo, CA
profile: Case Western electrical engineer who spent 12 years at SpaceX before founding Radiant in 2020. Radiant builds Kaleidos, a 1 MWe helium-cooled microreactor that fits in a shipping container, to replace diesel generators at bases and data centers. It has raised $575M+, shipped a demo unit to Idaho National Lab in 2026, and is building a factory in Oak Ridge, TN.
interesting_fact: Data-center operator Equinix signed a pre-order for 20 Radiant microreactors, and the US Army reportedly awarded up to $750M for as many as 15 Kaleidos units — a direct link between microreactors and AI/data-center power.
deep_cut_fact: At SpaceX he led avionics for Grasshopper and worked on 'Elon's side-projects' (Hyperloop, The Boring Company); tasked with powering a Mars colony, he found solar would need 'three football fields' of panels, built a nuclear trade-study model — and jokes that when asked where he went to school, he answers 'SpaceX.'
notes: Highly relevant for energy/data-center podcast; already does many podcasts (MCJ, Marketplace, Giant Ideas). His own origin essay: https://radiantnuclear.com/news/why-i-started-radiant. Recent releases name Agnes Gomes-Koizumi as media contact.

current_role: Co-founder, Radiant Industries (Radiant Nuclear), El Segundo, CA — CTO per company materials; an Apr-2025 report calls him 'former CTO'
profile: Bob Urberger is an ex-SpaceX engineer who co-founded Radiant in 2020 with CEO Doug Bernauer to build Kaleidos, a portable ~1 MWe nuclear microreactor meant to replace diesel generators at remote sites, bases and data centers. The pair learned nuclear engineering from Argonne and Idaho National Lab scientists; Radiant raised a Series D in Dec 2025 at a reported ~$1.8B valuation.
interesting_fact: Radiant's Kaleidos (1.9 MW thermal / ~1 MW electric) is built to fit in a shipping container for air, sea or road transport, and DOE funded Radiant (with Westinghouse) to prepare tests at Idaho National Laboratory's new DOME microreactor test bed.
deep_cut_fact: At SpaceX, Urberger worked with Doug Bernauer on the Grasshopper project (the reusable vertical-landing test rocket); the pair left SpaceX after a 2019 DoD call for a shipping-container-sized reactor to found Radiant.
notes: Low public profile. Title unclear: CTO in company materials vs 'former CTO' in an Apr-2025 Cyrus Ventures note; verify before outreach. radiantnuclear.com blocked automated fetches, so no press email confirmed; route via Radiant comms. Highly relevant: microreactors for data centers.

name: Wang Kai
current_role: Founder, Director and CEO, SiEngine Technology (芯擎科技), Wuhan/Shanghai
profile: Wang Kai (汪凯) is a chip-industry veteran (BS UESTC, EE PhD University of Illinois; ex-Broadcom and Freescale executive). He became CEO in 2019 of SiEngine, the automotive-chip company set up in 2018 by Geely's Li Shufu, ECARX's Shen Ziyu and Arm China. SiEngine shipped China's first 7nm automotive cockpit SoC (Longying-1), and at Auto China 2026 it unveiled the 5nm 'Longying-2' AI cockpit-driving chip.

deep_cut_fact: Before SiEngine he was at HXT Semiconductor (华芯通半导体), which he left in 2019. He has said SiEngine taped out its first chip in just over two years only because its founding team had done chip design and market-building before.
notes: Common name, but identity confirmed via SiEngine. The company is now a joint-stock company (股份有限公司) with an IR contact, which suggests IPO preparation. siengine@ is the business-cooperation address. Its new AI accelerator 'Tiangong 100' runs 3B-7B LLMs in cars, a possible AI/compute angle.

name: Ricardo Mendes
current_role: CEO, TEKEVER (Lisbon-headquartered drone/defence-tech company)

Vantaca bootstrapped to scale, then took JMI Equity and Cove Hill investment; it now serves 500+ community-management companies (~$1B+ valuation). CEO is Ben Currin.

current_role: CEO, Vantaca (HOA / community-association management software, Wilmington NC)
profile: US Naval Academy economics grad who spent nearly a decade as a Navy submarine officer and nuclear engineer, then joined founder Dave Sweyer at Vantaca in late 2017 and became CEO in 2020. He grew the bootstrapped vertical-SaaS company to ~500 management firms and 6M+ homes, bringing in JMI Equity (2022) and Cove Hill (2024); valued ~$1B+.

current_role: Founder, Vivix (real-time interactive AI models; Hangzhou/Shanghai, Hong Kong-registered)
profile: Liu Yu (born 1995) earned his PhD at CUHK's Multimedia Lab and spent about nine years at SenseTime, becoming one of its youngest executive research directors and running ~200 people. He joined SenseTime in late 2015 and helped it win ImageNet while commuting weekly between Beijing and CUHK.

current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Vivix (AI, ~$1B valuation); role not publicly confirmed
